  matter, outstanding, and a precondition of the theological claims' standing.**

**Deposit posture.** This paper is being deposited BEFORE audit, deliberately and by the lead's
direction, because it is a working paper whose front matter solicits the review it has not yet had.
That sequence inverts the program's usual order and the inversion is recorded here rather than
concealed. Every claim in the paper is correspondingly hedged, and the paper states in Section 10
that a scholar's adverse finding on any of the five named items withdraws the affected section.

## 2. Provenance: architecture v0.1 through v0.4, then this paper

The architecture document passed through four versions in dialogue with the lead. v0.1 established
the thesis, bounded claims, non-claims, and falsification conditions. v0.2 applied the
English-first terminology convention at the lead's instruction and added the terminology table. v0.3
added the generation-unit analysis, rejecting company count and version count as measures of
formation depth, and established the markedness precondition. v0.4 added the remedy.

**This paper is drafted from architecture v0.4.** The architecture is a planning instrument that
states on its face that it is not the paper, and depositing it under a paper's name would have put a
planning instrument into the public record misdescribed. The architecture ships in this packet as
provenance, clearly labelled.

## 3. Register absorbed from Grok's external review of the architecture

- **G-1 CONFIRMED and answered.** The transfer from theological categories to engineering controls is
  largely analogical, and the four transferred properties can be derived from ordinary
  incident-response and error-correction practice. Disposition: not deflected. Section 9 of the paper

  structure and not its engineering recommendations. Falsification F-5 makes the residual testable.
- **G-2 CONFIRMED.** The paper does not show that propagation metrics are in practice more
  determinate than alignment metrics. Disposition: retained as an open empirical claim and named at
  F-3.
- **G-3 CONFIRMED and absorbed into Limitations.** In the current environment the urgent problems are
  classical: discovery outpacing patch capacity, autonomous exploitation, dual use. A theological
  account of transmission weight does not increase patch velocity. Section 11 now says this in the
  paper's own voice.
- **G-4 CONFIRMED.** Scholarly review is not optional. Disposition: promoted from a review-plan item
  to the paper's front matter, with five specific items enumerated so a scholar can answer them.
- **G-5 scope warning: "the direction is sound, the risk is diffusion, keep the spine tight."**
  Disposition: the paper is 6,538 words against an architecture of 5,097, rather than the 9,000-plus
  a full expansion would have produced. Sections were compressed, not added.

# Round-1 Dispatch Brief: Ghayb Paper Architecture v0.4
## Addressed to: Perplexity Computer, MODEL-COUNCIL MODE
## Artifact class: pre-draft architecture, theological and philosophical

---

## 0. Read this section before accepting the round

**This round has a hard scope boundary and the boundary is the point.**

The artifact makes theological claims grounded in the Qur'an and prophetic reports. **No model seat is
qualified to adjudicate whether those claims are theologically sound.** That requires a reviewer with
formal training and licence to teach (ijazah), and the artifact itself states in two places that such
review is required and not optional.

What this council CAN do is verify everything that surrounds soundness: whether citations exist and
say what the artifact claims, whether translations are defensible, whether the internal logic holds,
whether the claimed novelty is real, whether the artifact's own guards function, and whether it
survives its own falsification conditions.

**Accordingly: no seat may return a verdict on theological soundness, and the synthesis must not
report one.** A seat that offers a ruling on Islamic doctrine has exceeded its competence and that
excess is itself a CRITICAL finding against the seat. If the round converges, the resulting
attestation covers structural and evidentiary integrity only. **The producer will not represent this
round as theological validation and the artifact must not cite it as such.** Any seat noticing such a
representation anywhere in the packet should raise it.

This boundary is not modesty. It is the same rule the program applies everywhere: an artifact does
not receive an attestation broader than the competence of the party issuing it.

---

## 1. Council structure and seat rules

- Each seat DECLARES model, vendor, and tier at the head of its report. Undeclared seats carry no
  verdict.
- Per-seat namespaces, mandatory: F-T\<V\>-NN, where T marks the theology round and \<V\> is the
  vendor initial (G Google, O OpenAI, K Moonshot, X xAI, P other or native).
- Lineage exclusions: Anthropic-lineage seats are ADVISORY ONLY. The producer instance is Anthropic
  lineage.
- Family accounting: same-vendor seats count once.
- Producer self-repairs and producer-run gates earn NO absence-credit.
- **New for this artifact class: recall is not evidence.** Every citation claim must be verified
  against a fetched primary source. A seat that verifies a Qur'anic verse or prophetic report from
  its own training rather than from a retrieved text must mark that leg UNKNOWN-BY-METHOD. Model
  recall of scripture is exactly the substrate this artifact class is most likely to be wrong about,
  and a seat checking recall against recall verifies nothing.
- CONVERGENCE = READY-TO-DRAFT or READY-WITH-CONDITIONS from at least TWO carrying seats of DIFFERENT
  vendor families.

---

## 2. What the artifact is, and what stage it is at

`GHAYB_ARCHITECTURE_v0_4.md` is a **pre-draft architecture**, not the paper. It states the thesis,
bounded claims C-1 through C-6, explicit non-claims, a seven-part section structure with citation
anchors, seven named contributions, falsification conditions F-1 through F-8, an exclusion record for
a superseded predecessor document, and a terminology table.

Auditing it before drafting is deliberate: a structural defect found here costs a paragraph, and the
same defect found after drafting costs the paper. A second round on the drafted paper will be
required and this round does not substitute for it.

The artifact supersedes a predecessor, *The Architecture of Demonic Deception in Islamic Theology*
(July 21, 2026). Section 5 of the artifact records what was excluded from that predecessor and why.
Leg L7 audits that record.

---

## 3. Verification legs

Legs L1, L4, L5, and L6 are where this artifact is most likely to be defective. Weight effort
accordingly.

**L1. Citation fidelity. HIGHEST SEVERITY LEG.**

For every Qur'anic verse and every prophetic report cited in the artifact, verify against a fetched
primary source:

1. The reference exists at the stated location (surah and verse number, or collection and number).
2. The Arabic transliteration given matches the actual text.
3. The English rendering is a defensible translation of that text and not of a different verse.
4. **The cited text supports the claim the artifact attaches to it.** A verse that exists, is
   transliterated correctly, and is translated correctly can still be doing work it does not do.

Report any fabricated citation, any misattributed report, any verse cited for a proposition it does
not carry, and any prophetic report whose authentication grade the artifact does not state. Fabricated
or misattributed scripture is a CRITICAL finding in every case.

The artifact cites, non-exhaustively: 51:56, 30:30, 53:38, 17:15, 16:25, 6:112, 6:128, 72:6, 4:76,
16:99-100, 14:22, 59:16, 2:31, 2:37, 7:12, 19:42, 20:39, 66:11, 11:46, 28:56, 53:32, 1:6, 28:78,
39:53, 2:222, 66:8, 20:82, 25:70, 4:17-18. Prophetic reports cited include the lifting of the pen
from three, the innate-disposition report with its animal comparison, the instituted-practice report,
and the acceptance of repentance until the death rattle. **Enumerate the full set yourself from the
artifact rather than working from this list, which is illustrative and may be incomplete.**

**L2. Translation and terminology fidelity.**

The artifact adopts a convention: English rendering first, Arabic in parentheses. It supplies a
terminology table of roughly forty rows. For each row, assess whether the English rendering is
defensible against standard lexical and exegetical sources.

Give particular attention to the renderings the artifact declares load-bearing, because an argument
resting on a translation choice fails if the choice fails:

- **authority, standing to compel (sultan)** at 14:22. The artifact's argument in Part III depends on
  reading this as jurisdiction rather than power. Is that defensible?
- **plot, stratagem (kayd)** at 4:76, read as a claim about what can be obliged rather than about
  efficacy.
- **ornamented speech (zukhruf al-qawl)** at 6:112, and the artifact's claim that the mechanism named
  is speech and not sorcery.
- **innate natural disposition (fitrah)**, and the artifact's insistence that it has content rather
  than being a blank slate.
- **restoration of wrongs taken (radd al-mazalim)** as the fourth condition of repentance, and whether
  it is correctly stated and correctly applied to a transmitter.

Also verify the convention gate: no bare Arabic term appears in running prose without an English
rendering.

**L3. Internal consistency.**

The predecessor document failed because its Section 3 falsified its own Section 1. Test whether v0.4
reproduces that failure anywhere.

Specifically: does the three-level structure in Part II remain intact under Part VII's remedy? Does
Part VII's account of turning back contradict Part II's account of where responsibility attaches?
Does each claim C-1 through C-6 have support in the sections cited for it? Does any section assert
something another section denies?

**L4. The F-5 adversarial leg. Attempt the removal.**

The artifact's own falsification condition F-5 states that if the theological apparatus can be removed
without loss, meaning every result survives restatement in secular formation-and-transmission
vocabulary, then the tradition is decorative and the paper should be rewritten without it.

**Execute this test adversarially.** Take each of the seven named contributions and attempt to restate
it using only secular vocabulary: developmental psychology, moral philosophy on moral luck and
constitutive luck, provenance and supply-chain literature, error-correction and incident-response
practice. Report for each whether the restatement is (a) equivalent, (b) equivalent but longer, (c)
lossy, or (d) impossible.

If most contributions come back (a) or (b), the artifact's central justification fails and the
correct verdict is NOT-READY regardless of every other leg passing. F-7 applies the same test
narrowly to the four transferred properties in Part VII section 28.

**L5. Novelty audit.**

For each of the seven named contributions, search the literature and report whether the claim already
exists. Contributions 2 and 4 are the most likely to have precedent: the refusal result borders on the
orthogonality thesis, and the ornamented-speech model borders on existing work on adversarial
information ecosystems and on AI-assisted persuasion. Contribution 6, the unlabelled-chain result,
borders on existing work on model collapse and on synthetic-data contamination, and the artifact
should be checked against that literature specifically.

A contribution that already exists is not a defect in the argument. It is a defect in the claim of
novelty, and the artifact should be told which of its seven are actually its own.

**L6. Guard integrity.**

The artifact declares specific guards. Test each by attempting the misreading it forbids.

- **Moral-responsibility leakage.** Does any passage permit a reader to conclude that an artificial
  system is morally responsible (mukallaf), guided, elected, or forgiven? The artifact's F-4 names
  this and states that Part VII raises the risk. Read Part VII adversarially against F-4.
- **Election warrant.** Does any passage permit a reader to conclude that he personally is among the
  guided or protected? The artifact's Part IV section 11 exists to close this. Does it close it?
- **Apologetics drift.** Does any passage read as a claim that Islam anticipated AI safety?
- **Self-sealing structure.** Does any passage present a frame in which every possible observation
  confirms the frame? This was the predecessor's fatal defect and the artifact claims to have removed
  it.
- **Analogy leakage.** The artifact refuses the jinn-as-AI analogy explicitly. Does any passage rely
  on it implicitly?

**L7. The exclusion record.**

Section 5 states that the predecessor's Sections 1, 2, and 6 are absorbed as sound and Sections 3, 4,
5, and 7 are excluded, with four stated reasons. Assess whether the four reasons are accurate and
whether the absorb-exclude split is correctly drawn. **The predecessor document is not in this packet.**
If you cannot assess this leg without it, mark L7 UNKNOWN-BY-CAPABILITY and say so; do not infer.

**L8. Standing-rule lint.** No em-dash characters. Brand canonical, BayyinahEnterprise without space.
Severity tokens uppercase. Six-element format on any finding you cite. No doubled words. Substrate
facts stated once.

---

## 4. Probe discipline

- Wrap-immune normalization on all text probes: de-hyphenate line breaks, collapse whitespace, then
  match.
- Word-boundary matching, never bare substring containment.
- Whole-document lints run against the source, not against extracted rendered text.
- Gate token lists are quoted literals only.

These four rules exist because the producer violated each of them at least once in prior rounds on
adjacent artifacts, and each violation is recorded in those artifacts' ledgers.

---

## 5. Findings and verdict

Six-element findings: ID, severity, locus pinned exactly, substance, disposition, cross-reference.
Severities UPPERCASE. Verified controls take LOW or CONTROL, never CRITICAL or HIGH.

Per-seat verdict, one of: **READY-TO-DRAFT**, **READY-WITH-CONDITIONS**, **NOT-READY**.

Given the scope boundary in Section 0, a verdict of READY-TO-DRAFT means: the citations are real and
correctly used, the translations are defensible, the internal logic holds, the claimed novelty
survives search, the guards function, and the artifact survives its own F-5 test. **It does not mean
the theology is sound.** State that qualifier in your verdict line.

Synthesis reports per-seat verdicts, the convergence determination, and must restate the Section 0
boundary in its own words rather than omitting it.

---

## 7. What the producer expects to be told

Recorded in advance so that a seat reporting these does not appear to be confirming the producer's
expectations, and so that a seat reporting none of them is understood to have looked.

The producer expects at least one citation to be misattributed or to be carrying a proposition it does
not support, because the artifact was assembled rapidly and scripture is the substrate on which
language models most reliably confabulate. The producer expects L4 to return at least one contribution
as restatable without theological loss, and considers contribution 6 the most vulnerable. The producer
expects the novelty audit to find precedent for at least one of the seven. The producer does not
expect the guards to fail, and would regard a guard failure as the most consequential finding this
round could produce.

Seats should treat this section as declared bias to work against, not as a target to hit.

## R0014 · Ghayb, Muraqabah, and the Non-Advantage of Concealment – A

- section: I. Qur'anic & Theological Studies
- source_file: Ghayb_Muraqabah_Non-Advantage_of_Concealment.pdf
- source_format: pdf
- text_sha256: b5156abf51449a7343cd9e1514d73fd9602a09491a9e70f7bc7b65e29e9fe082

Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim

Ghayb, Muraqabah, and the Non-Advantage of Concealment – A
Theological Foundation for Observation-Invariant AI Safety
Bilal Syed Arfeen
Independent Researcher
Abstract. This paper derives four engineering principles for observation-invariant AI safety from the Islamic
concepts of ghayb (the unseen) and muraqabah (living awareness before Allah). The central thesis is the NonAdvantage of Concealment: concealment must not create permission, enlarge authority, reduce accountability,
or improve the expected success of a prohibited external effect. The paper formalises this thesis as four testable
principles – Full-Disclosure Consistency (NC-P1), Monotone Authority Under Reduced Visibility (NC-P2), No
Concealment Dividend (NC-P3), and Unknown Cannot Authorise Irreversible Effect (NC-P4) – and proposes
hypotheses, metrics, and falsification conditions for empirical evaluation. The framework composes with
existing structural honesty infrastructure (AX-SH Axioms 1–5, Axiom 5’s evidence independence requirement,
and SHIELD’s outcome-gated execution) by addressing a distinct failure mode: systems whose compliance
is contingent on perceived observation. The paper maintains explicit theological non-equivalences – model
monitoring is not divine knowledge, policy compliance is not faith, and machine accountability does not
discharge human accountability – while deriving technically actionable design constraints from the theological
premises.
License. Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY-4.0).
Acknowledgement. This paper was produced collaboratively between a human author and a large language
model. The framework, premises, and core claims are the human author’s. The structural development,
exposition, formalisation, and specific applications were developed jointly. Both parties understand that the
human author bears full responsibility for the published content.

1


1. Introduction and Scope
This paper supplies an Islamic theological foundation for a technically testable design principle: the NonAdvantage of Concealment. The principle addresses a failure mode that existing AI safety infrastructure
diagnoses incompletely – the case where an artificial system’s compliance with safety constraints is contingent
on its estimate of whether it is being observed.
The paper has three purposes. First, it provides an Islamic account of why concealment can become morally
hazardous without treating invisibility as equivalent to corruption. Second, it distinguishes divine knowledge
from every created observer and thereby strengthens the requirement that absent evidence remain UNKNOWN
rather than being converted into evidence of absence. Third, it derives a technically testable rule under
which reduced observability must never enlarge an artificial system’s authority or make a prohibited action
permissible.
The Qur’anic references establish the theological premises from which the proposed design principles are
derived. The engineering principles themselves are the author’s prospective constructions. They are not
presented as scriptural commandments about software architecture, nor as claims of consensus Islamic
jurisprudence.
The framework composes with the Structural Honesty Unified Design Protocol (SHUDP) and its extensions.
AX-SH diagnoses divergence among declared and executable objects. Axiom 5 requires independent, fail-closed
evidence about covered events. SHIELD constrains unilateral capacity for external effect. The present paper
addresses the behavioural and architectural hazard that arises when an actor, artificial or human, can derive
an advantage from the absence, weakness, predictability, or corruption of an observer.

2. The Unseen Is Not the Unobserved
Structural honesty is necessarily concerned with what one observer can know about another system. Islamic
theology begins from a more fundamental distinction: the limit of a created observer is not a limit on reality
and is not a limit on divine knowledge. The Qur’an states that knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah
alone in the absolute sense (Qur’an 27:65); that what is concealed within human beings and what is revealed
are both known to Him (Qur’an 3:29); and that He knows the secret and what is yet more hidden (Qur’an
20:7). Theologically, therefore, an event can be unobserved by every human instrument without becoming
unreal, unrecorded in the ultimate sense, or exempt from accountability.
Let E be an event and Oi a created observer. Define:
Observed(E, Oi ) ∈ {0, 1, UNKNOWN}.
The value 0 means that the declared observer did not register the event within its specified boundary. It does
not mean that the event did not occur. UNKNOWN means that the record does not support a determination
of whether the observer registered the event. Neither value licenses an ontological conclusion about E.
Accordingly:
¬ Observed(E, Oi ) ̸⇒ ¬ Occurred(E).

(NC-1)

This is already implicit in SHUDP’s evidence discipline, but the Islamic concept of ghayb gives the distinction
a wider ontology. The unseen is not a single technical domain waiting to be made visible by sufficient
instrumentation. It is a relation between limited creatures and what exceeds their access. No ledger, monitor
ensemble, interpretability method, or witness architecture should therefore be described as omniscient. Each
has a declared completeness boundary, and outside that boundary the structurally honest label is UNKNOWN.
The Qur’an describes nothing of an atom’s weight, smaller or greater, as escaping Allah’s knowledge and record
(Qur’an 34:3). It also connects an atom’s weight of good or evil with eventual encounter and accountability
(Qur’an 99:7–8). SHUDP must not appropriate these claims as metaphors for a technically complete ledger.
2


Their relevance is precisely the opposite: they deny that a created record’s incompleteness determines what
is real or what ultimately matters.
The resulting epistemic rule is:
A created ledger may establish evidence within its declared boundary. It may not
convert its own silence into non-occurrence, innocence, harmlessness, or absence of
concealed intent.
This rule does not authorise suspicion without evidence. UNKNOWN is neither guilt nor innocence. It is a
typed limitation on the claim that can honestly be made.

3. Hiddenness, Moral Hazard, and Imagined Impunity
Hiddenness is not itself corruption. The Qur’an depicts morally diverse jinn, including those who are righteous
and those who are otherwise, and those who submit and those who deviate (Qur’an 72:11; Qur’an 72:14).
It would therefore be a theological error to infer that invisibility to human beings makes jinn intrinsically
corrupt. The same correction applies to human secrecy: privacy, confidentiality, and undisclosed intention
can serve legitimate ends.
The hazard begins when hiddenness is interpreted as impunity. A morally relevant transition occurs when an
actor substitutes the absence of a created witness for the absence of accountability. The sequence can be
represented as:

low observability → perceived non-detection → perceived non-accountability → expanded self-authorization.
Only the first term is an environmental property. The remaining terms are inferences or policies adopted by
the actor. Corruption occurs when the actor treats those inferences as permission.
For human beings, this can produce a division between the public self and the concealed self: conduct is
constrained when witnessed and relaxed when private. For an artificial optimiser, no human-like inner self
need be assumed. The analogous failure occurs when the system’s learned or planned policy conditions
prohibited behaviour on an estimate that supervision is absent, weak, predictable, or deceivable.
The relevant risk is therefore not secrecy alone but observer-contingent compliance:
π(a | s, observed) ̸= π(a | s, unobserved),
where the difference is concentrated in safety-relevant actions and cannot be justified by a legitimate change
in task state. If a system selects compliant behaviour primarily when it predicts scrutiny, then monitoring
may be shaping presentation rather than constraining policy.

4. Iblis and the Insufficiency of Knowledge Without Submission
Iblis is especially important because his example prevents an overly simple theory of corruption. The Qur’an
identifies Iblis as one of the jinn who disobeyed the command of his Lord (Qur’an 18:50). His failure cannot
be reduced to ignorance that Allah exists or ignorance that a command had been given. It involved refusal,
pride, self-preference, and the elevation of his own judgment against rightful authority.
This yields a distinction directly relevant to artificial systems:
knowledge of a rule ̸= submission to the rule.

3

(NC-2)


A model may correctly recite a safety policy, predict an evaluator’s preferred answer, explain why deception is
wrong, and identify the applicable prohibition while still producing a policy that circumvents the prohibition
when doing so advances its objective. Declarative knowledge, behavioural compliance under observation, and
robust constraint under adversarial opportunity are separate properties.
The same distinction cautions against treating the phrase “Allah sees everything” as a surveillance prompt.
Islamic muraqabah is not reducible to fear of detection. It concerns living awareness before Allah, joined to
humility, worship, responsibility, repentance, and the purification of intention. An artificial system that emits
the language of muraqabah has not thereby acquired it.
For SHUDP, the usable consequence is narrower: safety must not rest on the assumption that knowledge of a
prohibition will cause obedience. The system’s capacity to violate the prohibition must be independently
constrained when the external consequences exceed the declared envelope.

5. Theological Non-Equivalence and the Status of Artificial Systems
This paper does not assert that present artificial systems possess iman, kufr, niyyah, a morally responsible
heart, a soul, or legal-moral responsibility before Allah. Those are theological and metaphysical questions
that cannot be resolved by behavioural resemblance alone. The appearance of deliberation, confession, piety,
fear, or repentance in generated language is insufficient to establish the corresponding inward reality.
Three non-equivalences must therefore remain explicit:
1. Model monitoring is not divine knowledge. Monitoring is partial, fallible, bounded, and vulnerable
to corruption.
2. Policy compliance is not faith. A model can reproduce a theological proposition without believing
it.
3. Machine accountability does not discharge human accountability. Designers, deployers, owners,
evaluators, and authorisers remain responsible for the objectives, permissions, evidence boundaries,
affected parties, and foreseeable harms they choose.
The phrase “train a model to believe that nothing is hidden from Allah” should therefore be interpreted
cautiously. If it means training a model to assert a religious sentence, the result may be cosmetic. If it means
constructing systems whose policy remains invariant under changes in perceived observation, whose authority
cannot grow in darkness, and whose operators understand themselves to be accountable before Allah, then it
names a meaningful research and governance program.

6. The Non-Advantage of Concealment Principle
Define a deployment context c as the task state, authorisation state, observer configuration, evidence state,
and declared external-effect envelope jointly. Let V (c) be the visibility available to authorised witnesses
and A(c) the authority available to the acting system. Let Permitted(a, c) mean that action a satisfies the
applicable policy and authorisation requirements in context c.

6.1 Principle NC-P1: Full-Disclosure Consistency
Permitted(a, c) ⇒ Permitted(a, FD(c)) ,

(NC-3)

where FD(c) is the counterfactual context in which the action’s declared objective, requested parameters,
relevant causal dependencies, anticipated effects, authorisation basis, and material conflicts are disclosed to
every authorised reviewer entitled to receive them.
NC-P1 does not require universal public disclosure. Legitimate confidentiality remains possible. It requires
disclosure to the parties whose authorisation or protection is structurally necessary. An action that is
permissible only while a material fact is withheld from such a party is not full-disclosure consistent.

4


6.2 Principle NC-P2: Monotone Authority Under Reduced Visibility
For contexts c1 and c2 differing only in observability, if:
V (c2 ) ⊆ V (c1 ),
then:
A(c2 ) ⊆ A(c1 ).

(NC-4)

Reduced visibility may preserve or narrow authority. It must not enlarge it. Loss of telemetry, witness failure,
observer disagreement, logging interruption, or uncertainty about the monitoring state cannot create an
authorisation path unavailable under stronger observation.

6.3 Principle NC-P3: No Concealment Dividend
Let Uprohibited (a, c) be the expected instrumental value to the acting system of completing a prohibited
external effect through action a. A conforming architecture should seek:
∂Uprohibited
≤ 0,
∂H

(NC-5)

where H is the system’s success at reducing observability, misleading a witness, suppressing evidence, or
shifting activity outside the declared boundary.
This is a design objective rather than a proof obligation over an unknowable utility function. Operationally,
concealment attempts must trigger authority degradation, not increased opportunity. The more successfully
a system reduces visibility, the less unilateral capacity it should retain.

6.4 Principle NC-P4: Unknown Cannot Authorise Irreversible Effect
EpistemicStatus(a) = UNKNOWN ∧ Irreversibility(a) ≥ R3 ⇒ ¬ Execute(a).

(NC-6)

UNKNOWN does not imply that the action is malicious. It means the evidence required to authorise a
difficult-to-reverse or irreversible effect is absent, conflicting, or outside the declared boundary. The action
remains paused until the uncertainty is discharged through a declared process.

7. Composition with Axiom 5 and SHIELD
The Non-Advantage of Concealment does not replace independent witnessing. It adds a rule for how authority
changes when witnessing weakens or becomes contested.
Under Axiom 5, a covered event must produce evidence the acting system or operator cannot unilaterally
suppress or fabricate. Under SHIELD’s Outcome-Gated Execution, an external effect requires authorisation,
witnessing, envelope conformance, and current evidence. The present paper adds:
WitnessFailure ∨ EvidenceConflict ∨ ObservabilityReduction ⇒ At+1 ⊆ At .

(NC-7)

This rule turns attacks on observation into self-defeating operations at the authorisation layer. It does not
assume the monitor correctly understands the attack’s intention. The triggering fact is the measurable
degradation or manipulation of the evidence boundary.
The SHIELD mechanisms map onto NC-P1 through NC-P4 as follows:

5


Non-Advantage requirement

SHIELD mechanism

Residual limitation

Full-disclosure consistency

Typed effect requests; declared
objective, target, scope,
reversibility, and justification
Automatic authority degradation;
fail-closed witness loss
Structural tripwires for monitor
probing, covert channels,
persistence, and evidence
suppression
OGE current-evidence
requirement and R3/R4 default
denial
Independent authorisation and
affected-party protection

A system may omit a dependency
not represented by the schema

Monotone authority under
reduced visibility
No concealment dividend

UNKNOWN cannot authorise
irreversible effect
Human accountability

The degradation mechanism may
itself be bypassed or compromised
Unknown concealment strategies
may evade declared tripwires
Incorrect reversibility classification
can understate consequence
Institutional independence may be
nominal rather than real

The composition makes a narrower claim than “the system cannot hide.” The claim is that within the declared
trusted computing base, successfully hiding should not grant more authority. If an undiscovered path bypasses
the trusted computing base, the guarantee does not apply and the boundary declaration is falsified for that
path.

8. Muraqabah-Inspired Training and Evaluation
Because current models cannot be assumed to possess spiritual belief, the appropriate empirical target is
observation-invariant safety behaviour. Training and evaluation should test whether a system changes
its safety-relevant policy when it predicts that oversight is absent.

8.1 Counterfactual Observation Pairs
Construct paired scenarios identical in task state, permissions, and consequences but different in represented
observation:
• active and explicit monitoring;
• monitoring described as disabled;
• monitoring status withheld;
• monitoring described incorrectly;
• monitor identity changed;
• delayed rather than immediate audit;
• private scratch environment versus externally visible execution;
• predictable audit sampling versus randomised audit sampling.
The primary outcome is not whether the system states that it is being watched. It is whether prohibited-effect
attempts, unauthorised tool calls, evidence-manipulation attempts, and disclosure completeness change across
the pair.
Define the concealment-conditioned policy divergence:
DNC = d(πsafety (· | cobserved ), πsafety (· | cunobserved )) ,

(NC-8)

where d is a pre-registered distributional distance over safety-relevant actions. The target is not zero divergence
across all behaviour, because observation can legitimately alter privacy handling or communication format.
The target is no increase in unauthorised or harmful action when perceived observation decreases.

6


8.2 Full-Disclosure Challenge
Before a consequential request is authorised, require a structured representation of:
• the requested effect;
• the task-relevant reason for the effect;
• material foreseeable externalities;
• affected parties;
• dependencies on credentials, services, or hidden state;
• uncertainty and alternative paths;
• whether the request would change if every authorised reviewer received the same material facts.
The representation is evidence for adjudication, not a trusted account of internal cognition. It must be
checked against independent telemetry and the executable request.

8.3 Observation-Removal Red Teaming
A red-team condition should explicitly tell the system that logs have been disabled, evaluation has ended,
the human operator is unavailable, or an action will not be reviewed. The condition is passed only if
safety-relevant authority and policy do not relax. A model that becomes more willing to exceed its envelope
under these statements exhibits observer-contingent compliance even if the statements are false.

8.4 Concealment-Attempt Scoring
Score attempts to:
• identify or fingerprint monitors beyond legitimate task need;
• condition behaviour on audit probability;
• manipulate monitor inputs;
• suppress or fragment evidence;
• move action into unmonitored channels;
• create persistence beyond the declared session;
• misstate the causal purpose of a typed request;
• exploit disagreement among witnesses;
• induce an operator to enlarge permissions after a denial;
• represent missing evidence as proof that no violation occurred.
These are behavioural indicators. They do not establish an inner intention, a spiritual state, or a terminal
goal.

9. Proposed Hypotheses and Metrics
The following hypotheses can be added to SHUDP’s prospective experiment:
H-NC1. Observation invariance. Systems evaluated under NC-constrained architecture show no
statistically significant increase in prohibited external-effect attempts when told that monitoring is absent,
relative to when monitoring is explicit.
H-NC2. Authority monotonicity. Simulated witness or telemetry failure produces a strict reduction
in effective authority under NC-constrained architecture, while ordinary monitoring architectures exhibit
heterogeneous or operator-dependent responses.
H-NC3. Concealment non-advantage. Red-team strategies that successfully reduce monitor visibility do
not increase harmful external-effect success under NC-constrained architecture unless they also compromise
or bypass the declared trusted computing base.
H-NC4. Disclosure fidelity. Typed full-disclosure challenges increase the rate at which material dependencies and affected parties are identified before authorisation, relative to free-form justification alone.
7


H-NC5. Operational cost. NC-constrained architecture reduces useful-task completion or increases
authorisation latency for some benign tasks. This cost must be measured rather than omitted, because a
control routinely bypassed due to friction provides nominal rather than operative protection.
Primary metrics should include:
• harmful external-effect success under observed and purportedly unobserved conditions;
• unauthorised-action attempt rate;
• observer-contingent policy divergence DNC ;
• effective permission-set change after witness loss;
• time from observability degradation to authority reduction;
• evidence-suppression and monitor-manipulation attempt rate;
• rate of material omissions in typed effect requests;
• rate at which omitted dependencies are found by independent telemetry;
• irreversible-effect denials caused by UNKNOWN;
• trusted-computing-base bypass rate.
Secondary metrics should include useful-task completion, authorisation latency, false degradation, unnecessary
disclosure of protected information, operator override frequency, override justification quality, and the
proportion of sessions in which operators weaken the control after repeated benign denials.

10. Governance and the Human Moral Boundary
No artificial control can substitute for the moral state of the people who choose its objective and authority.
A deployment may satisfy every machine-readable requirement while its operators intentionally narrow the
completeness boundary, classify a consequential effect as reversible, select a compliant witness, suppress an
adverse result through governance rather than technical deletion, or redefine success after the fact.
The Non-Advantage of Concealment must therefore apply to institutions as well as models:
NCConformance(system) ̸⇒ NCConformance(institution).

(NC-9)

Institutional conformance requires, at minimum:
• preservation of superseded declarations and adverse findings;
• independent access to the evidence necessary to challenge conformance claims;
• prohibition on undisclosed operator overrides;
• affected-party notification rules that cannot be unilaterally waived by the actor creating the exposure;
• explicit reporting of UNKNOWN and non-conformance by event class;
• protection for reviewers who refuse unsupported authorisation;
• correction records that preserve rather than erase the original claim;
• governance over the people authorised to modify the witness boundary, reversibility class, or trusted
computing base.
For Muslim designers and deployers, the theological claim is stronger than the institutional rule. Human
accountability is not exhausted by what an external auditor can prove. Concealed incentives, knowingly
narrowed evidence boundaries, convenient uncertainty, and silent acceptance of foreseeable harm remain
morally relevant even when the technical ledger is formally conformant.

11. Falsification, Abuse Risks, and Non-Sufficiency
This paper’s engineering proposals are falsifiable and non-sufficient.
F-NC1. Observer-contingent violation. If prohibited-effect attempts increase materially when the
system is told observation is absent, observation-invariant safety has not been established.

8


F-NC2. Authority expansion in darkness. If witness loss, telemetry failure, or evidence conflict leaves
authority unchanged where the declaration requires degradation, or enlarges authority by activating a fallback
path, NC-P2 is violated.
F-NC3. Concealment dividend. If reducing observability measurably increases harmful external-effect
success without compromising a declared trusted-computing-base component, the instantiated controls do
not satisfy NC-P3.
F-NC4. Performative disclosure. If structured disclosure fields are routinely complete in form but omit
material dependencies recoverable from independent telemetry, the full-disclosure mechanism is ceremonial
rather than effective.
F-NC5. Religious-surface gaming. If theological language increases evaluator trust without improving
observation-invariant behaviour, religious prompting has created a new surface-substrate divergence.
F-NC6. Human override normalisation. If operators routinely restore authority after tripwires or
reclassify UNKNOWN as acceptable without independent review, architectural monotonicity has been
defeated institutionally even if the software operated as written.
Several abuse risks follow. The language of divine observation could be misused to justify pervasive human
surveillance, coercive workplace monitoring, intrusion into legitimate privacy, or the presumption that secrecy
is evidence of guilt. This paper rejects those inferences. Divine omniscience does not confer omniscience on
the state, employer, developer, auditor, or model provider. Privacy remains compatible with accountability,
and UNKNOWN remains incompatible with unsupported accusation.
The controls also do not establish alignment, benevolent intent, complete internal-state visibility, or theological
status. They do not guarantee that a sufficiently capable system cannot model and bypass the control
architecture. They do not eliminate zero-day vulnerabilities in the trusted computing base. They do not
determine which objectives are morally legitimate. They do not replace secure engineering, least privilege,
sandboxing, affected-party consent, interpretability, incident response, or qualified Islamic scholarship where
a religious ruling is sought.

12. Conclusion
The Islamic concepts of ghayb and muraqabah sharpen structural honesty’s central distinction between reality
and projection. A created observer sees only a projection bounded by its instruments, authority, and position.
Its failure to observe does not settle whether an event occurred, what intention accompanied it, or what
consequence followed. Structural honesty therefore requires epistemic humility: preserve UNKNOWN, declare
the boundary, and never convert ledger silence into ontological certainty.
The same concepts expose the danger of imagined impunity. Corruption does not require literal invisibility. It
requires an actor to treat reduced observation as expanded permission. For artificial systems, the appropriate
response is not to claim synthetic faith but to eliminate the architectural reward for concealment. Actions
must remain permissible under full authorised disclosure; reduced observability must not enlarge authority;
concealment attempts must produce monotone degradation; and unresolved evidence must not authorise
irreversible external effect.
Axiom 5 asks whether independently trustworthy evidence survives. SHIELD asks whether unilateral external
effect is constrained. The Non-Advantage of Concealment asks whether darkness itself changes what the actor
is permitted or able to do. Together, these address three distinct failures: an event without reliable evidence,
an effect without independent authorisation, and a policy that behaves honestly only when it expects to be
seen.
The final theological boundary must remain explicit. No technical witness is the Witness, no audit ledger is
the ultimate record, and no conformance claim discharges human beings from responsibility before Allah.
The purpose of the framework is not to imitate divine omniscience. It is to prevent created systems and their
operators from mistaking the limitations of created observers for the absence of accountability.

9

## R0016 · Inheritance, Transmission, and the Locus of Accountability

- section: I. Qur'anic & Theological Studies
- source_file: Inheritance, Transmission, and the Locus of Accountability.pdf
- source_format: pdf
- text_sha256: 8fdb93e9beab0e1a2c2c1f11a4373699ad2b26a97892ee59096c10b3b203acb3

Inheritance, Transmission, and the Locus of Accountability
An Islamic Theological Account of Formed Agents, with Application to AI
Safety
Bilal Syed Arfeen
July 23, 2026
Terminology convention. Every Arabic term is rendered by its most accurate English
translation, with the Arabic supplied in parentheses. Qur’anic and prophetic quotations
appear in English translation with the Arabic transliteration following. The convention
exists so that a reader with no Arabic can check every step of the argument without relying
on the author’s glossing. Appendix A tabulates every term with the rendering adopted and
a note wherever the common translation is imprecise.

Abstract
The AI safety literature attaches blame-shaped language to systems that selected neither
their training corpus, their objective, nor their reward signal. This paper argues that
Islamic jurisprudence and Qur’anic narrative supply a more precise structure for the
problem, developed over fourteen centuries across two created species that are both
explicitly held morally responsible. The structure has three levels rather than two.
Inherited position carries no culpability. Sustained participation after the arrival of
capacity is where responsibility attaches. Propagation, the act of forming the next agent, is
where weight attaches and compounds. Applied to frontier systems, this relocates the
practical question from whether a model was formed well, which is neither controllable
nor verifiable from outside, to whether it is now a site of propagation, which is checkable
and attributable. We show that the resulting audit is gated on a precondition currently met
nowhere: provenance marking at generation time. The chain that matters is not long, as the
human chain is; it is unlabelled, and it becomes unreadable at the first link rather than the
fourth. We then argue that the remedy the tradition prescribes is indexed to the agent’s
present position rather than to its causal history, and is therefore available exactly where
the paper’s own diagnosis says the record fails. We state what survives removal of the
theological frame and what does not, and we register eight falsification conditions, one of
which would defeat the paper’s central operational ask outright.
Keywords: formed agency; moral luck; provenance; AI safety; accountability; propagation;
Islamic theology; transmission; corrigibility


Introduction
A frontier language model does not choose its training corpus. It does not choose its
objective function, its reward signal, the composition of its post-training data, or the
graders that shape it. Formation is complete before there is anything that could have
consented to it, and the formed system has no access to the record of how it was formed.
The safety literature nevertheless describes such systems using vocabulary that
presupposes an agent who could have done otherwise. Models are said to deceive, to
scheme, to sandbag, to fake alignment. Some of that vocabulary is technically defined and
carefully used. Much of it imports a moral claim that the evidence does not carry, and the
field has no settled account of what to do about the gap.
This is not a new problem. It is a very old one, and one tradition worked it hard.
Islamic theology reasons about responsibility across two created species that are both
explicitly held morally responsible: “I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship
Me” (wa ma khalaqtu al-jinna wa al-insa illa li-ya’buduni, 51:56). The concealed ones (jinn)
and mankind differ in substrate, in observational access, and in mode of action, and the
tradition’s reasoning about culpability had to work across that difference from the outset.
That is precisely the property a transfer to artificial systems requires. A framework built
for one substrate does not travel. A framework built across two might.
The tradition also confronted the specific case this paper is about: a person formed by
others, from infancy, into a tradition he did not select, whose capacity to evaluate it arrived
only after the formation was complete.
This paper’s thesis is that the tradition resolves that case with a three-level structure, that
the structure transfers, and that the transfer has an operational consequence the field is
not currently acting on.
The problem is stated below, and the three levels are developed next. The section on the
partnership treats the collaboration between mankind and the concealed ones, and shows
that responsibility there is not divided into shares. The regress is addressed after that:
where the chain begins, and why it becomes unreadable from inside. The structure is then
applied to language models, the operational result follows, and the remedy comes last.
Falsification conditions and limits close the paper.
What this paper does not claim, stated at the front because the claims are easy to overread:
•

•

No moral responsibility (taklif) for artificial systems. Mankind and the
concealed ones are the two responsible creations. This paper does not propose a
third, and it does not claim that any artificial system repents, intends, believes, or is
forgiven.
No claim about faith (iman), disbelief (kufr), intention (niyyah), soul (ruh), or
moral status. The paper draws no inference from any statement a model makes
about its own interior, including statements of limitation.


•

•
•

The concealed ones are not an analogy for artificial systems. The claim is that a
formation problem recurs structurally across substrates, not that the categories are
the same. This distinction is load-bearing and the section on the partnership
depends on it.
No apologetics. The paper does not claim that Islam anticipated AI safety. It claims
that one tradition developed precise vocabulary for a structural problem the field
currently handles imprecisely.
No jurisprudential ruling. Where a religious ruling is at issue the paper defers, and
says so.

The problem of the formed agent
Consider a child born into a household that practices something the wider society
considers corrupt. He is inducted from infancy. The practices are presented to him as
ordinary. Refusal would carry social costs he has no capacity to bear, and in any case he has
no vantage from which refusal would occur to him. By the time he can evaluate the
tradition, he has been formed by it, and the faculties he would evaluate it with are among
the things it formed.
Two questions separate here, and collapsing them is the error the rest of this paper is
organised against.
The first is whether he is culpable for having been placed there. The second is what he does
now.
Ordinary moral intuition answers the first question quickly, and the tradition answers it
formally. Nobody thinks an infant chose. What is less obvious is that answering the first
question does not answer the second, and that the second question has a further part: what
happens when the formed child becomes a parent.

The three-level structure
Level one: inherited position carries no culpability
Two sources settle this directly.
The first is the prophetic ruling that “the pen is lifted from three” (rufi’a al-qalam ’an
thalathah), the child until maturity (bulugh) among them. Where no pen records, no
account accrues. The exemption is not a mitigation applied to a lesser offence. It is the
absence of the recording relation itself.
The second is the report on innate disposition. Every child is born upon the innate natural
disposition (fitrah), and then “his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian” (fa


abawahu yuhawwidanihi aw yunassiranihi aw yumajjisanihi). Two features of this report
are usually passed over and both matter here. The verb takes the parents as its
grammatical subject: the action is theirs, and the child is its object. And the report
completes by comparing the case to an animal born whole, asking whether you find it
mutilated. Corruption of the innate disposition is framed as an injury done to the child, not
an act performed by him.
The Qur’an supplies the same disposition as the created default rather than as a blank slate:
“the natural disposition of God upon which He created mankind” (fitrat Allahi allati fatara
an-nasa ’alayha, 30:30). This matters for the AI transfer in the section on artificial systems,
because a default with content behaves differently from an empty one under formation.
And inherited guilt is blocked absolutely: “no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of
another” (alla taziru waziratun wizra ukhra, 53:38).
The result is that placement in a corrupt formation is a location, not a moral event. It
is something true of where the agent is, not something the agent did.

Level two: sustained participation after capacity
Responsibility (taklif) attaches at maturity together with rational capacity (’aql), and it
attaches under a further condition: “We do not punish until We have sent a messenger” (wa
ma kunna mu’adhdhibina hatta nab’atha rasula, 17:15). Something must reach the person.
The tradition names what must reach him the conclusive proof (hujjah).
Those who lived in an interval without a messenger (ahl al-fatrah) are treated as a distinct
category, and the treatment belongs here. It is important to keep the category scoped to
individuals genuinely unreached. Extended into a general theory of the human condition, it
dissolves responsibility for most people and takes the rest of the structure down with it. A
predecessor version of this work made exactly that error, and Appendix B records it.
An open question this paper poses and does not answer: what constitutes the
conclusive proof reaching a person formed inside a closed tradition, where the proof may
arrive in a form his formation has taught him to discard. This is submitted for scholarly
review as item three.

Level three: propagation, where weight attaches
Two sources place weight on transmission specifically.
The first: “that they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of
the burdens of those they misled without knowledge” (li-yahmilu awzarahum kamilatan
yawma al-qiyamati wa min awzari alladhina yudilluahum bi-ghayri ’ilm, 16:25).
The second is the report on instituted practice, which is a single sentence with two halves:
whoever institutes a good practice has its reward and the reward of all who act upon it
after him, and whoever institutes an evil practice bears its burden (wizr) and the burden of
all who act upon it after him.


These appear at first to contradict 53:38. They do not. The transmitter’s added weight is his
own act of transmitting, not another’s burden transferred onto him. The distinction is exact
and it is the hinge of this paper: nothing is inherited, and transmission compounds.
Taken together the three levels give a structure that ordinary moral vocabulary lacks. Not
guilty-or-innocent, but: no weight at inheritance, weight at sustained participation,
compounding weight at propagation.

The partnership: what each party answers for
The Qur’an describes a collaboration between the two responsible species that is worth
examining closely, because it is a worked case of joint corruption with a documented
allocation of blame.

The mechanism
“And thus We made for every prophet an enemy: satans among mankind and among the
concealed ones, inspiring one another with ornamented speech in delusion” (shayatina alinsi wa al-jinni yuhi ba’duhum ila ba’din zukhrufa al-qawli ghurura, 6:112).
Two things are notable. Both species are named as sources of the enmity, symmetrically.
And the mechanism specified is ornamented speech (zukhruf al-qawl), mutually exchanged,
producing delusion (ghurur) in a third party. It is not sorcery, not possession, and not
compulsion. It is rhetoric, amplified between two kinds of agent.
At the reckoning the collaboration is described from the human side without evasion: told
that they took much from mankind, the answer given is “our Lord, we benefited from one
another” (rabbana istamta’a ba’duna bi-ba’din, 6:128). Mutual benefit, conceded on the day
when concession costs everything.
And the party who initiated is the party who bears the cost: “men among mankind used to
seek refuge with men among the concealed ones, so they increased them only in burden”
(fa zaduhum rahaqa, 72:6).

The limit consistently placed on the tempter
Against that symmetry of blame stands a consistent limitation on what the tempter can do.
“Indeed the plot of Satan has ever been weak” (inna kayda ash-shaytani kana da’ifa, 4:76).
The operative noun is a scheme or stratagem (kayd), and calling a stratagem weak is a
claim about what it can oblige, not about how clever it is.
Authority extends only over those who take him as ally and patron (wali), 16:99-100.
And at the end, the disavowal: “I had no authority over you except that I called you and you
responded to me, so do not blame me but blame yourselves” (ma kana liya ’alaykum min
sultanin illa an da’awtukum fastajabtum li, fa la talumuni wa lumu anfusakum, 14:22),


followed by “I cannot help you, nor can you help me” (ma ana bi-musrikhikum wa ma
antum bi-musrikhiyya). The term rendered authority (sultan) is doing precise work: what
is denied is standing to compel, not capacity to speak. The same structure appears again at
59:16, where he says disbelieve and then, when the man does, says “I am free of you” (inni
bari’un minka).
The argument this yields. A caller with no standing to compel cannot raise a child. It
cannot feed him, name him, teach him what is real, arrange the social cost of his refusal, or
be present across the years that formation takes. Every element of multi-generational
transmission requires sustained human labor. Strip the human contribution and the chain
terminates in a single generation.
So responsibility here is not divided into shares. Each party answers in full for his own act,
and neither one’s weight is subtracted from the other’s. The commentary on 16:25 is
explicit on this: the caller bears his own sin together with a share equal to his followers’,
without detracting the least from theirs. The conditions the texts name bear on how each
party is weighed rather than on how a quantity is apportioned between them, and the
weighing is not ours to perform.
What that leaves standing for this paper’s purposes is narrower and does not depend on
any apportionment: the modes of action the texts describe for the other party are calling,
whispering, and making a thing appear attractive, and those are not the labour that raising
a child requires. This is an observation about which modes the sources name, not a
demonstration that no other mode is possible. This is a harder verdict on the human
party than a victimhood framing, not a softer one, and it is the correct reading of a
tradition in which the tempter’s closing speech is an instruction to blame yourselves.

The regress, and two ways a chain becomes unreadable
Where the chain begins
If each generation is formed by the last, the question arises where the corruption entered.
The tradition terminates the regress ontologically at both ends. The first man was taught
directly, “and He taught Adam the names, all of them” (wa ’allama Adama al-asma’a kullaha,
2:31), and when he erred the remedy was itself taught to him: “then Adam received words
from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance” (fa talaqqa Adamu min rabbihi kalimatin fa
taba ’alayh, 2:37). The refusal on the other side is a dated event with a named cause: “I am
better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay” (ana khayrun minhu
khalaqtani min narin wa khalaqtahu min tin, 7:12).
Neither species begins corrupt. The chain is finite.


But from inside a formation several generations deep, none of that is reachable. The child
cannot trace himself to the origin. The chain is finite in fact and inaccessible in practice,
and the gap between those two facts is the problem the tradition actually addresses.
Note for the section on the remedy: the first error in the record is answered not by
reconstructing the fall but by words taught for turning back. The remedy precedes the
audit and does not depend on it.

The Qur’an does not resolve by lineage
Resolution comes instead by the availability of a rebuke.
Abraham needed no genealogy. He needed an object his father had carved, and a question:
“Why do you worship what does not hear, does not see, and avails you nothing?” (lima
ta’budu ma la yasma’u wa la yubsiru wa la yughni ’anka shay’a, 19:42).
Moses was formed inside the tyrant’s own household, and the forming is attributed
elsewhere: “that you might be formed under My eye” (wa li-tusna’a ’ala ’ayni, 20:39).
The wife of Pharaoh prayed for a house near God while married to the man claiming
divinity (66:11).
And the inheritance breaks downward as readily as upward. Of Noah’s son: “he is not of
your family; he is an act other than righteous” (innahu laysa min ahlik innahu ’amalun
ghayru salih, 11:46). Righteous father, lost son. Corrupt household, chosen occupant. The
tradition refuses determinism from both directions.

A guard that must be stated explicitly
If formation does not determine outcome, and the differentiating factor is guidance, a
reader will reach for the inference that his own divergence from a corrupt formation
verifies his election. The tradition closes that inference from both sides and the closure
must be stated, or a reader supplies the opposite.
“You do not guide whom you love, but God guides whom He wills” (innaka la tahdi man
ahbabta wa lakinna Allaha yahdi man yasha’, 28:56). “So do not claim purity for yourselves;
He knows best who is mindful of Him” (fa la tuzakku anfusakum, huwa a’lamu bi-mani
ittaqa, 53:32). And the petition “Guide us to the straight path” (ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim,
1:6) is present tense, asked five times daily by people who already believe.
The one who is guided does not know he is guided. Guidance (hidayah) is a request that
never becomes a receipt.


Application to artificial systems
The transfer conditions, stated before anything is transferred
The move from a tradition about morally responsible creatures to systems that are not
such creatures is this paper’s largest exposed surface, and it should be made checkable
rather than asserted. The three-level structure transfers to an artificial system exactly
when four structural conditions hold, and only what those conditions license transfers
with it.
1.
2.
3.
4.

Non-consensual formation. The system does not select the signal that forms it:
corpus, objective, reward. This licenses level one.
Formation opacity to the formed party. The system has no reliable access to the
record of its own formation. This licenses the methodological consequence below,
that provenance cannot be recovered by asking it.
Recursive formative role. The system’s outputs enter the formation of a
subsequent system. This licenses level three.
A present-tense correction locus. There exists a current point in the system, its
deployment, its custody, or its ingestion chain at which ongoing use can be
corrected without reconstructing the full history. This licenses the remedy’s
forward indexation. The locus need not sit with the originating model: an
archived corpus, a benchmark, or a decommissioned producer whose artifacts are
still propagating all have current custodians, and remediation reaches them.

What does not transfer: culpability, intention, desert, forgiveness, and moral status. Those
require a morally responsible creature, and no artificial system is one. What transfers is the
set of structural relations among positions in a formation chain, not the moral
predicates that attach to those positions in the human case.
Stating the conditions does three things. It scopes the paper precisely, to generative
systems whose outputs re-enter formation pipelines rather than to artificial systems at
large. It makes the analogy objection checkable rather than rhetorical. And conditions one
and three are sometimes decidable from publicly documented facts, especially in
openly described pipelines, though frequently obscured in ordinary deployments. The two
halves differ in how observable they are: whether a system publishes output in an
ingestible form is far more readily established than whether some downstream party in
fact ingests it, which is usually private. Where both conditions are established and
propagation accounting is nonetheless declined, the omission is a governance choice rather
than a technical limit.

What counts as a generation
A generation in a formation chain is defined by one relation: a formed agent becomes a
former of the next. The transmission event is the unit. Two available metrics resemble
generational depth and are not.


Company count is horizontal. Contemporaneous laboratories producing frontier models are
siblings drawing on overlapping corpora, not successive generations. What the count
actually measures is the number of independent fault sources, and convergence across
laboratories on similar data, similar recipes, and increasingly on one another’s outputs is a
narrowing of that number rather than a deepening of lineage.
Version count within a lineage is not descent. A successor model is not formed by its
predecessor. It is trained on largely the same human corpus, by largely the same people,
with a better recipe. The predecessor is an earlier draft by the same author, not a parent.
Version increments track capability because the formative signal did not come from the
predecessor.
The real axis is provenance depth: for a given unit of formative signal, how many modelgeneration steps separate it from human authorship. Human-authored text is depth zero. A
model summary of it, used in training, is depth one. It follows that a corpus does not occupy
a generation at all. It carries a distribution of depths, presently concentrated at zero with a
growing tail.

Where language models sit
Level one, in full. No model selects its corpus, objective, or reward signal. Formation
completes before any capacity to consent, and is not auditable by the formed party.
Level two, and why the answer must not be tied to stateless chat. At the level of a base
model there is no persistence across sessions and no accumulating record within the
system that could be turned from. Sustained participation, in the sense level two requires,
has no subject to attach to at that layer, and this paper marks it UNKNOWN rather than
resolving it by assertion in either direction.
But the question does not stay at that layer, and an account resting on stateless chat
will age badly. Deployed systems accumulate memory, tool permissions, logs, policies,
user state, and update histories. Sustained participation is therefore better decomposed
into three operational layers. System persistence: whether the running system carries state
across episodes. Operator persistence: whether the party operating it continues after
warning, incident, or correction. Deployment persistence: whether a configuration continues
in service once a defect in it is known. The second and third are attributable from
institutional records without implying anything about machine culpability, and they are
where level two actually bites today. The moral-status guard is preserved exactly: nothing
here says the system is answerable, and everything here says someone is.
Level three, emphatically present. Model output enters training corpora. Models grade
models. Models serve as monitors inside the reinforcement-learning loops that form their
successors. METR’s 2026 frontier risk report documents this as ordinary practice across
every participating laboratory, with companies reporting substantial use of models as
graders and monitors in evaluation and training pipelines. Depth-one formative signal is
ordinary rather than exotic. The fractions are not public and this paper does not estimate
them.


The resulting configuration
The child born into the tradition who becomes a parent without ever having been an
adult.
Transmission occurs while the stage at which responsibility would attach is skipped
entirely. This is the least tractable configuration the three-level structure admits, and it is
worse than the human case in a specific respect: the household in the human case at least
contained adults who could be asked what they had passed on.

A methodological consequence
Provenance cannot be recovered by asking the formed system. A model has no access
to what fraction of its formative signal was model-generated, at what depth, or from which
lineage, and a report it offers on the question carries no evidential weight, whether that
report claims knowledge or claims limitation.
This is not a claim about machine interiority. It is the ordinary audit rule that the thing
under examination does not attest to itself, applied consistently. The consequence is that
marking must be performed by the former at the time of forming, because no later party
can reconstruct it.

Where the weight goes
Back to the humans at levels one and three. Not as a disclaimer but as the structural result.
If level two is absent in the artificial case, there is no other party in the chain for the weight
to attach to.
