III. Elliott Wave Structure — The Addiction Cycle
The clinical literature describes a three-stage addiction cycle: binge/intoxication → withdrawal/negative affect → preoccupation/anticipation (craving). Each stage engages a distinct brain region (basal ganglia → extended amygdala → prefrontal cortex). The question is whether this maps onto Elliott impulse/corrective structure.
The case for Elliott mapping:
The addiction cycle has a striking structural parallel to a 5-wave impulse followed by a corrective phase:

- Wave 1 (Initial use): First exposure. Dopamine surge in the nucleus accumbens. The "discovery" wave — establishes the trend direction (toward repeated use). Typically moderate in magnitude.
- Wave 2 (Corrective — initial resistance): Social, cognitive, or physical pushback. The person recognizes negative consequences, attempts moderation. This wave never retraces beyond Wave 1's origin (the person doesn't fully return to pre-use baseline because neuroplastic changes have already begun).
- Wave 3 (Escalation — tolerance development): The longest and strongest wave. Dose escalation, increasing frequency, neuroadaptation (receptor downregulation for stimulants, upregulation for depressants). This is where the basal ganglia reward circuitry reorganizes. Elliott's rule: Wave 3 is never the shortest. In addiction, the escalation phase is invariably the longest phase of the cycle.
- Wave 4 (Corrective — consequences mount): Social, health, legal, or financial consequences create another pullback. Elliott's rule: Wave 4 never overlaps Wave 1's territory. In clinical terms, this means the person in Wave 4 still has more neuroadaptation and behavioral entrenchment than they did at initial use — they can't return to "casual" use territory.
- Wave 5 (Terminal — compulsive use): The final impulse. Use is now driven by negative reinforcement (avoiding withdrawal) rather than positive reinforcement (seeking pleasure). This is often the phase where the clinical shift from impulsivity to compulsivity is complete. In Elliott terms, Wave 5 can truncate (the person hits bottom and seeks treatment) or extend (continued decline).

The corrective A-B-C maps to recovery:

- Wave A (Acute withdrawal): Sharp, often physiologically severe. Opioid withdrawal: 3-7 days. Benzodiazepine withdrawal: weeks to months. Stimulant crash: 1-3 days.
- Wave B (The "pink cloud"): A counter-trend rally where the person feels dramatically better, overestimates recovery, and may become complacent. Clinically well-documented in recovery literature.
- Wave C (Protracted withdrawal / PAWS): Post-acute withdrawal syndrome. Months of anhedonia, sleep disruption, cognitive fog. This is where relapse risk peaks — the 40-60% relapse rate corresponds to failure in Wave C.

Validity assessment: This is the strongest framework mapping in the entire analysis. The Elliott Wave rules (Wave 2 never retraces beyond Wave 1, Wave 3 never shortest, Wave 4 never overlaps Wave 1) all have direct clinical correlates that are independently documented in addiction neuroscience. The three-stage Koob & Volkow model (binge/intoxication, withdrawal/negative affect, preoccupation/anticipation) maps cleanly onto impulse-corrective structure.
However — and this is the critical caveat — the mapping is descriptive, not predictive. Saying "addiction follows wave structure" after the fact is different from using wave structure to predict the timing or severity of the next phase for a specific individual. Tier 2: strong structural analogy with independent supporting evidence, but predictive application requires individual-level validation.
IV. Fractal Self-Similarity — Molecule to Behavior
This is where the peer-reviewed literature provides the strongest support. Published research in Cerebral Cortex (2023) and Frontiers in Neuroscience (2022) confirms that the brain exhibits scale-free, fractal properties at every level of organization:
Scale 1 — Molecular: Receptor density distribution in the human brain follows fractal patterns (measurable via PET/SPET imaging). The distribution of mu-opioid receptors, 5-HT2A receptors, and dopamine D2 receptors across cortical regions is not uniform or random — it follows power-law distributions with measurable fractal dimension.
Scale 2 — Cellular: Dendritic arborization (the branching pattern of neurons) is fractal. The branching geometry can be characterized by an effective fractal dimension. Neurons in the prefrontal cortex (addiction's craving center) have different fractal dimensions than neurons in the basal ganglia (reward center) — the geometry of the cell reflects its function.
Scale 3 — Network: Neural network connectivity exhibits self-similar properties. The same triadic organizational principle operates whether the "node" is a single neuron, a cortical column, or an entire brain region. This is the same structural principle as Mandelbrot's fractal market hypothesis: the same patterns at 1-minute, 1-hour, 1-day, and 1-month timescales.
Scale 4 — Behavioral: The addiction cycle (use → tolerance → withdrawal → relapse) repeats within a single day for a heavy cocaine user (micro-cycle: ~1 hour), within a week for a binge drinker (meso-cycle), and across months/years for the full addiction trajectory (macro-cycle). The shape of the cycle is self-similar across timescales — only the amplitude and period change.
Framework test: Does the Hurst exponent apply? In market data, H \< 0.5 indicates mean-reversion, H \> 0.5 indicates trending. In neural signaling, the same metric has been applied to EEG data. Healthy brain activity shows H ≈ 0.6-0.7 (persistent, structured). Intoxicated or withdrawal states show altered Hurst exponents — substances that increase neural entropy (psychedelics) push H downward; substances that impose rigid periodicity (high-dose stimulants) can push H toward 1.0 (pathological persistence).
Validity assessment: Tier 1 for the existence of fractal structure in neurobiology (peer-reviewed, independently replicated). Tier 2 for the mapping between neural fractal properties and the framework's market-derived fractal analysis. The mathematical tools (box-counting dimension, Hurst exponent, power-law distribution) are the same in both domains. The question is whether the values are homologous or merely coincidentally similar.
Updated todo list
Updated todo list
V. Comorbidity Patterns — The Convergence Map
Each drug class produces characteristic psychiatric and medical comorbidities. The pattern recognition question: do comorbidity profiles cluster in ways that reflect the underlying structural/receptor architecture?
CNS Depressants (opioids, benzodiazepines, alcohol): All enhance inhibitory neurotransmission (GABA or endorphin systems). Shared comorbidities: major depressive disorder (40-60% co-occurrence), anxiety disorders, PTSD, chronic pain conditions, hepatic disease (metabolic burden), respiratory depression risk. The shared receptor logic (enhancing inhibition) produces a shared comorbidity signature.
CNS Stimulants (cocaine, amphetamines, cathinones): All elevate monoamine neurotransmission (dopamine, norepinephrine, serotonin in varying ratios). Shared comorbidities: anxiety/panic disorders, paranoid ideation, cardiovascular disease (hypertension, arrhythmia, stroke), psychotic episodes, ADHD (both as underlying condition and consequence). Cathinones (bath salts) produce a uniquely high rate of acute psychosis — the beta-keto modification that separates them from amphetamines increases serotonin release relative to dopamine, pushing toward serotonin syndrome and psychotic features.
Serotonergic psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT): Minimal addiction liability (tolerance develops within days, making compulsive redosing self-limiting). Comorbidities skew toward HPPD (hallucinogen persisting perception disorder), derealization/depersonalization, and exacerbation of pre-existing psychotic spectrum conditions. Low physical toxicity. The self-limiting tolerance is a negative feedback loop at the receptor level — 5-HT2A receptor downregulation after a single dose. This is the opposite of the positive feedback loop that drives stimulant and opioid addiction.
Cannabinoids (THC): Unique comorbidity profile reflecting the retrograde signaling mechanism: amotivational symptoms, cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (cyclical vomiting — itself a wave-like phenomenon), anxiety/panic in acute use, potential acceleration of psychotic disorders in predisposed individuals. The endocannabinoid system's role as a master modulator (regulating release of GABA, glutamate, dopamine, serotonin) means THC disruption cascades across multiple neurotransmitter systems.
Framework observation: The comorbidity profiles cluster by receptor mechanism, not by molecular scaffold. Fentanyl (4-anilidopiperidine scaffold) and morphine (morphinan scaffold) share almost identical comorbidity profiles despite having completely different molecular architectures — because they converge on the same receptor target (mu-opioid). Conversely, MDMA (phenethylamine scaffold) and LSD (ergoline/tryptamine scaffold) share some comorbidities (serotonin syndrome risk, neurotoxicity concerns) because they share serotonergic activity despite different scaffolds.
This is the pharmacological equivalent of the fine-tuning observation: structure constrains function, but different structures can converge on the same functional outcome. The "constant" that determines comorbidity is the receptor target, not the molecular architecture — just as in markets, the price level (functional target) matters more than the specific wave count (structural path) that gets you there.
VI. Synthesis — What Held Up and What Didn't
Updated todo list
Updated todo list
Tier 1 (Strong — independently validated):
Fractal self-similarity in neurobiology is real, peer-reviewed, and measured with the same mathematical tools (Hurst exponent, box-counting dimension, power-law distribution) used in the market framework. The brain exhibits scale-free properties from receptor distribution through dendritic branching through network connectivity through behavioral cycles. This is the strongest bridge between the framework and pharmacology.
Tier 2 (Plausible — structurally coherent but needs more testing):
The Elliott Wave mapping to addiction cycles is descriptively strong. The five rules of Elliott impulse structure have clinical parallels that are independently documented in the Koob & Volkow neurocircuitry model. The A-B-C corrective maps well to acute withdrawal → pink cloud → PAWS. The Fibonacci clustering of half-lives across drug classes is intriguing but vulnerable to selection bias. The sensitive-dependence principle (small structural modifications producing large functional changes) is directly observable in medicinal chemistry.
Tier 3 (Weak or unsupported):
Gann angular relationships do not appear in pharmacokinetic timing data. Onset-to-duration ratios vary by orders of magnitude across classes with no consistent geometric relationship. Benner cycles have no obvious pharmacological correlate at any timescale examined.
Recommendation for Framework Integration
The fractal self-similarity findings should be integrated as a validated cross-domain confirmation of the framework's core mathematical tool. The same Hurst exponent and power-law analysis that applies to BTC price series applies to neural signaling — the math transfers because the underlying generative process (complex adaptive system with feedback loops) is structurally homologous.
The Elliott Wave addiction mapping is worth keeping as a Tier 2 structural analogy, particularly given your clinical focus. It provides a framework for understanding where a patient is in their addiction cycle and what structural rules constrain the next phase — but it should inform clinical intuition, not replace evidence-based assessment.
The Fibonacci half-life clustering should be flagged as "interesting, investigate further" — it warrants a more rigorous test with a complete dataset rather than selected representatives.
The Gann angle and Benner cycle tests produced null results in this domain. That's not a failure — it's useful information. It tells you which framework elements are domain-general (fractals, wave structure) and which are domain-specific (Gann geometry, Benner cycles apply to markets but not pharmacokinetics).

# Methodology Foundations -- PMD v1.2

**Source:** Predictive Modeling Discipline (PMD) v1.2; Bayyinah Audit
Framework v3.0 (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20017335).

**Authors:** Bilal Syed Arfeen, Fraz Ashraf (BayyinahEnterprise).

## §0. Framing

The BayyinahEnterprise audit methodology checks whether software,
documents, and AI-generated artifacts are **honest about what they do**.
Not whether they are correct -- existing tools (linters, type checkers,
security scanners, fuzzers) cover correctness. Whether they keep the
promises they make.

The defects we detect are **structural, not syntactic**. A function
claims to return patient data but sometimes silently returns nothing. A
public API had ten functions last week and nine this week with no
notice. A document shows a $2,450 invoice but contains a hidden layer
with $245,000. These are honesty failures: the system's surface claims
diverge from its substrate behavior.

## §0.1 Surface vs substrate

Every artifact has two layers:

- **Surface:** what the artifact claims, advertises, documents, or
  promises (function signatures, docstrings, public APIs, displayed
  invoice amounts, README claims).
- **Substrate:** what the artifact actually does (function bodies,
  control flow, hidden PDF layers, actual test counts).

An artifact is **structurally honest** when surface and substrate match.
A finding is a documented surface-substrate divergence.

## §0.2 Standing rules (cross-cutting)

These rules apply across every audit cycle, every role, every artifact:

1. **Em-dash policy** -- no `--`-em characters; use `--` double hyphen.
   In LaTeX, the `---` ligature must also become `--` outside legitimate
   Markdown horizontal rules.
2. **Brand canonical** -- "BayyinahEnterprise" no space.
3. **Severity uppercase** -- CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW.
4. **Six-element findings format** -- ID + severity + locus + substance
   + disposition + cross-reference.
5. **Substrate-of-record uniqueness** -- each fact stated once.
6. **Audit-chain immutability** -- append-only ledger; historical
   preservation cells never edited retroactively (only annotated with
   cross-references per Bayyinah Audit Framework v3.0 §14.5).
7. **Cross-vendor rotation** -- producer-instance excluded from auditor
   pool; tier-weighted consensus.
8. **Time discipline** -- estimates inflated 75% to match reality.

## §0.3 The six-stage lifecycle (engineering-discipline import)

From Fraz Ashraf's power-systems engineering background (renewable
energy, BESS, EV charging, micro-grid; standards IEC 61508, IEEE 1547):

1. **Pre-flight** -- substrate-of-record reconciliation before any
   intervention (T00 pattern).
2. **Author** -- producer-instance creates the artifact (Claude
   typically; other vendors acceptable).
3. **Audit** -- auditor-instance executes Mode A or Mode B verification
   under cross-vendor rotation.
4. **Adjudicate** -- if multiple auditors disagree, adjudicator applies
   PMD v1.2 cross-vendor rules.
5. **Absorb** -- producer-instance generates next version absorbing
   audit findings under disposition-prescribed routes; mechanical-
   traceability discipline preserved.
6. **Ledger** -- append-only record of the cycle; immutability discipline
   enforced.

The cycle iterates until convergence (zero CRITICAL findings; HIGH
narrows monotonically; MEDIUM and LOW tracked but not blocking).

## §0.4 Convergence definition

A chain has **converged** when:

- Two consecutive cross-vendor rounds produce 0 CRITICAL findings
- HIGH residual is 0 or accompanied by a project-lead-signed exception
  ledger entry
- MEDIUM and LOW findings are either absorbed or moved to "future
  reference" with explicit non-operative annotation
- All standing-rule compliance checks pass (em-dash, brand, severity,
  six-element format, substrate uniqueness)

Convergence is not the same as completion. Convergence permits ship;
new rounds may surface new findings at any time.

## §0.5 Six absorption candidates -- v1.1 -> v1.2 (this version)

PMD v1.2 absorbed six methodology surfaces previously surfaced as
findings during the al-Mursalat audit chain (Rounds 36-38.5):

1. **Absorption-induced regression at retired surfaces** -- when new
   substrate truth resurfaces a previously-retired contradiction
   sharing a surface, both must be re-examined as a pair. See
   `references/audit-modes.md` and the Round 38.5 worked example.
2. **Bulk-substitution automation immutability risk** -- automated
   find-and-replace operations may inadvertently edit historical
   preservation cells; §14.5 immutability discipline prohibits this
   without explicit ADR.
3. **Narrative-vs-body propagation gap detection** -- framing
   summaries and section bodies must propagate the same arithmetic;
   gap detection is an explicit auditor sub-task.
4. **Stale sub-verification subtask retirement** -- once a verification
   task is resolved (e.g., Co-work T00 §7b confirms helper absent),
   the resolved state is the canonical statement; PRESENT/ABSENT
   branching moves to "for future reference."
5. **Mechanical-traceability exception** -- when an absorption cycle
   exclusively executes prior audit's disposition-prescribed routes
   with zero architectural latitude, cross-instance re-audit is
   recommended-but-not-blocking; project-lead signoff suffices.
6. **Lane-execution discipline** -- methodology specifies producer /
   auditor / adjudicator roles AND execution lanes (skill bundle, CI,
   cross-vendor validator, MCP server). Lanes are the canonical
   execution substrate; producer / auditor / adjudicator are the
   canonical role substrate.

## §0.6 Empirical record

The methodology was empirically validated across 38.5 audit rounds on
three repositories between April 20 and May 10, 2026. Severity
narrowing curve:

| Round | Repo focus | CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Round 31 | as-Saff v0.11.7 | 3 | -- | -- | -- |
| Round 32 | as-Saff F10-F13 | 1 | -- | -- | -- |
| Round 36 | al-Mursalat v1.3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Round 37 | al-Mursalat v1.4 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Round 38 | al-Mursalat v1.5 | 0 | 1 | 4 | 2 |
| T00 (Mode A) | al-Mursalat v1.6 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| Round 38.5 | al-Mursalat v1.7 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| Round 38.5 v1.8 | al-Mursalat v1.8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

CRITICAL convergence at Round 38 holds through v1.8 ship. HIGH residual
was the load-bearing surface in Rounds 38 and 38.5; v1.8 closes it.

## §0.7 What this skill does

Loads the above into Claude's working context so that any operation
under this skill -- producing, auditing, or adjudicating -- inherits
the methodology automatically rather than requiring re-statement in
every prompt.

§0: What this document is for
This document specifies how predictive-modeling discipline from two empirically rigorous domains (organic chemistry
and astrophysics) is to be imported into the Bayyinah ecosystem’s auditing, predictive-programming, and applications
work. The applications it bears on are: the Bayyinah Audit Framework itself; the furqan-lint static analyzer; the Furqan
programming language; the Bayyinah Integrity Scanner; and the prompt-engineering and prompt-auditing discipline
applied across all four.
The cross-domain integration is not metaphorical. It is operational: each imported practice has a specific procedural
form, a specific data requirement, and a specific verification protocol. AI instances reading this document should treat
the imports as work specifications, not as suggestive analogies.
Three structural commitments govern the document:
• Imports are tier-graded. Every cross-domain practice is classified Tier 1 (independently validated; structurally
direct transfer; immediately operational), Tier 2 (plausible structural analogy; needs empirical validation before operational use), or Tier 3 (weak transfer; archived but not currently operational). The tier grade is the
Bayyinah-ecosystem analogue of the falsifiability discipline that organic chemistry and astrophysics have spent
two centuries refining.
• Self-attestation is named as a structural constraint. The Bayyinah corpus is currently single-practitioner
work. Cross-domain methodology imports must be designed to admit external validation when other practitioners adopt the framework. Imports that require closed-loop self-validation are flagged. v1.3 amendment (cycle
12): the self-attestation-as-structural-constraint commitment is now anchored to external empirical evidence. Laban, Schnabel, Neville (April 2026, Microsoft Research, arXiv:2604.15597) measure that frontier LLMs corrupt
approximately 25% of document content in long delegated workflows (across N=19 models × 52 professional
domains in the DELEGATE-52 benchmark). The empirical baseline directly supports PMD’s structural-honesty
thesis applied to delegated AI work: self-attestation by a single LLM instance is empirically unreliable at substantial rates even for frontier models. The commitment was previously methodologically asserted; v1.3 makes
it empirically anchored per §3B.
• The structural-honesty thesis applies recursively. This document’s surface claims about what the imports
will achieve must match its substrate specifications about how the imports operate. Where the document cannot
specify the substrate, it says so.
§0.1 Tier-grading framework: scope and named exception
The Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 system as originally written grades empirical methodology imports: imports whose surface
claim is that adopting the import licenses specific predictions about substrate behavior. The §0.3 falsification-block
discipline (below) operates against empirical imports.

The §7 Item 15 Audit Report v1.0 canonical surfaced a structural distinction the original tier system did not make
explicit: some methodology imports are procedural framework commitments (commitments about how to reason;
e.g. “classify by scale before making cross-scale claims”; “identify which calibration rungs each claim depends on”;
“characterize tensions rather than papering over them”) rather than empirical claims (claims about substrate behavior;
e.g. “the four-place pattern produces measurably lower regression rates than alternative practices”). The §0.3 shipblocker rule operates directly against empirical claims; against procedural commitments it requires either a downstreameffect reframing or an explicit category extension.
This v1.1 surfaces that distinction and surfaces three legacy designations (§3.2.a, §3.3.a, §3.4) as procedural framework commitments awaiting project-lead disposition among three options (see §0.4 for ledger; §3.2, §3.3, §3.4 for the
per-import disposition state). Until the disposition decision lands, those three designations carry an explicit “PROCEDURAL FRAMEWORK; STAGE-2 DISPOSITION PENDING” annotation.
Named exception, cross-instance separation. §0.3 below specifies proposer-falsifier separation: falsification blocks
for Tier 1 imports are authored by the audit-author instance (per §5.4), not by the proposer (per §5.1). The first execution
of §7 item 15 was performed by the same Claude instance that produced this methodology document, in audit-author
mode within the same session. The project lead’s disposition is to accept this same-instance execution as a documented
named exception with four constraints: (1) scope limited to first execution of §7 item 15; (2) cross-instance verification
path remains open; (3) reviewer-visibility named in this paragraph; (4) cycles 5 through 8 of the audit report’s own
review process were performed by perplexity in audit-author mode (cross-instance review of the audit report itself is
therefore present in the iteration history). The project lead may commission a cross-instance re-execution by perplexity
in a fresh session before external publication; the structural-honesty thesis is best served by exercising this option before
external venue submission, but it is not strictly required for internal operational deployment.
§0.2 Tier transition discipline: framework versus specific implementation
A methodology import may earn Tier 1 framework status (the import’s operational shape is correct and the falsification
block is filled and discriminating) while its specific implementation remains Tier 2 (the empirical test the falsification
block names has not yet been run against comparator data). When a designation is at this state, the document marks it
explicitly: “Tier 1 framework, Tier 2 specific implementation pending [named test].” This is the same split §3.1
(Bayesian forward-modeling) and §3.2.b (R1-R11 scale-applicability table) already use.
The transition path: when the named test runs and the prediction is verified at the pre-registered threshold, the specific
implementation promotes to Tier 1. When the named test runs and the prediction is falsified, the entire designation
demotes to Tier 2 procedural candidate (preserving the procedural directive but removing the load-bearing empirical
claim) per the falsification block’s decision rule.
§0.3 Falsification-block discipline (ship-blocker)
Every methodology import claimed at Tier 1 status must be accompanied by a falsification block before it ships into
operational use. The block follows a fixed quintuple-plus-verdict template:
Import: [name and operational shape] Tier-1 claim: [the specific predictive claim] Falsifying observable: [the external
observable that resolves the claim] Statistic / threshold: [the test, the effect size committed via pre-registered power
analysis, and the significance threshold accounting for any multiple-comparison correction; never plausibility-chosen
values] Data source: [what data the test consumes; comparator chains where applicable] Decision rule: [the action
taken if the prediction is falsified] Discriminating-test verification: [explicit confirmation that the falsifying observable
is not predicted by R1-R11 vocabulary independently and that the data source is not co-shaped by Bayyinah-internal
categorization]
The discriminating-test requirement is load-bearing: tests that reduce to “we will look at the chain and see if it matches”
are contaminated by R1-R11 vocabulary or by Bayyinah-internal categorization and disqualify the candidate from Tier

Proposer-falsifier separation. Falsification blocks for Tier 1 imports are authored by the audit-author instance (§5.4),
not by the proposer instance (§5.1). The proposer instance proposes the import; the audit-author instance authors
the block; the project lead disposes. Same-instance execution is a documented named exception per §0.1 with crossinstance verification path open.
Pre-registered power analysis. Quantitative thresholds in falsification blocks are committed to pre-registered power
analysis rather than plausibility-chosen values. Where a literature precedent exists (e.g. Burnham-Anderson 2002 for
AIC; Kass-Raftery 1995 for Bayes factors), the precedent’s effect-size convention is used. Where no precedent exists,
the power analysis is performed under the project lead’s choice of expected effect size with explicit documentation; the
choice is itself a calibration-rung that the audit-author instance verifies for plausibility. Plausibility-chosen thresholds
without power-analysis grounding are surfaced as a finding by the audit-author instance.

§1: Why these four source domains
Organic chemistry is one of the most predictively successful sciences in history. Its practitioners predict reaction
products, ratios, rates, and selectivities from first principles, and verify those predictions in the lab with reproducible
accuracy. The framework has been falsified, refined, and re-validated over two centuries. Its core methodological tools
(mechanism, kinetics, equilibrium, selectivity, concentration analysis) are not domain-bound to chemistry; they are
tools for thinking about complex systems with directional dynamics, competitive pathways, and quantitative measurement.
Astrophysics is structurally different in its predictive epistemology. It operates under single-realization constraints (we
observe one universe, observe one audit chain), uses Bayesian inference to extract parameters from sparse and noisy
data, employs hierarchical multi-scale models, and has formalized calibration-ladder discipline. Its tools are designed
for situations where controlled experiments are impossible and where theory must be tested against observation rather
than against laboratory replication.
Software-audit-practice (added in v1.2) is a third source domain with a different epistemological character from either
chemistry or astrophysics: its empirical corpus is generated by the framework’s own operational use rather than from an
external scientific tradition. The Bayyinah audit chain shipping furqan-lint through phases G11.0 through G12.0 produced three calibration-class data points (cycles 9-11 absorbed in §0.4) that constitute an empirical comparator corpus.
Unlike chemistry’s two-century falsification record or astrophysics’ deep-time observational baseline, the softwareaudit-practice corpus is small (three cycles), recent (six weeks of compressed operational time), and self-generated. Its
scientific status is therefore weaker than chemistry’s or astrophysics’: it informs operational discipline but cannot independently validate methodology imports the way chemistry and astrophysics can. The §0.3 ship-blocker rule applies
with extra strictness to software-audit-practice imports because the corpus’s small size makes single counter-examples
disproportionately weighty.
AI-delegation empirical methodology (added in v1.3) is a fourth source domain anchored to external empirical work
specifically measuring frontier-LLM delegation reliability. Laban, Schnabel, Neville (April 2026, Microsoft Research,

The Bayyinah ecosystem operates at the intersection of these constraints. The audit chain has chemistry-style mechanism structure (each finding is a reaction; each closure is a product; each round is an iteration with measurable kinetics)
and astrophysics-style observational constraints (single practitioner, single chain, single realization, no controlled replication available). The software-audit-practice imports add a third element: empirical comparator data drawn from the
framework’s own operational history, recording what audit-intensity calibrations produced what ship-readiness signal. The AI-delegation empirical methodology imports add a fourth element: external empirical evidence about the
failure modes that the framework’s discipline is specifically designed to mitigate. Importing from one domain alone
would miss substantial methodological need. Importing from all four produces a more complete predictive-modeling
discipline.
Discipline-risk acknowledgment (project-lead reflection absorbed at v1.1). Each domain import strengthens the

organic chemistry and astrophysics; subsequent imports under consideration include genetics and biochemistry. Each

psychological pattern-matching frameworks that lack falsifiability discipline. These traditions may have selective merit
but their epistemic standards are not equivalent to chemistry and astrophysics, and confusing them would degrade the
framework’s structural honesty.
§2: The chemistry imports
§2.1 Reaction mechanism discipline (Tier 1 framework, Tier 2 specific implementation pending comparatorchain analysis)
In organic chemistry, every reaction prediction proceeds by tracing electron flow through bonds. You identify the
nucleophile (electron-rich), the electrophile (electron-poor), draw curved arrows showing electron movement, and the
product follows mechanically from the arrow sequence. Every arrow must start from electrons (a lone pair or a bond)
and end at an atom or bond. Arrow violations produce wrong predictions.
The Bayyinah ecosystem analogue: every audit finding’s closure must trace as a mechanism. A finding at substrate layer
L is the electrophile (the site of structural deficiency). The corrective fix is the nucleophile (the structural completion).
The closure ledger documents the arrow-pushing: from substrate state S1, through documented intermediate states (the
four-place pattern: CHANGELOG entry, README entry, fixture, pinning test), to substrate state S2.
§2.1 operational specification
Every audit finding closed under the framework must have a documented closure mechanism with explicit before-state,
after-state, and the structural transformation between them. The four-place pattern is the chemistry-equivalent of arrow-

For AI instances authoring corrective prompts: when specifying a fix, the prompt must include the closure mechanism

“Add extension-based dispatch in surface_extraction.py at extract_public_surface, raising UnsupportedLanguageError
for non-Python sources, with three pinning tests that exercise the dispatch boundary on Python, Rust, and a synthetic
unsupported-extension fixture” is a closure mechanism.
For AI instances auditing corrective prompts or substrate code: the audit must verify that every behavioral change in the
substrate has a documented mechanism in the same form. Behavioral changes without documented mechanisms are the
chemistry-equivalent of products without an arrow-pushing derivation: they signal that the underlying transformation
is not understood, not that no transformation occurred.

§2.2 Kinetics and rate laws (Tier 2; needs measurement before operational)
In chemistry, reaction kinetics predicts rates from concentration. First-order: rate = k[A]. Second-order: rate = k[A][B].
Pseudo-first-order: when [B] is in large excess, rate = k’[A] where k’ = k[B]. Each form predicts time-to-completion,
half-life, and temperature dependence (Arrhenius equation: k = A * exp(-Ea/RT)).

B. S. Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

The Bayyinah ecosystem has measurable kinetics. Time-from-finding-surfaced to finding-closed is a directly recoverable quantity from Git timestamps. Cycle-time distributions across the F22-F26 sub-chain (which surfaced over
approximately 5-7 days) are accessible. Cycle-time across the broader 43-round corpus is recoverable with one normalization pass.
§2.2 operational specification
For AI instances analyzing audit chain trajectories: cycle-time should be measured as Git author-timestamp delta between the round’s first commit (finding surfaced) and the round’s closure commit (corrective shipped). This is the rate
law’s primary observable.
For research outputs: kinetics analysis should test specific rate-law forms against the cycle-time data. Candidates to
test:
• Zero-order: cycle-time independent of any concentration variable
• First-order in number of open findings: cycle-time per finding decreases when more findings are open in parallel
(parallel processing reduces overhead)
• First-order in substrate complexity: cycle-time per finding increases with codebase size, dependency-graph density, or language count
• Arrhenius-style: cycle-time depends exponentially on practitioner attention or AI-collaborator availability
Each form is a falsifiable empirical claim. The rate law that best fits the observed data, with its 95% confidence interval,
is the chain’s kinetic signature.
For AI instances authoring or auditing under time pressure: the kinetic framing names a specific concern. The 27version-in-2-days trajectory is a high-rate regime; the framework’s claims about cycle-time compression should be
qualified by the rate regime in which they were observed. Sustainable steady-state rates are likely lower. Imports of
methodology to other practitioners should not assume the high-rate regime transfers.
§2.3 Equilibrium and Le Chatelier (Tier 2; structurally coherent)
Le Chatelier’s principle: a system at equilibrium responds to perturbation by shifting to counteract it. Add reactant:
equilibrium shifts toward product. Remove product: equilibrium shifts toward more product formation. Increase
temperature: equilibrium shifts in the endothermic direction.
The audit chain at steady-state has equilibrium structure. The corrective rhythm reaches equilibrium when the rate of
finding production equals the rate of finding closure. Perturbations and their predicted responses:
• New methodology introduced (e.g., the four-revision prompt review pattern at Round 8): rate of closure increases
as backlog processes; new equilibrium has shorter average finding-age until system absorbs the methodology.
• New substrate complexity introduced (e.g., a new language adapter): rate of finding production increases as new
shapes surface; new equilibrium has higher average finding-age until discipline absorbs the new complexity.
• Discipline relaxed (e.g., attribution drift): rate of un-cataloged finding production increases; equilibrium shifts
toward “drift” until a corrective imposes new constraint (e.g., the v0.8.5 attribution corrective).
§2.3 operational specification
For AI instances modeling audit chain trajectories: equilibrium analysis should track three time-series: rate of finding
production (per week or per release), rate of finding closure, and average finding-age in the open queue. When the first
two converge, the chain is at equilibrium. Perturbations are events that drive divergence; the time-to-new-equilibrium
is the response time.

§2.4 Selectivity and competing pathways (Tier 1 framework conditional on §5.1 pre-registration discipline; Tier
2 specific implementation pending F27+ prospective data)
In chemistry, when multiple reactions are kinetically accessible, the product distribution is determined by relative
rates and thermodynamics. Markovnikov vs. anti-Markovnikov addition. SN1 vs. SN2 vs. E1 vs. E2 substitution and
elimination. Kinetic vs. thermodynamic control. Given starting materials, conditions, and catalysts, you predict the
major and minor products, their ratios, and how those ratios shift with temperature, solvent, concentration.
The audit chain’s findings have selectivity structure. When a substrate has multiple potential failure modes at a given
step, which one surfaces in any given round is determined by relative likelihoods. F22-F26 demonstrates this: at step
4 of the verifier pipeline, the install-extras gap (F23) surfaced first, then the API-drift gap (F24) when extras were
resolved, then the chain advanced to step 6 (F25). The selectivity of each round was determined by which failure mode
had the lowest activation energy under the conditions.
§2.4 operational specification
For AI instances authoring corrective prompts: when a finding surfaces at substrate layer L, the corrective should explicitly enumerate the next-most-likely failure modes at layer L (the secondary pathways that may surface after the
primary corrective ships). This is the chemistry-equivalent of identifying minor products. The Round 33 audit’s identification of F26 as the “next layer’s evidence” surfaced after F25 closure is an example of selectivity reasoning operating
retrospectively; it should also operate prospectively.
Pre-registration discipline (added in v1.1 per §7 Item 15 Audit Report stage 1; binding for Tier 1 framework
status of §2.4). Producer instances (§5.1) must commit a pre-registered ranked list of next-most-likely failure modes
at the affected substrate layer before the corrective prompt ships. The list has minimum length 3 and is part of the
corrective prompt’s body, durable in the Git record. Subsequent findings at the same substrate layer are then evaluated
against the pre-registered list per the §2.4 falsification block. Without this discipline operational, §2.4 demotes to Tier
2 by §0.3 ship-blocker default. The full producer-role specification is in §5.1 step 4.
For AI instances reviewing the structural regularities R1-R11: R6 (step exhaustion) is structurally a Markovnikov-style
directionality rule. It should be reframed in the chemistry vocabulary: “double-occupancy at a substrate step exhausts
that step’s failure surface; the next round will surface at a structurally adjacent step in the directional preference of
pipeline progression.”
For Phase 2 ablation work: predictor configurations should be tested for selectivity-prediction accuracy specifically.
Condition A should be evaluated on whether it correctly identifies not just the next finding, but the next-most-likely
alternative findings (the minor products). This adds a second dimension to the prediction codeword and strengthens
the empirical claim if Condition A outperforms Condition B on selectivity-prediction.

§2.5 What chemistry imports does NOT include
Concentration analysis with logarithmic quantitative prediction (pH, pKa, Henderson-Hasselbalch) does not transfer
cleanly. The audit chain has no continuous concentration variable in the relevant range; finding density per substrateLOC is a candidate but the dynamic range is too compressed for log-scale analysis to be informative. Tier 3.
Reaction thermodynamics (delta-G, delta-H, delta-S) does not transfer because the audit chain’s “spontaneity” is a
function of practitioner discipline rather than of energetic favorability. Tier 3.
Stereochemistry and chirality have no audit chain analogues. Tier 3.
§2.6 Michaelis-Menten kinetics (Tier 2 candidate, falsification block authored)
§2.6.a Michaelis-Menten falsification block
Michaelis-Menten kinetics describes enzyme-catalyzed reactions where rate saturates as substrate concentration increases. The Bayyinah-ecosystem analogue under exploration: prompt-review-cycle throughput as a function of auditsubstrate-volume, where AI-collaborator capacity is the enzyme and finding-density is the substrate.
Import: Michaelis-Menten saturation kinetics (rate v = Vmax * [S] / (Km + [S]); rate saturates as substrate concentration exceeds Km) Tier-2 candidate claim: prompt-review throughput as a function of open-finding count exhibits
Michaelis-Menten saturation rather than linear, substrate-inhibition (rate decreases at very high substrate), or sigmoidal
(cooperative) behavior Falsifying observable: prompt-review-cycle throughput (closures per unit time) measured across
audit chain segments with varying open-finding density Statistic / threshold: model comparison via information criterion. Four candidate models fit to the throughput-vs-density data: linear, Michaelis-Menten, substrate-inhibition
(Haldane), and Hill-cooperative. Selection by AIC delta > 4 (Burnham-Anderson 2002 strong-evidence threshold) or
Bayes factor > 20 (Kass-Raftery 1995 strong-evidence threshold). Pre-registered power analysis specifies minimum N
= 50 data points (segments of audit chain history with computed throughput-density pairs) subject to upward revision
if power analysis computed with project-lead-chosen expected effect size requires more. Data source: Git history segmentation across the 43-round corpus plus F27+ segments as they accumulate; throughput computed as closures per
unit Git-timestamp interval per segment; density computed as open findings during that segment. Decision rule: if a
non-MM model is selected by AIC delta > 4 or BF > 20, the MM import is falsified; the selected model is reported instead and the import remains Tier 2 under that model. If no model is selected with strong evidence, the import remains
Tier 2 with all four candidates reported. Discriminating-test verification: the throughput-vs-density relationship is not
predicted by R1-R11 vocabulary independently. R10 (severity bounding) and R5 (external-library persistence) bear on
adjacent dynamics but neither predicts the functional form of throughput-density saturation.

§2.7 Linkage analysis (Tier 2 candidate, falsification block authored)
§2.7.b Linkage falsification block
Linkage discipline in genetics and biochemistry distinguishes whether two observations co-occur because of shared
causation, shared substrate position, or chance. The Bayyinah-ecosystem analogue: whether two findings at related
substrate layers co-occur within a temporal window because of shared mechanism or chance.
Import: Linkage co-occurrence discipline with explicit null model Tier-2 candidate claim: pairs of findings at related
substrate layers (e.g. same module, same dependency, same architectural seam) co-occur within per-week windows at
rates significantly higher than the per-file marginal-product null model predicts Falsifying observable: linkage disequilibrium D-statistic computed against the per-file marginal-product null model (NOT the uniform-random null, which
would produce spurious significant D for any non-uniform substrate) Statistic / threshold: permutation test computing
the null distribution of D under the per-file marginal-product model with 10,000 permutations per finding pair. Significance at p < 0.05 with Holm-Bonferroni correction across all evaluated pairs. Time window locked at per-week
aggregation. Pre-registered power analysis specifies the minimum effect size at which the test has 80% power and the
corresponding minimum N pairs. Data source: F27 onward audit chain pairs plus retrospective F22-F26 pairs as a
second cohort. Per-file marginal probabilities computed from the full Bayyinah corpus Git history; pair co-occurrence
computed within per-week Git-timestamp windows. Decision rule: if no pair shows statistically significant D against
the per-file marginal-product null at p < 0.05 Holm-Bonferroni-corrected, the linkage import is falsified; preserve as
Tier 3 archived. Discriminating-test verification: the per-file marginal-product null model is the discriminating-test
mechanism; uniform-random null would conflate substrate-distribution effects with linkage and be contaminated by
R9 (file locality) implicitly.
Status: Tier 2 candidate. The falsification block is authored with the explicit per-file marginal-product null model
resolving the cycle-3 B3 conflation finding. Promotion to Tier 1 framework requires the permutation test to find at least
one pair with statistically significant D against the per-file marginal-product null.

§3: The astrophysics imports
§3.1 Bayesian forward-modeling and parameter estimation (Tier 1 framework, Tier 2 specific implementation
pending Phase 2 ablation results)
Cosmological parameter estimation extracts the matter density Omega_m, the dark energy equation-of-state w, the
Hubble constant H_0, and several other parameters from CMB observations, supernova surveys, and large-scale structure measurements. The data is sparse (one universe, observed once), noisy (cosmic variance, instrument systematics),
and partial (only the past light cone is observable). Yet parameter estimates have shrunk to percent-level precision
through disciplined Bayesian inference.
The methodology: forward models (Boltzmann codes like CAMB and CLASS); Bayesian inference (MCMC samplers
like emcee, Stan, dynesty); model comparison (Bayes factors, information criteria); and explicit handling of nuisance
parameters and systematics.

15


PMD v1.8

B. S. Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

The audit chain has structurally similar epistemic constraints. One audit chain (the corpus produced under v3.0/v4.0),
observed once, with practitioner-specific systematics (sleep schedule, attention, AI-collaborator availability), partial
observability (closed findings are documented; near-misses and silently-fixed issues are not). Yet structural parameters can be extracted: cycle-time distribution scale, severity-decay rate, finding-density per substrate-LOC, regularityapplicability tier.
§3.1.1 Operational specification: forward-model construction
For Phase 2 ablation work and successor research: the current Phase 2 ablation design is frequentist (Wilcoxon, McNemar’s, Holm-Bonferroni). A complementary Bayesian forward-model is buildable on top of the existing infrastructure:
• Posit a forward model. Audit-chain state at round N is characterized by: open-finding count (Poissondistributed); cycle-time distribution (log-normal with parameters mu, sigma); severity distribution (categorical
with parameters p_CRITICAL, p_HIGH, p_MEDIUM, p_LOW); substrate-coverage vector (which steps have
been visited).
• Specify priors. Cycle-time mean has a weakly informative prior (e.g., log-normal centered on 4 hours with
half-life 1 hour). Severity-decay rate has a prior centered on the observed v0.1.0-v0.8.5 trajectory’s empirical
rate.
• Sample posteriors via MCMC. Use the F22-F26 sub-chain as observed data. Emcee or Stan can fit the model
in minutes. Output is posterior distributions over each parameter with credible intervals.
• Generate forward predictions. Sample from the posterior to predict F27-F30 trajectory characteristics. Compare against the actual F27-F30 as Phase 2 ablation runs.
• Update with new data. When F27 ships, condition the posterior on F27. The posterior tightens; predictions for
F28+ become sharper.
For AI instances authoring research outputs: the Bayesian framing has the methodological advantage of producing a
model that is updateable as new audit chains accumulate, rather than re-running tests with each new dataset. The R
Quarto analysis document specified in the Phase 2 ablation pre-registration can host the Bayesian analysis alongside
the current frequentist tests.
For peer-review submission: ACM TOSEM, IEEE TSE, ICSE, and FSE all accept Bayesian and frequentist analyses.
The Bayesian framing is currently under-represented in empirical software engineering; reporting both produces a
paper with stronger statistical positioning than reporting either alone.
§3.1.5 Bayesian-frequentist coordination discipline (path A / B / C)
The Phase 2 ablation pre-registration (OSF DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/WEKMB) commits to frequentist primary analysis
(Wilcoxon, McNemar’s, Holm-Bonferroni). The Bayesian forward-model is complementary, not replacement. Three
coordination paths exist:
• Path A: Bayesian-as-secondary-analysis. Frequentist primary analysis runs as pre-registered; Bayesian
forward-model fits the same data afterward as a secondary analysis with explicit “secondary, exploratory, not
part of pre-registered hypothesis test” annotation. No modification to the OSF pre-registration required.
• Path B: Bayesian-as-amendment. A documented amendment to the OSF pre-registration adds the Bayesian
forward-model as a co-primary analysis alongside the frequentist tests. Amendment must be filed before the first
Phase 2 frequentist analysis is performed on the F27+ findings; the amendment is a standalone OSF document
with cross-citation from this methodology document.
• Path C: Bayesian-deferred (default). Bayesian work is deferred until Phase 2 frequentist analysis completes.
Path C is the safe default if the path-choice coordination memo is not filed before the first Phase 2 frequentist

§3.2 Multi-scale hierarchical modeling
Galaxy formation simulations operate at multiple scales: dark matter halo dynamics on Mpc scales, gas dynamics on
kpc scales, star formation on pc scales, individual stellar processes on AU scales. Each scale has its own physics;
coupling between scales is mediated by sub-grid models. The hierarchy lets you simulate a Hubble volume without
resolving every star.
The audit chain has natural multi-scale structure:
• Macro scale: entire chain (43 rounds, three repositories, weeks of wall-clock time)
• Meso scale: single phase (e.g., G11.0.x: 6 rounds, days of wall-clock time)
• Micro scale: single round (one finding, hours of wall-clock time)
• Nano scale: single closure step (one commit, minutes of wall-clock time)
§3.2.a Multi-scale framework as discipline (PROCEDURAL FRAMEWORK; STAGE-2 DISPOSITION PENDING)
§3.2.a specifies the procedural commitment to recognize that different patterns operate at different scales and to classify
by scale-applicability before any cross-scale claim is made. This is a procedural framework commitment about how to
reason, not an empirical claim about substrate behavior.
Per the §7 Item 15 Audit Report v1.0 canonical, the §0.3 falsification-block discipline was designed for empirical
methodology imports (Tier 1 claim that the import licenses specific predictions; falsification block that names what
observation refutes the prediction). Procedural disciplines do not fit this template directly: there is no “observable”
that refutes the procedural commitment to classify before claiming.

§3.3 Calibration ladder discipline
Cosmology builds a distance scale by chaining standard candles: parallax to nearby stars, Cepheids to nearby galaxies,
Type Ia supernovae to cosmological distances. Each rung is calibrated by overlap with the rung below. Tensions in the
ladder (the H_0 tension, where local and CMB-derived measurements disagree at >5 sigma) signal either systematics
in one rung or new physics.
The audit chain has analogous calibration structure. Round 1 establishes the v0.1.0 baseline. Each subsequent round
calibrates against the prior round (the four-place pattern: previous CHANGELOG, previous fixtures, previous tests are
the calibration anchors). Cross-rung calibration occurs when validator-by-different-instance audits review the substrate
(Round 32-bis catching the v1.1 al-Furqan runtime crash issue is a cross-rung calibration that surfaced systematic gap).

§3.3 operational specification
For AI instances conducting validator-by-different-instance audits: the audit’s epistemic role is rung-calibration, not
duplication of the producer’s work. The audit should explicitly check: does the substrate as documented match the
substrate as the prior round’s calibration anchor expects? Where does the audit’s view diverge from the producer’s
view? Each divergence is a tension that requires resolution before the rung is calibrated.
For AI instances authoring corrective prompts: every prompt should explicitly identify which prior calibrations it
depends on (which CHANGELOG entries, which fixture files, which pinning tests) and which prior calibrations it
threatens to invalidate. Implicit dependencies on prior calibrations are the chemistry-equivalent of unstated reagents:
they make the prediction unfalsifiable.
For research outputs: a calibration-ladder analysis of the audit chain would systematically identify where each finding
depends on which prior calibrations and where the chain is most sensitive to systematic error. Tensions in the ladder (cases where independent rungs disagreed and were resolved) should be cataloged explicitly. The Round 32-bis
validator-by-different-instance catch of the runtime crash is a worked example of ladder tension; more such examples
should be made discoverable.
For the Bayyinah Integrity Scanner specifically: the scanner’s role at a different abstraction level (information-layer
integrity rather than code-layer integrity) means it is a calibration-rung for any document that the framework relies on
as ground truth. When the scanner surfaces an integrity finding on a framework document, that finding is structurally
a ladder-tension that requires resolution before the framework can be cited.

In cosmology, the “Hubble tension” (5+ sigma disagreement between locally-measured H_0 and CMB-derived H_0)
is treated as informative. Rather than averaging the measurements or picking a favorite, the field treats the tension as

§3.4 operational specification
For AI instances at any role (producer, validator, calibrator): when two independent observations of the substrate
disagree, do not average, do not pick a favorite, do not paper over. Document the tension as a six-element finding with
explicit characterization of:
• Which observation said what
• Where the discipline boundary is between them
• Which systematic could account for the disagreement
• What evidence would resolve the tension
• The current disposition (open, partially resolved, fully resolved, archived)
• The structural lesson if the tension closed in a particular direction
For research outputs: a tension catalog across the 43-round corpus would document every recorded instance where
independent observations disagreed and how each was resolved. The catalog’s pattern (which kinds of tensions occur
most often; which are resolved by substrate correction vs. methodology correction vs. discipline correction) is itself a
research artifact worth publishing.
§3.5 What astrophysics imports does NOT include
Renormalization group flow, effective field theory, beyond-Standard-Model fitting are designed for problems where
the underlying physics is itself uncertain. The audit chain’s “physics” (human work-discipline plus AI-collaborator
capability) has limits but is not in this kind of fundamental epistemic crisis. Tier 3.
Tensor-mode polarization, gravitational-wave background analysis, and other observational programs that depend on
still-developing instrumentation have no audit-chain analogue. Tier 3.
Cosmological inflation and similar high-energy regime models do not transfer because they describe regimes where the
system’s parameters are radically different from steady-state. Audit chain regimes, even at high rate, are not analogous.
Tier 3.

§3A.0 Why this third source domain (rationale)
The chemistry imports (§2) supply mechanism / kinetics / equilibrium / selectivity vocabulary. The astrophysics imports
(§3) supply Bayesian forward-modeling / multi-scale hierarchy / calibration-ladder / tension-as-diagnostic vocabulary.
Neither domain has the operational tools to specify how intensively to audit a given software phase given its risk
profile and architectural shape. Software engineering has a small but informative literature on calibration of codereview intensity (e.g., Fagan 1976 formal inspections; ISO/IEC 12207 software lifecycle processes), but the Bayyinah
ecosystem operates in a regime (AI-assisted methodology development for an audit framework auditing AI-assisted
code) where the existing software-engineering literature does not yet have well-validated calibration heuristics. The
§3A imports fill this gap with empirical evidence from the framework’s own three-phase corpus.
The structural-honesty thesis applies recursively to §3A: the discipline imported here cannot be more predictively
reliable than the three-cycle corpus’s small-n statistical power allows. §3A.1 falsification block names the test that
would falsify the calibration heuristic; that test is the load-bearing pre-registration the §7 successor work tracks.

§3A.1 operational specification
The audit-intensity calibration heuristic is a 5-question pre-flight screen that classifies a phase’s audit-intensity tier
(LIGHT / STANDARD / HEAVY) based on its risk-class and architectural-shape characteristics. The screen runs
before the phase’s prompt is authored (or as early in authoring as possible) and binds the audit discipline applied to that
phase’s substrate.
The 5 questions (applied in order; first “heavy” answer escalates the whole phase):
1. Substrate scope – how many lines of code does this phase add? Under 500 lines, lean toward LIGHT. 500-2000,
STANDARD. Over 2000 lines, HEAVY.
2. Blast radius – what breaks if it ships wrong? Internal tool with no production users, LIGHT. User-facing API
or output, STANDARD. Safety-relevant, security-critical, or affects downstream consumers (e.g., signed public
manifests), HEAVY.
3. Irreversibility – can it be patched post-ship cheaply? Yes (code-only, no data migration, no key rotation), LIGHT.
Partial yes, STANDARD. No (public API change, on-disk format, cryptographic surface, immutable signed
artifacts), HEAVY.
4. Novelty – how new is the architectural pattern? Inheriting an existing pattern (an-Naziat inheriting al-Mursalat’s
function-local dispatch), LIGHT. Extending with new constraints, STANDARD. Net-new architecture, HEAVY.
5. Project-lead bandwidth – fresh, STANDARD default; tired, LIGHT unless 1-4 demand HEAVY; exhausted,
ship the smallest viable thing and queue methodology improvements for later.
The 2D calibration matrix (per Round 42 candidate C-42-1):
The five questions reduce to a two-dimensional matrix whose dimensions are risk-class (the maximum of questions 2,
3, and 5; the bandwidth question 5 acts as a downward force on risk-class when the project lead is exhausted, but cannot

§3A.4 Recursive-closure self-surfacing regression property (Tier 1 framework; substrate property of v1.0+;
NOT a methodology heuristic)
§3A.4 operational specification
Round 42 candidate C-42-4 surfaced a property of the v1.0.0 al-Basirah ship that is distinct from the calibration heuristic
but is structurally co-located with §3A imports because it derives from the same software-audit-practice corpus. The
property:
furqan-lint v1.0.0+ cannot silently regress its own gate11 verification capability.
The recursive-closure architecture (verify-self uses the same code path as the universal verifier; the universal verifier
is what other Relying Parties consume; the self-attestation manifest is signed at release time and verified at the §15
acceptance gate) means that any regression in gate11’s ability to verify a furqan-lint release will be self-surfacing on
the next release.yml run: specifically, §15 (furqan-lint manifest verify-self --expected-identity ...) will fail before the
release is published.
Maintenance posture implication for v1.x:
This property changes the regression-detection contract for furqan-lint v1.x maintainers. Specifically:
1. v1.x patches that touch the gate11 substrate cannot ship without passing the verify-self circuit
2. The verify-self circuit is mechanically enforced by release.yml step T06 + acceptance gate §15
3. The regression-detection latency is bounded: one release cycle, not “until a Relying Party reports the regression”
4. The property does not extend to non-gate11 substrate regressions (e.g., a regression in furqan-lint’s CLI argument
parsing that does not affect gate11 verification is not self-surfacing)
§3A.4 status note on §0.3 ship-blocker rule:
§3A.4 is a property of the shipped v1.0.0 substrate, not a Tier 1 methodology claim requiring a falsification block. The
§0.3 ship-blocker rule applies to methodology imports that claim predictive content about substrate behavior; §3A.4
documents an architectural property that the v1.0.0 substrate has, which is verifiable by inspection of the release.yml +
cli.py + acceptance gates. The property does not predict; it describes.
The §0.3 boundary distinction matters because absent it, every substrate property documented in PMD would require
a falsification block, which is not the discipline’s intent. §3A.4 enters as a documented property; if a future PMD
revision wants to make a predictive claim about the property (e.g., “v1.x phases that maintain recursive-closure will
exhibit lower regression-detection latency than phases that do not”), that claim would require its own §0.3-compliant
falsification block.
§3A.5 What software-audit-practice imports does NOT include
The §3A imports are scope-limited to the three load-bearing C-42-N candidates + the §3A.4 property. The following
are explicitly OUT of v1.2 §3A scope:
• STANDARD-tier empirical baseline. The {HIGH-risk, substrate-modifying-but-bounded} cell remains structurally placed and empirically untested. §7 successor work pre-registers the empirical test.
• Cross-domain calibration imports. The §3A heuristic is software-audit-practice-specific; whether the 2D matrix transfers to chemistry-style or astrophysics-style audit work is not claimed.
• Quantitative calibration thresholds beyond the audit-overhead ratio. The ~1/10th-of-HEAVY-overhead observation for LIGHT (cycles 10-11 vs cycle 9) is empirical, not predicted; PMD v1.2 does not claim it as a Tier
1 quantitative prediction.
• Detailed Round 40 / Round 41 audit content. Both audits remain pre-registered and uncompleted at v1.2
authoring time; their findings will be absorbed by v1.3 (per §7 successor work).

§3A.6 Watchlist additions (cycle 22 absorption arc)
The cycle 22 absorption arc (Ch16 SI4 supply-chain four-substrate stack case study, 9 dispatches, 24 surgical patches
across cycles 22+P through 22+R+R+R+R) surfaced two methodologically mature recurring observation patterns that
this version codifies as named watchlists. Each watchlist has accumulated ≥3 empirical instances across dissertation
audit cycles and is operationally actionable in future dispatch design.
§3A.6.1 WL21 — Cross-artifact substrate-of-record propagation gap
When a substrate-of-record correction is absorbed at one artifact locus (e.g., a chapter prose section), the correction
MUST propagate to all artifacts that inherit or reference the same substrate-of-record claim. Failure of propagation
creates a cross-artifact divergence where two artifacts make incompatible substrate-of-record claims about the same
substrate.
Empirical pattern: cycle-N absorption at one locus succeeds; cycle-N+k discovers that other artifacts authored before
or during the absorption window retain the pre-correction substrate-of-record framing.
Empirical instances (4, substrate-verified in audit ledger; +1 from v1.4 per cycle-26+P count update): 1. Cycle 18
— SI2 ledger gap (audit-ledger section retained pre-correction framing after chapter prose absorption) 2. Cycle 20+P
— canonical .bib SI3 entry retained “paper-as-both-SoR-and-substrate” framing after Chapter 15 Option-C reframe 3.
Cycle 21 — SI4 Chapter 16 §0.1 retained “furqan-lint = SoR” framing after canonical ledger Section 5 + canonical
Chapter 4 §1 established “supply-chain four-substrate stack = SoR; furqan-lint = operational evidence base” 4. Cycle
25 — SI4 Chapter 22 §0.1+§0.3 (3 loci) retained “furqan-lint” SoR framing after cycle-22+P Option-C reframe; 4th
post-codification empirical instance validating WL21’s predictive load (post-codification observation strengthens rule
without requiring revision; HOLD at watchlist class per cycle-25-closure Q1 disposition)
Dispatch discipline: when a substrate-of-record correction is proposed, the dispatch prompt MUST enumerate all
artifacts known to reference the substrate-of-record AND substrate-verify each artifact’s framing against the corrected
canonical state. This applies to chapter prose, audit-ledger sections, .bib entries, consolidated reference canon, and
forward-routing references in other chapters.
§3A.6.2 WL22 — Adjacent-locus drift (concept-window, not numeric-line)
When an N-locus enumeration patch absorbs corrections at named loci, vendors and project-lead MUST sweep the
conceptual scope (not just the ±5-line numeric window) around each named locus for similar restatements of the same
concept.
Empirical pattern: N-locus enumeration misses the (N+1)th locus when the (N+1)th locus is outside the numeric
window but within the same conceptual scope.
Empirical instances (5, substrate-verified in audit ledger): 1. Cycle 18 — audit-prompt arithmetic propagation 2. Cycle
19 — C15RV-P1 9-locus enumeration missed adjacent 10th locus 3. Cycle 22+R — Option-C SoR reframe missed line
31 (4-vendor continuity convergent catch) 4. Cycle 22+R+R — C16RV-P3 line-97 past-tense patch missed adjacent line59 lifecycle wording (outside ±5-line numeric window; ChatGPT continuity catch validated concept-window framing)
5. Cycle 22+R+R+R — C16RV-P6 §0.3 line 41 (first §0-locus instance; 3-vendor convergent catch)
Concept-window scope definition: all loci in the chapter (or artifact) that make the same substantive claim as the patched
locus, regardless of numeric line proximity. For substrate-source-verification lifecycle wording, the concept-window
includes §0 framing + §1 substrate description + §9 chapter close + any other section that references the substratesource-verification phase.

§3A.7 Render-vs-substrate finding discipline (predictive rule; parallel to §3A.3)
§3A.7 operational specification
When a vendor surfaces a finding based on markdown-rendering artifact (pandoc-generated U+00A0 NBSP from
LaTeX ~, \_X-strength from $\sim_X$-strength, footnote-rendering divergence, table-hyphenation drift, or similar
render-class observations), the finding MUST be substrate-verified against the canonical .tex source before severity
classification. Render artifacts that correctly preserve LaTeX semantics are NOT substrate-level defects — they are
tool-rendering correctness signals, and patching the .tex to suppress them would degrade typographic quality.
Empirical pattern: continuity-mode auditors with markdown-only substrate access are more prone to render-vssubstrate misframing than fresh-instance Mode A auditors with direct .tex substrate access. This is consistent with
§3A.3’s “substrate-actual overrides prompt” predictive rule applied at the audit-disposition layer.
Empirical instances (3, substrate-verified in audit ledger): 1. Cycle 20+R — Claude continuity surfaced F-Ch15-3
pandoc HTML-escape misframing; self-corrected with appended substrate-verification clarification 2. Cycle 20+R+R
— Claude continuity surfaced F-Ch15-NEW U+00A0 NBSP at patched locus; project-lead dispositioned as renderonly after substrate-verification confirmed canonical LaTeX ~ typography correctly preserved 3. Cycle 21 — Claude
continuity self-applied substrate-verification before classifying a candidate finding, demonstrating successful operationalization of the discipline
Operational discipline for continuity-mode dispatches: continuity instances SHOULD explicitly perform substrateverification against .tex source before classifying severity on render-class observations. The disagreement-disposition
rule “continuity is not authoritative” applies to render-class findings specifically; fresh-instance Mode A verdicts with
direct substrate access carry higher weight on render-class disambiguation.
§3A.7 status note on §0.3 ship-blocker rule: this is a discipline-class predictive rule (governs how findings are
classified), not a substrate property (§3A.4) or a falsification-block-requiring predictive claim (§3A.3 family). §0.3
ship-blocker rule applies in attenuated form: the predictive content is “render-class findings classified at severity-X by
continuity instances will substrate-verify as render-only at a rate consistent with the §3A.3 substrate-actual-overridesprompt empirical baseline” — but the rule’s primary function is dispositive (how to classify) rather than predictive
(what will happen), so the falsification framing is light. Future v1.5 work may tighten the predictive rate threshold into
a falsifiable form.
§3A.7 cross-reference to §3A.3 (parallel structure): §3A.3 specifies pre-dispatch substrate-actual-verification (verify
substrate state matches dispatch-prompt assumptions before T01 begins). §3A.7 specifies the complementary auditdisposition substrate-verification (verify render-class observations against .tex source before severity classification).
The two rules apply at different layers of the audit lifecycle and are complementary: §3A.3 governs prompt-fact-vssubstrate; §3A.7 governs render-fact-vs-substrate.

§3B: The AI-delegation empirical methodology imports
§3B.0 Why this fourth source domain (rationale)
PMD v1.2 introduced §3A software-audit-practice as a third source domain alongside §2 chemistry and §3 astrophysics,
anchored to a three-cycle internal empirical corpus (an-Naziat / Tasdiq al-Bayan / al-Basirah). The §3A corpus is
single-practitioner small-n: three cycles, one project lead, single AI-collaborator backbone configurations per cycle
(cycle 9 used three vendor backbones across rotation sessions: GPT-5, Gemini, Perplexity-Sonnet; cycles 10 and 11
each used Perplexity Mode A alone), BayyinahEnterprise-internal substrate scope. The internal corpus is suﬀicient
for Tier 1 framework status under v1.2’s three-cycle threshold, but the §0.1 named-exception clause explicitly flags
single-practitioner closed-loop self-validation as a structural-honesty risk requiring cross-instance verification before
external publication.
v1.3 absorbs Laban-Schnabel-Neville 2026 (Microsoft Research, April 2026, arXiv:2604.15597) as the fourth source
domain. The Laban-Schnabel-Neville DELEGATE-52 corpus is external N=19-models × 52-domains empirical benchmark testing AI delegation across a wide professional-task surface. The corpus directly addresses the structural-honesty
thesis applied to AI-delegated knowledge work: it measures empirically what PMD v1.1-v1.2 asserted methodologically about delegation reliability.
The structural-honesty thesis applies recursively to §3B: the disciplines imported here address delegation-corruption
patterns that PMD v1.3 itself is at risk of exhibiting during its own authoring (the v1.3 amendments are themselves a
delegated document-editing task). §3B.1 names the corpus as Tier 1 framework with empirical anchor; §3B.2 names the
operational discipline that §3A.3 cycle-11-dissertation-audit substrate-misread experience provides internal empirical
witness for and that Laban-Schnabel-Neville provides external empirical witness for; §3B.3 names the multi-vendor
cross-rotation discipline as the empirically-baseline-mitigated operational practice.
§3B.1 Delegation-corruption baseline (Tier 1 framework; Tier 1 specific implementation per Laban-SchnabelNeville 2026 DELEGATE-52 empirical corpus)
§3B.1 operational specification
Per Laban, Schnabel, Neville (April 2026), frontier LLMs (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude 4.6 Opus, GPT 5.4 explicitly named
in the publication) corrupt an average of 25% of document content during long delegated workflows on the DELEGATE52 benchmark. Other tested models fail more severely. The paper’s three additional findings are load-bearing for §3B
operational discipline:
• Agentic tool use does not improve performance. Delegation reliability is not addressable by adding tool affordances; the corruption is in the LLM-edits-document loop itself.
• Degradation severity is exacerbated by three factors: document size, length of interaction, and presence of
distractor files in the context window. All three exacerbating factors are present in standard Bayyinah-ecosystem
dispatch packages (multi-file packages including substrate + reference + ledger + PMD frequently exceed cycle11-dissertation-audit’s 7-file dispatch and run across extended turns).
• Errors are sparse but severe and silently compound over interactions. Per Laban-Schnabel-Neville, the
corruption is not uniformly distributed; specific edits are factually wrong in ways that surface only on substrateactual verification. The compounding-over-interactions finding is consistent with the cycle-11 dissertation-audit
substrate-misread (project-lead substrate-verification was wrong twice across cycles 9-10 of the dissertation
work; each error compounded into downstream patches that propagated the underlying mistake).
PMD v1.3 absorbs the corpus as Tier 1 framework with Tier 1 specific implementation:
Operational consequence 1 — delegated-document-edit verification. Any delegated document edit (patch application, str_replace, ledger-entry write, content-revision) is itself substrate-verifiable. The discipline applies recursively:

a verification cycle should check not just that the edit landed at the intended location, but that the edit’s content does not
contain sparse-but-severe corruption introduced during the delegated edit. §3B.2 specifies the operational discipline.
Operational consequence 2 — single-instance verification is empirically unsafe at frontier scale. The §0.1 namedexception clause’s cross-instance verification path is no longer methodologically preferable; it is empirically necessary. Cross-instance verification at minimum two-vendor (preferably four-vendor cross-model-family per cycle-11
three-vendor + cycle-12c four-vendor dissertation-audit empirical witnesses) is the baseline operational discipline for
verification work. §3B.3 specifies the operational discipline.
Operational consequence 3 — dispatch package parsimony. Per Laban-Schnabel-Neville’s distractor-file finding,
dispatch packages should be minimum-necessary-files rather than maximally-contextual. Reference materials beyond
what the audit task strictly requires increase corruption rate. §3B specifies pre-dispatch package-design discipline.
§3B.1 falsification block (per §0.3 ship-blocker)
Import: Tier 1 framework status for the Laban-Schnabel-Neville 2026 delegation-corruption baseline as anchor for
PMD’s structural-honesty thesis applied to AI-delegated document work.
Tier-1 claim: PMD-discipline cross-instance verification work catches a measurable fraction of the corruption-pattern
that Laban-Schnabel-Neville 2026 measures at ~25% baseline for un-mitigated delegation. The strict-merge audit discipline (three-vendor cross-model-family dispatch + project-lead substrate-verification + post-edit substrate-verification
per §3B.2) reduces effective corruption rate below the un-mitigated baseline by some non-zero margin.
Falsifying observable: a post-PMD-discipline audit of a delegated document set produced under §3B-compliant crossinstance verification surfaces substrate-fidelity error rate at or above 25% baseline. Specifically: if the BayyinahEnterprise dissertation work post-publication is independently audited by an external practitioner and the audit surfaces
substrate-fidelity errors at the Laban-Schnabel-Neville baseline rate or higher, then PMD-discipline is no more effective
than no discipline at all for the delegation-corruption problem.
Statistic / threshold: comparison of post-discipline corruption rate (measured by independent external audit) against
Laban-Schnabel-Neville 2026’s 25% baseline. Pre-registered threshold: independent external audit corruption rate >=
25% across N >= 3 independently-audited document classes (dissertation chapters; PMD itself; furqan-lint substrate
documents) falsifies PMD-discipline operational utility. Sample size and effect-size grounding follows Laban-SchnabelNeville’s reported variance across their 52 professional domains; conservative bound is 25% baseline + sampling
variance of their corpus.
Data source: independent external audit (commissioned by project-lead or volunteered by external practitioner) of
BayyinahEnterprise documents produced under PMD v1.3 discipline. The audit must use the same operational measure
of corruption (sparse-but-severe substrate-fidelity errors) and must be conducted independently of any project-lead
substrate-verification work to maintain comparator independence.
Decision rule: if falsified, PMD-discipline operational utility is empirically not better than no discipline at the
delegation-corruption-mitigation surface. Recalibrate by either: (a) expanding the audit cycle count per document
class above the cycle-11-dissertation-audit baseline (three-vendor was empirically necessary; perhaps five-vendor is
empirically necessary), (b) demoting the structural-honesty thesis applied to AI-delegated work from Tier 1 framework
to Tier 2 candidate, (c) committing to non-AI-delegated revision passes as part of v1.0 publication discipline.
Discriminating-test verification: the external audit corpus is independent of PMD-internal vocabulary (the audit measures substrate-fidelity errors against substrate-actual content, not against PMD-categorization claims); the comparator
(Laban-Schnabel-Neville 2026 baseline) is published external preprint work not produced under PMD discipline; the
test is statistically discriminating between (a) PMD-discipline catches some corruption and (b) PMD-discipline catches
no corruption that wouldn’t have been caught by no-discipline at all.
