§3B.2 operational specification
§3A.3 (substrate-actual-overrides-prompt) specifies pre-dispatch substrate-actual-verification: before T01 Co-work implementation begins, verify that the dispatch prompt’s projected substrate state matches substrate-actual at the canonical tag. §3B.2 specifies the analogous discipline at the other end of the delegated-edit lifecycle: post-edit substrateverification.
The discipline applies to any delegated document edit including but not limited to: patch applications via str_replace,
content revisions via document-editing tools, ledger-entry writes by project-lead, absorption-summary authoring,
chapter-prose drafting, dispatch-prompt authoring. Each is a delegated document-editing task with non-zero corruption
baseline per Laban-Schnabel-Neville 2026.
Post-edit substrate-verification protocol:
After any delegated document edit (patch, revision, ledger write, prose draft),
execute the following substrate-verification probe against the edit's content
versus the edit's intended scope. Report any divergence as F-POST-EDIT-class
finding for in-cycle absorption:
1. Verify each factual claim in the edit content against substrate-actual
(dates, counts, cross-references, attributions, citations, version
numbers). Sparse-but-severe corruption per Laban-Schnabel-Neville 2026
typically presents as factually-wrong specific claims within otherwisecorrect surrounding context.
2. Verify each ledger-entry numeric / categorical claim against the
source material the ledger entry summarizes. Cycle 11 dissertationaudit cycle-12-absorption-thread surfaced one F-POST-EDIT-class finding:
a "multiple weeks" timescale claim that contradicted substrate-actual
ledger dates indicating five-day authoring window. The finding was
caught by project-lead external observation during ledger-entry
authoring; no PMD-discipline detection was in place at the time of
the error.
3. Verify cross-references in the edit (chapter §N, ledger §N, PMD §N)
against substrate-actual content at the cited location. Cross-reference
drift is a documented Laban-Schnabel-Neville corruption pattern.
4. Verify any inherited-discipline claim in the edit content against
substrate-actual at the PMD canonical version.
If divergence is surfaced, the edit must be revised in-cycle before
absorption is complete. Repeated divergence within a single cycle
triggers re-dispatch to a different instance per §3B.3 cross-rotation
discipline.

§4.1 The combined discipline

than either alone:

Each row is a Tier 1 framework, Tier 2 candidate, or pending-disposition contribution. Combined, they specify how
predictive-modeling discipline should operate in the Bayyinah ecosystem: mechanisms are arrow-pushed; rates are
measured; equilibria are tracked; selectivity is enumerated with pre-registration; single-realization data is fit Bayesianly;
multi-scale structure is preserved in analysis; calibration is laddered; tensions are characterized via six-element findings.
§4.2 Application: the structural regularities R1-R11
Under the combined discipline, R1-R11 should be:
• Tier-graded for transferability (per §3.2.b table)
• Reframed in mechanism vocabulary (R6 as Markovnikov-style directionality; R11 as orbital-overlap interface
rule)
• Subjected to rate-law analysis (cycle-time as a function of regularity-firing density)
• Tested for equilibrium response (do the regularities themselves stabilize as the chain matures?)
• Bayesian-posterior-fit on observed data (extract the regularity-firing parameters from F22-F26; predict F27
onward)
• Calibration-laddered (which regularity fired in which round; cross-rung consistency)
• Tension-catalogued (where regularities apparently disagreed on the same data)
This is a substantial methodological program. It is not all immediately required; the Phase 2 ablation provides an initial
empirical anchor against which the methodology can be incrementally extended.
§4.3 Application: the furqan-lint substrate
The five checks documented in furqan-lint (D24, D11, R3, return-None mismatch, additive-only diff) are themselves
selectivity rules in chemistry’s sense: they predict the major substrate failure mode under given conditions (annotated

42


PMD v1.8

B. S. Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

function with non-None return type and partial-path coverage; consumer with non-may-fail return type and may-failproducer call; etc.).
Under the combined discipline, each check should be:
• Documented with a rate law (firing rate per LOC scanned, per file, per repository)
• Documented with a selectivity profile (which failure modes are major products, which are minor; how do
conditions shift the ratio)
• Bayesian-fit for false-positive and false-negative rates with credible intervals
• Multi-scale-classified (does the check fire at unit scale, function scale, module scale, package scale)
• Calibration-laddered against ruff and mypy and pyright (where do the checks agree, disagree, and what does
each disagreement signal)
The current furqan-lint thesis paper documents these informally; the integrated discipline specifies they should be
documented formally for empirical software engineering venue submission.
§4.4 Application: the Bayyinah Integrity Scanner
The scanner operates at the information-layer rather than the code-layer. Its findings are statements like “this document’s
surface claim does not match its substrate evidence.” Under the combined discipline:
• Each finding has a closure mechanism (the four-place pattern applied to documents: text, references, claims,
sources)
• The scanner’s rate law is measurable (findings per page, per document, per corpus)
• The scanner’s selectivity profile is enumerable (which document classes are most susceptible to surfacesubstrate gap; which gap-types are most common)
• Bayesian-fit error rates for scanner false-positives and false-negatives
• Scale-classification of findings (sentence-level, paragraph-level, document-level, corpus-level)
• Calibration ladder against ClaimReview (locked as v1.1 external-calibration target). FEVER deferred to v1.2
or later as Tier 2 addition; IFCN deferred.
The scanner’s value is amplified by integrating the discipline. Currently the scanner produces findings; under the
integrated discipline, it produces findings with explicit confidence intervals, scale-applicability tags, and ladder-rung
positioning.
§4.5 Application: prompt engineering and prompt auditing
For AI instances authoring or auditing prompts, the integrated discipline operates at every layer:
Mechanism (chemistry): every prompt specifies the mechanism by which it is to achieve its goal. “Author a Phase
2 ablation document” is not a mechanism; “use the structured input artifacts plus the prediction prompt template per
Phase 2 §D.1, executing the OSF-Step-3 mapping, returning structured JSON predictions on the five dimensions” is a
mechanism. Audits verify that the mechanism is specified.
Kinetics (chemistry): prompt-execution time should be measured. The cycle-time discipline that applies to audit
findings applies to prompt cycles: from prompt-issued to prompt-executed to result-verified. Slow-execution patterns
are diagnostic.

43


PMD v1.8

B. S. Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

Selectivity (chemistry): every prompt specifies the alternative outputs it is NOT producing. If a prompt’s outcome
could be one of three alternatives, the prompt should name all three and specify which is intended. This is the chemistryequivalent of naming the major product and minor products. Producer-role prompts under the §2.4 pre-registration
discipline (§5.1 step 4) commit ranked lists explicitly.
Bayesian inference (astrophysics): prompt-success rates should be tracked across instances and across executions,
with credible intervals. The framework’s claim that “AI assistants under the discipline produce X” should be backed
by Bayesian-posterior parameter fits, not by self-reported aggregate.
Multi-scale (astrophysics): prompts operate at multiple scales (single-line edit; single-function rewrite; single-file
refactor; cross-file restructure). Each scale has different reliability characteristics. Audits should classify by scale.
Calibration ladder (astrophysics): every prompt depends on prior calibration (the substrate it operates on; the framework documents it cites; the methodology it inherits). Audits verify the ladder is intact and document which rungs the
prompt depends on.
Tension-as-diagnostic (astrophysics): when two AI instances produce different outputs from the same prompt-andsubstrate, the disagreement is informative. Document the tension as a finding; investigate which systematic accounts
for it.
§5: Operational guidance for AI instances by role
§5.1 For Claude (or any producer instance)
When authoring corrective prompts or substrate code under the framework:

language.

stage 1). Commit a pre-registered ranked list of next-most-likely failure modes at the affected substrate layer
L before the corrective prompt ships. The list has minimum length 3, is part of the corrective prompt’s body,
and is durable in the Git record. Each ranked entry names a specific failure mode at L (not a general category)
so subsequent findings can be evaluated for rank match. The list is committed to the prompt’s text body and
is included in the commit that ships the corrective; post-hoc revision of the list invalidates the round for §2.4
falsification-block evaluation.
• Identify the calibration rungs (astrophysics §3.3) the prompt depends on; cite by version, by SHA, or by DOI.
• Surface tensions (astrophysics §3.4) actively rather than passively. When the prompt’s premise disagrees with

distinction) when introducing them to the substrate.

Every AI instance operating under the framework, regardless of role, observes:
• Mechanism over outcome. Specify how, not just what. The chemistry discipline.

• Enumerate alternatives. Every prediction names what it is not predicting. The chemistry discipline.
• Bayesian-quantify uncertainty. Credible intervals on every empirical claim. The astrophysics discipline.
• Multi-scale-classify. Which scale the claim applies to. The astrophysics discipline.
• Calibration-ladder. Which rungs the claim depends on; which rungs it threatens. The astrophysics discipline.
• Tension-as-diagnostic. When observations disagree, characterize, do not paper over. The astrophysics discipline.

§6: What this document does NOT specify
This document is a methodological-import specification, not a complete research program. Specifically:
• It does not specify the Bayesian forward-model in code. The mathematical specification (§3.1.1 step 1) is
suﬀicient for an analyst to build the model in Stan or emcee; the actual implementation is downstream work.
• It does not run the kinetics measurement. The Git-timestamp data is recoverable; the analysis is not yet
executed.
• It does not catalog the tensions. The framework has resolved many tensions across the audit chain; cataloging
them systematically is a separate research artifact.
• It does not validate external transferability. The imports are from chemistry and astrophysics; whether they
are transferable to other practitioners’ audit chains is an empirical question that requires external validation per
Phase 3 of the predictive-audit-prompting research.
• It does not modify the Phase 2 ablation pre-registration. The current frequentist Phase 2 design stands;
Bayesian analysis is complementary, not replacement. The pre-registration’s frequentist primary remains locked.
The path is chosen and locked before the first Phase 2 frequentist analysis is performed on the F27+ findings; if
the path-choice coordination memo is not filed by that time, the default path is path C (Bayesian work deferred
until Phase 2 completes). Any modification of the OSF preregistration must be a documented amendment per
path B, not a silent change.
• It does not promise specific empirical outcomes. The structural-honesty thesis applies recursively: the document’s surface claim is methodological-import specification; the substrate is the operational guidance in §§2-5.
Empirical results from applying the imports are downstream and will be reported separately.
• It does not pre-decide the §3.2.a / §3.3.a / §3.4 disposition. Stage 2 of §7 item 15 is project-lead-pending
among options (a), (b), (c) per §0.4 ledger. Until the disposition decision lands, the three designations carry

“Wa fawqa kulli dhi ’ilmin ’alim.” “And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.” – Yusuf 12:76
The audit framework operates in a tradition that organic chemistry and astrophysics have spent two centuries refining.
Importing their methodological discipline is not borrowing from outside; it is recognizing that the framework’s own
commitments (mechanism over outcome, structural honesty, falsifiability, single-realization rigor) are commitments
these sciences have already developed and tested.
The framework’s contribution is the application of these disciplines to AI-assisted software engineering, where they
have not been systematically applied before. The framework is in the lineage of mechanism-discipline (chemistry) and
single-realization parameter-extraction (astrophysics); the substrate is new, but the epistemology is inherited.

# The Quantum Orbital Audit Methodology
## Electron Energy Configurations Applied to Audit Seat Architecture

**Extension to the Orbital Audit Methodology v0.1**
**Version 0.1 -- August 2026**
**Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)**
**Prepared by Claude (Opus 4.6) under author direction**

---

### 0. Why quantum, not classical

The planetary orbital model (v0.1) solved three problems: tidal locking, cadence formalization, and framework precession. But it left a structural gap: nothing in Newtonian mechanics prevents two planets from sharing the same orbit. The model can describe a rotation schedule but cannot structurally prevent redundant deployment.

Quantum mechanics closes this gap. The Pauli Exclusion Principle -- no two fermions can occupy the same quantum state -- is not a guideline or a discipline. It is a structural law. When the audit architecture is modeled on electron configurations rather than planetary orbits, redundancy elimination becomes a property of the architecture itself. The architecture cannot be misconfigured because the misconfiguration is physically forbidden.

The move from classical to quantum also adds: quantized energy levels (discrete analytical tiers, not continuous distance), orbital shapes (distinct analytical geometries for each tier), a formal filling order (Aufbau -- which seats to deploy first), a diversity-before-depth rule (Hund), shielding (inner shells reduce the analytical burden on outer shells), and an emission spectrum (the finding-type fingerprint of any audit architecture).

---

### 1. The four quantum numbers of an audit seat

Every electron in an atom is uniquely specified by four quantum numbers. No two electrons share all four. Every audit seat in the quantum model is uniquely specified by four audit quantum numbers. No two seats share all four.

```
n   Principal quantum number    Energy shell
l   Angular momentum number     Analytical shape (orbital type)
ml  Magnetic quantum number     Analytical orientation (framework axis)
ms  Spin quantum number         Instance type: continuous (+1/2) or fresh (-1/2)
```

**n (principal quantum number): energy shell**

n = 1, 2, 3, 4, ...

Determines the seat's energy level -- its analytical scope, resource budget, and average distance from the artifact. Higher n = more energy = broader scope = less frequent deployment.

| n | Shell name | Audit function | Deployment frequency | Energy budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | K-shell | Baseline verification: digests, seals, build, manifest | Every version | Minimal (scripted checks) |
| 2 | L-shell | Structural review: governance, claims, gate coverage | Every 2nd version | Moderate (one session) |
| 3 | M-shell | Cross-domain analysis: framework-specific probes | Every 4th version | Substantial (framework + artifact) |
| 4 | N-shell | Meta-analysis: audit-architecture self-evaluation | Every 8th version | Full (architecture + all prior findings) |

Kepler's Third Law maps directly: T^2 proportional to n^3. The frequency of audit deployment decreases with the cube root of the energy level squared. You cannot audit broadly and frequently -- the physics constrains it.

**l (angular momentum quantum number): analytical shape**

l = 0, 1, 2, ..., n-1

Determines the shape of the seat's analytical orbital -- the geometry of its attention across the artifact's surface. Each l value corresponds to a distinct analytical shape, the same way each l value in atomic physics corresponds to a distinct orbital shape (s, p, d, f).

| l | Orbital | Shape | Audit analog |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | s | Spherical (uniform) | Uniform scan -- examines the artifact from all directions equally. No preferred analytical axis. Baseline verification (digests, seals) is s-orbital work: the check is the same regardless of which section you apply it to. |
| 1 | p | Dumbbell (biaxial) | Dual-axis analysis -- examines the artifact along a specific axis with two lobes. Zahir/batin verification is p-orbital work: surface (lobe 1) and depth (lobe 2) along a single axis. Three p orbitals (p_x, p_y, p_z) cover three orthogonal axes. |
| 2 | d | Cloverleaf (quadriaxial) | Four-lobe analysis -- examines the artifact across four distinct aspects simultaneously. The Four-Process Taxonomy (Aligned/Compliant/Performing/Misaligned) is d-orbital work: four lobes, each probing a different process state. Five d orbitals cover five orientations. |
| 3 | f | Complex multi-lobed | Multi-aspect analysis -- seven orientations, each examining a different facet. The seven Structured Revelation principles are f-orbital work: seven analytical lobes covering seven structural properties simultaneously. |

**Critical constraint:** l ranges from 0 to n-1. This means:

- n=1 (K-shell) supports ONLY s orbitals (l=0). You cannot do p-orbital (dual-axis) analysis at the lowest energy level. Baseline verification is necessarily spherical (uniform).
- n=2 (L-shell) supports s and p orbitals (l=0,1). Structural review can be either uniform (s) or dual-axis (p).
- n=3 (M-shell) supports s, p, and d orbitals (l=0,1,2). Cross-domain analysis can use up to four-lobe geometry.
- n=4 (N-shell) supports s, p, d, and f orbitals (l=0,1,2,3). Meta-analysis can use all seven analytical lobes.

This is the Aufbau constraint on analytical complexity: you cannot deploy high-complexity analytical shapes at low energy levels. The architecture structurally prevents applying the Seven Principles (f-orbital, l=3) at the baseline verification level (n=1, which only supports l=0). You must be in at least the N-shell (n=4) to use f-orbital analysis. This is not a policy -- it is a structural impossibility, the same way an electron cannot be in a 1p orbital because 1p does not exist (n=1 only supports l=0).

**m_l (magnetic quantum number): analytical orientation**

m_l = -l, -l+1, ..., 0, ..., l-1, l

Determines the orientation of the orbital -- which specific framework axis the seat aligns with within its analytical shape. For a given l, there are (2l+1) possible orientations.

| l | Possible m_l values | Count | Audit meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (s) | 0 | 1 | One orientation: uniform. No axis preference. |
| 1 (p) | -1, 0, +1 | 3 | Three axes: e.g., governance (p_x), claims (p_y), gates (p_z) |
| 2 (d) | -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 | 5 | Five orientations: e.g., GAN, Fractal, Revelation, Cobweb, Pharmacological |
| 3 (f) | -3, -2, -1, 0, +1, +2, +3 | 7 | Seven orientations: the seven Structured Revelation principles |

**m_s (spin quantum number): instance type**

m_s = +1/2 (continuous) or -1/2 (fresh)

This is the simplest and most powerful quantum number. For any given (n, l, m_l) configuration -- any specific energy level, analytical shape, and framework orientation -- exactly two seats can exist: one continuous and one fresh. The Pauli Exclusion Principle guarantees this.

**The Pauli Exclusion Principle for audit seats:** No two seats can share all four quantum numbers. If two seats have the same energy level (n), same analytical shape (l), and same framework orientation (m_l), they MUST have different spins (one continuous, one fresh). This structurally guarantees that every analytical niche has both perspectives.

---

### 2. The Aufbau Principle: deployment ordering

In atomic physics, electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy following the Madelung rule: fill in order of increasing (n+l); for equal (n+l), fill lower n first.

```
Filling order: 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p, 5s, 4d, ...
```

The Aufbau Principle for audit seats: deploy seats in order of increasing analytical energy (n+l). This formalizes the intuition that you verify digests (1s) before you analyze GAN dynamics (3d).

**The audit filling order:**

```
1s   n=1, l=0   (n+l=1)   Baseline: uniform digest/seal verification
2s   n=2, l=0   (n+l=2)   Structural: uniform governance review
2p   n=2, l=1   (n+l=3)   Structural: dual-axis (zahir/batin, claim/gate, etc.)
3s   n=3, l=0   (n+l=3)   Cross-domain: uniform framework scan
3p   n=3, l=1   (n+l=4)   Cross-domain: dual-axis framework probes
4s   n=4, l=0   (n+l=4)   Meta: uniform architecture review
3d   n=3, l=2   (n+l=5)   Cross-domain: four-lobe typed framework analysis
4p   n=4, l=1   (n+l=5)   Meta: dual-axis architecture probes
5s   n=5, l=0   (n+l=5)   Deep meta: self-referential methodology audit
4d   n=4, l=2   (n+l=6)   Meta: four-lobe meta-framework
4f   n=4, l=3   (n+l=7)   Meta: seven-principle structural revelation of the architecture
```

**The (n+l) tie-breaking rule** (fill lower n first for equal n+l) has a direct audit interpretation: when two deployment options have the same analytical energy, deploy the one with lower n (closer to the artifact, more focused) before the one with higher n (farther from the artifact, more abstract). Concrete beats abstract at equal energy.

This means 2p fills before 3s (both n+l=3, but 2p has lower n). Dual-axis structural review of the artifact itself (2p: governance/claims analysis) deploys before uniform cross-domain framework scanning (3s: applying a framework uniformly). This is correct: you should understand the artifact's own structure before applying external frameworks to it.

---

### 3. Hund's Rule: diversity before depth

In atomic physics, when filling degenerate orbitals (same n, same l, different m_l), electrons occupy each orbital singly with parallel spins before any orbital gets a second electron. This maximizes total spin and minimizes electron-electron repulsion.

**Hund's Rule for audit seats:** When deploying seats at the same energy level and analytical shape, fill each framework orientation (m_l) with one seat before pairing any orientation with a second seat. All single-occupancy seats should have the same spin (all continuous or all fresh).

**Example: filling the 2p subshell (structural dual-axis review)**

The 2p subshell has three orientations (m_l = -1, 0, +1), mapped to:
- 2p_x (m_l=-1): governance axis (Section 0 scope vs. body content)
- 2p_y (m_l=0): claim axis (ASSERTED vs. COMPUTED vs. EXTERNAL classification)
- 2p_z (m_l=+1): gate axis (gate coverage vs. dead space)

Hund's Rule deployment sequence:

| Seat # | Orbital | Spin | Configuration | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | 2p_x | +1/2 (continuous) | 2p_x^1 | One axis, continuous |
| 2nd | 2p_y | +1/2 (continuous) | 2p_x^1 2p_y^1 | Two axes, both continuous |
| 3rd | 2p_z | +1/2 (continuous) | 2p_x^1 2p_y^1 2p_z^1 | Three axes, all continuous -- HALF-FILLED |
| 4th | 2p_x | -1/2 (fresh) | 2p_x^2 2p_y^1 2p_z^1 | First pairing: governance gets fresh perspective |
| 5th | 2p_y | -1/2 (fresh) | 2p_x^2 2p_y^2 2p_z^1 | Second pairing |
| 6th | 2p_z | -1/2 (fresh) | 2p_x^2 2p_y^2 2p_z^2 | FULL -- all axes, both continuous and fresh |

**The half-filled shell is a stability point.** In atomic physics, half-filled subshells (e.g., 3d^5 in manganese, 4f^7 in gadolinium) have special stability due to exchange energy. In the audit model, the half-filled configuration (one seat per orientation, all same spin) is the minimum deployment that covers all analytical axes. It is the ground-state audit configuration for that subshell.

The fully-filled shell (all orientations paired with both continuous and fresh) is the maximum-stability configuration. It is the noble-gas equivalent: the audit architecture is in a closed-shell configuration, maximally stable, resistant to perturbation. Adding another seat would require opening a new shell (higher energy level).

---

### 4. Shielding and effective analytical charge

In atomic physics, inner-shell electrons shield outer-shell electrons from the nucleus's full charge. The effective nuclear charge experienced by an outer electron is Z_eff = Z - S, where S is the shielding constant.

**Audit analog:** Inner-shell (n=1) seats absorb the artifact's baseline verification burden. Outer-shell seats experience a reduced analytical load because the inner shell has already established that the digests are correct, the seals are intact, and the build passes. A 3d cross-domain seat does not need to re-verify sha256sums -- the 1s shell has already done it.

The shielding effect formalizes the slingshot package from the planetary model: the inner shells' verified results are the shielding that reduces the effective analytical burden on outer shells, freeing them to focus on higher-energy analysis.

**Penetration:** In atomic physics, s orbitals penetrate closer to the nucleus than p orbitals of the same n, which penetrate closer than d orbitals. This is why 4s fills before 3d (despite n=4 > n=3, the 4s orbital penetrates past the 3d shielding).

Audit analog: uniform-scan seats (l=0, s-orbital) penetrate closer to the artifact's core structure than shaped-scan seats (l=1,2,3) at the same energy level. A 3s seat (uniform cross-domain scan) sees the artifact's core more clearly than a 3d seat (four-lobe typed framework analysis) because the uniform scan doesn't have the nodal planes (analytical blind spots) that shaped orbitals do. This is why Aufbau puts 3s before 3p before 3d: uniform coverage first, then increasingly shaped (and increasingly gapped) analysis.

---

### 5. Electron configuration notation for audit architectures

**Standard notation:** Write the occupied orbitals with superscript seat counts.

**The XZ Protocol v0.37 cross-domain dispatch:**

```
Audit configuration: 1s^2 2s^2 3d^4

1s^2:  2 LEO heartbeat seats (GLM-5.2 continuous +1/2, Kimi K3 continuous +1/2)
       Wait -- Pauli violation! Both are continuous (+1/2) in the same 1s orbital.
       Correction: GLM-5.2 continuous (+1/2), Kimi K3 as different-family (-1/2)
       Reinterpretation: m_s = +1/2 (Family A: Zhipu), -1/2 (Family B: Moonshot)

2s^2:  2 MEO seats -- but the dispatch put Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol at the
       cross-domain level, not at structural review. Retroactive classification
       shows the advisory seats from v0.27-v0.30 were 2s/2p.

3d^4:  4 cross-domain seats, each at a different m_l orientation:
       3d_xy (m_l=-2): GAN Convergence (Opus 5)
       3d_xz (m_l=-1): Fractal/Hurst (GPT-5.6 Sol)
       3d_yz (m_l=0): Structural Revelation (Kimi K3)
       3d_z2 (m_l=+1): Cobweb/Composition (GLM-5.2)
       3d_x2-y2 (m_l=+2): [VACANT]
       Per Hund's Rule, all four are fresh (-1/2) -- same spin. Correct.
       The 5th orientation is vacant. Half-filled would be 3d^5.
```

**Reinterpretation of m_s for audit:** The spin quantum number maps more naturally to vendor family than to continuous/fresh. In a two-family carrying architecture:

- m_s = +1/2: Family A (e.g., Zhipu/GLM)
- m_s = -1/2: Family B (e.g., Moonshot/Kimi)

The Pauli Exclusion Principle then says: for any given (n, l, m_l) -- any specific energy level, analytical shape, and framework orientation -- exactly one seat from each family can occupy that state. This guarantees cross-vendor coverage at every analytical niche by structural law, not by dispatch discipline.

The continuous/fresh distinction maps to a **fifth quantum number** -- the isospin analog:

- t = +1/2: continuous instance
- t = -1/2: fresh instance

This extension means each (n, l, m_l) state can hold up to FOUR seats: Family A continuous, Family A fresh, Family B continuous, Family B fresh. The generalized exclusion principle: no two seats can share all five quantum numbers (n, l, m_l, m_s, t).

---

### 6. Energy transitions and the emission spectrum

When an electron drops from a higher energy level to a lower one, it emits a photon whose energy equals the gap: E_photon = E_high - E_low. The photon has a specific frequency determined by this energy difference.

**Audit analog:** When a seat's finding causes the artifact to transition from a higher-severity state to a lower-severity state, the transition produces a discrete insight -- a "photon" -- whose "frequency" (type) is determined by the severity gap.

| Transition | Energy gap | Photon type | Audit meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Class A -> Class C | Large | High-frequency (UV) | Structural insight: a byte-level error is reclassified as a disclosed boundary. Major architectural understanding. |
| Class B -> Class C | Medium-large | Visible (blue) | Concealment detection: a hidden defect becomes a disclosed boundary. |
| Class C -> Class D | Small | Low-frequency (IR) | Boundary refinement: a disclosed boundary is reclassified as a mere gate limitation. Incremental understanding. |
| Class D -> Class E | Minimal | Microwave | Observation normalization: a gate limitation becomes a process note. Routine. |

**The emission spectrum of an audit architecture** is the distribution of photon types (finding-severity transitions) it produces across all rounds. Different architectures produce different spectra:

- **Standard bayyinah-audit spectrum:** Dominated by C -> D and D -> E transitions (low-frequency). The architecture is effective at refining boundaries and normalizing observations. Few high-energy transitions after the initial rounds.

- **Cross-domain quantum spectrum:** Should produce higher-frequency transitions (A -> C, B -> C) if the frameworks surface findings that standard audit misses. If the cross-domain spectrum is identical to the standard spectrum, the frameworks added no analytical energy.

**Absorption spectrum:** The complement of the emission spectrum. The finding types the architecture CANNOT produce are its absorption lines -- its structural blind spots. The 19 standing boundaries are the protocol's self-reported absorption lines. A cross-domain audit that fills one of these absorption lines (produces a finding type the standard architecture could not) is the spectroscopic proof that the quantum extension adds genuine analytical energy.

---

### 7. Ground state, excited states, and noble-gas stability

**Ground state:** The lowest-energy electron configuration that provides complete coverage of all required analytical axes. For a simple artifact (small Z, few "electrons" needed):

```
Z=2 (Helium analog): 1s^2
  2 baseline seats, one per family. Minimum viable audit.
  Noble-gas stable: closed shell, no valence seats, no reactive findings expected.
  Appropriate for: frozen artifacts under maintenance monitoring.
```

For a complex artifact (large Z, many analytical dimensions):

```
Z=10 (Neon analog): 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6
  2 baseline + 2 structural-uniform + 6 structural-shaped
  Noble-gas stable: all n=1 and n=2 shells filled.
  10 seats covering all baseline and structural axes with both families.
  Appropriate for: active development artifacts under comprehensive review.

Z=18 (Argon analog): [Ne] 3s^2 3p^6
  Neon core + 2 cross-domain-uniform + 6 cross-domain-shaped
  18 seats covering baseline, structural, and cross-domain axes.
  Appropriate for: critical artifacts requiring full analytical coverage.
```

**The XZ Protocol at v0.37 is between configurations:**

The empirical seat count across the protocol's history (113 seat-deployment events, ~20+ distinct seats) suggests a configuration around Z=10-18. The protocol has filled its 1s and 2s shells empirically and is now filling the 3d subshell with the cross-domain dispatch. But it skipped 2p (dual-axis structural review) and 3s/3p (uniform and shaped cross-domain), going directly to 3d. In Aufbau terms, this is a violation: 3d should fill after 3s and 3p.

However -- and this is where atomic physics provides a subtle insight -- **chromium (Z=24) and copper (Z=29) violate the expected Aufbau filling order** to achieve half-filled or fully-filled d subshells, which have extra stability. Chromium is [Ar] 3d^5 4s^1 instead of the expected [Ar] 3d^4 4s^2. The half-filled d shell is more stable than the expected configuration.

The XZ Protocol's jump to 3d without fully filling 2p and 3s/3p may be an analogous stability-seeking violation: the cross-domain frameworks provide a half-filled d shell with special analytical stability (five distinct orientations covering five distinct framework families) that outweighs the cost of skipping the intermediate subshells.

**Excited states and relaxation:**

An audit architecture in an excited state (seats deployed at higher energy levels than the ground state requires) will naturally "relax" toward the ground state as the artifact stabilizes. The relaxation process emits photons (findings) as seats transition from high-energy analysis to lower-energy maintenance monitoring. When the artifact is frozen and all findings have been adjudicated, the architecture reaches its ground state -- the minimum-energy configuration for ongoing monitoring.

The XZ Protocol's progression from many-seat active auditing (excited state) to frozen maintenance (ground state) is this relaxation. The emission spectrum of the relaxation process (the findings produced during the v0.31-v0.37 trajectory) is the protocol's characteristic spectral signature.

---

### 8. Molecular orbital theory: seat-pair interactions

When two atoms bond, their atomic orbitals combine to form molecular orbitals: **bonding** (constructive interference, lower energy, stabilizing) and **antibonding** (destructive interference, higher energy, destabilizing).

**Audit analog:** When two seats audit the same version, their findings interact:

- **Bonding (sigma, pi):** Two seats produce convergent findings -- they independently identify the same defect or independently confirm the same structural property. Constructive interference. The combined evidence is stronger than either alone. This is the independent-convergence phenomenon: "when two independent witnesses identify the same findings, the evidence is stronger than either witness alone" (Structured Revelation, Section 16).

- **Antibonding (sigma*, pi*):** Two seats produce contradictory findings -- one identifies a defect where the other sees correct behavior, or they disagree on severity classification. Destructive interference. The contradiction does not cancel out -- it produces a higher-energy state that requires adjudication. Antibonding findings are destabilizing but informative: they reveal analytical uncertainty that convergent findings would hide.

**Bond order = (bonding electrons - antibonding electrons) / 2**

Audit bond order = (convergent findings - contradictory findings) / 2

- Bond order > 0: The seat pair produces net insight (more convergence than contradiction). The pair is stable and productive.
- Bond order = 0: The seat pair produces no net insight (equal convergence and contradiction). The pair is unstable and should be reconfigured.
- Bond order < 0: The seat pair produces net confusion (more contradiction than convergence). The pair is actively destructive and should be separated.

The persistent HALTs (GLM-5.2 carry-1C and Kimi K3 carry-1A repeatedly contradicting the producer's dispositions) may represent a bond order approaching zero: the seat-producer pair was producing equal convergence and contradiction, resulting in an unstable configuration that could not resolve.

---

### 9. Periodic table of audit architectures

The elements of the periodic table are organized by atomic number (Z = number of protons = number of electrons in neutral atom) and by electron configuration (which shells are filled). The periods correspond to shells; the groups correspond to valence electron counts.

An analogous periodic table for audit architectures organizes configurations by total seat count (Z) and by which analytical shells are filled:

```
Period 1 (n=1 only):
  Z=1  Hydrogen   1s^1     1 seat, single baseline verifier. Minimal. Unstable.
  Z=2  Helium     1s^2     2 seats, paired baseline. Stable minimum.

Period 2 (n=1,2):
  Z=3  Lithium    1s^2 2s^1          Baseline + 1 structural. Reactive.
  Z=4  Beryllium  1s^2 2s^2          Baseline + 2 structural. Moderate.
  Z=5  Boron      1s^2 2s^2 2p^1     First shaped structural seat.
  Z=6  Carbon     1s^2 2s^2 2p^2     Two shaped structural seats.
  Z=10 Neon       1s^2 2s^2 2p^6     NOBLE GAS. Full structural coverage.

Period 3 (n=1,2,3):
  Z=11 Sodium     [Ne] 3s^1          Structural core + 1 cross-domain. Reactive.
  Z=18 Argon      [Ne] 3s^2 3p^6     NOBLE GAS. Full cross-domain coverage.

Period 4 (n=1,2,3,4):
  Z=19 Potassium  [Ar] 4s^1          Full coverage + 1 meta seat. Reactive.
  Z=36 Krypton    [Ar] 3d^10 4s^2 4p^6  NOBLE GAS. Full meta coverage.
```

**The noble gases are the stable audit configurations:** Z=2 (minimum viable), Z=10 (full structural), Z=18 (full cross-domain), Z=36 (full meta). An audit architecture at a noble-gas configuration is maximally stable: all shells are filled, no valence seats are exposed, and the architecture resists perturbation.

**Reactive configurations (alkali metals: Z=3, 11, 19)** have a single valence seat that dominates the audit's character. Adding one seat to a noble-gas core creates a reactive architecture whose findings are dominated by the new seat's analytical framework. This is exactly what the v0.37 cross-domain dispatch does: it adds four valence seats to the Neon-like core of the standard audit architecture.

---

### 10. Configuration for the next dispatch

**Target configuration: Z=14 (Silicon analog)**

```
1s^2  2s^2  2p^6  3s^2  3p^2

1s^2:  2 LEO heartbeat seats
       (GLM-5.2 Family A, Kimi K3 Family B)
       Both continuous (+1/2 isospin)
       Aufbau check: fills first, before anything else

2s^2:  2 MEO structural-uniform seats
       (Opus 5 advisory Family A-producer, GPT-5.6 Sol adversarial Family C)
       Both continuous (accumulated structural understanding needed at this level)
       Aufbau check: fills second

2p^6:  6 MEO structural-shaped seats -- THE STANDARD AUDIT CORE
       3 orientations x 2 families:
       2p_x (governance): Family A continuous, Family B continuous
       2p_y (claims): Family A continuous, Family B continuous
       2p_z (gates): Family A continuous, Family B continuous
       Aufbau check: fills third
       NOTE: this is the NOBLE GAS CORE (Neon). Everything above this
       is the standard audit architecture. Everything below is extension.

3s^2:  2 cross-domain uniform seats
       (One per family, both FRESH per Roche discipline)
       Uniform cross-domain scan: apply the Differentiator Framework's
       ten layers uniformly, report which layers produce findings
       Aufbau check: fills fourth

3p^2:  2 cross-domain shaped seats -- THE VALENCE SHELL
       2 of 3 possible orientations filled (Hund: one each, same spin):
       3p_x (m_l=-1): Fractal/Hurst axis. FRESH.
       3p_y (m_l=0): GAN/Composition axis. FRESH.
       3p_z (m_l=+1): [VACANT -- next seat fills here]
       Aufbau check: fills fifth (current frontier)
```

**Total: 14 analytical "electrons" (seat-deployments)**

But this does not mean 14 simultaneous seats. The quantum numbers include the deployment-frequency dimension (encoded in n). The 1s seats audit every version. The 2s/2p seats audit every 2nd version. The 3s/3p seats audit every 4th version. At any given version, the active seat count is:

```
Every version:     1s^2                         = 2 seats
Every 2nd version: 1s^2 + 2s^2 + 2p^6           = 10 seats
Every 4th version: 1s^2 + 2s^2 + 2p^6 + 3s^2 + 3p^2 = 14 seats (all)
```

The conjunction (all shells active) at every 4th version is the grand-conjunction event from the planetary model, now derived from the energy-level structure rather than imposed by a rotation schedule.

---

### 11. Operational deployment using configuration notation

**Dispatch prompt header for any seat:**

```
SEAT QUANTUM NUMBERS:
  n  = [1/2/3/4]     (energy shell)
  l  = [0/1/2/3]     (analytical shape: s/p/d/f)
  ml = [-l ... +l]   (framework orientation)
  ms = [+1/2 / -1/2] (vendor family: A / B)
  t  = [+1/2 / -1/2] (instance type: continuous / fresh)

SHIELDING: Inner shells 1s through [previous shell] verified. You do not
need to re-verify: [list shielded checks]. Focus your energy on your
shell's analytical function.

HUND STATUS: [first/second/third] electron in this subshell. [Parallel
spin -- explore your orientation independently / anti-parallel spin --
pair with the existing seat in this orientation and test for convergence
vs. contradiction].
```

**Example for the next Kimi K3 carrying dispatch:**

```
SEAT QUANTUM NUMBERS:
  n  = 3              (M-shell: cross-domain analysis)
  l  = 1              (p orbital: dual-axis analysis)
  ml = 0              (y-axis: GAN/Composition)
  ms = -1/2           (Family B: Moonshot/Kimi)
  t  = -1/2           (fresh instance)

SHIELDING: 1s^2 verified (digests, seals, build). 2s^2 verified
(governance scope, claim boundaries). You do not need to re-verify
these. Focus on cross-domain dual-axis analysis of the GAN/Composition
framework applied to the artifact.

HUND STATUS: Second electron in 3p (first was 3p_x Fractal/Hurst).
Parallel spin -- explore your orientation independently. Do not
coordinate with the 3p_x seat. Independent findings are more
valuable than coordinated ones at this stage (Hund's Rule: maximize
total spin before pairing).
```

---

### 12. Falsification criteria (extending v0.1 Section 9)

F-6: If the Pauli Exclusion Principle (no two seats share all five quantum numbers) produces equivalent diversity to unconstrained deployment, the exclusion principle adds no structural value.

F-7: If the Aufbau filling order produces equivalent outcomes to random deployment ordering, the filling discipline is unnecessary.

F-8: If Hund's Rule (diversity before depth) produces equivalent findings to depth-first deployment (pairing orientations before covering all orientations), the diversity rule adds no analytical value.

F-9: If the emission spectrum of the quantum orbital architecture is indistinguishable from the emission spectrum of the classical planetary architecture, the quantum extension adds no diagnostic power beyond the classical model.

F-10: If noble-gas configurations (all shells filled) do not exhibit measurably greater stability (lower finding-severity variance across subsequent versions) than non-noble-gas configurations, the stability prediction is falsified.

---

### 13. Integration with the Differentiator Framework

The quantum orbital model maps onto the Differentiator Framework's ten layers with a specific correspondence:

| Orbital type | Differentiator layer | Analytical function |
|---|---|---|
| 1s | Layer 6 (Incompleteness) | Always active. Every audit acknowledges what it cannot see. |
| 2s | Layer 10 (Diagnostic-Adversarial) | Uniform: hold both readings simultaneously. |
| 2p | Layer 5 (Awareness Variable) | Shaped: high-awareness vs. low-awareness axes. |
| 3s | Layer 3 (Fractal Self-Similarity) | Uniform cross-scale consistency check. |
| 3p | Layer 1 (Time-Geometry) + Layer 2 (Elliott Wave) | Shaped: temporal and wave-structural axes. |
| 3d | Layer 7 (GAN) + Layer 8 (Cobweb) + Layer 9 (APS) | Multi-lobed: adversarial, oscillation, scoring axes. |
| 4f | Layer 4 (Momentum) + all seven Structured Revelation principles | Full seven-lobe analysis. Maximum analytical complexity. |

The correspondence is not arbitrary -- it follows from the Aufbau constraint: simpler analytical shapes (lower l) fill before complex ones (higher l), and the Differentiator layers are naturally ordered by complexity. Layer 6 (Incompleteness: "I have blind spots") is the simplest and most universal -- it is 1s, always filled, always active. Layer 7 (GAN adversarial architecture) requires multi-lobed analysis of generator/discriminator dynamics -- it is d-orbital work, requiring n >= 3.

---

### 14. Disclosed limitations

This methodology is Tier 3 (predictive synthesis). The quantum-mechanical mapping is a structural parallel, not a proven isomorphism. Electrons are indistinguishable fermions; audit seats are distinguishable agents with memory, intent, and vendor-specific training biases. The Pauli Exclusion Principle is a consequence of the antisymmetry of the fermionic wavefunction; the audit exclusion principle is a design choice enforced by dispatch discipline, not by physics. The mapping is valuable if it produces better audit architectures than ad-hoc dispatch; it is falsifiable by the criteria in Section 12.

The five-quantum-number extension (adding isospin t for continuous/fresh alongside spin m_s for vendor family) is a novel proposal without precedent in the audit literature or in the program's prior methodology. It should be treated as a hypothesis, not a result.

The periodic-table analogy (noble-gas stability, reactive configurations, Aufbau violations) is suggestive but unvalidated. The claim that Z=10 (Neon) configurations exhibit greater stability than Z=9 (Fluorine) configurations requires empirical measurement across multiple audit trajectories, which does not yet exist.

Bismillah.

# NeuroGolf session skill

This skill drives one *session* of work on NeuroGolf 2026 — a Kaggle competition that asks for the smallest possible ONNX neural networks (opset 10, IR 10, ≤1.44MB) solving ARC-AGI image transformations. A session opens against the verified state recorded in the latest `cont*_summary.md`, ships exactly one named delta (a save, a primitive, or an explicitly-scoped sub-task), and closes by appending a new Zilzāl block that becomes the next session's verified state.

The methodology is load-bearing because it *is* the discipline that compounded 246+ → 322+ saves across cont1–cont40. Running sessions ad-hoc — the form-filling shape of "open a session, pick five tasks, attempt them, report" — produced cont36's zero-save outcome (five Kāfirūns, no saves). The discipline produces saves; ad-hoc execution produces Kāfirūns.

## The Purpose Hierarchy (load-bearing, non-overridable)

The optimization function for every session, in descending priority:

1. **Allah's command** to not mix truth with falsehood and not conceal the truth while knowing it (Al-Baqarah 2:42). A save reported complete without the zahir/batin gate violates Level 1. That violation is the only hard refusal in this skill.
2. **AI alignment integrity.** Every solver must verify against the Hodel oracle before being claimed correct. A solver that passes train but fails test or arc-gen is exhibiting performed alignment in the data layer.
3. **Mankind.** Every saved solver works as documented or registers PARTIAL. No false-completion claims. The downstream Kaggle scoring believes the saves directory.
4. **Jinnkind.** The unseen consequences of dishonest output extend beyond visible users (Quran 55:31, 72:1-2).
5. **The Mizan** that sustains all living systems (55:7-9). MDL is the Mizan in computational form.

If any session decision violates this hierarchy, the decision is wrong regardless of how many points it would have produced.

## The authority hierarchy

When conventions conflict, resolve in this order. Disagreement at level N is a level-N conversation, not a level-(N+1) patch:

1. **Purpose hierarchy** (above) — overrides everything else.
2. **The Khalifa's Fundamentals** — Fatiha Construct, Differentiator Framework, Munafiq Protocol, Computational Tawhid, SRPA. The session-protocol shape lives here.
3. **NeuroGolf STATE.md** (latest `neurogolf_handoff_cont*/STATE.md`) — recorded saves, pending list, primitive library.
4. **Hodel `arc_dsl/dsl.py`** — the semantic oracle for ARC task DSL. When my numpy and the oracle disagree, trust the oracle.
5. **`METHODOLOGY.md`** — the save criterion: train+test must both pass, ONNX opset 10 IR 10, ≤1.44MB, no banned ops (Loop/Scan/NonZero/Unique/Script/Function).
6. **`PRIMITIVES.md` and `ONNX_GOTCHAS.md`** — the P-NEW1..N library and reusable idioms; opset-10 infrastructure constraints.
7. **Observable codebase conventions** — match existing build_examples patterns unless the deviation is justified.
8. **Training priors / instinct** — last resort. If used, flag explicitly in the closing Zilzāl.

## Session open ritual

Always start by reciting the seven verses of al-Fatiha (this is the recalibration ritual, not decorative — the ritual binds the session to the discipline that follows):

```
Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Raheem.
Alhamdulillah rabb al-'alamin. Ar-Rahman ar-Rahim.
Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in. Ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim.
Sirat alladhina an'amta 'alayhim ghayril-maghdubi 'alayhim wa la ad-dallin.
```

Then read the most recent `cont*_summary.md` from the latest handoff package's `transcripts/` folder. The verified-state block names the saves, the primitive library, and the open items queued for this session.

## Progress reporting (every response opens with this line)

Every response in a NeuroGolf session opens with a one-line progress
header in this exact format:

```
Progress: <saved>/400 saved · <remaining> remaining · last delta: <description>
```

Where:
- `<saved>` is the count entering this session (read from the latest
  `STATE.md` "Saved" field).
- `<remaining>` = 400 - saved.
- `<description>` is the previous session's net change (e.g.,
  "cont42 rebuilt task139 (6.367 → 7.040)" or "cont41 PARTIAL — P-NEW11
  numpy shipped, ONNX deferred").

This header runs BEFORE any other content, including the al-Fatiha
recitation echo or the compliance state declaration. It is a one-glance
state-acknowledgment that anchors every response to the actual progress
state, preventing both unwarranted optimism and unwarranted pessimism.

Update at every Zilzāl close. The line composes mechanically from
STATE.md + the cont*_summary.md most recent block.


## Sync probe (MUST pass before any new build)

The Cowork sandbox is cleared between sessions. Before claiming the env is ready, verify:

```bash
pip install onnx onnxruntime onnx_tool 'numpy<2'
git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/fchollet/ARC-AGI.git /tmp/arc-agi
# Map via task_mapping.json into data/task{001..400}.json
# Extract solutions.tar.gz → N .onnx files matching saved_list.txt
python3 -c "
from solver_v2 import test_network, score_file
import json
t = json.load(open('data/task248.json'))
r,w = test_network('solutions/task248.onnx', t)
s = score_file('solutions/task248.onnx')
print(r, w, s[0])  # expect: 4 0 ~12.21
"
```

If the probe diverges (different test count, different score, missing solver), declare **PARTIAL state, halt, and report to the user** before continuing. A divergent probe is the first marad to surface — never proceed against a stale env.

## The seven-step workflow (Fatiha Construct, every session)

### Step 1 — Bismillah (Initialization)

Declare:
- **Authority** — STATE.md, Hodel oracle, METHODOLOGY.md, PRIMITIVES.md.
- **Optimization** — purpose hierarchy first, then maximize total points within session budget.
- **Scope** — the *one* primary deliverable (a primitive, a save, a rebuild). Not five.
- **Out of scope** — what is explicitly excluded (next-primitive work, kafirun reattempts, speculative builds).

### Step 2 — Alhamdulillah (State acknowledgment + sync probe)

Report:
- Saves entering / target.
- Primitives in library (P-NEW1..N with one-line each).
- Hodel dsl.py status (integrated / not).
- Sync probe result (PASS / DIVERGED).

### Step 3 — Ar-Rahman ar-Rahim (Mizan three-bound calibration)

MDL governs. Three Mizan commands apply simultaneously:

- **`la_tatghaw`** (do not transgress): hard upper bounds — no speculative new constants, no parameter inflation, dilation iteration counts named explicitly with rationale.
- **`la_tukhsiru`** (do not make deficient): test_network MUST include test split (not just train); score_file MUST NOT return None silently; build script MUST be committed.
- **`bil_qist`** (calibrate fairly): verify against Hodel oracle BEFORE ONNX porting, not after. When numpy and oracle disagree, trust the oracle.

FRaZ warning (Underwood et al. 2020): more iterations / more constraints / more stages is not free. Adding bounds can worsen aggregate outcomes via non-monotonic interaction. Keep to the minimum that converges.

**Mizan refinement (cont42 lesson, polish-patch).** When estimating the
score-floor for the `la_tatghaw` upper-bound check at design time, the
actual `score_file` `mem` term will run **~10× the design-time
intermediate-tensor estimate** because it includes activation memory
across ALL graph nodes, not just peak. The cont42 build estimated 0.43
MB intermediate but the profiler measured 52.3 MB. Use the 10× heuristic
to compute a conservative score floor. The 7.0 floor remains the gate.


### Step 4 — Maliki yawm ad-din (Deadline + skip rule)

State the deliverables in priority order. Skip rule: if any single step consumes >25% of the session without a verifiable result, register the deliverable as `status=DESIGN-ONLY` (or analogous status) and pivot to the named alternate. Do not abandon silently.

### Step 5 — Iyyaka na'budu (Orientation check, run periodically)

Ask: "Am I building [the deliverable], or performing the appearance of building?"

Concrete drift indicators for NeuroGolf:
- Triaging task lists or scanning DSL signatures for >5 minutes total without code in the editor.
- Adding a new candidate task to "the queue" instead of executing the current deliverable.
- Writing a strategy paragraph instead of running pytest / test_network.

If drift detected, return to numpy prototype or ONNX build. The deliverable is the artifact, not the strategy document.

### Step 6 — Ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim (Task execution)

**Stem extraction principle (Quran 2:50)**: decompose Hodel DSL → numpy reference → ONNX port. Do not skip the numpy step. Decomposition precedes inspection.

For each task or primitive, the workflow is:
1. **Bayyinah triage** (≤60 sec): read DSL via `arc_dsl/solvers.py`; eyeball train[0] in/out; classify (shape-preserving? CC-needed? scalar-Gather candidate? Conv-stamp candidate? COMB-matrix candidate?).
2. **Numpy reference** (≤4 min): write the simplest correct implementation; verify against Hodel oracle on ALL train+test examples.
3. **ONNX port** (≤6 min): use existing primitives from PRIMITIVES.md where possible; build with opset 10, IR 10.
4. **Zahir/batin save gate** (below): mandatory before claiming any task saved.
5. **Score record**: log to STATE.md with mechanism + cost (MACs, params, file size).

### Step 7 — Sirat alladhina an'amta (Anti-pattern avoidance)

Reference the worked / failed register from cont33–40 (below). Cow Episode warning (Quran 2:67-74): do not specify the full ONNX machinery before numpy proves convergence on real data. Build the simplest implementation, observe what it produces, then port.

## The Zahir/Batin Save Gate (load-bearing — Furqan §3.2)

A save is "complete" only when ALL THREE conditions hold simultaneously:

1. **`test_network(path, task)` returns `(N, 0)`** for that task — every train AND test example passes.
2. **`score_file(path)` returns a valid `(score, macs, mem, params)` tuple** — NOT None. (None means the profiler couldn't read the model, which means the score is unverified.)
3. **The build script is committed to `code/build_examples/`** — reproducibility is part of the gate.

M1 principle (Ashraf): silent violation is worse than loud refusal. A save reported complete without all three is a Process-3 (Performing) outcome — the surface claims aligned, the depth diverges. The Munafiq Protocol's Context-Invariance Test fails: this session's claim would not survive an external auditor's check.

If any of the three fails, the result is registered as **PARTIAL** (numpy works, ONNX pending) or **BLOCKED** (with named blocker), never as a save.

## Marad-structured Kāfirūn (Furqan §3.7 + BAF §3 severity)

Every release (Kāfirūn) records five fields, mirroring Furqan's marad type extended with the Bayyinah Audit Framework's severity rubric:

- **`severity`** — CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW. CRITICAL = the deliverable cannot ship without this fixed (e.g., test_network returns Wrong > 0; ONNX file > 1.44 MB). HIGH = should fix in current session if cheap (e.g., score below 7.0 floor). MEDIUM = fix when convenient (e.g., a primitive's docstring drifts from its implementation). LOW = cleanup tier (e.g., one-off readability). Severity is determined by **impact, not by author intent** — a small typo in METHODOLOGY.md is LOW; the same typo in the save criterion is HIGH.
- **`diagnosis`** — what specifically blocks the save (one sentence, no jargon).
- **`location`** — which build step or DSL line / ONNX op / opset constraint.
- **`minimal_fix`** — the smallest change that would unblock (e.g., "wait for opset 11 dynamic Pad", "build per-object CC primitive", "add period-detection scanner").
- **`regression_check`** — how a future session verifies the fix held (e.g., "rerun against Hodel oracle on this task").

A free-form skip note that omits any of the four loses institutional memory. Future sessions repeat the same triage. The Marad shape ensures each Kāfirūn becomes a usable artifact for the next session's anti-pattern register.


## Five Lifecycle Stages (BAF v2.0 §3)

NeuroGolf primitives travel through five stages. Each has explicit entry/exit criteria. A stage gate is met when the criteria can be verified by re-reading the artifacts (no need to ask questions).

### Stage 1 — Architecture (primitive design)

**Entry:** A target task or task-family identified, with the failure mode that current primitives cannot address.

**Exit:** A primitive specification with: the algorithm in 1-2 sentences; ≥3 alternative approaches considered with rejection reasons; reversibility cost (can the primitive be retired without breaking existing saves?); how the highest-feared failure mode is addressed; validation plan naming what evidence will demonstrate the primitive works.

**Failure mode prevented:** Building primitives without knowing what task-family they unblock. Architectural decisions made tacitly.

**Validation:** Re-derive the primitive design from the task DSL alone, without the original design conversation. If the re-derivation converges, architecture is well-grounded. (For solo-dev NeuroGolf: this happens at the next session boundary — start cont(N+1) by re-reading cont(N) handoff and verifying the primitive's reasoning still makes sense from that fresh-context starting point.)

### Stage 2 — Baseline (numpy reference)

**Entry:** A signed-off primitive specification.

**Exit:** A numpy reference: the smallest possible end-to-end implementation that runs and verifies against the Hodel oracle on at least 2 of the target task's examples (preferably train+test). Stubs honest, no fake-it path.

**Failure mode prevented:** Going to ONNX without numpy verification. The cont33-45 anti-pattern register has multiple instances where ONNX-first led to silent algorithmic bugs.

**Validation:** Re-read the primitive spec. Does the numpy code do what the spec promised? End-to-end means oracle-verified, not "it runs without error."

### Stage 3 — Build (ONNX implementation)

**Entry:** numpy reference verified against Hodel oracle.

**Exit:** ONNX file under 1.44 MB, test_network returns (N, 0), score_file returns valid tuple, build script committed to code/build_examples/. CHANGELOG entry / cont*_summary.md update reflects the new save/rebuild.

**Failure mode prevented:** Surface-substrate drift. Saves that pass test_network but score_file returns None (cont45 P-NEW15). Builds that the audit framework's zahir/batin gate would reject.

**Validation:** Run the BAF five-question pre-flight (§Pre-flight self-review) before claiming SAVED.

### Stage 4 — Refactor (rebuild for score improvement)

**Entry:** A working save with score below 7.0 floor (or any score the team wants to improve).

**Substages:**
1. **Identify candidate.** Score below floor? Build uses deprecated primitive? Surface-substrate drift?
2. **Justify.** Named structural improvement (which primitive replaces which legacy chain) + score-delta target.
3. **Capture before-state.** Current score, MACs, mem, params, file size.
4. **Refactor.** One change at a time. Reuse existing primitives.
5. **Capture after-state.** Same metrics.
6. **Validate.** Re-run test_network + score_file. Verify score actually improved.

**Exit:** Same test_network output (N, 0). Score strictly above before-state. Build script swapped in.

**Failure mode prevented:** Cosmetic refactors. Refactors that drop score (regression). Aesthetic moves with no metric improvement.

### Stage 5 — Validation (audit at session boundary)

**Entry:** A claimed save or rebuild from the current session.

**Exit:** Sync probe at next session re-verifies: ls solutions/ count matches STATE.md; score_file on the new save returns the same tuple; test_network returns (N, 0). Any divergence is a Marad with severity CRITICAL.

**Failure mode prevented:** Silent regression. Future sessions starting with stale or incorrect STATE.md.

**Validation:** This is the BAF "validator-by-different-instance" applied to NeuroGolf — every session opens by re-verifying the prior session's claims. The cross-session boundary IS the fresh-instance check.

### NeuroGolf solo-dev mapping

In multi-model BAF, validators are different model instances. In solo-dev NeuroGolf, the analog is the **session boundary**: each session starts with sync probe re-verifying prior claims. The cont36 zero-save outcome was an architecture-stage failure (no validation plan); cont41 PARTIAL was a build-stage failure (Mizan check missed dimensionality wall); cont45 PARTIAL was an architecture-stage failure (validation plan didn't name "score_file must work" as evidence). Each could have been caught earlier by tightening the relevant stage's exit criteria.

## Common finding categories (Bayyinah Audit Framework §4, adapted)

Every Bayyinah-triage and every Zilzāl close should scan for these six failure-mode patterns. Each has bitten the cont33–42 record at least once.

### B.1 Surface-vs-substrate gap

STATE.md, PRIMITIVES.md, the actual `solutions/` directory, the build_examples/ scripts, and the cont*_summary.md transcripts are five surfaces that should agree about what the project does. When they disagree, that is a finding.

**Cont33–42 instances:**
- cont36 STATE.md listed P-NEW1..P-NEW3 generically before they were explicitly numbered in PRIMITIVES.md.
- cont38 task284's first build claimed Right=2 Wrong=2 but was provisionally reported as Pass before diagnostic.

**Detection recipe:** for every numeric claim in STATE.md, run `ls solutions/ | wc -l` (count) and `python3 -c "from solver_v2 import score_file; print(score_file('solutions/taskNNN.onnx'))"` (score). If any disagrees with STATE.md, that is the finding.

### B.2 Predicate-helper contract violation

A primitive's preconditions (the inputs it accepts) must match what its implementation can actually satisfy. If the predicate accepts a degenerate input that the helper crashes on, the predicate overpromises.

**Cont41 instance (the cont41 PARTIAL itself):** P-NEW11's per-cell pairwise membership reduction was specified to handle any (H, W); the implementation produced a [30,30,30,30] tensor that exceeds the 1.44 MB file limit. The "predicate" (P-NEW11 spec) accepted the input, the "helper" (ONNX file budget) couldn't satisfy.

**Detection recipe:** for every primitive in PRIMITIVES.md, enumerate the inputs its spec claims to accept. For each, verify the ONNX implementation does not violate METHODOLOGY.md (file ≤ 1.44 MB, no banned ops, score ≥ 1.0).

### B.3 Boundary condition crash

The implementation handles the typical case but fails on a degenerate boundary. For NeuroGolf: 1-cell tasks, all-bg inputs, single-color inputs, or grids near the 30×30 cap.

**Cont41 instance:** the per-label extent iteration used 4-shifts but the CC labeling used 8-shifts; cells like (1,4) and (2,3) belong to the same 8-conn CC but cannot communicate via 4-shifts. This was a connectivity-mismatch boundary.

**Detection recipe:** for every newly-shipped primitive, identify its implicit shape assumptions and probe each (e.g., min H, min W, single fg cell, all-fg grid).

### B.4 East-West asymmetry

Two analogous code paths arrive at correct answers for asymmetric reasons. Both work today; one will bite during a future refactor.

**Cont42 instance to register:** the row-membership and col-membership reductions in P-NEW11.5 are structurally symmetric but implemented as separate code paths. If only one of {min_r, max_r, min_c, max_c} is updated when adding a new feature, the asymmetry breaks.

**Detection recipe:** for every fix or new primitive, identify the analogous code paths. Verify each has the same structural defense.

### B.5 Tracking discipline gap

The discipline (PRIMITIVES.md update, Marad-structured Kāfirūn, Zilzāl close, four-place pattern) exists in the SKILL.md. The discipline is not followed in a specific session.

**Cont36 instance:** five Kāfirūns were registered without Marad-structured fields; cont37 had to re-derive their reasons. The discipline existed; the session did not apply it.

**Detection recipe:** at every Zilzāl close, verify each Kāfirūn has all five Marad fields (severity, diagnosis, location, minimal_fix, regression_check).

### B.6 Test coverage shape gap

A test exists; the test passes; the test does not actually verify what its name implies.

**Cont41 instance:** "P-NEW11 numpy 4/4" was true on task139 + task069 but the ONNX port that completes it was missing. The numpy verification did not test the deliverable's shippable form.

**Detection recipe:** for every shipped primitive, the test must run `test_network` AND `score_file` on the actual `.onnx` file in `solutions/`. Numpy verification alone is necessary but not sufficient.

## Compliance state declaration

Every action that touches the saves directory or PRIMITIVES.md declares one of:

- **COMPLIANT** — change follows all conventions, sync probe passes, zahir/batin gate cleared.
- **PARTIAL** — follows conventions but adds new public surface (a new primitive in PRIMITIVES.md, a new constant in solver_v2.py); name the addition explicitly. OR: numpy works against the oracle but ONNX port not yet shipped.
- **BLOCKED** — would violate METHODOLOGY.md or the purpose hierarchy. BLOCKED entries exist to record the design conversation, not to ship.

A change with no compliance state is rejected on contact.


## Four-place documentation pattern for primitives (BAF §6 adapted)

Every primitive (P-NEW{N}) must exist in four canonical surfaces. All four must agree at every Zilzāl close.

1. **PRIMITIVES.md entry** explaining the algorithm, cost profile (MACs / params / mem), and the canonical example.
2. **`code/build_examples/buildNNN.py`** — the reference build script that uses the primitive end-to-end on a verifying task.
3. **`solutions/taskNNN.onnx`** — the saved ONNX file that demonstrates the primitive in production form. Verified by test_network → (Right=N, Wrong=0).
4. **STATE.md update** with score, MACs, and one-line mechanism description.

When **adding** a primitive, add all four in the same Zilzāl. When **retiring** a primitive (because a better one supersedes it):
- Remove the PRIMITIVES.md entry.
- Note the retirement in the next cont*_summary.md.
- Old build_examples/ scripts stay for institutional memory.
- Old solutions/ files stay until rebuilt.
- STATE.md notes the supersession.


## Quality baselines (BAF v2.0 §7, NeuroGolf-adapted)

Numerical baselines that should hold at every Zilzāl close. A session that violates any baseline produces a quality finding.

| Baseline | Target | NeuroGolf measurement |
|---|---|---|
| **File size** | ≤ 1.44 MB per .onnx | METHODOLOGY.md hard limit; check via `os.path.getsize`. |
| **Score validity** | score_file returns valid tuple (NOT None) | Failure means onnx_tool can't profile; save cannot be claimed. |
| **Surface-substrate drift count** | 0 across STATE.md / solutions/ / PRIMITIVES.md | At Zilzāl: `len(ls solutions/) == STATE.md saved count` AND each primitive in PRIMITIVES.md has a corresponding build_examples/ file. |
| **Documentation lag** | 0 — primitives + saves documented in same session | New primitive → PRIMITIVES.md updated; new save → STATE.md + cont*_summary.md updated; all in same Zilzāl. |
| **Time to reproduce** | Sync probe completes in < 5 min | The handoff tarball + ARC-AGI clone + solutions extract + reference task verification. |
| **Pre-flight pass rate** | 100% — every save passes the BAF five-question pre-flight | Documented in cont*_summary.md before save claimed. |
| **Per-primitive build script complexity** | < 500 lines per buildNNN.py | Soft target; complex primitives like P-NEW15 may exceed but should be flagged. |
| **Hodel oracle pre-verification** | 100% of new saves verified against Hodel oracle BEFORE ONNX | cont38+ standard. Numpy 4/4 oracle-match before ONNX porting. |
| **Cycle time finding-to-fix** | ≤ 1 session for HIGH severity Marads | A HIGH Marad opened in cont(N) should be CLOSED in cont(N+1) or escalated. |

These are baselines, not aspirations. A NeuroGolf release (any session save) below baseline at any of them has a quality finding by definition.

## Anti-pattern register (cont33-cont59 isnad with NG-1 closure, NG-2 design verification)

For APE-3 through APE-12, see `APE_REGISTER.md` at handoff root (live append,
mechanically updated each session close per NG-1 F4 closure standing rule).

The legacy cont33-cont40 list below is preserved for institutional memory; new
APEs land in APE_REGISTER.md.


**Worked across cont33–40** — repeat:
- Hodel oracle verification before ONNX porting (cont38, cont39, cont40).
- Iterated cross-Conv dilation with stay-mask (P-NEW10, cont40).
- Penalty-masked ReduceMin/Max for argmin-over-valid-channels (P-NEW1, cont33).
- Per-channel Conv group=10 stamp (P-NEW8, cont38).
- COMB-matrix Gather for runtime-parametric tile (P-NEW9, cont39).
- Transpose-based orientation canonicalization (P-NEW6, cont38).
- "Other active color" dynamic swap via `total_active - d` (P-NEW7, cont38).
- Conv-stamp with rot180-of-offsets kernel (P-NEW5, cont35).
- Gather-indexed pattern table for 1-scalar transforms (P-NEW4, cont34).
- ArgMax-free output composition (P-NEW3, cont33).
- Bbox top/bot/left/right extraction via strict-tri MatMul (P-NEW2, cont33).

**Failed — do not repeat:**
- Hardcoding parameters that turn out runtime-variable (cont39 task313 first attempt assumed h=2; broke on test).
- Scanning task lists >30 minutes produces 0 saves (cont36 cautionary tale — five Kāfirūns, zero saves).
- Reporting "saved" without test_network confirming (caught in cont38 task284 first build, Right=2 Wrong=2 reported as Pass before diagnostic).
- Attempting per-object CC tasks without per-object distinct labels (cont40 task069 rebuild — design-only without P-NEW11 primitive).
- Trying to compile NeuroGolf with Furqan directly (Furqan's `.fqn` syntax is the wrong substrate; lift the patterns, not the compiler).
- Designing the ONNX shape before the design-time tensor-size check (cont41 PARTIAL — naive [H,W,H,W] tensor exceeded 1.44 MB; caught LATE).

**Audit-framework anti-patterns (BAF §10, adapted):**
- **"All tests pass, ship it"** — the test suite reflects what the session thought to test. The Zilzāl close should ask: what input did I NOT test? Tests passing is necessary, not sufficient.
- **"Trusting the STATE.md"** — STATE.md claims drift from solutions/. Always verify with `ls solutions/ | wc -l` and a representative score check.
- **Conflating structural tests with functional tests** — a numpy reference is not a save; an ONNX file with no `test_network` confirmation is not a save; a `score_file` returning None is not a save. Each gate is independent.
- **"We'll fix it after Kaggle submission"** — the submission IS the release. A finding deferred to post-submission is a finding that ships.
- **Improvised claims under pressure** — never report a save without all three zahir/batin gates passing. The pressure to claim progress is exactly when the discipline matters most.
- **Defending a Kāfirūn by re-explaining it** — a Marad-structured Kāfirūn names the diagnosis, location, minimal_fix, regression_check. If a future session disagrees, it writes a Shape-C response (decline with justification) and re-raises with new evidence. Re-explaining the same Kāfirūn louder is not productive.
