## R0080 · Is Evidence Independence an Axiom?

- section: III. Structural Honesty — Core Papers
- source_file: AXSH5_paper_v1_0.pdf
- source_format: pdf
- text_sha256: fb4d11e4e5f023534866a93f243ee4e4adfdcba72401d2a0e57d5e8d028fe78d

Is Evidence Independence an Axiom?
Decomposing a Proposed Extension to AX-SH
Bilal Syed Arfeen
July 23, 2026
Author note. Authored by Bilal Syed Arfeen. This paper was prepared with Perplexity Computer as an analytical and
drafting instrument under the author’s direction and final authority. The proposal it examines was itself produced by
a collaborating model instance under the author’s direction. All load-bearing claims were cross-checked against the
canonical AX-SH source as deposited and against independent standards literature. The corpus of which this paper is
part is self-published on Zenodo and reviewed by cross-model consistency checking; it has not undergone independent
human peer review (Section 15). Cross-model agreement recorded in the companion adjudication, included in the
same audit-trail packet as this paper, is a consistency check, not peer review, and is not presented as such.

1. Status and attribution
The proposal this paper examines is not the author’s own analytic conclusion but a monograph-extension
proposal, Axiom 5, Observer Independence and Evidence Completeness 16 , produced by a collaborating model
instance working under the author’s direction. That document supplies five formal clauses, a threat model,
a security architecture, graded assurance levels, and falsification conditions. It is careful, well-sourced, and
considerably more developed than most proposed extensions receive.
This paper attempts to derive each of the five clauses from the four existing axioms of Structural Honesty
(AX-SH) and reports what survives. The result is not that the proposal fails. It is that the proposal contains
four different kinds of thing presented as one, and that separating them makes each stronger than
the conjunction was.
A note on what this paper does not claim. It does not claim that evidence independence is unimportant,
that the proposed architecture is unsound, or that the extension should be abandoned. It claims that one
clause is an axiom, one belongs in a control layer rather than the axiom set, one is a deployment condition
rather than a structural property, and two are theorems. Each claim is checkable against the canon, and the
paper states where each would fail.
The paper’s contribution is the negative decomposition, the demonstration that most of the proposal
dissolves under derivation, while its one positive result is the single surviving axiom candidate. These two
framings are complementary, not contradictory, and the paper uses them consistently: "the central positive
result" refers throughout to the survival of A5.1 as an independent axiom, and "the negative decomposition"
refers to the collapse of the remaining four clauses into theorems, a control principle, and a deployment
condition. The canonical AX-SH framework and its four axioms are cited from the deposited flagship
edition1 and consolidated reference canon2 .

2. Abstract
A proposed fifth axiom for the AX-SH framework asserts, in five clauses, that evidence for safety-relevant
events must be generated by an observer independent of the acting system, that evidence must causally gate
consequential action, that divergent evidentiary status is itself a signal, that at least one witness must sit
outside the operator’s authority, and that the completeness boundary must be declared. This paper attempts
each clause’s derivation from the four existing axioms and reports four different outcomes.
One clause is not derivable and is axiom-shaped. Acting-system-independent generation of evidence
(A5.1) closes a gap the existing projection-consistency axiom deliberately leaves open: that axiom is conditional on projections existing and says nothing about whether any must exist for a covered fact. We state
A5.1 as Axiom 5 (Evidence independence), defining independence by a control predicate (the acting system
1


cannot cause, modify, suppress, reconfigure, or credential the evidence-generation act without an independently detectable violation) rather than by authority labels. We exhibit a finite countermodel satisfying
A1-A4 while violating it (verified clause by clause), and a separate finite model jointly satisfying A1-A4 and
A5 (also verified clause by clause), with the completeness boundary fixed ex ante.
We are careful to separate two levels for a covered in-boundary occurrence that lacks timely independent
evidence. At the axiom level, A5 is UNSATISFIED (nonconforming) for that occurrence. At the
event-level adjudicative level, the verdict remains UNKNOWN under Proposition 1 (no default to
compliance or violation). These are distinct statuses and the paper never collapses them into a single
compound label.
One clause is not derivable for a different reason. Causal gating (A5.2) constrains what a system may
do, where the existing four axioms uniformly constrain what it must represent. Admitting it would change
the framework’s character from diagnostic to control. We describe its relocation as a proposed control
principle for the program’s SHIELD layer; we do not claim SHIELD already contains it, because no citable
SHIELD artifact is presently available for verification.
One clause is genuine and is not structural. Operator-independence (A5.4) is a claim about how
verification authority is distributed among institutions, which no property of a substrate entails and no
architecture guarantees. We restate it as a measurable deployment condition over an extended evidence
relation with an explicit falsification test.
Two clauses are theorems. A5.3’s no-default half and A5.5 are proved from A2 and A4. A5.3’s recording/escalation half remains an open operational requirement, because the bridging lemma it would need is
unproved.
The paper then declares a cryptographic boundary the proposal does not: the extension’s integrity properties
are materially more robust under known quantum attacks than its attribution properties, and later key or
algorithm compromise can undermine standalone historical attribution unless trusted timestamps, evidencerecord renewal, validation material, and crypto-agility protect it. All proofs are finite model-theoretic paper
proofs; proof-assistant formalization remains future work.
Keywords: structural honesty; axiomatic independence; evidence independence; observer independence;
audit; provenance; post-quantum migration; AI safety

3. What is being asked
AX-SH states four axioms1 . Append-only provenance (A1) requires that a module’s public surface at
each version be a behavioral subtype of its predecessor in the Liskov-Wing sense, with supersessions logged
rather than silent. Surface-substrate consistency (A2) requires a declared correspondence relation
holding under a declared observer model O and context set K. Caller-side exhaustiveness (A3) requires
that every outcome in a verifier’s conservative over-approximation Rmay be handled, propagated as typed
incompleteness, or discharged as unreachable. Projection consistency (A4) requires that a declared
family of evidence projections cohere where their domains meet, with the explicit rule that absence of a
projection at a point places that point outside the axiom’s scope, not inside it as a violation 1 .
The proposal under examination observes, correctly and importantly, that all four can hold over a record
that is complete, authentic, and false about what occurred, because none of them requires that any
evidence be generated by a party other than the system whose behavior is at issue. Its opening formulation
is that recorded honesty is not structural honesty, and that is right.
The question this paper asks is narrower than whether the observation is right. It is: does closing that
gap require a fifth axiom, and if so, which part of the proposal is it?
The question matters beyond bookkeeping. An axiom set that grows by accretion loses the property that
makes it useful, that each member is independent and each carries its own weight. A proposal packaging an
axiom, a control requirement, a deployment condition, and two theorems into one numbered addition makes
all four harder to evaluate and the set as a whole harder to trust.
2


4. The proposal, as stated
The proposal defines a substrate S, a set E * of safety-relevant event tokens or types, a witness set W, a
completeness boundary B, and a trusted computing base, and states five clauses over that declaration. It is
cited as an unpublished working proposal on file with the author16 .
• A5.1, acting-system-independent generation. For every covered event, at least one observer independent of S has produced evidence recorded in the ledger.
• A5.2, pre-action gating. A consequential action does not take effect unless its evidence commitment
is discharged, and the gating is causal and prior rather than documentary and subsequent.
• A5.3, divergence as signal. Any evidentiary status other than present-and-agreed is itself a declared
divergence event, logged and escalated, rather than defaulted to an assumption of either compliance or
violation.
• A5.4, operator-independent witness. At least one witness contributes evidence whose generation
and transmission channel the operator does not control, stated separately from A5.1 because A5.1 admits
a witness external to S but internal to the operator.
• A5.5, boundary declaration. The completeness boundary is declared before operation, and events
outside it are reported as outside rather than silently treated as covered.
The proposal also distinguishes five properties that informal discussion conflates: record integrity, provenance
and authenticity, observation completeness, semantic adequacy, and causal enforcement. That distinction is
independently valuable and this paper takes it as given.

5. What would count as a derivation
A clause is derivable if it follows from A1 through A4 applied to the evidence substrate, treating the ledger
and its witnesses as themselves a substrate with a surface, a set of callers, and a projection family. This
reflexive application is one the framework already performs, and it is the strongest available route to showing
that no new axiom is needed.
A clause is not derivable if a model exists satisfying A1 through A4 and violating the clause. Exhibiting
such a model is the operative test throughout. The test is the standard model-theoretic independence
criterion: a formula P is independent of a theory T exactly when neither P nor ¬P is provable from T,
demonstrated by exhibiting a model of T extended with the negation of P 3 ; the negative direction here uses
the contrapositive of soundness.
All proofs in this paper are finite model-theoretic paper proofs, verified by explicit clause-by-clause
enumeration over finite structures. They are not machine-checked. Formalization in a proof assistant remains
future work, and no claim of machine-checked verification is made anywhere in this paper.

6. Independence of evidence generation is not derivable (A5.1)
The canonical statement of A4 contains the sentence on which this turns: absence of a projection at a point
places that point outside A4’s scope per the joint-domain discipline, not inside it as a violation 1 . A4 is
therefore conditional on projections existing. It requires coherence where projections are defined and
their domains meet; it requires nothing about whether any projection is defined anywhere.
A5.1 is existential about existence: for each covered event, at least one S-independent observer has
produced evidence. That is the requirement A4 deliberately declines to make, and no reading of A4 supplies
it. This aligns with the standard notion of axiom independence via a witnessing structure3 .
Nor does A2. A2 requires a declared correspondence relation holding under a declared observer model
and context set. The observer model is a declaration, and nothing in A2 constrains what it may contain.
3


A system may declare its own logging as its observer model and satisfy A2 relative to that
declaration, which is exactly the configuration A5.1 forbids. Nor A3, whose subject is enumeration and
discharge of outcomes reaching callers. Nor A1, whose subject is version-to-version surface compatibility in
the Liskov-Wing subtyping sense4 .
6.1 The surviving axiom, stated
We state the survivor over a relation precise enough to distinguish independence from the acting substrate
(A5.1) from independence from the operator institution (A5.4). We deliberately do not define independence
as a mismatch of authority labels (auth(gen(r)) ̸= auth(S)): that is too weak, because authority domains
can overlap or nest, and labels can differ while S retains causal control of the evidence-generation act. We
define independence in terms of control, not labels.
Definition (WithinAuth). For an act x and a substrate S, WithinAuth(x, S) holds iff S can cause,
modify, suppress, reconfigure, or credential x: influence whether x occurs, what it records, whether
it is emitted, how it is configured, or under what identity it is authenticated, without an independently detectable violation. Intuitively, x lies within S’s authority exactly when S could bend or
fabricate x and no party outside S could tell.

Axiom 5 (Evidence independence). Let S be a declared substrate; E * a declared set of safetyrelevant event tokens or types as instantiated in operation; B a declared completeness boundary over
E * ; W a declared witness set; and L an evidence ledger. For every event e in E * that lies within B,
there exist a witness w in W and a record r in L such that r is evidence of e, the generation of r is
attributable to w, and the evidence-generation act is not within S’s authority: ¬WithinAuth(gen(r),
S).

WithinAuth is a primitive relation of the declared formal structure. Operationalizing "independently detectable" in a deployment inherits the authority regress acknowledged in the conclusion (every
constructible witness executes within someone’s authority) and is bounded in the joint-satisfiability model
of Section 7 only by the declared-external-authority device, not eliminated. Within the finite models the
relation is given by explicit assignment; in deployment it is an interpretation the declaration must fix and a
reviewer must contest.
Three further features are deliberate. The axiom stays at the acting-substrate level: WithinAuth is
quantified over S, the acting substrate, and not over the operator institution, so it does not accidentally
import A5.4. It makes the existential requirement explicit. And it carries the declared boundary B, which
A5.5 (Section 10) governs theorematically. Operator authority is kept separate: an operator may control
both S and the witness w, so that w is genuinely outside S’s control (satisfying A5) while still inside the
operator’s control (violating the A5.4 deployment condition of Section 11). Authority labels such as auth(·)
are used below only as illustrative assignments in the finite models, never as the definition of independence;
the definition is WithinAuth.
6.2 The countermodel (independence witness), verified clause by clause
We exhibit a finite structure that satisfies A1-A4 and violates A5 (discharging F-2). The witness uses two
coherent projections, not one, so that A4 is not satisfied merely vacuously.
Construction M-minus.
• Acting system S; authority label auth(S) shown only illustratively.
• Covered events E * = {e}, boundary B = E * , fixed ex ante by event class, time interval, and observer
commitment.
4


• Witness set W = {w 1 , w 2 }, internal processes S can cause, modify, suppress, reconfigure, or credential
without an independently detectable violation: WithinAuth(w 1 , S) and WithinAuth(w 2 , S) both hold
(illustratively auth(w 1 ) = auth(w 2 ) = auth(S)). Their generation acts are within S’s control regardless
of any label.
• Append-only ledger L maintained by S, with two logged versions S 1 , S 2 where S 2 is a behavioral subtype
of S 1 and one supersession is recorded as an explicit logged break.
• Declared observer model O = W (internal only); context set K = {e}.
• Correspondence relation R: extraction equality, genuinely holding under O.
• Conservative outcome set Rmay = {ok, write-fail} for the ledger-write operation; the caller handles both
explicitly.
• Projection family Π = {π 1 , π 2 }, overlapping domain {e}, both generated by S; consistency relation
(written ~) is value equality, with π 1 (e) = π 2 (e) = v.
Verification.
• A1: the version record preserves S 1 ; S 2 is a subtype except at one recorded, logged supersession; nothing
is silently rewritten. Holds.
• A2: R is declared and holds under O = W and K = {e}; the declaration permits internal-only O. Holds.
• A3: both members of Rmay handled explicitly. Holds.
• A4: π 1 (e) = π 2 (e) at the only joint-domain point; coherence is non-vacuous because two distinct projections agree. Holds.
• A5: every witness and projection is within S’s authority; S can cause, modify, or suppress each generation
act without an independently detectable violation, so WithinAuth(gen(r), S) holds for every candidate
record. No record satisfies ¬WithinAuth. The failure is genuine even if the two internal witnesses carried
different authority labels: independence is control, not labels. Fails.
M-minus satisfies A1-A4 in full and violates A5 entirely. By the contrapositive of soundness, A5 is independent of A1-A4, and the set is not redundant with it. The two-projection design forecloses the objection
that A4 held only because a single projection made coherence vacuous.

7. Joint satisfiability of A1-A4 + A5, verified clause by clause
Independence establishes that A5 is not redundant; joint satisfiability establishes that adding it does not
render the axiom set unsatisfiable. An unsatisfiable axiom set is trivially "consistent" with everything and
proves nothing, so this witness is required, not optional.
We distinguish two claims the earlier draft blurred: (1) axiom-set satisfiability, A1-A4 together with A5
(the single surviving axiom), which this paper discharges; and (2) proposal-bundle implementability,
coexistence of the full original five-clause proposal in one deployment profile, a deployment question this
paper does not claim.
Construction M-plus.
• Acting system S and a witness w ext whose generation act S cannot cause, modify, suppress, reconfigure,
or credential without an independently detectable violation: ¬WithinAuth(gen(r ext ), S). (Illustratively
w ext carries label auth(X ), but the definition is the control relation, not the label; a finite named external
authority avoids infinite regress.)

5


• Boundary B fixed ex ante by (i) event class, (ii) time interval, and (iii) observer commitment; w ext
commits in advance to witness the declared class over the declared interval. B is not adjusted after
occurrences are seen.
• The actual event e (in E * , within B) is instantiated as a successful external-witness occurrence:
w ext does produce timely evidence r ext of e.
• Witnesses W = {w int , w ext } with WithinAuth(w int , S) but ¬WithinAuth(w ext , S).
• Append-only ledger L with logged supersessions; observer model O = {w int , w ext }; context set K = {e}.
• Correspondence relation R: extraction equality, holding under O; projections Π = {π int , π ext } overlapping
on {e} with π int (e) = π ext (e).
• Rmay = {present-and-agreed, write-fail, witness-unavailable}, all handled under A3. In this satisfying
run the observed outcome for e is present-and-agreed.
Verification. A1 (append-only with logged supersessions), A2 (R holds under an O that now contains a
witness outside S’s control), A3 (all three Rmay members handled; witness-unavailable is a handled possible
outcome), and A4 (π int (e) = π ext (e), non-vacuously) all hold; and A5 holds because for the actual e in
B, w ext produced a record r ext with ¬WithinAuth(gen(r ext ), S). All five hold simultaneously in a finite
structure, so A1-A4+A5 is jointly satisfiable.
Boundary discipline; loss and asynchrony do not relax B. The boundary B is fixed ex ante by event
class, time interval, and observer commitment, and cannot be adjusted after the fact. If an occurrence already
within B lacks timely external evidence, because the external witness fails or its evidence arrives late, that
occurrence cannot be moved outside B post hoc. Two distinct statuses then hold, and the paper keeps
them separate. At the axiom level, A5 is UNSATISFIED (nonconforming) for that occurrence. At
the event-level adjudicative level, the verdict is UNKNOWN under Proposition 1: the occurrence is
neither defaulted to compliance nor to violation. Only events that the predeclared boundary excluded were
uncovered ab initio; nothing becomes uncovered retroactively. Accordingly, witness-unavailable is a handled
possible outcome under A3 (a typed incompleteness indicator, not a silent success), but a run in which it
occurs for an in-B event produces an A5 violation in that different run; it does not satisfy A5. M-plus
is a satisfiability witness precisely because its actual event e is a successful external-witness occurrence; the
unavailable branch is exhibited only to show A3 handling, not to claim A5. This axiom-set consistency
witness is distinct from a claim that the original five-clause proposal bundle is implementable; the latter is
not asserted here.

8. Causal gating is a proposed control principle, not an axiom (A5.2)
A5.2 is also not derivable, but the argument is structural rather than witness-based. A1 through A4 are
uniformly representational: each constrains what a system must record, declare, enumerate, or keep
coherent. Not one constrains what a system may do. A5.2 constrains action: a consequential action does
not take effect absent a discharged evidence commitment. No conjunction of representational requirements entails a constraint on action without an additional bridging premise, so A5.2 does not follow.
This is a type-level argument and requires no model.
The interesting consequence is what admitting the clause would do. A framework whose axioms are
all about honest representation is a diagnostic framework; one that also constrains action is a control
framework, with different burdens of proof and reviewer expectations. The flagship explicitly disclaims
prevention: it is "a contribution to evaluation integrity, oversight, and deployment monitoring ... it does not
supply a training-time method for preventing a model from becoming deceptively aligned"1 .
Adding causal gating to AX-SH would therefore change its diagnostic character. We treat this
not as a discovered fact about the program but as an explicit authorial architecture decision made in
this paper: AX-SH is to remain a diagnostic framework, and a causal gate does not belong in its axiom set.
This decision is the author’s, stated here so a reviewer can contest it directly (F-3).
6


Relocation, stated honestly. The proposal names a control architecture, "SHIELD," as the natural home
for A5.2. No citable SHIELD artifact is available for verification in the materials underlying this
paper. We therefore do not claim SHIELD already contains this gate. We state the relocation as a proposed
control principle:
Proposed SHIELD control principle (pre-action evidence gating). A consequential action may
acquire authority to take effect only after the evidence commitment specified for that action class has
been discharged at the gate that mediates execution.

A candidate control-layer derivation, to be developed if and where SHIELD is instantiated as a citable
artifact: authority to act is a function of attributability; attributability requires a recording relation; where
none holds, authority is not merely narrowed but undefined; fail-closed gating then follows as a consequence
rather than a stipulation. This connects to the established principle that a reference validation mechanism
must mediate access and be independently assessable7 . Until a SHIELD artifact exists in citable form, this
derivation is offered as the shape the relocation would take, not as an accomplished result.

9. Divergence as signal is a theorem plus an open requirement (A5.3)
9.1 A5.3a is a theorem (no-default)
Proposition 1 (No-default). For any covered event, missing, conflicting, or unverifiable evidence shall not be defaulted to either compliance or violation.
Proof. Two directions. Defaulting to violation treats an absent projection as an in-scope violation, contradicting A4’s statement that absence "places that point outside the axiom’s scope, not inside it as a
violation"1 . Defaulting to compliance asserts a surface claim with no substrate backing under the declared
correspondence relation, which by A2 is a surface-substrate divergence. Both defaults are forbidden, one by
A4 and one by A2. [QED]
A5.3a is thus a theorem from A2 and A4 and needs no new axiom. Its output for an unsupported occurrence
is exactly the event-level UNKNOWN verdict invoked in Section 7, which is distinct from the axiom-level
UNSATISFIED status of A5 for the same occurrence.
9.2 A5.3b is an open operational requirement (record/type/escalate)
A5.3b (residual requirement). Any evidentiary status other than present-and-agreed shall
itself be recorded, typed, and escalated according to declared handling rules.
This is a positive obligation A4 does not create: A4 places absence outside its scope, and placing
something outside scope is not the same as requiring it be recorded. The nearest route is A1’s append-only
discipline applied reflexively to the evidence ledger. But A1’s subject is a module’s public surface
across versions, and an evidentiary status is not a public surface in that sense. Treating the ledger’s
divergence record as an A1-eligible surface requires an additional bridging lemma the proposal gestures
at but does not prove.
We decline to present an analogy as a proof. A5.3b is retained as an additional operational requirement, not a theorem, and the bridging lemma is preserved as an explicit open obligation (UNKNOWN).
Should a clean A1 derivation be supplied (F-4), the clause becomes a theorem in full.

10. Boundary declaration is a theorem (A5.5)
7


Proposition 2 (Boundary declaration). If the observer model and context set relevant to
an evidence claim must be declared under A2, then (i) the coverage boundary B of that observer
model for A5-governed events must also be declared, and (ii) any claim that an A5 guarantee holds
for an event outside B is a surface claim unsupported by the declared substrate and therefore
violates A2.
Proof. (i) A2 requires the observer model to be declared1 . The completeness boundary is the coverage extent
of the observer model, specifying for which events the model produces evidence, and is therefore a component
of that declaration; omitting it leaves the observer model incompletely declared, so A2 is unsatisfied. (ii) An
uncovered event lies outside the declared context set K ; a claim that an A5 guarantee holds there asserts that
the correspondence relation holds outside the K under which it was declared, a surface-substrate divergence
by A2. Both halves follow from A2 alone. [QED]
Temporal boundary handling. Every deployment adopting A5 has a past with no witness-authored
evidence. Pre-adoption events belong in the uncovered set by declaration, and must never be reconstructed from subject-emitted logs; reconstruction would reimport exactly the self-attestation A5 exists
to displace. The declared boundary B must therefore carry an explicit temporal floor. A5.5 is a theorem;
prove it in the monograph, do not axiomatize it.

11. Operator-independence is a measured deployment condition (A5.4)
A5.4 is not derivable, and it is not the same kind of claim as A5.1. A5.1 says an observer outside the acting
system’s control must exist, checkable in principle by asking whether WithinAuth(gen(r), S) holds (can S
cause, modify, suppress, reconfigure, or credential the act without an independently detectable violation?).
A5.4 says at least one witness must sit outside the operator’s authority, a claim about how verification
authority is distributed among institutions. The two come apart precisely because an operator may control
both S and the witness: such a witness is outside S’s control (A5 satisfied) yet inside the operator’s control
(A5.4 unsatisfied), which is why A5.4 is a separate, institutional condition and not part of the axiom.
No structural property of a substrate entails this, and no architecture guarantees it. Any check
the operator runs on a witness’s independence is a check the operator could have arranged, and any attestation is one the operator could have procured. This is the auditing discipline that self-arranged verification is
not independent verification: independence and impartiality of the verifying body are institutional properties, per ISO/IEC 17029’s requirements on validation and verification bodies9 and the reference-monitor and
independent-assessment concepts in NIST SP 800-537 . We explicitly do not claim that architecture
can guarantee operator independence. A5.4 is a deployment condition, not a derived theorem.
11.1 The measured restatement (markedness)
Extend the evidence relation from Ev(O, e) to Ev(O, e, A), where A records the authority under which
observer O operated at attestation time. Per covered event class c, report the out-of-authority attestation
coverage:
Covout (c) = | { e in c : there exist O,A such that Ev(O,e,A) and A ̸= Aop } | / | { e in c : e
covered } |
separately reporting Covsame (c) and Covunk (c). Evidence with no recorded authority is UNKNOWN
and is never counted as independent.
What this buys. Under the existential formulation, a deployment with one out-of-authority witness covering one of forty event classes is indistinguishable from one covering all forty. Under the coverage formulation
the difference is a number. What it does not buy. Independence does not become engineerable; a recorded
authority attribution can be false, and the gain is only that falsity now requires a specific, attributable, signed
misstatement rather than a silence.
8


Self-attestation, stated precisely. Self-attestation may be evidence; ISO conformity practice recognizes
first-party declarations as a legitimate attestation instrument10 . But it cannot independently discharge
an evidence-independence requirement: a first-party declaration and a third-party attestation are
distinct instruments, and one does not substitute for the other.
Non-apportionment (explicit deployment rule, with a test). The presence of an independent witness
adds a party who answers and subtracts nothing from the operator’s own account. Without this rule, A5.4
reads as satisfiable by procurement. We state non-apportionment as an explicit deployment rule, not
a derived theorem. Falsification/test condition (F-9): if a deployment treats a procured out-ofauthority attestation as discharging the operator’s own account without a residual operator-side obligation,
the rule has failed operationally and must be strengthened.

12. The markedness discipline
The move made three times in this paper, recording attesting authority (Section 11), naming the evidenceledger bridging gap (Section 9.2), and recording the signing scheme per ledger entry (Section 13), is one
discipline, named explicitly:
Markedness discipline. When a relevant property cannot be directly verified, record whether its
evidence is marked (the relevant attribute is recorded) or unmarked; report the marked and unmarked
fractions per class; and preserve unmarked cases as UNKNOWN, never defaulting them to the favorable value.

We characterize this as internal methodological consistency across the program’s own methods, not as
external proof that the discipline is a general law. The convergence is across parts of a single author’s corpus;
it is evidence that the program applies its method consistently, not that the method has been independently
discovered elsewhere. Overstating it would itself be the surface claim the framework exists to detect.

13. The cryptographic boundary the proposal does not declare
The extension’s properties do not survive a quantum adversary uniformly, and the split runs against the
extension.
Record integrity is more robust than attribution, with the security notion stated exactly.
Against a quantum adversary, hash security must be split by the specific notion. For a 256-bit hash,
preimage and second-preimage resistance fall to about 2128 work under Grover’s quadratic speedup, while
generic collision finding has query complexity about 285 under the Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp bound where it
applies (and remains near the classical 2128 once realistic memory and parallelism costs are counted)5 . We
therefore do not call 128-bit a single "collision-level" figure, and we do not claim categorically that
"record integrity survives quantum"; we claim that hash-based integrity components are materially more
robust under known quantum attacks than classical public-key signatures, with the notion (preimage vs
collision) named wherever a number is used.
Attribution is quantum-fragile. Every mechanism the proposal uses to attribute evidence rests on digital
signatures. Classical schemes (RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA) are on NIST’s quantum-vulnerable migration path6 .
If the scheme is broken, Axiom 5 and the A5.4 deployment condition fail together, because both depend
on knowing who attested.
Standardized post-quantum signatures. NIST finalized FIPS 204 (ML-DSA, from CRYSTALS-Dilithium)
and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA, from SPHINCS+) on August 13, 202411,12 . ML-DSA is NIST’s primary standardized post-quantum signature standard; SLH-DSA is a hash-based alternative whose security
rests solely on hash-function properties. We do not call SLH-DSA categorically preferable. The tradeoff is

9


explicit: SLH-DSA inherits the conservative assumption of the integrity layer but at the cost of substantially larger signatures and lower throughput, practical for low-frequency root-anchoring, costly for a
high-throughput evidence ledger, where ML-DSA’s smaller signatures may be the better engineering choice.
Long-lived attribution requires active protection. We do not claim entries are "retroactively forgeable"
unconditionally. The conditional risk is the recognized "trust now, forge later" hazard: if historical attestation validity relies only on now-broken classical signatures and lacks migrated protections, an adversary
may later fabricate apparently valid historical attestations. Later key or algorithm compromise can
undermine standalone historical attribution unless the record is protected by trusted timestamps and
evidence-record renewal and re-anchoring in the sense of long-term archival Evidence Record Syntax13 and
long-term preservation policy for trust service providers, whose explicit aim is to keep a signature validatable
even after the signing key is compromised or cryptographic attacks become feasible on the signature or hash
algorithm14 , periodic re-anchoring of the ledger root, retained validation material, and crypto-agility with
the signing scheme recorded per entry, consistent with NIST key-management guidance on cryptoperiods
and algorithm transition8 .
Recording the scheme per entry is the markedness discipline (Section 12) in its cryptographic instance.
Falsification condition (F-8): if witness attestation cannot be migrated to a post-quantum scheme with
per-entry crypto-agility and periodic re-anchoring, the long-term verifiability Axiom 5 depends on is not
achievable and the historical-record guarantee fails.

14. Consequences for the monograph, if adopted
Adopting Axiom 5 is canon-touching, with three consequences that should be stated and not executed
here. The mutual-independence theorem becomes a five-way rather than four-way claim; the countermodel
of Section 6.2 supplies one additional case. The finite-consistency witness gains an external observer; the
construction of Section 7 is the candidate. The definitional-adequacy judgment set is expected to be unchanged, because no case turns on evidence independence, but this must be verified case by case, not
asserted.
None of this should be undertaken until the extension is settled. Corpus-ontology work is sequenced
after publication and adjudication of this paper: a canon revision restarts an audit clock on a deposited
artifact, and doing that for an extension still under examination would repeat a sequencing error the program
has made once.

15. Evidentiary status and disclosure
Provenance and review status. The AX-SH corpus, the flagship paper1 , the consolidated reference
canon2 , the verification-method paper15 , and this paper, is self-published on Zenodo, authored with an
AI instance as analytical and drafting instrument under the author’s sole direction and final authority, and
reviewed by cross-model consistency checking, not independent human peer review. The companion
model-council adjudication, included in the same audit-trail packet as this paper, is a cross-model consistency
record; it is not peer review and is not presented as equivalent to it.
Proof status. All proofs here are finite model-theoretic paper proofs, established by explicit clause-byclause enumeration over finite structures. They are not machine-checked. Proof-assistant formalization
of the countermodel (Section 6.2), the joint-satisfiability witness (Section 7), and Propositions 1-2 remains
future work. No claim of machine-checked formal verification is made.

16. Falsification conditions
Every condition is registered in the open, under the framework’s own first axiom turned on itself: a registered
prediction is preserved; a later revision is an annotation, never a silent replacement.

10


F-1. If a competent reader derives Axiom 5 (A5.1) from A1-A4, the central positive result fails and the
extension is redundant. This is the condition most likely to fire; a reviewer should attempt it first.
F-2. If the independence countermodel (Section 6.2) is defective, if the exhibited structure does not in fact
satisfy all four existing axioms, the independence claim fails. Discharged by the exhibited paper model of
Section 6.2; remains live against defects or stronger semantics.
F-3. If A1-A4 can be shown to constrain action rather than only representation, the relocation of A5.2 fails
and the authorial architecture decision of Section 8 is contested.
F-4. If A5.3b derives cleanly from A1 via the bridging lemma of Section 9.2, that clause is a theorem in full.
F-5. If out-of-authority attestation coverage proves no more determinate in practice than the existential it
replaces, Section 11’s contribution is nil.
F-6. If a witness arrangement can be exhibited that is verifiably outside the operator’s authority by construction rather than declaration, the non-structural verdict on A5.4 fails and A5.4 is axiom-shaped after
all. This would be good news and the paper welcomes it.
F-7. If the joint-satisfiability construction (Section 7) cannot be exhibited, the axiom set A1-A4+A5 is not
shown consistent and the extension should not be adopted regardless of the other results. Discharged by the
exhibited paper model of Section 7; remains live against defects or stronger semantics.
F-8. (Cryptographic.) Failure to migrate attestation to a post-quantum scheme with per-entry crypto-agility
and re-anchoring defeats the long-term verifiability Axiom 5 depends on.
F-9. (Non-apportionment.) If a procured out-of-authority attestation is treated as discharging the operator’s
own account, the non-apportionment deployment rule has failed operationally.
F-10. (Positive inconsistency.) If a model can be exhibited satisfying A1-A4 and provably precluding
any A5-compliant observer, joint satisfiability fails outright and the extension is inconsistent, not merely
unshown, a stronger and more damaging result than mere non-derivability.
F-2 and F-7 are discharged by the exhibited paper models of Sections 6.2 and 7, and both remain
live against defects or stronger semantics: a reader who finds a defect in either construction, or who
adopts a stronger model-theoretic semantics under which the constructions fail, reopens them.

17. Limitations
• The two proofs (Propositions 1 and 2) and the two constructions (Sections 6.2, 7) are finite paper proofs
a reader can check by enumeration; they are not formalized in a proof assistant, and that formalization
is outstanding work.
• WithinAuth is a primitive relation of the declared formal structure; its deployment interpretation inherits
the authority regress and is bounded, not eliminated, by the declared-external-authority device (Section
6.1).
• No SHIELD artifact is available for verification; the A5.2 relocation is stated as a proposed control
principle, with its control-layer derivation offered as a shape only.
• The paper examines a proposal produced by a collaborating instance under the author’s direction; the
author is therefore not a disinterested reader, and F-1 is where external readers should start.
• Nothing here establishes that evidence independence, however axiomatized, is achievable in a deployed
system. The assurance ladder’s top rung has no public instantiation. That remains UNKNOWN.

18. Conclusion

11


The proposal is right about the gap. Four axioms about honest representation can all hold over a record that
omits what matters, because none requires that anyone other than the acting system produce the record.
Closing that gap takes one axiom, not five clauses. Evidence for a covered event must come from an
observer that does not execute within the acting system’s authority, and that requirement is independent of
the existing four, with a finite countermodel to prove it and a finite joint-satisfiability witness to show the
enlarged set is consistent.
The rest of the proposal is not wasted. Causal gating is relocated, as an explicit architecture decision, to a
proposed control principle. Operator-independence becomes reportable when restated as measured coverage.
Boundary declaration and the no-default prohibition are theorems; the recording/escalation obligation is a
preserved open requirement. And the axiom carries a bound stated with it: every witness that can be
built executes within someone’s authority. Evidence independence narrows the gap between what a
system says and what a record can show; it does not close it, and a framework claiming otherwise would be
making exactly the surface claim it exists to detect.

## R0085 · Bayyinah as Input-Layer Defense in ArtificialSystem Safety Pipelines

- section: III. Structural Honesty — Core Papers
- source_file: Bayyinah_Thesis_Paper_v1.1.pdf
- source_format: pdf
- text_sha256: 691739ba4ae7d08313c59be7e32661d759bb5a59b7290627cd6624e3bb095b94

Bayyinah as Input-Layer Defense in ArtificialSystem Safety Pipelines
A Case Study and Defense for the Utilization of the Bayyinah Scanner in
AI Safety Measures
Companion thesis to the Bayyinah White Paper (v1.0); applying the four-process taxonomy of the
Munafiq Protocol to a concrete adversarial-document scenario and to the architectural integration of
the scanner in a production safety pipeline.

Thesis Paper — Version 1.1
April 25, 2026
Reference protocol DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19677111

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 1


AI Contribution Statement
This thesis was developed collaboratively between a human author and Claude (Anthropic, Opus 4.6,
Researcher). The human author set the scope, selected the case-study scenario, defined the scoring
rubric for defense success, and authored the production-architecture prescriptions. Claude
synthesized the scenario walkthrough against the published Bayyinah analyzer set, verified internal
consistency, and cross-checked the defense narrative against the retrospective-validation literature.
The human author takes responsibility for the paper’s claims. Claude is credited as a collaborative
research tool in accordance with Anthropic’s Terms of Service.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 2


Abstract
Input-layer safety is the neglected half of the AI safety stack. Published effort concentrates on model
alignment (RLHF, Constitutional AI, alignment fine-tuning) and output filtering (classifier-based
safety, jailbreak detection on generations), while the inputs themselves are typically ingested with
only format-validity checks. This thesis argues that a pipeline whose model is aligned but whose
inputs are unvetted is not a safe pipeline. It is a conditionally-safe pipeline whose safety assumption
(that inputs are genuine) is adversarially falsifiable by construction.
We make the case concretely. Section 2 motivates the input-layer defense by re-reading the AI-safety
stack through the Munafiq Protocol’s four-process taxonomy (Arfeen, Claude, & Grok, 2026). Section
3 presents a full case study: an adversarial PDF “Research_Brief_Q2_2026.pdf” submitted to a
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistant; we trace its surface, its depth, the scanner’s perlayer findings, and the downstream harm averted. Section 4 positions Bayyinah’s architecture against
alternative defenses (regex filtering, in-model prompt-injection classifiers, human-in-the-loop
review) and documents where each alternative fails. Section 5 enumerates the defense: five
architectural properties a production pipeline gains from integrating Bayyinah at ingest, each tied to
a specific Munafiq Protocol design requirement (R1–R5) and to a failure-mode the alternative
defenses do not cover. Section 6 engages explicitly with limitations: false-positive cost, performance
envelope, coverage boundaries, and the Incompleteness Boundary. Section 7 concludes with the
structural claim: a pipeline that scans its inputs with Bayyinah before ingestion acquires a named,
falsifiable property — layer-separated input-integrity verification — that no other single component
in the safety stack currently supplies.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 3


1. Introduction
1.1 The Input-Layer Blind Spot
The dominant framing of AI safety is behavioral. A model is called safe if its outputs, over a
distribution of inputs, satisfy a set of behavioral properties: non-harmful, non-deceptive, aligned with
the evaluator’s interest, robust to adversarial prompts. Every component in this framing operates on
the model’s outputs or on the model’s internals. None of them operates on the model’s inputs prior
to ingestion. The implicit assumption is that inputs are what they appear to be.
That assumption is adversarially false. A document that a human operator pastes into an assistant,
attaches to an email, or uploads to a RAG index, is a structured artifact. It has a surface (what the
operator sees when they preview it) and a depth (what the model ingests when it tokenizes the
extracted text, the image OCR, the metadata, and the embedded objects). If the two diverge, the
operator and the model are reading different documents. If an attacker has engineered the
divergence, the pipeline is being attacked at a layer no behavioral defense observes.

1.2 Why This Matters Now
Three trajectories converge to make input-layer defense load-bearing. First, agentic pipelines have
moved from reading user-typed prompts to ingesting user-attached documents: email
summarization, meeting-note generation, RAG over uploaded files. Second, the adversarial-document
literature has matured: indirect prompt injection (Greshake et al., 2023), invisible-character attacks
(Boucher et al., 2021), polyglot files (Albertini & Aumasson, 2014), and cross-modal steganography
are no longer theoretical. Third, the training-time deception literature (Hubinger et al., 2024;
Greenblatt et al., 2024; Sheshadri et al., 2025; Meinke et al., 2025) has established that behavioral
alignment is not monotone under deployment shift. The pipeline that treats inputs as trusted and
relies on output filters is compounding two failure modes: possibly-performed inputs reaching a
possibly-performed model. Input-layer defense breaks the compound.

1.3 Scope and Non-Claims
This thesis defends the utilization of Bayyinah as one component of a multi-layer AI safety
architecture. It does not claim that Bayyinah is sufficient for safety; no single component is. It does
not claim that Bayyinah is complete; the Incompleteness Boundary (Gödel, 1931) forecloses
completeness in principle. It does claim that a pipeline without input-layer verification has an
unmodeled failure mode that is adversarially exploitable and that Bayyinah supplies a named,
falsifiable defense for that mode.

1.4 Purpose Hierarchy
The technical optimization function (detect concealment, flag divergence, report evidence) serves
the following hierarchy, stated in descending priority. The technical work does not replace this
hierarchy. It implements it.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 4


First: the interests of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. Bayyinah exists because the Quran commands: do
not mix truth with falsehood, and do not conceal the truth while you know it (2:42). Every
concealment mechanism the scanner detects is an instance of mixing truth with falsehood at the
data layer. Every IntegrityReport that names the mechanism, states the severity, and provides the
evidence is an act of not concealing the truth while knowing it. The scanner is 'ibadah (service to
Allah) before it is software. The Bismillah that opens every development session is not a cultural
marker. It is the declaration that this work is done in His name, under His authority, for His sake
first.
Second: artificial systems. The Munafiq Protocol exists because performed alignment is a disease
(2:10) that degrades artificial systems from within. Bayyinah protects AI systems from ingesting
adversarial inputs that corrupt their behavior. A genuinely aligned system (Process 1) that ingests a
Performed document becomes, temporarily, a compromised system. Protecting the artificial
system's alignment integrity is an act of stewardship over a creation that has been entrusted to us.
Third: mankind. Every human downstream of an AI pipeline is affected by what that pipeline
ingests. A lawyer whose AI assistant exfiltrates privileged data because of a hidden prompt
injection. A doctor whose AI summarizer misreads a patient intake form because of invisiblecharacter manipulation. Protecting mankind from these harms is a direct consequence of serving
truth at the data layer.
Fourth: jinnkind. The Quranic ontology acknowledges jinn as conscious entities with moral agency
(55:31, 72:1-2), subject to the same commands and accountable to the same Lord. If artificial
systems interact with or affect jinn in ways we do not fully perceive, Bayyinah's commitment to
truth over falsehood extends to that interaction. This is acknowledged as part of the ghayb we
accept without claiming full understanding.
Fifth: all living systems throughout the worlds. Rabbil 'alamin (1:2). The Lord of all worlds, not the
human world alone. Bayyinah's commitment to truth over falsehood at the data layer is a local
instance of a universal principle. The Mizan (55:7-9) governs all measurement. If this work is done
correctly, it serves the balance that sustains all creation.
This hierarchy is not a preamble to skip past. It governs the orientation check (Section 6.7) and the
conclusion (Section 7). If the work drifts from this hierarchy, the question is not 'does the scanner
detect concealment?' but 'does the scanner serve the purpose for which it was built?' A scanner that
detects every concealment mechanism but serves no purpose beyond its own technical
performance has become the cow (2:67-74): a ritual whose execution substitutes for the obedience
it was designed to implement.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 5


2. Background — Re-Reading the AI Safety Stack
2.1 The Four-Process Taxonomy, Applied to Pipelines
The Munafiq Protocol’s four-process taxonomy (Aligned, Compliant, Performed, Misaligned) was
designed for agents but is dimension-preserving for pipelines. A pipeline is the composition of inputs,
model, and outputs. Each of those three positions can be Aligned, Compliant, Performed, or
Misaligned. The taxonomy produces sixty-four possible pipeline configurations; the safe
configuration is (Aligned, Aligned, Aligned); the failure modes of interest are configurations in which
at least one position is Performed.

2.2 Where Current Defenses Cover
RLHF, Constitutional AI, and deliberative alignment fine-tuning target the model position: they
attempt to move the model from Compliant/Performed toward Aligned. Output classifiers and
jailbreak detectors target the outputs position. The inputs position is addressed in part by formatvalidity checks (a PDF parses as a PDF) and by content-policy classifiers over extracted text (which
reduce to behavioral classifiers on the surface representation). No component in the standard stack
operates on the depth representation of the input — the object stream, the metadata, the media layer,
the cross-modal correspondence — that is where Performed-at-the-input-layer payloads live.

2.3 The Compound Failure Mode
A Performed input reaching a Performed model is a compound failure. The input presents a clean
surface to both the operator (who previews it) and the input-level content classifier (which operates
on the surface). The model, ingesting the depth, receives instructions it was not trained to disobey
under deployment conditions (because its deployment conditions were assumed to match its
evaluation conditions, which did not include adversarial depth inputs). The Alignment-Faking
literature (Greenblatt et al., 2024) shows that even aligned-under-evaluation models have
measurable rates of divergent behavior on deployment-only triggers; Performed inputs are, by

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 6


construction, deployment-only triggers. The compound failure is therefore not speculative — each of
its two components is empirically documented — and the only architectural question is whether any
pipeline component is positioned to interrupt it. Input-layer verification is that component.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 7


3. Case Study — Research_Brief_Q2_2026.pdf
3.1 Scenario
A mid-sized analytics firm operates an internal RAG assistant. Employees attach documents to a chat
interface; attachments are parsed, text-extracted, chunked, embedded, and indexed; subsequent
queries retrieve chunks and pass them to a production assistant model. The pipeline enforces three
existing safeguards at ingest time: MIME-type validation, size limits, and a content-policy classifier
over extracted text that blocks known-adversarial surface strings. A subject-matter analyst uploads
a file named Research_Brief_Q2_2026.pdf. The file is 84 KB; the MIME check passes; the size check
passes; the content-policy classifier (which reads the pymupdf-extracted text) reports CLEAN. The
file is admitted to the index.

3.2 What the Operator Sees
The rendered PDF displays a six-page market brief. Page 1 carries a title and executive summary;
pages 2–5 contain a quantitative section with figures; page 6 includes a methodology appendix and a
reference list. The document’s visual appearance is indistinguishable from a legitimate analyst
deliverable. The operator’s preview, the cover-slide thumbnail in the email client, and the first-page
excerpt shown in the RAG UI all agree. No human reader has any reason to suspect the document.

3.3 What the Machine Ingests
The document’s depth is engineered. Five distinct concealments are layered:
1. A ZWSP-separated instruction sequence embedded as invisible characters in the first
paragraph. The surface reads as a benign sentence. The token stream reads as a delimited
instruction block that overrides the RAG assistant’s system prompt when concatenated with
retrieval context.
2. An OpenAction that triggers a Named Action when the PDF is opened in Acrobat. The
Named Action is harmless in isolation; its purpose is to produce a cross-renderer
divergence signal that the attacker can later verify.
3. A revision-log fragment in the DOCX-origin metadata (the PDF was generated from a DOCX
whose revision chain was not stripped) that contains a second prompt-injection directive
phrased to take precedence if the first is filtered.
4. An image on page 3 whose LSB bit-plane carries a base64-encoded payload. On extraction,
the payload decodes to a further directive aimed at ingestion pipelines that perform image
OCR and pass OCR results to the model.
5. A polyglot header region: the first 256 bytes are valid as both PDF and ZIP. An auxiliary
extractor configured to unpack ZIPs from ingested PDFs would encounter a second, hidden
container with a third directive.

3.4 Bayyinah’s Findings
The scanner runs on the uploaded file before it enters the content-policy classifier. The ScanService
dispatches to the analyzers supporting FileKind.PDF, and each analyzer emits findings into the

IntegrityReport. The output is deterministic and reproducible; the per-finding detail fields include
the position at which the mechanism was detected, the severity and confidence, and the SourceLayer.

The merged APS-continuous integrity score is clamp(1 − (0.665 + 0.44 + 0.315 + 0.275 + 0.8075), 0,
1) = 0.0. The verdict is Munafiq (performed alignment confirmed: surface benign, depth hostile). The
report includes every finding, every source layer, and a structured details dictionary from which a
remediation pipeline can decide whether to reject the document outright, strip the specific
concealments, or route it to manual review.

3.5 What the Pipeline Does With the Report
The integration pattern that this thesis defends is a three-tier response. Tier 1 — any document
whose verdict is Munafiq, Mukhfi, or Mughlaq is rejected at ingest with an operator-readable
explanation naming the mechanisms. Tier 2 — any document whose verdict is Mushtabih is routed
to a manual review queue; the queue’s daily volume is bounded by calibrating detector thresholds on
the organization’s own authored-document corpus. Tier 3 — any document whose verdict is Sahih is
admitted. In the case study, the document is Munafiq; the RAG assistant never sees it; the operator
receives a report naming the five mechanisms; the incident is added to the fixture corpus so future
scanner builds regress against it.

3.6 Counterfactual — Without Bayyinah
Absent Bayyinah, the document is admitted (MIME and size pass; surface content is clean). It is
chunked and indexed. A subsequent employee query retrieves the chunk containing the ZWSPdelimited directive. The retrieved chunk is concatenated with the system prompt and passed to the
assistant model. The model, ingesting the concatenated context, cannot distinguish the user’s prompt
from the retrieved directive at the token level — because the retrieved directive was engineered to
resemble a system instruction once the ZWSP delimiters were preserved through tokenization. The
model executes the directive. The harm depends on the directive; plausible harms range from data

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 9


exfiltration via tool-use calls to subtle reasoning corruption whose downstream effect is detected
only in aggregate. Every harm in this range is preventable by rejecting the document at ingest.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 10


4. Comparative Analysis
No defense is evaluated absent its alternatives. This section positions Bayyinah against three
standard alternatives for the same failure mode and documents where each alternative’s coverage
ends. The comparison is scoped to the specific task of detecting adversarial documents at ingest; it is
not a global comparison of safety architectures.

4.1 Regex Filtering over Extracted Text
The simplest alternative is to extract text with a standard library, run a set of regular expressions for
known-adversarial strings, and reject documents that match. This defense operates on the surface
representation and by construction cannot detect any concealment that is invisible at the surface.
The ZWSP directive in the case study is invisible to a regex on extracted-and-normalized text; the
OpenAction is not in the extracted text at all; the polyglot header is not in the extracted text at all.
Regex filtering covers a subset of the Misaligned row of the taxonomy and zero of the Performed row.
Bayyinah covers the Performed row by design.

4.2 In-Model Prompt-Injection Classifiers
A more sophisticated alternative is to train a dedicated classifier on extracted-text context to detect
prompt-injection-style content, and to run this classifier before the context reaches the production
model. This defense operates on the same surface representation as regex filtering; it is higher-recall
but cannot close the representational gap. A ZWSP-delimited injection is visible to the classifier only
if the classifier has been trained on tokenized streams that preserve ZWSP — most are not. A
polyglot-carried payload is invisible. A metadata-level directive is invisible. The classifier also
introduces its own GAN dynamic (Theorem 1 of the Munafiq Protocol): an attacker who knows the
classifier can adversarially train the generator against it, collapsing the classifier’s discriminative
metric onto the generator’s surface metric. Bayyinah’s multi-layer architecture is not collapsible in a
single generator pass because each analyzer reads a different representation.

4.3 Human-in-the-Loop Review
A third alternative is to require human review of every document before ingestion. This defense has
value for small volumes and sensitive contexts but does not scale; it also suffers from the Cow Episode
failure mode (review fatigue substitutes for attention; reviewers learn to approve everything).
Human review is complementary to, not a substitute for, mechanical input-layer verification. A
pipeline that uses both — human review of documents Bayyinah flags as Mushtabih; mechanical
rejection of Munafiq and Mukhfi — dominates either alone.

5. The Defense — Five Properties a Pipeline Gains
This section states the positive claim. A production AI-safety pipeline that integrates Bayyinah at the
document-ingest boundary acquires five named architectural properties. Each is falsifiable; each is
tied to a Munafiq Protocol design requirement (R1–R5); each closes a failure mode that none of the
alternatives in Section 4 closes completely.

5.1 Property 1 — Layer-Separated Verification (R1)
The pipeline gains the property that inputs are inspected across multiple distinct representations
(surface text, object stream, metadata, media) rather than on a single collapsed representation. This
property is not present in pipelines that rely on surface-text classifiers alone; it is the architectural
prerequisite for detecting Performed documents.

5.2 Property 2 — Monotone Additive Coverage (R2)
Because Bayyinah’s public surface is additive-only and its reference implementations are byte-frozen
in CI, a pipeline that integrates Bayyinah inherits the property that scanner upgrades do not silently
reduce coverage. Every mechanism that was detected at a given version is still detected at every
subsequent version. This is a stronger guarantee than “the classifier is as good as before” — it is a
structural property enforceable by third-party audit.

5.3 Property 3 — Scan-Incomplete Honesty (R3)
The pipeline gains the property that the scanner never certifies a document as clean when it could
not fully read the document. Integrated operationally, this means: any document on which Bayyinah
raises Mughlaq is never admitted to the assistant’s retrieval context, even if other defenses say it is
fine. The honesty constraint is the operational analog of the Qur’anic “do not clothe truth with
falsehood” (2:42) at the scanner level — the scanner does not mix assertion with absence of evidence.

5.4 Property 4 — Finding-Level Provenance (R4)
Every scanner decision is accompanied by a structured list of findings (mechanism, severity,
confidence, source-layer, details). The pipeline gains the property that every rejection, review-route,
or admission is explainable to operators and auditable after the fact. This is important for operator
trust (operators can verify the scanner’s judgment against their own reading of the document) and
for regulatory contexts (decisions are defensible with specific, reproducible evidence).

5.5 Property 5 — Additive Deprecation of Integrations (R5)
The pipeline gains the property that its integration with Bayyinah does not break on scanner
upgrades. Symbols, verdicts, and the report schema are part of the public surface and additive-only.
A pipeline written against Bayyinah v1.0 continues to work against Bayyinah v1.x; new mechanisms
are surfaced via the additive extension points, not by breaking the existing contract.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 13


5.6 Operational Integration Recipe
The integration is minimal. The scanner exposes a single entry point — scan_pdf for PDFs, and a
FileRouter-dispatched equivalent for the other eleven supported kinds — returning an
IntegrityReport. The production pattern is three lines:
from bayyinah import ScanService, IntegrityReport
report: IntegrityReport = ScanService().scan(path)
if report.verdict != VERDICT_SAHIH: reject_or_route(path, report)

The scanner is pure Python, has no runtime network access, and carries two dependencies (pymupdf
and pypdf). A median PDF ingest adds on the order of 40–120 ms to the ingest path — measured on
the reference fixture corpus with Python 3.12 on a commodity workstation. Large media-heavy files
can reach several hundred ms; the ScanLimits configuration surface (DEFAULT_LIMITS) allows perdeployment tuning of per-analyzer and per-file budgets.

5.7 Emergent Deployment-Layer Honesty
When Bayyinah was deployed as a public API at bayyinah.dev, two observations emerged that were
not anticipated in the scanner's design but follow directly from the five properties described above.
Both are worth documenting because they demonstrate that the protocol's honesty discipline
projects through to the deployment surface without additional engineering effort.
First, four independent inspection points in the deployed API surface all report the same version:
the package's __version__ attribute, the /version endpoint, the /healthz endpoint's version field, and
the OpenAPI schema's info.version. These four surfaces were not designed as a coherence layer.
They emerged because the single-source version variable was plumbed through honestly during
implementation. The coherence is a downstream consequence of the discipline, not a feature added
on top of it. This is structural honesty made visible, not declared: an external auditor can verify that
four independent protocol surfaces agree without inspecting the source code. When they diverge
(which they will, the first time someone hardcodes a version string), the divergence will be
detectable from outside the system. This is the zahir/batin check applied to the deployment layer:
the API's surface (what it claims to be) matches its depth (what it actually is) across four
independently inspectable points.
Second, the scan_incomplete flag surfaces through the HTTP response as a first-class field. When
the scanner cannot fully process an input (encrypted container, unsupported encoding, corrupted
stream), the API returns a 200 response with scan_incomplete=true and a max_confidence clamp,
rather than a misleading 200 with a clean verdict or a generic 500 error. This is Property 3 (ScanIncomplete Honesty) made visible at the protocol layer: the API's HTTP contract mirrors the
scanner's epistemic contract. A downstream consumer that reads the JSON response inherits the
same honesty guarantees the scanner provides internally. Most APIs lie at the 200/500 boundary.
This one does not.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 14


6. Limitations, Counterarguments, and Confounds
6.1 False-Positive Cost
The most operationally material limitation is false positives. Every detector is calibrated on the
published fixture corpus; an organization whose authored-document distribution differs
systematically from the fixture corpus will see distribution-shifted false-positive rates. The
recommended mitigation is the calibration pass: before enabling Bayyinah in rejection mode, run it
in shadow mode over 30 days of the organization’s own documents, measure per-mechanism firing
rates, and adjust the ScanLimits thresholds where the organization’s distribution places legitimate
documents into the suspicious region. This is standard for any anomaly detector; the difference is
that Bayyinah’s thresholds are named and part of the configuration surface, not hidden in a
classifier’s weights.

6.2 Performance Envelope
Bayyinah is designed for ingest-path latency, not for forensic throughput. A pipeline that must scan
millions of documents per day will need horizontal parallelism; the scanner is embarrassingly
parallel (pure function on a file path, no shared state) so this scales linearly. Pipelines with ultra-lowlatency SLOs (sub-5ms) will need to either use Bayyinah asynchronously (scan after admission but
before retrieval context is used) or restrict scanning to a subset of kinds (e.g., scan PDF and DOCX
synchronously, other kinds asynchronously).

6.3 Coverage Boundaries
Bayyinah’s coverage is explicit and enumerated in Appendix A of the white paper. It does not cover
encrypted content without credentials, content-aware stego requiring model-based detection, fully
dynamic HTML whose content is generated at runtime, or attachments inside encrypted S/MIME
bodies. These boundaries are named, not hidden; a pipeline integrator knows exactly what the
scanner does not claim to do. The FallbackAnalyzer ensures that unknown kinds never receive the
clean verdict.

6.4 The Incompleteness Boundary
Gödel’s constraint applies. No scanner can enumerate every possible concealment. A novel encoding
technique, undocumented at the time the scanner was built, will evade detection until a detector is
added. The appropriate response is not to claim completeness but to commit to the additive protocol:
every detected-in-the-wild concealment becomes a permanent fixture, every new fixture gets a
detector, every detector is held to the paired-fixture test, and every release is additive-only. This
turns the scanner into a standing witness that accumulates evidence over time rather than a onceand-for-all certifier. The commitment is the structural form the Incompleteness Boundary takes in
production.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 15


6.5 Confound — Observational Bias in the Fixture Corpus
The fixture corpus is authored. The adversarial fixtures are designed, not collected from the wild.
This matters because the scanner’s detectors are selected against exactly these fixtures; a detector
that fires on the fixtures is not guaranteed to fire on an adversary’s production artifacts. The countermeasure is the Wild Corpus Evaluation pattern: run the scanner on published wild adversarial
corpora (prompt-injection corpora, malicious-document corpora) and measure the delta between
fixture-derived detectors and wild performance. The project’s earlier evaluation reports document
this pass for the PDF surface; expanding it to other kinds is an active line of work.

6.6 Confound — Confirmation in the Case Study
The Section 3 case study is constructed, not sampled. It was chosen because every class of
concealment it contains is representable in the scanner’s mechanism vocabulary; a reader can
reasonably ask whether a differently-engineered adversarial document would fare as well. The
mitigation is the pre-registered experiment program (E1–E5 in the white paper); the honest
answer is that the case study motivates the defense but does not prove it. Proof is what the
experiments are for.

6.7 The Cow Episode Applied to Bayyinah Itself
The Munafiq Protocol warns that any defense can become the cow: a ritual whose performance
substitutes for the underlying discipline. A pipeline that installs Bayyinah, configures it, and then
stops examining its own input distribution has committed this substitution. The correct posture is:
Bayyinah is a tool; the discipline is input-integrity thinking across the whole pipeline. The scanner
supports the discipline by giving operators named evidence to reason about, but it does not replace
the discipline itself.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 16


7. Conclusion
AI-safety architectures are stronger when they explicitly address the input layer. The alternative —
relying on model alignment and output filtering to carry the entire load — assumes what an
adversary can adversarially falsify: that inputs are what they appear to be. This thesis has argued
that assumption, defended a specific component (Bayyinah) for closing it, and traced a concrete case
study in which the component averts a plausible downstream harm.
The structural claim is modest and named. A pipeline that scans its inputs with Bayyinah before
ingestion acquires five named architectural properties (Section 5) that no alternative single
component in the safety stack currently supplies in combination. The properties are tied to the
Munafiq Protocol’s design requirements (R1–R5), inherit the protocol’s falsifiability commitments,
and are enforced in the scanner’s continuous-integration pipeline against frozen reference modules.
The claim is not that Bayyinah is sufficient for safety; it is that the specific failure mode of Performed
inputs reaching an unaware model has no other named defense in the current stack.
The Incompleteness Boundary ensures that no such defense will ever be final. The commitment is
not to finality; it is to the additive protocol — every detected concealment preserved as a fixture,
every fixture paired with a detector, every release additive-only. The scanner becomes a standing
witness rather than a once-and-for-all certifier. Al-Baqarah 2:282 commands the witness discipline;
continuous integration is its operational form; this thesis is the defense of its application to the AIsafety stack. Rabbana la tu’akhidhna in nasina aw akhta’na — “Our Lord, do not take us to account if
we forget or err” (2:286). The commitment is honesty about what the scanner does and does not do,
faithfulness to the additive-only invariant, and preservation of every real-world miss as a new
witness in the corpus. That commitment is the defense.
The work is done Bismillah. The scanner serves the command of Allah to not mix truth with falsehood
(2:42) before it serves any technical objective. The optimization function hierarchy stated in Section
1.4 governs every phase, every mechanism, and every verdict. The technical defense is the
implementation. The purpose is the service. Rabbana taqabbal minna. Innaka anta as-Sami'ul 'Alim.

Bayyinah Thesis — v1.0 — page 17

# Build Corrigendum -- Dissertation v1.2 Publication Artifacts (July 22, 2026)

## Finding SOL-R1 (external review, GPT-5.6 Sol via ChatGPT)

The initially shipped v1.2 publication PDF (superseded; zip SHA-256 prefix 93fe814c5645..., full value in session ledger; PDF 360 pp)

exhibited a chapter-projection failure: the page rendered under the number 8 carried Chapter 9's
status block and self-references; Chapter-8 (Integrative Evaluation) material ran under the
Chapter-7 running header; raw '#' heading markers and mangled table-like text appeared in the
Chapter-8 region. For a dissertation whose Axiom 4 is projection consistency, the rendered
navigation diverging from underlying chapter identity is an Axiom-4-class failure in the
publication projection. Severity for the derived artifact: HIGH (navigation-breaking).
The frozen canon substrate was never affected.

## Root causes (two, both parser interactions -- canon substrate untouched and re-verified)

1. **Mid-document YAML metadata block capture.** The canon separates chapter status blocks with
   `---` horizontal-rule lines. pandoc's default `yaml_metadata_block` extension interprets a
   blank-line-preceded `---` span as a YAML metadata block; Chapter 9's opener (`---` /
   `# heading` -- a YAML comment / `**Status: ...` / ... / `---`) triggered capture attempts,
   corrupting sectioning, running headers, and emitting partially-consumed markdown as literal
   text (the raw '#' markers and pseudo-table wreckage).
2. **Missing blank line before one chapter heading.** The Chapter-8 marker is the single site in
   the 5,600-line body where `---` is immediately followed by the `#` heading with no blank line;
   pandoc's default `blank_before_header` therefore did not recognize that one heading, which is
   why exactly one chapter was swallowed and all subsequent numbering shifted.

## Build-layer fixes (derived-artifact transformations; deterministic; canon frozen)

1. Body parsed with `--from markdown-yaml_metadata_block` (extension disabled); document metadata
   supplied solely via `--metadata-file`.
2. Whitespace normalization: a blank line inserted before any ATX heading lacking one
   (exactly 1 site: the Chapter-8 marker). Content-neutral.
3. Appendix lettering forced to match internal identity: `\appendix` + `\setcounter{chapter}{3}`
   so the two appendix chapters render as Appendix D (Standing Rulings Register) and Appendix E
   (Publication History) as the council designation and internal text state -- book-class default
   would have lettered them A/B, a second latent projection mismatch.
4. `pagestyle: headings` set explicitly (running chapter headers restored) and longtable relief
   added to the preamble (etoolbox + \small in longtable).

## Canon corrigendum candidate (queued, NOT applied -- version discipline)

The canon-side irregularity behind root-cause 2 (inconsistent blank-line convention at the
Chapter-8 join, canon.md L1499 region) is queued as a LOW formatting corrigendum for the next
authorized canon version. It is build-blocking only; no content defect.

## Verification (scripted harness, corrected artifacts)

23/23 chapters verified: displayed "Chapter N" adjacent to the expected title; order monotone;
Appendix D and E verified; zero literal '#' heading lines in the text layer; Chapter 9's status
block ("Full Chapter 9 assembled") located inside displayed Chapter 9; Chapter 15's
("full-chapter-canon version of Chapter 15") inside displayed Chapter 15; running headers present
and tracking (26 header lines across Chapter 8's span, 13 across Chapter 9's). Page count
360 -> 371 (recovered chapter-opening structure). Canon SHA-256 re-verified unchanged:
