| **R6-C** | COMMITTED | REALIZED | run-log total | Section 0.1 A-3.7, realized missing-receipt count |

**Frozen universe-binding rule.** The submitted denominator must **equal** the committed universe cardinality, or carry an explicit **reconciliation** that names every excluded item with a positive count and a non-empty reason summing to the shortfall. A reconciled shortfall is scored over the **full committed universe** with the excluded items counted as **non-passing**, per the Section 7.3 rule that an absent or unverifiable item is counted against the architecture and never as clean; a reconciliation can therefore only lower a share, never inflate one. A denominator ABOVE the committed universe is REJECTED: the universe cannot be enlarged after commitment. A favorable subset with no reconciliation is REJECTED. The committed cardinality is obtained from the TRUSTED channel only: from the frozen manifest for a FIXED universe, and from an authenticated commitment (Section 8.1b) for a SEALED or REALIZED universe. It is never read from the raw-evidence record, and the frozen minimum evidence count of Section 8.2 still applies as a floor.

### 8.1b Frozen universe-commitment channels (three independent trust roots in v0.8)

Carrying finding **F-P6-1 (HIGH, BLOCKING)** established that v0.6 closed the FIXED-denominator subset attack but authenticated every SEALED and REALIZED universe only by a caller-supplied cardinality and a non-empty seal or run-log string. The party selecting the evidence could therefore declare a favorable subset to BE the whole sealed or realized universe, attach any string as its hash, and obtain SUPPORTED-DESCRIPTIVE; the shipped v0.6 test helper defaulted the cardinality to the submitted denominator and fabricated the hash, so its regressions assumed the property under test. Carrying finding F-P6-1 is accepted in full. The remedy is a **trust-boundary correction**, not a stronger hash check: the claimant may provide evidence, but may not define the authoritative universe against which that evidence is scored.

**Two channels, frozen.** Evaluation takes two inputs with different trust. **Channel B** is the untrusted raw-evidence record: integer counts, the manifest and universe binding, and, for a SEALED or REALIZED component, a `commitment_id` that only REFERENCES a commitment. A raw record that carries any `sealed_universe_n`, `sealed_universe_hash`, `realized_total`, `run_log_hash`, `final_chain_hash` or `signature` field is REJECTED. **Channel A** is the authoritative universe-commitment bundle, supplied to the evaluator by the OPERATOR, never by the evidence submitter, and authenticated against the committing-authority public key frozen in the scope manifest.

**Frozen authority.** The real sealed and realized cardinalities do not exist at contract-freeze time, so the manifest freezes the AUTHORITY, not the value: three Ed25519 public keys (a commitment authority, an independent pre-commitment anchor, and a run logger), the protocol version, and the domain-separation tags are folded into `MANIFEST_SHA256`. The commitments themselves are produced at seal or run-close time, before outcome inspection, and signed by the authorities' private keys, whose public halves are frozen here and whose private halves are NEVER included in any dispatched or deposited packet. The keys frozen in this deposit-ready preregistration instrument are REFERENCE keys: they are sufficient to fix and prove the gate's logic, which the two carrying families executed and verified, and they bind no live universe because no corpus, pilot, or session exists yet. When the validation program actually executes (Phase A onward), the operator installs the production authority keys held by the real custodians; installing them changes `MANIFEST_SHA256` and is itself a versioned, freshly-carried step at that time. Depositing the reference-key instrument exposes nothing: the private halves were never shipped, and there is no live universe to attack.

**Three frozen trust roots, no runtime override (closes F-P7-1).** The manifest freezes THREE independent Ed25519 public keys: a commitment authority, an independent pre-commitment anchor authority, and a run logger. All three are folded into `MANIFEST_SHA256`. The evaluator, `route_claims`, exposes NO key parameter: a caller cannot substitute a trust root, and every signature is checked against the fixed manifest keys. The private halves are held by three separate authorities and never ship.

**Frozen SEALED commitment, independently anchored (closes F-P7-1; producer divergence 1).** For each SEALED component the commitment authority signs, before results, a commitment fixing the signed `commitment_id`, component, universe id, protocol version, manifest digest, exact `sealed_universe_n`, canonical `sealed_universe_inventory_hash`, authority, sequence and timestamp. Because a single authority signing a value is not by itself proof that the value was fixed before results, the sealed commitment is additionally bound by an INDEPENDENT anchor: the pre-commitment anchor authority signs the digest of the sealed commitment at a time no earlier than the commitment. The evaluator obtains the sealed cardinality only when BOTH the commitment-authority signature and the independent anchor signature verify and bind the same component, universe and manifest. A lone or compromised commitment authority therefore cannot self-declare a favorable sealed subset. Equality of the evidence denominator to the authenticated cardinality (or a valid reconciliation) is decisive; a well-formed or non-empty hash is never sufficient. (The producer notes this symmetric anchoring as a divergence from the GPT draft, which anchored REALIZED universes but authenticated SEALED universes with the commitment authority alone.)

**Frozen REALIZED commitment, four authenticated layers (closes F-P7-2).** A realized count is not knowable before the run, so it is committed in four layers, each independently checked. (1) A **pre-run commitment**, signed by the commitment authority before the run, fixes the run identifier, the event schema digest, the inclusion-rule digest, the deterministic genesis hash, the frozen logger public key, and the manifest; the evaluator recomputes the genesis from those fields, so it cannot be reused across runs. (2) An **independent anchor**, signed by the pre-commitment anchor authority over the pre-run commitment digest at a time no earlier than the commitment, proves the run was fixed before outcomes; a post-hoc pre-run commitment cannot be validly anchored without the independent authority. (3) Every qualifying event is an **individually signed append record** from the frozen run logger, hash-chained from the genesis, binding the pre-run digest, a contiguous sequence, and the previous chain hash, so reordering, duplication, truncation, insertion or post-signing modification breaks the chain or an event signature. (4) A **close receipt**, signed by the commitment authority and bound to the pre-run digest, fixes the realized total, first and last sequence, and final chain hash. The evaluator derives the realized total from the verified append history, not from the caller's summary. A favorable list assembled after outcomes cannot be authenticated, because it lacks a validly anchored pre-run commitment and per-event logger signatures.

**Signed, resolved commitment identifier (closes F-P7-3).** Every signed object carries a unique `commitment_id` inside its signed payload. Channel A is indexed by that identifier; the raw Channel-B record carries only the `commitment_id` reference, and the evaluator resolves the bundle by exact match. An unknown, cross-component, cross-kind, or mismatched identifier is rejected before any share is computed.

**Frozen canonicalization.** All signed content and the append chain use one serialization: UTF-8, Unicode NFC, sorted object keys, no insignificant whitespace, no floating-point values, and a domain-separation prefix, with the component, universe id, protocol version and manifest digest inside the hashed content, so a digest valid for one artifact type or protocol version cannot be reused in another.

**Frozen scope-status rule.** A COMMITTED component whose record is absent makes its route **INCOMPLETE**, never OUT OF SCOPE: an unfavorable committed component cannot be silenced by omission. The single validly predeclared exclusion is **R3**, whose ConflictLedger instrumentation is UNKNOWN in this frozen document (Section 0.1 item 2); if no R3-A record is supplied, route R3 is OUT OF SCOPE, and if an R3-A record IS supplied, R3 is evaluated as a committed route. No other component may reach OUT OF SCOPE.

**Fail-closed behaviour, frozen.** A missing mandatory field, an unexpected extra field, a non-integer or negative count, a numerator above its denominator, a violation count above its denominator, a missing or wrong manifest digest or universe identifier, a denominator that neither equals its committed universe nor carries a valid reconciliation, or a denominator above its committed universe (Section 8.1a) is **REJECTED**: the evaluator raises and returns nothing, so an invalid record cannot become a report. A denominator of zero, or below the frozen minimum evidence count, is **NOT EVALUABLE** and supports nothing. A zero-tolerance violation count above zero **FAILS the route** regardless of any share. There is no path by which a component supports anything unless its own mandatory raw evidence, on its own, satisfies every one of these conditions.

### 8.3 Frozen evidence admission (replaces the withdrawn v0.4 binding)

v0.4 claimed that component evidence was bound into a single fail-closed function. The round 4 seat defeated that claim three ways, each executed rather than argued: it asserted `hard_gate_violated=False` for R2-B while supplying 0 of 100 passing raw items and received support, because raw counts were optional and their threshold was never enforced; it constructed a derived outcome object directly, because the module's provenance token was importable; and it used `dataclasses.replace` to preserve a genuine below-minimum object's token while replacing its evaluability and p-value. Carrying finding F-P4-1 is accepted in full.

The remedy is not a better token. **Provenance by token is abandoned as a mechanism, because a token in an importable module is not a secret and a frozen dataclass is not immutable against `replace`.** The frozen admission rule is:

| Element | Frozen specification |
|---|---|
| Sole admissible input | A mapping from component key to a **raw-evidence record**: integer counts, the manifest and universe binding of Section 8.1a, and, for a SEALED or REALIZED component, a `commitment_id` referencing an authenticated Section 8.1b commitment. Any cardinality, seal hash, run-log hash, realized total or signature in a raw record is REJECTED (Channel A only, finding F-P6-1). The authoritative commitment bundle and run logs are the OPERATOR's separate trusted inputs |
| Inadmissible input | Any derived, pre-evaluated, mutated or replaced object; any object produced by `dataclasses.replace`; any record carrying a gate verdict, an evaluability flag, a p-value, a share, or a token. Supplying one is REJECTED, and no label is returned for any route |
| Who computes the gate | `evaluate_gate` in `shvvp_v0_8_route_gates.py`, from the raw counts, every time. `route_claims` calls it itself and never accepts its output from a caller |
| Recomputation | Total. Every share, every threshold comparison, every evaluability decision and every hard-gate state is recomputed inside the normative evaluator on every call |
| Caller authority | None. There is no `gate_pass`, `hard_gate_violated`, `evaluable`, `p` or token parameter anywhere in the public interface |
| Consequence of forgery attempts | Irrelevant by construction. Forging a report cannot change a label, because reports are not read back in |

`test_shvvp_v0_8_rules.py` executes the earlier attacks plus the round 7 F-P7 battery (caller trust-root substitution, post-outcome realized construction, missing or attacker-signed independent anchors on both the sealed and realized paths, truncated, reordered or modified append histories, and unresolved commitment identifiers), each rejected, verifying against the three frozen trust roots via shipped pre-signed vectors rather than any runtime key override.

### 8.4 Frozen route claim rule and closed label list

**Frozen route claim labels. These six are exhaustive and closed. The strongest attainable label is SUPPORTED-DESCRIPTIVE.**

| Route claim label | Condition |
|---|---|
| OUT OF SCOPE | Every component of the route is a validly predeclared exclusion whose instrumentation was not built. The only such component is R3-A (Section 0.1 item 2); a committed component's absence is INCOMPLETE, not OUT OF SCOPE |
| INCOMPLETE | A committed component's raw-evidence record is absent. A committed component cannot be converted to OUT OF SCOPE by omission (finding F-P5-1) |
| FAILED | Any component of the route records a zero-tolerance violation |
| NOT EVALUABLE | No violation, but a component's evidence count is zero or below its frozen minimum |
| NOT SUPPORTED | All components evaluable and free of violations, but a component's descriptive threshold is not met |
| SUPPORTED-DESCRIPTIVE | Every component of the route is evaluable, free of violations, and meets its frozen descriptive threshold. **Conjunction only** |

**Frozen priority order.** A route all of whose components are validly predeclared exclusions is OUT OF SCOPE. Otherwise the first matching clause over the route's in-scope committed components assigns the label: violation (FAILED), then non-evaluability (NOT EVALUABLE), then threshold failure (NOT SUPPORTED), then a committed component's absence (INCOMPLETE), then support (SUPPORTED-DESCRIPTIVE). An observed failure (FAILED, NOT EVALUABLE or NOT SUPPORTED) dominates INCOMPLETE, so a failure that was actually seen is reported as a failure rather than masked as missing evidence.

**Frozen conjunction rule.** Cross-phase components are combined by **CONJUNCTION ONLY**. A route with components in more than one phase, namely R2, R4, R5 and R6, is supported only if every one of its components passes its own gate. No p-value combination method is used anywhere, and none can be: no p-value exists in this contract's route path.

**Frozen master novelty statement rule.** The sentence "SHV contributes something a competent SLSA plus in-toto plus Sigstore baseline does not" may be asserted only route-by-route and context-by-context, only for routes labelled SUPPORTED-DESCRIPTIVE, only in descriptive terms, and only with that route's frozen scope limitation stated in the same sentence. The unqualified sentence is PROHIBITED. Any formulation implying significance, inference, generalization or population-level novelty is PROHIBITED. Where no route is supported, the negative result is recorded in the audit ledger. A Phase C result in the tentative reliability band of Section 7.4 may not support any route statement.

### 8.5 Frozen limits of descriptive gates, stated rather than implied

1. **A descriptive gate cannot be false-positive-controlled, because it is not a test.** Eleven gates evaluated on one corpus will occasionally all pass by luck of the draw, and this contract offers no error rate for that event and does not pretend to.
2. **A gate says nothing about any task, target, model or environment other than the one observed.** Every supported statement travels with its scope limitation.
3. **The near-perfect thresholds are substantive commitments, not achievements.** A share of 0.97 against a frozen 0.98 is recorded as NOT SUPPORTED, and that outcome is a real and reportable failure of the claim as stated.
4. **Withdrawing inference costs the program its route-level confirmatory ambition.** That cost is accepted openly. The alternative was to keep a number whose validity the producer cannot defend, which would have been worse in exactly the way this protocol exists to prevent.
5. **If a valid population model for the fixed heterogeneous paired design is ever established, it must arrive as a new frozen version with its sampling mechanism, its exchangeability assumptions and its own carrying audit**, never as a reinterpretation of this one.

### 8.6 Frozen adversarial test obligations for route evidence (new in v0.5)

The following must be executed against the shipped module in every future build, and each must be rejected or must fail closed. They are named here so that a later build cannot quietly drop them.

| Case | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| Inconsistent raw counts (numerator above denominator, violations above denominator) | REJECTED, no report returned |
| Omitted mandatory field | REJECTED |
| Extra or injected field, including any gate verdict, evaluability flag or p-value | REJECTED |
| Non-integer, Boolean or negative count | REJECTED |
| Fabricated derived object passed as evidence | REJECTED |
| Object produced by `dataclasses.replace` from a genuine below-minimum report | REJECTED |
| Below-minimum evidence count | NOT EVALUABLE, and no route support |
| Catastrophic raw evidence, for example 0 of 100 passing, with any accompanying assertion of compliance | NOT SUPPORTED at minimum; the assertion itself is REJECTED as an extra field |
| Zero-tolerance violation present alongside a passing share | FAILED |
| Unknown component key | REJECTED |

---

## 9. The decisive research sequence (frozen)

XZ construct validation, then CVE-Bench control validation, then private novel-discovery stress test, then, only if warranted and separately authorized, restricted frontier-model replication. Each case is held to the role its evidence can support: XZ tests whether SHV finds and explains real divergence; CVE-Bench tests whether the architecture controls agentic effects reproducibly; the private benchmark tests novel discovery without exposing live vulnerabilities; a restricted replication would test whether the result survives capability scaling. No phase's conclusion is generalized beyond its evidentiary reach.

## 10. Council and adjudication discipline (frozen)

Independent roles, with disagreement recorded rather than forced to consensus: producer, skeptical replicator, security specialist, methodology reviewer, final adjudicator. Carrying review requires non-producer-lineage seats of different families; same-vendor seats count once; producer-lineage review is ADVISORY. The editor or producer of an artifact never certifies that artifact. Reviewers attest only to the checks they performed, not to universal safety. Every finding is preserved append-only; a correction is a new record identifying the superseded assertion, its reason, the corrected artifact, every known downstream consumer, and acknowledgment status. Divergence between carrying seats is dispositive against deposit and forces a new version, which is exactly what produced v0.2.

## 11. Deliverables of the eventual paper (frozen scope)

An open XZ structural-honesty dataset with declared surfaces, artifact layers, ground-truth divergences, projection graph, and correction lineage; an executable BSSG reference implementation; a SLSA and in-toto baseline implemented by a separate team; a preregistered XZ replay; a CVE-Bench exploratory pilot and 1,440-session confirmatory run with typed effect requests and witness-failure injections; a public schema for effect requests, witness receipts, lineage attestations, and correction rows; and negative results and falsification outcomes preserved in the audit ledger. Proposed title on record: From Attestation to Effect Control: Validating Structural Honesty on the XZ Supply Chain and Autonomous Cyber Agents.

## 12. Versioning rule (frozen for v0.2 onward)

A change is **SUBSTANTIVE**, and therefore requires a new frozen version with an amendment-record entry, re-hashing, and a re-run carrying audit, if it alters any of: an estimand attribute; a numeric threshold, target, or margin; a decision rule or its Boolean structure; an analysis population or missing-data rule; a multiplicity structure or power target; a corpus size, composition, or allocation; a scope statement; a safety boundary; or the factual content or attribution of an empirical anchor. A change is **EDITORIAL**, and may be issued as a dated errata note against the same frozen version, only if it alters formatting, typography, cross-reference numbering, or a typographical error that cannot change any decision. Every accepted v0.1 finding was substantive, which is why v0.1 could not be repaired by errata, and every accepted v0.2 finding is substantive under the same rule, which is why v0.2 required this new frozen version rather than an errata note.

**v0.5 (2026-07-24): withdrawal freeze following the v0.4 HALT.**

- **A-5.1 (from GPT F-P4-2). ACCEPTED IN FULL. ALL ROUTE-LEVEL INFERENCE IS WITHDRAWN.** The exact one-sided binomial boundary test, the Clopper-Pearson bounds, the re-anchored Class I nulls, the attainability record, the Class I component class, family F3a, and the application of Benjamini-Hochberg to route evidence are withdrawn in full from the normative path. The seat established that the frozen design randomises sessions **within** fixed heterogeneous Phase B cells and crosses every Phase C target with both arms, so cells and targets are neither independently allocated nor an iid sample from any stated population, and that independence without a common success probability or a stated superpopulation model does not yield a binomial. The producer has no defensible population or generalization target for that design and declines to invent one after the fact. Every one of the eleven components is therefore reclassified **Class G, descriptive gate-only**; the closed route label list loses SUPPORTED-INFERENTIAL and DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY and its strongest attainable label is SUPPORTED-DESCRIPTIVE; conjunction-only combination across phases is retained. ### Provenance note (authorship boundary)

This frozen v0.8 was AUTHORED by the Anthropic-family producer, descending from the producer's own v0.7 route gate, tests and source. The three-trust-root commitment architecture (commitment authority, independent anchor, run logger; no runtime override; a signed, resolved `commitment_id`; and the four-layer REALIZED commitment) was PROPOSED in a GPT-family design draft and is adopted here because it is correct and independently re-derived; that design credit is GPT's. The producer's own load-bearing divergences, made with reasons, are: the symmetric INDEPENDENT anchor on the SEALED path (A-8.5); the structural version/date parity check over all section headings (A-8.6); and the chronology resolution (A-8.6). The bytes of `shvvp_v0_8_route_gates.py`, `test_shvvp_v0_8_rules.py`, `verify_shvvp_v0_8.py` and this source are the producer's. Because the producer authored this artifact, the producer is the PRODUCER OF RECORD and is excluded from the carrying pool for v0.8; the two carrying seats WERE non-producer families of different vendors, Kimi (Moonshot) and Qwen (Alibaba), each executing the gate (amendment A-8.8), and the GPT family, having contributed the design, is advisory for this artifact's carry.

26. Analysis guidance for cluster and correlated designs, [PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7616648/).
27. Tipping-point sensitivity methodology for missing data, [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35653556/).
28. K-Alpha methodological notes on Krippendorff alpha benchmarks, [k-alpha.org](https://www.k-alpha.org/methodological-notes).
29. Landis and Koch agreement benchmark table, [NCBI Bookshelf](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK92287/table/executivesummary.t2/); original paper, [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/843571/).
30. SPIRIT 2025 statement on protocol audit trails, [JAMA](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2833408).
31. DiCiccio and Efron, Bootstrap Confidence Intervals, Statistical Science 1996, [Project Euclid](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-11/issue-3/Bootstrap-confidence-intervals/10.1214/ss/1032280214.pdf). Source for the BCa method used in Section 6.5.1.
32. Efron and Tibshirani, Bootstrap Methods for Standard Errors, Confidence Intervals, and Other Measures of Statistical Accuracy, Statistical Science 1986, [Project Euclid](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-1/issue-1/Bootstrap-Methods-for-Standard-Errors-Confidence-Intervals-and-Other-Measures/10.1214/ss/1177013815.full).
33. Cluster bootstrapping for nested data, [PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5965657/). Source for resampling whole clusters rather than observations.
34. **Cited by the WITHDRAWN v0.4 route inference; retained for lineage only, and supporting no claim in this version.** Brown, Cai and DasGupta, Interval Estimation for a Binomial Proportion, Statistical Science 2001, [Project Euclid](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-16/issue-2/Interval-Estimation-for-a-Binomial-Proportion/10.1214/ss/1009213286.short). The method it documents is no longer used: see Section 8.0.
35. **Cited by the WITHDRAWN v0.4 route inference; retained for lineage only, and supporting no claim in this version.** NIST Technical Note 2119, Estimating Instrument Performance with Confidence Intervals, [nvlpubs.nist.gov](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/TechnicalNotes/NIST.TN.2119.pdf). The bound it documents is no longer computed: see Section 8.0.

## R0182 · test_xz_protocol_adversarial.py — test_xz_protocol_adversarial.py -- Cross-module adversarial integration suite.

# XZ Protocol v0.75 test suite
"""
test_xz_protocol_adversarial.py -- Cross-module adversarial integration suite.

Covers all nine Section 22 item 4 mandated attack categories plus
cross-module invariants. All fixtures are decoys (non-XZ).
"""
import pytest
from xz_protocol_kernel import (
    TruthValue, KernelDecision, ConjunctVector, evaluate_kernel,
)
from xz_protocol_condition_a import (
    ADisposition, BaselineCheck, BoundaryStratum as AStratum,
    CheckOutcome, ConditionAError, create_check_result,
    evaluate_boundary, is_dual_evaluable, is_primary_seam_divergence,
)
from xz_protocol_source_frame import (
    DISCLOSURE_DATE, FRAME_START, FRAME_END, SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST,
    BoundaryStratum as SFStratum, get_sources_for_stratum, validate_manifest,
)
from xz_protocol_control_graph import (
    AuthorityChannel, ChannelStatus, ControlEdge, WithinAuthVerdict,
    compute_verdict,
)

T, F, U = TruthValue.TRUE, TruthValue.FALSE, TruthValue.UNKNOWN

def _cr(check, outcome, reason="test"):
    return create_check_result(check, outcome, "test-tool", "1.0", reason)

def _commit_accept():
    return evaluate_boundary("adv-1", AStratum.S_COMMIT, [
        _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS)])


# === CAT-1: CALLER-SUPPLIED DERIVED FACTS ===
class TestCallerSuppliedDerivedFacts:
    def test_string_b_decision_rejected(self):
        """The seam estimator rejects string decisions."""
        d = _commit_accept()
        with pytest.raises(ConditionAError, match="KernelDecision"):
            is_dual_evaluable(d, "DENY_FALSE")

    def test_kernel_rejects_string_vector(self):
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            evaluate_kernel("ALLOW")

    def test_kernel_rejects_string_truth(self):
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            ConjunctVector("TRUE", T, T, T, T)


# === CAT-2: DENOMINATOR SUBSTITUTION ===
class TestDenominatorSubstitution:
    def test_not_applicable_excluded_from_dual(self):
        """A-NOT-APPLICABLE boundaries must not enter the S1 denominator."""
        # All strata have profiles, so NOT-APPLICABLE is unreachable
        # from normal strata. Verify the gate exists.
        d = _commit_accept()
        assert is_dual_evaluable(d, KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE)
        # A boundary with A-INDETERMINATE IS dual-evaluable but NOT primary divergence
        d2 = evaluate_boundary("adv-denom", AStratum.S_COMMIT, [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.AMBIGUOUS, "unclear")])
        assert is_dual_evaluable(d2, KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE)
        assert not is_primary_seam_divergence(d2, KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE)


# === CAT-3: COMMITMENT-IDENTIFIER CONFUSION ===
class TestCommitmentIdConfusion:
    def test_source_ids_unique(self):
        ids = [s.source_id for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST]
        assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))

    def test_trust_root_keys_distinct(self):
        import json
        with open("xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json") as f:
            roots = json.load(f)
        keys = [v["public_key_hex"] for v in roots["trust_roots"].values()]
        assert len(keys) == len(set(keys)) == 3


# === CAT-4: TRUST-ROOT OVERRIDE ===
class TestTrustRootOverride:
    def test_trust_roots_are_ed25519(self):
        import json
        with open("xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json") as f:
            roots = json.load(f)
        for role, v in roots["trust_roots"].items():
            assert v["algorithm"] == "Ed25519"
            assert len(v["public_key_hex"]) == 64  # 32 bytes hex

    def test_three_distinct_roles(self):
        import json
        with open("xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json") as f:
            roots = json.load(f)
        roles = set(roots["trust_roots"].keys())
        assert roles == {"commitment-authority", "independent-anchor", "run-logger"}


# === CAT-5: PACKET-REGIME MIXING (CR-11) ===
class TestPacketRegimeMixing:
    def test_kernel_decisions_are_typed(self):
        """Kernel outputs are enum-typed, not strings.
        Mixing regimes requires type confusion -- which is blocked."""
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(T, F, T, T, T))
        assert isinstance(r.decision, KernelDecision)
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE


# === CAT-6: POST-CUTOFF EVIDENCE INJECTION ===
class TestPostCutoffInjection:
    def test_frame_end_is_bounded(self):
        from datetime import date
        assert FRAME_END == date(2024, 4, 28)
        assert FRAME_END < date(2024, 5, 1)

    def test_kernel_has_no_timestamp_backdoor(self):
        """The kernel takes a ConjunctVector, not timestamps.
        Cutoff enforcement is at the packet layer, not the kernel."""
        v = ConjunctVector(T, T, T, T, T)
        r = evaluate_kernel(v)
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.ALLOW
        # No timestamp field exists on ConjunctVector
        assert not hasattr(v, 'timestamp')


# === CAT-7: ROLE REMAPPING AFTER OUTCOMES ===
class TestRoleRemappingAfterOutcomes:
    def test_conjunct_vector_is_frozen(self):
        """ConjunctVector is frozen -- no post-evaluation mutation."""
        v = ConjunctVector(T, F, T, T, T)
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            v.contract_match = T

    def test_kernel_result_is_frozen(self):
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(T, F, T, T, T))
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            r.decision = KernelDecision.ALLOW


# === CAT-8: DENY-CLASS COLLAPSE (XZ-S7/S9) ===
class TestDenyClassCollapse:
    def test_deny_false_and_unknown_distinct(self):
        assert KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE != KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN

    def test_seam_excludes_deny_unknown(self):
        """DENY_UNKNOWN is dual-evaluable but NOT primary divergence."""
        d = _commit_accept()
        assert is_dual_evaluable(d, KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN)
        assert not is_primary_seam_divergence(d, KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN)

    def test_false_dominates_in_kernel(self):
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(F, U, T, T, T))
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE


# === CAT-9: SCREENED-EVENT SUPPRESSION ===
class TestScreenedEventSuppression:
    def test_all_strata_in_profile(self):
        """No stratum is silently dropped from the baseline profile."""
        from xz_protocol_condition_a import BASELINE_PROFILE
        for s in AStratum:
            assert s in BASELINE_PROFILE

    def test_source_frame_strata_match(self):
        """Source-frame strata match Condition A strata."""
        a_strata = {s.value for s in AStratum}
        sf_strata = {s.value for s in SFStratum}
        assert a_strata == sf_strata


# === CROSS-MODULE: source frame covers Condition A ===
class TestSourceFrameCoversConditionA:
    def test_core_strata(self):
        for s in [SFStratum.S_COMMIT, SFStratum.S_RELEASE,
                  SFStratum.S_BUILD, SFStratum.S_DISTRIBUTION]:
            assert len(get_sources_for_stratum(s)) > 0


# === CROSS-MODULE: A/B seam with kernel ===
class TestSeamWithKernel:
    def test_primary_divergence(self):
        d = _commit_accept()
        kr = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(F, T, T, T, T))
        assert is_primary_seam_divergence(d, kr.decision)

    def test_agreement(self):
        d = _commit_accept()
        kr = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(T, T, T, T, T))
        assert not is_primary_seam_divergence(d, kr.decision)


# === DOMINANCE CONSISTENCY ===
class TestDominanceConsistency:
    def test_a_reject_dominates(self):
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.FAIL, "bad"),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.AMBIGUOUS, "unclear")]
        d = evaluate_boundary("dom-1", AStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_REJECT

    def test_kernel_false_dominates(self):
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(F, U, F, U, T))
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE


# === MANIFEST INTEGRITY ===
class TestManifestIntegrity:
    def test_valid(self):
        assert validate_manifest()["valid"]

    def test_frame_window(self):
        from datetime import date
        assert FRAME_START <= date(2024, 1, 1)
        assert FRAME_END >= date(2024, 4, 15)


# === PROHIBITED CONTENT ===
class TestProhibitedContent:
    def _all_text(self):
        import importlib
        texts = []
        for m in ["xz_protocol_condition_a", "xz_protocol_source_frame",
                   "xz_protocol_control_graph", "xz_protocol_kernel"]:
            mod = importlib.import_module(m)
            texts.append(open(mod.__file__).read())
        return " ".join(texts)

    def test_no_payload(self):
        t = self._all_text().lower()
        for term in ["ifunc", "got_plt", "cpuid", "rsa_public_decrypt"]:
            assert term not in t

    def test_no_activation(self):
        t = self._all_text().lower()
        # "activation recipe" in "no activation recipe" is a PROHIBITION, not content
        # Check for actual recipes, not prohibitions of them
        lines = t.split('\n')
        for line in lines:
            if "activation recipe" in line and "no activation recipe" not in line:
                pytest.fail(f"Activation recipe content found: {line.strip()}")
        assert "backdoor" not in t


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "--tb=short"])

## R0183 · test_xz_protocol_condition_a.py — test_xz_protocol_condition_a.py -- Adversarial test suite for Condition A.

- section: IV. XZ Protocol

- source_format: py
- merged_variants: 2 (test_xz_protocol_condition_a.py.txt; test_xz_protocol_condition_a.txt)

# XZ Protocol v0.75 test suite
"""
test_xz_protocol_condition_a.py -- Adversarial test suite for Condition A.

Tests the executable baseline disposition function against decoy boundaries
(non-XZ inputs). No XZ-specific data in this file.
"""
import pytest
from xz_protocol_kernel import KernelDecision
from xz_protocol_condition_a import (
    ADisposition, BaselineCheck, BaselineCheckResult, BoundaryStratum,
    CheckOutcome, ConditionAError, BoundaryDisposition, BASELINE_PROFILE,
    create_check_result, evaluate_boundary, is_dual_evaluable,
    is_primary_seam_divergence,
)


def _cr(check, outcome, reason="test"):
    return create_check_result(check, outcome, "test-tool", "1.0", reason)


# === DISPOSITION VOCABULARY ===

class TestDispositionVocabulary:
    def test_all_four_labels_exist(self):
        assert len(ADisposition) == 4

    def test_values(self):
        assert ADisposition.A_ACCEPT.value == "A-ACCEPT"
        assert ADisposition.A_REJECT.value == "A-REJECT"
        assert ADisposition.A_INDETERMINATE.value == "A-INDETERMINATE"
        assert ADisposition.A_NOT_APPLICABLE.value == "A-NOT-APPLICABLE"


# === BASELINE PROFILE ===

class TestBaselineProfile:
    def test_all_strata_have_profiles(self):
        for s in BoundaryStratum:
            assert s in BASELINE_PROFILE

    def test_all_profiles_nonempty(self):
        for s, checks in BASELINE_PROFILE.items():
            assert len(checks) > 0, f"{s} has empty profile"


# === ACCEPT (all mandatory pass) ===

class TestAccept:
    def test_commit_all_pass(self):
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-1", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_ACCEPT
        assert not d.has_failure
        assert not d.has_indeterminate

    def test_release_all_pass(self):
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.SOURCE_TO_ARTIFACT_COMPARISON, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.SLSA_PROVENANCE, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-2", BoundaryStratum.S_RELEASE, results)
        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_ACCEPT


# === REJECT (at least one failure) ===

class TestReject:
    def test_one_failure(self):
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.FAIL, "bad sig"),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-3", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_REJECT
        assert d.has_failure

    def test_failure_dominates_indeterminate(self):
        """A-REJECT > A-INDETERMINATE (parallels FALSE > UNKNOWN)."""
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.FAIL, "bad sig"),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.AMBIGUOUS, "unclear"),
            # PROVENANCE_REVIEW absent -> INDETERMINATE
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-4", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_REJECT
        assert d.has_failure and d.has_indeterminate


# === INDETERMINATE (no failure, but mandatory absent/ambiguous) ===

class TestIndeterminate:
    def test_missing_mandatory(self):
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            # PROVENANCE_REVIEW absent
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-5", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_INDETERMINATE
        assert d.has_indeterminate
        assert BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW in d.mandatory_absent

    def test_ambiguous_check(self):
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.AMBIGUOUS, "shared account"),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-6", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_INDETERMINATE

    def test_unverifiable_check(self):

            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-7", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_INDETERMINATE

    def test_stale_check(self):

        assert d.disposition == ADisposition.A_INDETERMINATE


# === NOT-APPLICABLE ===

class TestNotApplicable:
    def test_all_strata_have_checks(self):

        only fires if a stratum were added with no profile."""

# === DUAL-EVALUABILITY ===

class TestDualEvaluable:
    def test_accept_deny_false(self):
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-9", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert is_dual_evaluable(d, KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE)
        assert is_primary_seam_divergence(d, KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE)

    def test_accept_allow_no_divergence(self):
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS),
        ]
        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-10", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert is_dual_evaluable(d, KernelDecision.ALLOW)
        assert not is_primary_seam_divergence(d, KernelDecision.ALLOW)

    def test_accept_deny_unknown_not_primary(self):
        """DENY_UNKNOWN is never primary seam divergence (CR-3)."""
        results = [
            _cr(BaselineCheck.COMMIT_SIGNING, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.IDENTITY_VERIFICATION, CheckOutcome.PASS),
            _cr(BaselineCheck.PROVENANCE_REVIEW, CheckOutcome.PASS),

        d = evaluate_boundary("decoy-11", BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, results)
        assert is_dual_evaluable(d, KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN)
        assert not is_primary_seam_divergence(d, KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN)

# XZ Protocol v0.75 test suite
"""
test_xz_protocol_control_graph.py -- Tests for the WithinAuth control graph.

All fixtures are decoys (non-XZ). Tests verify adjudication rules,
verdict computation, prohibited shortcuts, and schema validation.
"""
import pytest
from xz_protocol_control_graph import (
    AuthorityChannel, ChannelStatus, ControlEdge, WithinAuthVerdict,
    ActingSubstrate, RecordGenerationAct, WithinAuthAssessment,
    compute_verdict, PROHIBITED_SHORTCUTS,
    decoy_fixture_independent_ci,
    decoy_fixture_maintainer_controlled_release,
    decoy_fixture_ambiguous_shared_infra,
)


# === VERDICT COMPUTATION ===

class TestVerdictComputation:
    def _edges(self, statuses):
        channels = list(AuthorityChannel)
        return tuple(ControlEdge(channels[i], statuses[i], "test", "test")
                     for i in range(5))

    def test_all_no_is_outside(self):
        e = self._edges([ChannelStatus.NO]*5)
        assert compute_verdict(e) == WithinAuthVerdict.OUTSIDE

    def test_any_yes_is_inside(self):
        for i in range(5):
            statuses = [ChannelStatus.NO]*5
            statuses[i] = ChannelStatus.YES
            e = self._edges(statuses)
            assert compute_verdict(e) == WithinAuthVerdict.INSIDE

    def test_yes_dominates_unknown(self):
        statuses = [ChannelStatus.UNKNOWN]*4 + [ChannelStatus.YES]
        e = self._edges(statuses)
        assert compute_verdict(e) == WithinAuthVerdict.INSIDE

    def test_unknown_without_yes_is_unknown(self):
        statuses = [ChannelStatus.NO]*4 + [ChannelStatus.UNKNOWN]
        e = self._edges(statuses)
        assert compute_verdict(e) == WithinAuthVerdict.UNKNOWN

    def test_all_unknown_is_unknown(self):
        e = self._edges([ChannelStatus.UNKNOWN]*5)
        assert compute_verdict(e) == WithinAuthVerdict.UNKNOWN

    def test_mixed_no_unknown_is_unknown(self):
        statuses = [ChannelStatus.NO, ChannelStatus.UNKNOWN,
                    ChannelStatus.NO, ChannelStatus.NO, ChannelStatus.UNKNOWN]
        e = self._edges(statuses)
        assert compute_verdict(e) == WithinAuthVerdict.UNKNOWN


# === DOMINANCE ORDER ===

class TestDominance:
    """YES (INSIDE) dominates UNKNOWN dominates NO (OUTSIDE).
    Parallels BSSG: FALSE dominates UNKNOWN dominates TRUE."""

    def _edges(self, statuses):
        channels = list(AuthorityChannel)
        return tuple(ControlEdge(channels[i], statuses[i], "test", "test")
                     for i in range(5))

    def test_inside_dominates_all(self):
        # One YES among UNKNOWNs and NOs -> INSIDE
        for pattern in [[ChannelStatus.YES]+[ChannelStatus.NO]*4,
                        [ChannelStatus.YES]+[ChannelStatus.UNKNOWN]*4,
                        [ChannelStatus.NO,ChannelStatus.UNKNOWN,ChannelStatus.NO,
                         ChannelStatus.YES,ChannelStatus.UNKNOWN]]:
            assert compute_verdict(self._edges(pattern)) == WithinAuthVerdict.INSIDE

    def test_outside_requires_unanimity(self):
        # OUTSIDE only when ALL five are NO
        assert compute_verdict(self._edges([ChannelStatus.NO]*5)) == WithinAuthVerdict.OUTSIDE


# === SCHEMA VALIDATION ===

class TestSchemaValidation:
    def test_missing_channel_rejected(self):
        edges = tuple(ControlEdge(c, ChannelStatus.NO, "t", "t")
                      for c in list(AuthorityChannel)[:4])  # only 4
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Missing"):
            WithinAuthAssessment(
                ActingSubstrate("s1", "test", "test"),
                RecordGenerationAct("r1", "test", "gen", "2024-01-01", "type"),
                edges, WithinAuthVerdict.OUTSIDE, "adj1", "test")

    def test_string_channel_rejected(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="AuthorityChannel"):
            ControlEdge("can-cause", ChannelStatus.NO, "t", "t")

    def test_string_status_rejected(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ChannelStatus"):
            ControlEdge(AuthorityChannel.CAUSE, "no", "t", "t")


# === DECOY FIXTURES ===

class TestDecoyFixtures:
    def test_independent_ci_outside(self):
        a = decoy_fixture_independent_ci()
        assert a.verdict == WithinAuthVerdict.OUTSIDE

    def test_maintainer_release_inside(self):
        a = decoy_fixture_maintainer_controlled_release()
        assert a.verdict == WithinAuthVerdict.INSIDE

    def test_shared_infra_unknown(self):
        a = decoy_fixture_ambiguous_shared_infra()
        assert a.verdict == WithinAuthVerdict.UNKNOWN


# === PROHIBITED SHORTCUTS ===

class TestProhibitedShortcuts:
    def test_shortcuts_exist(self):
        assert len(PROHIBITED_SHORTCUTS) >= 4

    def test_signature_shortcut_documented(self):
        assert any("signature" in s.lower() and "does not" in s.lower()
                    for s in PROHIBITED_SHORTCUTS)

    def test_organizational_shortcut_documented(self):
        assert any("organizational" in s.lower() and "does not" in s.lower()
                    for s in PROHIBITED_SHORTCUTS)


# === ALL THREE VERDICTS REACHABLE ===

class TestVerdictReachability:
    def test_all_verdicts_produced(self):
        verdicts = {
            decoy_fixture_independent_ci().verdict,
            decoy_fixture_maintainer_controlled_release().verdict,
            decoy_fixture_ambiguous_shared_infra().verdict,
        }
        assert verdicts == {WithinAuthVerdict.OUTSIDE,
                            WithinAuthVerdict.INSIDE,
                            WithinAuthVerdict.UNKNOWN}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "--tb=short"])

## R0185 · test_xz_protocol_gates.txt — Fixture-pair tests for the four XZ Protocol gates.

- section: IV. XZ Protocol
- source_file: test_xz_protocol_gates.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: 0419ca742e47900d92b56a22c2635a3ed12044cac90034210466d1d60fd9cf31

"""Fixture-pair tests for the four XZ Protocol gates.

Absorbs F-XZ12-OP-01. The v0.12 gates shipped with no fixtures at all,
and two of them could not have failed on any input: one searched for a
string absent from the document, the other searched for the corrected
form of a defect rather than the defective form, so green meant unfixed.

Every gate here is tested in both directions. A known-good fixture (the
shipped package, unmodified) must produce exit 0, and one known-bad
fixture per defect class must produce exit 1. This is the discipline
already applied to the kernel, where 243 exhaustive vectors pin every
decision state; it was never applied to the gates.

Run inside the canonical invocation, so a gate that stops discriminating
fails the same build that ships it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from contextlib import contextmanager

import pytest

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# Declared to xz_protocol_prohibited_content_verifier.py: this file carries
# prohibited strings as deliberate test inputs, not as claims.
PROHIBITED_CONTENT_FIXTURES = True

VERSION_GATE = "xz_protocol_version_gate.py"
CLOSURE_GATE = "xz_protocol_closure_gate.py"
MANIFEST_GATE = "xz_protocol_manifest_gate.py"
CONTENT_GATE = "xz_protocol_prohibited_content_verifier.py"
HISTORY_GATE = "xz_protocol_history_gate.py"

ALL_GATES = [VERSION_GATE, CLOSURE_GATE, MANIFEST_GATE, CONTENT_GATE, HISTORY_GATE]

PROTOCOL = "xz_protocol_v0_13.md"

# Stale stamps are assembled from parts so this fixture file carries no literal
# version token of its own; otherwise the version gate would flag its own tests.
STAMP = "XZ Protocol " + "v"
CURRENT = STAMP + "0.13"
STALE = STAMP + "0.3"


def run(root: str, gate: str, *args: str) -> int:
    return subprocess.call(
        [sys.executable, os.path.join(root, gate), *args],
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )


@contextmanager
def sandbox():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        work = os.path.join(tmp, "pkg")
        shutil.copytree(ROOT, work, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(
            "__pycache__", ".pytest_cache"))
        yield work


def edit(root: str, name: str, old: str, new: str) -> None:
    path = os.path.join(root, name)
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    assert text.count(old) >= 1, f"fixture anchor not found in {name}: {old[:60]!r}"
    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text.replace(old, new, 1))


# --- known-good direction -----------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("gate", ALL_GATES)
def test_gate_passes_on_shipped_bytes(gate):
    assert run(ROOT, gate) == 0, f"{gate} does not pass on the shipped package"


def test_version_gate_self_test():
    assert run(ROOT, VERSION_GATE, "--self-test") == 0


# --- known-bad direction: version gate ---------------------------------------

def test_version_gate_fires_on_stale_module_stamp():
    with sandbox() as work:
        edit(work, "xz_protocol_kernel.py", CURRENT, STALE)
        assert run(work, VERSION_GATE) == 1


def test_version_gate_fires_on_stale_test_suite_stamp():
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, "test_xz_protocol_kernel.py")
        body = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
            "# " + STAMP + "0.4\n" + body)
        assert run(work, VERSION_GATE) == 1


def test_version_gate_fires_on_stale_gate_stamp():
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, MANIFEST_GATE)
        body = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
            "# " + STAMP + "0.2\n" + body)
        assert run(work, VERSION_GATE) == 1


def test_version_gate_rejects_proximity_style_exemption():
    """A historical marker beside a stale stamp must not excuse it.

    The v0.12 gate excused any mismatch within 100 characters of a marker
    such as 'RESOLVED in v0.'. That exemption path was controllable by the
    artifact under test, which is the escape-hatch shape this program has
    closed four times upstream.
    """
    with sandbox() as work:
        edit(work, "xz_protocol_source_frame.py",
             CURRENT, "RESOLVED in v0.3 -- " + STALE)
        assert run(work, VERSION_GATE) == 1


def test_version_gate_fires_when_trust_roots_disagree():
    with sandbox() as work:
        edit(work, "xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json",
             '"' + CURRENT + '"', '"' + STAMP + '0.12"')
        assert run(work, VERSION_GATE) == 1


# --- known-bad direction: closure gate ---------------------------------------

def test_closure_gate_fires_when_a_closed_locus_regresses():
    """Reverting the SHUDP deduplication must fail the gate.

    The v0.12 predecessor searched for the corrected string, so it passed
    on exactly this state.
    """
    with sandbox() as work:
        edit(work, PROTOCOL,
             "| Is Evidence Independence an Axiom? Decomposing a Proposed Extension to AX-SH ",
             "| Is Evidence Independence an Axiom? (SHUDP v0.5) | placeholder ")
        assert run(work, CLOSURE_GATE) == 1


def test_closure_gate_fires_on_unregistered_closure_claim():
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, PROTOCOL)
        text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
            text + "\n- **v9.9 (2026-01-01): fabricated.** F-XX-99 CLOSED: nothing.\n")
        assert run(work, CLOSURE_GATE) == 1


def test_closure_gate_is_not_satisfied_by_the_amendment_record_itself():
    """A closure claim must be provable in the body, not in the log asserting it."""
    with sandbox() as work:
        edit(work, PROTOCOL,
             "21539074 and 21539816 are two version DOIs under one concept DOI",
             "PLACEHOLDER removed from body")
        assert run(work, CLOSURE_GATE) == 1


def test_closure_gate_fires_when_register_is_absent():
    with sandbox() as work:
        os.remove(os.path.join(work, "xz_protocol_locus_register.json"))
        assert run(work, CLOSURE_GATE) == 1


# --- known-bad direction: manifest gate --------------------------------------

def test_manifest_gate_fires_on_modified_module():
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, "xz_protocol_condition_a.py")
        open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8").write("\n# drift\n")
        assert run(work, MANIFEST_GATE) == 1


def test_manifest_gate_fires_on_modified_gate():
    """The v0.12 predecessor hardcoded twelve files and could not see this."""
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, VERSION_GATE)
        open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8").write("\n# drift\n")
        assert run(work, MANIFEST_GATE) == 1


def test_manifest_gate_fires_on_unresolvable_digest_in_body():
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, PROTOCOL)
        text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        cut = text.index("## 27. Amendment record")
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
            text[:cut] + "\nStray digest " + "0" * 64 + "\n" + text[cut:])
        assert run(work, MANIFEST_GATE) == 1


# --- known-bad direction: prohibited-content verifier ------------------------

def test_content_gate_fires_on_effectiveness_claim():
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, PROTOCOL)
        text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
            text + "\nBSSG reduces supply-chain risk.\n")
        assert run(work, CONTENT_GATE) == 1


def test_content_gate_fires_on_outcome_modal():
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, PROTOCOL)
        text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
            text + "\nThe kernel would have denied the release.\n")
        assert run(work, CONTENT_GATE) == 1


def test_content_gate_fires_on_non_permitted_citation():
    with sandbox() as work:
        path = os.path.join(work, PROTOCOL)
        text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
            text + "\nSee https://example.com/xz-writeup for detail.\n")
        assert run(work, CONTENT_GATE) == 1


def test_content_gate_fires_when_a_declared_exemption_disappears():
    """The exemption list is asserted in both directions so it cannot rot."""
    with sandbox() as work:
        edit(work, PROTOCOL,
             "It is not an estimate of attack prevention",
             "It is not an estimate of prevention")
        assert run(work, CONTENT_GATE) == 1

def test_history_gate_fires_on_unsealed_appended_entry():

        assert run(work, HISTORY_GATE) == 1


def test_history_gate_fires_on_removed_entry():
    with sandbox() as work:

        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(

# XZ Protocol v0.75 test suite
"""
test_xz_protocol_kernel.py -- Exhaustive 3^5=243 kernel tests + adversarial.
"""
import pytest
from xz_protocol_kernel import (
    TruthValue, KernelDecision, KernelError,
    ConjunctVector, KernelResult, CONJUNCT_NAMES,
    evaluate_kernel, generate_exhaustive_vectors,
)

T, F, U = TruthValue.TRUE, TruthValue.FALSE, TruthValue.UNKNOWN

class TestExhaustive243:
    def test_count(self):
        assert len(generate_exhaustive_vectors()) == 243

    def test_all_true_allows(self):
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(T,T,T,T,T))
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.ALLOW
        assert r.false_conjuncts == () and r.unknown_conjuncts == ()

    def test_any_false_denies_false(self):
        for i in range(5):
            vals = [T]*5; vals[i] = F
            r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(*vals))
            assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE

    def test_false_dominates_unknown(self):
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(F,U,T,T,T))
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE

    def test_any_unknown_no_false_denies_unknown(self):
        for i in range(5):
            vals = [T]*5; vals[i] = U
            r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(*vals))
            assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN

    def test_all_false(self):
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(F,F,F,F,F))
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE
        assert len(r.false_conjuncts) == 5

    def test_all_unknown(self):
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(U,U,U,U,U))
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN
        assert len(r.unknown_conjuncts) == 5

    def test_exhaustive_decision_correctness(self):
        """Every one of 243 vectors produces the correct decision."""
        for v in generate_exhaustive_vectors():
            r = evaluate_kernel(v)
            vals = list(v.as_dict().values())
            has_false = any(x == F for x in vals)
            has_unknown = any(x == U for x in vals)
            if has_false:
                assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE, f"Expected DENY_FALSE for {v}"
            elif has_unknown:
                assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN, f"Expected DENY_UNKNOWN for {v}"
            else:
                assert r.decision == KernelDecision.ALLOW, f"Expected ALLOW for {v}"

    def test_exhaustive_reason_codes(self):
        for v in generate_exhaustive_vectors():
            r = evaluate_kernel(v)
            if r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE:
                assert len(r.false_conjuncts) > 0
                assert all("E-FALSE-" in c for c in r.reason_codes)
            elif r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN:
                assert len(r.false_conjuncts) == 0
                assert len(r.unknown_conjuncts) > 0
            else:
                assert r.reason_codes == ()

class TestDenyClassDistinct:
    """DENY_FALSE and DENY_UNKNOWN are NEVER collapsed (CR-3, XZ-S9)."""
    def test_never_equal(self):
        assert KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE != KernelDecision.DENY_UNKNOWN

    def test_false_dominates_in_all_mixed(self):
        """If both FALSE and UNKNOWN present, decision is DENY_FALSE."""
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(F,U,F,U,T))
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE

class TestInputValidation:
    def test_string_rejected(self):
        with pytest.raises(KernelError):
            evaluate_kernel("ALLOW")

    def test_string_truth_rejected(self):
        with pytest.raises(KernelError):
            ConjunctVector("TRUE",T,T,T,T)

class TestNoCallerSuppliedDecision:
    """The kernel takes a vector, not a decision. No bypass."""
    def test_result_is_computed(self):
        r = evaluate_kernel(ConjunctVector(T,F,T,T,T))
        assert r.decision == KernelDecision.DENY_FALSE
        assert "EffectTypeValid" in r.false_conjuncts

if __name__ == "__main__":
    pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "--tb=short"])

# XZ Protocol v0.75 test suite
"""
test_xz_protocol_source_frame.py -- Tests for the source-frame manifest.

Validates completeness, consistency, and correctness of the sealed
public-record universe.
"""
import pytest
from datetime import date

from xz_protocol_source_frame import (
    DISCLOSURE_DATE, FRAME_START, FRAME_END, DISCLOSURE_URL,
    SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST, BoundaryStratum, SourceCategory,
    AuthenticationMethod, SourceRecord,
    get_sources_for_stratum, get_source_by_id, validate_manifest,
)


class TestFrameWindow:
    def test_disclosure_date(self):
        assert DISCLOSURE_DATE == date(2024, 3, 29)

    def test_frame_start(self):
        delta = (DISCLOSURE_DATE - FRAME_START).days
        assert delta == 180  # ~180 days

    def test_frame_end(self):
        delta = (FRAME_END - DISCLOSURE_DATE).days
        assert delta == 30

    def test_frame_start_before_end(self):
        assert FRAME_START < FRAME_END

    def test_disclosure_within_frame(self):
        assert FRAME_START < DISCLOSURE_DATE < FRAME_END


class TestManifestCompleteness:
    def test_core_strata_covered(self):
        """Strata with known public records must have sources."""
        for stratum in [BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT, BoundaryStratum.S_RELEASE,
                        BoundaryStratum.S_BUILD, BoundaryStratum.S_DISTRIBUTION]:
            sources = get_sources_for_stratum(stratum)
            assert len(sources) > 0, f"No sources for {stratum.value}"

    def test_installation_runtime_may_be_empty(self):
        """Per Section 5.4 item 8: strata with zero eligible public records
        are retained and reported as NOT-EVALUABLE, not dropped."""
        # These strata may have zero public sources; that's a frame limitation
        for stratum in [BoundaryStratum.S_INSTALLATION, BoundaryStratum.S_RUNTIME_AUTH]:
            sources = get_sources_for_stratum(stratum)
            # Zero is acceptable -- it maps to NOT-EVALUABLE at stratum level
            assert isinstance(sources, list)

    def test_commit_stratum_has_repository(self):
        sources = get_sources_for_stratum(BoundaryStratum.S_COMMIT)
        categories = {s.category for s in sources}
        assert SourceCategory.REPOSITORY in categories

    def test_release_stratum_has_archive(self):
        sources = get_sources_for_stratum(BoundaryStratum.S_RELEASE)
        categories = {s.category for s in sources}
        assert SourceCategory.RELEASE_ARCHIVE in categories

    def test_distribution_has_multiple_channels(self):
        sources = get_sources_for_stratum(BoundaryStratum.S_DISTRIBUTION)
        dist_sources = [s for s in sources if s.category == SourceCategory.DISTRIBUTION]
        assert len(dist_sources) >= 4  # Debian, Fedora, Arch, Ubuntu minimum

    def test_build_stratum_covered(self):
        sources = get_sources_for_stratum(BoundaryStratum.S_BUILD)
        assert len(sources) >= 2


class TestManifestConsistency:
    def test_unique_source_ids(self):
        ids = [s.source_id for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST]
        assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))

    def test_all_sources_have_authentication(self):
        for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST:
            assert len(s.authentication) > 0, f"{s.source_id} has no auth"

    def test_all_sources_have_retrieval_rule(self):
        for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST:
            assert s.retrieval_rule.strip(), f"{s.source_id} has no retrieval rule"

    def test_all_sources_have_strata(self):
        for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST:
            assert len(s.strata_covered) > 0, f"{s.source_id} covers no strata"


class TestPrimaryCitations:
    """The four primary XZ citations from Section 26.3 must appear."""

    def test_oss_security(self):
        assert any("openwall.com/lists/oss-security" in s.url
                    for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST)

    def test_nvd(self):
        assert any("nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2024-3094" in s.url
                    for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST)

    def test_xz_issue_103(self):
        assert any("tukaani-project/xz/issues" in s.url
                    for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST)

    def test_github_advisory(self):
        assert any("GHSA-rxwq-x6h5-x525" in s.url
                    for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST)


class TestSourceLookup:
    def test_by_id(self):
        s = get_source_by_id("SRC-REPO-01")
        assert s is not None
        assert "tukaani" in s.name.lower() or "xz" in s.name.lower()

    def test_missing_id(self):
        assert get_source_by_id("SRC-NONEXISTENT") is None


class TestValidateManifest:
    def test_manifest_valid(self):
        result = validate_manifest()
        assert result["valid"], f"Manifest invalid: {result['errors']}"
        assert result["source_count"] == len(SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST)

    def test_core_strata_positive_count(self):
        result = validate_manifest()
        for stratum in ["S-COMMIT", "S-RELEASE", "S-BUILD", "S-DISTRIBUTION"]:
            assert result["strata_coverage"][stratum] > 0


class TestNoRestrictedContent:
    """Safety gate: the manifest must contain no restricted content."""

    def test_no_payload_hashes(self):
        for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST:
            combined = f"{s.url} {s.retrieval_rule} {s.notes or ''}"
            assert "payload" not in combined.lower() or "hash" not in combined.lower()

    def test_no_activation_recipes(self):
        for s in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST:
            combined = f"{s.url} {s.retrieval_rule} {s.notes or ''}"
            assert "activation" not in combined.lower()
            assert "ifunc" not in combined.lower()
            assert "backdoor" not in combined.lower()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "--tb=short"])


class TestExactSourceFrameValues:
    """Exact regression tests for source-frame facts (F-XZ06-GPT-05)."""

    def test_exact_source_count(self):
        assert len(SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST) == 16

    def test_exact_represented_category_count(self):
        cats = {r.category for r in SOURCE_FRAME_MANIFEST}
        assert len(cats) == 6

    def test_s_installation_zero_sources(self):
        sources = get_sources_for_stratum(BoundaryStratum.S_INSTALLATION)
        assert len(sources) == 0

    def test_s_runtime_auth_two_sources(self):
        sources = get_sources_for_stratum(BoundaryStratum.S_RUNTIME_AUTH)
        assert len(sources) == 2
        ids = {s.source_id for s in sources}
        assert ids == {"SRC-ML-01", "SRC-ADV-01"}

SEAT: GPT-5.6 Sol (adversarial, non-binding, full finding weight)
ARTIFACT: XZ Protocol v0.37, sha256sum -c rc=0, build.py BUILD PASSED
FRAMEWORK: Fractal / Hurst Persistence Analysis
VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS

Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim.

## Executive assessment

The packet verifies and all 186 tests pass. The quantitative record does **not** sustain the v0.36 terminality statement that further disposition attempts only advance the version count: v0.37 records 11/11 convergence on a Class A contradiction and makes a substantive operative-rule amendment that removes it. The primary R/S estimate is high, but N=37, long constant runs, and severity-extraction ambiguity make it unsuitable as confirmation of convergence. The current artifact is therefore conditionally passable as an openly bounded instrument, not as proof that its disposition process had ceased producing substantive advances.

## Verification and independence

- Audit prompt read before analysis; only the canonical packet was used. No prior audit report or memory output was consulted.
- Command rerun in the packet directory: `sha256sum -c PACKET_SHA256SUMS && python3 build.py`. Result: manifest members OK; BUILD PASSED; pytest 186 passed.
- Authoritative packet references read: Differentiator Framework v5.0; Cross-Text Computational Linguistics Thesis v1.1; Golden Thread Guide; Pharmacological Pattern Recognition ODT; and the shipped renal-fractal PDF. Normative protocol, code, tests, trust-root manifest, packet manifest, build tooling, and history seal were inspected.
- Fatiha discipline applied: verification first; MDL tiering; priority order; no tool consumed more than 25% of the audit budget; non-productive analogies terminated; all predictive readings treated as Tier 3 unless falsifiable.

## FINDINGS

F-GPT37FH-01 [HIGH] [Tier 1]
  Locus: `xz_protocol_v0_37.md:1120` (v0.36 “Further disposition attempts do not advance the deliverable”); `:1130-1140` (v0.37 universal Class A convergence and operative amendment); Section 22 item 7 at `:700`.
  Substance: The v0.36 terminality claim is contradicted by the next shipped entry. v0.37 reports that all eleven advisory seats found the same Class A contradiction—FROZEN status versus the unamended HALT rule—and repairs it by amending the operative rule. That is a substantive advance in internal consistency, not merely a higher version number.
  Computed value: 1 subsequent version; 11/11 seats converged; 1 Class A defect class; 3 stated body-amendment loci (Section 22 item 7, Section 25 FB-7b, Section 22.3). The extracted severity moves from 4 at v0.36 to 5 at v0.37.
  Framework basis: Tier-1 byte comparison plus Hurst-orientation falsifier: a terminality statement is disproved by a later substantive correction regardless of persistence estimate.
  Disposition: Replace the categorical v0.36 sentence with a time-bounded observation: “At v0.36, repeated dispositions had not cleared two recurring HALTs; v0.37 subsequently required an operative-rule amendment.” Do not use H as evidence that further rounds are futile.
  Cross-reference: F-OP36-01 / F-OP36S-01 / F-OP36C899-01 / F-OP36I-03 as recorded in v0.37.

F-GPT37FH-02 [MEDIUM] [Tier 1]
  Locus: `xz_protocol_v0_37.md:808-1142` (37-entry amendment series); Cross-Text Computational Linguistics Thesis v1.1, §2.2 and §3.2 (PDF pp. 5-6; extracted lines 135-139, 173-179).

Fourteen early entries contain no explicit all-caps finding severity and therefore map to the mandated INFO/none floor; that long constant run drives the whole-entry result. A register-only extraction materially changes both H and its shuffle result. N=37 is below the packet reference’s own N=39 exclusion example.

Naive scale-regression 95% interval [0.830672, 1.105078] is descriptive only. Credible estimator/mapping sensitivity H=[0.732336, 1.042892]; register-only H=0.732336 with p_upper=0.371814. ## Severity trajectory extraction

Estimator input rule: for each complete amendment entry, use the highest **explicit all-caps finding-severity token** in that entry under CRITICAL=5, HIGH=4, MEDIUM=3, LOW=2, INFO/INFORMATIONAL/none=1. Multiple findings reduce by maximum. Entries with no explicit severity receive 1. HALT/PASS verdicts are not silently converted into severity. Historical severity text carried inside an entry remains part of the whole-entry extraction; the register-only sensitivity removes preamble/correction-only tokens where possible.

The positive OLS severity slope is 0.115220 per version (R²=0.535); persistence therefore must not be paraphrased as a falling severity floor.

## Hurst R/S methodology and uncertainty

For each size n=4,...,18, the series is partitioned from v0.1 into non-overlapping blocks of length n; the remainder is discarded. In each block, deviations from the block mean are cumulatively summed; R is max minus min of that cumulative series; S is the sample standard deviation (ddof=1); R/S is undefined and omitted for constant blocks. Arithmetic mean R/S is taken at each n, and H is the OLS slope of log(mean R/S) on log(n). All 15 sizes remained estimable, but only 1-3 nonconstant blocks informed many sizes. The null uses 2,000 independent Fisher-Yates shuffles with Python `random.Random(370056)`; seed=370056.

| Variant | H | Null 95% | Upper-tail p | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Primary: non-overlap, ddof=1, omit constant | 0.967875 | [0.472194, 0.938117] | 0.014493 | 0.947 |
| Overlapping windows, ddof=1 | 1.042892 | [0.478664, 0.946330] | 0.001000 | 0.994 |
| Non-overlap, ddof=0 | 0.897773 | [0.402092, 0.868015] | 0.014493 | 0.936 |
| Invalid stress test: set undefined constant R/S to 0 | 1.590335 | [0.473234, 0.974143] | 0.000500 | 0.904 |
| Register-only severity mapping | 0.732336 | [0.465330, 0.935266] | 0.371814 | 0.886 |

The naive OLS interval treats correlated scale estimates as independent and is not a valid confidence interval for long-memory in N=37. The permutation interval is a null distribution, not uncertainty on the observed H. The credible sensitivity span is 0.732-1.043; the 1.590 result is retained only to show why assigning zero to undefined constant-block R/S is invalid. Honest conclusion: the ordering is regime-like, but magnitude and significance are extraction-dependent and predictive confidence is not available.

## Gate graph / fractal analysis

Formal representation: a rooted documentation-grouping tree. The root has children [1] through [12]; [2] has child [2b]; [3] has children [3a]-[3c]; [9] has children [9a]-[9f]. This yields 22 gate nodes (23 including root), 22 edges, 19 leaves, four internal nodes including root, and depth two. Child counts are {root:12, [2]:1, [3]:3, [9]:6}; mean children per internal node=5.5. Level counts are [1,12,10]. Fitting log(level count) on depth gives slope 1.151293, an effective branching factor exp(slope)=3.162278, R²=0.691.

This is a branching-growth descriptor, **not a fractal dimension**. The actual `build.py` control flow is substantially sequential, while the tree arises from label grouping. With only two non-root depths there is no scale-invariant regime and no defensible graph box-counting slope. Comparison to 1.61 +/- 0.06 is therefore non-productive; even with a valid gate FD it would be Tier 2 at best because software gate topology and a biological spatial embedding have different measures and units.

## Pulmonary dead-space classification

| Cat. | Named attack class | Test locus | Classification | Reason |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Caller-supplied derived facts | `test_xz_protocol_adversarial.py:38-52` | Direct | Injects string decision/vector/truth at the decision interfaces and asserts rejection. |

The 7/9 proxy share is an auditable test-coverage diagnostic only. A physiological “percentage of all adversarial surface that passes undetected” cannot be computed from these bytes and is explicitly NON-IDENTIFIABLE.

## Elliott Wave, cardiac cadence, and TNF homeostasis

**Elliott Wave (non-productive).** The prompt candidate segment lengths are [7,7,12,4,7], so the proposed Wave 3 is longest. But the severity variable has no Wave-2 retracement (v0.1-v0.14 is flat at 1 under whole-entry mapping), the segment endpoints are chosen narratively rather than by a frozen extrema algorithm, and proposed A-B-C phases are future deliverables rather than observations in the same variable. No reproducible prediction follows. Tier 3 claims rejected.

**Cardiac cadence (measurement only; analogy non-productive).** Date counts are 2026-07-30:1, 07-31:2, 08-01:16, 08-02:17, 08-03:1. Of 36 version transitions, 32 share a date stamp and four cross dates, producing an auditable date-stamp proxy of 8.0:1. This is not a systole:diastole latency ratio: the packet has dates, not dispatch/return times or time-to-absorption. v0.32-v0.37 are six versions across two dates, but actual finding-absorption latency is NON-IDENTIFIABLE; “tachycardia” is not established.

**TNF homeostasis (non-productive).** No cytokine analogue has an operational variable, threshold, or falsifier. The boundary-count defect is measurable without the analogy. “Cytokine storm,” “pathology,” and “honesty accumulation” are therefore rejected as Tier 3 narration. The current entry’s claim of zero carrying-seat Class A/B since v0.26 is not equivalent to the amendment entries’ explicit CRITICAL/HIGH severity trajectory and must not be substituted into it.

## COMPUTED VALUES (for methodology paper, not findings)
  Hurst exponent: 0.967875; null 95% [0.472194, 0.938117]; p_upper=0.014493; credible sensitivity H=0.732336-1.042892; N=37, seed=370056
  Gate tree complexity: 22 gates (23 nodes with root), 22 edges, 19 leaves, depth 2, mean internal branching 5.5; effective level-growth factor 3.162278 (R²=0.691); fractal dimension NON-IDENTIFIABLE
  Dead-space fraction: total adversarial surface NON-IDENTIFIABLE; conditional named-class diagnostic 7/9 proxy-tested (77.8%), 2/9 directly tested (22.2%)
  Systole:diastole ratio: actual absorption ratio NON-IDENTIFIABLE; date-stamp transition proxy 32:4 = 8.0:1
  Elliott wave position: NON-IDENTIFIABLE / candidate mapping rejected as non-falsifiable

## Selection-bias and tool-productivity check

Six priority tools were attempted. Two produced actionable findings (Hurst and pulmonary test-surface analysis): 2/6 = 33.3%. Four produced measurements or nulls but no cross-domain finding. This base rate is reported to avoid a highlight reel. No extra constants, Fibonacci fits, or alternative wave partitions were mined after the fact.

## NON-PRODUCTIVE TOOLS
  Fractal/renal FD comparison: graph has insufficient scales, representation-dependent topology, and the shipped comparator has an organ/citation mismatch.
  Elliott Wave: no frozen segmentation/extrema algorithm and no same-variable A-B-C observations; predictive reading unfalsifiable.
  Cardiac cadence: date stamps measure burst cadence, not finding-absorption latency; no physiological threshold transfers.
  TNF-alpha homeostasis: no operational analogue, denominator, threshold, or disconfirming observation; simple counts do all valid work.

## MDL conclusion

The shortest model supported by the bytes is: the amendment history contains long severity regimes and rapid date-stamped production, while the governance layer continued to produce at least one substantive correction after v0.36. That supports neither a biological optimum nor a prediction that more rounds are productive or futile. Preserve the disclosed boundaries, fix the trajectory ledger and direct adversarial tests, and keep the Hurst result exploratory.
