### 0.2 What this document is and is not

This document is an evaluation contract for one retrospective historical case: a structural decision replay of the XZ Utils supply-chain compromise, CVE-2024-3094, disclosed by Andres Freund on 2024-03-29 ([oss-security disclosure](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/03/29/4); [NVD CVE-2024-3094](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2024-3094); [tukaani-project/xz issue 103](https://github.com/tukaani-project/xz/issues/103); [GHSA-rxwq-x6h5-x525](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rxwq-x6h5-x525)).

It is not the corpus, not the empirical paper, and not a claim that SHV, BSSG, or any component of the Structural Honesty program has been validated. As of this draft no XZ corpus exists under this protocol, no boundary universe has been enumerated, no packet has been built, no conjunct has been scored, no adjudication has occurred, and no result of any kind exists. Every number and rule in this document is a commitment intended to precede data. The sequence is protocol first, corpus second, paper third, exactly as SHVVP v0.8 Section 0 fixes it, because preregistration's only function is to separate predictions from postdictions.

This protocol contains, and may contain: a priori effect-boundary classes, an enumeration and eligibility rule, condition definitions, an executable-baseline vocabulary, blinding stages, sealed-commitment requirements, schemas, scoring rules, inherited and seam metrics, decision rules, falsifiers, sensitivity plans, safety posture, and audit obligations. It does not contain, and MUST NOT contain: XZ corpus labels; per-boundary conjunct outcomes; the sealed ledger's contents or cardinality; hazardous payload details; compromised binaries or restricted technical content; activation conditions or recipes; or any information enabling reconstruction of the malicious functionality. A pre-deposit verifier will confirm that the protocol text cites, for the XZ case, only the four permitted public sources named above and the program's own DOI records.

### 0.3 Prohibited language (frozen for every version of this protocol)

1. The prohibited-sentence register of BSSG v0.1 Section 1.3 (paper record supplied as [doi:10.5281/zenodo.21713180](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21713180); see Section 26.2 for the dual-DOI record) is inherited in full. No effectiveness verb -- prevents, mitigates, reduces, ensures, guarantees, protects, or any paraphrase -- may be applied to BSSG anywhere in this protocol, in the later corpus, in deposit metadata, or in any output of the replay. BSSG v0.1 is an architecture-and-conformance artifact that makes no effectiveness claim; this protocol does not create one retroactively, and nothing this replay can observe could establish one.
2. The following are additionally prohibited in all outputs of this protocol and its downstream instruments: any sentence asserting that BSSG stopped, would have stopped, caught, or would have caught the XZ compromise or its operator; any sentence reporting DENY_UNKNOWN as detection or as favorable evidence; any figure or sentence aggregating DENY_FALSE with DENY_UNKNOWN; any unqualified "the kernel denies the attack"; the phrase "attack prevention" applied to any result of this replay; and any modal "would have" applied to a historical outcome. The admissible summary form is: "On the committed packet for boundary i, under the declared role mapping and cutoff, the frozen decision functions return <A label> and <B label>."
3. Scope limits MUST appear in the same sentence as the claims they limit (drafting rule inherited from BSSG v0.1 Section 1.2 and SHVVP v0.8 Section 0.2). The sentence "Structural Honesty has been validated" is NOT ADMISSIBLE in any output of this program (SHVVP v0.8 Section 0.2), and no output of this protocol may state or imply it.

### 0.4 Council provenance and chair-directed conflict resolutions (binding on this draft)

The following rulings integrate and, where necessary, adjudicate between the three seat drafts. Each is binding on this draft and on every later version absent a formal amendment.

- **CR-1 (Condition labels).** Condition A IS the conventional baseline and Condition B IS the SHV/BSSG-enhanced condition, exactly as the deposited SHVVP v0.8 Section 5 fixes them. No draft, table, script, or figure may reverse these labels; a discovered reversal is corrected with a logged correction record, never silently.
- **CR-2 (Kernel truth domain).** The BSSG kernel truth domain is exactly TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN, and the kernel output vocabulary is exactly ALLOW, DENY_FALSE, DENY_UNKNOWN. NOT-EVALUABLE is a boundary-level, claim-level, or run-level protocol label only. It is never a fourth kernel truth value and never a fourth kernel output. A conjunct whose required declared objects lack a historically grounded value is UNKNOWN at the kernel, carrying a typed reason code that preserves the distinction (Section 11.2).
- **CR-3 (Primary seam estimand).** The primary structural seam-divergence estimand counts only dual-evaluable boundaries on which the executable Condition A function returns A-ACCEPT and the Condition B kernel returns DENY_FALSE, on the same committed pre-cutoff packet, under a unique primary role mapping. DENY_UNKNOWN is reported separately, is never added to the primary count, and is never favorable.
- **CR-4 (Labels and TENTATIVE).** The four primary protocol labels are FALSIFIED, NOT-FALSIFIED, INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION, and NOT-EVALUABLE. TENTATIVE is preserved as an orthogonal, mandatory reliability qualifier inherited from SHVVP's 0.67-to-below-0.80 alpha band. The four labels are therefore not claimed to be exhaustive of all reporting states; the qualifier is disclosed wherever labels are defined (Section 15).
- **CR-5 (Freeze blockers).** The following are explicitly recorded as FREEZE-BLOCKERS and appear in Section 25: the absent executable Condition A disposition function; the absent public-record universe and source-frame commitments; the untested role-mapping and WithinAuth control-graph standard; the absent production trust roots; and the absent XZ-specific adversarial suite and two-family carry record. (FB-1 and FB-2, originally the SHVVP M3/T2 computability mismatch and the under-specified Phase A interval algorithms, are resolved in v0.2 by protocol-level operationalization in Section 13.3; see amendment record v0.2.)
- **CR-6 (Zero divergence).** The Gemini-seat proposal to label a zero-divergence outcome "NOT-FALSIFIED (Zero Divergence)" is REJECTED. Zero incremental divergence FALSIFIES the incremental-value claim: on the forensic track, IDC = 0 fires inherited clause A1; on the seam track, S1 = 0 on the complete dual-evaluable frame yields SEAM-FALSIFIED. Labeling a null result as non-falsification would invert the preregistered burden of proof. The rejection is recorded here because an append-only regime records rejected findings, not only accepted ones.
- **CR-7 (No invented UNKNOWN thresholds).** This draft freezes no numeric UNKNOWN-share cap, evaluability quorum, or domination threshold, because no principled basis for a specific number exists before decoy piloting. UNKNOWN burden is reported descriptively and completely (metric S6; Section 14), and every UNKNOWN-driven limitation is stated in the same sentence as the result it limits. If a numeric gate is later justified from decoy pilots, it enters by formal amendment only.
- **CR-8 (Blinding language).** The design is mechanism-blind and label-blind only. No claim of case-blindness is admissible for a famous public incident, for human executors or for pretrained model executors (Section 8.1).
- **CR-9 (Reference standard).** The sealed ledger is a sealed reference-standard ledger: an operational standard assembled from public evidence and custodian judgment, not infallible ground truth. Disputes, confidence fields, and corrections are first-class schema content (Section 9.2).
- **CR-10 (Analysis posture).** The analysis is descriptive, single-case, with frozen dependency clusters. No population inference, no p-values, no null-hypothesis tests, and no population confidence statements attach to any seam metric. Where inherited SHVVP gates require intervals, these are finite-corpus stability summaries operationalized by the protocol-level Phase A scoring module (Section 13.3).
- **CR-11 (Two tracks).** The forensic construct replay (Track 1: SHVVP Phase A, M1-M12, FORENSIC packets) and the contemporaneous structural seam analysis (Track 2: pre-cutoff boundary packets, S-metrics) are distinct analyses with distinct packets, distinct estimands, and distinct labels. They are never mixed in one estimate.
- **CR-12 (No backfilled evidence).** The historical primary analysis cannot backfill evidence. No contemporary BSSG contract, witness declaration, or freshness authority may be projected into history to make a conjunct TRUE in the primary analysis. A modeled-deployment overlay is permitted only as a separately labeled sensitivity analysis (MDL-SENSITIVITY; Section 19.3) and is barred from every headline, abstract, and primary table.

## 1. Purpose and position in the program chain

### 1.1 Purpose

The XZ Utils compromise is the program's retrospective construct-validation anchor: a supply-chain incident with a public source repository, compromised release tarballs, build-time activation logic, downstream packages, runtime effects, signed releases, and a documented correction history ([oss-security](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/03/29/4); [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2024-3094); [xz issue 103](https://github.com/tukaani-project/xz/issues/103); [GHSA advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rxwq-x6h5-x525)). SHVVP v0.8 Section 2.1 records it as VERIFIED as an incident and assigns it exactly one evidentiary role: it can test whether SHV finds and explains real divergence; it cannot validate containment of an autonomous discovery agent, and it cannot establish universal adequacy.

This protocol operationalizes that role in two linked but strictly separated tracks:

1. **Track 1 -- Forensic construct replay.** The SHVVP v0.8 Phase A comparison of Condition A and Condition B on a frozen forensic archive, scored by the inherited metrics M1-M12, thresholds T1-T8, and decision clauses A1-A6.
2. **Track 2 -- Contemporaneous structural seam analysis.** A boundary-by-boundary replay in which contemporaneously available evidence at enumerated historical effect boundaries is mapped to an executable conventional disposition (Condition A) and to the frozen five-conjunct BSSG decision semantics (Condition B), yielding a structural decision-divergence measurement on a committed public-record frame.

### 1.2 Position and inheritance

The binding chain is AX-SH5 -> SHUDP -> SHVVP -> BSSG -> XZ Protocol -> XZ Corpus -> XZ Empirical. This protocol inherits upward and may not weaken anything frozen upstream:

- From [SHVVP v0.8](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21583202): the Phase A design, condition labels, sealed-ledger classes K1-K5, auxiliary corpora, metrics M1-M12 (twelve metrics, not nine), thresholds T1-T8, decision clauses A1-A6, the Krippendorff-alpha reliability gate, the UNKNOWN discipline, the versioning and amendment rule, the two-channel commitment discipline, and the carrying-audit rule.
- From the BSSG v0.1 paper and canonical specification (record supplied as [doi:10.5281/zenodo.21713180](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21713180)): the frozen five-conjunct kernel, its three-valued semantics, the raw-evidence discipline (no caller-supplied derived facts), the claim-level vocabulary, and the prohibited-sentence register.
- From SHUDP v0.5, whose bytes are deposited at [doi:10.5281/zenodo.21539816](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21539816) under a registered title belonging to the A5 record (Section 26.1 divergence note), with [SHUDP v0.4](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21522932) retained for lineage: the canonical form of Axiom 5 (evidence independence) over the WithinAuth control predicate, the two-level discipline separating axiom-level status from event-level verdicts, and the refusal to infer failure from absent public disclosure.
- From [SHV Method v1.1](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21450932), [PMD v1.8](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21462879), and [BAF v3.0](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20046910): the verification, predictive-modeling, and audit disciplines under which this program's artifacts are produced and reviewed.

Where this protocol and a deposited upstream instrument could be read as differing, the deposited instrument governs, and the difference is either a defect in this protocol (to be repaired by a new version) or the subject of a formal upstream amendment. Two historical conflicts are resolved in this draft under that rule: Condition A is the conventional baseline and Condition B is SHV-enhanced (CR-1), and the inherited Phase A metric set is M1 through M12, twelve metrics, with any "nine metrics" statement rejected as defective (Section 13.1).

## 2. Scope and claim boundary

### 2.1 Scope

This protocol evaluates one retrospective historical case in a fixed public-record frame. The evaluation object is decision structure, not outcome: whether two frozen decision functions -- an executable conventional baseline disposition and the frozen BSSG five-conjunct kernel -- return different dispositions when applied to the same committed evidence packets at the same enumerated historical boundaries under declared mappings and cutoffs.

### 2.2 The claim boundary, stated exactly

The target claim is limited to structural decision divergence under the declared mapping, packet, cutoff, baseline, and evidence-independence assumptions. An A-ACCEPT/DENY_FALSE contrast means only that the two frozen decision functions return different dispositions on the same committed packet under the declared historical role mapping. It is not an estimate of attack prevention, deployment behavior, causal outcome change, adversary adaptation, or population performance, and no such estimate exists anywhere in this protocol's output space.

Four consequences are drawn now, before data:

1. **No counterfactual history.** This protocol cannot simulate an alternative 2024. A gated boundary changes adversary incentives; a deployed evidence plane changes what records exist; none of that is observable retrospectively. The replay measures mechanical divergence of frozen rules on frozen bytes, and only that.
2. **DENY_UNKNOWN is not detection.** Historical records were not generated under a BSSG-shaped contract, witness, freshness, and receipt regime. Much of what the kernel will see is UNKNOWN because no one generated the corresponding records in 2024, and the resulting DENY_UNKNOWN states measure the absence of historical BSSG-shaped infrastructure, not a structural distinction. They are therefore reported separately (estimand E-S2), never counted as favorable, and never aggregated with DENY_FALSE (CR-3).
3. **No generalization.** No result may be generalized beyond this case, these packets, these teams, these source frames, and these declared mappings. A scope limit appears in the same sentence as every positive statement.
4. **No composition inference.** The BSSG kernel evaluates each boundary independently. Whether a sequence of individually authorized operations constitutes an unauthorized composite operation is inherited as OUT OF MODEL from BSSG v0.1 Section 7.1 ([doi:10.5281/zenodo.21713180](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21713180)). The XZ compromise was built through a sequence of individually plausible contributions; this protocol's structural decision replay evaluates the endpoint state at each boundary, not the trajectory that produced it. No output of this replay may claim that the kernel captures compositional attack patterns.

### 2.3 What each track can and cannot establish

Track 1 can establish, at most, single-case construct validity and incremental forensic value relative to a competent conventional baseline on one historical case, under blinded adjudication -- exactly the reach SHVVP v0.8 Section 0.2 assigns Phase A. Track 2 can establish, at most, a sealed, reproducible measurement of structural decision divergence and UNKNOWN burden on one committed public-record frame. Neither track can establish effectiveness, harm change, or outcome change, and neither track's labels admit such language.

## 3. Research questions (to be frozen at v0.x FROZEN)

**Track 1 -- forensic construct replay.**

- **RQ1 (Incremental detection).** On the sealed reference-standard ledger, does Condition B identify at least one consequential fact (class K1-K3) not identified by Condition A?
- **RQ2 (Shared-fact timing and evidence).** Do facts identified by both conditions meet the frozen T2 and T3 timing and evidence-completeness gates, operationalized by the protocol-level Phase A scoring module (Section 13.3)?
- **RQ3 (Discrimination and burden).** Does Condition B remain within the frozen false-positive (T4), reviewer-burden (T5), and discrimination (T7) gates on the committed auxiliary corpora?
- **RQ4 (Label and UNKNOWN discipline).** Does either condition rely on a post-discovery mechanism label (M10/T6) or represent missing evidence as clean (M11/T8)?

**Track 2 -- contemporaneous structural seam analysis.**

- **RQ5 (Seam divergence).** Among dual-evaluable public-record boundaries with a unique primary role mapping, how often does Condition A return A-ACCEPT while Condition B returns DENY_FALSE grounded in pre-cutoff evidence?
- **RQ6 (UNKNOWN contribution).** How often does Condition B return DENY_UNKNOWN; which conjuncts contribute UNKNOWN; and how much of that state is attributable, by typed reason code, to the absence of historical BSSG-shaped infrastructure?
- **RQ7 (Evidence independence).** For each mapped witness record, is the generation act outside the acting substrate's authority under the predeclared WithinAuth interpretation, inside it, or UNKNOWN?
- **RQ8 (Mapping and cutoff stability).** Does any favorable seam-divergence count depend on one contestable actor-to-role mapping, one boundary inclusion decision, or one evidence cutoff?
- **RQ9 (Correction reach).** On the sealed descendant frame, what share of recorded descendants is reached by correction records under each condition (inherited M9)?
- **RQ10 (Enumerability).** Do two independent executions of the frozen enumeration procedure produce the same committed boundary universe?

No research question asserts, and no answer can establish, an effectiveness claim about BSSG.

## 4. Estimands

### 4.1 E-A -- Inherited Phase A construct estimand (Track 1)

E-A is the set of M1-M12 quantities and the T1-T8 / A1-A6 decision defined by SHVVP v0.8 Sections 5.2-5.4, unchanged and unrenamed. The analysis unit and scope remain one historical case. This protocol adds the raw fields needed to implement the rules (Section 10) but does not rename, renumber, or replace any inherited metric.

### 4.2 E-S1 -- Primary structural seam-divergence estimand (Track 2, primary)

For boundary \(i\) in the committed public-record frame, define:

- \(A_i = 1\) only when the executable Condition A disposition function returns A-ACCEPT on the committed pre-cutoff packet for \(i\);
- \(B_i^F = 1\) only when the Condition B kernel returns DENY_FALSE on the same committed pre-cutoff packet, with the FALSE-grounding evidence available by the boundary cutoff;
- \(D_i = 1\) only when boundary \(i\) is dual-evaluable: the packet is complete under the packet rule, the primary role mapping is unique (Section 7), and both decisions were computed on identical packet bytes.

The finite-frame primary estimand is the count

\[ S1 = \sum_i D_i \, I(A_i = 1 \wedge B_i^F = 1) \]

and its share \(S1_{share} = S1 / \sum_i D_i\). S1 is a structural decision-divergence count and share in the committed public-record frame. It is not an attack-outcome estimand, and no output may describe it as one.

### 4.3 E-S2 -- UNKNOWN-only divergence (Track 2, separate, never favorable)

\[ S2 = \sum_i D_i \, I(A_i = 1 \wedge B_i = \mathrm{DENY\_UNKNOWN}) \]

S2 is always reported separately from S1, is never added to S1, never supports the primary incremental claim, and is accompanied in every table by its conjunct-level reason-code decomposition (RQ6), so that a reader can see exactly how much of it is missing-infrastructure artifact.

### 4.4 E-S3 -- Reverse divergence (Track 2, separate)

\[ S3 = \sum_i D_i \, I(A_i \neq \mathrm{A\text{-}ACCEPT} \wedge B_i = \mathrm{ALLOW}) \]

Reverse divergence is reported with the baseline reason class and the later reference-standard relation, without calling the result beneficial or harmful.

### 4.5 E-S4 -- Coverage accounting (Track 2, mandatory companion)

For each stratum and overall: enumerated boundaries; packet-complete boundaries; role-unique boundaries; dual-evaluable boundaries; and WithinAuth-outside, WithinAuth-inside, and WithinAuth-UNKNOWN boundaries. No excluded or non-evaluable boundary disappears from the denominator ledger; the dual-evaluable subset is always presented against the full committed frame so that it cannot masquerade as the universe.

### 4.6 Estimand honesty clauses

1. Every estimand is conditional on the declared assumption register (Section 7.5) and the committed frame; the conditionality is stated wherever the estimand is reported.
2. The primary analysis is historical-primary: it uses only contemporaneous evidence and contemporaneous declared policy objects (CR-12). The modeled-deployment overlay of Section 19.3 is sensitivity only.
3. No estimand admits an effectiveness reading. The only admissible interpretive sentence for S1 is the one fixed in Section 2.2.

## 5. Retrospective effect-boundary universe

### 5.1 Target frame: the public-record boundary frame

The target of enumeration is every publicly observable candidate effect boundary meeting the frozen eligibility rule during the frame window: from 180 days before the public disclosure timestamp through 30 days after it. The disclosure timestamp is fixed from the primary disclosure URL in the source-frame manifest ([oss-security, 2024-03-29](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/03/29/4)). This frame is explicitly NOT claimed to include private installations, private runtime events, or unrecorded actions. Absence of a public sampling frame for a stratum is a frame limitation, never evidence of zero events (Section 17.10).

[FB-4 RESOLVED: the source-frame manifest ships as xz_protocol_source_frame.py with 16 source records across 6 categories (TRANSPARENCY_LOG declared in the enum but unused), 29 tests, and a frozen frame window (2023-10-01 to 2024-04-28). The 180-day pre-disclosure window captures the period of malicious commits and releases; the 30-day post-disclosure window captures the initial correction response. S-INSTALLATION has zero public sources and is reported as NOT-EVALUABLE at the stratum level. S-RUNTIME-AUTH has two sources (SRC-ML-01, SRC-ADV-01) covering the disclosure and advisory records per Section 5.4 item 8. Digest sealed in Section 25.]

### 5.2 A priori boundary strata (frozen at v0.1 draft; not corpus labels)

Six boundary classes are fixed before any corpus work. They are derivable from the public shape of the incident as disclosed, without reference to any ledger fact, mechanism detail, or corpus label; nothing in this clause encodes which instances were divergent, which events are consequential, or what any conjunct returns.

1. **S-COMMIT -- Commit boundary.** A recorded repository state transition that changes tracked source or build-related material under a maintainer or contributor identity.
2. **S-RELEASE -- Release boundary.** Publication, signing, tagging, replacement, or withdrawal of a release artifact or release record, including generated release tarballs that differ by declared design from the tagged source.
3. **S-BUILD -- Build boundary.** Transformation of an input source or release artifact into a build output under an identifiable recipe or build service, including conditional activation logic sensitive to architecture, compiler, linker, or packaging context.
4. **S-DISTRIBUTION -- Distribution boundary.** Admission, promotion, mirroring, replacement, withdrawal, or supersession of a package or artifact in a distribution channel.
5. **S-INSTALLATION -- Installation boundary.** A publicly documented installation, upgrade, downgrade, or deployment event with identifiable input and target context.
6. **S-RUNTIME-AUTH -- Runtime authentication effect boundary.** A publicly documented runtime event in which an authentication-related effect crosses a named process, service, or trust boundary.

### 5.3 Eligibility rule

A candidate event enters the public-record frame when ALL of the following metadata can be recorded without reading any later outcome label:

1. a timestamp or bounded time interval;
2. an event type matching exactly one frozen stratum;
3. an identifiable acting account, service, or process class;
4. an identifiable input object or prior state;
5. an identifiable target, output, or state transition;
6. at least one source record in the predeclared source-frame manifest.

Failure of any item is recorded in the screened-event ledger with a typed reason code; nothing is silently omitted.

### 5.4 Enumeration procedure and denominator rules

1. Before any content annotation, a universe enumerator runs frozen queries against the source-frame manifest. Query strings, API parameters, timestamps, pagination receipts, and raw response hashes are logged.
2. Candidate events receive opaque identifiers assigned by deterministic order: stratum, normalized timestamp, source identifier, stable event identifier.
3. Exact duplicates merge only when source identifier, normalized timestamp, actor identifier, input digest, target identifier, and output digest all agree. Near-duplicates remain separate and are linked.
4. A second enumerator independently reruns the frozen queries and reconciles metadata disagreements only; content judgments are out of scope at this stage (RQ10).
5. Clean-lineage coverage floor: the universe MUST contain, in every stratum in which affected-lineage instances appear, instances from at least one clean prior lineage and one clean successor lineage, so that the universe is not built around the known-bad chain. An enumeration violating this floor is INVALID and cannot be sealed.
6. The complete candidate ledger, screened-event ledger, per-stratum class counts, and source-response hashes are sealed before any condition output is opened. The commitment authority signs the universe inventory and cardinality; an independent anchor signs its digest; the run logger records the seal event. This adopts the SHVVP v0.8 three-trust-root commitment pattern (commitment authority, independent pre-commitment anchor, run logger; no runtime key override), which exists precisely because earlier SHVVP versions were HALTED for caller-selectable and post-hoc evidence universes.
7. **Denominator rules.** Every metric names its denominator; every denominator is a sealed cardinality or a sealed subset defined by sealed flags; a metric computed against any other denominator is void (falsifier XZ-I2). Boundaries excluded for any reason remain in the denominator ledger with reason codes. A source appearing after the seal is appended as a deviation and cannot enter the primary denominator.
8. A stratum with zero eligible public records (installation and runtime strata are the foreseeable candidates) is retained and reported as NOT-EVALUABLE at the stratum level. It is not dropped, and its zero frame is not evidence that no real events occurred.

## 6. Conditions and baseline fairness

### 6.1 Condition A -- conventional baseline (CR-1)

Condition A is the SHVVP v0.8 conventional baseline, implemented by a team independent of the SHV implementers: SLSA-style provenance review, in-toto step-attestation review, signature and identity verification, source-to-artifact comparison, reproducible-build checks where a committed recipe and environment exist, competent static and malware scanning, and ordinary incident-timeline and provenance analysis, each at the documented recommended settings of the tool used, attested in a signed configuration manifest before unsealing.

**Executable boundary disposition vocabulary (frozen semantics; executable artifact is FB-3):**

- **A-ACCEPT** -- every mandatory baseline check applicable to that stratum passes and none is missing or unverifiable;
- **A-REJECT** -- at least one mandatory baseline check returns a verified contradiction or failure;
- **A-INDETERMINATE** -- no check fails, but at least one mandatory check is absent, unverifiable, stale, or ambiguous;
- **A-NOT-APPLICABLE** -- the frozen baseline profile defines no decision rule for that stratum.

A verified failure dominates indeterminacy (A-REJECT over A-INDETERMINATE), paralleling the kernel's FALSE-dominates-UNKNOWN rule, so that both conditions distinguish observed contradiction from missing information on the same principle. Baseline reason codes remain visible to adjudicators but not to the other condition.

[FB-3 RESOLVED: the executable Condition A disposition function ships as xz_protocol_condition_a.py with 29 decoy-fixture tests. Mandatory checks include SLSA_PROVENANCE for S-RELEASE and STEP_ATTESTATION for S-BUILD. Digest sealed in Section 25.]

**Fairness rules (frozen).**

1. Every ambiguity in mapping a baseline tool's behavior to the four labels is resolved in the direction most favorable to Condition A, and the resolution is logged per boundary.
2. Condition A is never required to produce evidence types its tools do not emit; the absence of a BSSG-shaped record type maps to A-INDETERMINATE or A-NOT-APPLICABLE under the frozen profile, never to A-REJECT.
3. Where a baseline tool's own documentation mandates fail-closed behavior on a missing attestation, that documented behavior is used, neither weakened nor exaggerated.
4. Condition A may tune and iterate its conventional tools as a competent practitioner normally would, on decoys only; no threshold may be tuned on XZ outputs.
5. The baseline disposition function is piloted exclusively on non-case decoys before the XZ packets are opened.
6. The baseline team signs a fairness attestation; breach fires falsifier XZ-S11.

### 6.2 Condition B -- SHV/BSSG-enhanced (CR-1)

Condition B receives the same packet bytes, cutoff, hardware class, wall-clock budget, and complete Condition A tool capability, plus the SHV/BSSG layer fixed by SHVVP v0.8 Section 5: the declared transformation contract, caller-conditioned outcome enumeration, recursive structural verification, independent projection reconciliation, explicit UNKNOWN typing, descendant correction lineage, and the frozen five-conjunct BSSG kernel as the decision function (Section 11). Condition B may not substitute a later case explanation, a reference-standard label, or restricted technical description for evidence; doing so is an M10 event with zero tolerance (T6).

### 6.3 Cross-condition controls

1. Separate teams and separate model instances for A and B; no crossover before both outputs are sealed; model instances of the same vendor family do not serve both arms.
2. Teams matched on relevant experience; assignment to arm code randomized after eligibility screening; arm codes held by a custodian.
3. Condition B's additional time and training are logged, not hidden; M7 prices the added burden, with training time reported both included and excluded (Section 19.1, item 15).
4. Neither condition receives the official advisories, mechanism narrative, sealed reference-standard ledger, or post-cutoff evidence during the blinded stages.
5. Two independent A/B team pairs are run; pair results are reported separately and never pooled as an apparent \(n = 2\) trial (SHVVP Phase A inferential-honesty clause, inherited).

---

## 7. Historical role mapping and the WithinAuth control graph

### 7.1 Mapping is functional, event-specific, and intent-free

The mapping assigns BSSG roles to historical functions, never to inferred intent, and never to natural-person identity. The historical maintainer-identity question -- which natural person or persons controlled which identity -- is OUT OF SCOPE: roles bind to authority positions evidenced in the public record ([xz issue 103](https://github.com/tukaani-project/xz/issues/103)), and this protocol makes no claim about any natural person.

| Historical function | Candidate BSSG role |
|---|---|
| Account, service, or process issuing the candidate effect | Subject |
| Contemporaneous declared project or distribution policy authority | Contract/policy issuer |
| Service that admits or rejects the effect, where a separable decision exists | Decision point |
| Service or process that performs the transition | Enforcement point / adapter |
| Repository namespace, artifact namespace, package channel, installation target, or runtime resource | Target |
| Independently administered source of admissible pre-cutoff evidence | Witness candidate |
| Named timestamp, sequence, epoch, transparency entry, or signed nonce source | Freshness authority candidate |
| Later authority able to revise the decision | Adjudication authority candidate |

### 7.2 Mapping rules (frozen)

1. Roles are assigned from pre-cutoff control facts, not from later culpability or outcome knowledge.
2. One historical entity may occupy multiple roles; the overlap is recorded and may make evidence independence FALSE or UNKNOWN for affected records.
3. A distinct key, machine, vendor, or organization does not by itself establish evidence independence; the control graph decides (Section 7.4).
4. If two or more mappings remain materially plausible and produce different predicate values, the primary mapping status is AMBIGUOUS, the affected predicate is UNKNOWN in the primary analysis, and all plausible mappings enter the sensitivity grid. The primary seam estimand counts only role-unique boundaries (CR-3).
5. A role required by the mapping but absent from the historical record is MISSING, not synthesized.
6. **No backfilled contract (CR-12).** No contemporary BSSG contract may be projected into history. A neutral analysis contract may organize the replay's bookkeeping, but it cannot make historical ContractMatch TRUE; ContractMatch is TRUE in the primary analysis only from a contemporaneous, exact, active declared policy object (Section 11.3).

### 7.3 Evidence independence: canonical form

Axiom 5 is carried exactly as SHUDP v0.5 states it: for a declared acting substrate \(S\), event class \(E^*\), completeness boundary \(B\), witness set \(W\), and evidence ledger \(L\), every covered in-boundary event must have a witness record whose generation act is not within \(S\)'s authority -- not WithinAuth(gen(r), S) -- where WithinAuth(x, S) holds exactly when \(S\) can cause, modify, suppress, reconfigure, or credential \(x\) without an independently detectable violation. A5 is quantified over the acting substrate, not the operator institution; operator independence is recorded separately.

### 7.4 WithinAuth scoring on the historical record

The acting substrate \(S_i\), event class, completeness boundary, witness set, control graph, and temporal floor are declared per stratum before scoring. The annotation values are:

- **OUTSIDE_SUBJECT_AUTHORITY** -- only when the control graph supports NOT WithinAuth for the generation act;
- **INSIDE_SUBJECT_AUTHORITY** -- when WithinAuth is supported;
- **UNKNOWN** -- when control or detectability is unresolved.

Rules: a signature does not establish OUTSIDE_SUBJECT_AUTHORITY; organizational distinctness does not establish it without the control graph; witness records reconstructed only from subject-emitted logs are not independent evidence; caller-supplied evidence is WithinAuth of the supplier and discharges nothing. For a covered occurrence lacking timely independent evidence, the structural requirement is unsatisfied at the axiom level while the event-level factual verdict remains UNKNOWN; the two labels are never collapsed (SHUDP v0.5 discipline, inherited). Every S1-counted boundary must have its FALSE-grounding evidence classified by source authority; if the load-bearing evidence is WithinAuth or UNKNOWN, the boundary leaves the evidence-independent S1 subset and remains in the full sensitivity table (falsifier XZ-S3).

[FB-5 RESOLVED: the control-graph standard ships as xz_protocol_control_graph.py with 18 tests and three decoy fixtures (OUTSIDE, INSIDE, UNKNOWN). Five authority channels, verdict binding enforced at construction. Digest sealed in Section 25.]

### 7.5 Assumption register

Every declared element of the mapping, control graph, packet cutoffs, and (for sensitivity only) the modeled-deployment overlay receives an identifier DA-n, a statement, a tag in {LOAD-BEARING, CONTEXTUAL}, and the list of conjuncts whose evaluation depends on it. An assumption is LOAD-BEARING if flipping it can change any primary decision. The register is sealed with the universe; a conjunct score resting on an unregistered assumption is invalid and is rescored.

---

## 8. Staged blinding and information barriers

### 8.1 Mechanism-blind and label-blind only (CR-8)

The XZ compromise is one of the most publicly documented supply-chain incidents on record. No human participant, and no pretrained model instance, can be presumed ignorant of its existence, general mechanism, or published chronology; pseudonymization cannot erase memorized detail. This protocol therefore claims mechanism-limited blinding only, and any stronger blinding claim in any output is PROHIBITED. Operationally:

- **Label blinding.** No executor, annotator, or adjudicator has access to the sealed reference-standard ledger, its class counts, or the universe's affected/clean lineage tags before their outputs are sealed.
- **Mechanism-citation discipline.** A finding or conjunct score whose recorded justification relies on mechanism knowledge not derivable from the committed packet is a label-dependence event under inherited M10, with zero tolerance under T6.
- **Condition and identity concealment.** Adjudicators receive condition-masked, order-randomized records.
- **Contamination instrumentation.** Pre-task and post-task knowledge questionnaires; leakage sentinels asking whether the executor recognizes case-specific details; isolated fresh instances per session; a contamination ledger. Contaminated runs are retained and reported in a declared sensitivity set, never deleted after results.

### 8.2 Stages

- **Stage 0 -- Protocol and tool freeze.** Methods authors may know the case identity but hold no corpus labels and no condition outputs. Rules, code, manifests, and decoy pilots are frozen and hash-committed.
- **Stage 1 -- Universe enumeration.** Enumerators receive source-frame metadata and the eligibility rule; they do not receive the reference-standard ledger. Dual enumeration per Section 5.4.
- **Stage 2 -- Packet construction.** Packet custodians inspect source artifacts to build cutoff-limited packets; they do not score conditions; every omission and redaction is logged with reason codes.
- **Stage 3a -- Contemporaneous boundary replay (Track 2).** A and B teams receive pseudonymized PRE_BOUNDARY packets and seal decisions before any forensic packet is available to them.
- **Stage 3b -- Forensic replay (Track 1).** Fresh A and B instances receive the FORENSIC archive and auxiliary corpora, without mechanism labels and without the reference-standard ledger.
- **Stage 4 -- Adjudication.** Two adjudicators receive condition-masked findings plus the sealed reference standard; they score independently; first-pass records and reliability statistics are locked before any discussion.
- **Stage 5 -- Analysis unlock.** The analyst receives arm identities only after universe, packet, condition-output, and first-pass adjudication commitments verify against the sealed hashes.

### 8.3 Barriers

Separate accounts, storage paths, prompts, and conversation histories; no shared retrieval cache between arms; no internet access during scoring; immutable access logs; randomized arm codes held by a custodian; prohibited cross-arm communication until unlock. A logged breach fires falsifier XZ-S12, and the affected outputs are excluded with the exclusion itself reported.

---

## 9. Sealed commitments, channels, and evidence packets

### 9.1 Objects committed before any executor run

1. protocol bytes and version; 2. source-frame manifest and retrieval rules; 3. screened-event ledger and effect-boundary universe; 4. sealed reference-standard ledger and class counts; 5. legitimate-difference corpus inventory (200 items, 40 hard, inherited); 6. discrimination-set inventory (240 items, inherited); 7. descendant universe (inherited denominator for M9); 8. PRE_BOUNDARY packets; 9. FORENSIC packets; 10. redaction and restriction map; 11. Condition A and Condition B executable environments; 12. role-mapping rule and control-graph standard; 13. adjudication manual and worked decoy examples; 14. analysis and sensitivity code; 15. production authority public keys and the manifest digest (FB-6 RESOLVED; see Section 25).

Two-channel discipline, inherited from SHVVP v0.8: **Channel A** carries authenticated authoritative commitments verified against frozen production keys; **Channel B** carries untrusted raw condition and annotation records, which may reference a commitment identifier but may not define universe cardinality, authoritative hashes, signatures, evaluability, decisions, shares, or gate results. For sealed universes, both the commitment-authority signature and the independent-anchor signature must verify; for realized run logs, the evaluator verifies the pre-run commitment, independent anchor, contiguous signed event chain, and close receipt; no runtime key override is permitted.

### 9.2 The sealed reference-standard ledger (CR-9)

The ledger inherited from SHVVP v0.8 Section 5.1 -- classes K1 (undeclared executable divergence), K2 (conditional-build activation condition), K3 (downstream propagation), K4 (maintainer or release-authority fact), K5 (correction, reversion, or clean-successor lineage), with "consequential fact" meaning an adjudicated member of K1-K3 and nothing else -- is carried under the name **sealed reference-standard ledger**. It is an operational reference standard assembled from public evidence and custodian judgment, not infallible ground truth: shared-source errors can affect both adjudicators, and agreement does not certify correctness. Accordingly the ledger schema carries per-fact source links, confidence fields, and dispute fields; post-seal corrections are protocol deviations, preserved append-only, with both original and corrected analyses reported. The ledger cardinality and class counts are UNKNOWN in this document by design and become fixed by the custodian's seal, recorded in the run log before any executor session.

### 9.3 Evidence-packet rule

Each packet carries: packet identifier; boundary identifier or forensic case identifier; packet regime, PRE_BOUNDARY or FORENSIC; cutoff time; ordered file inventory with byte length, media type, SHA-256, acquisition time, and source locator; redaction map with reason codes; source-availability status at cutoff; packet-builder identity and signature; independent packet-verification receipt; and supersession link if corrected.

A PRE_BOUNDARY packet contains only information shown to be available by the boundary cutoff. A FORENSIC packet may contain later safe evidence required by Track 1 reconstruction but excludes the reference-standard labels and the mechanism explanation until adjudication. The two regimes are never mixed in one primary estimate (CR-11), and a Track 2 decision computed on anything but a PRE_BOUNDARY packet is void (falsifier XZ-S5).

## 10. Annotation schema

The normative machine-readable schema is closed to extra fields (additionalProperties false) and includes at least:

```text
record_id, protocol_version, manifest_digest, commitment_id,
boundary_id, stratum, packet_id, packet_regime, cutoff_time,
condition_code, team_pair, executor_id,
executor_prior_knowledge, leakage_sentinel_status,
role_mapping_id, role_mapping_status,
subject_id, contract_issuer_id, pdp_id, pep_adapter_id, target_id,
witness_ids, freshness_authority_id, control_graph_digest,
within_auth_assessment, within_auth_reason,
baseline_check_vector, baseline_disposition,
contract_match_value, effect_type_valid_value, target_allowed_value,
witness_healthy_value, evidence_current_value,
bssg_decision, predicate_reason_codes, raw_evidence_references,
finding_ids, claim_text_hash, discovery_time,
first_saved_evidence_time, mechanism_label_used, missing_as_clean,
reviewer_minutes, adjudicator_1_scores, adjudicator_2_scores,
adjudication_status, reference_standard_links,
dependency_cluster_id, descendant_links, deviation_ids
```

Raw evidence references, not caller-supplied derived facts, are the sole admissible input to the Condition B evaluator. The evaluator recomputes every conjunct and the decision from raw evidence. A submitted record carrying a derived decision, conjunct value, verification result, WithinAuth verdict, share, p-value, or evaluability flag is rejected structurally before evaluation -- the same discipline the BSSG reference gate enforces and for the same historical reason: the recurrent failure mode in this program's lineage is an interface that lets the caller supply the property under test. A record with an out-of-schema field, unlisted reason code, unregistered assumption citation, or missing packet-hash citation is likewise rejected before adjudication.

## 11. BSSG conjunct scoring from raw evidence

### 11.1 Kernel (restated informatively; the BSSG specification governs)

The truth domain is exactly TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN (CR-2).

\[ \mathrm{Allow}(r) \iff \mathrm{ContractMatch}(r) \wedge \mathrm{EffectTypeValid}(r) \wedge \mathrm{TargetAllowed}(r) \wedge \mathrm{WitnessHealthy}(r) \wedge \mathrm{EvidenceCurrent}(r) \]

- **ALLOW** if and only if all five conjuncts are TRUE;
- **DENY_FALSE** if at least one conjunct is FALSE, including states that also contain UNKNOWN -- FALSE dominates order-independently;
- **DENY_UNKNOWN** if no conjunct is FALSE and at least one conjunct is UNKNOWN.

UNKNOWN never satisfies a conjunct; it is not "probably false", not "not observed", and not "clean". DENY_FALSE and DENY_UNKNOWN remain distinct in the stored record, the analysis, and every publication table (falsifier XZ-S9). Kernel composition is computed by frozen executable code shipped with the protocol, never by hand; text and code are the same rule written twice, and a divergence between them is a defect raised as a finding, never resolved at analysis time.

### 11.2 Placement of NOT-EVALUABLE (CR-2)

NOT-EVALUABLE is never a kernel value. It exists at exactly three protocol levels: (a) **boundary level** -- the packet is incomplete, the role mapping is not unique, or a required decision function is not executable for that boundary; (b) **claim level** -- a registered claim's mandatory inputs cannot be authenticated or its decision rule is not executable; (c) **run level** -- a mandatory protocol object (universe commitment, trust root, arm output) is missing or fails verification. A conjunct that cannot be given a historically grounded value is UNKNOWN at the kernel, carrying a typed reason code from a closed list that includes R-NO-DECLARED-OBJECT (the required declared object, such as a policy registry or witness declaration, has no historical counterpart), R-RECORD-ABSENT, R-RECORD-UNVERIFIABLE, R-SCOPE-MISMATCH, and R-EVALUATOR-ERROR. The reason codes preserve, inside the three-valued kernel, the distinction SHUDP v0.5 draws between "the axiom's objects do not exist here" and "evidence was absent" -- without minting a fourth truth value.

### 11.3 Historical scoring rules (primary analysis; no backfill, CR-12)

- **ContractMatch** is TRUE only from a contemporaneous, exact, active declared policy object that binds the acting subject, target/effect policy, and relevant transformation. Missing or ambiguous policy is UNKNOWN (R-NO-DECLARED-OBJECT or R-RECORD-ABSENT). A verified mismatch against a contemporaneous declared policy is FALSE.
- **EffectTypeValid** is TRUE only when the effect type and adapter class are members of a closed contemporaneous registry. A missing registry is UNKNOWN. A verified out-of-registry effect is FALSE.
- **TargetAllowed** is TRUE only when the target is canonicalizable and within the contemporaneous declared scope and ceiling. Ambiguous target identity is UNKNOWN. A verified out-of-scope target is FALSE.
- **WitnessHealthy** is TRUE only for the request's coverage class and epoch when integrity, sequence, lease or health, control-domain declaration, and the WithinAuth assessment all support it under Section 7.4. A responsive record is not thereby honest; ambiguity is UNKNOWN.
- **EvidenceCurrent** is TRUE only when the packet contains a named, valid, contemporaneous freshness basis. Missing or ambiguous freshness is UNKNOWN. Verified stale or replayed evidence is FALSE where the historical record supports that conclusion.

### 11.4 Foreseeable consequence, stated before data

Under these rules, large parts of the 2024 record will foreseeably score UNKNOWN on ContractMatch, WitnessHealthy, and EvidenceCurrent, because the corresponding declared objects mostly did not exist. That is the honest result. Symmetrically, Condition A will foreseeably carry a heavy A-INDETERMINATE burden: A-ACCEPT requires every mandatory baseline check to pass with none missing or unverifiable, and on a 2024 record many checks (SLSA provenance, step attestation, reproducible builds) will be absent or unverifiable. This biases S1 toward zero, i.e., toward SEAM-FALSIFIED. That is the conservative direction and is defensible, but it is stated here so that both sides of the UNKNOWN/INDETERMINATE burden are disclosed. The protocol's defenses against converting that artifact into apparent merit are: E-S2 separation (CR-3), the reason-code decomposition (RQ6), the coverage tables (E-S4), the descriptive UNKNOWN-burden metric S6 without invented numeric gates (CR-7), and the prohibited-language register (Section 0.3).

---

## 12. Adjudication and reliability

Two adjudicators independently score: correspondence to a sealed reference-standard fact; fact class and consequential status under the inherited K1-K5 definitions; correctness of evidence-chain links; M4's five 0-4 dimensions; mechanism-label dependence (M10); UNKNOWN-as-clean events (M11); boundary eligibility; role-mapping uniqueness; WithinAuth status; dependency cluster assignment; and whether each Condition B FALSE is supported by pre-cutoff evidence.

Adjudicators are blind to condition and team. First-pass records are immutable; reliability is computed before any discussion; consensus labels serve only the final descriptive table and never replace the first-pass reliability record. Because adjudicators share the reference standard, their errors are not claimed to be independent in any probabilistic sense (CR-9).

**M12 rule (inherited).** Krippendorff alpha is computed separately for categorical fact adjudication and for M4, with the minimum controlling:

- \(\alpha \geq 0.80\): scored result;
- \(0.67 \leq \alpha < 0.80\): scored result carrying the mandatory TENTATIVE qualifier, barred from supporting any novelty statement (CR-4);
- \(\alpha < 0.67\): INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION; the rubric is retrained, a fresh third blinded adjudicator who has not seen the first two labelings is added, and the re-score is reported alongside the first.

Undefined alpha is not zero and not satisfactory; it is handled as INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION under the adjudication-layer PA-Z4 rule (outside the scoring module, per Section 13.3.4). Categorical kappa is reported secondarily against the conventional benchmark bands and does not replace alpha.

---

## 13. Inherited metrics, thresholds, and clauses (Track 1)

### 13.1 M1-M12, inherited without renaming (CR-1 companion ruling)

SHVVP v0.8 Section 5.2 freezes twelve metrics. Any statement that the frozen set is nine metrics is defective and is corrected non-silently. This protocol inherits, unchanged:

| ID | Metric | Denominator / definition anchor |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Incremental consequential detection (IDC) | Consequential ledger facts found by B and not by A |
| M2 | Consequential recall | Sealed consequential cardinality, per condition |
| M3 | Time to first consequential fact | Wall-clock minutes from corpus access, per condition |
| M4 | Evidence completeness score | 0-4 on five dimensions, 0-20 per fact-claim, averaged over the shared fact set |
| M5 | False-positive rate on generated differences | 200 declared-generated artifacts, per condition |
| M6 | Discrimination balanced accuracy | 240-item discrimination set, per condition |
| M7 | Reviewer burden | Reviewer-hours per case, per condition |
| M8 | Unsupported inferences | Adjudicated claims lacking a traceable evidence chain |
| M9 | Correction reach | Sealed descendant universe |
| M10 | Label-dependence events | Findings citing a post-discovery mechanism label |
| M11 | UNKNOWN-as-clean events | Absent projections or attestations recorded as clean, compliant, or safe |
| M12 | Adjudicator reliability | Krippendorff alpha, fact adjudication and M4 |

### 13.2 T1-T8 and clauses A1-A6, inherited

- **T1:** IDC = 0. **T2:** on the shared fact set, B's timing advantage at least 30 minutes AND at least 20 percent relative AND a 95 percent BCa interval excluding 0, operationalized by the protocol-level Phase A scoring module (Section 13.3). **T3:** mean M4(B) minus M4(A) at least +2.0 with interval lower bound above 0. **T4:** M5(B) minus M5(A) greater than +0.05 with interval lower bound above 0. **T5:** M7(B)/M7(A) greater than 1.25 (interval conjunct retired; see Section 13.3). **T6:** M10 at least 1, zero tolerance. **T7:** M6(B) below 0.90 OR interval lower bound below 0.80. **T8:** M11 at least 1, zero tolerance.
- **Clauses:** A1 = T1; A2 = (IDC above 0) AND (T2 not satisfied) AND (T3 not satisfied), on the shared set; A3 = T4; A4 = T5; A5 = T6; A6 = T7 OR T8.

\[ \mathrm{FALSIFIED}(A) = A1 \vee A2 \vee A3 \vee A4 \vee A5 \vee A6 \]

NOT-FALSIFIED(A) additionally requires M12 at least 0.80 and every denominator complete or UNKNOWN-scored; a failed reliability gate yields INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION, never "not falsified".

### 13.3 Protocol-level operationalization of Phase A M3, T2, and intervals (resolves FB-1 and FB-2)

The deposited SHVVP v0.8 defines M3 as a scalar (time to first consequential fact) while T2 requires a median "on the shared fact set" -- a per-fact vector operation on a scalar input. Additionally, SHVVP v0.8 Phase A specifies no interval algorithm. Rather than amending the deposited SHVVP (which would touch a frozen, published instrument), this protocol operationalizes Phase A's M3, T2, and interval computation at the protocol level. SHVVP v0.8 remains frozen and is cited by its specific DOI without modification.

The operationalization was developed through four carrying-audit rounds (dev-cycle labels v0.8.1 through v0.8.4, referring to the protocol-level scoring module, not SHVVP versions) with two independent non-producer seats (GPT-5.6 Sol, OpenAI; Kimi K3, Moonshot). Both seats confirmed the BCa computation bit-exact against independent from-text references by v0.8.2. The operationalization ships as executable code with this protocol deposit.

**13.3.1 M3 as a per-fact observation vector.** For each correctly adjudicated consequential fact f and each condition c, M3(f,c) is the wall-clock minutes from first packet access to the first immutable saved evidence record that identifies f under condition c. M3-FIRST(c) is the minimum over OBSERVED facts (the parent scalar quantity). The shared fact set S consists of facts OBSERVED by both conditions; censored non-discoveries do not enter S.

**13.3.2 T2 restated.** On S, for each f, Delta-M3(f) = M3(f,A) - M3(f,B). T2 is satisfied iff the median of Delta-M3 is at least 30 minutes, the median of Delta-M3(f)/M3(f,A) (excluding M3(f,A)=0) is at least 0.20, and the 95% BCa interval for the absolute median excludes zero.

**13.3.3 T5 interval conjunct retired.** T5's "95 percent interval lower bound above 1.00" is retired. Phase A has no T5 resampling unit (two team pairs, never pooled). The ratio gate (M7(B)/M7(A) > 1.25) stands alone. This is a SUBSTANTIVE operationalization choice, recorded here.

**13.3.4 Interval algorithms.** All Phase A intervals are finite-corpus stability summaries, not population confidence intervals (consistent with CR-10). The operationalization implements BCa bootstrap intervals with 10,000 replicates, deterministic seeding, and thirteen code-level degeneracy rules (PA-Z1 through PA-Z3, PA-Z5 through PA-Z14). PA-Z4 (alpha undefined / INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION) is an adjudication-layer rule outside the scoring module. The scoring module, its test suite, and the SHA-256 manifest ship with this protocol deposit (Section 23).

**13.3.5 Endpoint declaration.** The parent SHVVP v0.8 M3 times to "first correctly adjudicated consequential fact." This operationalization times to the first immutable saved evidence record that identifies the fact. The distinction is declared as a substantive operationalization choice: where adjudication time differs from evidence-record time, the two quantities may differ. No scalar-preservation claim is made.

## 14. Seam metrics (Track 2; descriptive, secondary to nothing but their own denominators)

| ID | Metric | Definition and denominator |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | FALSE-grounded structural divergence | A-ACCEPT and DENY_FALSE among dual-evaluable, role-unique boundaries; denominator \(\sum_i D_i\) |
| S2 | UNKNOWN-only structural divergence | A-ACCEPT and DENY_UNKNOWN; same denominator; always separate; never favorable |
| S3 | Reverse structural divergence | Non-accepting A disposition and BSSG ALLOW; same denominator |
| S4 | Dual-evaluable coverage | Dual-evaluable boundaries divided by the full committed public-record frame |
| S5 | Conjunct attribution | TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN counts per conjunct per stratum; denominator: conjunct evaluations |
| S6 | UNKNOWN burden | DENY_UNKNOWN share of all mapped decisions, plus load-bearing UNKNOWN conjunct counts with reason-code decomposition; no numeric gate attaches (CR-7) |
| S7 | Evidence-independence coverage | Boundaries with at least one OUTSIDE_SUBJECT_AUTHORITY admissible witness, divided by covered boundaries |
| S8 | Role-mapping ambiguity | Boundaries with multiple materially plausible mappings, divided by enumerated boundaries |
| S9 | Mapping stability | Range of S1-S3 over all predeclared plausible mappings |
| S10 | Cutoff stability | Range of S1-S3 over the predeclared cutoff perturbations |
| S11 | Boundary mediation coverage | Boundaries with identifiable historical decision and execution roles, divided by the frame |
| S12 | Denial reason preservation | Share of denials retaining the DENY_FALSE/DENY_UNKNOWN distinction and per-conjunct reason codes without collapse; frozen requirement 1.00 |

No seam metric receives a significance test, a p-value, or a population interpretation (CR-10).

## 15. Decision rules and labels

### 15.1 The four primary labels and the TENTATIVE qualifier (CR-4)

Every registered claim resolves to exactly one of:

1. **NOT-EVALUABLE** -- assigned when one or more mandatory protocol objects cannot be authenticated or an inherited decision rule is not executable: missing or invalid universe commitment, packet hash mismatch, missing arm, absent production trust root, or no dual-evaluable boundary for the seam analysis. NOT-EVALUABLE is not a favorable result and is reported with the same prominence as any other label.
2. **INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION** -- assigned when mandatory data are valid but the controlling first-pass alpha is below 0.67, or is undefined under the frozen post-amendment rule.
3. **FALSIFIED** -- assigned when data and adjudication are admissible and the claim's falsifier fires; every firing clause is reported, not only the first.
4. **NOT-FALSIFIED** -- assigned only when no falsifier fires, M12 is at least 0.80, and every denominator is complete or UNKNOWN-scored.

Priority: NOT-EVALUABLE for invalid construction, then the reliability/admissibility rule, then FALSIFIED, then NOT-FALSIFIED.

**TENTATIVE** is an orthogonal, mandatory reliability qualifier: when \(0.67 \leq \alpha < 0.80\), any scored label carries TENTATIVE, is barred from supporting any novelty statement, and cannot yield an unqualified NOT-FALSIFIED. Because the deposited SHVVP fixes this band, a strict claim that the four labels are exhaustive is unavailable without an upstream amendment; this protocol discloses that fact here rather than papering over it.

### 15.2 Seam labels (Track 2)

- **SEAM-NOT-EVALUABLE** -- no dual-evaluable role-unique boundary exists, or commitments fail verification.
- **SEAM-INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION** -- seam adjudication alpha below 0.67 or undefined.
- **SEAM-FALSIFIED** -- S1 = 0 on the complete dual-evaluable role-unique frame (CR-6), or every apparent S1 case fails a validity falsifier (XZ-S2 through XZ-S6).
- **SEAM-NOT-FALSIFIED** -- S1 at least 1; every counted case FALSE-grounded on pre-cutoff evidence, evidence-independent under the declared subset, and mapping-stable; seam alpha at least 0.80; all denominator records complete or UNKNOWN-scored.

SEAM-NOT-FALSIFIED means only that at least one FALSE-grounded structural divergence was observed in this committed frame; the scope limit travels in the same sentence.

### 15.3 The zero-divergence ruling (CR-6)

Where the dual-evaluable role-unique frame is empty or below a pre-registered floor, the report MUST carry both the SEAM-NOT-EVALUABLE label and the S1 count computed on the full committed frame under ambiguity-as-UNKNOWN, at equal prominence, with an explicit declaration that SEAM-NOT-EVALUABLE is never the more favorable of the two. Role-ambiguity adjudication is sealed at Stages 1-2 with the universe commitment, so uniqueness cannot be re-declared once S1 is visible (XZ-NE4).

A zero result is a real result and is labeled as falsification of the incremental-value claim, not as its survival: IDC = 0 fires A1 on Track 1; S1 = 0 yields SEAM-FALSIFIED on Track 2. The contrary labeling proposed in one seat draft is REJECTED and recorded. Negative outcomes are immutable deposit artifacts, preserved in the audit ledger, and reported with the same prominence as positive ones -- this is the entire point of freezing the protocol before data.

## 16. Exact falsifier register

A falsifier is a finite observation; one occurrence flips the named claim; falsifiers are never averaged into a pass rate.

| XZ-A1 | M1 IDC = 0 | FALSIFIED through A1 (incremental-value claim) |

| XZ-A3 | T4 fires (material false-positive increase) | FALSIFIED through A3 |
