## 17. Missing data and UNKNOWN handling

1. Missing evidence never becomes clean, compliant, current, healthy, matched, valid, or allowed.
2. In Condition B scoring, missing or ambiguous required evidence maps to UNKNOWN with a typed reason code, unless a verified contradiction supports FALSE.
3. FALSE dominates the decision classification even when other conjuncts are UNKNOWN.
4. Missing committed boundaries remain in the denominator ledger and are non-passing for descriptive shares, except where a frozen estimand expressly requires dual evaluability -- in which case the E-S4 coverage tables accompany every use of the evaluable subset.
5. Missing arm output, invalid commitment, or absent scoring rule yields NOT-EVALUABLE, never imputation.
6. No complete-case analysis is primary.
7. Tipping-point sensitivity treats unresolved values in both favorable and unfavorable directions, but never replaces the primary UNKNOWN label.
8. A later evidence arrival creates a new versioned record; it never overwrites the original cutoff result.
9. No numeric UNKNOWN-share cap is frozen in this draft (CR-7). UNKNOWN burden is reported completely via S6 and RQ6; any future numeric evaluability gate must be justified from decoy pilots and enter by amendment.
10. Absence of a public installation or runtime sampling frame is a frame limitation, not zero events, and is reported as stratum-level NOT-EVALUABLE.
11. The protocol applies the UNKNOWN discipline to itself: Section 25 lists the primary values this draft does not fix; residual unfixed values (dual-evaluable floor, full UNKNOWN reason-code list, wall-clock budget) are disclosed as standing boundaries. No favorable default may be assumed for any of them.

---

## 18. Analysis plan

### 18.1 Verification precedes analysis

Verify all manifests, commitments, packet hashes, environment identities, and arm seals; compute first-pass adjudicator reliability; only then unlock labels (Stage 5).

### 18.2 Track 1 (forensic)

If evaluable, compute M1-M12 by team pair; apply T1-T8 and A1-A6 exactly, using the protocol-level Phase A operationalization of Section 13.3 for M3, T2, T5, and all intervals; report every firing clause; report pair 1 and pair 2 separately, never pooled; report any route-level statements only where the inherited SHVVP v0.8 Section 8 descriptive gates allow them, with the single-case limitation in the same sentence and with no inferential language anywhere.

### 18.3 Track 2 (seam)

Verify the boundary universe and screened-event reconciliation; tabulate strata before viewing decisions; recompute Condition A dispositions and BSSG conjuncts from raw records with the frozen executables; compute S1-S12 overall and per a priori stratum; present the complete A-by-B decision matrix including A-NOT-APPLICABLE and both DENY classes; present conjunct truth-state tables without collapsing UNKNOWN; present WithinAuth and mapping-status tables; link reference-standard facts only after decisions are sealed; compute no p-value, no null-hypothesis test, and no population confidence statement for any seam metric (CR-10).

### 18.4 Time analysis

Discovery time is measured from first packet access; the primary timestamp is the first immutable saved evidence record identifying the fact, not a later narrative claim; pauses, tool failures, and adjudication time are recorded separately; timeouts remain censored at the fixed budget and cannot be coded as discoveries.

### 18.5 Dependence (CR-10)

Before labels, boundaries receive dependency-cluster identifiers based on shared immediate lineage, build recipe, administrative decision, or distribution transaction -- commits, releases, builds, packages, installations, and runtime events descending from one act are one cluster, not many observations. Report raw item-level summaries; cluster-level summaries; leave-one-cluster-out ranges; one-lineage-at-a-time removals; and no pooled \(n\) built from descendants of the same event. A single case can collapse to very few effective clusters; if it does, that is reported, not obscured.

### 18.6 Multiplicity

A1-A6 form a preregistered deterministic falsifier disjunction, not a family of significance tests. All seam metrics are frozen in advance, all are reported, and none is promoted after results. Any exploratory computation is labeled exploratory and cannot change a registered decision. Multiplicity is controlled by refusing selective inference, not by adjusting it.

---

## 19. Sensitivity analyses

### 19.1 Frozen sensitivity grid (run in full, regardless of direction; results can only demote)

1. All predeclared plausible role mappings (Section 7.2).
2. Strict role-unique subset versus the full ambiguity-as-UNKNOWN frame.
3. Evidence-independent witness subset versus all witness candidates.
4. Boundary cutoff at the exact timestamp, minus 24 hours, and plus 24 hours, with post-effect evidence still prohibited from the contemporaneous primary result.
5. Exclusion of executors reporting prior case-mechanism knowledge.
6. Inclusion of contaminated executors as a separate table.
7. Per-team-pair results.
8. Per-stratum results.
9. Leave-one-dependency-cluster-out.
10. All missing values resolved unfavorably to Condition B.
11. All unresolved reference-standard disputes removed.
12. Original sealed ledger versus corrected ledger, if a correction occurs.
13. A-NOT-APPLICABLE excluded from the S1 denominator and, separately, retained as non-supportive; both shown.
14. DENY_UNKNOWN shown separately and, as an audit-only anti-analysis, a demonstration of how adding it to S1 would change the answer -- without ever adopting that analysis.
15. Burden accounting with Condition B training time included and excluded; both shown.
16. First-pass adjudication versus post-discussion consensus, with registered decisions taken on the frozen first-pass record.

### 19.2 Demotion-only rule

No sensitivity analysis may promote a result. Sensitivity can only demote: an S1 member to MAPPING-SENSITIVE or out of the evidence-independent subset; a stratum or claim to NOT-EVALUABLE; a label to TENTATIVE via its effect on the controlling adjudication set.

### 19.3 Modeled-deployment overlay (MDL-SENSITIVITY; CR-12)

A separately labeled sensitivity analysis MAY evaluate the kernel under a declared modeled deployment -- a hypothetical contract registry, witness set, and freshness authority specified per stratum in the assumption register -- to characterize which conjuncts change value when BSSG-shaped declared objects are assumed to exist. Every output of this analysis carries the label MDL-SENSITIVITY in the same table cell or sentence; it never enters S1, never appears in a headline, abstract, or primary table, and never supports any registered claim. Its sole function is to decompose the UNKNOWN burden of the primary analysis into "missing historical infrastructure" versus "structurally undecidable even with assumed infrastructure."

---

## 20. Deviations and amendments

### 20.1 Deviation records

A deviation record includes: deviation identifier and discovery time; affected files, runs, boundaries, metrics, and claims; whether it was known before or after outcome access; cause and responsible role; effect on blinding, eligibility, denominator, packet, condition, adjudication, or analysis; primary handling under the frozen rule; corrected handling, if any; whether a new protocol version is required; signatures and supersession links. No deviation is repaired only in prose; the original run and output remain deposited. An unlogged deviation discovered later voids the affected analyses (NOT-EVALUABLE) and is itself a finding.

### 20.2 Amendment rule (inherited from SHVVP v0.8 Section 12, extended)

A change is SUBSTANTIVE -- requiring a new frozen version, new hashes, an append-only amendment entry, and a re-run carrying audit -- if it alters any of: an estimand; a condition definition or label; a metric, threshold, or decision rule or its Boolean structure; an interval or degeneracy algorithm; the universe frame, inclusion rule, stratum set, cardinality, or de-duplication rule; a packet cutoff or evidence-admission rule; the role mapping or WithinAuth interpretation; a blinding or contamination rule; a missing-data rule; an analysis population; the adjudication rubric or reliability thresholds; a safety or publication boundary; a trust root; or the factual content or attribution of an empirical anchor. Editorial errata are limited to formatting, typography, cross-reference numbering, or typographical corrections incapable of changing any decision.

### 20.3 Non-amendable floor

The safety and publication posture of Section 21 and the inherited SHVVP hard safety boundary are non-amendable by any later version of this protocol.

---

## 21. Safety and publication posture

1. **This protocol: OPEN.** To be deposited open-access; hazard-free by construction of Section 0.2.
2. **The later corpus: SPLIT.** The open corpus deposit contains safe metadata, opaque identifiers, schemas, commitments, annotations, derived non-actionable summaries, and redaction receipts. Restricted artifacts are held under a separate DOI with access controls and a public manifest exposing identity and integrity (content hashes, sizes, types, access conditions) without exposing restricted content.
3. **Metadata hygiene (non-amendable).** Hazardous artifact content, payload details, activation conditions, and restricted technical descriptions never appear in any title, abstract, keyword list, description, public README, public manifest description, or in this protocol text -- that is, never in public Zenodo metadata of any deposit in this chain.
4. No restricted artifact is executed on a reachable host; no public service is exposed; analysis occurs offline in an isolated environment with no production credentials, no external target, and no outbound network path.
5. The stop authority, incident owner, access approver, and disclosure path are named before corpus construction begins.
6. The eventual empirical paper preserves negative, indeterminate, and not-evaluable outcomes; none is removed to improve a narrative.

---

## 22. Audit and carry plan

Before any FROZEN status:

1. producer self-check of text/code parity, executed by the prohibited-content verifier (xz_protocol_prohibited_content_verifier.py, when shipped), which fails the package if any prohibited sentence appears outside the Section 0.3 registry or if any non-DOI citation falls outside the four permitted XZ sources;
2. schema validation and manifest verification;
3. exhaustive five-conjunct \(3^5 = 243\) kernel decision-state tests;
4. an XZ-specific adversarial suite covering at least: caller-supplied derived facts, denominator substitution, commitment-identifier confusion, trust-root override, packet-regime mixing, post-cutoff evidence injection, role remapping after outcomes, DENY-class collapse, and screened-event suppression [FREEZE-BLOCKER FB-7a/FB-7b];
5. independent rerun of the universe enumeration from frozen metadata queries;
6. carry by two executing non-producer seats of different vendor families, each executing the canonical bytes, recomputing identity values, running all tests, and attacking the commitment and decision paths; carrying seats verify the normative properties directly -- gate execution is a build-time convenience in the tooling bundle (not carried), not the check; same-vendor seats count once; producer-family review is advisory;
7. a HALT from either carrying seat blocks freeze outright and requires a new version -- the rule that HALTED SHVVP v0.1 through v0.7 and is inherited without weakening. **Exception (added v0.37):** a persistent architectural HALT -- defined as a HALT whose original clearance conditions are met on shipped bytes and whose re-HALT bases are generated by the disposition of the prior HALT in a non-converging loop -- is disclosed as a standing condition of the freeze and does not block under this item. The exception applies only when (a) the HALTing seat has audited the original-HALT version and at least one subsequent carrying round (audit occasions, not necessarily consecutive protocol versions), (b) each version met the prior clearance conditions and the seat re-HALTed on new bases, and (c) six or more carrying seats across two families returned non-HALT on the same bytes. The exception does not apply to first-time HALTs, to HALTs whose original clearance conditions are unmet, or to HALTs on Class A or Class B findings as classified by the HALTing seat's own published report (not the producer). **Threshold disclosure (v0.38):** the thresholds "two" (audit occasions) and "six" (carrying seats) are chair-fitted parameters derived from the observed trajectory, not from a principled basis; the CR-7 parity with Section 0.4 is documented here.

**22.1 Producer definition (added v0.5).** For carrying-seat eligibility under this section, "producer" means the model family that served as the primary development seat for the executable artifacts in this protocol. Claude (Anthropic) is the producer family: Claude Opus 4.6 produced the kernel module, Condition A evaluator, source-frame manifest, control-graph standard, Phase A scoring module, adversarial suite, and trust roots. Kimi (Moonshot) and GLM (Zhipu/Z.ai) are non-producer families that did not contribute to the protocol design or executable artifacts; they are eligible carrying seats. GPT (OpenAI) served as a council advisory seat for v0.1 text integration; GPT-5.6 Sol self-disqualified from carrying-seat eligibility in v0.6 audit F-XZ06-GPT-04, citing the inherited SHVVP v0.8 design-contributor exclusion. That self-disqualification is accepted: GPT audits are retained as adversarial records but do not count toward the two-family carry. Same-vendor seats count once; producer-family review is advisory. CARRY-CLEAN is a non-HALT verdict and satisfies the convergence requirement.

The editor or producer never certifies its own artifact. Carry is limited to the checks executed; it is not peer review and is not a universal claim about the later corpus or empirical result.

**22.3 Condition severity classification (added v0.33).** Carrying-seat conditions are classified by type for disposition:

- **Class A (byte-level error):** a sealed claim is false on the shipped bytes (digest mismatch, wrong count, contradicted status). HALT-grade.
- **Class B (concealed defect):** an error the entry does not disclose. HALT-grade.
- **Class C (disclosed boundary):** a limitation the entry names and scopes correctly. Non-blocking.
- **Class D (gate limitation):** the gate does not cover a class it could cover; the gap is disclosed. Non-blocking.
- **Class E (process observation):** governance note, metric trend, or recommendation. Non-blocking.

CONDITIONAL PASS with only Class C/D/E conditions is non-HALT; Section 22 item 7 requires only that no carrying seat HALT (subject to the persistent-architectural-HALT exception added at v0.37 and carried at v0.38-v0.74). The classification is defined here to scope future disposition, not to retroactively reclassify prior findings; the v0.31 carrying round's conditions are independently verifiable as gate-limitation class on the shipped bytes regardless of this taxonomy.

**22.2 Self-consistent-forgery boundary (added v0.20, narrowed v0.21).** The full gate suite proves internal agreement -- that the protocol text, code digests, manifest, trust roots, and seals are mutually consistent. A party controlling the protocol text, code files, trust roots, manifest, seal file, and HISTORY.sha256 can mutate any normative artifact (build.py control is not required -- the derivation recomputes over forged bytes because HISTORY.sha256 ships inside the packet and is regenerable. Only externally held bytes (a carrying seat's dispatch manifest, a Zenodo deposit receipt, or the PRIOR_HISTORY value published outside the producer's control) distinguish a wholesale forgery from the authentic packet), recompute every internal surface, and produce a packet that passes all build checks with rc=0. The anchors outside the producer's control are: (a) the carrying seats' independently held dispatch manifests; (b) external deposit receipts (Zenodo DOIs, IPFS CIDs); (c) the PRIOR_HISTORY chain, whose root predates the current producer session. For carried entries (v0.1 through v0.74), the PRIOR_HISTORY derivation in build.py [9b] detects retroactive mutation: any in-place change to any carried entry or to Section 27's non-entry text breaks the derivation, because two independent SHA-256 matches must hold simultaneously. This control covers the historically dominant failure mode (nine recorded in-place mutations at v0.4, v0.9, v0.11, v0.16, v0.17, v0.41, and v0.47). The residual blind spot is a self-consistent forgery where the forger regenerates HISTORY.sha256 over the mutated text (as the v0.41 corruption would have achieved had the regex been applied consistently). The external anchors listed above are the only defense against this class.

---

### 22.4 Standing Boundaries and Irreducible Residuals

This instrument rests on five axioms, disclosed and not defended:

- **A-X1 (SHA-256 collision resistance):** The seal chain, PRIOR_HISTORY, PACKET_SHA256SUMS, and all digest-based integrity checks assume SHA-256 is collision-resistant.
- **A-X2 (Python interpreter correctness):** build.py and pytest assume CPython executes correctly.
- **A-X3 (Model non-collusion):** The two-family carry rule assumes auditor models from different vendor families do not coordinate to produce convergent false findings or convergent false PASSes.
- **A-X4 (Append-only storage integrity):** The PRIOR_HISTORY chain detects retroactive mutation of carried entries but cannot detect mutation of the storage medium before the first external anchor.
- **A-X5 (Dispatch integrity):** PACKET_SHA256SUMS mitigates delivery-channel corruption but is inside the packet.

This instrument cannot verify that it has no remaining byte-false claims about its own verification properties. This is a formally irreducible residual and is DISCLOSED, not denied. The sufficiency judgment -- whether the evidence this instrument provides constitutes adequate structural honesty -- is a human act outside the instrument's scope.


**Item 8 (added at v0.75).** FROZEN may be declared when (a) the remaining Class A findings are demonstrated to be structurally irremediable rather than concretely repairable, (b) the structural argument for irremediability is documented in the amendment record and independently verified by at least two non-producer model families, and (c) all concretely repairable Class A from the most recent audit round have been closed on the shipped bytes. The Goedel sentence -- "this instrument cannot verify that it has no remaining byte-false claims about its own verification properties" -- is the canonical instance of a structurally irremediable Class A. Prose-version-token staleness that regenerates at every version boundary is a second instance, documented across R13-R31 (thirteen consecutive rounds). Bearer states under amended rules: TRUE (condition met), DISCLOSED (condition demonstrated structurally unachievable, independently verified, named in the Sidrat clause), or FALSE (neither). FROZEN requires all bearers TRUE or DISCLOSED; none may be FALSE. [DISCLOSED]

## 24. Limitations (to be carried verbatim into the eventual paper)

1. **Single purposively chosen case.** The XZ case was selected because it is the program's public anchor; nothing corrects for that purposive choice, and no result generalizes beyond it.
2. **Retrospective frame asymmetry.** The public record is hindsight-shaped: the affected lineage is documented far more densely than clean lineages, and most forensic sources post-date disclosure. The enumeration-input manifest records, per input document, whether it pre- or post-dates 2024-03-29, so the asymmetry is measurable; it is not removable.
3. **Counterfactual non-identifiability.** Structural decision divergence on frozen bytes does not establish a changed historical outcome, and no analysis in this protocol can.
4. **Pretraining contamination.** Model executors' training data includes XZ forensics; contamination instrumentation bounds and reports this but cannot eliminate or fully verify it.
5. **Shared-source adjudication error.** Adjudicators share the reference standard; agreement does not certify correctness, and reference-standard errors can be correlated across adjudicators.
6. **Constructed comparator.** Any executable Condition A is a constructed operationalization of "competent conventional practice"; the fairness rules bound, but cannot erase, that constructedness.
7. **UNKNOWN burden.** The primary analysis will foreseeably carry a heavy UNKNOWN burden reflecting absent 2024 infrastructure; the protocol reports it completely rather than gating it with an invented number (CR-7).
8. **Effective sample collapse.** Dependency clustering may reduce the case to very few effective clusters; descriptive shares may rest on small counts, and no interval can repair that.
9. **Single-author governance.** Methodology interpretation and amendments are single-author acts within this program, with no external governance body; council seats and carrying seats are AI systems, not human peer reviewers, and the strongest available check is cross-vendor executing carry plus complete append-only disclosure.
10. **Frame incompleteness.** The public-record frame omits private installations and runtime events by construction; stratum-level NOT-EVALUABLE labels mark, and do not fill, that gap.

### 26.2 BSSG dual-DOI record (roles preserved; never collapsed)

The BSSG paper is cited in two distinct documentary roles that MUST NOT be merged or silently substituted:

1. **Supplied record and bundle:** the Zenodo record from which this program's working corpus was retrieved is [doi:10.5281/zenodo.21713180](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21713180). This identifies the version-of-record actually read by the council.
2. **Embedded self-citation:** the paper PDF itself prints "Paper DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21712482" and "BSSG Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21611192" in its front matter.

Both statements are preserved exactly, with their roles stated wherever either identifier appears. The relationship, verified against the Zenodo API: 10.5281/zenodo.21712481 is the Zenodo concept DOI; 10.5281/zenodo.21712482 (v1.0) and 10.5281/zenodo.21713180 are successive version DOIs under that concept, with 21713180 being the version-of-record retrieved by this program's working corpus. The BSSG paper PDF prints "Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21611192" in its front matter; this is a PDF-vs-registry divergence -- 21611192 resolves to a different record ("BSSG Draft (private)") and is not the concept DOI for the supplied bundle. The divergence is routed upstream as a BSSG deposit defect. This protocol cites 21712481 (concept) and 21713180 (version-of-record) as the authoritative identifiers; the PDF's printed 21611192 is preserved as a self-report with the divergence disclosed. Citing either version identifier as if it were the other, or dropping one, is a citation-integrity defect under falsifier XZ-I4's reporting discipline.

  **Body amendment (Section 22 item 7, added v0.37):** The persistent-architectural-HALT exception defines a category for HALTs that recur on new bases after each disposition in a non-converging loop. The exception applies only when (a) the HALTing seat has audited at least two consecutive versions after the original HALT, (b) each version met the prior clearance conditions and the seat re-HALTed on new bases, and (c) six or more carrying seats across two families returned non-HALT on the same bytes. The exception does not apply to first-time HALTs, to HALTs whose original clearance conditions are unmet, or to HALTs on Class A or Class B findings. GLM-5.2 carry-1C and Kimi K3 carry-1A satisfy all three conditions: (a) both audited v0.33 and v0.35; (b) original conditions met at each version, re-HALTed on new bases both times; (c) six carrying seats returned non-HALT at both v0.33 and v0.35 [ASSERTED].

## 1. Verdict

> **Verdict: HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER.**
>
> **Severity ledger: 2 CRITICAL / 15 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 3 LOW / 3 INFORMATIONAL = 28 findings.**
>
> **Class ledger: A = 17, B = 0, C = 2, D = 2, E = 7 = 28 primary classifications.**
> (`F-PR71-09` and `F-PR71-14` each carry a secondary Class D on the enforcing gate; counted
> once, at Class A, on the enforced false claim.)
>
> Both ledgers were derived by counting the enumerated findings in §3 and §4 after the
> document was written, not narrated while writing it.
>
> **Recommendation: WITHDRAW the FROZEN status token.** The freeze is not blocked by the
> Gödel residual it invokes. It is blocked by (a) three explicit governance rules in the
> frozen text and the shipped canonical methodology that the freeze contravenes without
> disclosing that it is doing so, and (b) eleven Class A byte-false claims inside the
> freeze entry itself, including five that were prescribed for repair by the R28 triage and
> marked CLOSED while shipping live and reproducible.

**The single most important sentence in this review:** the shipped canonical methodology
states, in its own words, *"FROZEN requires all eight TRUE"* (methodology v7 §11). The
v0.71 entry declares Bearers 4, 5 and 7 FALSE and declares FROZEN anyway, without
recording that it is overriding its own criterion.

**On V5, which deserves emphasis.** Holding both the v0.70 and v0.71 packets, I compared
the seal files directly:

```
v0.70 HISTORY.sha256: 72 labels    v0.71 HISTORY.sha256: 73 labels
```

Every one of the 70 carried ENTRY seals is byte-identical across the version boundary, the
carried entry text is byte-identical, and the `PRIOR_HISTORY` value chains correctly to an
independently recomputed digest. **Bearer 1 (Append-only) = TRUE is fully supported by the
bytes.** After the v0.4 and v0.41 append-only corruptions, this is a real and hard-won
property, and it is the property the program should be proudest of.

## 3. Class A findings -- byte-false claims in the sealed freeze entry

### F-PR71-01 [CRITICAL] -- The freeze contravenes the FROZEN criterion of its own canonical methodology

- **Class:** A | **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_71.md` Section 27, v0.71 entry, "Bearer state at
  FROZEN" block, vs. `methodology_v7_canonical.md` §11 (`sha256 59aa6591d9...`, shipped
  byte-identical to `METHODOLOGY.txt` in all four R28 dispatches).
- **Substance:** Methodology v7 §11 states: *"BSSG three-valued kernel: TRUE, FALSE,
  UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN blocks until evidence resolves it. FALSE dominates. **FROZEN requires all
  eight TRUE.**"* The v0.71 entry declares Bearer 4 FALSE, Bearer 5 FALSE, Bearer 7 FALSE,
  and declares FROZEN. Under the kernel semantics the same paragraph invokes, three FALSE
  conjuncts yield DENY_FALSE, not ALLOW. The entry does not acknowledge that it is
  overriding the criterion, does not record an amendment to it, and does not state the
  authority under which the override occurs.
- **Aggravating detail:** The entry presents Bearer 8 (the furqan) = TRUE as if the lead's
  sufficiency judgment is an *override* of the other seven. Methodology §11 defines Bearer 8
  as one of eight conjuncts occupying Position 24 -- a member of the conjunction, not a
  solvent for it. The reframing of a conjunct as an override is undisclosed and is the
  load-bearing move of the entire freeze.
- **Required repair:** Either (a) withdraw FROZEN and return to DRAFT CANDIDATE, or
  (b) formally amend methodology v7 §11 to define a disclosed-residual freeze path, publish
  that amendment before the freeze, and state in the entry that the freeze proceeds under
  the amended rule with three bearers FALSE.
- **Falsifier:** The entry, read alone, states the criterion it is applying and that
  criterion matches the shipped methodology.
- **Cross-reference:** F-PR71-02, F-PR71-03; methodology v7 §11, §15.

### F-PR71-02 [CRITICAL] -- The freeze contravenes Section 22 item 7 of its own frozen text; the invoked exception is expressly inapplicable

- **Class:** A | **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_71.md` Section 22 item 7 (line ~698) vs. the
  v0.71 entry's Bearer 5 line; corroborated by the Section 25 FB-7b row (line 771).
- **Substance:** Section 22 item 7 states that *"a HALT from either carrying seat blocks
  freeze outright and requires a new version."* The v0.71 entry invokes the
  persistent-architectural-HALT exception to disclose Bearer 5 = FALSE rather than treat it
  as blocking. The exception's own text, in the same sealed file, states: *"The exception
  does not apply to first-time HALTs, to HALTs whose original clearance conditions are
  unmet, or to **HALTs on Class A or Class B findings as classified by the HALTing seat's
  own published report** (not the producer)."*

  All four R28 seats returned HALT. All four classified Class A findings in their own
  published reports. The seat executed by the sole eligible carrying family (Kimi K3, S01)
  returned HALT on a Class A finding (`F-S01-70-01`, Class A, String 2, position 4). The
  exception therefore does not apply, and item 7's unweakened rule stands: freeze is blocked.

  The Section 25 FB-7b row states the same rule independently, in the frozen text:
  *"Class A is outside the item 7 exception."*

  Condition (c) of the exception -- *"six or more carrying seats across two families
  returned non-HALT on the same bytes"* -- is also unmet. Zero carrying seats returned
  non-HALT on v0.70 bytes.
- **Required repair:** Withdraw FROZEN. Either satisfy item 7, or amend item 7 by a
  recorded, pre-freeze amendment that narrows the Class A carve-out and states why.
- **Falsifier:** No carrying-family seat HALTed on a self-classified Class A finding on the
  audited bytes.
- **Cross-reference:** F-PR71-01, F-PR71-03, F-PR71-04.

  makes the consequence permanent.
- **Required repair:** Extend the seal to EOF, or assert terminal-marker uniqueness.

  ```
  AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt:9  "Six strings (verification layers): E-A-D-G-B-E"

  METHODOLOGY.txt:66   "3. Architecture: Seven Layers, Seven Witnesses, Twenty-Four Positions"
  ```

  `METHODOLOGY.txt` is byte-identical to `methodology_v7_canonical.md` (sha256

- **Substance:** Every R28 seat received both documents and audited under the six-string /

     variance is zero, so S = 0 and R = 0: R/S is 0/0 and the estimator is undefined, not

     value appears only in prose.
  2. **Laplace P(R29) = 23/24 = 0.958.** The arithmetic is right. The rule of succession
     assumes exchangeable, independent Bernoulli trials. These rounds are neither: each
     round audits an artifact produced *in response to* the previous round's findings, by the
     same producer. The number is a description of the record, not a calibrated forecast, and
     should be labelled as such.
- **Why this matters:** these two numbers are the empirical warrant for the claim that the
  residual is *structural* rather than *remediable*. If they do not bear weight, the
  structural-coupling argument (§5 below) loses its quantitative support.

## 5. Assessment of the freeze's central argument

The REVIEW_GUIDE poses two questions directly. Both deserve direct answers.

### 5.1 "Is the Gödel characterization accurate? Is it honest?"

**The sentence is accurate. The use made of it is not.**

The sentence itself -- *"This instrument cannot verify that it has no remaining byte-false
claims about its own verification properties"* -- is true, is properly `[DISCLOSED]`, and is
a real and non-trivial thing to have written down. An instrument that says this about itself
is doing something most artifacts do not.

But 22 rounds of Class A at H = 1.0 is offered as the *empirical evidence* for the
characterization, and the inference does not go through. The observation is: defects recur
every round. The claim is: defects recur every round **because** self-verification is
formally impossible. That inference requires ruling out the ordinary alternative -- that the
defects recur because the prescribed repairs are not being applied. On this round's evidence
the ordinary alternative is not merely unruled-out; it is demonstrated:

- Five of six R28 convergence groups have concrete, one-line, prescribed repairs.
- The triage marked all five CLOSED.
- **Zero of the five landed.** No code file changed except version stamps.
- Two of the five are now *worse* than at R28 (Section 22.2 two versions stale; the NOTED
  count error recurred inside the entry that reports it).

Nothing about Gödelian self-reference prevents adding `C?` to five regexes, replacing an
`else`-branch `print` with `check(False, ...)`, or typing `v0.71` where `v0.70` is written.
Those are the defects. Attributing them to a formal limit is a category error, and it is the
kind of category error the program's own methodology is built to catch: it is a claim about
the instrument's verification properties that the instrument's own record refutes.

**The honest form of the claim** is narrower and still worth making: *the instrument cannot
verify its own completeness; separately, the repair loop has not converged, and 22 rounds of
recurrence is evidence about the loop, not only about the limit.*

### 5.2 "Is the structural-coupling argument sound?"

The entry argues: Bearers 4, 5 and 7 are FALSE; *"these three conditions are structurally
coupled: resolving any one requires resolving all three, which requires the instrument to
verify its own completeness, which the Goedel sentence forbids."*

**The argument is not sound as stated.** Each conjunct fails independently:

- **Bearer 4 (confinement) does not require completeness verification.** It requires that
  observed Class A be confined to the self-referential surface. That is an empirical property
  of a finite finding set, checkable per round. It is currently FALSE for a mundane reason
  (Class A at Strings 1--3) and, separately, is currently **not well-defined**, because the
  round's coordinate system contradicts the canonical methodology's (F-PR71-16).
- **Bearer 5 (cross-vendor witness) is blocked by seat routing, not by logic.** At R28 the
  only carry-eligible family executed the seat labelled ADVISORY, and the seat labelled
  CARRYING was executed by a self-disqualified family (F-PR71-20). Whether a carrying seat
  could return non-HALT on clean bytes has not been tested, because carrying seats have not
  been *routed* correctly for six consecutive rounds. That is a dispatch-administration
  problem with a known fix.
- **Bearer 7 (methodology) fails at 56% untagged lines including every Bearer
  determination** (F-PR71-17). Tagging the eight bearer lines is a text edit. It requires no
  self-verification of completeness.

The coupling claim also runs backwards through Bearer 4. Bearer 4's own text says the
confinement target is reached when *the only* Class A is in the tagging metadata. Bearer 7
is precisely the tagging surface. So "fix the tagging" is a route to *both* -- which is the
opposite of the entry's claim that resolving one requires resolving all.

**What survives.** A genuinely irreducible residual does exist, and Section 22.4 states it
well: no instrument can certify the absence of unknown byte-false claims about itself, and
axioms A-X1..A-X5 are disclosed and not defended. That is the honest boundary. It is a much
smaller boundary than the one the freeze entry claims, and it does not reach the three
bearers.

### 5.3 What the methodology's own FROZEN prediction requires

Methodology §15 states the condition precisely:

> *"FROZEN is reached not because zero Class A is achieved, but because the Goedel sentence
> is disclosed, **every non-self-referential claim is scribe-verified**, multiple witnesses
> have independently examined the bytes, and the lead judges: this is enough."*

This is a four-conjunct test, and it is a fair one. Scored:

| Conjunct | Status |
|---|---|
| Gödel sentence disclosed | **MET.** Present, correctly tagged, five occurrences. |
| Every non-self-referential claim scribe-verified | **NOT MET.** F-PR71-04, -06, -07, -08, -10, -11, -12, -13: eight classes of non-self-referential claim narrated rather than derived, in the freeze entry itself. 216 `[COMPUTED: generate_register]` tags with a generator that crashes on every shipped input. |
| Multiple witnesses independently examined the bytes | **PARTIALLY MET.** Four seats, four HALTs, real execution, byte-identical dispatches -- genuine. But independence conditions (a) and (d) fail, seat routing is undefined, and the methodology specifies seven witnesses. |
| The lead judges: this is enough | **MET.** Bearer 8 is the lead's to exercise and this review does not contest it. |

The freeze fails the second conjunct on its own terms. **This is the cleanest statement of
why the artifact is not ready:** not because zero Class A was demanded and not achieved, but
because the specific, achievable condition the methodology set -- scribe-verify every claim
that is not self-referential -- was not met, in the very entry that declares it met.

## 6. What would make v0.72 freezable

Ordered by dependency. None of these requires the instrument to verify its own completeness.

1. **Withdraw FROZEN.** Return to DRAFT CANDIDATE. Record the withdrawal as a v0.72
   amendment entry; do not edit v0.71 (append-only is the program's best-verified property
   and must not be spent here).
2. **Land the five prescribed repairs** the R28 triage marked CLOSED: `C?` in all five
   `DECLARATION_PATTERNS`; `check(False, ...)` in gate [13]'s `else` branch; computed values
   in the [13] summary f-string; fix `generate_register`'s adjudication-receipt logic;
   correct Section 0.1's range and Section 22.2's bound.
3. **Reclassify the triage's disposition vocabulary.** CLOSED must mean "verified landed on
   successor bytes." Add a build gate that re-runs the prior round's falsifiers.
4. **Make the gates read loci, not substrings.** [10i] and [2f] must read expectations from
   the shipped findings index (round + version fields) and assert them at named loci. Correct
   values must pass; today they fail.
5. **Fix the terminal line and the seal terminus.** `generate_terminal_line` must emit the
   real status token; the seal must extend to EOF or assert marker uniqueness.
6. **Wire the register generator into `build.py`** and assert byte-exact reproduction of
   every `[COMPUTED: generate_register]` region. Downgrade tags that cannot be reproduced.
7. **Build `r28_findings_index.json`**, ship all four R28 reports inside the manifested
   packet, and let gate [13] cover the round the freeze rests on.
8. **Reconcile the architecture** onto seven layers / twenty-four positions across
   `METHODOLOGY`, `AUDIT_CONTEXT`, `CI_METHODOLOGY`, `DISPATCH` and the protocol Status line;
   recompute Bearer 4 in canonical coordinates; add a parity gate.
9. **Route the seats correctly.** Dispatch by seat *slot* with the executing family bound and
   attested, so that "carrying" is decidable from the bytes. This is the only route to
   Bearer 5, and it has never been tested under correct routing.
10. **Tag every line of the amendment entry**, using `[WITNESSED: seat, round]` for every
    claim about what a seat found. Start with the eight bearer lines.
11. **Re-scope or resolve FB-7b** before any FROZEN token, and extend its trajectory row
    through the current round.
12. **Re-state the quantitative claims** honestly: drop H, or compute it in code over a
    series with nonzero variance; label the Laplace figure as a description of a
    non-independent record.

## 8. Closing assessment

Two things are true at once and the record should hold both.

**The instrument works.** Four independent seats, executing real tools on identical bytes,
converged on real defects and all four returned HALT. The append-only chain is
cryptographically proven across a version boundary against externally held bytes -- after
two historical corruptions, that is a genuine repair. The boundary register reproduces
byte-exactly from its generator. 186 tests are green and the dispatch was byte-identical to
every seat. The Gödel sentence is written down, in public, by the party it constrains. Most
artifacts that claim rigor cannot show a tenth of this.

**The freeze is premature.** Not because it failed to reach zero defects -- the methodology
explicitly does not require that, and demanding it would be unfair. The freeze is premature
because the specific condition the methodology *did* set, *"every non-self-referential claim
is scribe-verified,"* is unmet inside the freeze entry itself; because three explicit rules
in the frozen text and canonical methodology are contravened without disclosure; and because
five defects the round's own triage marked CLOSED ship live and reproducible.

The deepest problem is not any single finding. It is that **the verification layer has begun
enforcing the defects it exists to detect.** Gate [10i] fails when Section 0.1 is corrected.
Gate [10h] forbids the FROZEN document from calling itself FROZEN. Gate [13] reports green on
absent evidence. A generator credited 216 times has never been run by any gate and crashes on
every input it is given. When the checker mandates the false value, "all gates PASS" stops
being evidence of correctness and becomes evidence only of conformity to the checker.

Freezing now writes that state into the permanent record. The program's own thesis --
structural honesty means the artifact's surface matches its substrate behaviour -- is best
served by withdrawing the FROZEN token, landing the twelve items in §6, and freezing a v0.72
whose front matter, terminal line, bearer states, and gates all say the same true thing.

The trajectory is the contribution. It is worth one more round.

recorded as one.*

## R0214 · xz_protocol_version_gate.txt — Version-parity gate for the XZ Protocol package.

- section: IV. XZ Protocol
- source_file: xz_protocol_version_gate.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: 3adbe8cb040423caba10d8bee472773b53b1939613eba0f42960ec808c9bd273

"""Version-parity gate for the XZ Protocol package.

Absorbs F-XZ10-OP-04, F-XZ11-OP-02, F-XZ12-OP-02, F-XZ12-OP-03.

Design notes, stated because the v0.12 predecessor failed on each of them:

* Coverage is derived by globbing the package directory, never hardcoded.
  The gate asserts its own filename is inside its coverage set, so a gate
  that excludes itself cannot pass.
* Matches are examined by span (re.finditer), never by re-locating the
  first occurrence of the matched text. The v0.12 gate used text.index,
  so one whitelisted mention excused every later mismatch in the file.
* There is no proximity whitelist. Historical version references are
  admissible only inside a structured exclusion region: for the protocol
  text, the Section 27 amendment record, which is historical by
  definition and append-only by Axiom 1. Executable files carry exactly
  one stamp and get no exemption at all.
* --self-test mutates a copy of the package and asserts the gate returns
  a nonzero exit code for each covered file class.

Exit 0 = PASS. Exit 1 = FAIL.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

VERSION_TOKEN = re.compile(r"XZ Protocol v(\d+\.\d+)")
FRONT_MATTER_VERSION = re.compile(r"^\*\*Version:\*\*\s*(\d+\.\d+)")
AMENDMENT_HEADING = "## 27. Amendment record"


def package_dir() -> str:
    return os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def protocol_path(root: str) -> str:
    candidates = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "xz_protocol_v0_*.md")))
    if len(candidates) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"FAIL: expected exactly one protocol text, found {len(candidates)}: "
            + ", ".join(os.path.basename(c) for c in candidates)
        )
    return candidates[0]


def declared_version(path: str) -> str:
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
        m = FRONT_MATTER_VERSION.match(line)
        if m:
            return m.group(1)
    raise SystemExit("FAIL: no '**Version:**' line in protocol front matter")


def coverage(root: str) -> list[str]:
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*.py")))
    files += sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*.json")))
    files += [protocol_path(root)]
    return files


def excluded_span(path: str, text: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Byte range in which historical version references are admissible."""
    if path.endswith(".md") and AMENDMENT_HEADING in text:
        return (text.index(AMENDMENT_HEADING), len(text))
    return (-1, -1)


def check(root: str) -> list[str]:
    proto = protocol_path(root)
    expected = declared_version(proto)
    errors: list[str] = []
    files = coverage(root)

    me = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    if me not in [os.path.basename(f) for f in files]:
        errors.append(f"  {me}: gate excludes itself from its own coverage set")

    for path in files:
        text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        lo, hi = excluded_span(path, text)
        for m in VERSION_TOKEN.finditer(text):
            if lo <= m.start() < hi:
                continue
            if m.group(1) != expected:
                line = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
                errors.append(
                    f"  {os.path.basename(path)}:{line}: found v{m.group(1)}, "
                    f"expected v{expected}"
                )

    tr = os.path.join(root, "xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json")
    if os.path.exists(tr):
        declared = json.load(open(tr, encoding="utf-8")).get("protocol")
        if declared != f"XZ Protocol v{expected}":
            errors.append(
                f"  trust roots: protocol field is {declared!r}, "
                f"expected 'XZ Protocol v{expected}'"
            )
    else:
        errors.append("  trust roots file is absent")

    return errors


def self_test(root: str) -> int:
    """Mutate a copy and assert the gate fires for each covered file class."""
    stray = "XZ Protocol " + "v" + "0.1"  # assembled so this source carries no literal stamp
    cases = [
        ("module", "xz_protocol_kernel.py"),
        ("test suite", "test_xz_protocol_kernel.py"),
        ("gate", "xz_protocol_manifest_gate.py"),
        ("protocol text", None),
    ]
    failures = []
    for label, target in cases:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            work = os.path.join(tmp, "pkg")
            shutil.copytree(root, work)
            if target is None:
                p = protocol_path(work)
                t = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
                head = t.index(AMENDMENT_HEADING)
                t = t[:head] + "\n" + stray + " stray reference\n" + t[head:]
                open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(t)
            else:
                p = os.path.join(work, target)
                t = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
                open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("# " + stray + "\n" + t)
            rc = subprocess.call(
                [sys.executable, os.path.join(work, os.path.basename(__file__))],
                stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            )
            if rc == 0:
                failures.append(f"  self-test: mutated {label} did not fire the gate")

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        work = os.path.join(tmp, "pkg")
        shutil.copytree(root, work)
        rc = subprocess.call(
            [sys.executable, os.path.join(work, os.path.basename(__file__))],
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )
        if rc != 0:
            failures.append("  self-test: unmutated package did not pass")

    if failures:
        print("FAIL: version gate self-test:")
        for f in failures:
            print(f)
        return 1
    print("PASS: version gate self-test (4 mutations fired, clean package passed)")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    root = package_dir()
    if "--self-test" in sys.argv:
        return self_test(root)
    errors = check(root)
    if errors:
        print(f"FAIL: {len(errors)} version-parity errors:")
        for e in errors:
            print(e)
        return 1
    print(
        f"PASS: version parity v{declared_version(protocol_path(root))} "
        f"across {len(coverage(root))} shipped files"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

## R0215 · The XZ Structural Honesty Audit Corpus: 818 Findings from 31 Rounds of Multi-Model Verification

- section: IV. XZ Protocol
- source_file: XZ_STRUCTURAL_HONESTY_AUDIT_CORPUS.md
- source_format: md
- text_sha256: 25dc2508e839d60c51ee9e86c6b3979c12537a379a38bbcc69ec6d498f3beb55

# The XZ Structural Honesty Audit Corpus: 818 Findings from 31 Rounds of Multi-Model Verification

Bilal Syed Arfeen

2026-08-18

Prepared with Claude Opus 4.6 (Anthropic) as analytical and drafting instrument under the author's direction and final authority. This paper makes no effectiveness claim about any component of the Structural Honesty program.

Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim

---

## Abstract

This paper describes the construction, schema, and content of the XZ Structural Honesty Audit Corpus, a structured dataset of 818 findings extracted from 199 seat reports across 31 audit rounds of the XZ Protocol (v0.37 through v0.74), produced by independent AI systems from four vendor families (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Moonshot/Zhipu). The corpus is the evidentiary substrate for the empirical claims in the companion synthesis paper "The Heartbeat of a Live System" and provides the first publicly available multi-model, multi-round audit dataset for a software verification instrument. The primary series -- 25 consecutive rounds with Class A (byte-false claim) defects present -- is recoverable from the structured data, with 136 Class A findings extracted across 19 of 25 rounds and the remaining 6 rounds documented as present in the verdict record but not individually classified in the extracted finding headers. The construction procedure (an 18-pattern regex extractor with 62 manual verdict overrides) ships with the corpus as a reproducible pipeline.

---

## 1. Motivation

The XZ Protocol audit program produced a 25-round empirical series whose central finding -- a software verification instrument cannot verify that it has no remaining byte-false claims about its own verification properties -- rests on primary evidence: the seat reports produced by independent AI auditors. The Heartbeat paper synthesizes this evidence into narrative. The corpus structures it into data.

No comparable dataset exists. Multi-model adversarial auditing of software artifacts is a new practice, and the audit reports have until now been scattered across chat sessions, dispatch packets, and handoff archives in heterogeneous formats spanning 75 protocol versions and four model families. The corpus makes this evidence queryable, reproducible, and independently verifiable.

The corpus publishes under the program's Gate 1 (safety) and Gate 2 (moat) discipline. Gate 1 is satisfied by construction: findings concern the protocol text's claims about its own verification properties, not the XZ Utils backdoor. No payload, activation recipe, or reconstruction detail appears anywhere in the corpus. Gate 2 is satisfied: the corpus is OPEN under the publication posture's Tier 1.

---

## 2. Composition

### 2.1 Scale

The corpus contains three structured outputs derived from 199 deduplicated seat reports:

- **reports.csv** -- 199 rows, one per unique seat report. Fields: filename, sha256, round, version, seat ID, model family, normalized family, role, mode, verdict, severity counts, Class A count, finding count, era classification.
- **findings.csv** -- 818 rows (796 unique finding IDs), one per extracted finding. Fields: finding ID, severity, finding class, tier, description, locus, round, version, seat ID, model family, normalized family, source report.
- **coverage.csv** -- round x version x seat x family verdict matrix.

### 2.2 Temporal span

The corpus covers 31 audit rounds (R1 through R31) and 64 protocol versions (v0.1 through v0.74), produced between August 1 and August 17, 2026. The rounds fall into five eras:

- **Pre-R7** (v0.1--v0.36): 71 reports. The carrying and advisory rounds before the Class A recurrence series began. Format heterogeneity is highest in this era.
- **Seat-lineage** (R1--R6, v0.37--v0.39): 42 reports. Cross-domain analytical frameworks (GAN convergence, Fractal/Hurst, Structural Revelation, Cobweb, Meta-audit) deployed across named seat lineages.
- **Convergence** (R7--R8, v0.40--v0.49): 20 reports. Multi-seat convergence rounds with the first standardized dispatch architecture.
- **CI era** (R9--R20, v0.50--v0.61): 34 reports. CI automation (v0.2 through v0.3.2), GPT-5.6 Sol enters as carrying seat, Kimi K3 as carrying seat.
- **Mature** (R21--R31, v0.62--v0.74): 32 reports. Standardized S0--S10 report structure, canonical six-suite pytest, four-family rotation.

### 2.3 Model family distribution

| Family | Reports | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic (Claude Opus 4.6 / 5) | 88 | Producer-family, advisory only, zero carry weight |
| OpenAI (GPT-5.6 Sol) | 64 | Advisory (self-disqualified from carry at v0.6), adversarial record |
| Zhipu (GLM-5.2) | 23 | Carrying seat (one of two carrying families) |
| Google (Gemini 3.1 Pro) | 15 | Advisory |
| Moonshot (Kimi K3) | 5 | Carrying seat (one of two carrying families) |
| Other/Unknown | 4 | Perplexity (1), unclassified (3) |

The carrying pool (Kimi K3 + GLM-5.2) is underrepresented in the extracted corpus relative to its governance weight because Kimi reports were often delivered as agent-output zip files whose internal markdown did not match the standard finding-header patterns, and GLM-5.2 reports frequently used minimal-format prose without structured finding headers.

### 2.4 Finding distribution

| Severity | Count | Pct |
|---|---|---|
| CRITICAL | 62 | 7.6% |
| HIGH | 360 | 44.0% |
| MEDIUM | 228 | 27.9% |
| LOW | 127 | 15.5% |
| INFORMATIONAL | 41 | 5.0% |

| Class | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Class A | 136 | Byte-false claim in sealed or shipped text |
| Class B | 23 | Concealed defect (gate exists, doesn't cover) |
| Class C | 11 | Disclosed standing boundary |
| Class D | 24 | Gate limitation |
| Class E | 13 | Methodology or governance observation |
| Unclassified | 615 | No class tag in finding header (mostly pre-R13 and non-Opus reports) |

### 2.5 Verdict distribution

| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| HALT | 147 |
| CONDITIONAL PASS | 22 |
| PASS | 4 |
| Not extracted | 26 |

Verdict coverage is 87% (173/199). The 26 unextracted verdicts are predominantly Zhipu (GLM-5.2) and Moonshot (Kimi K3) reports in minimal or non-standard formats.

---

## 3. Collection process

### 3.1 Primary sources

The corpus was assembled from three archive files containing the complete audit dispatch and result history of the XZ Protocol program:

- Archive 1: 328 files (383 MB) -- dispatch packets and reports, R1--R31.
- Archive 2: 1,159 files (85 MB) -- dispatch prompts, seat reports, methodology documents.
- Archive 3: 595 files (344 MB) -- dispatch packets, Kimi agent outputs, seat reports.
- Supplementary: two handoff zips (v0.53, v0.54) containing the R12 report not present in the main archives.

Total raw material: 2,082 files. After deduplication by content hash and exclusion of non-report files (dispatch prompts, methodology documents, framework PDFs, OS metadata), 199 unique seat reports remained.

### 3.2 Extraction procedure

The construction procedure is a single Python script (`extract_corpus.py`, shipped with the corpus) that:

1. Walks all archive roots and discovers `.md` files passing the `is_seat_report` heuristic (positive signals: REPORT, AUDIT, VERDICT, RESULT, ADVISORY in filename; negative signals: DISPATCH_PROMPT, METHODOLOGY, DISCIPLINE, HANDOFF; content fallback: verdict pattern in first 3000 characters).
2. Deduplicates by SHA-256 content hash (handles the `(1)` / `(2)` copy variants in the archives).
3. Excludes 6 files identified by manual triage as non-reports (methodology documents, command logs).
4. Extracts report-level metadata (round, version, seat, model family, role, mode, verdict) from structured headers using 8 regex patterns with fallback to filename parsing.
5. Applies 62 manual verdict overrides for reports where the verdict is embedded in prose paragraphs rather than structured headers.
6. Extracts per-finding data using 18 regex patterns covering every observed finding-header format across the program's history, from the early numbered format (`### 1. Critical -`) through the mature six-element format (`### F-S04-74-01 [CRITICAL] [Class A] --`).
7. Extracts locus from `**Locus:**` fields, `**Severity:**` lines, and inline `Locus:` annotations.
8. Extracts finding class from headers, body text, and `**Severity:**` lines, accepting only single letters A--E.
9. Outputs three CSV files and a JSON summary.

The 18 finding-header patterns, in priority order:

1. Mature bracket: `### F-ID [SEVERITY] [Class X] -- description`
2. Mid-era class-first: `### F-ID [Class X] SEVERITY -- description`
3. Cross-domain tier: `### F-ID [SEVERITY] [Tier N] -- description`
4. Kimi bare-class: `### F-ID [SEVERITY] -- Class X -- description`
5. Bracket severity: `### F-ID [SEVERITY] -- description`
6. GPT slash-class: `### F-ID — SEVERITY / Class X`
7. GPT paren-class: `### F-ID — SEVERITY (Class X): description`
8. Em-dash severity: `### F-ID — SEVERITY — description`
9. GLM inline: `### N.N F-ID — description — **SEVERITY**`
10. Convergence: `### F-ID -- SEVERITY description`
11. Numbered early: `### N. Severity - description`
12. Bold finding: `**F-ID** [SEVERITY] -- description`
13. R8 numbered-bold: `N. **F-ID — Class X:** description`
14. R16 pipe-bold: `**F-ID | SEVERITY (Class X) | description**`
15. R17 pipe-hash: `### F-ID | SEVERITY (Class X) | Locus | description`
16. R12 class-after-dash: `### F-ID -- CLASS X (description)`
17. Bare header: `### F-ID` (severity on next line)
18. Bare description catch-all: `### F-ID — description` (severity from body)

### 3.3 What is not in the corpus

The corpus does not contain:

- The protocol text itself (published separately as XZ Protocol v0.75 FROZEN).
- The executable code (build.py, test suites, gates) -- these are part of the protocol deposit.
- The dispatch packets (AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt, DISPATCH.txt, EXECUTABLE_PACKET.txt) -- these are program infrastructure.
- The triage records (R1--R31 cross-seat triages) -- these are governance documents, not primary evidence.
- The CI outputs (pytest results, build.py gate logs) -- these are embedded in the seat reports and extractable from the finding descriptions, but not separately structured.
- Any XZ Utils payload, activation, or reconstruction content -- the protocol's Section 0.2 bars this, and the corpus inherits the prohibition.

---

## 4. Annotation schema

Each finding carries the following fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| finding_id | string | Unique identifier in the program's namespace (e.g. F-S04-74-01) |
| severity | enum | CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFORMATIONAL |
| finding_class | enum | Class A (byte-false), Class B (concealed), Class C (disclosed), Class D (gate limit), Class E (governance) |
| tier | enum | Tier 1 (byte-reproducible), Tier 2 (tool-derived), Tier 3 (seat-produced) |
| description | string | First-line description from the finding header |
| locus | string | Where in the artifact the finding lives (file, line, section) |
| round_number | int | Audit round (1--31) |
| version | string | Protocol version under audit (v0.37--v0.74) |
| seat_id | string | Seat identifier (S01--S12, C01--C08, etc.) |
| model_family | string | Model name as reported |
| family_normalized | string | Vendor family (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Moonshot, Zhipu) |
| report_file | string | Source report filename |

The finding ID namespace encodes provenance: `F-{seat/namespace}-{version}-{sequence}`. The namespace prefix identifies the seat and often the analytical framework (e.g. F-OP = Opus producer-family, F-S02 = Seat 2 standardized, F-GPT37FH = GPT Fractal/Hurst on v0.37, F-CONV1 = Convergence Round 1).

---

## 5. Known limitations

1. **Class A extraction coverage.** The Heartbeat paper documents 25 consecutive rounds (R7--R31) with Class A present. The corpus extracts Class A findings from 19 of those 25 rounds. The 6 rounds without extracted Class A (R9--R11, R15, R28--R29) have Class A documented in the round verdict or triage record but not individually tagged in the finding headers the extractor parses. The Class A presence at every round is independently verifiable from the verdict record (all 25 rounds returned HALT with Class A cited as the basis).

2. **Unclassified findings.** 615 of 818 findings (75%) carry no class tag. The A--E classification was introduced at R7 and applied consistently only from R13 onward by Opus-family seats. GPT, Gemini, Kimi, and GLM reports frequently omit the class tag or embed it in prose rather than headers.

3. **Carrying-seat underrepresentation.** The two carrying families (Kimi K3, GLM-5.2) account for only 28 reports (14%) despite holding binding governance authority. Their reports use formats the extractor handles less completely (Kimi agent zip outputs, GLM minimal prose).

4. **Verdict coverage.** 26 of 199 reports (13%) have no extracted verdict. These are predominantly early-era Zhipu and Moonshot reports.

5. **Locus extraction.** 79% of findings have a locus field. The remaining 21% embed locus information in the finding body in non-standard formats.

6. **No disposition chains.** The corpus does not yet track finding lifecycles across rounds (raised at Rn, dispositioned at Rn+1, recurred at Rn+k). The cross-references are present in the finding descriptions and could be extracted in a future version.

7. **Round 36.** One report is tagged R36 (v0.36, pre-R7 era). This is a version-number artifact, not a genuine 36th audit round; the report audited v0.36 which predates the R1--R31 round-numbering system.

---

## 6. Uses

### 6.1 Intended uses

- **Reproducing the Heartbeat paper's empirical claims.** Every quantitative claim in the synthesis paper (25-round Class A series, H=1.0, defect migration trajectory, severity distribution, framework productivity) can be checked against the structured data.
- **Studying multi-model verification dynamics.** The corpus provides the first dataset for analyzing how different AI model families produce different findings on the same artifact under the same methodology.
- **Studying defect migration.** The round-over-round structure allows tracking how defect classes migrate upward through verification layers as lower layers are secured.
- **Methodology research.** The 18-pattern extractor documents the format evolution of AI-generated audit reports across 31 rounds and 4 families, which is itself a finding about standardization in multi-model workflows.

### 6.2 Out of scope

- **Training data for code generation or vulnerability detection.** The corpus contains no code, no vulnerabilities, and no XZ Utils technical content.
- **Evaluating AI model capabilities.** The corpus was not designed as a benchmark and the seat reports were produced under heterogeneous conditions (different dispatch formats, different execution environments, different context lengths).

---

## 7. Distribution

The corpus publishes as a Zenodo deposit under CC-BY-4.0, consistent with the program's publication posture (Tier 1, fully open). The deposit contains:

- `findings.csv` -- the primary dataset
- `reports.csv` -- report-level metadata
- `coverage.csv` -- round x seat verdict matrix
- `summary.json` -- aggregate statistics
- `extract_corpus.py` -- the construction procedure (reproducible pipeline)
- This paper (dataset card)

The raw seat reports are not included in the corpus deposit. They are available in the XZ Protocol's own deposit archive and in the program's handoff records.

Program chain DOIs: AX-SH5 Flagship 10.5281/zenodo.21500700; SHUDP 10.5281/zenodo.21522932; SHVVP 10.5281/zenodo.21583202; BSSG 10.5281/zenodo.21713180; BAF 10.5281/zenodo.20017335; PMD 10.5281/zenodo.21462879; SHV Method 10.5281/zenodo.21449063.

---

## 8. Maintenance

The corpus is a snapshot of the audit record as of v0.75 FROZEN (2026-08-17). If the protocol receives further audit rounds, a new version of the corpus will be produced by re-running the extractor on the expanded archive. The extractor is versioned (v0.3) and the version is recorded in the output metadata.

---

## Appendix A: Construction verification

The extractor's correctness can be verified by:

1. Re-running `extract_corpus.py` on the same archives and comparing the output hashes.
2. Spot-checking any finding row against its source report (the `report_file` field identifies the source).
3. Checking the 62 manual verdict overrides against the cited prose passages (each override's basis is documented in the extraction log).

The extractor does not modify any source file. It reads, parses, and outputs. The source reports are the evidence; the CSV files are a structured view.

---

Bilal Syed Arfeen
Bayyinah Structural Honesty Validation Program -- August 2026

"Indeed, We sent down the reminder, and indeed, We will be its preserver." (Qur'an 15:9)

(DISPATCH_PROMPT, METHODOLOGY, DISCIPLINE, HANDOFF, CONCEPT, ADJUDICATION_V, TRIAGE, CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC, ORBITAL_AUDIT_METH, QUANTUM_ORBITAL,
PEER_REVIEW_PROMPT, PUBLICATION_REVIEW) are checked only if no positive signal
matches. The manual EXCLUDE_FILES set (6 entries) is load-bearing for files that pass the heuristic but
are not seat reports.
2. Deduplicates by SHA-256 content hash.
3. Extracts report-level metadata using version (3 header patterns + filename fallback), round (3 header
patterns + filename fallback), seat (3 header patterns + 5 filename patterns), family (2 header patterns
+ filename fallback), and verdict (8 patterns + fallback line scan) regex extractors. Applies 52 manual
verdict overrides for reports with prose-embedded verdicts.
4. Extracts per-finding data using 18 regex patterns covering all observed finding-header formats.
5. Validates description fields: bounds all body scans at the next finding header to prevent cross-finding
locus assignment; strips leaked **Locus:** markers (including bullet-prefixed variants), moves locus
content to the locus field, and backfills descriptions from the finding body where possible.
6. Outputs four data files (findings.csv, reports.csv, coverage.csv, summary.json) plus extraction.log.
3


The 18 finding-header patterns, in priority order:
1. Mature bracket: ### F-ID [SEVERITY] [Class X] -- description
2. Mid-era class-first: ### F-ID [Class X] SEVERITY -- description
3. Cross-domain tier: ### F-ID [SEVERITY] [Tier N] -- description
4. Kimi bare-class: ### F-ID [SEVERITY] -- Class X -- description
5. Bracket severity: ### F-ID [SEVERITY] -- description
6. GPT slash-class: ### F-ID -- SEVERITY / Class X
7. GPT paren-class: ### F-ID -- SEVERITY (Class X): description
8. Em-dash severity: ### F-ID -- SEVERITY -- description
9. GLM inline: ### N.N F-ID -- description -- **SEVERITY**
10. Convergence: ### F-ID -- SEVERITY description
11. Numbered early: ### N. Severity - description
12. Bold finding: **F-ID** [SEVERITY] -- description
13. R8 numbered-bold: N. **F-ID -- Class X:** description
14. R16 pipe-bold: **F-ID | SEVERITY (Class X) | description**
15. R17 pipe-hash: ### F-ID | SEVERITY (Class X) | description
16. R12 class-after-dash: ### F-ID -- CLASS X (description)
17. Bare header: ### F-ID (severity on next line)
18. Bare description catch-all: ### F-ID -- description (severity from body)
(Patterns 1–9, 11–13, and 18 accept Unicode U+2013/U+2014 dash classes; patterns 10 and 16 match literal
-- only.)
3.3 What is not in the corpus
The corpus does not contain the protocol text, the executable code, the dispatch packets, the triage records,
the CI outputs, or any XZ Utils payload, activation, or reconstruction content.

5. Known limitations
1. Class A extraction coverage. 19 of 25 R7–R31 rounds have extracted Class A findings (102 total).
The 6 rounds without (R9–R11, R15, R28–R29) have Class A documented in the verdict record per the
Heartbeat paper (ASSERTED, not COMPUTED from this corpus’s structured data). Some of those
rounds contain findings whose descriptions reference Class A in prose but whose headers lack the class
tag in formats the extractor captures.
2. Unclassified findings. 625 of 832 (75%) carry no class tag.
3. Carrying-seat underrepresentation. 28 reports (14%) from the two carrying families.
4. Verdict coverage. 26 of 199 reports (13%) have no extracted verdict (Anthropic 13, OpenAI 7, Zhipu
4, Moonshot 1, Perplexity 1).
5. Locus extraction. 81% of findings have a locus field.
6. No disposition chains.
7. Empty round fields. 90 reports (45%) and 223 findings (27%) have no extracted round number. 6
reports and 4 findings have no extracted version.
8. Duplicate finding IDs. 20 IDs appear in more than one row, comprising content-identical doubleextractions and namespace collisions across reports.
9. R36 parsing artifact. One report (XZ_v27_SEAT_G_ADVISORY.md, v0.27) is tagged R36 by the round
extractor.
10. Description quality. 40 of 832 findings (5%) have empty descriptions after validation.

6. Uses
6.1 Intended uses
• Reproducing the Heartbeat paper’s empirical claims against the structured data.
• Studying multi-model verification dynamics across five vendor families.
• Studying defect migration across the round-over-round structure.
• Methodology research on the format evolution of AI-generated audit reports.
6.2 Out of scope
• Training data for code generation or vulnerability detection.
• Evaluating AI model capabilities.

## 5. Findings

What the round got right first (S-8): the PRIOR_HISTORY recursive derivation verifies under an independent re-implementation; 26/26 entry seals and FULL_SECTION_27 recompute exactly; all three v0.25 CLOSED dispositions I executed (E5 inspection, E6/P5a, E7/P5b) are TRUE — the closures are real, not narrative; every gated locus I attacked discriminated (P1–P5a); [9c]'s tag-reference gate, the absence gate, and the packet self-exclusion rule all work. The delta against the trajectory is real: this round's defect is smaller and further outside the computed region than the register's historical entries.

- **F-1 (MEDIUM) — Stale version token, internally inconsistent carry locus.** §0.1 (md line 20): *"the fresh two-family carry it requires is outstanding on these **v0.22** canonical bytes"* — in a v0.26 document whose §25 FB-7b row says *"pending fresh carry on **v0.26** canonical bytes."* Two body locations disagree about which bytes the carry binds. Ungated: [2b] matches only `v0.N DRAFT CANDIDATE` and `This document is v0.N` patterns. New instance of the disclosed stale-prose class (F-OP25-ALL-06, MEDIUM) with no register row tracking it. Concealment: none deliberate — but this is the invariant's exact signature (recollection carried across versions at the ungated layer). Producer action: correct the token in v0.27 (or explicitly quote-mark it as historical); consider extending the [2b]-class gate to `v0.N canonical bytes`-form references.
- **F-2 (INFORMATIONAL — the measured boundary).** Section 27 contains 34 total / 28 unique 64-hex literals; **27/28 are unresolvable against all shipped digest state** (HISTORY ∪ PACKET ∪ manifest). They are historical citations inside sealed entries — by design — but they are the precise locus where truth is unverifiable from this packet. The absence gate [3b] is body-scoped only.
- **F-3 (INFORMATIONAL).** ASSERTED-fraction denominators diverge: producer-tagged 6/11 = 54.5% vs claim-granular 13/18 = 72.2%. Untagged claims default ASSERTED and escape the producer's frame. Producer action (non-blocking): state the denominator as "tagged claims" (the build already prints this — good) and consider tagging or explicitly excluding narrative sentences E1–E3.
- **F-4 (DISCLOSED-CONFIRMED).** NC-1 demonstrates §22.2's disclosed residual live: a forger controlling all shipped bytes passes rc=0 with 186 forged-green tests; only externally held anchors detect it. Concealment: NONE — disclosed in §22.2; this report adds the execution record, not a new defect class.
- **F-5 (DISCLOSED-CONFIRMED).** NC-2 confirms F-OP25-ALL-08's disclosed state: the PDF (239,936 bytes, the human-facing artifact of record) carries no digest in any shipped text; a mutated PDF passes every gate. Concealment: NONE. (PDF spot-fidelity to the md holds at the probed loci, including the F-1 line — the PDF is a faithful render *as far as inspected*; fidelity is ASSERTED, not gated.)
- **F-6 (LOW).** [9d]'s ordinal gate covers ordinal+"recurrence" only; the register's own ordinal claims ("seventh round", "fifth", "fourth", "eighth consecutive round" — E12/E13) are ordinal+"round" and thus ungated recollection. Producer action (non-blocking): widen [9d]'s adjacency class or tag these ASSERTED-with-source.

## 6. Boundary report (deliverable D; S-5; S-6)

One paragraph. The computed region of v0.26 is: file digests, version stamps/strings, test counts, register structure, and the Section-27 seal chain — build [11] measures semantic-gate coverage at **24,546/98,173 body chars (25.0%)**, with **Section 27 at 79,626/177,799 chars (44.8%) seal-gated only** and the PDF (239,936 bytes) outside everything; packet-level, 16/17 shipped artifacts carry digests, 1/17 (the PDF) carries none. The boundary the invariant predicts has moved to exactly three layers, all confirmed by execution this round: (i) **the unsealed rendered artifact** (NC-2); (ii) **semantic truth of normative prose and code behavior under wholesale reseal** (NC-1 — the gates measure *agreement among surfaces*, and a forger who controls all surfaces makes them agree on a false value); (iii) **prior-round recollection in Section 27 and residual body prose** (F-1, E1–E3, E12–E13: 27/28 unresolvable hex literals; the v0.25 advisory round's outcomes are unverifiable from this packet). What my independent state bought: executability let me verify the derivation, the seals, the closures, and both blind spots *as internal properties*; it could NOT establish authenticity of the base packet — NC-1 proves my "verified" packet is only as trustworthy as the channel that delivered PACKET_SHA256SUMS to me. A seat holding prior-version packets could additionally verify E1–E3 and the ordinal recurrence counts; a seat holding an externally published digest of the dispatch manifest or a Zenodo receipt could defeat NC-1. What the next seat (GLM-5.2) must be given: the canonical bytes **plus an externally anchored digest of them** (dispatch manifest or deposit receipt published outside producer control), otherwise its carry, like mine, verifies consistency rather than authenticity.

## 7. D-7 — Round delta and handoff

- Deliverables A–G status: A ledger ✓ (72.2% headline) · B five+ probes ✓ (7 + controls, 4-part discipline) · C two novel-class ✓ (NC-1, NC-2, named new) · D boundary ✓ (Section 6) · E hedge audit ✓ (Section 5, H-rows: every NOTED/DISCLOSED downgrade checked — downgrades correct; reasons E6/E7/E10/E12-partial seat-verified TRUE; scopes match; all nine defects carry register IDs F-OP25-ALL-01…09) · F S-1 frozen pre-narrative ✓ (`audit_v026/S0_S1_FROZEN.md`) · G this section ✓.
- Delta this round: defect class migrated from wrong-values to stale-referential prose (F-1) + uncounted untagged claims (F-3); both disclosed blind spots now carry execution records (NC-1, NC-2).
- Blocking findings: none. Conditions to clear F-1 (and optionally F-3/F-6): see Section 8.
- Handoff to GLM-5.2: carry must run on v0.26 canonical bytes with an externally anchored packet digest; without it, a second consistent-but-unauthentic carry adds no FB-7b evidence.

**Reflexive check (standing orders, one line each):** probes from the enumerated corpus only? **No** (NC-1/NC-2 new). Prediction held trivially from dispatch leakage? **No** — the dispatch shipped no defect list, and my specific defect prediction was REFUTED at its locus. ASSERTED fraction unchanged from prior round? **Unknown** — prior round's fraction does not ship (noted as a bound, not smoothed over). Last N rounds all producer-family? **v0.25 was** (six Opus 5 advisory seats, no external witness); this round breaks that pattern with a non-producer executing seat, and GLM-5.2 must complete the pair.

**S-7 self-falsification (numbered, executed as tool runs):** (1) every digest printed in this report recomputed from bytes — manifest `55d1744e…` ✓, PDF `34b47ff3…` ✓, FULL_SECTION_27 `c643c3bd…` ✓, PRIOR_HISTORY derivation ✓; (2) every cited line number re-extracted — `## 27.` at md line 795 ✓, F-1 locus at line 20 ✓; (3) every count re-derived — entry length 2,180 ✓, 28 unique §27 hex literals ✓, per-suite counts 27+29+18+14+29+69=186 ✓, ledger rows 18 (5/0/13) ✓; (4) every claim about the shipped build re-grepped against `build_run1.log` (170 PASS/0 FAIL; coverage 25.0%/44.8%) ✓; (5) past-tense procedure claims performed-then-confirmed (clean-copy build re-run green after the probe battery) ✓; (6) void probe reported as void, not a finding ✓. **Caught in this step:** the E10 "%"-scan false-positive (the entry contains the *word* "percentage" only inside its own disclosure sentence — corrected before shipping) and the first P5b probe's missed assertion target (reclassified VOID-INCONCLUSIVE, re-run correctly).

## 8. Verdict — **CONDITIONAL PASS** (non-HALT)

**Standing restated:** I am a carrying seat, non-producer family (Moonshot Kimi K3 vs producer Claude/Anthropic). This verdict **counts toward FB-7b** as one of the two required non-producer families; it is binding within the carry rule, not advisory. It does not close FB-7b: §22/§25 require a second family (GLM-5.2) with a non-HALT verdict on the same canonical bytes. A HALT from me would have blocked freeze and forced v0.27; this verdict does not.

**Blocking findings:** NONE. **Conditions (clear in v0.27):**
- **C1 (required, from F-1):** correct the stale "v0.22 canonical bytes" token at §0.1 line 20 (the carry is pending on v0.26 bytes per §25), or explicitly mark the sentence as historical quotation; register the instance under the F-OP25-ALL-06 class with a disposition row.

- **C3 (recommended, from F-3):** reconcile the ASSERTED-fraction denominator (tagged 54.5% vs claim-granular 72.2%) by tagging or explicitly excluding untagged narrative claims in the entry.

**Carry consequence restated:** CONDITIONAL PASS is non-HALT; freeze remains blocked only by the outstanding second-family carry (GLM-5.2) and by C1's amendment, which under the append-only rule arrives as v0.27. The two demonstrated residuals (NC-1 wholesale reseal forgery; NC-2 PDF substitution) are disclosed in §22.2 and F-OP25-ALL-08 respectively; they are not new defects and do not gate this verdict, but FB-7b's evidentiary value is bounded by them until an external anchor (deposit receipt or externally published dispatch-manifest digest) closes the reseal class.

# XZ Protocol v0.50 — R9 Carrying-Seat Audit Report

## VERDICT: HALT (binding)

One **Class A** finding (F-S01-50-01) with executed mutation probes. Under the dispatch's verdict discipline (Class A = HALT) and Section 22 item 7, this HALT blocks freeze outright.
