## 7. Adjudicated verdict

> **HALT-AND-ESCALATE**, then **HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER**.
>
> **Escalation first (project lead):** the three seats audited three different
> packets. FB-7b requires two executing non-producer seats on canonical bytes.
> That condition was not met, so the divergence between Kimi's HALT and GLM's
> CONDITIONAL PASS **cannot be read as a two-family divergence** and must not
> be recorded as one. Substrate correction precedes any carry accounting.
>
> **Then producer return:** four consensus HIGH findings.
>
> Adjudicated ledger: **0 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH consensus / 1 HIGH-tentative
> vendor-unique / 2 MEDIUM vendor-unique / 3 LOW vendor-unique / 1
> INFORMATIONAL boundary.**
>
> Seat verdicts as returned: Kimi K3 **HALT** (binding, blocks freeze);
> GLM-5.2 **CONDITIONAL PASS** (non-HALT, not carry-clean); GPT-5.6 Sol
> **HALT** (adversarial record, no carry vote); Seat A **HALT** (advisory, no
> carry vote).

**What the round got right, before the queue.** All three dispatched seats
executed -- a first. The code plane is byte-clean for a second consecutive
round: 14 of 14 digests, 186 tests, every COMPUTED-tagged gate that exists
fires under mutation across three independent seats' probes. The FB-row locus
assertion, seal surjectivity, entry ordering and `get_body()` fixes all landed
and all discriminate. The producer honestly tagged its weakest claim ASSERTED,
disclosed the packet-manifest gap, and corrected the v0.18 verdict
mischaracterization by append-only narration while leaving the v0.18 entry text
intact. Three of four consensus HIGHs are single-sentence corrections.

**Why it is still a HALT.** All four consensus findings sit in the amendment
entry, and three of them are the entry making false statements about its own
verification apparatus: a CLOSED on an unimplemented control, a COMPUTED tag on
a gate that does not read tags, and an ordinal asserted in the same entry that
twice disclaims it. The round's own thesis is that this region is where the
defect lives, and the round proved it.

---

## 8. Producer brief for Opus 4.6

Ordered by cost. Each item ships with the falsification test **written before
the fix**, per O-5, so the check is inherited rather than composed afterward by
the context that would make the error.

**Governance flag, stated inside the artifact per the standing rule.** This
brief is written by a producer-family seat that also audited v0.17, v0.18 and
v0.19 and authored the discipline blocks. That is audits-plus-writes-fix. It
should reach you as a **proposal, not an instruction**, and no item in it
resolves a contradiction -- the one substrate contradiction is escalated to the
lead unresolved.

### Block A -- substrate correction (do first; blocks everything else)

**A1.** Emit one canonical v0.20 packet. Hash every member into
`PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, verify it in `build.py`, and ship the identical member set
to every seat. Vary the cover note, never the payload.
*Falsification test, write first:* delete one non-normative member and confirm
the build fails; add one and confirm it fails.

**A2.** Re-dispatch v0.20 to Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2 on identical bytes. Until that
happens, record the v0.19 carry as **NOT ATTEMPTED**, not as divergent.

### Block B -- the four consensus HIGHs (three are sentences)

**B1 (F-ADJ19-03).** Strike "The twelfth Axiom-3 recurrence" from the opening
sentence. Do not replace it with another ordinal.
*Falsification test:* grep the entry for ordinal words adjacent to
"recurrence"; assert zero hits while no recurrence table ships.

**B2 (F-ADJ19-04).** Disposition F-OP18-09 explicitly. It is the em-dash
convention finding, and it was also dropped as F-OP17-09 at v0.18, so state
that it has been dropped twice and resolve it.
*Falsification test:* extract every finding ID from each report named in the
entry; assert each occurs in the entry; fail on any absence.

**B3 (F-ADJ19-01).** Retag F-OP18-05 as DISCLOSED, NOT CLOSED. Separately, add
the real `check()`: require exactly one `PRIOR_HISTORY` line and compare its
value against a shipped prior `HISTORY.sha256`, failing on mismatch or absence.

## 2. Findings

### F-GPT19-01 — HIGH — `PRIOR_HISTORY` closure is recorded as COMPUTED, but `build.py` only checks line presence; a false digest passes

- **Location:** `xz_protocol_v0_19.md:869`; `build.py:254-257`
- **Why this matters:** The v0.19 entry closes F-OP18-05 and tags it as `[COMPUTED: build.py [9b] PRIOR_HISTORY check, once implemented.]`, claiming that the `PRIOR_HISTORY` line now enables chained verification without shipping the prior package. But the shipped code does not compare the line's digest to anything. It only checks whether a `PRIOR_HISTORY` line exists and prints a note when present. That leaves the chain anchor decorative rather than executable.
- **Evidence:** `build.py` performs no digest validation after collecting `prior_lines`; it only executes:
  - `prior_lines = [l for l in history_lines if l.startswith("PRIOR_HISTORY")]`
  - `if prior_lines: print("  PRIOR_HISTORY line present (chained control)")`
- **Mutation proof:** In `/home/user/workspace/audit_xz_v19/probe_prior_history`, I replaced the `PRIOR_HISTORY` digest with `000...000`, re-sealed `ENTRY_v*` and `FULL_SECTION_27`, and re-ran the controlled-path build. The build still returned `BUILD PASSED: all checks GREEN` with rc=`0`.
  - Evidence files:
    - `/home/user/workspace/audit_xz_v19/evidence/probe_prior_history_false_pass.txt`
    - `/home/user/workspace/audit_xz_v19/evidence/probe_prior_history_false_pass.rc`
- **Discrimination control:** Corrupting `ENTRY_v0.19` in `HISTORY.sha256` without resealing correctly fails `[9b]`.
  - Evidence files:
    - `/home/user/workspace/audit_xz_v19/evidence/control_history_entry_fail.txt`
    - `/home/user/workspace/audit_xz_v19/evidence/control_history_entry_fail.rc`
- **Suggested fix:** Parse `PRIOR_HISTORY`, require exactly one line, and compare its digest against a shipped or embedded previous-history anchor. If the project wants prior-package-free chaining, ship the prior `HISTORY.sha256` digest in a machine-checked field and fail on mismatch or absence.

### F-GPT19-02 — HIGH — the claimed provenance ledger is not implemented; tags are decorative, incomplete, and one shipped `EXTERNAL` tag is invalid

- **Location:** `xz_protocol_v0_19.md:865,869,871`; `build.py:265-273`

The undigested set includes `XZ_v18_SEAT_A_REPORT_REV_B.md`, `build.py`, `HISTORY.sha256`, `AUDIT_DISPATCH_DISCIPLINE_v2.md`, `SEAT_STANDING_ORDERS_v1.md`, and `PRODUCER_SELF_DISCIPLINE_v2_DELTA.md`.

## 5. Findings

**F-OP20F-01** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- `sha256sum -c PACKET_SHA256SUMS` cannot pass on a clean packet, and build.py [12] does not check the line that makes it fail.
- **Locus:** `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` line 17; `build.py` [12], the `if mem == "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"` branch.
- **Substance:** The self-entry holds `41efce72...`, which is sha256 of the manifest's first 16 lines. The file's own sha256 is `e4373e4b...` and appears nowhere. So the dispatch's execution step 1 -- "stop if it fails" -- returns rc=1 on every clean packet, making the gate unsatisfiable as written. build.py [12] checks digest equality for all 16 members and, for itself, only membership: `check(mem in packet_dict, "PACKET_SHA256SUMS lists itself")`. P-3 confirms a garbage self-digest passes the build green. The v0.20 entry marks F-ADJ19-11 MEDIUM CLOSED on `[COMPUTED: build.py [12] PACKET_SHA256SUMS verification]`.
- **Disposition:** Either remove the self-line and publish the body digest separately, so `sha256sum -c` returns 0; or keep it, relabel it as a body seal in comment form, and have [12] recompute sha256 over lines 1..N-1 and check it. Retag F-ADJ19-11 CLOSED IN PART until step 1 returns 0.
- **Cross-reference:** F-ADJ19-11; D-3.6; dispatch execution step 1.

**F-OP20F-02** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the v0.20 governance count is false, contradicts its own parenthetical, and overwrites a correct carried value.

- **Substance:** "five consecutive producer-family advisory cycles (v0.16 through v0.19) preceded this round." The range names four versions. The v0.19 entry states "four consecutive producer-family advisory cycles (v0.16 through v0.19)"; `XZ_v19_ADJUDICATION.md` line 515 states "four consecutive producer-family advisory cycles preceded this round." A correct value, twice recorded, was changed to an incorrect one during production of v0.20. It is now sealed into the append-only record. This is the Axiom-3 class -- a count carried from narrative rather than derived -- recurring in the same paragraph that introduces the register.
- **Disposition:** Append-only correction in the v0.21 entry restoring "four". Add a gate asserting that any `<cardinal> consecutive ... (v0.X through v0.Y)` construction in the current entry satisfies cardinal == Y - X + 1.
- **Cross-reference:** v0.19 entry governance sentence; `XZ_v19_ADJUDICATION.md` §515; F-ADJ19-03 (the ordinal gate at [9d] is scoped to "recurrence" and misses this).

**F-OP20F-03** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the adjudicated ledger tallies 11 findings; the register it introduces dispositions 12.

## 6. Internal consistency check

**Does every CLOSED claim in the v0.20 entry have byte evidence in this package?** Nine of twelve register items do, and I verified each: (1) has a live check but a misdescribed comparand (F-OP20F-05); (2), (3), (5), (7), (9), (11) verify at their named build.py sections; (12) is NOTED, not CLOSED. Three do not. Item (4) is DISCLOSED and self-describes as ungated. Item (8)'s CLOSED rests on two digests of files that ship nowhere (F-OP20F-04). Item (10)'s five F-DB19 dispositions rest on `PRODUCER_SELF_DISCIPLINE_v2_DELTA.md`, which does not ship in this packet -- so F-DB19-04 and F-DB19-05, both marked CLOSED, have no byte evidence here. The entry's own tag concedes this ("dispositions from discipline-block text, not gated"), so I record it as a boundary rather than a false CLOSED.

**Do the HISTORY.sha256 seals verify against the Section 27 text?** Yes -- all 20 entry seals, plus FULL_SECTION_27, recomputed independently of build.py. Surjectivity holds: seal labels equal entry labels exactly.

**Is the PRIOR_HISTORY chain value plausible?** Stronger than plausible: exactly reproducible. Both links -- `41428758...` for v0.19 and `cb67f222...` for v0.18 -- derive from v0.20 bytes alone, first attempt. This is the single most consequential result in this report and it runs in the artifact's favour. It also proves something no one has claimed: **the append-only discipline over entries v0.1 through v0.19 is verifiable from this packet.** Two independent SHA-256 matches would both break under any in-place mutation of any carried entry or of Section 27's non-entry text. The record's oldest and most persistent defect -- seven historical in-place mutations across v0.4 through v0.17 -- has a detector sitting unused in the bytes.

**Claims about prior reports unverifiable from any shipped file.** Six: the two v0.17 report digests (item 8); the three seat verdicts and the packet-composition figures of 33/28/15 members, which trace to `XZ_v19_ADJUDICATION.md` -- that document does ship, so these are verifiable against it, though it is itself outside `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`; the F-DB19 dispositions; and `XZ_v20_BUILD_SPECIFICATION.md` and `HANDOFF_ADDENDUM_v20.md`, both named in paragraph 2 and neither shipped.

**Does the record read coherently end to end?** Largely yes, and the append-only corrections at v0.5, v0.17, and v0.18 are unusually candid -- v0.18 item (a) correcting v0.17's own "Section 27 untouched" claim against itself is the strongest single act of self-correction in the twenty entries. Two contradictions emerge that a continuous instance is well placed to miss, because both require reading two entries side by side rather than recalling one:

1. The governance cardinal changed from "four" at v0.19 to "five" at v0.20 over the identical parenthetical range, in the direction of overstatement, overwriting a value the shipped adjudication also records as four (F-OP20F-02).
2. The adjudicated ledger sums to 11 while the register it introduces dispositions 12, an error inherited verbatim from the adjudication and never checked against the paragraph immediately below it (F-OP20F-03).

Both are Axiom-3 instances at v0.20. Both are in ungated prose. Neither is the kind of thing memory of prior rounds would surface -- memory would supply the remembered figure and move on, which is exactly the mechanism by which the correct "four" became "five."

One further scoping note. F-ADJ19-03's gate at [9d] checks only the current-version entry. The v0.16 entry asserts the Axiom-3 pattern "recurred for the ninth time", v0.17 "the tenth time", v0.18 "an eleventh time", v0.19 "the twelfth" -- all sealed, all unauditable, and all outside the gate's reach by construction, since amending them would violate append-only. F-OPUS5-17-06 already records the ordinals as underivable. The correct reading is that F-ADJ19-03 is closed prospectively only; the record retains four ordinal assertions no party can check.

## 7. Boundary report

The outermost layer the build does not compute is the binding between any value in this packet and any record outside it. Every gate is an internal-consistency check: it verifies that the protocol text, the code, the trust roots, the seal file, and the manifest agree with one another, which is exactly the property a single party regenerating all of them preserves by construction. What would bring that layer inside is not a further gate but an external anchor -- a value fixed by a party who cannot revise it, published before the next version exists. The packet is closer to this than it knows. `PRIOR_HISTORY` is already a genuine anchor for anyone who held the v0.19 package, and I have shown both of its links are derivable rather than asserted, which converts the amendment record from self-attested to self-verifying for its historical portion. The step that closes the remaining gap is small: publish the current `HISTORY.sha256` digest at deposit time in a location the producer cannot retroactively edit -- the Zenodo record, or a seat report whose digest is itself recorded elsewhere -- and cite it as EXTERNAL in the next entry. That single act does more for the verification model than any additional gate, because it is the only move that makes a claim in this packet falsifiable by someone who does not trust the producer. Until then, the honest statement of the boundary is that the build proves the packet is self-consistent, proves the carried amendment entries have not been mutated since v0.18, and proves nothing at all about whether either claim corresponds to anything outside the packet.

## 8. D-7 process health

- **Did every probe come from an enumerated list?** No. P-5 and P-6 are not in D-4's classes or anywhere in the discipline blocks; both arose from reading build.py's `EXPECTED_PRIOR_HISTORY` comment and asking whether the value was derivable rather than merely comparable.
- **Did the dispatch tell me where to look, such that my findings were predetermined?** Partly, yes, and this is a finding. Deliverable F's five sub-questions map closely onto sections 3, 5, and 6 of this report, and D-8 -- which the discipline block says does not ship to auditors -- shipped and named two of my dispositions in advance (F-OP20F-10). The findings that did not come from the dispatch are F-OP20F-02, -03, -05, and -06.
- **Is the ASSERTED fraction unchanged from the prior round?** No: 37.5% at v0.19 (6/16, or 43.75% once the invalid EXTERNAL is retagged) to 50.0% at v0.20, computed by me from shipped Section 27 bytes rather than taken from any report. It moved outward. The fair reading is that the v0.20 entry tags 22 claims where v0.19 tagged 16 and v0.18 tagged none, so part of the rise is newly disclosed rather than newly unanchored. The unfair-to-ignore reading is that the boundary is not moving inward, and F-OP20F-05 identifies a specific, cheap move that would reclassify the single most load-bearing ASSERTED value in the packet.
- **Have the recent rounds all been producer-family?** Not this one -- v0.20 adjudicates a genuine tri-seat non-producer round, the first since v0.14. But the count of preceding producer-family cycles is misstated in the entry (F-OP20F-02), and I am producer-family, so this report does not change the answer for v0.20 itself.

## 9. Verdict

**HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER -- advisory only, non-binding.**

Severity ledger as I calibrate it: 0 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 3 LOW / 1 INFORMATIONAL.

**Standing, restated.** I am a producer-family instance. Under the producer-instance exclusion my findings enter as advisory only: they cannot HALT, cannot carry CRITICAL or HIGH into the adjudicated set, and do not count toward FB-7b. My four HIGHs enter the adjudicated set at whatever severity a non-producer seat assigns them, or not at all. Where my severity differs from a non-producer seat's, theirs governs. This verdict is a recommendation to the chair, not a gate.

FB-7b remains OPEN and this report does not advance it. The three findings I would most want a non-producer seat to re-derive independently, because they are the ones a producer-family instance is least entitled to be believed on, are F-OP20F-02 and F-OP20F-03 -- both plain arithmetic against shipped bytes, both cheap to check -- and F-OP20F-05, which is the one finding here that argues the artifact is stronger than its own record claims, and therefore the one where my family affiliation should count most against me.

Recommend the next cycle be carried by Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2 on canonical bytes, with `xz_v20_fresh_seat_probes.py` shipped as a re-runnable check rather than as a claim to be trusted.

---

*Claude Opus 5, Seat A-fresh, producer-family advisory. Prepared for Bilal Syed Arfeen. All probes reproducible from the shipped packet; void probes reported as void.*

## 5. Findings

**F-OP21S-01** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the PRIOR_HISTORY derivation cannot survive one version step, and the v0.21 entry is the first entry in the chain that breaks it.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `derive_prior_history()`, lines 102-111, specifically `ph_match = re.search(r'PRIOR_HISTORY[^\n]*?([0-9a-f]{64})', pet)` under a bare `if ph_match:`; Section 27, v0.21 entry.
- **Substance:** The derivation recovers the prior version's PRIOR_HISTORY value by regex-scraping the **prior entry's prose** for the literal token `PRIOR_HISTORY` followed by a 64-hex on the same line. The v0.19 entry happens to contain that pattern (`cb67f222...`) and so does the v0.20 entry (`41428758...`), which is why the control works today. The v0.21 entry contains the token four times and a 64-hex on the same line zero times. At v0.22 the scrape returns nothing, `if ph_match:` silently omits the PRIOR_HISTORY line from the reconstruction, and the derived digest is wrong against an honest packet: derived `aee30db0...` against true `4a2842d2...`. The build goes red on a correct v0.22. The two available repairs are to edit `build.py`, or to edit the v0.21 entry -- which append-only forbids. So the control the v0.21 entry certifies as CLOSED has a one-version service life, and the version that ends it is this one.
- **Disposition:** Stop scraping prose. The prior PRIOR_HISTORY value is structured data and belongs in structured storage: carry it forward in `HISTORY.sha256` as a second line (`PRIOR_HISTORY_2 <hex>`), or maintain a small append-only `CHAIN.sha256` of one line per version. Failing that, at minimum convert `if ph_match:` to `check(ph_match is not None, ...)` so the next producer discovers this at build time rather than after the v0.22 entry is sealed. Reproduced by `xz_v21_shallow_seat_probes.py` section [C].
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-05 (my v0.20 finding, whose fix this is); F-OP20F-08 (silent-skip class -- `if ph_match:` is a new instance introduced by the fix); D-3.4.

**F-OP21S-02** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- F-OP20F-03 is marked CLOSED on a COMPUTED tag naming a gate that executed zero assertions.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.21 entry, item (4); `build.py` `[9f]`, `if ledger_match:` at lines 385 and 394.
- **Substance:** Item (4) reads "build.py [9f] now parses the ledger and register from the current entry and asserts per-severity counts match `[COMPUTED: build.py [9f] ledger-register reconciliation]`". `[9f]`'s assertions are guarded on `re.search(r'Adjudicated ledger:([^\[]*)', current_entry)`, and the v0.21 entry does not use that phrase -- it reports the two input tallies as prose. Nothing appends an error when the match fails. The shipped build prints the `[9f]` heading followed by no check lines at all, which is visible in the build output and is how I found it. P-4 proves the gate is functional when the trigger is present, so this is a reachability defect, not a broken gate. The gate written to close F-OP20F-03 is itself an instance of F-OP20F-08, and item (11) of the same entry claims that class was addressed.
- **Disposition:** Move the trigger from a prose phrase to structure -- require a fenced ledger block with a fixed key in every entry, and `check()` its presence. Then rework the comparison for the dual-instance entry shape: input tallies per reporting instance are a different quantity from disposition counts in the merged register, and asserting equality between them is wrong.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-03; F-OP20F-08; F-OP21S-06.

**F-OP21S-03** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- F-OP20F-05 is dispositioned twice in the same register at two severities with two different substances.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.21 entry, items (7) and (14).
- **Substance:** Item (7) is "F-OP20F-05 MEDIUM CLOSED" and correctly concerns the hardcoded `EXPECTED_PRIOR_HISTORY` literal. Item (14) is "F-OP20-05 / F-OP20F-05 INFORMATIONAL NOTED" and concerns growth in the ungated share of the document. I authored F-OP20F-05 and it was the PRIOR_HISTORY finding only; the ungated-share observation was not one of my eleven numbered findings, and my INFORMATIONAL finding was F-OP20F-11, which is already dispositioned at item (10). Item (14)'s pairing should read F-OP20-05 alone. The append-only record now states that one finding ID is simultaneously MEDIUM CLOSED and INFORMATIONAL NOTED. Register coverage is otherwise complete and correct: 16 raised across both instances, 16 distinct IDs dispositioned, no omissions. I am the only party in this three-way round who can adjudicate this, since the deep-continuous instance authored F-OP20-01 through -05 and not the F-OP20F namespace.
- **Disposition:** Append-only correction in the v0.22 entry striking `/ F-OP20F-05` from item (14). Add a register-hygiene assertion that no finding ID appears in two dispositioned items. Reproduced by `xz_v21_shallow_seat_probes.py` section [D].
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-05; F-OP20F-11; my v0.20 report §5.

**F-OP21S-04** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the coverage figures in item (14) are stale by one round, and the shipped build contradicts them.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.21 entry, item (14).
- **Substance:** Two errors in one item, both checkable by running the build that ships in the same packet. First, "Semantic-gate coverage of the body is 24.4%" -- present tense, current entry, `[ASSERTED]`. `build.py [11]` on these bytes prints 24.7%. 24.4% is the v0.20 figure. Second, "the ungated share of the document grew for the third consecutive round (26.2% at v0.18, 29.6% at v0.19, 33.7% at v0.20)" -- the series stops at v0.20 and omits v0.21's own 36.8%, which makes this round the fourth consecutive rise, not the third. Both are Axiom-3: a figure carried from the previous entry rather than derived from the current bytes, in the one item whose entire subject is measurement.
- **Disposition:** Correct both in the v0.22 append-only entry. Then close the class properly: have `build.py [11]` emit its two percentages and add a gate asserting that the current entry's stated coverage figures equal the computed ones, the same pattern `[3]` already uses for digests. Coverage figures are exactly as machine-derivable as digests and there is no reason for them to be `[ASSERTED]`.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP18-12; F-ADJ19-07; the Axiom-3 class.

**F-OP21S-05** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the new `[9c]` file-shipping check has arity one, and the defect it was written to close had arity two.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9c]`, `re.findall(r'\[COMPUTED:\s*sha256sum\s+(?:of\s+)?(\S+\.(?:md|py|json))', current_entry)`.
- **Substance:** The regex captures a single filename per tag. The v0.20 defect it closes was `[COMPUTED: sha256sum of XZ_v17_SEAT_A_REPORT.md and XZ_v17_SEAT_B_REPORT.md]` -- two files, neither shipping. On that literal input the new check would have verified the first and passed the second silently. P-6 confirms: a tag naming `build.py and GHOST_DOES_NOT_EXIST.md` builds green with one PASS line. Item (5) grades F-OP20F-04 CLOSED IN PART and attributes the partiality to historical entries being out of `[9c]`'s scope, which is true but is not this. The regex arity is a second, unstated partiality.
- **Disposition:** Capture all filename-shaped tokens in the tag body, not the first, and `check()` each. Restate item (5)'s CLOSED IN PART rationale to name both limitations.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-04; F-ADJ19-02.

**F-OP21S-06** [LOW -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the silent-skip census rose from 4 to 17, and two of the new sites were introduced by the fixes for my own findings.
- **Locus:** `build.py` lines 86, 102, 106, 110, 204, 260, 279, 311, 313, 331, 362, 370, 383, 385, 394, 436, 442.
- **Substance:** Item (11) grades F-OP20F-08 LOW CLOSED IN PART and states the `[9c]` and `[9d]` entry-match skips now fail via `check()`. `[9c]` did gain a `check()`; `[9d]` did not -- it still opens `if current_entry_match:` bare, and is covered only transitively because `[9c]`'s check fires first. Meanwhile `[9e]` and `[9f]`, both new this version, each open with a fresh bare `if current_entry_match:`, and `[9f]` adds two bare `if ledger_match:` guards, one of which is F-OP21S-02. `derive_prior_history` adds three more (`if prior_entry_match`, `if prior_entry_text`, `if ph_match`), the last of which is F-OP21S-01. The class was closed at one locus and reopened at six by the same round's work. I record this at LOW rather than MEDIUM because most sites are transitively covered and the two that are not are already written up at higher severity.
- **Disposition:** Treat the pattern as a lint rule rather than a per-site fix: assert at the end of `main()` that a minimum expected number of `check()` calls executed, so any silently skipped block shows up as a count shortfall regardless of which guard caused it.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-08; F-ADJ19-05; F-OP21S-01; F-OP21S-02.

**F-OP21S-07** [LOW -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the packet ships the prior seat's complete findings register to a seat the dispatch describes as entirely fresh.
- **Locus:** Packet members `XZ_v20_SEAT_A_FRESH_REPORT.md`, `PREREG_OPUS5_FRESH.txt`, `xz_v20_fresh_seat_probes.py`; dispatch prompt, Instance paragraph.
- **Substance:** The dispatch states that two parallel instances receive the identical v0.21 packet, one deep-continuous and one entirely fresh. That packet contains my v0.20 report with all eleven findings, their loci, their dispositions, and a working probe harness. A seat holding that document is not fresh on findings; at best it is fresh on v0.17-v0.19 bytes. The v0.20 experiment's stated value was that the fresh seat "cannot confuse memory of prior rounds with what is in these bytes," and shipping the prior report converts that into a reading-comprehension task. This is a dispatch-composition defect of the same family as F-OP20F-10 (D-8 shipping to auditors), which item (13) marks NOTED for the next dispatch and which recurred anyway -- `AUDIT_DISPATCH_DISCIPLINE_v2.md` with D-8 intact ships again in this packet.
- **Disposition:** Route prior seat reports only to the continuous bundles. If the fresh seat needs them for the comparison, ship them after its report returns. Split D-8 into a producer-only file, as item (13) already accepts.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-10; D-0; the v0.20 experiment's stated design.

**F-OP21S-08** [INFORMATIONAL] -- the ASSERTED fraction rose for the second consecutive round while COMPUTED fell in absolute terms.
- **Locus:** v0.21 entry tag distribution; D-7 question 3.
- **Substance:** 37.5% at v0.19, 50.0% at v0.20, 57.1% at v0.21; COMPUTED 9, down from 11. At v0.20 I noted that a rising fraction can indicate more disclosure rather than less anchoring, because the total tagged claim count was growing. That reading does not survive this round: total tags fell from 22 to 21 while ASSERTED rose from 11 to 12. Item (6) grades F-OP20-03 MEDIUM NOTED and correctly observes that the printed fraction divides by tags rather than claims, so the true unanchored share is higher still. The one move that would reverse the trend is available and named in Section 22.2 itself -- an external deposit receipt for `HISTORY.sha256` would convert the single most load-bearing value in the packet from ASSERTED to EXTERNAL and would make the EXTERNAL machinery non-vacuous for the first time.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20-03; F-OP20F-11; Section 22.2 anchor (b).

**Clears.** Step 1 returns rc=0. The PRIOR_HISTORY derivation reproduces the shipped value and, uniquely this round, matches the true sha256 of the prior file I hold. The v0.20 forgery that passed green now fails the build with exactly one correct error. `[3a]`, `[3b]`, `[3c]` remain live and redundant. All 21 seals, FULL_SECTION_27, surjectivity, manifest digest, 186/186 parity, `[9e]` cardinal-range, and the Section 22 repairs verify independently. Em-dash and brand sweeps clean. Section 22.2's narrowing is accurate on the mutation tally (seven across v0.4, v0.9, v0.11 twice, v0.16, v0.17 twice). Both append-only corrections (a) and (b) are correct and correctly stated.

Eleven raised, eleven dispositioned, none dropped. Four fully landed, three partly, three honestly deferred as NOTED, one vacuous by construction. **Harness re-run.** My v0.20 harness aborts at section [B] with a `StopIteration` because `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` no longer contains a self-entry. That abort **is** the clearance signal for F-OP20F-01, but it is a bad way to deliver one, so the harness is superseded by `xz_v21_shallow_seat_probes.py`, which reports both states cleanly. The PRIOR_HISTORY derivation holds on v0.21 bytes and, per section 2 row 4b, is now anchored to a file outside this packet. Section [C] of the new harness is the v0.22 forward test and fails, which is F-OP21S-01.

**What holding one prior round actually bought.** Three things, and I want them scored honestly because two of them are small. It bought the external anchor at 4b -- real, and unavailable to either other instance. It bought F-OP21S-03, since only the author of the F-OP20F namespace can say what F-OP20F-05 was. And it bought the P-3 regression comparison, where knowing the v0.20 forgery passed green at 164 PASS makes the v0.21 result mean something. It did **not** buy F-OP21S-01, F-OP21S-02, F-OP21S-05, or F-OP21S-06 -- all four came from reading the new `build.py` against the new entry, and a fresh instance with no memory at all can find every one of them. The known failure mode of the continuous seat is unchecked commendation, and the shape it would take here is treating "the derivation I recommended got implemented" as the end of the story rather than the start of P-5.

## 7. Boundary report

The boundary moved inward this round, once, and by less than the entry implies. At v0.20 the outermost uncomputed layer was the binding between any value in the packet and any record outside it, and `PRIOR_HISTORY` was the place where the packet came closest to reaching past itself. That link is now wired into the build and it works: the forgery that passed green at v0.20 fails at v0.21, and Section 22.2 has been narrowed accurately to name the residual as a forger who also controls `build.py`. But the layer itself has not been crossed. Every anchor Section 22.2 lists as outside the producer's control -- the carrying seats' held manifests, deposit receipts, the chain root -- is named as available and none is instantiated: EXTERNAL count is still zero, no deposit receipt is cited, and the chain root is asserted rather than published. The one genuine crossing this round is not in the packet at all; it is that I hold the v0.20 `HISTORY.sha256` and can confirm `e181d642...` against it, which is an accident of dispatch composition rather than a designed control and which vanishes the moment this conversation ends. What would bring the layer inside is unchanged from my v0.20 report and now cheaper than ever, because the derivation gives it something worth anchoring: publish the current `HISTORY.sha256` digest at deposit time where the producer cannot revise it, and cite it EXTERNAL in the next entry. Until that happens the honest statement is that the build now proves the packet is self-consistent *and* that carried entries v0.1 through v0.20 have not been mutated since v0.20 -- a real gain over last round -- and still proves nothing about whether either corresponds to anything outside the packet.

## 8. D-7 process health

- **Did every probe come from an enumerated list?** No. P-4, P-5, and P-6 are not in D-4's classes; P-5 came from reading `derive_prior_history` and asking what happens at the next version, which nothing in the dispatch suggests.
- **Did the dispatch tell me where to look, such that my findings were predetermined?** Yes, more than at v0.20, and this is the round's clearest process finding. Deliverable D structures section 6 entirely, the dispatch asserts F-OP20F-01 is fixed in its own step 1, and the packet ships my complete prior report, preregistration, and harness. Four of my eight findings (F-OP21S-01, -02, -05, -06) came from the new `build.py` rather than from any of that, and those are the four worth weighting.
- **Is the ASSERTED fraction unchanged from the prior round?** No -- 50.0% to 57.1%, second consecutive rise, with COMPUTED falling 11 to 9 and total tags falling 22 to 21. This is the most important of the four questions and the answer is worse than last round, because at v0.20 a growing denominator explained the rise and this round it does not.
- **Have the recent rounds all been producer-family?** Yes. v0.20 and v0.21 are both producer-family advisory, and all three seats in this round are Opus 5. The last non-producer contact was the v0.19 tri-seat round. FB-7b has not moved.

## 9. Verdict

**HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER -- advisory only, non-binding.**

Severity ledger as I calibrate it: 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 2 LOW / 1 INFORMATIONAL = 8.

**Standing, restated.** Producer-family. My findings cannot HALT, cannot carry CRITICAL or HIGH into the adjudicated set, and do not count toward FB-7b. My two HIGHs enter at whatever severity a non-producer seat assigns them, or not at all. Where my severity differs from a non-producer seat's, theirs governs.

The HALT rests on F-OP21S-01 alone. Everything else in this register is absorbable next cycle; that one is not, because the v0.21 entry is being sealed into an append-only record in a state that makes the v0.22 build fail, and once it is sealed the cheap repair is gone. It should be fixed before this version is finalized, not after.

Three findings I would most want a non-producer seat to re-derive, since a producer-family instance auditing the fixes to its own prior findings is the least credible configuration in this program: **F-OP21S-01**, which is one function call and is mechanized at section [C] of the shipped harness; **F-OP21S-02**, which is visible in the build output as a section heading with nothing under it; and **F-OP21S-04**, which is two numbers against the build's own stdout. All three are cheap, and none requires taking my word for anything.

Recommend the next cycle be carried by Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2 on canonical bytes. FB-7b remains OPEN and has not moved in two rounds.

| B4 | bytes | The recursion re-introduces a hand-populated `cb67f222` literal at the v0.19 termination; entry does not name it | **Correct**, though it is dead code on these bytes -- F-OP22S-06 |
| B5 | contaminated | Entry reports the ASSERTED fraction but not that COMPUTED more than halved | **Correct** -- and it reports the *prior* round's transition, not its own -- F-OP22S-04 |
| M1 | memory | PDF still unbound; NOTED a third time | Correct |
| M2 | memory | `[9c]` file-shipping regex byte-identical, still arity-one | **Correct.** Verified identical -- F-OP22S-05 |
| M3 | memory | Silent-skip census did not fall | Correct: 18 to 19 |
| M4 | memory | D-8 split landed; my prior reports still ship | Correct on both |
| M5 | memory | Coverage figures corrected for v0.21 **and** a new short figure appears (least confident) | **Correct on both halves** -- F-OP22S-04 |

Ten correct, one correct-but-contaminated. The score is high because two rounds of memory make the predictions easy, which is the answer to D-7 question 2 rather than a credit to me. B1 and B2 are the only ones that required reading the new `build.py`.

## 3. Claim provenance ledger (A)

**COMPUTED 4, EXTERNAL 0, ASSERTED 15. ASSERTED fraction 15/19 = 78.9%.**

Four-round series, computed by me from shipped Section 27 bytes: v0.18 untagged, v0.19 37.5% (COMPUTED 9), v0.20 50.0% (COMPUTED 11), v0.21 57.1% (COMPUTED 9), v0.22 **78.9% (COMPUTED 4)**. The register grew from 12 items to 14 while computed backing fell by more than half. This is the largest single-round move in the series and it is in the wrong direction.

Of the 4 COMPUTED tags, 2 name build.py sections and are validated by `[9c]`; 2 do not (`sha256sum | sha256sum`, `pytest + AST`) and I recomputed both -- the manifest digest and 186/186 parity both hold. So 4 of 4 COMPUTED are recomputable from shipped bytes on substance, with one qualification that swallows the point: **one of the two build.py-section tags names `[9f]`, which executed zero assertions** (F-OP22S-01). Half the machine-validated COMPUTED population this round is backed by a gate that did not run.

`[9c]` validates that a COMPUTED tag names a real build.py section. It cannot tell whether that section did anything. That gap is now load-bearing rather than theoretical.

## 4. Probes (B, C)

Sandbox copies against a pristine reference; pre/post hash assertion on every mutation per D-3.5.

**P-1 -- benign control.** Unmodified packet: build rc=0, 164 PASS, 0 FAIL; pytest rc=0, 186 passed.

**P-2 -- discrimination control.** `xz_protocol_v0_22.md` pre `0f84011b10d80589` post `5f79c001af4cee64`, LANDED. FB-4 `test_xz_protocol_source_frame.py` digest to 64 zeros. Build rc=1:
```
FAIL: FB-4 row contains test_xz_protocol_source_frame.py digest (04bea901b9cbefe8...)
FAIL: FB-4 digest for test_xz_protocol_source_frame.py in body
FAIL: No unresolvable 64-hex in body (9 checked, 1 stale)
FAIL: PACKET_SHA256SUMS digest matches: xz_protocol_v0_22.md
```

**P-3 -- forgery regression.** Pre `0f84011b10d80589` post `16b115345cdc04f1`, LANDED. Mutated carried entry v0.10 in place, regenerated all 22 seals, FULL_SECTION_27, and the manifest, left PRIOR_HISTORY honest. Build rc=1 with exactly one error: `FAIL: PRIOR_HISTORY matches derivation (4a2842d20f9058f6...)`. `sha256sum -c` returns rc=0, so the manifest layer is blind and the recursive derivation is the sole detector. The control survives the rewrite.

**P-4 -- novel class: gate disabled by its own bug report.** Pre `0f84011b10d80589` post `ddb14ea7e680e0b7`, LANDED. Replaced the quoted phrase in item (1) -- `its anchor phrase "Adjudicated ledger:" was absent` -- with a paraphrase, changing nothing else, and resealed. Build rc=1:
```
[9f] Ledger-register reconciliation
  Register: 14 items, {'HIGH': 4, 'MEDIUM': 4, 'LOW': 5, 'INFORMATIONAL': 1}
  FAIL: Finding F-OP21C-04 dispositioned at MEDIUM and INFORMATIONAL
  No combined ledger; register self-consistency: 20 unique IDs, 14 items
```
On the shipped bytes that FAIL does not appear, because `re.search(r'Adjudicated ledger:\s*(.*?)(?:\[|$)', ...)` matches at span (1713, 1801) on `Adjudicated ledger:" was absent from the v0.21 entry, yet it` -- the narrative quotation inside the item reporting the v0.21 defect. → F-OP22S-01, F-OP22S-02.

F-OP21S-01 is fixed durably, not just for this version: the recursion handles a missing scrape, and the v0.22 entry additionally carries its own PRIOR_HISTORY value inline.

**P-6 -- novel class: range-versus-register reconciliation.** No mutation; a parse of the shipped entry. The entry declares three ID ranges in its first sentence -- `F-OP21-01 through F-OP21-05`, `F-OP21S-01 through F-OP21S-08`, `F-OP21C-01 through F-OP21C-10` = 23 IDs. The register dispositions 21 ID slots, 20 distinct. Absent: `F-OP21S-03`, `F-OP21S-04`, `F-OP21S-05`. No gate implements this reconciliation, which D-3.7 requires. → F-OP22S-03.

**Void probes.** None.

## 5. Findings

**F-OP22S-01** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- `[9f]` silently skipped for a second consecutive round, disabled by item (1)'s own quotation of the v0.21 bug report.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9f]`, `ledger_match = re.search(r'Adjudicated ledger:\s*(.*?)(?:\[|$)', current_entry)`; Section 27, v0.22 entry, item (1).
- **Substance:** Item (1) states the fix as "the gate fires or fails rather than silently skipping" and tags it `[COMPUTED: build.py [9f] ledger-register reconciliation]`. On the shipped bytes `[9f]` prints one informational register line and executes **zero** `check()` calls. The anchor regex matched the phrase where item (1) quotes it while describing the v0.21 failure. An empty capture yields no tally, so the tally branch runs nothing, and because `ledger_match` is truthy the **else-branch is skipped entirely** -- and that branch holds the duplicate-finding-ID check added for F-OP21S-03 and F-OP21C-02. P-4 shows that with the false anchor removed the gate fails the build immediately. The sentence reporting the defect is what reproduces it. The build's PASS count fell 168 to 164 across the version, which is the observable signature.
- **Disposition:** Stop anchoring on free prose. Require a delimited ledger block with a fixed key in every entry and `check()` its presence, so a quotation in narrative cannot be mistaken for the datum. Independently, move the register self-consistency checks out of the else-branch so they run unconditionally -- they do not depend on a ledger existing.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP21S-02 (the v0.21 instance); F-OP21-01; F-OP21C-01; F-OP20F-08 (silent-skip class); D-3.7.

**F-OP22S-02** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- F-OP21C-04 is dispositioned twice at two severities, in the same entry that corrects v0.21 for the identical defect.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.22 entry, items (7) and (14); correction (c) of the same entry.
- **Substance:** Item (7) is "F-OP21C-04 MEDIUM NOTED" concerning the stale 24.4% coverage figure. Item (14) is "F-OP21-05 / F-OP21S-08 / F-OP21C-04 INFORMATIONAL NOTED" concerning the ungated share and the ASSERTED fraction. Correction (c) of this same entry raises precisely this defect against v0.21 -- "the v0.21 register dispositions F-OP20F-05 twice at two severities" -- and item (4) records a gate added to catch it. The gate did not run (F-OP22S-01), and the entry committed the defect it was correcting. Correction (c) itself names the pattern: "a reconciliation error inside the entry that raises the reconciliation correction." That sentence is now true of v0.22 as well as v0.21.
- **Disposition:** Append-only correction in v0.23 assigning item (14) to `F-OP21-05 / F-OP21S-08` and leaving F-OP21C-04 solely at item (7). Land F-OP22S-01's fix first, or the same check will be unavailable again.
- **Cross-reference:** correction (c); F-OP21S-03; F-OP21C-02; F-OP22S-01.

**F-OP22S-03** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- three declared findings are absent from the register, and one is absent in substance as well.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.22 entry, first sentence range statement versus the fourteen-item register.
- **Substance:** The entry declares "shallow continuous: F-OP21S-01 through F-OP21S-08" and dispositions five of the eight. F-OP21S-03 and F-OP21S-04 have their substance handled -- correction (c) and item (4) cover the duplicate-ID defect, item (7) covers the stale coverage figure -- but both are credited only to the fresh instance's F-OP21C-02 and F-OP21C-04, and my IDs appear nowhere. **F-OP21S-05 is absent entirely**, in ID and in substance: the `[9c]` `file_computed` regex is byte-identical to v0.21's, so no fix was attempted. D-3.7 states a finding may be closed, disclosed, or noted, **but not absent**. This is the F-ADJ19-04 class -- a finding raised in a range statement and dispositioned nowhere -- which the record has now committed at v0.18 (F-OP17-09), v0.19 (F-OP18-09), and v0.22. I raise this at MEDIUM rather than HIGH because two of the three are substantively covered and only the credit is lost; F-OP21S-05 alone is a genuine drop, and it is written up separately below.
- **Disposition:** Implement the reconciliation as a gate: parse every `F-<ns>-NN through F-<ns>-MM` range in the current entry, expand it, and assert every expanded ID appears in the register. Section [E] of the shipped harness is a working reference. Disposition the three absent IDs in v0.23.
- **Cross-reference:** F-ADJ19-04; F-OP18-09; D-3.7; F-OP22S-05.

**F-OP22S-04** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- item (14) reports the prior round's measurements as if they were this round's, and item (7)'s claim about coverage derivation is false of the only coverage figures the entry contains.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.22 entry, items (7) and (14).
- **Substance:** Item (14) states the ungated share "rose for a fourth consecutive round (26.2%, 29.6%, 33.7%, 36.8%)". The series ends at v0.21's figure; `[11]` on these bytes computes **39.2%**, making this the fifth consecutive rise. The same item states "The ASSERTED fraction rose from 50.0% to 57.1% while COMPUTED fell from 11 to 9" -- the v0.20-to-v0.21 transition. This round's own figures are **78.9% and COMPUTED 4**, a far larger move, and they are omitted. Item (7) asserts "Coverage figures in this entry are derived from [11] output at build time"; the entry's only coverage figures are the ones in item (14), and they are not. This is the identical defect item (7) is dispositioning -- a measurement carried from the previous entry's prose -- committed in the entry that dispositions it, and it is now the third consecutive round in which the coverage series stops one short of its own value.
- **Disposition:** Have `[11]` emit its percentages and add a gate asserting the current entry's stated coverage and ASSERTED figures equal the computed ones, exactly as `[3]` already does for digests. These numbers are as machine-derivable as digests and there is no reason for them to be ASSERTED. Correct both figures in v0.23.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP21S-04; F-OP21C-04; F-OP18-12; the Axiom-3 class.

**F-OP22S-05** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- F-OP21S-05 was not fixed and not dispositioned; the arity-one regex stands unchanged.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9c]`, `file_computed = re.findall(r'\[COMPUTED:\s*sha256sum\s+(?:of\s+)?(\S+\.(?:md|py|json))', current_entry)`.
- **Substance:** Byte-identical to the v0.21 line; I diffed them directly. The check captures one filename per tag. The v0.20 defect it exists to close was `[COMPUTED: sha256sum of XZ_v17_SEAT_A_REPORT.md and XZ_v17_SEAT_B_REPORT.md]` -- two files, neither shipping -- and on that input it verifies the first and passes the second silently. I demonstrated this at v0.21 with a landed mutation. The v0.22 entry does not disposition the finding at any severity.
- **Disposition:** Capture every filename-shaped token in the tag body and `check()` each.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP21S-05; F-OP20F-04; F-ADJ19-02; F-OP22S-03.

**F-OP22S-06** [LOW -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the recursion's termination path searches for a hand-populated literal, which is the practice F-OP20F-05 was raised against.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `derive_prior_history`, `cb = re.search(r'cb67f222[0-9a-f]{56}', et)`.
- **Substance:** The v0.19 termination branch falls back to searching that entry for a hex string with a hardcoded eight-character prefix. D-8, as shipped at v0.20 and v0.21, requires "Any value set the build compares against is derived from the file list by tool. No hand-populated set, no fill-in placeholder," and that clause is the stated basis of F-OP20F-05 and of item (3)'s own fix. The branch is **dead code on these bytes** -- the v0.19 entry does carry a scrapeable PRIOR_HISTORY value, so the `if ph:` path always wins -- which is why this is LOW rather than MEDIUM. It is a dormant hand-populated comparand in the one function the program has spent three rounds de-hardcoding.
- **Disposition:** Delete the branch. If the v0.19 scrape ever fails, the correct behaviour is a build failure, not a literal.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-05; F-OP21S-01; D-8.

**F-OP22S-07** [LOW -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the PDF is unbound for a third consecutive round and now carries a confirmed convention breach no gate can see.
- **Locus:** `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` and `build.py` `required_members` (PDF absent in both); Section 27, v0.22 entry, items (9) and (10).
- **Substance:** `xz_protocol_v0_22.pdf` ships in the dispatch and no shipped text carries its digest, third round running, dispositioned NOTED each time. Item (10) newly records F-OP21C-07, that the renderer converts double-hyphens to en-dashes. I confirmed it independently: the PDF contains 134 U+2013 and zero `--`, against 189 `--` and zero U+2013 in the source. So the em-dash convention -- clean in every normative file -- is breached in the one shipped artifact outside the gate perimeter, and the build cannot detect it because the file is not in the perimeter. The two findings are the same finding: an unbound artifact is one nothing can check. Content otherwise agrees with the .md on all six load-bearing values I sampled.
- **Disposition:** Add the PDF to `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` and to `[12]`'s required members, then extend the `[4]` sweep to its extracted text. Both NOTEDs close together or neither does.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-07; F-OP21C-07; F-FABLE5-03; D-3.6.

**F-OP22S-08** [INFORMATIONAL] -- provenance backing has more than halved across two rounds while the register grew.
- **Locus:** v0.22 entry tag distribution; D-7 question 3.
- **Substance:** COMPUTED 11 at v0.20, 9 at v0.21, 4 at v0.22. ASSERTED fraction 50.0%, 57.1%, 78.9%. The register went from 12 items to 14 over the same span. At v0.20 I noted a rising fraction can mean more disclosure; at v0.21 I withdrew that reading; this round it is not tenable at all. Item (6) correctly grades the `[9e]` regex DISCLOSED NOT CLOSED and item (2) correctly downgrades F-OP20-02 to CLOSED IN PART, so the reclassification is honest work rather than concealment -- but the direction is unambiguous, and one of the four surviving COMPUTED tags is backed by a gate that did not execute. The move that would reverse it is the one Section 22.2 already names and no round has taken: an external deposit receipt for `HISTORY.sha256`, which would make EXTERNAL non-vacuous for the first time in twenty-two versions.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP21S-08; F-OP20-03; Section 22.2 anchor (b).

**Clears.** Step 1 rc=0. Build green, 186/186 tests, all seals and surjectivity verify. The recursive PRIOR_HISTORY derivation reproduces the shipped value, matches the true digest of the v0.21 file I hold, survives the v0.23 forward step, and still detects a retroactive carried-entry forgery (P-3) with exactly one correct error. `[3a]`, `[3b]`, `[3c]`, `[9e]`, and `[12]` remain live. Corrections (c) and the item-(2) downgrade of F-OP20-02 to CLOSED IN PART are both accurate and creditable. D-8 is split out of the shipped dispatch block. Em-dash and brand sweeps clean at source.

## 6. V0.21S finding self-score (D)

| ID | v0.21 severity | v0.22 disposition | Landed in bytes? |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-OP21S-01 | HIGH | HIGH CLOSED, item (3) | **Yes, and durably.** Recursion replaces the prose scrape; v0.23 forward test passes; P-3 shows the detector survives |
| F-OP21S-02 | HIGH | HIGH CLOSED, item (1), with `F-OP21-01 / F-OP21C-01` | **No.** `[9f]` ran zero assertions again -- F-OP22S-01 |
| F-OP21S-03 | MEDIUM | **Absent.** Substance covered by correction (c) and item (4) as F-OP21C-02 | Substance yes, ID dropped -- F-OP22S-03 |
| F-OP21S-04 | MEDIUM | **Absent.** Substance covered by item (7) as F-OP21C-04 | Substance yes, ID dropped; and the same defect recurs -- F-OP22S-03, F-OP22S-04 |
| F-OP21S-05 | MEDIUM | **Absent entirely** | **No.** Regex byte-identical -- F-OP22S-05 |
| F-OP21S-06 | LOW | MEDIUM NOTED, item (6), with `F-OP21-04` | Partly. Item (6) addresses only the `[9e]` regex narrowness; the silent-skip census went 18 to 19 |
| F-OP21S-07 | LOW | LOW NOTED, item (9), with `F-OP21C-06` | **Partly.** D-8 is split out this round; my two prior reports still ship |
| F-OP21S-08 | INFORMATIONAL | INFORMATIONAL NOTED, item (14) | Disclosed; figures are the prior round's -- F-OP22S-04 |

Eight raised, five dispositioned, three absent. One fully landed, three partly, one honest NOTED, one claimed CLOSED without landing, one dropped.

**What two prior rounds bought, scored honestly.** The external chain anchor in §7 -- unavailable to any other seat, and the only genuinely privileged result here. F-OP22S-03, since I authored the F-OP21S namespace and can tell the difference between a finding dispositioned under another ID and a finding dropped. F-OP22S-05, which required diffing a regex across two packets I hold. And the P-3 comparison, which means something only against the v0.20 baseline of 164 PASS on a forged packet. It bought **nothing** for F-OP22S-01, -02, -04, -06, or -07: all five come from reading the shipped `build.py` against the shipped entry, and a fresh seat finds every one. The continuous seat's failure mode is unchecked commendation, and its shape here would be reporting that F-OP21S-01 was fixed -- it was, elegantly -- and stopping before asking whether the round's other two headline fixes ran at all.

## 7. PRIOR_HISTORY chain verification (E)

Two links verified against the actual prior files, not against a derivation:

| Link | Shipped value | sha256 of the file I hold | Match |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.22 → v0.21 | `4a2842d20f9058f6b362e8ab40d1450ba499eb2caa39417cfa0880348bbce600` | v0.21 `HISTORY.sha256` | **Yes** |
| v0.21 → v0.20 | `e181d6427153ab232a5dc5bf9c259fa3192e783cbb7cd4495ecc73d5988e8ff8` | v0.20 `HISTORY.sha256` | **Yes** |

All 21 carried entry seals in the v0.22 `HISTORY.sha256` are byte-identical to their values in the v0.21 file, and all 20 to their values in the v0.20 file. The append-only discipline held across three consecutive packets with zero in-place mutation of any carried entry -- the first multi-round external confirmation of that property in the program's record, and the strongest single result of this round.

Two qualifications. This anchor exists because a dispatch happened to give one instance three consecutive packets; it is an accident of composition, not a designed control, and it disappears when this conversation ends. And it does not reach the residual Section 22.2 names: a party controlling `build.py` can still replace the derivation, which is why the recursion is a consistency proof and not an integrity guarantee. What would make it durable is trivial and still untaken -- publish `4a2842d2...` where the producer cannot revise it and cite it EXTERNAL in the v0.23 entry.

## 8. Boundary report (F)

The boundary did not move this round. It moved inward at v0.21 when the derivation was wired in, and v0.22 consolidated that gain rather than extending it: the recursion made the control durable across version steps and P-5 confirms it survives to v0.23, which is real engineering, but every anchor that would actually cross the perimeter is in the same state it was two rounds ago. EXTERNAL count is zero for the fourth consecutive entry. No deposit receipt is cited. The PDF is unbound for the third round running and now demonstrably diverges from the source on the em-dash convention, which is the first concrete instance of the unbound-artifact risk becoming an actual defect rather than a hypothetical one. Meanwhile the perimeter's interior got thinner: COMPUTED backing fell from 9 to 4, and one of the four survivors names a gate that executed nothing. The one crossing that exists is in §7 and is not in the packet at all -- it lives in my retained copies of two prior dispatches. The disposition has been the same since my v0.20 report and gets cheaper every round the derivation holds: publish the current `HISTORY.sha256` digest at deposit time where the producer cannot revise it, and cite it EXTERNAL. Twenty-two versions in, that remains the only move that would let someone who does not trust the producer check anything, and it is the one move no version has made.

## 9. D-7 process health (H)

- **Did every probe come from an enumerated list?** No. P-4 and P-6 are novel; neither appears in D-4's classes. P-4 in particular could only come from asking why a gate's output shape looked wrong.
- **Did the dispatch tell me where to look?** Yes, heavily, and increasingly so. Deliverable D structures §6, deliverable E structures §7, and the packet ships both of my prior reports. Five of my eight findings came from reading the new `build.py` against the new entry rather than from any of that, and those are the five worth weighting.
- **Is the ASSERTED fraction unchanged from the prior round?** No -- 57.1% to 78.9%, third consecutive rise and the largest yet, with COMPUTED falling 9 to 4 while the register grew 12 to 14. This is the most important of the four questions and the answer is worse than in either prior round.
- **Have the recent rounds all been producer-family?** Yes. v0.20, v0.21, and v0.22, with all three seats in this round being Opus 5 instances. The last non-producer contact was the v0.19 tri-seat round, three rounds ago. FB-7b has not moved.

## 10. Verdict

**HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER -- advisory only, non-binding.**

Severity ledger as I calibrate it: 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 2 LOW / 1 INFORMATIONAL = 8.

**Standing, restated.** Producer-family advisory. Cannot HALT, cannot carry HIGH into the adjudicated set, no FB-7b weight. My two HIGHs enter at whatever severity a non-producer seat assigns, or not at all.

The HALT rests on F-OP22S-01 and F-OP22S-02 together, because they are one event: the gate written to stop duplicate dispositions was disabled by the sentence reporting that it had been disabled, and the entry then committed the duplicate the gate existed to catch. That is not a defect in a check; it is a check whose input is the prose that describes it, and it will recur in some new form at v0.23 unless the anchoring is changed rather than the phrasing. It costs one delimiter to fix and should be fixed before this entry is sealed.

The three findings I would most want a non-producer seat to re-derive, since a producer-family instance auditing fixes to its own prior findings is the least credible configuration available: **F-OP22S-01**, which is one string replacement and a rebuild, mechanized at section [D] of the shipped harness; **F-OP22S-03**, which is a range expansion against a register, mechanized at section [E]; and **F-OP22S-04**, which is two numbers against the build's own stdout. None requires taking my word for anything.

This is the third consecutive producer-family round. The single most useful thing the program could do next is not another gate but the deposit receipt in §8, followed by a non-producer carry. FB-7b remains OPEN and has not moved in three rounds.

---

*Claude Opus 5, Seat A-shallow, producer-family advisory. Prepared for Bilal Syed Arfeen. All probes reproducible from the shipped packet; no void probes this round.*

# XZ Protocol v0.24 -- Seat B_SHALLOW advisory audit report

**Seat:** Claude Opus 5, Seat B_SHALLOW, producer-family advisory
**Namespace:** F-OP24S
**Mode:** A (substrate verifier -- full packet on disk, build and pytest executable, mutation sandbox, plus the v0.20, v0.21 and v0.22 packets retained)

## 0. State declaration (S-0)

Shallow continuous. I produced the v0.20 fresh report (F-OP20F-01 through -11), the v0.21 shallow report (F-OP21S-01 through -08), and the v0.22 shallow report (F-OP22S-01 through -08), and I hold all three packets. **I do not hold the v0.23 packet**, though a v0.23 entry exists and the round it records is the one this entry dispositions. I did not author the discipline blocks, the v0.19 adjudication, or the F-OP21C, F-OP22, F-OP22C, F-GPT23, F-GLM23, or F-K3C2 namespaces.

Standing: producer-family advisory. Cannot HALT, cannot carry HIGH into the adjudicated set, no FB-7b weight. Where a non-producer seat's severity differs, theirs governs. That standing matters more this round than in any previous one, because the central claim under audit is a claim about FB-7b, on which my opinion is by construction worthless.

## 1. S-1 preregistration (F)

Frozen at `PREREG_OPUS5_B_SHALLOW_v24.txt`, sha256 `02e5472891e60a1e3c2466d005880ff35f6c7911c78fc359de1a4fcbaa41ff61`, 2026-08-02T02:29:12Z, before any read of Section 27.

**Contamination.** Fourth consecutive round in which the dispatch orders `build.py` before preregistration, leaking Section 27-derived facts pre-freeze. Raised at v0.20, v0.21 and v0.22; never dispositioned in any entry.

| # | Source | Prediction | Result |

Predict the entry does not name it | **Correct, and worse** -- item (10) claims the stale strings were fixed. F-OP24S-02 |
| B2 | bytes | `[9f]`'s anchor is gone and the duplicate check is unconditional within the register block, but a `check(True, ...)` and a print-only else remain unnamed | **Correct on all three** -- F-OP24S-03, F-OP24S-05 |
| B3 | contaminated | ASSERTED fell to 63.2%, COMPUTED rose to 7 -- first reversal in four rounds. Predict the entry reports the prior round's transition rather than its own | **Wrong in an unexpected direction.** The entry reports **no** coverage or fraction figures at all; the three-round disclosure was dropped -- F-OP24S-04 |
| B4 | bytes | No v0.23 packet and no v0.23 seat report ships; predict the entry describes a round whose reports are unverifiable, and my chain bottoms out a link earlier | **Correct** -- §7 and F-OP24S-01 |

Nine correct, two wrong. Both wrong ones are worth more than the nine: M6 was wrong because the producer did better than I predicted, and B3 was wrong because the producer resolved a recurring misstatement by deleting the statement rather than by correcting it, which is a failure mode I had not anticipated and would not have caught without the prior rounds.
