## 3. Claim provenance ledger (A)

**COMPUTED 7, EXTERNAL 0, ASSERTED 12. ASSERTED fraction 12/19 = 63.2%.**

Five-round series computed from shipped Section 27 bytes: v0.19 37.5% (COMPUTED 9), v0.20 50.0% (11), v0.21 57.1% (9), v0.22 78.9% (4), v0.24 **63.2% (7)**. **The first improvement in four rounds** and a real one -- COMPUTED nearly doubled. Credit it plainly.

Four of the seven COMPUTED tags name build.py sections and are validated by `[9c]`; all four sections exist and, unlike v0.22, all four executed assertions this round. Two are `sha256sum | sha256sum` and `pytest + AST`, both of which I recomputed independently and both hold. So 7 of 7 COMPUTED are recomputable on substance, with no repeat of the v0.22 defect where a COMPUTED tag named a gate that did not run.

Two qualifications the number does not carry. **EXTERNAL is 0 for the fifth consecutive entry**, and this is the round where that stings most: item (13) records that a non-producer seat performed the first external verification in the program's record against a live Zenodo API, and that claim is tagged `[ASSERTED]`. I attempted to reach the cited record independently and could not from this seat. So the first external verification is itself recorded as an unanchored assertion. And the ASSERTED bucket now carries the FB-7b advance (F-OP24S-01), which is the single most consequential claim in twenty-four versions.

## 4. Probes (B, C)

Sandbox copies against a pristine reference; pre/post hash assertion on every mutation.

**P-1 -- benign control.** Unmodified: build rc=0, 169 PASS, 0 FAIL; pytest rc=0, 186 passed.

**P-2 -- discrimination control.** Pre `8f116c2bb4ab82db` post `d9b825c6a2d0f7a8`, LANDED. FB-4 `test_xz_protocol_source_frame.py` digest to 64 zeros. Build rc=1:
```
FAIL: FB-4 row contains test_xz_protocol_source_frame.py digest (b556aaa38bc93cc7...)
FAIL: FB-4 digest for test_xz_protocol_source_frame.py in body
FAIL: No unresolvable 64-hex in body (9 checked, 1 stale)
FAIL: PACKET_SHA256SUMS digest matches: xz_protocol_v0_24.md
```

**P-3 -- forgery regression.** Pre `8f116c2bb4ab82db` post `675afe48efe18ce5`, LANDED. Carried entry v0.10 mutated in place; all 24 seals, FULL_SECTION_27 and the manifest regenerated; PRIOR_HISTORY left honest. Build rc=1 with exactly one error: `FAIL: PRIOR_HISTORY matches derivation (cbacd073d7cdcb11...)`. The recursive detector survives its third version.

**P-4 -- novel class: the `[9f]` silent skip relocated.** Pre `8f116c2bb4ab82db` post `9e0432e569389e7e`, LANDED. Changed the register's item numbering from `(1)` to `[1]` throughout the v0.24 entry, resealed, nothing else touched. Build **rc=0, GREEN**:
```
[9f] Register self-consistency
  (no register items found in current entry)
```
Zero `check()` calls. The v0.23 fix removed the prose anchor -- correctly, and it was my finding -- but the register-item regex is now the single point of failure and its miss is still silent. The class survived the fix; only its locus moved. → F-OP24S-03.

**P-5 -- novel class: the tautological assertion.** Pre `8f116c2bb4ab82db` post `cc6b219dcfcac8ee`, LANDED. Relabelled item (11) to reuse `F-GPT23-01`, which item (2) carries at HIGH. Build rc=1:
```
FAIL: Finding F-GPT23-01 dispositioned at HIGH and LOW
PASS: No duplicate-severity finding IDs (20 unique)
```
Two contradictory lines in one section. The trailing `check(True, ...)` emits a PASS asserting the exact property the line above it has just falsified. The build goes red correctly, so this is not a correctness hole -- it is a build log that states both a proposition and its negation, in a program whose subject is structural honesty. → F-OP24S-05.

**P-6 -- `[9c]` arity, third round.** Pre `8f116c2bb4ab82db` post `bc938c8788d18efe`, LANDED. Replaced the v0.24 entry's `[COMPUTED: sha256sum | sha256sum]` with `[COMPUTED: sha256sum of build.py and GHOST_DOES_NOT_EXIST.md]` and resealed. Build **rc=0, GREEN**, one line: `PASS: COMPUTED-tagged file ships in packet: build.py`. The second filename is never examined. Open since v0.21, now correctly recorded DISCLOSED NOT CLOSED. → F-OP24S-07.

**Void probes.** One. My first P-6 run replaced the target string document-wide rather than within the v0.24 entry, landing in a carried historical entry; the derivation caught it and the run tested nothing I intended. Discarded and re-run correctly above. Separately, my own harness initially reported a false FAIL on the v0.20 chain link by looking for a prose PRIOR_HISTORY value in the v0.21 entry, which -- as F-OP21S-01 established -- does not have one. Corrected to a SKIP with the reason stated; the shipped harness carries the fix.

## 5. Findings

**F-OP24S-01** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the FB-7b advance is asserted on one conjunct of a four-conjunct definition, and every document evidencing it ships nowhere.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.24 entry, opening paragraph; Section 0.1 and the Section 25 FB-7b row.
- **Substance:** The entry states that two non-producer seats of different vendor families "returned non-HALT on canonical bytes where sha256sum -c returned rc=0. **This is the convergent two-family non-HALT that FB-7b requires**" `[ASSERTED]`. The Section 25 definition of FB-7b requires more: "Two executing non-producer seats of different vendor families, **each recomputing identity values, running all 186 tests, and attacking the commitment and decision paths**." The entry evidences the vendor-family and verdict conjuncts. It makes no per-seat claim that identity values were recomputed, that all 186 tests were run, or that the commitment and decision paths were attacked. The three seat reports -- GPT-5.6 Sol, GLM-5.2, Kimi K3 -- do not ship in this packet, so none of the three conjuncts is checkable against any shipped byte, and neither are the verdicts or the finding ranges. Compounding it: both seats returned **CONDITIONAL PASS**, and this record's own vocabulary reads "CONDITIONAL PASS (non-HALT, **not carry-clean**)". The entry maps two not-carry-clean verdicts onto a requirement whose name is "executing carry."
- **Mitigations, stated plainly because they matter here.** The entry does not declare FB-7b CLOSED. Its closing line correctly reads "pending re-carry on v0.24 bytes with absorbed findings," and both Section 0.1 and the Section 25 row still say OPEN. The document is not self-contradictory; the defect is that the middle sentence asserts satisfaction of a four-part definition on the strength of one part, and it is the sentence most likely to be quoted out of the paragraph.
- **Disposition:** Ship the three seat reports in the carry packet, or ship their digests and deposit them. Restate the sentence to name which conjuncts are evidenced and which are not. Decide explicitly, in the body rather than an entry, whether CONDITIONAL PASS satisfies "executing carry" -- the record currently says no in one place and yes in another.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 25 FB-7b row; Section 0.1; F-OP20F-04 (COMPUTED on non-shipping reports); D-3.2; item (13).

**F-OP24S-02** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- item (10) is a false CLOSED; the build prints two stale check messages on every run.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9]`, both `check()` calls; Section 27, v0.24 entry, item (10).
- **Substance:** Item (10) reads "F-GLM23-05 / F-K3C2-04 LOW CLOSED: build.py carried stale v0.22 docstring and check messages. **Re-stamped to v0.24** `[COMPUTED: build.py version stamps]`." The docstring was re-stamped. The check messages were not:
```
PASS: Entries: 24 (expected 22)
PASS: Protocol says 'twenty-two'
```
Both conditions are correct -- `entry_count == 24` and `"twenty-four amendment entries" in protocol` -- and both message strings are stale. The build therefore emits two green lines each of which states the opposite of what it just verified, in the build's own stdout, on every execution including the one this entry was written against. The `[COMPUTED]` tag names "build.py version stamps," which is `[2]`, and `[2]` checks version strings inside files; nothing in the build examines message-string freshness, so the tag points at a gate that cannot see the defect it certifies as fixed. This is the same shape as the v0.22 `[9f]` tag, and it is the third round in which a COMPUTED tag has been attached to a control that does not cover the claim.
- **Disposition:** Derive both messages from `VERSION` rather than literals -- `f"Entries: {entry_count} (expected {expected})"` -- so they cannot go stale. Reopen item (10) as CLOSED IN PART. Then generalize: any `check()` message containing a version-like literal that disagrees with `VERSION` should itself fail the build.
- **Cross-reference:** F-GLM23-05; F-K3C2-04; F-OP22S-01; F-OP20F-04.

**F-OP24S-03** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- `[9f]`'s silent skip was relocated, not removed.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9f]`, `if id_sev_pairs:` with a print-only `else`.
- **Substance:** The v0.23 fix for my F-OP22S-01 removed the `"Adjudicated ledger:"` prose anchor entirely, which was the right structural move and it worked -- the gate ran this round and reported 13 items. But the register-item regex is now the sole trigger, and when it misses, the else-branch prints `(no register items found in current entry)` and appends no error. P-4 shows a change of item numbering from `(1)` to `[1]` empties the gate at **rc=0 green**. The gate's correctness is therefore coupled to the entry's typographic convention, which no gate enforces and no document specifies. Two rounds ago the coupling was to a phrase; now it is to a numbering style. That is a narrower attack surface, and it is still a surface.
- **Disposition:** `check(bool(id_sev_pairs), ...)` so an empty register fails rather than prints. Better, specify the register's delimiter form in Section 22 and assert it, so the convention the gate depends on is itself normative.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP22S-01; F-OP22S-03; F-ADJ19-05; F-OP20F-08.

**F-OP24S-04** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- item (4) is CLOSED on coverage figures the entry does not contain, and a three-round standing disclosure was dropped in the round where it reached its highest value.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.24 entry, item (4); the absent trend item.
- **Substance:** Item (4) reads "MEDIUM CLOSED: v0.23 entry item (12) stated the v0.22 round's coverage figures rather than v0.23's. **This entry's figures are derived from build.py [11] output on v0.24 bytes**." The v0.24 entry contains **zero percentage figures** -- I parsed it; there are none. A CLOSED whose evidence is a property of a figure set that does not exist is not closed; the misstatement was resolved by deleting the statement. Separately, the v0.21, v0.22 and v0.23 entries each carried an INFORMATIONAL item disclosing the ungated share and the ASSERTED-fraction trend. The v0.24 entry carries no such item. `[11]` computes the ungated share at **42.6%**, up from 39.2%, a sixth consecutive rise and the largest value in the series. The one round in which the disclosure would have shown the highest number is the round in which the disclosure disappeared. I do not read this as concealment -- the number is printed by the shipped build and the entry made real provenance gains elsewhere -- but a disclosure that lapses exactly when it worsens is the pattern this program exists to catch, and it should not be left to a reader to notice by diffing four entries.
- **Disposition:** Restore the trend item with this round's figures. Then close the class properly: have `[11]` emit its percentages and gate the entry's stated figures against them, exactly as `[3]` gates digests. These numbers are as machine-derivable as digests and there is no reason for them to be ASSERTED, or absent.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP21S-04; F-OP22S-04; F-OP21C-04; F-GPT23-04; F-OP18-12.

**F-OP24S-05** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- `[9f]` ends with an assertion that cannot fail and whose message contradicts the failure above it.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9f]`, `check(True, f"No duplicate-severity finding IDs ({len(seen_ids)} unique)")`.
- **Substance:** The argument is the literal `True`. The call cannot fail under any input, and its message asserts a property -- that no finding ID is dispositioned at two severities -- which it never tests; the actual test is the `check(False, ...)` inside the loop. P-5 shows the consequence directly: with a duplicate injected the section emits `FAIL: Finding F-GPT23-01 dispositioned at HIGH and LOW` immediately followed by `PASS: No duplicate-severity finding IDs (20 unique)`. It also counts toward the build's 169 PASS total, so the headline number now includes one assertion that asserts nothing. The intent is legible -- it is a liveness indicator, added because the gate had been silently empty for three rounds -- and the intent is right. The implementation states a false thing to signal a true one.
- **Disposition:** Replace with a bare `print()` for liveness, or with `check(not duplicates_found, ...)` tracked by a real flag. A build whose subject is structural honesty should contain no `check(True)`.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP22S-01; the decorative-control class in F-ADJ19-11 and F-OP20F-01.

**F-OP24S-06** [LOW -- advisory, cannot carry] -- correction (f) miscounts its own defect class by folding in a correction that belongs to a different one.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.24 entry, correction (f); v0.23 correction (d).
- **Substance:** Correction (f) states "This is the fourth consecutive round of the duplicate-disposition class (corrections (b), (c), (d), now (f))." Correction (b), at v0.21, is a ledger-tally-versus-register-count mismatch -- eleven tallied against twelve dispositioned -- not a duplicate disposition. The duplicate-disposition instances are (c) at v0.22, (d) at v0.23, and (f) at v0.24: three, not four. The mislabel originates at v0.23 correction (d), which likewise calls (b) "the same duplicate-disposition class," and (f) carries it forward. Both are reconciliation errors of exactly the kind the corrections describe, committed inside the corrections that describe them.
- **Disposition:** Restate as three consecutive rounds, or define the class broadly enough to include tally mismatches and say so. Given `[9f]` now counts register items mechanically, the class census is derivable and should not be prose.
- **Cross-reference:** corrections (b), (c), (d); F-OP22S-02; the Axiom-3 class.

**F-OP24S-07** [LOW -- advisory, cannot carry] -- three findings are now correctly disclosed and none is closed: the `[9c]` arity-one regex (third round), the PDF (fifth round), and the `cb67f222` literal.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9c]` `file_computed`; `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`; `build.py` `derive_prior_history`.
- **Substance:** The `[9c]` regex is byte-identical to v0.21 and v0.22, confirmed by direct diff, and P-6 shows a COMPUTED tag naming a non-existent second file builds green. The PDF is absent from the manifest and from `required_members` for the fifth consecutive version and carries 145 en-dashes against a source with none -- the convention breach I confirmed at v0.22 persists in the one artifact the perimeter cannot see. The `cb67f222` literal remains in the derivation's v0.19 termination path. **The disclosure discipline is now working**: v0.23 item (8) records the regex DISCLOSED NOT CLOSED, item (9) NOTES the literal with an accurate rationale, item (11) NOTES the PDF, and v0.24 item (11) even records the PDF disclosure's own discontinuity. I raise this at LOW and as a single item precisely because the record is now honest about all three. The finding is that three known defects have been disclosed rather than fixed across three to five rounds, and disclosure is not a terminal state.
- **Disposition:** Each is a small edit. Capture all filenames per tag; add the PDF to the manifest and extend `[4]` to its extracted text; delete the literal and let a scrape miss fail the build. None needs a carry round to authorize.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP21S-05; F-OP22S-05; F-OP20F-07; F-OP22S-06; F-OP22S-07; F-K3C2-05.

**F-OP24S-08** [INFORMATIONAL] -- the provenance trend reversed and the coverage trend did not.
- **Locus:** `[9c]` and `[11]` output; the v0.24 entry's tag distribution.
- **Substance:** ASSERTED fell 78.9% to 63.2% and COMPUTED rose 4 to 7 -- the first improvement in four rounds, and unlike v0.22 every COMPUTED tag names a gate that actually executed. The silent-skip census fell 19 to 17. Both are real gains and both were driven by non-producer findings. Against that: the ungated share rose to 42.6%, a sixth consecutive rise, and EXTERNAL is 0 for the fifth consecutive entry. Item (13) reports that a non-producer seat verified a deposit against the live Zenodo API and calls it the first EXTERNAL verification in the record; it is tagged `[ASSERTED]`, the seat's report does not ship, and I could not reach the cited record from this seat to corroborate it. So the program's first external verification is currently recorded the same way as everything else. Converting it -- shipping the seat's report or the deposit receipt and citing it `[EXTERNAL]` -- would move the count off zero for the first time in twenty-four versions and is the only remaining step for the boundary.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP22S-08; F-OP21S-08; item (13); Section 22.2 anchor (b).

**Clears.** Step 1 rc=0; build green; 186/186. The recursive PRIOR_HISTORY derivation reproduces the shipped value, survives a third version, and still catches a retroactive carried-entry forgery with exactly one correct error (P-3). `[9f]` executed real assertions this round, which it had not done in three. Range-versus-register reconciles exactly: 21 declared IDs across three namespaces, 21 dispositioned, zero absent -- the D-3.7 defect I raised at v0.22 is genuinely gone. All eight of my v0.22 findings were dispositioned at v0.23. Correction (f) correctly identifies correction (d) as a false CLOSED and restates the mapping exactly as my v0.22 report recommended. `[9d]` now matches numeric ordinals and `[9e]` tolerates trailing content in the range parenthetical, both from non-producer findings. Section 22.2's forgery boundary was re-scoped again, correctly, in the direction of admitting more residual. Em-dash and brand sweeps clean at source.

Eight raised, eight dispositioned, none absent -- the first round in which that is true of my findings. Two landed, one landed after a failed first attempt, five disclosed rather than fixed.

**What three prior rounds bought.** The external chain anchors in §7, which no other seat can produce. B3's refutation: I predicted the entry would misstate the coverage figures and instead it omitted them, which I could only notice because I had the three prior entries to compare against. F-OP24S-06, which required tracing correction (b) back to the v0.21 entry to see it belonged to a different class. And the P-3 baseline. It bought **nothing** for F-OP24S-01, -02, -03, or -05 -- all four come from reading the shipped `build.py` and the shipped body against the shipped entry, and a fresh seat finds every one. F-OP24S-01 in particular needs only the Section 25 definition and the file listing.

## 7. Boundary report (E)

The boundary moved this round, for the first time since v0.21, and it moved in the one direction that counts: outward, past the packet. Three of the four chain links are now anchored against bytes I hold from prior dispatches -- the v0.22 entry's recorded PRIOR_HISTORY equals the sha256 of my held v0.21 `HISTORY.sha256`, and the v0.23 entry's equals the sha256 of my held v0.22 file -- and all 22 carried entry seals are byte-identical across v0.20, v0.21, v0.22 and v0.24. Append-only has now held across five packets with zero in-place mutation, and the v0.23 link is bridged by prose even though I never received that packet. The fourth link, v0.24 to v0.23, is derivation-only because I do not hold v0.23. More important than my anchors: item (13) records that a non-producer seat checked a deposit against the live Zenodo API, which is the first time in twenty-four versions that anything in this program has been compared against a record outside the producer's control. That is the crossing the last four of my reports have asked for. But it is currently recorded as `[ASSERTED]`, the seat's report does not ship, EXTERNAL remains 0, and I could not reach the cited record from this seat to corroborate it -- so the first external verification has the same evidentiary status inside the packet as the claims it was supposed to anchor. Meanwhile the interior kept thinning: the ungated share reached 42.6%, a sixth consecutive rise, and the entry that would have disclosed it does not. The step is now one line rather than a program: ship the Kimi K3 report or the deposit receipt, cite it `[EXTERNAL]`, and the count moves off zero. Everything else in this boundary paragraph has been true for four rounds.

## 8. D-7 process health (G)

- **Did every probe come from an enumerated list?** No. P-4, P-5 and the FB-7b conjunct audit are novel; none appears in D-4's classes. P-4 and P-5 came from reading the `[9f]` rewrite and asking what it does when its inputs change shape.
- **Did the dispatch tell me where to look?** Less than in any prior round -- this dispatch is four lines of deliverables with no per-finding direction, which is an improvement. But the packet still ships all three of my prior reports, and deliverable D still structures §6. Four of my eight findings came from bytes rather than memory.
- **Is the ASSERTED fraction unchanged from the prior round?** No, and for the first time the answer is favourable: 78.9% to 63.2%, with COMPUTED rising 4 to 7 and every COMPUTED tag naming a gate that executed. This is the first improvement in four rounds and it followed the first non-producer carrying round in ten versions. That correlation is the most useful process signal in this report.
- **Have the recent rounds all been producer-family?** No -- v0.23 was carried by GPT-5.6 Sol, GLM-5.2 and Kimi K3, the first non-producer contact since v0.14. This round is producer-family advisory again. FB-7b is claimed advanced on v0.23 bytes and remains OPEN in the body pending re-carry on v0.24 bytes.

## 9. Verdict

**CONDITIONAL PASS -- advisory only, non-binding.** Not a HALT.

Severity ledger as I calibrate it: 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 2 LOW / 1 INFORMATIONAL = 8.

I have returned HALT advisory in each of my three prior reports. I am not returning one here, and the reason is substantive rather than fatigue. At v0.21 and v0.22 the HALT rested on a defect that would be sealed into an append-only record in a state that could not be repaired cheaply afterward. Nothing in this round has that property: every finding below is a small edit against the current draft, the register reconciles exactly for the first time, the provenance trend reversed, and the chain is now anchored outside the packet at three links. The document is in better condition than at any point I have audited it.

**Standing, restated.** Producer-family advisory. Cannot HALT, cannot carry HIGH, no FB-7b weight. This matters more than usual: F-OP24S-01 concerns whether FB-7b's condition has been met, and my verdict on that question carries no weight by construction. I raise it, I do not adjudicate it.

Three findings I would most want a non-producer seat to re-derive, since a producer-family instance auditing a producer-family entry about a non-producer round is the weakest configuration in this program: **F-OP24S-01**, which needs only the Section 25 FB-7b definition, the entry's opening paragraph, and `ls`; **F-OP24S-02**, which is two lines of the build's own stdout; and **F-OP24S-04**, which is a grep of the entry for a percent sign against `[11]`'s output. None requires taking my word for anything, and the first should be re-rated by someone whose severity can carry.

The recommendation is unchanged from three reports running and is now one step from done: ship the Kimi K3 deposit verification or the receipt itself, cite it `[EXTERNAL]`, and re-carry on v0.24 bytes with the seat reports included in the packet. FB-7b should be settled by documents a reader can open, not by a sentence about them.

## 5. Findings

**F-OP25S-01** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- item (1) is a false CLOSED for the second consecutive round on the identical defect, and this time asserts a state the shipped build directly falsifies.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9]`, both `check()` calls; Section 27, v0.25 entry, item (1).
- **Substance:** Item (1) reads "F-OP24-01 / F-OP24S-02 / (E) HIGH CLOSED: build.py [9] check messages stated 'expected 22' and 'twenty-two' while the condition checked for 24. **The messages are now correct for v0.25 (25 entries, 'twenty-five')** `[COMPUTED: build.py [9] amendment record check]`." The shipped build prints:
```
PASS: Entries: 25 (expected 22)
PASS: Protocol says 'twenty-two'
```
The diff from v0.24 shows both lines were edited this round -- `entry_count == 24` became `== 25`, `"twenty-four amendment entries"` became `"twenty-five"` -- while both message strings were left untouched. So the producer had both lines open and changed the conditions without the messages, twice in a row. At v0.24 the entry claimed the strings had been "re-stamped"; at v0.25 it claims they "are now correct." Both are falsified by running the build that ships in the same packet. The `[COMPUTED]` tag names `[9]`, which counts entries and cannot see message text.
- **Disposition:** Derive both messages from `VERSION` and `entry_count` so they cannot desynchronise: `f"Entries: {entry_count} (expected {expected})"`. Then gate the class -- any `check()` message containing a version-like literal that disagrees with `VERSION` should fail the build. Reopen as CLOSED IN PART with the current strings quoted.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP24S-02; F-OP24-01; F-GLM23-05; F-K3C2-04; the COMPUTED-tag-coverage gap in §3.

**F-OP25S-02** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- three of twelve register rows are invisible to `[9f]`, reproducing the defect closed one round earlier, and the entry breaks its own stated convention to do it.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.25 entry, items (1), (2), (6); `build.py` `[9f]` register regex.
- **Substance:** Items (1), (2) and (6) each end their ID list with `/ (E)`, denoting the fresh instance. The `[9f]` regex requires the final alternation element to match `F-\w+-\d+`; `(E)` does not, so the match fails and the row is not seen. The build reports `Register: 9 items` against twelve rows in prose. This is a verbatim recurrence of the defect the **v0.24 entry item (1)** dispositioned HIGH CLOSED -- "the register-item regex did not parse parenthetical qualifiers ... causing 2 of 12 register items to be invisible ... All 12 rows parse" -- now at 3 of 12 instead of 2. And item (4) of this same entry states "The finding IDs in this entry use unique per-round prefixes and **no parenthetical qualifiers**," which the entry violates three times in the register that item (4) sits in. P-4 makes the consequence concrete: an injected duplicate severity fails the build in a parsed row and passes green in an invisible row, with `PASS: No duplicate-severity finding IDs (21 unique)` printed beneath it. The three invisible rows carry F-OP24S-01, F-OP24S-02 and F-OP24S-04 -- the FB-7b finding, the false-CLOSED finding and the coverage finding -- so the gate is blind precisely where last round's HIGHs were dispositioned.
- **Disposition:** Give the fresh instance a real ID namespace, as item (4) already prescribes; `(E)` is not an identifier. Independently, harden the regex to tolerate any bracketed token in the ID list rather than only parenthetical suffixes on well-formed IDs, and assert that the parsed row count equals the count of `(N)` markers in the register so an invisible row fails the build rather than shrinking the total.
- **Cross-reference:** v0.24 item (1); F-GPT23-02; F-GLM23-01; F-K3C2-01; item (4) of this entry; F-OP24S-03.

**F-OP25S-03** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- item (5) closes two findings on a misdescription of one of them, and neither is fixed.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.25 entry, item (5); `build.py` `[9f]`.
- **Substance:** Item (5) reads "F-OP24S-03 / F-OP24S-05 / F-OP24C-04 / F-OP24C-09 MEDIUM CLOSED: [9f] ended with an unconditional check(True,...) that could never fail, **making the gate green on zero parsed rows**. The unconditional PASS is removed; [9f] **now asserts at least one row was parsed**." Three problems, in ascending order of consequence. First, the `check(True)` never executed on zero parsed rows -- it sat inside `if id_sev_pairs:`, so the zero-row case took the else-branch, which is what my F-OP24S-03 was about and which is byte-identical this round. Second, the unconditional PASS was not removed; it was replaced by `check(len(id_sev_pairs) > 0, ...)` **in the same guarded block**, so its condition is provably true wherever it runs. Third, the claim that `[9f]` now asserts at least one row was parsed is falsified by P-5: an empty register still builds green with `(no register items found in current entry)` and no assertion. The item merges two distinct findings, restates one of them incorrectly, and fixes neither.
- **Disposition:** Move the assertion outside the guard: `check(bool(id_sev_pairs), ...)` with the else-branch deleted. Reopen F-OP24S-03 and F-OP24S-05 separately -- they are different defects and merging them is what produced the misdescription.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP24S-03; F-OP24S-05; F-OP22S-01; F-ADJ19-05.

**F-OP25S-04** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- D-3.7 reconciliation collapsed after one clean round: two of five instances declare findings by bare count, and two declared IDs are dispositioned nowhere.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.25 entry, preamble and register.
- **Substance:** The preamble declares "deep A: F-OP24-01..05; shallow B: F-OP24S-01..08; **one-round C: 11 findings**; two-round D: F-OP24C899-01..08; **fresh E: 11 findings**" -- 43 findings raised, of which 22 are declared by count with no ID namespace, making reconciliation structurally impossible for half the input. Of the 21 enumerable IDs, **F-OP24C899-01 and F-OP24C899-04 appear nowhere in the register**. Instance C's eleven findings appear as nine distinct `F-OP24C-` IDs. Instance E's eleven appear as three bare `(E)` mentions. v0.24 reconciled exactly -- 21 declared, 21 dispositioned, zero absent -- and I recorded that as a clear. One round later the property is gone, and this is the same class as F-ADJ19-04, F-OP18-09, F-OP22S-03 and v0.23 correction (e), now in its fifth instance.
- **Disposition:** Require every reporting instance to declare an ID range, never a count; a bare count cannot be reconciled and should be rejected at dispatch time. Then implement the reconciliation as a gate -- expand every `F-<ns>-NN..MM` in the current entry and assert each expanded ID appears in the register. v0.23 item (10) declined this as "a D-3.7 responsibility, not a build gate"; two rounds of evidence now say the responsibility is not discharged reliably by hand.
- **Cross-reference:** F-ADJ19-04; F-OP22S-03; v0.23 correction (e) and item (10); D-3.7.

**F-OP25S-05** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the entry states the favourable trend in prose and omits the unfavourable current figure by policy.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.25 entry, items (6) and (12); `[9c]` and `[11]` output.
- **Substance:** Item (6) closes my F-OP24S-04 by adopting a standing policy: "the entry does not restate any percentage as prose to avoid the stale-figure recurrence." That policy is defensible and I credit it -- the figures are in the shipped build's output, which is more verifiable than prose, and it eliminates the stale-figure surface I have raised in three consecutive reports. But item (12), in the same register, states in prose that "the ungated share rose for a sixth consecutive round; **the provenance trend reversed for the first time (ASSERTED fraction fell)**." That is accurate for v0.24, the round item (12) dispositions. It is not accurate now: ASSERTED rose 63.2% to **75.0%**, COMPUTED fell 7 to **4**, and the ungated share reached **44.1%**, a seventh consecutive rise. So the entry states the one favourable trend the series has produced and, by policy, states no figure that would show it reversed back. I do not read this as concealment -- item (6)'s reasoning is sound and the numbers are computed by the shipped build -- but a no-percentages policy that admits a prose exception for the good round is not a no-percentages policy. Separately, item (6) is graded CLOSED where CLOSED IN PART is right: my F-OP24S-04 had two parts and only the false-CLOSED half is resolved.
- **Disposition:** Apply the policy symmetrically -- no trend claims in prose either, or gate the entry's trend claims against `[11]` and `[9c]` output the way `[3]` gates digests. Regrade item (6) CLOSED IN PART.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP24S-04; F-OP22S-04; F-OP21S-04; F-OP18-12.

**F-OP25S-06** [LOW -- advisory, cannot carry] -- `[9e]` executed zero assertions because the entry dropped its governance sentence, and nothing requires one.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9e]`; Section 27, v0.25 entry.
- **Substance:** The `[9e]` section printed its heading and no check lines. The v0.25 entry contains no `Governance:` sentence and no cardinal-range construction of any kind -- the first entry since v0.19 without one. `[9e]` was added at v0.22 to catch my F-OP20F-02, a governance miscount, and widened at v0.24 after F-GPT23-07; it is inert this round not because it passed but because its subject is absent. Nothing in the build or in Section 22 requires a governance statement to exist, so a gate whose purpose is to check that statement can be silenced by omitting it. Given this is the round in which the FB-7b posture changed materially, the absence of a governance sentence is also a substantive gap in the record, not only a gate one.
- **Disposition:** Require a governance sentence per entry and `check()` its presence, so `[9e]` fails on absence rather than falling silent. This is the same shape as F-OP25S-03 and should be fixed with it.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP20F-02; F-GPT23-07; F-GLM23-03; F-OP24S-03.

**F-OP25S-07** [LOW -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the two long-running disclosed defects are unchanged and correctly NOTED.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9c]` `file_computed`; `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`.
- **Substance:** The `[9c]` regex is byte-identical to v0.21, v0.22 and v0.24 -- fourth round -- and P-6 confirms a COMPUTED tag naming a non-existent second file builds green. The PDF is absent from the manifest and from `required_members` for the sixth consecutive version and carries 149 en-dashes against a source with none. Item (10) NOTES both accurately and calls them DISCLOSED. I raise this at LOW and as one item because the record is honest about both; the finding is that a defect disclosed in four consecutive entries and fixable by one regex edit is being carried rather than closed, and disclosure is not a terminal state.
- **Disposition:** Capture all filename-shaped tokens per tag. Add the PDF to the manifest and extend `[4]` to its extracted text. Neither needs a carry round to authorize.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP21S-05; F-OP22S-05; F-OP24S-07; F-OP20F-07; F-K3C2-05.

**F-OP25S-08** [INFORMATIONAL] -- the FB-7b retraction is the strongest act in this entry and should be recorded as such.
- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.25 entry, "v0.24 status note"; item (2).
- **Substance:** The status note restates all four of my F-OP24S-01 grounds accurately -- unshipped carrying-seat reports, the four-conjunct definition against a single evidenced conjunct, the record's own "not carry-clean" annotation, and unbound seat reports -- adds a ground I did not raise, credits the v0.24 entry for correctly not declaring FB-7b closed, and states plainly: "This entry does not reassert the satisfaction claim. FB-7b remains OPEN pending a re-carry on bytes where the carrying-seat reports are verifiable." The body agrees. A producer-family entry retracting the program's most consequential claim, on advisory findings that cannot bind it, is the behaviour the whole apparatus exists to produce, and it happened here without a non-producer seat forcing it. That is worth more than any gate added this round. The residual is unchanged and named in item (3): the reports still do not ship, so the retraction is as unverifiable as the claim it retracts, and EXTERNAL remains 0 for a sixth entry.
- **Cross-reference:** F-OP24S-01; item (3); Section 25 FB-7b row; §7.

**Clears.** Step 1 rc=0; build green; 186/186. The recursive PRIOR_HISTORY derivation reproduces the shipped value, survives a fourth version, and still catches a retroactive carried-entry forgery with exactly one correct error. `[3a]`, `[3b]`, `[3c]` and `[12]` remain live and redundant (P-2). `[9f]`'s duplicate check works correctly on every row it can see (P-4a). Item (4)'s root-cause diagnosis of the F-OP22C namespace collision is the best piece of analysis in the entry and explains a defect I raised at v0.22 without identifying its cause. My four prior seat reports no longer ship -- the D-0 disposition landing after four rounds. Em-dash and brand sweeps clean at source.

## 6. Self-score of prior findings (D)

| ID | v0.24 severity | v0.25 disposition | Landed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-OP24S-01 | HIGH | item (2) HIGH NOTED | **Substantively yes.** The satisfaction claim is retracted, all four grounds restated accurately, FB-7b OPEN in entry and body. Reports still unship -- item (3) |
| F-OP24S-02 | HIGH | item (1) HIGH CLOSED | **No.** Second consecutive false CLOSED; build prints both stale strings -- F-OP25S-01 |

| F-OP24S-04 | MEDIUM | item (6) MEDIUM CLOSED | **Partly.** The false-CLOSED half is resolved by an honest no-percentages policy; the disclosure half is not, and item (12) breaks the policy for the favourable trend -- F-OP25S-05 |

Eight raised, eight dispositioned, none absent -- the second consecutive round with that property. But **three are CLOSED without landing** (items 1 and 5, covering three of my findings), which is the worst closure record of the four rounds I have audited: v0.21 closed one of eight falsely, v0.22 closed one of eight falsely, v0.24 closed none falsely, v0.25 closes three.

**What four prior rounds bought.** The chain anchors in §7. The F-OP25S-01 diagnosis, which needed the v0.24 build.py to see that the same two lines were edited and left stale twice. The F-OP25S-03 diagnosis, which needed my own v0.24 finding text to see that item (5) misdescribes it -- a fresh seat reading only v0.25 would see a plausible fix for a plausible defect. And the F-OP25S-04 comparison against v0.24's clean 21/21 reconciliation. It bought **nothing** for F-OP25S-02, which is the round's other HIGH: twelve rows in prose against nine in the build's own output, visible to anyone who counts.

## 7. Boundary report (E)

The boundary held where it was and did not extend. Three chain links are now anchored against bytes I hold from prior dispatches -- v0.22's recorded PRIOR_HISTORY equals the sha256 of my held v0.21 file, v0.23's equals my held v0.22 file, and v0.25's shipped `8660dfde...` equals the sha256 of my held v0.24 file exactly -- and all 24 carried entry seals are byte-identical across the v0.20, v0.21, v0.22 and v0.24 packets. Append-only has now held across six versions with zero in-place mutation, and P-3 confirms the detector still fires. That is a genuinely strong internal record. What has not moved is everything outside it: EXTERNAL is 0 for the sixth consecutive entry, no deposit receipt ships, the Zenodo verification recorded at v0.24 remains an `[ASSERTED]` claim about a seat whose report does not ship, and the three v0.23 carrying-seat reports -- on which the program's terminal freeze-blocker turns -- are absent from this packet as they were from the last. The entry is admirably clear about this: item (3) says adding the reports to `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` or citing their deposit digests is "deferred to the re-carry round," and the status note says FB-7b is open "pending a re-carry on bytes where the carrying-seat reports are verifiable." That is the correct diagnosis and it is now the whole of the remaining work. Meanwhile the interior thinned again -- ungated share 44.1%, seventh consecutive rise, COMPUTED back to 4, and two of those four tags naming gates that cannot see their claims. The step has not changed across five of my reports and is smaller now than it was: put the three carrying-seat reports in the packet, or their digests in the entry, and the terminal question becomes answerable by a reader instead of by assertion.

## 8. D-7 process health (G)

- **Did every probe come from an enumerated list?** No. P-4's visible/invisible pair and P-5 are novel; neither appears in D-4's classes. P-4 came from noticing that the build reported nine register items where the entry showed twelve.
- **Did the dispatch tell me where to look?** Less than any prior round, and the packet no longer ships my earlier reports, which is a real improvement in seat hygiene. Deliverable D still structures §6. One of my two HIGHs (F-OP25S-02) needed no prior context at all.
- **Is the ASSERTED fraction unchanged from the prior round?** No -- 63.2% to 75.0%, with COMPUTED falling 7 to 4. Last round's reversal did not hold, and the round in which it reversed back is the round whose entry, by policy, states no figure of its own. EXTERNAL 0 for the sixth entry.
- **Have the recent rounds all been producer-family?** Yes. v0.24 and v0.25 are producer-family advisory, five Opus 5 instances this round. The last non-producer contact was the v0.23 carrying round, and FB-7b is now correctly OPEN pending a re-carry.

## 9. Verdict

**HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER -- advisory only, non-binding.**

Severity ledger as I calibrate it: 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 2 LOW / 1 INFORMATIONAL = 8.

I returned CONDITIONAL PASS at v0.24 and I am returning HALT here, so the reason should be explicit. It is not the count -- the ledger is identical to last round's. It is that this entry contains **two closures that the build shipping in the same packet falsifies**: item (1) states the check messages "are now correct" while the build prints them stale, and item (5) states `[9f]` "now asserts at least one row was parsed" while an empty register builds green. Item (1) is the second consecutive false CLOSED on the identical defect, on lines the producer edited both times. Add a register gate blind to a quarter of its own rows and printing a green line asserting the property it cannot check for them, and the failure mode is no longer a defect in a gate -- it is an entry describing a build state that the build contradicts, three times, in one document that is about to be sealed append-only. Everything here is a small edit: two f-strings, one guard moved outside its `if`, one ID namespace. All four are cheaper before the seal than as corrections after it.

**Standing, restated.** Producer-family advisory. Cannot HALT, cannot carry HIGH, no FB-7b weight. My verdict is a recommendation to the chair.

Three findings I would most want a non-producer seat to re-derive: **F-OP25S-01**, which is two lines of the build's own stdout against one sentence of the entry; **F-OP25S-02**, which is counting `(N)` markers in the register against the build's `Register: 9 items`; and **F-OP25S-03**, which is one `if` statement read against one claim. None requires taking my word for anything, and none requires holding a prior packet.

Against all of that: **F-OP25S-08 is the most important thing in this round and it is a clear, not a finding.** The entry retracts the FB-7b satisfaction claim on advisory findings that could not bind it, restates the grounds accurately, adds one I missed, and credits its predecessor for what it got right. Five of my reports have asked for one thing. It is now the only thing left: ship the three carrying-seat reports, or their digests, and re-carry.

## 4. Findings

**F-OP32S-01** [CRITICAL -- advisory, cannot carry] -- Section 0.1 declares the document FROZEN and, 923 characters later in the same section, declares FB-7b OPEN.
- **Locus:** `### 0.1 Status`, offsets 208 and 1131; Section 25 FB-7b row; v0.32 entry.
- **Substance:** The status line reads "This document is **v0.32 FROZEN** -- carried on these bytes, pending deposit." Within the same subsection: "**FB-7b** (two-family executing carry on canonical bytes) **is OPEN**, pending fresh carry by Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2." Section 25 records FB-7b as RESOLVED and strikes the row through; the v0.32 entry states "FB-7b RESOLVED"; the freeze is licensed by that resolution. So the freeze candidate asserts both branches of its own decision path, in one subsection, and one of the two must be false. Under the severity vocabulary this is CRITICAL -- "identity value or decision path is false" -- and it is the only CRITICAL I have raised in nine rounds of auditing this instrument. The mechanism is mundane: the Section 0.1 FB-7b sentence has carried forward unedited since at least v0.28, where I verified it read "pending fresh carry by Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2." The amendment updated Section 25 and the entry and did not update Section 0.1. **My severity cannot carry. A non-producer seat must re-rate this, and it is the single item I would put in front of one first.**
- **Disposition:** Update the Section 0.1 sentence, or -- if FB-7b is in fact open pending deposit, which the status line's own "pending deposit" qualifier suggests -- withdraw FROZEN. Then gate it: assert that no body sentence containing "FB-7b" contains "is OPEN" while Section 25 records RESOLVED. That check is three lines and the class it covers (body prose left behind by an amendment) is the Kimi F-1 class the record has now committed at v0.27, v0.28 and here.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 25 FB-7b row; v0.32 entry; F-OP24S-01; Kimi F-1; F-OP25-ALL-06.

**F-OP32S-02** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the FB-7b amendment deleted an execution conjunct from the operative rule, and the entry describes it as a verdict-predicate change.
- **Locus:** Section 25 FB-7b row; v0.32 entry, opening paragraph; v0.28 Section 25 (held).
- **Substance:** The v0.28 packet on my disk defines FB-7b as: "Two executing non-producer seats of different vendor families, **each recomputing identity values, running all 186 tests, and attacking the commitment and decision paths**." In v0.32 that definition column is struck through and replaced with the amendment text. **The phrase "running all 186 tests" now occurs exactly once in the entire document, at offset 172112 -- inside Section 27, in the sealed v0.25 status note, quoting a prior seat's objection that the entry evidenced only the verdict conjunct.** The operative rule no longer contains it; it survives only as a quotation inside the complaint about its non-satisfaction. The entry frames the amendment narrowly -- "CONDITIONAL PASS with Class C/D conditions satisfies the two-family carry when no Class A/B finding exists" -- which is a change to the verdict predicate, and says nothing about the execution conjuncts being removed with it. A reader of v0.32 alone cannot detect the deletion; it requires diffing against a prior packet or reading a sealed objection.
- **What makes this more than bookkeeping.** Register item (5) reads: "**F-GPT31-01 HIGH NOTED: pytest absent from dispatched environment; first build returns rc=1.** Live instance of the disclosed execution-environment boundary. **Confirmed by three fresh seats this round.**" I hit this myself at v0.20 -- my first build returned rc=1 for exactly this reason. So the conjunct that was deleted from the rule is precisely the one the round's own register records at least three seats could not satisfy without out-of-band remediation, and whether any of them installed pytest and re-ran is nowhere recorded. The entry's compressed claim that six carrying seats were "all executing" is contradicted in substance by its own item (5), and the definition that would have made "executing" checkable is gone.
- **Disposition:** State the amendment's full scope in the entry: which conjuncts were relaxed, which were removed, and why. If the execution conjuncts are still intended to hold, restore them to Section 25 alongside the amended verdict predicate -- the two changes are independent. If they are not, say so plainly, because deleting them changes what FB-7b means rather than when it is satisfied. Separately, require each carrying seat to record its pytest exit code and test count in its report, and ship the reports.
- **Cross-reference:** v0.28 Section 25 (held); v0.25 status note; F-OP24S-01; register item (5); F-GPT31-01; F-GPT30-01/02.

**F-OP32S-03** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the EXTERNAL count was raised by two tags, neither examined by any gate, one of which its own text disqualifies.
- **Locus:** v0.32 entry, both EXTERNAL tags; `build.py` `[9c]`, `external_refs`.
- **Substance:** Three distinct defects in one claim.
  - **The gate cannot see either tag.** `[9c]` verifies EXTERNAL references with `re.findall(r'\[EXTERNAL:\s*(\S+\.(?:md|py|json|pdf|txt))', ...)` -- file-form only. Both shipped tags are prose. `external_refs` is empty; the loop body never runs; **zero checks execute against the EXTERNAL population**. P-4 is the discrimination pair: a file-form EXTERNAL naming a non-shipping file fails the build; a fabricated `doi:10.5281/zenodo.00000000-nonexistent` builds green and raises the count to 3. The metric the entry presents as a first is incrementable by typing.
  - **One tag is EXTERNAL by contradiction of its own text.** `[EXTERNAL: seat reports held by producer, digests below]` is attached to the sentence carrying the entire carry claim -- "Six non-producer carrying seats across two families, all executing, all non-HALT, on v0.31 canonical bytes." A producer-held document that does not ship is the paradigm ASSERTED claim; the tag says "held by producer" in the same breath as grading it EXTERNAL. The eight digests listed below it are tagged, correctly, `[ASSERTED: digests computed by producer from held report files]` -- so the entry grades the digests ASSERTED and the reports they digest EXTERNAL.
  - **The DOI tag anchors nothing in v0.32.** The two deposits are real and Zenodo bytes are genuinely outside the producer's reach once deposited -- that part of the claim is sound and I credit it. But they are deposits of *other artifacts* (BSSG v0.1, SHVVP v0.8), and the entry's own wording is that "the protocol body already inherits from these DOIs." Inheritance is not anchoring. No v0.32 value -- not `HISTORY.sha256`, not the manifest digest, not a seat report digest -- appears in either deposit by any claim the entry makes. The thing seven of my reports have asked for is a deposit receipt for **this packet's** chain root. That has not happened, and the EXTERNAL count moved without it.
  - **It is load-bearing.** Register item (9) dispositions adversarial HIGH `F-GPT31-06` -- "current-entry factual semantics remain self-attested after packet-internal seal regeneration" -- as "subsumed by ... **the EXTERNAL-count precondition now addressed in this entry**." A HIGH from an adversarial seat is NOTED on a precondition that consists of two ungated tags, one of them misgraded.
- **Disposition:** Regrade the seat-reports tag ASSERTED. Extend `[9c]`'s EXTERNAL check to DOI form: resolve the DOI or, at minimum, assert the entry states a digest that the deposit is claimed to contain, and fail when neither. Then do the thing itself -- deposit `HISTORY.sha256` and cite its DOI, which converts the chain root from self-attested to externally fixed and disposes of `F-GPT31-06` on its merits.
- **Cross-reference:** F-GPT31-06; F-K3B-04/05; F-OP24S-01; F-OP25S-08; F-OP27S; F-OP28S-07.

**F-OP32S-04** [HIGH -- advisory, cannot carry] -- the freeze register closes nothing, and two of the disclosed standing boundaries contradict the freeze.
- **Locus:** v0.32 entry, thirteen-item register and closing paragraph.
- **Substance:** Thirteen items: **zero CLOSED**, four DISCLOSED, nine NOTED. Both HIGH items are NOTED. Every finding from an eight-seat round -- six carrying, two adversarial -- is carried forward rather than fixed, in the entry that declares the document terminal. The closing paragraph then lists **thirteen disclosed standing boundaries**, and two of them are load-bearing against the freeze itself: **"packet non-closure"** and **"fresh-execution non-reproducibility."** The first says the packet does not contain the documents needed to verify its own claims. The second says a fresh seat cannot reproduce the build. Freezing an instrument while disclosing that a fresh party cannot reproduce its verification, and that the packet lacks closure, freezes the disclosure set rather than a verified artifact. That may be a defensible terminal form -- the document's stated intent is "a FROZEN **OPEN** preregistration instrument" -- but if so the entry should say that FROZEN means "no further changes," not "verification complete," because those are different claims and only the first is supported.
- **Disposition:** Either close some subset before freezing -- the `[9c]` arity regex, the `cb67f222` literal, and the duplicate-message guard are each a one-line edit and have been carried for six, six and three rounds respectively -- or state explicitly in Section 0.1 what FROZEN asserts and what it does not. A freeze with zero closures needs its semantics written down.
- **Cross-reference:** register items (1)-(13); closing paragraph; F-OP28S-06; F-OP27S-07.

**F-OP32S-05** [MEDIUM -- advisory, cannot carry] -- `[9f]`'s scoping leaves the append-only corrections block entirely ungated.
- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9f]`, `reg_section` scoping; v0.32 entry, corrections (q), (r), (s).
- **Substance:** `[9f]` scopes both its checks to text after "defect register disposition" (offset 4440). Corrections (q), (r) and (s) sit at 2436, 3370 and 3780 -- outside `declared_count`, outside the parse, and outside the duplicate-severity check. P-5b: a full register row placed in the corrections block re-dispositions an adversarial HIGH to `LOW CLOSED` and the build is green, with `PASS: Register parsed == declared (13 parsed, 13 declared)` and `PASS: No duplicate-severity finding IDs (16 unique)` both passing. The scoping was necessary -- correction (q) contains "(i)" and "(ii)" markers that would inflate `declared_count` -- so this is a cure that created a blind region, and it created it in the part of the entry whose function is to rewrite prior dispositions. That is the highest-leverage text in the document to leave unchecked.

## 5. Boundary report

The boundary did not move, and at a freeze that is the whole question. Internally the instrument is in the best condition I have audited: six externally anchored chain links, thirteen versions of unbroken append-only, a register that parses completely for the first time, and three corrections that concede rather than reframe. None of it reaches outside the packet, and this is the round where that stops being a trend and becomes a terminal property. **EXTERNAL is nominally 2 and effectively 0**: neither tag is examined by any gate, a fabricated DOI raises the count and builds green, one tag grades a producer-held non-shipping document EXTERNAL by its own text, and the two real deposits anchor other artifacts rather than any v0.32 value. No seat report from any of the thirty-two versions has ever shipped, so the eight verdicts, the finding IDs, the Class A/B/C/D assignment that triggers the amendment, and the "all executing" claim are all ASSERTED -- and the entry's own closing list discloses "packet non-closure" and "fresh-execution non-reproducibility" as standing boundaries while the status line declares FROZEN. The record already contains the precedent: Section 0.1 states that **v0.4 claimed FROZEN status and v0.5 reverted it to DRAFT CANDIDATE**. That reversion was for a worse cause -- v0.4 had erased a recorded HALT, and v0.32 records both adversarial HALTs faithfully, which is a real and creditable difference. But it establishes that in this record a FROZEN claim is not self-validating. The step has not changed across eight of my reports and is now one action: deposit this packet's `HISTORY.sha256`, cite the DOI, and ship the eight seat reports under manifest. That converts the chain root from self-attested to externally fixed, disposes of adversarial finding `F-GPT31-06` on its merits rather than by subsumption, and makes the carry claim checkable by a reader instead of by assertion. It is the difference between freezing a verified artifact and freezing a disclosure set.

## 6. D-7 process health

- **Did every probe come from an enumerated list?** No. P-4's DOI-form fabrication and P-5's corrections-block row are novel and appear in no D-4 class; both were built to test claims the entry makes about its own gates.
- **Did the dispatch tell me where to look?** More than in any prior round. The cover note names the five attack surfaces, states the conclusions in advance, and instructs "if the FROZEN claim is honest, say so." Preregistration against that brief is weak and I marked it so at freeze. Two findings did not come from the brief: F-OP32S-01 came from grepping the body for "FB-7b", and F-OP32S-02 required diffing Section 25 against the v0.28 packet on my disk.
- **Is the ASSERTED fraction unchanged from the prior round?** No -- 80.0% to **90.9%**, with COMPUTED falling 3 to **0**. The freeze candidate is the least machine-backed entry in the record, and per policy states neither figure, so the sealed document will not contain that fact.
- **Have the recent rounds all been producer-family?** No. v0.31 was carried by six non-producer seats across two families and adversarially audited by two more. That is the strongest round composition the program has achieved, and it is the reason the amendment has a factual basis to rest on even though the reports do not ship. This round -- v0.32 -- is producer-family advisory again, and my verdict has no weight in it.

## 7. Verdict

**HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER -- advisory only, non-binding. No carry vote. No FB-7b weight. This HALT does not bind the freeze; it is recorded and forwarded.**

Severity ledger as I calibrate it: **1 CRITICAL / 3 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM / 1 LOW / 1 INFORMATIONAL = 8.** Under the producer-instance exclusion none of it carries, and the CRITICAL in particular must be re-rated by a seat whose severity can.

**The FROZEN claim is not earned, and the reason is not a matter of judgement.** The document declares itself FROZEN in `### 0.1 Status` and declares FB-7b OPEN 923 characters later in the same subsection, while Section 25 and the entry declare it RESOLVED. A freeze licensed by a locker's resolution cannot ship stating that the locker is open. That alone returns the draft.

Three things compound it, in descending order of how much they should worry a carrying seat. The amendment that resolves FB-7b **removed** an execution conjunct from the rule rather than relaxing the verdict predicate as the entry describes -- "running all 186 tests" survives in this document only inside a sealed entry quoting a prior objection to its non-satisfaction -- and register item (5) records that pytest was absent from the dispatched environment for three fresh seats this round, which is the conjunct that was deleted. The EXTERNAL count that item (9) uses to subsume an adversarial HIGH consists of two tags no gate examines, one of which grades producer-held non-shipping reports EXTERNAL against its own text; a fabricated DOI raises the same count and builds green. And the register closes zero of thirteen findings while the closing paragraph discloses "packet non-closure" and "fresh-execution non-reproducibility" as standing boundaries.

**What would make the freeze honest.** Four of the five are edits, not investigations: update the Section 0.1 FB-7b sentence or withdraw FROZEN; state the amendment's full scope, including which conjuncts were removed; regrade the seat-reports tag ASSERTED; and either close some findings or write down what FROZEN asserts and what it does not. The fifth is the one that has been outstanding for eight of my reports: deposit `HISTORY.sha256`, cite the DOI, and ship the eight seat reports under manifest.

**Findings a non-producer seat should re-derive first**, since a producer-family seat is the least credible party to adjudicate a producer-family freeze: **F-OP32S-01**, which is `grep -n "FB-7b" ` against the status line; **F-OP32S-02**, which is `grep -c "running all 186 tests"` against any packet from v0.20 through v0.28; and **F-OP32S-03**, which is the P-4 pair and takes one rebuild. None requires taking my word for anything, and the first two require no prior packet at all.

The instrument is in the best internal condition I have audited in nine rounds. It is not ready to be called finished.

---

## D. BOUNDARY REPORT

**At v0.28 I located the boundary at claim-to-evidence binding. At v0.32 the
boundary is the external anchor, and the anchor has been named rather than
installed.**

The trajectory is consistent. Each version brings a layer inside the tooling, and
the defect relocates to the first layer outside. v0.32 does something genuinely new:
Section 22.2 states, precisely and without hedging, that a party controlling the
text, code, trust roots, manifest, and seal file can produce a packet passing every
check with rc=0, and that only externally held bytes distinguish forgery from
authenticity. That is an exact description of what my v0.28 probe P5 demonstrated,
written by the producer, in the normative body. It names the three anchor classes
that would close the gap.

And then the entry cites two anchors, neither of which is installed. Tag 1 is
producer-held custody with producer-computed digests, which Section 22.2's own
anchor (a) excludes by the word "independently." Tag 2 is an admissible anchor class
cited without the artifact that makes it operative: no pinned digest, no gate, no
statement of which bytes should match. The document has advanced from not knowing
what would close the gap to knowing exactly what would close it and labelling the
gap closed.

That is the current boundary, and it is a specific and narrow one. **The instrument
now computes everything internal and nothing external, and the label EXTERNAL is
applied by the same process that writes the claims.**

**What would bring it inside, concretely.** Three changes, none large. First, pin
the sha256 of each cited Zenodo deposit adjacent to its DOI and gate on the pin's
presence and well-formedness. Second, have one carrying seat publish its own report
digest where the producer cannot edit it, and cite that publication rather than the
producer's copy -- one seat, one line, and anchor (a) becomes real. Third, have
`check()` emit evidence records and require every COMPUTED and EXTERNAL tag to
resolve to one, which closes F-OP32H-07 and makes the headline number a
measurement.

**What it will not fix.** The patient-contributor adversary remains untested, as it
has in every round on record. Nothing here changes that, and Section 22.2 says so.

**Is the FROZEN claim earned?** No, and the reasons are structural rather than
byte-level. The document's own freeze precondition is that every FREEZE-BLOCKER
field be filled and that the Section 22 carry rule be satisfied. The FB-7b field is
filled by an amendment that (i) no seat has carried, because the taxonomy it
depends on appears only in v0.32 and zero times in the v0.31 entry, (ii) is
evaluated under a precondition that the seats most likely to trigger it are excluded
from triggering, and (iii) is not present in Section 22, the section the precondition
cites. The freeze's headline novelty, EXTERNAL above zero, is two labels over
unverifiable state. And the status word itself is gated by nothing: I changed it to
an invented string and the build passed.

**What the round got right, stated before the ledger because it is the actual
delta.** The append-only discipline held: 28 of 28 historical entry seals are
byte-identical to the copies I have held since v0.28, verified against bytes the
producer could not reach. Section 22.2 is an honest and precise statement of the
forgery boundary and it names the right anchors. Correction (q) rejects the
producer's own overwide closure claim. Correction (r) concedes a naming defect that
no seat would have been harmed by. Correction (s) concedes that a shipped instrument
document contains a false statement. The `[9f]` predicate I found missing at v0.28
now exists and fires correctly on malformed rows. The FB-7b register row states
outright that the amendment is "carried by the v0.31 round that demonstrates it" --
circular, and I count it as a HIGH, but it is stated in the open rather than
concealed, and the concealment is what S-9 says to grade. Zero COMPUTED tags means
zero false COMPUTED tags; the class that produced my sharpest v0.28 finding cannot
recur in this entry.

This is not a dishonest packet. It is an honest packet making a claim its own
machinery does not support.

---

## E. D-7 REFLEXIVE CHECK

**Did every probe come from an enumerated list?** No, but the risk was live and I
declared it before executing. PR1 and PR2 are new classes targeting surfaces that
did not exist before this version. PR3, PR4, and PR5 are deliberate re-runs of my
own v0.28 findings, and their purpose was verification in the bytes, not discovery
-- PR3 and PR3b changed my assessment of a repair I would otherwise have recorded as
clean.

**Did the dispatch tell me where to look?** Yes, substantially, and I flag it. The
cover note named the five attack surfaces: status change, FB-7b amendment, EXTERNAL
citations, register dispositions, standing boundaries. Four of my five HIGH findings
sit on those surfaces. This is leakage in the D-7 sense: a seat told where to look
will find things there. What was not supplied was the cross-version seal comparison,
which is the one result no dispatch could have predetermined because it depends on
bytes I happen to hold.

**Is the ASSERTED fraction unchanged from the prior round?** **Yes, for the third
consecutive round.** 91.7, 91.3, 90.9. COMPUTED fell 1, 2, 0. The freeze is being
declared at the point where the entry's verified fraction reached zero. See
F-OP32H-09.

**Have the recent rounds all been producer-family?** No, and this is a genuine and
significant improvement. The v0.31 round fielded six non-producer carrying seats
across two families plus two adversarial seats. The apparatus is no longer measuring
only itself. **This seat, however, is producer-family and advisory, and this report
discharges nothing.**

---

## VERDICT

**HALT -- ADVISORY ONLY.** I am a producer-family advisory seat. **This verdict does
not bind. It carries no carry vote and no FB-7b weight. It freezes nothing and
blocks nothing.** It is recorded and forwarded. Any record describing this as a
binding HALT misdescribes it.

Severity ledger: 0 CRITICAL / 5 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 1 LOW.

**The FROZEN claim is not earned.** Blocking findings and what clears each:

- **F-OP32H-01** -- clears when the seat-report anchor is retagged ASSERTED, or when
  a carrying seat publishes its own digest outside producer control and the entry
  cites that.
- **F-OP32H-02** -- clears when each cited DOI carries a pinned sha256 and a gate
  fails on its absence; verified when PR2's DOI mutation turns the build red.
- **F-OP32H-03** -- clears when a status gate exists and PR1 turns red.
- **F-OP32H-04** -- clears when the FB-7b row states the amendment is not yet
  carried, or when a round is dispatched under the amended rule with the taxonomy
  supplied to seats in advance.
- **F-OP32H-05** -- clears when Section 22 carries the operative rule in its own
  text.

Each is verified by re-running the probe that found it, not by inspection.

**Recommendation.** F-OP32H-01 and -04 are one sentence each and are the honest
form of the current state; they cost nothing but the word FROZEN. F-OP32H-02, -03,
and -05 are small mechanical changes. If the project lead wants a defensible freeze
rather than a fast one, the shortest honest path is: retag the two EXTERNAL claims,
state that the amendment is producer-authored and uncarried, amend Section 22 in
place, add the status gate and the DOI pins, then dispatch one round under the
amended rule to seats who are told the taxonomy in advance. That round -- not this
one -- is the one that can carry a freeze.

*Author of the instrument under audit: Bilal Syed Arfeen. This report is a seat
deliverable and ships unmodified.*

## R0234 · Seat S02-OPUS -- Advisory Audit Report, XZ Protocol v0.51, Round 10
