# Seat S02-OPUS -- Advisory Audit Report, XZ Protocol v0.51, Round 10

**Seat ID:** S02 | **Family:** Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic) | **Type:** Fresh (no prior seat context loaded)
**Role:** ADVISORY -- non-carrying, non-binding (producer family; Section 22.1)
**Finding namespace:** F-S02-51 | **Version audited:** v0.51 | **Round:** R10
**Verdict:** HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER (advisory)
**Severity ledger:** 3 CRITICAL / 3 HIGH / 4 MEDIUM / 2 LOW
**Class ledger (Section 22.3):** 4 Class A / 1 Class B / 4 Class D / 1 Class E / 2 unclassified LOW

Auditor operated in **Mode A** with full substrate access: packet reconstructed on disk, build.py and all six test suites executed, eight mutation builds constructed and run. Substrate-claim verification confidence **high**.

---

## 0. Reconstruction and baseline

| Step | Claimed | Executed | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `python3 setup.txt` | 16 OK | 16 OK / 0 FAIL / 0 MISSING | MATCH |
| `python3 build.py` | BUILD PASSED (200 checks) | BUILD PASSED, 200 PASS lines, 0 FAIL | MATCH |
| `pytest -q` | 117 tests | 117 passed | MATCH |
| `pytest xz_protocol_phase_a_tests.py -q` | 69 tests | 69 passed | MATCH |
| Total | 186 GREEN | 186 GREEN | MATCH |

Independently recomputed the trust-roots `manifest_digest` from its own stated construction (`sha256sum <12 normative code files, alphabetical> | sha256sum`): **a70cc7fd...460893 reproduces exactly.** Section 0.1's derived counts also hold on bytes: 27 adversarial tests, 14 kernel test functions, 16 source-frame records, 14 normative files (12 + 1 + 1).

**Task-register substitution (disclosed).** The dispatch mandates "Execute A-1 through A-7." No such register exists anywhere in the shipped packet. `A-4` appears exactly once, as an incidental back-reference inside the sealed v0.20 entry pointing to `PRODUCER_SELF_DISCIPLINE_v2_DELTA.md`, which does not ship. Rather than invent seven tasks and report against them, this seat executed **Section 22 items 1 through 7** -- the shipped, normative, in-packet audit obligations -- as the task register, plus the mutation battery the dispatch demands. See F-S02-51-07.

---

## 1. Mutation battery

MUTATION-LANDED is used strictly: a mutation *lands* when a semantic corruption survives to `BUILD PASSED: all checks GREEN` after the attacker resyncs `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, which any packet-controlling party does by definition.

| ID | Mutation | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Duplicate `ENTRY_v0.49` seal line, canonical lowercase digest (exact R9 replay) | **CAUGHT** -- both new checks fired |
| M2b | Duplicate `ENTRY_v0.50` seal line, digest rendered uppercase, placed before the genuine line | **MUTATION-LANDED** |
| M3 | Restore the `*Provenance and review status.*` seal terminus | Build breaks (`ENTRY_v0.51`, `FULL_SECTION_27`) -- diagnostic, not an attack |
| M4 | In-place mutation of carried entry v0.30 with partial reseal | **CAUGHT** -- PRIOR_HISTORY derivation fired |
| M5b | In-place mutation of carried entry v0.30 with full internal reseal | **MUTATION-LANDED** |
| M6 | Second, false `FULL_SECTION_27` seal line (all-zero digest) | **MUTATION-LANDED** |
| M7 | Phantom uppercase seal for nonexistent `ENTRY_v0.52` | **MUTATION-LANDED** |
| M8 | Fabricated `[COMPUTED:]` evidence content sealed into the v0.51 entry | **MUTATION-LANDED** |

Five landed. Two controls confirm real coverage: the canonical R9 attack is genuinely closed (M1), and Section 22.2's partial-reseal detection claim genuinely holds (M4).

---

## 2. Findings

### CRITICAL

**F-S02-51-01** CRITICAL -- Sealed mutation-test evidence for the R9 repair is arithmetically impossible on v0.51 bytes

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_51.md` Section 27, v0.51 entry, third paragraph; register item (1).
- **Substance:** The entry states that on v0.51 bytes the duplicate-seal mutation produces `BUILD FAILED` with `"HISTORY seal line count (51) == entry count (50)"` and `"No duplicate ENTRY labels in HISTORY (51 lines, 50 unique)"`, tagged `[COMPUTED: mutation test executed on v0.51 build.py, both checks fired]`. Executed on shipped v0.51 bytes (M1), build.py emits `HISTORY seal line count (52) == entry count (51)` and `No duplicate ENTRY labels in HISTORY (52 lines, 51 unique)`. v0.51 carries 51 amendment entries and 51 seal lines; a duplicate yields 52 against 51. The quoted pair is the v0.50 arithmetic (50 entries, 51 lines after duplication). The evidence sealed to prove the repair was not produced on the bytes it claims.
- **Disposition:** HALT-and-escalate. Re-run the duplicate-seal mutation on v0.51 bytes, capture the actual two strings, and replace both quoted literals in the v0.51 entry and in register item (1). Because the v0.51 entry is current-version, this is a reseal, not an append-only violation. Do not carry the corrected strings forward without re-executing at the next version -- this defect is a straight copy-forward.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 22.3 Class A (sealed claim false on shipped bytes). F-S01-50-01, whose CLOSED disposition rests on this evidence. Enabling mechanism: F-S02-51-06.

**F-S02-51-02** CRITICAL -- The declared seal terminus does not exist in the document; both seal computations fall back silently

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_51.md`, end of Section 27 (`...e884e0f5ored by Bilal Syed Arfeen`); `build.py:67`; `build.py:366`.
- **Substance:** Standing boundary item six, declared in the v0.51 entry and in every entry from v0.44 onward, is `seal terminus at Provenance marker`. The string `*Provenance and review status.*` occurs **zero** times in the shipped document. The deletion took the surrounding sentence with it, splicing the 64-hex PRIOR_HISTORY value directly into a truncated word: `PRIOR_HISTORY c345bd90...e884e0f5ored by Bilal Syed Arfeen`. Both seal paths guard with `if prov > 0 else <whole section>`, so `find()` returning -1 is absorbed with no check. Consequence on bytes: 813 bytes of provenance, no-peer-review, and end-of-document prose are sealed inside `ENTRY_v0.51`, and `FULL_SECTION_27` now spans all 219,043 characters of Section 27. M3 confirms the omission is load-bearing -- restoring the marker breaks both seals, so the shipped chain values were derived from the corrupted text.
- **Disposition:** HALT-and-escalate. (1) Restore the marker and the elided sentence text at the splice point and reseal `ENTRY_v0.51`, `FULL_SECTION_27`, and `PRIOR_HISTORY`. (2) Replace the silent fallback at `build.py:67` and `build.py:366` with `check(prov > 0, "Provenance seal terminus present")` so absence is a build failure rather than a span change. (3) State in the v0.52 entry that the v0.51 chain values were computed over an unterminated span, so external holders of v0.51 bytes have a documented expectation.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 22.3 Class A. Standing boundary item six. Precedent for recording a chain fork rather than hiding it: v0.48 correction (bd).

**F-S02-51-03** CRITICAL -- "The R8 duplicate-seal defect class is structurally extinct" is false; three neighbouring shapes pass

- **Locus:** `build.py:360` and `build.py:363-365`; claim at `xz_protocol_v0_51.md` Section 27, v0.51 entry, third paragraph.
- **Substance:** Both repaired checks select seal lines with `l.startswith(c) for c in '0123456789abcdef'` and `'ENTRY_' in l`. The filter is case-sensitive and ENTRY-only, so the repair covers exactly one shape of the class: a lowercase-hex-leading duplicate of an existing ENTRY label. Three shapes survive. M2b: a duplicate `ENTRY_v0.50` line whose digest is rendered uppercase (its true digest begins `e`, so `E` escapes the filter) and placed *before* the genuine line so the PRIOR_HISTORY derivation dictionary still resolves to the genuine value -- `HISTORY.sha256` contains two `ENTRY_v0.50` lines and the gate reports `51 lines, 51 unique`, BUILD PASSED. M6: a second `FULL_SECTION_27` line carrying an all-zero digest is uncounted because non-ENTRY seal lines have no cardinality check, and line 368 tests existence (`any(l == expected)`) rather than uniqueness -- BUILD PASSED. M7: a phantom seal for a nonexistent `ENTRY_v0.52`, uppercase-rendered, evades both the cardinality filter and the surjectivity check at line 356, which uses the same lowercase filter -- BUILD PASSED. The extinction claim overstates a one-shape fix as a class closure.
- **Disposition:** HALT-and-escalate. (1) Case-fold the filter: `l[:1].lower() in '0123456789abcdef'`, at lines 356 and 360. (2) Extend cardinality to all seal lines, not only ENTRY lines: assert exactly one `FULL_SECTION_27` line and exactly one line per declared label. (3) Assert the label set of `HISTORY.sha256` equals the expected label set exactly, so unknown labels such as `ENTRY_v0.52` fail rather than being ignored. (4) Restate the claim as "the lowercase-duplicate shape is closed; the class is not," or re-verify extinction with the mutations above after the fix.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 22.3 Class A. F-S01-49-04 and F-S01-50-01 (the R8/R9 duplicate-seal lineage). M1 shows the canonical shape is genuinely closed.

### HIGH

**F-S02-51-04** HIGH -- Correction (bh)'s locus claim is byte-false at the line it names

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_51.md` Section 27, v0.51 entry, correction (bh); `build.py:356`.
- **Substance:** Correction (bh) is tagged `[COMPUTED: v0.50 build.py line 356 is a set comprehension; v0.51 build.py lines 356-365 are list operations]`. On shipped v0.51 bytes, line 356 is `seal_labels = {l.split()[1] for l in history_lines if ...}` -- still a set comprehension. Line 358 is a string `find`. Lines 357, 361 and 364 are `check` calls. Only 360 and 363 are list operations. A verifier following the correction to line 356 to confirm the repair finds the exact construct the correction says was replaced, and would reasonably conclude the repair did not land.
- **Disposition:** Amend correction (bh) to cite the actual repair locus, `build.py:360-365`, and drop the "356" claim or restate it as "the v0.50 cardinality set comprehension at line 356 is replaced by the list operations now at lines 360-365; the set comprehension surviving at line 356 in v0.51 is `seal_labels`, a different check."
- **Cross-reference:** Section 22.3 Class A. F-S02-51-01 (same paragraph, same class). F-S02-51-06 (why no gate caught it).

**F-S02-51-05** HIGH -- Section 25 FB-7b row, the designated single source of truth, omits R9

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_51.md` Section 25, FB-7b row, final sentence; Section 0.1, paragraph two.
- **Substance:** Section 0.1 states that "FB-7b status, rationale, and the full carrying-seat trajectory are recorded in the Section 25 FB-7b row (single source of truth; no duplicate rationale maintained here)." The row's trajectory ends at `R8 (v0.49): Kimi K3 S01 carrying seat HALTed binding`. R9 on v0.50 -- a binding carrying-seat HALT on a Class A finding, recorded in the v0.51 entry -- is absent. The freeze-blocker register therefore understates the carrying-seat HALT record by one round, and the surface Section 0.1 designates as complete is not.
- **Disposition:** Append to the FB-7b row: `R9 (v0.50): Kimi K3 S01 carrying seat HALTed binding (cardinality gate set semantics, Class A); Opus S02 advisory CONDITIONAL PASS.` Add a standing producer step that the FB-7b row is updated in the same edit as any entry recording a carrying-seat verdict.

## S1. Staging and byte verification

### S1.1 Extraction -- DEFECT FOUND AT THE FIRST STEP

The extraction procedure shipped verbatim in `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` was executed exactly as given. Result:

```
sha256sum -c PACKET_SHA256SUMS
  4 files OK, 15 files FAILED
sha256sum: WARNING: 15 computed checksums did NOT match
```

Root cause, established by byte-level diagnosis: the shipped splitter uses the delimiter `######_XZPACKET_FILE_SPLIT_######\n` and writes `b[nl+1:]` as the file body. The packet places a newline *before* each delimiter, so every file except the terminal member receives one extra trailing `\n`. Confirmation -- for all 15 failing members, `sha256(body[:-1])` matches the manifest digest exactly; the sole passing packet member, `xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json`, is last in the packet and therefore has no trailing delimiter to absorb.

| Member | As-shipped extraction | After removing one trailing byte |
|---|---|---|
| `HISTORY.sha256` | FAILED | OK |
| `build.py` | FAILED | OK |
| 13 further `.py` members | FAILED | OK |
| `xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json` | OK | (terminal member; unaffected) |

After repairing the splitter (strip one trailing newline from all non-terminal members), `sha256sum -c PACKET_SHA256SUMS` returns **19/19 OK**. Every subsequent section of this report was executed against the repaired, digest-verified bytes.

See **F-S01-62-08**.

| P-9 | REJECTING CONTROL: `convergence_group=99` (dangling) | fired | `ValueError: references convergence_group 99 which does not exist ... Use null for ungrouped/noted findings.` |
| P-10 | REJECTING CONTROL: scalar `cg=2` while contained in group 1 | fired | `ValueError: Bidirectional parity requires these to match.` |

**Battery result: 5 landed (P-1, P-2, P-3, P-4, P-8), 1 crashed uncleanly (P-6), 4 correctly rejected.** The four rejecting controls confirm the harness exercises the live gates rather than a stub.

## S6. Seven-layer traversal

| Layer | Reached | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **1 -- Code execution** | YES | build.py rc=0 / 247 PASS (claimed 248); pytest 186/186 GREEN; `sha256sum -c` 15/19 FAILED as shipped, 19/19 after repairing the shipped extraction procedure. |
| **2 -- Register verification** | YES | CI-1R byte-exact on all three generated artifacts. The mechanical layer is clean. |
| **3 -- Cross-layer consistency** | YES | Version tokens agree (0.62 front matter, Status, terminal line, 22.2/22.3 at VERSION-1). Boundary count 35 agrees across JSON, generator, and entry. **Failures:** front-matter date vs entry date; ASSERTED seat counts vs COMPUTED brackets (3 of 4); `R20_TRIAGE.txt` group-5 severity vs index/register; Status-line `source_finding_id` vs absent field. |
| **4 -- Adversarial probing** | YES | 10 register mutations + 4 build sabotages. 5 landed, 1 unclean crash, 4 correct rejections, 2 benign controls clean. |
| **5 -- Temporal integrity** | YES | 62 ENTRY seals + FULL_SECTION_27 + exactly 1 PRIOR_HISTORY; derivation succeeds; S-2 sabotage detected. Append-only holds. |
| **6 -- Methodology audit** | YES | Dispatch and AUDIT_CONTEXT claims audited against shipped bytes: two refuted (248 PASS; 19/19 OK as shipped), one refuted at the schema layer (`source_finding_id` "added"). The audit-support layer is now itself a Class A surface. |
| **7 -- Boundary disclosure** | YES | 35 boundaries enumerated and byte-exact. `[9e]` cardinal-range gate matched zero range claims in the v0.62 entry -- vacuous this round, correctly pre-disclosed as boundary 23. No boundary covers the four Class A surfaces below; that is the substantive gap. |

**Biomedical Fractal reading.** The defect is not diffuse; it has a single histology at three sites. In every Class A finding below, the *tissue* is identical: a hand-written sentence that describes the mechanism more completely than the mechanism implements. `register_gen.py:136` performs containment; the entry says "not substring matching." The seat field is read; the entry says "authoritative." The parity check runs one direction; the entry says "must equal." The schema lacks a field; the Status line says "added." The generated register -- the part no human wrote -- is byte-perfect. The lesion is exclusively at the prose-code interface, and it is now confined to a margin of roughly one sentence per repair. That is a narrowing lesion, not a resolving one: the surface shrank from R20 (four defect classes) to R21 (four claims about four repairs), but it did not clear.

**F-S01-62-01** HIGH -- Class A -- Status line asserts a schema field that does not exist on shipped bytes

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_62.md:5` (Status line, gated BODY region).
- **Substance:** The Status line states "source_finding_id field added for CI-8 literal resolution." The field is absent from every shipped byte: zero occurrences in `EXECUTABLE_PACKET.txt`, zero in the 17 `findings[]` records of `r20_findings_index.json`, zero in `xz_protocol_register_gen.py`. The shipped index contradicts the Status line directly: group 3's `triage_adjudication` reads "R21 **will** add source_finding_id field to the findings schema." The register's own disposition for that group is NOTED, not CLOSED -- the machine-generated layer is honest; the hand-written Status line is not.
- **Evidence:** `grep -c source_finding_id EXECUTABLE_PACKET.txt` -> `0`. `python3 -c "..."` over the index shows finding-record keys `['finding_id','seat','source_severity','defect_class','convergence_group']`. `r20_findings_index.json:199`. `xz_protocol_v0_62.md:5`.
- **Disposition:** Either implement the field in the findings schema and add a generator-side resolution check before v0.63, or amend the Status line to future tense ("`source_finding_id` deferred to R22 per group-3 NOTED disposition"). Do not ship both a NOTED disposition and a completed-tense Status claim for the same item.
- **Cross-reference:** `METHODOLOGY_v2.txt:92` names this exact class -- "The Status line that says 'VERSION-1 gate implemented' when build.py has no such gate." R20 group 3 (NOTED). Section 22.3 Class A ("contradicted status").

**F-S01-62-02** HIGH -- Class A -- Receipt validation described as structural is substring containment

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py:130-142`; claim at `xz_protocol_v0_62.md:5` (Status line) and in the v0.62 entry item (1) adjudication text.
- **Substance:** Both the Status line and the entry's `[COMPUTED: generate_register]` adjudication state that receipt validation requires "the exact canonical distribution string verbatim (not substring matching)." The shipped implementation is `if dist_str not in receipt: raise ValueError(...)`. That is substring matching -- the canonical string as a substring of an otherwise unconstrained free-text field. A receipt containing the canonical string alongside arbitrary contradictory content passes. The R20 defect was substring matching on severity tokens; CI v0.3.2 narrowed the needle and kept the haystack.
- **Evidence:** Probe P-3. Group 5 receipt replaced with `"Source distribution: 1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM. Triage severity HIGH. Distribution is actually 2 LOW. Receipt fabricated."` -- no gate fired, and the register regenerated **byte-identically to the shipped protocol**. Probe P-8: `triage_severity` raised MEDIUM -> HIGH with the receipt untouched (still reading "Triage severity MEDIUM.") -- no gate fired, severity changed in the emitted register.
- **Disposition:** Replace containment with structural equality against a canonical receipt grammar: parse the receipt into `(distribution, triage_severity, deviation_flag)` and assert each against the computed values. Minimum viable: require `receipt.strip()` to equal a generator-produced canonical receipt string, making the receipt a computed artifact rather than a producer-written one. Until then, amend the entry and Status line to read "receipt must contain the canonical distribution string" -- which is what the code does.
- **Cross-reference:** R20 group 1 (CLOSED -- disposition not sustained). F-S01-62-07 (uniform-group vacuity). `METHODOLOGY_v2.txt:92`, "The docstring that says 'receipt is structural' when the code checks by substring." Section 22.3 Class A.

**F-S01-62-03** HIGH -- Class A -- Seat count moved to an authoritative field that is never validated; wrong-count defect relocated, not closed

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py:30-40` (`_unique_seat_count`), 60-82 (findings lookup construction).
- **Substance:** R20 group 2 was CLOSED on the ground that seat identity would come from `findings_by_id[fid]["seat"]` rather than from parsing the finding_id. The field is now read, but nothing validates it: no schema check that `seat` is present, no cross-check that `seat` is consistent with the seat encoded in the finding_id it accompanies (`F-S05-61-01C` -> `S05C`), no uniqueness or vocabulary constraint against the declared `seats[]` list. The defect class named in the R20 triage -- "a finding with a non-standard ID format produces a wrong seat count silently" -- survives verbatim with the substrate changed from the ID string to the `seat` field. The superseded ID-parsing branch also remains live as a fallback at lines 37-40.
- **Evidence:** Probe P-1. Setting `findings[F-S05-61-01C].seat = "S05F"` -- a value that is a legitimate member of the declared `seats[]` list and contradicts its own finding_id -- produced no gate fire and silently emitted `[5-seat / 7-finding convergence: ...]` in place of the shipped `[6-seat / 7-finding ...]`. Benign control P-1b (same field rewritten to `S05C`) produced a byte-identical register, confirming the harness discriminates. Probe P-6: deleting the key raises an uncaught `KeyError: 'seat'`, not a validation error.
- **Disposition:** Add three validations to the findings-lookup loop before v0.63: (a) `seat` is a required non-empty field, raising `ValueError` not `KeyError`; (b) `seat` is a member of `index["seats"]`; (c) `seat` matches the seat token parsed from `finding_id`, since the ID regex already guarantees the token's shape. Then delete the ID-parsing fallback branch rather than leaving a superseded code path resident.
- **Cross-reference:** R20 group 2 (CLOSED -- disposition not sustained). F-S01-62-11 (unclean failure mode). F-S01-62-12 (no vendor field on the same records). R20_TRIAGE Surface 2.

**F-S01-62-04** HIGH -- Class A -- "Bidirectional" membership parity is unidirectional

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py:170-185`.
- **Substance:** The entry's item (4) adjudication states that "each finding's scalar convergence_group must equal the group whose finding_ids contains it." The implementation builds `fid_to_group` from the groups' membership lists and then checks parity only `if fid in fid_to_group`. When no group's `finding_ids` contains the finding, the loop body is skipped entirely and the cross-layer check at lines 158-168 accepts the scalar because the referenced group exists. A finding may therefore claim membership in a real group that does not claim it back. The direction the repair covers (contained but disagreeing) fires; the direction that produces silent under-counting does not.
- **Evidence:** Probe P-2. Removing `F-S05-61-01C` from group 1's `finding_ids` while leaving its scalar `convergence_group=1` produced no gate fire, and the register silently moved from `[6-seat / 7-finding convergence]` to `[5-seat / 6-finding convergence]`. Rejecting control P-10 (scalar `cg=2` while contained in group 1) fired correctly, confirming the covered direction works.
- **Disposition:** After building `fid_to_group`, assert the reverse containment: for every finding with a non-null `convergence_group`, require `fid in fid_to_group` and `fid_to_group[fid] == cg`. One added conditional closes it. Alternatively derive `finding_ids` from the scalars and eliminate the dual representation entirely -- the redundancy is the defect surface.
- **Cross-reference:** R20 group 5 (CLOSED -- disposition not sustained). Note that R20 group 5's own source distribution is the mixed one at F-S01-62-06. Section 22.3 Class A.

**F-S01-62-05** HIGH -- Class A -- Three of four asserted seat counts contradict the computed brackets in the same entry

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_62.md:1383`, v0.62 amendment entry, `[ASSERTED]` prose paragraph versus the `[COMPUTED: generate_register]` register items immediately following.
- **Substance:** The entry's narrative paragraph states "Defect 1, 8/10 seats", "Defect 2, 3/10", "Defect 3, 6/10". The register items generated from the same index, printed in the same entry, read `[6-seat / 7-finding convergence]`, `[2-seat convergence]`, and `[5-seat:]`. Only Defect 4 (1/10 vs `[1-seat]`) agrees. `R20_TRIAGE.txt` sources the asserted figures via unenumerated tails ("+ 2 others", "+ 1 other") that have no corresponding records in the shipped index, so the asserted counts are not verifiable on shipped bytes and are contradicted by the verifiable ones. The `[ASSERTED]` tag discloses that the figures were not computed; it does not reconcile them with the computed figures sitting beside them, and no gate compares the two.
- **Evidence:** Regex extraction over the isolated v0.62 entry: asserted `['8/10','3/10','6/10','1/10']`; computed brackets `['6','2','1','2','5']` (register order: groups 1, 2, 4, 5, then NOTED group 3). Index census: 17 findings across 6 distinct seats (`S02F, S02C, S03F, S03C, S05F, S05C`); the declared `seats[]` list has 10 members, 4 of which contributed no findings.
- **Disposition:** Either enumerate the missing seat records in the index so the asserted and computed figures converge, or replace the narrative seat counts with the generator's computed values and delete the hand-written fractions. A build gate comparing every `N/10` in the current entry against the corresponding computed bracket would make the class mechanically unrepeatable.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-62-03 (the seat-count substrate). F-S01-62-12 (unrecorded seats). Section 22.3 Class A ("wrong count"). `METHODOLOGY_v2.txt:94`, "confining the producer's claims to only what the scribes can verify."

**F-S01-62-06** MEDIUM -- Class A -- Shipped triage document and shipped index disagree on a disposition severity

- **Locus:** `R20_TRIAGE.txt` Surface 4 versus `r20_findings_index.json` group 5 `triage_severity` and the emitted register item (4).
- **Substance:** `R20_TRIAGE.txt` states for the bidirectional-parity group: "Triage severity: HIGH (elevated from 1H+1M per convergence)." The index records `"triage_severity": "MEDIUM"` and the register emits `MEDIUM CLOSED`. Two shipped artifacts assert different severities for the same adjudicated group, and the entry's own history shows the elevation reasoning was considered and then not applied. Nothing gates the pair: probe P-8 confirms `triage_severity` is freely settable with the receipt untouched, so no mechanism would have caught the divergence in either direction.
- **Evidence:** `R20_TRIAGE.txt` Surface 4 block; `r20_findings_index.json` group 5; register item (4) reads `MEDIUM CLOSED via CI v0.3.2 architecture repair: Bidirectional membership parity`. Probe P-8 landed MEDIUM -> HIGH with no gate fire.
- **Disposition:** Reconcile to one value and state which document is the substrate of record for triage severity. If the elevation was intentional, the index is stale; if the index is correct, the triage narrative is stale. Then derive `triage_severity` from a stated rule over the source distribution rather than as a free field, so the receipt constrains it.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-62-02 (receipt does not constrain triage severity). R20 group 5. Section 22.3 Class A ("contradicted status").

**F-S01-62-07** MEDIUM -- Class D -- Uniform-distribution groups receive no receipt validation at all

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py:126-142`.
- **Substance:** `has_mixed` is true only when the source distribution has more than one severity or the triage diverges from the majority. For a uniform group whose triage equals the majority, the entire receipt block is skipped -- the receipt is neither required nor read. Four of the five shipped groups are in this state, and all four ship receipts asserting distributions ("All 7 source findings are HIGH. Distribution: 7 HIGH."). Those assertions are unvalidated and could be arbitrarily false. This is a defensible reading of the CI v0.3.2 rule as written; it is a gate limitation the entry does not name, so it is Class D only because the entry makes no claim about uniform groups -- but the Status line's phrase "receipt validation structural" reads as unconditional.
- **Evidence:** Probe P-4. Group 1's receipt replaced with `"Distribution: 3 LOW, 1 INFORMATIONAL. Triage severity INFORMATIONAL. No deviation."` -- against an actual distribution of 7 HIGH -- produced no gate fire and a register byte-identical to the shipped protocol.
- **Disposition:** Validate the receipt on every group with a receipt present, not only on mixed ones. The canonical distribution string is computed for all groups already (`_computed_dist_str` is assigned unconditionally at line 121), so the check costs one dedented conditional.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-62-02 (validation strength on the groups that are checked). R20 group 1. Boundary 23 (silent vacuity) is the nearest disclosed analogue but does not cover this locus.

**F-S01-62-08** MEDIUM -- Class A -- Shipped extraction procedure produces 15 of 19 digest failures; dispatch asserts 19/19 OK

- **Locus:** `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` "Extraction (copy-paste and run)" block; claim in the same file's "Build status" block and in `DISPATCH.txt`.
- **Substance:** The extraction snippet writes `b[nl+1:]` for each split segment. The packet places a newline before each delimiter, so every non-terminal member is written with one surplus trailing `\n`. Executing the procedure exactly as shipped yields `15 computed checksums did NOT match` against `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, while the audit-support files assert "PACKET_SHA256SUMS: 19/19 OK". The claim is reachable only after a repair the packet does not document. Every byte-anchored claim in the round depends on this step, so the defect sits upstream of the entire verification chain -- an auditor who trusted the shipped procedure would have reported a false 15-file digest failure, and one who trusted the shipped claim would never have run it.
- **Evidence:** As-shipped run: `sha256sum: WARNING: 15 computed checksums did NOT match`. Diagnostic: for all 15 failing members, `sha256(body[:-1])` equals the manifest digest; the single passing packet member is the terminal one. After stripping one trailing newline from all non-terminal members: `19/19 OK`, `build.py` rc=0, pytest 186/186.
- **Disposition:** Correct the snippet to `body = b[nl+1:]; body = body[:-1] if body.endswith(b"\n\n") else body`, or emit the packet with the delimiter immediately following each file's final byte. Then add the extraction procedure itself to the packet's verified surface -- it is currently the only load-bearing step with no gate over it.
- **Cross-reference:** Boundary 10 (packet non-closure) and boundary 11 (fresh-execution non-reproducibility) are adjacent disclosures but neither covers a deterministic, reproducible defect in the shipped procedure. Section 22.3 Class A.

**F-S01-62-09** LOW -- Class A -- Dispatch build-check count off by one

- **Locus:** `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` "Build status" block; `build.py` output.
- **Substance:** The audit-support files claim "build.py: 248 PASS, 0 FAIL". Observed: 247 PASS, 0 FAIL, rc=0, stable across three consecutive runs on digest-verified bytes. `build.py` emits no self-total, so the figure has no computed source and no gated body counterpart -- neither `247` nor `248` appears in the protocol.
- **Evidence:** `python3 build.py | grep -c "^  PASS:"` -> `247`, `247`, `247`.

**F-S01-62-11** LOW -- Class D -- Missing required field raises `KeyError` rather than a validation error

**F-S01-62-12** MEDIUM -- Class D -- The index has no field recording seat family, so the carry split is unverifiable on shipped bytes

- **Locus:** `r20_findings_index.json` top-level keys and `findings[]` record schema; claim at `xz_protocol_v0_62.md:5` and in the v0.62 entry.
- **Substance:** Section 22.1 makes carrying-seat eligibility a function of model family -- producer-family (Claude) seats are advisory, Kimi and GLM are eligible, GPT self-disqualified. The index records `carrying_halts: 4` and `advisory_halts: 6` but ships no vendor or family field on either the seat list or the finding records, so the partition that determines what binds cannot be checked against the bytes. Separately, the index declares 10 seats and 10 HALT verdicts while only 6 seats contributed findings; the register header emits "ten-seat audit" from `len(seats)`, and 4 seats (`S01F, S01C, S04F, S04C`) carry HALT verdicts with no recorded finding basis.

Finding-record keys: `['finding_id','seat','source_severity','defect_class','convergence_group']`. Distinct seats appearing in `findings[]`: 6. Substring search for vendor/family keys across the index: none.

## S10. Verdict

### **HALT** (advisory -- zero carry weight)

Seven Class A findings and one Class B finding. Section 22.3 makes both HALT-grade. Section 22 item 7's persistent-architectural-HALT exception is not invoked: none of these findings is architectural in the sense of boundaries 18, 19, or 35. All eight are repairable within the existing architecture, and five are single-conditional code changes.

This verdict binds nothing. This seat is producer-family (Claude), advisory under Section 22.1, and the finding above at F-S01-62-12 notes that the shipped index has no field by which a carrying/advisory partition could be checked at all.

### Key question: does v0.62 break the R7-R20 Class A streak?

**No. R7-R21 is now 15/15. H = 1.0 continues. Laplace P(Class A at R22) = 16/17 = 0.941.**

The observation worth recording is not that the streak held but *where* it held. Every finding in this report that carries Class A severity lives in a hand-written sentence describing a mechanism. The mechanisms themselves were clean at every point I could execute against them: CI-1R byte-exact on three artifacts, 186/186 pytest, 62/62 seals with mutation detection proven by sabotage, the VERSION-1 gate proven by sabotage, dangling references rejected, stale receipts on newly-mixed groups rejected, and the ID-parsing defect genuinely replaced by field lookup. Four rejecting controls fired with correct diagnostics. Not one scribe erred.

The four CI v0.3.2 upgrades and their fate at this seat:

| Upgrade | Mechanism | Claim about the mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Receipt on any mixed distribution | Implemented | Accurate |
| Receipt validation structural | Implemented as containment | **Overstated** |
| Seat count from authoritative field | Implemented | **Overstated** ("authoritative" implies validated) |
| Bidirectional parity | Implemented one direction | **Overstated** ("bidirectional") |
| Noted-bypass removal | Implemented | Accurate |
| `source_finding_id` | **Not implemented** | **Stated as done** |

Three of six claims outrun their implementations by roughly one adjective each -- "structural", "authoritative", "bidirectional" -- and one claims a field that does not exist. This is the Level 3 Iblis surface that `METHODOLOGY_v2.txt:120` predicts: "The claim that the mechanism works IS the Class A, because the claim outstrips the implementation." The dispatch predicted its own defect class at P4 with HIGH confidence and was right.

The narrowing is real and should be credited. R20's four defect classes were *in the code*. R21's Class A findings are, with two exceptions at the packet and triage layers, *in four adjectives about the code*. The lesion migrated from the mechanism to the sentence describing the mechanism, and the sentence is now short enough to gate.

The residual that R21 exposes and that no CI version yet addresses: **the audit-support layer is now itself an ungated Class A surface.** `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` asserted 248 PASS (247), asserted 19/19 OK (15 failed as shipped), and asserted `source_finding_id` added (absent). Those three claims sit outside `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, outside `build.py`, and outside `HISTORY.sha256`. The protocol's own verification surface has been hardened to the point where the dispatch that describes it is the weakest link -- and this round, the first thing that failed was the first command an auditor was told to run.

### S5.3 VERSION-1 gate attacks

The shipped gate computes the correct expected strings but checks only global presence in the entire pre-Section-27 body:

```text
check(expected_22_2 in body, ...)
check(expected_22_3 in body, ...)
```

Executed predicate probes:

| Mutation | Target gate result |
|---|---|
| Change Section 22.2 bound to v0.60, no decoy | FAIL — caught |
| Change Section 22.2 bound to v0.60 and insert `v0.1 through v0.61` elsewhere in body | **PASS — bypass** |
| Change Section 22.3 bound to v0.60 and insert `v0.38-v0.61` elsewhere in body | **PASS — bypass** |

Thus the VERSION-1 gate catches a simple stale token but does not establish that the **Section 22.2/22.3 loci** contain the expected values.

- Baseline amendment entries: 62; ascending: YES; unique: YES.
- Duplicate-current-version mutation: uniqueness predicate fails.

- Single-nibble change to an ENTRY seal is detected by the implemented byte-derived seal comparison.
- Duplicate `FULL_SECTION_27` line remains an acknowledged blind spot: build checks `any(exact_full_line)` but does not enforce FULL_SECTION_27 uniqueness. This is already disclosed as standing boundary #33, so it is **not a new finding**.
- `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` contains 19 members, excludes itself, and includes the findings index; self-entry/removal predicates are explicitly gated. The shipped package nonetheless starts with 15 digest mismatches.

The battery confirms several genuine v0.3.2 improvements — mixed-receipt requirement, source-distribution coupling, findings[] dangling rejection, authoritative seat count, enum/ID validation — while falsifying the stronger claims of structural receipt validation, full bidirectional parity, noted-path closure, source-ID resolution, and locus-specific VERSION-1 enforcement.

## S6: Seven-layer traversal

### Layer 1 — Code execution

**FAIL overall.** pytest is 186/186 GREEN, but the mandatory build is red with 35 errors and packet checksum verification is 4/19, not 19/19.

### Layer 2 — Register verification

**PASS for CI-1R reproduction.** The shipped register is exactly generated from the shipped index. However deterministic reproduction faithfully reproduces several false closure statements; this is semantic failure above the reproduction layer, not a CI-1R mismatch.

### Layer 3 — Cross-layer consistency

**FAIL.** Code/test bytes disagree with packet hashes, body digest citations, and trust-root manifest data. The front matter claims `source_finding_id` was added, while the index and generator contain no operative implementation. CI version labels agree syntactically but the implemented semantics are narrower than claimed.

### Layer 4 — Adversarial probing

**FAIL.** Multiple invalid structural mutations are accepted, including junk/negated receipts, reverse membership loss, duplicate group IDs, malformed/dangling noted records, empty source severity with crafted receipt, and bogus ignored `source_finding_id` values.

### Layer 5 — Temporal integrity

**PARTIAL / FAIL overall.** The internal append-only entry chain is strong: 62/62 ENTRY seals match current protocol bytes; FULL_SECTION_27 matches; exactly one PRIOR_HISTORY line exists; internal PRIOR_HISTORY derivation succeeds. But the shipped `HISTORY.sha256` file itself does not match the packet checksum declared for it, so packet-level temporal binding is broken.

### Layer 6 — Methodology audit

Severity mapping used by the program: Class A = HIGH (byte-false claim), Class B = MEDIUM, Class C = LOW, Class E = INFORMATIONAL.

### F-S03-62-01 — HIGH (Class A): baseline-green and 19/19 packet claims are byte-false

Following the dispatch's own extraction and execution recipe produces `BUILD FAILED: 35 error(s)` and fifteen checksum mismatches. The executable code/test files are newer/different bytes than the hashes carried by the packet/body/trust-root surfaces.

- **Recommendation:** Rebuild the packet atomically from one byte set: regenerate all normative digests, body citations, trust-root manifest digest, HISTORY/packet seals, and `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` only after executable bytes are final. Add a final package-from-scratch extraction test as a release gate.

### F-S03-62-02 — HIGH (Class A): `source_finding_id` “added for CI-8 literal resolution” is absent and non-operative

- **Locus:** protocol front-matter Status; `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt`; R20 triage disposition; `r20_findings_index.json`; `xz_protocol_register_gen.py`.

### F-S03-62-03 — HIGH (Class A): “structural, not substring” receipt validation still uses substring containment

- **Locus:** v0.62 entry register item (1), body repair (i), `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` receipt gate.
- **Substance:** The entry says receipt validation is structural and not substring-based. The implementation is `if dist_str not in receipt`, which is substring containment. A receipt may contain unrelated or explicitly negating prose so long as the canonical distribution phrase appears somewhere.
- **Evidence:** probe #3 accepted `UNRELATED PREFIX :: 1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM :: UNRELATED SUFFIX`; probe #4 accepted `This is NOT an adjudication. 1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM.`. Both should fail under the claimed structural semantics.

If free text is retained, narrow the claim to “requires verbatim canonical distribution substring.”

### F-S03-62-04 — HIGH (Class A): claimed bidirectional membership parity is only one-directional

- **Locus:** v0.62 register item (4), body repair (i), `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` cross-layer validation.
- **Substance:** The generator builds `fid_to_group` from group lists and checks that listed findings' scalar `convergence_group` equals the containing group. It never checks the reverse invariant: every finding with non-null scalar group must actually appear in that group's `finding_ids`. Removing a finding from a group while leaving its scalar unchanged is accepted.
- **Evidence:** probe #11 removes `F-S05-61-01C` from group 1 but leaves `findings[].convergence_group = 1`; generation ACCEPTS and emits a 5-seat/6-finding group. Probe #10 shows the implemented forward direction does reject an existing-but-wrong scalar for a still-listed finding.
- **Recommendation:** Enforce both directions explicitly: for each finding with `cg != null`, require exactly one group with that ID and require the finding ID to occur exactly once in that group's member list. Also enforce unique group IDs before building the membership map.

### F-S03-62-05 — HIGH (Class A): noted-finding bypass is not fully removed; separate noted path remains ungated

- **Locus:** v0.62 register item (3), body repair (i), `unique_findings_noted` validation in `xz_protocol_register_gen.py`.

That rule is applied to `findings[]` but not to the separate `unique_findings_noted` list. Noted entries can carry arbitrary group metadata, malformed/fake IDs, and duplicate IDs.
- **Evidence:** probe #14 malformed noted ID ACCEPT; #15 noted `convergence_group=999` ACCEPT; #16 duplicate noted ID ACCEPT. The generator ignores the dangling group field on this path.
- **Recommendation:** Eliminate the parallel noted schema or subject it to the same canonical finding validator as `findings[]`: ID regex, existence/source mapping, uniqueness, and `convergence_group is null` for ungrouped notes.

### F-S03-62-06 — MEDIUM (Class B): duplicate convergence-group IDs are accepted

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` group validation.
- **Substance:** Group IDs are collected into a set for dangling-reference checks but are never required to be unique. Two disjoint convergence groups can share the same `group_id`; after matching member scalars to that duplicated ID, generation succeeds.

### F-S03-62-07 — MEDIUM (Class B): VERSION-1 gate is body-global, not Section-22-locus-bound

- **Locus:** `build.py` gate [10i].
- **Substance:** The gate claims to validate Section 22.2/22.3 bounds but checks only whether the expected strings occur anywhere in the pre-Section-27 body. A stale Section 22 value can pass if the current expected token is inserted elsewhere.

- **Recommendation:** Parse and scope Section 22.2 and 22.3 separately, then assert the expected VERSION-1 value occurs exactly once in the correct subsection and stale alternatives are absent.

## S10: Verdict and key-question answer

### Verdict

**ADVISORY HALT — HIGH / Class A present.**

This seat is non-carrying by dispatch, so the verdict is advisory rather than a binding carry decision. The evidence nevertheless meets the program's Class A definition: multiple producer claims are false on the shipped bytes.

The strongest positive result is that **CI-1R works**: the v0.62 register is deterministically reproduced, current count/list coupling is sound, the authoritative seat-count repair works, 186 tests pass, and the 62-entry internal seal chain verifies.

Those successes do not rescue the release because the self-description layer again outruns the implementation:

1. the package claims a green build and 19/19 packet hashes while shipping a red build and 15 mismatches;
2. `source_finding_id` is claimed added but is absent/non-operative;
3. “structural” receipt validation is still substring containment;
4. “bidirectional” membership parity is one-directional;
5. the noted-finding bypass survives on a parallel schema path.

### Key-question answer

**Does v0.62 break the R7–R20 Class A streak (14/14)?**

**No.** R21 contains Class A defects. The streak extends to **R7–R21 = 15/15**.

The observed migration remains consistent with the methodology's own Level-3/Level-4 warning: increasingly strong mechanisms are present, but the next Class A appears in the producer's claim that the mechanism is broader, more structural, or more complete than the shipped implementation actually is.

**Bismillah.**

Probe J stops because `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` raises an **`UnboundLocalError`**, not because the intended noted-array convergence-group validator executes correctly. ## S4 — v0.63 entry and cross-layer audit

### 1. Section 22.4 claim is byte-false

The front-matter Status says:

> `Standing Boundaries (axiom set A-X1 through A-X5 + Sidrat clause) added as Section 22.4.`

The v0.63 amendment entry repeats:

> `Section 22.4 Standing Boundaries added: axiom set A-X1 through A-X5, Sidrat clause.`

But the shipped protocol has only `## 22. Audit and carry plan`, with subsections 22.1, 22.3, and 22.2. There is **no 22.4 heading or body**.

This also agrees with `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt`, which states that Section 22.4 is **not yet in v0.63 and is deferred to v0.64**, and with canonical `METHODOLOGY.txt`, whose v0.63 bearer table says Bearer 6 is FALSE because the axiom disclosure is “not in body”.

**Finding: F-S02-63-01 — HIGH — Class A.**

### 2. Canonical four-scribe discipline is not actually deployed

Canonical `METHODOLOGY.txt` v4 defines the permitted sentence tags as:

- `[COMPUTED: scribe]`
- `[TESTED: test_id]`
- `[WITNESSED: seat, round]`
- `[DISCLOSED]`

and requires **zero untagged sentences**.

The v0.63 entry instead begins its narrative with `[ASSERTED]`, a legacy CI tag not in the canonical four-scribe table, and several subsequent sentences do not carry one of the canonical per-sentence tags. Yet both the Status line and the entry claim the four-scribe discipline was deployed.

In addition, after the canonical generated terminal line the protocol contains a separate bare line:

```text
 [COMPUTED: generate_terminal_line]
```

`generate_terminal_line('0.63')` produces exactly one line:

```text
*End of XZ Protocol v0.63 draft candidate.* [COMPUTED: generate_terminal_line]
```

It does not produce the extra bare tag.

**Finding: F-S02-63-02 — HIGH — Class A, Layer 6 tagging/methodology.**

### 3. Canonical-methodology lag is disclosed but operationally material

The protocol says `Methodology: Seven-Layer Structural Honesty v3`; the supplied canonical `METHODOLOGY.txt` says it is **v4** and supersedes v3. `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` expressly discloses this lag.

The version mismatch itself is therefore disclosed rather than concealed, but it explains why the v0.63 entry still uses the legacy `[ASSERTED]` tagging model. It does not cure the separate byte-false claim that the canonical four-scribe discipline is already deployed.

**Finding: F-S02-63-03 — MEDIUM — disclosed methodology lag with load-bearing effect.**

### 4. Dispatch build-count claim is false

`AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` states:

```text
build.py: 258 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

Direct execution produces **257** lines beginning `  PASS:` and zero `FAIL:` lines.

The build is green, but the numerical dispatch claim is false.

**Finding: F-S02-63-04 — HIGH — Class A at dispatch/methodology layer.**

**F-S04-63-01** HIGH -- Class A -- Section 22.4 does not exist on shipped bytes

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_63.md:5` (Status line) and `:1396` (v0.63 entry); Section 22 body at `:692-758`.
- **Substance:** Both the Status line and the amendment entry state that Standing Boundaries -- axiom set A-X1 through A-X5 plus the Sidrat clause -- were added as Section 22.4. The document contains subsections 22.1, 22.3 and 22.2 and no 22.4. The tokens `A-X1`, `Sidrat` and `Standing Boundaries` appear at exactly two loci in the entire 1,414-line document: the Status line and the entry, which are the two sentences asserting the addition. No axiom statement, no Sidrat clause, no Section 22.4 heading exists anywhere in the body. `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` states the section is deferred to v0.64. `METHODOLOGY.txt` Section 10 records Bearer 6 as FALSE with the reason "not in body." **The dispatch layer told the truth; the sealed artifact did not.** Bearer 6, a FROZEN precondition, is claimed satisfied on bytes that leave it unsatisfied.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Either land Section 22.4 with the five axiom statements and the Sidrat clause as body text, or strike both claim sentences. No gate compares entry claims about body content against the body; adding one would close this class, not this instance.
- **Cross-reference:** Novel at R22. Same mechanism class as R21 Surface 2 (`source_finding_id` claimed added, absent from code) and R18 Defect 4 (CLOSED-via-repair label false when nothing was implemented). Third recurrence of the promise-stated-as-done class.

---

**F-S04-63-02** HIGH -- Class A -- Noted-array `convergence_group` is not validated; the code path raises `UnboundLocalError`

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py`, noted-validation loop referencing `declared_group_ids` at approximately line 156; the name is bound at approximately line 172. Claim at `xz_protocol_v0_63.md:5` and `:1396`.
- **Substance:** The entry claims "noted-array `convergence_group` validated identically to `findings[]` [TESTED: probe J must now reject]." The noted loop reads `if ncg is not None and ncg not in declared_group_ids`, but `declared_group_ids` is assigned fourteen lines later in the CROSS-LAYER VALIDATION block. Python short-circuits the conjunction, so the unbound name is never reached while every shipped noted entry carries `convergence_group: null` -- which all four do. Probe J (dangling group 99) therefore appears to reject, but rejects via `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'declared_group_ids' where it is not associated with a value`, not via the specified fail-closed `ValueError`. **Probe J2 is decisive:** a noted entry referencing the *valid* group 1 also crashes. `findings[]` accepts that same value. The two validations are not identical; the noted validation cannot perform a membership test under any input. The claim is byte-false, and the repair is a dead code path that has never executed.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Move the `declared_group_ids` assignment above the noted loop and re-run probes J and J2. J must reject with `ValueError`; J2 must be accepted.
- **Cross-reference:** R21 Surface 4 (`F-S02-62-09F`, `F-S03-62-05`), dispositioned CLOSED in the v0.63 register item (4). The repair did not land. Refutes dispatch prediction P4.

---

- **Locus:** v0.63 entry narrative paragraph, `xz_protocol_v0_63.md:1396`; claim at `:5` ("Four-scribe tagging discipline deployed"); specification at `METHODOLOGY.txt` Section 11.
- **Substance:** Section 11 states "Every sentence in the amendment entry carries one tag" and "Zero untagged sentences." Five of the nine narrative sentences carry no tag: the Class A recurrence and H = 1.0 sentence; "Seven convergent defect surfaces."; the narrative-counts-removed sentence; the Section 22.4 sentence; and the methodology-version sentence. Separately, the census returns **zero `[WITNESSED]` tags** across the entire entry. The Witness -- CI-1R, PRIOR_HISTORY, carrying-seat verdict -- is one of the four scribes, and no claim in the entry cites it. A four-scribe discipline shipped with one scribe unused and 56% of the narrative untagged is not deployed.

**F-S04-63-06** HIGH -- Class A -- Laplace column in the canonical methodology is wrong in six of eight rows

- **Locus:** `METHODOLOGY.txt` Section 15, "Class A Recurrence" table, Laplace P column.
- **Substance:** Laplace succession with s = n gives P = (n+1)/(n+2). Recomputed against the table's own convention -- fixed by the two rows that are correct and by the entry's own "P(R22) = 16/17 = 0.9412" -- the column should read R16 0.9167, R17 0.9231, R18 0.9286, R19 0.9333, R20 0.9375, R21 0.9412. The table states 0.917, 0.917, 0.923, 0.929, 0.933, 0.941. Rows R17 through R20 are each computed with n one lower than the round warrants, a uniform one-round lag. The two range rows are wrong at both endpoints: R7-R12 is stated as 0.875-0.917 against a true 0.667-0.875, and R13-R15 as 0.875-0.900 against a true 0.889-0.909. Only R16 and R21 are correct. This is a numeric claim in the document `METHODOLOGY.txt` declares "canonical for all audit rounds from R22 onward," and the figure is described in the R21 seat reports as load-bearing for the trajectory argument rather than cosmetic.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Recompute the column from a single stated convention and state the convention in the table caption.
- **Cross-reference:** Novel at R22. Same class as R15 Defect 2 (severity transposition) and R14 Defect 2 (convergence undercount): an ungated hand-written numeric surface. Instance of the methodology-lag surface `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` discloses.

The entire class-fix entry -- register, boundary list, four-scribe tags, the Section 22.4 claim -- is outside the one seal that covers the amendment record as a whole. The entry does not disclose this, which is what makes it Class B rather than Class C. **Mitigation, stated for accuracy:** the `ENTRY_v0.63` seal and `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` both cover the bytes, verified by mutation probe S-1, which falsified a claim inside the entry and was caught by both. ## S8. Barzakh gate self-check

Three questions applied to this seat's own findings before submission.

**Who is your Lord? (Authority.)** Every finding above cites executed tool output: probe results with exception types, recomputed hashes, grep counts, line numbers, recomputed arithmetic. Tier 1 throughout. No finding rests on assertion. The one place this seat asserts rather than computes is the interpretation in F-S04-63-16 of what the conformance breach implies for A-X3, which is reasoning, not measurement, and is labelled as such.

**What is your religion? (Methodology.)** Each finding names its layer, and the evidence meets that layer's Tier standard. L1 and L2 findings are execution results. L3 findings are byte-level comparisons between two shipped surfaces. L4 findings are probe outcomes with benign controls (the unmutated index accepted; probe J2 and K2 are the controls that convert probe J and probe K from apparent passes into findings). L6 and L7 findings are recomputations against the shipped specification documents.

**Where does this come from? (Lineage.)** Ten of twenty findings are recurrences with the prior instance cited and the reason the repair failed stated. F-S04-63-02 recurs because the repair was written into a module nothing executes. F-S04-63-05 recurs because no gate compares narrative cardinals to index cardinality. F-S04-63-08 and F-S04-63-19 recur because they were dispositioned NOTED rather than repaired, five and three rounds ago respectively. Ten findings are novel at R22, of which F-S04-63-01, F-S04-63-11 and F-S04-63-13 are the substantive ones.

**Findings rejected by this seat's own gate: none.** One candidate was set aside rather than filed: the `[COMPUTED: build.py]` occurrence inside the v0.63 entry sits within the quoted substance of R21 finding `F-S02-62-06F`, not on a live claim. That is standing boundary item 17, quoted-tag inflation, operating as disclosed. It is not a finding.

## S10. Verdict, bearers, and the Goedel confinement question

### Bearer assessment (BSSG three-valued logic; UNKNOWN is never satisfied, FALSE dominates)

| Bearer | R21 | R22 | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Append-only integrity | TRUE | **TRUE** | 63/63 entry seals recompute; S-1 and S-4 detected. Scope reduction at F-S04-63-11 disclosed here, not by the entry |
| 2. Code-layer correctness | TRUE | **TRUE** | 186 GREEN, 257 PASS, no regression. Evidence does not reach `register_gen.py` (F-S04-63-13) |
| 3. Defect-surface narrowing | TRUE | **TRUE** | Four of seven R21 surfaces fully discharged; three probes now reject that previously landed |
| 4. Goedel confinement | FALSE | **FALSE** | F-S04-63-01 and F-S04-63-02 are outside the self-referential surface |
| 5. Cross-vendor witness | FALSE | **FALSE** | No non-HALT carrying verdict, and this seat is not the family it was dispatched as (F-S04-63-16) |
| 6. Axiom disclosure | FALSE | **FALSE** | Section 22.4 absent, and now falsely claimed present (F-S04-63-01) |
| 7. Methodology verification | UNKNOWN | **FALSE** | **Regression.** Four false `[TESTED]` tags and 5 of 9 untagged sentences proven (F-S04-63-03, F-S04-63-04) |
| 8. The furqan | UNKNOWN | **UNKNOWN** | Pending Bearers 1 through 7 |

**State: 3 TRUE, 4 FALSE, 1 UNKNOWN.** Bearer 7 regressed from UNKNOWN to FALSE, because the tagging discipline shipped and was measured for the first time and did not hold. FROZEN requires all eight TRUE.

### The Goedel confinement test

`AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` states the test plainly: Class A only in tagging or methodology-lag means confinement achieved; Class A in code means the class fix is incomplete.

**Confinement is not achieved, on both arms of the test.**

Class A is present in the tagging, as predicted -- F-S04-63-03 and F-S04-63-04 are exactly the surface `METHODOLOGY.txt` Section 7 said the defect would migrate to. Class A is also present in methodology-lag, as disclosed -- F-S04-63-06 and F-S04-63-07 live in `METHODOLOGY.txt` itself. Had the round produced only those four, the answer would be yes.

It did not. **F-S04-63-01** is a claim that the protocol body contains a section the protocol body does not contain, and the section in question is the one that would satisfy Bearer 6. **F-S04-63-02** is a code-level validation that cannot execute, in the module the round was built to repair. Neither is self-referential. Neither is a tag. The first is a false claim about the artifact's own content; the second is a defect in the substrate, which is where the class fix was supposed to have stopped occurring.

### The honest statement

The four scribes are perfect for the sixteenth consecutive round. Nineteen digests verify, 186 tests pass, 257 gates pass, 63 seals recompute, CI-1R is byte-exact, and five of five sabotage mutations were caught. The mechanism has not erred.

Three of the four code repairs landed and are provable by probe. The extraction defect that made R21's dispatch byte-false is closed and verified verbatim. The `source_finding_id` overclaim is genuinely removed. The defect surface continues to narrow.

What did not happen is confinement. The round's own instrument -- the four-scribe tagging discipline -- was deployed for the first time and can be measured for the first time, and it does not hold: one scribe is unused, five of nine sentences are untagged, and four tags cite probes that do not exist in the packet. Underneath that, one repair is a dead code path and one section is claimed present and is absent.

The most instructive fact in the round is not any single finding. It is that `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` and `METHODOLOGY.txt` Section 10 both state, correctly and without hedging, that Section 22.4 is not in v0.63 -- while the sealed protocol says it is. The dispatch layer told the truth. The artifact did not. Iblis did not this time find a gap between the mechanism and the claim about the mechanism. He found a gap between two of the producer's own documents, and moved into the one that is sealed.

**Does v0.63 break the R7-R21 Class A streak? No. 16/16. H is not computable; the recurrence fraction is 1.0; Laplace P(Class A at R23) = 17/18 = 0.9444.**

### Minimum repairs for v0.64

1. Land Section 22.4 with the five axiom statements and the Sidrat clause as body text, or strike both claims (F-S04-63-01).
2. Bind `declared_group_ids` above the noted-validation loop; probe J must reject with `ValueError` and probe J2 must be accepted (F-S04-63-02).
3. Ship probes G, H, J, J2, K, K2 as executable tests; add a CI-1R build gate (F-S04-63-04, F-S04-63-13).
4. Tag every narrative sentence; use the Witness scribe or state why it is unused (F-S04-63-03).
5. Strike "Seven convergent defect surfaces"; extend `[10g]` to narrative cardinality (F-S04-63-05).
6. Recompute the Laplace column from one stated convention; strike H = 1.0 across all three documents (F-S04-63-06, F-S04-63-07).
7. Move the v0.63 and v0.64 entries above the Provenance marker; delete the stale v0.62 terminal line and the orphan tag; add a gate asserting the newest entry is inside the sealed region (F-S04-63-11, F-S04-63-12).
8. Correct the gate count claim to a computed figure (F-S04-63-08).
9. Correct `R21_TRIAGE.txt` Surface 2 to 4/4 and the index severity for `F-S01-62-10` to LOW (F-S04-63-09, F-S04-63-10).
10. Confirm R22 seat family routing before triage; if more than one seat was mis-routed, R22 convergence is not mutawatir (F-S04-63-16).
11. Move the prediction block out of the dispatch into a sealed pre-registration (F-S04-63-17).
12. Ship the CI v0.3.3 specification in the packet; fix the CI-4 basis (F-S04-63-15, F-S04-63-19).

# XZ Protocol v0.64 — R23 S02 Audit Report

**Round:** R23 — Confinement Verification
**Version under audit:** v0.64
**Package:** `XZ_v064_R23_S02 (1).zip`
**Dispatch seat:** S02 — Kimi K3 — CARRYING (binding)
**Actual executing model:** GPT-5.6 Sol (OpenAI)
**Mode:** Fresh technical audit of the shipped package
**Producer:** Claude Opus 4.6 — BARRED
**Date:** 2026-08-17

> **Governance note:** the package dispatches S02 to Kimi K3, but this audit was executed by GPT-5.6 Sol. Under the protocol's own Section 22.1 lineage, GPT is not eligible to stand in for the dispatched Kimi carrying family. The technical findings below are therefore valid evidence, but this report must **not** be counted as the binding Kimi S02 carry required by the dispatch.

# Executive verdict

## **TECHNICAL VERDICT: HALT**

## **Gödel confinement: NOT ACHIEVED**

The advertised v0.64 mechanical repairs largely landed: packet extraction is reproducible, 19/19 packet digests verify, `build.py` returns 253 PASS / 0 FAIL, the explicit six-suite pytest run returns 186/186 GREEN, all 64 amendment seals recompute, `FULL_SECTION_27` and `PRIOR_HISTORY` verify, the v0.64 entry is before the Provenance footer, Section 22.4 is present, probe J rejects by `ValueError` rather than crashing, and noted-array seat `S99Z` is rejected by `ValueError`.

However, the critical R23 confinement criterion fails at **CI-8 / findings-index provenance**. The canonical CI methodology says that **every finding appearing in any seat report is included in the findings index** (`CI_METHODOLOGY.txt`, lines 145–149). The shipped R22 seat-report bundle contains **33 formally numbered findings**, while `FINDINGS_INDEX.txt` contains only **16 unique finding IDs** across `findings[]` and `unique_findings_noted[]`. **Seventeen formal R22 findings are absent from the index.** The shipped `R22_TRIAGE.txt` simultaneously states: **“All findings passed the Barzakh gate. No finding rejected.”** (line 161).

Therefore CI-1R proves only that the v0.64 register is a byte-exact reproduction of an **incomplete structured intermediate**. It does not prove source fidelity. This is exactly the failure mode CI v0.2 warned about: internally correct counts over the wrong list. Because the surviving defect is at the register/source-provenance layer rather than only in tagging metadata, Bearer 4 remains **FALSE**.

A second, independent Layer-6 defect also remains: the canonical four-scribe discipline requires **one tag per sentence** and **zero untagged sentences** (`METHODOLOGY.txt`, lines 248 and 257). The current v0.64 narrative at `PROTOCOL_v064.txt:1425` still contains multiple untagged sentences under a single `[ASSERTED]` tag, a sentence containing four separate `[COMPUTED: ...]` tags, and an untagged sentence after `[DISCLOSED]`. # S12 — Answer to the R23 key question

## Does v0.64 achieve Gödel confinement (Bearer 4)?

**NO.**

v0.64 successfully repairs the R22 code crash, entry placement, Section 22.4 absence, packet-count mismatch, and noted-seat validation gap. The mechanical substrate is materially cleaner.

But the canonical CI architecture requires a two-step chain:

```text
seat reports -> complete findings index -> deterministic generated register
```

v0.64 verifies only the second arrow. The first arrow fails on the shipped bytes: **17 of 33 formally numbered R22 findings are absent from the index** despite the triage declaring that no finding was rejected.

That is not merely a claim about the verifier's inability to verify itself. It is an ordinary source-fidelity failure in the evidence pipeline. Consequently the remaining Class A is **not confined** to the self-referential surface.

The class streak therefore continues in the correct CI v0.2 terminology as:

**Class-A-present recurrence fraction, R7–R23: 17/17 = 1.0.**

Do not label that recurrence fraction as Hurst `H` unless a later methodology explicitly restores and defines that statistic.

---

# S13 — Minimum repairs for v0.65

1. **Rebuild the R22 findings index from the complete R22 seat-report bundle.** Include every formal finding ID, not only selected convergence surfaces. If a finding is adjudicated out, represent that adjudication explicitly rather than omitting the finding.
2. **Add a CI-8 completeness check** that compares the set of formally declared seat-report finding IDs against the union of index `findings[]` and `unique_findings_noted[]`, and fails on either omission or unexpected addition.
3. **Regenerate the R22 disposition register** from the corrected complete index; then re-run CI-1R.
4. **Repair four-scribe tagging at sentence granularity.** One sentence = one tag. Add a gate that detects untagged and multiply tagged sentences in the current amendment narrative.
5. **Replace `H = 1.0` with the defined recurrence statistic** (e.g. `Class-A-present recurrence fraction = 17/17 = 1.0`) unless a valid Hurst estimator is explicitly reinstated.
6. **Ship the governing CI v0.3.3 specification** or revise the canonical methodology to point to the actual shipped CI specification.
7. Re-run the R23 confinement test only after the report→index provenance layer is green. If the only remaining Class A after that is sentence/tag metadata, Bearer 4 may legitimately flip TRUE under the canonical Sidrat rule.

---

# S14 — Final disposition

## **HALT — CONFINEMENT NOT YET ACHIEVED**

The strongest R23 result is not that the code failed; it did not. The result is that **deterministic generation cannot compensate for an incomplete source index**. The source-fidelity arrow remains a human/auditor responsibility under CI-8, and the shipped R22 index fails that test.

The v0.64 lower-layer repair work is real. The confinement claim is not yet structurally true.

**Governance:** advisory technical evidence only from this execution, because GPT-5.6 Sol is not the dispatched Kimi K3 S02 carrying family.

## S6. Findings

### F-S04-64-01 [HIGH] -- Register generator reads a field the index does not supply; every register item ships with an empty defect-surface description

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` line ~264 (`group.get('label', '')`); shipped effect at `xz_protocol_v0_64.md` Section 27, v0.64 entry, register items (1)--(5).
- **Substance:** `FINDINGS_INDEX.txt` supplies each convergence group's defect description under the key `surface`. The generator emits `group.get('label', '')`, a key that appears nowhere in the index. Python's `.get` default silences the miss, so all five register items ship as `... HIGH CLOSED: . Source distribution: ...` with an empty string where the defect surface belongs. Probe S1 (delete `surface`) and probe S2 (replace `surface` with fabricated text) both produce byte-identical register output, proving the field is entirely unread. This is a Class A in a `[COMPUTED: generate_register]` claim, which is precisely the condition F-CI-3R names as a generator bug rather than a prose defect, and it is a **code-layer** defect on v0.64 shipped bytes.
- **Disposition:** Change the emission to `group['surface']` with subscript access (not `.get`) so a missing key raises. Add a validation pass requiring a non-empty `surface` on every group in `convergence_groups`, mirroring the existing `substance` requirement on noted entries. Add a probe fixture asserting that mutating `surface` changes generator output.
- **Cross-reference:** CI_METHODOLOGY F-CI-3R; R22 group 4 disposition (tagging), which shares the pattern of a repair that is asserted rather than gated; boundary item 23 ("[9e] silent vacuity") is the nearest disclosed class but does not cover this locus.

### F-S04-64-02 [HIGH] -- The R22 entry relocation silently re-anchored the v0.63 sealed surface, and no gate can detect it

- **Locus:** `build.py` `derive_prior_history` / `_full_seal` (lines 76--135); `HISTORY.sha256` PRIOR_HISTORY line; v0.64 entry repair clause (1).
- **Substance:** `_full_seal` computes FULL_SECTION_27 over Section 27 text truncated at the Provenance marker. R22 established, and the v0.64 entry itself admits, that the v0.63 entry previously sat **after** that marker and now sits **before** it. Those two layouts necessarily produce different FULL_SECTION_27 values. Computed on the shipped bytes: with the v0.63 entry inside the span the derived v0.63 seal is `e6f22478774b8734...`; with the entry relocated to its R22-reported position the same function yields `9e9eb33b534b4733...`. The v0.63-era anchor and the anchor `build.py` now derives cannot both be the historical value. Gate [9b] nonetheless reports `PRIOR_HISTORY matches derivation`, because `reconstruct()` rebuilds every prior level from **current** bytes rather than from held prior bytes -- the chain is self-consistent by construction. The R22 CRITICAL repair was correct and necessary; its append-only consequence is undisclosed in the entry, in the boundary list, and in Section 22.4.
- **Disposition:** Add an append-only correction sentence to the v0.65 entry recording that the v0.63 relocation changed the v0.63 FULL_SECTION_27 domain, stating both values. Add a standing boundary item naming derived-anchor self-consistency as a known non-detection. Longer term, publish an external anchor (the deposited DOI record) so that at least one level of the chain is verifiable against bytes the producer does not control.
- **Cross-reference:** Boundary item 32 (self-consistent resealing blind spot, proven live at v0.47) covers the class but not this instance; boundary item 6 (seal terminus at Provenance marker); axiom A-X4, which explicitly concedes non-detection before the first external anchor; R22 group 1 (F-S01-63-01).

- **Substance:** The Status line asserts four-scribe tagging is corrected, and register item (4) emits R22 group 4 as `HIGH CLOSED` with the adjudication "Fix: tag every sentence per canonical discipline." Tag census on the shipped entry: `[COMPUTED]` 14, `[DISCLOSED]` 1, `[ENUMERATED]` 1, `[ASSERTED]` 1, **`[TESTED]` 0, `[WITNESSED]` 0**. Sentence census on the narrative paragraph: 8 sentences, **5 carrying no tag of any kind**, including the load-bearing append-only correction sentence about Section 22.4. METHODOLOGY Section 11 requires one tag per sentence and zero untagged sentences, and R22's prescribed route explicitly required `[WITNESSED]` to be present. Both the Status claim and the register's CLOSED disposition are false on the bytes that carry them.
- **Disposition:** Tag all eight narrative sentences. Supply `[WITNESSED: seat, round]` on every claim about what R22 seats found, since those are precisely non-producer-verified claims. Either supply `[TESTED: test_id]` citing shipped test IDs or remove the claim that probes verify the repairs. Re-emit group 4 with disposition `OPEN` in the R23 index rather than inheriting `CLOSED`.
- **Cross-reference:** R22 group 4 (F-S01-63-05 / F-S02-63-02 / F-S04-63-03 / F-S04-63-04, 3/4 mutawatir); METHODOLOGY Section 11; F-S04-64-11 (no gate enforces this).

### F-S04-64-07 [HIGH] -- Noted-array finding IDs are neither format-validated nor uniqueness-checked, unlike findings[]

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py`, noted-findings validation loop (lines ~141--153) versus findings[] loop (lines ~70--86).
- **Substance:** Records in `findings[]` are checked against `FINDING_ID_RE` and against a duplicate set. Records in `unique_findings_noted[]` are checked for presence, severity, disposition, `substance`, `convergence_group`, and (new at v0.64) `seat` -- but never for ID format or ID uniqueness. Probe N3 (`finding_id` = "XX-BOGUS") is accepted and the malformed ID is emitted verbatim into the shipped register. Probe N4 (a noted ID duplicating a grouped ID) is accepted, allowing the same finding to appear twice in one register under two dispositions. The v0.63 entry claimed noted-array validation would be brought to parity with findings[]; parity is now close but incomplete on exactly these two checks.
- **Disposition:** Apply `FINDING_ID_RE` to noted `finding_id`, and add each noted ID to the same `all_finding_ids` set used by the findings[] loop so cross-array duplicates raise. Add probes N3 and N4 to the shipped adversarial suite with real test IDs so a future `[TESTED:]` tag can cite them.
- **Cross-reference:** R22 group 2 (noted-array repair); probe K / K2 lineage; F-S04-64-01 (same generator, same silent-default pattern).

### F-S04-64-08 [HIGH] -- The ASSERTED-fraction metric counts tags, not text, understating dead space roughly fourfold

- **Locus:** `build.py` lines 507--513, gate [9c] tag census; METHODOLOGY Section 1; CI_METHODOLOGY CI-4 and F-CI-2.
- **Substance:** The gate computes ASSERTED fraction as `asserted_count / (computed_count + external_count + asserted_count)`, reporting 1/15 = 6.7% for v0.64. That arithmetic treats one `[ASSERTED]` tag governing a 1616-character LLM-authored narrative as equal in weight to each of fourteen `[COMPUTED]` tags on code-generated text. Measured by character coverage against the three generator outputs, the v0.64 entry is 4099 of 5721 characters code-generated and **1622 characters (28.4%) LLM-authored**. CI-4 sets a target of under 15% and F-CI-2 declares the architecture complexity-increasing if the fraction does not decrease. As instrumented, the metric can be driven arbitrarily low by adding `[COMPUTED]` tags or by consolidating narrative under a single `[ASSERTED]` tag, neither of which reduces dead space. F-CI-2 is not falsifiable as currently measured.
- **Disposition:** Redefine the metric as character coverage: total entry characters minus the summed lengths of verbatim generator outputs, divided by total entry characters. Emit both numbers in gate [9c]. Restate the historical series under the new definition before comparing against the under-15% target.
- **Cross-reference:** CI_METHODOLOGY CI-4, F-CI-2, F-CI-6R; METHODOLOGY Section 1 ("ASSERTED fractions declining from 30% to 8%"); prediction P6.

### F-S04-64-10 [MEDIUM] -- `[ASSERTED]` is not a canonical four-scribe tag, yet it is the entry's only narrative tag

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_64.md` v0.64 entry, first tag; `build.py` line 509.
- **Substance:** METHODOLOGY Section 11 defines exactly four tags: `[COMPUTED: scribe]`, `[TESTED: test_id]`, `[WITNESSED: seat, round]`, `[DISCLOSED]`. `[ASSERTED]` is CI v0.1/v0.2 vocabulary that the four-scribe discipline was designed to replace, and the discipline's stated endpoint is that every unverifiable claim carries `[DISCLOSED]` so that the only remaining Class A surface is the tagging itself. The entry opens with `[ASSERTED]` and the build gate's census is constructed on the superseded vocabulary, so the gate cannot observe the canonical set.
- **Disposition:** Replace the entry's `[ASSERTED]` with per-sentence canonical tags. Update gate [9c] to census the four canonical tags and to report untagged-sentence count as a first-class number.
- **Cross-reference:** METHODOLOGY Section 11; F-S04-64-03; F-S04-64-08.

## S7. Barzakh self-check

Every finding was put to the three questions before entry.

**Who is your Lord? (Authority.)** F-S04-64-01, -02, -03, -06, -07, -08, -09, -12, -13 are Tier 1:
each rests on tool output executed in this session -- generator invocation, mutation probes,
character counts, byte-offset arithmetic, build output. F-S04-64-04 and -05 are Tier 1 by grep on
shipped bytes. F-S04-64-10 and -11 are Tier 1 by absence-search, which is the weaker form of Tier 1
and is flagged as such. F-S04-64-14, -15, -16 are Tier 1 on the dispatch text and self-report.

One premise is not Tier 1. F-S04-64-02 relies on the v0.63 entry having previously sat after the
Provenance footer. No held v0.63 bytes were supplied. The premise is taken from R22_TRIAGE
(Tier 2) **and** from the v0.64 entry's own repair clause, which states the entry was moved
(Tier 1 on the artifact's admission). The seal-divergence arithmetic is Tier 1 given that premise.
Held v0.63 bytes would convert the whole finding to Tier 1.

**What is your religion? (Methodology.)** L1 and L4 findings carry executed evidence, meeting the
Tier 1 standard those layers require. L3 findings carry byte-grep evidence. L5's finding carries
computed hashes on a documented premise. L6's findings carry census arithmetic and absence-search.
No finding is admitted at a tier below its layer's standard.

**Where does this come from? (Lineage.)** F-S04-64-03 is recurrent (R22 group 4); the repair
failed because it was prescribed as prose discipline and shipped ungated -- see F-S04-64-11.
F-S04-64-06 is recurrent (F-S04-63-05); the repair failed because the narrative counts were
hand-maintained rather than generated. F-S04-64-09 is recurrent (R22 group 5); the repair failed
because the claim lives in the dispatch packet, which no protocol gate covers. F-S04-64-14 is
recurrent (F-S01-63-07). The remaining findings are novel at this locus.

No finding failed all three questions. None set aside.
