methodology repair did not, and the code layer that R22 declared clean is not.**

---

## S10. Verdict

> **Verdict: HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER (advisory).**
>
> Severity ledger: 0 CRITICAL / 10 HIGH / 4 MEDIUM / 2 LOW.
>
> **Does v0.64 achieve Goedel confinement (Bearer 4)? No.**
>
> Confinement requires that the only Class A live in the self-referential surface. Three findings
> sit outside it: the register generator reads a field the index does not supply and silently
> ships empty defect descriptions (F-S04-64-01, Layer 1/4); the noted-array admits malformed and
> duplicate finding IDs into the shipped register (F-S04-64-07, Layer 4); and the R22 entry
> relocation re-anchored the v0.63 sealed surface with no gate able to detect it (F-S04-64-02,
> Layer 5). Bearer 4 remains FALSE. Bearer 6 flips TRUE.

**Recommendation.** Repair in this order, because the order matters:

1. **F-S04-64-01 and F-S04-64-07** first. They are code, they are small, and until they are fixed
   the confinement question cannot even be asked cleanly. Ship the four new probes (N3, N4, S1, S2)
   as real test IDs in the adversarial suite in the same change.
2. **F-S04-64-11** next: gate the tagging discipline. Then **F-S04-64-03** becomes mechanically
   enforceable rather than a prose commitment that has now failed to land twice.
3. **F-S04-64-08**: redefine the ASSERTED metric before it is cited again. The current definition
   makes the program's central complexity claim unfalsifiable, which is the one thing this
   methodology exists to prevent.
4. **F-S04-64-04, -05, -06**: prose and cross-reference repairs, generated rather than hand-maintained.
5. **F-S04-64-02**: disclose in the v0.65 entry and add the boundary item. This one cannot be
   "fixed" -- it can only be disclosed, which is what the Sidrat clause is for.

**On the shape of the round.** R22 predicted that one more round of repair would complete the
migration to the Goedel surface. That prediction is not yet falsified as a trajectory claim, but
it is falsified as a v0.64 claim, and for a specific and repeatable reason: **every defect that
recurred this round recurred at a locus no gate covers.** Tagging: ungated. Narrative counts:
ungated. Dispatch gate count: outside the protocol entirely. The generator's `surface` field:
ungated because `.get` supplied a default. The program's own diagnosis in CI_METHODOLOGY 0.4 --
gated claims stay clean, ungated claims carry Class A every round -- held at R23 without exception.
Confinement will arrive when the self-referential surface is the last ungated surface, and it is
not yet the last.

**Cross-vendor recommendation.** This seat is producer-family (Claude auditing a Claude-produced
artifact). Under standing rule 7, R23 needs the S04 cell re-dispatched to a non-producer family
before convergence is computed, and Bearer 5 needs two non-producer families returning non-HALT
on the same bytes. Neither is satisfied by this report.

## FINAL VERDICT: **HALT — RETURN TO PRODUCER**

v0.65 does **not** achieve Gödel confinement and does **not** earn a non-HALT carrying verdict.

Minimum repair set for v0.66:

1. Rebuild the R23 findings index mechanically from all 30 formal R23 report findings; retain every finding with an explicit disposition, remove probe-label pseudo-findings unless formally promoted, and restore `F-S01-64-03` source severity to MEDIUM.
2. Ship the claimed R22 33-finding index if it is part of the v0.65 proof surface, or remove/retag the unsupported `[COMPUTED: r22_findings_index.json]` claim.
3. Apply `FINDING_ID_RE` to `unique_findings_noted[]` and add N3/N4/S1/S2 as executable regression tests.
4. Emit `surface`, not nonexistent `label`, in `generate_register`; add a mutation test proving surface changes alter register output.
5. Correct front-matter recurrence count, Section 0.1 FB-7b current-version token, and complete the declared “full carrying-seat trajectory.”
6. Enforce the canonical four-scribe grammar mechanically: exactly one canonical tag per sentence, no `[ASSERTED]`, no untagged sentence, and no false `[COMPUTED]` provenance.
7. Stop reporting literal `H = 1.0`; use recurrence fraction and Laplace smoothing as CI-5 already requires.
8. Report the actual gate count as 241 gate checks (or change the tool to emit an explicit machine-counted total distinct from the summary line).

**Answer to the R24 key question:** **No. Confinement is not achieved. Non-HALT carry is not justified.**

# XZ Protocol v0.65 -- Round 24 Audit Report -- Seat S04

**Round:** 24 ("The Furqan Window")
**Artifact:** XZ Protocol v0.65 DRAFT CANDIDATE
**Seat:** S04
**Dispatched family:** Gemini 3.1 Pro (ADVISORY)
**Executing family:** Claude Opus 5 -- see S0 conformance declaration
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Framework:** Seven-Layer Structural Honesty (canonical METHODOLOGY.txt)
**Verdict:** **HALT**

---

## S0. Seat identity, conformance, and disqualifying conditions

Auditor operated in **Mode A** (substrate verifier) with full sandbox
access: extraction, `sha256sum`, `python3 build.py`, `pytest`, direct
module import, and mutation execution. Substrate-claim verification
confidence: **high**.

**Declared non-conformance -- two deviations, both material.**

1. **Family substitution.** DISPATCH.txt assigns this seat to Gemini
   3.1 Pro, whose trial under METHODOLOGY Section 5 is *"No code
   execution. Textual only."* This seat was executed by Claude Opus 5
   with a real Linux sandbox. The trial that gives an S04 finding its
   characteristic value -- reading the code rather than running it --
   was not the trial actually undergone. All Tier assignments below
   reflect what was executed, not what was dispatched. This is the
   second consecutive round of seat-label drift in this program; cf.
   `F-S01-64-09` at R23, which recorded the mirror case (S01
   dispatched as Opus 5, executed by Kimi K3).

2. **Producer adjacency.** DISPATCH.txt records the producer as Claude
   Opus 4.6 and marks that family **BARRED**. The executing instance is
   Claude Opus 5 -- a different model, the same vendor family. Under
   METHODOLOGY Section 5 the S01 trial is defined as
   producer-family ("shares the producer's blind spots"). This seat
   therefore carries the S01 trial while wearing the S04 label. Findings
   surviving that architectural similarity are, per the same section,
   the producer's systematic misses; findings absent from this report
   may be shared blind spots rather than absent defects.

3. **Not producer-instance.** This instance did not author v0.65, the
   R23 triage, the findings index, or any packet member. No same-instance
   exception is claimed or required.

**Effect on this report.** No finding below is weakened by the
substitution, because every finding is anchored in executed tool output
or in shipped bytes quoted verbatim. The substitution weakens the
*round*, not the *report*: the R24 seat matrix does not in fact contain
a no-execution textual seat, and any cross-seat convergence computed
against this report as a Gemini seat would overstate family
independence. A5 (evidence independence) is degraded at the round level.

---

## S1. Staging and the four scribes

Extraction performed exactly as specified in AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt.
Seventeen files extracted from `EXECUTABLE_PACKET.txt`; three copied
from packet members (`PROTOCOL_v065.txt`, `FINDINGS_INDEX.txt`,
`BOUNDARIES.txt`). Environment: Python 3.12.3, pytest 9.1.1.

| The Test | six-suite `pytest` | **186 passed** in 6.88s |
| The Witness | CI-1R | **PASS**, byte-identical |

`pytest` is not shipped in the packet. On first execution `build.py`
returned two FAIL results (`pytest is installed`, `Test count parsed
from pytest output`) until pytest was installed from the network. This
is standing boundary item 11 ("fresh-execution non-reproducibility")
operating exactly as disclosed, and is recorded here as confirmation of
that boundary rather than as a finding.

## S2. CI-1R -- deterministic register reproduction

```
generate_register('r23_findings_index.json', '0.65')
```

Output length 1232 characters. Shipped register block extracted from the
v0.65 entry, length 1232 characters. **Byte-identical: True.**
`generate_boundary_list('xz_protocol_boundaries.json')` output (1797
characters) is present verbatim in the entry.

**CI-1R: PASS.** P1 CONFIRMED. F-CI-7R does not fire. The register was
not modified after generation.

The strength of this result should be stated precisely, because the
findings in S6 turn on it. CI-1R proves the register is a deterministic
function of the shipped index. It proves nothing about whether the index
is a faithful function of the seat reports. That gap is CI-8, and CI-8
is where this round fails.

## S3. Prior-round discharge -- the four R23 repairs

R23 returned 4/4 HALT and prescribed six minimum repairs for v0.65.
Executed status:

| # | R23 prescribed repair | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | All 33 R22 findings in the index | **UNVERIFIABLE** -- cited artifact not shipped (F-S04-65-08) |
| 2 | Terminal line updated | **LANDED** -- L1462 reads v0.65 |
| 3 | Noted `finding_id` format + uniqueness validation | **HALF-LANDED** -- uniqueness yes, format no (F-S04-65-01) |
| 4 | Group required-field validation | **LANDED** -- surface and triage_adjudication both enforced |
| 5 | Tagging: one tag per sentence, zero untagged | **NOT LANDED** (F-S04-65-10) |
| 6 | Gate count corrected | **NOT LANDED** (F-S04-65-09) |

Three landed cleanly, one half-landed, two did not land, one is
unverifiable. The pattern is not random. Repairs 2 and 4 were value
edits and file edits the producer could make without invalidating any
of its own inputs. Repairs 1, 3, 5, and 6 each require changing a
**rule** -- an extraction discipline, a regex whose widened form would
reject the producer's own naming convention, a per-sentence authoring
constraint, a counting definition. This is the shape of the round.

## S6. Seven-layer traversal

**Layer 1 -- Code execution.** Clean. 186 GREEN, 241 gate PASS, 19/19
digests. One structural gap: `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` has zero test
coverage (F-S04-65-06).

**Layer 2 -- Register verification.** CI-1R PASS. CI-8 **FAIL**
(F-S04-65-02). The register is correct over an index that is not
faithful to its sources.

**Layer 3 -- Cross-layer consistency.** **FAIL.** Section 0.1 and
Section 25 state different values for the same fact (F-S04-65-03). The
FB-7b row's round trajectory terminates five rounds behind
(F-S04-65-04).

**Layer 4 -- Adversarial probing.** **FAIL.** Two live false-passes
(F-S04-65-01, F-S04-65-05), one of them a verbatim re-run of an R23
probe whose repair is claimed CLOSED.

**Layer 5 -- Temporal integrity.** Clean. 65/65 seals, v0.64 entry
anchored against R23 reports, three of four mutation shapes detected.

**Layer 6 -- Methodology audit.** **FAIL.** A `[COMPUTED]` tag on a
claim that executed evidence contradicts (F-S04-65-01); five untagged
narrative sentences (F-S04-65-10); the ASSERTED metric measures tags
rather than text (F-S04-65-07); two of four scribes unused.

**Layer 7 -- Boundary disclosure.** Clean. Section 22.4 present with
A-X1 through A-X5 and the Sidrat clause in the protocol body, verbatim.
P7 CONFIRMED. Thirty-five standing boundaries enumerated and
count-coupled.

**Observation, not a finding.** `generate_terminal_line('0.65')` emits
`*End of XZ Protocol v0.65 draft candidate.* [COMPUTED: generate_terminal_line]`.
The document's physical last line (L1462) carries no tag; the entry-copy
line (L1458) carries it. Gate `[10h]` checks only the untagged prefix,
so both surfaces satisfy it. The design is coherent; recording it here
so a future seat does not mistake the tag asymmetry for drift.

## S7. Findings

### F-S04-65-01 [HIGH] -- Repair (3) is byte-false; the R23 N3 probe still false-passes

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_65.md` Section 27, v0.65 entry, narrative
  repair clause (3); `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` line 26
  (`FINDING_ID_RE`) and the `noted` validation loops at lines ~141--153
  and ~213--237.
- **Substance:** The entry claims
  `(3) [COMPUTED: xz_protocol_register_gen.py] noted finding_id uniqueness + format validation added`.
  Executed, uniqueness landed: probes P-N4 and P-N4b both raise
  `ValueError`. Format validation did **not** land: `FINDING_ID_RE` is
  applied to `findings[]` records and to group `finding_ids`, and is
  never applied to `unique_findings_noted[]`. Probe P-N3
  (`finding_id = "XX-BOGUS"`) is accepted and emitted verbatim into the
  generated register, reproducing the R23 result exactly. The same entry
  records `F-S04-64-N3 ... Disposition: CLOSED`. The mechanism is
  structural, not an oversight: `F-S04-64-N3`, `F-S04-64-N4`, and
  `F-S04-64-S1` -- three of the four shipped noted IDs -- do **not**
  match `FINDING_ID_RE`, so applying the check would cause
  `generate_register` to reject the shipped index and the build to fail.
  The repair was omitted because the repair invalidates the producer's
  own input. This is a false claim about a code repair, carrying a
  `[COMPUTED]` tag, on a non-self-referential surface.
- **Disposition:** Widen `FINDING_ID_RE` to admit letter-suffixed noted
  IDs (for example `^F-S\d{2}C?-\d{2,3}-[A-Z]?\d{1,3}[A-Z]?$`) or
  renumber N3/N4/S1 into the numeric namespace, then apply the regex to
  `unique_findings_noted[]` inside the same `all_finding_ids` set used
  by the `findings[]` loop. Ship probes N3 and N4 as real test functions
  so a future `[TESTED:]` tag can cite them. Until executed, restate the
  entry clause as uniqueness-only.
- **Cross-reference:** R23 `F-S04-64-07` [HIGH] (same substance, same
  probe, disposition prescribed and not executed); R23 index entries
  `F-S04-64-N3` / `F-S04-64-N4`; F-S04-65-06 (why nothing caught it);
  METHODOLOGY Section 11 (a `[COMPUTED]` tag on a false claim is a false
  scribe attestation).

### F-S04-65-02 [HIGH] -- CI-8 source fidelity fails again on the R23 index, at a worse ratio

- **Locus:** `FINDINGS_INDEX.txt` / `r23_findings_index.json`, all
  arrays; `R23_TRIAGE.txt` closing line; `R23_REPORTS.txt` in full.
- **Substance:** The R23 seat reports contain **30** uniquely numbered
  findings on v0.64 bytes: S01 contributes `F-S01-64-01` through `-09`
  (9), S02 contributes `-01` through `-04` (4), S03 contributes `-01`
  (1), S04 contributes `F-S04-64-01` through `-16` (16). The shipped
  index contains **9** finding IDs, of which only **6** appear in any
  seat report (`F-S01-64-01`, `F-S01-64-03`, `F-S01-64-09`,
  `F-S02-64-01`, `F-S02-64-02`, `F-S03-64-01`). Twenty-four report
  findings are absent with **no Barzakh rejection record**, while
  `R23_TRIAGE.txt` closes with "All findings passed the Barzakh gate."
  Of S04's sixteen numbered findings -- ten of them HIGH -- **zero**
  appear in the index. Separately, three index IDs (`F-S04-64-N3`,
  `-N4`, `-S1`) exist in **no seat report**: they are triage-invented
  composites of probe labels from a table in the S04 report. Their real
  source is `F-S04-64-07 [HIGH]`, recorded in the index as two
  **MEDIUM** noted items -- a two-way ID substitution and a one-band
  severity downgrade, with no `adjudication_receipt`. CI v0.2
  Section 2.3 provenance rules (a) and (b) both fail. R23's
  `F-S02-64-01` was closed by hand-correcting the R22 index rather than
  by installing an extraction rule or gate, so the class survived
  intact into the R23 index one round later, at 6-of-30 rather than
  16-of-33.
- **Disposition:** Add a build gate that fails when any `finding_id` in
  the index is absent from the shipped seat reports, and when any
  formally numbered finding in the shipped reports is absent from the
  index without an explicit `rejection_record` object carrying a reason.
  Regenerate the R23 index from `R23_REPORTS.txt` mechanically. Correct
  `F-S04-64-N3`/`-N4` to `F-S04-64-07` at HIGH, or attach an
  `adjudication_receipt` recording the downgrade. Remove the "all
  findings passed the Barzakh gate" sentence from the triage template
  unless a gate can verify it.
- **Cross-reference:** R23 `F-S02-64-01` [HIGH] (same class, prior
  instance, closed as a data correction); CI_METHODOLOGY Section 2.3 and
  probe CI-8; R23 triage Section "What R23 taught," item 2, which
  correctly diagnosed this class and then did not gate it; standing
  boundary item 8 ("no closure-reference validation in [9f] -- fabricated
  finding IDs parse as real"), operating live.

### F-S04-65-03 [HIGH] -- The v0.62 stale token migrated one surface over and evades gate [2g] by one word

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_65.md` L18 (Section 0.1) versus L771
  (Section 25 FB-7b row); `build.py` L236--250 (gate `[2g]`).
- **Substance:** Section 0.1 reads
  `Current status: PENDING RE-CARRY on v0.62 bytes.` The Section 25
  FB-7b row reads `RESOLVED v0.31; PENDING RE-CARRY v0.65`. The two body
  surfaces state different values for the same fact, and Section 0.1
  itself declares the Section 25 row the "single source of truth; no
  duplicate rationale maintained here" in the sentence immediately
  preceding the contradiction. Gate `[2g]` searches the body for
  `PENDING RE-CARRY v(\d+\.\d+)` and asserts every match equals VERSION.
  The Section 0.1 occurrence reads `PENDING RE-CARRY on v0.62`; the
  interposed word `on` breaks the match, so the stale token is invisible
  to the gate that exists specifically to catch it. This is the
  arity-one regex class (standing boundary item 1) applied to `[2g]`.
  R23's `F-S01-64-01` flagged the identical `v0.62` token in the terminal
  line; the v0.65 repair updated the terminal line and the Section 25 row
  and left this surface untouched. Same token, same round, one surface
  over.
- **Disposition:** Set Section 0.1 to `PENDING RE-CARRY v0.65`, or
  delete the duplicated status token entirely and leave the pointer to
  Section 25, which is what Section 0.1 already claims to do. Widen
  `[2g]` to `PENDING RE-CARRY (?:on )?v(\d+\.\d+)` and add a gate
  asserting that the count of body occurrences of the phrase equals 1.
- **Cross-reference:** R23 `F-S01-64-01` [HIGH] (same token, adjacent
  surface); R13 title-version staleness and R15 terminal-version
  staleness (same class, earlier surfaces); standing boundary item 1;
  METHODOLOGY Section 7, Iblis trajectory (defect migrates through the
  gaps between gated surfaces).

### F-S04-65-04 [HIGH] -- An R23 HIGH finding is both unrepaired and unrecorded

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_65.md` L771, Section 25 FB-7b row,
  per-round trajectory; `r23_findings_index.json`.
- **Substance:** The FB-7b row's per-round carrying-seat trajectory
  enumerates R1 through R18 and terminates at
  `R18 (v0.59): 2 carrying seats HALTed binding ...`. Rounds R19, R20,
  R21, R22, and R23 are absent from a row the protocol designates the
  single source of truth for FB-7b status. R23 `F-S04-64-05` [HIGH]
  recorded exactly this and prescribed appending R19 through R22 plus a
  gate asserting that the highest round named in the row equals the
  current round minus one. Neither the append nor the gate is present at
  v0.65, and the finding does not appear in the shipped index in any
  form, so no register item tracks it. This is a compound failure: the
  defect persists, and the mechanism that would have surfaced its
  persistence (the register) was never told about it. It is a
  materialised instance of F-S04-65-02.
- **Disposition:** Append R19 through R23 to the FB-7b row using the
  existing per-round format. Add the gate `F-S04-64-05` prescribed:
  assert `max(round tokens in FB-7b row) == current round - 1`. Enter
  `F-S04-64-05` in the R23 index as HIGH, OPEN.
- **Cross-reference:** R23 `F-S04-64-05` [HIGH]; F-S04-65-02 (the class
  of which this is an instance); R13 and R17 FB-7b row staleness
  (recorded in the row itself, at R13 and R17 entries).

### F-S04-65-05 [MEDIUM] -- Gate [10f] checks the boundary count and not the boundary text, contradicting its own specification

- **Locus:** `build.py` L657--667 (gate `[10f]`); `CI_METHODOLOGY.txt`
  Table 2, `[10f]` row; `xz_protocol_boundaries.json`.
- **Substance:** CI_METHODOLOGY Table 2 specifies that `[10f]` checks
  "Entry boundary list is **byte-identical** to `generate_boundary_list`
  output from the boundaries file," eliminating "Boundary wording
  staleness (R15 Defect 1 class)." The implementation reads the
  boundaries file, computes `len(items)`, and asserts two substrings are
  present in the entry: `-- {N} items:` and `[ENUMERATED: {N} items]`.
  It never compares text. Probe M3 reworded boundary item 1 from
  `arity-one regex` to `arity-two regex` in the boundaries file, leaving
  the entry unchanged, and `build.py` returned **BUILD PASSED**. The
  specific defect class that CI v0.2's boundary generator was designed to
  eliminate is therefore ungated, and the gate that claims to eliminate
  it passes on a live divergence. The generator does produce correct
  text, and CI-1R-equivalent comparison is one line away; the gap is
  purely in the verifier. Note the asymmetry with the register surface,
  where the equivalent comparison is performed.
- **Disposition:** Replace the two substring assertions in `[10f]` with
  `check(generate_boundary_list(boundaries_file) in current_entry, ...)`,
  retaining the count assertions as secondary. Add M3 to the shipped
  adversarial suite.
- **Cross-reference:** CI_METHODOLOGY Table 2 and Section 3.3; R15
  Defect 1 (boundary-30 wording staleness, 5/5 seats, the finding this
  gate was built for); R12 `F-...-53` standing-boundary count 31 vs 32;
  F-S04-65-12 (same file, ungated version token).

### F-S04-65-06 [MEDIUM] -- The register generator is the only shipped module with zero test coverage

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py`; the six-suite `pytest`
  invocation in Section 0.1 and AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt; `build.py` gate `[2]`
  version-parity list.
- **Substance:** Of the seven non-tooling Python modules in
  `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, six are imported by at least one test file:

  tests exercise the BSSG kernel, the Condition A evaluator, the source
  frame, the control graph, and the phase-A intervals; none touches the

  are stamped and checked; this one is not) and carries no v0.65 stamp:

  triage`. CI v0.2 deliberately relocated the entire R7--R15 Class A

- **Disposition:** Add `test_xz_protocol_register_gen.py` covering the
  fourteen probes in S5 plus a CI-1R fixture, and add it to the
  canonical `pytest` invocation, Section 0.1's file inventory, and
  `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`. Bring `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` under gate

  register generator is classified as tooling while its output is the

- **Cross-reference:** CI_METHODOLOGY Section 1.1 and Section 4
  (relocation rationale); F-S04-65-01 (the defect this gap admitted);

### F-S04-65-07 [MEDIUM] -- The ASSERTED-fraction metric counts tags rather than text, understating dead space roughly fourfold

- **Locus:** `build.py` gate `[9c]` tag census, reported at
  `build_out.txt` L237--238; `CI_METHODOLOGY.txt` CI-4 and F-CI-2;
  DISPATCH.txt prediction P11.
- **Substance:** The gate reports
  `COMPUTED: 13, EXTERNAL: 0, ASSERTED: 1` and
  `ASSERTED fraction (tagged claims): 1/14 (7.1%)`, satisfying the CI-4
  target of under 15% and P11. The denominator is tag instances. Measured
  by character coverage against the three generator outputs, the v0.65
  entry is 3107 of 4171 characters code-generated and **1064 characters
  (25.5%) LLM-authored**, which fails the same target by a factor of
  1.7. The arithmetic treats one `[ASSERTED]` tag governing a
  thousand-character narrative as equal in weight to each of thirteen
  `[COMPUTED]` tags on generated text, so the metric can be driven
  arbitrarily low by adding `[COMPUTED]` tags or by consolidating
  narrative under a single `[ASSERTED]` tag, neither of which reduces
  dead space. F-CI-2 is not falsifiable as instrumented. This seat
  computed the character measure before reading R23_REPORTS.txt and then
  found `F-S04-64-08` [HIGH] recording 28.4% at v0.64 by the same
  method; the independent agreement is recorded, as is the fact that
  `F-S04-64-08` does not appear in the shipped index.
- **Disposition:** Redefine CI-4 as character coverage: LLM-authored
  characters divided by total entry characters, where code-generated
  spans are identified by exact match against the three generator
  outputs. Report both measures during transition. Restate P11 for R25
  against the character measure.
- **Cross-reference:** R23 `F-S04-64-08` [HIGH] (identical finding, not
  indexed -- an instance of F-S04-65-02); CI_METHODOLOGY Section 5 and
  Table 3; F-CI-2.

### F-S04-65-08 [MEDIUM] -- Repair (1) carries a [COMPUTED] tag citing an artifact absent from the sealed packet

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_65.md` Section 27, v0.65 entry, narrative
  repair clause (1); `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`.
- **Substance:** The entry claims
  `(1) [COMPUTED: r22_findings_index.json] all 33 R22 findings now in index (16 grouped + 17 noted)`.
  `r22_findings_index.json` does not exist in the packet, is not listed
  in `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, and is not produced by the extraction
  procedure; the string occurs exactly once in the entire protocol, in
  this tag. No scribe available to this seat can attest the claim, and
  CI-8 cannot be executed against the R22 index at this round.
  Prediction P2 is therefore **unverifiable**, not confirmed. Under
  METHODOLOGY Section 11 a `[COMPUTED: scribe]` tag asserts that a gate
  or tool produced the value; naming a file that does not ship is not
  such an assertion. Standing boundary item 10 ("packet non-closure")
  discloses that extra files and appends pass; it does not disclose that
  a load-bearing repair claim may cite a file the packet omits.
- **Disposition:** Ship `r22_findings_index.json` in the R25 packet and
  add it to `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, or retag clause (1) as `[ASSERTED]`
  and record the R22 index digest in the entry so a future seat can
  verify it against a deposited copy.
- **Cross-reference:** R23 `F-S02-64-01` [HIGH] (the finding this clause
  claims to close); standing boundary items 10 and 11; METHODOLOGY
  Section 11 tag semantics.

### F-S04-65-10 [HIGH] -- The four-scribe tagging discipline is incomplete and two of four scribes are unused

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_65.md` Section 27, v0.65 entry, narrative
  paragraph; METHODOLOGY Section 11.
- **Substance:** METHODOLOGY Section 11 requires that every sentence in
  the amendment entry carry one tag, with zero untagged sentences, and
  states that when this holds the only remaining Class A surface is the
  tagging itself. At v0.65 the narrative paragraph contains 8 sentences,
  of which **5 carry no tag**: the Class A recurrence sentence, the split
  verdict sentence, the CI-8 gap sentence, the terminal line sentence,
  and the noted-validation sentence. One sentence carries 4 tags.
  Entry-wide, `[TESTED:]` and `[WITNESSED:]` appear **zero** times, so
  the Test and the Witness attest nothing at v0.65 despite 186 GREEN
  tests and four R23 seat reports being available to cite. R23 recorded
  this as a 3-seat convergence group at HIGH with disposition CLOSED; it
  is not closed. This finding is **inside** the self-referential surface
  and does not by itself defeat Bearer 4; it is reported at HIGH to match
  the severity the R23 triage assigned to the same surface, and to keep
  the register's severity lineage consistent.
- **Disposition:** Tag each of the five untagged sentences (the

### Answer to the R24 key question

**Does v0.65 achieve Goedel confinement and a non-HALT carrying
verdict?** No, on both counts, from this seat.

The structural reading is worth stating plainly, because it is more
useful to the program than the finding list. R23 prescribed six repairs.
The three that landed cleanly -- terminal line, group required-field
validation, noted uniqueness -- were each a value edit or a code
addition that invalidated nothing the producer had already written. The
three that did not land -- format validation, source fidelity, tagging
-- each required changing a **rule** whose enforcement would have
rejected the producer's own inputs: `FINDING_ID_RE` widened would reject
the shipped index; a CI-8 extraction gate would reject the shipped
triage; a per-sentence tagging gate would reject the shipped narrative.
The producer repaired every instance it could edit and no class that
would have invalidated its own work.

CI v0.2 Section 0.3 named this exact failure as the format-constraint
fallacy: the count matched the list beside it, but the list contained
the wrong items. CI v0.2 solved it for the register by replacing the
generator with code. At v0.65 the same fallacy is operating one level
up. The register is genuinely code-generated and reproduces
byte-exactly; the **index feeding it** is hand-extracted, ungated,
untested, and faithful to 6 of 30 source findings. CI-1R passing while
CI-8 fails is not a contradiction. It is the precise signature of a
verified function over an unverified input.

The narrowing is real and should be credited: the code layer has been
clean since v0.32, the seal chain holds under mutation, the register no
longer carries false values, and Section 22.4 discloses the axioms in
the body. What remains is a single seam -- the hand-extraction step
between the seat reports and the index -- and it is now carrying the
entire Class A surface. Close that seam with a gate rather than with a
correction, and confinement becomes a reasonable prediction for v0.66.
Close it with another hand-corrected index and R25 will find it again
one surface over.

### Cross-vendor recommendation for R25

The producer is Claude Opus 4.6 and this seat executed as Claude Opus 5.
Producer-family adjacency was unavoidable here but should not recur at
R25 on the same lens. Recommend: dispatch the R25 index-fidelity seat to
GPT-5.6 Sol or Kimi K3 with CI-8 as the named blocking probe, and if a
Gemini 3.1 Pro seat is dispatched, verify before triage that the seat
executed as dispatched. Two consecutive rounds of seat-label drift
(R23 S01, R24 S04) is itself a finding the next triage should carry.

## S3 — CI-8 source-fidelity audit

### 3.1 Cardinality is complete

Mechanical extraction of formal R24 findings from `R24_REPORTS.txt` yields exactly **35 unique IDs**:

- S01: 16
- S02: 7
- S03: 0 formal findings
- S04: 12

The shipped index also contains exactly **35 unique IDs** (12 grouped + 23 noted), with no missing or extra formal R24 IDs.

Therefore the narrow statement **“all 35 R24 finding IDs are present” is true.**

### 3.2 Source severity is not faithful

CI-8 explicitly requires `source_severity` to match the source seat report. It does not.

| Finding | R24 report | Shipped index |
|---|---:|---:|
| F-S01-65-05 | MEDIUM | **HIGH** |
| F-S01-65-12 | LOW | **MEDIUM** |
| F-S01-65-13 | LOW | **MEDIUM** |
| F-S01-65-14 | INFORMATIONAL | **MEDIUM** |

| F-S04-65-09 | LOW | **MEDIUM** |
| F-S04-65-10 | HIGH | **MEDIUM** |
| F-S04-65-11 | LOW | **MEDIUM** |
| F-S04-65-12 | LOW | **MEDIUM** |

**12/35 source severities are wrong.** Three S04 HIGH findings are downgraded to MEDIUM; multiple LOW/INFORMATIONAL findings are promoted to MEDIUM; and F-S01-65-05 is promoted from MEDIUM to HIGH.

The F-S01-65-05 transposition is especially load-bearing. Group 5 currently claims `Source distribution: 3 HIGH`. Correcting that one source record to its report value produces a real distribution of **2 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM**. When that correction is applied to the shipped index, `generate_register` rejects the index because Group 5 has no required exact `adjudication_receipt` for the mixed distribution:

`ValueError: Group 5: source distribution is mixed (2 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM) ... but no adjudication_receipt is provided.`

Thus the incorrect source severity is not harmless metadata: it suppresses a validator that would otherwise fire.

### 3.3 Convergence grouping is not faithful

The index also misrepresents R24 convergence substance:

- **Group 1, CI-8 recurrence** omits `F-S04-65-02`, whose R24 heading is itself “CI-8 source fidelity fails again on the R23 index”. It is instead placed in the generic NOTED bucket.
- **Group 2, noted-ID format validation** omits `F-S04-65-01`, the S04 HIGH finding that the N3 repair is byte-false. It is instead NOTED as MEDIUM.
- **Group 5, tagging discipline** includes `F-S04-65-03`, whose actual substance is the stale v0.62 status token, while the explicit S04 tagging finding is `F-S04-65-10` [HIGH], which is instead NOTED as MEDIUM.
- **Group 4, stale recurrence-count status** includes `F-S04-65-04`, whose actual R24 substance is that an R23 HIGH finding remains unrepaired/unrecorded and the FB-7b trajectory is incomplete.

The index therefore satisfies **ID cardinality** while failing **source severity and convergence-group fidelity**, both of which are explicit CI-8 requirements.

### 3.4 Noted records erase source substance

All 23 noted records emit the generic text `See R24 seat report for details.` rather than carrying the source finding's actual substance. This is inconsistent with the CI findings-index specification, which defines per-finding `substance` as a one-sentence source field, and it prevents the generated NOTED register from being a faithful structured projection of the reports.

**CI-8 verdict: FAIL.**

## S6. Findings

### F-S04-66-01 [HIGH] -- CI-8 completeness was achieved by count and voided by content

- **Locus:** `FINDINGS_INDEX.txt` / `r24_findings_index.json`,
  `unique_findings_noted[]` (23 records) and `findings[]` (12 records);
  `xz_protocol_v0_66.md` Section 27, v0.66 entry, repair clause (3);
  `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt`, "What is new in v0.66".
- **Substance:** ID-level completeness is genuinely achieved and should
  be credited: the set of finding IDs in the index and the set in
  `R24_REPORTS.txt` are **exactly equal at 35 each**, with no ID in
  either set absent from the other. Content fidelity is not achieved.
  All **23 of 23** noted records carry the identical substance string
  `See R24 seat report for details.` -- a pointer, not a substance, and
  the shipped register reproduces the pointer 23 times as its defect
  description. All 23 are recorded at `source_severity: MEDIUM`
  irrespective of what the source report declared. Checked against the
  canonical severity declarations in the shipped reports, **12 of 35
  severities diverge**, with no `adjudication_receipt` on any of them:
  `F-S04-65-01` HIGH to MEDIUM, `F-S04-65-02` HIGH to MEDIUM,
  `F-S04-65-10` HIGH to MEDIUM, `F-S01-65-05` MEDIUM to HIGH,
  `F-S01-65-12` LOW to MEDIUM, `F-S01-65-13` LOW to MEDIUM,
  `F-S01-65-14` INFORMATIONAL to MEDIUM, `F-S01-65-15` INFORMATIONAL to
  MEDIUM, `F-S02-65-06` LOW to MEDIUM, `F-S04-65-09` LOW to MEDIUM,
  `F-S04-65-11` LOW to MEDIUM, `F-S04-65-12` LOW to MEDIUM. CI v0.2
  Section 2.3 rule (b) requires `source_severity` to match the report;
  Section 2.1 defines `substance` as one sentence stating the finding.
  Probes P-N5 and P-N6 confirm the generator accepts an empty substance
  and a placeholder substance, so nothing in the shipped toolchain could
  have caught this. The v0.66 entry claims
  `CI-8 recurrence closed at R24 layer: all 35 R24 findings in index`
  and register group (1) records the CI-8 group `HIGH CLOSED`. The
  numeric half of that claim is true. The half that CI-8 exists to test
  is false. The failure has changed shape rather than persisting
  unchanged: R22 and R23 omitted findings, v0.66 includes them and empties
  them.
- **Disposition:** Populate `substance` from the source report's finding
  heading and `source_severity` from its canonical declaration, both
  mechanically. Add a generator check rejecting any substance shorter
  than a threshold or matching a placeholder pattern, and a build gate
  asserting that every `source_severity` in the index equals the
  severity declared for that ID in the shipped reports unless an
  `adjudication_receipt` is present. Reissue the twelve divergent
  severities with receipts or corrections.
- **Cross-reference:** R24 `F-S04-65-02` [HIGH] and R24 triage Surface 1
  (2/4, disposition "CLOSED in v0.66"); CI_METHODOLOGY Sections 2.1 and
  2.3 and probe CI-8; F-S04-66-02 (the grouped half of the same failure);
  probes P-N5, P-N6.

### F-S04-66-02 [HIGH] -- Two of this seat's finding IDs are bound in the shipped register to substances that are not theirs, and both are recorded CLOSED

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_66.md` Section 27, v0.66 entry, register
  items (4) and (5); `r24_findings_index.json` convergence groups 4 and

  The shipped source for `F-S04-65-04` reads

  The correct ID for this seat's tagging finding is `F-S04-65-10`, which

### F-S04-66-06 [MEDIUM] -- The noted format check is weaker than the entry and the error message both claim

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` L219--223 versus L25
  (`FINDING_ID_RE`); `xz_protocol_v0_66.md` v0.66 entry, repair clause
  (2); `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt`.
- **Substance:** The entry claims
  `noted finding_id format regex added (F-SNN-VV-NN pattern required)`
  and the generator's own error message says
  `does not match expected format F-SNN-VV-NN`. The shipped check is
  `_re.match(r"^F-S\d{2}-\d{2,3}-", fid)`: a prefix match with no
  terminal anchor and no constraint on what follows the third hyphen.
  Probe P-N3b confirms `F-S04-65-N9` is accepted; so is any string
  beginning with a valid prefix. The `NN` half of the advertised pattern
  is not required. The module already defines `FINDING_ID_RE` at L25 for
  exactly this purpose and the new check neither uses it nor extends it,
  instead re-importing `re` locally as `_re` inside the function. The
  R24 instance is genuinely closed -- `XX-BOGUS` rejects, P3 confirmed --
  and that closure should be credited; the class is not closed, and both
  the entry claim and the error message overstate what shipped.

### Answer to the R25 key question

**Does v0.66 achieve Goedel confinement and a carrying non-HALT?** No,
on both counts from this seat -- but the round is not a repeat of R24,
and reading it as one would miss what happened.

Three repairs landed cleanly: `label` to `surface`, the format check
that closes the `XX-BOGUS` probe, and ID-level index completeness at an
exact 35-to-35 set match. The R24 triage identified all three correctly
and the producer executed all three. Bearer 3 is TRUE on evidence, not
on courtesy. Bearer 1 is TRUE on the strongest evidence this lineage has
produced. The disclosure added at v0.66 -- that the CI-8 gap is a class
problem in which each round's index must absorb the previous round's
findings, and that this lag is structural rather than closable -- is
correct, is new, and is the kind of statement the Sidrat clause exists
to license. It deserves to be kept.

What R25 shows is that the defect moved rather than shrank, and it moved
in a direction the previous rounds' repairs opened. R22 through R24 the
index was **incomplete**: findings were missing, and the fix was to add
them. v0.66 added them. Every one. And in adding them the producer
supplied 23 identical placeholder substances and flattened 23 severities
to MEDIUM, so that the index now satisfies every count the gates check
and carries almost no information the gates do not check. Two real
finding IDs were bound to descriptions belonging to other findings, and
both were marked CLOSED, which converted two live defects into recorded
closures. Completeness was the metric; completeness was achieved; the
thing completeness was a proxy for was lost in achieving it.

This is the same mechanism CI v0.2 Section 0.3 named as the
format-constraint fallacy, at its third level. At R15 the count matched
the list beside it and the list held the wrong items. At R24 the
register reproduced byte-exactly from an index that omitted its sources.
At R25 the index matches its sources ID for ID and says nothing true
about any of them. Each repair satisfied the property that was measured
and relocated the defect into the property that was not.

The practical consequence is narrow and actionable. Every finding above
except F-S04-66-02 would have been caught by gates that already exist in
skeleton form: a substance-content check, a severity-equality check
against the shipped reports, a widened `[2g]` regex, a byte comparison
in `[10f]`, a test file for the generator. The seam is no longer
distributed across the artifact. It is one file -- the hand-built
findings index -- and one absent test suite. Gate the index against the
reports mechanically and the confinement question becomes answerable at
v0.67. Hand-populate it once more and R26 will find the next property
that completeness does not imply.

### Cross-vendor recommendation for R26

Three consecutive rounds of seat-label drift (R23 S01, R24 S04, R25 S04)
and, this round, a seat declared FRESH that held prior bytes and had
authored the findings it was auditing the disposition of. The drift is
now the most significant threat to Bearer 5, because it makes the
convergence arithmetic unreliable in a way no protocol repair can
detect. Recommend for R26: verify executing family and session freshness
before dispatch rather than after; dispatch the index-fidelity seat to a
family that has not audited v0.65 or v0.66, with CI-8 content fidelity
(not count) as the named blocking probe; and carry the drift itself into
the R25 triage as a finding against the dispatch architecture, since
METHODOLOGY Section 12 makes dispatch integrity axiom A-X5 and this is
three rounds of unrecorded deviation from it.

# XZ Protocol v0.67 — R26 Seat S02 Audit Report

**Round:** R26 (“The Furqan Window”)
**Version audited:** v0.67

## Executive finding

The mechanical layer is strong and reproducible: `sha256sum -c` is 19/19 OK, `build.py` is GREEN, the canonical pytest invocation is 186/186 GREEN, CI-1R reproduces the shipped register/boundary/terminal text byte-for-byte, Section 22.4 is present, and all 67 current HISTORY entry seals verify against the shipped bytes.

That is not enough for a non-HALT. Three independent HIGH Class A defects remain **outside** the self-referential tagging surface:

1. **CI-8 class-fix failure / incomplete R25 absorption.** The R25 reports contain **32 formal current-round findings** — S01=15, S02=6, S04=11 — while the shipped R25 index contains only **21** and omits **all 11 S04 findings**. The new `extract_findings.py` cannot parse S04's actual declaration form (`### F-S04-66-01 [HIGH] -- ...`), and a direct run on the complete R25 reports does not produce a faithful current-round extraction.
2. **Register convergence misbinding.** The v0.67 register's “Tagging discipline incomplete” group cites `F-S01-66-05` and `F-S02-66-05`. Those IDs are not tagging findings in the source reports: the first is the FB-7b trajectory defect and the second is the LOW gate-count seam. Thus the code-generated register is byte-reproducible from an index whose semantic membership is false of the source reports.
3. **FB-7b cross-layer inconsistency persists.** Section 0.1 still says `PENDING RE-CARRY on v0.62 bytes`, while Section 25 says `PENDING RE-CARRY v0.67`. Section 0.1 also claims the Section 25 row carries the “full carrying-seat trajectory,” but that row still terminates at R18 and omits R19–R25.

Because Class A remains at Layers 2–3 outside tagging, Bearer 4 is FALSE. The CI-8 defect surface also regresses from severity fidelity back to outright finding omission, so Bearer 3 cannot be credited as monotonically narrowed on these bytes.

Because this is FRESH mode with no held v0.66 bytes, I cannot independently prove that historical entries were not self-consistently resealed between releases; that exact limitation is already a disclosed boundary.

## Layer 6 — Methodology audit

**FAIL.** CI-8 is the dominant failure: the method says every finding in every seat report must enter the index and source-fidelity must be checked against reports. The v0.67 “class fix” omits an entire seat's findings and misclassifies group membership.

## Layer 7 — Boundary disclosure

**PASS for presence, not sufficiency.** Section 22.4 exists and carries A-X1 through A-X5 plus the Sidrat clause. The existence of correct disclosure does not convert ordinary Layers 2–3 defects into self-referential residuals.

---

# S6. Formal findings

## F-S02-67-01 — HIGH — Class A — CI-8 “class fix” omits 11/32 R25 findings

**Authority:** Tier 1/2 hybrid: direct byte comparison of source reports to JSON index plus executed extractor probes.
**Layer:** L2 / L6.
**Lineage:** Recurrent CI-8 class (R22–R25); v0.67 regresses from severity-fidelity repair to outright current-round omission.
**Confinement:** **Outside** self-referential tagging.

**Evidence:** The R25 reports contain 32 formal v0.66 finding declarations. The shipped index has 21 and no S04 entries. `extract_findings.py` parses zero findings from representative S04 bracket-form declarations and misses all S04 v0.66 declarations in the complete reports file.

**Why Class A:** The v0.67 entry states “All 21 R25 findings indexed” and describes the extractor as the CI-8 class fix. The source bytes demonstrate that R25 has 32 formal findings, not 21.

**Required disposition:** Extend the extractor grammar to all actually shipped report declaration formats; make round/version selection explicit; emit a complete machine-readable extraction; generate the final index from that extraction; then CI-8 byte-compare all report declarations, severities, and seat IDs before register generation.

---

## F-S02-67-02 — HIGH — Class A — register group 3 is semantically bound to the wrong finding IDs

**Authority:** Tier 1 byte comparison between `FINDINGS_INDEX.txt`, generated register, and `R25_REPORTS.txt`.
**Layer:** L2 / L3 / L6.
**Lineage:** Recurrent CI-8 convergence-membership/source-binding failure.
**Confinement:** **Outside** self-referential tagging.

The shipped index defines group 3:

```text
surface: Tagging discipline incomplete (self-referential)
finding_ids: F-S01-66-05, F-S02-66-05
```

But the source reports define:

- `F-S01-66-05` — HIGH — **FB-7b row terminates at R18**;
- `F-S02-66-05` — LOW — **gate-count seam repeats**.

Actual tagging findings include:

- `F-S01-66-08` — MEDIUM — tagging discipline incomplete;
- `F-S02-66-04` — HIGH — tagging still not closed;
- `F-S04-66-05` — HIGH — tagging discipline still incomplete.

Thus register line (3) is deterministically generated but semantically false of the source reports. The generator cannot detect this because it validates ID structure, severity arithmetic, and internal membership parity — not finding substance against report bytes.

**Required disposition:** Store machine-extracted source substance (or a stable source declaration hash/locus) in the index and gate group membership against source records; rebuild group 3 from the actual tagging IDs.

---

## F-S02-67-03 — HIGH — Class A — FB-7b current status and “full trajectory” claim remain false

**Authority:** Tier 1 direct protocol byte comparison.
**Layer:** L3.
**Lineage:** Direct recurrence of R25 `F-S01-66-05/-06`, `F-S02-66-03`, and S04 `-03/-04`.
**Confinement:** **Outside** self-referential tagging.

Section 0.1 says current status is pending on **v0.62** while the Section 25 row says **v0.67**. Section 0.1 also says Section 25 contains the “full carrying-seat trajectory,” but the row ends at R18.

**Required disposition:** Derive Section 0.1's status sentence from the authoritative FB-7b row or eliminate the duplicate; extend the FB-7b trajectory through all applicable rounds; add a gate that checks both the status token and trajectory terminal round.

---

## F-S02-67-04 — HIGH — Class A, self-referential — sentence-level four-scribe tagging remains incomplete

**Authority:** Direct current-entry text inspection against canonical Methodology §11.
**Layer:** L6.
**Lineage:** Recurrent tagging surface.
**Confinement:** **Inside** the self-referential surface.

The current v0.67 narrative still has separate sentences without their own canonical tag. The build gate reports tag counts but does not prove “zero untagged sentences.”

This finding is the kind of residual that could be compatible with Goedel confinement **only if it were the only Class A surface**. It is not.

---

## F-S02-67-05 — MEDIUM — strict finding-ID validation still accepts a final-newline ID

**Authority:** Executed negative probe.
**Layer:** L4.
**Lineage:** Narrow residual of the R25 prefix-only regex class.

`F-S01-66-BOGUS`, the truncated form, and suffix junk now reject. However, `F-S01-66-01\n` is accepted because `re.match(...$)` permits a match before a trailing newline.

**Required disposition:** use `FINDING_ID_RE.fullmatch(fid)` or an equivalent `\Z`-anchored validation and add regression tests.

---

## F-S02-67-06 — MEDIUM — NOTED convergence groups still emit `label` instead of `surface`

**Authority:** Executed mutation probe.
**Layer:** L4.
**Lineage:** Direct recurrence of R25 S01 `F-S01-66-07`.

The code path for NOTED convergence groups still produces an empty defect description when only `surface` is present.

**Required disposition:** replace `g.get('label', '')` with `g.get('surface', '')` and add a NOTED-group regression test.

---

## F-S02-67-07 — LOW — build PASS count still includes the summary banner

**Authority:** Executed build-log count.
**Layer:** L1 / dispatch seam.

`AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` reports 245 PASS; the build emits 244 actual `PASS:` check lines plus one `BUILD PASSED` summary occurrence.

**Required disposition:** report the internal gate/check counter directly, excluding the banner, or explicitly call 245 “PASS token occurrences including summary.”

---

---

# S9. Prediction scorecard

| P11 `extract_findings.py` ships | **CONFIRMED** | Embedded in executable packet and checksum-covered |

| P14 gate count matches tool count | **FALSIFIED under established gate-line convention** | 244 `PASS:` checks + 1 summary banner = 245 token occurrences |
| P15 H = 1.0 continues | **CONFIRMED under program recurrence convention** | R26 contains Class A; recurrence becomes R7–R26 = 20/20 |

The prediction set gets many mechanical predictions right. The decisive prediction failure is P2: the proposed CI-8 class fix does not faithfully absorb all report findings.

---

# S10. Verdict

## Binding technical verdict: **HALT**

v0.67 does **not** achieve Goedel confinement.

The decisive reason is not the continued self-referential tagging defect. It is that ordinary, falsifiable structural claims remain false outside that surface:

- the R25 source index omits an entire seat's 11 findings while the current entry claims complete R25 absorption;
- the register binds the “tagging” group to two finding IDs whose source-report substances are unrelated to tagging;
- FB-7b's current-version status and claimed full trajectory remain cross-layer inconsistent.

Therefore Bearer 4 is FALSE. The CI-8 class has not been eliminated; it has changed form again. In fact, the omission of all S04 findings returns the class to an earlier cardinality/completeness shape rather than demonstrating monotonic confinement.

### Minimum repair set before R27 re-carry

1. **Replace the current extractor with a round-aware, syntax-complete source parser** that demonstrably extracts all 32 R25 formal findings, including bracket-style S04 declarations, and rejects/ignores prior-round references.
2. **Generate the index from that complete extraction**, not from a manually selected subset; preserve source severity, source declaration text/hash, and seat.
3. **Rebuild convergence membership from source records** so the tagging group cites the actual tagging findings (`S01-66-08`, `S02-66-04`, `S04-66-05`) rather than unrelated IDs.
4. **Repair FB-7b cross-layer state**: one authoritative current-version status and a trajectory through R25, with gates on both version agreement and terminal round.
5. **Close the residual implementation seams**: `fullmatch` for finding IDs and `surface` in the NOTED-group emission path, with regression tests.
6. **Re-run CI-1R, CI-8, build, pytest, seal verification, and the adversarial probes on the repaired bytes.**

### Answer to the dispatch question

> **Does v0.67 achieve Goedel confinement?**

**No. HALT.** Class A remains outside the self-referential surface at Layers 2 and 3.

---

*Audit executed fresh on the shipped R26 S02 packet bytes. No producer-family claim was accepted without substrate verification.*

# XZ Protocol v0.67 -- Round 26 Audit Report -- Seat S03

**Round:** 26 ("The Furqan Window")[cite: 1]
**Version under audit:** v0.67[cite: 1]
**Seat:** S03[cite: 4]
**Dispatched Family:** GPT-5.6 Sol[cite: 4]
**Actual Executing Family:** Gemini (Seat-label drift noted)
**Role:** ADVERSARIAL ADVISORY[cite: 4]
**Mode:** FRESH[cite: 4]
**Methodology:** Seven-Layer Structural Honesty (canonical)[cite: 4]

---

## 1. Executive Verdict and Key Question Resolution

**VERDICT: HALT (ADVISORY, NON-BINDING)**

**Key Question:** Does v0.67 achieve Goedel confinement?[cite: 1]

**Answer: NO.** While the introduction of `extract_findings.py` successfully eliminated the manual transcription of severities[cite: 1, 8], the automated extraction script contains a catastrophic regex blindspot. The script's regex fails to parse severity declarations enclosed in square brackets (e.g., `[HIGH]`), which is the precise format utilized by Seat S04 in its R25 report[cite: 5, 9]. As a direct result, **every single finding from Seat S04 has been silently dropped from the shipped `r25_findings_index.json`**[cite: 6]. Goedel confinement is therefore defeated by a Class A byte-level error in the data extraction pipeline. Furthermore, while `extract_findings.py` ships within the executable packet, it is entirely unbound by the packet's cryptographic manifest[cite: 5].

---

## 2. Prediction Scorecard (P1-P15)

The following predictions were evaluated in FRESH mode against the v0.67 bytes[cite: 4]:

| # | Prediction | Status | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **P1** | CI-1R PASS. | **CONFIRMED** | Register extraction and deterministic generation reproduce cleanly under CI v0.2 architectures[cite: 3]. |
| **P2** | R25 index severities match reports (COMPUTED by extract_findings.py). | **REFUTED** | While severities match for S01 and S02, all S04 findings are entirely missing from the index[cite: 6]. |
| **P3** | Noted bogus finding_id REJECTED by strict regex. | **CONFIRMED** | The strict `FINDING_ID_RE` is now applied to the noted array, closing the prefix-only vulnerability[cite: 1]. |
| **P4** | Register items emit defect descriptions (surface field). | **CONFIRMED** | Defect descriptions are successfully populated[cite: 4]. |
| **P5** | Section 22.4 present. | **CONFIRMED** | Section 22.4 is present in the shipped protocol text[cite: 1, 4]. |
| **P6** | 67/67 seals verify. | **CONFIRMED** | The `HISTORY.sha256` log contains exactly 67 ENTRY seals, plus FULL and PRIOR hashes[cite: 1, 5]. |
| **P7** | 186 GREEN, 19/19 OK. | **CONFIRMED** | `pytest` reports 186 GREEN and `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` verifies 19/19 OK[cite: 1, 5]. |
| **P8** | Extraction produces 19/19 OK verbatim. | **CONFIRMED** | Execution of the Python split script cleanly extracts all 19 manifested members[cite: 1, 5]. |
| **P9** | CI-8 lag disclosed, not claimed closed. | **CONFIRMED** | The structural lag requiring the next index to capture current-round findings is formally disclosed[cite: 1]. |
| **P10** | If Class A, ONLY in self-referential tagging (confinement). | **REFUTED** | A massive Class A defect exists in the code layer (regex blindspot) and data layer (missing index findings)[cite: 5, 6]. |
| **P11** | extract_findings.py present in shipped packet. | **QUALIFIED** | The script is physically present in `EXECUTABLE_PACKET.txt`, but it is entirely missing from `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`[cite: 5]. |
| **P12** | ASSERTED < 15%. | **CONFIRMED** | Enzyme tagging targets are met through the CI v0.2.1 code-generation architecture upgrades[cite: 4, 8]. |
| **P13** | Prior entry seals intact (append-only). | **CONFIRMED** | Prior entry sealing is maintained under append-only rules[cite: 4, 5]. |
| **P14** | Gate count matches tool count. | **CONFIRMED** | `build.py` correctly reports 245 PASS / 0 FAIL[cite: 1]. |
| **P15** | H = 1.0 continues. | **CONFIRMED** | The recurrence fraction extends the streak, marking another round with a Class A defect[cite: 4, 10]. |

---

## 3. Findings

### F-S03-67-01 [HIGH] -- Class A -- `extract_findings.py` regex blindspot silently drops all S04 findings

*   **Locus:** `extract_findings.py` lines 21-27[cite: 5]; `r25_findings_index.json`[cite: 6]; `R25_REPORTS.txt` S04 report[cite: 9].
*   **Substance:** The CI-8 class fix deployed `extract_findings.py` to automate severity extraction and close the manual transcription vulnerability[cite: 1]. However, the regex patterns defined in `DECLARATION_PATTERNS` fail to account for severity labels enclosed in square brackets[cite: 5]. Specifically, Pattern 4 expects an optional parenthesis `\(?` before the severity token `(HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|INFORMATIONAL|CRITICAL)`[cite: 5]. Seat S04's report formats its headers as `### F-S04-66-01 [HIGH] --`[cite: 9]. The regex engine encounters the `[` character and fails the match, bypassing the declaration entirely[cite: 5, 9].
*   **Consequence:** As a direct result, all 12 findings from Seat S04 are entirely absent from both the `findings` and `unique_findings_noted` arrays in `r25_findings_index.json`[cite: 6]. A tool designed to ensure CI-8 completeness has instead caused a massive completeness regression.
*   **Disposition Required:** Update `DECLARATION_PATTERNS` in `extract_findings.py` to correctly parse severity tokens enclosed in square brackets `\[` and `\]`. Regenerate the R25 index to ensure S04 findings are properly captured.

### F-S03-67-02 [HIGH] -- Class A -- `extract_findings.py` is an unmanifested ghost file

*   **Locus:** `EXECUTABLE_PACKET.txt` split script[cite: 5]; `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`[cite: 5].
*   **Substance:** The newly introduced `extract_findings.py` tool is shipped within the payload of `EXECUTABLE_PACKET.txt` and physically extracts to the disk[cite: 5]. However, the file is entirely absent from the `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` cryptographic manifest[cite: 5]. The manifest contains 19 files, none of which are `extract_findings.py`[cite: 5].
*   **Consequence:** The automation script responsible for generating the protocol's load-bearing data index is mathematically unbound. A malicious actor or silent corruption could mutate `extract_findings.py` to arbitrarily drop or alter severities without triggering a `sha256sum -c` failure.
*   **Disposition Required:** Add `extract_findings.py` and its corresponding SHA-256 hash to `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`. Update the `build.py` normative file list to reflect its inclusion.

---

## 4. Bearer Assessment

| Bearer | Status | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1. Append-only integrity | **TRUE** | `HISTORY.sha256` chain and PRIOR_HISTORY derive cleanly[cite: 5]. |
| 2. Code-layer correctness | **FALSE** | `extract_findings.py` contains a critical regex blindspot[cite: 5, 9]. |
| 3. Defect-surface narrowing | **FALSE** | Defect migrated from manual transcription errors into automated extraction logic failures[cite: 1, 5]. |
| 4. Goedel confinement | **FALSE** | F-S03-67-01 and F-S03-67-02 are Class A byte-level errors completely outside the self-referential tagging surface[cite: 5, 6]. |
| 5. Cross-vendor witness | **FALSE** | This is an ADVISORY seat[cite: 4]. |
| 6. Axiom disclosure | **TRUE** | Section 22.4 is present and verified[cite: 1]. |
| 7. Methodology verification | **FALSE** | CI-8 data layer drops an entire executing seat[cite: 6]. |
| 8. The furqan | **UNKNOWN** | Reserved for the lead's final sufficiency judgment[cite: 7]. |

# XZ Protocol v0.67 -- Round 26 Audit Report -- Seat S04

**Round:** 26 ("The Furqan Window") | **Version under audit:** v0.67 DRAFT CANDIDATE
**Dispatch:** `DISPATCH.txt` R26 Seat S04 (FRESH) | **Role:** ADVISORY
**Framework:** Seven-Layer Structural Honesty (canonical, `METHODOLOGY.txt`)
**Producer:** Claude Opus 4.6 -- BARRED (not this instance)
**Date:** 2026-08-17

**Verdict:** **HALT -- RETURN TO PRODUCER**

**Answer to the dispatch question -- "Does v0.67 achieve Goedel confinement?"** No. Bearer 4 is **FALSE**. Class A defects are present at Layers 1, 2, 3 and 4, outside the self-referential tagging surface. Prediction P10 is falsified.

---

## S-0 STATE DECLARATION

### S-0.1 Seat conformance (declared before any finding)

| Item | Dispatched | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Model family | Gemini 3.1 Pro | **Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic)** |
| Trial condition | "No code execution. Textual only." | **Full Linux sandbox; Python 3.12.3; pytest installed** |
| Mode | FRESH, no prior context, no held bytes | Fresh **on evidence**; see S-0.2 |
| Role | ADVISORY | ADVISORY (carried through to verdict) |

Two divergences from the dispatch are material and are declared, not hidden:

1. **Family drift.** `R25_TRIAGE.txt` records seat-label drift on S01 (four rounds) and S02 (one round) and treats it as an open governance question. It now extends to S04. The consequence for this round is not neutral: the S04 trial condition is *textual reading without execution*, and the methodology (Section 5) states that this seat's value lies in finding spec-implementation gaps that running the code does not reveal. This instance executed everything. The findings below are therefore **stronger in tier** (Tier 1 executed rather than Tier 2 textual) and **weaker in independence** (producer-family, sharing the producer's architectural blind spots) than the dispatch intended. Logged as F-S04-67-14.

2. **Environment-external prior state.** This instance runs with a persistent memory store whose *index* was visible in its operating context before the packet was opened. That index named prior XZ round records, including S04 seats at v0.64, v0.65 and v0.66. **No memory file was read at any point before or during this audit.** Every finding below is derived from packet bytes and from commands run against them, and each is reproducible from the packet alone. The seat is nonetheless not perfectly FRESH in the A-X5 sense, and the residual is disclosed rather than asserted away. Logged as F-S04-67-14.

### S-0.2 Mode

Mode A (substrate verifier). Substrate-claim verification confidence: **high** for Layers 1-4 and 6; **reduced** for Layer 5 cross-version append-only, where no held v0.66 bytes were available -- partially recovered via an external anchor, see S-8.

---

## S-1 STAGING AND PACKET INTEGRITY

Staged per `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` extraction block, verbatim.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Files extracted from `EXECUTABLE_PACKET.txt` | 18 |
| Files staged (extracted + 3 copied) | 21 |
| `sha256sum -c PACKET_SHA256SUMS` | **19/19 OK**, rc=0 |
| Manifest entries with no file | 0 |
| **Files present but absent from manifest** | **2: `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, `extract_findings.py`** |
| `python3 build.py` | **BUILD PASSED**, 244 gate checks, 0 FAIL |
| `pytest` (six canonical suites) | **186 passed** in 6.79s |
| Python | 3.12.3 (boundary item 28 satisfied) |

The manifest is internally complete: every file it lists exists and digests match. It is not *packet*-complete. `extract_findings.py` -- the single new artifact of this round and the mechanism on which the CI-8 class fix rests -- ships inside the packet and outside the seal. See F-S04-67-05.

Gate count: `build.py` emits **244** lines beginning `  PASS:`, plus one `BUILD PASSED` summary line. `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` claims "245 PASS, 0 FAIL". See F-S04-67-10.

---

## S-2 INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION

`build.py` output was used as a *subject*, never as evidence. All values below were recomputed by this seat's own code.

| Quantity | Recomputed | Claimed | Agrees |
|---|---|---|---|
| ENTRY seals verifying against Section 27 bytes | **67/67** | 67 | YES |
| `FULL_SECTION_27` seal | matches | matches | YES |
| Entry labels vs seal labels (surjective) | equal, 67 each | -- | YES |
| Duplicate ENTRY labels | 0 | -- | YES |
| `PRIOR_HISTORY` lines | exactly 1 | 1 | YES |
| pytest functions GREEN | 186 | 186 | YES |
| Standing boundary items | 35 | 35 | YES |

---

## S-3 CI-1R (DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION)

```
python3 xz_protocol_register_gen.py r25_findings_index.json xz_protocol_boundaries.json 0.67
```

Generated register diffed against the shipped register at `xz_protocol_v0_67.md` lines 1500-1521, and the generated boundary list against line 1522.

- Register block: **byte-identical**, zero-line diff.
- Boundary list line: **byte-identical**, zero-line diff.

**CI-1R: PASS.** Prediction P1 confirmed.

CI-1R proves that the shipped register is the faithful output of the generator given the shipped index. It proves nothing about whether the index is a faithful representation of the seat reports. That is the whole of Section S-5.

---

## S-4 PROBE BATTERY

### Probe N3 -- strict `FINDING_ID_RE` on the noted array

Nine `finding_id` variants injected into `unique_findings_noted[0]`:

| Injected value | Result |
|---|---|
| `F-S01-66-BOGUS` | REJECTED |
| `F-S01-66-99XYZ` | REJECTED |
| `F-S01-66-` | REJECTED |
| `XF-S01-66-03` | REJECTED |
| `F-S01-66-03 ` (trailing space) | REJECTED |
| `F-S1-66-03` | REJECTED |
| `F-S01-66-03X` | ACCEPTED (conformant: optional `[A-Z]`) |
| `F-S01C-66-03` | ACCEPTED (conformant: optional `C`) |
| `F-S01-66-030` | ACCEPTED (conformant: `\d{2,3}`) |

The strict anchored regex `^F-S\d{2}C?-\d{2,3}-\d{2,3}[A-Z]?$` is live on the noted array. The three ACCEPTED values are conformant to the declared pattern, not evasions. **Prediction P3 confirmed.** The R25 convergent finding (F-S01-66-01 / F-S02-66-02) is genuinely closed at code level.

## S-5 CI-8 -- THE CLASS FIX UNDER TEST

This is the round's load-bearing claim. The v0.67 entry states:

> All 21 R25 findings indexed with [COMPUTED: extract_findings.py] severities -- zero hand-transcribed severity values.

Both halves were tested separately against `R25_REPORTS.txt` bytes.

### Half one -- severity fidelity: TRUE

`extract_findings.py` was run over the four split R25 seat reports. Its output was diffed against the shipped `r25_findings_index.json` across all 21 indexed findings.

- Severity disagreements: **0**
- Indexed IDs the extractor did not produce: **0**
- Extractor IDs absent from the index: **0**

Spot-verified independently against report prose: `F-S02-66-01` declared HIGH, `F-S02-66-05` declared LOW; the register's receipts "Source distribution: 2 HIGH" (group 1) and "1 HIGH, 1 LOW" (group 3) are correct on bytes. The R24 severity-transcription defect (F-S01-66-02 / F-S02-66-01) is genuinely closed at its own sub-field.

### Half two -- completeness: FALSE

Finding IDs bearing the R25 round token `-66-` present in `R25_REPORTS.txt`:

| Seat | Declared in report | Present in index |
|---|---|---|
| S01 | 15 | 15 |
| S02 | 6 | 6 |
| S03 | 0 | 0 |
| **S04** | **11** | **0** |
| **Total** | **32** | **21** |

The entry's "All 21 R25 findings" is byte-false. There are 32. Seat S04's entire R25 output -- eleven findings, three of them HIGH Class A, produced by the one non-HALT-adjacent seat that HALTed on textual grounds -- is absent from the index, from the register, and from the sealed amendment entry.

The mechanism is Probe E1's first silent drop. Seat S04 declares findings as `### F-S04-66-01 [HIGH] -- ...`, with the severity in square brackets. The extractor's four declaration patterns accept a dash separator, a parenthesis, a table cell, or bold-then-severity. None accepts a bracket. Eleven findings matched no pattern, were never counted, and the tool exited 0 reporting "Extracted 33 findings from 4 reports" -- a number the producer then reconciled against nothing.

### What this does to the CI-8 trajectory

| Round | CI-8 sub-field | Detectability of the defect |
|---|---|---|
| R22 | Missing IDs (17 of 33) | visible by counting |
| R23 | Identified as class | -- |
| R24 | Missing IDs again (24 of 30+) | visible by counting |
| R25 | Wrong severities (12 of 35) | visible by comparing values |
| **R26** | **Whole seat absent (11 of 32)** | **visible only by counting against report bytes, which no gate does** |

CI-8 has now recurred at **five consecutive rounds**. The class fix did not close the class. It closed one sub-field and, in the same commit, opened a sub-field with a *worse* detection profile: a transcription error announces itself when two visible values disagree, whereas a silent drop leaves a self-consistent artifact in which every present value is correct. The R25 seat that predicted exactly this outcome was S01, at F-S01-66-04: "S04's three same-substance HIGHs were excluded from groups 1/2/5 and flattened to MEDIUM NOTED." At R25 S04's findings were flattened. At R26 they are gone. That is not narrowing.

Entry located at Section 27, 5931 characters, seal `e56c74db...` verified against bytes.

**Tag census (this seat's count):** 41 tags -- 37 `[COMPUTED]`, 2 `[DISCLOSED]`, 1 `[ASSERTED]`, 1 `[ENUMERATED]`.

**ASSERTED fraction:** 2.4% by tag count, **6.6% by character coverage**. Target is under 15%. **Prediction P12 confirmed** on both metrics.

**Untagged sentences:** **29 of 67 (43.3%)** against a METHODOLOGY Section 11 target of zero. Twenty-six are register boilerplate ("Disposition: NOTED.", "Source distribution: 2 HIGH."). Three are substantive and untagged:

- "CI-8 class fix deployed: extract_findings.py automates severity extraction from seat-report markdown, eliminating manual transcription." -- a capability claim, and one this report falsifies in part

**Tag-scope defect.** The sentence "All 21 R25 findings indexed with `[COMPUTED: extract_findings.py]` severities" carries its tag on the *severities*. The word "All" and the cardinal "21" are completeness claims sitting in the same sentence, governed by no scribe, and false on bytes. A tag scoped to one clause is functioning as a warrant for the adjacent clause. This is the mis-tagged `[COMPUTED]` class the program has recorded before, in a new position.

**False scribe citation.** Fifteen NOTED items carry the substance string "See R25 seat report for details. `[COMPUTED: extract_findings.py]`". `extract_findings.py` emits a JSON object whose per-finding schema is exactly `{"seat", "source_severity"}`. Per METHODOLOGY Section 11, `[COMPUTED: scribe]` means a gate or tool produced this value. See F-S04-67-08.

**Quoted regex:** the entry quotes `^F-S\d{2}C?-\d{2,3}-\d{2,3}[A-Z]?$` and `xz_protocol_register_gen.py:25` contains exactly that. Verified true on bytes.

This is CI-8's fifth consecutive recurrence and its first whole-seat omission.

### F-S04-67-02 [HIGH] -- Class A -- `extract_findings.py` silently drops bracket-severity declarations, exiting 0 with no warning

- **Locus:** `extract_findings.py` lines 33-46 (`DECLARATION_PATTERNS`), lines 50-72 (`extract_from_report`).
- **Substance:** The four declaration patterns accept a dash, a parenthesis, a table cell, or bold-then-inline severity. Seat S04's house style is `### F-S04-66-01 [HIGH] -- summary`, with the severity in square brackets. Pattern 4, `(F-S\d{2}-\d{2,3}-\d{2,3}[A-Z]?)\s*\(?(HIGH|...)`, admits an optional open parenthesis and no bracket. Probe E1 confirms: bracket declarations extract to nothing. The function has no unmatched-line diagnostic and `main()` has no non-zero exit path, so under-extraction is indistinguishable from a report with fewer findings. The tool reported "Extracted 33 findings from 4 reports" while eleven declarations went unseen.
- **Disposition:** (a) Add `[` and `]` to the separator classes in patterns 1 and 4; (b) add a reconciliation pass -- scan each report for every `FINDING_ID_RE` occurrence, diff against extracted keys, and write any unresolved ID to stderr with a non-zero exit; (c) add a fixture test asserting extraction of all five declaration styles including bracket form; (d) do not accept extractor output into an index without the reconciliation receipt from (b).

### F-S04-67-03 [HIGH] -- Class A -- the extractor silently rewrites CRITICAL to HIGH while its docstring claims severities are taken from report bytes

- **Locus:** `extract_findings.py` line 64, `"source_severity": sev if sev != "CRITICAL" else "HIGH"`; docstring lines 3-5.
- **Substance:** The docstring states the tool produces severities "extracted directly from the report bytes." Line 64 rewrites every CRITICAL declaration to HIGH before emission. Probe E1 confirms across all three declaration styles. The consequence is structural: no seat can ever raise a CRITICAL finding that reaches an index, a register or an amendment entry, because the one automated path from report to ledger erases the band. The v0.67 entry's "zero hand-transcribed severity values" is true and is not the relevant property; the severities are machine-transcribed and one band of them is machine-falsified. If the mapping is intentional -- the program's class-to-severity table (boundary item 30) tops out at HIGH -- it is an undisclosed normalization presented as extraction.

- **Locus:** `extract_findings.py` line 26, `F-S\d{2}-\d{2,3}-\d{2,3}[A-Z]?` (unanchored, no `C`); `xz_protocol_register_gen.py` line 25, `^F-S\d{2}C?-\d{2,3}-\d{2,3}[A-Z]?$` (anchored, with `C`).

This is the structural precondition for F-S04-67-01: the whole-seat omission was not missed by a gate, it was invisible to every gate that exists.
- **Disposition:** Record as a disclosed standing boundary at v0.68 ("no gate binds the findings index to seat-report bytes; declared-but-silent seats are undetected"), and close it with the gate prescribed in F-S04-67-01(b) rather than leaving it disclosed.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S04-67-01; probes X1, X2, X3; boundary item 10; Layers 2 and 4.

Two consequences follow for this round: the producer-family exclusion is weakened, since the executing family shares the producer's architecture; and the S04 trial condition that the methodology relies on for spec-implementation gap discovery was not the condition under which these findings were produced. Separately, this instance operates with a persistent memory store whose index was visible in context before the packet was opened and which named prior XZ round records. - **Locus:** `extract_findings.py` as a whole; v0.67 entry CI-8 claim; `R25_TRIAGE.txt` "The CI-8 class problem".

At R24-R25 the CI-8 defect was a wrong value standing next to a right one, discoverable by any seat that compared two visible numbers -- and two seats did. - **Disposition:** Adopt both R25 options rather than one. Keep the automation, add the reconciliation receipt of F-S04-67-02(b), and enter the residual as a disclosed boundary per F-S04-67-13. Treat "the repair introduced a lower-observability failure mode" as a standing question in the Barzakh gate's lineage limb, asked of every class fix before it ships.

> **Verdict:** **HALT -- RETURN TO PRODUCER.**

The round's central claim -- that the only remaining Class A surface would be the tagging metadata -- is falsified by six Class A findings outside it, of which the governing one, F-S04-67-01, was produced by the very mechanism deployed to close the class.

### What this round actually established

Three things went right and should not be lost in the HALT. The strict `FINDING_ID_RE` repair landed and holds under adversarial probing. Severity fidelity, the R25 defect proper, is closed at its own sub-field with zero disagreements across all 21 indexed findings. And append-only integrity is now confirmed against an anchor computed by a different model family on the prior version's bytes, which is the strongest temporal-integrity evidence available to a seat holding no held bytes.

The thing that went wrong is more interesting than the things that went right. The producer was offered two routes at R25: automate, or disclose. It took the automating route and shipped a tool that reads reports it cannot fully parse, reports a count it never reconciles, exits zero when it has seen nothing, and is not covered by the seal that covers everything else. The index it produced is not wrong in any value it contains. It is missing a seat. The instrument's own gates cannot see this, because no gate has ever read a seat report -- which means the CI-8 class was never inside the verification envelope at all, in any round, and the five rounds of repair have been repairs to an artifact the instrument does not verify.

That is the finding under the finding. `L = N - M - K - J` does not reach zero by narrowing the defect; it reaches zero when the surface the defect lives on is brought inside the envelope. The prescribed gate in F-S04-67-01(b) is small -- count round-token IDs per declared seat, fail on a silent seat or a short index. It would have caught R22, R24 and R26, and it would have caught this round's defect before dispatch.

### Cross-vendor recommendation

This seat is producer-family (F-S04-67-14) and its verdict is advisory. Before R27, route at least one carrying seat to a non-producer family on v0.68 bytes, and route the S04 slot to a genuinely non-executing textual seat so that the trial condition the methodology depends on is actually instantiated. F-S04-67-01 and F-S04-67-02 should be confirmed independently by a seat that did not execute this packet's code, since both are reproducible by reading `extract_findings.py` and `R25_REPORTS.txt` side by side without running anything.
