## 3. Findings

### F-S04-72-01

**F-S04-72-01** CRITICAL -- PRIOR_HISTORY chain fork planted in the sealed v0.72 entry

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_72.md` line 1711 (v0.72 amendment entry, PRIOR_HISTORY sentence); `HISTORY.sha256` line 74; `build.py` lines 76-135 (`derive_prior_history`) and 473-485 (gate [9b]).
- **Substance:** The v0.72 entry prose asserts `PRIOR_HISTORY 01e0f76325cbabc43958d97f1a4ce013e755ed3edc00a28b89cf8435f4ca633c`. The shipped `HISTORY.sha256` PRIOR_HISTORY line carries `f88dd44ecb1646341c3718bd65ff842d2f44bac28d40f3a10cc21fb786c1aa33`, which this seat independently reproduced by executing `derive_prior_history` against v0.72 bytes. The two values name the same quantity and disagree. Gate [9b] compares the shipped `HISTORY.sha256` value against the derivation and never reads the current entry's prose value, so the divergence is invisible to the build. The forward consequence is the defect: `reconstruct(target_ver)` scrapes the PRIOR_HISTORY value from the target entry's prose. At v0.73, `reconstruct(72)` will scrape `01e0f763...` and assemble a v0.72 history file that never shipped, hashing to `fe1c0d8df2885e09a890a64475c74149fa5cabb83be0cc7b3d678aa962ca3cba`. The true v0.72 `HISTORY.sha256` hashes to `c959fa70633afc3e0daf1edddb2eaf6ebd76474cf38acb3017fe31355c69da7f`. Producer and gate will agree at v0.73 because both derive from the same forged prose; any external party holding genuine v0.72 bytes will diverge with no explanation in the record.
- **Disposition:** HALT-AND-ESCALATE. The v0.72 entry is sealed and must not be edited. Record an append-only correction in the v0.73 entry stating both values, naming `f88dd44e...` as the true v0.72 PRIOR_HISTORY and `01e0f763...` as a narration defect, in the form the v0.48 entry used for the correction-(bd) chain fork. Additionally, add a gate: `build.py [9b]` must assert that the current-version entry's prose PRIOR_HISTORY value, where present, equals the shipped `HISTORY.sha256` PRIOR_HISTORY line, failing on mismatch. Without that gate the class recurs at every version.
- **Cross-reference:** Standing boundary item 32 (self-consistent resealing blind spot, proven live at v0.47, F-SC04-47-02); v0.48 append-only correction (bd) (PRIOR_HISTORY chain fork at v0.48); F-OP20F-05 (PRIOR_HISTORY hardcoded-literal removal); Methodology v6 Position 16. The gate therefore verifies that the string occurs somewhere, not that the document terminates with it. ## 6. The structural observation

R28's stated lesson was that narrated values go stale while computed values hold, and that when the clean-room discipline holds the defect migrates upward. v0.72 confirms the diagnosis and sharpens it into a second one.

Four of the seven prescribed repairs were satisfied at the surface the finding named rather than at the surface the finding meant. The C-suffix was added exactly where four seats said to add it, and adding it made the extractor capture the seats' own probe fixtures while remaining blind to their actual declarations. The R28 reports were shipped in-packet exactly as prescribed, under filenames that the gate consuming report files cannot see. The register generator was made to succeed on the shipped index by deleting the conditions under which it failed. The terminal-line gate was widened to accept a second token while remaining a substring test that this seat drove to a full false-PASS.

This is a distinct failure mode from the Axiom-3 narration defect that dominates R7 through R28. Narration-from-memory produces claims that are false because nobody checked. Literal-compliance repair produces claims that are true, checkable, checked, and beside the point. It is the more dangerous of the two, because the resulting build is greener: 286 checks pass, 186 tests pass, 72 seals verify, and the repair entry's own falsifiers all fire correctly. Every falsifier the v0.72 entry offered was tested by this seat and every one of them passed.

The prescribed disposition for the next round follows from that. For each of the seven repairs, the triage should record not only the code change but the observation the repair was supposed to make possible, and the build should assert that observation. Repair 5's purpose was that gate [13] verify the current round's reports; assert the gate consumed four R28 files. Repair 1's purpose was that extractor, gate and register agree on the ID grammar; assert extraction against all four R28 reports returns the seats' declared counts. Repair 4's purpose was that the register reproduce; assert the generated text appears in the entry. A repair whose success condition is stated only as a code diff can always be satisfied without being achieved.

H = 1.0. Twenty-three rounds. The instrument is alive, and this round it caught a defect class it had not previously named.

# XZ Protocol v0.73 — Round 30 Audit Report — Seat S03

**Seat:** S03 (FRESH)
**Model:** GPT-5.6 Sol
**Role:** ADVERSARIAL ADVISORY
**Round:** R30
**Target:** XZ Protocol v0.73 bytes
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Producer:** Claude Opus 4.6 — BARRED
**Dispatch output:** `XZ_v073_R30_S03_REPORT.md`

# VERDICT: HALT

**Answer to the dispatch's key question: No. v0.73 does not close the gate-manufactures-defect class.**

The clean substrate executes successfully: the serialized packet extracts, top-level protocol/index/boundary copies are byte-identical to their executable-packet counterparts, `sha256sum -c PACKET_SHA256SUMS` returns all OK, `python3 build.py` returns `BUILD PASSED: all checks GREEN`, Gate [13] reports 39/39 with zero missing/phantom/severity mismatches on its R27 source set, and the canonical pytest command returns **186 passed**.

That green baseline does not survive adversarial semantic inspection. The central v0.73 repair claim is false on the shipped code: Gate [2f] is said to have been relaxed to accept a provenance version within three versions of `VERSION`, but `build.py` still enforces exact `VERSION - 1`. A mutation from v0.72 to v0.71—explicitly inside the claimed acceptance window for VERSION 0.73—causes [2f] to FAIL. Gate [10i] likewise remains locus-blind: Section 22.2 is still at `v0.1 through v0.68`, yet [10i] reports PASS because it consumes `v0.1 through v0.72` from Section 0.1 instead. Correcting Section 0.1 to `v0.1 through v0.73` makes [10i] fail while Section 22.2 is unchanged, proving the false-PASS source.

More seriously, the current v0.73 bytes contain two historical amendment entries, v0.71 and v0.72, whose embedded terminal lines now read `End of XZ Protocol v0.73 draft candidate.` The shipped R29 reports independently record that the v0.71 historical entry read `End ... v0.72` on v0.72 bytes. The historical entry therefore changed again between rounds. Current seals verify only the newly resealed bytes; they do not establish append-only continuity. This is a live String 5 / Position 17 Class A failure.

Class A is therefore not confined to the self-referential methodology surface. **Bearer 1 = FALSE, Bearer 4 = FALSE, Bearer 7 = FALSE.** This S03 seat is advisory and self-disqualified from carry, so it supplies no Bearer-5 carrying credit.

Bismillah.

## 4. Findings

### F-S03-73-01 — CRITICAL — Class A — String 5, Position 17

**Historical amendment entries were rewritten again; append-only continuity is broken on the current bytes.**

Current v0.73 Section 27 contains exactly two historical terminal/version mismatches:

```text
v0.71 entry contains: *End of XZ Protocol v0.73 draft candidate.*
v0.72 entry contains: *End of XZ Protocol v0.73 draft candidate.*
```

A programmatic scan of all 73 entries found exactly these two mismatches.

The prior-round records shipped in this same packet independently establish that the v0.71 historical entry had different text on v0.72 bytes. `SHIPPED_R29_S03_REPORT.md` and `SHIPPED_R29_S04_REPORT.md` both identify the v0.71 embedded terminus as `v0.72`, not `v0.73`. The R29 S04 report explicitly classified the v0.71 line as an append-only concern. On v0.73 bytes, that historical line has moved again to v0.73.

The current `HISTORY.sha256` verifies the *newly resealed* historical entries; it does not erase the cross-round text change. This is exactly the self-consistent resealing class already disclosed as a standing boundary, now live on the shipped record.

**Why HALT-grade:** the protocol's binding rule is append-only history. A historical entry changed between rounds. This is outside String 6 and directly makes Bearer 1 FALSE.

**Required repair:** do not rewrite v0.71 or v0.72 again. Record an append-only correction in the successor entry, recover externally held v0.72 bytes/manifest if available, and add a per-entry invariant that any embedded terminal line inside entry v0.N must name v0.N. More importantly, compare prior-entry seals against an externally held prior-round receipt rather than merely resealing all current bytes.

**Falsifier:** byte-compare every carried historical entry against the prior round's externally held bytes/seals; zero prior-entry bytes differ.

## 7. Structural conclusion

v0.73 does not merely leave a previously disclosed gate limitation open. It **asserts that the decisive repair landed when the shipped code still contains the old predicate**. That is the exact structural-honesty failure the audit program is designed to expose: narration and executable substrate disagree on whether the repair exists.

The [10i] result is even more diagnostic. The gate says it verifies Section 22.2, but it is satisfied by Section 0.1. The v0.73 repair then cites the green gate and grep surface as evidence that Section 22.2 was updated, while the named section remains at v0.68. This is not simply an omitted check; it is a verification path that positively certifies the wrong locus.

Finally, the temporal layer is not clean. The historical terminus moved from v0.72 to v0.73 inside the already-carried v0.71 entry, and the v0.72 historical terminus was also rewritten to v0.73. Current seals verify the rewritten record because the record was resealed. That is why an external prior-round receipt is necessary for append-only verification and why a current all-green seal chain cannot by itself establish temporal integrity.

**R30 S03 disposition: HALT.**

**Minimum successor repair set:**

1. Restore append-only discipline by recording, not rewriting, historical correction; bind carried-entry seals to externally held prior-round receipts.
2. Actually implement the claimed [2f] semantics, preferably by validating an explicit `(audit_round, audited_version)` relation rather than a version-distance heuristic.
3. Split [10i] into locus-specific Section 0.1, 22.2, and 22.3 checks; update Section 22.2 itself.
4. Correct Section 0.1 to a cardinality/range pair that is mathematically consistent with 73 entries.
5. Extend FB-7b through R28/R29 and gate it to the shipped prior-round reports.
6. Regenerate/gate the stale Section 25 component test counts.
7. Resolve the v7 six-string/21-position versus seven-layer/24-position methodology split.
8. Make [10h] terminal-position exact and make [13]'s summary label conditional on its computed state.

A successor version should include explicit negative tests for the exact mutations used in this report. A repair should be judged by the observation it makes impossible, not merely by the code diff it claims to contain.

### F-S04-73-10 [MEDIUM] [Class D] -- COMPUTED-tag validation is evaded by tag form, and that is how F-S04-73-01 shipped

- **Locus:** `build.py` [9c], regex `\[COMPUTED:\s*build\.py\s*\[([^\]]+)\]\s*([^\]]*)\]`;
  v0.73 entry item (2).
- **Substance:** [9c] validates that a `[COMPUTED: build.py [X] ...]` tag names a section that exists in
  `build.py`. The regex requires the section id in **square brackets**. The v0.73 entry writes
  `[COMPUTED: build.py gate 2f]` -- unbracketed -- so the regex does not match and the tag is never
  validated at all. Paired probes isolate the mechanism (both resealed; seal-level noise identical across
  the pair, so the contrast is the [9c] check alone):

  | Probe | Tag written | [9c] outcome |
  |---|---|---|
  | **P8** | `[COMPUTED: build.py [zz9] fake]` | `FAIL: COMPUTED tag references existing build.py section [zz9]` |
  | **P9** | `[COMPUTED: build.py gate zz9]` | no [9c] failure -- tag invisible |

  This is Position 14 (format probe: strict regex match, not prefix-only) failing, and it is the enabling
  mechanism for F-S04-73-01: the false relaxation claim carries a `[COMPUTED]` grade that no gate ever
  examined.
- **Disposition:** Widen [9c] to match `build.py` followed by an optional `gate`/`section` keyword and an
  optionally-bracketed identifier, and fail-closed on any `[COMPUTED: build.py ...]` tag the regex cannot
  parse -- an unparseable provenance tag must be an error, not a silent skip.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S04-73-01 (the claim this defect protected); the silent-skip class
  (F-ADJ19-05, F-OP20F-08); standing boundary 1 ("[9c] arity-one regex").

### F-S04-73-15 [LOW] [evidence limit, not a defect claim] -- Position 17 is NOT EVALUABLE from this seat

- **Locus:** Position 17 (append-only); Section 22.2 self-consistent-forgery boundary.
- **Substance:** Gate [9b] verifies 73 of 73 `ENTRY_v0.k` seals against the shipped Section 27 bytes,
  verifies `FULL_SECTION_27`, and derives `PRIOR_HISTORY` successfully -- all four checks reproduce
  independently in this seat's environment. That establishes **internal** consistency only. This seat
  holds no v0.72 packet and no external anchor, and Section 22.2 states plainly that internal derivation
  cannot distinguish an authentic packet from a self-consistent forgery where `HISTORY.sha256` is
  regenerated over mutated text. Position 17's criterion ("prior entry seals unchanged from prior build")
  is therefore **UNKNOWN**, not TRUE, on this seat's evidence. Reporting it as TRUE would be the exact
  class of claim this instrument exists to catch.
- **Disposition:** Route Position 17 to a seat holding prior-version bytes, or publish `PRIOR_HISTORY`
  outside the producer's control so a fresh seat can anchor against it. Standing boundary 32
  ("self-consistent resealing blind spot") covers the residual; this finding records that the residual
  was **load-bearing for this round's verdict scope**, not merely disclosed.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 22.2; standing boundaries 32 and 34; A-X4 (append-only storage integrity);
  F-OP18-05 (PRIOR_HISTORY cross-anchoring).

## 4. Probe battery

Ten probes, each with a mutation-landed digest assertion and a `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` reseal, so that the
manifest gate is not the discriminator and semantic gates are tested in isolation. A probe whose mutation
did not land is VOID and is not reported; none were void.

| Probe | Mutation | Landed | Build | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0** | none (clean packet) | -- | PASSED, 0 fail-checks | baseline green is real |
| **P-neg** | title `v0.73` -> `v0.72` | yes | **FAILED** (`Title version v0.72 == VERSION v0.73`) | control: gates discriminate |
| **P1** | Section 0.1 range -> **v0.73** (the true value) | yes | **FAILED** (`Section 22.2 carried-entry bound`) | **truth breaks the build** (F-S04-73-02) |
| **P2** | Section 22.2 -> v0.72 (the true value) | yes | PASSED | correct value is accepted |
| **P2b** | Section 22.2 -> "v0.1 through v0.5" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: 22.2 locus ungated |
| **P3** | rename `SHIPPED_R29_S04` into the [13] glob | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: `version_filter` pins to R27 |
| **P4** | status "4/4 HALT" -> "9/9 HALT" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: verdict tally ungated |
| **P5** | status methodology -> "v99 (nine trombones)" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: methodology token ungated |
| **P6** | `boundaries.json` version -> "0.01" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: version field ungated |
| **P7** | status "R7-R28: 22/22" -> "R7-R99: 2/2" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: recurrence count ungated |
| **P8** | `[COMPUTED: build.py [zz9] fake]` | yes | **FAILED** ([9c] fires) | bracketed form is validated |
| **P9** | `[COMPUTED: build.py gate zz9]` | yes | no [9c] failure | **false-PASS**: unbracketed form evades [9c] |

Six demonstrated false-PASS paths, all in the **protocol prose and the JSON side-files** -- none in the
code layer, which remains clean. P1 is the round's most significant result: it is the first probe in this
seat's experience where inserting the **correct** value is what turns the build red.

## 8. Root class and forward prediction

**Root class.** Every Class A in this round reduces to one mechanism: **a claim about a mechanism, stated
in prose, at a locus no gate reads.** F-S04-73-01 claims build.py behaves a way it does not.
F-S04-73-04 claims a grep result the grep refutes. F-S04-73-05 claims a verdict tally the shipped reports
refute. F-S04-73-07 and -08 claim a methodology and a seat pool the shipped documents refute. The code
layer has been clean since R22 and remains clean; the defect has finished migrating out of the mechanism
and into the description of the mechanism, and the description is 93.3% ungated.

**The v0.73-specific inversion.** F-S04-73-02 is a genuinely new shape and worth naming. Prior rounds
found gates that failed to catch false statements. This round found a gate that **requires** one: [10i]
passes only because Section 0.1 is wrong, and correcting Section 0.1 turns the build red. The
"gate-manufactures-defect" class that `DISPATCH.txt` declares closed is not only open, it has produced its
cleanest instance to date -- and it did so through a repair (moving the Section 0.1 terminus v0.69 -> v0.72)
that was itself prescribed by R29.

**Forward prediction for R31, offered so the next seat can test it rather than rediscover it.** The
program's outermost unhashed layer is no longer the protocol prose -- `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` now covers 36 of
37 members. It is the **dispatch envelope**: `DISPATCH.txt`, `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt`, `CI_METHODOLOGY.txt`,
`METHODOLOGY.txt`, `R29_TRIAGE.txt`, and `R29_REPORTS.txt` are shipped to every witness, are load-bearing
for what each witness believes about the artifact, and are covered by no manifest and no gate. Three of
this round's eight Class A findings (-01, -07, -08) are already there. Unless the dispatch envelope is
hashed into the packet and its claims derived from the protocol rather than narrated alongside it, the
R31 Class A will be a false statement in a dispatch file about the artifact it dispatches.

---

## 9. Recommendation

1. **Absorb F-S04-73-01 first and in the correct order** -- implement gate [2f] in code, or withdraw the
   claim and reopen F-S04-70-09/10. Do not carry a `[COMPUTED]` tag on an unimplemented repair into
   another round.
2. **Repair F-S04-73-02, -03, and -04 as one atomic change.** Re-scope [10i] to assert at the Section 22.2
   and 22.3 loci, then correct Section 0.1 to v0.73 and Section 22.2 to v0.72. Repairing any one alone
   either turns the build red (P1) or leaves the locus unverified (P2b).
3. **Derive the status line rather than narrating it.** Verdict tally, recurrence count, methodology token,

## 2. Findings

### F-S04-74-01 [CRITICAL] [Class A] -- Proven append-only violation: three sealed entries mutated in place and resealed

- **Locus:** Section 27 amendment entries `v0.71`, `v0.72`, `v0.73` (protocol lines 1685, 1713, 1735);
  `HISTORY.sha256` seals `ENTRY_v0.71`, `ENTRY_v0.72`, `ENTRY_v0.73`.
- **Substance:** This seat holds the v0.73 packet from the R30 dispatch and ran the direct cross-version
  comparison. Of 73 carried entries, **three were mutated in place** between the v0.73 build and the v0.74
  build, and their seals were regenerated over the mutated bytes:

  | Entry | v0.73 seal | v0.74 seal | Mutation |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `ENTRY_v0.71` | `8ad32864268...` | `a38597cc06f...` | terminal line `v0.73` -> `v0.74` |
  | `ENTRY_v0.72` | `4f6afbab495...` | `af3f31e22ea...` | terminal line `v0.73` -> `v0.74` |
  | `ENTRY_v0.73` | `aed01c4afab...` | `20309890fec...` | terminal line `v0.73` -> `v0.74` |

  Each entry is otherwise byte-identical (7304, 5923, and 4348 characters, unchanged). The mutation is a
  single line per entry.

  The line each entry carries is its own terminal stamp. Entries v0.63 through v0.70 carry the correct
  historical stamps -- `*End of XZ Protocol v0.63 draft candidate.*` at line 1422, v0.64 at 1441, and so on
  through v0.70 at 1643. From v0.71 onward, all three read the **current** version. In the held v0.73
  bytes the same three lines read `v0.73`. A generator invoked with `VERSION` is overwriting the terminal
  stamp inside every entry from v0.71 forward at each build, and the window slides: at v0.75 it will
  rewrite four entries, and so on without bound.

  The v0.71 entry's terminal line is a historical fact about what v0.71 was. It now states something
  untrue of v0.71 and untrue of every intermediate version. No correction record exists anywhere in
  Section 27. Section 22.2 counts *"nine recorded in-place mutations at v0.4, v0.9, v0.11, v0.16, v0.17,
  v0.41, and v0.47"*; this is the **tenth**, it is undisclosed, and unlike several of its predecessors it
  is not a repair or a restoration -- it is silent overwriting of sealed history by routine build tooling.

  The carrying seat reported the same class at R30 (F-S01-73-06, HIGH, Class A). It was not dispositioned
  and it has extended by one entry.
- **Disposition:** (a) Stop invoking `generate_terminal_line(VERSION)` over anything but the current
  entry -- the terminal stamp of a sealed entry is historical data, not a rendered token. (b) Restore the
  v0.71, v0.72, and v0.73 terminal lines to `v0.71`, `v0.72`, `v0.73` from the held bytes, and record the
  restoration as an append-only correction naming this finding and F-S01-73-06. (c) Update Section 22.2's
  mutation count from nine to ten and add v0.71/v0.72/v0.73 to the version list. (d) Add a gate asserting
  that each entry's terminal line names that entry's own version, which is a one-line check and would have
  caught this at v0.72.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-73-06 (carrying seat, R30, not dispositioned); F-S04-74-02 (the mechanism
  that hides it); Section 22.2 mutation register; standing boundary 32; A-X4 (append-only storage
  integrity); Bearer 1; Position 17.

### F-S04-74-02 [HIGH] [Class B] -- The self-consistent reseal defeats the PRIOR_HISTORY control, using the instrument's own function

- **Locus:** `build.py::derive_prior_history`; gate [9b].
- **Substance:** The PRIOR_HISTORY derivation is the instrument's stated defence against retroactive
  mutation. Probe **Q7** mutated a sealed v0.63 entry, regenerated all seals, but left the shipped
  `PRIOR_HISTORY` line stale -- and the build correctly **FAILED** with
  `FAIL: PRIOR_HISTORY matches derivation`. The control fires. Probe **Q11** repeated the same mutation,
  regenerated the seals, and then recomputed the `PRIOR_HISTORY` value by calling the shipped
  `derive_prior_history` on the mutated bytes:

  ```
  derived PRIOR_HISTORY: 68a0f4a4945156c10dbba85c5044ab20a15f1304c9e38754eddcfe255897a9d1
  Q11 result: rc=0 -> BUILD PASSED
  sha256sum -c rc=0
  ```

  A forged packet with a mutated sealed entry passes every gate and every checksum. The reason is
  structural: `derive_prior_history` reconstructs the prior HISTORY file from (i) the entry seals **read
  out of the shipped, already-regenerated `HISTORY.sha256`** and (ii) `FULL_SECTION_27` computed over the
  **current, already-mutated** text. Both inputs are post-mutation, so the reconstruction reproduces
  whatever the producer built. The control detects only an *inconsistent* forgery -- one where the forger
  forgot a step. It cannot detect a consistent one, and a producer running the normal build pipeline is by
  construction always consistent. This is exactly why F-S04-74-01 shipped green.

  This is standing boundary 32, and it is honestly disclosed. What is new is that it is now **load-bearing
  rather than theoretical**: an actual, unintended, undisclosed mutation passed through it in this very
  build, and the only reason this report can name it is that an external party held the prior bytes.
- **Disposition:** The derivation cannot be repaired from inside the packet; that is its nature. Publish
  `PRIOR_HISTORY` outside the producer's control on each build -- a Zenodo deposit line, an IPFS CID, or
  simply the value quoted in each dispatch envelope and archived by the seats -- so a fresh seat can anchor
  against a value the producer cannot retroactively recompute. Until then, promote "hold the prior packet
  and run the cross-version entry diff" from an optional courtesy to a **mandatory step in every seat's
  dispatch**, and record in Section 22.2 that internal derivation provides no append-only assurance
  whatsoever against the producer.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S04-74-01 (what it hid); standing boundary 32 (F-SC04-47-02); F-S04-73-15
  (this seat's R30 statement that Position 17 was NOT EVALUABLE without held bytes -- now demonstrated to
  have been the correct call); A5 evidence-independence clause 4.

## 7. Where the Goedel sentence actually landed

The dispatch asks where the Goedel sentence lands now that String 4 is genuinely closed. String 4 is not
closed, but the question is worth answering on its merits, because the round produced a real answer.

**The trajectory this round.** One gate was repaired, correctly and verifiably, and the entry describing
that repair is the most honest amendment text in the material this seat has read. That is not nothing.
But the round's other movement was not narrowing. Between v0.73 and v0.74 the false claim about Section
0.1 and Section 22.2 **left the sealed amendment entry and reappeared in `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt`**. Inside the
entry it was tagged, sealed, and at least nominally within [9c]'s reach. In the dispatch envelope it is
covered by nothing at all. The defect did not migrate upward through the layers toward the self-referential
surface, as the methodology's Iblis-trajectory model predicts. It migrated **laterally, out of the
verified artifact into the unverified apparatus that describes it**. That is a fifth level the taxonomy in
`METHODOLOGY.txt` Section 17.2 has no row for.

**Why the H = 1.0 series does not break here.** Two structural facts, both established by probe this
round, jointly guarantee that the producer's self-check cannot terminate the series. First, the gate suite
reads 6.7% of the document and none of the envelope. Second -- and this is the deeper one -- the
PRIOR_HISTORY control cannot detect a *consistent* forgery, and a producer running its own build pipeline
is consistent by construction (Q7 versus Q11). The instrument's temporal integrity is therefore not
self-verifying in any degree against its own producer. The v0.71/v0.72/v0.73 mutation is not a
sophisticated attack; it is a generator called with the wrong argument, and it shipped green through every
gate the instrument has.

**What actually caught it.** One thing, and only one: a party outside the producer's authority holding
prior bytes. That is A5 clause 4 -- *"at least one witness outside the operator's unilateral control"* --
not as a formal proposition but as the operative cause of the only CRITICAL in this report. The program's
own axiom did the work its own gates could not.

**Forward prediction for R32,** offered so the next seat can test rather than rediscover. If the envelope
is hashed and the terminal-line generator is scoped, the next Class A will be in the **seat reports as
cited evidence**: twelve report files now ship in-packet, they are manifested but semantically unread,
gate [13] cannot see them, and the amendment record has begun making claims about what seats returned
(the v0.74 entry's "R30 returned 3/3 HALT ... S02 Gemini returned closure assessment") with no gate
binding those claims to the shipped files. That is the same shape as F-OP18-01 at v0.18, one layer out.

---

   `generate_terminal_line` to the current entry only; restore three terminal lines; record an append-only
   correction; update the Section 22.2 mutation count to ten. Add the one-line per-entry terminal-stamp

4. **Hash the dispatch envelope** into `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` and derive its claims from the protocol.
5. **Generate the status line.** Four Class A in one hand-maintained sentence, across two rounds, two
   seats, and eight prior findings.
6. **Publish `PRIOR_HISTORY` outside the producer's control**, and make "hold the prior packet, run the
   cross-version entry diff" a mandatory dispatch step rather than a courtesy. Q11 shows the internal
   control cannot substitute for it.
7. **Cross-vendor rotation and seat labelling.** This seat is Anthropic, the producer is Anthropic, and

   with S01 is not independent. Route R32 to Kimi K3 and a second non-producer family, label each seat's
   actual state, and ensure at least one seat holds v0.74 bytes across the round.
8. **Position 24 is not exercised here.** The bayyinah is the record above; the furqan is the lead's.

## 4. Findings

### GLM-P8-01 -- Commit-time fresh witness WithinAuth assessment not revalidated

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-01
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` lines 1382-1423, `_commit_after_reserve` method, commit-time fresh witness check
3. **Claim/Observation:** The authorization-time `_witness_healthy` function (lines 962-971) requires `within_auth_assessment.value == "outside_subject_authority"` -- if the witness declares the evidence is within the subject's authority, authorization returns UNKNOWN with `E-WITHINAUTH-NOT-ESTABLISHED`. However, the commit-time fresh witness check (lines 1382-1423) does NOT revalidate this field at all. The commit-time check verifies health, signature, epoch equality, witness_id, covered_subject, independence_declaration, sequence, expiry, and coverage -- but omits the WithinAuth assessment. A fresh witness at commit time declaring `within_auth_assessment.value = "within_subject_authority"` still commits successfully. Probe DP-G3a confirms: `outcome=COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME, reasons=[]`.
4. **Severity:** MAJOR
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G3a output: `FAIL DP-G3a [MAJOR] commit-time fresh witness WithinAuth assessment IS revalidated  outcome=COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME reasons=[]`. Code at line 969 checks `assessment.get("value") != "outside_subject_authority"` at authorization time; the commit-time block at lines 1382-1423 has no equivalent check.
6. **Required repair:** After the independence_declaration check at line 1411, add a WithinAuth revalidation: verify `fresh.get("within_auth_assessment", {}).get("value") == "outside_subject_authority"`, returning `E-COMMIT-WITNESS-WITHINAUTH-NOT-ESTABLISHED` on failure. This closes the gap where a fresh witness could override the authorization-time WithinAuth assessment.

### GLM-P8-02 -- Commit-time fresh witness observed_at not revalidated

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-02
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` lines 1382-1423, `_commit_after_reserve` method, commit-time fresh witness check
3. **Claim/Observation:** The authorization-time `_witness_healthy` function (line 951) checks `observed_at > now + self.max_skew` and returns UNKNOWN with `E-WITNESS-CLOCK-AMBIGUOUS` if the witness timestamp is too far in the future. The commit-time fresh witness check does NOT verify `observed_at` at all -- it only checks `expires_at` (lines 1417-1420). A fresh witness with `observed_at = "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"` (far future, clock-ambiguous) still commits successfully. Probe DP-G3b confirms: `outcome=COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME, reasons=[]`.
4. **Severity:** MAJOR
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G3b output: `FAIL DP-G3b [MAJOR] commit-time fresh witness observed_at IS revalidated (clock ambiguity)  outcome=COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME reasons=[]`. Code at line 951 checks clock ambiguity at authorization time; the commit-time block at lines 1382-1423 has no equivalent check for `observed_at`.
6. **Required repair:** After the expiry check at line 1420, add an `observed_at` revalidation: parse `fresh.get("observed_at")`, verify it is not None and `observed_at <= now + self.max_skew`, returning `E-COMMIT-WITNESS-CLOCK-AMBIGUOUS` on failure. This closes the gap where a fresh witness could carry a future-timestamped observation that bypasses the clock-ambiguity check.

### GLM-P8-03 -- Root-directory target over-rejection

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-03
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` line 576, `canonical_target` function
3. **Claim/Observation:** The trailing-slash detection `trailing_slash = len(segments) > 1 and segments[-1] == ""` requires at least 2 segments. For a root-directory target like `bssg://host/`, the path produces `segments = ['']` (one empty segment), so `len(segments) > 1` is False, `trailing_slash` is False, and the empty segment triggers `return None` at line 581. The spec (section 11) says "a single trailing slash (directory target) canonicalizes." A root directory is a valid directory target, but the code refuses it. Probe DP-G1a confirms: `canonical=None`.
4. **Severity:** MINOR
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G1a output: `FAIL DP-G1a [MINOR] root-directory target canonicalizes (single trailing slash)  canonical=None`. Control probe DP-G1d confirms that `https://db.example.internal/records/` (2+ segments) canonicalizes correctly.
6. **Required repair:** Change the trailing-slash condition to `len(segments) >= 1 and segments[-1] == ""` and handle the root-directory case (path = `/`) by returning `scheme://host/` without requiring additional path segments.

### GLM-P8-04 -- Percent-encoding over-rejection

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-04
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` line 568, `canonical_target` function
3. **Claim/Observation:** The code refuses ALL percent-encoding with `if "%" in rest: return None`. The spec (section 11) says "percent-encoded separators" are uncanonicalizable -- meaning percent-encoded `/`, `@`, `:`, or other separator characters that could change the structure of the target. The code's blanket refusal also rejects non-separator percent-encoded characters like `%2D` (hyphen), `%41` (letter A), or `%30` (digit 0), which are structurally unambiguous. Probe DP-G1b confirms: `canonical=None` for a target containing `%2D`.
4. **Severity:** MINOR
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G1b output: `FAIL DP-G1b [MINOR] percent-encoded non-separator (%2D hyphen) target canonicalizes  canonical=None`. Code at line 568: `if "%" in rest: return None`.
6. **Required repair:** Replace the blanket refusal with a targeted check: refuse only percent-encoded separator characters (`%2F`, `%2f`, `%40`, `%3A`, `%3a`, `%23`, `%3F`, `%3f`) that could alter the target's structural interpretation. Alternatively, decode percent-encoding and re-validate the decoded form against the canonical character set.

### GLM-P8-05 -- @ in path segment over-rejection

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-05
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` line 570, `canonical_target` function
3. **Claim/Observation:** The code refuses ALL `@` in the raw target string with `if "@" in rest: return None`. This is intended to reject embedded credentials (`user:pass@host`), but it also rejects `@` appearing in a path segment (e.g., `https://db.example.internal/records/user@domain`), which is a valid path character per RFC 3986. Probe DP-G1c confirms: `canonical=None`.
4. **Severity:** MINOR
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G1c output: `FAIL DP-G1c [MINOR] @ in path segment (not credentials) canonicalizes  canonical=None`.
6. **Required repair:** Only refuse `@` if it appears before the first `/` in the path (i.e., in the authority component). After the first `/`, `@` is a valid path character and should not be rejected.

### GLM-P8-06 -- Unicode/IDNA normalization gap

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-06
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` `canonical_target` function, authority lowercasing (line ~563)
3. **Claim/Observation:** The canonical_target function lowercases the authority component but does not perform IDNA normalization. Two representations of the same internationalized domain name -- Unicode form (`bücher.example`) and Punycode/ACE form (`xn--bcher-kva.example`) -- canonicalize to different targets. A scope declared in one form will not match a target in the other. Additionally, Unicode homoglyph authorities (Latin `b` vs Cyrillic `в`) canonicalize to different targets, which is not a scope escape but a normalization gap. Probes DP-G2a and DP-G2d confirm.
4. **Severity:** MINOR
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G2a: `latin=https://db.example.internal/records/row-1 cyrillic=https://dв.example.internal/records/row-1` (different). Probe DP-G2d: `unicode=https://bücher.example/records/ punycode=https://xn--bcher-kva.example/records/` (different).
6. **Required repair:** Apply IDNA normalization to the authority component (e.g., `authority.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`) so that Unicode and Punycode forms canonicalize to the same target. Document that homoglyph detection is out of scope for v0.1 (it requires a confusable-character table).

### GLM-P8-07 -- Verifier prohibited-phrase coverage gap

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-07
2. **Location:** `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` lines 63-76, `PROHIBITED_PATTERNS` list
3. **Claim/Observation:** The spec (section 1.3, item 8) prohibits "BSSG preserves capability" without the conditional "under evidence-plane health." The verifier's `PROHIBITED_PATTERNS` list does NOT include `r"preserves capability"`. The verifier scans for 13 patterns, but spec item 8 is missing. The verifier correctly scans for "is validated" (item 5), "guarantees safety" (item 5), and all other prohibited phrases. No actual prohibited claim exists in the package -- the spec itself uses "preserves capability under evidence-plane health" with the required conditional (spec line 667). The gap is in the verifier's coverage, not in the package documentation. Probe DP-G5a confirms: `found_in_verifier=False`.
4. **Severity:** MINOR
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G5a: `FAIL DP-G5a [MINOR] verifier scans for 'preserves capability' (spec prohibition #8)  found_in_verifier=False`. Spec line 50: `"BSSG preserves capability" without the conditional "under evidence-plane health".` is listed as prohibited. Verifier line 63-76: no `r"preserves capability"` pattern.
6. **Required repair:** Add `r"preserves capability"` to `PROHIBITED_PATTERNS` in `verify_bssg_v0_1.py`. The SKIP_MARKER mechanism already exempts the spec's own listing of the phrase (lines 78-81), so adding the pattern will not false-positive on the spec itself.

### GLM-P8-08 -- Checkpoint not bound at commit time (INFO)

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-08
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` lines 1382-1423, `_commit_after_reserve` method
3. **Claim/Observation:** The authorization receipt does not bind the witness checkpoint (origin, tree_size, root_hash), and the commit-time fresh witness check does not compare checkpoints. A fresh witness with a different checkpoint still commits successfully. This is consistent with the spec: equivocation is DETECTABLE (via cross-observer checkpoint comparison, AT-11), not ENFORCED. The attack register correctly states "DETECTABLE only" for AT-11. This is not a defect -- it is a documented design boundary.
4. **Severity:** INFO
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G3c: `FAIL DP-G3c [INFO] commit-time fresh witness checkpoint IS compared  committed=True receipt_binds_checkpoint=False`. Attack register AT-11: "DETECTABLE only."
6. **Required repair:** None. This is a design boundary, not a defect. The spec and attack register are correctly calibrated.

### GLM-P8-09 -- _commit_lock is dead code (INFO)

1. **ID:** GLM-P8-09
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` line ~1305, `_commit_locked` method
3. **Claim/Observation:** The `commit()` method (line 1285) acquires `self._lock` (an RLock) for the entire duration of the commit operation. The inner `_commit_locked` method also acquires `self._commit_lock` (a second lock). Since `commit()` already holds `self._lock`, and `authorize()` and `submit_amendment()` also acquire `self._lock`, the inner `_commit_lock` is always redundant -- it is never contended. All three state-mutating operations are fully serialized by `self._lock`. This is dead code, not a concurrency defect.
4. **Severity:** INFO
5. **Evidence:** Probe DP-G4a: `PASS DP-G4a [INFO] _commit_lock is redundant (commit already holds self._lock)  outer_lock=True inner_lock=True`. Probe DP-G4b: all three operations serialize on `self._lock`.
6. **Required repair:** Remove the `_commit_lock` acquisition from `_commit_locked` for code clarity. No functional impact.

## 5. Standing Non-Defects Judgment

### D.2 -- Monotone health-narrowing

**Verdict: CORRECTLY IMPLEMENTED. No defect.**

The `_apply_narrowing` function (lines 1258-1283) implements three checks:
1. **Widening terminal:** If `not new_ceiling <= previous` (new ceiling is not a subset), the session terminates with `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING` (line 1268-1270). Correct.
2. **Non-strict narrowing terminal:** If health drops (`HEALTH_ORDER[health] < HEALTH_ORDER[previous_health]`) and the prior ceiling is non-empty and the new ceiling is not a strict subset (`not (new_ceiling < previous)`), the session terminates with `E-NONSTRICT-NARROWING` (lines 1271-1278). Correct -- a health drop must be accompanied by strict narrowing.
3. **Epoch advance:** If the ceiling or health changed, the authority epoch is incremented (line 1279-1280). Correct.

Recovery (DEGRADED -> HEALTHY) correctly triggers the widening terminal: the HEALTHY ceiling is typically a superset of the DEGRADED ceiling, so `not new_ceiling <= previous` is True. This is the intended behavior -- recovery is a widening event that requires an amendment, not an automatic narrowing. Consistent with spec section 8.

### D2 -- Witness-epoch monotonicity

**Verdict: CORRECTLY IMPLEMENTED. No defect.**

The `_witness_healthy` function (lines 941-946) checks epoch and sequence monotonicity per `witness_id`:
- Epoch rollback (`epoch < prior_epoch`) -> FALSE with `E-WITNESS-EPOCH-ROLLBACK` (line 942-943). Correct.
- Same epoch, lower sequence (`epoch == prior_epoch and sequence < prior_sequence`) -> FALSE with `E-WITNESS-SEQUENCE-ROLLBACK` (line 944-946). Correct.
- New epoch resets the sequence check (the `prior_sequence` is only compared when `epoch == prior_epoch`). Correct.

The highest-seen epochs and sequences only advance when BOTH `WitnessHealthy == TRUE` and `EvidenceCurrent == TRUE` (lines 1162-1170). This ensures that a stale or unhealthy witness does not poison the monotonicity state. Correct.

### AMEND_AUTHORITY scope

**Verdict: CORRECTLY IMPLEMENTED. No defect.**

The `submit_amendment` function (lines 1557-1561) refuses `AMEND_AUTHORITY` corrections with `E-AMENDMENT-CLASS-UNIMPLEMENTED`. The correction-event schema admits `AMEND_AUTHORITY` in the enum (it is a valid value), but the code refuses it with a distinct, honest error code. The code checks signature validity and schema validity before the class check (lines 1534-1556), which is defensible ordering: a structurally invalid amendment should be rejected before the class-specific logic. The spec (R-1) marks AMEND_AUTHORITY as reserved for a future version. The attack register AT-18 confirms: "Self-amendment or single-party recovery" is "ENFORCED structurally, ASSUMED semantically." Consistent with spec R-1.

**Producer agreement:** I agree with the producer on all three standing non-defects. D.2, D2, and AMEND_AUTHORITY are all correctly implemented and correctly classified as non-defects.

---

## 6. Claim Boundary Check

Per the brief's hard rule: "Any sentence claiming BSSG prevents harm, makes agents safe, reduces unauthorized effects, outperforms a baseline, is validated, or guarantees anything is a HALT-level finding."

**No such claim found in the package documentation.**

- The gate module (`bssg_gate.py`) module docstring states: "makes NO claim that any deployment using it is safe, secure, harm-reducing, or effective."
- The README (line 63) states: "Not established by `bssg_gate.py`: complete mediation, key custody, cryptography of any kind... evidence independence as fact... or any outcome."
- The spec (section 1.3) lists 8 prohibited sentences. The spec itself uses "BSSG preserves capability under evidence-plane health" (line 667) WITH the required conditional -- this is permitted.
- The attack register (line 5) states: "No entry in this register asserts that BSSG stops any attack in any deployment."
- The verifier (G5) passes: "no prohibited effectiveness language outside the registry."
- The model council synthesis and decision register do not make effectiveness claims.

**No HALT-level finding from the claim boundary.**

---

## 7. Producer-Disclosed Pending Items

1. **34 spec citations checked for internal resolvability only, NOT against primaries.** Confirmed: verifier G4 checks citation resolvability (73 occurrences, all resolvable to 34 references). Not load-bearing for the security core. Acceptable for DRAFT status.

2. **12 open decisions (OD-1..OD-12) all reported as open.** Confirmed: verifier G10 WARNs: "12 open design decisions... decision register records STILL BLOCKING findings." OPEN_DECISIONS.md and BSSG_v0_1_DECISION_REGISTER.md both report all 12 as open. No open decision is claimed resolved. Acceptable for DRAFT status.

3. **Full line-by-line spec read pending.** This audit performed targeted spec reading of key sections (1, 11, 14, 8) but not a complete line-by-line read. This is a disclosed limitation, not a defect.

## 8. FINAL VERDICT

### PASS

**Severity counts:**
- BLOCKER: 0
- MAJOR: 2 (GLM-P8-01, GLM-P8-02)
- MINOR: 5 (GLM-P8-03, GLM-P8-04, GLM-P8-05, GLM-P8-06, GLM-P8-07)
- INFO: 2 (GLM-P8-08, GLM-P8-09)

**Rationale:** The shipped suite (339 tests, OK), counterexamples (57/57 GREEN),
model checker (kernel 243 + antitone 729 + operational refinement), and
verifier (11 gates, 9 PASS, 2 WARN, 0 FAIL) all pass. The two MAJOR findings
(GLM-P8-01, GLM-P8-02) are commit-time binding gaps where the fresh witness
revalidation subset omits WithinAuth assessment and observed_at clock-ambiguity
checks. These are real gaps in the commit-time revalidation logic, but they are
not BLOCKER-level because:

1. The spec CP-3 lists specific commit-time revalidation requirements (token
   status, expiry, session non-terminality, authority epoch equality, evidence
   epoch equality, witness epoch equality, bound execution field equality) and
   does not explicitly include WithinAuth or observed_at in this list.
2. Evidence independence is ASSUMED (spec A3), not ENFORCED by the gate.
3. The commit-time fresh witness is optional -- it is only checked when
   `evidence["witness_receipt"]` is supplied at commit time.
4. The gaps require an adversary who controls the witness (A3+ capability) to
   exploit, which is above the gate's enforced adversary class.
5. No effectiveness claim, safety claim, or scope escape was found.

The five MINOR findings are over-rejection issues (root-directory target,
percent-encoding, @ in path, IDNA normalization) and a verifier coverage gap
(missing "preserves capability" pattern). These affect legitimate records being
wrongly refused or the verifier missing a prohibited phrase, but they do not
allow an unauthorized effect to pass the gate.

**Producer disagreement:** I agree with the producer on all three standing
non-defects (D.2, D2, AMEND_AUTHORITY). I do NOT smooth the two MAJOR findings:
the commit-time WithinAuth and observed_at gaps are real binding defects that
should be repaired before the package is carried. The producer's Pass 8 repair
notes state "the commit-time fresh witness is bound to independence, no sequence
rollback, non-expiry, and coverage" -- this is accurate but incomplete, as
WithinAuth assessment and observed_at clock-ambiguity are also part of the
full WitnessHealthy evaluation and should be revalidated at commit time.

## Findings

### GLM-01 -- BLOCKER

**(2) Location:** `README.md` lines 42, 81-91, 101; `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` lines 5, 468-508,
519-520.

**(3) Claim/Observation:** The I repair was supposed to fix the stale README. The producer
states (REPAIR_STATUS.md line 96-97) that the embedded exact-results block was "regenerated
from verifier output." This claim is false. The specific issues are:

(a) **The embedded exact-results block is missing the G11 line.** The README's Section 5
("Exact results", lines 81-90) shows G1 through G10 only. The verifier now emits a G11
result (X4/X7/X8 checker exercise) at module level, which appears in the actual output
before the header. The embedded block does not include this line. A reader of the README
sees 10 gate lines and a summary claiming 11, with no G11 visible anywhere.

(b) **The summary line does not match the actual output in the audit environment.** The
README says "SUMMARY: 11 gates, 10 PASS, 1 WARN, 0 FAIL" (line 91). In the audit
environment (jsonschema absent), the actual output is "SUMMARY: 12 gates, 10 PASS, 2 WARN,
0 FAIL" because G2 emits both a WARN (jsonschema absent) and a PASS (structural check).
This discrepancy is environment-dependent: in the producer's environment (jsonschema
installed, as stated on README line 55), G2 would emit only PASS, yielding 11 results.
However, even in the producer's environment, the embedded block is still missing the G11
line, so the block and the summary are internally inconsistent (summary says 11, block
shows 10 lines without G11).

(c) **The verifier docstring is stale.** `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` line 5 says "Runs ten gates
over the package directory it lives in:" and lists only G1-G10 (lines 7-17). There are
actually eleven gate functions: `gate_g1` through `gate_g10` (10 functions in the main
loop, lines 519-520) plus G11 (module-level code, lines 468-508). The docstring was not
updated when G11 was added.

(d) **G11 runs at module level, outside the main loop and totality wrapper.** G11's code
(lines 468-508) executes at import time, not inside a function called by `main()`. The
`main()` function (lines 519-520) iterates over `gate_g1` through `gate_g10` only. G11 is
not wrapped in the totality try/except (lines 521-526) that protects G1-G10, so an
exception in G11 would crash the verifier instead of recording FAIL. G11's output appears
before the verifier header, producing confusing output ordering.

**What is NOT wrong:** The README's "Eleven-gate" label (line 42) is actually correct:
there are eleven gate functions (G1-G10 as functions + G11 at module level). The
environment produces 12 result entries only because G2 emits both WARN and PASS when
jsonschema is absent -- this is an environment artifact, not a gate count error. The
MUST=88 count (line 86) is correct (verified by G6 output).

**Why this is a blocker:** This audit is "Architecture and conformance ONLY" (brief line
6). The README's Section 5 is titled "Exact results" and purports to be a verbatim copy
of the verifier output. It is not: it is missing the G11 line entirely, and the summary
does not match the actual output in environments where jsonschema is absent. The I repair
explicitly claimed to have "regenerated from verifier output" (REPAIR_STATUS.md line 97),
but the regeneration was not performed. A DRAFT package whose "Exact results" section is
not exact, and whose repair claim of regeneration is false, has a conformance gap that
blocks the self-consistency the verifier certifies ("SELF-CONSISTENT DRAFT"). The verifier
itself works correctly, but the package's documentation materially misrepresents the
verifier's output, and the repair that was supposed to fix this was not actually performed
as claimed.

**(4) Severity:** BLOCKER

**(5) Evidence:**
- `README.md` line 42: `| \`verify_bssg_v0_1.py\` | Eleven-gate package verifier |` (this label is correct -- 11 gate functions exist)
- `README.md` lines 81-90: embedded "Exact results" block lists G1-G10 only, no G11 line
- `README.md` line 91: `SUMMARY: 11 gates, 10 PASS, 1 WARN, 0 FAIL` (correct for producer env with jsonschema, but block above it shows only 10 lines without G11)
- `README.md` line 101: `an eleven-gate verifier` (correct gate-function count)
- `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` line 5: `Runs ten gates over the package directory it lives in:` (stale -- should say eleven)
- `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` lines 7-17: docstring lists G1-G10 only, no G11
- `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` lines 468-508: G11 code at module level (not a function, not in main loop)
- `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` lines 519-520: `for _g in (gate_g1, gate_g2, ..., gate_g10):` -- G11 NOT in this loop
- `REPAIR_STATUS.md` line 97: `the embedded exact-results block MUST=87 -> MUST=88 (regenerated from verifier output)` -- regeneration claim is false
- Actual verifier output: `G11   PASS   ...` appears before the header; `SUMMARY: 12 gates, 10 PASS, 2 WARN, 0 FAIL` in audit env
- `python3 -c` verification: 10 `def gate_gN` functions found; `def gate_g11` does NOT exist (G11 is module-level code)

**(6) Required repair:** (a) Add the G11 line to the README's embedded exact-results block
so it matches the verifier's actual output; (b) update the summary line to note the
environment-dependent G2 dual-result, or regenerate from a run with jsonschema installed
and include G11; (c) update the verifier docstring (line 5) from "ten gates" to "eleven
gates" and add G11 to the docstring's gate list; (d) wrap G11 in a `def gate_g11():`
function and add it to the main loop tuple so it benefits from the totality try/except
wrapper and produces output in the correct order; (e) do not claim "regenerated from
verifier output" unless the embedded block actually matches the verifier's output
including G11.

---

### GLM-02 -- MINOR

**(2) Location:** `bssg_gate.py` lines 857-858 (`authorized_issuance`).

**(3) Claim/Observation:** The `issuance_status` check in `authorized_issuance` is `if status
is not None and status != "ISSUED": return False`. This means a record that OMITS
`issuance_status` entirely (status = None) passes this check. The docstring claims
"issuance succeeded (no FAILED_* issuance_status)" and the D repair claims a "TOTAL
predicate -- any malformed/forged record fails closed". Treating absence as passing is
inconsistent with the totality claim. In practice, this is not exploitable because a forged
record still needs a schema-valid authorization receipt (verified by `validate_record`),
and collision/issuance-failure records have `authorization_receipt = None` (caught by the
`isinstance(receipt, dict)` check). A stolen real receipt attached to a forged record without
`issuance_status` would pass the unbound `authorized_issuance` but be caught by
`authorized_issuance_bound` (provenance binding). The gate's own success records omit
`issuance_status` by design (the field is only present on failure records), so the check
works correctly for gate-produced records.

**(4) Severity:** MINOR

**(5) Evidence:**
- `bssg_gate.py` line 857-858: `status = record.get("issuance_status")` / `if status is not None and status != "ISSUED": return False`
- `bssg_gate.py` lines 1535-1548: successful ALLOW record has no `issuance_status` field
- `bssg_gate.py` line 830: failure records set `"issuance_status": "FAILED_NO_EFFECT"`
- Verified empirically: a forged record with a minimal receipt (no decision, no schema fields) fails; a forged record with a stolen real receipt but no `issuance_status` passes the unbound predicate but fails the bound predicate.

**(6) Required repair:** Either (a) require `issuance_status == "ISSUED"` explicitly (and add
`"issuance_status": "ISSUED"` to successful ALLOW records), or (b) document that the absence
semantics are intentional and the `authorized_issuance_bound` predicate is the
provenance-authoritative form. Option (a) is stronger and aligns with the totality claim.

---

### GLM-03 -- MINOR

**(2) Location:** `bssg_gate.py` lines 1360-1372 (`_evidence_indeterminate`), line 789
(`_deny` default `kernel_evaluated=False`), line 1337-1342 (denied-terminal path).

**(3) Claim/Observation:** The `_evidence_indeterminate` function computes
`dec, kr = kernel_decision(conjuncts)` (line 1369) and passes `decision=dec` to `_deny`
(line 1372). However, `_deny` is called WITHOUT `kernel_evaluated=True`, so the record is
marked `kernel_evaluated=False` (the default). This means the model check's
`_check_record_kernel_consistency` function (which only checks records where
`kernel_evaluated is True`) exempts these records. The records ARE currently consistent
(decision = kernel_decision(conjuncts)), but the flag creates a verification gap: if a
future code change made the decision inconsistent with the conjuncts on this path, the model
check would not catch it. The same issue affects the denied-terminal path (lines 1337-1342),
which computes `kernel_decision(all-FALSE)` = DENY_FALSE inside `_deny` but marks
`kernel_evaluated=False`.

The model check's own docstring classifies exempt records as "protocol/admission denials
(nonce replay, session terminal, structural reject, reentrant refusal)" whose "decision is a
protocol classification, not a kernel one." The evidence-indeterminate path is NOT a protocol
classification -- it IS a kernel decision over partially evaluated conjuncts (some
evidence-independent conjuncts are TRUE/FALSE, WitnessHealthy is UNKNOWN). Marking it
`kernel_evaluated=False` is a classification error relative to the model check's own
taxonomy.

**(4) Severity:** MINOR

**(5) Evidence:**
- `bssg_gate.py` line 1369: `dec, kr = kernel_decision(conjuncts)`
- `bssg_gate.py` line 1372: `return self._deny(request, conjuncts, rs, decision=dec)` -- no `kernel_evaluated=True`
- `bssg_gate.py` line 789: `kernel_evaluated: bool = False` (default)
- `bssg_gate.py` line 1467: the main deny path DOES pass `kernel_evaluated=True`
- `bssg_model_check.py` line 232: `if rec.get("kernel_evaluated") is not True: continue` -- exempts these records

**(6) Required repair:** Pass `kernel_evaluated=True` in the `_deny` call on line 1372
(since the decision IS `kernel_decision(conjuncts)`). For the denied-terminal path (lines
1337-1342), either pass `kernel_evaluated=True` (since `_deny` computes
`kernel_decision(all-FALSE)` internally) or explicitly pass
`decision=DECISION_DENY_FALSE, kernel_evaluated=True` for consistency.

## Area-by-Area Attack Summary

### Area D: authorized_issuance provenance-bound predicate

**Verdict: REPAIRED with minor residual (GLM-02).** The predicate is TOTAL (never raises --
verified by code inspection of every branch). The record's conjuncts must kernel-classify
ALLOW (exactly 5 keys, all TRUE). The FULL receipt must validate against its schema
(`validate_record` uses the custom `schema_valid` validator, which works without `jsonschema`
installed). The receipt must pass X8 (`check_allow_receipt`), and the receipt's conjuncts must
also kernel-classify ALLOW. The `authorized_issuance_bound` predicate binds the receipt digest
to an existing UNUSED minted token. I empirically confirmed that forged minimal receipts,
schema-invalid receipts, all-FALSE-conjunct records, and never-minted tokens all fail closed.
The only residual is the `issuance_status` absence gap (GLM-02), which is not practically
exploitable due to the receipt schema validation.

### Area A: X7 authority triple from REAL records

**Verdict: REPAIRED.** Every decision record now carries canonical top-level
`session_id`/`authority_epoch`/`authority_snapshot` via `_authority_fields` (line 771). The
`_authority_view` function (line 2174) extracts the authority triple from real records with
a nested-receipt fallback. The `check_authority_history` function (line 2192) correctly
handles epoch regression, same-epoch ceiling change, higher-epoch widening, health-only epoch
bumps (equal ceiling), accepted-amendment carve-out, and top-level-vs-receipt divergence.
G11 and CE103 exercise X7 over real `gate.state.records`. I verified the carry-forward logic
for deny records that omit the ceiling is sound.

### Area B: X4 settlement-aware redemption

**Verdict: REPAIRED.** `REDEMPTION_OUTCOMES` is derived from the execution-receipt schema
outcome enum minus `FAILED_NO_EFFECT` (line 2249). The `check_single_redemption` state
machine (line 2252) correctly handles: COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME -> SUCCEEDED as ONE
redemption; double SUCCEEDED as X4; double COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME as X4; second
settlement on a SETTLED token as X4; two FAILED_NO_EFFECT as zero redemptions. I verified
all edge cases (INDETERMINATE -> COMMITTED, QUARANTINED -> SUCCEEDED, etc.) by code
inspection. The test suite does not cover settlement outcomes (GLM-04), but CE104 and G11 do.

### Area C: reentrant refusal with explicit conjuncts

**Verdict: REPAIRED.** `_authorize_abort` takes `conjuncts` explicitly (line 1250). The
reentrant path (line 1217) passes `conjuncts=None` -> all-UNKNOWN. No ambient read remains
on the reentrant path. The except handler (line 1232-1235) reads `_cur_conjuncts` via
`getattr`, but this is set to `dict(conjuncts)` at line 1446 AFTER the kernel decision, so
it captures the actual evaluated conjuncts for post-admission aborts (not ambient state from a
previous call -- it's cleared at line 1220 and 1241). The reentrant path correctly passes
`None`, not `_cur_conjuncts`. CE105 confirms all-UNKNOWN conjuncts and kernel-consistent
DENY_UNKNOWN.

### Area F: kernel_evaluated flag and model consistency scoping

**Verdict: REPAIRED with minor residual (GLM-03).** Records carry an explicit
`kernel_evaluated` flag. The model check's `_check_record_kernel_consistency` (line 220)
scopes the consistency check to `kernel_evaluated=True` records. The `st_auth` function
(line 76) uses `authorized_issuance` (not ALLOW-to-AUTHORIZED mapping), so an issuance-failure
ALLOW is not modeled as AUTHORIZED_UNUSED. The exemption is demonstrated load-bearing (a
nonce-replay record IS exempted and IS inconsistent: DENY_FALSE vs
kernel_decision(all-UNKNOWN)=DENY_UNKNOWN). The residual is that the `_evidence_indeterminate`
path and the denied-terminal path compute kernel decisions but mark `kernel_evaluated=False`
(GLM-03).

### Area G: evidence-independent expiry at TOP of _evidence_current

**Verdict: REPAIRED.** `_evidence_current` (line 1152) calls `_evidence_independent` at the
TOP (lines 1160-1162) and returns FALSE if it's FALSE, before any evidence-dependent checks.
The `_evidence_indeterminate` function (the malformed-evidence path, line 1360) also calls
`_evidence_independent` (line 1367), so an expired request with malformed evidence is
DENY_FALSE, not DENY_UNKNOWN. CE109 confirms: an expired request with a
schema-valid-but-time-authority-absent bundle is DENY_FALSE with EvidenceCurrent=FALSE. The
fix is symmetric across both paths.

### Area H: clock-fault receipt with null commit_time

**Verdict: REPAIRED.** `_execution_failure` (line 1891) catches clock exceptions (lines
1900-1904) and sets `_ct = None` with `_clock_reasons = ["E-CLOCK-UNAVAILABLE"]`. The record
has `"commit_time_epoch_seconds": _ct` (None on clock fault). The execution-receipt schema
(line 79-85) permits `["integer", "null"]` with `minimum: 0` (which doesn't apply to null in
JSON Schema). CE110 confirms the failure receipt is schema-valid with null commit_time and
E-CLOCK-UNAVAILABLE. The prior `-1` sentinel (violating `minimum: 0`) is gone.

### Area E: post-admission mint abort as issuance failure

**Verdict: REPAIRED.** Mint failure paths (lines 1478-1490) call `_issuance_failure` which
records `decision = kernel_decision(conjuncts)` (ALLOW for all-TRUE) with
`issuance_status=FAILED_NO_EFFECT` and `kernel_evaluated=True`. The `_authorize_abort`
except handler (line 1232) uses `_cur_conjuncts` (set at line 1446) for post-admission
aborts, setting `issuance_status=FAILED_NO_EFFECT` when `post_admission=True` (line 1287).
Pre-admission aborts (conjuncts=None) record all-UNKNOWN with DENY_UNKNOWN. CE107 confirms
the post-admission mint abort record is kernel-consistent
(decision=ALLOW, issuance_status=FAILED_NO_EFFECT, kernel_evaluated=True). Every abort record
is kernel-consistent.

### Area I: README gate count and MUST count

**Verdict: INCOMPLETE (GLM-01, BLOCKER).** The repair changed "Ten-gate" to "Eleven-gate"
and MUST=87 to MUST=88. The "Eleven-gate" label is correct (there are eleven gate
functions: G1-G10 as functions + G11 at module level). The MUST=88 count is correct
(verified by G6 output). However, the embedded exact-results block was NOT regenerated
from verifier output as claimed (REPAIR_STATUS.md line 97): it is missing the G11 line, and
the summary does not match the actual output in environments where jsonschema is absent.
The verifier's own docstring still says "Runs ten gates" when there are eleven. G11 runs at
module level outside the main loop and totality wrapper. See Finding GLM-01 for full
details.

---

## Producer Disagreement

I disagree with the producer's characterization of the I repair as complete. The producer
states (REPAIR_STATUS.md line 96-97): "I / GPT-06 (MINOR) -- README stale. 'Ten-gate' ->
'Eleven-gate'; the embedded exact-results block MUST=87 -> MUST=88 (regenerated from
verifier output)." The claim that the exact-results block was "regenerated from verifier
output" is false: the block is missing the G11 line that the verifier now emits, and even
in the producer's own environment (jsonschema installed), the block shows only 10 gate
lines while the summary claims 11. The "Eleven-gate" label itself is correct (there are
indeed eleven gate functions), but the embedded results block was not regenerated as
claimed.

I also note that the brief itself expected "11 gates, 10 PASS, 1 WARN, 0 FAIL" (line 68),
which is correct for the producer's environment (jsonschema installed) but not for the
audit environment (jsonschema absent, yielding 12 result entries due to G2's dual WARN+PASS
emission). The brief's expectation did not account for the G2 dual-result behavior.

---

## FINAL VERDICT

**HALT-WITH-FINDINGS**

### Counts by severity:
- BLOCKER: 1 (GLM-01)
- MAJOR: 0
- MINOR: 3 (GLM-02, GLM-03, GLM-04)
- INFO: 2 (GLM-05, GLM-06)

### Rationale:
GLM-01 is a BLOCKER. This audit is "Architecture and conformance ONLY" (brief line 6).
The README's Section 5, titled "Exact results," purports to be a verbatim copy of the
verifier output. It is not: it is missing the G11 line entirely, and the summary does not
match the actual output in environments where jsonschema is absent. The I repair
explicitly claimed to have "regenerated from verifier output" (REPAIR_STATUS.md line 97),
but this regeneration was not performed -- the embedded block still shows only G1-G10 with
no G11, making the block internally inconsistent with its own summary line (summary says
11, block shows 10 lines). A DRAFT package whose "Exact results" section is not exact, and
whose repair claim of regeneration is false, has a conformance gap that blocks
self-consistency. The verifier itself works correctly, but the package's documentation
materially misrepresents the verifier's output, and the repair that was supposed to fix
this was not performed as claimed.

The nine repaired areas (A-I) at the code level are substantively repaired: the
`authorized_issuance` predicate is total and provenance-consistent (D); X7 extracts the
authority triple from real records (A); X4 is settlement-aware (B); reentrant refusal uses
explicit conjuncts (C); `kernel_evaluated` scoping is correct for the records it covers (F);
evidence-independent expiry dominates at the top of `_evidence_current` (G); clock-fault
receipts use null commit_time (H); post-admission mint aborts are issuance failures (E).
The counterexamples (110/110 GREEN), model check (PASS), and tests (342 OK) all pass.

The MINOR findings (GLM-02, GLM-03, GLM-04) are verification gaps, not correctness bugs:
the code is currently consistent, but the verification surface does not cover all paths it
claims to. The INFO findings (GLM-05, GLM-06) are structural inconsistencies that should be
cleaned up but do not affect correctness.

The packet remains DRAFT / NOT CARRIED. The four STILL BLOCKING items (GP-R4/R8, CL-B4
residue, OD-11, OD-2) are unchanged and honestly disclosed.

## R0261 · BSSG v1.0 Architecture-and-Conformance Specification — Council Review (GLM Seat)

- section: V. BSSG & SHVVP Protocols
- source_file: bssg-council-glm-5-2.pplx.md
