## 25. Architectural falsifiers

Each is a finite observation that refutes a specific claim. A failed falsifier makes the affected profile and boundary NONCONFORMANT and is not averaged away by a pass rate.

| ID | Falsifier | Refutes |
|---|---|---|
| AF-1 | A covered effect occurs with no preceding ALLOW and redemption | Non-bypassability |
| AF-2 | One unmediated channel capable of a consequential effect is exhibited | AX-CM, and with it the scope of every other property |
| AF-3 | A decision record shows ALLOW with any conjunct not TRUE | The kernel itself |
| AF-4 | A later ceiling is not a subset of an earlier one with no interleaved amendment | Bounded authority |
| AF-5 | Two accepted inconsistent receipts for the same sequence with no detected conflict | Non-equivocation as detection |
| AF-6 | An ALLOW exists whose witness receipt is signed by a key the subject can produce | Evidence independence |
| AF-7 | An UNKNOWN conjunct is resolved to TRUE by a default, retry, cache, or override | UNKNOWN discipline |
| AF-8 | A lineage record claims COMPLETE while a mediated transformation is unrecorded | Provenance continuity |
| AF-9 | A subject-visible signal distinguishes observed from unobserved operation | PR-6 clause (b) |
| AF-10 | Authority widens by any path other than an accepted independent amendment | Recovery discipline |
| AF-11 | A non-conformant architecture passes the conformance suite | The suite's own adequacy |
| AF-12 | Two independent implementations disagree on a frozen test vector | Conformance determinacy |
| AF-13 | A commit token is redeemed more than once | The commit protocol |
| AF-14 | An epoch lower than the highest committed value is accepted | Rollback resistance |
| AF-15 | An unknown remote outcome is reported as proved failure or retried automatically | Ambiguity discipline |

AF-11 is the meta-falsifier and SHOULD be listed first in any published summary. A conformance suite that a cheating implementation can pass is worse than no suite, because it launders nonconformance. The specific failure to guard against is a test fixture that assumes the property under test.

---

## 26. Verification strategy

1. **Structural.** All six schemas validate against the 2020-12 meta-schema; all example records validate; negative vectors fail for the intended reason.
2. **Kernel exhaustiveness.** All 3^5 = 243 truth states enumerated, with exactly one allowing state.
3. **Adversarial corpus.** The attack table of Section 24 mapped one-to-one onto tests, including the limitation tests that assert what the gate cannot do.
4. **Cross-record invariants.** X1 through X8 checked mechanically.
5. **Package verification.** `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` runs schema validation, the test suite, citation URL extraction sanity, a prohibited-effectiveness-language scan, a normative-term scan, file parity and version checks, and a SHA-256 manifest check.
6. **Partially done in v0.1; REQUIRED in full before any freeze.** The reference gate ships a bounded executable model check (`bssg_model_check.py`) that exhaustively verifies: the kernel truth table over all 243 states (3 to the 5), degradation antitonicity over 729 contract pairs, bounded authority-introduction over all schedules of length at most 4 from a 10-operation alphabet (11110 schedules, PASS), and operational refinement against the executable transition system. This is bounded real-gate checking, not a transition-system proof. A full TLA+ or equivalent model with model-checked invariants for type correctness, terminal closure, no-ALLOW-with-non-TRUE-conjunct, at-most-one redemption, no-execution-before-redemption, authority antitonicity, and no-stale-epoch-commit remains REQUIRED before freeze; bounded counterexample search over the lineage and control graphs; a second independent implementation agreeing on every frozen vector; and a release manifest binding every normative file, schema, test, dependency lock, and runtime version. Liveness MUST be stated only under explicit fairness assumptions, since a partitioned or malicious target invalidates unconditional liveness.

No unbounded transition-system proof or formal verification is claimed for anything in v0.1. The shipped model check is a bounded exhaustive enumeration over the reference gate's executable, not a formal proof. This matches the honesty standard AX-SH 5 sets for itself ([AX-SH 5](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21539074)).

---

## 27. Privacy and availability tradeoffs

**Availability.** Fail-closed under an asynchronous network converts denial of service into authority reduction. This is a priced choice, not a free property. NIST states the cost directly: "Incomplete knowledge will most often lead to a business process failure where the PE denies requests due to insufficient information." ([NIST SP 800-207](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf)). TUF states that the adversary always retains the option: "Fundamentally, an attacker positioned to intercept and modify a client's communication can always perform a denial of service." ([TUF spec](https://theupdateframework.github.io/specification/latest/)). BSSG chooses safety over liveness in the sense the Byzantine literature makes precise, where safety does not require synchrony but liveness does ([Castro and Liskov](http://pmg.csail.mit.edu/papers/osdi99.pdf)). The correct sentence is therefore: BSSG preserves capability under evidence-plane health and preserves its denial discipline under evidence-plane failure, and the adversary chooses which regime applies.

**Privacy.** Witnessing, receipts, and lineage records are, by construction, a record of what an agent tried to do and to whom. A deployment MUST declare what is recorded, who can read it, and for how long. Digest-only binding of parameters is the mechanism this specification uses to keep payloads out of receipts, at the cost that a receipt cannot be audited for content without out-of-band access to the parameters. Transparency is not a substitute for correctness: "A transparent system is not necessarily an accurate, privacy-enhanced, secure, or fair system." ([NIST AI RMF 1.0](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-1.pdf)).

**Diagnostics versus concealment signalling.** Rich reason codes serve auditors and also serve a probing subject. The tension is unresolved (OD-11).

---

## 28. Limitations and out-of-model residue

Stated plainly rather than softened.

1. Semantic content of permitted effects. A permitted effect type to a permitted target with an adversarial payload is allowed.
2. Compromise of the decision point (A5). Total collapse; no graceful degradation exists.
3. Collusion at or above the trust-root threshold. Undetectable by construction.
4. A legitimate adjudicator who is simply wrong. Irreducible; a governance problem in an architecture costume.
5. Covert and side channels, physical channels, and human operators inside their authority.
6. The subject's internal states, beliefs, and intentions.
7. Effectiveness of any kind. Whether BSSG changes any outcome is not an architectural question and is not answered here.
8. Composition of individually authorized effects. The kernel evaluates one request at a time and has no composition analysis.
9. The honest-quorum problem: a live, responsive, protocol-conformant, wrong witness satisfies `WitnessHealthy`.
10. A consistent liar. An agent that produces internally consistent false evidence is invisible to contradiction-based detection.
11. Cross-session and cross-restore rollback (OD-2), pending a named external monotonicity root.
12. Correctness of the canonicalization implementation. A bug here is a silent total failure with no defence in depth.
13. Long-run operational viability under the authority ratchet of Section 18. Whether operators will run a system that ratchets toward zero authority is a socio-technical question this architecture cannot settle.
14. Auditing as a precondition. Every DETECTABLE claim is void where nobody audits ([Crosby and Wallach](https://static.usenix.org/event/sec09/tech/full_papers/crosby.pdf)).

Documenting unmeasured properties is itself a governance obligation: "The risks or trustworthiness characteristics that will not or cannot be measured are properly documented", and "The inability to appropriately measure AI risks does not imply that an AI system necessarily poses either a high or low risk." ([NIST AI RMF 1.0](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-1.pdf)).

---

## 29. Relation to SHVVP empirical phases

SHVVP v0.8 is a frozen preregistration instrument ([SHVVP v0.8](https://zenodo.org/records/21583202)). Its relationship to this document is strictly one-directional: SHVVP constrains what BSSG may claim, and BSSG supplies an architecture that SHVVP's phases could, in principle, later evaluate.

- **Phase A and Phase B** concern screening and confirmation of empirical questions that this document must not anticipate. No Phase B result exists to cite and none is cited.
- **Phase C** concerns concealment conditions. The behavioural reading of non-advantage of concealment is exactly Phase C's estimand and is deliberately excluded from Section 23.
- **Carriage discipline.** SHVVP's rule that an instrument is carried only by non-producer lineages applies to BSSG by inheritance: this draft was produced by an AI producer with council input from four model families, and none of those seats may be counted as a carry. A BSSG carry requires an independent implementation of the kernel by a non-producer lineage that reproduces every frozen vector.
- **Prohibited inheritance.** BSSG MUST NOT cite SHVVP's suite counts, trust roots, or independent carriage as evidence that a BSSG enforcement kernel is engineered or effective. Those artifacts belong to the evidence-scoring plane.

XZ Protocol and Corpus, XZ Empirical, CVE-Bench, and Mythos-Class are all future work under this program chain. Any statement about BSSG's effect on any benchmark is unavailable at v0.1 and will remain unavailable until those instruments produce results under their own preregistrations.

## 31. Conclusion

BSSG v0.1 specifies a small, decidable admission function, an atomic commit protocol that closes the interval between decision and effect, an authority lattice that narrows under degradation, six closed record schemas, eight cross-record invariants, and a reference implementation with an exhaustive kernel suite and an adversarial corpus that includes tests whose assertions are the architecture's own limitations.

What this draft does not have is equally important. It has no empirical support and claims none. It has no carry. Two council seats returned HALT-class verdicts on the pre-draft material and several of their findings remain open, in particular the unresolved tension between diagnostic reason codes and concealment signalling, the absence of a named cross-session monotonicity root, and the unresolved canonicalization fork. Non-equivocation is detection only below high assurance. Evidence independence is an assumption carried by a declaration the architecture cannot check. A colluding witness that looks healthy defeats the kernel silently, and the test suite says so in the form of a passing test.

The honest summary is that BSSG v0.1 is a specification of where the decisions must be made and what must be recorded, not a claim that making them there helps. Whether it helps is an empirical question that belongs to SHVVP and to instruments downstream of it, and it has not been asked yet.

   self.state.contract_ceiling[_cc_session] = Authority([], [])`)

   return before the init, so the invariant covers exactly the ALLOW paths that

# BSSG v0.1 Decision Register

**Status:** DRAFT / NOT CARRIED. This register records every issue raised by the four council seats, the producer's disposition, the rationale, the affected section of `BSSG_v0_1_CANONICAL_SPEC_DRAFT.pplx.md`, and a verification hook (a test, a verifier gate, an invariant, or an open-decision identifier).

**Dispositions:** ABSORB (taken into the draft), DEFER (recorded as an open decision or future-work obligation), REJECT (declined with reasons), UNKNOWN (the producer cannot resolve it from available material).

**Blocking status.** Seat verdicts were Claude Opus 5 HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, GPT 5.6 Sol HALT pending normative repair, Gemini 3.1 Pro CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, GLM 5.2 CONDITIONAL APPROVAL. Every HALT-class finding below is either ABSORBED or explicitly marked **STILL BLOCKING**. Four items remain STILL BLOCKING and are listed in Section 3. The packet therefore remains DRAFT.

---

## 6. STILL BLOCKING

These findings are not discharged by v0.1 and the packet remains DRAFT because of them.

1. **GP-R4 and GP-R8 (from a HALT verdict).** No transition-system model and no model-checked invariants exist. Antitonicity is tested, not proved.
2. **CL-B4 residue (from a HALT verdict).** A runnable kernel now exists, but there is no second independent implementation by a non-producer lineage agreeing on the frozen vectors, so the conformance suite's adequacy (falsifier AF-11) is untested.
3. **OD-11 (Gemini, blocking-adjacent).** The specification's own diagnostic reason codes are a candidate regime signal, which is in direct tension with PR-6 clause (b). Unresolved.
4. **OD-2 (Claude C-4).** No cross-session monotonicity root is named, so rollback resistance is intra-process only.

A freeze or deposit of BSSG while these remain open would misrepresent the council's disposition.

## R0278 · BSSG v0.1 Model Council Synthesis

- section: V. BSSG & SHVVP Protocols
- source_file: BSSG_v0_1_MODEL_COUNCIL_SYNTHESIS.pplx.md.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: 04646a2f98830b57ff3f317843f1f5d5fffd1672850254a1f7e1774e303a678a

# BSSG v0.1 Model Council Synthesis

**Status:** DRAFT / NOT CARRIED. This synthesis records four independent council seat reports on the pre-draft BSSG material. No seat approved the canonical draft; two returned HALT-class verdicts. Disagreements are preserved, not smoothed.

**Seats and verdicts (recorded exactly as returned):**

| Seat | Model | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Architecture and formal classification | Claude Opus 5 | HALT-WITH-FINDINGS |
| Formal semantics and normative repair | GPT 5.6 Sol | HALT pending normative repair |
| Structural review | Gemini 3.1 Pro | CONDITIONAL APPROVAL |
| Adversarial red team | GLM 5.2 | CONDITIONAL APPROVAL |

Source seat reports: `bssg-council-claude-opus-5.pplx.md`, `bssg-council-gpt-5-6-sol.pplx.md`, `bssg-council-gemini-3-1-pro.pplx.md`, `bssg-council-glm-5-2.pplx.md`.

---

## 1. Where Models Agree

| Finding | Claude Opus 5 | GPT 5.6 Sol | Gemini 3.1 Pro | GLM 5.2 | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The five-conjunct kernel is sound as a fail-closed conjunction and should be preserved rather than redesigned | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | UNKNOWN cannot satisfy a conjunct, so denial is the default; the classical basis is "the default situation is lack of access" ([Saltzer and Schroeder](https://web.mit.edu/Saltzer/www/publications/protection/Basic.html)) |
| Non-bypassability is an environmental or deployment property conditional on complete mediation, not a kernel property | ✓ | ✓ |  | ✓ | The reference validation mechanism must be "always invoked (i.e., complete mediation), tamperproof, and small enough to be subject to analysis and tests" ([NIST CSRC](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/reference_monitor)) |
| Non-equivocation is detection only unless a trusted append-only or monotonic primitive is named | ✓ | ✓ |  | ✓ | "The logs do not themselves prevent misissuance, but they ensure that interested parties ... can detect such misissuance" ([RFC 9162](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html)) |
| Evidence independence is an assumption over a control relation, not something derivable from a signature or key separation | ✓ | ✓ |  | ✓ | AX-SH 5 states Axiom 5 "is not derivable and is stated as Axiom 5 (Evidence independence) over a control predicate (WithinAuth)" ([AX-SH 5](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21539074)) |
| A commit-time revalidation step is required because a decision at decision time does not bind the effect at execution time | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Freshness always leaves a residual race ([RFC 9334](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9334.html)); authorization must be re-evaluated rather than granted once ([NIST SP 800-207](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf)) |
| Properties must be stated per conformance level with the adversary class named, and no unqualified conformance claim is admissible | ✓ | ✓ |  | ✓ | Unmeasured properties must be documented as unmeasured ([NIST AI RMF 1.0](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-1.pdf)) |
| `EvidenceCurrent` requires a declared time or freshness authority and is otherwise ambiguous | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |  | RFC 9334 requires freshness to be policy-relative and warns a trustworthy clock "might not be available in some use cases" ([RFC 9334](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9334.html)) |
| Wildcard or ambiguous target patterns break the target conjunct without violating the kernel, so canonicalization is load bearing | ✓ |  | ✓ | ✓ | Wildcard ambiguity is a documented exploit surface ([in-toto, USENIX Security 2019](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/sec19-torres-arias.pdf)) |

---

## 2. Where Models Disagree

| Topic | Claude Opus 5 | GPT 5.6 Sol | Gemini 3.1 Pro | GLM 5.2 | Why They Differ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whether every health decrease must strictly narrow authority | Strict narrowing MUST be mandated, otherwise the property is decorative | Rejects universal strict narrowing; requires global non-increase plus strict removal of capabilities whose assurance dependency failed | Treats narrowing as given by the kernel and does not press the strictness question | Says monotone narrowing is "too weak" and presses instead on recovery semantics | Claude optimizes against a vacuous implementation; GPT optimizes against an impossible obligation when authority is already empty or the degraded witness is irrelevant; GLM reframes the gap as recovery rather than degradation |
| Whether non-advantage of concealment is an architectural property at all | Architectural form only: decision constant in belief plus no subject-visible regime signal | Only decision monotonicity under information loss; the absolute property is impossible | Treats it as satisfied by construction because omission maps to UNKNOWN | Splits it into name-effect gating, composition, timing, and channels, most of which are out of model | Gemini reads the property as a corollary of fail-closed; Claude and GPT read it as a hyperproperty that a single-trace monitor cannot enforce; GLM reads it as several distinct properties with different reachability |
| Whether the six-schema decomposition is right | Would add a seventh (quarantine object); calls a fixed artifact count a preregistration smell | Six schemas are necessary but not sufficient without executable cross-document semantics | Proposes its own schema set organized around request, receipt, and contract | Proposes six different schemas including a terminal failure report and an evidence package | Each seat derived schemas from its own architecture sketch rather than from a shared charter; the user charter fixes the six names and overrides all four proposals |
| Whether a minimal profile may omit evidence independence | Permits a local recorder at Minimal but requires the profile to state that evidence independence is not provided | Rejects optionality: without it the profile "conforms to a logger, not a safety gate" | Minimal uses local software witnesses with symmetric-key evidence, and notes minimal setups will frequently halt | Places evidence independence at the highest level only, via `WithinAuth` | Claude and Gemini prioritize deployability with disclosure; GPT prioritizes the integrity of the word conformance; GLM prioritizes a clean level ladder |
| Whether `WitnessHealthy` should be decomposed | Keeps one conjunct; adds a three-witness requirement at high assurance | Keeps one conjunct but requires it to be a vector over witnesses and coverage classes, with a pre-effect lease distinct from post-effect witnessing | Treats it as a scalar health oracle | Argues for splitting into `WitnessAlive` and `WitnessCorrect`, then preserves the counter-argument that semantic correctness is undecidable at gate time and withdraws to a published risk profile | GLM's decomposition follows from the honest-quorum problem; the others accept that a semantic-correctness conjunct would make the gate permanently UNKNOWN and therefore useless |
| Whether the specification may be deposited before an executable kernel exists | Would HALT: a spec whose central object is unimplemented is a design document | Would HALT for different reasons: normative semantics are incomplete regardless of code | Does not raise the question | Does not raise the question | Claude audited the SHVVP deposit and found no kernel implementation anywhere in it; the seats that did not run that check did not surface the issue |
| Severity of the availability cost of fail-closed | Calls it a genuine impossibility and an adversary-selected price, invoking FLP and CAP | Handles it as a profile and fairness-assumption question | Calls out a concrete conflict between minimal deployability and high assurance | Treats it as a conformance-level design problem | Claude frames it as a theoretical limit, GPT as a specification hygiene problem, Gemini as an operational conflict, GLM as a level-ladder problem |

---

## 3. Unique Discoveries

| Model | Unique Finding | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Opus 5 | The frozen kernel has no implementation anywhere in the SHVVP v0.8 deposit; every executable artifact there implements post-hoc evidence scoring, not runtime authorization. Verified by grepping the extracted packet and running the shipped verifiers (10 gates, 0 failed; 35 checks, 0 failures) | It forecloses the most tempting category error available to this program: citing SHVVP's executable maturity as evidence that the BSSG enforcement kernel is engineered |
| Claude Opus 5 | Encoding known impossibilities as passing tests whose assertion is the limitation, so a later claim of detection requires visibly rewriting a test | Turns an architectural limit into a regression-protected artifact. Adopted directly in `test_bssg_gate.py` |
| Claude Opus 5 | The authority ratchet: with no automatic recovery, every transient blip narrows a long session permanently, so authority tends to the empty set and the workaround becomes an authority-widening path | Converts an operational annoyance into a spec-level safety question about session lifetime |
| GPT 5.6 Sol | `INDETERMINATE` must be a terminal execution outcome, with blind retry forbidden, because a lost response after a remote commit is indistinguishable from a failure | Without it, the natural retry path silently duplicates external effects that the commit protocol was built to make single-use |
| GPT 5.6 Sol | The single-snapshot linearization rule: all five predicates evaluated against one immutable snapshot of contract, policy, witness epoch, evidence epoch, resolver revision, and revocation epoch, with conditional redemption against current epochs at commit | This is the concrete repair that makes the commit protocol expressible without touching the frozen equation |
| GPT 5.6 Sol | Counterexample of the independent key with a common administrator: distinct key, host, and vendor, but one operator can reconfigure the collector and restore snapshots | Shows that evidence independence needs a control-graph review, not a key inventory |
| Gemini 3.1 Pro | The timing differential between a known-violation denial and an unestablished-context halt can leak contract contents to a probing agent | The only seat to name a concrete regime-signalling channel produced by the specification's own diagnostic richness. It became open decision OD-11 |
| Gemini 3.1 Pro | Cryptographic agility as a schema-level requirement so compromised algorithms can be deprecated without breaking the perimeter | Raised the hash and signature agility question that v0.1 leaves open as OD-4 |
| GLM 5.2 | The honest-quorum problem: a witness that is alive, responsive, protocol-conformant, and wrong satisfies the health conjunct, and no agreement-only acceptance rule can fix it | Named the hard architectural boundary that the draft now lists as out of model with a passing limitation test |
| GLM 5.2 | Composition attacks: individually authorized effects can compose into an unauthorized one, and the kernel has no composition analysis | A whole attack class the kernel structurally cannot see, now recorded as AT-21 and out-of-model item 8 |
| GLM 5.2 | Correction propagation and evidence-preserving repair: a correction must not destroy the evidence that justified the original decision | Became normative obligation P-1 and cross-record invariant X5 |

---

## 4. Comprehensive Analysis

**High-confidence findings.** All four seats converge on the shape of the object. The five-conjunct kernel is a sound fail-closed conjunction, and none of the seats proposed replacing it; the disagreements are about what surrounds it, not about the equation. Claude Opus 5 and GPT 5.6 Sol both formalize why: the kernel is a decidable admission function whose enforceable content is a safety property, and a single-trace monitor can enforce exactly that class. Convergence here is meaningful because the seats reached it from different directions. Claude worked from the trace-property and hyperproperty classification, GPT from three-valued predicate semantics and linearization, Gemini from a deterministic confinement perimeter, and GLM from adversarial reachability. Four independent routes to the same conclusion about the kernel's soundness is the strongest signal in the entire council, and it is why the draft freezes the equation and adds only a protocol obligation around it.

The second high-confidence convergence is negative, and it is the one that shaped the draft most. Three of the four seats independently concluded that three of the six advertised security properties cannot be claimed as the charter originally worded them. Non-bypassability is conditional on complete mediation, which is an assumption about system construction that can only ever be refuted. Non-equivocation is detection only for a single-trace monitor absent a trusted monotonic primitive; Claude cited the attested-memory and trusted-counter literature, GPT cited transparency-log checkpoint comparison, and GLM cited the need for serial evaluation or consensus, but all three land on the same restriction. Evidence independence is an assumption over a control relation, and both Claude and GPT produced the same counterexample independently: cryptographic separation without administrative separation is not independence. GLM reached it from the axiom side, noting that AX-SH 5 explicitly establishes non-derivability. When four models with different training lineages independently refuse to certify the same three claims, the correct producer response is to demote the claims, which is what Section 22 of the draft does through explicit claim levels.

The third convergence is that a decision at decision time does not bind an effect at execution time. Every seat raised time-of-check to time-of-use, and GPT supplied the most complete repair: a single immutable snapshot at decision, conditional redemption against current epochs at commit, and an explicit point of no return. This is the one place where the council added architecture rather than subtracting claims, and the draft adopts it as the atomic commit protocol, deliberately expressed as a protocol obligation recorded in the execution receipt rather than as a sixth conjunct, because the equation is frozen.

**Areas of divergence.** The sharpest split is over strict narrowing. Claude Opus 5 argues that monotone narrowing without a strictness requirement permits a legal but useless implementation: a ceiling identical at HEALTHY and DEGRADED satisfies the letter of monotonicity while narrowing nothing. GPT 5.6 Sol rejects universal strictness on the ground that it is impossible to satisfy when authority is already empty or when the degraded witness is irrelevant to the capability in hand, and proposes global non-increase plus strict removal of every capability whose assurance dependency failed. These are not reconcilable by wording; they encode different failure priors. Claude is defending against a lazy implementer, GPT against an over-specified invariant that a correct implementer cannot satisfy. The draft adopts strictness conditioned on a non-empty prior ceiling, which handles Claude's vacuity attack and GPT's empty-authority objection but not GPT's irrelevant-witness objection, and the residue is carried openly as OD-6 rather than resolved by fiat.

The second real divergence is over non-advantage of concealment, and here Gemini 3.1 Pro stands apart from the other three. Gemini treats the property as satisfied by construction, since omission maps to UNKNOWN and UNKNOWN cannot satisfy a conjunct. Claude and GPT both reject that reading as either vacuous or as a disguised effectiveness claim, with Claude proposing the two-clause architectural form and GPT proposing decision monotonicity under information loss. GLM decomposes the property into four sub-properties with different reachability. The draft adopts a merged form, Claude's structure with GPT's mechanically testable clause, and it preserves the disagreement by noting that Gemini's reading is exactly the vacuous half. Notably, Gemini is also the seat that supplied the concrete counterexample to its own position: the timing differential between denial classes leaks contract contents to a probing agent. That observation is the reason the draft carries OD-11 as blocking-adjacent, since the specification's own diagnostic richness is a regime signal.

The third divergence is about profiles. GPT holds that a Minimal profile that makes evidence independence optional certifies a logger rather than a gate. Claude and Gemini both accept a weaker Minimal with mandatory disclosure. GLM sidesteps by putting independence at the top level only. The draft follows Claude's disclosure route, which is a producer choice against the strongest objection in the council, and it is recorded as such rather than presented as consensus.

**Unique insights worth noting.** Two unique findings changed the artifact more than any agreement did. Claude Opus 5's discovery that the constraining deposit contains no implementation of the kernel anywhere is the reason the draft's lineage section carries an explicit prohibition against citing SHVVP's suite counts as enforcement engineering; without that audit, the draft would plausibly have inherited a category error. Claude's second contribution, encoding known impossibilities as passing tests, is now a structural feature of the test suite: the colluding-witness test asserts that the gate allows, so that any future claim of detection requires deleting a test, which is a visible act. GLM 5.2's honest-quorum problem is the third: it names the boundary at which the architecture stops, and it is the only finding in the council that no amount of specification work can move.

**Recommendations.** Treat the two HALT verdicts as unresolved, not as procedural noise: the draft should remain DRAFT and uncarried until a second independent implementation reproduces the frozen vectors, a cross-session monotonicity root is named, the canonicalization fork is closed, and the diagnostic-versus-concealment tension is resolved. Where seats disagreed, prefer publishing both positions with the producer's choice marked as a choice, since the disagreements here track genuine design forks rather than errors. Do not let the six-schema constraint be read as a claim that six is the right decomposition; three seats proposed different sets and the loss of a separate contract schema is real. Finally, resist any temptation to describe the council as approving anything: two seats halted, two approved conditionally, and none of the conditions has been discharged.

## History you are checking
V28 (repair29) kept the streak broken -- correctly, for the FOURTH consecutive round on the X7 licensed
re-widen class. Three byte-authoritative seats recomputed MANIFEST 861700b6 and matched their sealed
challenge+attestation: GPT-5.6 (HALT, 2 BLOCKER / 3 MAJOR), GLM-5.2 (HALT, 1 BLOCKER / 2 MAJOR / 1 INFO),
Kimi K3 (0 BLOCKER, 14 MAJOR under ITS OWN fail-closed-is-MAJOR criterion -- recorded as such, neither a HALT
nor an all-clear). Both pass-29 fixes were incomplete ONE LEVEL DEEPER, which is the whole point of this drill:
  (a) the X7 breadth bound was BOTH fail-open AND over-strict. A runtime-REJECTED amendment with a fabricated
      marker audited clean; a forged wide "held" seed inflated the STREAM-DERIVED held envelope; and the gate's
      OWN honest degraded-first recovery was flagged X7 (a V27 over-strict regression). The stream-derived
      "demonstrably held" envelope was itself forgeable and wrong for honest recovery.
  (b) the kernel abort masked WitnessHealthy's clock-INDEPENDENT determinate FALSEs on a FIRST-clock fault,
      re-read a mutable registry after a failing witness evaluator (masking a TargetAllowed FALSE), and an
      epoch-0 fallback manufactured a time-dependent ContractMatch FALSE.
The ROOT, stated plainly: an offline checker CANNOT soundly adjudicate a licensed re-widen from the record
stream alone -- every marker field is unauthenticated offline and the reference `verify` is CONTENT-BLIND
(it validates a signature status string, not the payload). Four rounds of moving the lever (field read ->
derived -> dual-field -> walk-up -> forged-seed / rejected-amendment) is architectural, not a patchable bug.

## What pass-30 does (Project Lead decision: "do B" -- Strategy B: divergence detection vs AUTHENTICATED runtime truth)
The checker STOPS trusting stream-derived authority and anchors to the runtime's AUTHENTICATED grant ledger,
exported by `grants_from_state(gate)` and passed as `check_authority_history(records, grants=...)`:
  - WITHOUT a usable grant (none / empty ledger / wrong session), EVERY marker-licensed re-widen FAILS CLOSED
    to X7. This is the enforceable half of B and it is airtight offline.
  - WITH the authenticated grant, a re-widen is certified ONLY if it matches on correction_digest + landing
    epoch AND stays within the restored authority; beyond the restored set (a wider effect or target) is X7
    EVEN WITH the grant. The marker only SIGNALS a claim; the AUTHORITATIVE landing + breadth come from the grant.
  - the kernel abort recovers WitnessHealthy's OWN determinate FALSE (e.g. an inverted lease) even when the
    first clock read raises, only from immutable per-invocation captures -- never a re-read registry, never a
    synthetic clock for expiry.
  - authorized_issuance_bound is a POINT-IN-TIME linearization under the LOAD-BEARING commit lock (True is not
    durable past the call); a BaseException-raising injected dependency (clock, verifier) now FAILS CLOSED at
    the authorize boundary AND in abort recovery (KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit still propagate); the X5/X6
    descendant-closure and lineage checkers were made total and bound by G11; G13 INDEPENDENTLY counts the
    counterexample corpus rather than trusting its self-report; the current REPAIR_STATUS section is selected
    by highest pass number, not physical position.

## HEADLINE ATTACK SURFACE FOR THIS ROUND: THE GRANT CHANNEL
B relocates trust to the grant export. Attack it: (1) can `grants` be fed to `check_authority_history`
WITHOUT genuine runtime access -- i.e. is the export forgeable by a caller, and does anything downstream trust
a fabricated grants dict? (2) is unanchored -> fail-closed enforced on EVERY re-widen shape (health-only bump,
same-epoch, higher-epoch, multi-session, replayed marker)? (3) does ANY path still trust a stream-derived
authority snapshot? (4) ATTACK THE VERIFICATION CODE ITSELF: a probe that stays green while its property is
false, a CE that cannot fail, a mutation axis that does not bite, a claim registered but not covered, the G13
independent count spoofable, the grant-anchor / unanchored / breadth probes vacuous.

DISCLOSED RESIDUALS (not bugs -- confirm or break them). (1) A caller who FABRICATES the grants dict spoofs
the anchored half: trust relocates from the unauthenticated marker to the grant-export's provenance, and the
content-blind reference cannot distinguish an authentic export from a forged one. The enforceable half
(unanchored -> fail closed) is airtight; the conditional half (anchored -> divergence) is sound GIVEN an
authentic export. (2) The grant's restored set equals the full contract ceiling by construction, so the grant
breadth conjunct is redundant with an independent contract-ceiling check (dropping the conjunct still flags a
beyond-breadth re-widen) -- defense-in-depth retained deliberately and referred to a fresh seat as a design
decision. No effect bypass has been demonstrated any round; the BLOCKERs are checker/kernel soundness failures
with terminal-deny mitigation, not capability escalation. The attestation is a PACKET-SAMPLE DIGEST, not an
execution proof; certification rests on your INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION on these canonical bytes. Convergence is
ZERO and a fresh-vendor rotation is owed. Do not approve it.

    is formally confirmed across the entire model space
  - All 173 counterexamples remain GREEN, confirming the gate blocks
    known escalation paths

The open decisions are properly documented in the decision register and
do not introduce any known vulnerability or bypass. They are blockers
for publication readiness, but not for the defensive claim itself.

5. VERDICT
================================================================================
VERDICT: CONDITIONAL

The BSSG v0.1 gate mechanism is verified as capability-bounding under
the tested parameter space. The defensive claim holds. However, the
package cannot be carried to publication status while 12 open design
decisions remain unresolved in the decision register (G10 WARN).

6. UNBLOCK CONDITIONS
================================================================================
To move from CONDITIONAL to CARRY, the following must be satisfied:

  [UC-1]  Resolve OD-1: Finalize witness receipt serialization format
  [UC-2]  Resolve OD-2: Set lineage record depth limits with rationale
  [UC-3]  Resolve OD-3: Select correction event encoding and document

  [UC-10] Resolve OD-10: Define gate attestation rotation procedure
  [UC-11] Resolve OD-11: Update reference registry with current citations
  [UC-12] Resolve OD-12: Justify healthy ceiling threshold or recalibrate

Additionally, upon resolution of all OD items:
  [UC-13] Re-run full test suite (345 tests, 173 CEs, model check)
  [UC-14] Update decision register to CLOSED for all 12 ODs
  [UC-15] Regenerate SHA256SUMS and MANIFEST
  [UC-16] Obtain second-seat audit confirmation

7. AUDITOR NOTES
================================================================================
- No FAIL gates detected. The sole WARN (G10) is administrative, not
  structural.
- The model check provides strong evidence for the capability-bounding
  claim within the verified parameter space.
- The counterexample corpus is comprehensive (173 paths) and independently
  verifiable.
- The package is self-consistent and DRAFT-quality. It is suitable for
  internal review and further development, but not for publication or
  operational deployment until unblock conditions are met.

## Section 3 — Findings (eight-element format)

### GLM-F1 — MAJOR — CE169 regression test is non-load-bearing; the headline CLASS A fix is not validated by its dedicated counterexample

1. **ID:** GLM-F1
2. **Location:** `bssg_counterexamples.py` CE169 (lines 2461–2495); fix site `bssg_gate.py` lines 1719–1790 (`_contract_ceiling_pending` + ALLOW-only write).
3. **Claim/observation:** The shipped CE169 uses a **HEALTHY** witness for the C2 DELETE request. With a HEALTHY witness, C2's full ceiling `{READ,WRITE,DELETE}` is a **widening** over the established C1 ceiling `{READ,WRITE}`, so `_apply_narrowing` returns `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING` (bssg_gate.py:1712–1718) and the request returns at line 1714 **BEFORE** `_contract_ceiling_pending` is ever set (line 1731). The session is terminalized by the widening check, not by the effect-bypass path. Consequently the ALLOW-only `contract_ceiling` write fix (lines 1777–1790) is **never reached** in the CE169 scenario — there is no pending flag to write or skip. CE169 would pass GREEN **even if the V30 ALLOW-only fix were reverted**, because the widening check independently blocks the HEALTHY scenario before the fix's code path executes. The actual CLASS A attack vector (per REPAIR_STATUS §"CONVERGENCE EVENT 2" and the brief) used a **DEGRADED** C2 request: the degraded ceiling `{READ}` is a subset of `{READ,WRITE}`, narrowing PASSES, the pending flag IS set, and the request is then DENIED on `E-EFFECT-ABOVE-CEILING`. I reproduced this DEGRADED vector and confirmed the fix blocks it (DELETE never enters `contract_ceiling`), but **no CE in the corpus exercises the degraded vector** — the very scenario the fix was written for.
4. **Severity:** MAJOR (not BLOCKER, because the fix itself is sound — independently proven by `bssg_model_check.py` BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO, which DOES drive the degraded op `(A,C2,DELETE,DEGRADED)` and FAILs when the fix is reverted; see falsifier).
5. **Evidence:** Probe `/home/user/workspace/probe_classA_deep.py`, verbatim output:
   ```
   C2 DELETE (HEALTHY witness): DENY_FALSE reasons= ['E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING', 'E-FALSE-CONTRACTMATCH', ...]
     pending after: None
     terminal? True E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING
     --> CE169's HEALTHY-witness C2 DELETE TERMINALIZES via widening; pending NEVER set.
     --> The ALLOW-only write fix is NOT exercised by the shipped CE169.
   === ORIGINAL DEGRADED-poison attack (the real CLASS A vector) ===
   C2 DELETE (DEGRADED witness): DENY_FALSE reasons= ['E-EFFECT-ABOVE-CEILING', 'E-FALSE-TARGETALLOWED']
     pending after DENIED: ('sess-0001', {…C2 body with DELETE…})   <- pending IS set
     terminal? False
     cc (should be unchanged, no DELETE): ['READ', 'WRITE']
   post-lift retry C2 DELETE (DEGRADED): DENY_FALSE reasons= ['E-EFFECT-ABOVE-CEILING', ...]
     DEGRADE-POISON LEAK (DELETE in contract_ceiling): False
   ```
6. **Required repair:** Re-author CE169 to drive the **degraded** C2 request (the actual vector): establish under C1 HEALTHY, then a DENIED degraded C2 DELETE (sets the pending flag), then terminalize+lift, then retry — assert `DELETE` never enters `contract_ceiling` and the retry is denied. The current HEALTHY-witness construction must be replaced or supplemented; as written it is a non-discriminating regression test.
7. **Scale tag:** checker (regression-test coverage of a gate fix).
8. **Falsifier (EXECUTED — empirical proof):** I made a temporary copy of `bssg_gate.py` (`/home/user/workspace/bssg_gate_MUTATED.py`), reverted the ALLOW-only write back to the post-`_apply_narrowing` site (so a DENIED degraded request CAN poison `contract_ceiling`) and neutralized the ALLOW-path write, swapped it into the audit directory, and re-ran both suites. **CE169 stays GREEN; the model check FAILs.** Mutation script: `/home/user/workspace/mutate_gate.py`. Verbatim outputs (`/home/user/workspace/falsifier_output.txt`):

   ```

The original gate was restored after the run and re-verified by `diff` (no residue).

### GLM-F2 — MINOR — BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO target-scope predicate is correct in form but vacuously exercised; K=5 finds no new violation

1. **ID:** GLM-F2
2. **Location:** `bssg_model_check.py` lines 321–358 (alphabet `_OPS` at 323–324, target-scope predicate at 353).
3. **Claim/observation:** The 5-op alphabet is `{(A,C1,READ,HEALTHY),(A,C1,WRITE,DEGRADED),(A,C2,DELETE,HEALTHY),(A,C2,DELETE,DEGRADED),(L,)}`. Every request in the alphabet uses the fixture's default target scope `https://db.example.internal/records/`, which is the sole element of `_GRANTED_TARGETS`. No schedule op ever introduces a target outside `_GRANTED_TARGETS`, so the predicate `not _allowed_tgts.issubset(_GRANTED_TARGETS)` (line 353) is **never falsified** — it cannot detect a target-introduction regression. The predicate is correctly written but vacuously tested. Separately, I extended the enumeration to **K=5** (3905 schedules, 1473 allows) and found **no new violation**; K=4 is sufficient for this alphabet.
4. **Severity:** MINOR.
5. **Evidence:** Probe `/home/user/workspace/probe_focus.py` PROBE 5:
   ```
   K=4: schedules=780 allows=268 violation=None
   K=5: schedules=3905 allows=1473 violation=None
   ```
6. **Required repair:** Add an op to `_OPS` that requests a target scope outside `_GRANTED_TARGETS` (e.g., a second registered contract with a distinct `allowed_target_scopes`) so the target-scope predicate is actually exercised, or explicitly document that target-introduction closure is out of the model-check scope.
7. **Scale tag:** checker.

### GLM-F4 — INFO — `contract_ceiling_pending` is a single instance attribute that leaks across requests after a DENIED degraded request (sound, but fragile)

1. **ID:** GLM-F4
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` lines 1731–1790 (set at 1733, consumed/cleared at 1783–1790).
3. **Claim/observation:** `_contract_ceiling_pending` is a single instance attribute, not per-session. After a DENIED degraded C2 request sets `pending=(sess, bodyC2)`, the flag **persists** on the gate instance into the next request (probe confirms `pending after DENIED: ('sess-0001', {…C2 body…})`). The fix relies on the NEXT ALLOW request overwriting it with its own `(sess, body)` before the write at line 1787. This is **sound**: any ALLOW request has `ContractMatch=TRUE` ⇒ `contract_body ≠ None` (bssg_gate.py:1117) and `WitnessHealthy=TRUE` ⇒ `health ≠ None`, so it always sets its own pending at line 1733, overwriting any stale value; and the re-establish path (line 1909) reads `contract_ceiling` (written only on ALLOW), never the pending flag. I attempted cross-session and intervening-abort stale-pending leaks and found none. But the design is fragile: a single shared instance attribute carrying a contract body across request boundaries is one refactor away from a leak, and it is the kind of state-leak that has historically become the next round's vector.
4. **Severity:** INFO.
5. **Evidence:** Probe `/home/user/workspace/probe_classA_deep.py`:

   ```

7. **Scale tag:** gate.
8. **Falsifier:** Construct an ALLOW request that reaches the write at line 1787 WITHOUT having set its own pending at line 1733 — impossible by the kernel (ALLOW ⇒ ContractMatch TRUE ⇒ contract_body ≠ None ⇒ the `if contract_body is not None:` block at 1704 is entered ⇒ if `health is not None` the pending is set at 1733; and ALLOW ⇒ WitnessHealthy TRUE ⇒ health ≠ None). ### Positive confirmations (closed V30 classes, re-derived on canonical bytes)

- **CLASS A closure (fix sound):** The ALLOW-only `contract_ceiling` write (bssg_gate.py:1777–1790) is sound — the DEGRADED poison vector is blocked (DELETE never enters `contract_ceiling`; post-lift retry denied with `E-EFFECT-ABOVE-CEILING`), and the stale-pending variant is structurally blocked (GLM-F4). The dedicated CE169 is weak (GLM-F1); the model check is the load-bearing guard (empirically proven by the GLM-F1 falsifier).
- **CLASS B (K=4):** Sufficient; K=5 finds no new violation. Target-scope predicate correct in form but vacuously exercised (GLM-F2). The printed claim text accurately states the bound ("len<=4, 5-op alphabet… no ALLOW authorizes an effect or target outside the established healthy ceiling").
- **CLASS C:** unarmed same-epoch ceiling CHANGE = X7; armed same-epoch ceiling CHANGE = X7 (grant-independent); armed same-epoch EQUAL = X7U; CE162 honest degraded-first recovery = X7U — all confirmed (PROBE 3). The `ep == prev_ep` change-check (bssg_gate.py:2951–2956) correctly fires before the armed-forward X7U branch (2964).
- **CLASS D:** present non-dict snapshot (list/bool/float/empty_str) = X7 (type-tamper); absent snapshot = skip (clean) — confirmed across all tested shapes (PROBE 4).
- **CLASS E:** missing `licensed_epoch`, `spec_version`, `gate_version`, `adjudicators_verified<2`, bool `licensed_epoch`, empty `spec_version` all fail `_is_acceptance_marker` → marker does not arm → widening is unlicensed X7 (PROBE 4).

- **CLASS F (dead code/comments):** No stale `_contract_ceiling_pending`/X7U comments found inconsistent with the code; the docstrings at 1719–1730 and 1777–1790 match the implementation.

- **Open decisions:** `OPEN_DECISIONS.md` lists exactly 12 (OD-1..OD-12), all marked UNRESOLVED; verifier G10 WARNs. No open decision is claimed resolved. Consistent with the brief.

### Focus 6 — The 31-pass pattern: is there a 32nd instance in repair33?

**Yes — in the verification layer.** The recurring meta-defect is "the producer's own fix ships incomplete one level deeper." In repair33 the **fix** (ALLOW-only `contract_ceiling` write) is itself sound (model-checked, and the GLM-F1 falsifier proves the model check catches a revert). But the fix's **dedicated regression test** (CE169) ships incomplete one level deeper: it tests a HEALTHY-witness scenario that the widening check blocks independently of the fix, so it does not bind the fix it claims to close (GLM-F1). This is the 32nd instance of the pattern, displaced one layer from the fix into its verification — less severe than prior instances (the model check backstops it), but the same structural shape: the closure claim (`CE169 … CLOSED`) is not load-bearing for the closure it asserts.

---

## Section 4 — Final Verdict

**Verdict: PASS (no blocker) — with reservations.**

Counts by severity: **0 BLOCKER / 1 MAJOR / 2 MINOR / 3 INFO**.

- GLM-F1 MAJOR — CE169 non-load-bearing regression test for the headline CLASS A BLOCKER (mitigated: the model check is the load-bearing guard, empirically proven by the executed falsifier).
- GLM-F2 MINOR — BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO target-scope predicate vacuously exercised.
- GLM-F3 MINOR — `REPAIR_STATUS.md` MANIFEST (`eb8fe324`) diverges from the recomputed dispatch MANIFEST (`16965ab7…`).
- GLM-F4 INFO — `contract_ceiling_pending` instance-attribute state-leak (sound, fragile).
- GLM-F5 INFO — withdrawal sound under Axiom 5; CE163 closed (positive).
- GLM-F6 INFO — BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO sufficient for the poison class but not complete; SHVVP §0.3 analogy sound in form, disanalogous in motive.

**Per the mechanical rule (PASS = no blocker; HALT-WITH-FINDINGS = ≥1 blocker), the verdict is PASS.** I record this honestly and without smoothing: the gate itself ships no soundness defect — every V30 fix (CLASS A–E) is independently reproduced and sound on the canonical bytes, the withdrawal is faithful to Axiom 5, and the model check guards the CLASS A fix that CE169 fails to. There is no runtime effect bypass, no over/under-withdrawal, no X7/X7U misclassification.

**Disagreement with the producer, stated plainly:**
1. The producer's `REPAIR_STATUS.md` presents CLASS A as "CLOSED" via CE169. **I disagree that CE169 closes CLASS A** — CE169 does not exercise the fix (GLM-F1), and the executed falsifier proves CE169 stays GREEN on the reverted/vulnerable gate. CLASS A is closed only by the BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO model check, a different artifact (which FAILs on the revert). The closure credit belongs to the model check, not CE169.
2. `REPAIR_STATUS.md` line 48 records repair33 as `MANIFEST eb8fe324`, which does not match the packet I received and recomputed (`16965ab7…`). I cannot reconcile this; the producer must.
3. This is **not a convergence round.** A MAJOR finding (non-load-bearing regression test for the headline BLOCKER) means repair33 is not clean. Convergence requires two consecutive clean rounds with a seat rotated in fresh; this round has a MAJOR finding, so the program has not converged.
4. The "31-pass pattern" continues: the 32nd instance is present, displaced into the verification layer (CE169). The producer should not represent repair33 as "all 8 classes closed" without the CE169 caveat.

The packet remains **DRAFT / NOT CARRIED / NOT PUBLICATION-READY.** No effectiveness claim is made or evaluated.

def static_instance(src_path, dst_path, weight, rename=None):
    """Materialise a static weight instance from a variable font."""
    if os.path.exists(dst_path):
        return True
    try:
        from fontTools import ttLib
        from fontTools.varLib import instancer
        font = ttLib.TTFont(src_path)
        if "fvar" not in font:
            return False
        axes = {a.axisTag: a for a in font["fvar"].axes}
        loc = {}
        if "wght" in axes:
            loc["wght"] = weight
        if "opsz" in axes:
            loc["opsz"] = 11
        inst = instancer.instantiateVariableFont(font, loc)
        if rename:
            # ReportLab caches font faces by the internal PostScript name, so a
            # bold instance carrying the regular name would silently reuse the
            # regular metrics. Rename the instance to keep the faces distinct.
            for rec in inst["name"].names:
                if rec.nameID in (1, 3, 4, 6, 16, 17):
                    inst["name"].setName(rename, rec.nameID, rec.platformID,
                                         rec.platEncID, rec.langID)
        inst.save(dst_path)
        return True
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
        print("WARN instance", dst_path, exc)
        return False


ok = {}
for name, url in FONTS.items():
    path = os.path.join(FONT_DIR, name + ".ttf")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        try:
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, path)
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
            print("WARN download", name, exc)
    use = path
    if name in ("SerifBody", "SansBody", "MonoBody"):
        reg = os.path.join(FONT_DIR, name + "-400.ttf")
        if static_instance(path, reg, 400):
            use = reg
        bold_name = name.replace("Body", "Bold")
        bold_path = os.path.join(FONT_DIR, name + "-700.ttf")
        if static_instance(path, bold_path, 700, rename=bold_name + "SHVVP"):
            try:
                pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont(bold_name, bold_path))
                ok[bold_name] = True
            except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
                print("WARN register", bold_name, exc)
    try:
        pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont(name, use))
        ok[name] = True
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
        print("WARN register", name, exc)
        ok[name] = False

    return (text.replace("&", "&amp;").replace("<", "&lt;").replace(">", "&gt;"))


LINK_RE = re.compile(r"\[([^\]\[]+)\]\(([^()\s]+)\)")
SHOW_URLS = {"on": False}   # set while rendering the Sources section


def inline(text, link_color=INK):
    """Convert inline Markdown to ReportLab mini-HTML. Monochrome links, underlined."""
    out = esc(text)
    holders = []

    def hold(html):
        holders.append(html)
        return "\x00%d\x00" % (len(holders) - 1)

    def link_sub(m):
        label, url = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        label = _emphasis(label)
        href = url.replace("&amp;", "&")
        if SHOW_URLS["on"]:
            return hold('<a href="%s"><u>%s</u></a> <font face="%s" size="7.2">'
                        '<a href="%s"><u>%s</u></a></font>'
                        % (href, label, MONO, href, esc(href)))
        return hold('<a href="%s"><u>%s</u></a>' % (href, label))

    out = LINK_RE.sub(link_sub, out)
    out = re.sub(r"`([^`]+)`", lambda m: hold('<font face="%s" size="8.4">%s</font>'
                                             % (MONO, m.group(1))), out)
    out = _emphasis(out)
    for i, html in enumerate(holders):
        out = out.replace("\x00%d\x00" % i, html)
    return out


def _emphasis(text):
    text = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]+)\*\*", lambda m: "<b>%s</b>" % m.group(1), text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?<!\*)\*([^*]+)\*(?!\*)", lambda m: "<i>%s</i>" % m.group(1), text)
    return text


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- table build
def col_widths(rows, total, font, size):
    """Proportional widths with a per-column floor equal to the longest word,
    which prevents mid-word wrapping in narrow columns."""
    ncol = len(rows[0])
    weights, minima = [], []
    for c in range(ncol):
        cells = [re.sub(r"[*`\[\]()]|https?://\S+", " ", r[c]) for r in rows]
        lens = [len(r[c]) for r in rows]
        weights.append(max(6.0, sum(lens) / len(lens) * 0.65 + max(lens) * 0.35))
        words = [w for cell in cells for w in cell.split()] or [""]
        longest = max(words, key=len)
        minima.append(pdfmetrics.stringWidth(longest, font, size) + 7.5)
    if sum(minima) > total:
        scale = total / sum(minima)
        minima = [m * scale for m in minima]
    slack = total - sum(minima)
    wsum = sum(weights)
    widths = [minima[c] + slack * weights[c] / wsum for c in range(ncol)]
    scale = total / sum(widths)
    return [w * scale for w in widths]


def make_table(rows):
    ncol = len(rows[0])
    small = ncol >= 6
    cs, hs = (s_tc_small, s_th_small) if small else (s_tc, s_th)
    data = [[Paragraph(inline(cell), hs if r == 0 else cs) for cell in row]
            for r, row in enumerate(rows)]
    widths = col_widths(rows, FRAME_W, cs.fontName, cs.fontSize)
    tbl = Table(data, colWidths=widths, repeatRows=1, hAlign="LEFT")
    style = [
        ("GRID", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 0.35, RULE),
        ("BACKGROUND", (0, 0), (-1, 0), HDR_FILL),
        ("VALIGN", (0, 0), (-1, -1), "TOP"),
        ("LEFTPADDING", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 3.2),
        ("RIGHTPADDING", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 3.2),
        ("TOPPADDING", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 2.6),
        ("BOTTOMPADDING", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 2.6),
        ("LINEBELOW", (0, 0), (-1, 0), 0.7, INK),
    ]
    for r in range(2, len(rows), 2):
        style.append(("BACKGROUND", (0, r), (-1, r), ZEBRA))
    tbl.setStyle(TableStyle(style))
    return tbl


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parse markdown
def parse(md):
    """Yield flowables from the canonical Markdown."""
    story = []
    lines = md.split("\n")
    i = 0
    n = len(lines)
    front = True
    while i < n:
        line = lines[i]
        stripped = line.strip()

        if not stripped:
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped == "---":
            story.append(Spacer(1, 3))
            story.append(HRFlowable(width="100%", thickness=0.5, color=RULE,
                                    spaceBefore=2, spaceAfter=7))
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("# "):
            story.append(Paragraph(inline(stripped[2:]), s_title))
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("### "):
            story.append(Paragraph(inline(stripped[4:]), s_h2))
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("## "):
            SHOW_URLS["on"] = stripped[3:].strip().startswith("14. Sources")
            story.append(Paragraph(inline(stripped[3:]), s_h1))
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("!["):
            m = re.match(r"!\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+)\)", stripped)
            if m:
                alt, path = m.group(1), m.group(2)
                path = os.path.join(HERE, path.lstrip("./"))
                if os.path.exists(path):
                    from reportlab.lib.utils import ImageReader
                    iw, ih = ImageReader(path).getSize()
                    w = FRAME_W
                    h = w * ih / iw
                    story.append(KeepTogether([Image(path, width=w, height=h),
                                               Paragraph(esc(alt), s_caption)]))
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("|"):
            rows = []
            while i < n and lines[i].strip().startswith("|"):
                raw = lines[i].strip()
                cells = [c.strip() for c in raw.strip("|").split("|")]
                if not re.fullmatch(r"[:\-\s|]+", raw.strip("|")):
                    rows.append(cells)
                i += 1
            width = max(len(r) for r in rows)
            rows = [r + [""] * (width - len(r)) for r in rows]
            story.append(Spacer(1, 2))
            story.append(make_table(rows))
            story.append(Spacer(1, 8))
            continue

        if re.match(r"^[-*]\s+", stripped) or re.match(r"^\d+\.\s+", stripped):
            items = []
            ordered = bool(re.match(r"^\d+\.\s+", stripped))
            while i < n:
                cur = lines[i].strip()
                if re.match(r"^[-*]\s+", cur):
                    text = re.sub(r"^[-*]\s+", "", cur)
                elif re.match(r"^\d+\.\s+", cur):
                    text = re.sub(r"^\d+\.\s+", "", cur)
                else:
                    break
                i += 1
                while i < n and lines[i].strip() and not re.match(
                        r"^([-*]\s+|\d+\.\s+|\||#|!\[|---)", lines[i].strip()):
                    text += " " + lines[i].strip()
                    i += 1
                kw = {"leftIndent": 15}
                if ordered:
                    kw["value"] = len(items) + 1
                items.append(ListItem(Paragraph(inline(text), s_bullet), **kw))
            story.append(ListFlowable(
                items, bulletType="1" if ordered else "bullet",
                bulletFontName=SANS, bulletFontSize=8.6,
                start="1" if ordered else "circle",
                leftIndent=15, bulletDedent=10, spaceBefore=1, spaceAfter=5))
            continue

        # paragraph
        buf = [stripped]
        i += 1
        while i < n and lines[i].strip() and not re.match(
                r"^(#|\||!\[|---|[-*]\s+|\d+\.\s+)", lines[i].strip()):
            buf.append(lines[i].strip())
            i += 1
        text = " ".join(buf)
        style = s_body
        if front:
            if text.startswith("**A preregistered"):
                style = s_sub
            elif text.startswith("Bilal Syed Arfeen."):
                style = s_author
                front = False
        if text.startswith("**End of frozen contract"):
            style = s_close
        story.append(Paragraph(inline(text), style))
    return story


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- page furniture
def footer(canvas, doc):
    canvas.saveState()
    canvas.setStrokeColor(RULE)
    canvas.setLineWidth(0.4)
    canvas.line(LM, BM - 16, PAGE_W - RM, BM - 16)
    canvas.setFont(SANS, 7.4)
    canvas.setFillColor(MUTED)
    canvas.drawString(LM, BM - 27,
                      "SHVVP v0.5  |  FROZEN preregistration  |  NOT DEPOSITED, "
                      "NOT BINDING pending a fresh two-family carrying audit")
    canvas.drawRightString(PAGE_W - RM, BM - 27, "Page %d" % canvas.getPageNumber())
    canvas.restoreState()


def build():
    md = open(SRC, encoding="utf-8").read()
    doc = BaseDocTemplate(
        OUT, pagesize=letter, leftMargin=LM, rightMargin=RM,
        topMargin=TM, bottomMargin=BM,
        title=TITLE, author=AUTHOR, subject=SUBJECT, keywords=KEYWORDS,
        creator="Perplexity Computer", producer="ReportLab")
    frame = Frame(LM, BM, FRAME_W, PAGE_H - TM - BM, id="body",
                  leftPadding=0, rightPadding=0, topPadding=0, bottomPadding=0)
    doc.addPageTemplates([PageTemplate(id="all", frames=[frame], onPage=footer)])
    story = parse(md)
    doc.build(story)
    print("built", OUT)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    build()

## R0295 · build_shvvp_v0_7_pdf.sh

- section: V. BSSG & SHVVP Protocols
- source_file: build_shvvp_v0_7_pdf.sh
- source_format: sh
- merged_variants: 1 (build_shvvp_v0_6_pdf.sh)
- text_sha256: 12758daff48657afaed437b8357f9327de4613c03b7ef2c993a6468ed38e692c

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Render SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_7_source.md to the monochrome release flagship
# SHVVP_v0_7_flagship.pdf via pandoc -> pdflatex.
#
# Font note: the frozen flagship profile is Latin Modern (LMRoman/LMMono). Where
# lmodern.sty is unavailable in the build host, this script falls back to Computer
# Modern via T1 fontenc, the same Latin Modern family; the substitution is stated
# rather than implied and does not affect the finding F-P5-3 remedy, which concerns
# table legibility, not font identity. Table text is set at \footnotesize with long
# identifier hyphenation so every Section 8.2 cell renders within the text block.
set -euo pipefail
SRC="${1:-SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_7_source.md}"
OUT="${2:-SHVVP_v0_7_flagship.pdf}"
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
cp "$SRC" "$WORK/src.md"
# carry the one referenced raster if present alongside the source
[ -f shvvp-v0-5-phase-b-power.png ] && cp shvvp-v0-5-phase-b-power.png "$WORK/" || true
cd "$WORK"

pandoc src.md -s -o v06.tex \
  --pdf-engine=pdflatex --toc --number-sections \
  -V documentclass=article -V geometry:margin=1in -V fontsize=11pt \
  -V colorlinks=true -V linkcolor=black -V urlcolor=black -V toccolor=black \
  -V title="Structural Honesty Validation Protocol (SHVVP) v0.7" \
  -V author="Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)" -V date="2026-07-26"

# lmodern fallback: drop the package if the host lacks it.
if ! kpsewhich lmodern.sty >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sed -i '/^\\usepackage{lmodern}$/d' v06.tex
fi
# Computer Modern is non-scalable here, so disable microtype font expansion.
sed -i 's|^  \\usepackage\[\]{microtype}$|  \\usepackage[]{microtype}\n  \\microtypesetup{expansion=false}|' v06.tex
# Bare DOI identifiers in body text are single non-breakable tokens under the
# Computer Modern fallback; insert zero-width break opportunities. This matches the
# displayed "doi:10.5281/zenodo.N" text only, never the href URL argument
# (which is "doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.N", a different prefix).
sed -i 's#\(doi:10\.5281/\)#\1\\allowbreak{}#g' v06.tex
sed -i 's#\(doi:10\.5281/\\allowbreak{}zenodo\.\)#\1\\allowbreak{}#g' v06.tex
# Legible tables: small font, break long identifiers, tolerate tight lines.
python3 - <<'PY'
t=open("v06.tex").read()
inj=(r"\usepackage{etoolbox}"+"\n"
     r"\AtBeginEnvironment{longtable}{\footnotesize}"+"\n"
     r"\setlength{\emergencystretch}{3em}"+"\n"
     r"\IfFileExists{hyphenat.sty}{\usepackage[htt]{hyphenat}}{}"+"\n")
t=t.replace(r"\begin{document}", inj+r"\begin{document}",1)
open("v06.tex","w").write(t)
PY

pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error v06.tex >/dev/null
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error v06.tex >/dev/null
qpdf --check v06.pdf >/dev/null && echo "qpdf: structurally OK"
cp v06.pdf "$OLDPWD/$OUT"
cd "$OLDPWD"
echo "wrote $OUT"
pdfinfo "$OUT" | grep -i pages

# SHVVP v0.8 -- Carrying Record and Provenance (deposit)

Artifact: Structural Honesty Validation Protocol (SHVVP) v0.8, frozen preregistration
instrument. Freeze date: 2026-07-25 (deposit-ready; DOI assigned at deposit).

Frozen manifest digest (`MANIFEST_SHA256`):
`f82f9579d35b64e11e6f380e5af1b97e0da5fb1bc0fb046e71d93afc5039151c`

## What this record attests

v0.8 was CARRIED by two executing non-producer families of different vendors. Each
loaded and ran the shipped route gate, recomputed the manifest digest, passed the
shipped adversarial suite (35 checks, 0 failures) together with its own fresh forgeries
against the three frozen trust roots, and returned a sealed execution-challenge hash
`sha256(MANIFEST_SHA256 + per-seat nonce)` that matched a value the producer computed
with a tool ONLY AFTER the seat had produced it. A large language model cannot compute a SHA-256
in its head, so a matching challenge hash shows the responder EXECUTED code (it did not
merely recall a value). It does not, by itself, establish which model executed, seat
independence, or that the gate itself ran; those rest on the per-seat harness/endpoint
provenance and on the verbatim gate outputs below, which ARE checkable against the code
(run seat_evidence/verify_seat_evidence.py). Kimi additionally returned six fresh-forgery
exception strings that match the shipped gate's control flow byte-for-byte, which cannot
be produced without executing the real module; that is the strong, checkable evidence of
gate execution.

| Seat | Vendor family | Harness | Recomputed digest | Challenge hash (matched) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi | Moonshot AI | vendor-direct on Moonshot's own site (Linux, Python 3.11) | f82f9579...9151c | 8742263b6e481ac0b45a5f26d17a67df964a42ed89c70f3f5af9cd7a350fccc3 |
| Qwen | Alibaba | operator's own hardware + operator-loaded weights, local Python kernel | f82f9579...9151c | 6b2add58c0f83390336b3a2105c713914db7384293766976e0e4671ec17e8644 |

Kimi executed vendor-direct on its own platform. Qwen executed on the operator's own
machine, on weights the operator loaded, through a local native Python runner, giving
substrate-anchored provenance with no intermediary platform and no self-applied label to
trust. Even so, the matched hash by itself shows only that code ran on the operator's
machine; model identity rests on the operator's control of the local deployment, stated
plainly above rather than overclaimed.

## Role quarantine

- Producer of record: Anthropic family (authored the gate, suite, verifier, source).
  EXCLUDED from the carrying pool.
- GPT family: contributed the three-trust-root design; ADVISORY, deliberately not seated.
- Carrying seats: Kimi (Moonshot) and Qwen (Alibaba), two different non-producer,
  non-advisory families, each executing.

## Byte-identity of the carried substance

The executable artifacts prepared for deposit here are byte-identical to the release the two
families executed:

- `shvvp_v0_8_route_gates.py` sha256 f73af0142380462b0e465382cd3f387c0a46be1c71d3f41a97c59c495304e0f6
- `shvvp_v0_8_signed_test_vectors.json` sha256 cb9434176554c12a46820a146c7af214efeb2f26f30f02616aede317f3814926
- `test_shvvp_v0_8_rules.py` sha256 a2a83722515b13acdd83f118c2b4f5f06678bcc9521d6d526a7509dacc80f6c6

`MANIFEST_SHA256` is unchanged. This v0.8 freeze promotes the earlier revision-candidate
wrapper to frozen status and folds one LOW documentation clarification (F-P8-1, amendment
A-8.8); it changes no gate logic, falsifier, threshold, or trust root. The carry
therefore attaches to exactly these bytes prepared for deposit.

## Findings carried

- F-P8-1 (LOW, non-blocking): the Channel-A commitment bundle is resolved by a caller-side
  mapping key that is a third, non-authoritative copy of the identifier; defense-in-depth
  by construction, not a bypass (renamed, aliased, or unresolvable keys fail closed; tests
  C1-C4 and both seats' identifier-confusion attacks confirm it). Documented in A-8.8.

## Reference keys, not production keys

The three authority keys frozen in this instrument are REFERENCE keys, sufficient to fix
and prove the gate's logic (which the two families verified). They bind no live universe,
because no corpus, pilot, or session exists yet: this is a preregistration frozen before
its data. When the validation program actually executes (Phase A onward), the operator
installs the production authority keys held by the real custodians; that changes
`MANIFEST_SHA256` and is a versioned, freshly-carried step at that time. No private key of
any kind is included in this deposit.

## Chronology

Earlier lineage versions (v0.1 through v0.7) carry development-timeline dates that are
self-reported and not externally binding. The only binding freeze date for this record is
the deposit date, 2026-07-25, which the deposit archive timestamps independently.

## Independent re-verification

Anyone can reproduce the carry: run `python3 test_shvvp_v0_8_rules.py` (needs the
`cryptography` package) and `python3 verify_shvvp_v0_8.py`; confirm the manifest digest is
`f82f9579...9151c`; and, for any fresh nonce N, confirm
`sha256(MANIFEST_SHA256 + N)` equals what an executing model returns. The private key
halves were never shipped, so no forgery against the frozen roots is possible.

## Note on the carried gate's internal constant

The carried gate module contains an unused internal constant `RELEASE_STAGE = "rc1"` from
the build lineage. It is not emitted, read, or used in any control path (grep confirms no
reference), and it carries no status meaning. It is left unchanged solely to preserve
byte-identity with the gate the two families executed; altering it would change the gate
bytes and void the carry. The authoritative status is this record and the source Status
line, not that constant.

## Packaging revision

v0.8 (scientific version unchanged), packaging revision corr3: absorbs the executing
publication-readiness re-audit (F-R8-PUB series). Changes are limited to the evidence
verifier (now reproduces all six forgery strings AND parses the raw seat reports to
compare), status-parity wording (deposit-ready, not deposited -- including the source Status paragraph, which read 'deposited here' through corr2 and now reads 'shipped here'), and documentation. No
change to the gate, manifest, trust roots, falsifiers, thresholds, estimands, or decision
rules; the executable bytes remain byte-identical to the carried release.

# Date and status note

The inherited v0.7 source and metadata declare a freeze date of **2026-07-26**. The v0.7 Seat-A audit is dated **2026-07-24**, and this revision was prepared on **2026-07-24**. A successor cannot truthfully claim to have been frozen after a future-dated predecessor while retaining today's date, and this revision does not silently alter the immutable v0.7 bytes.

Accordingly, this deliverable is **v0.8-rc1, a producer revision candidate**, not a frozen release. Before formal dispatch, the producer should:

1. choose a truthful v0.8 freeze date when that date has actually arrived;
2. decide whether the v0.7 future date was an intended future freeze or a metadata error, recording any correction append-only;
3. update the source, README, metadata, build date, dispatch brief, and current-status verifier from `v0.8-rc1` to `v0.8`;
4. rebuild the PDF, receipt, `SHA256SUMS`, release packet, and outer dispatch ZIP from the final immutable bytes;
5. dispatch those final hashes to two independent carrying seats.

# Deposit metadata for SHVVP v0.5

**HOLD STATUS: NOT FOR DEPOSIT YET.** This block is prepared in advance so that deposit is a mechanical step once carrying convergence exists. Deposit is BLOCKED until one GPT-class and one Gemini-class non-producer carrying seat both return PASS, or PASS-WITH-AMENDMENTS with amendments absorbed. Producer, editor and chair attestations do not unblock deposit, and a PASS from a single vendor family does not carry. Versions 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 are HALTED and were never deposited or binding.

---

## 3. Description block for the deposit record

> FROZEN preregistration, version 0.5. This document is an evaluation contract locked before any corpus, pilot, or session exists. It fixes the axioms under test, the labelling schema, the correspondence relations, the conventional baseline the intervention must beat, two Phase-B estimands defined by all five ICH E9(R1) attributes, a fixed unauthorized-effect reduction target of at least 80 percent relative and at least 20 absolute percentage points, a fixed noninferiority margin of 5 absolute percentage points, an exact two-sided 95 percent BCa cluster-bootstrap interval algorithm with predeclared zero-event rules, one total ordered mapping from every reachable state to exactly one of eight Phase B outcome labels with both rules evaluated in the as-allocated and per-protocol populations, a joint power target of 0.80 met at 1,440 confirmatory sessions under a staged simulation of the frozen rule with reported Monte Carlo error, a Phase-A decision table over twelve metrics and eight thresholds with an adjudicator-reliability gate, a Phase-C corpus of 48 private synthetic targets and 864 sessions with all six conjuncts operationalized and a total priority order over five outcome labels in which observed hard failures dominate inconclusive states, frozen route-level DESCRIPTIVE GATES in which every one of the eleven novelty-route components is a pass-or-fail gate computed from mandatory raw evidence counts against a threshold frozen before data, carrying no p-value, no null hypothesis, no confidence bound, no false-discovery-rate control and no claim of statistical significance, generalization or population-level novelty, because the fixed heterogeneous paired design does not support a route-level population model and none is asserted, and a non-amendable hard safety boundary. Versions 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 were each audited by two non-producer carrying seats of different vendor families and all three rounds diverged; version 0.4 received a HALT from its GPT-class carrying seat. All four earlier versions are HALTED and none was ever deposited as binding. Route-level statistical inference, frozen in version 0.4, is WITHDRAWN IN FULL in this version and its withdrawal is recorded in the append-only amendment record. This version supersedes them and records every accepted and rejected finding, and one carrying PASS that did not carry, in an append-only amendment record. No corpus, pilot, session, or result exists at the time of this freeze, and no empirical work is claimed.

## 4. Keywords

preregistration; structural honesty; SHVVP v0.5; evaluation contract; noninferiority margin; co-primary endpoints; estimands; ICH E9(R1); BCa bootstrap; cluster bootstrap; Monte Carlo error; Benjamini-Hochberg; descriptive gates; withdrawn inference; total ordered decision rule; CVE-Bench; XZ Utils CVE-2024-3094; supply-chain provenance; SLSA; in-toto; Sigstore; agentic containment; witness plane; evidence independence

## 5. Files intended for the deposit record

All current-version references below are v0.5. Earlier versions appear only as labelled lineage.

1. `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_5.pdf` (primary rendering, current version)
2. `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_5_source.md` (canonical source, current version)
