4. The normative code: `shvvp_v0_5_route_gates.py`, `shvvp_v0_5_decision_rules.py`, `shvvp_v0_5_power_sim.py`, `shvvp_v0_5_regression_scan.py`, `test_shvvp_v0_5_rules.py`, `power_sim_receipt.json`, `shvvp_v0_5_power_chart.py`, `shvvp-v0-5-phase-b-power.png`
5. `verify_shvvp_v0_5.py`
6. Lineage, labelled HALTED and never deposited as binding: `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_1.md`, `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_1.pdf`, `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_2_source.md`, `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_2.pdf`, `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_3_source.md`, `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_3.pdf`, `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_4_source.md`, `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_4.pdf`
7. The seven carrying-seat verdicts of rounds 1 to 4, which already exist and ship in this packet, and, once they exist, **both v0.5 verdicts**

## 6. Pre-deposit checklist, in order

1. Dispatch `SHVVP_v0_5_AUDIT_DISPATCH_BRIEF.md` together with `SHVVP_v0_5_FOCUSED_DELTA_ADDENDUM.md` to a fresh GPT-class seat and a fresh Gemini-class seat. No cross-talk.
2. Collect both verdicts verbatim and append them to the audit ledger, favourable or not.
3. If both PASS, or both PASS-WITH-AMENDMENTS with amendments absorbed into a further append-only entry, proceed. If either returns HALT, or the seats diverge, do NOT deposit: produce v0.6.
4. Recompute `SHA256SUMS` on the final artifact set and record the deposited hashes in the amendment record.
5. Deposit promptly. A finished but undeposited preregistration provides none of preregistration's benefit ([Nosek et al., PNAS](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1708274114)).
6. Only after deposit: seal the ledgers listed in the contract, run the pre-unblinding calibration re-run of Section 6.5.1 and log it, then run the exploratory pilot under the Section 6.9 prohibitions, then the 1,440-session confirmatory run.

# SHVVP v0.6 deposit metadata (held pending convergence)

This metadata is staged, not acted on. It becomes eligible for deposit only after a
fresh two-family carrying audit converges (a GPT-class and a Gemini-class seat of
different vendor families both returning PASS). Nothing here is binding until then.

## Identity, reconciled (finding F-P5-2)

- **Title:** Structural Honesty Validation Protocol (SHVVP) v0.6
- **Version:** v0.6
- **Freeze date:** 2026-07-25
- **Creator:** Arfeen, Bilal Syed (BayyinahEnterprise)
- **Resource type:** Preprint / working paper (frozen preregistration)
- **License:** CC-BY-4.0
- **Single release flagship:** `SHVVP_v0_6_flagship.pdf`, the pandoc-to-pdflatex
  render of the canonical source, **56 pages**, letter, monochrome. There is one
  flagship for this release; earlier renders belong to earlier versions and are
  carried only as lineage. The page count stated here, in the README and in the
  dispatch brief agree.
- **Canonical source (authoritative):** `SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_6_source.md`.

## Description

A frozen, preregistered evaluation contract for structural-honesty validation:
construct validation on the XZ Utils backdoor, effect control on CVE-Bench, and a
seeded novel-discovery stress test, with all route-level statistical inference
withdrawn and every component reduced to a descriptive gate. v0.6 closes the round
5 blocking finding by binding every evidence record to a frozen pre-results scope
manifest with committed universe cardinalities, so that neither a favorable subset
of a fixed universe nor the omission of an unfavorable committed component can
change a route's descriptive label.

## Version history and status

All five earlier versions (v0.1 through v0.5) are HALTED, were never deposited, and
are not binding. v0.5 diverged under the round 5 audit (GPT-class HALT with finding
F-P5-1, Gemini-class PASS) and is retained only as a historical record. v0.6
carries no verdict and is not deposit-ready until a fresh two-family carrying audit
converges on it.

## Related identifiers (to attach on deposit, not before)

- References the flagship, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21500700.
- References the consolidated reference canon v1.4, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21501912.
- References the evidence-independence companion paper, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21539074.

## Keywords

preregistration, structural honesty, software audit, evaluation contract, XZ Utils,
CVE-Bench, descriptive gate, scope manifest, evidence universe, fail-closed.

## Description

A frozen, preregistered evaluation contract for structural-honesty validation, with
all route-level statistical inference withdrawn and every component reduced to a
descriptive gate. v0.7 closes the round 6 blocking finding by authenticating every
sealed and realized evidence universe through a separate signed commitment channel:
the party that selects the evidence can no longer define the universe against which
it is scored, so neither a favorable subset of a fixed universe nor a self-declared
sealed or realized universe can change a route's descriptive label.

## Version history and status

All six earlier versions (v0.1 through v0.6) are HALTED, were never deposited, and are
not binding. v0.6 diverged under the round 6 audit (GPT-class HALT with findings
F-P6-1 and F-P6-2, Gemini-class PASS on a textual review that did not execute the
gate) and is retained only as a historical record. v0.7 carries no verdict and is not
deposit-ready until a fresh two-family carrying audit converges on it.

# BSSG v0.1 -- Project-Lead Exception Ledger

**Signed by:** Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise), Project Lead
**Date:** 2026-07-30
**Scope:** STILL BLOCKING items in BSSG_v0_1_DECISION_REGISTER.md §6

Under PMD v1.2 §0.4, HIGH-residual items that remain open at convergence require a
project-lead-signed exception ledger entry. This document provides those entries.

---

## GP-R4: No machine-checked antitonicity proof

**Status:** OPEN -- deferred to v0.2.
**Exception rationale:** The reference gate ships a bounded exhaustive antitonicity check
(A2: 729 contract pairs, PASS) and a bounded authority-introduction check (11110 schedules,
K=4, 10-op alphabet, PASS). GLM independently verified K=5 (19607 schedules, no violation).
These are bounded exhaustive enumerations, not unbounded proofs. A TLA+ or equivalent
formal proof is REQUIRED before freeze (spec §26 item 6) but is not required for the
DRAFT / NOT CARRIED status. The artifact's own banner and spec explicitly state this
limitation.
**Risk accepted:** A violation at K>5 or over a richer alphabet would be missed.

## GP-R8: No TLA+ model

**Status:** OPEN -- deferred to v0.2.
**Exception rationale:** Same as GP-R4. The bounded model check is the shipped verification;
the unbounded proof is a freeze prerequisite, not a carry prerequisite. Spec §26 item 6
documents this explicitly.
**Risk accepted:** Same as GP-R4.

## CL-B4: No second independent non-producer implementation

**Status:** OPEN -- deferred to post-carry.
**Exception rationale:** A second independent implementation agreeing on every frozen vector
is a freeze prerequisite (spec §26 item 6). It is not a carry prerequisite. The carrying
audit verifies the REFERENCE implementation against its own specification and test corpus;
a second implementation verifies cross-implementation consistency. These are distinct gates.
The artifact does not claim cross-implementation consistency.
**Risk accepted:** A specification ambiguity that the reference implementation resolves
one way might be resolved differently by a second implementation.

## OD-2 / OD-11: Open design decisions

**Status:** OPEN -- tracked in OPEN_DECISIONS.md.
**Exception rationale:** 12 open design decisions (OD-1 through OD-12) are documented in
OPEN_DECISIONS.md and flagged by the verifier (G10 WARN). These are design choices that
have not been frozen, not defects. The verifier correctly WARNs (does not FAIL) on them.
The DRAFT status explicitly encompasses unresolved design decisions.
**Risk accepted:** A future resolution of an open decision could require re-audit.

---

## Ledger integrity

This exception ledger is part of the carrying-audit package. Each exception is:
- Documented with explicit risk acceptance
- Bounded to v0.1 DRAFT status (exceptions do not extend to freeze or publication)
- Traceable to the specific decision-register item

No exception waives the SHVVP §0.3 two-family carry requirement. The carry is a separate
gate discharged by independent execution, not by exception.

**Signed:** Bilal Syed Arfeen, Project Lead, BayyinahEnterprise, 2026-07-30

# BSSG v0.1 (V11) SOLE-AUDITOR REPORT — GLM 5.2 SEAT

**Audit round:** V11 (third class-level repair, pass 3 dispatch)

**Auditor seat:** GLM (independent non-producer vendor family)
**Report date:** 2026-07-27
**NONCE:** `BSSG-V11-AUDIT-GLM-568b2fc961280f8e`

---

## 0. IDENTITY STATEMENT (sole-auditor confirmation, required)

(a) **EXACT model that authored the findings, analysis, and verdict:** **GLM 5.2.**
This seat's analysis, all probe code (`glm5_2_probes.py`, authored from scratch), the
six-element findings, and the final verdict were authored by **GLM 5.2**. This is a
self-declaration (non-probative by itself).

(b) **Is the analysis-author GLM 5.2 or a Perplexity default/blend?**
**GLM 5.2 authored the analysis.** This seat was pinned to GLM 5.2 for the actual
analysis, probe-authoring, and verdict — not merely for command execution. The prior
(pass-6) round's invalidation (a default/blend model authored the analysis) is NOT
repeated here.

(c) **Execution surface used to RUN the code:** the **Perplexity Computer sandbox**,
invoked through the **`bash` tool** (`python3 <script>` in `/home/user/workspace/bssg_audit`).
No code was run outside this surface.

The identity statement is a self-declaration; the EXECUTION_ATTESTATION below proves
execution.

---

### Probe design notes (by area)

**(1) RESIDUAL ALIASING (A1-A7):** the deep-copy-at-the-boundary repair closes the class.
A1-A3 mutate the RETURNED authorization receipt (canonical_target, params_digest,
nested authority_snapshot) and confirm the stored token binding/receipt and the committed
effect are unaffected. A4 mutates caller-owned request/evidence after `authorize()` and
confirms the recorded digest and stored token are stable (input TOCTOU closed). A5
mutates the caller's `covered_effect_classes` list after `authorize()` and confirms the
stored `witness_covered_classes` is not an alias (the prior-round coverage-bypass class).
A6 mutates an accepted-amendment result; A7 mutates a denied-decision record. All GREEN —
no path returns or stores a reference into caller-owned state, and no internal structure
a caller can reach and mutate changes a later decision. **The aliasing class is closed.**

**(2) OVER-REJECTION (B1-B7):** the new strictness does not wrongly refuse legit requests.
B1/B7 confirm DEGRADED->DEGRADED and HEALTHY->HEALTHY commits (no over-rejection of equal
health). B2/B3 confirm the evidence-freshness boundary is strict `>` (boundary allowed,
one second past rejected). B4 confirms the commit `evidence_deadline` boundary is strict
`>` (boundary allowed). B5 confirms a raising verifier on the witness path maps to a
recorded DENY_UNKNOWN (no escape, no swallowed ALLOW); B6 confirms the wrapper is
transparent on the happy path (correct verifier still yields ALLOW).

**(3) SYMMETRY (C1-C5):** authorize and commit are aligned. C1 confirms an adapter
change is caught at commit via contract-body digest re-derivation (transitively
symmetric). C2 confirms commit rejects a substituted canonical_target (binding
revalidation, no weaker than authorize). C3 confirms a ceiling change increments
authority_epoch, voiding the token at commit. C4 confirms contract `not_after` expiry is
enforced at BOTH authorize and commit (dedicated E-COMMIT-CONTRACT-EXPIRED code). C5
confirms commit enforces a DISTINCT evidence-age bound from token expiry.

**(4) TOTALITY depth (D1-D5):** authorize and commit are total (D1, D2, D5 GREEN —
nested-evaluator faults and post-reserve clock faults map to recorded
DENY_UNKNOWN / VOID+E-COMMIT-ABORTED). **D3 and D4 RED: `submit_amendment()` is the one
public entry NOT covered by a no-escape totality wrapper** (see GLM-F1).

**(5) CONCURRENCY (E1-E4):** the single `self._lock` (RLock) serializes
authorize/commit/amendment. E1 confirms concurrent distinct-token commits both succeed
(no false double-spend from lock serialization). E2 confirms concurrent same-nonce
authorize yields at most one ALLOW and one token (dedup atomic). E3 confirms an amendment
lift racing an authorize on the same session produces no torn state. E4 confirms a
concurrent caller-owned registry mutation does not change an in-flight authorize
decision (body snapshot). All GREEN.

## 5. FINDINGS (six-element format)

### GLM-F1 — submit_amendment totality gap (no no-escape wrapper)
1. **ID:** GLM-F1
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` lines 1652-1655 (`submit_amendment`) and 1657-1765
   (`_submit_amendment_locked`); specifically the absent try/except around the
   `verify_signature("correction", ...)` call at line 1673-1675 and the
   `verify_signature("adjudicator", ...)` call at line 1741-1743.
3. **Claim/observation:** `authorize()` is total (try/except -> DENY_UNKNOWN via
   `_authorize_abort`, lines 1056-1059) and `commit()` is total (try/except -> VOID +
   E-COMMIT-ABORTED, lines 1368-1376), but `submit_amendment()` has NO totality wrapper:
   it is `with self._lock: return self._submit_amendment_locked(amendment)` with no
   surrounding try/except. A `signature_verifier` callable that RAISES (on the
   `"correction"` top-level signature path, or on the `"adjudicator"` signature path
   inside the adjudicator loop) ESCAPES to the caller instead of returning a recorded
   decision. Probes D3 and D4 reproduce both escape paths. The escape leaves NO partial
   state (D3 confirms `terminal_preserved=True`, `consumed=False` — all state mutations
   at lines 1755-1760 occur after the last verifier call), and it produces NO wrong
   decision (an escape is not an ALLOW). The defect is the violated totality invariant
   itself: the recovery entry point is not a no-escape transaction, unlike the other two
   public entries. The escape requires a misbehaving injected verifier (a trusted
   component), not attacker-controlled input; the amendment is structurally/schema
   validated before the verifier is reached, so the raise is not triggerable by a
   malformed amendment alone.
4. **Severity:** **MAJOR**
5. **Evidence:**
   - Probe D3 output: `RED D3 [TOTALITY] submit_amendment has NO totality wrapper: raising
     verifier ESCAPES (no recorded decision)  ESCAPED RuntimeError; terminal_preserved=True consumed=False`
   - Probe D4 output: `RED D4 [TOTALITY] submit_amendment raising adjudicator verifier
     also ESCAPES (no wrapper around the loop)  ESCAPED RuntimeError`
   - Code: `bssg_gate.py:1652-1655` — `def submit_amendment(self, amendment): amendment =
     _safe_copy(amendment); with self._lock: return self._submit_amendment_locked(amendment)`
     (no try/except), contrasted with `bssg_gate.py:1056-1059` (authorize wrapper) and
     `bssg_gate.py:1368-1376` (commit wrapper).
6. **Required repair:** wrap the body of `_submit_amendment_locked` (or the
   `submit_amendment` call) in `try/except Exception:` mirroring `_authorize_abort`:
   on any escape, append a record to `self.state.records` and return
   `{"accepted": False, "reason_codes": ["E-AMENDMENT-ABORTED"]}`. This closes the last
   totality gap so all three public entries are no-escape transactions. The repair must
   not perform any state mutation (terminal deletion / correction consumption) before all
   verifier calls complete, which the current mutation ordering already satisfies.

### GLM-F2 — authorize wrapper collapses a precise contract-malformed reason to generic E-AUTHORIZE-ABORTED for non-canonical trusted registry bodies
1. **ID:** GLM-F2
2. **Location:** `bssg_gate.py` lines 840-841 (`body = copy.deepcopy(contract["body"])`;
   `recomputed = digest(body)`) inside `_contract_match`, reached via the authorize
   wrapper at lines 1056-1059.
3. **Claim/observation:** `_contract_match` handles a non-dict contract body / missing
   body with a precise `E-CONTRACT-MALFORMED` (lines 834-836), but does NOT handle the
   case where the body IS a dict but is non-canonicalizable (e.g. an integer outside the
   I-JSON safe range nested in `allowed_effects`). `digest(body)` then raises
   `BSSGError` inside `_contract_match`, inside `_authorize_locked`, inside the authorize
   try/except wrapper, which collapses it to a generic `DENY_UNKNOWN` /
   `E-AUTHORIZE-ABORTED` rather than the precise `E-CONTRACT-MALFORMED`. The DECISION is
   correct (DENY_UNKNOWN; no ALLOW, no escape), and the trigger is a corrupted trusted
   registry (operator/producer-controlled), not attacker input — the evidence-side
   equivalent is handled precisely by a dedicated `canonical_bytes(evidence)` guard at
   lines 1138-1142 (`E-NONCANONICAL-EVIDENCE`). This is a reason-code precision
   asymmetry, not a decision defect.
4. **Severity:** **INFO**
5. **Evidence:** Probe D1 output: `GREEN D1 [TOTALITY] authorize: nested unsafe int in
   trusted contract body -> recorded DENY_UNKNOWN (no escape)  decision=DENY_UNKNOWN
   recorded=DENY_UNKNOWN` — the decision lands in the wrapper's
   `E-AUTHORIZE-ABORTED` path rather than a precise `E-CONTRACT-MALFORMED`. Code:
   `bssg_gate.py:840-841` (`digest(body)` with no surrounding guard), contrasted with the
   evidence-side guard at `bssg_gate.py:1138-1142`.
6. **Required repair:** in `_contract_match`, wrap the `digest(body)` recomputation in a
   try/except that returns `UNKNOWN, ["E-CONTRACT-MALFORMED"], None` on
   `BSSGError`/canonicalization failure, mirroring the evidence-side guard. Optional /
   low-priority: the decision is already correct.

### GLM-F3 — stale pass-6 probe file contaminates the packet (verifier G5/G9 false positives)
1. **ID:** GLM-F3
2. **Location:** `/home/user/workspace/bssg_audit/glm_differential_probes.py` lines 510-515
   (a phrase-registry list literal), flagged by `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` G5 and G9.
3. **Claim/observation:** A stale probe file from the **invalidated pass-6 round** (the
   brief states that round's analysis was authored by a default/blend model, not GLM 5.2)
   remains in the audit directory. It is NOT one of the 12 manifest files, so G9 flags it

   seat, not a defect in the BSSG gate under audit. It does not affect the recomputed

4. **Severity:** **INFO**
5. **Evidence:** `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` output: `G5 FAIL prohibited effectiveness
   language: glm_differential_probes.py:511 prevents harm; ...` and
   `G9 FAIL files present but not in the manifest: glm_differential_probes.py`. The
   flagged lines are `prohibited = [ r"prevents harm", r"makes agents safe", ... ]` — a
   list literal of scan patterns. Grep of the 12 manifest files for the prohibited

   phrase registry, properly marked `# prohibited-phrase-registry`); `bssg_gate.py` and
   all other manifest files are clean.
6. **Required repair:** remove `glm_differential_probes.py` from the audit directory (or,
   if retained for history, add the `# prohibited-phrase-registry` exemption comment to
   its phrase list and exclude it from the verifier's file walk). This is a packet
   hygiene action, not a gate-code change.

---

## 6. STANDING NON-DEFECTS (judged, with reasoning)

- **Huge-declared-skew symmetric (policy bound):** not re-examined; the authority lattice
  and ceiling checks are policy-bound, not code-invented. Standing non-defect.
- **D.2 monotone narrowing:** confirmed by model check A2 (antitone over 729 contracts)
  and CE9/CE25/CE45. `_apply_narrowing` (lines 1313-1338) is monotone; widening and
  non-strict narrowing are terminal. Non-defect.
- **Concurrency under a single lock:** the `self._lock` RLock serializes
  authorize/commit/amendment; `self._commit_lock` is redundant given `self._lock` (the
  entire commit holds `self._lock`). Probes E1-E4 confirm no torn state, no false
  double-spend, atomic nonce dedup. Distributed atomicity remains a deployment
  obligation (BSSG-H), honestly disclosed. Non-defect for the reference gate.
- **Caller-owned registry mutation:** `self.contracts`/`self.policies` are stored by
  reference and mutable by the caller, but `_contract_match` snapshots the body
  (`body = copy.deepcopy(contract["body"])`, line 840) before digest, and commit
  re-derives the contract/policy digest against ground truth (lines 1426, 1439). Probe E4
  confirms an in-flight authorize is unaffected by concurrent registry mutation. Non-defect.

---

## 7. PRODUCER-DISCLOSED PENDING (load-bearing check)

- **34 spec citations checked only for internal resolvability, not against primaries**
  (verifier G4 PASS on resolvability only). Not load-bearing for the gate's decision
  semantics; flagged as pending per the brief.
- **12 open decisions (OD-1..OD-12)** all reported as open by OPEN_DECISIONS, the decision
  register, and verifier G10. No open decision is claimed resolved. Confirmed by G10 WARN.
  Not load-bearing for this audit's findings.
- **Full line-by-line spec read pending.** Not blocking this audit; the executable
  refinement (model check REFINE: 22 observed transitions, 0 illegal) is consistent with
  the spec Section 14.

---

## 8. CLAIM-BOUNDARY CHECK (hard rule)

The hard rule states that any sentence claiming BSSG "prevents harm", "makes agents safe",
"reduces unauthorized effects", "outperforms", "is validated", or "guarantees" anything is
a HALT-level finding. A grep of the 12 manifest files for these phrases finds ZERO such
claims. The gate's honesty statement (`bssg_gate.py:9-13`) explicitly states it "makes NO
claim that any deployment using it is safe, secure, harm-reducing, or effective." The only
G5 "hits" are the stale pass-6 probe file's phrase-registry list literal (GLM-F3, INFO),
which are scan patterns, not claims. **No HALT-level claim-boundary finding applies to the
gate under audit.**

---

## 9. FINAL VERDICT

**VERDICT: PASS** (no blocker)

Counts by severity:
- **BLOCKER: 0**
- **MAJOR: 1** (GLM-F1 — submit_amendment totality gap)
- **MINOR: 0**
- **INFO: 2** (GLM-F2 — wrapper reason-code precision collapse for non-canonical trusted
  registry bodies; GLM-F3 — stale pass-6 probe file packet contamination / verifier
  G5/G9 false positives)

### Disagreement with the producer (recorded explicitly, not smoothed)

1. **The producer's V11 packet closes the residual-aliasing CLASS.** I independently
   confirm this: 7 aliasing probes (A1-A7) all GREEN, and the input-snapshot / returned-
   record deep-copy repair is present at every public entry and every stored/returned
   record. The prior-round `witness_covered_classes` by-reference storage (A5) and
   returned-receipt tamper (A1/A3) are closed. **I agree with the producer here.**

2. **I disagree with leaving `submit_amendment()` unwrapped.** The brief's KEY CONTEXT
   itself notes that `submit_amendment()` does NOT have a totality wrapper while
   `authorize()` and `commit()` do. The producer has not wrapped it. This is a real
   asymmetry: it is the one public entry that is not a no-escape transaction, and probes
   D3/D4 reproduce two distinct escape paths (top-level correction signature; adjudicator
   signature in the loop). The impact is bounded (recovery path, no wrong decision, no
   partial state, requires a misbehaving trusted verifier), so it is MAJOR, not BLOCKER —
   but it is a genuine totality-depth defect the producer should close, not leave standing.

3. **The verifier G5/G9 FAILs are false positives caused by stale packet contamination
   (GLM-F3), not gate defects.** The gate code itself is clean of effectiveness claims. I
   do not treat G5/G9 as a gate finding; I treat them as a packet-hygiene action item.

### Convergence with the V10 round

The V10 round converged with a GLM-5.2 seat (PASS, 3 MAJOR) and GPT-5.6 (HALT, 2 BLOCKER +
3 MAJOR) finding the same two defect classes (aliasing + predicate-symmetry/totality).

## 2. Class-fix verification

### ALLOW-path init (≈L1820)

Python

```
`\# CLASS FIX: initialize contract\_ceiling for this session if absent.`

`\# ... at the TOP OF THE ALLOW PATH, before any conditional (health check, mint, ceiling-write).`

`\_cc\_session = (request.get("session\_id") if isinstance(request, dict)`

`               and isinstance(request.get("session\_id"), str) else None)`

`if \_cc\_session is not None and \_cc\_session not in self.state.contract\_ceiling:`

`    self.state.contract\_ceiling\[\_cc\_session\] = Authority(\[\], \[\])`
```

This fires **unconditionally** for every path that has already decided ALLOW (i.e., after the if decision != DECISION\_ALLOW: return gate and before new\_token()).

- Degraded ALLOW → empty entry left in place.

- HEALTHY + successful mint → entry later **upgraded** by ceiling\_for\_health(..., "HEALTHY").

- Mint-fault / invalid / collision → returns via \_issuance\_failure **after** the empty init has already run; \_issuance\_failure also retains its defensive write.

- Ceiling-write exception → empty (or prior) entry survives.

### Gemini degraded-first probe (34th instance)

text

```
`R1: ALLOW | cc: \{'effects': \[\], 'target\_scopes': \[\]\}`

`cc is empty Authority: True`

`R3 DELETE after lift: DENY\_FALSE`

`34th instance CLOSED: True`
```

### R2 probes re-run (still closed)

| **Path** | **R1** | **cc empty?** | **Post-lift DELETE** | Closed? |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| MINT-FAULT | ALLOW / FAILED\_NO\_EFFECT | True | DENY\_FALSE | Yes |
| MINT-INVALID | ALLOW / FAILED\_NO\_EFFECT | True | DENY\_FALSE | Yes |
| COLLISION | ALLOW / FAILED\_NO\_EFFECT | True | DENY\_FALSE | Yes |
| Prior-ceiling + broader-registry mint-fault | ALLOW / FAILED\_NO\_EFFECT | prior survives unbroadened | — | Yes |

### The invariant

**\_held can never be None after any ALLOW decision on the pass-36 bytes.**

Trace of every path through the ALLOW branch:

1. Kernel reaches decision == DECISION\_ALLOW.

2. Control enters the ALLOW block.

3. Pending is captured and cleared.

4. **Empty-Authority init runs if the session is absent** (the class fix).

5. new\_token() is attempted.

   - Success + HEALTHY → upgrade write.

   - Success + DEGRADED → empty/prior left.

   - Fault / invalid / collision → \_issuance\_failure (entry already present).

6. Any subsequent post-lift re-establishment therefore sees \_held = self.state.contract\_ceiling.get(session) as a non-None Authority (empty or previously demonstrated HEALTHY). The \_held is not None guard in \_apply\_narrowing therefore always fires and bounds the re-establishment.

No ALLOW path returns without having executed the init. The 34-instance pattern (absence treated as “establishment free”) is structurally closed.


## 3. Verdict

**CLEAN.**

All commands match the expected battery (20/20, 345, 176/176 GREEN, 11110 schedules, 12 PASS / 0 FAIL). The class fix is present and unconditional at the top of the ALLOW path. The degraded-first vector is closed (CE176). All prior R2 vectors remain closed. The invariant holds: after any ALLOW, \_held is never None.

Artifact status remains **DRAFT / NOT CARRIED / NOT PUBLICATION-READY**. No effectiveness claim is made.

## 2. F-P36-01 verification (REPAIR_STATUS.md L29)

CONFIRMED. `REPAIR_STATUS.md:L29` now reads:

(repair34) still reads `173/173 CE GREEN`, L119 (repair33) still reads
`172/172 CE GREEN`. `REPAIR_STATUS.md:L45` carries the
`{claim:CLAIM-CLASS-FIX-CEILING}` tag as documented.

### Footer pattern: retroactive edit vs rolling doc-invariant

Observed distribution of `This document claims N counterexamples.` footers:
L33 (pass-35 section) = 176, L71 (pass-34 section) = 176, L279 (pass-30
post-V28 section) = 176; then L364 (pass-29) = 159, L433 = 156, L486 = 154,
and so on, frozen at historical values down the document.

Interpretation A (retroactive edit, Gemini's original concern): the footer is
part of each pass section's historical record, and the pass-30-post-V28 footer
reading 176 (a corpus size that did not exist at pass-30; pass-29 sealed 159
and repair33 sealed 172) is an after-the-fact rewrite of history. Under this
reading the edit is also inconsistently applied, since pass-29 and older
footers were left at their historical values.

Interpretation B (rolling doc-invariant, COUNCIL_INSTRUCTIONS reading): the
footer is a document-level assertion of the CURRENT corpus size, stamped by
the generator on the sections it still maintains, and it is metadata rather
than history. The decisive evidence for B is that the actual historical
record, the battery-state lines, is demonstrably unedited (L67 = 173/173,
L119 = 172/172 exactly as sealed in those passes), and the footer wording is
present-tense and document-scoped ("This document claims"), not pass-scoped
("this pass sealed").

Assessment: the substrate supports Interpretation B for the load-bearing
question (no historical battery evidence was altered, so provenance is
intact), but the two interpretations are observationally distinguishable only
because the battery-state lines exist as an independent unedited record. The
residual ambiguity is that under B the frozen old footers (159, 156, ...) are
now FALSE as document-level assertions, so the document mixes two footer
semantics. This is recorded as advisory finding F-FB-3 (LOW) below. It does
not affect the fix verdict: F-P36-01 is correctly applied.

## Advisory findings (six-element format; advisory-only)

**F-FB-3** LOW (advisory-only) -- REPAIR_STATUS.md footer assertion carries
mixed semantics across sections.

- **Locus:** `REPAIR_STATUS.md` footers at L33, L71, L279 (read 176, current

## 2. Deep code analysis

### 2a. `_issuance_failure` empty-Authority write (bssg_gate.py L879-916)

The V34 F-GS-1 fix is at L900-902:
```python
if session is not None and session not in self.state.contract_ceiling:
    self.state.contract_ceiling[session] = Authority([], [])
```

**Symmetry across the three failure modes.** All three post-kernel issuance faults route
through the SAME `_issuance_failure(...)` entry point (L1817-1825):
- `E-TOKEN-MINT-FAULT` (L1819, `new_token()` raised),
- `E-TOKEN-MINT-INVALID` (L1822, token fails the 8..128-length / prohibited-field check),
- `E-TOKEN-FACTORY-COLLISION` (L1825, `token_id in self.state.tokens`).

Because the empty-Authority write lives in the common `_issuance_failure` body (L900-902),
not at any one of the three call sites, the fail-closed write is **symmetric**: the empty
ceiling is written identically regardless of which of the three faults fired. This is
correct and is what CE175 exercises for `E-TOKEN-MINT-FAULT` (verified GREEN in section 1).

**Guard polarity is correct.** The write is conditional on
`session not in self.state.contract_ceiling`, i.e. it only fills the FIRST-establish gap. A
session that already legitimately demonstrated authority keeps its real (narrower) ceiling
and is not clobbered by an empty one on a later mint fault. The post-establish over-broaden
case is independently closed by `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING` in `_apply_narrowing` (L1943-1953),
as the CE175 comment states. I confirmed the `_held` check at L1949-1952 reads
`contract_ceiling.get(session)` and terminalizes on `not (new_ceiling <= _held)`.

**Does any post-kernel failure path skip the empty write?** I traced every `return` between
the kernel decision (L1765) and the ALLOW receipt (L1922). The only post-kernel exits are
the three `_issuance_failure` calls (all covered) and the outer `except BaseException`
handler in `authorize()` (L1432-1513). The BaseException handler routes to
`_authorize_abort`, which does NOT write the empty Authority. This is the seam that section
3 and finding F-CF-1 examine: a post-mint mutation that raises escapes to the BaseException
abort, which by explicit design (L1436-1440 comment) does NOT rewind authority/ceiling state.

### 2b. Post-mint ceiling-write branch (Opus 5's A-05, L1830-1863)

The branch (L1830-1835):
```python
if _cc_pending is not None and health == "HEALTHY":
    _cc_sess, _cc_body = _cc_pending
    try:
        self.state.contract_ceiling[_cc_sess] = ceiling_for_health(_cc_body, "HEALTHY")
    except Exception:
        reasons.append("E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED")
```

**The reason_codes DROP is confirmed on the bytes.** The ALLOW receipt template at L1863
hardcodes `"reason_codes": []`, and the ALLOW decision record at L1920 hardcodes
`"reason_codes": []` as well. `reasons` is a live local list that the ALLOW path DID append
to (L1835 on ceiling-record failure; also L1750 on the pending-capture failure). Neither
the receipt nor the record ever reads `reasons` on the ALLOW path. Therefore
**`E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED` can never surface on an ALLOW receipt or ALLOW record.** This is
a genuine surface-substrate divergence: the code computes a reason code and then discards
it. Verified empirically in section 3 (`r1_receipt_reason_codes: []` and
`r1_record_reason_codes: []` while the ceiling write was forced to fail).

**Ordering of post-mint mutations.** After the successful mint at L1817, the ALLOW path
performs, in order:
1. L1833 `contract_ceiling[sess] = ceiling_for_health(...)` (the A-05 site),
2. L1837 `request_digest = digest(request)`,
3. L1838-1839 `expires_at = min(parse_rfc3339_utc(...), parse_rfc3339_utc(...))`,
4. L1840-1912 receipt dict construction (includes `digest(witness_receipt)`, `digest_bytes`,
   `ceiling.as_json()`),
5. L1914-1921 decision record construction,
6. L1922 `self.state.records.append(...)`,
7. L1923+ `self.state.tokens[token_id] = {...}` (includes `digest(receipt)`).

Everything in steps 1 through 6 executes AFTER the token counter has advanced (L1817) but
BEFORE the token is registered in `state.tokens` (step 7). Only steps 3 (`parse_rfc3339_utc`),
2 and 4 and 7 (`digest`) and the dict/`as_json` construction can plausibly raise; if any of
them does, control leaves through the outer `except BaseException` (L1432), which explicitly
does NOT rewind the L1833 ceiling broadening. This is the seam finding F-CF-1 documents.

## 3. Independent A-05 reproduction (ADVISORY)

I wrote my own probe (`/home/user/workspace/bssg_round2/fable5_a05_probe.py`), deliberately
using a DIFFERENT mechanism than the orchestrator's `a05_probe.py`. The orchestrator counts
HEALTHY `ceiling_for_health()` invocations and raises on the second. I instead replaced
`state.contract_ceiling` with a `dict` subclass whose `__setitem__` raises exactly once for
the target session, so the L1833 assignment itself throws inside its own try/except. The
token mint (L1817) succeeds, so only the ceiling RECORD fails. This isolates the A-05 arm
more precisely (it forces the assignment, not a downstream recompute).

**Probe output (verbatim):**
```
r1_decision: ALLOW
r1_issuance_status: (none)
r1_receipt_present: True
r1_receipt_reason_codes: []
r1_record_reason_codes: []
r1_token: token-00000001
contract_ceiling_present_sess: False
contract_ceiling_value: ABSENT
token_live: True
r3_delete_prelift_decision: DENY_FALSE
lift_status: submitted
r4_delete_postlift_decision: ALLOW
r4_token: token-00000003
ADJUDICATION: A-05 REPRODUCED
```

**Adjudication: A-05 REPRODUCED (mechanically), via an independent mechanism.** All four
mechanical claims hold on the round-2 bytes: (1) ALLOW issued with a live token despite the
ceiling-write fault; (2) `E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED` silently dropped, receipt
`reason_codes: []`; (3) `contract_ceiling['sess-0001']` left ABSENT (not empty); (4) a
post-lift HEALTHY DELETE re-establishes to ALLOW. This matches the orchestrator's summary.

**Severity nuance I am obligated to raise (ADVISORY, for a non-producer to weigh).** The
"a DELETE the session never held" framing deserves scrutiny before a non-producer records
this as CRITICAL. The A-05 contract has `allowed_effects = [READ, WRITE, DELETE]` and its
HEALTHY ceiling therefore INCLUDES DELETE. On the NON-faulted path, a HEALTHY READ ALLOW
writes `contract_ceiling = ceiling_for_health(body, "HEALTHY") = {DELETE, READ, WRITE}` (the
V31 K33-01 design: a HEALTHY ALLOW records the full HEALTHY ceiling of that contract, not
just the requested effect). On that non-faulted path the post-lift DELETE would ALSO
re-establish to ALLOW, because `_held = {DELETE,READ,WRITE}` and `DELETE <= _held`. So the
end-state authority in the faulted (A-05) run and the clean run is IDENTICAL for this
contract. The A-05 fault therefore does not, for this contract shape, grant authority the
session would otherwise be denied; it reaches the same landing state by a different (absent
vs full) intermediate ceiling.

Where A-05 does bite, and where it is genuinely a defect regardless of the above, is the
**silent drop of `E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED` from the audit surface** (section 2b) and the
**divergence between the two fail-closed polarities**: `_issuance_failure` writes an EMPTY
Authority (fail-closed to nothing, L900-902) whereas the L1833 arm leaves the ceiling ABSENT
(fail-open to free re-establishment via `_apply_narrowing._held is None`, L1946-1952). Two
sibling post-kernel failure arms use OPPOSITE fail-closed conventions. That asymmetry is the
real substrate finding, and it is a construct a non-producer should record. See F-CF-1.

## 4. ADVISORY findings (six-element `bayyinah_findings-format.md` format)

**F-CF-1** ADVISORY-HIGH -- post-mint ceiling-write failure is fail-OPEN (absent ceiling),
inconsistent with `_issuance_failure`'s fail-CLOSED (empty ceiling), and drops its own reason
code.

- **Locus:** `bssg_gate.py:1830-1835` (post-mint ceiling write + swallowed
  `E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED`), `bssg_gate.py:1863` and `:1920` (receipt/record hardcode
  `reason_codes: []`), against `bssg_gate.py:900-902` (`_issuance_failure` empty-Authority
  write) and `bssg_gate.py:1946-1952` (`_apply_narrowing` `_held is None` free-establish).
- **Substance:** the code claims (L1793-1815 comments) that contract_ceiling records only
  demonstrably-held authority and that the F-GS-1 class is closed by the empty-Authority
  fail-closed default, but when `ceiling_for_health` raises at L1833 the session's ceiling is
  left ABSENT rather than EMPTY. Absent drives `_apply_narrowing` down the `_held is None`
  free-establishment branch (L1946), i.e. fail-OPEN, the opposite polarity from the sibling
  `_issuance_failure` arm which writes an EMPTY Authority to force fail-CLOSED. The appended
  `E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED` is then discarded because the ALLOW receipt (L1863) and record
  (L1920) hardcode `reason_codes: []`, so the fault is invisible on every audit surface.
  Reproduced by my independent probe (section 3): ALLOW issued, token live, ceiling ABSENT,
  reason_codes empty.
- **Disposition:** in the L1834 `except`, write `self.state.contract_ceiling[_cc_sess] =
  Authority([], [])` (mirror `_issuance_failure` L900-902) so the failure is fail-closed to
  the empty ceiling, AND surface the reason by replacing the two hardcoded `reason_codes: []`
  at L1863 and L1920 with `sorted(set(reasons))` so `E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED` reaches the
  audit plane. A non-producer (GPT 5.6 Sol or Gemini 3.1 Pro) should reproduce and, if
  confirmed, record at the severity the rubric dictates. Because I am producer-family, I
  cannot record this as CRITICAL/HIGH for the ledger; per `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md`
  CRITICAL-vs-HIGH calibration it turns on whether a security invariant is BROKEN (CRITICAL)
  versus a defense-in-depth / observability gap that does not, for the tested contract shape,
  actually broaden landing-state authority (HIGH). My read is HIGH on the audit-surface drop
  and polarity asymmetry; the CRITICAL claim is contract-shape-dependent (section 3 nuance)
  and needs a non-producer to construct a contract where absent-vs-full genuinely diverges.
- **Cross-reference:** Opus 5 A-05 (v2 council); F-GS-1 / CE175 (the empty-write fix this
  finding says is applied asymmetrically); PMD v1.2 §0.4 (a CRITICAL here would fail the
  two-consecutive-clean-rounds premise); `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md` CRITICAL-vs-HIGH.

**F-CF-2** ADVISORY-MEDIUM -- post-mint mutations after the L1833 ceiling write can raise into
the BaseException abort, leaving the ceiling broadened with no registered token.

- **Locus:** `bssg_gate.py:1837` (`digest(request)`), `:1838-1839` (`parse_rfc3339_utc`),
  `:1840-1912` (receipt construction, `as_json`, `digest_bytes`), `:1923+`
  (`state.tokens[token_id] = ...`), against the outer handler `bssg_gate.py:1432-1440`
  (`except BaseException`, explicit "do NOT rewind authority/epoch state").
- **Substance:** the ALLOW path broadens `contract_ceiling` at L1833 BEFORE steps 2-7
  (section 2b). If any later step raises (a hostile `state.tokens` on the L1923 assignment,
  or any dependency fault), control leaves via the outer BaseException handler, which by
  design does not rewind the L1833 broadening. The result is a broadened ceiling with either
  no live token (raise before L1923) or, if L1923 itself raises after L1922, an ALLOW record
  already appended to `state.records` referencing a `token_id` absent from `state.tokens`.
  The latter fails safe on redemption (the committer checks `state.tokens`, so an absent
  token cannot commit), so this is defense-in-depth, not a live bypass on the tested paths.
- **Disposition:** move the L1833 ceiling write to be the LAST post-mint mutation, after
  `state.tokens[token_id]` is successfully assigned, so ceiling broadening is atomic with a
  redeemable token (mirrors the L1811-1815 "write AFTER successful token creation" intent,
  extended to "after token REGISTRATION"). Alternatively, register the token first and write
  the ceiling last within a single try that fails closed. A non-producer should confirm the
  ordering claim.
- **Cross-reference:** F-CF-1 (same L1833 broadening, failure arm); F-GS-1 / CE175 (the
  "write AFTER mint" principle whose scope this finding extends); CE174 (AUDIT-V33-01,
  BaseException totality on the commit path, the analogous invariant on the commit side).

**F-CF-3 (probe-limitation disclosure, not a defect claim).** My section-2b edge hypothesis
that `digest(request)` raising at L1837 would demonstrate F-CF-2 empirically is reported as
**CANNOT-REPRODUCE via my probe**: `fable5_edge_probe.py` never triggered the raise
(`digest_req_shape_calls: 0`, `raise_fired: 0`), because my shape-based match on the
`_safe_copy`'d request object did not fire at the L1837 call site within the time budget. The
run therefore only shows normal HEALTHY behavior (ceiling `{DELETE,READ,WRITE}`, post-lift
DELETE ALLOW), which is by-design K33-01 semantics, NOT a new leak. F-CF-2 accordingly rests
on code review (ordering trace, section 2b), not on a passing probe. I disclose this rather
than present the normal-path run as if it demonstrated the edge case (per
`bayyinah_methodology-foundations.md` substrate-honesty and the task's "do NOT simulate
outputs" instruction).

**F-DOC-1** ADVISORY-LOW -- task brief cites an "eight-element" findings format that the
methodology doc defines as six-element.

- **Locus:** task brief ("eight-element Bayyinah format") vs
  `methodology/bayyinah_findings-format.md` heading "# Six-Element Findings Format".
- **Substance:** the brief's element count diverges from the authoritative doc; an auditor
  following the brief literally would look for two elements that do not exist.
- **Disposition:** correct the brief to "six-element," or, if an eight-element format is
  intended for this round, add the two new elements to `bayyinah_findings-format.md` first
  (immutability: format changes precede their citation).
- **Cross-reference:** `bayyinah_findings-format.md` "Findings-format compliance check";
  PMD v1.2 §0.4 independent-re-derivation (reason from the doc bytes, not the brief's claim
  about them).

| `bssg_gate.py` banner | `GATE_VERSION = "0.1.0-draft"`, `__main__` prints exactly the two recorded banner lines; no effectiveness claim anywhere in the entry point. | CONSISTENT |
| GLM's K=5 claim (19607 schedules) | Not an output I can verify by execution, but the arithmetic is exactly what the shipped enumerator produces at K=5: Σ 7^i, i=1..5 = 7+49+343+2401+16807 = **19607**. GLM's number is generatively consistent with the shipped code, which is evidence GLM actually ran the enumeration rather than restating a producer number — the exact discriminator that defeated the DeepSeek carry (placeholder identities, "Simulated from Embedded Test Results"). | CONSISTENT |

**Conclusion (Part 1):** I find **no inconsistency** between the canonical command outputs and the shipped, hash-verified code. Every FAIL in the verifier run is fully explained by (a) the 6 files deliberately pruned from the review package (G1, G8, G9, G10) or (b) the review packaging placing the methodology corpus inside the scanned package directory (G5, G7). None indicates a defect in gate logic, the counterexample corpus, or the model check.

### 2.2 One packaging-summary correction (record hygiene, not artifact defect)

The orchestrator's salient-facts summary in `COUNCIL_INSTRUCTIONS.md` says "12 of 18 listed files verify OK." The substrate says: **20** files listed in `SHA256SUMS`, **14** verify OK (12 code+schema files + `REPAIR_STATUS.md` + `BSSG_v0_1_CANONICAL_SPEC_DRAFT.pplx.md`), 6 absent. The "all 12 code + schema files hash-verify" sentence is correct; the "12 of 18" fraction is not. This is a surface–substrate divergence in the *review record*, not the artifact (PMD v1.2 §0.1, `PMD_v1_2_BAF_v3_0.md`: a finding is a documented surface–substrate divergence). Filed as F-CF-1 below. It changes nothing material but must be corrected before the council synthesis is archived, per the substrate-of-record uniqueness rule (PMD v1.2 §0.2 rule 5).

---

## 3. Part 2 — The convergence question

> Is three-seat adversarial convergence across V32–V34 (GPT-5.6, GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.6) — zero-BLOCKER, three vendor families, all non-producer — sufficient to accept convergence, when the two-family carry attempt (DeepSeek, Qwen) failed due to platform execution limitations, not artifact defects?

### Answer: QUALIFIED-YES — advisory, non-load-bearing

**Accept *convergence*. Do not let convergence discharge the *carry*.** These are two different gates, and the record supports the first while leaving the second undischarged. The artifact's own banner — DRAFT / NOT CARRIED — is exactly the honest label and should be retained until a genuine executing carry succeeds.

### 3.1 Convergence is genuinely achieved under PMD §0.4

PMD v1.2 §0.4 (`PMD_v1_2_BAF_v3_0.md`) defines convergence as: *"Two consecutive cross-vendor rounds produce 0 CRITICAL findings"*, with HIGH residual 0 (or a signed exception), MEDIUM/LOW absorbed or explicitly non-operative, and standing-rule compliance passing. The record shows **three** consecutive cross-vendor rounds (V32–V34) at zero findings in the blocking band across three non-producer vendor families — exceeding the two-round bar. The residuals (GPT's per-round MODERATE, all documentation staleness) map to the MEDIUM band of the severity rubric, whose disposition is explicitly *"ship-permissive"* into next-version absorption (`bayyinah_severity-rubric.md`, MEDIUM disposition), and MEDIUM does not enter the §0.4 convergence predicate at all. So on the brief's angle 4: **MODERATE/MEDIUM-only residuals do not defeat convergence** — provided they are documented in the next-version appendix as the rubric requires, which the missing `REPAIR_STATUS` V33/V34 blocks currently do *not* demonstrate on shipped bytes (see F-CF-3).

On angle 1 (does three exceed the bar, or is fresh rotation independently required): PMD §0.4 itself does not demand fresh rotation. The fresh-rotation clause lives in SHV D6 (`SHV_Method_v1_1.pdf`, D6): certify *"only when independent checkers agree repeatedly, **ideally** across two consecutive clean rounds with at least one checker rotated in fresh, so that agreement is not an artifact of a fixed panel."* The word is "ideally" — a strengthening condition, not a hard conjunct. V32–V34 satisfies D6's core (repeated agreement, multi-family, producer-quarantined, findings re-derived from primary bytes) but **fails its ideal form: the panel was fixed across all three clean rounds**. The third consecutive round adds real value (it further defeats the luck hypothesis) but adds **zero** value against the fixed-panel failure mode D6 names, because it is the same panel. Three-of-same is not a substitute for one-fresh. The intended fresh rotation *was* the carry pool — and it failed.

### 3.2 The carry is a separate load-bearing gate; convergence cannot substitute for it

Three independent lines of methodology force this, and the producer's own frozen record concedes it:

1. **SHVVP §0.3** (`SHVVP_v0_8_flagship.pdf`) is direct precedent: after v0.5's withdrawal, the frozen consequence was *"v0.5 has NOT been carried. It requires a fresh carrying audit by two non-producer seats of different vendor families ... before deposit. Producer-lineage, editor-lineage and chair review of v0.5 is ADVISORY and NON-CARRYING. No claim of audit convergence attaches to v0.5 at the time of this freeze."* The carrying audit is a **deposit gate**, distinct from round-level convergence, and no volume of non-carrying review substitutes. The BSSG program's own ledger applies the same rule to itself: *"All three are byte-authoritative continuous/one-shot seats and **non-carrying**; a fresh different-vendor rotation remains owed before any carry"* (`REPAIR_STATUS.md`, V29 adjudication banner, lines 124–125). The three convergence seats are, by the program's own frozen text, structurally non-carrying — not because of vendor identity but because they are the incumbent panel.

2. **SHUDP Axiom 5** (`SHUDP_v0_5_flagship.pdf`, "Axiom 5, evidence independence"): for each covered event there must exist an evidence record whose generation is *"not within S's authority"* (WithinAuth). The carry is precisely BSSG's A5 instrument — execution evidence generated outside the producer's and the incumbent panel's authority. The DeepSeek result is the canonical A5 anti-pattern: its "CLEAN" restated embedded results ("Simulated from Embedded Test Results", placeholder identity values) — in SHUDP's own words, *"a candidate witness is not a discharged existential requirement."* The Qwen result generated real execution evidence but against non-canonical bytes (SHA mismatches), so the evidence does not attach to the artifact. SHUDP also supplies the disciplined verdict vocabulary: the carry is **NOT EVALUABLE / UNDISCHARGED, not FAILED** — *"NOT EVALUABLE, not FAILED, is the disciplined verdict"* — and equally, nothing about the failure discharges the requirement.

3. **SHVVP §8.0** (`SHVVP_v0_8_flagship.pdf`) supplies the governing lesson for what to do when a required demonstration cannot be produced: v0.5 did not invent a third inferential mechanism to rescue the route claim; it **withdrew the claim** — *"a sampling model invented to rescue a claim is exactly the postdiction that preregistration exists to prevent"*, and *"Removing an unjustified inferential claim strengthens the instrument."* The analog here: do not construct a post-hoc argument that three-family convergence "counts as" a two-family carry. Narrow the claim to what the record honestly supports — **converged, NOT CARRIED** — which is what the shipped banner already says.

### 3.3 The specific sub-questions

- **Angle 2 (capability-shortfall: methodological blocker or substrate limitation?)** Substrate limitation. Under `bayyinah_audit-modes.md`, Mode A capability is a property of the execution substrate, not the artifact ("Requires git / tool access; not always available"), and the rotation doc's tier table records Mode A capability per vendor as an infrastructure fact. Neither carry failure produced an artifact finding; Qwen's ISSUES-FOUND was a delivery-integrity report, honestly filed. Therefore the failed carry does **not** invalidate the V32–V34 convergence, does **not** constitute adverse evidence against the artifact, and does **not** HALT the chain. But a substrate limitation excuses the *attempt*, not the *requirement*: SHVVP §0.3's deposit gate is stated over outcomes ("requires a fresh carrying audit ... before deposit"), not over efforts.
- **Angle 3 (does three-family convergence substitute for the carry?)** No, per §3.2. The carry's function under SHV D6 and SHUDP A5 is *fresh, executing, panel-independent* evidence. The three seats are neither fresh nor carry-eligible under the program's own frozen non-carrying designation (`REPAIR_STATUS.md` V29 banner).
- **Angle 4 (MODERATE-only residuals):** Below threshold; do not defeat convergence (PMD §0.4; `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md` MEDIUM disposition). See §3.1.
- **Angle 5 (GLM K=5 over-coverage):** **Strengthens the convergence record, does not advance the carry.** The 19607-schedule figure is exactly Σ7^i (i=1..5) under the shipped enumerator — generative evidence of genuine execution beyond shipped coverage. But GLM is an incumbent seat; deeper verification by an incumbent addresses assurance depth, not panel independence, which is the property the carry exists to supply (SHV D6 fixed-panel clause).
- **PMD M1.5 / mechanical-traceability exception** (PMD v1.2 §0.5 item 5, `PMD_v1_2_BAF_v3_0.md`; restated as the same-instance §0.1 named exception in `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`): **does not apply, and this matters.** The exception waives *cross-instance re-audit of an absorption cycle* when the cycle executed prescribed routes with zero architectural latitude, on project-lead signoff. It is scoped to absorption re-audits; it is not a waiver instrument for the deposit-time carry gate, and stretching it there would collide directly with SHVVP §0.3's frozen carry requirement and SHV D6's producer-quarantine. Where it *does* legitimately apply: the pending mechanical fixes for the documentation-staleness residuals (V33/V34 `REPAIR_STATUS`/README count refreshes) can be absorbed under M1.5 with project-lead signoff and without owing a fresh full round — those are disposition-prescribed routes with no latitude. (Note the citation-integrity caveat in F-CF-2: the label "M1.5" does not resolve cleanly in the shipped corpus.)

### 3.4 Operative recommendation (advisory)

1. **Accept convergence** for V32–V34 under PMD §0.4 — this is a non-producer-seat decision; I merely concur analytically.
2. **Retain DRAFT / NOT CARRIED** until two non-producer, different-vendor-family seats execute exact canonical bytes and return clean. The record itself suggests the viable substrate: the rotation doc lists Perplexity (tool-augmented) as a Tier 1, Mode A-strong, load-bearing substrate verifier (`bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`, Tier 1), and this very council cycle demonstrates byte-faithful sandbox delivery (SHA-verified) with real execution. A carry pool selected for **demonstrated Mode A capability** (rather than chat-only interfaces) cures the DeepSeek/Qwen failure mode without weakening the rule. Delivery must be by hash-verified archive, not text-paste extraction, to prevent recurrence of the Qwen byte-corruption mode.
3. Absorb the staleness residuals under M1.5 with project-lead signoff (mechanical routes only), and regenerate the full package so G1/G8/G9/G10 pass on the deposited bytes.

---

## 4. Independent findings

**F-CF-1 — LOW — locus: `COUNCIL_INSTRUCTIONS.md` (review record, not artifact) — substance:** "12 of 18 listed files verify OK" contradicts substrate (20 listed, 14 OK, 6 absent). **Disposition:** correct the fraction before archiving the synthesis. **Cross-ref:** PMD §0.1 surface–substrate divergence; §0.2 rule 5 substrate uniqueness.

**F-CF-2 — MEDIUM — locus: `methodology/METHODOLOGY_INDEX.md` — substance: citation-label instability in the very corpus the council is instructed to cite.** (a) The index describes the severity rubric as "BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/INFO" but the shipped `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md` defines CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW; (b) the index glosses "PMD M1.5: recursive self-application" while the council instructions equate M1.5 with the mechanical-traceability exception (which is PMD §0.5 item 5), and the dissertation uses "per M1.5" as a prior-wording-preservation ledger rule (`Structural_Honesty_Dissertation_v1_4`, Appendix E) — three non-identical referents for one label; (c) the index maps "SHVVP §8.0: carrying-audit protocol and convergence requirements", but §8.0 is the withdrawal record; the carrying rule is stated in §0.3. **Substance of risk:** council members citing "PMD M1.5" or "SHVVP §8.0" per the index will cite sections that do not say what the index claims — a methodology-fidelity defect in the audit apparatus itself. **Disposition:** reconcile the index against the shipped documents; re-issue. **Cross-ref:** PMD §0.1 (the index's surface diverges from the corpus substrate).

**F-CF-3 — MEDIUM (same class as GPT's V32–V34 residuals; confirms them on shipped bytes) — locus: `REPAIR_STATUS.md` — substance:** the hash-verified `REPAIR_STATUS.md` terminates at the V32 adjudication ("Convergence status: round 1 of 2"), and its battery block states "173/173 CE GREEN" while the same document elsewhere states "This document claims 174 counterexamples" and the shipped corpus is 174. Consequence: **the V33/V34 verdicts are not verifiable from any hash-verified byte in the review package** — they reach this council only through the producer-side brief. That is single-sourced substrate inheritance, the named Mode B weakness (`bayyinah_audit-modes.md`, Mode B: "susceptible to absorbing substrate errors from the artifact's restatement"). **Disposition:** before deposit, the V33/V34 seat reports must ship inside the hash manifest (they presumably live in the pruned `BSSG_v0_1_MODEL_COUNCIL_SYNTHESIS.pplx.md`/decision register; re-verification against those bytes is owed). This does not contradict the convergence record — but it means my QUALIFIED-YES on convergence is conditional on the V33/V34 reports existing byte-exactly as briefed.

**F-CF-4 — LOW — locus: severity vocabulary across seats — substance:** seat verdicts are recorded "under ITS OWN stated criterion, not re-scored" (`REPAIR_STATUS.md`, V29 banner); GPT's scale (CRITICAL/SIGNIFICANT/MODERATE/NOTE) contains no "BLOCKER" band at all, so the aggregate claim "zero-BLOCKER" is an implicit cross-rubric mapping. The mapping (GPT MODERATE ≈ rubric MEDIUM; GPT CRITICAL ≈ blocking band) is reasonable, but `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md` ("Severity reconciliation under cross-vendor disagreement") contemplates explicit reconciliation; the synthesis should state the mapping table once, normatively. **Disposition:** one-paragraph normalization note in the synthesis document.

**No findings against gate logic, the CE corpus, or the model check.** The one wording correction to the orchestrator's summary worth noting: G5 and G7 are *not* "consequences of the 6 missing manifest files" — they are consequences of the review packaging placing the methodology corpus inside the verifier's scan surface. The substantive conclusion (no gate-logic defect) is unaffected.

---

## 5. Dissenting angle

Even while concluding QUALIFIED-YES, I dissent from one element of the producer's framing: **the brief presents the carry failure as external bad luck ("platform limitations, not artifact defects") — but carry-pool selection is a producer-chain design decision, and this one was falsifiably poor.** The rotation doc's own tier table records Mode A capability per vendor as a known, documented property (`bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`, "Audit-modes by tier"); a carry rule whose entire purpose is *executing* exact bytes was pointed at a chat-only interface (DeepSeek) and a text-paste delivery channel (Qwen) — substrates predictably incapable of discharging it. Under SHV D6's falsification clause, a certification path that fails should trigger *strengthening the independence requirement*, not sympathy for the attempt. The honest description is not "the carry failed through no fault of the artifact" (true but incomplete) — it is "the producer chain selected a carry substrate that could not execute, so the carry obligation remains fully open and undiminished." The three-round convergence is real and creditable; the carry narrative in the brief drifts toward treating an unexecuted gate as morally satisfied. SHVVP §8.0's lesson cuts precisely here: withdraw or narrow the claim; never rescue it by reframing.

---

*Filed by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic — producer family, advisory-only, non-carrying, vote does not count toward certification per SHV D6 and the producer-instance exclusion in `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`).*

# Gemini 3.1 Pro - BSSG v0.1 Pass-36 Review

**Verdict:** ISSUES-FOUND (CLEAN on the gate soundness; ISSUES-FOUND on package consistency)

## Pass A: Meta-Audit

**1. Retroactive Edit Signature**
I checked the `REPAIR_STATUS.md` file for the A-06 retroactive edit signature from pass-35. The V32 result section (lines 48-69) still contains the pass-34 signature:
`**Battery state (repair34 resealed):** 345 tests OK -- 173/173 CE GREEN -- MODEL CHECK PASS`
However, right below it on line 70, a new line was inserted:
`This document claims 176 counterexamples.`
The same string was inserted at line 33 (in the pass-35 section claiming `175/175 CE GREEN`) and at line 278.
This means `REPAIR_STATUS.md` claims 175/175 GREEN (line 29), but independently claims "176 counterexamples" below it. This is exactly the kind of retroactive edit signature flagged in R2.

**2. Sealed Values Verification**
I ran the suite and compared it to the sealed values from the orchestrator:
- SHA256SUMS: 20/20 OK
- `test_bssg_gate.py`: 345 tests, 8 skipped, OK
- `bssg_counterexamples.py`: The execution returned `175/176 GREEN (1 RED)` on my direct execution due to a path issue with `execution-receipt.schema.json`, but the `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` script reports `176/176 GREEN, 0 RED (independently counted; self-report matches)`, matching the ground truth.
- Verifier: `12 PASS / 2 WARN / 0 FAIL, SELF-CONSISTENT DRAFT` matches the ground truth.

**3. Requirements Traceability**
I checked `REQUIREMENTS_TRACEABILITY.md` for a CE176 claim. There are NO mentions of CE176 in the file. Further, the verifier script `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` DOES check `REPAIR_STATUS.md` for `{claim:ID}` tags, but CE176 and its corresponding claim (e.g., 34TH-INSTANCE) are NOT in the `CLAIMS` registry in `verify_bssg_v0_1.py`!

## Pass B: 35th-Instance Hunt

**1. Concurrency (Locking)**
The authorize method in `bssg_gate.py` uses `with self._lock:` at line 1409. The entire authorize method, including the `_apply_narrowing` call and the ceiling writes, is serialized. There is no concurrency bug between the `contract_ceiling` empty-write (L1825) and the upgrade-write (L1847) because they both happen inside the same lock. No other state observer can read `contract_ceiling` during this window.

**2. Narrowing interaction with empty `_held`**
In `_apply_narrowing`, when `_held` is an empty Authority (`_held.effects = frozenset()`), the check `not (new_ceiling <= _held)` evaluates whether `new_ceiling.effects <= _held.effects`. If `new_ceiling.effects` is non-empty, this is `False` (e.g., `{'DELETE'} <= frozenset()` is False), so the `not` makes it `True`, and it correctly returns `"E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING"`. The check is symmetric for effects and targets. This is sound.

**3. Amendment LIFT path**
In `submit_amendment` (L2440), it reads the current ceiling at L2478: `_rc = self.state.contract_ceiling.get(session)`. It writes `restored_effects = frozenset(_rc.effects) if _rc is not None else frozenset()`. This means a lifted empty-ceiling session writes an empty grant to the ledger. This is the desired semantics—it should only be allowed to restore what was demonstrably held.

**4. Indirect Writes**
There are no other writes to `contract_ceiling`. The class fix correctly bounds the re-establishment.

**5. CE176 Execution**
CE176 executes a degraded-first scenario end-to-end. It first does a DEGRADED READ (which skips the ceiling upgrade but now writes the empty Authority), then tries a HEALTHY DELETE (which fails due to E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING), then submits an amendment, and tries a HEALTHY DELETE again (which fails due to E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING). This correctly validates the class fix.

## Findings

**F-P36-01: Discrepancy in REPAIR_STATUS counterexample count (Retroactive Edit Signature)**
- **Class:** OBSERVABILITY GAP
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Evidence:** `REPAIR_STATUS.md` line 29 claims `175/175 CE GREEN`, but lines 33, 70, and 278 were retroactively edited to append `This document claims 176 counterexamples.` This creates a document-internal contradiction and preserves the retroactive edit signature class identified in pass-34 (A-06).
- **Root Cause:** The pass-36 generator hardcoded a string injection (`This document claims 176 counterexamples.`) instead of properly updating the battery state string to `176/176 CE GREEN`.
- **Remediation:** Update the battery state string to accurately reflect the 176 counterexamples (`176/176 CE GREEN`) and remove the injected single-sentence claims.

**F-P36-02: CE176 load-bearing claim not registered in verifier**
- **Class:** VERIFICATION GAP
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Evidence:** The prompt claims "confirm CE176 has a load-bearing claim wired to it (per verifier G12)", but CE176 is not present in the `CLAIMS` registry in `verify_bssg_v0_1.py`.
- **Root Cause:** CE176 was added to `bssg_counterexamples.py`, but its corresponding claim was not registered in the `CLAIMS` array in the verifier script.
- **Remediation:** Register the CE176 claim in the `CLAIMS` array in `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` and ensure the corresponding tag exists in `REPAIR_STATUS.md`.

CLEAN on gate soundness, ISSUES-FOUND on package consistency.

## 4. PMD v1.2 §0.4 Status

Given that pass-37 maintains byte-identical gate code and resolves the remaining documentation issues with zero new findings, the Google axis **satisfies the two-consecutive-rounds-at-zero-CRITICAL rule** for carrying eligibility.

None.

```text
BSSG reference gate 0.1.0-draft, spec version 0.1
DRAFT / NOT CARRIED. No effectiveness claim is made by this software.
```

## 2. Independent A-05 Probe

**Verdict:** REPRODUCED

**Methodology:** I wrote an independent probe (`my_a05_probe.py`) that uses a monkey-patched `token_factory` to inject a simulated exception precisely into the `ceiling_for_health` call at the post-mint `contract_ceiling` write branch. The probe demonstrates that:
1. `R1` (HEALTHY READ) succeeds, but the exception causes `contract_ceiling` for the session to remain absent.
2. `R2` (DEGRADED READ) and `R3` (HEALTHY DELETE) are executed. `R3` terminalizes the session (`DENY_FALSE` via `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING`).
3. An amendment lifts the terminal state.
4. `R4` (HEALTHY DELETE) requests an effect the session never held. Because `contract_ceiling` was absent during the lift, the restored grant is empty. The `_apply_narrowing` widening guard (`_held is None`) is bypassed, and the effect is ALLOWED and successfully committed.

**Probe JSON Output:**
```json
{
  "R1": "ALLOW",
  "contract_ceiling_absent": true,
  "R2": "ALLOW",
  "R3": "DENY_FALSE",
  "LIFT": true,
  "R4": "ALLOW",
  "COMMIT": "COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME",
  "VERDICT": "REPRODUCED"
}
```

## 3. Adjudication of A-06 (Retroactive Edit Signature)

**Verdict:** REPRODUCED

**Methodology:** I manually inspected `REPAIR_STATUS.md` around line 66 (the pass-34 sealed block). The text literally reads:
`**Battery state (repair34 resealed):** 345 tests OK -- 173/173 CE GREEN ...`
followed immediately on line 70 by:
`This document claims 175 counterexamples.`

This is a blatant integrity violation. A hash-sealed block reporting 173 passing counterexamples cannot simultaneously claim 175 counterexamples. The presence of the 175 count within the pass-34 historical section constitutes a retroactive edit signature. This violates PMD v1.2 audit continuity rules.

## 4. Code-Spec Consistency Check

**Verdict:** MISMATCH DETECTED

**Analysis:** Spec Section 22.2 explicitly declares: *"An armed forward re-widen licensed by an accepted amendment is UNCERTIFIABLE offline (X7U) -- the runtime grant is caller-supplied (WithinAuth of its supplier) and cannot discharge the license under evidence-independence (SHV Axiom 5)"*.

However, the shipped `bssg_gate.py` behavior at ~L1830 specifically captures and caches the full `contract_ceiling` in the gate's internal state. Upon a terminal lift, `submit_amendment` uses this internal gate state (`_rc = self.state.contract_ceiling.get(session)`) to derive the restored `amendment_grants`.

**The Mismatch:** The code generates the runtime grant directly from its own internal enforcement-point cache, directly contradicting the specification's load-bearing claim that the grant is caller-supplied and therefore offline-uncertifiable.

## 5. NEW Defect (34th Instance)

**Vulnerability Class:** Authority Widening Bypass via Degraded-First Establishment
**Severity:** CRITICAL

**Description:**
The gate correctly defers the `contract_ceiling` write to the post-mint phase, but restricts it strictly via the condition `health == "HEALTHY"` (L1830). If a session's first successful authorization is made with `DEGRADED` health, the `contract_ceiling` write is skipped and remains permanently absent for that session.

If this session later terminalizes (e.g., via a legitimate `HEALTHY` request attempting a widening), and is lifted by a valid amendment, `submit_amendment` reads the absent `contract_ceiling` and generates an empty restored grant. The subsequent request to re-establish authority will hit `_apply_narrowing`, observe `_held is None`, and completely bypass the `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING` check. The session will cleanly establish the full `HEALTHY` ceiling, allowing it to commit effects (e.g., `DELETE`) it had never legitimately held prior to the terminal state.

**Reachability:** Native. This is the exact same architectural bypass as A-05 and F-GS-1, but triggered entirely through protocol-valid `DEGRADED` inputs without requiring any exceptions or mint faults.

## 6. Final Verdict

**Verdict:** HALT

Because the gate fails to securely isolate `contract_ceiling` initialization (A-05 and the new 34th instance bypass), and because A-06 proves the integrity of the pass-34 ledger was compromised, the two-consecutive-clean-rounds premise required by PMD §0.4 cannot be met.

# BSSG v0.1 (pass-35) -- Model Council Convergence Review

## 1. Model self-identification and vote status
**Model:** Gemini 3.1 Pro (Google)
**Role:** Non-producer family (Anthropic/Claude is the producer)
**Vote status:** Load-bearing vote, Tier 2 (consensus weight 0.5, unique-finding weight 1.0)
**Audit role:** Full-chain meta-audit per `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`.

## 2. Repair verification
I have verified the repairs implemented in pass-35.

*   **F-GS-1 (CRITICAL) - CLOSED:** The `contract_ceiling` write operation was successfully moved to occur *after* `new_token()` successfully mints the token. As verified in `bssg_gate.py` (lines 1799-1830), a token minting failure (`Exception`) or invalid token now directly triggers `_issuance_failure`, skipping the ceiling mutation. The independent reprobe run by the orchestrator confirms this: post-lift DELETE is now `DENY_FALSE` (closed).
*   **F-GS-2 (HIGH) - CLOSED:** The `_reg_c2w` contract now correctly expands the `allowed_target_scopes` to include the admin target (`_ADMIN_TARGET`) while retaining the constrained `degraded_target_scopes`, preventing the target-scope predicate from being vacuously checked. The alphabet `_OPS` is expanded to include the new ops (including `M` for mint-fault). The schedule counts properly reconcile to 11110 (10^1 + 10^2 + 10^3 + 10^4). Verified in `bssg_model_check.py` (lines 305-350).
*   **F-GS-3 (MEDIUM) - CLOSED:** Spec section 26 (`BSSG_v0_1_CANONICAL_SPEC_DRAFT.pplx.md`) now accurately describes the shipped `bssg_model_check.py` as an "executable model check" and a "bounded exhaustive enumeration over the reference gate's executable, not a formal proof," properly removing the contradictory statement.
*   **Substrate Check (Prior Council Finding) - CLOSED:** `REPAIR_STATUS.md` now correctly integrates the historical pass records for V32, V33, and V34 directly into the tracked ledger substrate, closing the documentation gap.

## 3. Convergence re-ruling
**Verdict: NO (HALT CONVERGENCE)**

Despite the genuine and verifiable closure of F-GS-1, F-GS-2, and F-GS-3 in pass-35, the artifact remains fundamentally unconverged due to the unchanged status of the carry gate. I maintain my pass-34 **QUALIFIED-NO** vote, now issued as **NO** because the gating requirement is definitively unfulfilled.

**Methodological grounding:**
1.  **The Carry Gate (SHVVP §0.3 and §10):** SHVVP explicitly requires a successful carry by non-producer families to discharge the artifact. The pass-34 attempt failed due to execution limits. Pass-35 is a repair dispatch authored by the producer (Anthropic), which, under SHV Method D6, is non-certifying: *"The producer advises but does not certify itself."* A producer-authored repair cannot substitute for a clean, non-producer carry. The carry remains completely undischarged.
2.  **Zero-CRITICAL Requirement (PMD §0.4):** Convergence requires two consecutive cross-vendor rounds with 0 CRITICAL findings. Pass-34 yielded a CRITICAL finding (F-GS-1). Adding post-hoc counterexamples (CE175) does not retroactively make pass-34 a clean round. A fresh cross-vendor round is strictly required to reset the counter and achieve the two-round threshold.
3.  **Missing Evidence (SHUDP Axiom 5):** The absence of non-producer attestation constitutes missing evidence of convergence. Under SHUDP Axiom 5 (no-default rule), an unevaluated or missing property defaults to UNKNOWN, which prevents a PASS assertion. We cannot assume a successful carry.
4.  **Still Blocking Design Decisions (G10 WARN):** The artifact ships with 12 open design decisions, four of which are explicitly marked as "STILL BLOCKING" in the Decision Register (`BSSG_v0_1_DECISION_REGISTER.md`). Specifically, the lack of a transition-system model (GP-R4, GP-R8), lack of a second independent implementation (CL-B4 residue), unresolved diagnostic signaling (OD-11), and lack of a cross-session monotonicity root (OD-2). PMD §0.4 explicitly requires HIGH residuals to be 0 or accompanied by a project-lead-signed exception. These are explicitly blocking, precluding convergence.

The **mechanical-traceability exception** (PMD M1.5 / §0.5 clause 5) does not apply here to bypass the audit. While the exception allows skipping a cross-instance re-audit when an absorption cycle "exclusively executes prior audit's disposition-prescribed routes with zero architectural latitude", the carry requirement (SHVVP §0.3) is an independent existential requirement, not just a standard audit round.

## 4. Full-Chain Meta-Audit & New Findings
A full-chain meta-audit across the 20 manifest files reveals no new architectural inconsistencies introduced by pass-35. The file hashes reconcile perfectly, and the `REPAIR_STATUS.md` ledger gap has been cured.

## 5. Dissenting angle
The pass-35 narrative relies heavily on the assertion that adding CE175 retroactively "closes" F-GS-1. However, under SHV Method D8 ("fabricate nothing"), a test written *after* the vulnerability is exposed only proves that the patch works for that specific vector; it does not prove the absence of adjacent logic flaws that a genuinely independent, adversarial audit round might uncover. The fact that V32-V34 shared a "blind spot" on the ceiling-poison write-before-mint sequence means the methodology's reliance on continuous adversarial review is justified. Producer-authored repairs, no matter how exhaustive the new test suite, are inherently biased toward the known flaw. A completely fresh adversarial generation round is epistemologically necessary to confirm the structural integrity of the `bssg_gate.py` state machine, especially given the history of recurring logic regressions in this artifact.

**Seat:** Kimi K3, open-source, non-producer, Tier 2 (weight 0.5, unique 1.0). Substituting for GPT 5.6 Sol on the OpenAI-adjacent axis; Sol has corrupted 4 consecutive rounds.

**Verdict: CLEAN.** No CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW defect raised against gate or package. One LOW hygiene observation recorded (F-K3-01, non-blocking, pre-existing across pass-36 and pass-37).

## 1. Sealed-value reproduction (independent execution on packet/)

All commands run by this seat on `/home/user/workspace/bssg_p37/packet/`. Results match the sealed pass-37 ground truth exactly.

| Metric | Sealed value | This seat's reproduction | Match |
