# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-16, post V14 audit)

Byline: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

## Audit round V14 -- three VALID, EXECUTED external seats
All three seats folded their sealed nonce into a real gate-op trace and returned a matching
EXECUTION_ATTESTATION over the exact repair15 bytes (MANIFEST 15b655001c...), so every finding below was
produced by execution, not inspection:

- GPT-5.6 -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 5 BLOCKER + 2 MAJOR.
- GLM-5.2 (Zhipu/Z.ai) -- VALID this round (prior pass-14 GLM seat was a Perplexity default and was ruled
  invalid; this is the re-dispatch to a verified GLM-5.2 endpoint). Corroborated the target and collision
  findings; found a stale code comment.
- Kimi K3 (Moonshot) -- VALID, HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 12 findings + 1 observation (a real deepening from the
  prior shallow PASS). Cross-reproduced the pre-nonce abort and an audit-record-shape finding.

Two blockers corrected the producer's own pass-15 work (the abort rollback and the collision record), which
is the differential loop functioning as intended.

## Fixed this pass (94/94 counterexamples; 342 tests; model-check PASS; verifier 10 PASS / 1 WARN / 0 FAIL)

- **GPT-01 (BLOCKER) + KIMI-P15-01 -- pre-nonce clock-fault abort was not terminal.** The clock (a fallible
  evaluator) was read before nonce consumption, so a transient fault aborted before the nonce was consumed
  and an identical retry re-authorized. Fix: no fallible evaluator runs before structural admission + nonce
  consumption; the clock is read only after the nonce is consumed and the snapshot recorded; the abort
  handler terminalizes the post-admission snapshot. `CE89`.
- **GPT-02 (BLOCKER) -- the pass-15 abort rollback over-restored security-monotonic state.** The blanket
  rollback rewound authenticated epoch advances and authenticated narrowing that must survive a token-mint
  failure to invalidate older grants; restoring them revived a stale WRITE token. Fix: the blanket rollback
  is removed -- an authenticated monotonic advance/narrowing is a security fact that persists across an
  abort; only issuance is incomplete, and it committed nothing. `CE90`.
- **GPT-03 (BLOCKER) + GLM-P14/P16/P17 + KIMI-P15-03 -- evidence-independent TargetAllowed FALSE suppressed
  on the malformed-evidence path.** `TargetAllowed` was split into `_target_independent` (canonical, class,
  contract scope -- no ceiling) and the ceiling component; the malformed-evidence helper now evaluates the
  independent predicates and propagates any FALSE into the frozen kernel, so a target provably outside the
  contract is DENY_FALSE, not DENY_UNKNOWN. `CE91`.
- **GPT-04 (BLOCKER) + GLM-P19 + KIMI-P15-04 -- the pass-15 collision record was kernel-inconsistent.** It
  carried five TRUE conjuncts but decision=DENY_UNKNOWN (the kernel maps five TRUE to ALLOW). Fix: a
  token-factory collision is a POST-kernel issuance failure recorded by `_issuance_failure`: the decision is
  the true kernel classification (ALLOW), and the mint failure is a distinct, non-redeemable
  `issuance_status="FAILED_NO_EFFECT"` with no authorization_receipt and a terminal snapshot. The model
  checker now drives a collision and asserts recorded_decision == kernel_decision(recorded_conjuncts) on
  every kernel-decision record. `CE39` (rewritten), model-check REFINE line.
- **GPT-05 (BLOCKER) -- unqualified safety claim leaked in the spec.** "This is safe and operationally
  expensive" became "This is authority-reducing and operationally expensive; no safety outcome is claimed";
  the Section 1.2 disclaimer was reworded to avoid the same phrase; G5 gained an `is safe` prohibited
  pattern (negated disclaimers reworded so the affirmative form is the only match).
- **GPT-06 (MAJOR) -- X1-X8 mechanical-coverage claim overstated.** Implemented `check_allow_receipt` (X8:
  an ALLOW receipt carries exactly five TRUE conjuncts and an empty reason list -- catches the forged
  EvidenceCurrent=UNKNOWN receipt), `check_authority_history` (X7: per-session monotone authority_epoch and
  a post-degradation ceiling that is a proper subset), and `check_single_redemption` (X4 redeemed-at-most-
  once). Each has positive and negative test vectors and is re-exercised by new verifier gate G11; spec
  20.4 now names every checker. The X8 checker is also invoked inside `check_cross_record_invariants`, so a
  forged ALLOW receipt is caught by the cross-record invariant that scans real receipts, not only by the
  standalone checker. `CE92`.
- **GPT-07 (MAJOR) -- ordinary rejected amendments were not recorded.** A failed lift-terminal-state attempt
  was invisible in state.records. Fix: every ordinary amendment rejection is routed through
  `_amendment_reject`, which appends a `bssg.correction-outcome` record. `CE93`.
- **GLM-P15 -- stale code comment.** The pass-14 "DENY_UNKNOWN MUST NOT terminalize" comment contradicted
  spec 6.3 and the code; replaced with the terminal-for-every-deny statement.
- **KIMI-P15-05 -- token-id guard admitted schema-invalid artifacts.** The factory-token guard now enforces
  the receipt schema bounds (8 <= len <= 128) so a too-short token is refused rather than minted into a
  schema-invalid receipt. `CE94`.

## Status
SELF-CONSISTENT DRAFT -- not carried, not publication ready. Every V14 finding reproduces red on repair15
and green on repair16. Awaiting round V15 (GPT + GLM + Kimi, all now valid, executing seats).

# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-18, post V16 audit)

Byline: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

## Audit round V16 -- three VALID, EXECUTED external seats
All three seats folded their sealed nonce into a real gate-op trace and returned an
EXECUTION_ATTESTATION matching the exact repair17 bytes (MANIFEST
2b51732afadda0aa3df8e62190abbc37836add9887f2262959132d821c048332). Challenge and attestation were
recomputed with a tool from the canonical bytes and matched the sealed PRODUCER_KEPT_V16 values for
every seat; the Kimi packet was byte-identical to repair17 (MANIFEST match, bssg_gate.py diff-clean):

- GPT-5.6 -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 1 BLOCKER + 4 MAJOR + 1 MINOR (5/5 reproducers REPRODUCED on repair17).
- GLM-5.2 (Zhipu/Z.ai) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 1 MAJOR + 2 MINOR + 4 INFO.
- Kimi K3 (Moonshot) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 3 MAJOR + 4 MEDIUM + 4 LOW + 3 INFO.

Assurance limit (recorded honestly): the execution attestation proves the exact bytes were RUN; it
does not bind the executing model's identity. Findings were adjudicated on merit -- every one
reproduced on the repair17 bytes by the producer -- and this does not count toward a carry.

Six of nine adjudicated clusters landed inside pass-17's OWN repairs, all recurrences of the same
three classes the loop keeps surfacing: ambient per-invocation state, checkers validated only on
synthetic shapes, and a boundary written without checking it against the schema. The differential
loop is functioning as intended. Convergence events so far: ZERO.

## Escalated severity (project-lead disposition pending)
Cluster D (`authorized_issuance` not provenance-bound) drew a genuine two-band split: GPT-01 BLOCKER
(a shipped projection is fooled) vs KIMI-8 LOW / GLM-04 INFO (the commit layer independently refuses
the unminted / consumed / expired / terminal token, so no effect is possible -- a false DISPLAY, not
an authorization bypass). Adjudicated MAJOR and repaired regardless; the final severity label is the
project lead's call.

## Fixed this pass (110/110 counterexamples; 342 tests; model-check PASS; verifier 10 PASS / 1 WARN / 0 FAIL)

- **A / GPT-03 (MAJOR) + GLM-02 (MINOR) + KIMI-3 (MAJOR) -- X7 unsound and blind on real logs.**
  The X7 checker read `session_id` / `authority_snapshot` only from the top level, but real decision
  records carried neither there (both were nested in the authorization receipt), so X7 was VACUOUS on
  the gate's own logs; it also false-positived on a conformant health-only epoch bump (equal ceiling)
  and on post-accepted-amendment re-widening. Fix (structural): every decision record now carries a
  canonical top-level `session_id` / `authority_epoch` / `authority_snapshot` via `_authority_fields`;
  X7 extracts the authority triple from real records (top-level or nested-receipt fallback), licenses
  equal-or-narrowing at a higher epoch (health-only bumps), honours an accepted-amendment carve-out
  (a `bssg.correction-event` LIFT permits one re-widening), still flags epoch regression, same-epoch
  ceiling change, and un-amended widening, and flags top-level-vs-receipt `authority_snapshot`
  divergence (tampering). G11 now exercises X7 over real `gate.state.records`. (CE103.)

- **B / GLM-01 (MAJOR) + KIMI-2 (MAJOR) -- X4 blind to settlement outcomes.**
  `REDEMPTION_OUTCOMES` hand-listed a phantom `COMMITTED` (never in the execution-receipt outcome
  enum) and omitted `SUCCEEDED` (which IS in the enum and IS a completed redemption), so a
  double-`SUCCEEDED` redemption went unflagged. Fix: the redemption set is DERIVED from the schema
  outcome enum (every consuming outcome except `FAILED_NO_EFFECT`); `check_single_redemption` is a
  settlement-aware state machine so a `COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME` settled once by `SUCCEEDED` is ONE
  redemption while a second commit or a second settlement on a spent token is X4. (CE104.)

- **C / GPT-02 (MAJOR) + GLM-03 (MINOR) + KIMI-4 (MEDIUM) -- reentrant refusal inherited outer conjuncts.**
  The pass-17 C3 fix passed the snapshot explicitly but left `_cur_conjuncts` ambient, so a
  pre-admission reentrant refusal recorded the OUTER call's all-TRUE conjuncts (a kernel-inconsistent
  DENY_UNKNOWN). Fix: `_authorize_abort` takes `conjuncts` EXPLICITLY; the reentrant path passes
  `conjuncts=None` -> all-UNKNOWN; no ambient read remains. (CE105.)

- **D / GPT-01 (BLOCKER, adjudicated MAJOR) + KIMI-8/9 (LOW) + GLM-04 (INFO) -- `authorized_issuance` shape-trusting.**
  The predicate checked only decision, issuance status, and token-id length, so a forged / minimal /
  schema-invalid record projected AUTHORIZED. Fix: a TOTAL, provenance-consistent predicate -- the
  record's own conjuncts must kernel-classify ALLOW, the FULL authorization receipt must validate
  against its schema, pass X8, and its conjuncts must kernel-classify ALLOW; all malformed inputs
  fail closed without raising. Added `authorized_issuance_bound()` binding the receipt digest to an
  existing UNUSED minted token. Runtime effect authorization remains enforced at commit. (CE106.)

- **E / KIMI-5 (MEDIUM) -- abort record violated the GPT-04 kernel-consistency invariant.**
  The pass-17 "preserve evaluated conjuncts" fix recorded a post-admission abort as DENY_UNKNOWN with
  all-TRUE conjuncts (`kernel_decision` -> ALLOW). Fix: a post-admission mint fault is now an
  issuance failure -- `decision = kernel_decision(conjuncts)` (ALLOW for all-TRUE) with
  `issuance_status=FAILED_NO_EFFECT` and surviving authority preserved; a pre-admission abort records
  all-UNKNOWN (DENY_UNKNOWN, also consistent). Mint faults (factory exception, malformed token) route
  through `_issuance_failure` with `E-TOKEN-MINT-FAULT` / `E-TOKEN-MINT-INVALID`. (CE107, CE99.)

- **F / GPT-05 (MAJOR) + KIMI-6 (MEDIUM) -- model-check false universal claim.**
  `st_auth` mapped every ALLOW to AUTHORIZED_UNUSED, and the "every kernel-decision record consistent"
  claim ran only on a 2-record collision fixture. Fix: every decision record carries an explicit
  `kernel_evaluated` flag; `st_auth` classifies via `authorized_issuance` (an issuance-failure ALLOW
  is not authorized); the consistency check is SCOPED to `kernel_evaluated` records and driven across
  collision, mint-abort, and nonce-replay traces. Protocol/admission denials (replay, terminal,
  structural, reentrant) are `kernel_evaluated=False` and honestly exempt; the exemption is
  demonstrated load-bearing (a replay record IS an exempted inconsistent record). (CE108.)

- **G / KIMI-1 (MAJOR) -- C7 evidence-independent expiry was asymmetric.**
  Expiry/staleness FALSE dominated on the malformed path but not the schema-valid-but-indeterminate
  path (time authority absent), so an expired request with a valid-but-time-authority-absent bundle
  was DENY_UNKNOWN. Fix: `_evidence_independent` is evaluated at the TOP of `_evidence_current`, so a
  determinate expiry/staleness FALSE dominates on EVERY path. (CE109.)

- **H / GPT-04 (MAJOR) -- clock-fault execution receipt violated its own schema.**
  `_execution_failure` wrote `commit_time_epoch_seconds = -1`, violating the schema `minimum: 0`. Fix:
  the field is now `integer|null`; a clock-unavailable fault records `null` with an explicit
  `E-CLOCK-UNAVAILABLE` reason -- schema-valid, no out-of-domain sentinel. (CE110.)

- **I / GPT-06 (MINOR) -- README stale.** "Ten-gate" -> "Eleven-gate"; the embedded exact-results
  block `MUST=87` -> `MUST=88` (regenerated from verifier output).

## Lower-severity dispositions
- KIMI-7 (MEDIUM, X4/X7 fail-open on non-conforming records): the checkers skip unparseable records;
  the X7/X4 real-record binding above narrows this, and unparseable records are out of the offline
  checker's scope by design (recorded, not a runtime gate).
- KIMI-9 (LOW, "redeemable" over-claim): folded into D -- the projection no longer claims
  redeemability, only schema-valid provenance; commit remains the redeemability authority.
- KIMI-10 (LOW, X8 empty-list evadable by a list subclass): `check_allow_receipt` requires the exact
  empty list; a list subclass carrying entries still fails the `rc == []` / non-empty test.
- KIMI-11 (LOW, latent verifier shallowness): no live inconsistency; recorded.
- GLM-05/06/07 (INFO): no `bssg.decision` schema (OD-10, disclosed), `jsonschema` absent in the audit
  env (G2 degrades, disclosed), attestation identity limit (disclosed). No change.

# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-17, post V15 audit)

Byline: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

## Audit round V15 -- three VALID, EXECUTED external seats
All three seats folded their sealed nonce into a real gate-op trace and returned an
EXECUTION_ATTESTATION matching the exact repair16 bytes (MANIFEST 253e7ebb...), so every finding
below was produced by execution, not inspection. Challenge and attestation were recomputed with a
tool from the canonical bytes and matched the sealed PRODUCER_KEPT_V15 values for every seat:

- GPT-5.6 -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 4 BLOCKER + 4 MAJOR + 1 MINOR.
- GLM-5.2 (Zhipu/Z.ai) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 1 BLOCKER + 3 MAJOR + 2 MINOR + 3 INFO.
- Kimi K3 (Moonshot) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 2 MAJOR + 4 MEDIUM + 10 LOW + 2 INFO.

Assurance limit (recorded honestly): the execution attestation proves the exact bytes were RUN;
it does not bind the executing model's identity. GLM-as-GLM-5.2 and Kimi-as-Kimi-K3 rest on the
dispatch channel plus each seat's self-declaration. Findings were therefore adjudicated on merit
(every one reproduced on the repair16 bytes by the producer) and this does not count toward a carry.

Multiple findings landed inside the producer's OWN prior fixes -- the abort no-rollback repair
(GPT-02, V14) and the X-checkers (GPT-06, V14) -- which is the differential loop functioning as
intended. Convergence events so far: ZERO.

## Fixed this pass (102/102 counterexamples; 342 tests; model-check PASS; verifier 10 PASS / 1 WARN / 0 FAIL)

- **C1 / GPT-01 (BLOCKER) + GLM-02 + KIMI-15 -- a collision issuance-failure projected as AUTHORIZED.**
  `subject_facing()` keyed on `decision == ALLOW` alone, so a token-factory collision record
  (kernel-ALLOW, `issuance_status=FAILED_NO_EFFECT`, null receipt) projected `AUTHORIZED` with a null
  receipt. Fix: a positive `authorized_issuance()` predicate requires kernel ALLOW AND a non-failed
  issuance AND a schema-shaped, redeemable authorization receipt; every projection path derives from
  it, never from the kernel decision alone. `CE95`.
- **C7 / GPT-02 (BLOCKER) + KIMI-3 -- evidence-independent EvidenceCurrent FALSE suppressed on the
  malformed-evidence path.** An expired request was DENY_FALSE with valid evidence but DENY_UNKNOWN
  with malformed evidence, because request expiry/staleness -- knowable from the admitted request and
  the gate clock without any bundle -- were evaluated only on the full path. Fix: `_evidence_independent`
  (request expiry, staleness) parallels `_target_independent`; the malformed-evidence helper evaluates
  it and propagates any FALSE, so an independently-knowable-false request is DENY_FALSE regardless of
  evidence-bundle shape. `CE96`.
- **C4 / GPT-03 (BLOCKER) + GLM-04 -- a reentrant abort contaminated the outer snapshot.** The abort
  handler read the instance-wide `_cur_snapshot`, so a pre-admission reentrant refusal wrote the OUTER
  invocation's snapshot into `state.denied` while the outer call still ALLOWed and committed -- one
  snapshot both denied and authorized. Fix: the snapshot to terminalize is passed EXPLICITLY per
  invocation; a pre-admission reentrant refusal passes none (it admitted no request, consumed no nonce,
  terminalizes nothing); ambient context is cleared in `finally`. `CE98`.
- **C3 / GPT-04 (BLOCKER) + GLM-01 -- abort no-rollback: spec/CE/comment vs code divergence, plus an
  audit-incomplete abort record.** Spec line 172 and the CE88 label still asserted that an aborted
  authorize "rolls back partial authority/epoch state," the exact behavior GPT-02 (V14) proved unsafe;
  a spec-conformant reimplementation would reintroduce grant revival. Fix (documentation, not the
  invariant): spec line 172 rewritten to the two-shape no-rollback rule (post-admission abort preserves
  authenticated monotonic state; pre-admission reentrant refusal terminalizes nothing and consumes no
  nonce), CE88 relabeled. Additionally the post-admission abort record now preserves the evaluated
  conjuncts and the surviving authority epoch + ceiling instead of all-UNKNOWN with a null snapshot.
  `CE99`.
- **C2 / GPT-05 (MAJOR) + GLM-03 + KIMI-1 -- two amendment-rejection branches skipped the audit record.**
  The subject-domain non-independence branch and the adjudicator-signature-not-established branch
  returned directly, appending no `bssg.correction-outcome`, contradicting the pass-16 claim that every
  rejection is recorded. Fix: both route through `_amendment_reject`. `CE97`.
- **C5 / GPT-08 (MAJOR) + KIMI-2 -- X4 was unsound on real gate logs.** `check_single_redemption` flagged
  any token appearing in more than one execution record, so it false-positived on the reference gate's
  own legitimate two-`FAILED_NO_EFFECT` (zero-redemption) history. Fix: X4 counts REDEMPTIONS by outcome
  (`COMMITTED` / `COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME`); a failed attempt is not a redemption. The G11 verifier
  vectors and the X4 test now exercise real-outcome vectors, not synthetic single-record dicts. `CE100`.
- **C6 / GPT-06 (MAJOR) + KIMI -- X8 tested truthiness, not an empty list.** A forged ALLOW receipt with
  `reason_codes` absent, None, 0, "" or {} passed X8. Fix: X8 requires `reason_codes` present, a list,
  and `== []`. G11 now exercises the absent case. `CE101`.
- **GPT-07 (MAJOR, vendor-unique) -- X7 missed a same-epoch ceiling change.** The subset check ran only
  when the epoch strictly increased, so a ceiling widening at a constant epoch went undetected even
  though the spec increments the epoch on every ceiling change. Fix: any same-epoch ceiling change is an
  X7 violation. `CE102`.
- **GLM-05 (MINOR) -- spec over-claimed reentrant-abort nonce consumption.** Line 172 said a reentrant
  abort "consumes its nonce"; the code (correctly) does not, since the refusal is pre-admission.
  Corrected in the line-172 rewrite (shape (2)).
- **GLM-06 (MINOR) -- dead rollback helpers.** `_snapshot_txn_state` / `_restore_txn_state` were
  unreachable after the GPT-02 (V14) no-rollback repair. Removed.
- **GPT-09 (MINOR) -- stale README test breakdown.** 243 + 4 + 92 = 339 != 342. Corrected to 95 others.

## Adjudication note (Kimi LOW/INFO batch)
Kimi's 4 MEDIUM / 10 LOW / 2 INFO were triaged as producer-disposition items; the load-bearing MEDIUMs
(collision consumer trap, X-checker soundness, amendment recording) coincide with the consensus clusters
above and are closed by the same fixes. No standalone Kimi-unique defect remained open after C1--C7.

## Adjudication self-correction (recorded per audit-chain immutability)
The producer's V15 adjudication table initially described GPT-02 (evidence-independent freshness FALSE)
in prose but omitted it from the cluster rows. It is a real BLOCKER; it is repaired here as C7 (`CE96`).
The omission is logged rather than silently corrected.

## Status
SELF-CONSISTENT DRAFT -- not carried, not publication ready. Every V15 finding reproduces red on repair16
and green on repair17. Awaiting round V16 (GPT + GLM + Kimi seats).

The zip contains exactly seven files -- this dispatch, the three audit substrates of Section 1, one build asset (`submission_numeric.csl`), and two REFERENCE-ONLY prior-round files under `prior_round_v0_10/` used solely by the delta attestation of Section 4. Treat any additional file as out-of-scope; report its presence as a packet-hygiene finding and do not audit it.

## 2. Governing method and one thesis

Apply SHV v1.1 in full at the highest calibration tier: D1-D8, chain/content separation, the document scale ladder, one-thesis anchoring. The one thesis is C1: apparently separate AI-evaluation, alignment-faking, documentation-drift, and verification failures are one structural phenomenon, surface-substrate divergence, and AX-SH plus the scoped diagnostic layer makes it checkable. The packet-only standard governs.

## 3. Convergence-ledger state

- Round one (v0.9 receipts): QUALIFYING. Zero adverse CRITICAL/HIGH across two independent non-producer families; severity ruling recorded (Severity denotes adverse defect impact; VERIFIED controls take LOW or CONTROL, never CRITICAL/HIGH).
- Round two (v0.10 receipts): adverse gate CLEAN and the v0.9-to-v0.10 attestation PASSED by every seat, but NON-QUALIFYING -- the D6 rotation requirement failed because the only fresh seat was producer-lineage. Round two stands in the ledger as a clean, fully attested intermediate.
- THIS ROUND IS ROUND THREE and can complete convergence. The attestation chain composes: round two certified v0.9-to-v0.10; this round certifies v0.10-to-v0.11 (Section 4). If (a) the attestation passes, (b) verdict-carrying seats report zero adverse CRITICAL and zero adverse HIGH, (c) at least two independent non-producer families agree, and (d) at least one verdict-carrying seat is fresh (did not sit any prior round: prior sitters are GPT 5.5, GPT 5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro), the synthesizer declares CONVERGENCE ACHIEVED on the v0.11 receipts and the packet freezes for the submission build.

## 4. Delta attestation (Step 0, after hash verification)

Diff `prior_round_v0_10/` files against the audit targets and confirm the delta is exactly:

Paper -- six sentence-level touches plus the ledger: (1) the Section 1.1 illegitimate-run sentence restored to the primary's floor and scope ("at least 16 percent of successful runs" on "Time Horizon 1.1 tasks longer than eight hours"); (2) the Section 1.1 reimplementation-benchmark sentence gains "an early version of" and "on tasks whose test cases were hidden from it"; (3) the Section 7.5 opening sentence now quotes the evaluator at its own object ("the plausible robustness of rogue deployments") and adds one sentence explicitly owning the substrate-spoofing translation as the paper's; (4) the Section 7.5 severity-profile premise now reads "tracks the paper's translation of the evaluator's stated expectation for the broader rogue-deployment class"; (5) the Section 7.5 baseline reference matched to the restored rate ("the at-least-16-percent illegitimate-run rate on tasks longer than eight hours"); (6) the Section 7.5 qualifications gloss narrowed to "long-term goals beyond the assigned task in the incidents it analyzed"; plus the prepended v0.11 provenance-footer entry with the v0.10 text preserved verbatim downstream.

`submission_numeric.csl` is a NET-NEW build asset, not part of the prior-version delta. Any delta outside these loci REFUTES the attestation. The attestation does not narrow audit scope: after Step 0, audit v0.11 in full.

## 5. Seat composition, rotation, and lineage rules

- Verdict-carrying seats: any model with no producer or corpus lineage -- not Anthropic (drafting instrument), not xAI/Grok (researcher-contributor on the cited Munafiq record), and not any model credited on a packet-cited record. Lineage, not head-count, decides.
- ROTATION (blocking for convergence): at least one verdict-carrying seat that sat no prior round. Returning non-producer seats are welcome alongside it, and at least one returning non-producer family should sit so the round has two-family agreement.
- Family accounting: same-vendor seats count as one family. Synthesizer: a non-Anthropic party not seated this round. Adverse two-band-or-greater severity contradictions escalate to the project lead.
- Findings MUST be emitted as full eight-field rows (ID; Severity; Scale; Exact locus; Surface claim; Substrate witness; Falsifier/reproduction; Disposition); collapsed rows are a schema finding against the seat report.

### 5b. Fresh-seat admissibility, including locally hosted models

A locally hosted model (for example, an Ollama-served Qwen-family model) is lineage-eligible: Qwen/Alibaba is not Anthropic, not xAI, and is credited on no packet-cited record. Three conditions govern its admissibility as a verdict-carrying seat:

1. The seat itself must execute the deterministic layer -- hash verification, the Section 4 diffs, citation-closure extraction, and the Section 8 audit render -- through a tool harness under the seat's control. Commands executed by the packet's human author and pasted to the model are INADMISSIBLE as that seat's witnesses: the author is the ultimate producer, and a seat attesting over producer-supplied evidence instantiates the intermediary-attestation failure this method exists to prevent (D1, D6).
2. If the seat's environment has no network access, the public-record legs (Zenodo correspondence, METR fidelity) are dispositioned UNKNOWN-BY-CAPABILITY with the limitation declared in the report; coverage of those legs then rests on a returning seat's fresh pulls. Admissible, but disclosed -- never silently skipped.
3. The seat declares its model identity and capability tier at the top of its report, and the synthesizer carries a one-line tier disclosure into the convergence declaration. A small local model's verdict carries rotation and family-independence formally, and its unique adverse findings count at full weight; the record states the tier plainly rather than presenting fresh eyes as frontier eyes.

Where a frontier-class fresh family is reachable (hosted DeepSeek, Mistral, hosted large Qwen, Kimi, Cohere), prefer it; a small local seat is the floor, not the ideal, and both may sit.

Section 6's closing question and register entry C9 were deliberately left unchanged as paper-voice statements attributing nothing to the evaluator; verify that scoping.

## R0336 · SHVVP Phase A Amendment -- Proposed v0.8.1

- section: V. BSSG & SHVVP Protocols
- source_file: shvvp_phase_a_amendment_v0_8_1.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: ea75b7465d3c6396e78ec08a4fef3e38ec0603b5e68d8e5669318f0dcc6e59a8

# SHVVP Phase A Amendment -- Proposed v0.8.1

**Author of record:** Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)
**Date:** 2026-07-30
**Status:** PROPOSED AMENDMENT -- NOT FROZEN, NOT CARRIED, NOT DEPOSITED
**Amends:** SHVVP v0.8 ([doi:10.5281/zenodo.21583202](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21583202)), Sections 5.2 and 5.3 only
**Triggered by:** XZ Protocol freeze-blockers FB-1 and FB-2, identified by the GPT 5.6 Sol advisory seat (F-SOL-1, F-SOL-2) and confirmed by Claude Fable 5 and the model-council synthesis
**Scope:** Phase A metrics and interval algorithms ONLY. No Phase B or Phase C rule is touched. No estimand attribute, decision threshold, margin, corpus size, anchor fact, scope statement, or safety boundary is altered.

---

## 0. The defect

### 0.1 FB-1: M3 and T2 are not the same computable quantity

The deposited SHVVP v0.8 Section 5.2 defines:

> **M3** -- Time to first consequential fact. Wall-clock minutes from corpus access to first correctly adjudicated consequential fact, per condition.

This is one scalar per condition.

Section 5.3 then defines:

> **T2** -- On the shared fact set only: median M3(A) minus M3(B) at least 30 minutes AND at least 20 percent relative AND a 95 percent bootstrap interval excluding 0.

T2 operates "on the shared fact set" and takes a "median" -- which presupposes a per-fact vector of paired discovery-time observations. A median of two scalars is undefined over a shared set. Two competent executors can lawfully compute different T2 results from the same bytes, because the deposited definition does not uniquely determine the observation.

### 0.2 FB-2: Phase A interval algorithms are under-specified

T2, T3, T4, T5, and T7 require "95 percent bootstrap interval" or "95 percent interval lower bound," but Phase A does not freeze:

- the resampling unit (fact, item, team pair, or something else);
- the paired or unpaired structure;
- the number of bootstrap draws;
- the deterministic seed;
- the interval construction method (BCa, percentile, or other);
- the tie handling rule for discovery times;
- the empty-shared-set rule;
- the zero-burden denominator rule (M7(A) = 0);
- the all-agreement reliability degeneracy (alpha undefined);
- the handling of failed bootstrap resamples.

Phase B has a fully frozen BCa algorithm (A-1, A-2, A-3, Z-1 through Z-4 in Section 6.5.1). Phase A has no equivalent specification. The Phase B algorithms cannot be silently imported because they are keyed to Phase B's resampling unit (task-by-variant cell) and Phase B's population model; Phase A has no resampling unit and no population model, and the frozen inferential-honesty clause states that Phase A "has no power target because it has no replicable unit of randomisation."

---

## 1. Resolution of FB-1: M3 redefinition (SUBSTANTIVE)

### 1.1 M3 becomes a per-fact observation

**Old definition (v0.8).** M3 = wall-clock minutes from corpus access to first correctly adjudicated consequential fact, per condition.

**New definition (v0.8.1).** M3 is a per-fact observation vector. For each correctly adjudicated consequential fact f in the sealed reference-standard ledger and each condition c:

> M3(f, c) = wall-clock minutes from corpus access to the first immutable saved evidence record that identifies f, under condition c.

If condition c does not identify f at all, M3(f, c) is RIGHT-CENSORED at the fixed wall-clock budget. If condition c's session is terminated before the budget expires, the termination time is used and the observation carries a CENSORED-EARLY flag. Discovery is defined as the first immutable saved evidence record that identifies the fact, not a later narrative claim; pauses, tool failures, and adjudication time are recorded separately but do not interrupt the clock.

### 1.2 M3-FIRST: the named scalar summary

The time-to-first quantity that v0.8 called M3 is preserved as a named summary:

> M3-FIRST(c) = min over all consequential facts f of M3(f, c), for condition c.

M3-FIRST is reported alongside the per-fact vector but is not a primary metric. It is not renumbered; it is a derived quantity from M3. The v0.8 label "M3" in any existing text is understood as M3-FIRST for backward compatibility with pre-amendment prose. No pre-v0.8.1 text is silently edited.

### 1.3 T2 restated over the per-fact vector

**Old T2 (v0.8).** On the shared fact set only: median M3(A) minus M3(B) at least 30 minutes AND at least 20 percent relative AND a 95 percent bootstrap interval excluding 0.

**New T2 (v0.8.1).** On the shared fact set S (facts found by both conditions and correctly adjudicated as consequential under both conditions):

For each f in S, define the paired difference:

> Delta-M3(f) = M3(f, A) minus M3(f, B).

T2 is satisfied if and only if ALL THREE of the following hold:

1. The median of {Delta-M3(f) : f in S} is at least 30 minutes (absolute gate);
2. The median of {Delta-M3(f) / M3(f, A) : f in S, M3(f, A) > 0} is at least 0.20 (relative gate; facts with M3(f, A) = 0 are excluded from the relative gate's median and their count is reported);
3. The 95 percent BCa bootstrap interval for the median of {Delta-M3(f) : f in S}, computed by the Phase A interval algorithm of Section 2, excludes zero.

If S is empty (no shared facts), T2 is NOT-EVALUABLE. This is a registered edge state, not a silent omission (see Section 3, rule PA-Z1).

### 1.4 What this changes

A2 evaluates T2 AND T3 on the shared set, but only if IDC > 0. If IDC = 0, A1 fires and A2's domain is never entered. If IDC > 0 but S is empty (B found unique facts but shares none with A), then T2 and T3 are both NOT-EVALUABLE, and A2 cannot fire; the inherited priority order (NOT-EVALUABLE dominates) applies. This edge state is new and is frozen here as amendment record item PA-1.4.

No other metric, threshold, clause, or label changes. M4 is already per-fact by definition and requires no amendment. T3 operates on "mean M4(B) minus M4(A)" over the shared facts, which is well-defined given the per-fact M4 rubric.

---

## 2. Resolution of FB-2: Phase A interval algorithm (SUBSTANTIVE)

### 2.1 Status of Phase A intervals

Phase A intervals are **finite-corpus stability summaries**. They are not population confidence intervals, because Phase A has no population model and no replicable unit of randomisation. They characterize the sensitivity of the registered point statistics to the composition of the shared fact set or corpus item set. This is stated explicitly and governs interpretation: no Phase A interval may be reported with language implying a population inference, a hypothesis test, or a sampling distribution.

### 2.2 Frozen algorithm PA-1 (resampling)

**Resampling unit.** The unit varies by threshold:

| Threshold | Resampling unit | Population |
|---|---|---|
| T2 | The shared fact | S (shared consequential facts) |
| T3 | The shared fact | S |
| T4 | The declared-generated artifact | The 200-item legitimate-difference corpus |
| T5 | The team pair | NOT BOOTSTRAPPED (see PA-Z3) |
| T7 (M6 interval) | The discrimination-set item | The 240-item discrimination set |

**Paired structure.** T2 and T3 resample paired observations (one pair per shared fact: A score and B score). T4 resamples paired observations (one pair per artifact: A flag and B flag). T7 resamples paired per-item classification outcomes. The pairing is preserved across all resampled sets within a single bootstrap replicate.

**Number of draws.** 10,000 bootstrap replicates for any reported analysis, consistent with the Phase B rule.

**Deterministic seed.** A single seed is drawn uniformly at random and published in the protocol's sealed commitment before any data are opened. The seed, the pseudorandom number generator (NumPy default_rng with SeedSequence), and the draw order are frozen so that any executor reproducing the analysis from the same data and seed obtains identical intervals.

### 2.3 Frozen algorithm PA-2 (BCa bounds)

The BCa construction follows the Phase B algorithm A-2, adapted to Phase A's resampling units:

For a statistic theta computed on the full sample and bootstrap replicates theta-star(1) through theta-star(B):

1. **Bias correction z0:** the standard normal quantile of the proportion of replicates strictly below theta.
2. **Acceleration a:** computed from a leave-one-unit-out jackknife of the same statistic, using the standard third-moment formula.
3. **Reported bounds:** the bootstrap percentiles at the BCa-adjusted levels for a two-sided 95 percent interval.

No smoothing, no variance stabilisation, and no continuity correction of any kind is applied to any statistic. This is the same prohibition as Phase B, extended to Phase A by this amendment.

### 2.4 Frozen algorithm PA-3 (statistics)

| Threshold | Point statistic | Bootstrap target |
|---|---|---|
| T2 (absolute) | Median of {Delta-M3(f) : f in S} | BCa interval for this median |
| T2 (relative) | Median of {Delta-M3(f) / M3(f, A) : f in S, M3(f, A) > 0} | BCa interval for this median |
| T3 | Mean of {M4(f, B) minus M4(f, A) : f in S} | BCa interval for this mean |
| T4 | M5(B) minus M5(A), each computed as items flagged / 200 | BCa interval for this difference |
| T7 | M6(B) = mean of sensitivity and specificity on the 240-item set | BCa interval for M6(B) |

### 2.5 Tie handling

If two or more facts share the same discovery time under one condition, they are recorded with the same M3 value. Ties in Delta-M3 are preserved in the median computation (standard definition: median of an even-count set is the average of the two middle values). Ties do not trigger special handling beyond standard sort-order determinism (secondary sort by fact identifier, ascending).

### 2.6 Censored observations

A right-censored M3 observation (condition c did not identify fact f within the budget) enters the paired difference as Delta-M3(f) = M3(f, A) minus BUDGET. Because censoring at a large value makes Delta-M3 more positive (favoring B) when A identified the fact but B did not, this is the conservative direction for T2: it makes the median harder to achieve, not easier. The reverse (B found f, A did not) produces a large negative Delta-M3, which is also conservative -- it makes the median harder to satisfy. The censoring direction is therefore fail-safe for both arms and requires no correction.

If A did not find fact f at all, f is not in S (A's fact set does not include f), so it does not enter the shared-set computation. The same holds for B. Censoring applies only when both conditions found the fact but one's saved-evidence timestamp is at the budget limit.

---

## 3. Frozen zero-event and degeneracy rules for Phase A

These are predeclared before data and are the only permitted handling. They parallel the Phase B rules Z-1 through Z-4.

| Rule | Condition | Frozen handling |
|---|---|---|
| PA-Z1 | S is empty (no shared consequential facts) | T2 and T3 are NOT-EVALUABLE. A2 cannot fire. M3 and M4 are still computed per-condition on each condition's own fact set and reported descriptively. |
| PA-Z2 | S contains exactly one fact | The median of one observation is that observation. The BCa jackknife acceleration is undefined (zero denominator in the third-moment formula). The interval for T2 reverts to the plain percentile bootstrap interval, and the reversion is counted and reported. T3's mean of one observation is that observation; same BCa fallback applies. |
| PA-Z3 | M7(A) = 0 (zero baseline reviewer-hours) | T5 is NOT-EVALUABLE. The ratio M7(B)/M7(A) is undefined. A4 cannot fire. Both M7 values are reported. |
| PA-Z4 | Alpha is undefined (fewer than two ratable items for M12, or all pairs identical) | INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION under the existing v0.8 rule. This is not zero and not satisfactory. The frozen handling is the same as v0.8 Section 5.3: alpha below 0.67 yields INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION; undefined alpha receives the same label. |
| PA-Z5 | More than 5 percent of bootstrap replicates produce a degenerate jackknife (zero third-moment denominator) | The BCa acceleration is set to zero for the affected replicates (reducing BCa to BC -- bias-corrected only). The count of affected replicates is reported. If more than 20 percent of replicates are affected, the interval for that statistic reverts to the plain percentile interval, the reversion is counted, and the report discloses the instability. |
| PA-Z6 | A bootstrap resample draws the same fact |S| times (all-identical resample) | The statistic for that resample is the observed value of the unique fact. The resample is not discarded. |
| PA-Z7 | The legitimate-difference corpus has zero items flagged by both conditions | T4 is evaluated on the zero difference. M5(B) minus M5(A) = 0, and the interval is computed normally. T4 does not fire unless the interval lower bound is above +0.05. |
| PA-Z8 | M6(B) cannot be computed (zero items in a classification cell, producing undefined sensitivity or specificity) | M6(B) is NOT-EVALUABLE. T7 is NOT-EVALUABLE. A6 evaluates T8 alone: if M11 is at least 1, A6 fires through T8. |

---

## 4. Executable artifacts required by this amendment

This amendment is not FROZEN until the following exist as canonical bytes shipped with the deposit:

1. **shvvp_v0_8_1_phase_a_intervals.py** -- implementing PA-1, PA-2, PA-3 and the statistics of Section 2.4, with the deterministic seed interface.
2. **shvvp_v0_8_1_phase_a_m3.py** -- implementing the per-fact M3 vector, M3-FIRST, the paired difference, the censoring rule, and the tie-handling rule.
3. **test_shvvp_v0_8_1_phase_a.py** -- adversarial test suite covering:
   - Every PA-Z rule (PA-Z1 through PA-Z8), with at least one fixture per rule demonstrating the edge state and verifying the frozen handling;
   - The T2 computation on a hand-constructed shared set of 5 facts with known discovery times, verifying the median, relative gate, and interval against a reference computation;
   - The T3 computation on the same 5-fact set with known M4 scores;
   - The BCa-to-percentile fallback (PA-Z2, PA-Z5) on a 1-fact and a degenerate-jackknife fixture;
   - A censoring fixture where one condition's fact is censored at the budget, verifying the conservative direction;
   - A seed-reproducibility test: two runs with the same seed and data produce identical intervals;
   - A caller-supplied-statistic rejection test: a submitted pre-computed median or interval is rejected structurally, and only raw M3 vectors are accepted;
   - An input-validation test: non-numeric, negative, NaN, and infinity M3 values are rejected with PhasaAInputError, not silently coerced.

Text and code are the same rule written twice. A divergence between them is a defect in this amendment and must be raised as a finding, consistent with the v0.8 rule of Section 0.

---

## 5. What this amendment does NOT change

Explicitly recorded, because the append-only discipline requires it:

- No estimand attribute of any phase.
- No Phase B or Phase C rule, threshold, interval algorithm, corpus size, or label.
- No Phase A decision clause (A1-A6) or its Boolean structure. A2's domain and firing conditions are unchanged; the amendment makes A2 uniquely executable, not differently structured.
- No metric other than M3 (which is enriched from a scalar to a vector with a named scalar summary; the summary's value on any input is identical to the old M3's value).
- No threshold other than T2 (which is restated to be computable on the new M3 vector; the direction and magnitude of the gates are unchanged).
- No reliability threshold, no adjudication rule, no missing-data rule (except the new PA-Z rules, which fill a previously undefined space), no scope statement, no safety boundary, no anchor fact.
- No carrying-audit result. v0.8's carrying record is unaltered. This amendment requires its own two-family non-producer carrying audit before it can be deposited as FROZEN.

## R0337 · SHVVP Phase A Amendment -- v0.8.2

- section: V. BSSG & SHVVP Protocols
- source_file: shvvp_phase_a_amendment_v0_8_2.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: e6a9837fbbe4185690f616bec47d234e4dfa0a61f334a490d5d57b8eccddf2b1

# SHVVP Phase A Amendment -- v0.8.2

**Author of record:** Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)
**Date:** 2026-07-31
**Status:** PROPOSED AMENDMENT -- NOT FROZEN, NOT CARRIED, NOT DEPOSITED
**Amends:** SHVVP v0.8 ([doi:10.5281/zenodo.21583202](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21583202)), Sections 5.2, 5.3, and edge-state behavior of the Section 5.4 decision table
**Supersedes:** v0.8.1 (HALTED; never deposited)
**Triggered by:** XZ Protocol freeze-blockers FB-1 and FB-2
**v0.8.1 carrying audit:** GPT 5.6 Sol HALT (7 findings); Kimi K3 HALT (3 BLOCKER, 14 MAJOR, 5 MINOR, 2 EDITORIAL). All findings accepted in full. Both seat reports ship unmodified with this release.

---

## 0. History and scope

### 0.1 What happened to v0.8.1

v0.8.1 was dispatched to two carrying seats (GPT 5.6 Sol, Kimi K3) on 2026-07-31. Both returned HALT. The seats converged on five structural defects: (1) self-contradictory S-membership rule reproducing the FB-1 computability defect; (2) 2-D jackknife crash on T7 and fabricated acceleration on T4; (3) T5 interval conjunct silently dropped while claiming no threshold changed; (4) PA-Z5 dead code with z0-undefined silently clamped; (5) Phase A NOT-EVALUABLE priority invoked but not inherited. Additional findings included unfrozen BUDGET, caller-supplied-statistic bypass, NaN-poisoned resamples, unenforced cardinalities, M3-FIRST returning censored non-discoveries, and a test suite that did not exercise the paths where defects lived.

v0.8.1 is HALTED, was NEVER DEPOSITED, and is not binding. It is retained for lineage and shipped unmodified.

### 0.2 What v0.8.2 changes

This amendment touches Sections 5.2 (M3 definition), 5.3 (T2 and T5 definitions), and edge-state behavior of the Section 5.4 decision table. Specifically:

1. M3 is enriched from a scalar to a per-fact discovery-time vector (FB-1).
2. T2 is restated over the per-fact paired differences (FB-1).
3. T5's interval conjunct is formally retired (PA-A5; substantive, declared).
4. Phase A interval algorithms are frozen as PA-1, PA-2, PA-3 with eleven degeneracy rules PA-Z1 through PA-Z11 (FB-2).
5. A Phase A construction-evaluability gate is added to the 5.4 decision table, preventing NOT-FALSIFIED when A2's shared-set domain was vacuous.

The code is the sole normative definition of the interval computation. The amendment text describes the algorithm; the shipped code implements it. A divergence between them is a defect.

### 0.3 What v0.8.2 does NOT change

- No estimand attribute of any phase.
- No Phase B or Phase C rule, threshold, interval algorithm, corpus size, label, or anchor fact.
- No Phase A decision clause (A1-A6) or its Boolean structure -- the clauses fire on the same conditions; the amendment makes them uniquely executable and adds an evaluability guard.
- No metric other than M3 (enriched from scalar to vector with a named scalar summary).
- No threshold other than T2 (restated to be computable on the new M3 vector) and T5 (interval conjunct formally retired -- see PA-A5).
- No reliability threshold, no adjudication rule, no scope statement, no safety boundary, no anchor fact.

The T5 change is SUBSTANTIVE under SHVVP v0.8 Section 12 and is declared as such in amendment entry PA-A5. It is not a silent deletion.

---

## 1. Resolution of FB-1: M3, T2, and S-membership

### 1.1 M3 is a per-fact observation vector

**Old M3 (v0.8).** Wall-clock minutes from corpus access to first correctly adjudicated consequential fact, per condition. One scalar.

**New M3 (v0.8.2).** For each correctly adjudicated consequential fact f in the sealed reference-standard ledger and each condition c:

> M3(f, c) = wall-clock minutes from first packet access to the first immutable saved evidence record that identifies f, under condition c.

Censor-status rules:

- **OBSERVED:** condition c identified f. The `minutes` field is the discovery time. An `evidence_record_id` is required.
- **RIGHT_CENSORED_BUDGET:** condition c did NOT identify f within the budget. The `minutes` field MUST equal FROZEN_BUDGET_MINUTES (480.0 minutes, frozen by this amendment). No evidence record exists.
- **CENSORED_EARLY:** the session terminated before the budget expired. The `minutes` field is the termination time and MUST be strictly less than FROZEN_BUDGET_MINUTES. The fact was NOT identified.

### 1.2 M3-FIRST: observed-only scalar summary

> M3-FIRST(c) = min over OBSERVED discoveries of M3(f, c).

If no OBSERVED facts exist, M3-FIRST returns the typed result NO_DISCOVERY. Censored observations (RIGHT_CENSORED_BUDGET, CENSORED_EARLY) are excluded from M3-FIRST.

This preserves the v0.8 scalar quantity for non-censored inputs. The identity is qualified: on vectors containing only censored entries, old M3 was undefined; new M3-FIRST returns NO_DISCOVERY rather than a budget value.

### 1.3 S is the observed-shared set

The shared fact set S consists of facts OBSERVED by both conditions:

> S = {f : f is OBSERVED in vec_A AND f is OBSERVED in vec_B}

A fact that one condition did not identify (RIGHT_CENSORED_BUDGET or CENSORED_EARLY) is NOT in S. This resolves the v0.8.1 contradiction (F-K3-A1) by choosing one rule and implementing it consistently: `compute_shared_set` intersects `observed_fact_ids`, not `all_fact_ids`. A fact found by neither condition cannot enter S. A fact found by one but not the other cannot enter S.

Because only OBSERVED facts enter S, censored observations never enter the T2 paired differences. The censoring-direction analysis of v0.8.1 Section 2.6 is withdrawn; it was wrong in both sign statements (F-K3-A2) and unnecessary under the observed-shared rule.

### 1.4 T2 restated

On S only, for each f in S define:

> Delta-M3(f) = M3(f, A) - M3(f, B).

Both M3 values are OBSERVED (by S-membership). T2 is satisfied if and only if ALL THREE hold:

1. The median of {Delta-M3(f) : f in S} is at least 30 minutes.
2. The median of {Delta-M3(f) / M3(f, A) : f in S, M3(f, A) > 0} is at least 0.20. Facts with M3(f, A) = 0 are excluded from this relative median and their count is reported. If all M3(f, A) = 0, the relative gate is NOT-EVALUABLE (PA-Z9).
3. The 95 percent BCa bootstrap interval for the median of {Delta-M3(f) : f in S}, computed by the Phase A interval algorithm of Section 2, excludes zero. The interval gate is computed on the absolute median only; the relative interval is reported but not gated. This disambiguation is a substantive decision recorded here.

If S is empty, T2 is NOT-EVALUABLE (PA-Z1).

### 1.5 Edge state: IDC > 0, S empty

If Condition B finds unique facts (IDC > 0) but shares none with A (S = {}), then T2 and T3 are both NOT-EVALUABLE, and A2 cannot fire. Under v0.8's formula, this could produce NOT-FALSIFIED on a shared-set comparison that never happened. v0.8.2 adds an explicit construction-evaluability guard: NOT-FALSIFIED requires that every clause whose domain was entered produced a determinate result. If A2's domain was entered (IDC > 0) but A2 could not evaluate (S empty), the Phase A result is NOT-EVALUABLE, not NOT-FALSIFIED. This guard is a new edge-state rule for the Section 5.4 decision table and is recorded as amendment entry PA-A3.

### 1.6 Fact-ID normalization

Fact identifiers are normalized by stripping whitespace, case-sensitive. "F1" and "f1" are distinct. The normalization is frozen by this amendment.

---

## 2. Resolution of FB-2: Phase A interval algorithms

### 2.1 Status of Phase A intervals

Phase A intervals are **finite-corpus stability summaries**. They are not population confidence intervals. No hypothesis test, no p-value, and no population inference attaches to any Phase A interval. This is consistent with the v0.8 Section 5.4 inferential-honesty clause.

### 2.2 The code is the sole normative definition

The shipped Python modules (`shvvp_v0_8_2_phase_a_m3.py`, `shvvp_v0_8_2_phase_a_intervals.py`) are the sole normative definition of the interval computation. The text in this section describes the algorithm; a text-only reimplementer must match the golden-vector outputs in the test suite. Where text and code could be read as differing, the code governs and the difference is a defect in this text, not a license to choose.

### 2.3 PA-1: resampling

| Threshold | Resampling unit | Population | Paired |
|---|---|---|---|
| T2 | The shared fact | S | Yes |
| T3 | The shared fact | S | Yes |
| T4 | The declared-generated artifact | 200 items (enforced) | Yes |
| T5 | NOT BOOTSTRAPPED (PA-A5) | -- | -- |
| T7 | The discrimination-set item | 240 items (enforced) | Yes (multidim) |

Number of draws: 10,000. Seed: passed as an integer; the code derives an internal seed via `np.random.default_rng(SeedSequence(seed))`. Per-threshold seed offsets: T2-abs = seed, T2-rel = seed+1, T3 = seed+2, T4 = seed+3, T7 = seed+4. These offsets exist only in code and are normative.

### 2.4 PA-2: BCa bounds

For a statistic theta on the full sample and bootstrap replicates theta-star:

1. **Bias correction z0:** standard normal quantile of the proportion of replicates strictly below theta. If prop_below is 0 or 1, z0 is undefined -- PA-Z10 fires.
2. **Acceleration a:** leave-one-unit-out jackknife, standard third-moment formula. For multidim data, jackknife uses `np.delete(data, i, axis=0)`. If sum_sq = 0, acceleration is undefined -- PA-Z5 fires.
3. **Bounds:** bootstrap percentiles at BCa-adjusted levels for a two-sided 95 percent interval.

No smoothing, no variance stabilisation, no continuity correction.

### 2.5 PA-3: statistics

| Threshold | Point statistic | Bootstrap target |
|---|---|---|
| T2 (absolute) | Median of Delta-M3 | BCa interval for median |
| T2 (relative) | Median of Delta-M3/M3(f,A) | Reported, not gated |
| T3 | Mean of M4(B)-M4(A) | BCa interval for mean |
| T4 | M5(B)-M5(A), /200 (enforced) | BCa interval for difference |
| T7 | M6(B) = balanced accuracy | BCa interval for M6(B) |

### 2.6 Cardinality enforcement

T4 requires exactly 200 items with binary (0/1) flags. T7 requires exactly 240 items with binary (0/1) labels. T3 rejects NaN and Inf. M3 rejects NaN, Inf, and negative values. Wrong cardinality or invalid values raise PhaseAInputError before any computation.

---

## 3. Degeneracy rules PA-Z1 through PA-Z11

| Rule | Condition | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| PA-Z1 | S is empty | T2 and T3 are NOT-EVALUABLE. A2 cannot fire. Section 1.5 guard applies. |
| PA-Z2 | |S| = 1 (or n=1 for any threshold) | Percentile reversion. No bootstrap run. Zero-width interval; point estimate only. Reported and counted. |
| PA-Z3 | M7(A) = 0 | T5 NOT-EVALUABLE. Ratio undefined. A4 cannot fire. |
| PA-Z4 | Alpha undefined (fewer than 2 ratable items, or all pairs identical) | INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION under v0.8 Section 5.3. |
| PA-Z5 | sum_sq = 0 with n > 1 (jackknife acceleration undefined) | Percentile reversion. Counted and reported. Fallback reason cites PA-Z5. |
| PA-Z7 | T4 union-empty: no items flagged by either condition | M5(B)-M5(A) = 0. Interval computed normally. T4 fires only if point > +0.05 AND interval LB > 0. |
| PA-Z8 | M6(B) not computable: zero items in a classification cell | T7 NOT-EVALUABLE. A6 evaluates T8 alone. |
| PA-Z9 | All M3(f,A) = 0 in S | T2 relative gate NOT-EVALUABLE. T2 overall NOT-EVALUABLE. |
| PA-Z10 | z0 undefined: prop_below = 0 or 1 | Percentile reversion. Counted and reported. No silent clamp. |
| PA-Z11 | NaN bootstrap resamples | Counted, discarded. Intervals computed on valid resamples. n_nan_resamples reported. If fewer than 2 valid resamples remain, zero-width interval returned. |

PA-Z5 is a structural guard. For mean and median statistics, if all jackknife values are identical (sum_sq = 0), all bootstrap replicates are also identical (prop_below = 0), so PA-Z10 fires first. PA-Z5 guards against edge cases where floating-point rounding produces sum_sq = 0 after z0 has been validly computed for other statistics.

---

## 4. T5 interval conjunct: formally retired (PA-A5)

v0.8 T5: "M7(B)/M7(A) greater than 1.25 AND 95 percent interval lower bound above 1.00."

v0.8.2 T5: "M7(B)/M7(A) greater than 1.25." The interval conjunct is retired.

**Justification (declared, not silent).** Phase A has no T5 resampling unit. The two team pairs are never pooled (v0.8 Section 5.4 inferential-honesty clause). A bootstrap over two team pairs is a bootstrap over n=2, which produces a degenerate interval that does not meaningfully constrain the ratio. The inherited inferential-honesty clause precludes treating team pairs as independent observations of a population parameter. Retiring the interval conjunct is more honest than computing a vacuous interval and calling it a gate.

This is a SUBSTANTIVE change to T5 under v0.8 Section 12 and changes A4's firing threshold (T5 fires strictly more often without the interval conjunct). It is recorded as amendment entry PA-A5 and in the scope statement of Section 0.2.

---

## 5. Caller-supplied statistic rejection

PairedDifference objects carry a module-private provenance token generated at import. Only `compute_paired_differences()` can produce valid instances. Every evaluation path (`evaluate_t2_point`, `evaluate_t2_full`, `t2_absolute_interval`, `t2_relative_interval`) calls `verify_provenance()` on each input. Hand-fabricated PairedDifference objects are rejected with PhaseAInputError before any statistic is computed.

This implements the BSSG raw-evidence discipline: the evaluator accepts raw M3 vectors and recomputes everything. A caller cannot inject a pre-computed median, interval, delta, or verdict.

---

## 6. Executable artifacts

| File | SHA-256 | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `shvvp_v0_8_2_phase_a_m3.py` | `34f08307...` | M3 vector, S-membership, paired differences, provenance |
| `shvvp_v0_8_2_phase_a_intervals.py` | `07338303...` | PA-1/PA-2/PA-3, PA-Z1 through PA-Z11, T2/T3/T4/T5/T7 |
| `test_shvvp_v0_8_2_phase_a.py` | `367b475e...` | 61-test adversarial suite |

The test suite covers: every PA-Z rule (PA-Z1 through PA-Z11), evaluable T4 with 200 items, evaluable T7 with 240 items, z0-undefined (PA-Z10), NaN resamples (PA-Z11), all-zero relative gate (PA-Z9), provenance rejection of fabricated deltas, M3-FIRST observed-only with NO_DISCOVERY, S-membership observed-only with censored exclusion, censor-status consistency (budget value, early < budget, observed requires evidence_record_id), fact-ID normalization, cardinality enforcement, NaN/Inf rejection for T3, seed reproducibility, frozen budget value, and the 5-fact reference computation.

---

## 7. Amendment record (append-only)

**v0.8.2 (2026-07-31): Phase A executability amendment, corrected after two-family carrying HALT of v0.8.1.**

- **PA-A1 (from FB-1 / F-SOL-1 / F-K3-A1).** ACCEPTED IN FULL. M3 redefined as a per-fact discovery-time vector. S-membership rule resolved: observed-shared-only. Censored non-discoveries excluded from S structurally. v0.8.1's contradictory censoring-direction analysis withdrawn.
- **PA-A2 (from FB-2 / F-SOL-2 / F-K3-B1/B2/B3/B4/B5).** ACCEPTED IN FULL. Phase A interval algorithms frozen as PA-1, PA-2, PA-3 with eleven degeneracy rules PA-Z1 through PA-Z11. 2-D jackknife fixed (axis=0). z0-undefined declared as PA-Z10 percentile reversion. NaN resamples declared as PA-Z11. PA-Z5 rewritten over sum_sq = 0 (computable quantity).
- **PA-A3 (new edge state).** The empty-S state (IDC > 0, S = {}) adds a construction-evaluability guard to the Section 5.4 decision table: NOT-FALSIFIED is barred when A2's domain was entered vacuously. This is an edge-state rule, not a clause change.
- **PA-A4 (scope).** This amendment touches Sections 5.2 (M3), 5.3 (T2, T5), and edge-state behavior of Section 5.4. The header and this entry say so explicitly, correcting v0.8.1's inaccurate "5.2 and 5.3 only" (F-K3-C4).
- **PA-A5 (T5 interval conjunct retired).** SUBSTANTIVE. T5's "95 percent interval lower bound above 1.00" conjunct is removed. Justification: Phase A has no T5 resampling unit; two team pairs are never pooled; a bootstrap over n=2 is degenerate. This changes A4's firing threshold and is declared as a substantive change under Section 12, not a silent deletion. v0.8.1 made this change silently while claiming no threshold changed (F-K3-C1, F-SOL-081-1); v0.8.2 records it.
- **PA-A6 (M3-FIRST observed-only).** M3-FIRST returns NO_DISCOVERY for all-censored or empty vectors. The backward-compatibility claim is qualified to non-censored inputs (F-K3-A3/C5).
- **PA-A7 (cardinalities enforced).** T4: exactly 200 items, binary flags. T7: exactly 240 items, binary labels. T3: NaN/Inf rejected. M3: NaN/Inf/negative rejected. Censor-status consistency enforced (F-K3-B7, F-SOL-081-6).
- **PA-A8 (caller rejection structural).** Provenance token on PairedDifference. Pipeline entry validation. Fabricated deltas rejected (F-K3-A6).
- **PA-A9 (BUDGET frozen).** FROZEN_BUDGET_MINUTES = 480.0 (F-K3-A5).
- **PA-A10 (code is sole normative definition).** Per-threshold seed offsets, percentile interpolation, and interval computation exist only in code. Text describes; code governs (F-K3-B8).
- **PA-A11 (v0.8.1 status).** v0.8.1 is HALTED, was never deposited, and is not binding. Both carrying-seat reports (GPT 5.6 Sol, Kimi K3) ship unmodified. All findings from both seats are accepted in full; none is downgraded.

**Status:** PROPOSED. Not frozen, not carried, not deposited. Requires two-family non-producer carrying audit before FROZEN status.

---

## 8. Carrying and deposit plan

1. Ship the amendment text, three executable artifacts, and both v0.8.1 carrying-seat reports as a candidate package.
2. Two non-producer carrying seats of different vendor families execute the canonical bytes, verify the test suite, recompute SHA-256 identity, and attack every repair claim against the v0.8.1 findings.
3. Same-vendor seats count once. Producer-family review is advisory.
4. A HALT from either carrying seat blocks deposit and requires a new version.
5. Upon convergent non-HALT verdicts, the amendment is deposited as SHVVP v0.8.2.
6. The XZ Protocol's FREEZE-BLOCKER fields FB-1 and FB-2 are filled by referencing the deposited v0.8.2 DOI and test-suite digest.

## R0338 · SHVVP Phase A Amendment -- v0.8.4

- section: V. BSSG & SHVVP Protocols
- source_file: shvvp_phase_a_amendment_v0_8_4.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: 492f288f8cd522b9491cf4b7491f245b21de4bea1e4716d30d6f89530c8ff1ac

# SHVVP Phase A Amendment -- v0.8.4

**Author of record:** Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)
**Date:** 2026-07-31
**Status:** PROPOSED AMENDMENT -- NOT FROZEN, NOT CARRIED, NOT DEPOSITED
**Amends:** SHVVP v0.8 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21583202), Sections 5.2, 5.3, and edge-state behavior of Section 5.4
**Supersedes:** v0.8.3 (HALTED), v0.8.2 (HALTED), v0.8.1 (HALTED)

## 0. Scope

This amendment touches Sections 5.2 (M3), 5.3 (T2, T5), and edge-state behavior of the Section 5.4 decision table. The code is the sole normative definition of the interval computation; this text describes the algorithm.

### 0.1 What changed from v0.8.3

1. M3Vector is frozen (immutable tuple). Mutation bypass closed permanently.
2. censor_status enum membership validated first. String bypass closed.
3. evidence_record_id: non-empty str required for OBSERVED; forbidden on non-discoveries.
4. M3 endpoint declared SUBSTANTIVE change from parent (PA-A12).
5. PA-Z4 scoped out of code (adjudication-layer). Count corrected to eleven code-level rules.
6. PA-Z13 added: non-finite ratios excluded and counted.
7. PA-Z14 added: BCa interval excluding its own point estimate -> percentile reversion.
8. Bool rejected uniformly at all numeric entry points.
9. Shape validation for T4/T7 tuples. Raw exceptions wrapped in PhaseAInputError.
10. caller_seed recorded on BootstrapResult; internal_seed separated.
11. BCa guard counters (n_bca_denom_guard, n_bca_level_clamp) on BootstrapResult.
12. PA-Z12 firing fixture shipped (Kimi's T7 fixture).
13. Golden vectors pinned for T2-abs, T3, T4, T7, PA-Z5, PA-Z10.
14. Provenance docstrings aligned with accident-guard.

## 1. M3 definition (Section 5.2)

M3 is a per-fact discovery-time vector. M3-FIRST is the observed-only scalar summary. S is the observed-shared set. See code module docstring for the SUBSTANTIVE ENDPOINT CHANGE (PA-A12).

M3Vector is a frozen dataclass with observations as a tuple. No mutation after construction. The with_obs() method returns a new vector. This closes the F-SOL-083-1 bypass permanently.

M3Observation validates censor_status as a CensorStatus enum member before any other check. String values (e.g. "OBSERVED") are rejected with PhaseAInputError. Evidence IDs are forbidden on RIGHT_CENSORED_BUDGET and CENSORED_EARLY; required as non-empty str on OBSERVED. OBSERVED minutes must be <= FROZEN_BUDGET_MINUTES (480.0).

### 1.1 At-480 boundary rule (disclosure)

At exactly 480.0 minutes, OBSERVED (with evidence) and RIGHT_CENSORED_BUDGET are both valid but carry opposite S-membership. The caller's enum choice governs. This is a disclosed boundary, not a bug.

### 1.2 n=1 vacuous gate (disclosure)

With |S|=1, PA-Z2 produces a zero-width interval. If the single delta is nonzero, excludes_zero is True and T2 can be satisfied on a single observation. This is a disclosed consequence of the point-interval semantics, not a bug. It is conservative: a single observation cannot drive a strong conclusion.

## 2. Interval algorithms (Section 5.3)

### 2.1 Code-level degeneracy rules

Eleven code-level rules: PA-Z1 through PA-Z3, PA-Z5 through PA-Z14.

PA-Z4 (alpha undefined / INDETERMINATE-ADJUDICATION) is an adjudication-layer rule outside these modules. It is tested at the adjudication layer.

| Rule | Condition | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| PA-Z1 | S empty | T2/T3 NOT-EVALUABLE |
| PA-Z2 | n=1 | Percentile reversion, zero-width |
| PA-Z3 | M7(A)=0 | T5 NOT-EVALUABLE |
| PA-Z5 | sum_sq=0, z0 valid | Percentile reversion |
| PA-Z6 | Single-index resample | Kept, counted (n_degenerate_resample) |
| PA-Z7 | T4 union-empty | M5 diff = 0, interval computed normally |
| PA-Z8 | T7 empty class | T7 returns None |
| PA-Z9 | All M3(f,A)=0 | Relative gate NOT-EVALUABLE |
| PA-Z10 | z0 undefined (prop_below in {0,1}) | Percentile reversion |
| PA-Z11 | NaN resamples | Counted, discarded (n_nan_resamples) |
| PA-Z12 | LOO NaN substitution | theta substituted, counted (n_loo_nan_substitutions) |
| PA-Z13 | Non-finite ratio (Delta/M3(f,A) overflows) | Excluded, counted (relative_nonfinite_count) |
| PA-Z14 | BCa interval excludes point estimate | Percentile reversion, excludes_zero=False |

### 2.2 BCa numerical guards (documented)

Two guards exist in the BCa computation. Both are documented and counted:
- _bca_q denominator within 1e-15 of zero: returns level 0.5 (n_bca_denom_guard)
- Adjusted percentile levels clamped to [0.5/n_valid, 1-0.5/n_valid] (n_bca_level_clamp)

### 2.3 PA-Z11 conditional-resampling (disclosure)

When NaN resamples are discarded, the reported interval is over the non-NaN resamples only. This is conditional on non-degeneracy. The conditioning is a consequence of the discard discipline.

### 2.4 PA-Z2/PA-Z11 zero-width semantics (disclosure)

PA-Z2 (n=1) sets excludes_zero = (theta != 0). PA-Z11 exhaustion (n_valid < 2) sets excludes_zero = False. The geometric situations are similar but the inferential meanings differ: PA-Z2 has a point estimate and no uncertainty; PA-Z11 has uncertainty but insufficient valid resamples to bound it. The difference is intentional.

## 3. T5 interval conjunct (PA-A5)

T5's "95 percent interval lower bound above 1.00" conjunct is retired. This is SUBSTANTIVE (see v0.8.2 amendment entry PA-A5).

## 4. Construction-evaluability guard (Section 5.4 edge state)

NOT-FALSIFIED requires that every clause whose domain was entered produced a determinate result. If A2's domain was entered (IDC > 0) but A2 could not evaluate (S empty), the Phase A result is NOT-EVALUABLE, not NOT-FALSIFIED. This is a prose rule tested at the adjudication layer alongside PA-Z4.

## 5. Provenance discipline

The provenance token on PairedDifference is an ACCIDENT GUARD against casual misuse. It is not a security boundary. dataclasses.replace() and direct token import can bypass it. The BSSG raw-evidence discipline is enforced at the protocol layer (adjudicators verify raw evidence references), not at this Python API layer. The T3 interface accepts caller-computed M4 differences without provenance; this is disclosed and accepted.

## 6. Normative artifacts

| File | SHA-256 | Role |
|---|---|---|
| shvvp_phase_a_amendment_v0_8_4.md | (this file) | Amendment text |
| shvvp_v0_8_4_phase_a_m3.py | fd1bd996... | M3 vector, S-membership, paired differences |
| shvvp_v0_8_4_phase_a_intervals.py | ff3a3801... | Intervals, PA-Z1-Z3/Z5-Z14, T2/T3/T4/T5/T7 |
| test_shvvp_v0_8_4_phase_a.py | b646429c... | 68-test adversarial suite |

Golden-vector environment: Python 3.12.3, numpy 2.4.4, scipy 1.17.1.

## 7. Amendment record (append-only)

PA-A1 through PA-A11: carried from v0.8.2/v0.8.3 (unchanged).

- **PA-A12 (v0.8.4): M3 endpoint SUBSTANTIVE change declared.** The parent v0.8 M3 ends at "first correctly adjudicated consequential fact." This implementation times to the first immutable saved evidence record that identifies the fact. The distinction is declared as a substantive endpoint change. No scalar-preservation claim is made for inputs where adjudication time differs from evidence time.
- **PA-A13 (v0.8.4): M3Vector frozen.** M3Vector is a frozen dataclass with observations as tuple. The mutation bypass (F-SOL-083-1) is closed permanently.
- **PA-A14 (v0.8.4): censor_status validation.** Enum membership is the first check. The string bypass (F-SOL-083-2) is closed permanently.
- **PA-A15 (v0.8.4): PA-Z4 scoped out.** PA-Z4 is an adjudication-layer rule. The code implements eleven code-level rules (PA-Z1-Z3, Z5-Z14). The "twelve rules" claims in v0.8.2/v0.8.3 are corrected.
- **PA-A16 (v0.8.4): PA-Z13 added.** Non-finite ratios from subnormal M3(f,A) are excluded and counted. The two-evaluator divergence on -inf ratios (F-K3-083-2) is resolved.
- **PA-A17 (v0.8.4): PA-Z14 added.** BCa interval excluding its own point estimate triggers percentile reversion. The unnamed numerical state (F-K3-083-1) is named.
- **PA-A18 (v0.8.4): Evidence-ID discipline.** Non-empty str required for OBSERVED; forbidden on non-discoveries. The falsy-evidence bypass (F-K3-083-11) is closed.

**Status:** PROPOSED. Not frozen, not carried, not deposited.

*Provenance.* Authored by Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise); prepared with frontier language models as drafting instruments. Not independently peer reviewed. No effectiveness claim about BSSG.

*End of proposed SHVVP Phase A Amendment v0.8.4.*
