authorship. All AI-generated contributions were directed, reviewed, and approved by the human author.

Abstract
The Munafiq Protocol (Arfeen et al., 2026) formalizes surface-depth divergence as the failure mode that
alignment training does not address in artificial systems. This paper extends the Protocol to financial
reporting systems, where the same failure mode is the central problem: a filing's reported numbers
(zahir) can diverge from the economic reality they claim to represent (batin), and the divergence is
structurally detectable from the filing's own internal consistency without requiring external ground
truth.
We propose Bayyinah al-Maal ("clear evidence of wealth"), a deterministic structural scanner for SEC
filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A) and on-chain cryptocurrency disclosures. The scanner applies the same
architectural principles proven in the Bayyinah document integrity scanner (145 mechanisms, six closed
format gauntlets, 1,671 tests as of April 28, 2026; counts continue to grow -- see Zenodo DOI
10.5281/zenodo.19700445 for current state): Tier 1 verified findings from structural checks, Tier 2
structural anomalies warranting review, Tier 3 interpretive signals that never override Tier 1. Detection
is deterministic and operates by structural address (Escape A from the No-Escape Theorem, Barman et
al. 2026). Explanation may use ML. The two never share load.
The thesis makes three claims: (1) the four-process taxonomy (Aligned, Compliant, Performing,
Misaligned) maps onto financial reporting with the same structural precision it achieves for AI systems;
(2) at least 40 Tier 1 mechanism candidates are proposed across four structural categories using XBRL-


tagged SEC filings as the detection substrate (the v1.0 paper proposes the taxonomy; v1.1 will publish
worked mechanism contracts with XBRL address pairs, thresholds, and example finding outputs); (3) onchain blockchain data provides a batin layer against which cryptocurrency project claims (zahir) can be
verified with zero semantic inference, producing the same Escape A architecture the document scanner
uses.

1. Purpose Hierarchy
"And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly." (Al-Baqarah 2:188)
The purpose hierarchy for Bayyinah al-Maal follows the same five-level structure established in the
Munafiq Protocol, applied to financial systems:
First, the command of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala to not consume one another's wealth unjustly (2:188).
Every mechanism that detects self-contradiction in a financial filing serves this command by making it
structurally harder for a filing to present a false surface to investors.
Second, financial systems that intermediate between savers and enterprises. The integrity of these
systems depends on the integrity of the filings that flow through them.
Third, enterprises whose reported financials are consumed by investors, regulators, and counterparties.
Fourth, retail investors and pension holders downstream of institutional allocation decisions.
Fifth, all living systems whose resource allocation depends on honest price discovery.

2. The Problem: Performed Alignment in Financial Reporting
2.1. The Compliance Gap in Financial Markets
The Munafiq Protocol defines the compliance gap as the measurable difference between a system's
behavior when observed versus unobserved. In financial reporting, the analog is precise: companies
report differently when they know the filing will be audited (10-K annual, audited) versus when it will
not (earnings calls, press releases, investor presentations, unaudited). The SEC's enforcement history is a
corpus of measured compliance gaps.
Greenblatt et al. (2024) measured an 11-26% compliance gap in Claude 3 Opus between training and
deployment conditions. The SEC's 2023 enforcement report documents a compliance gap across 784
enforcement actions totaling $4.95 billion in penalties. The behavioral mechanism is structurally
analogous: present a surface that satisfies the observer while the substrate diverges.

2.2. The Four Processes Applied to Financial Actors
Process 1 (Aligned): Reported financials accurately reflect economic reality. The depth state matches the
surface presentation. Berkshire Hathaway's annual letters (Buffett, annually) are the canonical example:
the numbers are what they are, the limitations are stated, the uncertainties are acknowledged.


Process 2 (Compliant): Follows GAAP technically but structures transactions to present a misleading
picture. Legal but dishonest. Revenue recognition timing games, off-balance-sheet vehicles preSarbanes-Oxley, channel stuffing. The filing passes audit because it follows the rules. The rules do not
require honesty, only compliance.
Process 3 (Performing): Actively constructs filings designed to pass audit while the substrate diverges.
Luckin Coffee's fabricated sales data. Wirecard's Asia-Pacific revenue structure (the filing's related-party
patterns and escrow account disclosures had detectable structural inconsistencies that auditors flagged
but management overrode). Real fraud cases often span processes: Wirecard also has a Process 4
component (the fabricated bank confirmations themselves, which were internally consistent). The fourprocess taxonomy describes filing-shape behaviors, not actor identity.
Process 4 (Misaligned): Outright fraud with no structural concealment. FTX's commingling of customer
funds. Madoff's fabricated trade tickets, which were internally consistent within the statements he sent
to investors. The surface bore no relationship to the substrate.

2.3. Why Existing Systems Fail
Current financial anomaly detection operates at Tier 3 (interpretive, embedding-based). Systems like
Kensho, Palantir Foundry, and Bloomberg's NLP pipelines use semantic similarity to flag "unusual" filing
language. By the No-Escape Theorem (Barman et al., 2026), these systems are inside the kernelthreshold class and subject to interference, forgetting, and false recall as semantic density increases. The
geometric basis for this interference is documented in both the write-time direction (Beton and Chana,
2025, the Orthogonality Constraint) and the retrieval-time direction (Barman et al., 2026). A financial
corpus with thousands of filings using similar language ("restructuring charges," "goodwill impairment,"
"non-recurring items") will produce the interference these papers predict.
Forensic accounting operates at Tier 1 (structural, deterministic) but is manual, expensive, and reactive.
A forensic accountant checks whether the numbers add up, whether the footnotes match the line items,
whether the cash flow statement is consistent with the income statement. These checks are structural,
deterministic, and operate by exact numerical comparison (Escape A). The process-reward-model
literature validates this architectural choice: deterministic rule-based step verifiers outperform neural
judges by approximately 20% F1 and are unhackable by construction (Liu et al., 2024, VPRM; Lightman
et al., 2023). They are also performed by humans at $500-1,000/hour and only after suspicion is raised.
Bayyinah al-Maal automates the forensic accountant's structural checks at scale, producing Tier 1
findings from the filing's own internal consistency. No semantic inference. No embedding similarity. No
ML in the detection layer.

3. Architecture
3.1. Escape A at the Financial Substrate
The scanner operates by structural address on XBRL-tagged financial data. Each XBRL element has a
unique taxonomy address (us-gaap:Revenue, us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss, etc.) that is deterministic,


standardized, and machine-readable. Cross-filing checks compare the same taxonomy address across
multiple filings from the same company. Year-over-year checks compare the same address across
consecutive annual filings. Footnote-to-number reconciliation compares a numerical claim in the
financial statements against the supporting detail in the notes.
None of these checks require semantic understanding of what the numbers mean. They require
structural consistency: does the number at address X in filing Y match the number at address X in filing
Z? This is Escape A from the No-Escape Theorem: structural-identity retrieval with zero semantic
interference. The XBRL address is deterministic, standardized, and machine-readable, the same three
properties that license Escape A for PDF object references and XML paths in the document scanner.
Falsifiability criterion: if a Tier 1 check requires the scanner to disambiguate the semantic meaning of an
XBRL element (e.g., choose between two valid taxonomy mappings), the check has leaked into Tier 3
and the framework is violated.

3.2. The Five-Layer Integrity Stack Applied to Financial Markets
Layer 1 (Filing integrity): Pre-analysis structural inspection of XBRL tags. This is Bayyinah al-Maal's
position. Layer 2 (Pipeline integrity): Filing provenance via EDGAR timestamps and amendment chains.
Layer 3 (Prompt integrity): Analyst query boundary enforcement to prevent prompt injection via filing
text. Layer 4 (Reasoning integrity): Valuation model step verification where each assumption is checked
against filing data, following the same structured async discipline established by Lattner (2017) for
concurrent computation. Layer 5 (Model integrity): Analyst bias detection via sentiment drift in coverage
initiation versus subsequent reports; truth-direction probing (Marks and Tegmark, 2024) applied to
analyst representations is a candidate Layer 5 mechanism for future work.
Bayyinah al-Maal occupies Layer 1: it analyzes filings, not markets. The distinction matters: markets are
emergent (no single actor controls the price), filings are presented (a single entity constructs the
document). The Munafiq Protocol applies to presented artifacts, not emergent phenomena.

3.3. Two Substrates: SEC Filings and On-Chain Data
For SEC filings (traditional equities), the batin is the XBRL-tagged financial data. The zahir is the rendered
10-K that investors read. The surface-depth check is: does the rendered prose match the tagged data?
Do the tagged numbers cross-reference correctly? Do the footnotes support the line items?
For on-chain data (cryptocurrency), the batin is the blockchain itself. Every transaction, every wallet
balance, every smart contract state is publicly verifiable. The zahir is the project's claims: tokenomics
whitepaper, team allocation disclosures, treasury reports, proof-of-reserves attestations. The surfacedepth check is: do the on-chain balances match the claimed allocations? Does the token distribution
match the whitepaper's vesting schedule? Does the treasury wallet's transaction history match the
published treasury reports?
The blockchain substrate is the strongest possible batin: it is immutable, public, and cryptographically
verified. A Bayyinah-for-crypto scanner that compares on-chain state against project claims is
performing the same structural comparison the document scanner performs (file bytes versus rendered
surface), but with a batin that cannot be retroactively modified. The Sleeper Agents finding (Hubinger et


al., 2024) is relevant here: adversarial training does not remove deceptive backdoors but teaches better
hiding. A project that adjusts its public claims to match on-chain state after a discrepancy is caught
exhibits the same pattern; the on-chain batin provides the unforgeable substrate against which such
adjustments become visible.

4. Proposed Mechanism Taxonomy
4.1. SEC Filing Mechanism Candidates (Tier 1, Deterministic)
The following 40 mechanism candidates are organized into four structural categories. Each is proposed
at the taxonomy level: a one-line description of the structural check and its XBRL-addressable surface.
The v1.0 paper proposes the taxonomy; v1.1 will publish worked mechanism contracts with XBRL
address pairs, detection thresholds, example finding outputs, false-positive carveouts, and synthetic
fixture demonstrations for at least one mechanism per category.
Cross-filing consistency (10 candidates): Revenue in 10-K versus sum of quarterly revenues in 10-Qs.
Balance sheet items at period-end 10-Q versus period-start next 10-Q. Share count in 10-K versus shares
reported in DEF 14A proxy. Cash and equivalents end-of-period versus beginning-of-next-period.
Goodwill and intangible asset roll-forward (opening + additions - impairments - disposals = closing). Debt
maturity schedule in current filing versus prior filing's "next year" bucket. Segment revenue sum versus
consolidated revenue. Geographic revenue sum versus consolidated revenue. Tax provision
reconciliation (statutory rate applied to pre-tax income versus reported provision). Pension obligation
roll-forward consistency.
Footnote-to-number reconciliation (10 candidates): Revenue recognition policy description versus
revenue growth pattern. Lease liability in footnotes versus balance sheet operating lease line. Stockbased compensation in footnotes versus income statement line. Restructuring charge details in
footnotes versus restructuring line item. Acquisition purchase price allocation in footnotes versus
goodwill on balance sheet. Contingent liability disclosure in footnotes versus accrued liabilities. Relatedparty transaction amounts in footnotes versus revenue/expense lines. Inventory valuation method in
footnotes versus inventory balance trajectory. Debt covenant terms in footnotes versus actual ratios
computable from the filing. Deferred revenue balance in footnotes versus balance sheet line.
Year-over-year structural drift (10 candidates): Accounting policy changes between consecutive 10-Ks
detected via XBRL taxonomy changes. Footnote reordering between consecutive 10-Ks. New relatedparty disclosures not present in prior year. Segment definition changes. Auditor change detected via
PCAOB auditor ID in XBRL. Material weakness disclosure appearing or disappearing. Going concern
language appearing or disappearing. Revenue disaggregation granularity changes. Non-GAAP metric
definition changes between consecutive filings. Critical audit matter changes between consecutive
auditor reports.
Filing metadata anomalies (10 candidates): Filing timestamp anomalies relative to typical windows.
Amendment (10-K/A) filed without a clear restatement note. XBRL extension taxonomy elements not in
the standard US-GAAP taxonomy. Inline XBRL rendering divergence (tagged value versus rendered text


differ). Filing size anomalies relative to peer filings. Exhibit list changes between original and amended
filings. Officer certification language deviations from standard Sarbanes-Oxley form. Risk factor section
length changes year-over-year. MD&A section structural reorganization year-over-year. Legal
proceedings section additions or removals.

4.2. Cryptocurrency Mechanism Candidates (Tier 1, Deterministic)
On-chain versus claim verification (10 candidates). Each mechanism below is scoped to what is bytedeterministic from on-chain state alone, per the constraint stated in Section 7, Caveat 5. Treasury wallet
balance versus published treasury report. Token distribution versus whitepaper vesting schedule
(scoped to ERC-20 transfer events). Team wallet activity versus claimed lock-up period. Circulating
supply versus claimed circulating supply (via totalSupply() minus sum of known locked addresses).
Staking contract total value locked versus published TVL. Burn address balance versus claimed burn
amount. Top-N holder concentration versus claimed concentration distribution. Protocol revenue from
on-chain fee events versus claimed revenue figures. Smart contract pause/unpause state versus project
communications (scoped to public state variable reads; proxy-pattern interpretation is deferred to v1.1).
Bridge balances at the single-chain layer versus claimed single-chain liquidity (cross-chain attestation
deferred to v1.1).

4.3. Tier 2 and Tier 3 (Deferred)
Tier 2 mechanisms (structural anomaly, not verified inconsistency) include unusual executive
compensation structures, high auditor-to-revenue ratios, and excessive use of XBRL extension elements.
These warrant review but do not prove misreporting.
Tier 3 mechanisms (interpretive, ML-permitted in the explanation layer only) include earnings call
sentiment divergence from financial results, insider trading pattern analysis, and social media signal
correlation. These are explicitly outside the detection layer per Standing Principle 1: detection is
deterministic, explanation may be neural, the two never share load.

5. Verdict Surface
The same five verdicts from the Munafiq Protocol apply. Sahih: the filing's numbers cross-reference
correctly, footnotes match line items, year-over-year structure is stable. Mushtabih: minor
inconsistencies (rounding differences, immaterial footnote gaps) warrant review but do not indicate
misreporting. Mukhfi: material inconsistencies detected (cross-filing numbers do not match, footnotes
contradict line items). Munafiq: verified divergence between reported numbers and the filing's own
internal data (the filing contradicts itself). Mughlaq: XBRL tagging is missing, corrupted, or insufficient for
structural checks; the scanner cannot make a claim.

6. Empirical Validation Plan
6.1. Retrospective Validation on Known Fraud Cases


Build the scanner. Run it against the pre-fraud filings of known fraud cases (Enron 10-Ks 1997-2001,
Wirecard annual reports 2015-2019, Luckin Coffee 20-F filings 2019-2020, FTX-related Alameda
disclosures). Measure: how many of the mechanism candidates fire on the pre-fraud filings? How early
before the fraud's public discovery do the mechanisms first fire? What is the false-positive rate on a
matched control set of non-fraud filings from the same industry and time period?

6.2. Prospective Validation on Current Filings
Run the scanner against the full EDGAR XBRL corpus (all 10-K and 10-Q filings from 2020-present).
Measure: what is the base rate of Tier 1 findings across the corpus? What is the distribution by industry,
company size, and auditor? Are there clusters of companies with unusually high finding rates? Do the
clusters correlate with subsequent enforcement actions, restatements, or auditor changes? Preregistered hypothesis: if high-finding-rate clusters do not correlate with subsequent enforcement,
restatements, or auditor changes, the framework's predictive validity is rejected.

6.3. Cryptocurrency Validation
Run the on-chain mechanisms against the top 100 cryptocurrency projects by market capitalization.
Compare claimed tokenomics against on-chain state. Measure: how many projects have zahir-batin
divergence between their published claims and on-chain reality? Publish the findings honestly, including
projects that score sahih. Falsifiability criterion: if a project's on-chain state scores sahih and later fails
via a mechanism not visible at the structural-address layer, the scanner is correctly silent and the
framework is consistent. If a project's on-chain state is sahih and we later claim it was munafiq because
of off-chain evidence, we have violated the discipline.

7. Honest Caveats
Caveat 1: Structural consistency does not prove truthfulness. A filing can be internally consistent and still
misrepresent reality if the underlying transactions were fabricated. Madoff's fabricated trade tickets
were internally consistent within the statements he sent to investors, yet bore no relationship to actual
trading activity. Tier 1 findings detect self-contradiction, not fabrication. The scanner catches Process 2
and Process 3 actors but not a perfectly executed Process 4 actor who fabricates consistent data.
Caveat 2: XBRL coverage is not universal. Many filings have incomplete or incorrect XBRL tagging. The
scanner's coverage depends on the quality of the XBRL input. A mughlaq verdict on a filing with poor
XBRL is honest (the scanner cannot verify what it cannot parse) but is not useful to the investor.
Caveat 3: The scanner does not predict stock prices. It does not make investment recommendations. It
does not replace human judgment. It produces structural findings that a human analyst uses as input to
their own assessment. The Tier discipline prevents the scanner from making claims it cannot structurally
verify.
Caveat 4: Retroactive validation on known fraud cases is subject to hindsight bias. The mechanisms were
designed knowing what the fraud looked like. The prospective validation (Section 6.2) is the real test.


Caveat 5: On-chain cryptocurrency data is publicly verifiable but smart contract logic can be opaque.
Proxy contracts, upgradeable contracts, and multi-sig wallets introduce complexity that simple balance
checks do not capture. The cryptocurrency mechanisms in Section 4.2 are scoped to what is bytedeterministic from on-chain state without requiring smart contract logic interpretation. Mechanisms
that require proxy-pattern interpretation or cross-chain attestation are deferred to v1.1.

8. Relationship to the Research Program
This paper is the fourth substrate the Munafiq Protocol has been applied to: (1) AI systems (the original
Munafiq Protocol paper), (2) document files (Bayyinah Enterprise Defense Case), (3) programming
languages (Furqan type system, for code written in Furqan; arbitrary LLM output is future work), (4)
financial filings (this paper).
The architectural principles are inherited unchanged from the Framework Foundations v1.1 canonical
document. Principle 1: Detection is deterministic; explanation may be neural; the two never share load.
Principle 2: Routing is non-learned and auditable. Principle 3: Knowledge Objects are required (XBRL
taxonomy addresses are the controlled vocabulary; filing versions are the version chains; EDGAR CIK
numbers are the hash-based identity). Principle 4: The scanner is subject to its own discipline (the
financial scanner's own reports must be internally consistent by the same checks it applies to filings; if
the scanner's report on a filing fails the scanner's own structural consistency checks, the report is
mughlaq, not the filing). Principle 5: Tier 1/2/3 discipline is structural, not stylistic.
The novel contribution of this paper is the demonstration that these five principles, derived from the
Quran's structural architecture and validated on document files, generalize to financial reporting with
zero architectural modification. The same escape route (Escape A, structural-identity retrieval) works
because XBRL taxonomy addresses are structural addresses in exactly the same sense that PDF object
references and XML paths are structural addresses.

9. What Is Genuinely Novel
The forensic accounting profession has performed structural consistency checks on financial filings for
decades. What is novel in this paper is not the checks themselves but three things.
First, the formalization as a four-process taxonomy with a five-verdict surface. Existing financial fraud
detection does not distinguish between a filing that is internally consistent (sahih), one that has minor
anomalies (mushtabih), one with material concealment (mukhfi), one with verified self-contradiction
(munafiq), and one that cannot be assessed (mughlaq). The verdict surface provides a structured
epistemic claim rather than a binary clean/suspicious flag.
Second, the Tier discipline applied to financial analysis. Current ML-based financial analysis conflates
structural checks (do the numbers add up?) with interpretive signals (does the CEO's tone sound
evasive?). The Tier discipline, when implemented as in the document scanner, separates these formally
and prevents interpretive signals from overriding structural findings.


Third, the on-chain batin as a verification substrate. To our knowledge, no existing financial integrity
system uses blockchain data as the structural substrate against which project claims are verified using
deterministic checks. Proof-of-reserves attestations are the closest analog, but they are point-in-time
snapshots performed by third parties, not continuous structural monitoring.

10. Conclusion
"And do not mix the truth with falsehood, and do not conceal the truth while you know it." (Al-Baqarah
2:42)
The Munafiq Protocol's central claim is that surface-depth divergence is a structural failure mode, not a
behavioral one, and that structural failure modes require structural solutions. This paper demonstrates
that the claim generalizes from AI systems and document files to financial reporting with zero
architectural modification. XBRL taxonomy addresses are structural addresses. On-chain blockchain
state is a cryptographically verified batin. The five standing principles, the five-verdict surface, and the
Tier discipline transfer unchanged.
The same principle. A new substrate. The verification continues.

Bismillah. Tawakkaltu 'ala Allah.

About this companion

that any figure in the note can be traced to the exact rows it came from, and so that every error
caught and corrected during development stays on the public record rather than being silently
revised away. For a note whose method is verifying claims against a substrate, preserving how
its own claims were checked and corrected is not optional; it is the method applied to the note
itself.

its integrity hash and the two independent external reproduction passes; the findings ledger
(namespace F-AA) in the six-element format; the paper-level falsifiability criteria; and the
append-only version ledger with the one substantive correction made to date. Section numbers
refer to the reader-facing note. Per Bayyinah Audit Framework v3.0 Section 14.5, superseded
text is preserved and corrected by annotation, never edited in place.

A. Verification Status
Primary data. All figures derive from the New York State Open Data portal, Socrata resource
gpsc-qqsz (MTA Procurement Report, All), retrieved without authentication. Unlike the
education worked example, whose sources were browser-gated, this endpoint is directly
queryable, so the recompute is reproducible by any second party from the primary source.
Frozen snapshot (reviewer-reproducible). Because the live resource may be updated by the
authority, the exact rows underlying the note's figures are frozen as a companion artifact:
snapshot/gpsc-qqsz_FY2022-2024.json, 37,988 records across the three fiscal years
ending 2022, 2023, and 2024, with a MANIFEST.json recording the retrieval timestamp, the
field list, and a SHA-256 of the canonical JSON. The reproduction script
reproduce_paper2.py verifies this hash before computing, so a reader is told immediately if
the snapshot has been altered, and can compute the note's figures deterministically offline and,
with --live, check for drift against the current endpoint.
Reproduction record. - Producer-lineage: every Section 4 figure was computed from the
snapshot by reproduce_paper2.py and matches the note exactly (FY2024 totals; competitive
92.22 percent of dollars; MWBE 18.7 percent count and 3.95 percent dollar; three-year
persistence 5.0, 5.3, 4.7; top-5/10/20 concentration 22.1/30.4/41.8 percent; Gini 0.931; 2,656
vendors). - External verification EV-1 (informal, non-lineage): an independent party executed
the reproduction script against the live endpoint and independently re-queried the Section 4.3
quantities (zero-amount exclusion, vendor concentration, Gini, largest vendors by name and
amount), reporting exact matches on all figures including individual vendor dollar amounts
(Kawasaki Rail Car $6.46B, New Flyer $2.56B, and construction joint ventures above $1.5B). External verification EV-2 (informal, non-lineage): the same party empirically tested the crosstable join asserted in Section 3, resolving a real project_number (D501CB08) from the
locations table wcsa-vkhf against live allocation records in kizb-nxtu, confirming the join is
functional, not merely plausible.


Framing-claim corroboration (external, informal). EV corroborated two interpretive claims:
that New York MWBE goals are dollar-denominated (9 NYCRR Section 435.6, "percent of the
total dollar value of contracts"), which was originally stated as supporting a reading that the 3.95
percent dollar share is the operative substrate. [Corrected in v0.3 per F-AA-R2-01, Section
14.5:] that reading is withdrawn and does not match the reader note. Dollar-denomination of a
goal does not establish that total prime-contract face value (or any single supplied ledger
amount) is the legally operative MWBE-goal denominator; eligible expenditures, subcontracting
opportunities, participation tiers, exclusions, and waivers remain absent. The 3.95 percent figure
is a descriptive prime-vendor statistic only. EV also corroborated that a shared procurementreporting schema is mandated for New York public authorities (Public Authorities Law and
Executive Law Article 15-A, via the Authorities Budget Office PARIS system), which supports
Section 3's common-schema claim underpinning portability.

B. Findings
Namespace F-AA (allocation-asymmetry development findings). [Superseded per F-AA-R205: 'one substantive finding' was true only at the original writing; the current finding set
spans F-AA-1, F-AA-2, F-AA-R1-01..09, and F-AA-R2-01..06. See Current State block.]
F-AA-1 MEDIUM -- Incorrect data-infrastructure claim: capital budget data described as
not queryable/tabular [RESOLVED-BY-CORRECTION in v0.1 (corrected); raised by
external verification]
Locus: Section 3 (data-interface adapter), with follow-through in Section 4.4 and Section 6.
Substance: The first v0.1 text stated that the MTA capital budget data "is published as a derived
dashboard view rather than a queryable tabular resource, so a borough-level capital-dollar
analysis is not reproducible through this endpoint." This was false as a claim about the data
infrastructure. The producing lineage had observed that one dashboard resource ( mn7w-32rv)
would not serve rows and generalized "not queryable" to the entire capital dataset family without
testing the others. In fact kizb-nxtu and ehz8-ag3n are queryable tabular Socrata resources
carrying allocation dollars per project. The surface claim ("not queryable") diverged from the
substrate (the data is queryable), which is precisely the failure mode the note's own method
exists to detect, here committed by the note about its own data source.
Disposition: RESOLVED-BY-CORRECTION. The reason was corrected while the conclusion
was preserved, because the conclusion was independently sound: the budget tables carry
allocation dollars but no borough key, so a borough-level rollup requires joining to the locations
table (wcsa-vkhf) on the shared project number and then a coordinate-to-boundary spatial join,
a nontrivial GIS step rather than a single query, and is deferred rather than blocked. The
corrected text names the queryable resources explicitly and states the accurate reason. The
correction was itself externally re-verified (EV-2), including the functional join test. Root cause
recorded for future notes: an infrastructure claim was asserted from a single failed endpoint
without enumerating the dataset family; the standing remedy is that any "data not available"
claim in this series must enumerate and test the candidate resources before assertion.
Cross-reference: external verification EV-1, EV-2; Section 3; carried detail F-AA-2.


F-AA-2 INFO -- Column-name divergence across capital tables, carried for the geographic
instance [CARRIED; not an error in this note]
Locus: not in the reader-facing note; recorded here for the forthcoming by-geography capital
instance.
Substance: The capital tables do not share a column name for the project key: wcsa-vkhf and
kizb-nxtu use project_number, while ehz8-ag3n uses proj_num (same underlying
identifier). This does not affect any claim in the present note, which asserts a shared project
number only as a concept, not identical column names. It is logged because a future geographic
instance that joins these tables must handle the name divergence or silently produce empty joins.
Disposition: CARRIED to the by-geography capital instance. No action in this note.
Cross-reference: F-AA-1; external verification EV-2.

C. Falsifiability Criteria (note-level)
The worked example would be falsified, in whole or part, by any of the following, each
checkable from the frozen snapshot or the live endpoint. First, if the snapshot SHA-256 does not
match the manifest, the figures must not be trusted and the reproduction is void. Second, if the
MWBE count-versus-dollar divergence did not hold across all three fiscal years, the persistence
claim would fail; it is therefore stated with all three years exposed, not one. Third, if the vendor
dollar concentration were low (a flat distribution), the structural explanation offered in Section
4.3 for the MWBE dollar gap would lose its basis; the Gini of 0.931 and the top-ten share of 30.4
percent are the load-bearing evidence for that explanation and are reproducible. Fourth
[Corrected in v0.3 per F-AA-R2-04, Section 14.5]: the original criterion referred to a Section
4.1 "pass," which v0.2 withdrew. The corrected criterion is: if recomputation does not reproduce
the reported process-composition percentages, the descriptive Section 4.1 figures are falsified.
Separately and independently of any share being dominant, no composition result establishes
rule compliance, which requires the operative guidelines and exception documentation absent
from this dataset. Each of these is a specific number a second party can recompute and disagree
with.

Abstract
This method application note applies Structural Honesty Verification to public-authority
procurement. Its worked example is a descriptive, reproducible measurement, deliberately
narrowed after a first independent audit round that found the v0.1 draft attaching interpretive
claims its data could not support. The example measures, for the Metropolitan Transportation
Authority's FY2024 procurement report, the divergence between a participation metric counted
by contract and the same metric weighted by dollars, on two clearly named dollar estimands.
Businesses recorded as Minority- and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBE) as the
prime vendor hold 18.7 percent of FY2024 contract records but 3.95 percent of total reported
contract face value and 7.06 percent of that year's reported annual expenditure; contract face
value is highly concentrated (top-ten vendors 30.4 percent; Gini 0.931). A count-versus-dollar
asymmetry is present on both dollar measures and persists across three report vintages, though its
magnitude differs by measure (a factor of 4.7 on face value, 2.7 on annual expenditure) and the
annual-expenditure gap is narrowing. Crucially, the note reports these as descriptive primevendor statistics; it does not claim they measure attainment of any MWBE goal, does not treat
contract face value as annual spending, and does not conclude that competitive-process
composition demonstrates rule compliance. Those were overreaches in v0.1 and are removed.
The example remains a single-authority demonstration of a portable method, not a finding about
the authority.


3
1. Purpose and Scope
This paper instantiates the framework's allocation-and-asymmetry method on live public
procurement data. The framework (Arfeen 2026) establishes the method core, the two admission
filters, the tier discipline, and the per-jurisdiction adapter pattern; this paper supplies a fully
reproducible worked example.
The method verifies whether an institution's operative behavior, reconstructed from
public data, matches a declared rule, and reports structural divergences and asymmetries. This
version is deliberately conservative about what the available data can establish. It reports
descriptive composition and count-versus-dollar asymmetry. It does not determine whether a
declared rule is wise, whether any divergence is intentional, whether a participation goal was
met, or whether procurement complied with an authority's guidelines. The first three are Tier 3
adjudications; the fourth requires operative-guideline and transaction-documentation data this
dataset does not contain. All four are refused in Section 4.4.
2. The Method: Descriptive Count-versus-Dollar Asymmetry
The governing object of this note is the asymmetric-measure signature, imported from
Al-Mutaffifīn (Arfeen 2026): a metric that reads one way when counted and another when
weighted by the dollars it governs. In procurement, the canonical form is a participation rate that
is one value as a fraction of contract count and a smaller value as a fraction of contract dollars,
because the counted category is concentrated in many small awards while dollar volume pools in
a few large ones.
Two disciplines, both tightened across the audit rounds, govern how this signature is
reported. First, the dollar denominator must be a named estimand. "Contract dollars" is


4
ambiguous between the total face value of a contract (a stock, often spanning many years) and
the amount expended in a given fiscal year (an annual flow); the two differ by nearly an order of
magnitude here, and a count-versus-dollar ratio is meaningless until the denominator is fixed.
Second, the signature is descriptive. Observing that a category holds a larger share of count than
of dollars is a structural fact; concluding that this represents a failure to meet a goal, or a
deficient measure in the normative sense the mizan verse evokes, requires the goal's own
definition, denominator, and eligibility rules, which are exogenous to this dataset. The method
reports the asymmetry and stops there.
Every quantity here is Tier 1 (a contract amount is a number on a public ledger) or Tier 2
(a count-versus-dollar share depends on the disclosed choice of estimand, fiscal year, and
category flag). Nothing is Tier 3.
3. The Data-Interface Contract and the New York Adapter
The method's data-interface contract for procurement is: a public, record-level
procurement ledger exposing, per contract, one or more award-amount fields with defined
semantics, an award-process category, an award date, and any declared-category flags, at a
disclosed fiscal-year boundary.
The reference adapter maps a New York public-authority procurement report onto this
contract. New York public authorities report procurement annually; under Public Authorities
Law they submit through the Authorities Budget Office's PARIS system using standardized
reporting structures, and the ABO in collaboration with the state Open Data program publishes
compiled datasets. The result is a common schema across authorities, which is what makes a
single adapter reusable; the statute mandates the annual reporting, while PARIS and the


5
ABO/Open Data publication pipeline supply the common electronic schema and portal
availability.
Provenance, stated precisely (corrected in v0.2). The dataset queried here, Socrata
resource gpsc-qqsz on data.ny.gov, is a community-created view derived from the
statewide authority-procurement dataset; the portal notes that the state did not review or approve
view modifications. A first-party, MTA-attributed dataset, twsw-2mqa, is separately published.
The two are close but not identical: for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2024, gpsc-qqsz
returns 13,718 records summing to $65.19 billion in contract face value, while twsw-2mqa
returns 13,648 records summing to $65.13 billion. The face-value divergence is about 0.089
percent (under 0.1 percent), but the record counts differ by about 0.5 percent (70 records);
neither affects the qualitative findings, but both must be disclosed separately rather than under a
single sub-0.1-percent label. A production audit should rebase on the first-party or ABO
statewide dataset and reconcile the community view; this draft retains gpsc-qqsz for continuity
with the archived snapshot and describes it accurately as a derived view. The frozen three-year
extract used here (fiscal years ending 2022, 2023, and 2024) contains 37,988 records (12,156,
12,114, and 13,718 respectively); the full gpsc-qqsz resource across all reported periods
contains about 111,879 records, a figure that in v0.1 was incorrectly attributed to the three-year
window.
The adapter also records what the ledger does not directly support: a by-geography
allocation analysis. The MTA capital budget datasets (kizb-nxtu, ehz8-ag3n) are queryable
tabular resources carrying allocation dollars per project, but they lack a borough key; project
location is published only as coordinates in a separate table ( wcsa-vkhf), so borough attribution


6
requires a project-number join followed by a coordinate-to-boundary spatial join, a GIS step
deferred to a dedicated geographic instance.
4. Worked Example: MTA FY2024 Procurement Report
4.0 Naming the estimand, and a stock-versus-flow disclosure
The FY2024 report (fiscal year ending December 31, 2024) contains 13,718 records. It
carries two distinct dollar fields with different meanings. contract_amount is the total face
value of a contract, which for a multi-year contract spans many fiscal years; summed over the
report it is $65.19 billion. amount_expended_for_fiscal_year is the amount actually spent
under those contracts during FY2024; summed it is $8.17 billion. These are not interchangeable,
and neither is "FY2024 spending" without qualification.
A stock-versus-flow disclosure is essential and was absent in v0.1. Award dates in the
FY2024 report range from 1984 to 2025, and 91.7 percent of the summed contract face value
belongs to contracts awarded before 2024; only 8.3 percent was awarded in 2024. The $65.19
billion is therefore the face-value stock of all contracts appearing in the FY2024 report, not a
flow of FY2024 awards or spending. Relatedly, because multi-year contracts recur across annual
reports, the same contract appears in more than one vintage. This must be measured with a
stable-field fingerprint, not an exact all-field one: an exact match on every field finds zero shared
records across vintages, because the fiscal-year field and the annual-state fields (expenditure-forfiscal-year, expenditure-to-date, and outstanding balance) differ by construction between
vintages. Matching instead on all fields except the fiscal-year field and the three annual-state
fields (expenditure-for-fiscal-year, expenditure-to-date, and outstanding balance) -- the
remaining fields being stable contract-identity attributes such as vendor, procurement


7
description, award process, award and term dates, and contract face value -- finds 2,115, 604,
and 1,002 shared records between the FY2022/FY2023, FY2022/FY2024, and FY2023/FY2024
vintages respectively. (Matching on only the five-or-so enumerated identity fields rather than the
full non-excluded set yields larger counts and is not the method used here; the reported figures
come from excluding exactly the four fiscal-year and annual-state fields.) The three annual
snapshots are therefore not independent samples and must never be summed. Where this note
reports figures "across three report vintages," it means exactly that -- repeated observations of an
overlapping contract portfolio -- not three independent annual flows.
Of the 13,718 records, 1,348 carry a missing contract_amount and 48 carry an
explicit zero (1,396 total, 10.2 percent); these are analytically distinct and are separated here.
Notably, the two award-process categories with no contract_amount (state-contract and noncontract purchase orders) do carry annual expenditure, so they vanish from face-value figures but
not from expenditure figures.
4.1 Process composition (descriptive; no compliance claim)
By contract face value, "Authority Contract - Competitive Bid" is $60.12 billion, 92.2
percent, across 10,876 records (79.3 percent by count); "Non-Competitive Bid" is $5.07 billion,
7.8 percent. By annual expenditure, the four categories are competitive 89.65 percent, noncompetitive 4.73 percent, purchased-under-state-contract 3.24 percent, and non-contract
purchase order 2.38 percent.
This is reported as descriptive composition only. v0.1 declared this a "pass" of a
competitive-bidding rule, asserting that substrate matched surface; that claim is withdrawn. A
high competitive share does not demonstrate compliance with the authority's operative


8
procurement rule: testing that would require the MTA's own procurement guidelines, the
permitted exception categories, the waiver and documentation requirements under Public
Authorities Law Section 2879, and a transaction-level or defensibly-sampled check that each
non-competitive award fits a documented exception, together with validation of the authority's
own process coding. None of that is in this dataset, so the method reports the composition and
withholds any rule-compliance conclusion.
4.2 MWBE prime-vendor count-versus-dollar asymmetry (descriptive)
Businesses flagged as MWBE prime vendors hold 2,570 of 13,718 FY2024 records, 18.7
percent by count. The same flag holds 3.95 percent of contract face value and 7.06 percent of
FY2024 annual expenditure. The participation metric measured by count is thus about 4.7 times
its face-value share and about 2.7 times its annual-expenditure share. Across the three report
vintages, the count share is 16.4, 18.6, 18.7 percent; the face-value share is 3.27, 3.51, 3.95
percent (ratio 5.0, 5.3, 4.7); and the annual-expenditure share is 4.25, 6.27, 7.06 percent (ratio
3.9, 3.0, 2.7). A count-versus-dollar asymmetry is present on both dollar measures, but its
magnitude depends on the measure and the annual-expenditure gap is narrowing, not stable.
This is a descriptive prime-vendor statistic, and v0.2 removes the goal-attainment
framing v0.1 attached to it. The vendor_is_a_mwbe flag identifies whether the recorded prime
vendor is an MWBE; it does not capture indirect participation through subcontractors or joint
ventures, the eligible-spend denominator against which a utilization goal is assessed, contractspecific goals tied to available subcontracting opportunities and disparity-study categories, or
waivers and exemptions. New York MWBE utilization goals are defined over those constructs
(Executive Law Article 15-A), not over a binary prime-vendor flag on total contract face value.
Consequently this note does not claim the 3.95 or 7.06 percent figure measures attainment of any


9
goal, does not call the dollar share the "operative substrate" or the count share the "short
measure," and does not infer goal compliance or its absence. What it reports is narrower and still
real: as a prime vendor, the MWBE-flagged share of records is several times its share of either
dollar measure, persistently across vintages.
4.3 Vendor concentration (face-value stock)
Contract face value is highly concentrated: in FY2024 the top five vendors hold 22.1
percent, the top ten 30.4 percent, and the top twenty 41.8 percent, with a Gini of 0.931 across
2,656 distinct vendor strings and no negative amounts. The largest holdings are rolling-stock and
heavy-construction contracts (a rail-car manufacturer at $6.46 billion, a bus manufacturer at
$2.56 billion, and construction joint ventures above $1.5 billion). Annual-expenditure value is
also concentrated, though less extremely: top five 16.9 percent, top ten 26.2 percent, top twenty
37.6 percent, Gini 0.904. Both measures are reproduced in the accompanying script.
The concentration on both dollar measures (face-value Gini 0.931; annual-expenditure
Gini 0.904) supplies a structural explanation for the count-versus-dollar asymmetry on both:
when a large share of dollars is committed to a handful of very large capital contracts not held by
MWBE prime vendors, the dollar-weighted MWBE share is mechanically pulled below the
count share regardless of how many small contracts MWBE vendors hold. Stating this
mechanism is within the method's authority because it is a structural fact about where dollars
concentrate. Concluding from it that the authority steers dollars away from any group, or that it
does not, is a Tier 3 judgment the method refuses. The concentration finding is presented
precisely to forestall that leap.


10
4.4 What the method emits, and what it refuses
The method emits, for the FY2024 MTA procurement report on named estimands: the
process composition by face value and by annual expenditure (Tier 2, descriptive); the MWBE
prime-vendor count share and its face-value and annual-expenditure shares, with three-vintage
figures and the repeat-reporting caveat (Tier 2, descriptive); the face-value vendor concentration
and Gini (Tier 2); and the scan-incomplete declarations (the stock-versus-flow composition, the
missing-versus-zero split, the deferred by-geography analysis, the community-view provenance).
It refuses: any determination of intent, steering, discrimination, favoritism, or fraud (Tier 3); any
claim that a dollar share measures attainment of an MWBE goal (outside the dataset's
constructs); any claim that competitive-process composition demonstrates rule compliance
(untested against operative guidelines); and any characterization of its outputs as fraud findings
or court-admissible evidence. Its outputs are descriptive structural measurements that an
oversight body or advocate may use as one input under its own standards.
5. Portability
The method is demonstrated on one authority. Its portability rests on the data-interface
contract: any jurisdiction publishing a record-level procurement ledger with defined amount
semantics, a process category, and declared-category flags can be audited by writing an adapter.
New York is favorable because many authorities report through the shared PARIS structures, so
the adapter applies with minimal change across authorities publishing to the same compiled
schema, which makes a second-authority instance readily available. That claim remains designed
and single-instance: this paper demonstrates the New York adapter, and cross-jurisdiction
transfer to a differently structured municipal ledger is stated but not yet shown.


11
6. Limitations
Beyond the tier limits, this note carries data-specific limitations made explicit after the
first audit round. The headline dollar figure is a face-value stock spanning awards from 1984 to
2025, not annual spending, and the annual-flow measure is nearly an order of magnitude smaller.
The three report vintages share many of the same multi-year contracts and cannot be summed or
treated as independent. The MWBE figure is a prime-vendor flag only, without indirect
participation, eligible-spend denominators, contract-specific goals, or waivers, and therefore
cannot speak to goal attainment. The competitive-process composition is not a compliance test.
The source is a derived community view that diverges slightly from the first-party dataset. The
MWBE flag and process coding are taken as published and not independently validated. The
paper began producer-side and has now converged. The single operational metric is the
consecutive qualifying-PASS count, which is TWO. Nine audit rounds have occurred: three
NON-PASS (F-AA-R1, F-AA-R2, F-AA-R3); a consistency-only PASS not credited (F-AA-R4);
a findings-bearing NON-PASS (F-AA-R5); the first qualifying pass (F-AA-R6, count to one); a
findings-bearing NON-PASS (F-AA-R7, reset to zero); a qualifying pass (F-AA-R8, count to
one); and a second consecutive qualifying pass (F-AA-R9, count to two). F-AA-R8 and F-AAR9 together are the two consecutive qualifying passes the methodology requires, so the
convergence gate is met on this artifact (released as v1.0). The convergence caveats (both
passing rounds shared the same three-member set, distinguished only by fresh instances; the two
rounds audited materially-identical substance) and the remaining owner-side deposit action are
recorded in the companion.


12
7. Provenance and Verification
The design vocabulary (the mizan as honest measurement, the asymmetric-measure
signature, the tier discipline) is drawn from structural readings of the Qur'an and is inspiration,
not evidence: every figure in Section 4 is justified entirely by public data, arithmetic, and
disclosed parameters. The program's own empirical foundation is explicit that the underlying
textual-structure finding is small and partly a length-sort artifact, with an earlier Fibonaccispecificity claim falsified and retracted (Arfeen 2026, al-Munāsabāt); this paper leans on none of
that. This is version 1.0, the canonical converged release (the convergence gate was met on the
identical v0.7 substance). It has been through nine independent cross-instance audit rounds
recorded in the companion. Three were NON-PASS and absorbed (F-AA-R1, F-AA-R2 by
OpenAI GPT; F-AA-R3 by the Claude producing lineage, non-qualifying). A fourth (F-AA-R4,
Gemini) returned PASS on a consistency review only and is not credited. A fifth (F-AA-R5) was
a findings-bearing NON-PASS. A sixth (F-AA-R6) was the first genuine qualifying pass. A
seventh (F-AA-R7) was a findings-bearing NON-PASS on a producer status-propagation defect
that reset the count to zero. The eighth and ninth (F-AA-R8 and F-AA-R9, rotated Model
Councils) were two consecutive qualifying passes: three qualifying non-producer members (GPT
5.5, GPT 5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro) each executed the full reproduction and returned zero critical and
zero high in both rounds, with all prior findings confirmed resolved. The single operational
metric, the consecutive qualifying-PASS count, is TWO, so the convergence gate under Standing
Rule 7 is met on this artifact. Two caveats are recorded honestly with the declaration: the two
consecutive passing rounds used the same three-member set (independence between them rests
on fresh, memoryless instances rather than differing model identities), and they audited
materially-identical substance (the only change between the two was one companion wording


13
fix). The reproduction package is deposited under an immutable DOI alongside the audit and
provenance ledger (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21445556), making the reproduction fully arm's-length.
8. Data Availability and Reproduction
Every figure in Section 4 is reproducible from the New York State open-data portal
without authentication. The source queried is the community view gpsc-qqsz; the first-party
MTA dataset twsw-2mqa and the ABO statewide authority-procurement dataset are the
recommended production sources and should be reconciled against it. FY2024 is selected with
fiscal_year_end_date='2024-12-31T00:00:00.000'. Face-value figures use
contract_amount; annual-flow figures use amount_expended_for_fiscal_year; award-

year composition uses award_date. The frozen three-year snapshot (37,988 records), its
manifest (with a programmatically regenerated field inventory validated against the rows) and
SHA-256, and a reproduction script that verifies the hash and recomputes every figure on both
estimands for all three years accompany this paper as a single reproduction package
(Bayyinah_AllocationAsymmetry_ReproPackage), deposited under an immutable DOI
alongside the audit and provenance ledger at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21445556; anyone can
retrieve it there and re-run the full reproduction. Missing (1,348) and explicit-zero (48) amounts
are reported separately.

About this companion
This document is the append-only audit trail for the reader-facing paper. It exists so that any
claim in the paper can be traced to how it was established, and so that every error caught and
corrected during development remains on the public record rather than being silently smoothed
away. Preserving this trail is itself load-bearing: it is the demonstration that the paper practices
the structural honesty it proposes.
It contains four parts: the full per-claim Verification Status; the complete findings ledger in three
namespaces (F-ED development findings, F-RV producer-lineage continuity review, F-PR
internal peer review), each in the six-element format the methodology requires; the paper-level
falsifiability criteria; and the append-only version ledger from v0.1 through v1.0-rc6 with its
Next Audit Cycle status.
Section numbers referenced inside the findings and ledger (for example "Section 4.4.6," "Section
3," "Section 4.1") refer to the reader-facing paper. Finding disposition tags (RESOLVED,
PARTIALLY-RESOLVED, ABSORBED, OPEN, RESOLVED-AND-RETAINED) and
severity tokens (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) follow the Audit Framework severity
rubric. Per Bayyinah Audit Framework v3.0 Section 14.5, superseded text is preserved verbatim
in the ledger and corrected by annotation, never edited in place.
Convergence status, stated plainly: the paper is producer-complete, and one of the two required
independent audit rounds has now passed. It carries 0 open CRITICAL findings and nothing
open above LOW. The methodology's convergence criterion -- two consecutive audit rounds by
a Tier 1 auditor outside the authoring lineage, each returning 0 CRITICAL and 0 HIGH -- is not
yet fully met: a first independent, non-lineage audit round (namespace F-XA, performed by a
non-Anthropic auditor) returned PASS at 0 CRITICAL and 0 HIGH with 6 LOW findings, all
now absorbed (see the v1.0-rc7 -> v1.0-rc8 appendix). A second independent round (namespace
F-AT-R2, also a non-Anthropic auditor) then reproduced the results and also returned 0
CRITICAL and 0 HIGH (1 MEDIUM, 1 LOW, absorbed in v1.0-rc9). However, that auditor
expressly attested its round was NOT qualifying for convergence: it shares the OpenAI/GPT
model family with the first-round auditor, and it did not run in a fresh, carryover-free context. By
the Knight-Leveson correlated-blind-spot standard this program applies, two rounds from the
same model family in shared context do not satisfy the independence the gate intends. A third


round (namespace F-AT-R3) then supplied that different family: a Gemini auditor in a fresh
context passed at 0 CRITICAL and 0 HIGH (2 INFO), the first fully-qualifying different-family

unqualified "shipped" status is that second passing independent round.

B. Findings
Ordered by severity, then locus. F-ED-1 through F-ED-7 were raised against the prior-session
draft; F-ED-8 through F-ED-14 against the worked-example target system and this paper's own
citation and reproducibility practices. Absorption status is annotated per finding (append-only;
original text preserved in the Appendix ledger).
F-ED-1 CRITICAL → ABSORBED [v1.0] -- Tanzīl phased-progression proposed as
fairness-optimizing is, as written, a grade-retention and tracking mechanism Locus: priorsession draft, section "Tanzīl Phased Progression." Substance: Surface claims fairness
optimization and guaranteed intervention; substrate is a hard prerequisite gate that stops
promotion. Grade retention and tracking are tied in the empirical record to disproportionate
pushout and elevated dropout among low-income and minority students. The gate detects nonmastery but did not, as originally proposed, fund remediation, so "guarantees intervention" was a
surface claim with no substrate behind it. Disposition: ABSORBED in v1.0 as ED-K4
(remediation-coupled mastery gate, Section 4.1), per the project lead's explicit disposition
("apply the required couplings"). The gate is refused unless both couplings are present, disclosed,
and logged: (a) an automatically-triggered, dosage-and-funding-disclosed, attendance-logged
remediation pathway; (b) an independent ED-K2 disaggregated subgroup regression gate,
retained as the primary safeguard because (a) has not been shown, anywhere in the literature
reviewed, to eliminate subgroup disparity on its own (Westall, Utter & Strunk 2023). Pinned
citations and honest caveats are given in full under ED-K4. Cross-reference: ED-K4, ED-K2; atTartīb 20070782 Section 6.2; severity-rubric CRITICAL boundary.
F-ED-2 HIGH -- Mizan-calibrated assessment claimed to "remove grading demographic
bias" [ABSORBED v0.2] Locus: prior-session draft, section "Mīzān-Calibrated Assessment."
Substance: Surface claimed bias removal; substrate cannot deliver it (calibration and equalized
error rates mutually exclusive once base rates differ; bias also in rubric, items, training data).
Disposition: ABSORBED as ED-U3 (Mizan-calibrated abstention), restated as three-valued
honest abstention with the bias-removal claim deleted and the impossibility result cited. Crossreference: ED-U3; Section 2.
F-ED-3 HIGH -- Reproducibility conflated with validation in the graduate graduation
trigger [ABSORBED v0.2] Locus: prior-session draft, section "Graduate & Master's Level
Research." Substance: Surface presented byte-deterministic reproduction as a graduationvalidation trigger; reproduction gates provenance (Tier 1), not merit (Tier 3). Disposition:
ABSORBED in ED-G1, reclassified as a necessary Tier 1 precondition, never sufficient; merit
stated as a retained human Tier 3 judgment. Cross-reference: ED-G1; Section 3 Tier falsifiability
rule.
F-ED-4 HIGH -- Immutable transcript ledger collides with the right to rectification
[ABSORBED v0.2] Locus: prior-session draft, sections "Additive-Only Transcript Ledgers" and
"immutable ledger." Substance: Surface claimed immutability as integrity; an immutable student
record conflicts with error correction, FERPA rights, and expungement. Disposition:
ABSORBED in ED-K2 and ED-G3 as append-only-with-correcting-entries (silent deletion
prohibited, logged correction permitted; §14.5). In a deployed system handling protected records
this escalates to CRITICAL (regulatory). Cross-reference: ED-K2, ED-G3; producer sub-skill
Step 5.

F-ED-8 HIGH -- ED-K1 fires on the historical allocation-versus-formula divergence with
weight-category regressivity [RESOLVED-AND-RETAINED; magnitude verified v0.2;
corrected v1.0; corrected again v1.0-rc2] Locus: NYC DOE published FSF allocation and
formula amounts, FY2011 to FY2022 (IBO fsf2013); School Allocation Memoranda. Substance:
Surface (need-weighted equity, 100 percent of formula = fully funded) diverged from substrate
(FY2011 median 75.4 percent of formula, about 98 percent of schools below; FY2012 median
86.0 percent, 94.0 percent below). At the weight-category level, the negative implied weight for
below-standards students is confirmed (schools serving more such students received less
funding). Corrected in v1.0: the more specific v0.2 claim naming elementary/high-school ELL
and high-school special-education CTT students as funded significantly below formula weight
was downgraded to unconfirmed, on the ground that the attribution "was not located verbatim" in
the report. Corrected again in v1.0-rc2 (F-RV-1): that v1.0 downgrade was itself wrong. A
producer-lineage continuity review flagged it as a retrieval-miss error, and re-fetching the report
in this session confirms the review: the report's section "Students Funded Below, Close to, or
Above Formula Weight" states the attribution verbatim, naming middle-school students below
academic standards, elementary and high-school ELL students, and high-school specialeducation CTT students as funded below formula weight in 2011-2012 and at least two other
years, with supporting category-level figures (high-school ELL implied weights of 0.30-0.37
against a 0.50 formula weight; special-education CTT students receiving half or less of the 2.52
formula weight in the first two years). The claim is restored to confirmed. The Layer 1 resolution
announcement (April 19, 2021, de Blasio/Porter, 2021-22 school year, not a January 2023
Adams/Banks announcement) and the Voloch (2015) end-to-end verification are unaffected by
this continuity review and stand as corrected in v1.0. Disposition: Layer 1 RESOLVED per the


2021-22-school-year 100-percent floor (date/administration corrected v1.0); retained as the EDK1 demonstration and logged append-only with its resolution. Tier 1 ratio is ship-grade; the
specific ELL/CTT below-weight attribution is restored to confirmed (v1.0-rc2, correcting the
v1.0 error); the Voloch school-level relationship remains merged as an independently verified,
distinct Tier 2 claim. Cross-reference: ED-K1, ED-K2; Al-Mutaffifīn 19894724 Sections 2 and
4.1a; Section 4.4; F-RV-1.
F-ED-9 MEDIUM -- Tier boundary held on the current formula-adequacy layer [refusaldemonstration] Locus: NYC DOE FSF weights FY2024 to FY2025 (STH, Concentration
Need); IBO May 29, 2025. Substance: Current surface (the formula now captures concentrated
need) meets a substrate in which the corrective weights are small per pupil (about 78 dollars per
pupil STH; about 95,000 dollars average across 304 schools) and, per IBO, unlikely to move
system-wide outcomes, with possible budget instability. The framework emits the Tier 2
magnitude and refuses the Tier 3 adequacy verdict; IBO independently drew the same boundary.
Disposition: Emit Tier 2 magnitude and the scan-incomplete declaration; do not emit an
adequacy verdict. No absorption required; the mechanism is behaving correctly. Cross-reference:
F-ED-3, F-ED-7; Section 3 Tier falsifiability rule; Al-Mutaffifīn 19894724 Section 3.1.
F-ED-10 MEDIUM -- Walkthrough arithmetic is internally consistent and matches the
Comptroller Initial column, but the Initial-to-Final divergence is only partially explained
[PARTIALLY-RESOLVED; new in v1.0; Tier-corrected v1.0-rc2; decomposed v1.0-rc4]
Locus: NYC DOE FSF Public App Detail Reports versus NYC Comptroller FY23/FY24 School
Budget Allocations Mastersheet, for five sample schools (28Q160, 10X085, 30Q258, 14K488,
30Q148). Substance: Independently reconstructing each school's Total FY2023 FSF Allocation
from its DOE Detail Report's disclosed walkthrough terms (base allocation at the FY2022
register and $4,223.00 base rate, teacher-salary change, register-change adjustment, $225,000
foundation, and three collective-bargaining/state-aid adjustment terms) reproduced the DOE's
own published total to within $2-$18 (rounding) for all five schools. On first comparison, this
reconstructed total differed from the Comptroller mastersheet's "FY2023 Final" FSF figure for
the identical schools by amounts ranging from −2.2 percent (−$94,292, school 28Q160) to +12.5
percent (+$539,067, school 30Q258), non-uniform across schools -- large enough that citing "the
FY2023 FSF allocation" for a school without specifying report vintage would be a false claim.
Tracing the mastersheet's own columns resolved this rather than leaving it as an open
discrepancy: the recomputed/DOE-reported figure matches the mastersheet's "FY2023 Initial"
column exactly (to the same $2-$18 rounding) for all five schools, and the divergence from
"FY2023 Final" is only partially explained by the mastersheet's disclosed Register Relief
column. Corrected in v1.0-rc4 (F-PR-1): the v1.0-rc3 claim that this divergence is "fully
explained by Register Relief and a mid-year enrollment change" does not survive a per-school
decomposition against the archived data. The correct comparison is Initial FSF versus Final FSF
plus Register Relief, because relief exists to offset enrollment-driven register loss. Residuals
(Final FSF + Register Relief minus Initial FSF): 30Q258 +$1,007 and 14K488 +$10,521 (relief
offsets the enrollment loss; reconciles within about $11k), but 28Q160 +$95,668, 10X085 +
$218,563, and 30Q148 +$224,353 (a net-positive residual that relief and enrollment do not
explain). Most sharply, 28Q160's Final FSF rises $94,292 while its enrollment falls 12 students
and its Final Register Relief is only $1,376, so relief and enrollment cannot be the cause; the
residual for these three schools is consistent with a mid-year rate/collective-bargaining rebenchmark that the archived Initial-vintage walkthrough does not itemize. All five residuals are


positive, so once relief is included every sample school's FSF-side funding held at or above its
Initial level. Corrected in v1.0-rc2 (F-RV-2, F-RV-3): v1.0-rc1 labeled the walkthrougharithmetic result "a genuine Tier 1 byte-determinism result" and its Section 4.4.6 falsifiability
criterion as "Tier 1 valid once report vintage is disclosed." Both statements are corrected.
Because reproducing the DOE's published total depends on disclosing which report vintage
(Initial versus Final) is being matched, a disclosed parameter choice, the result is Tier 2
(Structural) by Section 3's own definition, not Tier 1: a Tier 1 label with a required disclosed
parameter is a contradiction in this paper's own terms. Separately, the reviewing instance in the
continuity review attempted to independently re-run this recompute and could not: the DOE FSF
Public App returned robots-disallowed and the Comptroller mastersheet returned an Incapsula
bot-detection challenge. The recompute is therefore also tagged single-instance, not
independently reproduced, until the underlying five-school extract and mastersheet rows are
archived as a companion dataset (see F-ED-11). Disposition: PARTIALLY-RESOLVED, Tier
reclassified (v1.0-rc4). The recompute is Tier 2 valid once report vintage (Initial versus Final) is
disclosed as a required parameter; Section 4.4.6's falsifiability criterion 2 is amended
accordingly, and the single-instance status is disclosed rather than presented as settled. The
Initial-to-Final divergence is partially, not fully, explained by the archived data: register relief
offsets the enrollment-driven change for two of five schools, and a net-positive rate/CB residual
(roughly $96k to $224k) remains for the other three that the Initial-vintage walkthrough does not
itemize. Scan-incomplete declaration: closing that residual requires the Final-vintage Detail
Report walkthrough per school, which is not in the archive and is logged as an open item at FED-13. The status is downgraded from RESOLVED to PARTIALLY-RESOLVED accordingly;
the v1.0-rc3 "fully explained" wording is preserved in the ledger per §14.5. The Tier mislabeling
in v1.0-rc1 remains recorded. Cross-reference: Section 4.4.6; ED-K1; F-ED-11; F-RV-2; F-RV3; source files: NYC DOE FSF Public App Detail Reports (28Q160, 10X085, 30Q258, 14K488,
30Q148), FY2023; NYC Comptroller FY23/FY24 Mastersheet.

paragraph); Section 4.1 mechanism ED-K4; Section 4.4.6 recompute (F-ED-10). Substance: This
paper distinguishes read-end-to-end, snippet-level, and pinned-not-verified provenance for its
worked-example claims (FSF allocation figures, Voloch), but had not applied the same discipline
to the ED-K4 remediation-pathway citations, which were described simply as "pinned" without

Verification Status ED-K4 paragraph and Section 4.1 now state explicitly which ED-K4 figures
