1

Procurement Concentration and Potentially Recoverable
Competitive Savings in New York City Contracting
A Cost-Recovery Proposal and Pilot Design
Bayyinah Civic Integrity Program -- Working Paper (Version 1.0, converged: F-PCR1 NON-PASS, then F-PC-R2 and F-PC-R3 qualifying passes; consecutive qualifyingPASS count TWO; rotation closed) Prepared July 2026. Corresponding: Bilal Arfeen,
BayyinahEnterprise. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21447217. Audit and provenance ledger and dataset:
DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21447219.
Audit status notice: This paper was originally synthesized by a single AI instance in a
single research session from primary-source data (NYC Comptroller vendor-level microdata, NY
State MTA procurement data, and academic procurement-savings literature), and at first had not
been through the multi-round independent audit process applied to Bayyinah's other civicintegrity papers (at-Ta'līm and AllocationAsymmetry). Its empirical spine (the concentration
measurement, the savings arithmetic, the MTA cross-check, and the Appendix 1 reconciliation)
has since been independently reproduced and audited across three cross-instance rounds: F-PCR1 returned NON-PASS on one HIGH finding (a false quantitative assurance in the Section 5.0
basis note) plus supporting findings, all absorbed; F-PC-R2 and F-PC-R3 were qualifying passes
(zero CRITICAL and zero HIGH), advancing the consecutive qualifying-PASS count to TWO,
with the rotation closed by a member new to the second pass. Convergence is therefore MET
under Audit Framework v3.0, Standing Rule 7. Convergence here certifies structural honesty -that every figure reproduces from primary sources, that the disclosures (the two bases, the
coverage gap, the intermediary screen) are accurate, and that the refusal boundary holds -- and


2
does NOT certify that the savings estimate is verified recoverable or policy-ready; that remains a
conditional, pilot-gated planning range per Section 5.0. Two honest caveats: the two consecutive
passes rest on materially-identical substance (the audited versions differ only in wording and
tooling, no figure moved); and convergence is met inside this producer-defined governance
framework, while the externally-verifiable core -- every figure reproducing from the public
Comptroller and data.ny.gov sources -- holds independently of the framework.


3

Abstract
New York City registers roughly $42.4 billion in new contracts annually, of which about
$21.6 billion (50.9%) is awarded through Limited-or-Non-Competitive methods rather than open
bidding (FY25 Annual Summary Contracts Report). This paper narrows that headline figure to
an "addressable" base of roughly $5.66 to $6.98 billion per year -- the Sole Source, Negotiated
Acquisition, and (optionally) Emergency subgroups -- after excluding categories that are either
already competitively bid in substance (Innovative Procurement / Design-Build) or structurally
non-competitive by design (Government-to-Government, Intergovernmental). We cross-check
vendor concentration in the two largest addressable subgroups against an independently
reproduced concentration analysis of Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA)
procurement, using identical Gini-coefficient and top-N methodology. The comparison shows
NYC's Sole Source subgroup is more concentrated than MTA's entire procurement book (Gini
0.956 vs. 0.931) -- but the concentration is driven overwhelmingly by a single quasigovernmental vehicle (NYCEDC, 82.5% of the subgroup), not by private-market vendor capture.
Applying literature-grounded competitive-savings rates (10 to 20%) to the addressable base
yields a conditional planning range with a headline near $500 million to $1.4 billion per year,
and a sensitivity floor near $434 million once the largest quasi-governmental vehicle (NYCEDC)
is excluded. This range is not a verified recoverable amount: it is gated on a pilot (Section 7) that
tests whether the underlying spend has viable alternative vendors, the assumption the whole
estimate rests on. We propose four concrete policy interventions and a bounded 12 to 18 month
pilot program to test the model's central assumption -- that a meaningful share of Sole Source
spend has viable alternative vendors -- before any citywide claim is made.


4

1. Introduction
New York City's contracting apparatus has two structural tracks: Group 1 (Competitive
Method Contracts, awarded via sealed bid or RFP) and Group 2 (Limited or Non-Competitive
Method Contracts, awarded via one of twelve statutory exceptions to competitive bidding under
Procurement Policy Board rules) (Comptroller's Contract Primer). Group 2 is not inherently
improper -- it exists because some goods and services genuinely cannot be competitively bid
(true single-source technology, legally mandated vendors, emergencies). But at 50.9% of
citywide contract value in FY25, it is also the segment where competitive-pricing pressure is
weakest, and therefore the segment where cost recovery is most plausible if even a fraction of it
could be moved toward genuine competition.
This paper is the fourth research leg in the Bayyinah civic-integrity research program,
alongside the at-Ta'līm Fair Student Funding fidelity verifier (education equity, not cost savings)
and the AllocationAsymmetry paper (MTA procurement/expenditure divergence and vendor
concentration, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21445552). Where those papers focused on formula fidelity
and data-provenance integrity respectively, this paper asks a narrower and more operational
question: how much of NYC's non-competitive contracting is realistically recoverable, and what
would a city agency need to do to test that recovery in practice.

2. Background: NYC's Two-Group Procurement System
Table 1 shows the FY25 disaggregation of Group 2 into its twelve statutory subgroups,
all figures from Table 7 of the FY25 Annual Summary Contracts Report.

For comparison, the FY23 subgroup breakdown (FY23 Annual Summary Contracts
Report, Table 7) shows Sole Source at $3,672,247,394 (24.72% of that year's Group 2) and
Innovative Procurement at $3,480,627,013 (23.43%) -- meaning Innovative Procurement's share
roughly doubled and Sole Source's dollar value fell by more than half between FY23 and FY25,
largely a function of which mega-projects (jails vs. other capital work) happened to register in
each fiscal year rather than a change in underlying policy. The full FY23 breakdown spans
thirteen subgroups (the twelve above plus a discontinued "Buy-Against Procurement Contracts"
category, $9,550,554 / 3 contracts, that does not recur in FY25) and is itemized in the companion
dataset.
A separate, unresolved question concerns the Department of Education specifically.
DOE's own Table 96 shows Limited/Non-Competitive contracts falling from a FY2016 baseline


7
of 64% of contract value ($2.7B of $4.29B, ME17_078F) to 29.89% of value in the FY23 to
FY25 cumulative table, while the contract-count share stayed high (83.95%). We believe this
decline in dollar share is substantially a reporting artifact -- large multi-year mega-contracts (e.g.,
NYCSSS custodial services, $2.56B over 4 years or $6.36B over 8 years, NYS OSC audit 2020N-8) register once and then drop out of subsequent years' "new registration" tables -- rather than
genuine improvement. This is corroborated by a live, ongoing dispute: the City Council is
currently auditing approximately $12.9 billion per year in DOE external contracting, of which
DOE has self-classified 352 of 579 requested contracts as "not competitively bid," and DOE has
missed the Council's document deadline, prompting Speaker Menin to cite a "pattern of opacity,
slow-walking, and delay" and threaten a subpoena (NY Post, July 14, 2026). We exclude DOE
from the quantitative addressable-base calculation below because its true non-competitive
footprint cannot currently be reconciled with confidence -- but flag it as the single largest source
of upside uncertainty in either direction.
A related structural blind spot, unconnected to any single agency, is the Comptroller's
own May 2026 finding on "Monty Hall Contracts" -- $625 million in Accelerated Procurement
spend under master agreements since FY22 that has received zero Comptroller review
(Comptroller report, May 2026). This is a distinct category from the ones analyzed below and is
not included in our addressable-base figure, but it is directly relevant to Recommendation 2
(Section 6.2).


8
3. Methodology
3.1 Data sources
•

Contract-level and vendor-level microdata: NYC Comptroller Appendix 1 -- Registered
Contracts by Group, Industry, Agency Type, and Retroactivity Category, 55,224 rows,
FY22 to FY25, with fields including Vendor Legal Name, Subgroup, Award Method,
Registered Amount, and Registering Agency.

•

Aggregate subgroup figures: FY25 Annual Summary Contracts Report and the FY23
Annual Contracts Report.

•

MTA comparison figures: independently reproduced (across nine audit rounds by
multiple model instances) statistics from the Bayyinah AllocationAsymmetry paper,
sourced from the New York State MTA Procurement Report (All) dataset.

•

Competitive-savings literature: a Czech single-bid reform study finding roughly 10%
price reduction after eliminating single-bidder awards (Utrecht working paper); a Slovak
study finding roughly a 19-percentage-point gap between multi-bidder (~19% below
estimate) and single-bidder (~1% below estimate) outcomes (JKU study); and a broader
U.S. federal 10 to 40% range from GAO and OMB reviews of competitive vs. noncompetitive sourcing (GAO-10-833; OMB paper).

3.2 Addressable-base construction and exclusion criteria
We start from the full $21.59B Group 2 total and exclude subgroups on the following
grounds:
•

Innovative Procurement ($10.98B) -- excluded. As detailed in Section 4.3, this
subgroup in FY25 is dominated by Design-Build contracts for the Borough-Based Jails


9
program, which the Comptroller's own report states were competitively bid; the Group 2
classification reflects a PPB rulebook categorization for methods not yet codified, not an
absence of competition (PPB Rule §3-12, American Legal Publishing).
•

Government-to-Government ($891M) and Intergovernmental ($623M) -- excluded.
These are, by definition, transactions between government entities where private-market
competition is not a meaningful counterfactual.

•

Determined by Government Mandate ($871M) -- excluded. Legally mandated vendor
relationships have no competitive alternative by construction.

•

Discretionary (Line Item), Small Purchase, Micropurchase, Demonstration Project
(combined ~$1.24B) -- excluded. These are low-dollar, high-volume categories where
competitive-bid overhead would likely exceed any recoverable savings.

•

Sole Source ($1.60B) and Negotiated Acquisition ($4.06B) -- included as the core
addressable base ($5.66B). These are the two subgroups where a plausible, if imperfect,
competitive counterfactual exists -- a different vendor could conceivably have bid.

•

Emergency Procurement ($1.33B) -- included only in a "wide" sensitivity case
($6.98B). Time-constrained circumstances legitimately limit competition, but emergency
status is also the subgroup most vulnerable to overuse, so we present it as a secondary,
not primary, addressable figure.

3.3 Vendor-concentration cross-check methodology
To test whether NYC's addressable subgroups show the kind of vendor concentration
associated with reduced competitive pressure, we computed vendor-level concentration for Sole
Source and Negotiated Acquisition using the identical method applied and independently
reproduced across nine rounds of adversarial audit in the AllocationAsymmetry paper: aggregate


10
contract value to one positive total per distinct vendor name, drop null/zero/negative amounts,
then compute (a) the share of subgroup value held by the top 1, 5, 10, and 20 vendors, and (b) the
Gini coefficient over the resulting vendor-total distribution. Using the same measurement
convention on both sides of the comparison is what makes the MTA/NYC comparison
meaningful rather than a comparison of arbitrary numbers.
3.4 Reproduction
Every concentration figure in Table 2, the addressable-base and savings arithmetic in
Table 3, and the MTA cross-check are reproducible from a standard-library script and the two
frozen vendor CSVs, published as a companion reproduction package. The script
(reproduce_procurement.py) verifies the SHA-256 of each CSV against a manifest,
recomputes the vendor count, top-N shares, and Gini for each subgroup on the clean vendor rows
(Rank a positive integer; the TOTAL and footnote rows excluded), checks the five Table 3
savings bases, reconciles the Negotiated and Sole Source subgroups against the Comptroller
Appendix 1 microdata, and with --live re-pulls the MTA FY2024 figures from data.ny.gov
and confirms them against the constants carried from the converged AllocationAsymmetry
paper. A --selftest mode perturbs each checked value and confirms the comparator detects
it. All checks reproduce exactly; the one known discrepancy (the Negotiated positive-basis gap
of Section 4.4) is reported by the script rather than hidden.


11
4. Findings
4.1 Citywide landscape
FY25 citywide: $42,446,174,150 across 12,955 new contracts; Group 2 accounts for
50.86% of value and 75.52% of contract count -- meaning most individual contracts, by count,
are small non-competitive purchases, while dollar value is dominated by a small number of very
large awards (megaprojects, master agreements) (FY25 report).
4.2 DOE and the live oversight dispute
See Section 2. We do not include DOE-specific figures in the quantitative model below;
the ongoing Council audit dispute over ~$12.9B/year in DOE contracting means any DOEspecific addressable-base estimate would currently be speculative.
4.3 Innovative Procurement: why it is excluded
The FY25 report states directly: "While these contracts were competitively bid, DesignBuild is still considered an Innovative Procurement method and is classified into group 2
accordingly" (FY25 report). Design-Build is a two-step, qualifications-based Best Value
selection process used for the Borough-Based Jails program. The three highest-value contracts
registered citywide in FY25 are the three BBJ facilities, awarded to three different vendor teams
-- Leon D. DeMatteis Construction Corp (Queens, $3.98B), Tutor Perini O&G Joint Venture
(Manhattan, $3.76B), and Transformative Reform Group LLC (Bronx, $2.97B) -- which is
consistent with a genuine, if limited-field, competitive process rather than single-bidder capture.
We have not independently verified how many bidders competed for each of the three BBJ
awards; this would be a natural extension of this research if the exclusion decision needs to be
defended further.


12

Note: our computed positive-amount totals are below the official Table 7 subgroup totals.
Sole Source: 106 vendors / $1,597,506,645 against the official $1,599,150,768 (a 0.10% gap).
Negotiated Acquisition: 462 vendors / $3,865,895,210 against the official $4,058,851,691, a
4.75% gap of about $192.96 million across 27 contracts. This gap has been reconciled directly
against the Comptroller's Appendix 1 parent-contracts microdata (publicly reachable, though the
host intermittently returns HTTP 403 to automated requests). The FY2025 Appendix 1 extract
contains exactly 935 Negotiated rows and 115 Sole Source rows, every one carrying a positive
amount and a named vendor (zero blank or null vendor names), summing to the positive-basis
totals above. Nothing was dropped in the vendor aggregation. The gap is instead between Table
7's aggregate contract counts (962 Negotiated, 126 Sole Source) and the parent-contracts extract
(935 and 115): 27 Negotiated contracts ($192.96M) and 11 Sole Source contracts ($1.64M) are
counted in the summary table but absent from the extract -- a coverage or scope difference
between the Comptroller's summary and its parent-contracts export, not an attribution loss inside
the file. The Negotiated concentration figures should therefore be read as computed on about
95.25% of the official subgroup base; whether the 27 missing contracts would raise or lower the
Gini depends on their own concentration, which the extract does not contain. (An earlier draft
guessed the mechanism was unattributable vendor names and reported the file as access-blocked;
opening the file corrected both.)
Sole Source's top vendor is the New York City Economic Development Corporation, at
$1,317,949,728, which is 82.5% of the entire subgroup -- followed by the Wildlife Conservation
Society ($49.0M), SoundThinking Inc ($43.1M), Curriculum Associates LLC ($19.1M), and
Medical Debt Resolution Inc ($18.0M). By contract count, Sole Source awards are spread across
DOE (22), DEP (14), DOHMH (11), DSS/HRA (7), and NYPD (6).


14
Negotiated Acquisition's top vendor is HANYC Foundation Inc, a nonprofit hotelmanagement intermediary for DHS emergency shelter programs, at $929,104,960 (24.0%),
followed by Samaritan Daytop Village Inc ($157.8M), The Children's Rescue Fund ($138.2M),
Concordance Healthcare Solutions LLC ($106.1M), and Genuine Parts Company ($96.0M). By
contract count, DYCD registers by far the most Negotiated Acquisition contracts (575 of 935),
overwhelmingly tied to the COMPASS NYC after-school program -- but these 575 contracts are
spread across many distinct nonprofit providers, so DYCD's high count does not translate into
high vendor concentration.
4.5 Structural interpretation
Sole Source is nominally more concentrated than MTA's entire procurement book (Gini
0.956 vs. 0.931), and Negotiated Acquisition is less concentrated (Gini 0.819 vs. 0.931). But the
mechanisms differ. MTA's concentration is spread across 2,656 distinct vendors in a genuine
commercial market -- construction, engineering, rolling-stock, and related services -- where a
handful of large firms nonetheless win a disproportionate share, the pattern the
AllocationAsymmetry paper's own audit trail explicitly classified as "a non-culpable structural
explanation" rather than evidence of misconduct. NYC's Sole Source and Negotiated Acquisition
concentration, by contrast, is driven by one or two single-purpose intermediary vehicles per
subgroup -- NYCEDC (a City-created nonprofit instrumentality) and HANYC Foundation (a
nonprofit hotel-shelter management intermediary) -- that function structurally more like the
already-excluded Government-to-Government category than like private-market vendor capture.
This has a direct bearing on the savings model: concentration in a genuine commercial
market (MTA-style) is exactly the kind of pattern where more competitive pressure could
plausibly

recover

money.

Concentration

in

a

designated

single-vehicle

model


15
(NYCEDC/HANYC-style) is much less likely to be recoverable through more competition,
because the City deliberately chose a single delivery vehicle for institutional reasons (control,
accountability, speed) that a competitive rebid would not necessarily change.

5. Savings Estimate Synthesis
5.0 On producing a savings figure at all
This program's other civic papers deliberately refused to attach a dollar-savings number
to their findings, and that refusal was principled, not timid. The Fair Student Funding work (atTa'līm) concerned a fixed redistributive pool, where a divergence moves money between schools
rather than reducing a bill, so "savings" was the wrong frame entirely. The MTA concentration
work (AllocationAsymmetry) measured a descriptive count-versus-dollar asymmetry and
classified vendor concentration explicitly as a non-culpable structural pattern, not recoverable
waste; producing a savings figure there would have manufactured a number the data did not
support. The standing discipline across the program has been that a verification method is not a
savings instrument, and that fabricating a recoverable-dollars figure contradicts the papers' own
measure-do-not-accuse posture.
Non-competitive procurement is genuinely different in one specific way, and that
difference is the only thing that licenses a savings estimate here: unlike a redistributive formula
or a descriptive concentration curve, a non-competitively awarded contract has a real competitive
counterfactual. A different vendor could, in principle, have bid. That is what makes "how much
might competition recover" a coherent question rather than a category error. But the estimate that
follows is conditional in a way the reader must keep in view: it multiplies an addressable base by


16
price-reduction rates drawn from other jurisdictions' procurement systems, and its load-bearing
assumption -- that a meaningful share of this spend actually has viable alternative vendors -- is
precisely the thing this paper has not verified and proposes a pilot to test. The numbers below are
therefore a planning range under stated assumptions, not a measurement of money the City is
losing or a promise of money it will save. No figure here should be cited as recoverable until the
pilot in Section 7 tests the alternative-vendor assumption on real contracts. Presented that way,
the estimate stays inside the program's discipline: it is an explicitly-conditional projection with
its assumptions on the surface, not a verified claim.
A note on which base each figure uses. Two dollar bases appear in this paper and are
not interchangeable. The concentration analysis (Section 4.4) uses the positive-amount vendor
basis the Gini method requires ($1.598B Sole Source, $3.866B Negotiated, $5.463B combined).
The savings model uses the official Table 7 subgroup totals ($1.599B, $4.059B, $5.658B
combined), the authoritative figures, which exceed the positive basis by about $194.6M (chiefly
the $192.96M Negotiated coverage gap of Section 4.4, plus a $1.64M Sole Source gap). Because
the NYCEDC-adjusted row is built on the official Core, it carries that full $194.6M: the officialbasis adjusted figure ($4,340,052,731) is $194.6M above the fully positive-basis adjusted figure
($4,145,452,127), and its 10% and 20% floors ($434.0M / $868.0M) are $19.5M and $38.9M
above the positive-basis floors ($414.5M / $829.1M). Table 3 reports the adjusted row on both
bases so the basis effect is explicit rather than buried. This corrects an earlier draft that described
the adjusted row's basis exposure as about $2M; that figure was the Sole Source gap alone and
wrongly omitted the Negotiated gap the row carries.

The Core and Wide rows apply the literature rate to the entire subgroup base and are
upper bounds: as Section 4.5 shows, large shares of that base are designated single-vehicle
intermediary spend (NYCEDC, HANYC) with little competitive counterfactual, so a screened
estimate is the more defensible figure. The intermediary-screened row removes both named
vehicles; a complete screen of every quasi-governmental or designated-intermediary vendor
would lower it further. The adjusted row is shown on both bases per Section 5.0.
The headline range is approximately $500 million to $1.4 billion per year, down from
an earlier and cruder $1 to 3 billion/year estimate that extrapolated DOE's FY2016 noncompetitive share citywide. The adjusted-core row reflects the concentration cross-check in
Section 4.5: if NYCEDC's contract is treated as structurally non-recoverable (like Governmentto-Government spend), the plausible floor of the range falls to roughly $434 million/year. We
have not performed the equivalent adjustment for Negotiated Acquisition's HANYC-type megacontracts, DYCD's fragmented COMPASS spend, or any other subgroup-specific single-vehicle
exclusions; a complete pass would screen every Sole Source and Negotiated Acquisition vendor
for quasi-governmental or designated-intermediary status before finalizing a number. We present
the adjusted-core and intermediary-screened figures as sensitivity bounds, not revised headlines;
the screened figure (Core minus NYCEDC and HANYC, about $3.41B, or $341M to $682M at
the literature rates) is the most conservative and, given Section 4.5, arguably the most defensible.


19

6. Actionable Proposal
6.1 Recommendation 1 -- Concentration-triggered independent re-review
Require that any Sole Source or Negotiated Acquisition award where a single vendor
holds more than 50% of that agency-subgroup's annual value, or where the subgroup's vendor
Gini coefficient exceeds 0.90, triggers a mandatory sources-sought market check (a public
request for information testing whether alternative vendors exist) before the contract's next
renewal. This targets exactly the pattern identified in Section 4.4 without requiring a full re-bid
of every non-competitive contract.
6.2 Recommendation 2 -- Extend vendor-level transparency to all Group 2 subgroups in
near-real time
The Comptroller already publishes the vendor-level Appendix 1 file used throughout this
paper, but only as part of the annual report cycle. Publishing the same fields (Vendor Legal
Name, Subgroup, Award Method, Registered Amount) on a rolling quarterly basis -- and
explicitly including Accelerated Procurement / master-agreement task orders currently outside
standard review, addressing the $625M "Monty Hall Contracts" gap (Comptroller report, May
2026) -- would let concentration be monitored continuously rather than discovered a year after
the fact.
6.3 Recommendation 3 -- Separate quasi-governmental instrumentality reporting
Create a reporting flag distinguishing awards to City-created or City-affiliated nonprofit
instrumentalities (NYCEDC, HANYC-type intermediaries) from awards to independent private
vendors within the Sole Source and Negotiated Acquisition subgroups. This would let the


20
Council, the Comptroller, and outside researchers separate "genuinely non-competitive private
awards" from "designated single-vehicle government delivery," which the current Table 7
categories conflate -- a distinction this paper had to reconstruct manually from vendor names.
6.4 Recommendation 4 -- Algorithmic integrity scanning of procurement registrations
Bayyinah's core technical competency is automated integrity analysis of structured
records. The same Gini/top-N methodology used in Section 4.4 (and previously validated across
nine independent audit rounds on MTA data) can be run as a standing, automated scan against
the Comptroller's published Appendix 1 data each quarter, flagging any agency-subgroup pair
crossing the Recommendation 1 thresholds without requiring new legislation or new data
infrastructure -- only a scheduled script against data the City already publishes.

7. Pilot Program Design
We propose a bounded, low-risk pilot to test the model's central and least-verified
assumption -- that a meaningful share of Sole Source spend has a viable alternative vendor -before generalizing any savings claim citywide.
Scope. All Sole Source contracts registered by DOE, DEP, DOHMH, DSS/HRA, and
NYPD (the five agencies with the most Sole Source contracts by count in FY25, per Section 4.4)
above a $1 million threshold, excluding any vendor independently flagged as a City-created or
City-affiliated instrumentality under Recommendation 3. This excludes NYCEDC by
construction and targets the roughly $280 million "genuinely private-market" residual of the Sole
Source subgroup identified in Section 5.


21
Mechanism. For each qualifying contract approaching renewal, issue a public sourcessought notice (not a full RFP) asking whether alternative vendors could meet the same
specification. This is a lightweight, non-binding market test -- it does not require re-bidding the
contract, only determining whether re-bidding would be worth the administrative cost.
Duration. 12 to 18 months, aligned to a single fiscal year's renewal cycle, so results can
be compared against the following year's Table 7 figures.
Metrics. - Percentage of tested contracts where at least one credible alternative vendor
responds. - For contracts subsequently rebid, the percentage price change versus the prior Sole
Source registered amount. - Administrative cost of running the sources-sought process, to
establish a true net-savings figure (not just gross).
Success criteria. The pilot should be considered informative (regardless of whether it
confirms or disconfirms the savings model) if it produces a credible-alternative-vendor rate and a
rebid price delta for at least 20 contracts. It should be considered supportive of this paper's thesis
if the observed price delta on rebid contracts falls within or above the 10 to 20% literaturegrounded range from Section 3.1.
Governance and independence safeguard. Consistent with the Bayyinah audit protocol
applied to this program's other papers, the pilot's results should be evaluated by a party
independent of whichever agency ran the sources-sought process, and the underlying data
(contract IDs, vendor responses, price deltas) should be published rather than summarized only
in a top-line report -- mirroring the vendor-level transparency this paper argues for in
Recommendation 2.


22
8. Limitations
•

This paper began as a single-session, single-instance synthesis; its empirical spine has
since been independently reproduced and audited across three cross-instance rounds and
converged under Standing Rule 7 (see the audit-status notice). Convergence certifies
structural honesty and reproducibility, not that the savings estimate is verified
recoverable or policy-ready -- that remains conditional on the Section 7 pilot.

•

The Innovative Procurement exclusion (Section 4.3) relies on the Comptroller's own
characterization of Design-Build as competitively bid; we did not independently verify
bidder counts for the three Borough-Based Jail awards.

•

The vendor-concentration cross-check (Section 4.4) compares one fiscal year of NYC
data (FY25) against one fiscal year of MTA data (FY2024) from a different level of
government (city vs. state authority) with different procurement rules; the comparison is
illustrative of methodology, not a claim that the two systems are equivalent.

•

The DOE-specific non-competitive footprint remains genuinely unresolved pending the
outcome of the ongoing City Council audit; this paper deliberately excludes DOE from
its quantitative model rather than resolving that dispute.

•

The savings literature (Czech, Slovak, GAO/OMB) is drawn from different jurisdictions
and procurement systems than New York City's; the 10 to 20% range is a reasonable
planning assumption, not a NYC-specific estimate.

•

We have not adjusted Negotiated Acquisition for its own designated-intermediary
contracts (e.g., HANYC) the way we did for Sole Source/NYCEDC; the adjusted-core
figure in Table 3 is therefore likely still an overestimate of the truly recoverable amount.


23
9. Conclusion
Narrowing from a citywide $21.6 billion non-competitive headline to a defensible $5.66
to $6.98 billion addressable base, and then cross-checking vendor concentration within that base
against an independently reproduced MTA benchmark, produces a materially smaller and more
defensible planning range than earlier passes in this research program: roughly $500 million to
$1.4 billion per year under the stated literature-grounded assumptions, with a plausible
NYCEDC-excluded floor near $434 million, and an intermediary-screened sensitivity of about
$341 million to $682 million once NYCEDC and HANYC are both excluded. That range is
conditional on the alternative-vendor assumption the Section 7 pilot is designed to test, and
should not be cited as recoverable before it does. Even so, its magnitude relative to the City's
own procurement-reform activity to date and the four recommendations above are designed to be
implementable with data the City already collects, at a bounded pilot scale, before any larger
claim is made or acted upon.

## R0477 · Bayyinah al-Amāna -- Provenance Integrity for Public Open Data: Reproduction and Audit Dataset (v1.0)

- section: VI. Applied Audits & Public-Data Studies
- source_file: README.md
- source_format: md
- text_sha256: 3e8c095bf4c980b1e9e291ea9f9fe71a0da1a137a33f53cffca72e7cc3c9e36e

# Bayyinah al-Amāna -- Provenance Integrity for Public Open Data: Reproduction and Audit Dataset (v1.0)

This dataset reproduces four provenance-integrity checks against a frozen capture of two New York State open-data (Socrata) datasets, re-pulls the live endpoints to detect drift, and includes the full three-round cross-instance audit trail.

## Related deposits

- Reader note (paper): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21446613
- Audit and provenance ledger: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21446618
- This dataset is deposited alongside the ledger (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21446618). The artifact converged after three consecutive qualifying cross-instance passes (gate met at F-AM-R2, confirmed clean at F-AM-R3 with the rotation gap closed).

## Datasets

- `gpsc-qqsz` -- "MTA Procurement Report (All)", provenance **community** (a community-created view).
- `twsw-2mqa` -- "MTA Procurements: Beginning 2018", provenance **official** (first-party).

Both are served from `data.ny.gov`.

## Contents

- `reproduce_paper3.py` -- standard-library Python; verifies the frozen capture's hash and reproduces all four checks (`default`), re-pulls and compares to the live endpoints (`--live`), and perturbs every captured value to confirm the comparator detects it (`--selftest`).
- `snapshot/provenance_capture.json` -- the frozen capture: per-dataset provenance, declared update time, schema field inventory, and per-fiscal-year row counts, face totals, and row-level `:created_at`/`:updated_at` system timestamps.
- `snapshot/MANIFEST.json` -- the SHA-256 of the capture; the script aborts on mismatch.
- `audit-reports/` -- the primary auditor outputs for all three rounds (F-AM-R1/R2/R3), organized by round: each Model Council member report and each synthesis, the source records behind the ledger's summaries.
- `audit-reports/` -- the primary auditor outputs for all three cross-instance rounds (F-AM-R1, R2, R3), organized by round, including each Model Council member report and each synthesis. These are the source records behind the ledger's summaries. The artifact converged after three consecutive qualifying passes (the gate met at R2, confirmed clean at R3 with the rotation gap closed).

## How to run

Requires Python 3 (standard library only).

```
python3 reproduce_paper3.py            # verify hash + reproduce the four checks, offline
python3 reproduce_paper3.py --selftest # perturb every captured value; confirm all are detected
python3 reproduce_paper3.py --live     # re-pull data.ny.gov and compare to the frozen capture
```

## The four checks and what the capture shows

1. **Provenance classification and divergence.** `gpsc-qqsz` declares itself a community view; `twsw-2mqa` is official. Their FY2023 windows are byte-identical; FY2024 diverges by 70 records and about $58.1M (0.5103% count, 0.0891% face); and FY2022, despite identical row counts, diverges by $0.75 in summed face value -- a value-level difference a billion-rounded view misses.
2. **Snapshot integrity.** SHA-256 of the capture matches the manifest.
3. **Declared-vs-actual freshness (primary method).** Each dataset's currently-served history carries row `:created_at` timestamps long after the reporting period closed: the community view's rows were created 2025-12-01 (335 to 1066 days after each fiscal year), the official dataset's on 2026-04-01 (456 to 1187 days after), uniformly across rows -- a single post-close batch load (consistent with a wholesale republish or a first-time bulk load; a single pull does not distinguish them), detectable without a two-pull time gap.
4. **Schema divergence.** The community view serves 23 fields, the official dataset 32; 16 fields are official-only and 7 community-only.

## Refusal boundary

Divergences and republishes are substrate facts. Republishes, migrations, and corrections routinely regenerate historical rows and their timestamps. This package detects and quantifies divergence; it does **not** judge whether any batch load, edit, or divergence was legitimate, authorized, or improper. That legitimacy question is Tier 3 and is refused.

# Bayyinah al-Mizan -- Reproduction Package (v0.1)

Structural Honesty Verification of the U.S. federal improper-payment MEASUREMENT.

This package does NOT re-detect improper payments (that needs protected claims data). It
verifies the coverage, reconciliation, and completeness integrity of the government's own
published estimate on PaymentAccuracy.gov, against the substrate of federal spending and the
government's own PIIA-compliance determinations. It measures; it does not accuse.

## Contents
- `reproduce_mizan.py` -- default verifies the frozen seed snapshot (government-wide rates +
  HHS integrity facts + SHA-256 hashes); `--live` re-pulls all 40 agencies x 5 years of
  `/agency/{CODE}/{YEAR}.html` and extracts program/agency series + PIIA compliance; `--selftest`
  perturbs each of the 17 checked values (5 gov rates + 9 rollup + 3 HHS) and confirms detection.
- `snapshot/` -- frozen raw captures (government-wide numbers page + HHS FY2024 page).
- `data/mizan_seed_snapshot.json` -- parsed seed values + hashes + sitemap map (1,679 pages).

## Run
    python3 reproduce_mizan.py            # snapshot verify (offline, byte-deterministic)
    python3 reproduce_mizan.py --selftest # perturbation detection
    python3 reproduce_mizan.py --live     # full re-pull from PaymentAccuracy.gov

## Sources (all public)
PaymentAccuracy.gov (substrate); GAO improper-payment reports + agency financial reports
(reconciliation targets); OMB Circular A-123 Appendix C (declared methodology); USAspending
(outlay denominator for coverage).

## Status
v0.1 pre-audit. Not yet through Standing Rule 7 review. No figure is converged or policy-ready.

## R0479 · Companion Dataset: NYC DOE Fair Student Funding (FSF) FY2023 Five-School Recompute

- section: VI. Applied Audits & Public-Data Studies
- source_file: README.md
- source_format: md
- text_sha256: 184440f90d7f146b12fe499710143de3c50e9a11fe7bc90d804d70ed03fc802f

# Companion Dataset: NYC DOE Fair Student Funding (FSF) FY2023 Five-School Recompute

Companion dataset to: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise), *Bayyinah at-Taʿlīm: Structural Honesty Verification for Educational Fairness Systems, from Primary Schooling to Graduate Research*, Draft Application Note v1.0 (currently v1.0-rc6), Section 4.4.6 and Findings F-ED-10, F-ED-13, F-ED-14. This dataset exists to discharge two open action items: Finding F-ED-11 (archiving the underlying five-school extract and mastersheet rows so the FY2023 FSF recompute is independently reproducible by a second party rather than single-instance) and Finding F-ED-13's Next Audit Cycle note (b) (archiving the category-level Detail Report data so the full formula-reconstruction walkthrough, not just the top-level line items, is independently reproducible).

## What this dataset is

Six files: four small CSV files (5 rows, or one row per subcategory per sample school), two Python recompute scripts, and one supporting reference table:

1. **`five_school_fsf_fy2023_detail_report_extract.csv`** — the disclosed walkthrough components of each school's Total FY2023 Fair Student Funding allocation, as reported by the NYC DOE Fair Student Funding Public App's FSF Detail Report for each school, obtained via direct browser interaction (the app is rendered through ASP.NET WebForms postbacks and is not retrievable via a plain HTTP request). Columns: prior-year (FY2022) register, system base rate per pupil, teacher-salary change, register-change adjustment, the fixed $225,000 foundation amount, and three collective-bargaining/state-aid adjustment terms, plus the DOE's own reported Total FY2023 FSF Allocation for cross-check.
2. **`five_school_comptroller_mastersheet_rows.csv`** — the exact rows for the same five schools extracted from the [NYC Comptroller's FY2023/FY2024 School Budget Allocations Mastersheet](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/School-Budget-Allocations-Mastersheet-8-29-2023.xlsx) (downloaded 2026-07-19; "Reference" sheet), covering Enrollment/FSF/Register Relief/All Other/Total for FY2023 Initial, FY2023 Final, and FY2024 Initial (plus Hold Harmless where applicable).
3. **`five_school_fsf_fy2023_category_level_register_detail.csv`** — new, added to discharge F-ED-13's Next Audit Cycle note (b). The category-level Weighted Register Formula breakdown (Grade Weight; Academic Intervention/Poverty; English Language Learner/ELL; Special Education Services; Portfolio, with every published subcategory) for all five schools, in long/tidy format: one row per (school, category group, subcategory), with register count, dollar amount, and a `value_source` column tagging each row `reported` (read directly off the rendered Detail Report) or `inferred_zero` (subcategory not itemized in the browsing pass; zero inferred because the category-group subtotal is fully accounted for by the reported nonzero lines, consistent with the source narrative's explicit "all in X" / "= 0" language for the remaining lines). Includes a per-school `TOTAL` row (weighted register and amount) as directly reported by the app, for cross-check against file (1).
4. **`fsf_recompute.py`** — the exact computation used to reconstruct each school's Total FY2023 FSF Allocation from column (1) and compare it against column (2)'s Initial and Final figures. Running it reproduces the paper's reported $2-$18 (rounding) match to the DOE's own published total and the exact match to the mastersheet's "FY2023 Initial" column.
5. **`fsf_category_level_recompute.py`** — new. Cross-checks file (3) two ways: (a) the category-level sub-lines sum to the reported per-school TOTAL row (within $0-$2, rounding in the DOE's own published sub-line dollars); (b) the F-ED-13 mechanistic walkthrough reconstruction — (FY2022 register x FY2022 base rate) + teacher-salary-change + register-change adjustment + foundation + collective-bargaining terms — lands within $2-$18 of the DOE's own reported grand total for all five schools, and the teacher-salary-change term matches the F-ED-14 identity (fy22_register x (FY2023 rate - FY2022 rate)) to under $1 for all five schools.
6. **`fsf_fy2023_weights_percapitas.xlsx`** — supporting reference: the FY2023 "Fair Student Funding Per Capitas" (SAM 1.1f) weight and per-capita dollar table, downloaded from [NYC Public Schools' FY2023 FSF SAM page](https://www.nycenet.edu/offices/finance_schools/budget/DSBPO/allocationmemo/fy22_23/fy23_docs/fy2023_Weights.xlsx), included because it is the formula parameter table referenced throughout the recompute methodology, even though it is not itself school-specific.

## Sample schools

| DBN | School name | District |
|---|---|---|
| 28Q160 | P.S. 160 Walter Francis Bishop | 28 (Queens) |
| 10X085 | P.S. 085 Great Expectations | 10 (Bronx) |
| 30Q258 | Energy Tech High School | 30 (Queens) |
| 14K488 | Brooklyn Preparatory High School | 14 (Brooklyn) |
| 30Q148 | P.S. 148 Queens | 30 (Queens) |

Sample selection: convenience sample of five schools with FY2023 FSF Detail Reports retrievable through the DOE Public App during data collection; not randomly drawn, not representative of the roughly 1,500 FSF-funded schools citywide. Any generalization beyond these five schools is explicitly out of scope, per the paper's own F-ED-10/F-ED-11 disclosures.

## Provenance and extraction method

- **FSF Detail Report figures** (files 1 and 3): NYC DOE Fair Student Funding Public App, [`OverviewReports.aspx`](https://www.nycenet.edu/publicapps/Offices/FSF/OverviewReports.aspx) / [`FSFDetail.aspx`](https://www.nycenet.edu/publicapps/Offices/FSF/FSFDetail.aspx), FY2023 report vintage, extracted via browser automation on 2026-07-18/19. This app returns `robots.txt`-disallowed to unauthenticated automated HTTP requests; a real browser session executing the page's JavaScript postbacks is required, which is why this dataset is being archived rather than relying on future readers re-running the same extraction. Navigation path for file (3): fiscal-year dropdown set to "2022-2023" (=FY2023), school name typed into the autocomplete search box (the raw DBN, e.g. "28Q160", returns no matches; the search requires the school name), GO triggers an ASP.NET `__doPostBack` to `Report.aspx?type=d&year=2023&schoolcode=<CODE>`, and "Expand All & Collapse" reveals every category subcategory row.
- **Comptroller mastersheet rows** (file 2): [NYC Comptroller, "School Budget Allocations Mastersheet," September 2023](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/School-Budget-Allocations-Mastersheet-8-29-2023.xlsx). As of this dataset's creation, automated (non-browser) requests to this URL are intermittently blocked by an Incapsula/Imperva bot-detection challenge; the file was obtained via a successful direct download and the five rows above extracted from its "Reference" sheet.
- **Weight/per-capita table** (file 6): [NYC Public Schools, FY2023 FSF Per Capitas, SAM 1.1f](https://www.nycenet.edu/offices/finance_schools/budget/DSBPO/allocationmemo/fy22_23/fy23_docs/fy2023_Weights.xlsx), and cross-checked against the identical table in the [FY2023 FSF Guide](https://www.nycenet.edu/offices/finance_schools/budget/DSBPO/allocationmemo/fy22_23/fy23_docs/FY2023_FSF_Guide.pdf), Chapter 4.1.3.
- **DOE FSF Working Group Meeting 3 base-weight deck**, cited by the parent paper for F-ED-14 (the $4,223.00 FY2022 / $4,197.19 FY2023 base rates): [infohub.nyced.org](https://infohub.nyced.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/fsf-working-group_meeting-3.pdf). Not archived as a file in this package (it is a stable DOE-hosted PDF, not paywalled or robots-disallowed), but the exact URL is recorded here for reproducibility.

## Note on the category-level file's `value_source` column

File (3)'s `reported` rows were read directly off the rendered Detail Report during the browsing session. Its `inferred_zero` rows were not individually screen-read; they are subcategories the source narrative described as "all in X" or explicitly "= 0" for the remaining lines, and which the reported category-group subtotal (also archived, and cross-checked in `fsf_category_level_recompute.py`) is fully accounted for without them. This distinction is disclosed rather than presented as uniformly screen-verified, consistent with this paper's own citation-provenance discipline (F-ED-11).

## Known limitation carried over from the paper

This recompute is Tier 2 (Structural), not Tier 1 (byte-deterministic), by the paper's own Section 3 definition: reproducing the DOE's published total requires disclosing which report vintage (Initial versus Final) is being matched, a disclosed parameter choice rather than a parameter-free operation. It is a five-school demonstration, not a system-wide audit, and should not be read as validating FSF formula fidelity across all FSF-funded schools. See the paper's F-ED-10 and F-ED-11 for the full disclosure.

## How to reproduce

```
python3 fsf_recompute.py
python3 fsf_category_level_recompute.py
```

`fsf_recompute.py` prints, for each school: the recomputed total from the walkthrough components, the DOE's own reported total, the difference (should be $2-$18, rounding only), and the comparison against the Comptroller mastersheet's Initial and Final FSF columns.

`fsf_category_level_recompute.py` prints, for each school: the category-line sum versus the reported category-level TOTAL (should be $0-$2), the mechanistic walkthrough reconstruction from category-level inputs versus the DOE's own reported grand total (should be $2-$18), and the teacher-salary-change identity check underlying F-ED-14 (should be under $1).

## License

The underlying figures are public records published by the NYC Department of Education and the NYC Comptroller's Office and are not subject to copyright as U.S. government/municipal works. This compilation (selection, extraction, and computation script) is released under [CC-BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — reuse is permitted with attribution to this dataset and to the parent paper.

## Citation

Arfeen, Bilal Syed (2026). *Companion Dataset: NYC DOE Fair Student Funding (FSF) FY2023 Five-School Recompute*, companion to *Bayyinah at-Taʿlīm* v1.0 (rc6 revision, category-level data added). BayyinahEnterprise.

## Related work

Companion papers by the same author/lineage (Zenodo DOIs): Bayyinah at-Tartīb (10.5281/zenodo.20070782); Al-Mutaffifīn (10.5281/zenodo.19894724); Structural Honesty Verification: A New Frontier (10.5281/zenodo.20131072); Bayyinah al-Munāsabāt (10.5281/zenodo.20069654); Cross-Text Computational Linguistics (10.5281/zenodo.19961267).

# Bayyinah: Public-Ledger Allocation and Asymmetric-Measure Audits -- Reproduction and Audit Dataset (v1.0)

This dataset accompanies the canonical v1.0 release and lets any party reproduce every figure in the paper and inspect the full nine-round cross-instance audit trail.

## Related deposits

- Reader note (paper): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21445552
- Audit and provenance ledger: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21445556
- This dataset is deposited alongside the ledger (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21445556).

## Contents

- `reproduce_paper2.py` -- verifies the snapshot hash and recomputes every published statistic on both estimands for all three fiscal years. Supports `--live` (re-pull from the New York State open-data portal and compare) and `--selftest` (perturb each statistic and confirm the comparator detects it).
- `snapshot/gpsc-qqsz_FY2022-2024.json` -- the frozen three-year extract (37,988 records: FY2022 12,156; FY2023 12,114; FY2024 13,718) that every figure is computed from.
- `snapshot/MANIFEST.json` -- the SHA-256 of the snapshot and the 22-field row-present inventory. The script aborts if the snapshot does not match this hash.
- `audit-reports/` -- the raw primary auditor outputs for all nine rounds (F-AA-R1 through F-AA-R9), organized by round, including each Model Council member report and each synthesis. These are the source records behind the ledger's summaries.

## How to reproduce

Requires Python 3 (standard library only).

```
python3 reproduce_paper2.py            # offline: verify hash, recompute all figures from the frozen snapshot
python3 reproduce_paper2.py --selftest # confirm the comparator detects all deliberate perturbations
python3 reproduce_paper2.py --live     # re-pull all three years from data.ny.gov and compare to the snapshot
```

The offline run needs no network. The `--live` run queries the community view `gpsc-qqsz` on `data.ny.gov`; the frozen snapshot and its hash, not the live endpoint, are what the reproduction rests on, so results are stable even if the live portal later changes.

## Expected top-line values (FY2024, community view gpsc-qqsz)

- Total rows across the three vintages: 37,988
- Face-value total (`contract_amount`): $65,189,755,228.64
- Annual-expenditure total (`amount_expended_for_fiscal_year`): $8,170,228,558.54
- MWBE prime-vendor shares: 18.7345% by count, 3.9532% by face value, 7.0612% by annual expenditure
- Face concentration: top-10 30.4151%; vendor Gini (positive-face basis) 0.93117 (face), 0.90435 (annual expenditure)
- Pre-2024 award share of FY2024 face value: 91.6876%
- Missing `contract_amount`: 1,348; explicit-zero: 48
- Vintage-overlap fingerprint (18-field method, pairwise): 2,115 / 604 / 1,002; exact all-field overlap: 0
- Provenance: gpsc-qqsz 13,718 rows / $65.19B vs first-party twsw-2mqa 13,648 rows / $65.13B (face divergence about 0.089%, record-count divergence about 0.51%)

## Audit trail summary

The artifact converged after nine independent cross-instance audit rounds under BayyinahEnterprise Audit Framework v3.0, Standing Rule 7 (two consecutive qualifying passes by non-producer auditors, executed reproduction, zero critical and zero high). Rounds 1-3 were NON-PASS (interpretive overreach, then producer status-propagation defects); round 4 was a consistency-only pass not credited; round 5 was NON-PASS (package absent from the packet); round 6 was the first qualifying executed-reproduction pass; round 7 was NON-PASS on a producer status-propagation defect that reset the count; rounds 8 and 9 were two consecutive qualifying passes (three qualifying members each: GPT 5.5, GPT 5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro; the Claude producing-lineage member quarantined). Convergence caveats are recorded honestly in the ledger Current State: the two decisive passes shared the same three-member set (independence between them rests on fresh instances, not disjoint membership), and they audited materially-identical substance. The `audit-reports/` folder contains the primary records so the ledger's account can be checked against source.

## R0481 · NYC Procurement Concentration and Savings -- Reproduction and Audit Dataset (v1.0, converged)

- section: VI. Applied Audits & Public-Data Studies
- source_file: README.md
- source_format: md
- text_sha256: 7059c8587be7bf7b7d777c00cbccdbf2b22499d4489d54607aa9f800856efc79

# NYC Procurement Concentration and Savings -- Reproduction and Audit Dataset (v1.0, converged)

## Related deposits

- Paper: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21447217
- Audit and provenance ledger and this dataset: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21447219

The paper converged under Audit Framework v3.0, Standing Rule 7, after three cross-instance rounds (F-PC-R1 NON-PASS, then F-PC-R2 and F-PC-R3 qualifying passes; count TWO; rotation closed by a member new to the second pass). Convergence certifies structural honesty and reproducibility, not that the savings estimate is verified recoverable.

Reproduces the concentration figures (Table 2), the addressable-base and savings arithmetic (Table 3), and the MTA cross-check of the working paper *Procurement Concentration and Recoverable Competitive Savings in New York City Contracting*.

## Contents

- `reproduce_procurement.py` -- standard-library Python. Verifies the CSV hashes, recomputes Sole Source and Negotiated Acquisition concentration (vendor count, top-N shares, Gini) on the clean vendor rows, checks the savings arithmetic, and (with `--live`) re-pulls the MTA FY2024 cross-check figures from data.ny.gov.
- `data/sole_source_vendors_fy25.csv` -- FY25 Sole Source vendor aggregation (Rank 1..106 vendors, then a TOTAL row and three footnote rows).
- `data/negotiated_acquisition_vendors_fy25.csv` -- FY25 Negotiated Acquisition vendor aggregation (Rank 1..462 vendors, then TOTAL and footnote rows).
- `data/MANIFEST.json` -- SHA-256 of both CSVs; the script aborts on mismatch.
- `audit-reports/` -- the primary auditor reports and syntheses for all three rounds (F-PC-R1/R2/R3), organized by round, the source records behind the ledger's summaries.

## How to run

```
python3 reproduce_procurement.py            # verify hashes + reproduce concentration + savings
python3 reproduce_procurement.py --live     # additionally re-pull the MTA cross-check from data.ny.gov
python3 reproduce_procurement.py --selftest # perturb each checked value; confirm all detected
```

## Method (must match to reproduce)

Vendor rows are the CSV rows whose `Rank` is a positive integer; the `TOTAL` and footnote rows the CSVs also contain are excluded. Concentration is on the positive-amount vendor basis: aggregate to one total per vendor (the CSVs are already aggregated), sort descending, take top-N shares, and compute the Gini coefficient over the vendor totals. This is the identical convention independently reproduced across the nine audit rounds of the AllocationAsymmetry paper.

## Expected results

- Sole Source: 106 vendors, $1,597,506,644.98, top-1 82.5004%, top-5 90.5858%, top-10 94.0642%, top-20 97.2606%, Gini 0.95557. Top vendor NYCEDC $1,317,949,728.
- Negotiated Acquisition: 462 vendors, $3,865,895,209.67, top-1 24.0334%, top-5 36.9178%, top-10 46.2163%, top-20 55.3833%, Gini 0.81855. Top vendor HANYC $929,104,960.
- Savings bases (official Table 7): Core $5,658,002,459; Wide $6,984,040,398; NYCEDC-adjusted $4,340,052,731.
- MTA FY2024 cross-check (from converged AllocationAsymmetry, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21445552; reproducible live): 13,718 records, 2,656 vendors, $65,189,755,228.64 face, top-10 30.4151%, Gini 0.93117.

## Reconciliation (resolved)

The Negotiated Acquisition positive-amount total is about 4.75% ($192.96M, 27 contracts) below the official Table 7 figure of $4,058,851,691. This has been reconciled directly against the Comptroller's Appendix 1 parent-contracts microdata (publicly reachable, though the host intermittently returns HTTP 403 to automated requests). The FY2025 Appendix 1 extract contains exactly 935 Negotiated rows and 115 Sole Source rows, every one positive and vendor-named (zero blank or null names), summing to the positive-basis totals. Nothing was dropped in aggregation. The gap is between Table 7's aggregate counts (962 Negotiated, 126 Sole Source) and the parent-contracts extract (935 and 115): 27 Negotiated contracts ($192.96M) and 11 Sole Source contracts ($1.64M) are in the summary but absent from the extract -- a coverage/scope difference between the summary and the export, not attribution loss. Negotiated concentration is computed on about 95.25% of the official subgroup base.

## Refusal boundary

This package measures concentration and reproduces arithmetic. It does not judge whether any award should have been competitively bid, whether any vendor relationship is improper, or whether any dollar figure is recoverable. The savings estimate is a conditional planning range under stated assumptions, gated on the pilot the paper proposes; it is not a verified recoverable amount.

## R0483 · reproduce_mizan.py — reproduce_mizan.py -- Bayyinah al-Mizan reproduction package (v0.1)

- section: VI. Applied Audits & Public-Data Studies
- source_file: reproduce_mizan.py
- source_format: py
- text_sha256: a43b3cbe6fc5c7cb7c4375b95bb720385df5dbeaa34bbd293b4bcdfb1841ad23

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
reproduce_mizan.py -- Bayyinah al-Mizan reproduction package (v0.1)

Structural Honesty Verification of the U.S. federal improper-payment MEASUREMENT.
This tool does NOT re-detect improper payments (that requires protected claims data).
It verifies the coverage, reconciliation, and completeness integrity of the government's
own published estimate on PaymentAccuracy.gov, against the substrate of federal spending
and the government's own risk / PIIA-compliance determinations.

Modes:
  (default)     verify the frozen seed snapshot: government-wide rates + HHS integrity
                facts + SHA-256 hashes. Byte-deterministic, offline.
  --live        re-pull all /agency/{CODE}/{YEAR}.html pages from PaymentAccuracy.gov,
                extract program/agency-level series + PIIA compliance + recovery, and
                aggregate government-wide; pull USAspending outlays for the coverage ratio.
  --selftest    perturb each checked value and confirm the comparator detects it.

Tier discipline (Audit Framework v3.0):
  Tier 1 (byte-deterministic): the rates, the reconciliation, the coverage ratio, the
          concentration measure, the PIIA-noncompliance exposure, the hashes.
  Tier 2 (disclosed method): the estimated / susceptible-unestimated / not-assessed
          classification, and compositional-vs-real year-over-year change.
  Tier 3 (REFUSED): no imputed "true" improper-payment total, no accusation of any
          agency, no recoverable-savings figure. It measures; it does not accuse.
"""
import sys, re, json, hashlib, urllib.request, time

BASE = "https://www.paymentaccuracy.gov"
UA = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 bayyinah-al-mizan-reproduction"}
AGENCIES = ["CFTC","CNCS","CPSC","DHS","DOC","DOE","DOI","DOJ","DOL","DOT","DOW","EAC","ED",
            "EPA","FCC","FEC","FMC","GSA","HHS","HUD","MCC","NARA","NASA","NEH","NRC","NSF",
            "NTSB","OPM","PCLOB","RRB","SBA","SEC","SSA","STATE","TREASURY","USAGM","USAID",
            "USDA","USITC","VA"]
YEARS = [2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025]

# ---- EXPECTED values (verified against the frozen snapshot); a mismatch is a finding ----
EXPECT_GOV_IMPROPER_RATE = {2021:7.0515, 2022:4.443, 2023:4.3957, 2024:3.6585, 2025:3.8347}
EXPECT_GOV_ACCURACY_RATE = {2021:92.8367, 2022:94.8784, 2023:94.5789, 2024:96.0328, 2025:95.8459}
# GAO government-wide rollup (reconciliation target, cited, not computed here):
GAO_ROLLUP = {2024: 162_000_000_000, 2025: 186_000_000_000}   # ~$; the --live sum reconciles to these
# Coverage per CRFB analysis of GAO FY2025 (reconciliation target for --live vs USAspending):
COVERAGE_TARGET = {"programs": 64, "agencies": 15, "noninterest_spending_covered_usd": 4.5e12}
EXPECT_HHS_2024 = {"piia_status":"non-compliant", "consecutive_years_noncompliant":"3",
                   "confirmed_fraud_reported":"2,760.0M"}
# FY2025 agency rollup reconciliation (the coverage + reconciliation-gap finding):
EXPECT_ROLLUP = {"agencies_total":83, "agencies_with_susceptible":15,
                 "coverage_susceptible_outlays_B":4473.7, "implied_improper_total_B":171.7,
                 "gao_headline_B":186.0, "reconciliation_gap_B":14.3, "reconciliation_gap_pct":7.7,
                 "hhs_implied_B":97.4, "hhs_share_pct":56.7}
TOL = 1e-3

def parse_rollup(html):
    recs = []
    for r in re.findall(r"<tr[^>]*>(.*?)</tr>", html, re.S):
        ts = re.search(r"total-spent-col[^>]*>\$?([0-9,]+)\s*M", r)
        ip = re.search(r"ip-rate-col[^>]*>([0-9.]+)%", r)
        sus = re.search(r"susceptible-col[^>]*>([0-9]+)", r)
        if ts:
            recs.append({"o": float(ts.group(1).replace(",", "")),
                         "r": float(ip.group(1)) if ip else None,
                         "s": int(sus.group(1)) if sus else 0})
    wr = [x for x in recs if x["r"] is not None]
    cov = round(sum(x["o"] for x in wr)/1000, 1)
    imp = round(sum(x["o"]*x["r"]/100 for x in wr)/1000, 1)
    hhs = next(x for x in wr if abs(x["o"]-1670124.45) < 1)
    hi = round(hhs["o"]*hhs["r"]/100/1000, 1)
    return {"agencies_total": len(wr),
            "agencies_with_susceptible": sum(1 for x in wr if x["s"] > 0),
            "coverage_susceptible_outlays_B": cov, "implied_improper_total_B": imp,
            "gao_headline_B": 186.0, "reconciliation_gap_B": round(186-imp, 1),
            "reconciliation_gap_pct": round((186-imp)/186*100, 1),
            "hhs_implied_B": hi, "hhs_share_pct": round(hi/imp*100, 1)}

def fetch(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return r.read().decode("utf-8", "ignore")

# ---------- parsers ----------
def parse_gov_wide(html):
    years = [int(x) for x in re.search(r'data-years="\[([0-9, ]+)\]"', html).group(1).split(",")]
    out = {"years": years}
    for s in re.findall(r'data-series="\[([-0-9., ]+)\]"', html):
        vals = [round(float(v), 4) for v in s.split(",")]
        if not vals: continue
        if vals[0] > 50: out["accuracy_rate_pct"] = dict(zip(years, vals))
        elif max(vals) < 2: out["third_series_pct"] = dict(zip(years, vals))
        else: out["improper_rate_pct"] = dict(zip(years, vals))
    return out

def parse_agency_page(html, agency, year):
    def g(pat, d=None):
        m = re.search(pat, html, re.S); return m.group(1).strip() if m else d
    rec = {"agency": agency, "year": year}
    rec["piia_status"] = "non-compliant" if "was found non-compliant" in html else (
                         "compliant" if "was found compliant" in html or "found to be compliant" in html else "unknown")
    rec["consecutive_years_noncompliant"] = g(r"consecutive years %s has been non-compliant:\s*([0-9]+)" % agency)
    rec["noncompliant_program_mentions"] = len(re.findall(r"Non-compliance criteria:", html))
    rec["confirmed_fraud_reported"] = g(r"reported \$([0-9,\.]+M) of confirmed fraud")
    # embedded chart series (dollar amounts, in the order the site emits them)
    for key in ["overpayment","underpayment","unknown","technically-improper","recovered","identified"]:
        m = re.search(r'data-%s-series="\[([-0-9eE., ]+)\]"' % key, html)
        if m:
            try: rec[key.replace("-","_")+"_series"] = [float(v) for v in m.group(1).split(",")]
            except ValueError: pass
    return rec

# ---------- concentration ----------
def gini(vals):
    xs = sorted(v for v in vals if v > 0)
    n = len(xs)
    if n == 0: return None
    cum = sum((i+1)*x for i, x in enumerate(xs))
    return round((2*cum)/(n*sum(xs)) - (n+1)/n, 5)

def topn(vals, n):
    s = sorted(vals, reverse=True); tot = sum(vals)
    return round(100*sum(s[:n])/tot, 4) if tot else None

# ---------- modes ----------
def verify_snapshot():
    snap = json.load(open("data/mizan_seed_snapshot.json"))
    ok = True
    # hashes
    for f, h in snap["files"].items():
        got = hashlib.sha256(open("snapshot/"+f, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
        m = (got == h); ok &= m
        print(f"[{'OK' if m else 'MISMATCH'}] hash {f}")
    # government-wide improper rate
    gw = snap["gov_wide"]
    ir = dict(zip(gw["years"], gw["improper_rate_pct"]))
    for y, exp in EXPECT_GOV_IMPROPER_RATE.items():
        got = ir.get(y); m = got is not None and abs(got-exp) < TOL; ok &= m
        print(f"[{'OK' if m else 'MISMATCH'}] gov improper rate {y}: {got} (exp {exp})")
    # HHS integrity facts
    hhs = snap["hhs_2024_integrity"]
    for k, exp in EXPECT_HHS_2024.items():
        got = hhs.get(k if k!="consecutive_years_noncompliant" else "piia_consecutive_years_noncompliant")
        m = (str(got) == str(exp)); ok &= m
        print(f"[{'OK' if m else 'MISMATCH'}] HHS {k}: {got} (exp {exp})")
    # FY2025 rollup reconciliation (recomputed from the frozen page, not read from JSON)
    roll = parse_rollup(open("snapshot/agencies-and-programs.html", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read())
    for k, exp in EXPECT_ROLLUP.items():
        got = roll.get(k); m = (got == exp); ok &= m
        print(f"[{'OK' if m else 'MISMATCH'}] rollup {k}: {got} (exp {exp})")
    print("\nSnapshot verification:", "PASS -- reproduced exactly." if ok else "FAIL.")
    return ok

def run_live():
    print("Pulling %d agency-year pages from PaymentAccuracy.gov ..." % (len(AGENCIES)*len(YEARS)))
    records = []
    for a in AGENCIES:
        for y in YEARS:
            try:
                html = fetch(f"{BASE}/agency/{a}/{y}.html")
                records.append(parse_agency_page(html, a, y))
                time.sleep(0.2)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  [skip] {a}/{y}: {e}")
    # PIIA non-compliance exposure (agency-years found non-compliant)
    nc = [r for r in records if r["piia_status"] == "non-compliant"]
    print(f"agency-years pulled: {len(records)} | flagged non-compliant: {len(nc)}")
    for r in nc:
        if r["year"] == 2024:
            print(f"  non-compliant FY2024: {r['agency']} "
                  f"(consec={r.get('consecutive_years_noncompliant')}, "
                  f"flagged-programs={r['noncompliant_program_mentions']})")
    json.dump(records, open("data/mizan_agency_records_live.json","w"), indent=1)
    print("wrote data/mizan_agency_records_live.json")
    print("\nNOTE: government-wide dollar reconciliation to GAO rollup "
          f"({GAO_ROLLUP}) and program-level concentration are computed from the "
          "extracted series; coverage ratio requires the USAspending outlay pull. "
          "These populate the Tier-1 tables in the paper and are re-verified in audit.")

def _detects(exp, perturbed):
    """Return True if the comparator (same logic verify_snapshot uses) flags the
    perturbed value as a mismatch. Numeric: abs-diff >= TOL. String: inequality."""
    if isinstance(exp, (int, float)) and not isinstance(exp, bool):
        return abs(float(perturbed) - float(exp)) >= TOL   # mismatch correctly detected
    return str(perturbed) != str(exp)

def selftest():
    """Genuinely perturb EVERY checked value (government-wide rates, HHS facts, and
    all nine rollup values) and confirm the comparator detects each perturbation.
    Reports the true number of checks; 'missed' counts perturbations that would slip
    through. (Round-1 fix: prior selftest had 3 vacuous HHS checks and did not test
    the rollup values at all.)"""
    checks = 0
    missed = 0
    # numeric fields: perturb by a detectable delta
    numeric_sets = [("gov_improper_rate", EXPECT_GOV_IMPROPER_RATE),
                    ("rollup", EXPECT_ROLLUP)]
    for label, d in numeric_sets:
        for k, exp in d.items():
            if isinstance(exp, (int, float)) and not isinstance(exp, bool):
                checks += 1
                if not _detects(exp, exp + max(0.5, abs(exp) * 0.01 + TOL * 10)):
                    missed += 1
                    print(f"  [MISS] {label}.{k} perturbation not detected")
    # string/categorical fields: HHS facts + any non-numeric rollup fields
    for k, exp in EXPECT_HHS_2024.items():
        checks += 1
        if not _detects(exp, str(exp) + "_PERTURBED"):
            missed += 1
            print(f"  [MISS] hhs.{k} perturbation not detected")
    print(f"[selftest] perturbed {checks} values; missed {missed}")
    return missed == 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--live" in sys.argv: run_live()
    elif "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        sys.exit(0 if selftest() else 1)
    else:
        ok = verify_snapshot()
        print("\nExit 0." if ok else "\nExit 1.")
        sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

## R0484 · reproduce_paper2.py — Reproduce every figure in Bayyinah Allocation & Asymmetric-Measure Audits (Paper 2, v0.3).

- section: VI. Applied Audits & Public-Data Studies
- source_file: reproduce_paper2.py
- source_format: py
- text_sha256: 74fa6ef7b9dd32e57fe0707e44b5c4487e4a19a41873e583f55e02e8ddef9f84

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Reproduce every figure in Bayyinah Allocation & Asymmetric-Measure Audits (Paper 2, v0.3).

A single stats() object holds EVERY published statistic. It drives three modes:
  python3 reproduce_paper2.py           # offline report from the frozen snapshot (hash + field-inventory validated)
  python3 reproduce_paper2.py --live    # re-pull all 3 years live; compare EVERY statistic + schema + row count
  python3 reproduce_paper2.py --selftest# perturb each statistic and confirm the comparator detects it
Exit status is nonzero on any integrity failure, any live drift beyond tolerance, or any missed perturbation.
Source: NY State Open Data, community view gpsc-qqsz (first-party: twsw-2mqa).
"""
import json, hashlib, sys, os, copy
from collections import defaultdict
HERE=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SNAP=os.path.join(HERE,"snapshot","gpsc-qqsz_FY2022-2024.json")
MAN =os.path.join(HERE,"snapshot","MANIFEST.json")
FYS=('2022','2023','2024')
PCT_TOL=0.05      # percentage-point tolerance
REL_TOL=1e-4      # relative tolerance for dollar totals

def _num(r,f):
    try: return float(r.get(f))
    except (TypeError,ValueError): return None
def _fy(rows,y): return [r for r in rows if r.get('fiscal_year_end_date','').startswith(f"{y}-12-31")]

def stats(rows):
    """Complete structured statistics object: every number the note publishes."""
    S={"total_rows":len(rows),
       "field_inventory":sorted({k for r in rows for k in r.keys() if not k.startswith(':')})}
    for y in FYS:
        ry=_fy(rows,y); n=len(ry)
        face=sum(_num(r,'contract_amount') or 0 for r in ry)
        ae  =sum(_num(r,'amount_expended_for_fiscal_year') or 0 for r in ry)
        S[y]={"n":n,"face_total":face,"ae_total":ae,
              "missing":sum(1 for r in ry if r.get('contract_amount') in (None,'')),
              "zero":sum(1 for r in ry if _num(r,'contract_amount')==0.0),
              "mwbe_count_pct":sum(1 for r in ry if r.get('vendor_is_a_mwbe')=='Y')/n*100,
              "mwbe_face_pct":sum(_num(r,'contract_amount') or 0 for r in ry if r.get('vendor_is_a_mwbe')=='Y')/face*100,
              "mwbe_ae_pct":sum(_num(r,'amount_expended_for_fiscal_year') or 0 for r in ry if r.get('vendor_is_a_mwbe')=='Y')/ae*100}
    # FY2024 detail
    r24=_fy(rows,'2024')
    pf=defaultdict(float); pae=defaultdict(float); tf=0.0; tae=0.0
    for r in r24:
        a=_num(r,'contract_amount') or 0; e=_num(r,'amount_expended_for_fiscal_year') or 0
        pf[r.get('award_process')]+=a; pae[r.get('award_process')]+=e; tf+=a; tae+=e
    S["proc_face_pct"]={k:pf[k]/tf*100 for k in pf}
    S["proc_ae_pct"]={k:pae[k]/tae*100 for k in pae}
    def conc(field):
        byv=defaultdict(float)
        for r in r24:
            v=_num(r,field)
            if v: byv[r.get('vendor_name')]+=v
        vals=sorted(byv.values(),reverse=True); tot=sum(vals)
        x=sorted(vals);N=len(x);cum=sum(i*v for i,v in enumerate(x,1))
        gini=(2*cum)/(N*sum(x))-(N+1)/N
        return {"vendors":len(byv),"top5":sum(vals[:5])/tot*100,"top10":sum(vals[:10])/tot*100,
                "top20":sum(vals[:20])/tot*100,"gini":gini}
    S["conc_face"]=conc('contract_amount'); S["conc_ae"]=conc('amount_expended_for_fiscal_year')
    def yr(r):
        d=r.get('award_date'); return int(d[:4]) if d else None
    S["pre2024_face_share"]=sum(_num(r,'contract_amount') or 0 for r in r24 if (yr(r) or 9999)<2024)/tf*100
    return S

def _flatten(S,prefix=""):
    out={}
    for k,v in S.items():
        key=f"{prefix}{k}"
        if isinstance(v,dict): out.update(_flatten(v,key+"."))
        elif isinstance(v,(int,float)): out[key]=float(v)
        elif isinstance(v,list): out[key]=("|".join(map(str,v)))
    return out

def compare(a,b,label_a="frozen",label_b="live"):
    """Compare every numeric and schema field. Returns list of mismatches."""
    fa,fb=_flatten(a),_flatten(b); miss=[]
    keys=set(fa)|set(fb)
    for k in sorted(keys):
        if k not in fa or k not in fb: miss.append(f"{k}: present in only one ({label_a if k in fa else label_b})"); continue
        va,vb=fa[k],fb[k]
        if isinstance(va,str) or isinstance(vb,str):
            if va!=vb: miss.append(f"{k}: {label_a}={va} vs {label_b}={vb}")
        else:
            tol = PCT_TOL if ("pct" in k or "top" in k or "gini" in k or "share" in k) else max(abs(va)*REL_TOL,0.5)
            if abs(va-vb)>tol: miss.append(f"{k}: {label_a}={va:.4f} vs {label_b}={vb:.4f} (tol {tol:g})")
    return miss

def load_verify():
    raw=open(SNAP).read(); man=json.load(open(MAN))
    if hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()!=man["sha256_of_canonical_json"]:
        sys.exit("ABORT: snapshot hash mismatch.")
    rows=json.loads(raw)
    if sorted({k for r in rows for k in r.keys() if not k.startswith(':')})!=sorted(man["fields"]):
        sys.exit("ABORT: manifest field inventory != actual fields.")
    print(f"[integrity] hash OK, field inventory OK ({len(man['fields'])} fields), {man['row_count']} rows")
    return rows

def report(S):
    print("\n[4.2] MWBE count vs dollar share (both estimands), by vintage:")
    for y in FYS:
        d=S[y]
        print(f"  FY{y}: count {d['mwbe_count_pct']:4.1f}%  face {d['mwbe_face_pct']:4.2f}% (x{d['mwbe_count_pct']/d['mwbe_face_pct']:.1f})"
              f"  exp {d['mwbe_ae_pct']:4.2f}% (x{d['mwbe_count_pct']/d['mwbe_ae_pct']:.1f})  "
              f"[face ${d['face_total']/1e9:.1f}B exp ${d['ae_total']/1e9:.1f}B miss {d['missing']} zero {d['zero']}]")
    print("[4.1] FY2024 process (face | exp):")
    for k in sorted(S['proc_face_pct'],key=lambda k:-S['proc_face_pct'][k]-S['proc_ae_pct'][k]):
        print(f"  {k[:38]:40} face {S['proc_face_pct'][k]:5.2f}%  exp {S['proc_ae_pct'][k]:5.2f}%")
    cf,ce=S['conc_face'],S['conc_ae']
    print(f"[4.3] face conc  top5 {cf['top5']:.1f}% top10 {cf['top10']:.1f}% top20 {cf['top20']:.1f}% gini {cf['gini']:.3f} (vendors {cf['vendors']})")
    print(f"[4.3] exp  conc  top5 {ce['top5']:.1f}% top10 {ce['top10']:.1f}% top20 {ce['top20']:.1f}% gini {ce['gini']:.3f}")
    print(f"[4.0] pre-2024-award face share {S['pre2024_face_share']:.1f}% (stock, not FY2024 flow)")

def live_compare(frozen_stats):
    import urllib.request
    print("\n[live] pulling all three years and comparing EVERY statistic + schema + row count...")
    base="https://data.ny.gov/resource/gpsc-qqsz.json"; live=[]
    for y in FYS:
        off=0
        while True:
            u=f"{base}?$where=fiscal_year_end_date='{y}-12-31T00:00:00.000'&$limit=20000&$offset={off}"
            b=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(u,timeout=60))
            if not b: break
            live+=b; off+=len(b)
            if len(b)<20000: break
    miss=compare(frozen_stats,stats(live))
    if miss:
        print(f"[live] DRIFT on {len(miss)} field(s):"); [print("   "+m) for m in miss]
        return 2
    print("[live] no drift on any published statistic, schema, or row count"); return 0

def selftest(S):
    print("\n[selftest] perturbing each statistic to confirm the comparator detects it...")
    fails=[]
    flat=_flatten(S)
    numeric=[k for k,v in flat.items() if isinstance(v,float)]
    for k in numeric:
        pert=copy.deepcopy(S)
        # navigate to the leaf and bump it by 10x tolerance
        parts=k.split("."); ref=pert
        for p in parts[:-1]: ref=ref[p]
        ref[parts[-1]]=ref[parts[-1]]+ (1.0 if ("pct" in k or "top" in k or "gini" in k or "share" in k) else max(abs(flat[k])*1e-3,1000))
        if not compare(S,pert,"orig","perturbed"):
            fails.append(k)
    # schema perturbation
    pert=copy.deepcopy(S); pert["field_inventory"]=pert["field_inventory"][:-1]
    if not compare(S,pert): fails.append("field_inventory")
    if fails:
        print(f"[selftest] FAIL: comparator missed {len(fails)} perturbation(s): {fails}"); return 1
    print(f"[selftest] PASS: comparator detected all {len(numeric)+1} deliberate perturbations"); return 0

if __name__=="__main__":
    rows=load_verify(); S=stats(rows); report(S)
    code=0
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv: code=max(code,selftest(S))
    if "--live" in sys.argv: code=max(code,live_compare(S))
    sys.exit(code)
