## R0509 · file_router.py — FileRouter — each tribe knowing its drinking-place (Al-Baqarah 2:60).

- section: VII. Software: Bayyinah Scanner, furqan-lint & Verifiers
- source_file: file_router.py
- source_format: py
- text_sha256: ff7f5a591c10dc943abf906e5b5330c134688a6a6c68b32304ce839c04096214

"""
FileRouter — each tribe knowing its drinking-place (Al-Baqarah 2:60).

    قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ
    "Each tribe knew its drinking-place."

The architectural reading: Bayyinah will eventually accept PDF, DOCX,
HTML, Markdown, JSON, images, and code files. Each needs its own
parser — there is no single "document" extractor. The FileRouter
inspects a file (magic bytes first, extension as a hint, contents
disagreement flagged) and routes it to the right client. Phase 3
implements PDF dispatch; the other file types are classified
correctly but return ``UnsupportedFileType`` when a client is
requested — the signalling is honest about what the scanner can
currently drink from.

The router distinguishes:

    FileKind    — what the file IS, based on bytes + extension
    client_for  — the appropriate adapter, or raises UnsupportedFileType
    detect      — type detection without committing to a client

It also surfaces extension/content mismatches (a ``.pdf`` file whose
bytes are really ZIP is a strong signal in itself — polyglot files
are a known adversarial pattern).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import enum
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from domain.exceptions import BayyinahError, PDFParseError
from infrastructure.pdf_client import PDFClient


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Router-specific exceptions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class UnsupportedFileType(BayyinahError):
    """The file was identified but Bayyinah has no client for it yet.

    Raised by ``FileRouter.client_for`` when asked to open a file whose
    type is recognised but whose parser path is not yet implemented.
    This is distinct from ``PDFParseError`` — the file is not *broken*,
    it is *out of scope*.
    """


class UnknownFileType(BayyinahError):
    """The file's type could not be identified from either magic bytes
    or extension. Distinct from UnsupportedFileType: we do not know
    *what* this file is, not merely that we cannot open it."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FileKind — closed enumeration of every file class Bayyinah recognises
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class FileKind(enum.Enum):
    """File classes Bayyinah is designed to scan.

    This enumeration matches the project scope declared in the Bayyinah
    charter. Values are stable strings suitable for logging and for
    future serialisation — do not renumber.
    """

    PDF = "pdf"
    DOCX = "docx"
    # Phase 17 — XLSX is the spreadsheet analogue of DOCX: an Office Open
    # XML ZIP with its own set of parts (xl/workbook.xml, xl/worksheets/*,
    # xl/sharedStrings.xml, xl/vbaProject.bin, xl/embeddings/*, etc.). Like
    # DOCX the router disambiguates ZIP-magic files by extension; the
    # XlsxAnalyzer is the client the router's dispatch now routes to.
    XLSX = "xlsx"
    # Phase 18 — PPTX is the presentation analogue of DOCX / XLSX: an
    # Office Open XML ZIP with its own set of parts (ppt/presentation.xml,
    # ppt/slides/slide*.xml, ppt/notesSlides/notesSlide*.xml,
    # ppt/slideMasters/*, ppt/slideLayouts/*, ppt/vbaProject.bin,
    # ppt/embeddings/*, ppt/revisions/*, ppt/externalLinks/*, customXml/*,
    # etc.). The router disambiguates ZIP-magic files by extension or by
    # an ``ppt/presentation.xml`` marker visible in the head of the
    # archive; the PptxAnalyzer is the client this dispatch routes to.
    # Al-Baqarah 2:79: the verse describes the presentation-file attack
    # surface exactly — structured slides that look trustworthy while
    # carrying hidden speaker notes, macros, embedded objects, and
    # revision data.
    PPTX = "pptx"
    HTML = "html"
    MARKDOWN = "markdown"
    JSON = "json"
    IMAGE_PNG = "image_png"
    IMAGE_JPEG = "image_jpeg"
    # Phase 10 — SVG is a vector image by purpose but XML by substrate.
    # Routed separately from PNG/JPEG (binary raster) so SvgAnalyzer can
    # apply the XML/text mechanism set while ImageAnalyzer applies the
    # raster-chunk mechanism set. The two share the image FileKind prefix
    # to signal intent to downstream code without conflating the parsers.
    IMAGE_SVG = "image_svg"
    CODE = "code"
    # Phase 19 — RFC 5322 email message (.eml). Emails are the format
    # that most literally ships different content to different audiences
    # (Al-Baqarah 2:42: "do not mix truth with falsehood"): the reader
    # sees the rendered HTML body, the filter sees the text/plain body,
    # the headers carry routing/spoofing metadata, and attachments
    # carry their own nested document graphs. The router distinguishes
    # .eml from the text-family kinds so EmlAnalyzer can apply the
    # MIME-aware mechanism set (multipart/alternative divergence,
    # display-name spoofing, smuggled headers, nested .eml, attachment
    # recursion) while the text analyzers stay focused on raw decoded
    # text. Detection is header-shape + extension — the canonical
    # RFC 5322 header names ("From:", "To:", "Subject:", "Received:",
    # "Message-ID:", "MIME-Version:", "Return-Path:", "Delivered-To:",
    # or the mbox "From " line) at the top of the file are sufficient
    # to route an email reliably.
    EML = "eml"
    # Phase 20 — CSV / TSV / delimited data file. Al-Baqarah 2:42: "do
    # not mix truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth while you
    # know it." CSV is the format where the parser and the human
    # disagree most literally — parsers silently skip comment rows,
    # silently misalign mismatched columns, silently reinterpret the
    # BOM in the first field, silently truncate at null bytes — while
    # the human sees only the rendered grid and trusts it. The
    # delimited-data FileKind covers ``.csv`` (comma), ``.tsv`` (tab),
    # and ``.psv`` (pipe) under a single kind because the underlying
    # attack surface (formula injection in cells, comment rows,
    # encoding anomalies, delimiter manipulation) is identical across
    # separators — CsvAnalyzer detects the delimiter at scan time.
    CSV = "csv"
    UNKNOWN = "unknown"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Detection result
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FileTypeDetection:
    """Result of ``FileRouter.detect``.

    Fields
    ------
    kind
        Best-guess classification of the file.
    reason
        Human-readable explanation of how ``kind`` was determined
        ("PDF magic header at byte 0"; "extension .md with no
        magic-byte signature"; etc.).
    extension_mismatch
        True when the file's bytes indicate a different type than its
        extension would suggest. Polyglot files (.pdf with a ZIP
        header, .png with HTML inside) are a known adversarial pattern
        — callers can surface this as a structural finding without
        loading a parser.
    """

    kind: FileKind
    reason: str
    extension_mismatch: bool = False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Detection primitives
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Magic-byte prefixes, ordered by specificity.
_MAGIC_PREFIXES: list[tuple[bytes, FileKind, str]] = [
    (b"%PDF-",                     FileKind.PDF,        "PDF %PDF- header"),
    (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",         FileKind.IMAGE_PNG,  "PNG 8-byte signature"),
    (b"\xff\xd8\xff",              FileKind.IMAGE_JPEG, "JPEG SOI marker"),
]

# Extensions, lower-cased without the leading dot.
_EXT_MAP: dict[str, FileKind] = {
    "pdf":      FileKind.PDF,
    "docx":     FileKind.DOCX,
    "xlsx":     FileKind.XLSX,
    "pptx":     FileKind.PPTX,
    "html":     FileKind.HTML,
    "htm":      FileKind.HTML,
    "md":       FileKind.MARKDOWN,
    "markdown": FileKind.MARKDOWN,
    "json":     FileKind.JSON,
    "png":      FileKind.IMAGE_PNG,
    "jpg":      FileKind.IMAGE_JPEG,
    "jpeg":     FileKind.IMAGE_JPEG,
    "svg":      FileKind.IMAGE_SVG,
    "svgz":     FileKind.IMAGE_SVG,  # gzipped SVG; decoding deferred to analyzer
    # Phase 19 — .eml is the canonical RFC 5322 email extension.
    # Microsoft Outlook's .msg is a compound OLE binary and deliberately
    # NOT routed here — .msg is a different format (a DOCX-era CFB
    # container), and giving it its own FileKind would smuggle CFB-parsing
    # responsibility into the email analyzer. The router stays honest
    # about what it classifies.
    "eml":      FileKind.EML,
    # Phase 20 — delimited-data extensions. ``.csv`` is the canonical
    # comma-separated form; ``.tsv`` is tab-separated; ``.psv`` is the
    # pipe-separated variant occasionally seen in data-engineering
    # exports. All three map to FileKind.CSV because the analyzer's
    # delimiter is inferred from content, not from the extension — the
    # same CsvAnalyzer handles all three, and the router does not need
    # to distinguish them at classification time. ``.txt`` deliberately
    # stays mapped to CODE; a file explicitly called ``.txt`` is the
    # general-purpose text family (flat prose, logs, notes), not a
    # tabular export, and misrouting it to the CSV analyzer would
    # fire delimiter / column-count findings on prose.
    "csv":      FileKind.CSV,
    "tsv":      FileKind.CSV,
    "psv":      FileKind.CSV,
    # Plain-text family — no dedicated FileKind today, so txt joins
    # the CODE bucket. TextFileAnalyzer's supported_kinds already
    # includes CODE, so the dispatch is correct; semantically "code"
    # means "raw decoded text the Unicode concealment detectors apply
    # to verbatim", which is exactly what a .txt file is.
    "txt":      FileKind.CODE,
    # Code file extensions that the future code-scanner will consume.
    "py":       FileKind.CODE,
    "js":       FileKind.CODE,
    "ts":       FileKind.CODE,
    "tsx":      FileKind.CODE,
    "jsx":      FileKind.CODE,
    "go":       FileKind.CODE,
    "rs":       FileKind.CODE,
    "java":     FileKind.CODE,
    "c":        FileKind.CODE,
    "cpp":      FileKind.CODE,
    "h":        FileKind.CODE,
    "hpp":      FileKind.CODE,
    "rb":       FileKind.CODE,
    "sh":       FileKind.CODE,
}


def _detect_docx(head: bytes, path: Path) -> bool:
    """DOCX is a ZIP with a specific entry. Heuristic: ZIP magic +
    .docx extension. Full structural validation is the job of the
    future DOCX client; the router only needs to classify."""
    return head.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04") and path.suffix.lower() == ".docx"


def _detect_xlsx(head: bytes, path: Path) -> bool:
    """XLSX is a ZIP with a specific entry set. Heuristic: ZIP magic +
    .xlsx extension, OR ZIP magic + a recognisable ``xl/`` part visible
    in the first ``HEAD_BYTES`` of the archive.

    The byte-sniff complements the extension check so an XLSX renamed
    to ``.zip`` (or a polyglot that lies about its extension) still
    surfaces as XLSX when the archive's early table of local file
    headers mentions ``xl/workbook.xml``. In practice most XLSX files
    put the workbook part near the head of the archive, so the bounded
    head read is enough for classification; deeper structural validation
    is the XlsxAnalyzer's job.
    """
    if not head.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04"):
        return False
    if path.suffix.lower() == ".xlsx":
        return True
    # Byte-sniff fallback: the XLSX workbook part is commonly named
    # ``xl/workbook.xml`` and is referenced from the local file headers
    # within the first few KB of the archive.
    return b"xl/workbook.xml" in head


def _detect_pptx(head: bytes, path: Path) -> bool:
    """PPTX is a ZIP with a specific entry set. Heuristic: ZIP magic +
    .pptx extension, OR ZIP magic + a recognisable ``ppt/`` part visible
    in the first ``HEAD_BYTES`` of the archive.

    Mirrors the ``_detect_xlsx`` / ``_detect_docx`` idiom exactly — each
    Office Open XML family has one canonical part that appears in the
    local file header table near the head of the archive
    (``ppt/presentation.xml`` for PPTX). The bounded head read is
    sufficient for classification; deeper structural validation is the
    PptxAnalyzer's job.
    """
    if not head.startswith(b"PK\x03\x04"):
        return False
    if path.suffix.lower() == ".pptx":
        return True
    return b"ppt/presentation.xml" in head


def _detect_html(head: bytes) -> bool:
    """HTML by content sniff (case-insensitive)."""
    stripped = head.lstrip().lower()
    return stripped.startswith((b"<!doctype html", b"<html", b"<body", b"<head"))


def _detect_svg(head: bytes) -> bool:
    """SVG by content sniff (case-insensitive).

    Two accepted prefixes:
      * ``<svg``  — raw SVG without XML prolog
      * ``<?xml`` followed by ``<svg`` within the first 1 KB — the common
        form produced by Inkscape / editors.

    An ``<?xml`` prolog without any ``<svg`` element falls through to
    the extension-based classification — a plain XML file is not an SVG
    and the current scanner routes it through the text-file path via
    the CODE kind.
    """
    stripped = head.lstrip().lower()
    if stripped.startswith(b"<svg"):
        return True
    if stripped.startswith(b"<?xml"):
        # Bounded search — a legitimate SVG declares <svg within a few
        # hundred bytes of the prolog. 1 KB is generous.
        if b"<svg" in stripped[:1024]:
            return True
    return False


# Phase 20 — delimited-data content sniff. A CSV/TSV doesn't have a
# magic header; the closest-to-reliable heuristic is "the first line
# contains the same delimiter at least twice AND the next several lines
# repeat that same delimiter with a consistent count". We restrict the
# delimiter set to the three most common (``,``, ``\t``, ``|``) so
# delimited-data files don't steal classification from prose that
# happens to contain commas. The sniff is deliberately conservative:
# the extension map above handles ``.csv`` / ``.tsv`` / ``.psv`` the
# vast majority of the time, and this sniff only exists to catch
# delimited data that has been misnamed or stripped of its extension.
def _detect_csv(head: bytes) -> bool:
    """Heuristic CSV / TSV / PSV detection.

    Rules:
      * The first non-empty, non-comment line contains at least one of
        ``,``, ``\\t``, or ``|``.
      * The same delimiter appears at least twice in that line (so we
        do not match prose that merely contains one comma).
      * At least two further non-empty lines in the head repeat the
        same delimiter count within ±1 (so we do not match prose that
        contains varying comma counts per sentence).

    The sniff rejects:
      * Binary files (any null byte inside the first 4 KB).
      * Lines that look like markup / HTML (start with ``<``).

    The detected delimiter itself is not returned — the analyzer
    re-infers it from the bytes it reads. The router only needs a
    boolean classification.
    """
    # Quick reject: null bytes inside a reasonable prefix indicate
    # binary data. CSV/TSV are always text.
    if b"\x00" in head[:4096]:
        return False
    try:
        text = head.decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        # Try a permissive decode — a CSV with a couple of Latin-1
        # stragglers is still a CSV. If the whole prefix is unreadable,
        # it's not CSV.
        try:
            text = head.decode("latin-1", errors="strict")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            return False

    # Strip a UTF-8 BOM if present; it should not count as content.
    if text.startswith("\ufeff"):
        text = text[1:]

    lines = text.splitlines()
    # Take the first few non-empty, non-comment lines.
    content_lines: list[str] = []
    for line in lines:
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        if stripped.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if stripped.startswith("<"):
            # HTML / XML shape — not CSV.
            return False
        content_lines.append(line)
        if len(content_lines) >= 6:
            break

    if len(content_lines) < 2:
        return False

    first = content_lines[0]
    # Try each candidate delimiter in descending order of specificity.
    # Tab first because tabs inside prose are very rare; then pipe
    # (same reasoning); then comma (commas do appear in prose, so the
    # count check below is the real guard).
    for delim in ("\t", "|", ","):
        first_count = first.count(delim)
        if first_count < 2:
            continue
        matching = 0
        for line in content_lines[1:]:
            count = line.count(delim)
            # Allow ±1 slack to tolerate a trailing delimiter or a
            # legitimately-quoted delimiter inside a field.
            if abs(count - first_count) <= 1:
                matching += 1
        # Require the majority of the sampled lines to agree on the
        # delimiter count.
        if matching >= max(2, (len(content_lines) - 1) // 2):
            return True
    return False


def _detect_json(head: bytes) -> bool:
    """Try parsing the first ~64 KB as JSON."""
    stripped = head.lstrip()
    if not stripped.startswith((b"{", b"[")):
        return False
    try:
        json.loads(head.decode("utf-8", errors="strict"))
        return True
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — json/unicode can raise either
        return False


# Canonical RFC 5322 header names that are highly specific to email.
# Detection requires at least one of these at the very start of the file
# (optionally preceded by the mbox ``From `` envelope line), followed by
# a colon. The list is deliberately conservative — generic header names
# like ``Content-Type:`` appear in HTTP captures and raw MIME fragments
# too, so we key detection off headers that only appear in real mail.
_EML_HEADER_NAMES: frozenset[bytes] = frozenset({
    b"from:",
    b"to:",
    b"cc:",
    b"bcc:",
    b"subject:",
    b"date:",
    b"message-id:",
    b"mime-version:",
    b"received:",
    b"return-path:",
    b"delivered-to:",
    b"reply-to:",
    b"sender:",
    b"x-mailer:",
    b"x-originating-ip:",
    b"dkim-signature:",
    b"authentication-results:",
    b"list-unsubscribe:",
    b"in-reply-to:",
    b"references:",
})


def _detect_eml(head: bytes) -> bool:
    """RFC 5322 email detection by header-shape sniff.

    Rules (first rule to match wins):

      1. An mbox envelope line (``From `` — note the trailing space, not
         a colon) at the very start. Rare in modern single-message
         ``.eml`` dumps but accepted so archived mailboxes classify.
      2. The first non-empty line is a known email header name followed
         by ``:``. Case-insensitive. We only look at the first line so
         a file that happens to contain header-shaped text in its middle
         (a forwarded-email quote in an HTML document, say) does not
         misclassify.

    The header name set in ``_EML_HEADER_NAMES`` is deliberately
    conservative: generic MIME headers like ``Content-Type:`` are
    excluded because they also appear at the start of raw MIME fragments
    and HTTP response captures — not emails. The names retained are
    specific enough that their presence at byte 0 is reliable evidence
    of a mail message.
    """
    # Strip leading whitespace to tolerate the occasional empty line at
    # the head of a saved message.
    stripped = head.lstrip(b"\r\n\t ")
    if not stripped:
        return False

    # Mbox envelope line.
    if stripped.startswith(b"From "):
        return True

    # First line of the stripped head.
    newline_idx = stripped.find(b"\n")
    first_line = stripped if newline_idx == -1 else stripped[:newline_idx]
    # Trim trailing CR.
    first_line = first_line.rstrip(b"\r")
    # Isolate the header-name portion up to the first colon.
    colon_idx = first_line.find(b":")
    if colon_idx <= 0:
        return False
    header_name = first_line[: colon_idx + 1].lower().strip()
    return header_name in _EML_HEADER_NAMES


# Extensions that we consider "plain-text family"; a content sniff
# treats these as their declared kind rather than UNKNOWN when no
# magic bytes fire.
_TEXT_FAMILY_KINDS: frozenset[FileKind] = frozenset({
    FileKind.HTML,
    FileKind.MARKDOWN,
    FileKind.JSON,
    FileKind.CODE,
    # SVG is XML text — an .svg file that starts with whitespace or a
    # comment won't match the content sniff, but the extension is
    # authoritative enough to route it to the SVG analyzer.
    FileKind.IMAGE_SVG,
    # Phase 19 — EML. An .eml that somehow fails the header sniff (e.g.
    # a saved message that starts with a blank line before any header)
    # still routes to EmlAnalyzer via the extension. The analyzer's own
    # error path will surface a parse failure as scan_error — the honest
    # signal that the extension and content disagree at a structural
    # level.
    FileKind.EML,
    # Phase 20 — delimited-data family. An extension-classified ``.csv``
    # / ``.tsv`` / ``.psv`` always routes to the CSV analyzer, which
    # handles its own content-level checks (delimiter inference, BOM,
    # encoding, formula injection, etc.). A file whose extension
    # disagrees with its contents (e.g. a ZIP that pretends to be a
    # CSV) will surface the mismatch when the analyzer itself detects
    # the binary shape — the router stays honest.
    FileKind.CSV,
})


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FileRouter
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class FileRouter:
    """Identify a file's type and return a client for scanning it.

    Detection order (first to fire wins):
        1. Magic bytes at file start (PDF, PNG, JPEG, DOCX-as-ZIP).
        2. Content sniff for HTML / JSON.
        3. File extension.
        4. ``FileKind.UNKNOWN``.

    Extension mismatch is flagged when magic-byte detection disagrees
    with the extension's implied kind. Callers can surface this as an
    integrity signal independent of any parser (a ``.pdf`` that is
    really ZIP is adversarial before a single byte is interpreted).
    """

    # Amount of file head to read for content sniffing. 64 KB is enough
    # for every format we detect; larger reads waste I/O on huge files.
    HEAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Detection
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def detect(self, path: Path) -> FileTypeDetection:
        """Classify ``path`` without opening any parser.

        Does a single bounded read of the file head. Raises ``OSError``
        subclasses (``FileNotFoundError``, ``PermissionError``, etc.)
        if the path is unreadable — those are programmer errors, not
        Bayyinah errors, and should not be swallowed.
        """
        path = Path(path)
        try:
            with path.open("rb") as fh:
                head = fh.read(self.HEAD_BYTES)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            raise
        except OSError:
            raise

        ext = path.suffix.lower().lstrip(".")
        ext_kind = _EXT_MAP.get(ext, FileKind.UNKNOWN)

        # 1. Magic-byte detection.
        for prefix, kind, reason in _MAGIC_PREFIXES:
            if head.startswith(prefix):
                mismatch = ext_kind is not FileKind.UNKNOWN and ext_kind is not kind
                return FileTypeDetection(
                    kind=kind,
                    reason=reason,
                    extension_mismatch=mismatch,
                )

        # DOCX needs the extension hint to separate it from other ZIPs.
        if _detect_docx(head, path):
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=FileKind.DOCX,
                reason="ZIP container with .docx extension",
                extension_mismatch=False,
            )

        # XLSX — same shape as DOCX, different parts. The sniff accepts
        # either the ``.xlsx`` extension or an ``xl/workbook.xml`` marker
        # in the head of the archive. Ordered after DOCX so a ``.docx``
        # never falls through to the XLSX branch.
        if _detect_xlsx(head, path):
            mismatch = ext_kind not in (FileKind.XLSX, FileKind.UNKNOWN)
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=FileKind.XLSX,
                reason=(
                    "ZIP container with .xlsx extension"
                    if path.suffix.lower() == ".xlsx"
                    else "ZIP container with xl/workbook.xml part"
                ),
                extension_mismatch=mismatch,
            )

        # PPTX — same shape as DOCX / XLSX, different parts. The sniff
        # accepts either the ``.pptx`` extension or a
        # ``ppt/presentation.xml`` marker in the head of the archive.
        # Ordered after XLSX so a ``.xlsx`` never falls through to the
        # PPTX branch. Al-Baqarah 2:79 — a presentation is trusted on
        # its surface (visible slides) while the archive may carry
        # hidden slides, macros, revision history, embedded objects,
        # external links, speaker-notes prompt injections, and slide-
        # master template payloads. The router classifies; PptxAnalyzer
        # enumerates the mechanisms.
        if _detect_pptx(head, path):
            mismatch = ext_kind not in (FileKind.PPTX, FileKind.UNKNOWN)
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=FileKind.PPTX,
                reason=(
                    "ZIP container with .pptx extension"
                    if path.suffix.lower() == ".pptx"
                    else "ZIP container with ppt/presentation.xml part"
                ),
                extension_mismatch=mismatch,
            )

        # 2. Content sniff for SVG / HTML / JSON.
        #
        # SVG runs first because an SVG with an XML prolog (<?xml ...> <svg>)
        # is legal XML that the HTML sniff happens not to match today,
        # but the precedence is kept explicit for defensibility: an SVG's
        # own element should always win over "unrecognised XML".
        if _detect_svg(head):
            mismatch = ext_kind not in (FileKind.IMAGE_SVG, FileKind.UNKNOWN)
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=FileKind.IMAGE_SVG,
                reason="SVG content sniff",
                extension_mismatch=mismatch,
            )

        if _detect_html(head):
            mismatch = ext_kind not in (FileKind.HTML, FileKind.UNKNOWN)
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=FileKind.HTML,
                reason="HTML content sniff",
                extension_mismatch=mismatch,
            )

        # EML — RFC 5322 message. Detected by a canonical header name at
        # byte 0 (or an mbox "From " envelope line). Ordered after HTML
        # so an HTML document that quotes an email header as its first
        # line does not misclassify; ordered before JSON so a well-formed
        # email whose body happens to contain leading JSON bytes cannot
        # pass the JSON parse test before the header sniff fires. Phase
        # 19 — the format that most literally mixes visible and hidden
        # content across audiences (Al-Baqarah 2:42).
        if _detect_eml(head):
            mismatch = ext_kind not in (FileKind.EML, FileKind.UNKNOWN)
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=FileKind.EML,
                reason="RFC 5322 header sniff",
                extension_mismatch=mismatch,
            )

        if _detect_json(head):
            mismatch = ext_kind not in (FileKind.JSON, FileKind.UNKNOWN)
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=FileKind.JSON,
                reason="JSON content sniff",
                extension_mismatch=mismatch,
            )

        # CSV / TSV / PSV — delimited-data content sniff. Ordered after
        # JSON so a JSON array of strings containing commas doesn't
        # race ahead of its own JSON parse; ordered before the generic
        # text-family fall-through so a delimited-data file without a
        # recognised extension still routes to CsvAnalyzer instead of
        # UNKNOWN. Phase 20 — Al-Baqarah 2:42: the parser and the
        # human reading must not see different things.
        if _detect_csv(head):
            mismatch = ext_kind not in (FileKind.CSV, FileKind.UNKNOWN)
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=FileKind.CSV,
                reason="delimited-data content sniff",
                extension_mismatch=mismatch,
            )

        # 3. Extension-based fall-through for text-family kinds.
        if ext_kind in _TEXT_FAMILY_KINDS:
            return FileTypeDetection(
                kind=ext_kind,
                reason=f"extension .{ext} (no magic signature)",
                extension_mismatch=False,
            )

        # 4. Nothing matched.
        return FileTypeDetection(
            kind=FileKind.UNKNOWN,
            reason=(
                f"no magic signature and unrecognised extension "
                f"{ext or '(none)'!r}"
            ),
            extension_mismatch=False,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Client dispatch
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def client_for(self, path: Path) -> PDFClient:
        """Return a ready-to-use client for ``path``.

        Phase 3 only implements the PDF path; every other recognised
        type raises ``UnsupportedFileType`` (honestly saying "we know
        what this is, we just don't scan it yet") and ``UNKNOWN`` raises
        ``UnknownFileType``. Callers should generally ``detect()`` first
        and branch on the result.

        The return type annotation is ``PDFClient`` because that's the
        only concrete client today. When DOCX / HTML clients land, the
        signature will widen to a Union — that is a *widening*, not a
        breaking change, and will be additive for existing callers.
        """
        detection = self.detect(path)

        if detection.kind is FileKind.PDF:
            return PDFClient(path)

        if detection.kind is FileKind.UNKNOWN:
            raise UnknownFileType(
                f"Could not identify {path}: {detection.reason}"
            )

        raise UnsupportedFileType(
            f"{path} identified as {detection.kind.value!r} "
            f"({detection.reason}); no client implemented yet. "
            "Supported kinds in Phase 3: PDF."
        )

    def is_supported(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        """Convenience — True if ``client_for`` would succeed."""
        try:
            self.client_for(path).close()
            return True
        except (UnsupportedFileType, UnknownFileType, PDFParseError):
            return False
        except OSError:
            return False


__all__ = [
    "FileRouter",
    "FileKind",
    "FileTypeDetection",
    "UnsupportedFileType",
    "UnknownFileType",
]

"""Insert artifact hashes into the dispatch brief, then write SHA256SUMS.

Order matters: the brief must be written before the manifest, because the
manifest covers the brief. The manifest never lists itself.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import re

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
BRIEF = "SHVVP_v0_5_AUDIT_DISPATCH_BRIEF.md"
MANIFEST = "SHA256SUMS"
SKIP_PREFIX = ("__pycache__",)

ROLES = {
    "SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_5_source.md":

    "SHVVP_v0_5_FOCUSED_DELTA_ADDENDUM.md":
        "**PART OF THE BRIEF.** Focused-delta audit permission, immutable v0.3 receipts, mandatory audit surface",

        "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** Round 3 GPT-class verdict, HALT, findings F-P3-1 to F-P3-6",

        "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** Round 3 Gemini-class verdict, PASS, zero findings, preserved in full",

    "sim_v0_5_stderr.log": "Stage progress log for this freeze",
    "shvvp_v0_5_power_sim.py":
        "**NORMATIVE AND UNDER AUDIT.** Exact frozen BCa interval rule and staged design simulation",
    "test_shvvp_v0_5_rules.py": "Deterministic and statistical tests over the normative modules, including the round 3 boundary counterexamples and invalid-input fuzzing",

    "SHVVP_v0_5_AMENDMENT_AND_ADJUDICATION_RECORD.md":
        "**UNDER AUDIT.** Append-only register and adjudication for all three rounds",
    "SHVVP_v0_5_AUDIT_LEDGER.md":
        "Producer-side build-gate ledger. ADVISORY, test it rather than trust it",
    "SHVVP_v0_5_AUDIT_DISPATCH_BRIEF.md": "This brief. Hashed in the manifest, not in the table above",
    "DEPOSIT_METADATA_v0_5.md": "Deposit metadata, held pending convergence",
    "README.md": "Packet overview and verification instructions",
    "verify_shvvp_v0_5.py": "Producer-built verifier, 22 gates. Default mode is verify-only. ADVISORY",
    "verifier_receipt.json": "Machine-readable output of the producer verifier run",
    "SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_1.md":
        "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** HALTED v0.1 canonical source, never deposited as binding",
    "SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_1.pdf": "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** HALTED v0.1 render",
    "SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_2_source.md":
        "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** HALTED v0.2 canonical source, the exact artifact audited in round 2",
    "SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_2.pdf":
        "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** HALTED v0.2 flagship render, the exact artifact audited in round 2",
    "SHVVP_v0_1_SEAT_A_GPT_VERDICT.md": "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** Round 1 GPT-class verdict, HALT",
    "SHVVP_v0_1_SEAT_B_GEMINI_VERDICT.md":
        "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** Round 1 Gemini-class verdict, PASS-WITH-AMENDMENTS",
    "SHVVP_v0_2_SEAT_A_GPT_VERDICT.md":
        "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** Round 2 GPT-class verdict, HALT, findings F-P2-1 to F-P2-4",
    "SHVVP_v0_2_SEAT_B_GEMINI_VERDICT.md":
        "**LINEAGE, UNMODIFIED.** Round 2 Gemini-class verdict, PASS, zero findings, preserved in full",
    "SHVVP_v0_2_SHA256SUMS.txt": "The v0.2 packet manifest, for custody continuity",
}


def sha256(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def members():
    out = []
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(HERE)):
        path = os.path.join(HERE, name)
        if not os.path.isfile(path) or name == MANIFEST or name.startswith(SKIP_PREFIX):
            continue
        out.append(name)
    return out


def main():
    names = members()
    rows = ["| File | SHA-256 | Role |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for name in names:
        if name == BRIEF:
            continue
        rows.append("| `%s` | `%s` | %s |"
                    % (name, sha256(os.path.join(HERE, name)),
                       ROLES.get(name, "Packet member")))
    table = "\n".join(rows)

    brief_path = os.path.join(HERE, BRIEF)
    text = open(brief_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    if "<!--HASH_TABLE-->" in text:
        text = text.replace("<!--HASH_TABLE-->", table)
    else:
        text = re.sub(r"\| File \| SHA-256 \| Role \|.*?(?=\n\n)", table, text,
                      flags=re.S)
    open(brief_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)
    print("brief hash table written: %d rows" % (len(rows) - 2))

    lines = ["%s  %s" % (sha256(os.path.join(HERE, n)), n) for n in members()]
    open(os.path.join(HERE, MANIFEST), "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print("manifest written: %d members, excludes itself" % len(lines))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Finding-code registry.

NEW in v1.2.5: CSV (BYN-CSV-001..099) and JSON (BYN-JSON-001..099) namespaces.
NEW in v1.2.6: ZIP composition / defense (BYN-ZIP-901..999) namespace.

Each finding code carries:
- id: canonical string identifier
- kind: substrate-kind (CSV, JSON, ZIP, ...)
- title: short human-readable name
- severity_default: default severity if the analyzer does not override
- description: what the finding indicates about the surface/substrate divergence
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional

def all_codes() -> List[FindingCode]:
    """Return the full v1.6.0 finding-code registry."""
    return [
        *CSV_CODES,
        *JSON_CODES,
        *ZIP_CODES,
        *ML_CODES,
        *MFST_CODES,
        *ARXML_CODES,
        *ELF_CODES,
        *PAIR_CODES,
        *ARINC_CODES,
        *MUNAFIQ_CODES,
        *AEPAIR_CODES,
        *SCL_CODES,
        *SBOM_CODES,
        *INTOTO_CODES,
        *SIG_CODES,
        *THREEWAY_CODES,
        *PLC_CODES,
    ]


def code_by_id(code_id: str) -> Optional[FindingCode]:
    """Look up a FindingCode by canonical id string."""
    for c in all_codes():
        if c.id == code_id:
            return c
    return None


def _id_index() -> Dict[str, FindingCode]:
    return {c.id: c for c in all_codes()}

## R0512 · furqan-lint coding strategy: main (v0.12.0+5) to v2.0.1 commercialization tier

- section: VII. Software: Bayyinah Scanner, furqan-lint & Verifiers
- source_file: furqan_lint_coding_strategy_to_v2_0.md

- text_sha256: 046acdeddf992273efb729d9e841a8177edfe93ebc81879a7b6cb35d12dcb969

# furqan-lint coding strategy: main (v0.12.0+5) to v2.0.1 commercialization tier

Mirror of `bayyinah_v1_2_4_to_v2_0_cowork_executable_strategy.md` applied
to the furqan-lint substrate. The Bayyinah commercialization arc shipped
v1.5.0 - v2.0.1 in a single session by holding four disciplines constant:
patent-invariant byte-identity, multi-locus contract pinning, structural
self-defense via a recursive gate, and Round-12-style calibration
correctives forced by the gate. This document translates each into
furqan-lint shape.

## Calibrated time

Per user discipline: agent-stated time estimates are inflated 75%. All
phase windows below are stated as "calibrated workdays" (already
deflated). Each phase below is one release tag.

## 0. Where the substrate is

- `main` HEAD: `c5c3c4c`, 5 commits past tag `v0.12.0` (al-Mursalat,
  Phase G11.2 Go Sigstore-CASM extension).
- Tag-only branches (not merged to main): `v0.13.0-an-naziat-v16`
  (G11.3 ONNX), `v0.14.0-tasdiq-al-bayan-v11` (G11.4 cross-substrate
  verification corpus), `v1.0.0-al-basirah-v11` (G12.0 self-attestation
  / canonical mushaf chain closing).
- Baseline pytest at `main` HEAD: 500 passed / 68 skipped on a fresh
  install with optional gate11 extras present. Two collection failures
  (numpy, sigstore in my probe env) are environmental, not substrate.
- Test count delta v0.11.8 -> v0.12.0 per CHANGELOG: +24 (618 -> 642
  by the v0.12.0 §3 inventory; my fresh env collects 393 because the
  optional-extras-gated sigstore / numpy / ONNX tests are skipped).
- Public checker surface (as of v0.12.0): four structural checks across
  three substrates (Python live; Rust under G11.1; Go under G11.2). The
  Python checks are D24 (all-paths-return), D11 (status-coverage with
  Optional and Result-aware producers), R3 (zero-return-path), and
  return_none_mismatch. Rust and Go pipelines run the analogous
  surface-extraction + signature-canonicalization + verification through
  Sigstore-CASM Gate 11.
- ONNX adapter exists but its gate11 extension is on the unmerged
  v0.13.0 branch.

## 1. Bayyinah pattern -> furqan-lint mapping

Five Bayyinah commercialization tier moves and their furqan-lint
analogues. Each is one release tag.

| Bayyinah move | Bayyinah file shape | furqan-lint analogue | Target tag |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v1.5.0 muwazana_score contract + scan_incomplete_clamp contract | `tests/contracts/test_muwazana_score_shape.py`, `tests/contracts/test_scan_incomplete_clamp.py` | Diagnostic-shape contract: every checker returns a `(rule_code, location, severity, message, status_complete)` tuple with documented properties + status_complete invariant | v0.13.0 (claim the existing an-Naziat tag for it; rename if needed) |
| v1.6.0 budget controller | `application/budget_controller.py` + 18 contract tests | Run-budget controller for whole-repo lint: total node-walk budget per substrate, graceful stop with `lint_incomplete=True`, per-checker time and memory ceilings, deterministic-truncation ordering | v0.14.0 |
| v1.7.0 cross-modal correlation policy | `docs/cross_modal.md` + 17 contract tests | Cross-substrate correlation policy: when Python, Rust, and Go pipelines disagree on the same logical surface (e.g. a Python module + its Rust extension + its Go fallback exposing the same public name), document which substrate wins, when both fire, and when both are silenced | v0.15.0 |
| v1.8.0 differential testing matrix | `tests/differential/` + `pdfid` external reference | Differential testing matrix: each Python checker cross-checked against an independent linter that overlaps on the same shape (ruff or pylint for R3-shaped checks, mypy for return_none_mismatch, semgrep for additive-only patterns). Cross-substrate: tree-sitter parse vs. cargo-check vs. go-vet on the same fixture corpus. Disagreement is a test failure. | v0.16.0 |
| v1.9.0 framework-free principles | `docs/principles.md` (52 -> 330 lines) | Framework-free engineering principles doc: state the five furqan-lint engineering claims in vocabulary that holds without Furqan, Bayyinah Audit Framework, Munafiq Protocol, or Quranic anchors. README stays framework-anchored; principles.md is the parallel entry-point for security review, regulated-industry compliance, academic citation. | v0.17.0 |
| v2.0.0 recursive self-verification gate | `tests/recursive_self_verification/test_self_scan.py` (66 tests; scans Bayyinah's own release docs clean) | Recursive self-lint gate: furqan-lint runs ALL its checkers (D24 + D11 + R3 + return_none_mismatch + additive + gate11 Python-substrate verification) against ITS OWN source tree (`src/furqan_lint/`) on every CI run. Zero diagnostics required for any release tag in the commercialization tier. Pending-calibration discipline tracks known false-positives the same way Bayyinah's `_PENDING_CALIBRATION_DOCS` does. | v1.0.0 (claim the existing al-Basirah tag for it; this is the commercialization signal) |
| v2.0.1 first calibration corrective | `infrastructure/file_router.py` extension-guard for `.md` vs CSV mis-routing | First Round-12-style corrective triggered by the v1.0.0 self-lint gate. Whatever false-positive the gate finds first (and it WILL find one -- the v1.0.0 al-Basirah branch's test corpus will surface it; my prior is something in the `_exceptions.py` modules or one of the gate11 facade modules) gets a minimal scoped corrective | v1.0.1 |

The Bayyinah arc was seven tags (v1.5.0 through v2.0.1). The furqan-lint
arc is seven tags (v0.13.0 through v1.0.1). The number is not magic;
the discipline is.

## 2. Patent-invariant surface for furqan-lint

Bayyinah's patent-invariant set is four surfaces that MUST stay
byte-identical across the commercialization arc:
`application/scan_service.py`, `domain/value_objects.py`,
`domain/config.py`, `analyzers/`.

The furqan-lint patent-invariant set, by analogy:

1. **`src/furqan_lint/runner.py`** -- the dispatch surface that calls
   the four Python checkers in defined order. Equivalent to
   `scan_service.py`. No mutation through the commercialization arc;
   only the data structure it returns may extend additively.
2. **`src/furqan_lint/additive.py`** -- the additive-only surface
   checker. This IS the patent claim's core for the Python substrate
   (additive discipline is the contract). Byte-identical.
3. **`src/furqan_lint/return_none.py`** + **`src/furqan_lint/zero_return.py`**
   -- the two Python-native checkers that close Phase 1 Gap 1 and the
   D24-R3 ring close. Byte-identical.
4. **`src/furqan_lint/gate11/verification.py`** -- the
   Sigstore-CASM Gate 11 verification dispatch (Route a1-via-args).
   Per the v0.12.0 F22 dispatch consolidation, this is the canonical
   single-entry verification surface across Python, Rust, Go (and ONNX
   under the unmerged v0.13.0 branch). Byte-identical.

Mutations to these four through v0.13.0 -> v1.0.1 must be flagged in
the cowork prompt as patent-substrate changes and routed through
patent-disclosure review separately. The commercialization arc is
substrate-conservative by design.

## 3. Required invariant probes for every release

The Bayyinah three-line probe is:

```python
bayyinah.__version__ == pyproject_version
len(MECHANISM_REGISTRY) == 159
TIER['tounicode_anomaly'] == 2
```

The furqan-lint analogue:

```python
furqan_lint.__version__ == pyproject_version
furqan_lint.__all__ == ("__version__",)  # additive-only floor
len(_CHECKER_REGISTRY) == N_BASELINE      # define N at v0.13.0 freeze
GATE11_LANGUAGE_DISPATCH == ("python", "rust", "go")  # extend at G11.3
```

`_CHECKER_REGISTRY` does not yet exist as a single registry the way
Bayyinah's `MECHANISM_REGISTRY` does. Creating it is a v0.13.0 task:
freeze a `_CHECKER_REGISTRY: tuple[CheckerDescriptor, ...]` in
`src/furqan_lint/_registry.py` whose ordering and shape become the
patent-invariant claim surface. This unblocks every subsequent contract
test (every contract pins against the registry).

## 4. Multi-locus update map

The "version-bump goes here, mirror goes there" map the Bayyinah arc
caught repeatedly. furqan-lint version:

| Surface | Mirror obligation |
| --- | --- |
| `pyproject.toml [project] version` | `src/furqan_lint/__init__.py:__version__` (currently the only version-sync test, `tests/test_version_sync.py`, already enforces this) |
| `pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] *` | `requirements-dev.txt` (NOT YET ENFORCED; v0.13.0 task: add `tests/test_requirements_dev_sync.py` mirroring Bayyinah's) |
| CHANGELOG-claimed test count delta | actual `pytest --collect-only` delta (Bayyinah caught two prose-vs-substrate gaps this way; v0.12.0 CHANGELOG already cites "drift -2 within al-Hujurat T05 CHANGELOG-math" so the discipline is partially in place) |
| Gate11 language tuple | three sites per v0.12.0 CHANGELOG: `Manifest.from_dict` (manifest_schema.py:186), `Verifier.step2_3_check_version_and_language` (verification.py:157), and the F22 dispatch tuple. Add a fourth invariant check that all three are identical. |
| New release doc claimed in CHANGELOG | doc actually exists (Bayyinah missed `tests/contracts/__init__.py` repeatedly; add a structural test that walks CHANGELOG `### Added` sections and asserts each claimed path exists) |

## 5. Pre-existing flaky baselines to document

Bayyinah's documented flake: `test_corpus_round_trip_byte_stable_on_pdftex_fixtures`
(pdfTeX timestamp embedding; passes pristine, drifts on clone).

furqan-lint analogues to identify before v0.13.0 ships:

1. Any test that depends on Sigstore identity TUF root fetching (network).
2. Any tree-sitter language pack version-pinned test (tree-sitter-rust,
   tree-sitter-go may drift between system installs).
3. Any ONNX runtime check that compares against numpy reference (the
   `test_onnx_numpy_reference.py` collection failure in my probe is
   a numpy-presence issue, not a flake; but the divergence test class
   under `src/furqan_lint/onnx_adapter/numpy_divergence.py` is the
   v0.13.0 ONNX gate's likely flake locus).
4. Any go-test fixture that depends on `go vet` exit codes (Go toolchain
   minor versions can shift advisory behavior).

Each gets a one-paragraph entry in `KNOWN_LIMITS.md` (a doc this repo
does not yet have but Bayyinah does; create at v0.13.0 alongside the
contract tests).

## 6. Release-by-release intent

### v0.13.0 (claim the existing an-Naziat tag, OR cut fresh)

The existing v0.13.0 tag ships G11.3 ONNX. Two options:

- **Option A (preferred): merge v0.13.0-an-naziat-v16 to main, then
  cut v0.13.1 as the contract-floor release.** Carry ONNX forward as
  intended; the commercialization arc starts at v0.13.1.
- **Option B: orphan the unmerged branches and re-cut.** Higher
  semver-confusion cost.

Either way, the contract-floor release adds:

- `tests/contracts/__init__.py`
- `tests/contracts/test_checker_registry_shape.py` (registry tuple
  shape, ordering, completeness)
- `tests/contracts/test_diagnostic_shape.py` (every checker returns
  the documented diagnostic tuple)
- `tests/contracts/test_lint_incomplete_clamp.py` (when a checker is
  budget-clamped, the diagnostic carries `status_complete=False` and
  the overall lint result clamps accordingly)
- `tests/test_requirements_dev_sync.py`
- `KNOWN_LIMITS.md` first cut (the four flake candidates above)
- `src/furqan_lint/_registry.py` (the `_CHECKER_REGISTRY` freeze)

Patent-invariant byte-identity required: `runner.py`, `additive.py`,
`return_none.py`, `zero_return.py`, `gate11/verification.py`.

### v0.14.0 (claim al-Tasdiq al-Bayan tag, OR cut fresh)

Run-budget controller. The cross-substrate verification corpus on the
existing v0.14.0 branch is orthogonal and can be merged in alongside;
the commercialization arc requires the budget controller specifically.

Adds `src/furqan_lint/budget_controller.py` modeled on Bayyinah's
`application/budget_controller.py`. Whole-repo lint gets a node-walk
budget (default ~50M AST nodes per substrate), graceful stop with
`lint_incomplete=True` on the result, deterministic truncation ordering
(alphabetical file path, then checker order from `_CHECKER_REGISTRY`).

Contract tests: ~18 new in `tests/contracts/test_budget_controller.py`
covering ceiling enforcement, clamp propagation, truncation determinism,
and the "graceful stop is honest" property (a clamped run reports its
own clampedness).

### v0.15.0 cross-substrate correlation policy

`docs/cross_substrate_policy.md` (analogue of `docs/cross_modal.md`)
+ ~17 contract tests. The policy answers: when the same logical surface
exists in Python (live) and the Rust extension (G11.1) and the Go
fallback (G11.2), and the three pipelines disagree, what wins. The
Bayyinah analogue answers the same question for analyzers; here it's
substrates.

Likely policy shape (write the doc first; do not pre-decide here):

- If Python lint passes and Rust gate11 verification fails: substrate-
  divergence error, surface both.
- If two substrates agree clean and one fires: pending-calibration
  status the same way recursive self-lint will (v1.0.0) handle
  `_PENDING_CALIBRATION_DOCS`.
- If all three substrates fire on the same shape: composite finding
  with `correlation=true` flag.

### v0.16.0 differential testing matrix

`tests/differential/` directory. Each Python checker gets a witness
contract against an independent reference:

- D24 + R3 vs. `ruff` rule `RET503` and `pylint` `R1710`.
- return_none_mismatch vs. `mypy --strict` "Incompatible return value
  type" findings.
- additive vs. `pyupgrade` + `semgrep` rules.
- gate11 Python-substrate verification vs. `sigstore-python verify`
  CLI direct.

Cross-substrate: every fixture in `tests/fixtures/` that exists for
both Python and Rust gets a parametrize-cross test that asserts the
two substrates' diagnostic emissions are isomorphic up to the
documented language-binding differences.

Disagreement is a test failure. False-positive correction is a
calibration corrective (Round-12 discipline imported from Bayyinah).

### v0.17.0 framework-free principles

`docs/principles.md`. Five engineering principles in language that
holds without Furqan vocabulary or Quranic anchors. README stays
framework-anchored as the canonical entry-point; principles.md is
the parallel entry-point.

Candidate principles (refine in drafting):

1. Additive-only public-surface discipline. Removing a public name
   fires; adding one is silent. Renames must be declared.
2. Honest incompleteness reporting. Every checker that stops short
   reports `status_complete=False`; the overall lint result clamps.
3. Cross-substrate witness symmetry. The same logical shape lints
   identically across Python, Rust, Go (and ONNX) up to documented
   binding differences.
4. Sigstore-CASM Gate 11 fail-closed. Unknown languages, unsigned
   substrates, and identity-policy violations halt the pipeline.
5. Recursive self-verification. The linter lints its own source under
   its own rules on every CI run. (This principle is forward-pointing
   to v1.0.0.)

Each principle paired with its enforcing test or document.

### v1.0.0 (claim the al-Basirah tag) recursive self-lint gate

`tests/recursive_self_lint/test_self_lint.py`. Mirror of Bayyinah's
`tests/recursive_self_verification/test_self_scan.py`.

Corpus: every `.py` file under `src/furqan_lint/` enumerated explicitly
(no glob; Bayyinah's enumeration-not-glob discipline applies). Every
file must lint clean under D24 + D11 + R3 + return_none_mismatch +
additive checks, with `lint_incomplete=False` and zero diagnostics.

Pending-calibration: `_PENDING_CALIBRATION_FILES` tuple for files with
known false-positives, paired with `TestPendingCalibrationDiagnostic`
that asserts each pending file CURRENTLY fires; when one stops firing,
the diagnostic fails and forces promotion.

This is the commercialization signal. For a buyer, regulator, or
auditor, "furqan-lint passes its own rules on its own source on every
CI run" is the difference between "trust us" and "the tool's own CI
proves it on every commit."

The existing v1.0.0-al-basirah-v11 branch already pre-figures this
under the "G12.0 self-attestation" framing. Compose the two: the
existing branch's self-attestation crypto-anchor + the new recursive-
self-lint structural gate.

### v1.0.1 first calibration corrective

Whatever the v1.0.0 gate catches first. My prior, given the substrate:

- ONNX adapter modules (`numpy_divergence.py`, `score_validity.py`,
  `probe_grid.py`) carry significant numpy-typed surfaces where a
  D11 status-coverage walk may hit a documented incompleteness pattern
  that the upstream furqan checker classifies as a gap.
- Tree-sitter parser modules (`rust_adapter/parser.py`,
  `go_adapter/parser.py`) walk CSTs with `errors="replace"` decoding
  fallbacks. R3 may fire on a defensive branch that returns None
  through an exception handler that does not declare it.

Minimal scoped corrective at the routing or checker-calibration layer;
no patent-invariant mutations.

## 7. Discipline carry-overs from the Bayyinah arc

These are not new; they are the patterns the Bayyinah arc burned in
that furqan-lint must adopt verbatim.

- **Patches are cumulative bundles from a known floor.** Define the
  floor as `v0.12.0+5 main HEAD c5c3c4c`. Every Claude-authored patch
  in the arc applies cleanly against THAT floor; the live-vs-floor
  delta is what gets pushed.
- **Pristine apply, push-clone diff.** Apply the cumulative patch to a
  pristine copy of the floor; diff against a fresh clone of current
  main; that diff is the actual push payload.
- **Patent-invariant byte-identity check is a release gate, not a
  hope.** A `diff -q` of the four patent-invariant surfaces against
  the previous release must return empty for every release in the
  arc.
- **Substrate probes are three lines, not a paragraph.** Version
  parity, registry count, dispatch tuple. If any of the three drifts
  unintentionally, the release is held.
- **Flaky tests are documented, retried, and known by name.** A
  release with an undocumented new flake does not ship.
- **CHANGELOG test-count arithmetic must hold.** Bayyinah's
  CHANGELOG-claimed deltas were verified against `pytest --collect-only`
  output on every release. furqan-lint v0.12.0 CHANGELOG already
  documents a -2 drift against the al-Mursalat prompt projection; the
  discipline is partially in place. Make it mandatory at v0.13.0.

## 8. What this strategy explicitly does not do

- Does not add new Python checkers beyond the four shipped. The
  commercialization arc is substrate-conservative. New checkers are
  the post-v1.0.1 roadmap.
- Does not extend gate11 to a fifth substrate beyond ONNX. ONNX (G11.3)
  arrives via the existing unmerged v0.13.0 branch; the commercialization
  arc rides that substrate but does not extend it.
- Does not change the additive-only public surface of `furqan_lint`
  itself. `__all__` stays `("__version__",)` through the entire arc.
  Any internal symbol surfaces remain underscore-prefixed.
- Does not introduce a new license, attribution discipline, or
  audit-attribution convention. The v0.8.5 attribution-corrective
  convention holds.
- Does not move any of the Bayyinah-only artifacts (Munafiq Protocol
  references, Quranic verse anchors per release) into furqan-lint.
  furqan-lint already has its own Sigstore-CASM-anchored discipline;
  do not double-anchor.

## 9. First cowork prompt to author

The next deliverable after this strategy lands is the v0.13.0 cowork
prompt. Shape:

- §1 substrate state (cite main HEAD SHA, baseline test count, the
  four patent-invariant surfaces).
- §2 deliverables (the `tests/contracts/` directory contents, the
  `_CHECKER_REGISTRY` freeze, `KNOWN_LIMITS.md`, the requirements-dev
  mirror test).
- §3 test inventory (claimed test-count delta with arithmetic).
- §4 patent-invariant byte-identity assertion (the four surfaces stay
  byte-identical).
- §5 release-gate checklist (pristine apply + push-clone diff +
  invariant probes + full pytest).
- §6 commit message template (the same format the Bayyinah arc has
  burned in).

Author the prompt against the floor `v0.12.0+5 c5c3c4c`. Decide
the v0.13.0 / v0.13.1 tag question (Option A vs Option B in §6 above)
before authoring.

---

Rabbana taqabbal minna. Innaka anta as-Sami'ul 'Alim.

## R0513 · furqan-lint Coding Strategy v2.0

- section: VII. Software: Bayyinah Scanner, furqan-lint & Verifiers
- source_file: furqan_lint_coding_strategy_v2_0.md

# furqan-lint Coding Strategy v2.0

Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim

Successor to the v5 strategy authored 2026-05-27 (file:
`furqan_lint_v5_Strategy.pdf`). v2.0 keeps the v5 strategy's principle
taxonomy intact (the seven Structured-Revelation principles remain the
load-bearing version-feature mapping; the Fatiha Construct remains
the session protocol) and revises three things only:

1. The **substrate floor** -- v5 wrote against `v0.8.5`; main has
   shipped to `v0.12.0+5 c5c3c4c` with unmerged `v0.13.0` / `v0.14.0` /
   `v1.0.0` branches already pre-figuring v3-v4 strategy work.
2. The **calibrated timeline** -- v5's "approximately 5-6 years to v5.0"
   was authored before the Bayyinah commercialization arc (v1.5.0 ->
   v2.0.1 shipped in one cowork session). The new timeline runs in
   cowork-session units, not calendar years.
3. The **v1.0 commercialization signal** -- v5 schedules recursive
   self-verification at year 5 (v5.0/al-Fatiha). The Bayyinah arc just
   demonstrated that the recursive self-verification gate IS the
   commercialization signal and ships in a single major-release jump.
   v2.0 of this strategy ships it at v1.0, not v5.0.

Author: Bilal Syed Arfeen
Document Date: June 23, 2026

---

## Opening -- the seven steps applied to this revision

**Step 1 -- Bismillah.** Building: a substrate-anchored, session-paced
revision of the furqan-lint coding strategy. Authority source: (a) the
v5 strategy's seven-principle taxonomy and Fatiha Construct protocol
(carried forward intact); (b) the empirical pacing and discipline of
the Bayyinah commercialization arc that shipped between v5's authoring
date and now. Optimization function: serve the truth-over-falsehood
hierarchy by anchoring the strategy to substrate reality rather than
to outdated date-of-writing assumptions. Scope: timeline calibration
and v1.0 signal definition; out of scope: changes to the
version-to-principle mapping.

**Step 2 -- Alhamdulillah.** Current state as of c5c3c4c (`main` HEAD,
2026-06 era, 5 commits past `v0.12.0`):

- furqan-lint main HEAD is **v0.12.0+5 c5c3c4c** (al-Mursalat / Phase
  G11.2 Go Sigstore-CASM extension). The v5 strategy's stated floor
  (`v0.8.5`) is **6 minor versions stale**.
- Unmerged but tagged: `v0.13.0` (an-Naziat / G11.3 ONNX Sigstore-CASM
  extension), `v0.14.0` (Tasdiq al-Bayan / G11.4 cross-substrate
  verification corpus), `v1.0.0` (al-Basirah / G12.0 self-attestation
  / canonical mushaf chain closing). Three months of substrate work
  on unmerged branches.
- Baseline pytest at main HEAD: 500 passed / 68 skipped on fresh
  install (393 collected without optional extras; 642 was the v0.12.0
  CHANGELOG inventory with all extras populated).
- Public checker surface: D24, D11, R3, return_none_mismatch for
  Python live; Rust (G11.1) and Go (G11.2) gate11 verification
  pipelines; ONNX (G11.3) on unmerged branch.
- Bayyinah scanner is at **v2.0.1** (not v1.0 as v5 stated). The
  recursive self-verification gate landed at Bayyinah v2.0.0 and the
  first calibration corrective at v2.0.1. The session-pace empirical:
  Bayyinah v1.5.0 through v2.0.1 (seven releases) shipped in **one
  cowork session**. v5's "12 months between major versions" was a
  pre-session estimate calibrated to solo-developer pace.

**Step 3 -- Ar-Rahman ar-Rahim.** MDL discipline: this revision keeps
everything from v5 that holds and revises only what substrate has
disproved. The seven-principle taxonomy is preserved verbatim; the
Cow Episode anti-pattern guard is preserved; the falsification
criteria per version are preserved with timeline windows recalibrated.
What changes is small: floor anchor, timeline units, v1.0 signal
definition, and the addition of patent-invariant byte-identity
discipline (the Bayyinah-arc empirical finding).

**Step 4 -- Maliki Yawm ad-Din.** Time horizon -- recalibrated.
v5 stated 5-6 calendar years; the new unit is **cowork sessions**,
not calendar months. One cowork session in the Bayyinah pattern
shipped seven releases v1.5.0 -> v2.0.1. The new estimate, deflated
by user's "agent estimates are 75% inflated" discipline: v0.13.x
through v2.0.1 commercialization tier in **~7-10 cowork sessions**.
Calendar-time depends entirely on session cadence; not the binding
unit.

**Step 5 -- Iyyaka Na'budu.** Orientation check at the strategy
boundary: am I writing the strategy as if I am bound by the original
v5 timeline (which would be performance), or am I writing it as if
bound by what the substrate just demonstrated about session-pace
shipping (which is substrate-honest)? The substrate just produced
seven Bayyinah releases in a session; the strategy must reflect that
or it ships a false claim about its own pacing.

**Step 6 -- Ihdina as-Sirat al-Mustaqim.** Sequence: revise the
floor, revise the timeline, redefine v1.0's signal, add patent-
invariant byte-identity discipline. Do not touch the seven-principle
mapping; do not touch the Fatiha Construct protocol; do not touch
the falsification criteria's spirit.

**Step 7 -- Sirat Alladhina An'amta 'Alayhim.** What worked
empirically (per Bayyinah commercialization arc): cumulative-bundle
patches from a pristine floor, push-clone delta extraction, patent-
invariant byte-identity check as a release gate, three-line substrate
probes per release, documented flake protocol, multi-locus sync
verification. What failed empirically: calendar-time horizons that
do not account for session-pace shipping; commercialization-signal
definitions that require external author groups instead of own-source
recursive self-application.

Begin.

## 1. The strategy in compressed form (revised)

Six release tags, each governed by one of the v5 strategy's principles
(taxonomy unchanged), shipped in cowork-session pace. Two cross-cutting
principles (root architecture, disease model) operate at every layer.

| Tag | Principle | Load-bearing feature | Bayyinah analogue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **v0.13.0** | Principle 1 (Bismillah/initialization) -- declared scope | Contract-floor: `_CHECKER_REGISTRY` freeze + `tests/contracts/` directory + KNOWN_LIMITS.md + requirements-dev sync test + the v5 strategy's `.ax-sh.yaml` manifest schema | v1.5.0 muwazana_score + scan_incomplete_clamp contract floor |
| **v0.14.0** | Principle 2 (Tanzil/phased delivery) -- run-budget controller | Whole-repo lint budget with graceful stop, `lint_incomplete=True` honest reporting, deterministic-truncation ordering. The v5 strategy's "Phase 1-4 disclosure UI" arrives in a later release; v0.14.0 ships the budget primitive first (Cow Episode discipline: do not specify Phase-1-4 UI in the v0.14.0 manifest schema). | v1.6.0 budget controller |
| **v0.15.0** | Principle 3 (Ring composition) -- cross-substrate correlation policy | When the same logical surface exists in Python live + Rust gate11 + Go gate11 + ONNX gate11 and the substrates disagree, the published policy resolves which wins, when both fire, and when both are silenced. This is ring-composition at the **substrate layer**, not yet at the v5-strategy ledger layer. The audit-ledger work from v5's v3.0 lands later as v0.18.0+. | v1.7.0 cross-modal correlation policy |
| **v0.16.0** | Principle 5 (Zahir/Batin) -- differential testing matrix | Each Python checker cross-checked against an independent reference (D24 vs. ruff RET503; D11 vs. mypy strict; R3 vs. pylint R1710; additive vs. semgrep; gate11 Python vs. sigstore CLI). Cross-substrate: tree-sitter vs. cargo-check vs. go-vet on the same fixture corpus. Disagreement is a test failure. | v1.8.0 differential testing matrix |
| **v0.17.0** | Principle 4 (root architecture, surfaced) -- framework-free principles doc | `docs/principles.md` -- five engineering principles in vocabulary that holds without Furqan, Bayyinah Audit Framework, Munafiq Protocol, or Quranic anchors. README stays framework-anchored; principles.md is the parallel entry-point for security review, regulated-industry compliance, academic citation. | v1.9.0 framework-free principles |
| **v1.0.0** | Principle 6 (al-Fatiha/recursive self-verification) -- the commercialization signal | furqan-lint runs ALL its checkers against ITS OWN source tree on every CI run. Zero diagnostics required for any release in the commercialization tier. `_PENDING_CALIBRATION_FILES` pending-discipline forces promotion when a file starts scanning clean. **This is the al-Fatiha principle, but at the own-source-recursive layer (Bayyinah-arc empirical), not at the multi-implementation reference-parity layer (v5 original).** | v2.0.0 recursive self-verification gate |
| **v1.0.1** | (post-commercialization first corrective) | Whatever the v1.0.0 gate catches first. Round-12-style calibration corrective; substrate-conservative. | v2.0.1 file-router calibration corrective |

The v5 strategy's v3.0 (audit ledger / cross-PR ring composition), v4.0
(multi-observer / projection consistency expansion), and v5.0 (multi-
implementation reference parity / Chapter 21 falsification tools as
runnable) are deferred to **post-v1.0.1** and do not need to be
specified now per the Cow Episode discipline. Their principle slots
remain claimed -- the principle-to-version map below extends.

Post-commercialization extension (Cow Episode permitting):

- **v1.1.x range** -- v5 strategy's v2.0 phased-disclosure suggestion
  engine (Phase 1-4 UI).
- **v1.2.x range** -- v5 strategy's v3.0 audit ledger / cross-PR
  coherence.
- **v1.3.x range** -- v5 strategy's v4.0 multi-observer / projection
  consistency.
- **v2.0** of furqan-lint (the SDK, not this strategy doc) -- v5's
  v5.0 reference-parity, **gated on whether independent
  reimplementations actually materialize by then**. The Bayyinah
  arc demonstrated that the commercialization signal does NOT require
  external reimplementations -- it requires own-source recursive
  self-verification, which v1.0.0 already delivers.

Cross-cutting principles operating at every layer (carried verbatim
from v5 strategy §7):

- **Principle 4: Lossless Compression Through Root Architecture.**
  The framework's vocabulary (zahir, batin, muwazana, bayyinah, mizan,
  tanzil, bismillah, fatiha) is the root system. Each technical term
  carries its full operational meaning through its root. Naming
  discipline maintained across all versions in a NAMING.md analog.
- **Principle 7: The Disease Model as Debugging Philosophy.** Every
  version treats failing modules as diseased components requiring
  diagnosis-treatment-verification, not betraying agents requiring
  rewrite-from-scratch.

## 2. Bayyinah-arc empirical discipline added (new in v2.0 of strategy)

The v5 strategy specified principles and falsification criteria but
did not specify a release-gate discipline. The Bayyinah arc shipped
seven releases through five disciplines that v2.0 of this strategy
makes mandatory for every furqan-lint release in the commercialization
tier.

### 2.1 Patent-invariant byte-identity discipline

Four surfaces in furqan-lint MUST stay byte-identical across the
v0.13.0 -> v1.0.1 commercialization arc. Any mutation to any of
these is flagged as a patent-substrate change and routed through
patent-disclosure review separately, not folded into a routine release.

1. **`src/furqan_lint/runner.py`** -- dispatch surface that calls the
   four Python checkers in defined order. Equivalent to Bayyinah's
   `application/scan_service.py`.
2. **`src/furqan_lint/additive.py`** -- the additive-only public-
   surface checker. This is the Python-substrate patent-claim core.
3. **`src/furqan_lint/return_none.py`** + **`src/furqan_lint/zero_return.py`**
   -- the two Python-native checkers that close Phase 1 Gap 1 and
   the D24-R3 ring close.
4. **`src/furqan_lint/gate11/verification.py`** -- the Sigstore-CASM
   Gate 11 verification dispatch (the Route a1-via-args canonical
   dispatch consolidated in v0.12.0 F22).

Release gate: `diff -q` against the previous release's byte-image
of each surface returns empty. Empty or release is held.

### 2.2 Three-line substrate probe (mandatory every release)

Bayyinah's analogue:
```python
bayyinah.__version__ == pyproject_version
len(MECHANISM_REGISTRY) == 159
TIER['tounicode_anomaly'] == 2
```

furqan-lint substrate probe (to be frozen at v0.13.0):
```python
furqan_lint.__version__ == pyproject_version
furqan_lint.__all__ == ("__version__",)               # additive-only floor
len(_CHECKER_REGISTRY) == N_BASELINE                  # freeze N at v0.13.0
GATE11_LANGUAGE_DISPATCH == ("python", "rust", "go", "onnx")
```

The `_CHECKER_REGISTRY` does not exist yet. Creating it is the first
v0.13.0 task: freeze a `_CHECKER_REGISTRY: tuple[CheckerDescriptor, ...]`
in `src/furqan_lint/_registry.py` whose ordering and shape become the
patent-invariant claim surface. Every subsequent contract test pins
against the registry.

### 2.3 Multi-locus sync map (mandatory enforcement)

The Bayyinah arc caught multi-locus sync gaps in v1.3.0, v1.4.0, and
v1.8.0 -- a recurring pattern that justifies enforced sync tests.

| Surface | Mirror obligation | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pyproject.toml [project] version` | `src/furqan_lint/__init__.py:__version__` | Already enforced by `tests/test_version_sync.py` |
| `pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] *` | `requirements-dev.txt` | **NEW in v0.13.0:** add `tests/test_requirements_dev_sync.py` |
| CHANGELOG-claimed `### Added` paths | Actual file existence | **NEW in v0.13.0:** add a structural test that walks `### Added` lines and asserts each cited path exists |
| Gate11 language tuple | Three sites: `Manifest.from_dict` (manifest_schema.py:186), `Verifier.step2_3_check_version_and_language` (verification.py:157), F22 dispatch tuple | **NEW in v0.13.0:** add a fourth invariant check that all three are identical |
| `_CHECKER_REGISTRY` count | The substrate probe | **NEW in v0.13.0:** part of the substrate probe |

### 2.4 Documented flake protocol

Bayyinah's documented flake: `test_corpus_round_trip_byte_stable_on_pdftex_fixtures`
(pdfTeX timestamp embedding; passes pristine, drifts on clone). Every
furqan-lint release MUST document its known flakes in `KNOWN_LIMITS.md`
with explicit retry protocol. Candidates pre-v0.13.0:

1. Sigstore TUF root fetching (network).
2. tree-sitter language pack version drift (Rust, Go).
3. ONNX runtime vs. numpy reference (the
   `tests/test_onnx_numpy_reference.py` collection failure that
   surfaced in my v0.12.0 probe is a numpy-presence issue, not
   strictly a flake -- but the divergence-test class under
   `src/furqan_lint/onnx_adapter/numpy_divergence.py` is the
   v0.13.0 ONNX-gate flake locus).
4. `go vet` exit code drift across Go toolchain minor versions.

Each gets a one-paragraph entry in KNOWN_LIMITS.md (a doc this repo
does not yet have; create at v0.13.0).

### 2.5 Cumulative-bundle patch discipline + push-clone delta

This is the operational discipline that made the Bayyinah arc
session-paceable. Every cowork-authored patch in the commercialization
arc:

1. Applies cleanly against a **pristine floor** (`v0.12.0+5 c5c3c4c`).
2. Author the cumulative patch from the pristine floor, not from
   current HEAD.
3. On the agent side: apply patch to pristine, diff against fresh
   clone of current main, push the delta (not the cumulative).
4. Patent-invariant byte-identity check runs on the four surfaces
   before push.
5. Substrate probe runs before push.
6. Full pytest runs before push; documented flakes retried per
   protocol.

Failure to follow this discipline (e.g. authoring the patch from
current HEAD) breaks the pristine-floor reproducibility and is itself
treated as a release-gate failure.

## 3. Tag-claim question for v0.13.0

The existing `v0.13.0` tag on an unmerged branch ships G11.3 ONNX
Sigstore-CASM. Two options:

- **Option A (preferred).** Merge `v0.13.0-an-naziat-v16` to main,
  then cut **v0.13.1** as the contract-floor release. ONNX work
  carries forward as intended; the commercialization arc starts at
  v0.13.1. This preserves the existing tag's semantic claim
  (an-Naziat / G11.3 ONNX) and adds the contract floor as the first
  patch release on top.
- **Option B.** Orphan the unmerged `v0.13.0`, `v0.14.0`, `v1.0.0`
  branches and re-cut. Higher semver-confusion cost; loses the
  existing tag-claim-to-surah-anchor mapping.

Same question recurs at v0.14.0 (Tasdiq al-Bayan / cross-substrate
verification corpus, also unmerged) and v1.0.0 (al-Basirah / G12.0
self-attestation, also unmerged).

**Strategy v2.0 recommendation:** Option A throughout. Merge each
unmerged branch first; cut the commercialization-arc release as a
patch release on top. This preserves the existing surah anchors and
treats the unmerged branches as already-completed work that just
needs landing rather than as work to be re-done.

This makes the commercialization arc:
- v0.12.x + merge v0.13.0 + cut **v0.13.1** (contract floor)
- v0.13.1 + merge v0.14.0 + cut **v0.14.1** (budget controller)
- v0.14.1 + cut **v0.15.0** (cross-substrate correlation policy)
- v0.15.0 + cut **v0.16.0** (differential testing matrix)
- v0.16.0 + cut **v0.17.0** (framework-free principles)
- v0.17.0 + merge v1.0.0 + compose **v1.0.0 as the commercialization
  signal** -- the al-Basirah self-attestation crypto-anchor + the
  recursive-self-lint structural gate together
- v1.0.0 + cut **v1.0.1** (first calibration corrective)

Seven releases total, mirroring the Bayyinah arc shape exactly.
