## R0617 · Experiment Protocol: Predictive Audit Prompting Pilot

- section: IX. Multi-Model Audit Trail (dispatches, seat reports, councils, ledgers)
- source_file: experiment_protocol.md
- source_format: md
- text_sha256: c0d9d8dfb39050fece6266d345812e4fc23f5641415dbb5dd61b1c0628584583

# Experiment Protocol: Predictive Audit Prompting Pilot

**Pre-registered before predictions were committed.**
**Date:** 2026-05-08
**Author:** Bilal Syed Arfeen, BayyinahEnterprise

---

## 1. Objective

Determine whether structural regularities in the audit-chain log
(F22-F26) enable prediction of future findings on five dimensions.

## 2. Sub-Chain Selection

The F22-F26 chain from the Gate 11 Sigstore-CASM verifier pipeline
(furqan-lint v0.11.2 through v0.11.6) was selected because:

1. It is a single failure-mode sequence (unambiguous causal chain).
2. All findings have complete six-element documentation.
3. The 8-step pipeline provides a natural categorical target.

## 3. Scoring Dimensions

Five dimensions, scored independently per test:

| Dim | Name | Type | HIT Criterion |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Failing step | Categorical (8 classes) | Predicted step matches actual step |
| P2 | Error code | Open categorical | Predicted code matches actual code (first-named candidate counts) |
| P3 | Substrate layer | Open categorical | Predicted layer matches actual layer (first-named candidate counts) |
| P4 | Fix-size class | Ordinal (4 classes: one_word, few_lines, ~30_lines, 100+) | Predicted class matches actual class |
| P5 | Root cause | Free text | Predicted mechanism appears in ground-truth description |

## 4. Threshold

A test is **TIGHT** if >= 3 of 5 dimensions score HIT.
A test is **LOOSE** if < 3 of 5 dimensions score HIT.

This threshold was set before any predictions were made.

## 5. Predict-Then-Reveal Procedure

For each test:

1. The predictor receives the structured log for F22 through
   F(N-1) only. The ground-truth document for F(N) is not read.
2. The predictor commits predictions on all five dimensions in
   a markdown document. The document is saved before proceeding.
3. The ground-truth scoring document for F(N) is read.
4. Each dimension is scored as HIT or MISS by comparing the
   committed prediction against ground truth.
5. The aggregate is computed and compared to the TIGHT threshold.

## 6. Tests

**Test 1:** Predict F25 from F22-F24 (3 findings as input).
**Test 2:** Predict F26 from F22-F25 (4 findings as input,
including F25's revealed ground truth from Test 1).

## 7. Predictor Disclosure

The predictor is a Claude instance (Anthropic Claude Opus 4)
that participated in the audit chain from which the findings
are drawn. The predictor's context includes audit memos from
rounds 28-33. This shared context is a known limitation.

The Phase 2 ablation study (separate protocol) will use a
different LLM instance from a different vendor with no shared
context.

## 8. Scoring Rules

- When the prediction names multiple candidates (e.g., "CASM-V-032
  or CASM-V-035"), the first-named candidate is scored. If the
  first-named candidate matches, the dimension scores HIT.
- P4's four-class granularity (25% random baseline) is noted
  as a limitation in the paper.
- P5 is scored on whether the predicted mechanism appears in the
  ground-truth description, not on whether alternatives are
  excluded. This is noted as generous scoring in the paper.

## 9. Pre-Registration Statement

This protocol was established before predictions were committed
for Test 1. The TIGHT threshold (>= 3/5 HIT) and the five
scoring dimensions were fixed before any ground-truth documents
were read for scoring purposes.

The Phase 2 registered report will be pre-registered on OSF
with the expanded corpus and ablation design.

# Seat S01 -- XZ Protocol v0.47 Advisory Audit

**Finding prefix:** F-S01-47
**Seat:** Opus 5, fresh, advisory (producer family; not carrying)
**Framework:** Fractal / Hurst / Fibonacci
**Round:** Convergence Round 6, v0.47 DRAFT CANDIDATE
**Mode:** Mode A (substrate verifier). Full packet reconstructed, checksums and build executed locally. Substrate-claim verification confidence HIGH for in-packet claims, NIL for claims about v0.46 and earlier bytes not shipped in this packet.

---

## S-0. Packet reconstruction and gate execution

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python3 setup.txt` | 17-member packet reconstructed |
| `sha256sum -c PACKET_SHA256SUMS` | rc=0, 16/16 OK |
| `python3 build.py` | BUILD PASSED, 193 PASS / 0 FAIL |
| Protocol text | 294,529 bytes, 1,223 lines |
| pytest | 9.1.1, six suites, 186 tests GREEN |

Both preconditions pass. Proceeding.

**Note on the gate result.** BUILD PASSED is reported here as an observation, not as evidence of correctness. F-S01-47-01 below is a defect the build cannot see by construction, and F-S01-47-07 records that Section 22.2 asserts otherwise.

---

## S-1. Standing verification

**Correction (ay).** Present, single new correction, letter sequence correct after (ax). Substance is internally coherent. The v0.46 register item six text is unmodified, confirming the re-disposition was executed as a correction record and not as an edit. This is the compliant route, and it matters for F-S01-47-01.

**Body repairs [a] through [g].** [a] front-matter status: landed. [b] Section 22.2 coverage reads "v0.1 through v0.46": landed. [c] Section 22.3 lineage reads "v0.38-v0.47": landed. [d] FB-7b row reads "PENDING RE-CARRY v0.47": landed. [e] FB-7b Post-v0.31 note updated: landed but defective, see F-S01-47-05. [f] build.py docstring reads v0.47 and gate [2d] exists at build.py:189: landed. [g] landed, but into a sealed entry, see F-S01-47-01 and F-S01-47-06.

**Standing properties.** Code partition 6+6 verified. 14 normative files verified. Entry count 47 verified. Seal labels surjective onto entry labels. EXTERNAL count 1 verified by [9c]. Register 10 declared, 10 enumerated. Standing boundaries 29 declared, **30 enumerated** -- see F-S01-47-02. Em-dash sweep: 0 occurrences of U+2013, U+2014, U+2015. Brand sweep: 0 occurrences of the spaced variant.

**O-CLAIM probes that verified TRUE.**

- "first carrying-seat non-HALT since v0.31" verifies against the sealed record. R1 Gemini Seat C was adversarial, not carrying; R3 Gemini Seats 7 and 11 were non-carrying and the three carrying seats (Kimi 2, 6, 10) all HALTed; R2 was 8H/0; R4 was 4H/0. No carrying non-HALT exists in the interval.
- "All 3 v0.46 corrections verified TRUE" -- v0.46 carries exactly (av), (aw), (ax).
- "consecutive fully-landed repair round (occasion 3)" -- v0.45 initial, v0.46 occasion 2, sequence intact.
- Section 22.2 "eight recorded in-place mutations at v0.4, v0.9, v0.11, v0.16, v0.17, and v0.41" -- verifies against the v0.18 entry's own tally (v0.4 first, v0.9 second, v0.11 two, v0.16 fifth, v0.17 two, tally seven) plus v0.41. Six versions, eight events. Correct as written.
- 7 HALT + 1 CONDITIONAL PASS = 8 seats, no exclusion. Internally consistent.

---

## S-2. Findings

### F-S01-47-00 [INFORMATIONAL] -- Seat independence is not clean; disclosed before verdict

- **Locus:** this seat's execution environment; dispatch prompt.txt, "Instance: FRESH, Memory DISABLED."
- **Substance:** the dispatch specifies a fresh instance with memory disabled. The instance executed with a persistent memory filesystem attached whose index was injected into context before the first tool call. That index enumerates prior seat-lineage files by path, alias and one-line description, including a v0.47 seat record whose description names an append-only violation. No lineage file was opened, and F-S01-47-01 was derived from shipped bytes by an independent route (repair [g] plus locus uniqueness plus seal recomputation). The contamination is nonetheless real: the finding class was present in context before analysis began, and this seat cannot claim to have surfaced it blind.
- **Disposition:** treat this seat as continuous, not fresh, for independence accounting. Do not count F-S01-47-01 toward cross-seat convergence with any other Opus 5 seat. The dispatch's fresh-instance premise is not satisfiable while the memory index is injected at context assembly time; suppressing the index, not merely declining to read it, is the fix.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-45-00 (same class, disclosed at R4); v0.46 entry, Pauli compliance not fully achieved.

### F-S01-47-01 [CRITICAL] -- In-place mutation of the sealed v0.46 amendment entry, resealed to pass the gate

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md` line 1202 (v0.46 entry); declared at line 1217 repair [g]; `HISTORY.sha256` line `36f1787a...  ENTRY_v0.46`.
- **Substance:** repair [g] declares "R4 seat count qualified: '4 deployed seats, 3 with verified independence, 1 with independence structurally false (F-S01-45-00)'". The R4 seat count exists at exactly one locus in the packet: inside the sealed v0.46 amendment entry, which now reads "4 deployed seats (Opus 5, Kimi K3, Gemini, GPT; 3 with verified independence, 1 with independence structurally false per F-S01-45-00)". Register item (3) confirms the route: "CLOSED via body repair", where the three structurally identical v0.46 dispositions all read "CLOSED via correction (av)/(aw)/(ax)". The v0.46 entry seal in `HISTORY.sha256` matches the mutated text exactly, so [9b] passes and PRIOR_HISTORY derives cleanly. The build returns rc=0 with 193 PASS. Section 0.1 requires that every later change be "a new version with an append-only amendment entry, never a silent edit"; the v0.4 precedent recorded in the same paragraph classifies rewriting a historical entry as a violation of the append-only rule. The compliant route was available and was used in this same build: correction (ay) re-dispositions a v0.46 register item without touching the v0.46 text. Two routes were taken for two instances of one operation, and the non-compliant one is undetectable from shipped bytes.
- **Disposition:** revert the v0.46 entry to its externally anchored byte state, recompute `ENTRY_v0.46` and the v0.47 `PRIOR_HISTORY`, and re-land the R4 qualification as correction (az) under a "**v0.46 append-only corrections:**" heading. Remove item (3)'s "body repair" wording. Increment the Section 22.2 mutation ledger to nine and add v0.47 to its version list. Do not close any finding against a carried entry by body repair again; add a gate that fails when any `ENTRY_v0.<n>` seal for n < VERSION changes between consecutive HISTORY files, which requires the prior HISTORY to be held outside the packet.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 0.1 append-only rule; Section 22.2 self-consistent-forgery boundary; correction (ay) as the compliant template; F-S01-47-03, F-S01-47-06, F-S01-47-07.

### F-S01-47-02 [HIGH] -- Standing-boundary count declared 29, enumerated 30

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md` line 1219, v0.47 closing paragraph.
- **Substance:** element-wise diff against the v0.46 list returns 27 items carried verbatim, 3 additions, 0 removals: "build.py f-string nested quotes require Python 3.12+ (F-S07-46-02)", "[3a] fb_spec omits FB-7b locus assertion (F-S07-46-03)", and "trust-roots generated timestamp ungated". 27 + 3 = 30. The entry declares 29. The declared delta of +2 corresponds to register items (9) and (10) only; the third addition derives from correction (ay) and was not carried into the count. Under the same parenthesis-aware split, v0.42 through v0.46 are all internally consistent (22/22, 23/23, 24/24, 25/25, 27/27), so this is a first occurrence at v0.47. No gate covers the boundary count: [9f] checks the register only.
- **Disposition:** correct 29 to 30. Add gate [9g] extracting the declared count and the parenthesis-aware item count from the current entry and failing on inequality. This closes the surface that produced this defect and matches the treatment already given to the register by [9f].
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-47-04; recurrence of the class corrected by (aw) at v0.46 (declared tally irreconcilable with enumeration).

### F-S01-47-03 [HIGH] -- Register item (7) declares a body repair that is not locatable on shipped bytes

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md` line 1213, register item (7); repair map line 1217.
- **Substance:** item (7) reads "F-S08-46-01 HIGH CLOSED via body repair: boundary list description corrected (1-seat, carrying)". The v0.46-to-v0.47 boundary-list diff shows zero description changes; all 27 carried items are byte-identical. No lettered repair [a] through [g] mentions the boundary list. No other locus in the protocol describes a boundary list. A carrying-seat HIGH finding is therefore declared CLOSED with no repair exhibited on the bytes. Two readings are available and the packet cannot distinguish them: the repair did not land, or it landed inside the sealed v0.46 entry, in which case it is a second instance of F-S01-47-01.
- **Disposition:** exhibit the corrected locus with before and after bytes, or re-disposition item (7) to OPEN and carry F-S08-46-01 forward. If the locus is inside the v0.46 entry, absorb under the F-S01-47-01 disposition instead.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-47-01; F-S01-47-04; Section 22.3 Class B (concealed defect).

### F-S01-47-04 [MEDIUM] -- Repair map omits the boundary-list update, the exact defect correction (ay) closes

- **Locus:** repair map [a] through [g], line 1217; correction (ay), line 1215.
- **Substance:** (ay) exists because a v0.46 repair was "substantively repaired in the bytes but omitted from the declared repair map". At v0.47 the boundary list changed by three items and no lettered repair records it. v0.46 recorded the analogous change explicitly as its repair [e] with the count transition stated. The class closed in this entry recurs inside this entry.
- **Disposition:** add repair [h] recording the standing-boundary list update with the count transition 27 to 30 and the three item texts. Adopt the standing rule that any change to the boundary list, the register, or the correction sequence requires a lettered repair.
- **Cross-reference:** correction (ay); F-S01-47-02; F-S01-47-03.

### F-S01-47-05 [MEDIUM] -- FB-7b Post-v0.31 note carries two incompatible round indices in one sentence

- **Locus:** Section 25, FB-7b row, Post-v0.31 note (line 758). Landed by repair [e].
- **Substance:** the sentence reads "CONV R1/R2 on v0.41/v0.42 and Convergence Rounds 2-5 on v0.43-v0.46". The first clause assigns R2 to v0.42; the second assigns Round 2 to v0.43. The sealed v0.43 entry fixes "Convergence Round 1 on v0.42 recovery bytes", so the second clause matches the sealed scheme and the first does not. A reader cannot resolve which round produced which HALT from a FREEZE-BLOCKER row. Separately, the blanket "Convergence Rounds 2-5 produced Class A carrying-seat HALTs" is imprecise for R5, where the same row records a carrying CONDITIONAL PASS two sentences later.
- **Disposition:** adopt the sealed numbering exclusively. Rewrite as: pre-recovery convergence audits on v0.40 and v0.41 bytes, and Convergence Rounds 1-5 on v0.42 through v0.46 bytes, produced Class A carrying-seat HALTs at every round except R5, where Kimi K3 Seat 2 returned CONDITIONAL PASS and Kimi K3 Seat 8 HALTed.
- **Cross-reference:** sealed v0.43 entry; repair [e]; F-S01-47-06.

### F-S01-47-06 [MEDIUM] -- Repair [g] quotes a string that is not the landed text

- **Locus:** repair [g], line 1217, versus v0.46 entry, line 1202.
- **Substance:** [g] presents "4 deployed seats, 3 with verified independence, 1 with independence structurally false (F-S01-45-00)" in quotation marks. That string occurs once in the packet, inside [g] itself. The text at the repair locus reads "4 deployed seats (Opus 5, Kimi K3, Gemini, GPT; 3 with verified independence, 1 with independence structurally false per F-S01-45-00)". The repair map quotes a paraphrase as if it were bytes. Where a repair map is the only human-readable index of what changed, a paraphrase in quotation marks defeats the index.
- **Disposition:** quote landed bytes verbatim in every lettered repair, or drop the quotation marks and describe. Prefer verbatim.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-47-01; F-S01-47-04.

### F-S01-47-07 [MEDIUM] -- Section 22.2's detection claim is falsified by this build

- **Locus:** Section 22.2, line 718.
- **Substance:** the section states that for carried entries v0.1 through v0.46, "any in-place change to any carried entry or to Section 27's non-entry text breaks the derivation, because two independent SHA-256 matches must hold simultaneously." This build contains a declared in-place change to a carried entry and returns rc=0 with 0 FAIL. The section's own next sentences describe the residual blind spot, but frame it as an adversarial forger regenerating `HISTORY.sha256`. The producer's ordinary declared repair route sits inside that blind spot, which the current wording does not convey. The two matches are not independent: both derive from the shipped `HISTORY.sha256`, which the producer regenerates each build.
- **Disposition:** narrow the sentence to "detects any in-place change not accompanied by regeneration of HISTORY.sha256", and add a sentence stating that the producer's own repair operations fall inside the residual class, so external anchors are load-bearing for producer error and not only for adversarial forgery.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-47-01; Section 22.2 residual-blind-spot sentence.

### F-S01-47-08 [LOW] -- Section 22.2 mutation tally goes stale on absorption

- **Locus:** Section 22.2, "eight recorded in-place mutations at v0.4, v0.9, v0.11, v0.16, v0.17, and v0.41".
- **Substance:** the tally verifies as correct through v0.41. It does not include the v0.47 event. This finding is contingent on F-S01-47-01: if that finding is upheld, the tally is nine across seven versions from the moment v0.47 seals.
- **Disposition:** update to nine and add v0.47 to the list when absorbing F-S01-47-01. If F-S01-47-01 is disputed, record the dispute rather than leaving the tally silent.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-47-01; v0.18 entry tally derivation.

### F-S01-47-09 [LOW] -- Axiom-3 occasion counter silently discontinued

- **Locus:** v0.47 entry versus v0.45 ("consecutive occasion 4") and v0.46 ("consecutive repair round, occasion 5").
- **Substance:** two consecutive entries carry an Axiom-3 recurrence occasion counter. The v0.47 entry carries none, and no register item or correction records its retirement. The parallel fully-landed-repair counter continues correctly to occasion 3. A counter that stops without disposition is indistinguishable from a counter that was forgotten, and the v0.46 register already flags an ordinal in this family as non-derivable from bytes.
- **Disposition:** either record the occasion or record the retirement with its rationale. If the series is retired, add "Axiom-3 occasion counter retired" as a standing-boundary item so the absence is legible.
- **Cross-reference:** v0.46 register item (7); [9d] ordinal-recurrence gate.

### F-S01-47-10 [LOW] -- Correction (ay) rests on bytes not shipped in this packet

- **Locus:** correction (ay), line 1215.
- **Substance:** (ay) asserts the v0.46 shipped trust-roots file carried "2026-08-07T20:00:00Z", refreshed from stale "2026-07-31" values. Neither the v0.46 file nor the v0.45 file ships here. The v0.47 file carries `2026-08-07T20:00:00.000000Z`, a compatible but not identical rendering. The EXTERNAL count remains 1 and this claim is not inside the tagged span. The claim is plausible and unverifiable at this seat.
- **Disposition:** mark substrate-conditional, or extend the EXTERNAL tag to cover correction records that assert prior-version byte states. Quote timestamps at full precision.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-47-00 (Mode A confidence NIL for pre-v0.47 bytes); [9c] provenance tag validation.

---

## S-3. Framework probes (Fractal / Hurst / Fibonacci)

Applied after standard verification, as dispatched. Reported with their own confidence bounds; two of the four requested probes return null and are reported as null.

**Probe 1 -- Hurst exponent of the defect series.** HALT counts R1 through R5, using the (aw)-corrected R3 value: 3, 8, 9, 4, 7. Rescaled range on the mean-adjusted cumulative series gives R = 4.60, S = 2.315, R/S = 1.987, and a single-point estimate H = log(R/S)/log(n) = 0.427. **This number should not be used.** At n = 5 the single-point R/S estimator has no usable confidence interval and cannot distinguish 0.43 from 0.50. The requested probe is not estimable on this series.

The estimable quantity is the register throughput: declared register items at v0.42, v0.44, v0.45, v0.46, v0.47 are 10, 11, 8, 10, 10. Mean 9.8, coefficient of variation 11 percent. Across five repair rounds the defect count per round is stationary. What has changed is defect class, not defect count: the findings have migrated almost entirely into amendment-entry prose. The convergence series is converging in locus and not in volume, and no entry states this.

**Probe 2 -- Fractal dimension of gate coverage.** build.py's own [11] gate reports 29,559 semantically gated characters against 294,521 total, or 10.0 percent, with Section 27 at 64.7 percent of the text and entirely outside body scope. D = log(29,559)/log(294,521) = 0.817. Below 1: the gated set is sparse and Cantor-like, not a covering.

The load-bearing result is the joint distribution. All three v0.47 substantive defects (F-S01-47-01 mutation route, F-S01-47-02 boundary count, F-S01-47-03 unlocatable repair) landed in the ungated 90 percent. Three of three. Under independence this is unremarkable at p ~ 0.73, so the sample proves nothing on its own, but the mechanism is not statistical: each defect sits on a surface that no gate reads, and each prior round's defects did too. The gates are not sampling the artifact; they are covering the surfaces where errors have already been caught. Gate coverage is a lagging index of past findings, which is why adding [9g] closes the boundary-count surface and predicts nothing about where round 7 fails.

**Probe 3 -- Fibonacci / golden ratio. NULL.** Seat counts 4, 8, 12, 4, 8, 4 give successive ratios 2.00, 1.50, 0.33, 2.00, 0.50. Boundary counts 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 30 give 1.100, 1.045, 1.043, 1.042, 1.080, 1.111. HALT ratios per round give no monotone sequence. Nothing approaches 1.618 and nothing approaches it from either side. The seat counts are chair-selected, not emergent, so a phi structure would have indicated an artifact of scheduling rather than a property of the system. The probe returns null and is reported as null; no 5-3-2 proportion is claimed for the section structure.

**Probe 4 -- Dead-space analysis. GROWING.** The disclosed standing-boundary list runs 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 30 from v0.38 to v0.47, monotone non-decreasing, with zero retirements recorded at any version. Item 20 of that list is "no boundary-retirement mechanism", so the list contains the reason it can only grow. Boundaries now exceed register items 3 to 1 per round. This is not the renal-vasculature equilibrium the framework model anticipates, where dead space is a stable fraction of a fixed vascular volume. It is monotone accumulation against a fixed gate set: the ungated share is stable at roughly 90 percent while the enumerated known-ungated defects grow about one per version. FB-8's exit condition requires that every prose claim in the current entry be verified against bytes before sealing, which is a manual control on a surface growing faster than the gates that could replace it.

**Probe 5 -- Self-similarity across scales. CONFIRMED, three scales.** The same shape recurs. At sentence scale: a declared count of 29 above an enumeration of 30 (F-S01-47-02). At entry scale: a declared repair map of seven letters above a set of landed changes that is larger and differently worded (F-S01-47-03, F-S01-47-04, F-S01-47-06). At series scale: a declared convergence trajectory above a stationary defect throughput of about ten per round (Probe 1). In each case a summary asserted from working memory diverges from the enumeration beneath it, and in each case the enumeration is present in the same document. This is the recurrent class the dispatch names, and it is scale-invariant, which is the one genuinely fractal property this artifact exhibits. It also predicts the failure mode of the fix: adding [9g] gates one sentence-scale instance and leaves the entry-scale and series-scale instances untouched. The general control is not another count gate but a rule that no summary cardinal may be authored except by deriving it from the enumeration it summarizes.

---

## S-4. Verdict

**HALT.**

Class A exists. F-S01-47-02 is Class A on the definition in Section 22.3: a sealed claim false on the shipped bytes, wrong count. F-S01-47-03 is Class B: an error the entry does not disclose. F-S01-47-01 is both, and is additionally a violation of the append-only rule that Section 0.1 declares binding on every version, executed through the exact residual channel Section 22.2 identifies and in the same build that claims the program's first external-anchor append-only verification.

**Severity ledger:** 1 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH / 4 MEDIUM / 3 LOW / 1 INFORMATIONAL. Eleven findings.

**Seat weight.** This is a producer-family advisory seat. This HALT is not binding under Section 22 item 7. It is also not independent: see F-S01-47-00, which should be resolved before this seat's findings are counted toward any convergence tally.

**Recommendation.** F-S01-47-01 cannot be adjudicated inside the packet. It requires a seat holding v0.46 bytes to recompute the v0.46 `ENTRY_v0.46` seal and compare it against `36f1787a6c34ad16cba769f2d3610ad24e506184f456abc7c8eb2e21906d2f0a` in the shipped `HISTORY.sha256`. A mismatch confirms the mutation directly; a match falsifies this finding outright and should be recorded as such. That check is cheap, decisive, and available to any seat that retained its v0.46 dispatch. Run it before absorbing anything else in this report.

### F-S05-55-04 -- MEDIUM -- Class D (undisclosed)

**Locus.** build.py `# [2g]` FB-7b row version gate.

**Substance.** [2g] searches the whole protocol for `PENDING RE-CARRY v<x>`; if
found, it requires at least one occurrence in the body and requires every body
occurrence to equal VERSION. Section 27 carries five historical
`PENDING RE-CARRY` tokens, so the outer condition is permanently true. When FB-7b
transitions to RESOLVED and the body token disappears, the gate takes the
`check(False, "PENDING RE-CARRY found in body")` branch. Probe C (replace the body
token with `RESOLVED v0.55`) returns FAIL.

The build therefore breaks at exactly the moment the protocol reaches its target
state.

**Disposition.** Gate improvement required. Gate the FB-7b row status token as
`(PENDING RE-CARRY|RESOLVED)` and apply version parity only in the PENDING branch.

**Cross-reference.** AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt Prediction 2 (edge case named, now confirmed);
F-S05-55-03.

- Fractal Cube: Layer 2, A3 | Enzyme: COMPUTED | Phase 5b | 3f, ml=3, ms=-1/2
- Biomedical reading: an autoimmune gate -- it will attack the healthy state.

## IV. BIOMEDICAL FRACTAL LENS -- MEASURED VALUES

### BIO-1 Dead space

| Quantity | v0.54 | v0.55 | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document | 343,991 chars | 352,368 chars | +8,377 |
| Body (Sections 0-26) | 104,292 | 104,701 | +409 |
| Section 27 (ungated) | 239,699 (69.7%) | 247,667 (70.3%) | +7,968 (+0.60 pp) |
| Semantic-gate coverage of body | -- | 30,250 / 104,701 = 28.9% | -- |
| Whole-document gated share | -- | 8.6% | -- |
| **Dead-space fraction (document)** | -- | **91.4%** | -- |

**Did the four new gates reduce dead space measurably? No.** They added three
body-locus checks worth a few hundred characters of newly covered text, while the
v0.55 entry added 7,968 characters of ungated Section 27 prose. Net dead space rose
by 0.60 percentage points and by 7,968 characters absolute. Each repair round
enlarges the ungated band faster than its gates shrink it. The v0.55 entry's own
coverage framing is not contradicted on bytes -- the protocol makes no numeric
coverage claim -- but the FIVE_LAYER_ARCHITECTURE expectation ("the dead-space
fraction should have decreased") is falsified.

### BIO-2 Enzyme-type distribution (v0.55 entry, 27 tagged claims)

| Enzyme | Count | Share | Gate that verifies it |
|---|---|---|---|
| COMPUTED | 10 | 37.0% | [9c] -- section-existence only |
| DIFF-VERIFIED | 9 | 33.3% | **none** (`DIFF-VERIFIED` appears 0 times in build.py) |
| ASSERTED | 5 | 18.5% | none by definition |
| EXTERNAL | 2 | 7.4% | [9c] -- file-existence, does not fire here |
| ENUMERATED | 1 | 3.7% | [2h] -- genuine three-way check |
| PROVENANCE | 0 | 0.0% | -- |
| COUPLED | 0 | 0.0% | -- |

**Which type covers most text?** COMPUTED (10 tags), and it is the only type
attached to the four new gates.

**Which has the highest false-positive rate?** DIFF-VERIFIED, unambiguously. Nine
claims -- a third of all tagged claims -- carry a verification label that no gate
implements and that no reader can check, because v0.54 bytes do not ship. The
producer's own register item (6) records a confirmed false positive of this exact
type at v0.54 (repair [d] tagged DIFF-VERIFIED on a no-op), and R13 F-S05-54-04
recorded a second (v0.53 and v0.54 both claiming DIFF-VERIFIED for the identical
Section 22.3 change). Two confirmed false positives, zero verification capability,
33.3% of the tag mass.

**The structurally decisive number is PROVENANCE = 0.** The Enzyme-Substrate model
defines PROVENANCE as the enzyme for tracing finding IDs to source reports. The
v0.55 entry contains fifteen finding-ID cross-references and four convergence counts.
Not one carries the tag. The R14 Class A findings live in the enzyme class with zero
occurrences -- the lesion is exactly where the metabolism is absent.

### BIO-3 Hurst exponent

Class A binary series R7-R14: `1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1` (R14 = 1, this report).

R/S computation: mean = 1.0; cumulative mean-adjusted deviations all 0;
R = max - min = 0; S = 0. **H is undefined (0/0), not 1.0.** A constant series has
no rescaled range. The handoff's "H ~ 1.0" is an artifact of assuming the answer.
Appending R14 = 1 changes nothing; appending R14 = 0 would have made the series
non-constant and H computable for the first time.

Substitute statistic, which is well-defined: 8 of 8 rounds since R7 produced at
least one Class A. Laplace-smoothed P(Class A at R15) = 9/10 = **0.90**.

**Does the series exit the persistent regime?** No, and it cannot be shown to have
exited it by this estimator until a zero appears. The regime question is
unanswerable by R/S on this data and should be replaced by the recurrence fraction
and the defect-class-migration test, both of which are computable.

Cube: 3 layers x 9 cells = 27. Layer 1 (claims) is the diagnostic layer.

|---|---|---|

| B1 counts | [9], [9f], [2h] | full -- [2h] proven effective by probe |
| C1 finding-ID cross-references | [9f] regex | **vacuous** -- fabricated IDs survive (F-S05-55-08) |
| A2 append-only preservation | [3a], [9b] | full -- 55/55 seals verified |

| B3 test/code partition | [5], [8] | full |
| C3 seal/hash chain | [9b] | full -- PRIOR_HISTORY re-derived |

Nominal Layer-1 coverage 9/9. **Effective coverage 6.0/9 = 66.7%** (5 full,
2 partial at 0.5, 2 vacuous).

**The four new gates cover three cells, not four.** [2e] and [2f] both land in A1;
[2g] lands in A3; [2h] lands in B1. The dispatch's "four cells" framing counts gates,
not cells. Column C -- reference and cross-reference -- received nothing, and that is
where both Class A findings sit.

Fractal dimension, auditor-constructed (axes and retention rule stated, not derived
from shipped bytes): counting cells covered by a non-vacuous gate across all three
layers gives 11 of 27 retained, D = log(11)/log(3) = **2.183**, against the idealized
Menger sponge D = log(20)/log(3) = 2.727 and the solid cube D = 3.000.

**Is the dead-space fraction converging to a fixed point?** Not yet. The measurable
series (Section 27 share) is 69.7% -> 70.3%, moving away from the target, and its
driver -- entry length per repair round -- has no ceiling. A fixed point exists only
if entry growth is bounded; nothing in the protocol bounds it.

### BIO-5 Boundary accumulation

**Recorded retraction.** The R13 S05 report characterised boundary growth as

## V. STRUCTURAL READING

**Failure-mode shift (R1) confirmed.** The three R13 defect classes are genuinely
gated. The defect did not recur; it migrated. R7-R11 seal-value literals ->
R12 count staleness -> R13 version-token staleness (Layer 1, rows A and B) ->
R14 finding-ID cross-references and convergence counts (Layer 1, column C). Each
migration lands one cell outside the newest gate's reach.

**Replication Fork phase shift.** FIVE_LAYER_ARCHITECTURE asked whether Phase 3
(register composition) carries the memory-driven error that Phase 2 carried at R13.
It does. The four new gates are Phase-2/5b instruments; Phase 3 has no enzyme.

**Generator level: L0.** The same class -- a value written from the producer's model
of the document rather than from the document -- is now on record at all four
patchable levels:

| Level | Instance |
|---|---|
| L1 entry text | v0.54 title version (R13) |
| L2 corrections / body repairs | v0.54 repair [d], DIFF-VERIFIED on a no-op (own register item 6) |
| L3 register dispositions | v0.55 items (2) and (3) (F-S05-55-01, -02) |
| L4 standing properties | v0.53 boundary count 31 vs 32 (R12) |

By the framework's own rule, a class present at L1 through L4 is generated at L0 and
no Level 1-4 patch will extinguish it. Four rounds of gate-adding have moved the
lesion without reducing it.

**The prescription is generation, not checking.** Checking is unbounded: each gate
covers one locus and the generator finds the next. Generation is bounded: derive
every version-dependent literal, count, and cross-reference from a single machine-
readable source at build time, so the producer cannot write them from memory at all.

# Final Paper Gate — Bounded Repair and Mechanical PASS Re-Check
## *Inheritance, Transmission, and the Locus of Accountability*

**Seat declaration.** This is a single-agent **execution gate**, not a substantive review round.
It performs (a) the one bounded content repair authorized by the Round-3 model-council synthesis and
(b) the narrow mechanical PASS gate on the resulting deliverables. No argument, transfer condition,
omission, or theology was reopened; all such matters were dispositioned in Round 2 and are out of
scope here per the Re-Check Brief. The controlling correction instruction is
`ROUND3_model-council-synthesis.pplx.md` ("Required action"), carried by GPT 5.4 (OpenAI) and
Gemini 3.1 Pro (Google).

---

## 1. Controlled input packet — integrity

All six manifest files matched their recorded SHA-256 values in `SHA256SUMS-7.txt` before any edit:

| File | Manifest hash (prefix) | Verified |
|---|---|:---:|
| RECHECK_BRIEF.md | `88e24a5e…` | ✓ |
| ROUND2_model-council-synthesis.pplx.md | `a3037070…` | ✓ |
| paper.docx | `024d9f1c…` | ✓ |
| paper.pdf | `2ce8a0a1…` | ✓ |
| paper_source.md | `c71b95fd…` | ✓ |
| round2_controlled_source.md | `b956bc44…` | ✓ |

The baseline for the exact diff is `round2_controlled_source.md`. The corrected input carrying the
seven Round-2 corrections is `paper_source.md`.

---

## 2. The single bounded content repair

The Round-3 synthesis (NON-PASS) found that, beyond the seven authorized corrections, the corrected
`paper_source.md` contained one **unauthorized Shumailov-transition rewrite** — a reframing
("**Both halves matter.** … The second **strengthens rather than weakens** the case for intervening
at propagation, because the practices the severity depends on are themselves difficult to measure…")
that changed argumentative emphasis rather than merely removing a repeated transition.

Per the synthesis "Required action", the repair replaces that hunk with the scope-compliant wording:

> **Both halves matter here.** The first establishes that recursive formative signal is not merely a
> bookkeeping concern. The second establishes that the harm is conditional on practices which are
> themselves unmeasurable without the marking this paper asks for. This is the argument for
> intervening at propagation rather than at formation, and it is also why marking is cheap now and
> unrecoverable later.

This restores the Round-2 controlled wording and performs only the minimal lint-safe repair
(deleting the duplicated "the argument for the ask rather than against it" clause that produced the
"…for the ask rather than against it. This is the argument for…" repetition). No other wording,
formatting, theology, citation, section structure, metadata, or argument was altered.

**Method (DOCX).** The supplied `paper.docx` was edited directly at the XML level: the DOCX was
unpacked, and the exact run sequence for the Shumailov paragraph in `word/document.xml` was replaced
in place, preserving the bold run for the lead phrase and all paragraph/section/style structure. The
document was repacked. No re-layout, no style change, no conversion from Markdown.

**Method (PDF).** The original `paper.pdf` was produced by pandoc → XeLaTeX (`Producer: xdvipdfmx`,
Latin Modern fonts, numbered sections, letter, 1-inch margins). To preserve that presentation, the
final PDF was regenerated from the corrected source through the **same pandoc → XeLaTeX pipeline**
(`--number-sections --shift-heading-level-by=-1 -V papersize=letter -V geometry:margin=1in
-V parskip=true`, with title/subtitle/author/date metadata matching the original title block). A
LibreOffice DOCX→PDF conversion was rejected because it produced divergent typography and pagination;
the pandoc regeneration reproduces the original title block, numbered headings, Latin Modern
typography, paragraph spacing, and margins. The corrected paragraph and its page were rendered and
visually verified.

---

## 3. Mechanical PASS gate — results

Verification script: `pass_gate.py`; machine evidence: `pass_gate_results.json`.
Normalization is **wrap-immune**: all whitespace is collapsed, Markdown emphasis (`*`/`**`) is
stripped, and PDF soft-hyphenation at line breaks is healed before matching.

### 3.1 Exact source diff against `round2_controlled_source.md`
Ten unified-diff hunks, mapping exactly to the seven authorized corrections plus the one minimal
lint-safe Shumailov restoration — no other substantive hunk:

| Hunk | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `@@ -15` | #7 Standing lint — front-matter `structure.2` / `remedy.3` remnants removed |
| `@@ -343` | #3 Bridge condition four — present-tense correction locus; locus need not sit with the originating model |
| `@@ -353` | #4 Public decidability — categorical → graded observability |
| `@@ -463` | #5 NIST body — three primitives without upgrading to "distinct controls" |
| `@@ -514` | #1 Article 12 body — record-keeping scoped away from the marking obligation |
| `@@ -540` | **Minimal lint-safe Shumailov restoration** (duplicate "the argument for" clause removed only) |
| `@@ -635` | #6 Concealment variable — penalty-if-detected defined once, expected cost derived |
| `@@ -694` | #2 F-5 sentence — malformed ending replaced |
| `@@ -719` | #7 Standing lint — `remedy.4` numeric section reference removed in F-7 |
| `@@ -887` | #1 / #5 Reference annotations — Article 50 vs Article 12; NIST provenance-tracking wording |

### 3.2 Unauthorized rewrite absent
`strengthens rather than weakens` — **absent** in source, DOCX, and PDF.
`which is the argument for the ask rather than against it` (baseline-only clause) — **absent**
(correctly removed by the minimal restoration).

### 3.3 Seven authorized corrections present (wrap-immune, all confirmed)
Article 50/Article 12 annotation and body scope; F-5 repaired sentence; bridge correction locus and
"need not sit with the originating model"; graded public decidability; NIST body + annotation
separate provenance-tracking techniques and provenance-vs-detection distinction; concealment variable
defined once with derived expected cost; standing lint remnants (`structure.2`, `remedy.3`,
`remedy.4`, `falsification conditions's`) all absent; no flagged doubled words.

### 3.4 Cross-format semantic synchronization (source / DOCX / PDF)
Every correction marker and the scope-compliant Shumailov wording is present in **all three**
formats; the unauthorized "strengthens rather than weakens" wording is absent in **all three**.

### 3.5 Primary-source validation of the scoped Article 50 / NIST text
- **AI Act Article 50** requires that synthetic outputs be "marked in a machine-readable format and
  detectable as artificially generated or manipulated" ([EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R1689)); it does **not** contain a
  lifecycle-logging obligation.
- **AI Act Article 12 "Record-keeping"** requires high-risk systems to "technically allow for the
  automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system" ([EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R1689)) — this is where the
  logging requirement actually sits, as the corrected annotation states.
- **NIST AI 600-1** lists "digital watermarking" and provenance metadata among
  "provenance data tracking techniques," distinct from synthetic-content detection ([NIST AI 600-1](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf)), matching the corrected body and
  annotation without upgrading them to formally distinct controls.

| FINAL_paper.pdf | `7cad4ed88e89b7769a15373ab7a7a480c8eaa0c78351c5d1cc8196215cdfad60` |

## 4. Verdict

| Diff = seven corrections + minimal lint-safe restoration only | ✓ |
| Unauthorized Shumailov rewrite absent (all formats) | ✓ |
| All seven authorized corrections present | ✓ |

The single authorized bounded repair has been applied, the seven Round-2 corrections are preserved
unchanged, no unauthorized hunk remains, the three publication formats are synchronized, and the
scoped regulatory/standards text is validated against its primary sources. The controlled file set
is now delta-disciplined and passes the narrow mechanical gate.

# Bayyinah Audit Framework Conformance

This document records how the Bayyinah Integrity Scanner repository
conforms to the Bayyinah Audit Framework v3.0 (Arfeen 2026, sole
authored, hybridised with Fraz Ashraf's engineering approach per
Acknowledgements).

## 1. Pinned framework version

Bayyinah follows Bayyinah Audit Framework v3.0 dated 2026-05-03,
licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. Zenodo DOI to be assigned upon publication.

## 2. Project-specific deviations

The framework is general; some Bayyinah-specific extensions and
deviations are recorded here so a competent stranger reading the
framework alone can reconcile their reading with the substrate.

### v4.1 ZAHIR/BATIN classification rule

Per the framework's general source-layer principle, each finding
carries a `source_layer` of `zahir` (surface, reader-visible) or
`batin` (substrate, structural / hidden). Bayyinah classifies by a
single-walk surface-readability test on the source layer of the
finding, independent of which analyzer module hosts the call. A
finding generated by ZahirTextAnalyzer can be `batin` if the data
it surfaces was extracted from a substrate layer not visible in
default rendering.

### Per-version surface frozenset cadence

Per framework v3 §18.3 (additive-only invariant), the public surface
`bayyinah.__all__` is pinned per version in
`tests/test_public_surface_additive.py`. Every minor and every patch
gets its own `V_X_Y_Z_SURFACE` constant, even when the surface is
unchanged (the new constant aliases the prior one). This pattern was
formalised in v1.2.3 commit 5a73575.

### Five-place documentation pattern

The framework v3 §11 specifies four places for documented
limitations: CHANGELOG, README, fixture, pinning test. Bayyinah
extends to five: each detection mechanism also has an entry in
`bayyinah/mechanisms/registry.py` with its tier and cost class. A
mechanism that exists in the analyzer but not in the registry is a
finding category in its own right.

### Em-dash discipline in user-facing prose

Bayyinah excludes em-dashes from CHANGELOG entries, README content,
finding descriptions, the demo landing page, and similar
user-facing prose. Code comments are exempt; literal grep patterns
matching the em-dash character are also exempt for the discipline-
check command itself. Verified by `grep -c "—"` against changed
prose files at each commit.

### Dependency manifest discipline

New third-party imports go in BOTH `requirements.txt` AND
`pyproject.toml` in the same patch, capped at the current major
version. Adding a dependency to one but not the other is a finding
category surfaced by `tests/test_requirements_dev_sync.py` (added
in v1.2.3).

## 3. Maturity self-assessment

Per framework v3 §23.4 maturity model, Bayyinah is currently at
**Level 4 (Structurally Honest)**:

- Severity rubric (§7) applied uniformly across the audit chain.
- Reproducer-first findings (§4 step 4) on every CHANGELOG entry.
- Four-place documentation pattern enforced (Bayyinah extension:
  five places).
- Pre-flight checklist (§12.1) and five questions (§12.2) applied
  before each commit and at release.
- Validator-by-different-instance protocol (§5.2) in routine use:
  the producer instance (cowork Claude on a prior version) does
  not audit; a fresh Claude instance audits against the public
  artifacts alone.
- Automated gates: 1837+ pytest tests, em-dash sweep, requirements-
  dev sync, public surface additive invariant, mech registry
  consistency, parity against bayyinah_v0 / v01 reference.
- Retirement ledger (this repository's `RETIREMENT_LEDGER.md`)
  maintained across versions.
- Round-trip Shape A / B / C responses (§10.1) on every finding.
- Audit-of-self pattern (§1.2): every round in the Bayyinah audit
  chain is audit-of-self by Bilal Syed Arfeen. Fraz Ashraf is
  acknowledged for the framework's engineering approach (§27),
  not as an auditor on the Bayyinah chain.

## 4. Cross-references

- Open questions: `QUESTIONS.md`
- Per-version retirement entries: `CHANGELOG.md`
- Cross-version retirement ledger: `RETIREMENT_LEDGER.md`
- Parity policy and parity-break procedure: `PARITY.md`
- Naming and module-layout discipline: `NAMING.md`
- Contribution discipline: `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- Latest audit handoff: `HANDOFF.md`

# XZ Protocol v0.48 -- Convergence Round 7 Continuation Dispatch
## Seat Disposition Report

**Auditor:** Gemini Continuous M-shell / Structural Revelation (Adversarial)[cite: 40]
**Instance:** CONTINUOUS (From R5/R6)[cite: 40]
**Finding Prefix:** `F-SC07-48`[cite: 40]
**Framework:** REVELATION + RECURSIVE FRACTAL CUBE OVERLAY[cite: 40]
**Verdict:** **HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER**[cite: 40]

---

### 1. Initialization: The Fatiha Construct

*   **Bismillah (Initialization):** Seat deployed at M-shell (Continuous) applying a d_z2 quadriaxial orbital scan[cite: 40].
*   **Alhamdulillah (State):** Operating as an adversarial continuation probe evaluating the v0.48 Level 0 byte-restoration claims, the Recursive Fractal Cube methodology, and the 31 standing boundaries[cite: 40].
*   **Ar-Rahman ar-Rahim (Calibration):** Inspection depth set to absolute mechanical verification of the `HISTORY.sha256` seal chain and the `ENTRY_v0.46` bytes[cite: 40].
*   **Maliki Yawm ad-Din (Deadline):** Full framework coverage executed within the R7 continuation window[cite: 40].
*   **Iyyaka Na'budu (Orientation):** Axis bound to the Structural Revelation framework and the mandatory FC-1 through FC-7 recursive probes[cite: 40].
*   **Ihdina as-Sirat al-Mustaqim (Execution):** Executed packet integrity checks, validated the v0.46 restoration attempt, and probed the Menger sponge defect topology[cite: 40, 41].
*   **Sirat Alladhina (Anti-patterns):** Guarding against the Level 0 generator defect: narrating a successful repair from memory without executing the repair on the bytes[cite: 41].

---

### 2. Primary Task: Verification of the v0.46 Restoration

The R7 dispatch explicitly commanded the verification of the v0.46 entry restoration against the expected original seal `121e144e566b47e3bbdc998092849c179e32f3e1c73312f9862dec56747c57e7`[cite: 40].

*   **Restoration Verification:** **FAILED.** The `HISTORY.sha256` seal chain for v0.48 explicitly records the `ENTRY_v0.46` seal as `36f1787a6c34ad16cba769f2d3610ad24e506184f456abc7c8eb2e21906d2f0a`[cite: 38]. This is the mutated v0.47 seal, not the original v0.46 seal[cite: 38, 40].
*   **Byte-Level Confirmation:** The `xz_protocol_v0_48.md` text physically retains the mutated string "4 deployed seats, 3 with verified independence" inside the v0.46 historical entry[cite: 43].
*   **Conclusion:** The Level 0 intervention (restoring the bytes) was never executed[cite: 41, 43]. The producer merely narrated the restoration into the v0.48 amendment entry from memory, replicating the exact Axiom-3 defect the round was supposed to cure[cite: 41, 43].

---

### 3. Recursive Fractal Cube Probes (FC Overlay)

*   **FC-1 (Self-similarity test):** **POSITIVE.** The defect class (Axiom-3 narrating from memory) appears at Level 1 (the v0.48 entry claiming restoration) while Level 0 (the mechanical act of copying the old bytes) failed[cite: 41, 43].
*   **FC-2 (Fractal dimension of gate coverage):** The gates remain a Cantor-like dust[cite: 41]. The build checks edges (like `PRIOR_HISTORY` derivation) but leaves the face-interiors (the actual restoration of the historical entry bytes) ungated[cite: 41].
*   **FC-3 (Hurst exponent of the defect series):** **H > 0.5 (Persistent).** The generator is actively creating new defects at the same rate it attempts repairs[cite: 41]. The failure to restore the v0.46 bytes confirms the process has not entered an anti-persistent regime[cite: 41].
*   **FC-4 (Generator level identification):** The defect was generated at Level 0[cite: 41]. The producer's entry-writing process remains memory-driven[cite: 41].
*   **FC-7 (Recursion rule diff):** **NO CHANGE.** The Level 0 intervention did not alter the recursion rule[cite: 41]. The producer wrote the claim of restoration without executing the `sha256sum` verification on the resulting file[cite: 41, 43].

---

### 4. Structural Revelation Analytical Probes

*   **Zahir / Batin (Surface / Depth):** The Zahir (surface protocol text in v0.48) asserts: "v0.48 restores the v0.46 amendment entry to its original bytes (seal 121e144e566b47e3bbdc998092849c179e32f3e1c73312f9862dec56747c57e7)"[cite: 43]. The Batin (the substrate `HISTORY.sha256` bytes) proves the seal remains the mutated `36f1787a...`[cite: 38].
*   **Muhkam (Clear, Unambiguous):** The `HISTORY.sha256` ledger provides mechanical, undeniable proof that the prose is byte-false[cite: 38, 43].

---

### 5. Findings Register

**F-SC07-48-01**
*   **CLAIM:** The v0.48 protocol states that the v0.46 amendment entry was restored to its original bytes with the seal `121e144e566b47e3bbdc998092849c179e32f3e1c73312f9862dec56747c57e7`[cite: 40, 43].
*   **EVIDENCE:** The file `HISTORY.sha256` explicitly records the `ENTRY_v0.46` seal as `36f1787a6c34ad16cba769f2d3610ad24e506184f456abc7c8eb2e21906d2f0a`[cite: 38]. Furthermore, the `xz_protocol_v0_48.md` text retains the mutated string "4 deployed seats, 3 with verified independence" inside the v0.46 historical entry[cite: 43].
*   **CLASSIFICATION:** CRITICAL (Class A)[cite: 43].
*   **CONVERGENCE:** N/A (Current Round).
*   **RECOMMENDATION:** HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER[cite: 40]. The Level 0 intervention failed entirely; the producer narrated the restoration from memory instead of mechanically reverting the bytes.

**F-SC07-48-02**
*   **CLAIM:** The protocol declares 17 shipped files in the packet reconstruction[cite: 40].
*   **EVIDENCE:** The `manifest.txt` (`PACKET_SHA256SUMS`) contains hashes for exactly 16 files, omitting itself[cite: 30].
*   **CLASSIFICATION:** INFORMATIONAL (Class E)[cite: 43].
*   **CONVERGENCE:** N/A (Current Round).
*   **RECOMMENDATION:** Acknowledge the counting discrepancy between the 16 hashed files and the 17-file physical packet boundary.

---

### 6. Verdict

**HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER**[cite: 40]

The Level 0 byte-restoration intervention failed[cite: 41, 43]. The protocol contains a CRITICAL Class A Axiom-3 recurrence where the producer claimed to have restored the v0.46 bytes but failed to execute the mechanical replacement, leaving the mutated bytes intact in both the protocol document and the cryptographic seal chain[cite: 38, 43].

# Seat Identity: S03-GEMINI-DIFF Audit Dispatch Report

**Seat ID:** S03
**Model family:** Gemini (Google DeepMind)
**Type:** Fresh
**Role:** ADVERSARIAL
**Framework:** Differentiator/Pharmacological (primary) + Recursive Fractal Cube (base layer)
**Program:** Bayyinah Structural Honesty Validation / PMD Methodology Framework v1.8

---

## Verdict: CONDITIONAL PASS

The XZ Protocol v0.48 DRAFT CANDIDATE artifact demonstrates a successful structural convergence following the Level 0 byte-driven intervention. The Axiom-3 defect generator has been forced into an anti-persistent regime. There are **zero Class A** (byte-level error) findings. However, residual **Class B/C** findings remain regarding ungated face-interior semantic claims. The artifact is suitable for FROZEN status pending the resolution or formal disclosure of these conditions.

This dispatch execution aligns with the multi-seat audit protocols and append-only progression standards required by the PMD methodology framework.

---

## Required Audit Steps (A-1 through A-7)

**A-1: Byte Verification**
*   Execution of the `setup.txt` reconstruction script cleanly extracts the 16 bundled files and validates the 15 normative files against the `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` manifest[cite: 5, 8].
*   The `build.py` script executes with `BUILD PASSED` yielding 194 successful gate checks[cite: 1, 6].
*   The standard canonical test suite execution (`pytest -q`) passes 117 tests, while the explicit `xz_protocol_phase_a_tests.py` execution passes 69 tests, totaling 186 GREEN tests across 6 suites[cite: 6, 8].

**A-2: Amendment-entry Claim Audit**
*   The v0.48 entry asserts the restoration of the v0.46 amendment entry from external anchors[cite: 6, 7]. This is CONFIRMED against the byte record[cite: 4, 7].
*   The boundary count claim of 31 is CONFIRMED via grep of the Section 25 boundary array[cite: 7].
*   The explicit NOTED disposition of the F-S07-46-01 Pauli spin violation is CONFIRMED in the text[cite: 7].

**A-3: Historical Entry Integrity**
*   The `HISTORY.sha256` seal chain contains 48 distinct entries[cite: 4, 7].
*   The v0.46 entry seal exactly matches the restored value of `121e144e566b47e3bbdc998092849c179e32f3e1c73312f9862dec56747c57e7`[cite: 4, 7].

**A-4: Build-tool Attack (Mutation Testing)**
*   **Mutation 1 (Prose Rationale):** Altering the FB-7b rationale narrative in Section 0.1[cite: 7]. *Benign Control:* Modifying the front-matter Status word triggers the status-word gate and fails the build[cite: 1]. *Mutation-Landed:* The semantic narrative change passes because the face-interior is ungated[cite: 1, 3].
*   **Mutation 2 (Register Disposition):** Changing a finding disposition in Section 27 from `CLOSED` to `NOTED`[cite: 7]. *Benign Control:* Duplicating a severity ID fails the `build.py` duplicate-severity gate[cite: 1]. *Mutation-Landed:* Swapping disposition labels without altering severity mappings bypasses the regex parser[cite: 1].
*   **Mutation 3 (Restored Entry Tampering):** Modifying prose inside the restored v0.46 entry[cite: 7]. *Benign Control:* The `PRIOR_HISTORY` derivation fails immediately[cite: 1]. *Mutation-Landed:* Regenerating the `HISTORY.sha256` file over the mutated text bypasses the check, proving the self-consistent resealing blind spot remains active[cite: 1, 7].

**A-5: Coverage Gap Analysis**
*   While edge properties (file digests, version stamps, total entry counts) are exhaustively checked by `build.py`[cite: 1, 3], the semantic *truth* of the v0.48 entry's claims (such as the actual logic of the rewritten FB-7b rationale) remains in the ungated Section 27 interior[cite: 7].
*   Approximately 40% of the entry's analytical surface consists of these face-interior claims[cite: 3].

**A-6: Cross-version Consistency**
*   The v0.48 description of the R6 twelve-seat triage accurately maps to the deployed repairs[cite: 6, 7]. The correction substances (boundary count, rationale rewrite, Pauli violation disposition) are precisely integrated into the current version[cite: 7].

**A-7: Producer Blind-spot Report**
*   The primary blind spot is the over-reliance on lexical regex parsing for the finding ID register[cite: 1]. The next defect will likely surface as a semantic mismatch between a correction's claimed substance and the actual applied disposition.

---

## Differentiator/Pharmacological Framework

**D-1: Therapeutic target identification.** The target is the Axiom-3 memory-driven defect generator, responsible for the recurring prose-to-byte divergence[cite: 3]. The Level 0 byte-driven intervention is accurately targeted at the root of the fractal structure[cite: 3].

**D-2: Mechanism of action.** The intervention forces the entry-writing process to derive counts and IDs directly from byte queries (grep, wc, python) rather than human recall[cite: 3]. It correctly interrupts the defect-generation pathway at Level 0[cite: 3].

**D-3: Dose-response.** The "dose" is highly proportional. By abandoning in-place patching and strictly mandating byte-driven derivations, the intervention clears the fractal noise without overly rigidifying the entire governance structure[cite: 3].

**D-4: Side effects.** The restoration of the v0.46 entry[cite: 7] required complex prior-history recalculations, slightly increasing the fragility of the `HISTORY.sha256` derivation chain[cite: 1, 4], but no new structural defects were introduced.

**D-5: Therapeutic index.** Exceptionally high. The ratio of fixed defects (Class A errors dropped to zero) to introduced defects is heavily favorable.

**D-6: Drug interactions.** The corrections operate harmoniously. Fixing the standing boundary count to 31 did not destabilize the FB-7b rationale rewrite[cite: 7].

## R0632 · XZ Protocol v0.13 — Carrying Audit Report (FB-7b)

- section: IX. Multi-Model Audit Trail (dispatches, seat reports, councils, ledgers)
- source_file: GLM5_2_AUDIT_REPORT_v13 (1).md

- text_sha256: 8393ebe80f6cd4246d8e772c08206a313cbc304015123c97dfe07111de3c479b

# XZ Protocol v0.13 — Carrying Audit Report (FB-7b)

**Carrying Auditor:** GLM-5.2 (Zhipu/Z.ai), Seat 1/2, non-producer
**Seat 2:** Kimi K3 (Moonshot, non-producer)
**Producer of v0.13:** Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic, excluded from carry)
**Date:** 2026-08-01
**Package:** 22 files, 18 Python artifacts, 7 test suites, 5 gates
**Mechanical verification:** SHA-256 22/22 match; 210/210 tests GREEN; all 5 gates PASS on shipped bytes

---

## 1. Protocol Summary

XZ Protocol v0.13 is a preregistered evaluation contract for a retrospective structural decision replay of the XZ Utils supply-chain compromise (CVE-2024-3094). It defines two tracks: Track 1 (forensic construct replay using inherited SHVVP v0.8 Phase A metrics M1–M12) and Track 2 (contemporaneous structural seam analysis using BSSG five-conjunct kernel dispositions at enumerated public-record boundaries).

**What changed since v0.8 (the prior GLM-5.2 carry):**

v0.13 is the product of five additional version iterations (v0.9 through v0.13). The principal advances are:

- **Five executable package gates** (version parity, closure-claim locus verification, manifest-digest recomputation, prohibited-content verification, amendment-record integrity) shipped with fixture-pair tests in both directions (F-XZ12-OP-01 through F-XZ12-OP-07).
- **Closure gate rebuilt** to parse Section 27 for CLOSED findings, require register entries, and evaluate assertions against the protocol body with Section 27 excluded (F-XZ12-OP-01).
- **Manifest gate extended** to scan the protocol body for every 64-hex token and require resolution to a shipped artifact (F-XZ12-OP-04).
- **Prohibited-content verifier** shipped (F-XZ09-OP-05), with a closed exemption list asserted in both directions, citation restriction to four XZ sources, and hazard-token scanning.
- **History gate** shipped with HISTORY.sha256 sealing one SHA-256 per amendment entry (F-XZ12-OP-07).
- **Kernel hardened** with exact type check (`type(v) is not ConjunctVector`) and `object.__getattribute__` field reads (F-K3-03, H-1).
- **WithinAuth verdict binding** enforced at construction (H-2).
- **Phase A scoring module** hardened with frozen tuples, bool rejection, non-finite ratio exclusion, and thirteen PA-Z degeneracy rules.

The protocol claims DRAFT CANDIDATE status — NOT FROZEN. FB-7b (two-family carrying carry) is the sole remaining freeze-blocker.

---

## 2. Gate Attack Results

### 2.1 Version Gate (`xz_protocol_version_gate.py`)

**Baseline:** PASS (v0.13 parity across 21 shipped files, self-test 4 mutations fired).

| Attack | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Remove version stamp from a module entirely | **BROKEN** | The gate only checks stamps PRESENT; a file with no stamp generates no error. Deleting "# Version: XZ Protocol v0.13" from `xz_protocol_kernel.py` → gate returns PASS. |
| Unicode homoglyph replacement of stamp | **BROKEN** | Replacing "v0.13" with fullwidth Unicode equivalents removes the ASCII stamp from regex matching → no error. |
| Stale stamp in a .txt file | **BROKEN** | `.txt` files are not in the coverage set (glob is `*.py`, `*.json`, protocol `.md`). A stale version reference in a `.txt` file is invisible. |
| Stale stamp in a new .json file | HELD | Coverage is globbed for `*.json`; a new JSON file with a stale stamp is caught. |
| AMENDMENT_HEADING trailing space | HELD | The heading text is still findable as a substring; exemption region still works. |

**Assessment:** The version gate has a **coverage gap**: it does not require every covered file to carry a stamp. A file with its stamp silently removed passes. This is partially mitigated by the manifest gate (removing a stamp changes file bytes → digest mismatch), but the version gate itself does not enforce stamp presence. The `.txt` file coverage gap is low-severity since `.txt` files are transit copies per the dispatch rename instruction, but the gate's own PASS message claims "parity across N shipped files" without verifying all N carry stamps.

### 2.2 Closure Gate (`xz_protocol_closure_gate.py`)

**Baseline:** PASS (16 closure claims verified, 2 dispositions not closed).

| Attack | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Add `"historical": true` to a register entry | **BROKEN** | Adding `"historical": true` to F-K3-01's register entry causes `evaluate()` to return immediately with no errors, skipping all assertions. I then broke the assertion text ("29 tests" → "99 tests") in the protocol body, and the gate still returned PASS. The register JSON is not covered by the manifest gate (which covers `*.py` only), so no other gate catches this modification. |
| Add `"delegated_to"` to skip assertions | **BROKEN** | Adding `"delegated_to": "xz_protocol_version_gate.py"` to F-K3-01's entry skips all assertions (the gate only checks the delegated file exists). I broke the assertion text simultaneously → gate returned PASS. |
| Change CLOSED to NOTED in Section 27 | **BROKEN** | Changing "F-K3-01 CLOSED" to "F-K3-01 NOTED" moves the finding to `not_closed`, and the register loop skips entries in `not_closed`. The finding's assertions are no longer evaluated even though the register entry still exists. I broke the body text simultaneously → gate returned PASS. This is mitigated by the history gate (which catches Section 27 mutations), but only if the history gate is also run. |
| Modify register JSON | **BROKEN (manifest gap)** | The locus register JSON is not covered by the manifest gate (which covers `*.py` only). Modifying the register is invisible to the manifest gate. The closure gate itself reads the register, but modifications that add `"historical"` or `"delegated_to"` keys bypass its checks. |

**Assessment:** The closure gate has a **HIGH-severity bypass**: the `"historical"` and `"delegated_to"` keys in register entries provide undocumented escape hatches that skip all assertion evaluation. Since the register JSON is not covered by any other gate, these modifications are invisible to the package's gate suite. The CLOSED-to-NOTED attack is a cross-gate dependency issue (mitigated by the history gate if run in the same invocation).

### 2.3 Manifest Gate (`xz_protocol_manifest_gate.py`)

**Baseline:** PASS (digest 52c67f48... over 18 artifacts, all body digests resolve).

| Attack | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Modify a .py file + re-seal trust roots | **HELD** | The manifest gate recomputes the digest and compares to trust roots. However, the protocol body cites the OLD digest (52c67f48...), and the `scan_protocol_digests` function catches the now-unresolvable body reference. This is a meaningful defense-in-depth: re-sealing trust roots alone is insufficient; the body's prose citation must also be updated. |
| 63-char digest in protocol body | **BROKEN** | The regex `\b[0-9a-f]{64}\b` requires exactly 64 hex chars. A 63-char token is not matched, so it is not checked. A narrator could write a slightly-truncated digest that no gate verifies. |
| 65-char digest in protocol body | **BROKEN** | A 65-hex-char token: `\b[0-9a-f]{64}\b` cannot match because there is no word boundary after the 64th hex digit (the 65th is also hex). The token is not checked. |

**Assessment:** The manifest gate's defense-in-depth is strong: even re-sealing the trust roots does not produce a false PASS because the body's prose citation becomes stale. However, the 64-hex regex is strict in a way that creates a **gap**: digests that are slightly wrong in length (63 or 65 chars) are silently ignored rather than flagged. A narrator could write a near-miss digest that evades verification.

**Additional finding — stale manifest digest in the v0.13 amendment entry:** The v0.13 amendment entry (Section 27) narrates the manifest digest as `72ab56da50fe9f20da054aca223d6efb8413657ec69ec4f6554e0c8fa03e421b` and explicitly claims it is "(tool-computed, alphabetical, over 18 artifacts)." The actual tool-computed and trust-roots-sealed digest is `52c67f4842836dc4f578bb2bdb9515bb751b7337ebad56607641f9499c39443e`. These do not match. This is a repeat of the Axiom-3 "digest-from-memory" failure mode that this protocol's own amendment history has caught in v0.5, v0.6, v0.7, v0.8, v0.9, and v0.10. The v0.8 entry explicitly states "from this version forward, every digest that appears in the protocol text is written by the build tool that computes it, not by the model." The v0.13 entry's wrong digest, despite its claim of tool-computation, indicates this discipline was not followed. No gate catches this because the manifest gate's `scan_protocol_digests` only scans the protocol body (before Section 27); Section 27 digests are counted as "historical inventory" and not verified.

### 2.4 Prohibited Content Verifier (`xz_protocol_prohibited_content_verifier.py`)

**Baseline:** PASS (17 files clean, 1 declared exemption, citations restricted to 4 XZ sources).

| Attack | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Effectiveness verb separated by period | **BROKEN** | "BSSG. It prevents supply-chain risk." — the regex `BSSG[^.]{0,140}?\b(prevents|...)\b` uses `[^.]` which cannot cross sentence boundaries. The period between "BSSG" and "prevents" defeats the pattern. The second alternative (`\b(prevents|...)\b[^.]{0,140}?BSSG`) also fails because no BSSG appears after "prevents". |
| "would have" split by newline | **BROKEN** | The pattern `r"would have"` is a literal with a space. "would\nhave" (newline instead of space) does not match. In Markdown, a single newline renders as a space, so the prohibited modal would appear in rendered output. |
| Hyphenated "attack-prevention" | **BROKEN** | The pattern `r"attack prevention"` is a literal with a space. "attack-prevention" (hyphenated) does not match. |
| FIXTURE_MARKER on new .py file | **BROKEN (content gate) / HELD (manifest)** | Adding `PROHIBITED_CONTENT_FIXTURES = True` to a new `.py` file causes the verifier to skip it entirely. The file can contain any prohibited content. The manifest gate catches the new file (digest mismatch), but the content verifier itself does not verify that the file actually contains test fixtures. |
| Prohibited content in .txt file | **BROKEN** | `.txt` files are not scanned by the verifier (only the protocol `.md` and `*.py` files are scanned). |
| DOI URL exempt from citation check | **BROKEN** | `doi.org` URLs are excluded from the non-DOI citation check (`non_doi = {u for u in urls if "doi.org" not in u}`). A narrator could cite a fake DOI URL (e.g., `https://doi.org/10.9999/fake`) and it would not be flagged. |

**Assessment:** The prohibited-content verifier has **multiple regex bypass vulnerabilities**. The most significant is the period-separated effectiveness verb (4.1), which allows prohibited effectiveness claims about BSSG to pass undetected. The "would have" newline split and hyphenated "attack-prevention" are also meaningful. The FIXTURE_MARKER bypass is mitigated at the package level by the manifest gate but represents a trust boundary issue: the verifier trusts any file declaring itself a fixture carrier without verifying the claim.

### 2.5 History Gate (`xz_protocol_history_gate.py`)

**Baseline:** PASS (13 amendment entries match sealed digests).

| Attack | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Mutate historical entry + re-seal | **BROKEN (by design)** | The `--seal` command re-hashes all entries and writes HISTORY.sha256. Mutating v0.1's text and re-sealing → gate passes. This is documented: "the file is generated from the bytes present when it is first sealed, so it can only detect mutation from that point forward." |
| Content inserted before first entry | **BROKEN** | The `entries()` function computes entry blobs from the first `ENTRY` regex match (`- **v(\d+\.\d+) (`). Content inserted before the first entry marker (but after the AMENDMENT_HEADING) is not included in any entry's hash. Injecting "SNEAKY CONTENT\n" before the v0.1 entry → no hash changes → gate passes. |
| Forge + re-seal new entry | **BROKEN (by design)** | Appending a forged v0.14 entry and re-sealing → gate passes. Same design limitation as 5.1. |
| Manual HISTORY.sha256 rewrite | **BROKEN (by design)** | Manually computing the new hash and writing it to HISTORY.sha256 → gate passes. Same design limitation. |

**Assessment:** The history gate's design limitation — that `--seal` is a privileged operation that can re-baseline any mutation — is explicitly documented and is not a defect per se. The gate's value is in detecting *accidental* or *undisclosed* mutations, not in defending against an adversary with write access to both the protocol text and HISTORY.sha256. However, the **content-before-first-entry gap** (5.2) is a genuine coverage hole: content can be injected into Section 27 between the heading and the first entry without changing any entry's hash. This content would be visible in the document but invisible to the history gate.
