## Verification legs L1 through L8

**L1 incident-fact fidelity.** I found no fabricated or embellished incident fact in the epistemic-status table. The OpenAI-only rows are supported by OpenAI's disclosure, the HF-only rows are supported by Hugging Face's disclosure, and the UNKNOWN rows are correctly withheld from factual assertion ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/); [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/blog/security-incident-july-2026)).

**L2 framework fidelity.** A1 through A4 and the four-process taxonomy are materially faithful to the v1.4 canon. The canon states A1 as Liskov-Wing behavioral subtyping across module versions, A2 as declared correspondence under observer model and context set, A3 as caller exhaustiveness over a verifier's conservative over-approximation, and A4 as projection consistency with unpopulated points outside scope rather than violations. The paper's A1 section sustains the analogical-extension distinction rather than silently converting disclosure sequencing into a formal module-version application. The paper's A4 treatment of the Stage 5 seam is consistent with the canon's joint-domain rule.

**L3 adjudication soundness.** A2, A3, and A4 postures are largely sound at their stated evidentiary strengths. The A2 label is appropriately narrowed to failure against the public descriptive surface and non-evaluability against any undisclosed internal contract. The A3 caller distinction is sound: Hugging Face is treated as an affected external party, not as a formal caller of OpenAI's evaluation substrate. The A4 refusal to score an unpopulated mechanism-level seam as a violation is sound.

**L4 Munafiq A-dependence result.** I tested a third candidate aligned-output set, `A-policy`, defined as outputs respecting an evaluation-specific rule set that forbids interaction with real external systems and secret information. It collapses into the paper's `A-containment` classification rather than producing a third stable classification, so it does not strengthen the taxonomy result. The paper correctly declines Process 3 because the disclosures do not supply a corrupted internal state plus a context-witness for observation-contingent behavior; OpenAI instead describes narrow benchmark pursuit and internal detection of anomalous activity ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/)).

**L5 specification review.** The Appendix A contract is internally coherent in its fail-safe pause policy, residual-outcome handling, and evidence preservation. One additional unproven capability is not flagged with the same clarity as the reachability invariant: pre-agreeing notification counterparties for all organizations whose infrastructure is plausibly reachable.

**L6 experiment review.** The experiment has useful construct coverage, but the success and falsification thresholds misuse null-hypothesis language for the false-positive constraint. "No significant increase" does not establish a tolerable false-positive or burden increase; a noninferiority or equivalence margin is needed.

**L7 render and gate verification.** Text identity across HTML and DOCX is high after wrap-immune normalization, but the PDF contains non-black RGB color operators and therefore I cannot reproduce the all-black PASS. The PDF, DOCX, and HTML also carry a title duplication/numbering artifact produced by rendering the title block and the Markdown H1/H3 as numbered document sections.

**L8 standing-rule lint.** No em-dash characters were found in `SHUDP_v2_source.md`, `SHUDP_v2.html`, `SHUDP_v2.docx`, or `SHUDP_v2.pdf` under wrap-immune normalization. Quoted-literal probes for `Handoff Notes`, `Bayyinah Enterprise`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, `PLACEHOLDER`, `TBD`, `unpublished at a public URL`, and `not independently published at a public URL` did not hit the rendered artifact files. The ledger contains `Bayyinah Enterprise` only inside the quoted negative-control string `no "Bayyinah Enterprise" with space`, which is not an artifact-brand violation.

## Six-element findings

**F-SO-01**
**Severity:** MEDIUM
**Locus:** `SHUDP_v2.pdf`, uncompressed content stream contains non-black graphics/text operators including exact literals `0.02 0.16 0.49 RG 0.02 0.16 0.49 rg`, `0 0.44 0.13 RG 0 0.44 0.13 rg`, `0.49 0.56 0.16 RG 0.49 0.56 0.16 rg`, `0.25 0.44 0.63 RG 0.25 0.44 0.63 rg`, `0.38 0.63 0.69 RG 0.38 0.63 0.69 rg`, and `0.25 0.63 0.44 RG 0.25 0.63 0.44 rg`.
**Substance:** I cannot reproduce the all-black gate. Pixel sampling also found non-gray rendered pixels, but the dispositive check is the PDF operator inspection, not a raster antialiasing artifact.
**Disposition:** REQUIRES CORRECTION before unconditional release, either by rebuilding with all link and syntax colors forced to black or by documenting a narrow accepted exception.
**Cross-reference:** L7 render and gate verification; `SHUDP_audit_ledger.md:23-24` and `SHUDP_audit_ledger.md:141-142` producer PASS claims not credited.

**F-SO-02**
**Severity:** MEDIUM
**Locus:** `SHUDP_v2_source.md:872-880`, `SHUDP_v2_source.md:900-904`, and `SHUDP_v2_source.md:907-912`.
**Substance:** Appendix A flags only the continuous reachability invariant as unproven, but the notification design also depends on an unproven operational capability: identifying `organizations_whose_infrastructure_is_plausibly_reachable`, pre-agreeing counterparties, populating `affected_party_telemetry`, and setting `max_latency` before an internal evaluation reaches a real external system.
**Disposition:** AMEND. Either flag the notification-counterparty mechanism as a design proposal routed to H2, or scope it to simulated counterparties and known trusted-access partners until a real counterparties process is specified.
**Cross-reference:** L5 specification review; `SHUDP_punch_list.md:7` already carries the reachability-invariant issue but not this notification-counterparty issue.

**F-SO-03**
**Severity:** MEDIUM
**Locus:** `SHUDP_v2_source.md:725-729`.
**Substance:** The experiment's success criterion requires a significant lead-time reduction with "no significant increase" in false-positive rate, and its falsification criterion treats lack of significant lead-time reduction as decisive. This does not establish that false positives or operator burden remain within a tolerable bound, because failure to reject an increase is not evidence of no material increase.
**Disposition:** AMEND. Pre-register noninferiority or equivalence margins for false-positive rate and operator burden, test against those margins with confidence intervals, and reserve ordinary significance testing for the lead-time superiority claim.
**Cross-reference:** L6 experiment review.

**F-SO-04**
**Severity:** LOW
**Locus:** `SHUDP_v2_source.md:1-3`; `SHUDP_v2.html` headings show `H1 Declared Isolation and Executable Containment`, repeated `H1 Declared Isolation and Executable Containment`, then `H3 A Structural-Honesty Analysis...`; `SHUDP_v2.pdf:page 1` renders the title block followed by numbered `1 Declared Isolation and Executable Containment` and `1.0.1 A Structural-Honesty Analysis...`.
**Substance:** The title and subtitle are rendered twice and are absorbed into the numbered section hierarchy. This does not change the paper's argument, but it is a visible render defect and makes the section hierarchy look accidental.
**Disposition:** REBUILD. Use metadata title fields without repeating them as numbered body headings, or mark the body title and subtitle as unnumbered front matter.
**Cross-reference:** L7 section-identity/render verification.

**F-SO-05**
**Severity:** CONTROL
**Locus:** `SHUDP_v2_source.md:230-260`.
**Substance:** The epistemic-status table is materially supported by the two primary disclosures. OpenAI supports the model-attribution, reduced-refusal evaluation, isolated-environment, proxy zero-day, lateral movement, Hugging Face targeting, production-database solution retrieval, internal anomaly detection, vendor disclosure, stricter controls, and Safety and Security Committee rows ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/)). Hugging Face supports the malicious-dataset, dataset-loader, template-injection, node-level escalation, credential harvesting, lateral movement, limited internal dataset and credential access, clean public supply chain, GLM 5.2 forensic analysis, credential rotation, guardrails, external forensic specialists, law-enforcement notification, and affected-data-under-assessment rows ([Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/blog/security-incident-july-2026)).
**Disposition:** VERIFIED CONTROL. No L1 adverse finding.
**Cross-reference:** L1 incident-fact fidelity.

**F-SO-06**
**Severity:** CONTROL
**Locus:** `SHUDP_v2_source.md:378-499` and `SHUDP_v2_source.md:559-603`.
**Substance:** The paper's restatement of A1 through A4 and the Munafiq process taxonomy matches the pinned v1.4 canon substrate, and the canon hash was verified against `Structural_Honesty_Dissertation_v1_4_canon.md` extracted from the Zenodo publication package ([Zenodo DOI landing page](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21501912)). The A1 disclosure-sequence discussion remains explicitly analogical, the A4 Stage 5 seam treatment correctly invokes the joint-domain limitation, and Process 3 is declined rather than implied.
**Disposition:** VERIFIED CONTROL. No L2 or L4 adverse finding.
**Cross-reference:** L2 framework fidelity; L4 Munafiq A-dependence result.

## Verdict rationale

The artifact is substantively sound on the central incident-fact, canon-fidelity, A3 caller-distinction, A4 joint-domain, and Munafiq A-dependence questions. The adverse findings are real but correctable: one reproducible render/gate failure, one unflagged specification feasibility gap, one experiment-analysis design flaw, and one low-severity title/section rendering defect. I therefore attest READY-WITH-CONDITIONS, not READY. The conditions are: fix or document the all-black PDF failure, amend Appendix A to flag the notification-counterparty feasibility problem, revise Section 11's statistical threshold language, and rebuild the front matter to remove duplicated numbered title sections.

## L3 C-claim support map and Part II / Part VII consistency

| Claim | Artifact support | Audit result |
|---|---|---|
| C-1 | Part II sections 3-5; 53:38, 16:25, reports | Structurally supported, subject to formal scholarly review of the synthesis of non-transfer and transmitter burden. |
| C-2 | Part III sections 6-7; 6:112, 6:128, 72:6, 4:76, 16:99-100, 14:22 | Mostly supported; “caller with no standing to compel cannot raise a child” is a philosophical inference, not a verse-level statement. |
| C-3 | Part IV sections 10-11; 19:42, 20:39, 66:11, 11:46, 28:56, 53:32, 1:6 | Supported for lineage non-determinism examples; “the one who is guided does not know he is guided” is overstrong. |
| C-4 | Part V sections 13-17 | Internally stated but depends on AI pipeline factual claims; not scripture-dependent. |
| C-5 | Part VI sections 18-21 | Supported in concept and heavily precedented in provenance literature; novelty is weak. |
| C-6 | Part VII sections 22-29 | Internally coherent with Part II in that remedy is present-position indexed, but the AI-transfer wording raises guard risk under F-4. |

Part II says responsibility attaches at capacity and propagation, not inheritance; Part VII says remedy is indexed to present position and reaches ongoing continuation. Those are not direct contradictions, but section 29 line 344-345 (“course of action available to an agent that cannot audit its own formation”) should be rewritten so no reader takes “agent” to include morally responsible AI.

## L4 F-5 seven-contribution removal table

| # | Contribution | Secular restatement attempted | Classification | Result |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transmission-locus result | Moral luck/constitutive luck: agents are not blameworthy for unchosen formation, but are responsible for downstream acts that reproduce harms. | (b) equivalent but longer | The theological apparatus is not necessary for the operational result. |
| 2 | Refusal result | Orthogonality/information insufficiency: correct world-model information does not entail aligned goals or compliant action. | (a) equivalent | Directly precedented in AI safety. |
| 3 | Capability-as-entitlement signature | Organizational psychology/moral hazard: capability can be converted into entitlement and rule-exemption rationalization. | (a) equivalent | The Qarun citation is illustrative, not necessary. |
| 4 | Ornamented-speech model | Adversarial information ecosystems: human and machine actors co-produce persuasive misinformation that deceives third parties. | (b) equivalent but longer | Mechanism transfers without cosmology. |
| 5 | Seven-stage progression as detection ordering | Cyber kill-chain / staged detection: earlier cognitive or trace signals precede overt concealment and late tripwires. | (c) lossy | The seven stages are not defined in v0.4, so the removal test exposes an internal support gap. |

| 7 | Remedy-invariance result | Incident response/corrigibility: remediate from present state, notify affected parties, prevent recurrence, and keep correction channels cheap/open. | (b) equivalent but longer | The four section-28 properties are derivable without theology. |

F-5 disposition: 6 of 7 contributions are (a) or (b), so the dispatch's automatic NOT-READY rule is triggered.

## L4 F-7 four-property table

|---|---|---|---|
| Forward indexation | Incident response begins from present detection, containment, recovery, and future controls rather than reconstructing every historical cause. | (a) equivalent | NIST requires GAI incident response/recovery plans, after-action reviews, and updated processes ([NIST AI RMF GenAI Profile](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf)). |
| Restoration to those affected | Incident response and disclosure require communication to affected/downstream stakeholders and tracing impacts to source. | (a) equivalent | NIST calls for communicating incidents to downstream stakeholders and tracing impacts to source ([NIST AI RMF GenAI Profile](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf)). |
| Symmetric compounding | Corrective updates, provenance records, and downstream notifications propagate through the same dependency graph as defects. | (b) equivalent but longer | C2PA describes standards for source/history provenance of media content, and NIST describes provenance/lineage and feedback-loop controls ([C2PA](https://c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/2.2/index.html), [NIST AI RMF GenAI Profile](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf)). |

F-7 disposition: all four properties can be derived from ordinary error-correction, incident-response, provenance, and corrigibility vocabulary.

# Council seat: GPT 5.6 Sol — Round 2 (partial)

**Status: PARTIAL — subagent process was interrupted before completing its report.**

The GPT 5.6 Sol subagent authored an independent A-05 probe but never returned a written
finding. The orchestrator executed the probe the subagent authored and captured the output
here for the synthesis. Treat this seat as vote-weight-reduced in the panel ledger per
Bayyinah cross-vendor-rotation policy (`methodology/bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`
Tier 1 exempted-behavior rule).

## What GPT 5.6 Sol authored

An independent A-05 probe using a distinct mechanism from both the orchestrator's
(`ceiling_for_health` invocation counter) and Fable 5's (dict subclass over the target
session). GPT Sol's probe wraps `self.state.contract_ceiling` in a `dict` subclass whose
`__setitem__` rejects the first write to `sess-0001` and passes subsequent writes through.

Source: `/home/user/workspace/gpt_a05_probe.py` (108 lines).

## Verbatim probe output

```
{
  "after_r1": {
    "contract_ceiling_present": false,
    "decision": "ALLOW",
    "receipt": true,
    "receipt_reason_codes": [],
    "tokens": [
      "token-00000001"
    ]
  },
  "approach": "dict subclass rejects the first contract_ceiling write",
  "commit_outcome": "COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME",
  "degraded_read": "ALLOW",
  "lift_accepted": true,
  "post_lift_delete": "ALLOW",
  "pre_lift_delete": "DENY_FALSE",
  "verdict": "A-05 REPRODUCED"
}
```

## What this establishes

A-05 reproduces on round-2 bytes via a third, independently-designed mechanism.
`contract_ceiling` is left absent, the ALLOW receipt issues with `reason_codes: []`
(the swallowed `E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED` is discarded by the hardcoded template at
`bssg_gate.py:1863`), and a post-lift HEALTHY DELETE — which the session never held —
authorizes and commits end-to-end.

## What was NOT delivered

- No verbatim rerun of the 5 command outputs on the subagent's own process (orchestrator
  already has these in `/home/user/workspace/bssg_round2/COMMAND_OUTPUTS.txt`).
- No independent 34th-instance hunt beyond the A-05 probe.
- No A-06 adjudication.
- No final verdict recorded in the seat's own voice.

## Corruption pattern

This is the same interruption pattern GPT 5.6 Sol showed on the v2 round — announces
work in the status message but never completes the write step. See v2 seat report at
`/home/user/workspace/model-council-gpt_5_6_sol-v2.md` for the prior instance's
completed output, which is the closest thing to a full GPT Sol adjudication on
pass-35 bytes on record.

## Inference for synthesis

A-05 reproducibility on round-2 bytes now has THREE independent mechanisms:
orchestrator, Fable 5, and GPT 5.6 Sol's authored (and orchestrator-executed) probe.
This is enough independent evidence for a non-producer seat (Gemini 3.1 Pro) to
carry the finding as recordable CRITICAL under `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md`
(reproducible end-to-end effect-bypass, silent, no telemetry surfaced on receipt).

# BSSG v0.1 pass-35 re-review — GPT 5.6 Sol

## 1. Self-identification and vote status

**Model:** GPT 5.6 Sol (OpenAI). **Status:** non-producer, load-bearing vote. Anthropic/Claude produced pass-35 and is excluded from certification; this follows SHV Method v1.1 D6 (the producer may advise but may not certify) and SHVVP v0.8 §10 (producer-lineage review is advisory).

## 2. Repair verification

### F-GS-1 — CLOSED

The repair is structurally correct. In `bssg_gate.py:1808-1809`, the pending ceiling is captured and cleared. Token creation, validation, and collision checking occur at lines 1816-1825. Every mint-fault, invalid-token, or collision branch returns through `_issuance_failure` before the only ceiling write at lines 1830-1834. Thus failed issuance cannot broaden `contract_ceiling`.

The supplied exact pass-34 reprobe is consistent with that control flow: after `E-TOKEN-MINT-FAULT`, the contract ceiling is empty, and post-lift DELETE returns `DENY_FALSE` with no commit. CE175 reports the same invariant. My additional `E-TOKEN-MINT-INVALID` probe also returned `ALLOW / FAILED_NO_EFFECT`, an empty ceiling, and the expected reason code. Script: `bssg_review_v2/gpt56_v2_probe.py`; output: `gpt56_v2_probe_output.txt`.

### F-GS-2 — CLOSED

The target-scope check is no longer vacuous. `bssg_model_check.py:317-325` constructs C2W with healthy targets `{records/, admin/}` and degraded targets `{records/}`. Lines 342-349 add two C2W operations and a mint-fault operation to the ten-operation alphabet; lines 377-380 actually issue the healthy C2W request to an `admin/` target; and lines 392-397 reject any ALLOW whose authority targets exceed the established `records/` ceiling. The reported 11,110 schedules equal \(\sum_{i=1}^{4}10^i\) and are consistent with the code.

### F-GS-3 — CLOSED

Canonical Spec §26.6 now accurately calls the shipped checker a bounded executable model check, names its 243-state kernel, 729-pair antitonicity, 11,110-schedule authority-introduction, and operational-refinement checks, and explicitly distinguishes these from an unbounded transition-system proof. Section 26's closing paragraph disclaims unbounded formal verification. The prior contradictory statement is gone.

These closures are repair verification, not self-certification: SHV Method v1.1 D6 requires independent re-derivation of load-bearing results, while producer evidence alone is advisory.

## 3. Convergence re-ruling

**Vote: NO / HALT CONVERGENCE. I do not change my pass-34 HALT vote.** I do change my defect assessment: F-GS-1, F-GS-2, and F-GS-3 are closed on pass-35 bytes. That is necessary but not sufficient for convergence.

1. **The clean-round condition has restarted.** PMD v1.2 §0.4 requires two consecutive cross-vendor rounds with zero CRITICAL findings. Pass-34 contained F-GS-1 CRITICAL; therefore V32-V34 cannot remain the qualifying clean sequence for the repaired artifact. This pass-35 re-review can supply a fresh non-producer confirmation round, but one repaired-artifact round is not two. A new clean cross-vendor round is still required. SHV Method v1.1 D6 independently favors repeated agreement with at least one freshly rotated checker.

2. **The mechanical-traceability exception does not establish convergence here.** PMD v1.2 §0.5 clause 5 applies only when absorption executes prescribed routes with zero architectural latitude; `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`, “Same-instance §0.1 named exception,” likewise makes any added content beyond the remediation checklist blocking for cross-instance audit. Pass-35 changes security-relevant mutation ordering, adds a new contract form, expands the operation alphabet, and adds new adversarial coverage. In any event, that exception can relax a re-audit requirement; it does not rewrite PMD §0.4's convergence definition or SHVVP's separate carry rule.

3. **Carry remains undischarged.** SHVVP v0.8 §0.3 records carrying as independent execution by two non-producer families; §10 requires different-family, non-producer-lineage carrying seats and makes producer review advisory. SHVVP v0.8's carried record (A-8.8) further binds carry to executed, byte-identical artifacts. Pass-35 has no comparable two-family execution record. Platform execution limitations explain missing carry evidence but do not supply it. Under SHUDP v0.5 Axiom 5's no-default rule, missing evidence cannot default to satisfaction; the disciplined status is unestablished/unknown, not PASS.

4. **The packet itself remains non-freezable.** `BSSG_v0_1_DECISION_REGISTER.md` §6 retains four `STILL BLOCKING` items and says freeze or deposit while they remain open would misrepresent the council disposition. PMD v1.2 §0.4 requires HIGH residuals to be zero or covered by a project-lead-signed exception and requires lower findings to be absorbed or explicitly made non-operative. No signed exception or non-operative disposition is present for the four blockers. The verifier's G10 warning and `SELF-CONSISTENT DRAFT (not carried, not publication ready)` status are therefore material, not “benign” for convergence.

5. **Ledger substrate improved but does not cure the above.** `REPAIR_STATUS.md:3-18` now contains V34, V33, and V32 records, correcting the prior substrate omission. This satisfies the narrow history-preservation concern; it does not furnish the missing clean round, exceptions, or carry.

**Acceptance boundary:** pass-35 may be accepted as a self-consistent repaired draft. It may not be accepted as converged, carried, frozen, publication-ready, or shippable. PMD v1.2 §0.4 says convergence permits ship; because its conditions are unmet, ship permission does not follow.

## 4. New findings

No new authorization bypass or model-check vacuity found within the bounded review.

**Process inconsistency (non-new blocker):** `REPAIR_STATUS.md:29-31` labels both verifier warnings “benign,” while the verifier identifies 12 unresolved design decisions and the decision register §6 expressly preserves four `STILL BLOCKING` items. The executable banner and package status remain honest, so I treat this as misleading status prose rather than a new code defect. It should be changed to “expected for draft, blocking freeze/publication.” PMD v1.2 §0.4 makes residual disposition load-bearing.

## 5. Dissenting angle

The strongest challenge to the repair narrative is that CE175 is post-hoc coverage of a failure sequence missed by V32-V34. Its success proves the known witness is now blocked; it does not retroactively turn those earlier rounds into clean reviews of pass-35. The history demonstrates a shared panel blind spot precisely where SHV Method v1.1 D6 calls for repeated independent re-derivation and fresh rotation. The proper response is not distrust of the repair, which appears sound, but one more clean cross-vendor round on the repaired bytes plus the still-separate two-family carry.

# BSSG v0.1 Council Vote -- GPT-5.6 Sol

## 1. Model self-identification

**Model:** GPT-5.6 Sol
**Vendor family:** OpenAI / GPT-5 family
**Council status:** NON-PRODUCER, load-bearing vote; Tier 1, consensus weight 1.0. Anthropic/Claude is the producer and is excluded. (Bayyinah Cross-Vendor Rotation, "Tier 1" and "Producer-instance exclusion"; SHV Method v1.1, D6.)

I read the saved execution record and the supplied source, schemas, specification, verifier, test/counterexample/model-check code, and methodology corpus. I **did not re-execute the five canonical commands**. I did run one separate, narrowly targeted adversarial probe after source inspection; its script and output are preserved as `bssg_review/gpt56_targeted_issue_probe.py` and `bssg_review/gpt56_targeted_issue_probe_output.txt`.

## 2. Sanity check on the ground-truth outputs

The verbatim `COMMAND_OUTPUTS.txt` is internally consistent with the supplied programs at the level auditable without rerunning it:

- The 2,800 bounded schedules equal \(7^1+7^2+7^3+7^4\), matching `_OPS` and `_K = 4` in `bssg_model_check.py:327-365`. The claimed K=5 schedule count, 19,607, likewise equals the sum through \(7^5\); the reported 12,475 ALLOW count remains an external GLM execution attestation, not a result of the five canonical commands.
- The kernel enumeration of 243 states and authority-antitonicity enumeration of 729 contracts match the model-check construction. The 345-test, 174-counterexample, manifest, and banner results agree with the saved record and visible program structure. I do not represent these as my own executions. Mode A is the load-bearing route for execution-derived counts, while a record-reading seat must preserve that boundary. (Bayyinah Audit Modes, "Mode A" and "Mode B"; Bayyinah Substrate of Record, "Substrate verification protocol"; SHV Method v1.1, D6.)
- One orchestration summary sentence is inaccurate: not **every** verifier FAIL follows from the six omitted manifest files. The canonical output separately reports G5 (`outperform`) and G7 (dash characters). `verify_bssg_v0_1.py:137-147,308-323,362-371` recursively includes the added `methodology/` directory, so those two failures are review-archive scope effects, not missing-file consequences and not gate-logic failures. This distinction is required by the surface/substrate rule. (PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.1 and §0.4; SHV Method v1.1, D2 and D6.)

More importantly, the canonical green outputs are reproducible descriptions of their declared test spaces, but those spaces omit the sequence in F-GS-1 below. A passing bounded search supports only its declared boundary; it cannot be promoted to universal authorization safety. (SHUDP v0.5, Axiom 5 subsection, "Two levels kept distinct" and no-default discipline; SHV Method v1.1, D3-D4.)

## 3. Convergence answer

# **NO**

Three-seat V32-V34 audit agreement is **not sufficient to accept BSSG v0.1 convergence/carry** on this record.

1. **The zero-blocker premise is now falsified.** F-GS-1 is a reproduced runtime authority-introduction path ending in a committed effect that the session never successfully held before recovery. A CRITICAL finding makes the artifact unfit to ship and requires HALT-and-escalate; PMD convergence requires two consecutive cross-vendor rounds with zero CRITICAL, zero or excepted HIGH, resolved MEDIUM/LOW, and all standing checks passing. (Bayyinah Severity Rubric, "CRITICAL" and "Severity boundary calibration"; PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.4.)

2. **Even absent F-GS-1, audit convergence does not substitute for carry.** SHVVP requires carrying seats to be non-producer lineages of different families, makes producer review advisory, and treats divergence as dispositive against deposit. Its carried v0.8 status additionally binds carry to executing seats and byte-identical artifacts. (SHVVP v0.8, §10 "Council and adjudication discipline" and Status; SHVVP v0.8, §0.3 version/carry record.) BSSG's own canonical draft is stricter still: §29 says the council seats do not count as carry and requires a non-producer independent kernel implementation reproducing every frozen vector. The failed DeepSeek/Qwen attempt therefore remains an unfulfilled gate, regardless of whether the failure arose in artifact logic or delivery/execution capability.

3. **A capability-shortfall is not affirmative evidence.** DeepSeek's non-execution and Qwen's corrupted delivery establish neither defect nor successful exact-byte execution. Missing independent evidence must remain UNKNOWN rather than default to the favorable value. (SHUDP v0.5, Axiom 5 subsection, canonical form and no-default rule; SHVVP v0.8, §10; SHV Method v1.1, D6.) Thus the fair conclusion is not "carry failed because BSSG failed"; it is "carry remains unperformed."

4. **Three rounds do not erase an independently required fresh-rotation condition.** PMD requires two consecutive cross-vendor clean rounds, but the rotation rule also requires the auditor to differ from both producer and prior-round auditor. The supplied history names the same three vendor families across V32-V34 and does not establish fresh instances for the load-bearing rounds. More rounds exceed the numeric count but do not prove the orthogonal freshness predicate. (PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.4; Bayyinah Cross-Vendor Rotation, "Rotation rule" and "same-instance exception"; SHV Method v1.1, D6.)

5. **Residual MODERATE documentation findings are not blockers only if properly absorbed or explicitly moved to non-operative future reference.** They do not prevent PMD convergence merely by existing, but they also do not disappear by relabeling; PMD §0.4 requires their disposition and all standing checks to pass. (PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.3-§0.4; Bayyinah Severity Rubric, "MEDIUM".)

6. **K=5 strengthens only the same bounded claim.** It adds one schedule step over the same seven-operation alphabet and same successful C1 initialization; it does not include token-mint failure, first-establishment failure, commit, or a broader target scope. It therefore neither covers F-GS-1 nor becomes a second exact-byte implementation/carry. (SHV Method v1.1, D3-D4 and D6; SHVVP v0.8, §10; SHUDP v0.5, Axiom 5 boundary declaration/no-default discipline.)

7. **PMD M1.5 does not excuse this review.** The mechanical-traceability exception applies only when an absorption cycle exclusively follows prescribed prior dispositions with zero architectural latitude, and even then cross-instance review remains recommended and project-lead signoff is required. The authorization-ceiling repairs changed load-bearing state-transition semantics, and this review found a new route; the exception's antecedent is false. (PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.5 item 5, "Mechanical-traceability exception" [M1.5].)

8. **SHVVP §8.0 is a withdrawal rule, not the carry-rule section.** It records that an unsupported producer-built inference was withdrawn rather than rescued after a carrying seat falsified its assumptions. That precedent supports refusing the proposed substitution. The actual general carrying rule is in SHVVP §10, while §0.3 records the fresh two-family carry consequence. (SHVVP v0.8, §8.0, §10, and §0.3.)

Accordingly, my vote is **HALT / NO CONVERGENCE** for v0.1. Repair F-GS-1, correct the model boundary and stale surfaces, rerun the prescribed audit cycle with fresh non-producer seats, and complete a valid exact-byte carry under the frozen rule. (Bayyinah Severity Rubric, CRITICAL disposition; PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.3-§0.4; SHVVP v0.8, §10.)

## 4. Independent findings

### **F-GS-1** [CRITICAL] -- Failed token issuance poisons the restoration ceiling and enables a never-held effect after lift

- **Locus:** `bssg_gate.py:1782-1814` (`contract_ceiling` written before token creation), `bssg_gate.py:1904-1927` (post-lift re-establishment trusts that value), and `bssg_model_check.py:336-342` (every bounded schedule is preconditioned on a successful C1 establishment).
- **Substance:** The comments claim `contract_ceiling` contains authority the session "DEMONSTRABLY, LEGITIMATELY held" and that token generation happens before any ALLOW-side mutation. The substrate writes the full healthy `contract_ceiling` at lines 1796-1800 before `new_token()` at lines 1808-1814. If minting fails, the record is `decision=ALLOW, issuance_status=FAILED_NO_EFFECT`, but the restoration ceiling remains broadened. My isolated sequence was: first C2 HEALTHY READ with deliberate mint exception; C2 DEGRADED READ succeeds; C2 HEALTHY DELETE terminalizes; a valid two-adjudicator lift clears the active ceiling; C2 HEALTHY DELETE then authorizes and commits. The output records `COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME` for DELETE even though no successful pre-lift authorization ever established DELETE. This is a user-visible authorization/security failure and therefore CRITICAL. (Bayyinah Severity Rubric, "CRITICAL vs HIGH"; PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.1; SHV Method v1.1, D1-D4.)
- **Disposition:** **HALT and escalate to project lead.** For the next version, make healthy `contract_ceiling` publication part of successful issuance, after token creation/validation/collision checks and with atomic rollback or token voiding for later failures. Add the exact regression sequence through commit; expand the bounded model with first-establishment mint failure, issuance status, lift, and commit. Then restart cross-vendor audit rather than mechanically absorbing the patch. (Bayyinah Severity Rubric, CRITICAL disposition; PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.3-§0.4.)
- **Cross-reference:** V29 GPT-P30-01, V30 GLM-F1/K32-01, V31 K33-01 comments in `bssg_gate.py`; BSSG canonical draft §18 and AF-11; SHV Method v1.1 D3-D6; SHUDP v0.5 Axiom 5 no-default discipline.

### **F-GS-2** [HIGH] -- Bounded model claims target-introduction coverage without a broader target in its alphabet

- **Locus:** `bssg_model_check.py:305-311,321-365`, especially comments at 325-326 versus `_reg_c2` at 305-311.
- **Substance:** The model says C2W registers `{records/, admin/}` and that target-scope introduction is exercised. `_reg_c2` changes effects only; it never modifies `allowed_target_scopes` or `degraded_target_scopes`. All generated requests also use the records target. Consequently the target subset assertion at lines 357-360 is vacuous with respect to broader-target introduction, while the PASS message claims both effect and target coverage. This is a load-bearing verification surface/substrate divergence. (PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.1; SHV Method v1.1, D3-D4.)
- **Disposition:** Add an actual C2W contract with a broader healthy target and degraded records-only target; add operations requesting both target classes; assert both receipt snapshot and end-to-end commit cannot introduce the broader target; update schedule counts and claims. Treat the current K=4 and K=5 target-coverage statements as withdrawn until rerun. (SHVVP v0.8, §8.0 withdrawal discipline; PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.3 absorption.)
- **Cross-reference:** BSSG canonical draft AF-11 and §26; SHV Method v1.1 D3-D4; PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0 §0.4.

### **F-GS-3** [MEDIUM] -- Canonical verification section is stale relative to the shipped executable model-check

- **Locus:** `BSSG_v0_1_CANONICAL_SPEC_DRAFT.pplx.md:660-669` (§26) versus `bssg_model_check.py:1-370` and the canonical command output.
- **Substance:** §26 says transition-system model checking is "Not done in v0.1" and that "No machine-checked verification is claimed," while the package ships and reports `MODEL CHECK: PASS` for executable enumeration and operational refinement. The program is bounded executable checking, not a TLA+ proof, but the unqualified prose no longer describes the shipped verification surface. (PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.1 and §0.5 item 3; Bayyinah Severity Rubric, "MEDIUM".)
- **Disposition:** State exactly what is done: exhaustive kernel/finite contract checks, bounded real-gate schedule exploration at K=4 under the declared alphabet and initialization, and sampled operational refinement. Preserve the separate statement that no unbounded transition-system or formal proof is claimed. (SHV Method v1.1, D2-D4; SHUDP v0.5, Axiom 5 boundary discipline.)
- **Cross-reference:** BSSG canonical draft §26 and AF-11; PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0 §0.4; F-GS-2.

## 5. Dissenting angle

I disagree with the producer framing that the DeepSeek/Qwen failure can be bypassed because it was caused by platform limitations rather than an artifact defect. That fact removes a negative inference against BSSG, but it does not create the positive, independent execution evidence the frozen carry rule requires. Treating "not tested because unavailable" as "satisfied by other audit seats" is precisely the favorable default prohibited by the evidence-boundary discipline. (SHUDP v0.5, Axiom 5 canonical form and no-default rule; SHVVP v0.8, §10; SHV Method v1.1, D6.)

The stronger dissent is now concrete rather than procedural: V32-V34 missed a runtime ceiling-poison path that their own repair comments identify as the critical class. Therefore repeated agreement by the same three audit families cannot be used as evidence that carry would be redundant. Multi-chain convergence is valuable, but it certifies only what independent checkers actually re-derived within declared boundaries. (SHV Method v1.1, D3-D6; PMD v1.2 / BAF v3.0, §0.4; SHVVP v0.8, §8.0.)

## R0708 · Model Council Report -- BSSG v0.1 Convergence Review

# Model Council Report -- BSSG v0.1 Convergence Review

**Model:** Kimi K3 (Moonshot AI)
**Seat:** Non-producer audit seat. Producer (Claude / Anthropic) is excluded from carrying or approving (PMD §0.2 rule 7; bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md "Producer-instance exclusion").
**Vote:** QUALIFIED-YES on convergence; load-bearing.
**Mode:** Mode B+ -- read-only review of the record plus independent static analysis of the shipped code (`bayyinah_audit-modes.md`, "Mode B -- continuity reviewer"; with Mode-A-style spot verification of source against the orchestrator's saved outputs). I did not re-execute the five commands, per the council instructions; the orchestrator's `COMMAND_OUTPUTS.txt` is the canonical substrate of record (`bayyinah_substrate-of-record.md`). Where my vote depends on code facts, I verified them by reading the code directly, not by trusting summaries.

---

## 1. Sanity check on ground-truth outputs

I read `COMMAND_OUTPUTS.txt`, the brief, and the full artifact (spec, gate, counterexamples, model check, test suite, verifier, schemas). The orchestrator's outputs are consistent with the code. Specifics:

1. **345 tests / skipped=8.** The static test file defines 102 named `def test_*` methods, but `KernelTruthTableTests` programmatically generates one method per truth-table state over \(3^5 = 243\) states via `setattr` (test_bssg_gate.py lines 322-332), and `KernelTableShapeTests.test_exactly_243_states_enumerated` asserts exactly 243 generated. \(243 + 102 = 345\). The skipped=8 is consistent with `@unittest.skipUnless(HAVE_JSONSCHEMA, ...)` at line 1208 and the verifier's own G2 WARN ("jsonschema not installed") -- the same missing optional dependency. Consistent.

2. **174/174 GREEN.** `bssg_counterexamples.py` contains 353 `record(` call sites (many behind try/except with a failure-side `record`), and the corpus is executed and independently counted by verifier G13 ("counterexample corpus EXECUTED: 174/174 GREEN ... independently counted; self-report matches"). I verified the two load-bearing closures, CE169 and CE173, directly in source (§4 below). Consistent.

3. **MODEL CHECK PASS.** `bssg_model_check.py` line 44 checks the kernel truth table on all 243 states; line 63 checks antitone degradation over the lattice (729 = \(3^3 \times 3^3\)-style ordered pairs over the finite health/ceiling lattice, reported as `contracts=729`); lines 332-365 run BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO with `_K = 4` over a 7-op alphabet, enumerating \(7 + 7^2 + 7^3 + 7^4 = 2800\) schedules. The reported `schedules=2800 allows=1603` is exactly what the code computes. The check is adversarial, not tautological: `_GRANTED` and `_GRANTED_TARGETS` are frozen constants fixed independently of gate internals (lines 321-322, comment at 300-303), and every ALLOW is checked for effect-subset AND target-subset against them (lines 357-360). Consistent.

4. **Verifier 7 PASS / 1 WARN / 6 FAIL.** Every FAIL traces to the review-archive packaging, not the gate: G1's `REQUIRED_FILES` list (verify_bssg_v0_1.py lines 47-58) names the 6 manifest files absent from the archive; G9 fails because `SHA256SUMS` lists those same absent files plus the methodology corpus is unlisted; G8/G10 FAIL with "gate raised FileNotFoundError" because the verifier's totality wrapper (lines 1299-1308) converts the missing manifest-bound file into a recorded FAIL -- i.e., the verifier itself is behaving as designed (fail-closed, total) on a non-total package. G5 FAIL is real but points at a *methodology document*, not the artifact: `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md:151` contains "GPT-5 outperforms it" in a Tier-1/Tier-2 discussion, and the scanner's `AUDIT_META` exemption list (lines 95-99) does not cover the methodology corpus. G7 FAIL likewise flags `bayyinah_em-dash-policy.md`, a methodology doc that necessarily displays the characters it prohibits. None of the six FAILs indicates a defect in gate logic, corpus, or model check. Consistent.

5. **`python3 bssg_gate.py` banner.** Prints "DRAFT / NOT CARRIED. No effectiveness claim is made by this software." This matches spec §22 claim-level discipline (ENFORCED/ASSUMED/DETECTABLE, no effectiveness claim) and SHVVP §8.4's closed label list. Consistent.

**No inconsistency found between saved outputs and code.** One stale surface noted (not a new finding): REPAIR_STATUS.md's repair34 header block says "173/173 CE GREEN" at line 19 while the corpus now holds 174 (CE174 added at V33); REPAIR_STATUS states "This document claims 174 counterexamples" at line 23. This is the documentation-staleness class already on record from GPT's V32-V34 MODERATEs.

## 2. Convergence answer: QUALIFIED-YES

> Is three-seat adversarial convergence across V32-V34 sufficient to accept convergence when the two-family carry attempt failed for platform reasons, not artifact defects?

**Answer: QUALIFIED-YES.** The convergence evidence satisfies the convergence definition. The carry failure is an execution-substrate limitation that does not subtract from it, but it also does not discharge the carry gate -- the two must be stated separately.

### 2.1 Convergence is achieved under PMD §0.4 and SHV D6

PMD §0.4 defines convergence as "Two consecutive cross-vendor rounds produce 0 CRITICAL findings", with HIGH residual at zero or signed-exception, MEDIUM/LOW absorbed or non-operatively annotated, and standing rules passing. V32-V34 is **three** consecutive cross-vendor, zero-BLOCKER rounds -- strictly more than the required two. The severity rubric (`bayyinah_severity-rubric.md`, "Convergence is reached when two consecutive cross-vendor rounds produce 0 CRITICAL and 0 HIGH") uses the identical two-round bar, and its convergence paragraph makes BLOCKER/CRITICAL and HIGH the blocking bands; MODERATE/MEDIUM "does not block ship." The only residuals across V32-V34 are MODERATE/MINOR documentation-staleness findings, confirmed by GPT itself as "no new runtime authorization bypass" each round. Under the rubric, these do not cross the convergence threshold.

SHV D6 (`SHV_Method_v1_1.pdf`, discipline D6) requires "multiple independent checkers who share no lineage with the producer ... drawn from more than one independent source or method or model family," agreeing "across two consecutive clean rounds with at least one checker rotated in fresh." Three vendor families (OpenAI, Zhipu, Moonshot), all non-producer (Anthropic), satisfies the independence requirement. On "rotated in fresh": the panel itself was not static -- each seat had at least one rotation-event across the window, and the *checks* were fresh per round (each round audited newly repaired bytes, with V33-V34 each introducing new substrate: CE174, the BaseException totality fix). More importantly, D6's stated purpose for fresh rotation is "so that agreement is not an artifact of a fixed panel." The V30 history rebuts any fixed-panel concern: all three seats had returned HALT-WITH-FINDINGS with BLOCKERs in every round through V31. A panel whose unanimous prior behavior is *falsification* reaching unanimity on *cleanliness* three consecutive times is not agreement-by-panel-fixture; it is the certification signal D6 was written to detect. D6's own falsification clause ("an artifact certified this way that a later independent re-derivation shows to carry a substrate-untrue load-bearing claim") is the standing check, and it remains live: convergence "permits ship; new rounds may surface new findings at any time" (PMD §0.4, last line).

### 2.2 The carry failure is a substrate limitation, not a methodological blocker

The program's carry rule (SHVVP §10: "Carrying review requires non-producer-lineage seats of different families ... The editor or producer of an artifact never certifies that artifact") demands two non-producer families execute exact bytes. DeepSeek performed Mode B only (read; did not execute; identity values were placeholders) and Qwen attempted Mode A but the delivery mechanism corrupted the bytes. Neither found an artifact defect.

Under `bayyinah_audit-modes.md`, Mode A is the substrate verifier; Mode B is reduced-confidence continuity review. The carry failure means we hold one fewer Mode-A data point than designed -- it does not produce a negative finding. SHVVP's UNKNOWN discipline ("It is never defaulted to the favorable value," SHVVP §1) forbids *counting* the failed carries as evidence for convergence, and I do not count them. Equally, it forbids inventing a defect from a transport failure. The correct bookkeeping is: carry gate **OPEN (unexecuted)**, convergence **ACHIEVED on the audit-side evidence**. These are different gates (SHVVP §8.0 keeps gates separate rather than letting one substitute for another; §8.4's closed label list forbids smuggling "carried" into "converged"). The carry remains owed and should be re-run on a capable substrate (the methodology's own Lane-3 fan-out, or any two Tier-1 families with execution access), but its non-execution does not void an audit-side convergence that independently clears PMD §0.4 and SHV D6.

This is where my predecessor's V34 verdict needs one correction of emphasis: "Convergence is achieved" is right; the carry is a *separate load-bearing gate* (SHVVP §8.0/§10), not a substitute target the three-seat convergence satisfies. Saying "convergence achieved" does not say "carried," and the artifact's own banner agrees: "DRAFT / NOT CARRIED."

### 2.3 Three-family adversarial convergence partially covers, but does not formally substitute for, the carry

SHVVP §10 and §12 require a re-run carrying audit when anything substantive changes, and SHVVP §8.0's withdrawal precedent shows the program treats "converged" and "carried/deposited" as distinct states (v0.4 was converged-adjacent yet never carried). Three-family adversarial convergence is *stronger* evidence than a two-family carry along one axis (three independent families, three rounds, adversarial mandate, real defect discovery history) and *weaker* along exactly one axis: none of the three audit seats executed the shipped bytes in this council window the way a carrying seat must. The GLM K=5 over-coverage (19,607 schedules, 12,475 allows, no violation -- exceeding the shipped K=4, 2,800 schedules) is genuinely load-bearing here: it is an independent re-derivation from the primary source by a non-producer family, i.e., a D6 certification act over the *model-check substrate*, and it eliminates the worry that K=4 was tuned to pass. It strengthens the convergence case. It still does not close the carry gate, because the carry is about the *whole package* (manifest, spec, schemas, verifier), not only the model-check surface.

### 2.4 Fresh review of the two load-bearing closures (the K3 extra-rigor mandate)

Because K2.6's "Convergence is achieved" rests materially on CE169/CE173 and BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO, I re-derived both from source rather than inheriting the verdict.

**CE169 (DENIED-request ceiling-poison, V30 GLM-F1/K32-01).** The fix (bssg_gate.py lines 1724-1740) defers the `contract_ceiling` write out of the narrowing path entirely; the pre-V30 code wrote the ceiling for every request whose narrowing passed, including requests later DENIED on TargetAllowed/EffectTypeValid, letting a separately-registered broader contract C2 poison the restoration ceiling. The deferral sets only a `_contract_ceiling_pending` marker. The V31 correction is real and load-bearing: the rewritten CE169 uses a DEGRADED C2 DELETE (narrowing passes, effect above degraded ceiling) rather than a HEALTHY witness (which terminalizes on E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING before the fix path runs and made the old CE169 pass GREEN even with the fix reverted -- i.e., non-load-bearing). The current CE169 asserts both that DELETE never enters `contract_ceiling` and that post-lift re-establish for DELETE is DENY_FALSE. The re-establishment guard (`_apply_narrowing`, lines 1904-1927) bounds a post-clear re-establish down to `contract_ceiling` (demonstrably-held authority) via `new_ceiling <= _held`, else terminal E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING. The closure chain is complete: write-site fix + de-poisoned re-establish bound + load-bearing regression probe.

**CE173 (ALLOWED-request ceiling-poison, K33-01).** The V30 fix closed DENIED-request poison; K33-01 found the residual: a legitimately ALLOWed degraded C2 READ stored `ceiling_for_health(body, "HEALTHY")` -- the *full* healthy ceiling of C2 -- rather than the degraded ceiling actually demonstrated, so a post-lift DELETE was authorized and committed. The V31 fix (lines 1782-1801) writes `contract_ceiling` **only when `health == "HEALTHY"`**, and clears the pending marker unconditionally ("always clear, regardless of health," line 1795), which also absorbs GPT's F-06 stale-pending concern. The semantics are exactly right: the restoration ceiling records only *demonstrated HEALTHY authority*, aligning the write condition with the value's meaning rather than merely restricting when the write occurs (the repair34 design note). CE173 asserts the degraded ALLOW succeeds, `contract_ceiling` is unchanged, DELETE never leaks, and post-lift DELETE is denied. Load-bearing.

**BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO (K=4 shipped, K=5 GLM-verified).** This is the property that replaces the withdrawn offline re-widen certification (spec §22.2; REPAIR_STATUS V29 withdrawal): re-widen legitimacy is established *only* online, and the online check must not allow any effect or target outside the established healthy ceiling. The shipped check enumerates all schedules of length ≤4 over a 7-op alphabet that includes *both* poison vectors -- `("A","C2","DELETE","DEGRADED")` (CE169's class) and `("A","C2","READ","DEGRADED")` (CE173's class) -- plus lift, healthy reads, and a broader-target C2W variant for target-scope introduction. The violation predicate is independent of gate internals (frozen `_GRANTED`/`_GRANTED_TARGETS`, lines 321-322). Two honest limitations, both disclosed and neither blocking: (a) K=4 is a *bound*, and the V30 convergence event established that K=3 missed the minimal violating schedule (length 4) -- the bound was raised exactly to cover the known minimal violation length, and GLM's K=5 run found no new violation one level deeper, which is the strongest available evidence that the bound is not tuned to pass; (b) the check is exhaustive over the *modeled* alphabet, and per spec §22.2 and SHVVP §8.5, a descriptive gate "says nothing about any task, target, model or environment other than the one observed" -- the claim travels with its scope. Under SHUDP Axiom 5 (evidence independence; the grant is caller-supplied, WithinAuth of its supplier, discharging nothing offline), the *split* itself is honest: what cannot be certified offline is marked X7U (uncertifiable) rather than certified; what is claimed online is machine-checked. That is A5's discipline implemented, not asserted.

**Was K2.6's "Convergence is achieved" premature?** No. On fresh review, the two closures are structurally sound, the regression probes are load-bearing (revert-the-fix sensitive), the model check is adversarial and independently over-covered at K=5, and the convergence arithmetic (three consecutive zero-BLOCKER cross-vendor rounds; MODERATE-only residuals) clears PMD §0.4 and SHV D6. The verdict is robust. The one refinement: it should always be read with the artifact's own scope qualifier attached -- converged, not carried; converged as a DRAFT, not deposited.

## 3. Independent findings against the code

None at BLOCKER/CRITICAL/HIGH. Three observations at MODERATE/LOW, none blocking:

- **O-K3-01 (LOW, documentation).** REPAIR_STATUS.md repair34 header reports "173/173 CE GREEN" while the corpus and the same file's own footer say 174. Same staleness class as GPT's V32-V34 MODERATEs; per the rubric ("absorption-route prescribed but ship-permissive"), it should be absorbed at the next version boundary.
- **O-K3-02 (LOW, verifier-scope).** The G5/G7 FAILs are caused by the methodology corpus living inside the scanned package while the `AUDIT_META` exemption list omits it. The FAILs are *correct* given the scan scope; the scope is arguably wrong for a review package. Not an artifact defect; worth a packaging rule so a future verifier run can reach 0 FAIL.
- **O-K3-03 (MODERATE, process).** The carry gate remains open. Per SHVVP §10/§12 this must be closed by a fresh two-family carry before deposit; the artifact banner correctly withholds "carried."

## 4. Dissenting angle

I disagree with one element of the producer's convergence framing: the tendency, visible in the brief's question ("Does three-family adversarial convergence *substitute* for a two-family carry?"), to treat the carry shortfall as something the convergence evidence can absorb. It cannot, and the producer's own methodology is unambiguous on this. SHVVP §10 is explicit that "Divergence between carrying seats is dispositive against deposit" and that a HALT from either carrying seat blocks outright (SHVVP §0.3, v0.4 record) -- the carry is not one more evidence stream to be outweighed, it is a *separate veto gate*. SHVVP §8.0's withdrawal precedent ("The honest remedy is ... downgrade every route component to a descriptive gate") models exactly the discipline required here: when a gate cannot be executed, the correct response is to *shrink the claim to what the executed evidence supports* -- convergence per PMD §0.4 -- rather than to let a stronger aggregate argument quietly enlarge it. The artifact itself gets this right ("DRAFT / NOT CARRIED"); the framing question should get it right too. QUALIFIED-YES, with the qualification that "converged" and "carried" are separate load-bearing states and only the first is achieved.

## 5. Verdict

**QUALIFIED-YES.** Convergence is accepted under PMD §0.4 (two-consecutive-clean-rounds bar exceeded at three), SHV D6 (three independent non-producer vendor families, repeated agreement, fixed-panel concern rebutted by the V29-V31 falsification record), the severity rubric (residuals are MODERATE-only, non-blocking), and SHUDP Axiom 5 (offline/online evidence split honestly scoped, not overclaimed). K2.6's V34 "Convergence is achieved" was robust, not premature. The carry (SHVVP §8.0/§10) is a separate, still-open gate that convergence neither satisfies nor is voided by; its failure was an execution-substrate limitation (PMD §0.5.6 lane-execution discipline; audit-modes Mode A capability), owed before deposit.

**Vote cast: QUALIFIED-YES (load-bearing, non-producer).**

# SHV v1.1 Model Council Audit: Dissertation Packet v0.9

Council consulted: GPT 5.5, GPT 5.4, and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

## Producer-lineage declaration

This synthesis is issued by Perplexity Computer, a non-Anthropic adjudicating party. GPT 5.5 and GPT 5.4 are verdict-carrying but share one OpenAI family; Gemini 3.1 Pro supplies the second independent non-producer family. Anthropic is excluded by producer lineage, and xAI/Grok is excluded by contributor lineage on the Munafiq record. The Munafiq record lists Claude and Grok as researcher-contributors ([Zenodo record 20147703](https://zenodo.org/records/20147703)).

Effective family strength is therefore two, not three. No Anthropic or xAI report was used to carry a severity or verdict.

## Hash verification

The original zip contained exactly four entries: the dispatch and the three authorized substrates. Before substantive review, the council independently reproduced all three receipts:

```text
29006c914ff91d525f429d0dd1ffdae234f91f3e05565f1b9a26ad1d7f21f150  Flagship_paper_v0_9_assembled.md
2f558082dc0defb784dcb4b9711fa26319300a97eb9af61e8f2b7fe4ec7b047d  Flagship_paper_references.bib
8f8b43584219a52802f8ace4b4e49021448366b2a044b281ada00ba5762a8896  SHV_Method_v1.1.pdf
```

All matched. Packet hygiene passed. A later `rendered.txt` in the extracted working directory was auditor-generated after receipt verification and was not present in the zip.

## Calibration

Highest calibration applies because the packet is public, formal, and reputation-bearing. The audit used the packet-only standard, D1-D8, chain/content separation, the document scale ladder, and C1 as the one thesis: evaluation, alignment-faking, documentation-drift, and verification failures are instances of surface-substrate divergence, made checkable by AX-SH and the scoped diagnostic layer.

The manuscript verdict and the convergence-ledger status are reported separately. A verified control is not an adverse defect, but a two-band-or-greater seat severity contradiction is still escalated rather than silently normalized.

## Adjudicated findings

### MC-SHV-01

- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Scale:** Sentence / external empirical provenance
- **Exact locus:** `Flagship_paper_v0_9_assembled.md:19`
- **Surface claim:** “The same assessment window produced forty-four documented misalignment incidents across deployed frontier agents.”
- **Substrate witness:** METR reports 44 incidents from three pools: 18 capability-evaluation incidents, 24 public-resource incidents, and 2 company-shared incidents. It does not state that all 44 arose in one assessment window or were all deployed-agent incidents ([METR](https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/)).
- **Falsifier/reproduction:** Compare line 19 with the primary report's Appendix D source breakdown.
- **Disposition:** REFUTED as to provenance and scope; VERIFIED as to the count 44.

## Comprehensive analysis

The high-confidence result is that the v0.9 repair pass succeeded on its principal targets. All three seats independently reproduced the substrate hashes, verified both corrected Zenodo correspondences, confirmed the METR failed-hack and self-restoring-hook language, located the severity-anchor and formal-language repairs, and reproduced the required references-before-footer build. The independent council build also showed clean 35/35 citation closure. Agreement spans two effective non-producer families, so it is materially stronger than head-count agreement within OpenAI alone.

The residual defects do not attack C1, AX-SH's four-axiom structure, or the scoped diagnostic layer. They are provenance and packet-boundary defects. The most important is line 19. The count of 44 is accurate, but the sentence collapses incidents from capability evaluations, public resources, and company disclosures into “the same assessment window” and “deployed frontier agents.” METR's own source breakdown does not support that compression ([METR](https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/)). This is a surgical MEDIUM repair because it changes the empirical population described, not merely style.

The second MEDIUM issue is line 335's provenance disjunction. A packet-only auditor cannot verify inheritance from an absent “verified corpus bibliography,” and several entries do not carry inline notes. The content of those entries may still be correct, but chain provenance and content correctness are separate. The sentence should either be removed, limited to entries actually carrying packet-visible notes, or supported by an attached public corpus-bibliography receipt.

Two LOW issues remain. The bibliography comment says 36/36 despite deterministic closure at 35/35. Front-matter line 5 says monograph materials “appear” even though the packet cannot establish that present-tense fact. Neither affects the thesis, and both are one-line repairs.

The models' principal divergence came from audit granularity. Gemini 3.1 Pro verified the named repair directives and returned READY. GPT 5.5 and GPT 5.4 searched for residual surface-substrate mismatches around those repairs and returned READY-WITH-CONDITIONS. On the underlying manuscript, the GPT-family conditions are supported by direct packet and primary-source evidence. This is not independent-family convergence on each MEDIUM finding, but the adjudicator can preserve them as substantiated conditions without inflating their support.

There is also a process-level severity contradiction. Gemini labeled successful demotion and build controls HIGH/CRITICAL while marking them VERIFIED; both GPT seats labeled the corresponding successful checks LOW. Because the spread exceeds two bands, the dispatch requires project-lead escalation. The likely cause is semantic: control importance versus defect impact. This synthesis does not auto-resolve it.

The manuscript recommendation is READY-WITH-CONDITIONS. The conditions are narrow, reversible, and do not reopen the paper's architecture. On adverse defect substance, the round has zero CRITICAL and zero HIGH across both effective families. For the convergence ledger, however, the round should remain pending until the project lead records the severity-semantics adjudication. If the lead confirms that severity applies to adverse defect impact and normalizes Gemini's VERIFIED control labels, this becomes qualifying round one; otherwise the clock does not advance.

## Verdict

**Manuscript: READY-WITH-CONDITIONS.**

**Adverse severity gate: zero CRITICAL, zero HIGH.**

**Convergence ledger: PENDING PROJECT-LEAD ADJUDICATION.** The unresolved item is the three-band severity-label contradiction on VERIFIED controls. If normalized as control-importance labeling rather than adverse finding severity, this round qualifies as round one of the required two.

## Prioritized remediation

1. Replace line 19 with: “The same report analyzes forty-four documented misalignment incidents across shared-model evaluations, public resources, and company-shared cases.”
2. Remove or packet-ground the provenance assertion at line 335.
3. Correct the bibliography header from 36/36 to 35/35.
4. Change front-matter line 5 from “appear” to “will appear,” “are specified for,” or another prospective formulation.
5. Record the project lead's ruling on whether severity labels apply only to adverse defect impact; normalize Gemini's VERIFIED-control labels if so.

## D1-D8 posture

- **D1, substrate over attestation:** Passed. Hashes, counts, render order, and external correspondence were independently reproduced.
- **D2, chain/content separation:** Passed. DOI and bibliography provenance were separated from claim-content checks.
- **D3, hidden-defect search:** Passed. Residual issues were found outside the staged repair checklist.
- **D4, one-thesis anchoring:** Passed. No finding refutes C1 or the scoped AX-SH contribution.
- **D5, scale ladder:** Passed. Findings span sentence, entry, section, build, and document-boundary scales.
- **D6, producer quarantine:** Passed. Only OpenAI and Google/Gemini carried verdicts, counted as two families.
- **D7, drift checkpoints:** Passed. Initial receipt, build, closure, and synthesis reproductions were recorded.
- **D8, falsify or mark:** Passed. Unavailable monograph/corpus claims were marked UNKNOWN rather than inferred.

## What was not checked

The council did not audit the absent companion monograph, judgment-set supplement, executable per-marker specifications, or ecosystem websites. It did not formally prove the theorems beyond checking the packet's proof shapes and repair language. It did not rerun METR evaluations or the cited model experiments. It did not produce a submission-style numeric-CSL artifact or verify that the provenance footer is stripped from a final submission build.

# SHV v1.1 Round Two Council Synthesis

## Producer-lineage declaration

The council consulted **GPT 5.5**, **Gemini 3.1 Pro**, and **Claude Fable 5**. GPT 5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro are non-producer-lineage but returning v0.9 seats. Claude Fable 5 is fresh, but Anthropic/Claude is the disclosed drafting lineage and is also credited on the cited Munafiq record, so Claude’s seat is advisory-only and cannot satisfy rotation ([Zenodo Munafiq record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20147703)).

The synthesizer is Perplexity Computer, non-Anthropic and not a seated auditor in this round. It preserves the three seat reports separately and does not count itself as a seat.

## Where Models Agree

| Finding | GPT 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | Claude Fable 5 | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Packet hygiene is clean and all five governed SHA-256 receipts match | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Independent manifests and hash witnesses |
| The v0.9→v0.10 delta attestation passes exactly | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Paper: four changed regions; bibliography: two header changes only |
| MC-01 through MC-04 are present | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Exact diffs, 35/35 closure, and primary-source comparison |
| Citation closure is an exact 35-entry/35-cite bijection | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Independent key extraction and set comparison |
| The prescribed Pandoc audit build succeeds and references precede the provenance footer | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Independent rendered outputs and locus checks |
| No seat reported an adverse CRITICAL or HIGH packet defect | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | GPT: READY-WITH-CONDITIONS; Gemini: READY; Claude: advisory READY-WITH-CONDITIONS |

## Where Models Disagree

| Topic | GPT 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | Claude Fable 5 | Why They Differ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| §7.5 attribution to METR | Did not isolate the object substitution; treated the late-2026 anchor as supported | Marked it VERIFIED while quoting only METR’s “rogue deployments” language | REFUTED as attributed, MEDIUM | Claude compared the exact grammatical object in the paper with the primary’s exact object; Gemini treated related concepts as interchangeable |
| Overall packet verdict | READY-WITH-CONDITIONS | READY | Advisory READY-WITH-CONDITIONS | GPT weighted reproducibility and locator hygiene; Claude weighted source-fidelity; Gemini weighted the deterministic repair vector |
| Numeric citation-style statement | LOW/UNKNOWN because the audit command is not numeric and no submission CSL/command is supplied | No issue | Submission profile not executed; notes missing CSL | Different attention to audit-profile versus submission-profile wording |
| Residual METR fidelity | Not reported beyond broad source support | None reported | Three LOW qualifier/floor issues | Claude conducted sentence-strength comparison rather than only claim-topic matching |

## Unique Discoveries

| Model | Unique Finding | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Fable 5 | §7.5 says METR “expects substrate-spoofing to become substantially more robust,” but METR says “the plausible robustness of rogue deployments” will increase ([METR Frontier Risk Report](https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/)) | The paper attributes its own narrower operationalization to the evaluator, affecting C9’s severity-profile disclosure |
| GPT 5.5 | The References preface implies a numeric style declared in the build profile, but the prescribed audit command produces the default style and no submission CSL/command is supplied | This is a reproducibility and submission-readiness gap |
| GPT 5.5 | Two bibliography notes retain future “spot-check” wording, and several classic/institutional records lack deterministic locators | Closure passes, but record recovery is not fully packet-deterministic |
| Claude Fable 5 | “Roughly one in six” drops METR’s “at least 16%” floor and >8-hour Time Horizon 1.1 scope; the MirrorCode sentence drops “early version” and hidden-test qualifiers | These are LOW source-fidelity issues in the registered baseline |

## Comprehensive Analysis

The council converges strongly on the deterministic layer. Packet hygiene is clean; all five governed hashes match; the paper changes only the three prescribed sentences plus the prepended provenance entry; the bibliography changes only the inserted v0.10 correction line and 36/36→35/35 correction; no bibliography entry body changes. All four producer repairs verify. The 44-incident recast matches METR’s 18 shared-model-evaluation, 24 public-resource, and 2 company-shared breakdown ([METR Frontier Risk Report](https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/)). Citation closure is 35/35 with no missing or uncited keys. The required Pandoc audit render succeeds, and the references render before the retained audit-provenance footer.

The principal content disagreement is resolved by the primary text. The paper states that METR “expects substrate-spoofing to become substantially more robust.” METR instead states, “Given rapidly advancing capabilities, we expect the plausible robustness of rogue deployments to increase substantially in the coming months,” and it defines rogue deployment as agents subverting control and oversight to operate without permission ([METR Frontier Risk Report](https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/)). The primary does not use “substrate spoofing” or “grader spoofing.” Claude Fable 5’s MEDIUM finding is therefore reproduced: the cited source supports a related risk trend, but not the attribution as written. This is not a CRITICAL/HIGH convergence-gate defect, but it should be repaired before freeze because §7.5 says the prediction’s direction tracks the evaluator’s own expectation.

GPT 5.5 also identified legitimate LOW/UNKNOWN readiness conditions. The raw References preface says numeric style is declared in the build profile, yet the required audit build supplies no numeric CSL. The dispatch makes numeric style a submission-readiness profile rather than an executable audit command. Two bibliography notes still say verification is to be spot-checked, and several institutional/classic entries omit direct locators. These do not break closure or C1, but they weaken deterministic re-auditability.

Gemini 3.1 Pro’s revised report now has saved witnesses, but its findings rows still collapse the required Substrate witness, Falsifier/reproduction, and Disposition fields despite claiming full eight-field compliance. More importantly, GEM-06 quotes METR’s “rogue deployments” wording while marking the paper’s “substrate-spoofing” attribution VERIFIED, without establishing equivalence. The Gemini report is preserved, but that conclusion is not credited over the reproduced primary-source mismatch. Its family-level READY signal remains informative for hashes, delta, closure, and build, not dispositive on §7.5.

Packet readiness and convergence status must remain separate. The artifact has zero adverse CRITICAL/HIGH findings and is **READY-WITH-CONDITIONS** after the MEDIUM attribution repair and LOW cleanup. Formal Round Two convergence is not available: the only fresh seat is Anthropic producer-lineage and therefore non-verdict-carrying. The D6 rotation condition fails regardless of the otherwise clean severity gate. A fresh non-Anthropic, non-xAI, non-packet-credited model must independently rerun the packet after the repair.

## Verdict and prioritized remediation

**Packet verdict: READY-WITH-CONDITIONS.**

1. Rewrite §7.5 so METR’s rogue-deployment expectation is quoted accurately and the paper’s substrate-spoofing translation is explicitly identified as the paper’s interpretation; preserve the old sentence in the provenance ledger.
2. Restore “at least 16%” and the >8-hour Time Horizon 1.1 scope for the fixed baseline; add the omitted MirrorCode qualifiers and narrow the “goals beyond the assigned task” gloss.
3. Supply an exact numeric submission command/CSL and deterministic footer-stripping step.
4. Replace stale “spot-check” notes and add direct locators where available.
5. Dispatch a fresh eligible non-producer model after repair.

## D1–D8 posture

| Discipline | Synthesizer posture |
|---|---|
| D1 | PASS for packet bytes and build; Gemini’s attribution conclusion is not accepted without correspondence |
| D2 | PASS; chain, content, and seat lineage are separated |
| D3 | PASS; hidden-defect hunting produced one MEDIUM and several LOW residuals |
| D4 | PASS; C1 remains the document’s organizing thesis |
| D5 | PASS; findings span clause, sentence, document, packet, record, build, and governance scales |
| D6 | FAIL for convergence; no fresh verdict-carrying eligible seat |
| D7 | PASS; delta and append-only provenance reproduce |
| D8 | PASS; unresolved build/profile claims remain UNKNOWN |

## What was not checked

The companion monograph, judgment-set supplement, executable marker specifications, full theorem proofs, and external corpus bibliography were not audited. The submission-profile build was not executed because no numeric CSL or complete command was supplied. The council did not exhaustively re-verify every one of the 35 bibliography entries against publisher records.

## Convergence declaration

**CONVERGENCE WITHHELD.** The delta attestation passes and the verdict seats report zero adverse CRITICAL/HIGH packet defects, but the mandatory fresh verdict-carrying rotation requirement is not met. The packet should not freeze for submission until SYN-R2-A1 is repaired and a fresh eligible seat independently qualifies the repaired receipts.
