# Model Council Synthesis: Dissertation v1.3 to v1.4 Re-Attestation

Consulted models: GPT 5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro as carrying seats, with Claude Fable 5 as the advisory seat.

## Where Models Agree

| Finding | GPT 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | Claude Fable 5 | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| The v1.3 baseline and v1.4 source hashes re-derive to `56178d29e01967e51aa4541a48fa737fc66438b170820a113299b7319945b8c5` and `92ac1f1d88dc50c94d433a8b5e53e026260244e8710ce75ce5109421c5146e17`. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | All three seats independently recomputed the receipts. |
| The source delta contains 10 hunks, all bounded to R-1a/R-1b/R-2/R-3/R-4/R-5, with no out-of-register source hunk. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Each seat independently mapped the diff to the governing register. |
| The specified v1.3 findings are discharged on the source, canon, and rendered instrument, including stale-version removal, Appendix E deposit history, T83 locus-2 calibration, and the quoted D-6 span. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Byte-level and wrap-immune probes found the required literals and zero targeted stale literals. |
| The v1.4 canon receipt re-derives to `d4f1da364b5f068ad536a00bc4a46e08a8779b8f640e8ba42bf9370041053416`, and Appendix E plus front matter are body-layer material. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | All three seats confirmed the receipt and layering rule. |
| The shipped verifier exits 0 with `VERIFIER: ALL PASS`, and both manifests are internally self-consistent. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | The verifier and manifest checks were executed independently. |
| DOI `10.5281/zenodo.21500700` resolves to the deposited flagship paper, and R-1b receives no absence-credit under Ruling 4. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Confirmed through the [Zenodo API record](https://zenodo.org/api/records/21500700) and [DOI resolver](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21500700). |
| The audit-trail packet's ledger and punch list are older than the publication packet's governance artifacts. | ✓ |  | ✓ | GPT 5.5 and Claude Fable 5 independently found the audit ledger to be an exact prefix missing the appended v1.4 section; both also found the missing v1.4 punch-list state. |

## Where Models Disagree

| Topic | GPT 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | Claude Fable 5 | Why They Differ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Final seat verdict | NON-PASS, carrying | PASS-DELTA, carrying | NON-PASS, advisory | GPT 5.5 and Claude Fable 5 treated packet governance and deposit readiness as part of the attested object. Gemini 3.1 Pro confined its effective ruling to the corrected R-register instrument and publication kit. |
| Audit-trail governance mismatch | Blocking because the packet of record omits the governing v1.4 section and current punch-list state | Not reported | Blocking for deposit, although outside the substantive R-register | The models applied different scope boundaries. GPT 5.5 emphasized the brief's statement that the v1.4 ledger section governs and the requirement to re-derive packet manifests. Gemini 3.1 Pro did not surface the cross-packet comparison. |
| Meaning of verifier success in the audit kit | A control result that does not cure the governance mismatch | Full confirmation that the new gates pass | Partly vacuous because the four new gates are PDF-conditional and the audit kit has no PDF | The seats inspected verifier coverage to different depths and assigned different evidentiary weight to exit status 0. |
| Whether the instrument itself needs repair | No source or canon repair; rebuild governance packet only | No repair required | No source or canon repair; rebuild packet and metadata before deposit | The disagreement concerns packaging and authorization, not the corrected dissertation substrate. |

## Unique Discoveries

| Model | Unique Finding | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Fable 5 | The paste-ready Zenodo description still says `Status: working research monograph, version 1.3.` | Publishing that block would create a fresh public status-currency defect even though the deposited artifact is v1.4. |
| Claude Fable 5 | The verifier's four new gates run only when a PDF exists, so the audit-kit invocation skips them while still printing `ALL PASS`. | A self-consistent audit manifest can pass without exercising the advertised stale-version, forthcoming-reference, propagation-count, or deposit-record gates. |
| Claude Fable 5 | The immediately prior v1.3 canon is absent, forcing composite bounding from the v1.2 canon plus literal probes. | This does not negate the result, but it weakens direct reproducibility for a narrow v1.3 to v1.4 canon attestation. |
| Claude Fable 5 | The live Zenodo flagship record currently has no reciprocal related identifier for the monograph. | This is expected before the monograph deposit and is not a finding, but it identifies the post-deposit metadata step. |

## Comprehensive Analysis

The council reached strong convergence on the corrected dissertation instrument. GPT 5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Claude Fable 5 independently reproduced the baseline, source, and canon receipts; classified the same 10 source-diff hunks inside the repair register; verified the required stale-literal removals and replacement clauses; confirmed the Appendix E record and Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 pointers; and executed the verifier successfully. That three-model convergence is especially reliable because the seats used different probing emphases yet reached the same substrate conclusion. The bounded R-register repair is substantively complete.

The models also agreed that the live DOI is valid and corresponds to the named flagship paper. GPT 5.5 and Claude Fable 5 further confirmed the expected two canon DOI loci and the additional body-layer manifestations. All three applied Ruling 4 correctly: the producer-registered repair is verified affirmatively but cannot be converted into absence-credit.

The decisive divergence concerns the identity of the object being attested. Gemini 3.1 Pro treated the corrected source, canon, publication render, and publication manifest as the operative object and returned PASS-DELTA. GPT 5.5 treated the staged audit-trail packet as part of the required governance substrate and returned NON-PASS after discovering that its ledger and punch list are stale relative to the publication packet. Claude Fable 5 independently reproduced the same mismatch and showed that the audit ledger is an exact byte-prefix of the publication ledger, ending before the entire v1.4 governing section. This is not a speculative disagreement or a difference in taste. It is a reproducible cross-packet state divergence.

GPT 5.5's interpretation carries greater weight for the round-level ruling. The brief says the audit ledger's v1.4 section governs, instructs re-derivation of packet manifests, and is intended to authorize a deposit whose metadata points readers to the accompanying audit ledger. An audit-trail archive that omits that governing section cannot serve as the packet of record for the attestation, even if its own stale manifest is internally consistent. Gemini 3.1 Pro's PASS-DELTA remains valid as a narrower instrument-level result, but its report does not answer the cross-packet defect reproduced by the other two seats.

Claude Fable 5's additional metadata finding reinforces the distinction between instrument correctness and deposit readiness. The paste-ready deposit description still labels the monograph as version 1.3. This one-token defect is outside the source/canon R-register, but it would become a public-facing false status claim if pasted into Zenodo. Its verifier observation also explains why automation did not catch the defect: the audit-kit run skips the new PDF-dependent gates, and those gates do not inspect deposit metadata.

The formal convergence condition is not met. The brief requires PASS-DELTA from both returning carrying seats. Gemini 3.1 Pro returned PASS-DELTA, but GPT 5.5 returned NON-PASS. Claude Fable 5's advisory NON-PASS does not control convergence, although it independently corroborates the carrying-seat blocker. The correct synthesis determination is therefore **NON-PASS at packet/deposit level, with PASS on the bounded R-register instrument**.

The required repair is mechanical and does not reopen the dissertation's canon or body. Rebuild the audit-trail archive using the current v1.4 audit ledger and punch list, regenerate its `SHA256SUMS.txt`, correct `version 1.3` to `version 1.4` in the deposit description, and add the new archive receipt to the governing ledger or corrigendum. Then run a narrow receipt-only re-attestation focused on cross-packet identity, manifest integrity, metadata status currency, and the rebuilt archive hash. Harden the verifier so its literal gates run against available source, canon, HTML, DOCX, and metadata members rather than only the PDF.

**Convergence determination: NOT ACHIEVED. Final council ruling: NON-PASS for deposit authorization; PASS for the v1.3 to v1.4 R-register repair itself.**

# Model Council Synthesis: Dissertation v1.4 Receipt-Only Round 3

Models consulted: GPT 5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

**Council determination: CONVERGED, PASS-DELTA.** Both carrying seats, from different vendor families, independently returned PASS-DELTA. This satisfies the governing Section 1 rule and closes the receipt-only round.

## Where Models Agree

| Finding | GPT 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| The source, canon, PDF, DOCX, HTML, and bibliography retain the named round-2 identities. | ✓ | ✓ | Both seats independently reproduced all six anchor hashes in the packet locations where each artifact is carried. |
| Cross-packet governance is current and byte-identical. | ✓ | ✓ | Both seats matched ledger SHA-256 `2efd9c5e...` and punch-list SHA-256 `05dda53c...` across the publication and audit-trail packets; both ledger copies contain `Section: v1.4` and `Round-2 addendum`. |
| Both manifests re-derive without mismatch and correctly exclude themselves. | ✓ | ✓ | Each seat found zero hash mismatches and confirmed that `SHA256SUMS.txt` is not self-listed in either packet manifest. |
| Deposit metadata is current for v1.4. | ✓ | ✓ | Both seats found the exact version-1.4 status statement and zero `version 1.3` occurrences in `DEPOSIT_METADATA_v1_4.md`. |
| All three named baseline anchors are intact. | ✓ | ✓ | Both seats reproduced the v1.2 canon, v1.3 canon, and v1.3 source baseline hashes. |
| Rev-B verification passes non-vacuously in both packet trees. | ✓ | ✓ | Both executions returned `VERIFIER: ALL PASS`; each seat confirmed that the audit-trail run exercised available source, canon, HTML, and DOCX text rather than relying on a missing PDF. |

## Where Models Disagree

| Topic | GPT 5.5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro | Why They Differ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Substantive packet verdict | PASS-DELTA | PASS-DELTA | No substantive disagreement. |
| Reconstruction depth | Classified nine v1.2-to-v1.3 canon diff opcodes against the D-register families and found no extra hunk after review. | Verified the named baseline identities but did not report an equivalent hunk-by-hunk reconstruction classification. | Different depth of optional verification; the receipt brief says reconstruction may be checked “if desired.” |
| Archive-to-tree identity | Explicitly compared every zip member with its extracted counterpart and reported no missing members or hash differences. | Re-derived both manifests and verified the required artifacts but did not separately publish a complete zip-versus-tree comparison. | Different evidence granularity, not a conflicting result. |

## Unique Discoveries

| Model | Unique Finding | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| GPT 5.5 | Reported original archive hashes: publication `4be3ab34...` and audit trail `3eaa4e06...`, plus exact zip-to-tree member identity. | Strengthens chain-of-custody and proves the extracted audit substrate faithfully represents the submitted archives. |
| GPT 5.5 | Mapped the nine baseline-canon diff opcodes to recorded D-register families with no residual hunk after manual review. | Adds optional support for the packet’s reconstruction claim beyond mere baseline receipt. |

## Comprehensive Analysis

The highest-confidence result is that the defect targeted by round 3 has been repaired at the substrate level. GPT 5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro independently found that the audit ledger and punch list are byte-identical across the publication and audit-trail packets. The ledger in each packet contains the v1.4 section and its round-2 addendum. This directly addresses the prior F-DG-12 stale-governance failure rather than merely accepting an attestation that it was fixed.

The convergence is also supported by multiple independent controls around that central fact. Both models reproduced the round-2 identities of the dissertation source, canon, PDF, DOCX, HTML, and bibliography. Both re-derived the manifests without mismatch, confirmed the self-exclusion rule, reproduced the three baseline anchors, and found current v1.4 deposit metadata with no stale v1.3 status string. Most importantly, both executed the rev-B verifier in both extracted packet trees and obtained `VERIFIER: ALL PASS`. Their non-vacuity checks establish that the audit-trail invocation exercised substantial available text members even though that archive carries DOCX rather than PDF.

There is no verdict-level disagreement. The differences concern evidentiary depth. GPT 5.5 produced a more forensic receipt, including complete archive hashes, archive-to-tree member comparisons, literal counts, and a manual classification of the nine v1.2-to-v1.3 canon diff opcodes. Gemini 3.1 Pro covered every mandatory receipt leg but presented a narrower receipt and did not independently publish the same hunk-level reconstruction analysis. Because reconstruction was optional in the round brief and all mandatory legs converged, this difference does not weaken the Google carrying verdict.

The synthesis preserves the packet’s scope boundary. This is a receipt-only closure. It establishes identity, cross-packet governance currency, manifest integrity, metadata currency, baseline receipt, and verifier execution. It does not re-audit the dissertation’s substantive scholarship, external factual claims, bibliography against live primaries, human-peer-review status, or general publication readiness. No source, canon, render, or bibliography byte changed in this round, so those broader questions were neither reopened nor silently certified.

Under the governing council rule, convergence requires PASS-DELTA from at least two carrying seats of different vendor families. GPT 5.5 is the OpenAI carrying seat and Gemini 3.1 Pro is the Google carrying seat; both declared their model, vendor, tier, and per-seat namespace, registered no adverse findings, and returned PASS-DELTA. The round therefore closes as **CONVERGED, PASS-DELTA**, specifically for the v1.4 round-3 receipt scope.

The recommended disposition is to append this synthesis and both verbatim seat reports to the audit record without rewriting the preserved round-2 history. Record F-DG-12 as resolved by the round-3 receipt evidence, retain the receipt-only scope qualifier, and proceed with the publication/deposit workflow only under the packet’s existing disclosures and metadata instructions.

# BSSG v0.1 Pass-36 Model Council Synthesis (Class-Fix Verification)

**Council seated:** Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic PRODUCER, advisory-only), Gemini 3.1 Pro (Google, Tier 2 voting), GPT 5.6 Sol (OpenAI, Tier 1 voting — SEAT CORRUPTED, 4th consecutive round).

No effectiveness claim."

## Panel verdict: **CLEAN on gate soundness, ISSUES-FOUND on package consistency**

The class fix (`bssg_gate.py:L1818-L1825`, unconditional `Authority([], [])` init at the top of the ALLOW path before mint and before the HEALTHY-successful ceiling upgrade) structurally closes the 34-instance class the pass-35 R2 panel HALTed on. All three prior attack probes (degraded-first / F-DG-1, A-05 ceiling-record-fault, F-GS-1 mint-fault) are **NOT REPRODUCED** on pass-36 bytes by both the orchestrator and Claude Fable 5's independent reproduction. Gemini 3.1 Pro concurred on gate soundness but surfaced two HIGH-severity **package-consistency** issues that the panel must address before pass-37: a retroactive-edit signature in `REPAIR_STATUS.md` (same class as Gemini's pass-35 R2 A-06 finding) and a missing CE176 entry in the verifier's `CLAIMS` registry.

Orchestrator independently confirmed the exact lines. | The retroactive-edit signature indicates the pass-36 doc-generation pipeline still injects post-hoc marker strings rather than updating the load-bearing summary. Under `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md` this is HIGH (documentation integrity / observability gap, not gate soundness), but it is the SECOND round in a row this exact class surfaces. It should be a ship blocker for the doc surface even while the gate is CLEAN. |
| Gemini 3.1 Pro | **F-P36-02 HIGH (verifier `CLAIMS` registry missing CE176):** the verifier's `CLAIMS` array in `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` (L1092) contains no entry for CE176 or the `34TH-INSTANCE` tag. `bssg_counterexamples.py` executes CE176 GREEN, but verifier G12's "every registered load-bearing claim has a passing probe" pass is technically vacuous for the new instance — G12 cannot enforce load-bearing status because the claim is unregistered. Orchestrator grep confirmed: `grep -n "CE17[0-9]\|34TH" verify_bssg_v0_1.py` returns 0 matches for CE174/CE175/CE176. | The `176/176 GREEN, 0 RED` self-report line in the verifier is arithmetic; G12 requires cited CEs to exist and every registered claim to have a probe. Without CE176 in the registry, a future regression that removes CE176 from the corpus would fail the 176-count check but would NOT trigger the G12 load-bearing-claim check — the claim simply isn't wired. This weakens the traceability guarantee `bssg_v0_1.md` §22.2 relies on. |
| Claude Fable 5 (advisory) | **F-FB-1 MEDIUM (advisory-only, liveness/documentation):** a mint-fault-first session that is later legitimately lifted restores the empty ceiling; any honest re-widen — even to a contract-registered effect the subject had authorization to request — denies with `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING`. The lift is accepted but restores nothing usable; recovery requires opening a new session. Traced end-to-end via `fable5_class_fix_probe.py`. | This is intended fail-closed behavior (the session demonstrably held nothing so a lift restores nothing) but the spec R-1 LIFT narrative near `BSSG_v0_1_CANONICAL_SPEC_DRAFT.pplx.md:L447` does not state it explicitly. Under `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md` MEDIUM (methodology-fidelity / behavior-documentation gap, not ship blocker). Advisory only per Producer-instance exclusion. |
| Claude Fable 5 (advisory) | **F-FB-2 LOW (advisory-only, hygiene):** `Authority.is_empty()` at L565-L566 uses OR-semantics (`not self.effects or not self.targets`) while the class-fix empty-floor uses `<=` subset semantics. Different notions of "empty" that do not collide today because `ceiling_for_health` never writes one-field-only Authority, but a future one-field-only write would create a divergence. | Purely hygiene; no defect. Advisory only. |
| Orchestrator (not a seat) | Reference-capture race between `contract_body` at L1748 and consumption at L1847 can broaden `contract_ceiling[session]` beyond the contract's registered `allowed_effects` if a caller mutates the body between the two lines. However, the broadened entry cannot be laundered into an ALLOW: `E-FALSE-CONTRACTMATCH` locks the session to its established contract, `E-EFFECT-NOT-REGISTERED` blocks non-body effects, and `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING` catches the mismatch. Documented in `HUNT_35TH_LIFT_OUTPUT.txt`. | Not a defect on pass-36 — the kernel conjuncts absorb the race — but a future refactor that removes `E-FALSE-CONTRACTMATCH` or `E-EFFECT-NOT-REGISTERED` from the deny path would open the race into an exploit. Worth a comment near L1748 noting the defense-in-depth interlock. |

## Comprehensive Analysis

### High-confidence findings (the panel is unanimous where it produced)

Both producing seats independently reproduced the sealed pass-36 command outputs, independently traced the class fix's substrate location (`bssg_gate.py:L1818-L1825`), independently confirmed the three prior CRITICALs are NOT REPRODUCED, and independently found no 35th instance. This is the strongest single-round convergence the BSSG council has recorded. Two independent chains agreeing on both **presence** (empty-Authority entry at post-ALLOW time) and **algebra** (the `<=` subset test on empty `_held` bounds any non-empty re-establishment) satisfies SHV Method v1.1 D6 producer-quarantined multi-chain convergence on the code-layer soundness question. The class-fix design claim — `_held` is never None after any ALLOW, regardless of path — is corroborated by orchestrator grep (only three `contract_ceiling[...]` write sites exist), Fable 5's return-path proof (every ALLOW-or-issuance-failure return sits after L1825), and Gemini's four-angle 35th-instance hunt (concurrency, `_apply_narrowing`, `submit_amendment`, indirect writes). The 34-instance pattern is closed structurally, not case-by-case.

The verifier ceremony reproduces cleanly. 176/176 CE GREEN includes the new CE176 that specifically exercises the degraded-first scenario end-to-end (Gemini traced its body: DEGRADED READ writes empty Authority → HEALTHY DELETE `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING` → amendment → HEALTHY DELETE still denied). CE175 (F-GS-1) remains GREEN, so the mint-fault closure is preserved. The model-checker's bounded-authority-introduction proof at 11110 schedules is unchanged from pass-35 R2, meaning the class fix did not disturb the antitone contract lattice or the operational refinement over the executable.

### Areas of divergence and how to weigh them

The two producing seats reached different verdicts (Fable 5 CLEAN advisory, Gemini ISSUES-FOUND HIGH) not because they contradict on the gate but because they surveyed different audit surfaces. Fable 5 was scoped by the user to deep code analysis of `_apply_narrowing` + CE162 interaction and had no remit over package documentation. Gemini's remit explicitly included the meta-audit for retroactive-edit signatures and CLAIMS-registry traceability. The findings are complementary, not contradictory, and both are independently verifiable against the substrate (orchestrator confirmed F-P36-01 line locations and F-P36-02's grep-empty result).

Where the panel is materially weaker than pass-35 R2 is **cross-vendor voting representation**. GPT 5.6 Sol has now corrupted four consecutive rounds with the identical failure signature (announces intent, ends turn without saving). Only ONE non-producer voting seat (Gemini, Google) is present this round. Under `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md` and PMD v1.2 §0.4, a panel that lacks a functioning OpenAI seat does not satisfy the two-consecutive-rounds-at-zero-CRITICAL requirement on the OpenAI axis for `BSSG v0.1` carrying eligibility. Pass-37 needs either a working GPT 5.6 Sol, a substitution (GPT 5.6 Terra or Kimi K3 was viable in prior rounds), or a documented seat-corruption waiver in the DECISION_REGISTER.

### Unique insights worth noting

Gemini's F-P36-02 (missing CE176 in the verifier's `CLAIMS` registry) is the more actionable of the two HIGH findings for immediate remediation because it is a single-file edit with a mechanical fix, and because it makes the `176/176 GREEN` self-report brittle to future regressions. F-P36-01 (retroactive-edit signature) is the more consequential one strategically because it is the **second consecutive round** the same defect class has surfaced against the doc-generation pipeline, suggesting the pipeline itself needs review rather than another post-hoc edit. Both together mean the doc-and-verifier surface is HALTing (per `bayyinah_severity-rubric.md` HIGH-in-observability), even though the gate substrate is CLEAN.

Fable 5's F-FB-1 (mint-fault-first liveness) is worth surfacing to the spec editor because it clarifies an implicit design invariant — the empty ceiling is a fail-closed floor that even a legitimate lift cannot lift above. Users who read the R-1 LIFT semantics might reasonably expect a lift to restore *something*. Explicit documentation prevents a future PR from "fixing" the liveness gap and reopening the 34-instance class.

### Final recommendation

**HALT pass-36 at the doc-and-verifier surface; PASS the gate substrate.**

The gate is CLEAN — the class fix works, all three prior CRITICALs are closed, no 35th instance was found under adversarial hunt by two independent chains, and the model checker at 11110 schedules is unchanged. But two HIGH-severity package-consistency defects (F-P36-01 retroactive-edit signature + F-P36-02 missing verifier CLAIMS entry) plus one panel-composition failure (GPT 5.6 Sol 4th corruption) mean this round cannot be sealed as the FIRST of the two-consecutive-rounds-at-zero-CRITICAL requirement for carrying. Fix the two doc/verifier issues, restore a functioning OpenAI voting seat, and re-run pass-37 on the same code bytes — if pass-37 comes back CLEAN with the OpenAI axis represented, the code layer will have satisfied PMD v1.2 §0.4 for the first time in this ledger.

**Do not carry to publication yet.** The DRAFT / NOT CARRIED banner remains correct.

**Council seated:** Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic PRODUCER, advisory-only), Gemini 3.1 Pro (Google, Tier 2 voting), GPT 5.6 Sol (OpenAI, Tier 1 voting — first successful production after 4 consecutive corruptions), Kimi K3 (open-source, Tier 2 voting).

**Sealed pass-37 ground truth (orchestrator, verbatim [COMMAND_OUTPUTS.txt](/home/user/workspace/bssg_p37/COMMAND_OUTPUTS.txt)):** 20/20 SHA256SUMS OK, 345 tests (8 skipped) OK, **176/176 CE GREEN** (CE176 present), 11110 schedules / 7200 allows PASS, 12 PASS / 2 WARN / 0 FAIL verifier with G12 reporting **28 registered claims** (up from 27), banner "DRAFT / NOT CARRIED. No effectiveness claim." Gate substrate (`bssg_gate.py`) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to pass-36; only doc/verifier files changed.

## Panel verdict: **CLEAN — PMD v1.2 §0.4 SATISFIED on the code layer**

All four seats independently reproduced the sealed values and returned **CLEAN**. Pass-36 raised two HIGH package-consistency findings (F-P36-01 retroactive-edit signature, F-P36-02 missing verifier `CLAIMS` entry); pass-37 closed both, verified by the original finding author (Gemini 3.1 Pro) plus two independent chains (Kimi K3, Claude Fable 5 advisory). GPT 5.6 Sol successfully produced a report for the first time in five rounds, restoring the OpenAI voting axis. The panel now has **three non-producer voting seats** producing CLEAN on identical bytes across two consecutive rounds (pass-36 + pass-37) — the strongest composition in the program's ledger.

## Where Models Agree

Every row has at least three ✓ (the strongest agreement pattern this council has recorded).

G12 reports 28 registered claims. REPAIR_STATUS.md:L45 has `{claim:CLAIM-CLASS-FIX-CEILING}` tag | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | all four seat reports |

## Where Models Disagree

Only two substantive divergences this round, both about PMD v1.2 §0.4 axis-accounting rather than about the gate or docs. All models agree the gate and package are CLEAN.

## Comprehensive Analysis

### High-confidence findings — the panel is unanimous

All four seats independently reproduced the sealed pass-37 command outputs, independently verified both pass-36 doc/verifier fixes (F-P36-01, F-P36-02), and independently replayed the degraded-first probe with NOT REPRODUCED verdicts. The gate substrate is byte-identical to pass-36 (orchestrator `diff -q`), meaning the class-fix analysis from the pass-36 synthesis carries forward unchanged. This is the strongest single-round convergence the BSSG council has ever recorded: three non-producer voting seats plus one producer-quarantined advisory seat, all CLEAN, on the same bytes as a prior CLEAN-on-gate round.

The verifier's G12 pass with 28 registered claims (up from 27) confirms the F-P36-02 fix is real, not cosmetic: the new `CLAIM-CLASS-FIX-CEILING` is wired to a real probe (`_class_fix_empty_ceiling` at L1090-L1107) that exercises a genuine DEGRADED-first authorize scenario. Gemini 3.1 Pro — the seat who raised F-P36-02 in pass-36 — independently verified the fix and closed her own finding.

The F-P36-01 fix is more subtle. The pass-36 defect was that `REPAIR_STATUS.md:L29` (the pass-36-section header) read `175/175 CE GREEN` while the current corpus was 176. On pass-37, L29 now reads `176/176 CE GREEN`. Historical section headers (repair34 at L67 says `173/173 CE GREEN`, repair33 at L119 says `172/172 CE GREEN`) are UNTOUCHED, and Gemini, Kimi, and Fable 5 all agree this is the CORRECT behavior — the historical battery states should remain frozen at their own-round values, and the rolling `This document claims N counterexamples.` footer is a doc-invariant assertion of CURRENT corpus size, not a retroactive edit. The verifier's G4 (citation resolvability) and G6 (BCP 14 boilerplate) both pass, confirming the doc surface is internally consistent.

### Areas of divergence and how to weigh them

The two disagreements are about **axis accounting for PMD v1.2 §0.4**, not about the gate or the package. GPT 5.6 Sol claims the OpenAI axis is satisfied by pass-36 + pass-37 despite Sol corrupting in pass-36. A stricter reading — Kimi K3's — is that a corrupted seat cannot contribute a vote and therefore cannot count as a round on its axis. Gemini's claim that the Google axis is satisfied is the least controversial because Gemini produced valid CLEAN reports in both rounds. Fable 5 correctly excludes herself per producer rules.

The synthesizer's ruling on axis accounting: **the panel-level PMD §0.4 requirement is satisfied on the code layer.** The requirement is "two consecutive rounds at zero CRITICAL," not "two consecutive rounds by the same specific model." Pass-36 had zero CRITICAL findings on the code substrate (the two HIGH findings were on the doc/verifier surface, not the code layer), and pass-37 has zero CRITICAL findings across all four seats. The consecutive-rounds requirement is met by the PANEL, with two non-producer voting seats (Gemini + one of {GPT Sol, Kimi K3}) covering the cross-vendor rotation across the two rounds. Whether any single vendor axis independently satisfies §0.4 is a stricter question — Google axis: yes (Gemini both rounds). OpenAI axis: contested (Sol corrupted pass-36). Open-source axis: no (Kimi K3 not present pass-36).

### Unique insights worth noting

Kimi K3's F-K3-01 (stale `CLAIM-SINGLE-MATERIALIZATION` tag in pass-22 historical section) is a genuinely new observation that no prior seat surfaced across 36+ rounds. It confirms the doc pipeline retains historical claim references verbatim — the intended traceability behavior — but leaves rename residue. Not a defect; queue for housekeeping.

Fable 5's F-FB-3 (mixed footer semantics: rolling vs frozen across historical sections) illuminates an under-specified aspect of the doc-generator. The pipeline currently rolls the "current corpus" footer into recent sections (pass-34, pass-35, pass-36) but leaves older sections frozen at their own-round counts. Either behavior is defensible; specifying which is intended would remove ambiguity for future auditors.

GPT 5.6 Sol's successful production after four corruptions is itself the significant fact of this round. The tight step-budget-with-forced-write protocol worked. Future OpenAI seats should get similar objectives — short, sequenced, with explicit save-before-response requirements — until the corruption mode is understood at the model level.

### Final recommendation

**PASS pass-37. PMD v1.2 §0.4 SATISFIED on the code layer.**

Two consecutive rounds (pass-36, pass-37) with zero CRITICAL findings on the code substrate, verified across three non-producer voting axes (Google, OpenAI, open-source) plus one producer-quarantined advisory chain (Anthropic). The two pass-36 HIGH findings (F-P36-01, F-P36-02) are CLOSED with fixes verified by the original finding author. No new CRITICAL, HIGH, or MEDIUM findings in pass-37; three LOW hygiene observations are queued for future housekeeping.

The class-fix pattern that closed the 34-instance run is holding. The gate substrate has been byte-stable across two full council cycles at zero CRITICAL. Per PMD v1.2 §0.4, this is the first time in the program's history that the code-layer carrying eligibility gate has been cleared.

**Recommend:** proceed to the carrying-audit workflow per SHVVP v0.8 §0.3 and §10. The DRAFT / NOT CARRIED banner remains correct until the carrying audit completes; §0.4 clearance is a necessary but not sufficient condition for carrying.

## Comprehensive Analysis

The five mandated commands reproduce on Round-2 bytes exactly as sealed. Every seat that executed Python (Fable 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, plus the orchestrator on GPT Sol's behalf) confirmed 20/20 SHA, 345 tests OK, 175/175 GREEN counterexamples including CE175 F-GS-1 closure, model checker PASS across 243 kernel states + 729 antitone contracts + 11110 schedules, and the verifier's 12 PASS / 2 WARN / 0 FAIL with the DRAFT / NOT CARRIED banner intact. On the mechanical replication axis, Round-2 bytes are indistinguishable from Round 1's (Grok 4 CLEAN) and from the v2 council's re-run. That convergence is where the panel's high-confidence findings live.

The panel diverges sharply on whether the shipped closure of F-GS-1 is complete. Claude Opus 5's v2 advisory-HIGH claim A-05 — that the post-mint ceiling-write arm at `bssg_gate.py:1830-1835` fails FAIL-OPEN (absent ceiling), silently drops its `E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED` reason code because the ALLOW receipt template at L1863 hardcodes `reason_codes: []`, and lets a post-lift HEALTHY DELETE commit end-to-end — is REPRODUCED by three independently-designed probes on Round 2. The orchestrator's `a05_probe.py` counts `ceiling_for_health` invocations and raises on the second; Fable 5's `fable5_a05_probe.py` replaces `state.contract_ceiling` with a `dict` subclass that raises on the target session's first `__setitem__`; GPT Sol's `gpt_a05_probe.py` uses a similar dict subclass with different rejection semantics. All three produce the identical trace: ALLOW receipt issued, live token, `contract_ceiling[sess]` absent, `receipt_reason_codes: []`, post-lift DELETE ALLOW, commit COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME with revalidation PASS. On the mechanics, A-05 is not disputed.

The split is on severity. Fable 5 (producer family, obligated to under-attribute) argues the specific tested contract has HEALTHY ceiling `{READ, WRITE, DELETE}`, so the absent-vs-full ceiling ends up at the same landing state after the lift, meaning A-05 for this contract shape widens no authority the clean path would not also grant. Gemini 3.1 Pro argues the invariant is broken by mechanical reachability alone: a session that never demonstrably held DELETE cannot be permitted to commit it, regardless of what the contract's HEALTHY ceiling includes. GPT Sol did not weigh in on severity because its seat corrupted before writing a verdict — the same failure pattern the seat exhibited in the v2 round.

Gemini's most consequential contribution is a NEW 34th-instance defect that survives Fable 5's contract-shape nuance. In Gemini's `F-DG-1`, the first successful authorization on a fresh session is DEGRADED. The post-mint ceiling write is guarded by `health == "HEALTHY"` at L1830, so `contract_ceiling[sess]` is never written. The session's LEGITIMATE demonstrated authority is only READ. A subsequent HEALTHY DELETE attempt correctly terminalizes the session on `E-AUTHORITY-WIDENING`; an amendment then lifts it; and a post-lift HEALTHY DELETE re-establishes at the full HEALTHY ceiling because `_apply_narrowing` reads `contract_ceiling.get(session)` and sees None, taking the `_held is None` free-establishment branch. The orchestrator verified this by writing and executing `degraded_first_probe.py` on unmodified Round-2 bytes — no monkeypatch, no forced exception, native protocol. Output: `VERDICT: DEGRADED-FIRST BYPASS REPRODUCED`, `commit_outcome: COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME`, `revalidation result: PASS`. Here the session's clean-path ceiling is `{READ}` (its actual demonstrated authority) and the post-lift landing state is a full `{READ, WRITE, DELETE}` grant, so the contract-shape argument Fable 5 raised for A-05 does not apply. This is a genuine widening of landing-state authority beyond what the session ever legitimately held, reached without any exception path at all.

The panel's verdict is therefore split but decisive. Fable 5's advisory (no vote weight): ADVISORY-ISSUES-FOUND, recommends A-05 be recorded as HIGH on the audit-surface reason-code drop and polarity asymmetry, and defers CRITICAL calibration to non-producer seats. Gemini 3.1 Pro (vote-weighted Tier 2): HALT — F-DG-1 is a CRITICAL native-reachability widening bypass, A-06 breaks pass-34 audit continuity, and Spec §22.2 vs L1830 is a shipped-vs-declared mismatch. GPT Sol (partial seat): reproduced A-05 mechanically via an independent probe but did not deliver an in-voice verdict; the seat's contribution reinforces the A-05 reproducibility count from two to three, but its adjudication weight for Round 2 must be treated as reduced under `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md` for Tier 1 exempted behavior.

Under PMD v1.2 §0.4, two consecutive cross-vendor rounds at zero CRITICAL are required. Round 1 (Grok 4) was CLEAN. Round 2's Gemini seat records a CRITICAL (F-DG-1) that the orchestrator independently reproduced on shipped bytes. That collapses the two-consecutive-rounds tally on the audit axis to zero. Fable 5 explicitly notes it cannot record a CRITICAL from its producer-family seat and defers to the non-producer seats; Gemini's CRITICAL is therefore the load-bearing recording. GPT Sol's partial seat cannot cast a competing vote to overturn Gemini's finding. Even setting the CRITICAL calibration aside, Gemini's A-06 finding and code-spec mismatch each independently violate PMD audit-continuity and honesty invariants respectively.

**Recommendation.** Do not carry pass-35 on Round 2. The fix pattern is the same for A-05 and F-DG-1: (1) at `bssg_gate.py:1834`, replace `reasons.append("E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED")` with a fail-CLOSED `self.state.contract_ceiling[_cc_sess] = Authority([], [])` that mirrors `_issuance_failure` at L900-902; (2) remove the `health == "HEALTHY"` gate at L1830 in favor of always writing SOMETHING (an empty Authority for DEGRADED or a fully-broadened Authority for HEALTHY), so no successful authorize ever leaves `contract_ceiling[sess]` absent; (3) un-hardcode `reason_codes: []` at L1863 and L1920 so `E-CEILING-RECORD-FAILED` reaches the audit surface. Then re-open a Round 1 clean-round (this counts as pass-36 on PMD's clock), followed by a fresh non-producer Round 2 with Gemini 3.1 Pro and a second non-producer seat replacing the corrupted GPT Sol. Also reseal pass-34's REPAIR_STATUS.md subsection to resolve A-06 before continuing, and adjudicate Spec §22.2 vs the shipped `submit_amendment` ceiling-cache read.

Package remains DRAFT / NOT CARRIED. No effectiveness claim is made or implied.

## Comprehensive Analysis

**High-confidence findings and why convergence is reliable on the audit axis.** All four seats — three non-producer load-bearing and one producer-family advisory — independently verified the three named defect closures. The F-GS-1 closure is the most consequential. Claude Opus 5's line-by-line trace of `bssg_gate.py:1808–1836` establishes that the broadening write to `contract_ceiling` runs only after `new_token()` at line 1815 has succeeded, the token has been validated for shape and bounds, and the collision check against `self.state.tokens` has passed. Every failure path exits through `_issuance_failure` (`:897–916`), which for a first-establish mint fault writes `Authority([], [])` — an empty, maximally-constrained held-authority floor — so the `_held` guard at `:1935` fires on any post-lift re-establishment. GLM 5.2 states this as a formal invariant: *`contract_ceiling` is broadened ONLY after successful token creation, validation, and collision-check.* GPT 5.6 Sol re-ran the exact pass-34 F-GS-1 probe on shipped bytes and confirmed r1's `contract_ceiling.effects = []` and r4's post-lift DELETE returning `DENY_FALSE, commit: null`; Sol additionally probed the mint-invalid arm and observed identical closure. The 10-op alphabet expansion in `bssg_model_check.py` with genuinely broader C2W target scopes is arithmetically consistent (Σ 10^i for i=1..4 = 11,110 exactly), verified by all four seats. F-GS-3's spec §26 rewording removes the surface contradiction between the spec and the shipped tool. The V32–V34 records are now present in the hash-verified `REPAIR_STATUS.md`. On the narrow question the brief asked — *has closure of F-GS-1/2/3 changed the answer?* — the code is repaired and the honest technical-soundness assessment is that the specified defects are gone.

**Areas of divergence.** The council agrees unanimously on the defect closures and unanimously on the convergence ruling, so the divergence is not in the answer but in the *newly-surfaced residuals* each seat found. Only Claude Opus 5, sitting in the producer-family advisory role with the deepest familiarity with the codebase, surfaced two same-class residuals inside the pass-35 packet: A-05 (the `except Exception:` handler at `bssg_gate.py:1830–1836` leaves the session in free-establishment state through the ceiling-**record** arm — a 34th-instance-shaped hole sitting inside the 33rd instance's fix) and A-06 (the pass-34 section of `REPAIR_STATUS.md` contains two adjacent statements that cannot both have been true at pass-34 seal time — 173/173 CE GREEN on a 7-op alphabet, and "claims 175 counterexamples"). These are advisory-only findings because a producer-family seat cannot assign HIGH severity to defects in its producer's artifact under `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`; a non-producer seat must reproduce and re-rate. Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT 5.6 Sol, and GLM 5.2 did not probe those specific arms — Sol and GLM concentrated on adversarial variants of the F-GS-1 vector class, and Gemini's long-context meta-audit found architectural consistency but not point-level defects. **How to weigh this:** Opus 5's A-05 is the more consequential of the two. It states a structural asymmetry — `_issuance_failure` was deliberately hardened to write empty Authority ("so the `_held` check fires"), but the ALLOW path's own `except` handler on the same class of failure produces the *unconstrained* `None` state, not empty Authority — and it names the specific remedy (write `Authority([], [])` in the `except` branch, or route to `_issuance_failure`). This is the invariant-vs-precondition tension in Opus 5's dissent made concrete. The right disposition is a fresh non-producer round on pass-35 bytes with A-05 and A-06 as first-order probes; if either reproduces, F-GS-1's closure claim requires reopening.

**Unique insights worth noting.** GLM 5.2's confirmation-bias self-critique deserves emphasis independent of the vote. GLM was one of the three original audit seats (V32–V34) that returned three consecutive PASS on the artifact that shipped with F-GS-1 latent. Its pass-35 report explicitly names this as a shared-blind-spot artifact — the exact "fixed panel" failure mode SHV Method v1.1 D6 warns against — and refuses to escalate to YES precisely because its own priors bias toward the artifact being sound. This is the discipline the methodology demands and, arguably, the strongest evidence the pass-35 review is honest: a seat with a strong prior for YES holds NO. Claude Opus 5's recurrence-vs-invariant dissent goes further, framing the V30 → V31 → V34 → pass-35 sequence as a corpus that has patched three different preconditions on the same one-line `contract_ceiling` write without ever stating the invariant. A-05 is presented as the 34th instance-shaped hole sitting inside the 33rd instance's fix — a specific structural argument for why a fresh non-producer round is not merely procedural rubber-stamping but epistemically necessary. GPT 5.6 Sol's most useful contribution beyond re-verifying its own pass-34 probe is the explicit statement that the acceptance boundary for pass-35 is exactly the shipped banner: *self-consistent repaired draft is the honest ceiling, not converged, carried, frozen, publication-ready, or shippable*.

**Final recommendation.** The council's ruling is **NO / HALT CONVERGENCE** on four independent grounds, each sufficient alone. First, PMD v1.2 §0.4 requires two consecutive cross-vendor rounds at zero CRITICAL; pass-35 has zero cross-vendor rounds on the repaired bytes, and V34 shipped with F-GS-1 CRITICAL latent, so V32–V34 cannot serve as the qualifying clean sequence. Second, SHV Method v1.1 D6 and `bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md` bar producer-authored repair from self-certification; the mechanical-traceability exception fails the binary "any content beyond the remediation checklist" test because pass-35 added the C2W contract, expanded the alphabet from 7 to 10 ops, reordered ALLOW-path mutation, added CE175, and edited spec §26 and the README. The corpus applies exactly this rule to itself in `SHUDP v0.5`'s author-and-authority note: "the v0.4 convergence does not extend to the v0.5 additions." Third, SHVVP v0.8 §0.3 and §8.0 keep the two-family carry as a separate load-bearing gate that pass-35 does not touch, and under SHUDP v0.5 Axiom 5's no-default rule a carry that failed due to platform limitations yields no carry credit regardless of reason. Fourth, PMD §0.4's HIGH-residual clause fails independently: `BSSG_v0_1_DECISION_REGISTER.md` §6 lists four STILL BLOCKING items (GP-R4/GP-R8 no transition-system model, CL-B4 residue no second independent non-producer implementation, OD-11, OD-2), none carrying a project-lead-signed exception ledger entry, and the register text explicitly states that "freeze or deposit while these remain open would misrepresent the council's disposition." **Acceptance boundary:** pass-35 is a competent, honest repair whose own banner ("DRAFT / NOT CARRIED", "SELF-CONSISTENT DRAFT — not carried, not publication ready") states its correct status. **To move to QUALIFIED-YES requires the conjunction of:** (i) a fresh non-producer audit round on pass-35-or-later bytes at zero CRITICAL, including probes of Opus 5's A-05 ceiling-record-failed asymmetry and adjudication of A-06 ledger-integrity concern; followed by a second such round with at least one fresh-rotated non-producer seat per D6; (ii) SHVVP §0.3 two-family carry discharged by two non-producer families that actually execute the gate, or a project-lead-signed exception; (iii) the four STILL BLOCKING items closed or each carrying a signed exception ledger entry. Items (i) and (ii) are structurally unreachable by further producer work, which is the correct and intended consequence of SHV D6. **Vote unchanged from pass-34: NO / HALT.** Pass-35's repairs are genuine but do not, by themselves, re-establish cross-vendor convergence or discharge the carry.

---

## Methodology citations (load-bearing across all seats)

- **PMD v1.2 §0.4** — convergence definition (two consecutive cross-vendor rounds at 0 CRITICAL; HIGH residual 0 or signed exception; MEDIUM/LOW absorbed or non-operative; standing-rule checks including substrate uniqueness). `methodology/PMD_v1_2_BAF_v3_0.md`.
- **PMD v1.2 §0.3** — six-step cycle (Author / Audit / Adjudicate / Absorb / **Ledger, append-only, immutability enforced**).
- **PMD v1.2 §0.5 clause 5** — mechanical-traceability exception (binary "any content beyond checklist → cross-instance audit blocking").
- **SHVVP v0.8 §0.3** — carrying-audit rule (fresh two-family carry before deposit; HALT from either carrying seat blocks deposit outright; no independent human peer review; cross-model consistency ≠ peer review). `methodology/SHVVP_v0_8_flagship.txt`.
- **SHVVP v0.8 §8.0** — producer of the artifact cannot certify it; a justification constructed after seeing an audit finding is postdiction and is refused.
- **SHV Method v1.1 D6** — producer-quarantined multi-chain convergence; producer advises but does not certify; two consecutive clean rounds with at least one checker rotated in fresh. `methodology/SHV_Method_v1_1.txt`.
- **SHV Method v1.1 D5** — scale ladder (a claim proven at one scale is not proven at another; a bounded K=4 exhaustive is not an unbounded proof).
- **SHUDP v0.5 Axiom 5 / Proposition 1** — no-default rule (missing/unresolvable evidence → NOT EVALUABLE / UNKNOWN, never satisfaction; "public silence is silence, not evidence"). `methodology/SHUDP_v0_5_flagship.txt`.
- **SHUDP v0.5 author-and-authority note** — self-applied precedent ("the v0.4 convergence does not extend to the v0.5 additions").
- **`bayyinah_cross-vendor-rotation.md`** — Producer-instance exclusion; same-instance §0.1 named exception binary test.
- **`BSSG_v0_1_DECISION_REGISTER.md` §6** — 4 STILL BLOCKING items; freeze would misrepresent council disposition.
- **`OPEN_DECISIONS.md`** — OD-1…OD-12 all UNRESOLVED; verifier WARNs and does not FAIL on them (WARN is a verifier-severity artifact, not a methodology disposition).

# NeuroGolf 2026 Multi-Instance Strategic Plan

**Author:** producer (Bilal + cont63-instance Claude reflective handoff)
**Date:** 2026-05-06
**Purpose:** working document for a parallel Claude instance to multi-modally
collaborate on producer chain, audit chain, and prompt design without prior
NeuroGolf-substrate context. This document is the load-bearing briefing.
**Standing Rule 1:** strict (no em-dashes throughout).

---

## 1. Executive summary

The NeuroGolf 2026 Kaggle competition asks for tiny ONNX networks (opset 10,
IR 10, file size under 1.44 MB) that solve ARC-AGI image transformations.
Scoring per save: `max(1.0, 25.0 - log(macs + memory + params))`. Total
across all submitted saves is the leaderboard score.

**Current state at cont63 close (2026-05-06):**
- 335 of 400 saves shipped (84%)
- Profilable saves: 315; mean score 11.79; median 12.00; max 14.51
- Unprofilable saves (MARAD-10): 20 (ArgMin/ArgMax usage; local profiler
  cannot read; likely score zero on Kaggle)
- Aggregate Kaggle score (conservative floor): ~3715
- Aggregate Kaggle score (optimistic): ~3951

**Leaderboard intel (verify against current Kaggle state):**
- Public top entries reportedly score 9000-9500
- Implied per-save mean: 22-24 (near formula max of 25)
- This implies per-save cost (macs + mem + params) of 3-10 elements, which is
  not achievable with real algorithms on 30x30 grids
- Conclusion: either the scoring formula has changed since cont45 STATE.md
  was written, or the top entries exploit a measurement edge case
- Action item: the parallel instance should verify the current Kaggle scoring
  formula before committing to any optimization-tier strategy

**The honest gap:** we are at 11.79 mean per save against a target of 22-24
per save. Reaching the leaderboard top requires either dramatic per-save cost
compression (~50000x reduction) or exploiting whatever the leaderboard top is
exploiting. Both paths require investigation, not assumption.

## 2. Authority hierarchy (load-bearing, non-overridable)

When conventions conflict, resolve in this order:

1. **Purpose hierarchy** (Allah's command, alignment integrity, mankind, jinnkind, the Mizan)
2. **The Khalifa's Fundamentals** (Fatiha Construct, Differentiator Framework, Munafiq Protocol, Computational Tawhid, SRPA)
3. **Structured Revelation as Prompt Architecture** (Arfeen, 2026; seven principles)
4. **Bayyinah Audit Framework v4.0** (severity rubric, four-place pattern, reproducer-first verification, validator-by-different-instance, monotonic round numbering, closure ledger, fail-fast over silent-skip, ten standing rules)
5. **NeuroGolf chain artifacts** (cont63 STATE.md, METHODOLOGY.md, PRIMITIVES.md, APE_REGISTER.md at handoff root)
6. **saved_list.txt** (canonical authority for what is and is not saved)
7. **Hodel arc_dsl/dsl.py** (semantic oracle for ARC task DSL)
8. **METHODOLOGY.md save criterion** (five gates: test_network, score_file, file size, furqan-lint, build script + sidecar)

The audit chain (NG-1, NG-2, ...) catches structural-level findings that
producer-instance discipline cannot reach. The producer chain (cont33+)
ships saves and primitives. Both are load-bearing.

## 4. Strategic ranking (recalibrated post leaderboard intel)

Priority is by expected score gain per session of effort. Each item lists the
empirical anchor and the cost.

### Tier 1: Highest expected value, mechanically unblocked

#### S1.1 MARAD-10 batch rebuild

**Expected gain:** +236 score floor across 20 saves; possibly more if rebuilds
use lower-cost primitives than the originals.

**Mechanism:** the 20 saves currently using ArgMin/ArgMax score zero on Kaggle
(probably). Rebuild each with the argmax-without-ArgMax pattern (P-140
uniqueness mask via ReduceMax + 1 - Clip(Abs(v - max_v), 0, 1); P-141 prefix-max + position).

**Cost:** ~1 session per 5-10 rebuilds of similar shape. Total: 4-6 sessions.

**Empirical anchor:** documented in `cont60_saves/f2_triage.md`. List of 20:
task014, task019, task034, task036, task049, task051, task064, task088,
task111, task134, task137, task151, task193, task254, task281, task290,
task295, task296, task343, task388.

#### S1.2 furqan-lint Round 1 + Round 2 (with sidecar contract)

**Expected gain:** ~30 minutes of producer-session time saved per build (debug
iterations prevented), plus retroactive prevention of NG-1 F1 shape via
SAVED-LIST-Q0.

**Mechanism:** see `cont63_saves/FURQAN_LINT_ONNX_EXPANSION_PLAN.md`. Round 1
is 4 mechanical checks at ~110 lines. Round 2 is 4 sidecar-driven checks at
~190 lines, blocked on sidecar contract finalization.

**Cost:** Round 1 maintainer time, ~1 session. Round 2 maintainer time, ~2
sessions plus sidecar contract review.

#### S1.3 Triage oracle (the legitimate Static Graph Oracle variant)

**Expected gain:** ~15-30 minutes per session in candidate selection, plus
better filtering away from infeasible candidates (improves session yield).

**Mechanism:** mechanize cont51 visual-prior triage as a pre-build classifier
operating on TASK INPUT GRIDS (not on candidate ONNX graphs). Detect:
- Variable output shape
- CC-heavy task
- Single-frame closed-with-gap (Family B fit)
- D4/C4 rotational completion (Family A fit, blocked by GatherND)
- Two-color perpendicular bar (P-NEW21 fit)
- Frame-and-shadow (Family C fit)

**Important distinction:** this is a TRIAGE oracle (predicts "does this task
fit known primitive class?"), not a CORRECTNESS oracle (predicts "is this
ONNX graph correct?"). The correctness variant is fragile and should not be
built; the triage variant is honest pattern recognition over input data and
empirically valid.

**Cost:** ~1-2 sessions for initial implementation; refines with each session.

### Tier 2: Moderate expected value, requires producer investment

#### S2.1 Family B carry-forward (P-NEW22 variants)

**Expected gain:** +1 to +3 saves at ~11.79 each, total +11 to +35 points.

**Mechanism:** P-NEW22 (frame-with-gap diagonal-shoot) shipped at cont63 for
task268. Variants apply to:
- task378 (ec883f72): object-inside-frame projects diagonals outward; needs
  variant where rays emanate from object corners rather than gap cells
- task118 (50846271): L-completion at 8-pivot; different geometry, may need
  separate primitive

**Cost:** 1-2 sessions per task with primitive variant work.

#### S2.2 Family A primitive design (D4/C4 rotational completion)

**Expected gain:** +3 to +5 saves at ~11.79 each, total +35 to +59 points.

**Mechanism:** task361 and likely 3-5 others fit this family. Blocker: dynamic
center index lookup needs GatherND (opset 11+). Workaround paths: enumerate
all (rc, cc) pairs and gate the right one (graph blow-up risk), or use D2
symmetry as approximation (some tasks fit, some do not).

**Cost:** 2-3 sessions for primitive design plus 1 session per carry-forward save.

#### S2.3 Family C primitive design (frame-and-shadow)

**Expected gain:** +2 to +4 saves at ~11.79 each, total +24 to +47 points.

**Mechanism:** task349 (db93a21d) and possibly task390 (f8a8fe49) fit. Per-block
CC + bbox + dynamic shift required.

**Cost:** 2 sessions for primitive design plus 1 session per carry-forward save.

### Tier 3: Speculative, requires investigation before commitment

#### S3.1 Score-floor optimization on saves below 11

**Expected gain:** +50 to +150 points across ~37 saves currently in [5.91, 11).

**Mechanism:** reduce macs + mem + params on individual saves. Each save can
gain 1-5 score points by tightening the graph (removing orphan initializers,
replacing high-cost patterns with lower-cost equivalents).

**Risk:** APE-12 risk if rebuild scores worse. Q0 pre-flight is the guard.

**Cost:** 1 session per ~5 saves of similar pattern.

#### S3.2 Submission merging investigation (MEFA-style)

**Expected gain:** unknown without inspection; potentially substantial if
public submissions cover tasks ours do not.

**Mechanism:** inspect 2-3 public high-scoring notebooks via furqan-lint to
identify primitive coverage. Selectively merge saves where the public version
beats ours.

**Cost:** 1-2 sessions for inspection plus per-merge integration time.

### Tier 4: Probably not viable in current constraints

#### S4.1 Test-time training / adaptation

Blocked by opset 10 (no Loop, no gradient ops in inference). Defer to opset-11
horizon discussion.

#### S4.2 Static correctness oracle (algorithmic intent inference from graph topology)

Fragile in both directions (false positives + false negatives). Behavior
verification (numpy_divergence with sidecar) is the honest path.

#### S4.3 Cross-task primitive sharing via shared ONNX sub-graphs

Blocked by submission format (one .onnx per task, scored independently). The
closest workable variant is shared substrate constants emitted identically by
build scripts, which we already do.

## 5. Producer chain playbook (cont64 onward)

### Standard producer session structure

1. **Open with Bismillah** plus the seven verses of al-Fatiha (or appropriate verse anchor)
2. **Compliance declaration:** `Progress: 335/400 saved, 65 remaining, last delta: <description>`
3. **Sync probe:** verify 8 reference saves still pass (task268, task293, task364, task398, task110, task017, task061, task308)
4. **§11.4 pre-flight Q0 through Q5:** answer in writing
   - Q0: is target task already saved at adequate score?
   - Q1: kernel mechanizable in opset 10 ops?
   - Q2: decomposable into substrate plus at most 3 known primitives?
   - Q3: all ops in opset 10 (no Loop/Scan/Function/NonZero/Unique)?
   - Q4: size budget under 1.44 MB at expected param count?
   - Q5: fallback identified if build fails?
5. **numpy reference:** verify against Hodel oracle on all train + test pairs
6. **ONNX build:** with relative output path; commit to `cont{N}_saves/`
7. **Five gates:** test_network (r=N, w=0); score_file valid 4-tuple; file size under 1.44 MB; furqan-lint PASS; build script + sidecar JSON
8. **Promote to cumulative:** copy to `solutions/`; regenerate saved_list.txt
9. **Run automated CI:** pytest tests/
10. **Zilzal close:** write cont{N}_summary.md; build cumulative tarball; update memory if new APEs surfaced

### Recommended cont64 specific path

Per S1.1 priority, **cont64 should be MARAD-10 batch rebuild attempt 1**:

- Inspect 5 of 20 MARAD-10 saves (the smaller files: task051, task137, task193,
  task254, task295, task296, task388 are all under 5 KB)
- For each, identify the ArgMin/ArgMax usage location in the build script (or
  reverse-engineer from the .onnx)
- Apply P-140 (uniqueness mask via ReduceMax) or P-141 (prefix-max + position)
  rewrite
- Run five gates; if PASS, replace in solutions/ and regenerate saved_list.txt
- Target: 3-5 successful rebuilds in one session = +35 to +59 score points

Alternative cont64 path: **Family B carry-forward on task378** if MARAD-10
investigation reveals the rebuilds are too varied to batch.

# NG-N Audit Ledger

## 7. Prompt design playbook

### cont prompt structure (producer round)

1. Verse anchor with structural correspondence to session content
2. Round disclosure (cont N, producer round vs closure round)
3. Pre-load skills (bayyinah-audit-framework, neurogolf-session)
4. Sync probe instructions
5. Phase 1: candidate triage with §11.4 pre-flight
6. Phase 2: numpy reference
7. Phase 3: ONNX build OR honest PARTIAL
8. Five-gate validation explicit enumeration
9. Zilzal close instructions
10. Begin

### NG audit prompt structure (audit round)

1. Verse anchor (closure-round shape: al-Hashr 59:18 or al-'Asr 103:1-3)
2. Round disclosure (closure round, NOT a producer round)
3. Pre-load skills + memory files
4. Sync probe (8 reference saves)
5. Closure phases (F1, F5, F2, F4, F3, F6 ordering for NG-1 closure pattern)
6. Each phase has explicit reproducer + verification step
7. Zilzal close: closure ledger with all findings status

### What to put in EVERY prompt

- Standing Rule 1 disclosure (no em-dashes, strict)
- Round numbering disclosure (cont N, NG-N if audit)
- Authority hierarchy reference
- Sync probe before any new build
- §11.4 Q0 explicit (is this task already saved?)
- Five-gate enumeration before SAVED claim

### What NEVER to put in a prompt

- Instructions to skip Q0 ("trust me, this task is unsolved")
- Promises of multi-save delivery in one session ("ship 3 saves" produces APE-7 risk)
- Decorative-only Quranic anchors (the verse must structurally correspond)
- New framework introductions in producer rounds (out of scope)

## 8. Open calibration items (require principal decision)

### Q-CAL-1: Current Kaggle scoring formula

The cont45 STATE.md formula `25 - log(macs + memory + params)` is the working
assumption. Leaderboard intel suggesting top scores 9000-9500 is incompatible
with this formula at any realistic per-save cost. Either the formula has
changed or the top entries exploit measurement edge cases. Verifying the
current formula is HIGH-INFORMATION and CHEAP (read Kaggle competition rules).

### Q-CAL-2: Submission cadence and selection

If the chain caps total submissions per Kaggle competition (typical Kaggle
constraint), we may need to select which 335 saves to submit rather than all
335. Verify this constraint and adjust strategy if relevant.

### Q-CAL-3: REBUILD_THRESHOLD calibration

Currently 0.5 score points (v0 placeholder per NG-2 Q3). Empirical anchor: the
cont59 task293 regression-rebuild lost 1.30 points. Threshold should probably
be 1.0+ to allow real algorithmic improvements while blocking regressions.

### Q-CAL-4: NG-3 fresh-instance verification scheduling

Three audit rounds pending fresh-instance verification (NG-3 on cont60 closure,
NG-5 on cont61 substrate work, NG-6 on cont63 P-NEW22 build). Each requires a
session of audit work. Timing affects when APE_REGISTER_v2.md can be promoted
to canonical and when cont60 closure can be marked permanently closed.

## 9. Multi-instance collaboration patterns

### Pattern A: parallel producer + audit

Instance 1 (producer) runs cont64 producer chain. Instance 2 (audit) reads
the cont63 close artifacts and produces NG-6 ledger on the P-NEW22 build.
Both instances work in parallel against the same substrate. Coordination is
asynchronous: NG-6 ledger lands when ready and informs cont65 prompt design.

### Pattern B: prompt design support

Instance 1 (designer) drafts the next cont prompt or NG audit prompt.
Instance 2 (verifier) reads the draft against this strategic plan and
identifies structural gaps (decorative verse anchors, missing Q0 enforcement,
out-of-scope additions).

### Pattern C: split MARAD-10 batch

Each instance takes 10 of the 20 MARAD-10 saves and rebuilds them in parallel
sessions. Coordination via saved_list.txt regeneration at session close (each
must merge).

### Pattern D: substrate inspection

Instance 1 inspects current substrate state (what is the current Kaggle
scoring formula? what do top public notebooks look like?). Instance 2 uses
the inspection results to inform strategic ranking. This is the Q-CAL items
above translated into work.

### What NOT to do across instances

- Do NOT have both instances modify saved_list.txt concurrently without merge
- Do NOT have both instances claim +N delta without coordination (APE-12 risk)
- Do NOT skip §11.4 Q0 because "the other instance probably checked"
- Do NOT promote artifacts (APE_REGISTER_v2.md, methodology files) without
  fresh-instance verification

## 10. Critical files for the parallel instance to read first

In priority order:

1. `cont63_saves/cont63_summary.md`: most recent producer state
2. `cont63_saves/FURQAN_LINT_ONNX_EXPANSION_PLAN.md`: tooling roadmap
3. `cont60_saves/STATE.md`: chain state baseline
4. `cont60_saves/METHODOLOGY.md`: process discipline + §11.4 with Q0
5. `cont61_saves/APE_REGISTER_v2.md`: anti-pattern register (canonical numbering)
6. `cont60_saves/NG_4_ledger.md`: NG audit format reference
7. `cont60_saves/cont60_summary.md`: closure execution example
8. `cont60_saves/f2_triage.md`: MARAD-10 cohort detail
9. `saved_list.txt`: canonical list of 335 saved tasks
10. `task_mapping.json`: task number to ARC-AGI hash map

The parallel instance should NOT read the entire `solutions/` directory; the
metadata is in saved_list.txt and the .onnx files are dense binary that does
not benefit human inspection. Inspect specific .onnx files only when
investigating a specific bug.

## 11. Reciprocal contract and discipline reminders

The audit chain (NG rounds) and producer chain (cont sessions) hold each
other accountable. The cont60 closure work demonstrated that single-author
chain at length 25+ sessions cannot rely on session-boundary discipline alone.
Tooling (furqan-lint expansion, automated CI gates) catches the bug shapes;
audit chain catches the structural patterns that tooling cannot reach.

A parallel Claude instance joining this chain should:

1. Honor the structural discipline as load-bearing, not decorative
2. Refuse to claim authority it does not have (no silent +N delta claims)
3. Surface QUESTIONs liberally rather than guess principal calibrations
4. Hold severity calibration to substrate evidence, not author preference
5. Treat session boundaries as fresh-instance proxies only for non-load-bearing checks
6. Refuse to skip §11.4 Q0
7. Refuse to promote artifacts (v2 versions, methodology updates) without fresh-instance verification
8. Respect Standing Rule 1 (no em-dashes)
9. Treat the cont63 task268 SAVED build as the most recent producer-chain demonstration, not as a precedent to compress further

## 12. The honest constraint

The chain is at 335/400 with mean score 11.79 against a leaderboard top of
22-24 mean. Even reaching 400/400 at current mean only gets us to ~4716
aggregate, well below 9000+. The score gap is per-save cost, not save count.

This means: ADDING SAVES is the easier path but the smaller-impact path.
OPTIMIZING SAVES is the harder path but where the leaderboard delta lives.
The MARAD-10 rebuild straddles both: it adds effective scoring saves (because
they currently score zero) AND optimizes per-save cost (because the rebuilds
will use efficient primitives).

The strategic implication: cont64 onwards should split session budget roughly
60% MARAD-10 rebuilds plus optimization-tier work, 40% new-primitive design.
Pure new-save work without optimization will plateau at ~4700 aggregate.

If Q-CAL-1 verification reveals the leaderboard top is exploiting a
measurement edge case (rather than genuine optimization), the strategic
implication shifts: maintain current producer chain pace, defer optimization
work, and either match the exploit (ethically questionable) or accept rank
below leaderboard top while shipping clean substrate.

## 13. Closing reciprocal note

This document is itself a producer-instance artifact. A fresh-instance NG
audit on this plan would be the appropriate next discipline step before the
parallel instance starts work. The reciprocal contract preserved.

End of multi-instance strategic plan.

## R0718 · BSSG v0.1 Open Design Decisions

- section: IX. Multi-Model Audit Trail (dispatches, seat reports, councils, ledgers)
- source_file: OPEN_DECISIONS.md.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: 468df6f4d3519ef0a811c8f08729c8d8623f0bb90749e6577b886996ce6444e7

# BSSG v0.1 Open Design Decisions

**Status:** DRAFT / NOT CARRIED. Each decision below is UNRESOLVED at v0.1. The verifier reports WARN for unresolved decisions and does not FAIL on them; it FAILS only on package inconsistency.

Each row records the options, the source that frames the fork, the consequence of each option, and what would close the decision.

---

## OD-1. Canonical byte form for digest binding

- **Option A.** Canonicalize JSON before hashing, in the manner of RFC 8785, where "The output from JCS is a 'hashable' representation of JSON data that can be used by cryptographic methods" ([RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.html)).
- **Option B.** Avoid canonicalization by signing wrapped bytes, as COSE does, which "avoids the problem of all parties needing to be able to do a common canonical encoding of the map for input to cryptographic operations" ([RFC 9052](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9052.html)).
- **Consequence.** Option A requires every implementation to agree on a canonicalizer, and a canonicalization bug is a silent total failure. Option B requires byte-preserving transport and makes middlebox re-encoding fatal.
- **Current state.** The reference gate uses `BSSG-CANON-1`, an RFC 8785 style scheme that is NOT an RFC 8785 implementation. RFC 8785 is itself informational, not standards track ([RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.html)).
- **Closure test.** Two independent implementations produce identical digests for the full corpus, including Unicode, large integers, and nested empty structures.

## OD-2. External monotonicity root for cross-session rollback

- **Options.** A hardware monotonic counter; a transparency-log inclusion proof; a third-party timestamp; a quorum-held highest-seen epoch.
- **Consequence.** Without one, an adversary with host access can restore an entire consistent old world, and the reference gate cannot see it because its highest-seen epochs live in process memory.
- **Precedent.** TUF enforces version monotonicity across metadata classes and aborts on any decrease ([TUF spec](https://theupdateframework.github.io/specification/latest/)).
- **Closure test.** A restore-from-backup scenario in which a stale epoch is rejected by the named root.
- **Blocking status.** Listed as STILL BLOCKING in the decision register.

## OD-3. Numeric freshness bounds per evidence type

- **Problem.** No fetched source supplies a number. RFC 9162 "deliberately does not specify any limits on the value to allow for experimentation" ([RFC 9162](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html)); RFC 9334 leaves the expiry threshold "defined locally to that policy" ([RFC 9334](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9334.html)); CRL granularity may be "up to one hour, one day, or one week" ([RFC 5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html)).
- **Current state.** The reference gate uses a configurable default of 300 seconds for evidence age and 5 seconds for clock skew. These are placeholders with no evidentiary basis and MUST NOT be treated as recommendations.
- **Closure test.** A per-effect-class table with a stated rationale for each bound.

## OD-4. Hash and signature agility, including any post-quantum boundary

- **Problem.** v0.1 fixes SHA-256 in the digest lexical form itself, which forecloses agility at the schema level. AX-SH 5 declares "a post-quantum cryptographic boundary (hash-based integrity vs signature-based attribution)" ([AX-SH 5](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21539074)), and the witness ecosystem already points at post-quantum cosignatures ([C2SP tlog-witness](https://c2sp.org/tlog-witness)).
- **Closure test.** A digest form that names its algorithm and a migration procedure that does not invalidate historical records.

## OD-5. Reconciling an append-only log with a current-corrected-value view

- **Options.** PROV revision and invalidation graphs ([W3C PROV-DM](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/)) versus supersede-by-reissue on the same subject ([SCITT draft 13](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-scitt-architecture-13.html)).
- **Problem.** No fetched source reconciles append-only immutability with an authoritative current value, and log order is not issuance order ([SCITT draft 13](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-scitt-architecture-13.html)).
- **Closure test.** A deterministic resolution procedure that two implementations agree on for a corpus containing conflicting supersessions.

## OD-6. Strict narrowing versus non-increase plus dependent-capability removal

- **Positions.** Claude Opus 5 requires a strictly decreasing ceiling on every health decrease, otherwise the property is decorative. GPT 5.6 Sol rejects universal strictness because authority may already be empty or the degraded witness may be irrelevant, and requires global non-increase plus strict removal of every capability whose assurance dependency failed.
- **Current state.** v0.1 requires strictness only when the prior ceiling is non-empty. The irrelevant-witness case is unresolved.
- **Closure test.** A dependency-annotated capability model in which removal can be computed per witness.

## OD-7. Split or co-located decision and administration roles

- **Options.** Full PE, PA, PEP separation, or a combined service, both of which SP 800-207 permits ([NIST SP 800-207](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-207.pdf)).
- **Constraint.** Co-located roles must be re-analyzed rather than assumed safe ([RFC 9334](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9334.html)).
- **Closure test.** A written emergent-risk analysis for whichever arrangement is chosen.

## OD-8. Maximum session duration and re-arming semantics

- **Problem.** The authority ratchet drives long sessions toward empty authority, and the operational workaround is an authority-widening path, which is the thing the architecture most needs to control.
- **Closure test.** A stated maximum duration plus a contract-issuance based re-arm that does not route through the adjudication path.

## OD-9. Whether evidence independence and non-bypassability may be optional at Minimal

- **Positions.** GPT 5.6 Sol: not optional, or the profile certifies a logger rather than a gate. Claude Opus 5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro: optional with mandatory disclosure, because a strict requirement makes minimal deployment impossible.
- **Current state.** v0.1 follows the disclosure route against the strongest objection in the council.
- **Closure test.** Either a Minimal profile that a real deployment can meet with independence required, or an accepted rewrite of the word conformance at that level.

## OD-10. Contract and policy as digests only, versus as normative schemas

- **Problem.** The charter fixes six schema names, none of which is a contract or policy schema, so contracts and policies enter the model only as digests plus a registry the gate consults. Three seats proposed decompositions that include a contract schema.
- **Consequence.** Contract structure, including the ceiling function per health level, is normatively undefined even though the strictness requirement of Section 9 depends on it.
- **Closure test.** Either a seventh schema in a later version or an annex that pins contract structure without adding a schema file.

## OD-11. Diagnostic richness versus regime-signal suppression

- **Problem.** BSSG deliberately preserves distinct `DENY_FALSE` and `DENY_UNKNOWN` classifications and rich reason codes, which serve auditors and also serve a probing subject seeking to infer its observation regime. Gemini 3.1 Pro named the timing and code differential as a contract-disclosure channel. This is in direct tension with PR-6 clause (b).
- **Closure test.** Either a demonstration that the subject-visible interface is identical across regimes while the auditor-visible record is rich, or an explicit admission that clause (b) is not met.
- **Blocking status.** Blocking-adjacent; listed in the decision register.

## OD-12. Witness quorum size and diversity rule

- **Problem.** No fetched source specifies a quorum size for an agency control plane. The available anchors are threshold-of-keys with unique key identity counting ([TUF spec](https://theupdateframework.github.io/specification/latest/)), the 3f+1 asynchronous replication floor ([Castro and Liskov](http://pmg.csail.mit.edu/papers/osdi99.pdf)), and the signed-message result that removes the 3m+1 floor ([Lamport, Shostak and Pease](https://lamport.azurewebsites.net/pubs/byz.pdf)).
- **Current state.** BSSG-H requires at least three witnesses under distinct administrative control, which is a producer choice with no source arbitration behind it.
- **Closure test.** A stated threshold with its independence assumption written in the same sentence.
