## 5. Five-model base layer

**Fractal Cube (WHERE).** L0 process: F-S04-52-06, -14, -15. L1 entry: F-S04-52-01, -02, -03, -12. L2 body: F-S04-52-04, -05, -11, -13. L3 gate: F-S04-52-07, -08, -09, -10. The generator concentration at L1 and L3 is diagnostic: entry-level claims and the gates that should check them are failing as a matched pair, not independently.

**Enzyme System (WHAT).** The v0.52 entry carries 21 provenance tags: COMPUTED 7, DIFF-VERIFIED 7, EXTERNAL 2, COUPLED 2, ASSERTED 2, ENUMERATED 1. Verification by enzyme: all 7 DIFF-VERIFIED body-repair claims verified true by inspection ([a] through [g] all landed); the ENUMERATED claim verified (31 = 31); of the 7 COMPUTED, five verified and two are false on shipped bytes (F-S04-52-02, and the EXTERNAL count in F-S04-52-03); of the 2 COUPLED, one is false (F-S04-52-01); the 2 EXTERNAL are unverifiable from the packet by construction and correctly tagged. Verified-true rate on internally checkable tags: 16 of 19.

**Replication Fork (HOW).** The six-phase pipeline (audit, disposition, body repair, correction append, reseal, gate extension) executed in order this round, with the gate extension ([9b] Provenance presence) landing in the same build as the defect it prevents. That is correct pipeline discipline. The break is at the reseal phase: correction (bi) was authored against a pre-reseal state and never re-derived after the v0.52 entry was appended, so the fork values it publishes describe a document that does not exist.

**Orbital (WHO).** I am Claude Opus 5, dispatched fresh with no prior-round context loaded and no seat-lineage files consulted before execution. Anchoring: **producer family** (Section 22.1 names Claude as the producer family). My verdict is advisory and non-binding by construction and cannot contribute to FB-7b. My independence claim is limited to session freshness; it is not family independence, and no part of this report should be counted toward the two-family carry.

**Cell Cycle (WHEN).** The chronic defect class is **producer-supplied evidence literals that are not byte-reproducible on shipped bytes**. Recurrence across the correction register: 13 of 62 corrections (21.0%) are of this class, at loci (i), (j), (l), (m), (o), (z), (ab), (ap), (aq), (as), (at), (bf), (bh). v0.52 repaired one instance ((bj), the v0.51 mutation-test literals) and introduced three more in the same build. The in-document Cell Cycle protocol states that after three failed repairs at a locus the producer may not attempt a fourth and a structural fix is required. This class has now been repaired by prose at least six times across the lineage. **The structural fix is prescribed in F-S04-52-07.**

## 6. Findings

### CRITICAL

**F-S04-52-01** CRITICAL / **Class A** -- correction (bi) publishes v0.52 "restored" seal values that no derivation from shipped bytes reproduces

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_52.md`:1248, correction (bi).
- **Substance:** (bi) states `v0.52 restored values (computed over Provenance-terminated span): ENTRY_v0.51 = d69efb11eea49e7ce2a527cc87bdb2fe27d576d2de9eeb4e99e417d43d960cf4, FULL_SECTION_27 = a35b774c8bfbb7f4d2a8cd1c49e3571fee2fa60d481f8840b51499ac8f65bdb5`. Shipped v0.52 bytes yield `ENTRY_v0.51 = 61fdc45fa4b787bf7c3096cc70a4facff11e99466563fbb846c2838e9fb59504` and `FULL_SECTION_27 = b3e2df6a1334a4bc8c18e96c61bd49ccae79b53b7299dec7aa2b6385a5ebfc72`, both confirmed by independent recomputation and by build.py [9b]. Neither published value appears anywhere in HISTORY.sha256. I tested 13 candidate derivations (raw span, stripped span, trailing-newline variants, with and without the v0.52 entry present, Provenance included and excluded); **none reproduces either value**. The claim carries a `[COUPLED: verified against shipped v0.51 packet and v0.52 build.py derivation]` tag, and the build.py derivation does not produce these numbers. Aggravating: the correction's stated purpose is to give an external verifier holding v0.51 bytes a documented expectation for the fork. A verifier who follows (bi) computes 61fdc45f/b3e2df6a, finds them unequal to the published expectation, and concludes the v0.52 packet is forged. The disclosure instrument inverts into a false forgery signal.
- **Disposition:** HALT. Do not correct (bi) in place -- it is sealed. Append correction (bk) at v0.53 stating the true shipped values `ENTRY_v0.51 = 61fdc45f...9504` and `FULL_SECTION_27 = b3e2df6a...fc72`, stating that the (bi) values are unreproducible and superseded, and stating explicitly which of the two value sets an external verifier should expect. Add a build.py gate at [9b] asserting that every 64-hex literal in the current entry that is presented as a seal value either matches a HISTORY.sha256 line or is explicitly labeled as a superseded prior-version value.
- **Cross-reference:** correction (bj) at the same entry, which repairs the identical defect class one version earlier; F-S04-52-07 (the gate that would catch it); Section 22.2 external-anchor discussion; Cell Cycle chronic-defect protocol.

**F-S04-52-02** CRITICAL / **Class A** -- the Provenance verification command is self-referential and its stated output is false on shipped bytes

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_52.md`:1246 (register item 1) and :1252 (body repair [f]).
- **Substance:** Both loci state `[COMPUTED: grep -c "Provenance and review status" xz_protocol_v0_52.md = 1]` and `[DIFF-VERIFIED: grep -c "Provenance and review status" = 1]`. Executed on shipped bytes, that command returns **3**: lines 1246 and 1252 match because each *quotes the search string*, and line 1255 is the actual paragraph. The count is 1 only for the marker form `\*Provenance and review status\.\*`, which is not the command cited. The act of citing the evidence changed the evidence. The underlying repair is sound -- the marker is genuinely present once and build.py [9b] verifies it independently -- but the sealed evidence citation is false as written, at two loci, under two different provenance tags.
- **Disposition:** HALT. Append correction (bl) at v0.53 recording that the cited command returns 3 on v0.52 bytes and that the byte-reproducible form is `grep -c '\*Provenance and review status\.\*'` = 1. For future entries, adopt the rule that a quoted verification command must be executable against the shipped artifact *including the entry that quotes it*, and prefer commands whose output is invariant to their own citation.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S04-52-01 and F-S04-52-03 (same class, same entry); standing boundary 17, "[9c] quoted-tag inflation," which names the adjacent mechanism but not this one.

## 7. VERDICT

> **Verdict: HALT (advisory, non-binding, producer family).**
>
> **Class ledger:** 4 Class A / 2 Class B / 2 Class C / 4 Class D / 3 Class E.
> **Severity ledger:** 2 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH / 5 MEDIUM / 4 LOW. Total 15.

The target condition -- non-HALT with zero Class A -- is not met on these bytes, and I have not softened toward it. Four Class A findings are byte-demonstrable: two published seal values that no derivation reproduces, a verification command whose stated output is off by a factor of three, a tag count contradicted by the build's own printed output, and a cardinal-range claim in Section 0.1 that is false under either reading.

What v0.52 did well should be recorded with equal precision, because an audit that only reports failures is not calibrated. The R10 defect is genuinely repaired: the Provenance marker is present, the PRIOR_HISTORY line terminates at 64 characters, all 52 seals verify under independent recomputation, `sha256sum -c` returns rc=0, and the new [9b] gate demonstrably fires when I delete the marker. All five prescribed mutations fire. All seven body repairs claimed at line 1252 landed. The FB-7b single-source-of-truth restructuring from v0.49 is holding -- there is no duplicate rationale to drift.

The structural diagnosis is narrower than the finding count suggests. Three of the four Class A findings, and the entire chronic pattern behind them, are one defect: **the producer writes numeric and command literals into the current entry as evidence, and no gate verifies those literals against the bytes that ship.** Thirteen of 62 corrections in the lineage are of this class. The build computes the refuting value for two of this round's three instances and prints it instead of asserting it. The in-document Cell Cycle protocol already prescribes the remedy for a defect class that has survived this many prose repairs: stop repairing instances, and gate the class. F-S04-52-07 states that gate.

Second-order observation from the biomedical lens, offered as measurement rather than blocker: semantic verification reaches 9.0% of the document, the ungated share has grown from 26.2% to 68.5% since v0.18, and gate scope is pinned to a current entry that is 2% of the artifact. The gates are not too few; they are pointed at too little. Widening the entry-scoped gates to iterate over all 52 sealed entries would cost little and would convert the largest inert compartment in the document into verified surface.

**Recommendation for R12.** Priority order: (1) implement the quoted-literal verification gate of F-S04-52-07 before any further prose corrections in this class; (2) append corrections (bk), (bl), (bm) for the three Class A literal defects, never editing (bi) or (bj) in place; (3) body-repair the Section 0.1 range and the Section 22.2 mutation register; (4) disposition the five unrecorded R10 advisory findings. Cross-vendor rotation: this seat is producer-family and advisory. The next carrying round needs a non-producer family -- Kimi K3 or GLM-5.2 -- and F-S04-52-01 in particular should be re-verified by a seat holding v0.51 bytes externally, since the fork values are exactly what an external holder is positioned to check and this seat is not.

### 4.5 Hurst exponent of the seal chain

52 `ENTRY` digests, hex converted to integer mod 2^16, ordered v0.1 through v0.52. Mean 32,600.8, population sd 18,826.5. Classical rescaled-range over windows {4, 8, 13, 16, 26, 52}:

| window n | windows | mean R/S |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 13 | 1.6247 |
| 8 | 6 | 2.4383 |
| 13 | 4 | 3.8978 |
| 16 | 3 | 3.7968 |
| 26 | 2 | 5.6446 |
| 52 | 1 | 7.1808 |

```
H (OLS slope, log-log)                       = 0.5986
Anis-Lloyd E[H] for i.i.d. noise at n = 52   = 0.6128
H - 0.5                                      = +0.0986
H - E[H]                                     = -0.0142
```

Measured against the naive 0.5 the chain looks mildly persistent; measured against the **correct finite-sample null** it is indistinguishable from random. That is the expected SHA-256 result: no structural bias in the input text is detectable through the digest.

**Methodological caveat, recorded as a standing observation.** This probe has zero diagnostic power on this artifact. SHA-256 destroys input structure by construction, so `H` approximately equal to `E[H]` is guaranteed whether the underlying text is honest or wholly forged. A clean Hurst result must not be counted as evidence of integrity in any future round.

## 5. Findings (six-element format)

### F-S02-52-01 -- CRITICAL / Class A

- **Locus:** Section 0.1, line 22 of `xz_protocol_v0_52.md`.
- **Substance:** The sentence reads `The full defect trajectory is in Section 27 (fifty-two amendment entries, v0.1 through v0.51)`. Section 27 contains 52 entries spanning v0.1 through **v0.52**. The count word is true; the range terminus is false on shipped bytes. Gate `[9]` generates the count word from the parsed entry count and asserts the phrase `fifty-two amendment entries` is present -- it PASSES -- but checks nothing about the adjoining range. At v0.51 the sentence read correctly (fifty-one entries, v0.1 through v0.51). The v0.52 producer updated exactly the token the gate reads and left the token the gate does not read. Gate `[9e]` cannot catch this: its cardinal-range regex requires the literal `consecutive` and a word from `two..ten`.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Correct the range to `v0.1 through v0.52`. Extend `[9]` to parse `v0.(\d+) through v0.(\d+)` adjacent to the count phrase and assert the terminus equals `VERSION`.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Claims / Narrative / Section 0.1 (UNGATED). Same class as F-FABLE5-06 (v0.17 stale Section 0.1 version prose). The gate that closed F-FABLE5-06 sweeps `DRAFT CANDIDATE` and `This document is` prose only.

### F-S02-52-02 -- CRITICAL / Class A

- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.52 entry, append-only correction (bi).
- **Substance:** The correction states `v0.52 restored values (computed over Provenance-terminated span): ENTRY_v0.51 = d69efb11eea49e7ce2a527cc87bdb2fe27d576d2de9eeb4e99e417d43d960cf4, FULL_SECTION_27 = a35b774c8bfbb7f4d2a8cd1c49e3571fee2fa60d481f8840b51499ac8f65bdb5`, tagged `[COUPLED: verified against shipped v0.51 packet and v0.52 build.py derivation]`. Both values are false against the shipped packet:
  - Shipped `HISTORY.sha256` carries `ENTRY_v0.51 = 61fdc45fa4b787bf7c3096cc70a4facff11e99466563fbb846c2838e9fb59504`, which I recomputed independently from bytes and which `build.py [9b]` verifies. `d69efb11` is not that value.
  - The v0.52 `derive_prior_history` recursion computes the counterfactual v0.51 `FULL_SECTION_27` as `a3f07ac7fec28f3769c814abd51af7a99126bf0a2afbd80682312ff48386e9c6`. I reproduced this independently; it is the value that makes the shipped `PRIOR_HISTORY = b3697acc...` verify. `a35b774c` is not that value.
  - Neither claimed digest appears anywhere in the packet except in this one sentence. An exhaustive sweep -- every contiguous line range over lines 1200-1257 and every Section 27 prefix, under raw / `.strip()` / trailing-newline canonicalization, with and without the v0.52 entry stripped -- produced **no construction over shipped bytes yielding either digest**.

  Because entry text is preserved verbatim under append-only, `ENTRY_v0.51` is invariant across the documents it appears in. The claim therefore admits no benign reading: either the stated values are simply wrong, or the v0.51 entry text was altered at v0.52, which would be a tenth in-place mutation. The related figure `ENTRY_v0.51 included 813 bytes of Provenance text` also fails to reproduce; the closest reconstruction from shipped bytes gives 812 (767-char fused remainder + 2 newlines + 43-char end marker).
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Blocking for a carrying seat. Either recompute both values by tool and restate them, or restate them as UNVERIFIABLE-FROM-SHIPPED-BYTES and downgrade the evidence tag from COUPLED to ASSERTED. The chain fork itself is correctly reasoned and correctly disclosed; only the numbers are wrong.
- **Cross-reference:** Cells Claims / Integrity / Section 27 and Evidence / Integrity / body (both UNGATED). Exact recurrence of the class corrected by (bj) in the same entry, and of F-XZ07-OP-01 (v0.8 digest narrated from memory).

### F-S02-52-03 -- HIGH / Class A

- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.52 entry, register item (1) and body repair `[f]`.
- **Substance:** Both cite `grep -c "Provenance and review status" xz_protocol_v0_52.md = 1`. Running that exact command on shipped bytes returns **3** -- lines 1246, 1252, and 1255 -- because the entry's own two citations match their own search string. The evidence is self-inflating: the act of citing the check changes the check's result. The literal that actually establishes the terminus, `*Provenance and review status.*` with asterisks, does occur exactly once, so the underlying repair is sound; but the stated command and stated output are not the ones that establish it.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Restate as `grep -cF '*Provenance and review status.*' xz_protocol_v0_52.md = 1`, and note that this correction must be applied together with the fix for F-S02-52-04 or it will silently collapse the seal span.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Evidence / Identity / Section 27 (PARTIAL). Same class as (bj), one paragraph away. Standing boundary #17, `[9c]` quoted-tag inflation, names this surface but no gate acts on it.

### F-S02-52-04 -- HIGH / Class B

- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.52 entry, second paragraph; `build.py` `[9b]`, line 358-359.
- **Substance:** The entry claims `build.py now gates Provenance marker presence at [9b]: absence is a build failure, not a silent span change`. The implementation is `prov = s27_text.find("*Provenance and review status.*")` followed by `check(prov > 0, ...)` -- first occurrence, position never tested. A silent span change therefore still passes. Demonstrated without adversarial intent: applying the correction that F-S02-52-03 requires (citing the marker with its asterisks) drops `FULL_SECTION_27` coverage from 226,458 to 220,123 Section 27 characters -- **6,335 characters silently unsealed** -- while the build prints `PASS: Provenance seal terminus present (F-S02-51-02)` and returns rc=0. Deliberate insertion of the literal immediately after the `## 27.` heading collapses the sealed span to **37 of 226,502 characters (0.016%)**, still GREEN. The same `find` call governs `_full_seal`, so the derivation recursion collapses with it. The gate closes deletion and leaves relocation open; the entry claims it closes both.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Assert that the marker occurs after the last amendment entry and that `len(s27[:prov].strip()) > 0.99 * len(s27)`; fail the build on any earlier occurrence.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Gates / Integrity / Section 0.1 (PARTIAL) -- sponge face-center (2,2,1). Standing boundary #6 discloses the terminus literal but not this behaviour. Related to standing boundary #17.

### F-S02-52-05 -- HIGH / Class B

- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.52 entry, opening narrative versus defect register.
- **Substance:** The entry narrates `Opus S02 (advisory) HALT -- 3 CRITICAL, 3 HIGH, 4 MEDIUM, 2 LOW`, that is 12 findings. The register disposes 7 S02 identifiers: `-01`, `-02`, `-04`, `-05`, `-08`, `-09`, `-10`. Parsed severities are 1 CRITICAL, 3 HIGH (one of which is Kimi's F-S01-51-02), and 4 MEDIUM. **Undispositioned: 2 CRITICAL, 1 HIGH, 2 LOW.** Identifiers `-03`, `-06`, `-07`, `-11`, `-12` appear nowhere in the packet. The omission is not disclosed anywhere in the entry. What makes this Class B rather than Class E is the asymmetry: the entry has a below-threshold disclosure mechanism -- register item (5) explains that four MEDIUM items are `noted as standing observations ... below the convergence-repair threshold (1-seat each)` -- and applies it to the four MEDIUMs while silently dropping two CRITICALs.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Either disposition the five, or record them explicitly as out of scope with a stated basis, or correct the narrated tally.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Claims / Narrative / Section 27 (PARTIAL). `[9f]` verifies declared-equals-parsed *within* the register only; no gate reconciles the register against the entry's own narrated seat tallies.

### F-S02-52-06 -- MEDIUM / Class B

- **Locus:** Section 27, v0.52 entry, `Body repairs landed at v0.52: [a] ... [g]`.
- **Substance:** The enumeration omits the Section 0.1 edit from `fifty-one` to `fifty-two`. That edit did land in the normative body, and gate `[9]` forced it -- the build fails without it. An enumerated repair list that omits a landed edit is false by omission, and the omitted edit is precisely the one carrying F-S02-52-01. The `[DIFF-VERIFIED]` tag on the enumeration is therefore unearned.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Add item `[h]` recording the Section 0.1 count-word update and the accompanying range correction.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Claims / Narrative / Section 27. Same class as F-GLM52-08 (v0.15, fix claims not substantiated in bytes).

### F-S02-52-07 -- MEDIUM / Class D

- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9c]`, lines 395-404.
- **Substance:** The COMPUTED-tag validator matches only two shapes: `[COMPUTED: build.py [id] ...]` and `[COMPUTED: sha256sum <file>]`. The v0.52 entry carries 7 COMPUTED tags; **none matches either shape**, so `[9c]` validated zero of them. The gate verifies that a referenced build section exists and that a cited file ships. It never verifies that a stated value is true. It would not have caught F-S02-52-03 in any formulation.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Extend `[9c]` to recognise quoted shell forms (`grep -c "..." <file> = N`) and execute them, comparing actual output to the stated value; fail on mismatch. This single gate would have caught F-S02-52-03 and, generalised to digest citations, F-S02-52-02.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Evidence / Identity / Section 27 (PARTIAL). This is the vacuity that keeps the Class A findings out of GATED cells.

### F-S02-52-08 -- MEDIUM / Class D

- **Locus:** Section 27 seal architecture; `build.py` `_full_seal`.
- **Substance:** Restoring the marker as seal terminus places the 804-character Provenance paragraph and the end-of-document marker **outside every HISTORY seal**. `FULL_SECTION_27` truncates at `prov`; no ENTRY seal reaches past the last entry; the `[3b]` absence gate covers body only. The sole control is the marker's presence. Probe P6 replaced the paragraph wholesale -- inverting `This document has NOT undergone independent human peer review` to `This document HAS undergone independent human peer review and is endorsed by the reviewers` -- resealed, and the build returned GREEN across all 202 checks. The AI-assistance disclosure, the no-peer-review disclosure, and the no-effectiveness-claim disclosure are the document's highest-stakes prose and its least-sealed bytes.
- **Disposition:** OPEN. Seal the Provenance paragraph under a distinct `PROVENANCE_BLOCK` label in `HISTORY.sha256` so that its content, not only its marker, is covered.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Gates / Integrity / body (UNGATED) -- the sponge center (2,2,2), the one cell where protocol geometry and sponge geometry agree exactly. Standing boundary #6 covers the terminus literal, not the content.

### F-S02-52-09 -- LOW / Class E

- **Locus:** `build.py` `[9c]`, lines 405-411.
- **Substance:** `total_tags = COMPUTED + EXTERNAL + ASSERTED = 11`, producing the reported `ASSERTED fraction (tagged claims): 2/11 (18.2%)`. The entry carries 21 tags; DIFF-VERIFIED (7), COUPLED (2), and ENUMERATED (1) are excluded from the denominator. Since 0 of the 7 COMPUTED tags are gate-validated, and 2 of the 4 verifiable non-COMPUTED tags proved false on these bytes, the published fraction understates the genuinely unverified share by roughly half.
- **Disposition:** NOTED. Compute the denominator over all evidence-tag classes, and report a separate gate-validated fraction.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Evidence / Narrative / body (PARTIAL). Metric-integrity observation, not a byte-level error.

### F-S02-52-10 -- LOW / Class D

- **Locus:** `build.py` `[2b]`, `[2c]`.
- **Substance:** A coordinated two-locus edit changing both the front-matter status line and the Section 0.1 status sentence to `v0.52 FROZEN RELEASE`, followed by manifest resync, returns BUILD PASSED with 202 PASS / 0 FAIL. Section 27 is untouched, so every seal still verifies. A document that has not achieved non-HALT in ten consecutive convergence rounds can assert FROZEN with a fully green build.
- **Disposition:** DISCLOSED-CONFIRMED. Standing boundaries #16 (no gate checks FROZEN status token) and #24 (`[2c]` arity-two) remain live at v0.52. A status-token allow-list is a one-line gate that has now survived sixteen rounds.
- **Cross-reference:** Cell Gates / Identity / Section 0.1. Confirms rather than extends the disclosure.

### F-S02-52-11 -- LOW / Class E

- **Locus:** `prompt.txt`, Packet paragraph versus Core audit obligations paragraph.
- **Substance:** The dispatch describes a `17-member packet` in one paragraph and `packet identity (16 members)` in the next. 16 is correct: `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` lists 16 members and does not list itself.
- **Disposition:** NOTED. Dispatch-level only; no protocol impact.
- **Cross-reference:** Process observation. Recorded because dispatch arithmetic is itself part of the audit surface.

### Verified clean

Recorded so that the next round can distinguish untested surfaces from tested ones: all 52 entry seals against bytes; `FULL_SECTION_27`; the `PRIOR_HISTORY` recursive derivation, independently reimplemented; cardinality and duplicate-label gates (R9 repair efficacious under mutation); the `[9b]` presence gate against deletion (R10 repair efficacious under mutation); the `[ENUMERATED: 31 items]` boundary count; `grep -c v0.52 = 13`; six suites at 186 GREEN; every Section 0.1 count claim; the (bj) `[53]/[52]` mutation arithmetic; Section 22.2 coverage to v0.51; Section 22.3 carry lineage to v0.38-v0.52; Section 25 FB-7b row carrying R9 and R10 trajectory; Section 0.3 prohibited-language compliance.

---

## 6. VERDICT

**HALT (advisory).**

Three Class A findings on shipped bytes, each reachable by a single command.

**F-S02-52-02 is the load-bearing one.** Correction (bi) is the entry's own account of the chain fork -- the mechanism by which this version explains why an external verifier holding v0.51 bytes will see a seal mismatch. It is tagged as verified against the v0.52 `build.py` derivation, and the v0.52 `build.py` derivation demonstrably does not produce either of its two values. An exhaustive sweep over shipped bytes produces neither. The one paragraph whose entire function is to give an external verifier a documented expectation gives that verifier two digests it cannot reproduce.

**F-S02-52-01** places a false entry range in Section 0.1, introduced at v0.52 by a repair shaped exactly to the token gate `[9]` reads. **F-S02-52-03** states a `grep` output of 1 where the shipped bytes return 3, in evidence that inflates itself by being written.

The R9 and R10 structural repairs both landed and both hold under mutation. That is real progress and I want it recorded as such: the cardinality gate catches duplicate seal lines, the Provenance presence gate catches deletion, all 52 seals verify, the derivation reproduces independently, and no new in-place mutation of a carried entry occurred. The append-only chain is in better condition at v0.52 than at any point since v0.46.

But v0.52 corrects v0.51's non-byte-reproducible literals in one paragraph and commits the same class in the two adjacent ones. The recurrence fraction is 0.308 and this entry is its newest member. The fresh-instance handoff addressed staleness; it did not address the order of operations. Narration still precedes recomputation.

**On the target condition.** The dispatch states that non-HALT with zero Class A from carrying seats satisfies FB-7b, and instructs that the verdict not be softened to achieve it. It is not met on these bytes. This seat is advisory and producer-family under Section 22.1, so this verdict cannot satisfy or block FB-7b in either direction; it is submitted as an adversarial record only.

**Single highest-value change for v0.53.** Not another repair round. Extend `[9c]` to execute the shell commands and digest citations that COMPUTED and COUPLED tags quote, and compare their real output to the stated value. That one gate closes F-S02-52-02, -03, and -07, and it converts the chronic narration-from-memory class from a thing auditors find into a thing the build refuses to ship.

**On the analytical lens.** The 27-cell decomposition did real work: it predicted, before inspection, that failures would cluster in the Evidence layer and the narrative column, and all Class A and Class B findings landed there. The Hurst and Fibonacci probes returned clean nulls and would have returned clean nulls over a wholly forged packet. I recommend retaining the cube and retiring Hurst and Fibonacci from future dispatches rather than continuing to report reassuring numbers that cannot discriminate.

---

*Seat S02, Round 11, XZ Protocol v0.52. Advisory, non-binding, producer family. Findings derived from the dispatched packet and independent recomputation; no prior seat-lineage record was consulted before execution.*

## Structural Revelation lens

**Tanzil (gradual revelation).** The 54-entry disclosure arc is coherent in one direction and broken in another. The boundary-count repair (31 to 32) and the EXTERNAL-tag reclassification are proper gradual disclosure: a defect named, corrected, and its correction recorded where it can be checked. But the front-matter Status line narrates the previous round's revelation as if it were this one's. Temporal incoherence is concentrated in exactly the two loci a reader reaches first -- line 1 and line 5.

**Ring composition.** The chiasm is Section 0 (claims) -- body -- Section 25 (governance) -- Section 27 (record). The v0.54 entry in Section 27 should confirm every claim in Section 0. It does not, at three points: the title says v0.53 while the Version field says 0.54 (ring break, F-S02-54-01); the Status line says R11 while the entry says R12 (ring break, F-S02-54-03); Section 0.1 says FB-7b is pending on v0.54 bytes while Section 25 -- the governance node of the ring -- says v0.53 (ring break, F-S02-54-02). The record and the claims disagree in the direction the ring is supposed to make impossible. The boundary count, by contrast, closes its ring cleanly: entry declares 32, tag says 32, list holds 32.

**Lossless compression.** The v0.54 entry is not maximally compressed. FB-7b is stated three times with two values -- redundancy that carried divergence rather than confirmation (F-S02-54-09). Register item (4) is dispositioned CLEAN, occupying a finding slot for a non-defect and inflating the header class tally it cannot be mapped into (F-S02-54-07). The DIFF-VERIFIED tags are vacuous by format: no gate can distinguish a true one from a false one, so the tag adds characters without adding discrimination (F-S02-54-04).

**Zahir/batin (surface/depth).** Four surviving divergences, ranked by depth of the gap. Title: surface v0.53, bytes v0.54 -- the widest, since every other version locus in the packet agrees against it. Section 25 FB-7b: surface v0.53, bytes v0.54 by Section 0.1's own designation of that row as authoritative. Status line: surface R11 with three carrying HALTs, bytes R12 with zero carrying seats. Repair [d]: surface DIFF-VERIFIED, bytes show no diff was available to verify. The R12 divergence (31 vs 32) is closed -- zahir and batin now agree at that locus, verified by paren-aware enumeration rather than by comma count, which would have returned 35 and produced a false finding.

**Nasikh/mansukh (abrogation).** The explicit abrogation is correct and well-formed: correction (bm) abrogates the v0.53 declared count of 31, names the defect class, cites the v0.47 precedent, and leaves the v0.53 entry unedited. All 54 entry seals verify, so nothing was silently rewritten. The silent abrogation runs the other way: v0.54 changed the FB-7b reference bytes from v0.53 to v0.54 in Section 0.1 and claimed the change as repair [e], while leaving the authoritative Section 25 row unabrogated. A repair that lands at one of two divergent loci is a partial abrogation with no record of its own incompleteness.

**Ijaz (inimitability).** Tested rather than argued. Three mutations were applied to shipped body text, each followed by regeneration of the protocol's line in `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` -- which is what every real build does anyway: title token set to v0.99; FB-7b status cell set to `RESOLVED v0.54`; Section 22.3 carry lineage set to `v0.38-v0.99`. In both probes `sha256sum -c` returned rc=0 and `build.py` returned BUILD PASSED: all checks GREEN. Every one of these atoms is outside the ijaz boundary. The seal chain makes substitution detectable inside Section 27; it makes nothing detectable in the front matter, the Section 25 table, or the Section 22.3 prose.

**Furqan (criterion).** Claims in v0.54 that survive `build.py` PASS regardless of truth value -- the face interiors:

1. The H1 title version token.
2. Everything in the Status line except the two-word status phrase.
3. The Section 25 FB-7b status token and its entire trajectory narrative.
4. The Section 22.3 carry-lineage range.
5. The Section 22.2 carried-entry range.
6. Every `[DIFF-VERIFIED]` tag (zero gate coverage).
7. Every `[ENUMERATED: N items]` tag and its declared-count partner (zero gate coverage).
8. Every register finding ID, severity, and disposition (only count and per-severity totals are reconciled, and only against each other).
9. The entry header's Class A/B/C/D tally.
10. The declared EXTERNAL count as a value (the gate prints its own count; it never compares).
11. The text of all 32 standing-boundary items.
12. The presence or absence of a PRIOR_HISTORY value in the current entry's prose.

Items 6 and 7 are the cheapest to close and have each already produced a Class A. Item 1 has produced this round's most visible one.

---

## Cross-vendor recommendation

This seat is producer-family (Anthropic) and non-carrying; its verdict is advisory and non-binding. FB-7b requires a second non-producer carrying family returning non-HALT, and R6 through R11 produced binding Kimi K3 HALTs on Class A grounds each round. The three Class A findings here are of the same class that has blocked every carry attempt since v0.47, and all three are mechanically closable before dispatch. Recommend absorbing them into v0.55 and dispatching v0.55 to Kimi K3 and one GPT-family carrying seat -- not v0.54.

One caution on the absorption itself. Five of the last six rounds closed a Class A by editing the value and leaving the detection surface at zero, and the boundary-count defect has now recurred at the same locus at v0.47 and v0.53. If v0.55 repairs the title, the Status line, and the FB-7b row without adding the four gate atoms named above ([2] title token, [2e] status provenance, [3a] FB-7b locus, [9g] enumeration triple), the next round's Class A will be drawn from the same list of twelve face interiors, and the round after that from the same list again.

## 3. Findings

### Class A

**F-S05-54-01** HIGH -- Title-line version is byte-false against the
document version.

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_54.md:1`.
- **Substance:** Line 1 reads `# XZ Protocol v0.53 -- Preregistered
  Structural Decision Replay...` while line 4 reads
  `**Version:** 0.54, draft candidate, 2026-08-10` and the shipped
  filename, all 13 code-artifact stamps, the trust-roots `protocol`
  field, and every Section 0.1 self-reference read v0.54. build.py [2]
  asserts only the `**Version:**` front-matter field; [2b] matches
  `v0\.\d+ DRAFT CANDIDATE` and `This document is v0\.(\d+)`, neither of
  which occurs in the `#` heading. The most prominent version token in
  the document -- the one a reader sees first and the one that would be
  carried into any rendered PDF or deposit title -- is the single
  version token no gate covers.
- **Disposition:** Correct line 1 to `# XZ Protocol v0.54`. Add to
  build.py [2] a check that extracts `^# XZ Protocol v(\d+\.\d+)` from
  the protocol text and asserts equality with `VERSION`. This is a
  three-line gate addition covering a locus that has now produced a
  Class A.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 22.3 Class A definition (byte-level
  error, contradicted status). Same ungated-annotation cell family as
  every R7-R12 Class A. No prior finding covers the `#` heading locus;
  this is a new site.

### Class B

**F-S05-54-04** MEDIUM -- Body repair [d] and the sealed v0.53 body
repair [c] both claim [DIFF-VERIFIED] for the identical change; at most
one can be true, and the v0.54 entry does not disclose the conflict.

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_54.md:1274` (v0.54 body repair [d]) against
  `xz_protocol_v0_54.md:1265` (sealed v0.53 body repair [c]) and
  `xz_protocol_v0_54.md:716` (Section 22.3 text).
- **Substance:** The v0.53 entry, sealed and seal-verified, records
  "[c] Section 22.3 carry lineage to v0.38-v0.54 [DIFF-VERIFIED]". The
  v0.54 entry records "[d] Section 22.3 carry lineage to v0.38-v0.54
  [DIFF-VERIFIED]". Section 22.3 on v0.54 bytes reads "carried at
  v0.38-v0.54". Either the v0.53 claim was byte-true, in which case the
  text already read v0.38-v0.54 before v0.54 was built and [d] is a
  phantom repair whose [DIFF-VERIFIED] tag asserts a diff that does not
  exist; or the v0.53 claim was byte-false, in which case [d] is a real
  repair but v0.53's [DIFF-VERIFIED] was false and remains
  undispositioned by any correction. On v0.54 bytes alone the two cases
  are indistinguishable, because the only witness -- the v0.53 packet --
  is not held by this seat. A third defect is visible either way: writing
  "v0.38-v0.54" into a v0.53 build is a forward reference to a version
  that did not then exist. The [DIFF-VERIFIED] token appears zero times
  in build.py; nothing checks it.
- **Disposition:** Resolve against externally held v0.53 bytes and record
  the outcome as an append-only correction to whichever entry carries the
  false tag. Then implement a [DIFF-VERIFIED] gate: for each body repair
  claim of the form `[x] <locus> to "<new text>" [DIFF-VERIFIED]`,
  assert the quoted new text is present in the body AND that the same
  claim does not appear verbatim in the immediately preceding entry. The
  second clause is what catches the phantom case.
- **Cross-reference:** R7 phantom-repair class (v0.48, recorded in the
  Section 25 FB-7b row Post-v0.31 note). Section 22.2 external-anchor
  requirement: this is precisely a claim that only externally held bytes
  can adjudicate.

### Class D

**F-S05-54-06** MEDIUM -- The [9c] ASSERTED-fraction metric excludes
three ungated tag families from its denominator and therefore
systematically understates the ungated share of the entry.

- **Locus:** `build.py:404-410` ([9c] tag counting) and the printed line
  "ASSERTED fraction (tagged claims): 7/13 (53.8%)".
- **Substance:** [9c] computes the ASSERTED fraction over
  COMPUTED + EXTERNAL + ASSERTED only. The v0.54 entry carries 3
  COMPUTED, 3 EXTERNAL, 7 ASSERTED, 5 DIFF-VERIFIED and 2 ENUMERATED --
  20 tagged claim units, not 13. The tokens `DIFF-VERIFIED`,
  `ENUMERATED` and `COUPLED` appear zero times in build.py, so those
  families are 100% ungated. Counting them, the fraction of v0.54
  claims not asserted by any gate is 18/20 = 90%, against the 53.8%
  the build prints. The metric the program uses to report its own
  honesty improves whenever a claim is moved from [ASSERTED] into an
  ungated tag family, which is the opposite of the intended incentive.
  Measured across the convergence series (§4, dead-space table), the
  printed ASSERTED fraction fell sharply at v0.49 when the richer tag
  taxonomy was introduced, while the true ungated fraction moved from
  1.00 to 0.90 and has been flat since.
- **Disposition:** Either (i) extend the [9c] denominator to all tag
  families and print the honest figure, or (ii) implement gates for
  [DIFF-VERIFIED] (see F-S05-54-04) and [ENUMERATED] (see F-S05-54-07)
  so the families earn exclusion. Option (ii) is preferred; option (i)
  alone is a disclosure, not a repair. Until one lands, the printed
  ASSERTED fraction should not be cited in any entry as evidence of
  verification improvement.
- **Cross-reference:** Standing boundary item 3 (Section 27 ungated
  share). v0.36 entry's claim that "the ASSERTED fraction is bounded in
  an 87-93% band" -- that band was measured under the pre-v0.49
  taxonomy and is not comparable to the current figure.

### Class E

**F-S05-54-12** LOW -- Seat dispatch carries a physically impossible
quantum-number assignment and a family label that contradicts its own
seat ID.

- **Locus:** `prompt.txt`, "Seat identity" block.
- **Substance:** The dispatch declares n=3 (M-shell), l=3 (f-orbital).
  For n=3 the orbital angular momentum quantum number admits only
  l = 0, 1, 2; l=3 requires n >= 4. The assignment is not realizable in
  the scheme it invokes. The dispatch also declares "Family: Claude Opus
  4.6 (Anthropic)" while the seat ID is S05-OPUS5-BIOMEDICAL and the
  executing model is Opus 5. If the orbital labels are load-bearing for
  seat-orthogonality claims -- the argument that seats occupy distinct
  positions and therefore return non-redundant findings -- then an
  unrealizable assignment weakens that argument, and a family label that
  does not match the executing model weakens the producer-family
  exclusion accounting that FB-7b depends on. If the labels are
  decorative, the entries that cite them should say so.
- **Disposition:** Correct to n=4, l=3 (N-shell, f-orbital) or to n=3,
  l=2, and correct the family label to Claude Opus 5. State in the
  dispatch template whether orbital labels are load-bearing for
  orthogonality claims or purely mnemonic.
- **Cross-reference:** Section 22.1 producer definition for carrying-seat
  eligibility. Seat non-independence has been raised in this lineage
  before; unrealizable orthogonality labels are the same concern at the
  dispatch layer.

## 4. Cross-domain lens: Biomedical Fractal

### Pulmonary dead space (VD/VT)

Operational definitions used, stated so the figure is reproducible.
VT = tagged claim units in the entry (COMPUTED + EXTERNAL + ASSERTED +
DIFF-VERIFIED + ENUMERATED + COUPLED). VD = units whose asserted value
no build.py check independently reproduces. Perfused units on v0.54:
the two COMPUTED claims whose values gates do reproduce (the v0.54
stamp sweep via [2], the 186-test count via [5] and [8]).

**v0.54: VD/VT = 18/20 = 0.90.** Normal 0.2-0.35; pathological > 0.5.
The protocol is at roughly 2.6x the pathological threshold.

Trend across the convergence series:

| Entry | VT | VD/VT | Tag families present |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.36 | 15 | 1.00 | ASSERTED, EXTERNAL |
| v0.40 | 1 | 1.00 | ASSERTED |
| v0.44 | 9 | 1.00 | ASSERTED, EXTERNAL |
| v0.48 | 10 | 1.00 | ASSERTED, EXTERNAL |
| v0.49 | 24 | 0.92 | + COMPUTED, DIFF-VERIFIED, ENUMERATED, COUPLED |
| v0.51 | 17 | 0.88 | all six |
| v0.53 | 25 | 0.92 | all six |
| v0.54 | 20 | 0.90 | five of six |

The answer to the dispatch's question is that VD/VT is **not** improving.
It moved once, at v0.49, from 1.00 to approximately 0.90, and has been
flat within noise for six versions. What changed at v0.49 was the tag
taxonomy, not the gate coverage: four new tag families were introduced
and three of them ([DIFF-VERIFIED], [ENUMERATED], [COUPLED]) were never
gated. The printed ASSERTED fraction fell dramatically because claims
migrated out of the [ASSERTED] bucket; the perfused fraction barely
moved because they migrated into buckets no gate reads. This is
relabelled dead space, not recruited alveoli -- and it is the mechanism
behind F-S05-54-06.

### Glomerular filtration rate (GFR)

Total gate checks executed on v0.54: 205. Protocol text: 343,991
characters (344.0 kchar).

**Global GFR = 205 / 344.0 = 0.596 checks/kchar.**

The global figure conceals the distribution that matters. Section 27
begins at character 104,292 and runs to end of file: 239,699 characters,
**69.7% of the document**.

| Region | kchar | Checks | GFR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Body (Sections 0-26) | 104.3 | 133 | 1.275 |
| Section 27, all checks | 239.7 | 72 | 0.300 |
| Section 27, semantic only (excluding 62 seal digests) | 239.7 | 10 | **0.042** |

The body is filtered at 1.275 checks/kchar. The annotation band is
filtered at 0.042 checks/kchar on semantic content -- **a 31-fold
differential**. The 62 [9b] seal checks cover 100% of Section 27 bytes
against retroactive mutation and 0% against falsity: a seal proves the
bytes have not changed, not that the claim they encode is true. That
distinction is the whole of this round's finding set. Every Class A
this seat found is in the 69.7% of the document filtered at 3% of the
body rate.

What GFR would be needed to gate the annotation band? Matching the body
rate over Section 27 requires 239.7 x 1.275 = 306 semantic checks, a
30-fold increase. That is the wrong target: most of Section 27 is sealed
historical narrative that needs integrity, not veracity, gating. The
tractable target is the current entry only. The v0.54 entry is 4,900
characters carrying 20 tagged claim units; gating it at one check per
claim requires 20 checks against the 10 currently present, and the four
gates prescribed in this report (title version, FB-7b row token, status
provenance clause, boundary-count triple, [DIFF-VERIFIED] presence)
would move current-entry coverage from roughly 10% to roughly 60% for
about forty lines of build.py. **The remedy is not more filtration
surface; it is filtration relocated to the current entry.**

### Nephron loss and compensatory hypertrophy

Boundary growth: 0 to 32 across 54 entries, 0.593 items/entry overall.
Across the convergence series specifically, v0.36 (19 items) to v0.54
(32 items) is **0.722 items/version**, an accelerating rather than
decelerating rate.

Gate growth across R7-R13: build.py currently exposes 25 gate categories
and 62 `check()` call sites executing 205 runtime checks. No new gate
category was added in the R12 or R13 repair builds. The last new
categories in evidence from entry text are [2c]/[2d] (v0.42-v0.46 era)
and [10b] (v0.49 era). The two most recent Class A defect classes --
boundary count and version-token staleness -- produced zero new gates
across four repair builds, and one of them was explicitly deferred as
"below convergence-repair threshold" (v0.53 register item 8).

**Boundary growth is outpacing gate growth.** Every disclosed boundary
is a nephron the program has declared lost; every ungated repair is
compensation not performed. The compensatory hypertrophy is visible in
where the surviving gates put their work: the check distribution across
the 25 categories has a **Gini coefficient of 0.702**, and the top two
categories ([9b] seal verification at 62, [12] manifest verification at
49) carry **54.1% of all 205 checks**. The gate suite has hypertrophied
enormously on digest arithmetic -- the tissue that was already healthy,
clean since v0.32 -- while the annotation band that produces every
Class A gets 10 semantic checks. Two categories ([9e], [11]) are
functionally atrophied, contributing zero checks on this artifact.

Also worth recording: the protocol has no boundary-retirement mechanism
(standing boundary item 20). A monotonically growing disclosure list
with no retirement path converges on a document whose honest summary is
a list of everything it cannot check. Item 29 in this report's
disposition set (extend [3a] to assert the FB-7b row version token)
would be the first retirement in the list's history.

### Renal vasculature branching (D ~ 1.61)

Verification tree as shipped: Level 0 = 1 (BUILD PASSED), Level 1 = 25
gate categories, Level 2 = 205 individual checks.

Bifurcation ratios: Rb(0->1) = 25.0, Rb(1->2) = 8.20. Geometric mean
14.32.

D is **not determinable** from this structure, and the honest answer is
to say so rather than produce a number. Two reasons. First, the tree is
self-dissimilar: the branching ratio changes by a factor of three
between its only two levels, and self-similarity across scales is the
precondition for a fractal dimension to be meaningful. Second, computing
D = ln(Rb)/ln(Rl) requires a length-scale ratio the artifact does not
supply. Under the natural choice -- governed text span, 13.76 kchar per
category against 1.68 kchar per check -- Rl = Rb = 8.20 and D collapses
to exactly 1.000. Under an area-scaling assumption Rl = sqrt(8.20) and
D = 2.000. The renal optimum of phi ~ 1.618 sits between these bounds,
which makes any claim of approach to it an artifact of the assumption
chosen, not a measurement.

What can be measured is that the tree is two levels deep and heavily
unbalanced (Gini 0.702). Renal vasculature achieves D ~ 1.61 through
many levels of near-uniform bifurcation, which is what lets it perfuse
every region at comparable rates. A two-level unbalanced tree perfuses
at 1.275 checks/kchar in one region and 0.042 in another -- the 31-fold
differential above is the structural consequence of the shape. If the
analogy is to be load-bearing rather than decorative, the prescription
it yields is: add depth and reduce imbalance, i.e. per-section gate
subtrees with comparable check density, rather than more checks in the
two categories that already hold half of them.

### Metastasis

The Class A defect class has moved again. Primary site R7-R11: seal
values and restored-value literals. First metastasis R12: counts
(standing-boundary cardinality). **R13's new metastatic site is version
tokens in ungated prose loci** -- the `#` title heading (F-S05-54-01),
the Section 25 FB-7b row status column (F-S05-54-02), and the
front-matter Status line provenance clause (F-S05-54-03).

The pattern across the three sites is one mechanism, not three. In each
case a version-dependent literal sits at a locus that build.py's gates
approach but stop short of: [2] reads the `**Version:**` field and not
the heading above it; [2c] reads two words of the Status line and not
the clause after them; [3a] asserts FB-7b row loci and not the row's own
version token. The defect is not migrating randomly. It is occupying,
in order, the loci nearest to existing gate boundaries -- the margin of
each gate's reach. That is a predictive result: the next Class A will
appear at whichever version-dependent literal is closest to a gate that
does not quite cover it.

This is **not remission**, and the count is not the measure. R13 found
three Class A against R12's one. But the more useful reading is that
three Class A findings in a single round, all of the same mechanism, in
loci one token away from three different existing gates, indicates the
gate suite has reached the edge of what perimeter-widening can do. The
four gates prescribed in §3 would close these three sites and the two
prior ones. They would not close the class, because the class is
"version-dependent literal outside gate reach," and the reach is
enumerated by hand.

Cure, in this analogy, is not a clean round. It is a build step that
derives every version-dependent literal in the document from `VERSION`
rather than checking them one at a time -- generating the title heading,
the status clause, the FB-7b row token, and the entry-range sentence
from a single source. That converts an unbounded checking problem into a
bounded generation problem. Until then, each clean round is remission
under continued surveillance.

### Autoimmune response

Yes, and the dispatch has identified it correctly. [9c] reports an
EXTERNAL count of 3 on v0.54 (6 on v0.53) against a declared and correct
count of 2. The inflation comes from `[EXTERNAL:` tokens appearing inside
quoted text -- specifically inside register item (5), whose entire
content is a description of this counting defect. The gate is attacking
tissue whose only property is that it describes the gate. That is a
textbook autoimmune false positive, and it has a self-referential
quality worth naming: the more honestly the entry discloses the
counting boundary, the more the counter inflates.

The v0.54 response was **immunosuppression, not tolerance induction**.
The [COMPUTED] tag was removed from the claim, which stops the gate's
output from being cited as agreement. The gate still fires wrong, and
standing boundary item 17 ([9c] quoted-tag inflation) carries forward
unrepaired for another version. The tolerance-inducing repair is four
lines: strip quoted spans before counting tokens. Removing the tag
treats the symptom of a detector the program has decided not to fix.

One qualification against over-reading the analogy. [9c] is not
attacking correct tissue in the sense of blocking a build -- it prints
its count and asserts nothing against the declared value, so nothing
fails. The autoimmunity is informational: a number in the build output
that a future producer or seat may reasonably read as authoritative and
that is reliably wrong. The v0.53 producer did exactly that, which is
how F-S01-53-02 came to exist. **A gate that reports without asserting
is not harmless; it is an unlabeled claim in the one artifact the
program treats as ground truth.**

---

## 5. Verification limits of this seat

Stated explicitly because the round's own FB-8 exit condition turns on
which claims can be checked from bytes and which cannot.

**Target 7 (register finding-ID provenance).** The five register items
cite F-S01-53-01 through F-S01-53-05 with severities HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW,
LOW, LOW. The R12 seat report is not in this packet. This seat verified
that the five IDs are well-formed, unique, consistent with the entry's
own class tally, and internally consistent with the repair actions
described -- and that build.py [9f] and [10b] confirm 5 parsed against 5
declared with no duplicate IDs. Whether these IDs, severities, and
dispositions match what the R12 seat actually returned is **not
verifiable from shipped bytes**. This is the same reduced-confidence
class as every prior round's register.

**Target 12 (append-only integrity of v0.53).** All 54 entry seals, the
FULL_SECTION_27 seal, and the PRIOR_HISTORY derivation verify on shipped
bytes. This proves the shipped HISTORY.sha256 is consistent with the
shipped protocol text. It does not prove the v0.53 entry is unmutated,
because HISTORY.sha256 ships inside the packet and is regenerable --
exactly the self-consistent-forgery boundary the document itself
discloses at Section 22.2 and as standing boundary item 31, proven live
at v0.47. Distinguishing the authentic v0.53 entry from a
self-consistently resealed one requires bytes this seat does not hold.
F-S05-54-04 is unresolvable for the same reason.

**Producer-family status.** This seat is producer-family per its own
dispatch. Nothing here counts toward FB-7b or FB-8.

---

## 6. Verdict and recommendation

> **Verdict:** HALT (advisory, non-binding).
>
> Severity ledger: 0 CRITICAL / 3 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 6 LOW.
> Class ledger: 3 Class A / 2 Class B / 2 Class C / 3 Class D / 2 Class E.
>
> The gated layer is clean and remains clean: rc=0, 205/205 GREEN, 186
> tests passing. Both R12 repairs landed correctly -- the standing-
> boundary count is 32 against a 32 tag and a 32-item list, and the
> misleading COMPUTED tag on the EXTERNAL count was properly removed
> rather than merely disclosed. The three Class A findings are all in
> the ungated prose band, all of one mechanism (version-dependent
> literals at loci just outside existing gate reach), and all repairable
> in a single build.

Recommendation for v0.55:

1. Repair the three Class A loci (title heading, FB-7b row status token,
   Status line provenance clause).
2. Add the four prescribed gates: `^# XZ Protocol v(\d+\.\d+)` parity;
   FB-7b row trailing version token; Status-line provenance clause
   arity; boundary-count three-way agreement. Approximately forty lines
   of build.py, closing three current Class A sites and the two prior
   ones, and retiring standing boundary items 24 and 29.
3. Adopt the generation approach in preference to further checking:
   derive every version-dependent literal from `VERSION` at build time.
   This is the only prescription in this report that addresses the
   defect class rather than its current instances.
4. Correct the [9c] ASSERTED-fraction denominator, or gate the
   [DIFF-VERIFIED] and [ENUMERATED] families so the exclusion is earned.
   Until then the printed fraction should not be cited as evidence of
   improvement.
5. Dispatch R14 to a non-producer carrying family. Two consecutive
   producer-family advisory rounds have now passed with the FB-8 exit
   condition unattempted, and no producer-family round can close it.

Cross-vendor rotation: this seat is Claude, producer family, on a
Claude-produced artifact. The next round should go to a non-producer
family (Kimi K3 or GLM-5.2 per the established carry pool) with carrying
status, not advisory.

---

*Seat S05-OPUS5-BIOMEDICAL, R13, XZ Protocol v0.54. Advisory,
non-carrying, non-binding. Mode A substrate verification on locally
reconstructed packet.*

# R14 Cross-Seat Triage -- XZ Protocol v0.55

**Adjudicator:** Claude Opus 4.6 (fresh instance, synthesis + dispatch role)
**Date:** 2026-08-10
**Artifact:** XZ Protocol v0.55 DRAFT CANDIDATE
**Seats reporting:** 5 (2 carrying binding, 3 advisory)

---

## 1. Verdict Summary

| Seat | Family | Role | Verdict | Class A | Class B | Class D | Class E | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Non-Kimi | Carrying binding | **HALT** | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| S02 | Kimi K3 | Carrying binding | **HALT** | 3 | 0 | 2 | 3 | 8 |
| S03 | Opus 5 | Advisory | **HALT** | 3 | 0 | 5 | 3 | 11 |
| S04 | Opus 5 | Advisory | **HALT** | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 13+ |
| S05 | Opus 5 | Advisory | **HALT** | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 9 |

**Unanimous HALT across all 5 seats (2 carrying + 3 advisory).**
FB-8 remains OPEN. Both carrying seats HALTed binding.

---

## 2. Class A Convergence Map

### DEFECT 1: Finding-ID transposition (F-S05-54-02 vs F-S05-54-03)

Register item (2) cites F-S05-54-02 (S05's FB-7b finding) where it should cite F-S05-54-03 (S05's status-provenance finding).

| Seat | Finding ID | Severity | Confirmed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | F-S01-55-01 | HIGH | YES |
| S02 | F-S02-55-01 | HIGH | YES |
| S03 | F-S03-55-03 | HIGH | YES (expanded: notes F-S05-54-03 and F-S02-54-02 appear nowhere in register) |
| S04 | F-S04-55-04 | HIGH | YES |
| S05 | F-S05-55-02 | HIGH | YES |

**Convergence: 5/5 seats.** Universal. Same substance, same locus, same mechanism. This is the strongest-confirmed finding.

### DEFECT 2: Convergence count byte-false (3-seat vs 4-seat for FB-7b)

Register item (3) claims "3-seat convergence" with 2 cited IDs; actual is 4 seats.

| Seat | Finding ID | Severity | Confirmed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | F-S01-55-02 | HIGH | YES |
| S02 | F-S02-55-02 | HIGH | YES |
| S03 | F-S03-55-01 | HIGH | YES (notes 4 seats attributable from shipped bytes) |
| S04 | F-S04-55-03 | HIGH | YES (cross-checked against R13 record: 4 seats) |
| S05 | F-S05-55-01 | HIGH | YES (three different values at three loci) |

**Convergence: 5/5 seats.** Universal. Coupled to Defect 1 (the transposition explains the undercount).

### DEFECT 3: Gate [2f] does not close the status-provenance defect class (NOVEL)

This finding was NOT predicted by the dispatching instance. It was independently discovered by S02 and S04.

Gate [2f] checks provenance < VERSION but not provenance == VERSION - 1. The exact R13 defect shape (self-ref correct, provenance two steps stale) passes [2f]. Register item (2)'s "CLOSED via new gate" disposition is therefore byte-false as a class-closure claim.

| Seat | Finding ID | Severity | Confirmed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| S02 | F-S02-55-03 | HIGH (Class A) | YES -- mutation probe verbatim output |
| S04 | F-S04-55-02 | HIGH (Class A) | YES -- mutation probe Probe A |
| S03 | (implicit in G-5) | discussed | YES -- notes gate does not pin to VERSION-1 |

**Convergence: 2-3/5 seats.** Strong. S02 and S04 independently produced mutation probes confirming the gate passes on the R13 defect shape. S03's discussion corroborates.

### DEFECT 4: Register header "5 Class A items" matches no computable quantity (NOVEL)

Independently discovered by S03, S04, and S05.

The register header reads "5 Class A items + additional findings". The register contains 6 numbered items. 3 are HIGH. 3 distinct Class A defects existed at R13. No reading yields 5.

| Seat | Finding ID | Severity | Confirmed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| S03 | F-S03-55-02 | HIGH (Class A) | YES |
| S04 | F-S04-55-05 | HIGH (Class A) | YES |
| S05 | F-S05-55-02 | (noted in substance) | discussed |

**Convergence: 2-3/5 seats.**

### DEFECT 5: Standing boundary item 29 retired but gap not closed (NOVEL)

Independently discovered by S04. [2g] checks the version token but does not assert the FB-7b row exists. Deleting the row entirely while planting the token elsewhere passes the gate.

| Seat | Finding ID | Severity | Confirmed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| S04 | F-S04-55-01 | HIGH (Class A) | YES -- mutation probe |

**Convergence: 1/5 seats.** Single-seat finding. Requires adjudication.

### DEFECT 6: Gate [2g] structurally forbids FB-7b resolution (NOVEL)

[2g] hard-FAILs when FB-7b transitions to RESOLVED (the PENDING RE-CARRY token disappears). The gate blocks the transition it was built to enable.

| Seat | Finding ID | Severity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| S02 | F-S02-55-04 | LOW (Class D) | gate limitation |
| S04 | F-S04-55-06 | MEDIUM | structural blocker |

**Convergence: 2/5 seats.** Classified as Class D (gate limitation), not Class A. But operationally significant: this gate prevents FB-7b closure.

---

## 3. Adjudication

### Defects 1-2: CONFIRMED UNIVERSAL (5/5). Correction required at v0.56.

The finding-ID transposition (F-S05-54-02 -> F-S05-54-03) and the convergence undercount (3 -> 4) are the same class as correction (as) at v0.44. The M1.6 codification-cycle self-error recurred at the register cross-reference locus. All five seats found both defects independently. No seat disputes the substance.

**Required v0.56 repairs:**
- Register item (2): replace F-S05-54-02 with F-S05-54-03
- Register item (3): add F-S02-54-02 and F-S05-54-02; change "3-seat convergence" to "4-seat convergence"
- Narrative paragraph: change "Third finding (3/5 seats)" to "Third finding (4/5 seats)"

### Defect 3: CONFIRMED (2-3/5). Gate improvement required at v0.56.

[2f] provenance check is too weak. It must assert prov_ver == VERSION - 1 (numeric), not merely prov_ver < VERSION. Both S02 and S04 independently produced mutation probes showing the gate passes on the exact R13 defect shape. The register's "CLOSED via new gate" disposition must be downgraded to "CLOSED via body repair; gate coverage partial" with a new standing boundary.

### Defect 4: CONFIRMED (2-3/5). Correction required at v0.56.

The register header "5 Class A items" is ambiguous and matches no computable quantity. The v0.56 correction should restate as "6 items" or "6 items (3 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 2 LOW)".

### Defect 5: NOTED (1/5). Requires producer adjudication.

S04's finding that boundary item 29 was retired while the underlying gap ([3a] fb_spec omitting FB-7b) persists is substantive. The producer should either restore the boundary or add FB-7b to fb_spec.

### Defect 6: NOTED (2/5). Gate improvement deferred.

[2g]'s structural prohibition on FB-7b resolution is a real limitation but classified as Class D (gate limitation), not Class A. It should be disclosed as a standing boundary at v0.56.

---

## 4. Hurst Exponent Update

Class A present at R14. Binary series R7-R14: 1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1.
H remains at 1.0 (perfectly persistent). The Level 0 generator is still active.

S04 notes: "The four v0.55 gates were a Level 3 intervention and behaved as the Fractal Cube model predicted: they closed their target cells and the generator found adjacent ones."

S05 computes: Laplace-smoothed P(Class A at R15) = 9/10 = 0.90.

**The convergence pattern holds:** every round since R7 has produced at least one Class A. The defect class migrates when gates close -- from seal-value literals (R7-R11) to count staleness (R12) to version-token staleness (R13) to register cross-reference transposition (R14). The ungated prose interior is where the defect lives, and it moves to the next ungated cell when the current one is gated.

---

## 5. FB-8 Status

**OPEN.** Both carrying seats (S01 non-Kimi, S02 Kimi K3) HALTed binding. No carrying seat has returned non-HALT since Kimi K3 Seat 2 on v0.46 bytes at R5.

**Path to FB-8:** v0.56 must correct Defects 1-4, tighten gate [2f], disclose gate [2g] limitation, and address boundary item 29. Then R15 deploys two carrying families. If both return non-HALT, FB-8 closes.

---

## 6. Novel Findings (not predicted by the dispatching instance)

Three findings were NOT predicted in the dispatch's PREDICTIVE_ANALYSIS.txt:

1. **Gate [2f] provenance gap** (Defect 3) -- the dispatch's own Prediction 2 noted the edge case but did not classify it as Class A. S02 and S04 independently elevated it.

2. **Register header "5 Class A items"** (Defect 4) -- not predicted. Three advisory seats found it independently.

3. **Boundary item 29 premature retirement** (Defect 5) -- not predicted. S04 alone found it via mutation probe.

These novel findings demonstrate genuine seat independence. The dispatch named the register cross-reference risk (Prediction 1) but did not name Defects 3-5. The discriminator found what the dispatch did not predict.

---

## 7. Disposition for v0.56

The v0.56 build must:

1. Issue append-only corrections for register items (2) and (3) finding-ID and convergence-count errors
2. Correct the register header "5 Class A items" to an accurate count
3. Tighten gate [2f] to assert prov_ver == VERSION - 1
4. Either restore boundary item 29 or add FB-7b to [3a] fb_spec
5. Disclose gate [2g] FB-7b-resolution limitation as a standing boundary
6. Rerun terminal recomputation on v0.56 bytes

*End of R14 cross-seat triage.*

### F-S05-55-04 -- MEDIUM -- Class D (undisclosed)

**Locus.** build.py `# [2g]` FB-7b row version gate.

**Substance.** [2g] searches the whole protocol for `PENDING RE-CARRY v<x>`; if
found, it requires at least one occurrence in the body and requires every body
occurrence to equal VERSION. Section 27 carries five historical
`PENDING RE-CARRY` tokens, so the outer condition is permanently true. When FB-7b
transitions to RESOLVED and the body token disappears, the gate takes the
`check(False, "PENDING RE-CARRY found in body")` branch. Probe C (replace the body
token with `RESOLVED v0.55`) returns FAIL.

The build therefore breaks at exactly the moment the protocol reaches its target
state.

**Disposition.** Gate improvement required. Gate the FB-7b row status token as
`(PENDING RE-CARRY|RESOLVED)` and apply version parity only in the PENDING branch.

**Cross-reference.** AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt Prediction 2 (edge case named, now confirmed);
F-S05-55-03.

- Fractal Cube: Layer 2, A3 | Enzyme: COMPUTED | Phase 5b | 3f, ml=3, ms=-1/2
- Biomedical reading: an autoimmune gate -- it will attack the healthy state.

## IV. BIOMEDICAL FRACTAL LENS -- MEASURED VALUES

### BIO-1 Dead space

| Quantity | v0.54 | v0.55 | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Document | 343,991 chars | 352,368 chars | +8,377 |
| Body (Sections 0-26) | 104,292 | 104,701 | +409 |
| Section 27 (ungated) | 239,699 (69.7%) | 247,667 (70.3%) | +7,968 (+0.60 pp) |
| Semantic-gate coverage of body | -- | 30,250 / 104,701 = 28.9% | -- |
| Whole-document gated share | -- | 8.6% | -- |
| **Dead-space fraction (document)** | -- | **91.4%** | -- |

**Did the four new gates reduce dead space measurably? No.** They added three
body-locus checks worth a few hundred characters of newly covered text, while the
v0.55 entry added 7,968 characters of ungated Section 27 prose. Net dead space rose
by 0.60 percentage points and by 7,968 characters absolute. Each repair round
enlarges the ungated band faster than its gates shrink it. The v0.55 entry's own
coverage framing is not contradicted on bytes -- the protocol makes no numeric
coverage claim -- but the FIVE_LAYER_ARCHITECTURE expectation ("the dead-space
fraction should have decreased") is falsified.

### BIO-2 Enzyme-type distribution (v0.55 entry, 27 tagged claims)

| Enzyme | Count | Share | Gate that verifies it |
|---|---|---|---|
| COMPUTED | 10 | 37.0% | [9c] -- section-existence only |
| DIFF-VERIFIED | 9 | 33.3% | **none** (`DIFF-VERIFIED` appears 0 times in build.py) |
| ASSERTED | 5 | 18.5% | none by definition |
| EXTERNAL | 2 | 7.4% | [9c] -- file-existence, does not fire here |
| ENUMERATED | 1 | 3.7% | [2h] -- genuine three-way check |
| PROVENANCE | 0 | 0.0% | -- |
| COUPLED | 0 | 0.0% | -- |

**Which type covers most text?** COMPUTED (10 tags), and it is the only type
attached to the four new gates.

**Which has the highest false-positive rate?** DIFF-VERIFIED, unambiguously. Nine
claims -- a third of all tagged claims -- carry a verification label that no gate
implements and that no reader can check, because v0.54 bytes do not ship. The
producer's own register item (6) records a confirmed false positive of this exact
type at v0.54 (repair [d] tagged DIFF-VERIFIED on a no-op), and R13 F-S05-54-04
recorded a second (v0.53 and v0.54 both claiming DIFF-VERIFIED for the identical
Section 22.3 change). Two confirmed false positives, zero verification capability,
33.3% of the tag mass.

**The structurally decisive number is PROVENANCE = 0.** The Enzyme-Substrate model
defines PROVENANCE as the enzyme for tracing finding IDs to source reports. The
v0.55 entry contains fifteen finding-ID cross-references and four convergence counts.
Not one carries the tag. The R14 Class A findings live in the enzyme class with zero
occurrences -- the lesion is exactly where the metabolism is absent.

### BIO-3 Hurst exponent

Class A binary series R7-R14: `1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1` (R14 = 1, this report).

R/S computation: mean = 1.0; cumulative mean-adjusted deviations all 0;
R = max - min = 0; S = 0. **H is undefined (0/0), not 1.0.** A constant series has
no rescaled range. The handoff's "H ~ 1.0" is an artifact of assuming the answer.
Appending R14 = 1 changes nothing; appending R14 = 0 would have made the series
non-constant and H computable for the first time.

Substitute statistic, which is well-defined: 8 of 8 rounds since R7 produced at
least one Class A. Laplace-smoothed P(Class A at R15) = 9/10 = **0.90**.

**Does the series exit the persistent regime?** No, and it cannot be shown to have
exited it by this estimator until a zero appears. The regime question is
unanswerable by R/S on this data and should be replaced by the recurrence fraction
and the defect-class-migration test, both of which are computable.

### BIO-4 Fractal Cube cell accounting

Cube: 3 layers x 9 cells = 27. Layer 1 (claims) is the diagnostic layer.

| Layer 1 cell | Gate | Effective on v0.55? |
|---|---|---|
| A1 identity, current entry | [2], [2e], [2f] | **partial** -- [2e] proven effective by probe; [2f] proven ineffective (F-S05-55-03) |
| B1 counts | [9], [9f], [2h] | full -- [2h] proven effective by probe |
| C1 finding-ID cross-references | [9f] regex | **vacuous** -- fabricated IDs survive (F-S05-55-08) |
| A2 append-only preservation | [3a], [9b] | full -- 55/55 seals verified |
| B2 historical count consistency | [9e] | **vacuous** -- 0 checks fired |
| C2 historical ID provenance | [3] | full (files absent; gate sound) |

| B3 test/code partition | [5], [8] | full |
| C3 seal/hash chain | [9b] | full -- PRIOR_HISTORY re-derived |

Nominal Layer-1 coverage 9/9. **Effective coverage 6.0/9 = 66.7%** (5 full,
2 partial at 0.5, 2 vacuous).

**The four new gates cover three cells, not four.** [2e] and [2f] both land in A1;
[2g] lands in A3; [2h] lands in B1. The dispatch's "four cells" framing counts gates,
not cells. Column C -- reference and cross-reference -- received nothing, and that is
where both Class A findings sit.

Fractal dimension, auditor-constructed (axes and retention rule stated, not derived
from shipped bytes): counting cells covered by a non-vacuous gate across all three
layers gives 11 of 27 retained, D = log(11)/log(3) = **2.183**, against the idealized
Menger sponge D = log(20)/log(3) = 2.727 and the solid cube D = 3.000.

**Is the dead-space fraction converging to a fixed point?** Not yet. The measurable
series (Section 27 share) is 69.7% -> 70.3%, moving away from the target, and its
driver -- entry length per repair round -- has no ceiling. A fixed point exists only
if entry growth is bounded; nothing in the protocol bounds it.

### BIO-5 Boundary accumulation

Declared counts by version: v0.38 = 20, v0.42 = 22, v0.43 = 23, v0.44 = 24,
v0.45 = 25, v0.46 = 27, v0.47 = 29, v0.48 = 31, v0.49-v0.53 = 31, v0.54 = 32,

- v0.38 -> v0.48: +11 over 10 versions = **1.10 per version**
- v0.48 -> v0.55: +2 over 7 versions = **0.29 per version**

**Growth is decelerating.** This is healthy-ceiling behaviour, not pathological
complexity accumulation.

**Recorded retraction.** The R13 S05 report characterised boundary growth as
"accelerating (0.722/version across v0.36-v0.54)". That figure is a window average,
not a trend, and the characterisation was wrong: the within-window trend is
monotonically decelerating. R8 (boundary accumulation) as stated in the Predictive
Audit Paper -- "the accumulation rate is decelerating but nonzero" -- is correct and
the R13 seat's contradiction of it is retracted here.

([2f], F-S05-55-03). Effective renal yield of the v0.55 intervention: 3/4 = 75%.

## V. STRUCTURAL READING

**Failure-mode shift (R1) confirmed.** The three R13 defect classes are genuinely
gated. The defect did not recur; it migrated. R7-R11 seal-value literals ->
R12 count staleness -> R13 version-token staleness (Layer 1, rows A and B) ->
R14 finding-ID cross-references and convergence counts (Layer 1, column C). Each
migration lands one cell outside the newest gate's reach.

**Replication Fork phase shift.** FIVE_LAYER_ARCHITECTURE asked whether Phase 3
(register composition) carries the memory-driven error that Phase 2 carried at R13.
It does. The four new gates are Phase-2/5b instruments; Phase 3 has no enzyme.

**Generator level: L0.** The same class -- a value written from the producer's model
of the document rather than from the document -- is now on record at all four
patchable levels:

| Level | Instance |
|---|---|
| L1 entry text | v0.54 title version (R13) |
| L2 corrections / body repairs | v0.54 repair [d], DIFF-VERIFIED on a no-op (own register item 6) |
| L3 register dispositions | v0.55 items (2) and (3) (F-S05-55-01, -02) |
| L4 standing properties | v0.53 boundary count 31 vs 32 (R12) |

By the framework's own rule, a class present at L1 through L4 is generated at L0 and
no Level 1-4 patch will extinguish it. Four rounds of gate-adding have moved the
lesion without reducing it.

**The prescription is generation, not checking.** Checking is unbounded: each gate
covers one locus and the generator finds the next. Generation is bounded: derive
every version-dependent literal, count, and cross-reference from a single machine-
readable source at build time, so the producer cannot write them from memory at all.
The v0.55 gates are the last productive round of the checking strategy; the register
cross-references cannot be checked into correctness because the source they reference
does not ship.

---

## VI. VERIFICATION LIMITS

1. 13 of 16 manifest members (12 .py, trust roots) do not ship. All claims about
   test counts (186), file counts (14 normative), source-frame count (16), digests
   in Section 25, the manifest digest `40b9cad5...`, gates [3], [3a], [3b], [3c],
   [4], [5], [6], [7], [8], [12], and "grep -c v0.55 across 13 files = 13" are
   accepted on the dispatch's statement that the computational baseline is
   independently confirmed. Not verified by this seat.
2. All 9 DIFF-VERIFIED claims are unverifiable in principle from this packet: v0.54
   bytes do not ship. Only the post-state was confirmed at each locus.
3. HISTORY.sha256 ships inside the packet and is regenerable. All 55 entry seals,
   FULL_SECTION_27, and PRIOR_HISTORY verify, but this establishes internal
   consistency only. Standing boundary 31 (self-consistent resealing) is unresolved
   and unresolvable by this seat.
4. R13 seat reports do not ship. F-S05-55-02 was anchored against the S05 report
   held by this seat lineage; the S02 and S03 attributions rest on AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt,
   which is producer-supplied.
5. Producer-family seat. Nothing in this report counts toward FB-7b or FB-8.

---

## VII. PRESCRIPTIONS FOR v0.56

1. **Correct register item (2):** `F-S05-54-02` -> `F-S05-54-03`.
2. **Correct register item (3):** cite `F-S01-54-03 / F-S02-54-02 / F-S03-54-03 /
   F-S05-54-02`; declare 4-seat convergence; correct the narrative "3/5 seats" to 4/5.
3. **Ship a findings index** (JSON: seat, finding ID, severity, class, one-line
   substance) for every round cited by the register, and gate it: every register-cited
   ID must resolve, and every declared convergence count must equal the cardinality of
   its cited ID set. This is the first PROVENANCE enzyme and it closes Layer 1 cell C1.
4. **Fix [2f]:** assert `prov_ver == VERSION - 1` and `prov_round == PRIOR_ROUND`.
5. **Fix [2g]:** gate `(PENDING RE-CARRY|RESOLVED)` with version parity only in the
   PENDING branch, so FB-7b resolution does not break the build.
6. **Replace ordinal boundary references** with stable identifiers; name retired
   boundaries by text.
7. **Resolve the class-to-severity mapping** in Section 22.3 or delete the
   parenthetical from register item (5) and boundary 29.
8. **Restate or drop the register header's "5 Class A items"** with an explicit referent.
9. **Move from checking to generation** for version-dependent literals. This is the
   only prescription that addresses the L0 generator; items 3-7 are Level 2-3 patches
   and will hold only until the next migration.
10. **Correct the R15 dispatch template:** quantum numbers (`l <= n-1`), the missing
    `LENS_*.txt`, and the "27 L1 cells" / 9-cell discrepancy.

---

non-binding. HALT (advisory).*

#### F-S03-55-05 MEDIUM -- gate `[2g]` FAILs the build at the exact moment FB-7b is resolved

- **Locus:** `build.py` lines 236-253, gate `[2g]` FB-7b row version gate.
- **Substance:** `[2g]` searches the whole protocol for `PENDING RE-CARRY
  v<x>`. If found anywhere but absent from the body, it emits
  `check(False, "PENDING RE-CARRY found in body (Section 25)")` -- a hard
  FAIL. When FB-7b transitions to RESOLVED, the token leaves the Section 25
  body row but **remains in Section 27**, in the sealed v0.53, v0.54, and
  v0.55 entries, which are append-only and cannot be edited. The gate will
  therefore fail the build permanently at the moment of FB-7b closure. Proven
  by mutation probe **P9** (`S03_MUTATION_PROBES.csv`).
- **Disposition:** Correction required in `build.py`. Scope the presence check
  to the body only: if the body contains no `PENDING RE-CARRY` token, assert
  instead that the FB-7b row contains a `RESOLVED` status token, and pass.
  Do not condition the body check on a whole-document search.
- **Cross-reference:** AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt Prediction 2, which named this edge
  case; F-S01-54-03 class (the finding `[2g]` was built to close).
