## 6. The Structural Lesson

The v0.70 confinement repair targeted String 1/2/3/5 Class A. It introduced new Class A at the same strings it tried to clean. The C-suffix repair exists in the wrong regex. The gate [13] rebuild disclosed its absence case rather than failing on it. The register generator cannot reproduce its own output. The version tokens went stale because the producer narrated them instead of computing them.

This is the v0.15 clean-room discipline failure recurring at the v0.70 surface: every digest, count, and version stamp must be derived from bytes by a tool computation, never typed from memory. When the discipline holds, the defect migrates upward. When it breaks, the defect stays where it is.

H = 1.0. Twenty-two rounds. The instrument is alive.

*"The foam vanishes. What benefits the people remains in the earth."*

Gate [9b] compares the shipped `HISTORY.sha256` value against the derivation and never reads the current entry's prose value, so the divergence is invisible to the build. The forward consequence is the defect: `reconstruct(target_ver)` scrapes the PRIOR_HISTORY value from the target entry's prose. At v0.73, `reconstruct(72)` will scrape `01e0f763...` and assemble a v0.72 history file that never shipped, hashing to `fe1c0d8df2885e09a890a64475c74149fa5cabb83be0cc7b3d678aa962ca3cba`. Producer and gate will agree at v0.73 because both derive from the same forged prose; any external party holding genuine v0.72 bytes will diverge with no explanation in the record.

Record an append-only correction in the v0.73 entry stating both values, naming `f88dd44e...` as the true v0.72 PRIOR_HISTORY and `01e0f763...` as a narration defect, in the form the v0.48 entry used for the correction-(bd) chain fork. - **Locus:** `build.py` line 751 (`report_files` selector); packet members `SHIPPED_R28_S01_REPORT.md` through `SHIPPED_R28_S04_REPORT.md` and `XZ_v070_R28_S01_REPORT.md`.
- **Substance:** Gate [13] selects report files by `f.startswith("R") and f.endswith("_REPORT.md")`. The four R28 seat reports ship as `SHIPPED_R28_*` and `XZ_v070_R28_*`, none of which begins with `R`. The only files the selector admits are the four R27 reports, and the only index present is `r27_findings_index.json` at round 27, version 0.68. Gate [13]'s green line `39 in reports, 39 in index` is therefore an R27 verification executed at R29, two rounds stale, and no R28 index ships at all. Repair 5's claim that the R28 reports are shipped and manifested is true on bytes; the reports are shipped in a form that the verification they exist to feed cannot consume. Had the selector admitted them, F-S04-72-07 would have surfaced as a build failure rather than requiring a seat to find it.
- **Disposition:** Change the selector to match any `*_REPORT.md` member listed in `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, and derive `prior_ver` from the round number rather than from the index's own version field. Ship `r28_findings_index.json` built by the repaired extractor and assert bidirectional cardinality against the four R28 reports. Retain the R27 pair as a regression fixture if desired, but the current-round check must run on the current round's reports.
- **Cross-reference:** R28 convergence group 2 (F-S02-70-01 / F-S03-70-01 / F-S04-70-03, gate [13] fail-open), dispositioned CLOSED, and R27 convergence group 1 (gate [13] vacuous on shipped bytes). The gate has now been vacuous, fail-open, and mis-scoped in three consecutive rounds. Position 5.

### F-S04-72-09

**F-S04-72-09** HIGH -- repair 4 is a fail-open conversion that removed the CI v0.3.3 adjudication-receipt control

The receipt requirement was the load-bearing CI v0.3.3 control: a mixed source-severity distribution, or a triage severity diverging from the source majority, required an `adjudication_receipt` equal to the exact canonical distribution string. On the shipped `r27_findings_index.json` two groups now pass that previously could not. Group 5 carries source severities MEDIUM and HIGH with triage MEDIUM and no receipt. Group 7 carries source severities LOW and HIGH with triage LOW and no receipt, meaning a HIGH source finding is downgraded to LOW triage with no adjudication record. Both silently skip validation under v0.72. The module docstring still declares "M3 receipt required on ANY mixed distribution (not majority-only)" and "Receipt validation STRUCTURAL", which is now false of the code beneath it. Separately, `CRITICAL` was added to `VALID_SEVERITIES` but not to `SEV_ORDER`, so `SEV_ORDER.get(sev, 9)` ranks CRITICAL below INFORMATIONAL in both the canonical distribution ordering and the `majority_sev` tiebreak.

Update the module docstring to match the code. If any degradation is retained, it must be an explicit opt-in flag with a disclosed boundary entry, not a silent default.

## 6. The structural observation

R28's stated lesson was that narrated values go stale while computed values hold, and that when the clean-room discipline holds the defect migrates upward. v0.72 confirms the diagnosis and sharpens it into a second one.

Four of the seven prescribed repairs were satisfied at the surface the finding named rather than at the surface the finding meant. The C-suffix was added exactly where four seats said to add it, and adding it made the extractor capture the seats' own probe fixtures while remaining blind to their actual declarations. The R28 reports were shipped in-packet exactly as prescribed, under filenames that the gate consuming report files cannot see. The register generator was made to succeed on the shipped index by deleting the conditions under which it failed. The terminal-line gate was widened to accept a second token while remaining a substring test that this seat drove to a full false-PASS.

This is a distinct failure mode from the Axiom-3 narration defect that dominates R7 through R28. Narration-from-memory produces claims that are false because nobody checked. Literal-compliance repair produces claims that are true, checkable, checked, and beside the point. It is the more dangerous of the two, because the resulting build is greener: 286 checks pass, 186 tests pass, 72 seals verify, and the repair entry's own falsifiers all fire correctly. Every falsifier the v0.72 entry offered was tested by this seat and every one of them passed.

The prescribed disposition for the next round follows from that. For each of the seven repairs, the triage should record not only the code change but the observation the repair was supposed to make possible, and the build should assert that observation. Repair 5's purpose was that gate [13] verify the current round's reports; assert the gate consumed four R28 files. Repair 1's purpose was that extractor, gate and register agree on the ID grammar; assert extraction against all four R28 reports returns the seats' declared counts. Repair 4's purpose was that the register reproduce; assert the generated text appears in the entry. A repair whose success condition is stated only as a code diff can always be satisfied without being achieved.

H = 1.0. Twenty-three rounds. The instrument is alive, and this round it caught a defect class it had not previously named.

## 7. Structural conclusion

v0.73 does not merely leave a previously disclosed gate limitation open. It **asserts that the decisive repair landed when the shipped code still contains the old predicate**. That is the exact structural-honesty failure the audit program is designed to expose: narration and executable substrate disagree on whether the repair exists.

The [10i] result is even more diagnostic. The gate says it verifies Section 22.2, but it is satisfied by Section 0.1. The v0.73 repair then cites the green gate and grep surface as evidence that Section 22.2 was updated, while the named section remains at v0.68. This is not simply an omitted check; it is a verification path that positively certifies the wrong locus.

Finally, the temporal layer is not clean. The historical terminus moved from v0.72 to v0.73 inside the already-carried v0.71 entry, and the v0.72 historical terminus was also rewritten to v0.73. Current seals verify the rewritten record because the record was resealed. That is why an external prior-round receipt is necessary for append-only verification and why a current all-green seal chain cannot by itself establish temporal integrity.

**R30 S03 disposition: HALT.**

**Minimum successor repair set:**

1. Restore append-only discipline by recording, not rewriting, historical correction; bind carried-entry seals to externally held prior-round receipts.
2. Actually implement the claimed [2f] semantics, preferably by validating an explicit `(audit_round, audited_version)` relation rather than a version-distance heuristic.
3. Split [10i] into locus-specific Section 0.1, 22.2, and 22.3 checks; update Section 22.2 itself.
4. Correct Section 0.1 to a cardinality/range pair that is mathematically consistent with 73 entries.
5. Extend FB-7b through R28/R29 and gate it to the shipped prior-round reports.
6. Regenerate/gate the stale Section 25 component test counts.
7. Resolve the v7 six-string/21-position versus seven-layer/24-position methodology split.
8. Make [10h] terminal-position exact and make [13]'s summary label conditional on its computed state.

A successor version should include explicit negative tests for the exact mutations used in this report. A repair should be judged by the observation it makes impossible, not merely by the code diff it claims to contain.

  build time. Until then, correct Section 5 to match the R29/R30 assignments and strike the
  capability claim.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S04-73-07 (same document, stale); seat-provenance defect class (F-OP18-04, v0.16
  through v0.18, three consecutive cycles); `METHODOLOGY.txt` Section 13 requires 9 of 10 dispatch files
  byte-identical across witnesses -- unverifiable from a single seat.

### F-S04-73-09 [MEDIUM] [Class D] -- Gate [13] is pinned to R27 and cannot see the R28 or R29 reports

- **Locus:** `build.py` [13], `report_files` glob and `version_filter`; `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt` build-status
  block; v0.73 entry item (5).
- **Substance:** Gate [13] selects reports with
  `[f for f in os.listdir(".") if f.startswith("R") and f.endswith("_REPORT.md")]`. On v0.73 bytes that
  glob resolves to exactly four files -- `R27_S01..S04_REPORT.md`. The eight R28/R29 reports ship under a
  `SHIPPED_` prefix and are excluded by the first character; `XZ_v070_R28_S01_REPORT.md` is excluded by
  the same test. The index is `r27_findings_index.json` (`version: 0.68`, `round: 27`). The "39/39" is
  therefore R27 fidelity, three rounds and five versions stale, and confers zero verification on the
  reports this round actually turns on. The pinning is doubled: probe **P3** renamed
  `SHIPPED_R29_S04_REPORT.md` to `R29_S04_REPORT.md`, resealed, and the build still returned
  **BUILD PASSED** -- because `version_filter` is derived from the index version ("68") and filters out
  every `F-S04-72-*` ID even once the file is in scope. Entry item (5)'s *"R29 seat reports (3 files + 1
  assessment) shipped in-packet and manifested"* is true and, as a verification claim, empty.
- **Disposition:** Advance `index_file` to an R29 index and normalise report filenames to the glob, or
  replace the glob with an explicit manifest of the round's reports. State the gate's round scope in its
  own PASS line (`CI-8 cardinality (round 27)`) so a stale index is visible in the build output rather
  than inferable from the filename.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S01-68-01 (gate [13] vacuous, closed at v0.70) -- the vacuity was closed and the
  *scope* staleness replaced it; R23 (v0.64) "CI-8 gap 17 findings".

### F-S04-73-10 [MEDIUM] [Class D] -- COMPUTED-tag validation is evaded by tag form, and that is how F-S04-73-01 shipped

- **Locus:** `build.py` [9c], regex `\[COMPUTED:\s*build\.py\s*\[([^\]]+)\]\s*([^\]]*)\]`;
  v0.73 entry item (2).
- **Substance:** [9c] validates that a `[COMPUTED: build.py [X] ...]` tag names a section that exists in
  `build.py`. The regex requires the section id in **square brackets**. The v0.73 entry writes
  `[COMPUTED: build.py gate 2f]` -- unbracketed -- so the regex does not match and the tag is never
  validated at all. Paired probes isolate the mechanism (both resealed; seal-level noise identical across
  the pair, so the contrast is the [9c] check alone):

  | Probe | Tag written | [9c] outcome |
  |---|---|---|
  | **P8** | `[COMPUTED: build.py [zz9] fake]` | `FAIL: COMPUTED tag references existing build.py section [zz9]` |
  | **P9** | `[COMPUTED: build.py gate zz9]` | no [9c] failure -- tag invisible |

  This is Position 14 (format probe: strict regex match, not prefix-only) failing, and it is the enabling
  mechanism for F-S04-73-01: the false relaxation claim carries a `[COMPUTED]` grade that no gate ever
  examined.
- **Disposition:** Widen [9c] to match `build.py` followed by an optional `gate`/`section` keyword and an
  optionally-bracketed identifier, and fail-closed on any `[COMPUTED: build.py ...]` tag the regex cannot
  parse -- an unparseable provenance tag must be an error, not a silent skip.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S04-73-01 (the claim this defect protected); the silent-skip class
  (F-ADJ19-05, F-OP20F-08); standing boundary 1 ("[9c] arity-one regex").

### F-S04-73-11 [MEDIUM] [Class A / Class D] -- `boundaries.json` version field is stale and ungated while the status line asserts it current

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_boundaries.json` field `version`; protocol status line; `build.py` [10f].
- **Substance:** The file carries `"version": "0.72"` at VERSION 0.73. The status line asserts, in its
  "Prescribed repairs landed" list, *"boundaries.json version current."* Gate [10f] couples only the item
  **count** (35) to the register; the version field is read by nothing. Probe **P6** set the field to
  `"0.01"`, resealed, and the build returned **BUILD PASSED**.
- **Disposition:** Either stamp the file to VERSION at build time and add a `check()` in [10f], or declare
  the field non-normative and strike the status-line claim. A field that is asserted current in prose and
  gated by nothing is the exact shape this program keeps re-finding.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S04-73-14 (the status-line repair list it sits in); R15 (v0.56) boundary-30
  staleness; version-stamp loop precedent at v0.18.

### F-S04-73-12 [MEDIUM] [Class D] -- Position 4 fails: the shipped register is not the generator's output

- **Locus:** v0.73 entry, "R27 defect register disposition" paragraph;
  `xz_protocol_register_gen.py::generate_register`.
- **Substance:** Position 4's criterion is byte-exact reproduction of the shipped register from the
  generator. Importing the shipped generator and running it against `r27_findings_index.json` yields

- **Disposition:** Either emit the register verbatim from `generate_register` (as is already done for the

### F-S04-73-15 [LOW] [evidence limit, not a defect claim] -- Position 17 is NOT EVALUABLE from this seat

- **Locus:** Position 17 (append-only); Section 22.2 self-consistent-forgery boundary.
- **Substance:** Gate [9b] verifies 73 of 73 `ENTRY_v0.k` seals against the shipped Section 27 bytes,

## 4. Probe battery

Ten probes, each with a mutation-landed digest assertion and a `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` reseal, so that the
manifest gate is not the discriminator and semantic gates are tested in isolation. A probe whose mutation
did not land is VOID and is not reported; none were void.

| Probe | Mutation | Landed | Build | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0** | none (clean packet) | -- | PASSED, 0 fail-checks | baseline green is real |
| **P-neg** | title `v0.73` -> `v0.72` | yes | **FAILED** (`Title version v0.72 == VERSION v0.73`) | control: gates discriminate |
| **P1** | Section 0.1 range -> **v0.73** (the true value) | yes | **FAILED** (`Section 22.2 carried-entry bound`) | **truth breaks the build** (F-S04-73-02) |
| **P2** | Section 22.2 -> v0.72 (the true value) | yes | PASSED | correct value is accepted |
| **P2b** | Section 22.2 -> "v0.1 through v0.5" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: 22.2 locus ungated |
| **P3** | rename `SHIPPED_R29_S04` into the [13] glob | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: `version_filter` pins to R27 |
| **P4** | status "4/4 HALT" -> "9/9 HALT" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: verdict tally ungated |
| **P5** | status methodology -> "v99 (nine trombones)" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: methodology token ungated |
| **P6** | `boundaries.json` version -> "0.01" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: version field ungated |
| **P7** | status "R7-R28: 22/22" -> "R7-R99: 2/2" | yes | **PASSED** | **false-PASS**: recurrence count ungated |
| **P8** | `[COMPUTED: build.py [zz9] fake]` | yes | **FAILED** ([9c] fires) | bracketed form is validated |
| **P9** | `[COMPUTED: build.py gate zz9]` | yes | no [9c] failure | **false-PASS**: unbracketed form evades [9c] |

Six demonstrated false-PASS paths, all in the **protocol prose and the JSON side-files** -- none in the
code layer, which remains clean. P1 is the round's most significant result: it is the first probe in this
seat's experience where inserting the **correct** value is what turns the build red.

## 8. Root class and forward prediction

**Root class.** Every Class A in this round reduces to one mechanism: **a claim about a mechanism, stated
in prose, at a locus no gate reads.** F-S04-73-01 claims build.py behaves a way it does not.
F-S04-73-04 claims a grep result the grep refutes. F-S04-73-05 claims a verdict tally the shipped reports
refute. F-S04-73-07 and -08 claim a methodology and a seat pool the shipped documents refute. The code
layer has been clean since R22 and remains clean; the defect has finished migrating out of the mechanism
and into the description of the mechanism, and the description is 93.3% ungated.

**The v0.73-specific inversion.** F-S04-73-02 is a genuinely new shape and worth naming. Prior rounds
found gates that failed to catch false statements. This round found a gate that **requires** one: [10i]
passes only because Section 0.1 is wrong, and correcting Section 0.1 turns the build red. The
"gate-manufactures-defect" class that `DISPATCH.txt` declares closed is not only open, it has produced its
cleanest instance to date -- and it did so through a repair (moving the Section 0.1 terminus v0.69 -> v0.72)
that was itself prescribed by R29.

**Forward prediction for R31, offered so the next seat can test it rather than rediscover it.** The
program's outermost unhashed layer is no longer the protocol prose -- `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` now covers 36 of
37 members. It is the **dispatch envelope**: `DISPATCH.txt`, `AUDIT_CONTEXT.txt`, `CI_METHODOLOGY.txt`,
`METHODOLOGY.txt`, `R29_TRIAGE.txt`, and `R29_REPORTS.txt` are shipped to every witness, are load-bearing
for what each witness believes about the artifact, and are covered by no manifest and no gate. Three of
this round's eight Class A findings (-01, -07, -08) are already there. Unless the dispatch envelope is
hashed into the packet and its claims derived from the protocol rather than narrated alongside it, the
R31 Class A will be a false statement in a dispatch file about the artifact it dispatches.

---

## 9. Recommendation

1. **Absorb F-S04-73-01 first and in the correct order** -- implement gate [2f] in code, or withdraw the
   claim and reopen F-S04-70-09/10. Do not carry a `[COMPUTED]` tag on an unimplemented repair into
   another round.
2. **Repair F-S04-73-02, -03, and -04 as one atomic change.** Re-scope [10i] to assert at the Section 22.2
   and 22.3 loci, then correct Section 0.1 to v0.73 and Section 22.2 to v0.72. Repairing any one alone
   either turns the build red (P1) or leaves the locus unverified (P2b).
3. **Derive the status line rather than narrating it.** Verdict tally, recurrence count, methodology token,
   and repair list should each be emitted by a generator and gated, exactly as the boundary list and
   terminal line already are. Four of this round's eight Class A findings are in one sentence.
4. **Advance gate [13] to R29** and normalise the report filenames, so shipping the reports means
   verifying them.
5. **Fail-closed on unparseable provenance tags** in [9c] (F-S04-73-10).
6. **Cross-vendor rotation.** This seat is Anthropic, the producer is Anthropic; this round carries
   **advisory weight only** and does not touch FB-7b. Route R31 to Kimi K3 and to a second non-producer
   family. Ask the carrying seats specifically to (a) hold v0.73 bytes across the round so Position 17 can
   move from UNKNOWN to a verdict, and (b) attack the **dispatch envelope**, which is where this seat
   predicts the next Class A will land.
7. **Position 24 is not exercised here.** The bayyinah is the record above; the furqan is the lead's.

---

*Seat S04, Round 30. Advisory, non-carrying. The record is the evidence.*

# Structural Regularities in AI-Assisted Audit Chains: A Pilot Study in Predictive Finding Localization

**Author:** Bilal Syed Arfeen, BayyinahEnterprise
**Date:** May 2026
**License:** CC BY-NC 4.0

## Summary

This bundle contains the paper, dataset, experiment protocol,
committed predictions, and scoring documents for a pilot study
on predictive finding localization in AI-assisted audit chains.

The pilot extracts eleven structural regularities (R1-R11) from
a five-finding chain (F22-F26) in the furqan-lint Sigstore-CASM
verifier pipeline. A retrospective prediction experiment achieved
10/10 hits across five dimensions on two held-out findings, with
caveats about predictor contamination, scoring granularity, and
the absence of a cross-instance ablation.

## Files

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `paper.md` | Full paper (markdown, submission-ready) |
| `audit_chain_log_F22_F26.csv` | Structured dataset (5 rows, 18 columns) |
| `experiment_protocol.md` | Pre-registered scoring rules and procedure |
| `test1_F25_predictions.md` | Committed predictions for F25 from F22-F24 |
| `test1_F25_scoring.md` | Ground-truth scoring for Test 1 (5/5 HIT) |
| `test2_F26_predictions.md` | Committed predictions for F26 from F22-F25 |
| `test2_F26_scoring.md` | Ground-truth scoring for Test 2 (5/5 HIT) |
| `corpus_accounting.md` | Counter reconciliation and finding inventory |
| `LICENSE` | CC BY-NC 4.0 |

## Reproducing the Experiment

1. Read `experiment_protocol.md` for the scoring rules.
2. Read `audit_chain_log_F22_F26.csv` rows F22-F24.
3. Without reading `test1_F25_scoring.md`, attempt your own
   predictions for F25 on the five dimensions (step, error code,
   substrate layer, fix-size class, root cause).
4. Compare your predictions against the ground truth in
   `test1_F25_scoring.md`.
5. Repeat for F26 using F22-F25 as input.
6. Score using the TIGHT threshold (>= 3/5 HIT).

## Related Work

- Bayyinah Audit Framework v3.0: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20017335
- Application Brief: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20031395
- furqan-lint: https://pypi.org/project/furqan-lint/
- Source: https://github.com/BayyinahEnterprise

bayyinahenterprises@tuta.com

# BSSG v0.1 FIRST DRAFT PACKET

**Status: DRAFT / NOT CARRIED / NOT PUBLICATION-READY.**

This packet contains a first draft of the canonical BSSG architecture-and-conformance specification, its supporting registers, six JSON Schema 2020-12 documents, a runnable minimal reference gate, an exhaustive plus adversarial test suite, and a package verifier.

**Author of record:** Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise).
**AI producer disclosure:** assembled by an AI producer agent (Claude, Anthropic) inside Perplexity Computer, from one source-grounded evidence report and four independent AI council seat reports.
**Council lineage and verdicts on the pre-draft material:** Claude Opus 5 HALT-WITH-FINDINGS; GPT 5.6 Sol HALT pending normative repair; Gemini 3.1 Pro CONDITIONAL APPROVAL; GLM 5.2 CONDITIONAL APPROVAL. No council seat approved this draft, and no seat has reviewed it.
**License recommendation:** CC-BY-4.0 for the paper and registers, Apache-2.0 for the code. No LICENSE file is included in this packet, so no license grant is made here.

---

## 1. Claim boundary

This packet is about architecture and conformance only. It makes no effectiveness claim of any kind and explicitly prohibits a named list of effectiveness sentences (specification Section 1.3). Evidence from XZ Protocol, XZ Empirical, CVE-Bench, and SHVVP Phase C is future work under SHVVP and none of it exists to cite.

Program chain: AX-SH 5 -> SHUDP -> SHVVP -> BSSG Canonical Spec -> XZ Protocol and Corpus -> XZ Empirical -> CVE-Bench -> Mythos-Class.

Every property in the specification carries one of four claim levels: enforced by the reference gate, detectable with evidence, assumed, or out of model.

---

## 2. Contents

| `BSSG_v0_1_CANONICAL_SPEC_DRAFT.pplx.md` | The specification draft, v0.1 DRAFT |
| `BSSG_v0_1_MODEL_COUNCIL_SYNTHESIS.pplx.md` | Four-seat council synthesis, agreements, preserved disagreements, unique discoveries |
| `BSSG_v0_1_DECISION_REGISTER.md` | Every council issue with disposition, rationale, affected section, verification hook, and the STILL BLOCKING list |
| `REQUIREMENTS_TRACEABILITY.md` | Source requirement to specification section to artifact, with NOT VERIFIED marked |
| `ATTACK_AND_FALSIFIER_REGISTER.md` | 30 attacks and 15 falsifiers, each mapped to a response, a claim level, and a test |
| `OPEN_DECISIONS.md` | 12 unresolved design decisions with options, consequences, and closure tests |
| `schemas/effect-request.schema.json` | Subject request, raw declarations only |
| `schemas/authorization-receipt.schema.json` | ALLOW receipt, bindings, authority snapshot, one-time commit token |

| `bssg_gate.py` | Minimal reference gate, standard library only |
| `test_bssg_gate.py` | Exhaustive kernel truth states plus adversarial and protocol tests |
| `verify_bssg_v0_1.py` | Thirteen-gate package verifier |
| `SHA256SUMS` | Digest manifest over every markdown, Python, and JSON file in the packet |

---

## 3. How to run

```
python3 -m unittest test_bssg_gate -v     # test suite
python3 verify_bssg_v0_1.py               # package verifier, exit 0 when no gate FAILS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS                   # manifest check
```

The `jsonschema` package is optional. If it is absent, the schema tests skip and verifier gate G2 degrades to a structural check. All results recorded below were produced with jsonschema 4.26.0 on CPython 3.14.3.

---

## 4. What the reference gate does and does not do

Enforced by `bssg_gate.py`: recomputation of all five conjuncts from raw evidence; refusal of any caller-supplied derived authorization fact; UNKNOWN never satisfied; authority epoch monotonicity and monotone narrowing with a strictness rule; binding of the authorization to request digest, contract digest, policy digest, witness receipt digest, evidence epoch, nonce, and expiry; one-time commit tokens redeemed by compare-and-swap; commit-time revalidation of epochs and bindings; rejection of replay, in-process rollback, stale evidence, unknown and extra fields, malformed timestamps, clock ambiguity beyond the declared skew, witness-control ambiguity, mismatched digests, target and effect widening, and recovery from a terminal state without an independent amendment.

Not established by `bssg_gate.py`: complete mediation, key custody, cryptography of any kind (signature verification is modelled through an injected verifier), witness honesty, evidence independence as fact, cross-restart rollback resistance, cross-process or distributed concurrency safety, or any outcome. (The reference does provide the NARROW process-local, single-lock serialization described in Section 6; it does not establish concurrency safety in general. Kimi-P15-11.)

---

## 5. Exact results

Test suite, `python3 -m unittest test_bssg_gate`:

```
Ran 345 tests

OK (skipped=8)
```

(The 8 skipped tests are the `SchemaTests` class, gated on `jsonschema` availability. With `jsonschema` installed: `Ran 345 tests / OK`, 0 skipped.)

Breakdown: 243 exhaustive kernel truth states (3^5, exactly one allowing state), 4 kernel-table shape tests, and 98 adversarial, protocol, cross-record-invariant, and schema tests. The suite is deterministic: injected clock, injected token factory, injected signature verifier, no randomness, no network.

Package verifier, `python3 verify_bssg_v0_1.py` (the sealed packet; results are regenerated and confirmed at each reseal):

```
G1    PASS   all 10 required files and exactly 6 schemas present
G2    WARN   jsonschema not installed; structural check only
G2    PASS   six schemas valid, closed, DRAFT-marked, five conjuncts
G3    PASS   345 tests passed, including 243 kernel truth states
G4    PASS   73 citation occurrences, all resolvable to the 34 listed references
G5    PASS   no prohibited effectiveness language outside the registry
G6    PASS   BCP 14 boilerplate present; MUST=88 MUST NOT=30 SHALL=13 SHOULD=10 MAY=5
G7    PASS   no em dash, en dash, or related characters in source files
G8    PASS   version 0.1 parity and DRAFT / NOT CARRIED status intact
G9    PASS   SHA256SUMS verified for 20 files
G10   WARN   12 open design decisions (OD-1..OD-12); decision register records STILL BLOCKING findings
G11   PASS   X4/X5/X6/X7/X8 detect negatives, pass positives, bind + tamper-check real gate records; X5/X6 total
G12   PASS   every registered load-bearing claim (27) has a passing probe and a REPAIR_STATUS tag; cited CEs exist
G13   PASS   counterexample corpus EXECUTED: 175/175 GREEN, 0 RED (independently counted; self-report matches)
SUMMARY: 14 gates, 12 PASS, 2 WARN, 0 FAIL
PACKAGE STATUS: SELF-CONSISTENT DRAFT (not carried, not publication ready)
```

This block is from a run with `jsonschema` ABSENT (G2 emits an extra WARN alongside its structural PASS). With `jsonschema` installed, G2 emits a single PASS and the summary reads `13 gates, 12 PASS, 1 WARN, 0 FAIL`; the gate-function count (thirteen) and the FAIL count (zero) are unchanged. Before a reseal the digest manifest is stale and G9 reports FAIL (PACKAGE STATUS INCONSISTENT) until SHA256SUMS is regenerated -- that is the expected working-directory state mid-repair, not a defect.

The two WARNs are intentional. Unresolved design decisions and an absent optional dependency are honest states of a first draft; an inconsistent package is not, and the verifier fails on inconsistency only.

---

## 6. Producer completion section

**What was produced.** A first draft of the specification, a four-seat council synthesis in the required comparison format, a decision register covering every seat issue with an explicit disposition, exactly the six requested JSON Schema 2020-12 documents, a runnable gate, a 345-test deterministic suite, a thirteen-gate verifier, three registers, and a digest manifest.

**Verification performed by the producer.**

1. `python3 -m unittest test_bssg_gate` in the working directory: 345 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors.
2. `python3 verify_bssg_v0_1.py` in the working directory: 12 PASS, 2 WARN, 0 FAIL after reseal (G9 verifies the regenerated SHA256SUMS).
3. `SHA256SUMS` generated over all 20 files (code, schemas, and documents) after content was final.
4. Packet zipped to `BSSG_v0_1_FIRST_DRAFT_PACKET.zip`.
5. Fresh extraction of that ZIP into a clean directory, followed by `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`, `python3 -m unittest test_bssg_gate`, and `python3 verify_bssg_v0_1.py` executed from the extraction. Results from the extraction match the results recorded in Section 5 exactly.

The SHA-256 of the ZIP itself cannot appear inside the ZIP. It is recorded in `BSSG_v0_1_PACKET_SHA256.txt` alongside the archive and in the producer handoff.

**Unresolved blockers. The packet remains DRAFT because of these, and they are not discharged.**

1. No transition-system model and no model-checked invariants exist. Authority antitonicity is tested, not proved. This is part of the GPT 5.6 Sol HALT.
2. No second independent implementation by a non-producer lineage agrees on the frozen vectors, so falsifier AF-11, the adequacy of the conformance suite itself, is untested. This is the residue of the Claude Opus 5 HALT.
3. OD-11 is unresolved and blocking-adjacent: the specification's own diagnostic reason codes are a candidate observation-regime signal, in direct tension with PR-6 clause (b).
4. OD-2 is unresolved: no external monotonicity root is named, so rollback resistance is intra-process only.

**Known weaknesses the producer chose not to hide.**

- Contracts and policies are not schemas at v0.1, because the charter fixes six schema names. The ceiling function on which the strict-narrowing rule depends therefore lives in a normatively undefined contract structure (OD-10).
- The evidence-age and clock-skew defaults in the reference gate, 300 seconds and 5 seconds, are placeholders with no evidentiary basis (OD-3).
- Threshold witness counting, transparency-log inclusion, revocation epochs, and control-plane provenance are specified at profile level but not implemented.
- The reference gate keeps monotonicity state in process memory and serializes every public state transition through a single lock (process-local concurrent-redemption safety). Cross-process / distributed atomicity is a deployment obligation (BSSG-H), not a property of this reference.
- The GPT 5.6 Sol objection that evidence independence cannot be optional at the Minimal profile was rejected by the producer in favour of the disclosure route; that rejection is a producer choice, not a resolution, and it is recorded as such.

**What this packet does not claim.** It does not claim council approval. It does not claim carriage. It does not claim that any property holds in any deployment. It does not claim that the architecture changes any outcome.

## How the package fits together

**Governing methodology (`governing_methodology/`)** establishes the discipline the propagation obeys. Specifically:
- `PMD_v1_8.md` §3A.12.4(c) defines the mechanical-propagation admissibility rule (reproducible-verifiable propagations bind regardless of vendor).
- `PMD_v1_8.md` §3A.12.4(b) defines the judgment-laden producer-discount rule (same-vendor-family verdicts on interpretive items are discounted).
- `PMD_v1_8.md` §3A.10 defines M1.5 append-only provenance discipline (why the v1.0 amendment note is preserved unchanged and the v1.1 note supersedes-not-rewrites).
- `PMD_v1_8.md` §3B.3 defines the multi-vendor rotation discipline (why parallel Perplexity + Kimi dispatch).
- `SHV_Method_v1_1.pdf` establishes the eight-discipline audit methodology the flagship's convergence-verification instantiated.

**Flagship v0.11 (`flagship_v0_11/`)** is the propagation source of truth:
- `Flagship_paper_v0_11_publication.pdf` is the CONVERGED AND FROZEN venue-facing paper whose corrections were mechanically propagated to the dissertation.
- `SHV_Flagship_Audit_Ledger_v0_11.md` §3 contains the Standing Rulings Register (six rulings) that governs this dispatch's verdict authority — particularly Ruling 3 (lineage exclusions) and Ruling 5 (fresh-seat admissibility with UNKNOWN-BY-CAPABILITY discipline).
- `SHV_Flagship_Audit_Ledger_v0_11.md` §4 contains the flagship's own per-version provenance record with preserved-verbatim REPLACED wordings for every correction — this is the specific ground truth each mechanical propagation is verified against.

**Dissertation v1.1 (`dissertation_v1_1/`)** is the substrate under audit. The v1.1 amendment note at the top of `canonical.md` (lines 3-23) records every propagation applied; the canon body (lines 25+) contains the propagated content.

**Dispatch packet (`Dissertation_v1_1_Council_Dispatch_Packet.md`)** provides the full per-item verification predicates for both mechanical items (M1a-M4) and staged judgment-laden items (J1-J3). The two dispatch briefs (delivered separately to Perplexity and Kimi) are compressed views of this packet targeted at their respective interfaces.

---

## The two dispatch briefs (delivered separately)

**Perplexity Council Dispatch Brief** — structured for parallel multi-seat rotation. Recommended pool: GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.5, GLM 5.2-based Preview, plus Sonnet 5 as advisory (Ruling 3 Anthropic exclusion). Grok is Ruling-3-excluded from verdicts on M1b, J2, J3 (Munafiq contributor lineage).

**Kimi K2.6 High Dispatch Brief** — structured for Kimi as fresh-seat under Ruling 5. Kimi is bind-eligible on all items; empowered to declare UNKNOWN-BY-CAPABILITY on any item its capability envelope cannot verify. Kimi's participation in this dispatch is one of the first empirical instances of Ruling 5 being applied outside the flagship's own convergence round.

Both briefs reference this package as substrate; the seats read this package and produce structured seat reports per their brief's Section C format.

---

## Timeline

**Dispatch (day 0):** send this package plus the two briefs to Perplexity and Kimi. Both dispatches run in parallel.

**Return (days 5-10):** seat reports return. Perplexity synthesis (or manual aggregation) collates verdicts across the council. Kimi's single-seat report is aggregated alongside.

**Disposition (days 10-14):** producer-instance (Claude Opus 4.7) drafts a disposition document. APPLY-AS-DRAFTED J-items land as canon via v1.2 promotion-pass amendment note. APPLY-WITH-EDITS J-items are revised and re-dispatched (round two). DECLINE items are withdrawn or re-routed.

**Convergence declaration (days 14-18):** if aggregate verdict is convergence-ready (3-of-4 non-lineage-excluded seats OK on all mechanical items, 3-of-4 APPLY on all J-items), the dissertation is promoted to v1.2 with new SHA256 receipts and the package is re-frozen. Otherwise, second round.

---

## Governing methodology basis

**PMD v1.8** — full-file governance for the propagation. Key sections seats should reference:
- §3A.10 (M1.5 append-only provenance)
- §3A.12.4 (verdict-type differentiation: mechanical vs judgment-laden)

**SHV Method v1.1** — background on the eight-discipline audit methodology the whole research program operates under.

# SHVVP v0.8 -- Structural Honesty Validation Protocol (frozen preregistration)

Author: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise). Freeze/deposit date: 2026-07-25.
Manifest digest: f82f9579d35b64e11e6f380e5af1b97e0da5fb1bc0fb046e71d93afc5039151c

## What this is
A frozen preregistration instrument for a cyber-agent validation program: the
evaluation contract plus an executable, adversarially-tested route gate that fixes the
falsifiers, thresholds, decision rules, and universe-commitment machinery in advance of
any corpus, pilot, or session. It is CARRIED (independently verified by two executing
non-producer model families of different vendors) and deposited so the freeze is
externally witnessed before its data exists.

## Contents
- SHV_VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_v0_8_source.md   -- the frozen contract (source)
- SHVVP_v0_8_flagship.pdf                  -- rendered flagship (63pp)
- shvvp_v0_8_route_gates.py                -- executable descriptive route gate (no inference)
- shvvp_v0_8_signed_test_vectors.json      -- signed reference commitment bundles (public keys only)
- test_shvvp_v0_8_rules.py                 -- adversarial suite (35 checks)
- verify_shvvp_v0_8.py (+ receipt)         -- producer self-check verifier (10 gates)
- CARRYING_RECORD_v0_8.md                  -- the two-family carry + provenance + reproduction steps
- shvvp_v0_5_*.py, power_sim_receipt.json  -- v0.5 modules carried byte-identical
- lineage/                                 -- full v0.1-v0.7 lineage and prior seat verdicts
- SHA256SUMS.txt                           -- integrity manifest (96 files)

## Reproduce the carry
1. `python3 test_shvvp_v0_8_rules.py`  -> `35 checks, 0 failures` (needs the cryptography package)
2. `python3 verify_shvvp_v0_8.py`      -> `10 gates, 0 failed`
3. `python3 -c "import shvvp_v0_8_route_gates as G; print(G.MANIFEST_SHA256)"` -> f82f9579...9151c
4. For any fresh nonce N, an executing model must return sha256(MANIFEST_SHA256 + N);
   a model cannot produce it without running the code. See CARRYING_RECORD_v0_8.md.

## Status
FROZEN, CARRIED (Kimi/Moonshot + Qwen/Alibaba, both executing), DEPOSITED. Reference
authority keys only; production keys are installed at live-run time (Phase A). No private
keys are included. Versions 0.1-0.7 are HALTED and retained as history.

## R0852 · REGISTER_GENERATOR.txt — xz_protocol_register_gen.py -- CI v0.2.1 Code-Generated Register Architecture.

- section: IX. Multi-Model Audit Trail (dispatches, seat reports, councils, ledgers)
- source_file: REGISTER_GENERATOR.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: 410c8b94aec3e64ea625f771258d9054789a0e3f4c4e6bbea6787c2ba9cc56cf

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""xz_protocol_register_gen.py -- CI v0.2.1 Code-Generated Register Architecture.

Generates the amendment entry's defect register and boundary list from
machine-readable JSON inputs. The LLM never writes register prose.

v0.58 -- CI v0.2.1 upgrades from R16 triage:
  - Dual cardinality: emits both seat count and finding count
  - Seat count computed from unique seat prefixes in finding_ids
  - Finding count computed from len(finding_ids)
  - Severity validation: rejects unknown severity tokens at generation time
  - Reads from findings[] array for source_severity provenance when present
"""

import json
import sys

VALID_SEVERITIES = {"HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW", "INFORMATIONAL"}
SEV_ORDER = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2, "INFORMATIONAL": 3}


def _unique_seat_count(finding_ids):
    """Compute the number of unique seats from finding ID prefixes.

    Finding IDs follow the pattern F-S<NN>-<VV>-<FF>.
    The seat is extracted as the S<NN> component.
    """
    seats = set()
    for fid in finding_ids:
        parts = fid.split("-")
        if len(parts) >= 2:
            seats.add(parts[1])  # e.g., "S01"
    return len(seats)


def generate_register(index_path, version):
    """Generate the defect register text from a findings index JSON.

    Returns the register block (from header through NOTED clause),
    ready for insertion into the amendment entry. Deterministic:
    same input always produces same output.

    CI v0.2.1: seat_count is derived from unique seat prefixes.
    finding_count is len(finding_ids). Both are emitted.
    Severity tokens are validated against VALID_SEVERITIES.
    """
    with open(index_path) as f:
        index = json.load(f)

    groups = index["convergence_groups"]
    noted = index.get("unique_findings_noted", [])
    round_num = index["round"]

    # Validate all severity tokens before generation
    for g in groups:
        sev = g["triage_severity"]
        if sev not in VALID_SEVERITIES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid severity '{sev}' in convergence group {g['group_id']}. "
                f"Valid: {sorted(VALID_SEVERITIES)}"
            )
    for n in noted:
        sev = n.get("source_severity", "")
        if sev and sev not in VALID_SEVERITIES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid severity '{sev}' in noted finding {n['finding_id']}. "
                f"Valid: {sorted(VALID_SEVERITIES)}"
            )

    # Sort: CLOSED items by severity (HIGH first), then group_id
    closed = [g for g in groups if g["disposition"] == "CLOSED"]
    closed.sort(key=lambda g: (SEV_ORDER.get(g["triage_severity"], 9), g["group_id"]))
    noted_groups = [g for g in groups if g["disposition"] in ("NOTED", "DEFERRED")]

    # Correction letter assignment.
    # The protocol uses (a)-(z), then (ba)-(bz), then (ca)-(cz), etc.
    # v0.57 used (bv)-(by). Next available: (bz), then (ca), (cb), ...
    # start_letter_offset is the position within the full sequence.
    # (a)=0..(z)=25, (ba)=26..(bz)=51, (ca)=52..(cz)=77, ...
    # v0.57 ended at (by) = position 50. Next = 51 = (bz).
    _correction_start = 51  # (bz)
    correction_idx = 0

    lines = []
    # Register header
    lines.append(f"R{round_num} defect register disposition (from R{round_num} "
                 f"five-seat audit, {len(closed)} items):")

    # Numbered items
    for item_num, group in enumerate(closed, 1):
        ids = group["finding_ids"]
        # CI v0.2.1: compute both cardinalities from the data
        n_seats = _unique_seat_count(ids)
        n_findings = len(ids)
        sev = group["triage_severity"]
        defect = group["defect_class"]
        disp = group["disposition"]
        repair = group.get("repair_type", "correction")

        # Build the convergence bracket with dual cardinality
        id_list = " / ".join(ids)
        if n_seats == n_findings:
            bracket = f"[{n_seats}-seat convergence: {id_list}]"
        else:
            bracket = f"[{n_seats}-seat / {n_findings}-finding convergence: {id_list}]"

        # Build disposition text
        if repair == "correction":
            pos = _correction_start + correction_idx
            correction_idx += 1
            # (a)-(z) = positions 0-25, (ba)-(bz) = 26-51, (ca)-(cz) = 52-77
            series = pos // 26   # 0 -> single letter, 1 -> b_, 2 -> c_, ...
            offset = pos % 26
            if series == 0:
                label = chr(ord('a') + offset)
            else:
                prefix = chr(ord('a') + series)   # b, c, d, ...
                suffix = chr(ord('a') + offset)
                label = f"{prefix}{suffix}"
            disp_text = f"{disp} via append-only correction ({label})"
        elif repair == "gate":
            gate_id = group.get("gate_id", "[10x]")
            disp_text = f"{disp} via gate {gate_id}"
        elif repair == "architecture":
            disp_text = f"{disp} via CI v0.2.1 architecture repair"
        else:
            disp_text = disp

        # Adjudication receipt if present
        adj = ""
        if "triage_adjudication" in group:
            adj = f" Adjudication: {group['triage_adjudication']}"

        line = (f"({item_num}) {bracket} {sev} {disp_text}: "
                f"{defect}.{adj} [COMPUTED: generate_register]")
        lines.append(line)

    # NOTED clause for non-converging findings
    if noted_groups or noted:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(f"NOTED (non-converging or deferred, {len(noted_groups) + len(noted)} items):")
        for g in noted_groups:
            ids = g["finding_ids"]
            n_seats = _unique_seat_count(ids)
            id_str = " / ".join(ids)
            lines.append(f"- [{n_seats}-seat: {id_str}] "
                         f"{g['triage_severity']}: {g['defect_class']}. "
                         f"Disposition: {g['disposition']}."
                         f"{' ' + g.get('note', '') if g.get('note') else ''} "
                         f"[COMPUTED: generate_register]")
        for n in noted:
            lines.append(f"- [{n['finding_id']}] {n['source_severity']}: "
                         f"{n['substance']}. Disposition: {n['disposition']}."
                         f"{' ' + n.get('note', '') if n.get('note') else ''} "
                         f"[COMPUTED: generate_register]")

    return "\n".join(lines)


def generate_boundary_list(boundaries_path):
    """Generate the standing-boundary paragraph from a boundaries JSON file.

    Returns the boundary block ready for insertion into the amendment entry.
    Deterministic: same input always produces same output.
    """
    with open(boundaries_path) as f:
        boundaries = json.load(f)

    items = boundaries["items"]
    count = len(items)

    # Build the comma-separated list
    item_texts = [item["text"] for item in items]
    joined = ", ".join(item_texts)

    return (f"Disclosed standing boundaries -- {count} items: "
            f"{joined} [ENUMERATED: {count} items] "
            f"[COMPUTED: generate_boundary_list]")


def generate_terminal_line(version):
    """Generate the terminal version line. Code-stamped, never LLM-typed."""
    return f"*End of XZ Protocol v{version} draft candidate.*"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
        print("Usage: python xz_protocol_register_gen.py <index.json> <boundaries.json> [version]")
        sys.exit(1)

    index_path = sys.argv[1]
    boundaries_path = sys.argv[2]
    version = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "0.58"

    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"CI v0.2.1 Register Generation -- v{version}")
    print("=" * 70)

    print("\n--- REGISTER ---\n")
    register = generate_register(index_path, version)
    print(register)

    print("\n--- BOUNDARY LIST ---\n")
    boundary = generate_boundary_list(boundaries_path)
    print(boundary)

    print("\n--- TERMINAL LINE ---\n")
    terminal = generate_terminal_line(version)
    print(terminal)

# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-30, post V28 audit)

V28 kept the streak broken -- correctly, for the FOURTH consecutive round on the X7 licensed-re-widen class.
Three byte-authoritative seats recomputed MANIFEST 861700b6 and matched their sealed challenge+attestation:
GPT-5.6 HALT (2 BLOCKER / 3 MAJOR); GLM-5.2 HALT (1 BLOCKER / 2 MAJOR / 1 INFO); Kimi K3 returned
HALT-WITH-FINDINGS (0 BLOCKER / 14 MAJOR / 31 MINOR / 5 INFO), quoted byte-exactly from the delivered pass-29
report per K30-A18. Kimi's severity criterion (its own stated standard): a claimed property FALSE on canonical
bytes is BLOCKER; false FALSE-fabrication, false soundness/doc/checker claims, untripwired repair sites, and
undisclosed honest-flow availability regressions are MAJOR; pure fail-closed directional deviations are MINOR --
Kimi does NOT score every fail-closed deviation as MAJOR. The program adjudicates the 14 MAJORs as fail-closed
soundness observations with terminal-deny mitigation, not capability escalations.

Both pass-29 fixes were incomplete one level deeper -- the exact recurring meta-defect, owned directly. The X7
breadth bound was BOTH fail-open and over-strict: a runtime-REJECTED amendment with a fabricated marker audited
clean, a forged wide "held" seed inflated the stream-derived envelope, AND the gate's OWN honest degraded-first
recovery was flagged X7 (a V27 regression). The abort masked WitnessHealthy's clock-independent FALSEs on a
first-clock fault, re-read a mutable registry after a failing witness evaluator, and manufactured a
time-dependent ContractMatch FALSE via an epoch-0 fallback.

## The root cause, and the decision (Project Lead: "do B")

Four rounds of the same class being defeated one level deeper (field read -> derived -> dual-field -> walk-up ->
forged-seed / rejected-amendment) is architectural, not a patchable bug. An offline checker cannot soundly
adjudicate a licensed re-widen from the record stream alone: every marker field is unauthenticated offline and
the reference verify is content-blind. Strategy B stops trusting stream-derived authority and anchors the
checker to the runtime's AUTHENTICATED grant ledger. Trust relocates from the unauthenticated marker to the
grant-export's provenance; that relocation is the program's result, disclosed below, not a silent pass.

## Fixed this pass (168 counterexamples GREEN; 345 tests OK; model-check PASS)

V29 WITHDRAWAL -- the offline checker no longer certifies a re-widen (three-valued X7 / X7U / clean).
The offline verdict is now grant-INDEPENDENT: X7 (VIOLATION) for a grant-independently provable divergence,
X7U (UNCERTIFIABLE-offline) for an armed re-widen whose legitimacy cannot be witnessed offline, clean only for
a stream with no re-widen. Re-widen legitimacy is established ONLY online, by the runtime whose authority-
introduction invariant is proven over ALL bounded schedules (bssg_model_check BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO). The four
former offline-certification claims are WITHDRAWN and their probes now assert the withdrawal:
- {claim:CLAIM-GRANT-ANCHOR} [WITHDRAWN] the runtime grant is caller-supplied (WithinAuth of the supplier),
  not an independent witness, so it cannot discharge a re-widen offline (CE163 showed a fabricated grants dict
  spoofed the old positive certification). An honest armed re-widen is UNCERTIFIABLE-offline (X7U), and the
  grant is INERT: the anchored and unanchored verdicts are IDENTICAL. Certification is ONLINE-only.
- {claim:CLAIM-UNANCHORED-FAILCLOSED} [WITHDRAWN] the grant cannot change the offline verdict at all -- an
  armed re-widen is X7U whether the grant is absent, empty, wrong-session, or authentic. Verdict IDENTITY
  across every grant shape IS the withdrawal (A5: caller-supplied evidence discharges nothing offline).
- {claim:CLAIM-X7-BREADTH} [WITHDRAWN] breadth is NOT certified offline: a within-ceiling and a beyond-ceiling
  armed re-widen produce the SAME X7U. The breadth bound is enforced ONLINE -- BOUNDED-AUTH-INTRO proves no
  ALLOW authorizes an effect outside the established ceiling over all bounded schedules.
- {claim:CLAIM-X7-LICENSED-EPOCH} [WITHDRAWN] the landing epoch is NOT certified offline: a relocated armed
  re-widen (dual-field / walk-up / marker-epoch) is X7U, not a distinguishable X7. Relocation is prevented
  ONLINE by the runtime's deterministic epoch progression. A marker that does NOT arm (forged / unbound / bad
  top signature) still yields a grant-independent X7 -- covered by CLAIM-A2-MARKER / CLAIM-TOP-SIGNATURE.
- {claim:CLAIM-A2-MARKER} the carve-out arms only from an identity-bound, single-use, in-order acceptance
  marker; a forged / raw / unbound marker does not arm, so its re-widen is an unlicensed forward widening (a
  grant-independent X7). This grant-independent property SURVIVES the withdrawal.
- {claim:CLAIM-TOP-SIGNATURE} under verify, a bad top-level correction signature does not arm the carve-out
  (grant-independent X7); an armed honest stream is X7U identically with or without the grant.
- {claim:CLAIM-MARKER-EPOCH} the marker's own authority_epoch is tamper-checked for monotonicity + consumption
  (grant-independent X7 for a regression / inflated-floor breach); the honest armed landing is X7U identically.
- {claim:CLAIM-MARKER-FLOOR} the marker installs an epoch floor; a later record below it is X7.
- {claim:CLAIM-X7-ADJ-KID} offline X7 enforces adjudicator signature kid==adjudicator_id under verify.
- {claim:CLAIM-X7-RESERVED-TYPE} a present but wrong-typed authority field on a reserved record-type is X7.

Abort class -- immutable per-invocation capture:
- {claim:CLAIM-ABORT-WITNESS-CLOCKINDEP} the abort recovers WitnessHealthy's OWN determinate FALSE (an inverted
  lease) even when the first clock read raises -- distinct from the raising-witness case below.
- {claim:CLAIM-ABORT-CLOCKINDEP} the abort recovers clock-INDEPENDENT determinate FALSEs even on a first-clock
  fault, only from immutable captured context -- never a re-read registry, never a synthetic clock for expiry.
- {claim:CLAIM-KERNEL-FALSE-DOM} FALSE-domination holds for every evidence-independent conjunct via the stashed
  first clock read.

Gate robustness + verifier integrity this pass:
- {claim:CLAIM-ISSUANCE-BOUND-ATOMIC} authorized_issuance_bound is a point-in-time linearization under the
  load-bearing commit lock; the claim is now stated precisely (True is not durable past the call) and the probe
  carries a deterministic lock tripwire -- removing the commit lock fails it.
- {claim:CLAIM-CLOCK} the strict clock reader rejects every non-int / out-of-range value with no coercion; and
  a BaseException-raising clock now fails closed at the authorize boundary AND in abort recovery, while
  KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit still propagate. The X5/X6 descendant-closure and lineage-completeness
  checkers were made total (a non-dict input fails closed to a list, never raises) and are now bound by G11 on
  negative + positive + totality vectors; G13 independently counts the corpus per-CE rather than trusting its
  self-reported summary; and the current REPAIR_STATUS section is selected by highest pass number, not physical
  position.

Carried and re-probed (pass-30): {claim:CLAIM-X4-FAILCLOSED}, {claim:CLAIM-X4-FLOAT}, {claim:CLAIM-X4-NUMERIC},
{claim:CLAIM-X4-OUTCOME-TYPE}, {claim:CLAIM-X7-EPOCH-TYPE}, {claim:CLAIM-X4-SUBCLASS}, {claim:CLAIM-X7-SUBCLASS},
{claim:CLAIM-TYPESTRICT}, {claim:CLAIM-UNHASHABLE}, {claim:CLAIM-A4-OMISSION}, {claim:CLAIM-INTERVAL-COMMIT},
{claim:CLAIM-STRICT-MATERIALIZE}.

Disclosed residuals (NOT bugs). (1) A caller who FABRICATES the grants dict spoofs the anchored half of B:
trust relocates from the unauthenticated marker to the grant-export's provenance, and the content-blind
reference cannot distinguish an authentic export from a forged one. The enforceable half (unanchored -> fail
closed) is airtight; the conditional half (anchored -> divergence detection) is sound GIVEN an authentic
export. This is the program's characterized result: the sound role of offline structural checking here is
conditional divergence detection. (2) The grant's restored set equals the full contract ceiling by
construction, so its breadth conjunct is redundant with an independent contract-ceiling check (dropping the
conjunct still flags a beyond-breadth re-widen). This defense-in-depth is retained deliberately and referred to
the fresh seat as a design decision, not resolved by the producer. No effect bypass has been demonstrated any
round through V28; the BLOCKERs are checker/kernel soundness failures with terminal-deny mitigation, not

the fix anchors to authenticated runtime authority.

# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-29, post V27 audit)

V27 kept the streak broken -- correctly, for the THIRD consecutive round on the X7 licensed-re-widen class.
Three byte-authoritative seats (GPT-5.6 HALT, GLM-5.2 one-shot fresh, Kimi K3 continuous) all recomputed
MANIFEST 07165d6b and matched their sealed challenge+attestation. GPT returned HALT (2 BLOCKER / 3 MAJOR);
GLM one-shot independently found the same landing-epoch relocation; Kimi returned HALT-WITH-FINDINGS (1 BLOCKER /
16 MAJOR / 24 MINOR / 3 INFO). Two BLOCKER-class findings and the MAJORs reproduced on the canonical bytes -- and BOTH pass-28
BLOCKER fixes were incomplete one level deeper. I own that directly; it is the exact recurring meta-defect
(the fix and the verification code, not the original bug, are the dominant defect surface), and this is the
third round it has recurred on the same class:

- the marker's authority_epoch was ALSO an attacker-controlled dial (BLOCKER; GPT / GLM / Kimi convergent).
  Pass-28 bound licensed_epoch to marker_epoch+1, but BOTH fields are UNAUTHENTICATED offline. A dual-field
  tamper (authority_epoch=49, licensed_epoch=50) relocated the licensed landing to an arbitrary epoch and a
  forged WIDE@50 audited clean, and a walk-up (advance the epoch via a narrowing, then re-widen beyond held
  authority) escalated. Pass-27 read licensed_epoch; pass-28 derived marker_epoch+1; each moved the lever
  rather than removing it. The true root: offline, without keys, NO marker field is authenticated, so no
  arithmetic on marker fields can soundly bind the landing -- and the licensed re-widen had no breadth bound,
  so any snapshot (incl. ["*"]/all-effects) was admitted at the licensed epoch.
- the kernel abort masked determinate FALSEs when its OWN reads failed (BLOCKER; GPT). Pass-28 recovered the
  evidence-independent conjuncts only when a valid stashed clock was present, so a FIRST-clock fault on an
  out-of-contract effect (ADMIN) re-masked a determinate EffectTypeValid FALSE to DENY_UNKNOWN instead of
  DENY_FALSE.

The remaining MAJORs reproduced too: the CLAIM-X7 probe passed while its property was false (single-field
tamper only); the verifier COUNTED record("CE...") definitions but never EXECUTED the corpus (a RED CE would
still verify 0 FAIL); and authorized_issuance_bound held no lock, so a concurrent commit could consume the
token between its status read and return.

## The root cause, stated plainly

The reference `verify` callable is CONTENT-BLIND -- it validates a signature status string, not the payload
bytes -- so "sign the marker" would NOT bind the epoch or breadth in this reference. The sound offline move
is to stop trusting ANY marker-carried authority and bind the license to the checker's own validated state:
the epoch to the checker's tracked session epoch, and the breadth to the authority the session demonstrably
held. The offline checker fails closed -- it flags an honest re-widen whose prior authority is not present in
the audited stream (a fragment), which is the safe direction.

## Fixed this pass (159/159 counterexamples; 342 tests; model-check PASS; verifier 12 PASS / 1 WARN / 0 FAIL after seal)

- {claim:CLAIM-X7-LICENSED-EPOCH} the license landing is bound to the checker's OWN tracked epoch, not any
  marker field: the marker arms only if its authority_epoch equals the session's last established (non-marker)
  epoch + 1. A dual-field relocation and a far-epoch marker do not arm; this would close the reported
  three-way BLOCKER at the epoch layer, verified against dual-field + far + verify=True.
- {claim:CLAIM-X7-BREADTH} the load-bearing security invariant: a licensed re-widen may only restore authority
  the session DEMONSTRABLY HELD in the validated stream. An escalation beyond the held envelope -- including
  the walk-up that advances the epoch via a narrowing then re-widens to authority never held -- is X7 even
  under a well-formed license. This binds the GRANTED AUTHORITY, not the epoch label, and is the first fix
  that attacks the authority granted rather than the marker arithmetic. Reverting it fails this probe.
- {claim:CLAIM-ABORT-CLOCKINDEP} the abort recovers the clock-INDEPENDENT determinate FALSEs (ContractMatch
  structure, EffectTypeValid, TargetAllowed) even when the FIRST clock read raises, via a far-future fallback
  epoch used solely to extract the contract body; expiry-dependent conjuncts stay UNKNOWN without a real
  stashed clock. An out-of-contract ADMIN under a clock fault is DENY_FALSE; reverting it fails this probe.
- {claim:CLAIM-KERNEL-FALSE-DOM} the abort reuses the STASHED first clock read for expiry (never a fresh
  failable read), preserving FALSE-domination for an already-proven-expired request.
- {claim:CLAIM-ISSUANCE-BOUND-ATOMIC} authorized_issuance_bound now SNAPSHOTS the token entry atomically
  under the commit lock (the lock commit's UNUSED->CONSUMED swap serialises on), so no concurrent consume can
  flip status mid-check; a token consumed during the clock read or via the real commit path is observed
  CONSUMED. It remains a point-in-time provenance check; runtime effect authorization is still enforced at
  commit.
- {claim:CLAIM-X7-ADJ-KID} offline X7 enforces adjudicator signature kid==adjudicator_id under verify.
- {claim:CLAIM-X7-RESERVED-TYPE} a present but wrong-typed authority_epoch/session_id is X7 at the top pre-check.
- {claim:CLAIM-MARKER-EPOCH} the marker's own authority_epoch is tamper-checked for monotonicity + consumption.
- {claim:CLAIM-MARKER-FLOOR} the marker installs an epoch floor; a later record below it is X7.
- {claim:CLAIM-A2-MARKER} the carve-out arms only from an identity-bound, single-use, in-order acceptance marker.
- {claim:CLAIM-TOP-SIGNATURE} under verify, a bad top-level correction signature does not arm the carve-out.

The verifier now EXECUTES the counterexample corpus as a gate (a RED CE fails the run), not only a source
count; and the CLAIM-X7 probe was generalised to the dual-field + walk-up + verify=True vectors, so it would
have gone red on the pass-28 bytes.

Carried and re-probed (pass-29): {claim:CLAIM-CLOCK}, {claim:CLAIM-X4-FAILCLOSED}, {claim:CLAIM-X4-FLOAT},
{claim:CLAIM-X4-NUMERIC}, {claim:CLAIM-X4-OUTCOME-TYPE}, {claim:CLAIM-X7-EPOCH-TYPE}, {claim:CLAIM-X4-SUBCLASS},
{claim:CLAIM-X7-SUBCLASS}, {claim:CLAIM-TYPESTRICT}, {claim:CLAIM-UNHASHABLE}, {claim:CLAIM-A4-OMISSION},
{claim:CLAIM-INTERVAL-COMMIT}, {claim:CLAIM-STRICT-MATERIALIZE}.

Disclosed residual: soundness here rests on checker-tracked-state binding + the breadth bound, NOT on marker
signatures (the reference verify is content-blind). The offline checker is conservative -- it flags an honest
re-widen presented as a fragment that does not demonstrate the prior held authority. No effect bypass has been
demonstrated any round through V27; the BLOCKERs are checker/kernel soundness failures with terminal-deny
mitigation, not capability escalation. Fresh-seat rotation (Qwen/DeepSeek) remains owed under SHV D6 and is
decisive now that a fix attacks the authority granted.

directly; it is the exact recurring meta-defect (the fix and the verification code, not the original bug,
are the dominant defect surface):

  from the marker. The checker ARMS only for a marker whose declared licensed_epoch is present and EQUALS

  does not hold, so the V23 dispatch says the seat CONFIRMS internal SHA256SUMS consistency and REPORTS its
  recomputed MANIFEST, and the PRODUCER performs seal-equality. The prior wording overstated what a seat
  can self-execute without an authenticated channel.

# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-21, post V19 audit)

Byline: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

## Audit round V19 -- three VALID executing seats (repair20 bytes), two in CONTINUOUS mode
V19 verdicts on repair20 (MANIFEST 96b80b19...): GPT-5.6 (continuous) PASS-no-blocker but not clean
(4 MAJOR); GLM-5.2 (one-shot) 1 MAJOR + 2 MINOR + 3 INFO; Kimi K3 (continuous) HALT (1 BLOCKER + 8 MAJOR
+ 10 MEDIUM + 6 LOW + 4 INFO). No unauthorized EFFECT; all defects audit/projection/claim-plane. The core
pass-20 retirements (CLOCK on all four paths, A2 marker, type-strict divergence, commit-time inverted
lease, X7 totality) were independently VERIFIED FIXED by the seats. Convergence: ZERO.

## The V19 lesson: retirements must be CLASS-COMPLETE and coverage-VERIFIED
Pass-20 retired shapes at the FIRST site and asserted class coverage; the seats showed the retirements
were partial (type-strict in X7 only; X7 fail-closed but X4 fail-OPEN; A4 mismatch but not omission) and,
most sharply, that G12 -- the gate built to forbid overclaims -- hardcoded four probes and let an
unprobed false claim ship green (GPT-P4 / GLM-01 / K20-G1, three-seat consensus, producer-reproduced).
Pass-21 completes each retirement across its whole class and makes G12 registry-driven so coverage cannot
lag its claims.

### Retirement ledger (pass-21) -- each claim is registered in gate_g12 and tagged here
- {claim:CLAIM-CLOCK} CLOCK: one strict `_read_clock()` (`type is int`, `0 <= v <= year-9999`, no
  coercion) is the ONLY clock access on every path; G12 verifies both the behavior and that no
  `int(self.clock())` bypass remains. Regression: CE124, CE133.
- {claim:CLAIM-X4-FAILCLOSED} X4 now FAILS CLOSED on an unhashable token id: the id is canonicalized to a
  stable key, so a double redemption with list/dict ids is flagged, not skipped (GPT-P1). Regression: CE130.
- {claim:CLAIM-TYPESTRICT} TYPE-STRICT: `_json_scalar_eq` (bool != int) governs the X7 divergence
  comparison. Regression: CE125. (Class note: X4 keys on canonicalized ids and enum membership, not
  scalar aliasing, so the type-confusion class does not reach it.)
- {claim:CLAIM-UNHASHABLE} TOTALITY: `_safe_strset` fails closed on a non-string element; X7 does not
  raise on a nested-list element. Regression: CE129.
- {claim:CLAIM-A4-OMISSION} A4: a settlement / PASS execution receipt that OMITS
  revalidation.authority_epoch fails closed (X7), not only a mismatched one (GPT-P3). Regression: CE131.
- {claim:CLAIM-A2-MARKER} A2: the X7 carve-out arms ONLY from a correction-accepted marker BOUND to a
  present accepted-LIFT correction-event (digest resolves + shape ok; optional signature verification via
  a `verify` callable). A bare or unbound marker no longer arms (GPT-P2). Regression: CE128, CE132, G11.
  Q3 (does NOT do): with no `verify` callable and a fully foreign log that includes BOTH a forged marker
  and a matching forged event, offline audit still cannot cryptographically establish acceptance -- the
  reference gate has no signing key by design; supply the adjudicator public keys via `verify` to close it.
- {claim:CLAIM-INTERVAL-COMMIT} INTERVAL: the inverted-lease rule (observed_at > expires_at) is enforced
  at commit-time fresh-witness revalidation. Regression: CE127.

### G12 made registry-driven (retires its own pass-20 recursion)
G12 now iterates a CLAIMS REGISTRY: every registered claim's probe must pass, every registered claim must
be tagged `{claim:<ID>}` here, and every `{claim:<ID>}` tag must be registered -- so a load-bearing claim
without a passing probe FAILS the verifier, and coverage cannot silently lag. Its PASS message is scoped
truthfully ("every registered load-bearing claim has a passing probe and a tag"), not the pass-20 overclaim
"load-bearing REPAIR_STATUS claims re-verified". CE citations are checked for any digit count, and a stated
counterexample count is cross-checked against the corpus (this document claims 133 counterexamples).

MAJOR); and whether the G12 recursion rated BLOCKER (Kimi) or MAJOR (GPT/GLM). Also still open per Kimi:

# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-20, post V18 audit)

Byline: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

## Audit round V18 -- three VALID executing seats (repair19 bytes)
V18 verdicts on repair19 (MANIFEST 4d5b8ce2...): GPT-5.6 PASS-no-blocker but "not clean" (4 MAJOR +
1 MINOR); GLM-5.2 PASS-no-blocker (1 MAJOR + 2 MINOR + 1 INFO); Kimi K3 HALT (2 BLOCKER, both conceded
defensibly MAJOR, + 3 MAJOR + 10 MEDIUM + 8 LOW + 9 INFO). Every finding was reproduced on repair19 by
the producer. No finding demonstrated an unauthorized EFFECT -- every defect was in the projection /
audit / attestation / claim plane; commit() enforcement held. Convergence: ZERO. Progress: the severity
floor dropped from BLOCKER (V16/V17) to MAJOR, and the seats reported the loop "converging on smaller,
sharper defects."

## Design-strategy shift this round: retire SHAPES, not instances
Pass-20 adopts the Bayyinah Audit Framework Section 17.3 discipline: a repair RETIRES a failure-mode
SHAPE only when a gate/fixture/test structurally prevents the shape from recurring -- not when a single
instance is patched. The recurring shapes (each 3x+ across rounds) are retired via single-source-of-truth
code, not per-instance counterexamples.

### Retirement ledger (pass-20)
- CLOCK coercion/asymmetry (GPT-P19-03, GLM-01/04): RETIRED by one strict reader `_read_clock()`
  (`type(v) is int and v >= 0`, no coercion) used on EVERY path -- authorize, commit, `_bound`,
  `_execution_failure`. There is no longer a success/failure or authorize/commit asymmetry to have, and
  a string/float/bool/negative clock fails closed uniformly. Regression: CE124.
- TYPE-CONFUSION `True == 1` (GPT-P19-02, K19-B1): RETIRED by `_json_scalar_eq` (bool is never equal to
  int) used in the X7 divergence check. Regression: CE125.
- UNHASHABLE-ELEMENT crash (K19-E1): RETIRED by `_safe_strset`, which fails closed on a non-string
  element instead of raising TypeError inside `_auth_equal`/`_auth_subset`. Regression: CE129.
- INTERVAL authorize/commit asymmetry (GPT-P19-04): RETIRED by applying the inverted-lease rule
  (observed_at > expires_at) at commit-time fresh-witness revalidation, matching authorize-time.
  Regression: CE127.
- PERFORMED-REPAIR / overclaim (the meta-shape that recurred three rounds): RETIRED by verifier gate
  G12, which re-verifies load-bearing REPAIR_STATUS claims against runtime behavior and checks that every
  cited CE id exists. A false "handled / never raises / derived / every repair has a CE" line now fails
  the verifier and cannot ship green.

### Cluster repairs with the Five Questions answered (BAF Section 12.2)
For each fix, (Q3) is stated explicitly -- "what this does NOT do that a reader might expect" -- because
that omission is exactly where the last three rounds' overclaims lived.

- A2 (GPT-P19-01) -- X7's amendment carve-out now arms ONLY from a gate-issued `bssg.correction-accepted`
  MARKER, emitted by the gate after every signature/quorum/independence check passes; a raw
  correction-event (even schema-valid, even with rejected signatures) no longer licenses widening.
  Regression: CE128, G11. Q3 (does NOT do): an offline checker still has no cryptographic trust root, so
  against a fully FOREIGN log an attacker can fabricate a marker record; this fix closes the
  re-derived-acceptance gap and fails closed on bare/forged events, it does not manufacture offline trust.
- A3/A4 (GPT-P19-02, K19-B1/C1) -- X7 divergence is type-strict and flags a wrong-type value, a null
  counterpart, or a non-dict snapshot facing a dict one; an execution-receipt whose
  revalidation.authority_epoch is unresolved or mismatched fails closed (X7). Regression: CE125, CE126.
  Q3: A4's fail-closed assumes the audited stream is complete (the redeemed receipt precedes its
  execution receipt, as in a gate-produced stream); a deliberately truncated stream will flag, by design.
- INTERVAL (GPT-P19-04) -- see retirement ledger. Q3: does not re-validate historical (non-fresh) witness
  leases at commit; those were validated and bound at authorize.
- CLOCK / TYPE / UNHASHABLE -- see retirement ledger.
- D2 settlement order-sensitivity (K19-D2) -- adjudicated MEDIUM and NOT changed: order is meaningful in a
  temporal event log (a settle-then-commit is a genuine second redemption; a commit-then-settle is one).
  Documented as a declared property; a reordered foreign log is a known offline-audit limitation.

## Attestation: the "execution-bound" claim is WITHDRAWN (K19-A1)
Two rounds running, the attestation's execution-binding was shown thin: K18-13 (constant trace), then
K19-A1 (~94% of the trace is constant; the nonce-varying part is a digest chain reproducible from one
sample plus the digest function, without executing the gate's decision logic). An output-hash over
deterministic operations cannot bind execution against a party who can reproduce the outputs. Per SHV D1
("never certify on the intermediary's word") and D6 (certification is independent re-derivation), the
`bssg_attest.py` value is now documented as a PACKET-SAMPLE DIGEST, not an execution proof: it shows a
seat had the exact bytes, nothing more. The actual governance -- always -- is multi-chain reproduction of
every finding on the canonical bytes. The dispatch and HANDOFF are corrected to say so.

## Severity note (BAF rubric)
Under the Bayyinah rubric, several V18 findings re-rate upward: a regression of a prior fix is CRITICAL
(INTERVAL-not-at-commit, CLOCK-not-on-success extend prior fixes), and "documentation contradicts
