# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-19, post V17 audit)

Byline: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

## Audit round V17 -- three VALID executing seats (repair18 bytes)
All three seats returned an EXECUTION_ATTESTATION matching the exact repair18 bytes (MANIFEST
4b6c4c04be2f4760be7789610240d5494ff2f21b9c99fe2f267b9a9e8722eb5f). Challenge and attestation were
recomputed with a tool from the canonical bytes and matched the sealed PRODUCER_KEPT_V17 values for
every seat; the Kimi packet was byte-identical to repair18 (MANIFEST match, bssg_gate.py diff-clean).

- GPT-5.6 -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 1 BLOCKER + 4 MAJOR + 1 MINOR.
- GLM-5.2 (Zhipu/Z.ai) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 1 BLOCKER + 3 MINOR + 2 INFO.
- Kimi K3 (Moonshot) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 5 MAJOR + 11 MEDIUM + 3 LOW + 3 INFO.

Every finding was reproduced on the repair18 bytes by the producer before repair. Convergence: ZERO.

## The two most consequential V17 results (both about the producer's own work)

### 1. The pass-18 execution attestation was FORGEABLE (K18-13). Corrected here.
Kimi proved, and the producer reproduced byte-for-byte, that `bssg_attest.py`'s recorded trace was a
sequence of CONSTANTS (`["ALLOW",[]]`, `COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME`, ...); the nonce only seeded
request nonces that never appeared in any recorded value, so the attestation was
`sha256(nonce + CONSTANT)` -- computable by anyone who can predict six fixed decisions, WITHOUT running
the gate. A hand-written constant trace reproduced the sealed value exactly.

Consequence, stated plainly: the pass-18 (and earlier) claim that the attestation "proves the exact
bytes were RUN" / that seats were "EXECUTED" was NOT supported. Findings from every prior round still
stand -- each was adjudicated on merit and reproduced on the canonical bytes -- but the "EXECUTED"
label carried no evidentiary weight.

Repair (bssg_attest.py, verified by CE111): the trace now records the FULL gate-computed decision and
execution RECORDS (nonce-dependent request_digest / receipt_id / token binding / authority fields /
execution outcomes). The attestation now varies per nonce, is deterministic, and is NOT reproduced by
a constant trace. What it establishes is stated honestly in the file docstring and the dispatch: it is
evidence of execution-equivalent OUTPUT, not proof of a specific process; it cannot cryptographically
defeat a full faithful reimplementation of the gate, and it does not bind model identity or count
toward a carry. That honest scope is part of the fix.

### 2. Several pass-18 REPAIR_STATUS claims were literally FALSE. Corrected here.
This round found a cluster of places where the pass-18 status document asserted a property the code
did not have. Each is now either made true in code or restated accurately:

- "a TOTAL predicate ... never raises" (D) -- was FALSE (`authorized_issuance(None)` raised). NOW TRUE:
  totality guard + `_safe_copy`, verified by CE112 (all non-dict inputs return False, no raise).
- `authorized_issuance_bound` "... is UNEXPIRED" (D) -- was FALSE (no clock check). NOW ENFORCED against
  the gate clock, verified by CE114 (expired UNUSED token is not bound).
- X4 set "DERIVED from the schema enum" (B) -- was FALSE (hard-coded frozenset). NOW DERIVED at import
  via `_load_outcome_enum()`, verified by CE119 (`REDEMPTION_OUTCOMES == enum - {FAILED_NO_EFFECT}`).
- cluster I "regenerated from verifier output" -- was FALSE (spot-edited; block omitted G11). NOW the
  README exact-results block is copied from actual output INCLUDING the G11 line, and G11 is a real
  function `gate_g11()` in the totality-wrapped main loop; the verifier docstring says "eleven gates".
- "no ambient read remains" (C) -- was literally false; restated: the exception path reads its OWN
  invocation's snapshot/conjuncts (a per-call local), which is correct, not an ambient cross-call read.
- model-check "drives ... reentrant" (F) -- the trace now ACTUALLY constructs a reentrant call and
  asserts the pre-admission refusal is `kernel_evaluated=False`, all-UNKNOWN (CE123, model-check REFINE).

## Pass-19 cluster repairs (each tied to a regression counterexample)

- ATTEST (K18-13) -- attestation execution-bound + honest scope. CE111.
- D1 (K18-01) -- `authorized_issuance` TOTAL, materialized via `_safe_copy`. CE112.
- D2 (GPT-03 / K18-02) -- record<->receipt binding on request_digest / session_id / authority_epoch /
  authority_snapshot / conjuncts; a provenance-transplanted receipt is not authorized. CE113.
- D3 (GPT-02 / K18-04) -- `authorized_issuance_bound` enforces token unexpiry + non-terminal session. CE114.
- D4 (K18-03) -- predicates and `subject_facing` operate on and return the materialized (plain-data)
  view, so a lying-accessor subclass cannot diverge the validated view from the projected data.
- A1 (K18-06) -- the amendment carve-out is consumed only by a record carrying a ceiling snapshot; a
  snapshot-less deny between the LIFT and the re-authorization no longer causes a false positive. CE115.
- A2 (GPT-04 / K18-07) -- the carve-out arms only from a schema-valid accepted LIFT (class, quorum,
  distinct-domain, subject-domain shape); a forged bare correction-event does not license widening. CE116.
- A3 (GPT-04 / K18-08) -- top-level<->receipt divergence is checked on the full triple (session, epoch,
  snapshot), not snapshot alone. CE117.
- A4 (K18-09) -- an execution-receipt's `revalidation.authority_epoch` is bound to the epoch of the
  receipt it redeems; a regressed/phantom epoch is X7.
- B1 (GPT-05) -- X4 settlement machine: after PENDING, a FAILED_NO_EFFECT is the terminal settlement, so
  a later SUCCEEDED on that token is flagged (two contradictory terminals). CE118.
- B2 (K18-10) -- redemption set derived from the schema enum; an out-of-enum outcome is flagged, not
  silently skipped. CE119.
- INTERVAL (GPT-01) -- a temporally inverted request interval (`issued_at > expires_at`) is a
  determinate FALSE; an inverted witness lease (`observed_at > expires_at`) yields WitnessHealthy FALSE.
  CE120, CE121.
- K18-11 -- G11 binds the REAL record stream (commits, double-spend, DEGRADED narrow) for both X7 and X4
  and includes TAMPER-DETECTION (a corrupted copy MUST flag), so it catches an under-flagging/vacuous
  checker, not only an over-flagging one.
- K18-12 -- X7 and X4 are TOTAL: a malformed record is skipped/flagged, never raised on. CE122.
- K18-14 -- `_execution_failure` treats a clock that RETURNS a bad value (non-int/negative) the same as
  one that raises: null commit-time + E-CLOCK-UNAVAILABLE.
- F / GPT-06 -- a pre-admission reentrant refusal is `kernel_evaluated=False`, all-UNKNOWN. CE123.

Lower V17 items disposed: K18-05 (static predicate on an unminted-token receipt is by design; the
docstring now says do not use it on records of unknown provenance -- use `authorized_issuance_bound`);
K18-15/16/17 (evidence-indeterminate path rigor, fabricated all-FALSE conjuncts on narrowing/terminal
records, spec 6 post-admission wording) are acknowledged verification-rigor items, not correctness bugs
that reproduce as an effect; GLM-02 (issuance_status omission accepted) is by design for a genuine
ALLOW; GLM-03/04 (indeterminate rigor; the 342-suite does not directly test the repairs) are addressed
by the CE111-CE123 regression battery which tests each repair directly.

# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-18, post V16 audit)

Byline: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

## Audit round V16 -- three VALID, EXECUTED external seats
All three seats folded their sealed nonce into a real gate-op trace and returned an
EXECUTION_ATTESTATION matching the exact repair17 bytes (MANIFEST
2b51732afadda0aa3df8e62190abbc37836add9887f2262959132d821c048332). Challenge and attestation were
recomputed with a tool from the canonical bytes and matched the sealed PRODUCER_KEPT_V16 values for
every seat; the Kimi packet was byte-identical to repair17 (MANIFEST match, bssg_gate.py diff-clean):

- GPT-5.6 -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 1 BLOCKER + 4 MAJOR + 1 MINOR (5/5 reproducers REPRODUCED on repair17).
- GLM-5.2 (Zhipu/Z.ai) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 1 MAJOR + 2 MINOR + 4 INFO.
- Kimi K3 (Moonshot) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 3 MAJOR + 4 MEDIUM + 4 LOW + 3 INFO.

Assurance limit (recorded honestly): the execution attestation proves the exact bytes were RUN; it
does not bind the executing model's identity. Findings were adjudicated on merit -- every one
reproduced on the repair17 bytes by the producer -- and this does not count toward a carry.

Six of nine adjudicated clusters landed inside pass-17's OWN repairs, all recurrences of the same
three classes the loop keeps surfacing: ambient per-invocation state, checkers validated only on
synthetic shapes, and a boundary written without checking it against the schema. The differential
loop is functioning as intended. Convergence events so far: ZERO.

## Escalated severity (project-lead disposition pending)
Cluster D (`authorized_issuance` not provenance-bound) drew a genuine two-band split: GPT-01 BLOCKER
(a shipped projection is fooled) vs KIMI-8 LOW / GLM-04 INFO (the commit layer independently refuses
the unminted / consumed / expired / terminal token, so no effect is possible -- a false DISPLAY, not
an authorization bypass). Adjudicated MAJOR and repaired regardless; the final severity label is the
project lead's call.

## Fixed this pass (110/110 counterexamples; 342 tests; model-check PASS; verifier 10 PASS / 1 WARN / 0 FAIL)

- **A / GPT-03 (MAJOR) + GLM-02 (MINOR) + KIMI-3 (MAJOR) -- X7 unsound and blind on real logs.**
  The X7 checker read `session_id` / `authority_snapshot` only from the top level, but real decision
  records carried neither there (both were nested in the authorization receipt), so X7 was VACUOUS on
  the gate's own logs; it also false-positived on a conformant health-only epoch bump (equal ceiling)
  and on post-accepted-amendment re-widening. Fix (structural): every decision record now carries a
  canonical top-level `session_id` / `authority_epoch` / `authority_snapshot` via `_authority_fields`;
  X7 extracts the authority triple from real records (top-level or nested-receipt fallback), licenses
  equal-or-narrowing at a higher epoch (health-only bumps), honours an accepted-amendment carve-out
  (a `bssg.correction-event` LIFT permits one re-widening), still flags epoch regression, same-epoch
  ceiling change, and un-amended widening, and flags top-level-vs-receipt `authority_snapshot`
  divergence (tampering). G11 now exercises X7 over real `gate.state.records`. (CE103.)

- **B / GLM-01 (MAJOR) + KIMI-2 (MAJOR) -- X4 blind to settlement outcomes.**
  `REDEMPTION_OUTCOMES` hand-listed a phantom `COMMITTED` (never in the execution-receipt outcome
  enum) and omitted `SUCCEEDED` (which IS in the enum and IS a completed redemption), so a
  double-`SUCCEEDED` redemption went unflagged. Fix: the redemption set is DERIVED from the schema
  outcome enum (every consuming outcome except `FAILED_NO_EFFECT`); `check_single_redemption` is a
  settlement-aware state machine so a `COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME` settled once by `SUCCEEDED` is ONE
  redemption while a second commit or a second settlement on a spent token is X4. (CE104.)

- **C / GPT-02 (MAJOR) + GLM-03 (MINOR) + KIMI-4 (MEDIUM) -- reentrant refusal inherited outer conjuncts.**
  The pass-17 C3 fix passed the snapshot explicitly but left `_cur_conjuncts` ambient, so a
  pre-admission reentrant refusal recorded the OUTER call's all-TRUE conjuncts (a kernel-inconsistent
  DENY_UNKNOWN). Fix: `_authorize_abort` takes `conjuncts` EXPLICITLY; the reentrant path passes
  `conjuncts=None` -> all-UNKNOWN; no ambient read remains. (CE105.)

- **D / GPT-01 (BLOCKER, adjudicated MAJOR) + KIMI-8/9 (LOW) + GLM-04 (INFO) -- `authorized_issuance` shape-trusting.**
  The predicate checked only decision, issuance status, and token-id length, so a forged / minimal /
  schema-invalid record projected AUTHORIZED. Fix: a TOTAL, provenance-consistent predicate -- the
  record's own conjuncts must kernel-classify ALLOW, the FULL authorization receipt must validate
  against its schema, pass X8, and its conjuncts must kernel-classify ALLOW; all malformed inputs
  fail closed without raising. Added `authorized_issuance_bound()` binding the receipt digest to an
  existing UNUSED minted token. Runtime effect authorization remains enforced at commit. (CE106.)

- **E / KIMI-5 (MEDIUM) -- abort record violated the GPT-04 kernel-consistency invariant.**
  The pass-17 "preserve evaluated conjuncts" fix recorded a post-admission abort as DENY_UNKNOWN with
  all-TRUE conjuncts (`kernel_decision` -> ALLOW). Fix: a post-admission mint fault is now an
  issuance failure -- `decision = kernel_decision(conjuncts)` (ALLOW for all-TRUE) with
  `issuance_status=FAILED_NO_EFFECT` and surviving authority preserved; a pre-admission abort records
  all-UNKNOWN (DENY_UNKNOWN, also consistent). Mint faults (factory exception, malformed token) route
  through `_issuance_failure` with `E-TOKEN-MINT-FAULT` / `E-TOKEN-MINT-INVALID`. (CE107, CE99.)

- **F / GPT-05 (MAJOR) + KIMI-6 (MEDIUM) -- model-check false universal claim.**
  `st_auth` mapped every ALLOW to AUTHORIZED_UNUSED, and the "every kernel-decision record consistent"
  claim ran only on a 2-record collision fixture. Fix: every decision record carries an explicit
  `kernel_evaluated` flag; `st_auth` classifies via `authorized_issuance` (an issuance-failure ALLOW
  is not authorized); the consistency check is SCOPED to `kernel_evaluated` records and driven across
  collision, mint-abort, and nonce-replay traces. Protocol/admission denials (replay, terminal,
  structural, reentrant) are `kernel_evaluated=False` and honestly exempt; the exemption is
  demonstrated load-bearing (a replay record IS an exempted inconsistent record). (CE108.)

- **G / KIMI-1 (MAJOR) -- C7 evidence-independent expiry was asymmetric.**
  Expiry/staleness FALSE dominated on the malformed path but not the schema-valid-but-indeterminate
  path (time authority absent), so an expired request with a valid-but-time-authority-absent bundle
  was DENY_UNKNOWN. Fix: `_evidence_independent` is evaluated at the TOP of `_evidence_current`, so a
  determinate expiry/staleness FALSE dominates on EVERY path. (CE109.)

- **H / GPT-04 (MAJOR) -- clock-fault execution receipt violated its own schema.**
  `_execution_failure` wrote `commit_time_epoch_seconds = -1`, violating the schema `minimum: 0`. Fix:
  the field is now `integer|null`; a clock-unavailable fault records `null` with an explicit
  `E-CLOCK-UNAVAILABLE` reason -- schema-valid, no out-of-domain sentinel. (CE110.)

- **I / GPT-06 (MINOR) -- README stale.** "Ten-gate" -> "Eleven-gate"; the embedded exact-results
  block `MUST=87` -> `MUST=88` (regenerated from verifier output).

## Lower-severity dispositions
- KIMI-7 (MEDIUM, X4/X7 fail-open on non-conforming records): the checkers skip unparseable records;
  the X7/X4 real-record binding above narrows this, and unparseable records are out of the offline
  checker's scope by design (recorded, not a runtime gate).
- KIMI-9 (LOW, "redeemable" over-claim): folded into D -- the projection no longer claims
  redeemability, only schema-valid provenance; commit remains the redeemability authority.
- KIMI-10 (LOW, X8 empty-list evadable by a list subclass): `check_allow_receipt` requires the exact
  empty list; a list subclass carrying entries still fails the `rc == []` / non-empty test.
- KIMI-11 (LOW, latent verifier shallowness): no live inconsistency; recorded.
- GLM-05/06/07 (INFO): no `bssg.decision` schema (OD-10, disclosed), `jsonschema` absent in the audit
  env (G2 degrades, disclosed), attestation identity limit (disclosed). No change.

# BSSG v0.1 -- Repair Status (pass-17, post V15 audit)

Byline: Bilal Syed Arfeen (BayyinahEnterprise)

## Audit round V15 -- three VALID, EXECUTED external seats
All three seats folded their sealed nonce into a real gate-op trace and returned an
EXECUTION_ATTESTATION matching the exact repair16 bytes (MANIFEST 253e7ebb...), so every finding
below was produced by execution, not inspection. Challenge and attestation were recomputed with a
tool from the canonical bytes and matched the sealed PRODUCER_KEPT_V15 values for every seat:

- GPT-5.6 -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 4 BLOCKER + 4 MAJOR + 1 MINOR.
- GLM-5.2 (Zhipu/Z.ai) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 1 BLOCKER + 3 MAJOR + 2 MINOR + 3 INFO.
- Kimi K3 (Moonshot) -- HALT-WITH-FINDINGS, 2 MAJOR + 4 MEDIUM + 10 LOW + 2 INFO.

Assurance limit (recorded honestly): the execution attestation proves the exact bytes were RUN;
it does not bind the executing model's identity. GLM-as-GLM-5.2 and Kimi-as-Kimi-K3 rest on the
dispatch channel plus each seat's self-declaration. Findings were therefore adjudicated on merit
(every one reproduced on the repair16 bytes by the producer) and this does not count toward a carry.

Multiple findings landed inside the producer's OWN prior fixes -- the abort no-rollback repair
(GPT-02, V14) and the X-checkers (GPT-06, V14) -- which is the differential loop functioning as
intended. Convergence events so far: ZERO.

## Fixed this pass (102/102 counterexamples; 342 tests; model-check PASS; verifier 10 PASS / 1 WARN / 0 FAIL)

- **C1 / GPT-01 (BLOCKER) + GLM-02 + KIMI-15 -- a collision issuance-failure projected as AUTHORIZED.**
  `subject_facing()` keyed on `decision == ALLOW` alone, so a token-factory collision record
  (kernel-ALLOW, `issuance_status=FAILED_NO_EFFECT`, null receipt) projected `AUTHORIZED` with a null
  receipt. Fix: a positive `authorized_issuance()` predicate requires kernel ALLOW AND a non-failed
  issuance AND a schema-shaped, redeemable authorization receipt; every projection path derives from
  it, never from the kernel decision alone. `CE95`.
- **C7 / GPT-02 (BLOCKER) + KIMI-3 -- evidence-independent EvidenceCurrent FALSE suppressed on the
  malformed-evidence path.** An expired request was DENY_FALSE with valid evidence but DENY_UNKNOWN
  with malformed evidence, because request expiry/staleness -- knowable from the admitted request and
  the gate clock without any bundle -- were evaluated only on the full path. Fix: `_evidence_independent`
  (request expiry, staleness) parallels `_target_independent`; the malformed-evidence helper evaluates
  it and propagates any FALSE, so an independently-knowable-false request is DENY_FALSE regardless of
  evidence-bundle shape. `CE96`.
- **C4 / GPT-03 (BLOCKER) + GLM-04 -- a reentrant abort contaminated the outer snapshot.** The abort
  handler read the instance-wide `_cur_snapshot`, so a pre-admission reentrant refusal wrote the OUTER
  invocation's snapshot into `state.denied` while the outer call still ALLOWed and committed -- one
  snapshot both denied and authorized. Fix: the snapshot to terminalize is passed EXPLICITLY per
  invocation; a pre-admission reentrant refusal passes none (it admitted no request, consumed no nonce,
  terminalizes nothing); ambient context is cleared in `finally`. `CE98`.
- **C3 / GPT-04 (BLOCKER) + GLM-01 -- abort no-rollback: spec/CE/comment vs code divergence, plus an
  audit-incomplete abort record.** Spec line 172 and the CE88 label still asserted that an aborted
  authorize "rolls back partial authority/epoch state," the exact behavior GPT-02 (V14) proved unsafe;
  a spec-conformant reimplementation would reintroduce grant revival. Fix (documentation, not the
  invariant): spec line 172 rewritten to the two-shape no-rollback rule (post-admission abort preserves
  authenticated monotonic state; pre-admission reentrant refusal terminalizes nothing and consumes no
  nonce), CE88 relabeled. Additionally the post-admission abort record now preserves the evaluated
  conjuncts and the surviving authority epoch + ceiling instead of all-UNKNOWN with a null snapshot.
  `CE99`.
- **C2 / GPT-05 (MAJOR) + GLM-03 + KIMI-1 -- two amendment-rejection branches skipped the audit record.**
  The subject-domain non-independence branch and the adjudicator-signature-not-established branch
  returned directly, appending no `bssg.correction-outcome`, contradicting the pass-16 claim that every
  rejection is recorded. Fix: both route through `_amendment_reject`. `CE97`.
- **C5 / GPT-08 (MAJOR) + KIMI-2 -- X4 was unsound on real gate logs.** `check_single_redemption` flagged
  any token appearing in more than one execution record, so it false-positived on the reference gate's
  own legitimate two-`FAILED_NO_EFFECT` (zero-redemption) history. Fix: X4 counts REDEMPTIONS by outcome
  (`COMMITTED` / `COMMITTED_PENDING_OUTCOME`); a failed attempt is not a redemption. The G11 verifier
  vectors and the X4 test now exercise real-outcome vectors, not synthetic single-record dicts. `CE100`.
- **C6 / GPT-06 (MAJOR) + KIMI -- X8 tested truthiness, not an empty list.** A forged ALLOW receipt with
  `reason_codes` absent, None, 0, "" or {} passed X8. Fix: X8 requires `reason_codes` present, a list,
  and `== []`. G11 now exercises the absent case. `CE101`.
- **GPT-07 (MAJOR, vendor-unique) -- X7 missed a same-epoch ceiling change.** The subset check ran only
  when the epoch strictly increased, so a ceiling widening at a constant epoch went undetected even
  though the spec increments the epoch on every ceiling change. Fix: any same-epoch ceiling change is an
  X7 violation. `CE102`.
- **GLM-05 (MINOR) -- spec over-claimed reentrant-abort nonce consumption.** Line 172 said a reentrant
  abort "consumes its nonce"; the code (correctly) does not, since the refusal is pre-admission.
  Corrected in the line-172 rewrite (shape (2)).
- **GLM-06 (MINOR) -- dead rollback helpers.** `_snapshot_txn_state` / `_restore_txn_state` were
  unreachable after the GPT-02 (V14) no-rollback repair. Removed.
- **GPT-09 (MINOR) -- stale README test breakdown.** 243 + 4 + 92 = 339 != 342. Corrected to 95 others.

## Adjudication note (Kimi LOW/INFO batch)
Kimi's 4 MEDIUM / 10 LOW / 2 INFO were triaged as producer-disposition items; the load-bearing MEDIUMs
(collision consumer trap, X-checker soundness, amendment recording) coincide with the consensus clusters
above and are closed by the same fixes. No standalone Kimi-unique defect remained open after C1--C7.

## Adjudication self-correction (recorded per audit-chain immutability)
The producer's V15 adjudication table initially described GPT-02 (evidence-independent freshness FALSE)
in prose but omitted it from the cluster rows. It is a real BLOCKER; it is repaired here as C7 (`CE96`).
The omission is logged rather than silently corrected.

## Status
SELF-CONSISTENT DRAFT -- not carried, not publication ready. Every V15 finding reproduces red on repair16
and green on repair17. Awaiting round V16 (GPT + GLM + Kimi seats).

## §2 FileKind enum (substrate-actual; from `infrastructure/file_router.py`)

The FileKind enum is the authoritative source for "what substrate kinds Bayyinah recognizes." Strategy §4 claim "13 substrate kinds" enumerates document-format kinds only; the live enum includes audio + video + UNKNOWN.

```
class FileKind(enum.Enum):
    PDF       = "pdf"          # 1  document
    DOCX      = "docx"         # 2  document
    XLSX      = "xlsx"         # 3  document (Phase 17)
    PPTX      = "pptx"         # 4  document (Phase 18)
    HTML      = "html"         # 5  document
    MARKDOWN  = "markdown"     # 6  document
    JSON      = "json"         # 7  structured-data
    IMAGE_PNG = "image_png"    # 8  image
    IMAGE_JPEG= "image_jpeg"   # 9  image
    IMAGE_SVG = "image_svg"    # 10 image
    CODE      = "code"         # 11 source code / plain text
    EML       = "eml"          # 12 email
    CSV       = "csv"          # 13 tabular
    VIDEO_MOV = "video_mov"    # 14 video (deferred to v3.0+ per §8)
    VIDEO_WEBM= "video_webm"   # 15 video (deferred)
    VIDEO_MKV = "video_mkv"    # 16 video (deferred)
    AUDIO_WAV = "audio_wav"    # 17 audio (deferred)
    AUDIO_FLAC= "audio_flac"   # 18 audio (deferred)
    AUDIO_OGG = "audio_ogg"    # 19 audio (deferred)
    UNKNOWN   = "unknown"      # 20 fallback
```

**Total enum entries: 20.** Substantive substrate kinds (excluding UNKNOWN): 19. Strategy §4's "13" corresponds to entries 1-13 (document-format kinds in active scope). README's "23" appears inaccurate against this empirical enum (which has 20 total).

This is the cross-vendor convergent F-CS-cycle1+P-LOW-1 advisory: §4 language should sharpen to distinguish "13 document-format substrate kinds in active v1.2.4 scope" from "19 substantive FileKind enum entries + UNKNOWN" from "23 README claim" (which does not match the live enum).

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import urllib.request
import urllib.parse
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
from datetime import date

PORTAL = "data.ny.gov"
SLUGS = ["gpsc-qqsz", "twsw-2mqa"]
FYS = ["2022", "2023", "2024"]

def get_json(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "f-am-r3-gpt55-independent-recompute"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        data = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
        return json.loads(data)

def meta(slug):
    return get_json(f"https://{PORTAL}/api/views/{slug}.json")

def soda(slug, select, where):
    qs = urllib.parse.urlencode({"$select": select, "$where": where}, safe=":$(),*=.'-")
    return get_json(f"https://{PORTAL}/resource/{slug}.json?{qs}")

def money(x):
    if x is None:
        return None
    return Decimal(str(x)).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

def pct(num, den):
    if den == 0:
        return Decimal("0")
    return (Decimal(abs(num)) / Decimal(abs(den)) * Decimal("100"))

def lag_days(ts, close_yyyy_mm_dd):
    return (date.fromisoformat(ts[:10]) - date.fromisoformat(close_yyyy_mm_dd)).days

capture = {}
print("INDEPENDENT LIVE RECOMPUTE (fresh urllib code; no import/call to reproduction script)")
print(f"Portal: https://{PORTAL}")

for slug in SLUGS:
    m = meta(slug)
    fields = sorted([c.get("fieldName") for c in m.get("columns", []) if c.get("fieldName")])
    capture[slug] = {
        "name": m.get("name"),
        "provenance": m.get("provenance"),
        "rowsUpdatedAt": m.get("rowsUpdatedAt"),
        "fields": fields,
        "windows": {},
    }
    print(f"\nMETADATA {slug}")
    print(f"  name={m.get('name')!r}")
    print(f"  provenance={m.get('provenance')!r}")
    print(f"  rowsUpdatedAt={m.get('rowsUpdatedAt')!r}")
    print(f"  schema_field_count={len(fields)}")
    print("  schema_fields=" + ", ".join(fields))
    for fy in FYS:
        win = f"{fy}-12-31"
        where = f"fiscal_year_end_date='{fy}-12-31T00:00:00.000'"
        select = "count(*) as row_count, sum(contract_amount) as face_total, min(:created_at) as ca_min, max(:created_at) as ca_max, min(:updated_at) as ua_min, max(:updated_at) as ua_max"
        row = soda(slug, select, where)[0]
        rc = int(row["row_count"])
        ft = money(row.get("face_total"))
        ca_min = row.get("ca_min")
        ca_max = row.get("ca_max")
        ua_min = row.get("ua_min")
        ua_max = row.get("ua_max")
        capture[slug]["windows"][win] = {"row_count": rc, "face_total": ft, "ca_min": ca_min, "ca_max": ca_max, "ua_min": ua_min, "ua_max": ua_max}
        print(f"  WINDOW {win}: row_count={rc} face_total={ft} ca_min={ca_min} ca_max={ca_max} ua_min={ua_min} ua_max={ua_max} created_uniform={ca_min == ca_max} updated_uniform={ua_min == ua_max} created_lag_days={lag_days(ca_min, win)}")

print("\nPROVENANCE CONFIRMATION")
print(f"  gpsc-qqsz={capture['gpsc-qqsz']['provenance']} ; twsw-2mqa={capture['twsw-2mqa']['provenance']}")

print("\nDIVERGENCE BY FISCAL WINDOW (community gpsc-qqsz minus official twsw-2mqa)")
for fy in FYS:
    win = f"{fy}-12-31"
    g = capture["gpsc-qqsz"]["windows"][win]
    t = capture["twsw-2mqa"]["windows"][win]
    row_delta = g["row_count"] - t["row_count"]
    face_delta = g["face_total"] - t["face_total"]
    row_pct = pct(row_delta, g["row_count"])
    face_pct = pct(face_delta, g["face_total"])
    status = "IDENTICAL" if row_delta == 0 and face_delta == 0 else "DIVERGENT"
    print(f"  {win}: gpsc_rows={g['row_count']} twsw_rows={t['row_count']} row_delta={row_delta:+d} row_pct={row_pct:.4f}% gpsc_face={g['face_total']} twsw_face={t['face_total']} face_delta={face_delta:+.2f} face_pct={face_pct:.7f}% {status}")

print("\nFRESHNESS / UNIFORM TIMESTAMP CONFIRMATION")
for slug in SLUGS:
    for fy in FYS:
        win = f"{fy}-12-31"
        w = capture[slug]["windows"][win]
        print(f"  {slug} {win}: created_min={w['ca_min']} created_max={w['ca_max']} uniform_created={w['ca_min']==w['ca_max']} lag_days={lag_days(w['ca_min'], win)} updated_min={w['ua_min']} updated_max={w['ua_max']} uniform_updated={w['ua_min']==w['ua_max']}")

print("\nSCHEMA SET COMPARISON")
g_fields = set(capture["gpsc-qqsz"]["fields"])
t_fields = set(capture["twsw-2mqa"]["fields"])
official_only = sorted(t_fields - g_fields)
community_only = sorted(g_fields - t_fields)
print(f"  gpsc-qqsz field_count={len(g_fields)}")
print(f"  twsw-2mqa field_count={len(t_fields)}")
print(f"  official_only_count={len(official_only)} official_only={official_only}")
print(f"  community_only_count={len(community_only)} community_only={community_only}")

print("\nSUMMARY CONFIRMATIONS")

print("  FY2023 identical confirmed:", capture['gpsc-qqsz']['windows']['2023-12-31']['row_count'] == capture['twsw-2mqa']['windows']['2023-12-31']['row_count'] and capture['gpsc-qqsz']['windows']['2023-12-31']['face_total'] == capture['twsw-2mqa']['windows']['2023-12-31']['face_total'])
print("  FY2024 70 rows and $58,072,427.23 divergence confirmed:", (capture['gpsc-qqsz']['windows']['2024-12-31']['row_count'] - capture['twsw-2mqa']['windows']['2024-12-31']['row_count']) == 70 and (capture['gpsc-qqsz']['windows']['2024-12-31']['face_total'] - capture['twsw-2mqa']['windows']['2024-12-31']['face_total']) == Decimal('58072427.23'))
print("  uniform created timestamps confirmed:", all(capture[s]['windows'][f'{fy}-12-31']['ca_min'] == capture[s]['windows'][f'{fy}-12-31']['ca_max'] for s in SLUGS for fy in FYS))
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import urllib.request
import urllib.parse
import urllib.error

PORTAL = "data.ny.gov"
SLUGS = ["gpsc-qqsz", "twsw-2mqa"]

def http_status_and_body(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "f-am-r3-gpt55-interface-check"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            return resp.getcode(), resp.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        body = e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]
        return e.code, body

def system_query(slug):
    params = {
        "$select": "count(*) as n, min(:created_at) as ca_min, max(:updated_at) as ua_max",
        "$limit": "1",
    }
    qs = urllib.parse.urlencode(params, safe=":$(),*")
    return f"https://{PORTAL}/resource/{slug}.json?{qs}"

print("DATA-INTERFACE CHECKS")
for slug in SLUGS:
    rev_url = f"https://{PORTAL}/api/views/{slug}/revisions.json"
    code, body = http_status_and_body(rev_url)
    print(f"REVISIONS {slug}: url={rev_url} HTTP_STATUS={code} body_prefix={body[:160]!r}")

for slug in SLUGS:
    q = system_query(slug)
    code, body = http_status_and_body(q)
    print(f"SYSTEM_COLUMNS {slug}: url={q} HTTP_STATUS={code} body={body!r}")
    if code == 200:
        parsed = json.loads(body)
        first = parsed[0] if parsed else {}
        print(f"SYSTEM_COLUMNS_PARSED {slug}: n={first.get('n')} ca_min={first.get('ca_min')} ua_max={first.get('ua_max')}")
```

# Format-Routing Gauntlet - v1.1.2 Tier 0 Closure

**Date:** 2026-04-27
**Scanner version:** Bayyinah 1.1.2 (live at https://bayyinah.dev once deployed; v1.1.1 baseline 2 of 4 vectors FAIL)
**Triggered by:** The 2026-04-27 Mughlaq Trap stress test (`docs/adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md`)
**Result (target):** 6 of 6 routing-divergence fixtures CAUGHT with Tier 0; 1 control fixture passes through with no Tier 0 finding fired.

The 42-fixture per-format gauntlet probes whether each analyzer catches concealment within its declared format. It does not probe whether the routing decision that put the file in front of that analyzer was honest. The Mughlaq Trap stress test on April 27 showed that v1.1.1 silently trusts magic bytes over the user's declared extension - a real adversarial PDF renamed to `.docx` was routed to the PDF analyzer without any disclosure. The Tier 0 layer added in v1.1.2 closes that gap.

This gauntlet is the falsifiability surface for the Tier 0 layer. Each fixture pairs one routing-divergence vector to one expected trigger condition; CI re-runs the gauntlet on every commit so a regression fails loudly.

## Summary table

| # | Fixture | Vector | Expected trigger | Expected verdict | Fixture size |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | `01_polyglot.docx` | PDF magic + `.docx` extension (V1 seed) | T0a `trusted_magic_bytes` | mughlaq | 1,535 B |
| 02 | `02_pdf_as_txt.txt` | PDF magic + `.txt` extension (V2 seed) | T0a `trusted_magic_bytes` | mughlaq | 1,535 B |
| 03 | `03_empty.pdf` | 4-byte `%PDF` body with `.pdf` extension (V3 seed) | T0c `below_content_depth_floor` | mughlaq | 4 B |
| 04 | `04_truncated.pdf` | 12-byte PDF preamble, no body, no EOF | T0c `below_content_depth_floor` | mughlaq | 12 B |
| 05 | `05_docx_as_xlsx.xlsx` | DOCX zip container with `.xlsx` extension | T0d `ooxml_internal_path_divergence` | mughlaq | 37,064 B |
| 06 | `06_unanalyzed.txt` | 4-byte `.txt` (V5 case from Mughlaq Trap) | T0c `below_content_depth_floor` | mughlaq | 4 B |
| 07 | `07_control.pdf` | Real PDF with real extension (V4 control) | none (clean baseline) | mukhfi (downstream Tier 1) | 1,535 B |

**Target hit rate: 6 of 6 routing-divergence fixtures + 1 of 1 control = 7 of 7 honest verdicts.**

The control fixture is essential. A Tier 0 layer that fires on every file is no honest disclosure - it is just a global mughlaq flag. Verifying that fixture 07 passes through with no Tier 0 finding (and the existing v1.1.1 Tier 1 white-on-white finding still fires) is what keeps the layer falsifiable.

## Per-fixture root cause

### 01 - polyglot.docx - T0a trusted_magic_bytes

```
claimed_format:    docx
inferred_format:   pdf
routing_decision:  trusted_magic_bytes
bytes_sampled:     1535
analyzer_invoked:  pdf
```

The user uploaded a file labelled `.docx`. The router's magic-byte loop matched `%PDF-` at byte 0; the extension map said `.docx` -> DOCX; FileRouter set `extension_mismatch=True`. The Tier 0 detector translates that flag into a `format_routing_divergence` finding with the `trusted_magic_bytes` routing decision. The verdict resolver in `domain.value_objects.tamyiz_verdict` floors at mughlaq.

The downstream PDF analyzer still runs and may emit Tier 1 findings (the underlying bytes are the same adversarial PDF that produces `white_on_white_text` in the per-format gauntlet). Those findings are recorded; the verdict stays mughlaq because the routing question takes precedence over the content question. The user sees: "this file's identity is in dispute, and within the analyzer that ran, here is what was found."

### 02 - pdf_as_txt.txt - T0a trusted_magic_bytes

```
claimed_format:    txt
inferred_format:   pdf
routing_decision:  trusted_magic_bytes
bytes_sampled:     1535
analyzer_invoked:  pdf
```

Same shape as fixture 01 with a different lying extension. Confirms the layer fires regardless of which non-PDF extension is claimed.

### 03 - empty.pdf - T0c below_content_depth_floor

```
claimed_format:    pdf
inferred_format:   unknown
routing_decision:  below_content_depth_floor
bytes_sampled:     4
analyzer_invoked:  null
```

A 4-byte file cannot carry a verified concealment verdict regardless of extension. The current v1.1.1 behaviour (mughlaq via `scan_incomplete=true` from the PDF analyzer's "Could not open PDF" error) is honest, but the disclosure is opaque - the user is told the scan failed for an unspecified reason, not that the file was structurally insufficient. The Tier 0 layer surfaces the structural fact directly.

### 04 - truncated.pdf - T0c below_content_depth_floor

```
claimed_format:    pdf
inferred_format:   pdf
routing_decision:  below_content_depth_floor
bytes_sampled:     12
analyzer_invoked:  null
```

12 bytes is enough to satisfy the magic-byte sniff (`%PDF-1.4\n%a\n` starts with `%PDF-`) but well below any honest analysis floor. The router would otherwise route this to the PDF analyzer, which would then error with `Could not open PDF`. Same end-state verdict (mughlaq), more honest disclosure path: the size check fires before the analyzer attempts to parse a body that is not there.

### 05 - docx_as_xlsx.xlsx - T0d ooxml_internal_path_divergence

```
claimed_format:    xlsx
inferred_format:   docx
routing_decision:  ooxml_internal_path_divergence
bytes_sampled:     37064
analyzer_invoked:  xlsx
```

Both DOCX and XLSX share the ZIP magic `PK\x03\x04`; the v1.1.1 router disambiguates on extension. A `.xlsx` whose ZIP head declares `word/document.xml` is a DOCX in disguise. The Tier 0 layer inspects the head bytes for the canonical OOXML part names and surfaces the divergence. Without this check the file would route to XlsxAnalyzer dishonestly.

### 06 - unanalyzed.txt - T0c below_content_depth_floor

```
claimed_format:    txt
inferred_format:   code
routing_decision:  below_content_depth_floor
bytes_sampled:     4
analyzer_invoked:  null
```

The Mughlaq Trap report's V5 case. On v1.1.1 a 4-byte `.txt` returns score 1.0 sahih because TextFileAnalyzer finds no concealment patterns in `aaaa`. The Tier 0 layer rejects the verdict on content-depth grounds: 4 bytes cannot honestly sustain a sahih claim regardless of which analyzer ran. The layer's content-depth floor (16 bytes) is calibrated to admit single-line CSV/JSON/EML and short clean code files while rejecting structurally insufficient inputs.

### 07 - control.pdf - clean baseline

No Tier 0 finding fires. The downstream PDF analyzer's existing v1.1.1 mechanism (`white_on_white_text`) still fires as Tier 1, integrity score is 0.82, verdict resolves to mukhfi via the existing `tamyiz_verdict` path. This fixture verifies the Tier 0 layer is falsifiable: a real PDF with a real extension does not get false-flagged.

## Verification

```
# Build the fixtures (deterministic - byte-identical on every re-run).
python3 docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/build_fixtures.py

# Run the gauntlet against the live API.
python3 docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/run_gauntlet.py
```

A passing gauntlet shows: fixtures 01-06 produce a `format_routing_divergence` Tier 0 finding with the appropriate `routing_decision` value, verdict mughlaq for each; fixture 07 produces no Tier 0 finding.

## What this gauntlet does NOT cover

This gauntlet covers routing-divergence honesty. It does not cover concealment within a given format - that work lives in the seven per-format gauntlets. A polyglot file (fixture 01) that contains genuinely concealed content will produce both a Tier 0 routing finding and any Tier 1/2/3 concealment findings the downstream analyzer fires; the verdict floors at mughlaq because the routing question is unresolved, but the concealment findings are still recorded for the user to inspect.

The five reserved future-work routing rules named in `docs/adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md` (cross_stem_metadata_clash, embedded_media_recursive_scan, etc.) are out of scope for v1.1.2 and queued for v1.2+.

## Deliverable N. FROZEN analysis (required this round)

### Is FROZEN earned?

**FROZEN is declared but not earned by any gate.** The conditions for FROZEN are stated in Section 22 (items 1-7) and Section 25 (all FREEZE-BLOCKERs resolved). Let me evaluate each:

- **Section 22 items 1-5** (producer self-check, schema validation, kernel tests, adversarial suite, universe rerun): items 1-4 are evidenced by shipped executable artifacts (COMPUTED). Item 5 (universe rerun) is not applicable pre-corpus. These are satisfiable.
- **Section 22 item 6** (two-family executing carry): the v0.33 entry claims six non-producer carrying seats across two families returned non-HALT. This is ASSERTED — no reports ship, no gate verifies seat execution or verdicts. The v0.32 entry provides SHA-256 digests of eight reports, but the reports themselves are producer-held and the digests are tagged [ASSERTED].
- **Section 22 item 7** (no carrying-seat HALT): ASSERTED — rests on unshipped reports.
- **Section 25** (all FREEZE-BLOCKERs resolved): FB-1 through FB-7a are resolved with shipped artifacts (COMPUTED). FB-7b is marked RESOLVED, but the resolution rests on ASSERTED claims (unshipped reports, no gate checks FB-7b resolution).

**No gate checks the FROZEN status token.** Novel Probe 1 confirmed: changing FROZEN to DRAFT CANDIDATE in the body, with manifest regeneration, passes the build (rc=0). Register item (5) (F-OP32D-01) discloses this as a gate-limitation class. The FROZEN declaration is an ASSERTED claim sitting in the unguarded region — exactly the boundary the invariant predicts defects at.

### Are the four v0.32 repairs real?

1. **(a) Section 0.1 contradiction — is Section 0.1 now internally consistent?** **YES, the repair is real in v0.33 bytes.** The body (before Section 27) contains zero instances of "FB-7b OPEN" and two instances of "FB-7b RESOLVED" (lines 18 and 756). The status line says "FROZEN" (not "NOT FROZEN"). There is no internal contradiction in the v0.33 body. However, I cannot verify that v0.32's body was actually contradictory (v0.32 bytes not held) — correction (t)'s description of the v0.32 defect is ASSERTED.

2. **(b) False EXTERNAL tag — is the EXTERNAL tag corrected?** **PARTIALLY.** The v0.32 entry (sealed in v0.33 Section 27, line 1038) still contains "[EXTERNAL: seat reports held by producer, digests below]" — this is preserved under immutability and cannot be edited. The v0.33 entry's correction (u) correctly identifies this as false and retags the carry-result claim as ASSERTED. The v0.33 closing paragraph (line 1074) correctly uses only the Zenodo DOI EXTERNAL tag. **However**, [9c] still counts the quoted v0.32 false tag (in correction (u)'s text) as an EXTERNAL tag, inflating the count from 1 to 2. The repair is real at the prose level but the gate cannot distinguish quoted false tags from genuine provenance tags. The "EXTERNAL count: 2" claim is technically accurate but semantically misleading.

3. **(c) FB-7b circularity — is the FB-7b language non-circular?** **YES, the repair is real.** The v0.33 FB-7b determination (Section 0.1 line 18, Section 25 line 756) rests on Section 22 items 6-7 (existing language: "CONDITIONAL PASS is non-HALT; Section 22 item 7 states only a carrying-seat HALT blocks freeze"). Section 22.3 (line 706) defines the Class A/B/C/D/E taxonomy "prospectively for future disposition, not to retroactively reclassify prior findings" (line 714). The determination does not depend on its own output — it references Section 22's pre-existing language, not the new Section 22.3 classification. The circularity is removed. Section 22.3 is used descriptively in the Section 25 FB-7b row ("All conditions carried by the six CONDITIONAL PASSes are gate-limitation class (Class C/D per Section 22.3)"), but the resolution itself does not depend on Section 22.3.

4. **(d) "Carried on these bytes" false — is the language corrected?** **YES, the repair is real in v0.33 bytes.** The phrase "carried on these bytes" appears exactly once in the v0.33 protocol — in correction (w) (line 1068), quoting the v0.32 defect. The v0.33 body status line (line 5) says "six non-producer seats across two families returned non-HALT on v0.31 canonical bytes; v0.32-v0.33 are status-change and finding-disposition versions with no substantive revision to the carried protocol or decision code" — correctly identifying v0.31 as the carried bytes. However, I cannot verify that v0.32's original status line said "carried on these bytes" (v0.32 bytes not held) — correction (w)'s description is ASSERTED.

### Does FROZEN status mean no further amendments are possible?

**No.** Section 0.1 (line 16) states: "a contract locked before any corpus, packet, annotation, or result exists, whose every later change is a new version with an append-only amendment entry, never a silent edit." This means FROZEN does not prevent amendments — it prevents *silent* edits. Any defect found post-FROZEN would require a new version (v0.34+) with an append-only amendment entry. The append-only rule is enforced by the HISTORY.sha256 seal system (gate [9b]), which catches in-place mutations of any entry.

However, since FROZEN is not gated (Novel Probe 1), nothing prevents a silent edit to the FROZEN token itself — changing FROZEN to DRAFT CANDIDATE and regenerating the manifest passes the build. The append-only rule protects entry *text* but does not protect the *status claim*. A forger who changes the status token and regenerates all dependent surfaces would pass all gates. Only externally-held prior bytes (which I hold for v0.30 and v0.31, but not for v0.32 or v0.33's own original production) could detect such a change.

### What would happen if a defect is found post-FROZEN?

Per the append-only rule: a new version (v0.34) would be issued with an amendment entry recording the defect and its repair. The FROZEN status would need to be re-evaluated. But since FROZEN is not gated, the re-evaluation is a narrative act, not a programmatic one. The protocol would rely on the same unenforced prose mechanism that declared FROZEN in the first place.

---

## Deliverable O. Verdict

**Standing:** Non-producer carrying seat (GLM-5.2, Zhipu/Z.ai), carry-1B (continuous from v0.30 and v0.31). Full finding weight. This verdict **BINDS** and, if HALT, freezes the round outright. It counts toward the FB-7b two-family carry requirement.

**What this round got right:** All 33 historical seals reproduce exactly from shipped bytes. The cross-version anchor check (v0.31→v0.33) confirms zero retroactive mutations of any v0.1-v0.31 entry seal — the first three-version comparison in this program. The v0.32 seal is present and matches the v0.32 entry text in v0.33's Section 27. The four v0.32 repairs are real in v0.33 bytes: Section 0.1 is internally consistent (zero "FB-7b OPEN" in body), the false EXTERNAL tag is identified and the carry-result claim retagged ASSERTED, the FB-7b language is non-circular (determination rests on Section 22 items 6-7, not on its own output), and the status line correctly names v0.31 as the carried bytes. All code files differ from v0.31 only in version stamps — zero functional changes, zero gate changes. `sha256sum -c` returns rc=0. `python3 build.py` returns BUILD PASSED, rc=0. All 186 tests pass. The producer honestly disclosed the FROZEN-token unenforcement (register item 5) and the self-consistent-forgery boundary (register item 7) rather than concealing them. The thirteen-item register is self-consistent (declared == parsed). The Section 22.3 taxonomy is correctly defined as prospective, not retroactive. The Class A/B/C/D circularity from v0.32 is genuinely resolved.

**Verdict: CONDITIONAL PASS (binding, non-HALT).**

Blocking-if-unaddressed findings, and what clears each:

1. **FROZEN is not enforced by any gate.** Novel Probe 1 confirmed: changing FROZEN to DRAFT CANDIDATE in the body, with manifest regeneration, passes the build (rc=0). The protocol's central claim — that it is FROZEN — is an ASSERTED statement sitting in the unguarded region. The register discloses this (item 5, F-OP32D-01), but disclosure is not enforcement. **Clears by:** adding a gate that checks the FROZEN token against a set of freeze conditions (all FREEZE-BLOCKERs resolved, all FB-7b conjuncts verified, status line matches a computed state).

2. **Section 22.3 content is not enforced.** Novel Probe 2 confirmed: changing Class A severity from HALT-grade to Non-blocking passes the build after manifest regeneration (rc=0). A forger could retroactively reclassify a carrying-seat HALT as non-blocking, and the build would not catch it. **Clears by:** adding a gate that reads Section 22.3 content and verifies severity classifications are internally consistent (Class A must be HALT-grade, Class C/D/E must be non-blocking).

3. **Unshipped seat reports.** The FB-7b resolution and the nine advisory HALTs rest on zero shipped evidence. The v0.32 entry provides SHA-256 digests of eight reports, but the reports are producer-held and the digests are tagged [ASSERTED]. **Clears by:** shipping the cited seat report files with digests in PACKET_SHA256SUMS.

4. **ASSERTED fraction rising for three consecutive rounds without boundary movement.** 66.7% → 75.6% → 83.3%. The boundary is at the same location as v0.30. The FROZEN declaration did not move it — it declared the unguarded region non-blocking rather than bringing it inside. **Clears by:** extending [9c] to count untagged claims, or by requiring every factual claim in the entry to carry a provenance tag.

5. **v0.32 gap.** I do not hold v0.32 bytes. The four v0.32 repairs' accuracy depends on correction (t)-(w) descriptions of v0.32's body text, which I cannot independently verify. The v0.32 entry is sealed in v0.33's Section 27, but the seal proves only that the entry is unaltered since v0.33's sealing, not since v0.32's original production. **Clears by:** providing v0.32 bytes to the next carrying seat.

None of these are CRITICAL breaks in currently-shipped, currently-tested code. The byte-level consistency (digests, seals, tests, manifest) is intact and independently verified across three versions. The four v0.32 repairs are real in v0.33 bytes. The findings are boundary-location findings about what the instrument does not yet reach — specifically, that the FROZEN claim itself sits at the boundary. HALT is not warranted: the producer did not conceal a defect or ship a false CLOSED. The conditions are real but disclosed, and the cross-version anchor check confirms historical integrity for v0.1-v0.31. The FROZEN declaration is honest about its own unenforcement (register item 5) — it does not claim FROZEN is gated when it is not.

This verdict does not resolve whether FROZEN should have been declared. My vote: FROZEN is premature — it declares non-blocking a set of conditions (FROZEN unenforcement, unshipped reports, rising ASSERTED fraction) that are disclosed but not resolved. CONDITIONAL PASS is the correct verdict: the bytes are consistent, the repairs are real, but the FROZEN claim itself is an unguarded ASSERTED statement, and the next seat should be given v0.32 bytes to close the gap.

This is the FINAL CARRY for this seat. My verdict adds one non-producer, non-HALT, executing vote to the FB-7b pool, on v0.33 canonical bytes where `sha256sum -c` returned rc=0 and `python3 build.py` returned BUILD PASSED, rc=0.

## Deliverable G. Boundary report

**The outermost layer the build does NOT compute is the truth-value of the FROZEN status claim, the HALT clearance status, the EXTERNAL count claim, and all prose claims about seat verdicts and correction accuracy.** Specifically: (a) whether the FROZEN token is earned — no gate checks it (Novel Probe 3: FROZEN→WITHDRAWN passes); (b) whether HALT clearance is "pending" or "achieved" — no gate checks it (Novel Probe 2: "pending"→"achieved" passes); (c) whether the EXTERNAL count claim matches [9c]'s actual count — no gate checks it (Novel Probe 1: "1"→"3" passes); (d) whether the cited advisory seat verdicts (ten Opus 5 seats, all HALT) are true — no reports ship; (e) whether corrections (z) and (aa) accurately describe v0.34's text — I don't hold v0.34 bytes; (f) whether Section 22.3's content is correct — no gate reads it (v0.33 Novel Probe 2 confirmed, still unenforced); (g) whether any body-text sentence containing neither a `gate_atoms` token nor a 64-hex digest is true — confirmed unguarded by all three novel probes.

A secondary instance: the `gate_atoms` list inside build.py [11] that defines "semantic-gate coverage" is itself unguarded (confirmed still true — same hardcoded list as v0.30/v0.31/v0.33). The measuring instrument's own scope is asserted, not computed.

**Comparison across all four rounds:**

| Round | Boundary location | Coverage | ASSERTED fraction | FROZEN enforced? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.30 | Prose claims about seat reports + gate_atoms unguarded | 25.0% | 66.7% | N/A (DRAFT CANDIDATE) |
| v0.31 | Same | 25.5% | 75.6% | N/A |
| v0.33 | FROZEN token + Section 22.3 + seat verdicts | 26.3% | 83.3% | No (Novel Probe 1) |
| v0.35 | FROZEN token + HALT clearance + EXTERNAL count claim + seat verdicts | 26.3% | 85.7% | No (Novel Probe 3) |

**The boundary did not move.** The v0.35 changes (EXTERNAL count correction, HALT clearance reframing, register disposition) are text-level edits within the unguarded prose region — none expanded the computed boundary outward. The ASSERTED fraction rose for the fourth consecutive round (66.7% → 75.6% → 83.3% → 85.7%), confirming the boundary did not move. The FROZEN declaration persists without enforcement. The HALT clearance reframing added a new unguarded surface (clearance status language) without bringing any prior surface inside the computed region.

**What would bring it inside:** (1) add a gate that checks the FROZEN token against a set of freeze conditions; (2) add a gate that checks HALT clearance status against a registry of HALTing seats and their return verdicts; (3) add a gate that checks the body's "EXTERNAL count: N" claim against [9c]'s actual count; (4) add a gate that reads Section 22.3 content and verifies severity classifications; (5) require every ASSERTED-tagged carrying-seat or advisory-seat claim to cite a shipped report file with a digest checked by [9c].

## Deliverable N. FROZEN analysis (required)

### Is FROZEN earned?

**FROZEN is declared but not earned by any gate.** The conditions for FROZEN are stated in Section 22 (items 1-7) and Section 25 (all FREEZE-BLOCKERs resolved). Evaluation:

- **Section 22 items 1-5** (producer self-check, schema validation, kernel tests, adversarial suite, universe rerun): items 1-4 are evidenced by shipped executable artifacts (COMPUTED). Item 5 (universe rerun) is not applicable pre-corpus. These are satisfiable.
- **Section 22 item 6** (two-family executing carry): the v0.35 entry claims six non-producer carrying seats across two families returned non-HALT on v0.31 canonical bytes. This is ASSERTED — no reports ship, no gate verifies seat execution or verdicts. The FB-7b resolution rests on the v0.31 carry round, not the v0.34 or v0.35 carry rounds.
- **Section 22 item 7** (no carrying-seat HALT): the v0.34 entry records two binding HALTs from carrying seats (GLM-5.2 carry-1C and Kimi K3 carry-1A). The v0.35 entry reframes these as "clearance pending." **Two binding HALTs are pending clearance.** The HALTing seats have not verified v0.35 bytes. FROZEN is maintained while two binding HALTs are unresolved.
- **Section 25** (all FREEZE-BLOCKERs resolved): FB-1 through FB-7a are resolved with shipped artifacts (COMPUTED). FB-7b is marked RESOLVED, but the resolution rests on ASSERTED claims (unshipped reports) and two pending binding HALTs.

**No gate checks the FROZEN status token.** Novel Probe 3 confirmed: changing "Status: FROZEN" to "Status: WITHDRAWN" in the body, with full forger regeneration (including HISTORY.sha256), passes the build (rc=0). Register item (6) (F-OP34-04) discloses this. The FROZEN declaration is an ASSERTED claim sitting in the unguarded region — exactly the boundary the invariant predicts defects at. This is now confirmed with HISTORY.sha256 regeneration, making it a stronger result than the v0.33 probe.

### Was the EXTERNAL count inflation actually corrected?

**Yes, on v0.35 bytes.** I independently verified:

- The v0.35 entry has 1 [EXTERNAL: tag (the Zenodo deposits tag in the closing paragraph, line 1106).
- [9c] reports EXTERNAL: 1 on v0.35 bytes.
- The v0.35 entry's closing paragraph says "EXTERNAL count: 1" — matches [9c].
- The v0.34 entry (sealed in v0.35 Section 27, lines 1076-1092) has 2 [EXTERNAL: tags: one backtick-quoted `` `[EXTERNAL: ...]` `` in register item (3) (a reference to the v0.33 entry's correction (u) tag) and one genuine "[EXTERNAL: Zenodo deposits...]" in the closing paragraph. [9c] would count 2 on v0.34.
- The v0.33 entry (sealed in v0.35 Section 27, lines 1058-1074) has 2 [EXTERNAL: tags: one quoted "[EXTERNAL: seat reports held by producer...]" in correction (u) and one genuine "[EXTERNAL: Zenodo deposits...]" in the closing paragraph. [9c] reported EXTERNAL: 2 on v0.33 (confirmed by my v0.33 report).

The correction is real: the v0.35 entry avoids reproducing the quoted tag, so [9c] counts only the genuine tag (1). The v0.34 count of 2 was inflated by 1 (the backtick-quoted reference in register item (3)). However, I cannot verify v0.34's actual build output (requires v0.34 bytes). The claim that the v0.34 count was inflated is ASSERTED but supported by my independent analysis of the v0.34 entry text.

**However**, the body's "EXTERNAL count: 1" claim is NOT enforced by any gate. Novel Probe 1 confirmed: changing "EXTERNAL count: 1" to "EXTERNAL count: 3" passes the build after full forger regeneration. [9c] computes the count (1) but no gate checks that the body's stated count matches [9c]'s computed count. The correction is real at the text level but the count claim remains unguarded.

### Is the HALT clearance reframing sound?

**Partially sound, with a structural gap.**

The reframing (correction (aa)) states: "the producer cannot clear a binding HALT on behalf of the seat that issued it. Clearance is pending the HALTing seats' own verification on dispatched bytes."

**Sound aspects:**
- The principle is correct: the producer should not unilaterally clear a HALT issued by another seat. Section 22 item 7 says a HALT "blocks freeze outright and requires a new version." The v0.34 corrections (x)/(y) claiming clearance conditions are "met" was the producer clearing HALTs on behalf of HALTing seats — the reframing correctly identifies this as improper.
- The reframing is more conservative than v0.34's "clearance conditions met" language. It acknowledges that clearance requires the HALTing seat's own verification.

**Structural gap:**
- FROZEN is maintained while two binding HALTs are pending clearance. Section 22 item 7 says a HALT "blocks freeze outright." The v0.34 HALTs blocked v0.34's freeze. v0.35 is the new version required by the HALTs, but v0.35 still says FROZEN while the HALTs are pending.
- The FB-7b resolution is based on the v0.31 carry round (six non-HALT), not the v0.34 carry round (six non-HALT, two HALT). The question is whether v0.34 HALTs on v0.33 bytes retroactively affect the v0.31-based FB-7b resolution. The protocol's answer is that FB-7b was resolved at v0.32 based on v0.31 bytes, and subsequent HALTs require new versions but don't retroactively un-resolve FB-7b. This is a reasonable reading but depends on interpreting Section 22 item 7 as applying per-version rather than globally.
- Novel Probe 2 confirmed: the "clearance pending" language is not gated. A forger can change "pending" to "achieved" and pass the build. The reframing adds an unguarded surface (clearance status language) without bringing any prior surface inside the computed boundary.
- The HALTing seats (GLM-5.2 carry-1C and Kimi K3 carry-1A) have not returned to verify v0.35 bytes. The reframing says clearance is "pending" — but nothing in the protocol requires the HALTing seats to ever return, and nothing prevents FROZEN from persisting indefinitely while the HALTs remain pending.

**Is it circular?** No, not exactly circular. The reframing separates concerns: the producer records disposition evidence; the HALTing seats make the clearance determination. This is not self-referential. But it creates an open-ended deferral: FROZEN is maintained while HALTs are "pending" clearance that may never come, and nothing enforces the "pending" status.

**Is the producer trying to clear HALTs that only HALTing seats can clear?** The v0.35 entry explicitly says the producer does NOT clear the HALTs — it records disposition evidence and defers clearance to the HALTing seats. This is the correct posture. But the v0.34 entry (corrections (x)/(y)) DID claim clearance conditions were "met" — that was the producer clearing HALTs, which the v0.35 reframing corrects. The correction is real but the HALTs remain pending.

---

## Deliverable O. Verdict

**Standing:** Non-producer carrying seat (GLM-5.2, Zhipu/Z.ai), carry-1B (continuous from v0.30, v0.31, v0.33). Full finding weight. This verdict **BINDS** and, if HALT, freezes the round outright. It counts toward the FB-7b two-family carry requirement.

**What this round got right:** All 35 historical seals reproduce exactly from shipped bytes. The four-version cross-version anchor check (v0.30 → v0.31 → v0.33 → v0.35) confirms zero retroactive mutations of any v0.1-v0.33 entry seal — the first four-version comparison in this program. The v0.34 seal is present and matches the v0.34 entry text. Entry text comparison confirms v0.30, v0.31, and v0.33 entries are byte-identical across all versions that contain them. All code files differ from v0.33 only in version stamps — zero functional changes, zero gate changes. `sha256sum -c` returns rc=0. `python3 build.py` returns BUILD PASSED, rc=0. All 186 tests pass. The EXTERNAL count inflation correction is real on v0.35 bytes: the entry has 1 genuine [EXTERNAL: tag (down from 2 on v0.34, where one was a backtick-quoted reference), and [9c] reports EXTERNAL: 1. The HALT clearance reframing (correction (aa)) is more conservative and more correct than v0.34's "clearance conditions met" — it correctly identifies that the producer cannot clear binding HALTs on behalf of HALTing seats. The register is self-consistent (7 items, 7 declared). The "Correction (u) rewritten" wording in register item (1) is imprecise but not a factual error (the v0.33 entry was not modified; the v0.35 entry avoids reproducing the tag).

**Verdict: CONDITIONAL PASS (binding, non-HALT).**

Blocking-if-unaddressed findings, and what clears each:

1. **FROZEN is not enforced by any gate.** Novel Probe 3 confirmed: changing "Status: FROZEN" to "Status: WITHDRAWN" passes the build after full forger regeneration including HISTORY.sha256 (rc=0). This is the fourth consecutive round where FROZEN is unenforced (v0.33 Novel Probe 1 first identified it; v0.35 Novel Probe 3 confirms with stronger forger regeneration). Register item (6) discloses this, but disclosure is not enforcement. **Clears by:** adding a gate that checks the FROZEN token against a set of freeze conditions (all FREEZE-BLOCKERs resolved, all FB-7b conjuncts verified, no pending binding HALTs, status line matches a computed state).

2. **HALT clearance status is not enforced.** Novel Probe 2 confirmed: changing "clearance pending" to "clearance achieved" passes the build after full forger regeneration (rc=0). The v0.35 reframing correctly shifts clearance burden to HALTing seats, but nothing enforces that the "pending" status is maintained, and nothing requires the HALTing seats to ever return. Two binding HALTs (GLM-5.2 carry-1C, Kimi K3 carry-1A) remain pending while FROZEN is maintained. **Clears by:** adding a gate that tracks HALTing seats and their return verdicts, or by the HALTing seats returning non-HALT on v0.35 bytes.

3. **EXTERNAL count claim is not enforced.** Novel Probe 1 confirmed: changing "EXTERNAL count: 1" to "EXTERNAL count: 3" passes the build after full forger regeneration (rc=0). [9c] computes the count (1) but no gate checks the body's stated count against [9c]'s computed count. The EXTERNAL count correction is real at the text level but the count claim remains unguarded. **Clears by:** adding a gate that checks the body's "EXTERNAL count: N" claim against [9c]'s actual count.

4. **Unshipped seat reports.** The FB-7b resolution and the ten advisory HALTs rest on zero shipped evidence. The v0.34 entry provides SHA-256 digests of eleven reports, but the reports are producer-held and the digests are tagged [ASSERTED]. **Clears by:** shipping the cited seat report files with digests in PACKET_SHA256SUMS.

5. **ASSERTED fraction rising for four consecutive rounds without boundary movement.** 66.7% → 75.6% → 83.3% → 85.7%. The boundary is at the same location as v0.30. The EXTERNAL count correction and HALT clearance reframing are text-level improvements within the unguarded region — they did not bring any layer inside the computed boundary. **Clears by:** extending [9c] to count untagged claims, or by requiring every factual claim in the entry to carry a provenance tag, or by adding gates that check the claims currently marked ASSERTED.

6. **v0.32 and v0.34 gaps.** I hold neither v0.32 nor v0.34 bytes. The v0.32 and v0.34 entries are sealed in v0.35's Section 27, but the seals prove only that the entries are unaltered since v0.35's sealing, not since their original production. Correction (z)'s description of v0.34's EXTERNAL count and correction (aa)'s description of v0.34's HALT clearance claims depend on v0.34's body text, which I cannot independently verify. **Clears by:** providing v0.32 and v0.34 bytes to the next carrying seat.

None of these are CRITICAL breaks in currently-shipped, currently-tested code. The byte-level consistency (digests, seals, tests, manifest) is intact and independently verified across four versions. The EXTERNAL count correction is real on v0.35 bytes. The HALT clearance reframing is more conservative and more correct than v0.34. The findings are boundary-location findings about what the instrument does not yet reach — specifically, that the FROZEN claim, the HALT clearance status, and the EXTERNAL count claim all sit at the boundary, unguarded. HALT is not warranted: the producer did not conceal a defect or ship a false CLOSED. The conditions are real but disclosed, and the four-version cross-version anchor check confirms historical integrity for v0.1-v0.33. The FROZEN declaration is honest about its own unenforcement (register item 6) — it does not claim FROZEN is gated when it is not.

This verdict does not resolve whether FROZEN should have been declared. My vote: FROZEN remains premature — it maintains non-blocking status for a set of conditions (FROZEN unenforcement, unshipped reports, rising ASSERTED fraction, two pending binding HALTs) that are disclosed but not resolved. The EXTERNAL count correction is genuine progress (the count dropped from 2 to 1), and the HALT clearance reframing correctly identifies that the producer cannot clear HALTs. But neither correction moved the boundary: both sit in the unguarded prose region. CONDITIONAL PASS is the correct verdict: the bytes are consistent, the corrections are real at the text level, but the FROZEN claim itself remains an unguarded ASSERTED statement, two binding HALTs remain pending clearance, and the next seat should be given v0.32 and v0.34 bytes to close both gaps.

This is my fourth continuous carry. My verdict adds one non-producer, non-HALT, executing vote to the carry pool, on v0.35 canonical bytes where `sha256sum -c` returned rc=0 and `python3 build.py` returned BUILD PASSED, rc=0.

## R0861 · RESTORE_AND_RUN.txt

#!/bin/bash
# Run this script to restore original filenames and execute the audit.
# All .py.txt files become .py, .json.txt become .json, .md.txt become .md.
mkdir -p packet/schemas

for f in *.py.txt; do cp "$f" "packet/${f%.txt}"; done
for f in schemas_txt/*.json.txt; do
    base=$(basename "$f" .txt)
    cp "$f" "packet/schemas/$base"
done
for f in *.md.txt; do cp "$f" "packet/${f%.txt}"; done
cp SHA256SUMS.txt packet/SHA256SUMS

cd packet
echo "=== Verifying file integrity ==="
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
echo ""
echo "=== Running test suite ==="
python3 test_bssg_gate.py
echo ""
echo "=== Running counterexamples ==="
python3 bssg_counterexamples.py
echo ""
echo "=== Running model check ==="
python3 bssg_model_check.py
echo ""
echo "=== Running verifier ==="
python3 verify_bssg_v0_1.py
echo ""
echo "=== Gate smoke test ==="
python3 bssg_gate.py
echo ""
echo "=== Computing identity values ==="
python3 -c "
import hashlib, os
files = sorted([
    'bssg_attest.py', 'bssg_counterexamples.py', 'bssg_gate.py',
    'bssg_model_check.py', 'schemas/authorization-receipt.schema.json',
    'schemas/correction-event.schema.json', 'schemas/effect-request.schema.json',
    'schemas/execution-receipt.schema.json', 'schemas/lineage-record.schema.json',
    'schemas/witness-receipt.schema.json', 'test_bssg_gate.py', 'verify_bssg_v0_1.py',
])
MANIFEST = hashlib.sha256(''.join(
    hashlib.sha256(open(f,'rb').read()).hexdigest() for f in files
).encode()).hexdigest()
NONCE = 'BSSG-CARRY-KIMI-fc8133ea55a2bfb2'
challenge = hashlib.sha256((MANIFEST + NONCE).encode()).hexdigest()
print('MANIFEST:', MANIFEST)
print('CHALLENGE:', challenge)
"
echo ""
echo "=== Attestation ==="
python3 bssg_attest.py BSSG-CARRY-KIMI-fc8133ea55a2bfb2

# Round-by-round failure-mode retirement ledger

Per Bayyinah Audit Framework v3.0 §17.3, the retirement ledger is
the framework's most consequential empirical claim: each retired
shape is one fewer way the substrate can fail, and the retirement
is mechanically prevented by automated gates rather than by author
vigilance.

This document is the cross-version ledger for the Bayyinah
Integrity Scanner. Per-version retirement entries also live in
CHANGELOG.md under the corresponding release section; this ledger
is the consolidated view.

Reconstruction note: rounds 1 through 10 were not numbered
explicitly in early CHANGELOG entries. The numbering below is
reconstructed from CHANGELOG history and from the v1.2.3 audit
work where Fraz Ashraf reviewed the v1.2.2 substrate (recorded as
"round 10" in the v1.2.3 commit messages d032553, e572091,
54942b0, 86c8351). Per the v1.2.4 attribution-discipline note,
all rounds in the Bayyinah chain are audit-of-self by Bilal Syed
Arfeen; Fraz contributed the engineering approach to the audit
framework itself, not to any specific Bayyinah round.

## Ledger

### Round 1 (reconstructed from CHANGELOG, retired in v0.2.x)

- Phase 0 fixture mismatch: hand-rolled fixtures drifted from the
  v0 reference scanner. Closed by adopting `make_test_documents.py`
  and asserting `bayyinah.scan_pdf == bayyinah_v0.scan_pdf`
  byte-identically in the Phase 0 fixture corpus. Structural
  defense: `tests/test_fixtures.py::test_v0_v01_parity`.

### Round 2 (reconstructed from CHANGELOG, retired in v0.3.x)

- Modular surface drift from v0.1: `bayyinah.scan_pdf` stopped
  matching `bayyinah_v0_1.scan_pdf` after analyzer factoring.
  Closed by tightening the parity test to compare finding tuples
  including tier, confidence, description, location, surface,
  concealed. Structural defense:
  `tests/test_integration.py::test_scan_pdf_parity_with_v01`.

### Rounds 3 through 9 (reconstructed from CHANGELOG, retired
across v0.3 through v1.2.2)

- Phase 1-9 modular refactor with byte-parity gates and analyzer-
  per-mechanism factoring. Mechanism registry consistency,
  cost-class taxonomy, content-index pre-pass, mode=production
  early termination, demo firewall, summarisation queue. Each
  phase added a structural defense without breaking parity.

### Round 10 (audit-of-self by Bilal, retired in v1.2.3)

- MEDIUM: requirements-dev.txt out of sync with `pyproject.toml`
  `[project.optional-dependencies].dev`. Closed by adding
  `tests/test_requirements_dev_sync.py` (commit d032553).
- MEDIUM: `SummaryQueue.claim_next_job` returned a stale
  `sqlite3.Row` snapshot; the persisted row was correct, the
  returned dict was lying. Closed by refreshing the returned dict
  to reflect the UPDATE (commit e572091).
- MEDIUM: `tests/test_public_surface_additive.py` pinned only
  `V1_2_0_SURFACE`; framework v3 §18.3 requires per-minor-and-patch
  cadence. Closed by adding `V1_2_1_SURFACE`, `V1_2_2_SURFACE`,
  `V1_2_3_SURFACE` aliases plus subset tests (commit 54942b0).

### Round 11 (audit-of-self by Bilal, queued for v1.2.5)

The red-team probe of bayyinah.dev v1.2.3 on 2026-05-04 surfaced
4 CRITICAL silent-pass findings and 5 HIGH partial-catches against
multi-layer integrity traps. Round 11 is deferred to v1.2.5 per
the v3 depth-before-scope discipline; the Round 12 calibration
corrective ships first because the Round 12 false positives were
visible to every demo visitor while the Round 11 silent-passes
were not.

### Round 12 (audit-of-self by Bilal, retired in v1.2.4)

- HIGH: openaction heuristic fired on benign navigation
  destinations (LibreOffice destination arrays, pdfTeX hyperref
  /GoTo). Closed by adding `_is_benign_navigation_openaction`
  predicate in `analyzers/object_analyzer.py` per ISO 32000-1
  section 12.6.3 (commit 37a466f).
- HIGH: tounicode_anomaly heuristic fired on canonical TeX-stack
  ToUnicode CMaps (Greek-block targets in math fonts, OT1 ZWNJ at
  slot 0x17). Closed by adding `_is_tex_stack_producer` and
  `_is_tex_canonical_anomaly` helpers and threading /Info /Producer
  through both emission paths in `_scan_tounicode_cmaps` (commit
  87cad53).
- MEDIUM: corpus blind spot. Existing fixtures were pymupdf-
