# Round-2 Delta Audit — OpenAI carrying seat

**Seat declaration.** Model: GPT 5.4. Vendor: OpenAI. Tier: frontier. Standing: carrying. Round-1 participation: none. [Round-2 dispatch brief](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/AI_PAPER_DISPATCH_R2-2.md)

**Intake.** The controlled packet passed hash verification: the baseline source, current source, PDF, DOCX, dispatch brief, Round-1 synthesis, and insertion memo all matched the authoritative packet sums. [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md) [Packet SHA256SUMS](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/SHA256SUMS-8.txt)

**Seat verdict.** **NON-PASS.** [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [Round-2 dispatch brief](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/AI_PAPER_DISPATCH_R2-2.md)

**Convergence status.** This single carrying-seat result does not establish convergence. [Round-2 dispatch brief](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/AI_PAPER_DISPATCH_R2-2.md)

## Leg-by-leg determination

### L1. Delta scope

The source diff is exactly 7 hunks with 143 lines added and 8 removed, matching the brief’s stated delta envelope. [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md) [Round-2 dispatch brief](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/AI_PAPER_DISPATCH_R2-2.md)

All 7 hunks map to the six adopted recommendation clusters named in the brief, with the final cluster split across two hunks: one for the corrigibility inequality and one for the F-5 reframe. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [Round-2 dispatch brief](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/AI_PAPER_DISPATCH_R2-2.md)

I found no out-of-scope substantive insertion. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)

### L2. Adoption fidelity

The transfer conditions were adopted directly and placed before the transfer to artificial systems, which is faithful to the Round-1 ask. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [Round-1 synthesis](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/ROUND1_model-council-synthesis.md)

The Level-2 revision was also adopted directly: the paper now preserves the moral-status guard while decomposing sustained participation into system, operator, and deployment persistence. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [Round-1 synthesis](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/ROUND1_model-council-synthesis.md)

The three provenance primitives were adopted directly and clearly differentiated as watermark, cryptographic manifest, and lineage attestation. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [Round-1 insertion memo](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/ROUND1_artificial-systems-insertion-7.md)

The ledger recommendation was adopted in a **weakened but still functional** form: the paper now has an append-only markedness ledger, UNKNOWN-never-defaults, multi-agent lineage carriage, and producer-versus-accountable-institution separation, but it omits the full typed schema and named metrics proposed in Round 1. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [Round-1 synthesis](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/ROUND1_model-council-synthesis.md)

The model-collapse evidence was adopted faithfully and, importantly, in two-sided form rather than as a one-way alarm citation. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)

The F-5 restatement toward economy rather than exclusivity was adopted directly, and the corrigibility claim was upgraded into an explicit inequality. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [Round-1 synthesis](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/ROUND1_model-council-synthesis.md)

### L3. The two deliberate omissions

**Omission 1: the full typed propagation-ledger schema.** This omission was **correct** under the length constraint. The paper now supplies enough of the ledger to make the governance architecture legible, while stopping short of pretending to be a technical specification; adding full entity-activity-agent typing and named metrics here would push the manuscript further from a tight argument and further toward a companion standard. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md) [Round-2 dispatch brief](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/AI_PAPER_DISPATCH_R2-2.md)

I therefore do **not** think the paper now claims an implementable, turn-key governance architecture while refusing to specify it; it claims a governance object and its minimum invariants, which is a different and acceptable level of ambition for this genre. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)

**Omission 2: the four proposed experiments.** This omission was also **correct**. At 8,345 words versus 6,865 in the baseline, the paper is already carrying a large delta, and the experiments belong more naturally in a companion implementation or empirical paper than in this manuscript. [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md) [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)

### L4. Citation fidelity on imported sources

On NIST AI 600-1, the paper is substantively right that the relevant transparency stack is not one thing: NIST distinguishes provenance data tracking from synthetic-content detection, and within provenance tracking it separately names watermarking and metadata recording techniques. [NIST AI 600-1](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf)

On C2PA, the paper is also substantively right: the explainer describes Content Credentials as securely bound provenance assertions and tamper-evident under alteration, while the official FAQ explicitly says manifests are typically embedded but can be separated and that metadata may be stripped, with soft bindings used as a recovery mechanism. [C2PA Explainer](https://spec.c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/1.4/explainer/Explainer.html) [C2PA FAQ](https://c2pa.org/faqs/)

On the EU AI Act, however, the paper overstates Article 50. Article 50(2) does require synthetic outputs to be marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated, but the article does **not** itself impose lifecycle logging obligations. [EUR-Lex Regulation (EU) 2024/1689](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R1689)

That overstatement is not in the main body language at the insertion point; it appears in the empirical-and-standards source note, which currently says Article 50 is cited both for machine-readable marking and for lifecycle logging obligations on covered systems. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [EUR-Lex Regulation (EU) 2024/1689](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R1689)

On watermark robustness, the new text is fair in aggregate. Paraphrasing weakens watermark strength even when some schemes remain detectable with enough tokens, translation-based attacks can drive detection toward random-guessing levels, low-entropy instruction responses are harder to watermark robustly, and published attacks have removed several schemes with only minor quality degradation. [On the Reliability of Watermarks for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.04634) [Can Watermarks Survive Translation?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14007) [Robust Distortion-free Watermarks for Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.15593) [Watermarks in the Sand](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.04378)

On Shumailov and the qualification literature, the paper’s use is fair to both halves. Shumailov et al. do support the claim that recursive training on generated data shrinks distribution support and loses tails first, while follow-up work does support the narrower qualification that collapse depends strongly on whether real human data are retained or accumulated alongside synthetic data. [Shumailov et al. via PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11269175/) [Is Model Collapse Inevitable?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01413) [How Bad is Training on Synthetic Data?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05090)

### L5. The bridge principle, adversarially

The bridge principle is much better than Round 1, but it still overstates two things.

First, condition 4 is framed too narrowly if it is part of the **exact applicability** test rather than the remedy test. A decommissioned synthetic corpus, benchmark, or archived model-output artifact can still propagate formative harm downstream even if the original producing system no longer has a live present-tense action locus. In those cases, the relevant correction point sits with the current custodian, deployer, or ingester, not necessarily with the originating system.

Second, the sentence claiming that conditions 1 and 3 are decidable from public facts does **not** survive real deployment opacity as written. In openly documented pipelines this can be true, but in ordinary frontier deployments outsiders often cannot tell, from public facts alone, whether outputs are being re-ingested into later training or evaluation loops.

Those are not fatal objections to the bridge principle itself, but they do require narrowing edits before circulation.

### L6. Whether the paper still says what it said

The insertions do not silently collapse the producer-versus-accountable-owner distinction back into machine culpability. The new transfer paragraph, the Level-2 decomposition, and the ledger paragraph all preserve the moral-status guard and keep accountability assigned to human or institutional actors. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)

The non-apportionment frame also remains stable across the new material: the added text enlarges observability and remediation, not blame attribution to the model. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)

I found no new numeric section cross-reference. [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md)

### L7. Standing lint

The source passes the stated global lints for em dashes, doubled words, and numeric section references. [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md)

There is, however, one sentence-level repair still needed: the F-5 paragraph now reads "makes. the falsification conditions's condition F-5 makes this testable," which is malformed and should be cleaned before circulation. [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md) [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)

## Findings

### F-AG-01
1. **SEVERITY:** **CRITICAL**.
2. **LEG:** L4 — citation fidelity on imported sources.
3. **ISSUE:** The paper attributes lifecycle logging obligations to Article 50 of the EU AI Act, but Article 50 supports the machine-readable-marking/detectability claim only, not the logging claim. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [EUR-Lex Regulation (EU) 2024/1689](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R1689)
4. **WHY IT MATTERS:** The brief makes overstated standards or legal claims highest-severity because this paper is making governance recommendations that lean on those authorities. [Round-2 dispatch brief](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/AI_PAPER_DISPATCH_R2-2.md)
5. **EVIDENCE:** The source note says Article 50 is cited "for machine-readable marking of synthetic content and for lifecycle logging obligations on covered systems," while the official Article 50 text, as fetched from EUR-Lex, states the marking/detectability obligation and contains no lifecycle logging obligation. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md) [EUR-Lex Regulation (EU) 2024/1689](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R1689)
6. **REQUIRED EDIT BEFORE CIRCULATION:** Replace the current sentence with: **"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act), Article 50. Cited for machine-readable marking of synthetic content and detectability requirements for such outputs."** If the author wants to retain a logging claim, it must be sourced to the correct provision in a separate citation rather than attributed to Article 50.

### F-AG-02
1. **SEVERITY:** **MAJOR**.
2. **LEG:** L5 — bridge principle, adversarial test.
3. **ISSUE:** The new transfer conditions overclaim decidability from public facts and frame the present-tense action locus too narrowly for archived or decommissioned artifacts that still propagate downstream. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)
4. **WHY IT MATTERS:** These four conditions are load-bearing. As written, they risk excluding propagation cases that plainly matter and overstating what outside observers can actually know about opaque deployments.
5. **EVIDENCE:** The current text says the structure transfers "exactly when" four conditions hold and then says conditions 1 and 3 are "decidable from public facts." It also defines condition 4 as the existence of a point where "current behaviour" can be corrected. An archived synthetic corpus or benchmark can still shape later systems even when the originating model has no live current behaviour, and public facts often do not reveal downstream re-ingestion practices. [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)
6. **REQUIRED EDIT BEFORE CIRCULATION:** Narrow both claims. A clean repair would be: **"4. A present-tense correction locus. There exists a current point in the system, deployment, or ingestion chain at which ongoing use can be corrected without reconstructing history."** And revise the later sentence to: **"Conditions one and three are sometimes decidable from publicly documented facts, especially in openly described pipelines, but are often obscured in ordinary deployments."**

### F-AG-03
1. **SEVERITY:** **MINOR**.
2. **LEG:** L7 — standing lint / sentence integrity.
3. **ISSUE:** One malformed sentence remains in the F-5 paragraph. [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md) [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)
4. **WHY IT MATTERS:** It is not conceptually serious, but it is visible enough to distract a careful reader in a paragraph carrying one of the paper’s main scope limitations.
5. **EVIDENCE:** The sentence presently reads: "makes. the falsification conditions's condition F-5 makes this testable". [Audit notes](file:///home/user/workspace/ROUND2_gpt-5-4-audit-notes.md) [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)
6. **REQUIRED EDIT BEFORE CIRCULATION:** Replace the last two sentences of that paragraph with: **"That is a weaker claim than exclusivity and a considerably more defensible one, and it is the claim this paper makes. F-5 makes this testable; if the normative structure proves fully restatable, the paper should be rewritten without the tradition."**

## PASS-DELTA / NON-PASS

**NON-PASS.** The Article 50 overstatement is disqualifying for this round until corrected, and I would also repair the bridge-principle overclaim before circulation. [EUR-Lex Regulation (EU) 2024/1689](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32024R1689) [Current paper source](file:///home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/7dc1167c4d504e07a260721d02ca5533/paper_source-4.md)

## Is it done?

Not in this exact file state.

But **yes, almost certainly yes after the three edits above**. I would not spend another full council round on this manuscript once the Article 50 citation is corrected, the transfer-condition overclaim is narrowed, and the malformed F-5 sentence is repaired. At that point the remaining open work belongs to implementation, experiments, or specialist domain readers rather than another general delta audit.

## Precise edits required before circulation

1. **Correct the Article 50 source note** as specified in F-AG-01, and do not attribute lifecycle logging to Article 50 without a different citation.
2. **Narrow the transfer-condition language** as specified in F-AG-02 so condition 4 reaches the current deployment or ingestion locus and the public-facts decidability claim is no longer categorical.
3. **Repair the malformed F-5 sentence** as specified in F-AG-03.

If those three edits are made, my seat would be prepared to move this to **PASS-DELTA** on re-check without asking for another substantive expansion.

# Round 36 Audit -- Phase G11.2 al-Mursalat (v1.3)

**Reviewer:** Perplexity (cross-instance)
**Subject:** al-Mursalat v1.3 prompt at `/home/user/workspace/paste.txt` (1873 lines)
**Substrate baseline:** v0.11.8 shipped 2026-05-10; main `cace1c0`; tag `v0.11.8` -> commit `cac6917`
**Producer (Claude) prior absorption passes:** v1.0 -> v1.1 (Round 31 cross-instance) -> v1.2 (Round 32 cross-instance) -> v1.3 (self-review same-instance per methodology v1.1 §0.1)
**Methodology:** v1.1 §0 (cross-instance discipline), six-element findings, severity uppercase
**Verdict:** **HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-v1.4** (3 CRITICAL, 3 HIGH, 4 MEDIUM, 2 LOW)

---

## Recognition

v1.3 correctly identifies the as-Saff cycle as the architectural prerequisite, cites the actual ship SHAs (`cac6917` / `cace1c0`), preserves the v1.1 / v1.2 absorption ledgers cleanly, and acknowledges the same-instance limitation explicitly in the v1.3 amendments closing note (lines 1852-1865). The narrative reconstruction in the closing audit-chain section is accurate through the v0.11.8 ship. F-AL-3 (test-count baseline shift), F-AL-7 (F22 closure attribution), F-AL-8 (Round 35 finding-seed inheritance), F-AL-9 (pre-registration sources), F-AL-10 (audit-chain narrative) are substrate-true.

The same-instance limitation note in the appendix (lines 1852-1865) explicitly anticipates the failure mode this audit caught: "the as-Saff Round 35 cycle demonstrated that same-instance review can miss substrate-true findings... v1.3's amendments are substrate-evidence-traceable rather than architectural reframings, which reduces but does not eliminate the same-instance miss risk." The prediction proved correct. The findings below are precisely that class: substrate-untrue symbol claims that v1.3 self-review could not catch because it did not consult the actual v0.11.8 substrate.

---

## CRITICAL findings -- substrate-untrue symbol claims at load-bearing T02 / T04 / T05 sites

### F-RM-1 CRITICAL -- `python_verification.verify` and `rust_verification.verify` are NOT public substrate symbols at v0.11.8

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Locus:** F-AL-1 (line 28-32), F-AL-2 (line 36-39), F-AL-4 (line 49-57), T02 `_VERIFIER_DISPATCH` code block (lines 935-964), T02 test fixtures #1, #2 (lines 967-981), T02 prose (lines 905-916), Closing audit-chain narrative (lines 1719-1722), F-AL-1 / F-AL-4 / F-AL-7 appendix entries (lines 1830-1836)
- **Observation:** v1.3 asserts as a substrate fact that as-Saff v0.11.8 provides public `python_verification.verify` and `rust_verification.verify` symbols that al-Mursalat T02 will wire into `_VERIFIER_DISPATCH`. The prompt's T02 code block reads `_VERIFIER_DISPATCH = {"python": python_verification.verify, "rust": rust_verification.verify, "go": go_verification.verify}`.
- **Substrate truth (verified at tag `v0.11.8` / commit `cac6917`):**
  - `src/furqan_lint/gate11/python_verification.py` line 53 defines `def _verify_python(manifest, args)` -- underscore-prefixed, private.
  - `src/furqan_lint/gate11/python_verification.py` line 86 declares `__all__ = ("_verify_python",)` -- only the underscore-prefixed symbol is exported.
  - `src/furqan_lint/gate11/rust_verification.py` line 54 defines `def _verify_rust(manifest, args)` -- underscore-prefixed, private.
  - `src/furqan_lint/gate11/rust_verification.py` line 87 declares `__all__ = ("_verify_rust",)`.
  - There is no public `python_verification.verify` or `rust_verification.verify` symbol anywhere in the v0.11.8 substrate.
- **Why CRITICAL:** This is the F-AS-2-class regression the as-Saff Round 35 cycle was instituted to prevent. The v1.3 self-review codified substrate-nonexistent symbols as load-bearing public API for al-Mursalat to consume; if Co-work implements T02 verbatim, the dispatch table construction will raise `AttributeError` at import time when Python attempts to resolve `python_verification.verify`. The CI lint guard will not catch this (it's a runtime / import-time failure, not a syntactic em-dash). The T02 test fixtures encode the same wrong target and will fail collection.
- **Closure:** v1.4 must reframe T02 to dispatch through the substrate-actual public surface. The architecturally clean choice is to call `verification.verify(manifest, args)` -- the module-level facade that v0.11.8 actually exports (line 556 of `verification.py`, listed in `verification.__all__`). The CLI's `manifest verify` subcommand inspects `manifest.module_identity["language"]`, then routes through `verification.verify(manifest, args)` which internally dispatches to `_verify_python` or `_verify_rust` via its function-local dispatch dict. al-Mursalat's substrate task becomes (a) extending `python_verification`, `rust_verification` to optionally expose public `verify` aliases if the per-language-module symmetrization is desired (separate ADR; not necessary for F22 closure), AND (b) adding `_verify_go` (private) plus `go_verification.py` mirroring the v0.11.8 facade pattern, AND (c) extending `verification.verify`'s function-local dispatch dict to include `"go": _verify_go`. The F-AL-4 framing ("CLI saves one indirection by dispatching to per-language modules directly") is architecturally permissible but requires first introducing the public `python_verification.verify` / `rust_verification.verify` aliases as a separate prerequisite phase or as an explicit task within al-Mursalat (a new T01.5: "extend per-language modules with public verify aliases"). The v1.3 prompt treats those aliases as preexisting; v1.4 must either drop the F-AL-4 symmetrization (route through `verification.verify`) or explicitly introduce the aliases as a new task with its own substrate edits, tests, and acceptance criteria.
- **Reference:** as-Saff v1.2 F-XR-1 reversed an analogous F-AS-2 codification (verification.verify portrayed as preexisting); the v1.3 self-review replicated the same anti-pattern one layer down (per-language-module verify aliases portrayed as preexisting).

### F-RM-2 CRITICAL -- `_LANGUAGE_DISPATCH` is NOT a module-level symbol in v0.11.8 substrate

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Locus:** F-AL-2 (line 39), §0 framing (line 339-341), Calibration rung v0.11.8 (lines 470-471), T00 step 4 expectations (lines 714-716), F-AL-5 appendix entry (line 1834), Closing audit-chain narrative (line 1721-1722)

- **Substrate truth (verified at v0.11.8 / `verification.py` lines 556-612):** `_LANGUAGE_DISPATCH` is a **function-local dict** constructed inside `def verify(manifest, args)` after a lazy import of `_verify_python` and `_verify_rust`. It is NOT a module-level symbol; it cannot be imported, inspected externally, monkeypatched for tests, or extended from outside the function body. The lazy-import-inside-function pattern was chosen specifically to avoid circular imports between `verification.py` and the per-language modules (which import `Verifier` from `verification`).
- **Why CRITICAL:** Multiple v1.3 specifications depend on `_LANGUAGE_DISPATCH` being externally accessible. T00 step 4 will record `_LANGUAGE_DISPATCH PRESENT` as a substrate fact -- which is false. If al-Mursalat T01 attempts to extend `_LANGUAGE_DISPATCH` to include `"go"` by appending at module-load time, it will not find the symbol. If al-Mursalat T02 test fixture #6 (`test_dispatch_does_not_call_unmatched_verifiers`) attempts to mock entries in a module-level `_LANGUAGE_DISPATCH`, the mock target does not exist.
- **Closure:** v1.4 must reframe: extending dispatch to Go means editing the function-local dispatch dict inside `verification.verify()` (adding a third lazy-import line `from furqan_lint.gate11.go_verification import _verify_go` and a third dict entry `"go": _verify_go`). T00 step 4 inventory expectation revised to record the substrate-actual shape (module-level `verify` function; function-local dispatch dict). T02 test fixtures that need to inspect or mock dispatch routing must either patch at the per-language-module level (`_verify_python` etc.) or refactor `verification.verify` to lift the dispatch dict to module level as a separate ADR -- which is a real architectural change with its own acceptance criteria, NOT a substrate-already-true fact al-Mursalat can rely on.
- **Reference:** Substrate read of `src/furqan_lint/gate11/verification.py` lines 556-612 at tag `v0.11.8` / commit `cac6917`.

## Section 3: Findings (six-element format: ID, severity, locus, substance, disposition, cross-reference)

### F-S02-CM-01 -- MAJOR
- **Locus:** Part II, Productivity Analysis (p. 24-25).
- **Substance:** The paper states "YES-or-PARTIAL rate: First edition: 31 / 39 = 79.5%" and "Second edition (all entries): 38 / 47 = 80.9%". Counting the paper's own per-entry verdict labels gives 35/39 (89.7%) first edition (18 YES + 17 PARTIAL: #2, #3, #9, #10, #12, #15, #19, #27-#33, #36-#38) and 42/47 (89.4%) all entries (35 + #40-#44, #46, #47 minus NO/#45 -> 24 YES + 18 PARTIAL). The YES counts on the same page (18, 24) reproduce exactly, so the verdict-label set is not in doubt; the YES-or-PARTIAL numerators 31 and 38 match no counting rule derivable from the printed verdicts.
- **Disposition:** Repair the two numerators or state the alternative counting rule explicitly. Falsifier: recount the printed "Productivity verdict" labels; if YES-or-PARTIAL totals 35 and 42, the printed 31 and 38 are wrong.
- **Cross-reference:** dispatch check (g); productivity figures are load-bearing for the paper's methodological-defense argument (46.2% vs 51.1% discussion).

### F-S02-CM-02 -- MAJOR
- **Locus:** #12 Pulmonary Dead Space, #15 Pharmacological Pattern Recognition (twice), #24 Structural Revelation (twice) -- all cite "the Iblis Trajectory (#30)"; written entry #30 is "Al-Kuttab al-Arba'a (The Four Recording Scribes)".
- **Substance:** Five body references direct the reader to framework #30 as the Iblis Trajectory, but no Iblis Trajectory entry exists anywhere in the document, and #30 as written is a different framework. A fresh executor following these references lands on the wrong entry. Evidence (verbatim, dashes normalized): "The metastasis concept feeds into the Iblis Trajectory (#30)"; "this observation was already captured by the Iblis Trajectory (#30) as 'Level 3: Pride in understanding.'"
- **Disposition:** Either restore the Iblis Trajectory entry at a number matching all five references and renumber the Four Scribes entry, or repoint all five references to the correct number. Falsifier: resolve every "(#30)" reference against the entry headings; if any lands on a non-Iblis entry, the defect stands.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S02-CM-03 (the Iblis Trajectory is named in the Family 6 TOC enumeration but has no written entry).

### F-S02-CM-03 -- MAJOR
- **Locus:** p. 15 (the "25-38" enumeration paragraph) vs the written Family 6 / #39 entries.
- **Substance:** Three defects in one locus. (i) The enumeration names fourteen frameworks including "the 24-Fret Six-String Standard Tuning Model, the Iblis Trajectory, ... Barzakh Gate / Munkar and Nakir" -- none of these three has a written entry anywhere in the paper (each name occurs exactly once, in this paragraph). (ii) The written entries #36 Al-Isnad, #37 Al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil, and #38 Surah Classification (Makki/Madani) appear in no enumeration. (iii) The paragraph truncates mid-sentence: "and Family 7 (The are presented below." -- and no Family 7 heading or label exists anywhere in the paper; #39 (Differentiator) is presented without a family label even though the abstract promises seven families.
- **Disposition:** Reconcile the enumeration with the written entries, complete or delete the truncated Family 7 sentence, and label #39's family. Falsifier: diff the enumerated names against the written entry headings; any name present on exactly one side is a mismatch.
- **Cross-reference:** F-S02-CM-02; dispatch checks (a) and (d) (a reference document whose table of contents does not match its body is not fully executable).

### F-S02-CM-04 -- MAJOR
- **Locus:** #6 Hurst Exponent (p. 5) vs #47 Cross-Instrument Recurrence Observation (p. 28).
- **Substance:** #6 reports "H = 1.0 across 25 consecutive rounds (R7-R31)... p < 0.001 by Monte Carlo permutation" and calls H "the single most important computed quantity in the XZ Protocol's audit trajectory." #47 states, in a parenthetical retraction: the "H = 1.0" label "conflates the recurrence fraction (25/25 = 1.0) with the Hurst exponent... A constant all-recurrence binary sequence provides no variance from which to estimate H... This paper reports the recurrence fraction directly and does not use the 'H = 1.0' label." Both cannot be true of the same document: #6 uses the label and derives a p-value from a series that #47 proves has no estimable variance. The correction and the corrected-against claim ship side by side, unreconciled.
- **Disposition:** Rewrite #6's "In the XZ Protocol" and "Productivity verdict" passages to report the recurrence fraction (25/25) and remove the H = 1.0 / p < 0.001 statistic, or withdraw the #47 retraction. Falsifier: attempt R/S estimation on a constant binary series of length 25; if the estimator is undefined (zero variance), the #6 statistic cannot have been computed as described.
- **Cross-reference:** lens (b)/(c) for sampled framework #6; this is the paper's self-described "headline metric."

### F-S02-CM-05 -- MINOR
- **Locus:** Family 6 header (p. 14).
- **Substance:** "This family contains twelve frameworks derived from the Quran, hadith, and classical Islamic sciences." The family's written span is #24-#38, i.e., 15 entries, and the paper's own enumeration says "the remaining fourteen frameworks" follow #24 (14 + 1 = 15). "Twelve" matches neither count.
- **Disposition:** Correct "twelve" to the actual count. Falsifier: count the numbered entries between the Family 6 header and #39.
- **Cross-reference:** dispatch check (e)/(f) numbering integrity.

### F-S02-CM-06 -- MINOR
- **Locus:** #39 Differentiator, "Interaction with other frameworks" (p. 23).
- **Substance:** #39 claims it "is referenced by GAN Convergence (#1, 'the true distribution the generator should be targeting')". That quotation does not appear in #1; it appears in #4 Mode Collapse ("provides the ten-layer structure that defines the 'true distribution' the generator should be targeting"). The attribution number is wrong; #39's own next clause correctly cites #4 for a different paraphrase.
- **Disposition:** Change "(#1, ...)" to "(#4, ...)" or supply the actual #1 passage. Falsifier: search #1's text for the quoted string; absence confirms the misattribution.
- **Cross-reference:** dispatch lens (d).

### F-S02-CM-07 -- MINOR
- **Locus:** #7 Fractal Dimension / Box-Counting, "Operational procedure" step 4 and "In the XZ Protocol" (p. 5).
- **Substance:** The procedure defines "the effective fractal dimension: D = log(27 - A)/log(27)". For A = 7 this gives log(20)/log(27) = 0.908, but the same entry reports "The effective D = 2.727 (Menger sponge Level 1)", which equals log(20)/log(3). The defined quantity and the reported quantity use different denominators; an executor following the procedure cannot reproduce the reported value. (The entry gestures at a "log-normalized form used in that document" for the D > 0.95 target, confirming two conventions are in play, but the procedure/report mismatch within the entry itself is unresolved.)
- **Disposition:** State one formula and make the reported values consistent with it, or label the two forms explicitly at every occurrence. Falsifier: compute log(20)/log(27) and log(20)/log(3); if they differ (0.908 vs 2.727), a single formula cannot yield both reported numbers.
- **Cross-reference:** dispatch lens (b).

### F-S02-CM-08 -- MINOR
- **Locus:** #9 Fibonacci / Golden Ratio, "Productivity verdict" (p. 6-7).
- **Substance:** The claimed genuine finding rests on "the 19 normative objects... correspond to the 19 retained cells at Level 1 of the Menger sponge (27 - 7 = 20, but the protocol counts 19...)". Level 1 of the Menger sponge retains 20 cells (the paper's own #7 and #21 both say "20 of 27"); there is no "19 retained cells" structure to correspond to. The parenthetical concedes the arithmetic (27 - 7 = 20) and then asserts the correspondence anyway.
- **Disposition:** Restate the finding as a 19-objects-vs-20-cells near-correspondence, or drop the Menger mapping. Falsifier: count retained cells at Level 1 per the paper's own construction; if 20, "19 retained cells" is wrong.
- **Cross-reference:** #21 Menger Sponge; #9's only claimed independent finding.

### F-S02-CM-09 -- MINOR
- **Locus:** #25 Al-Fatiha Structural Analysis, "Interaction with other frameworks" (p. 15) vs Part II Classification Scheme (p. 24).
- **Substance:** #25 states "This is a specialization of Crystallographic Ijaz (#22) applied to the micro-structure of a single artifact." The Classification Scheme declares "The original 39 frameworks (Families 1-7, first edition) are classified as INDEPENDENT/PROSPECTIVE" and counts exactly 3 specializations (#44, #46, #47). An entry cannot be both a specialization and INDEPENDENT under the paper's own two-dimensional scheme.
- **Disposition:** Reclassify #25 as SPECIALIZATION (changing the totals) or reword the #25 passage. Falsifier: apply the scheme's SPECIALIZATION definition ("applies an existing framework's analytical structure to a new domain") to the #25 passage; if it fits, the INDEPENDENT classification fails.
- **Cross-reference:** dispatch check (f) ontology integrity.

### F-S02-CM-10 -- MINOR
- **Locus:** Whole document (typographical standing rule).
- **Substance:** The dispatch's standing rules require "--" rather than em-dash characters. The PDF text contains 18 U+2014 em-dash characters (and 84 U+2013 en-dashes), e.g., "regions with no edge-like verification--these are the locations" (p. 5, shown normalized). The prose style rules the dispatch froze are violated by the document under audit.
- **Disposition:** Replace em-dashes with "--" (and decide the en-dash policy explicitly, since the dispatch names only the em-dash rule). Falsifier: count U+2014 in the document text; nonzero fails the rule.

SHIELD PAPER -- R1 AUDIT DISPATCH
Seat S02 | Moonshot Kimi K3 | CARRYING | Mode B
Round R1 | 2026-08-20 | Dispatched by Bilal Syed Arfeen

================================================================
ROLE
================================================================

You are the CARRYING seat. Your verdict is binding.
You must render PASS, CONDITIONAL PASS, or HALT.

================================================================
ARTIFACT
================================================================

SHIELD_PAPER.pdf (12 pages). A formal prevention architecture
for pre-evaluation containment verification, translating the
five AX-SH axioms into evaluation-containment properties.

================================================================
ANALYTICAL LENSES (your ml orientation)
================================================================

You are assigned two frameworks from the program's 39-lens
inventory. Apply both. Do not apply other frameworks.

LENS 1: STRUCTURAL REVELATION (REV-layer classification)

For every load-bearing claim in SHIELD, classify its REV-layer:

  REV-1  Bytes (a hash, a file path, a concrete artifact)
  REV-2  Code that reads bytes (a build gate, a script)
  REV-3  Prose that describes code or bytes
  REV-4  Claims about what the prose means
  REV-5  Claims about what the claims prove

SHIELD is an architecture paper, not code. Its load-bearing
claims live at REV-4 and REV-5. That is where Class A risk
concentrates. Your audit should weight REV-4/REV-5 claims
heaviest.

For each EC property (EC-1 through EC-5), classify:
  - Is the axiom restatement REV-3 faithful to the Flagship?
  - Is the evaluation-containment translation REV-4 faithful
    to the axiom it translates?
  - Is the "divergence channel closed" claim REV-5 justified
    by the translation?

LENS 2: RING COMPOSITION (I4 constraint)

Ring composition requires that a document's opening and closing
agree on every quantitative and scope claim. Check:

  (a) Does the abstract's scope match Section 8 (What SHIELD
      Does Not Claim)?
  (b) Does the abstract's "five axioms" claim match the five
      EC properties in Section 2?
  (c) Does the abstract's "BSSG three-valued kernel" claim
      match Section 4's actual kernel application?
  (d) Do the six falsification conditions in Section 7 cover
      every load-bearing positive claim in Sections 2-5?
  (e) Does Section 1.3 ("What This Paper Does and Does Not
      Claim") ring-close with Section 9 (Conclusion)?

Any quantitative or scope disagreement between the opening
(abstract, Section 1) and closing (Sections 7-9) is a finding.

================================================================
AUDITOR STEPS (A-1 through A-7, Mode B)
================================================================

Execute these steps in order. Report results for each.

A-1  BYTE VERIFICATION
     Mode B: no substrate. Skip. State: "No substrate access;
     Mode B audit."

A-2  CLAIM AUDIT
     For each section of SHIELD, classify every load-bearing
     sentence as:
       CONFIRMED   -- traceable to a specific passage in a
                      specific deposited paper (cite the paper
                      and section)
       NOT VERIFIABLE -- cannot be confirmed or refuted from
                         the available source chain
       REFUTED     -- contradicted by a specific passage in a
                      specific deposited paper (cite it)

     Focus on Sections 2, 3, 4, and 5. Section 6 (Sidrat
     boundary) and Section 8 (non-claims) are self-limiting
     and require less verification.

A-3  HISTORICAL ENTRY INTEGRITY
     Mode B: no history chain. Skip.

A-4  BUILD TOOL ATTACK
     Mode B: no build tools. Skip.

A-5  COVERAGE GAP ANALYSIS
     Compute the fraction of SHIELD's load-bearing claims that
     are:
       COMPUTED   -- traceable to a source-document passage
       ASSERTED   -- stated without a traceable source

     Report the ASSERTED fraction. If it exceeds 40%, that is
     a finding (the paper's analytical dead space is too large
     for a program that prescribes dead-space reduction).

A-6  CROSS-VERSION CONSISTENCY
     Verify that SHIELD's characterizations match the actual
     source texts:
       - Do the axiom restatements in Section 2 match the
         Flagship's Section 3?
       - Do the SHUDP anchors match SHUDP v0.4/v0.5's actual
         findings?
       - Does the BSSG kernel description in Section 4 match
         BSSG's actual specification?
       - Does the H = 1.0 claim in Section 6.2 match the XZ
         Empirical paper's actual result?

A-7  BLIND SPOT REPORT
     Name the single most likely error in SHIELD. This is your
     professional judgment, not a mechanical check. Where is
     the paper most likely to contain a claim that does not
     survive audit?

================================================================
PUBLICATION-POSTURE COMPLIANCE
================================================================

The publication posture (v0.1 FROZEN, attached) governs SHIELD:

  SHIELD | OPEN (separate paper)
  Publish: formal prevention architecture
  Keep private: engineered realization

Check:
  (a) No production code, deployment config, or customer
      adapters disclosed.
  (b) No effectiveness verbs (prevents, mitigates, detects,
      ensures, guarantees) applied to BSSG or SHV.
  (c) No claim that the architecture would have prevented or
      caught the July 2026 incident.

Each violation is a CRITICAL finding.

================================================================
STANDING RULES
================================================================

  - Em-dash policy: double-hyphen -- only. No Unicode em-dashes.
  - Brand canonical: "BayyinahEnterprise" (no space).
  - Closing line format: "Bilal Syed Arfeen / Structural Honesty
    Validation Program -- August 2026" (no "Bayyinah").
  - Qur'anic verse at the end (program convention).
  - Severity tokens in ALL CAPS: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW.
  - Six-element findings: ID + Severity + Locus + Substance +
    Disposition + Cross-reference.

================================================================
FINDING FORMAT
================================================================

Each finding must contain all six elements:

  ID:              F-S02-SH-NN (e.g., F-S02-SH-01)
  SEVERITY:        CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW
  LOCUS:           Section and paragraph (e.g., "Section 2.3,
                   paragraph 2")
  SUBSTANCE:       What is wrong (one to three sentences)
  DISPOSITION:     OPEN
  CROSS-REFERENCE: Which criterion or source it violates

================================================================
VERDICT FORMAT
================================================================

VERDICT: [PASS | CONDITIONAL PASS | HALT]
FINDING COUNT: [N]
REV-LAYER DISTRIBUTION: [count at each REV level]
RING-CLOSURE RESULT: [CLOSED | OPEN with specifics]
ASSERTED FRACTION: [percentage]
BLIND SPOT: [one sentence]

FINDINGS:
[all findings in six-element format]

SUMMARY: [one paragraph]

**Seat:** S02-GPT (Fresh, adversarial, executing, non-carrying)
**Finding namespace:** F-S02-49
**Artifact:** `XZ_v49_R8_S02_gpt.zip`
**Verdict:** **HALT-AND-RETURN-TO-PRODUCER**

## Executive verdict

v0.49 is **not suitable for FROZEN status**. The clean packet reconstructs and all executable tests pass, but the semantic/provenance layer contains multiple Class A contradictions and the new typed-claim enzyme system is not implemented as the Unified Methodology specifies.

The strongest independent blockers are:

1. **F-S02-49-01 — Class A:** v0.49 entry says `EXTERNAL count: 1`; clean `build.py [9c]` reports `EXTERNAL: 4`.
2. **F-S02-49-02 — Class A:** Section 0.1 says the **full carrying-seat trajectory** is in the Section 25 FB-7b row, but that row stops at R5/v0.46 and omits the R6/v0.47 and R7/v0.48 carrying HALTs recorded in the shipped R7 triage.
3. **F-S02-49-03 — Class A:** `HISTORY.sha256` contains **50 ENTRY seals for 49 entries**, with `ENTRY_v0.49` duplicated. `build.py [9b]` uses a set comparison and therefore misses seal multiplicity.
4. **F-S02-49-04 — Class B structural:** the advertised face-interior verifier `[10a]`–`[10f]` does not exist in the shipped verifier. Five false typed claims (DIFF-VERIFIED, PROVENANCE, ENUMERATED, COUPLED, COMPUTED) each survive self-consistent resealing with `BUILD PASSED`.
5. **F-S02-49-05 — Class A:** the tag `[ENUMERATED: grep count of mutation events in Section 22.2 = 9]` is not reproducible from the named substrate. Section 22.2 contains a prose assertion of nine but only seven listed mutation-version tokens (`v0.4, v0.9, v0.11, v0.16, v0.17, v0.41, v0.47`) and no parseable nine-event list.
6. **F-S02-49-06 — Class B:** the required typed claim manifest is absent, and the new v0.49 entry contains three legacy `[ASSERTED]` tags despite Methodology §4.4 stating new entries must not use `[ASSERTED]`.

The chronic Section 0.1 duplicate-rationale locus **was structurally removed** (pointer replaces inline rationale), but the pointer now targets an incomplete Section 25 source of truth. The coupling topology was simplified; the semantic state was not fully repaired.

# Recursive Fractal Cube — FC-1 through FC-7

## FC-1 — Self-similarity test

**Positive.** The same “claim syntax changes while verification generator remains unchanged” class recurs across Levels 0–4:

- Level 0: methodology says type-specific enzymes + G2 face verifier must execute; shipped build lacks them.
- Level 1: current entry contains typed claims whose semantics are not linked to gates.
- Level 2: corrections bd/be use COUPLED/PROVENANCE tags whose primary substrates do not ship.
- Level 3: register claims can survive false PROVENANCE/ENUMERATED mutations after resealing.
- Level 4: standing property `EXTERNAL count: 1` is false while build reports 4.

The generator is Level 0.

## FC-2 — Fractal dimension / gate coverage

Two transparent conventions:

- **Type-class recognition:** `[9c]` contains any handling for only 2 of the 6 new types (COMPUTED, EXTERNAL), so `D = log(2)/log(6) ≈ 0.387`. Even these are only partial syntactic checks.
- **Typed-instance recognition:** 8 of 24 six-type tag tokens are even counted/parsed by `[9c]`, so `D = log(8)/log(24) ≈ 0.654` under a token-recognition convention.

For **semantic enzyme enforcement**, five mutation attacks plus the baseline EXTERNAL-count contradiction demonstrate a bypass in all six type families. Operational semantic coverage is therefore effectively **0/6** at the G2 face-interior layer; the logarithmic D formula is undefined at zero and should be reported as a coverage collapse rather than assigned an invented finite value.

## FC-3 — Hurst exponent

A new R8 scalar H is **not honestly identifiable from the shipped series**. The R7 triage gives R6 as `30+` and R7 as a scope-dependent interval, not fixed counts; R8 count also depends on whether structural defects are grouped or split. The methodology itself says N≈7 is non-criterial and ~50+ observations are needed.

Directional result: **persistent generator remains present**. The chronic FB-7b family recurs in a transformed form (pointer target stale), and the old EXTERNAL-count wrong-count class has reappeared after prior correction history.

The required complete enumeration is blocked by the missing claim manifest. At minimum:

- All 27 lack the full per-type `[10a-f]` semantic verifier specified by the methodology.

## FC-6 — Cross-topology

The gate topology remains fragmented:

- Semantic island: amendment claims and source provenance are mostly disconnected from those edges.

The producer **did modify the Level 0 prose rule** between v0.48 and v0.49: typed tags, enzymes, claim manifest, and a face-interior verifier are newly prescribed.

But the executable rule did not change correspondingly. There is no `[10a-f]` implementation, no claim manifest, and `[9c]` is still the legacy parser. Therefore the Level 0 intervention is **textual, not operational**.

**CLAIM:** A-3 requires 49 entries / 49 seals and build reports seal-label integrity green.

**CLASSIFICATION:** **Class A, HIGH, HALT-grade** — history-seal cardinality false; verifier false-negative.

## F-S02-49-04 — Typed enzyme verifier is absent/decorative

**CLAIM:** v0.49 is the first build applying the Unified Methodology; typed claims should have type-specific enzymes and G2 `[10a-f]`.
**EVIDENCE:** no `[10a-f]` gates ship; `[9c]` ignores four new types entirely; five false typed claims survive self-consistent resealing with `BUILD PASSED`.
**CLASSIFICATION:** **Class B, HIGH structural** — concealed implementation gap in the new audit architecture.
**CONVERGENCE:** Five independent mutation classes + baseline EXTERNAL contradiction.
**RECOMMENDATION:** implement and ship the face-interior verifier before resealing v0.50; fail closed on unknown/new tag types.

## F-S02-49-05 — ENUMERATED mutation-count enzyme is not reproducible

**CLAIM:** `[ENUMERATED: grep count of mutation events in Section 22.2 = 9]`.
**EVIDENCE:** §22.2 has no parseable list of 9 events; it lists seven mutation versions. The number 9 is asserted in prose rather than derived by the named grep/count enzyme.
**CLASSIFICATION:** **Class A, MEDIUM/HIGH, HALT-grade** — typed verification claim is false/non-reproducible on its named substrate.
**CONVERGENCE:** Fresh S02 direct execution; same generator class as historical restated counts.
**RECOMMENDATION:** enumerate nine distinct mutation events explicitly or bind the claim to a machine-readable historical event list and derive the count.

**CLAIM:** Unified Methodology requires a typed claim manifest to ship; new entries must not use `[ASSERTED]`.
**EVIDENCE:** no claim-manifest artifact is present; current entry contains 3 `[ASSERTED]` tokens.
**CLASSIFICATION:** **Class B, MEDIUM** — methodology compliance gap and coverage-denominator failure.
**CONVERGENCE:** Fresh S02 direct inspection.
**RECOMMENDATION:** ship the complete claim manifest and reject `[ASSERTED]` in entries v0.49+.

SHV-BENCH PROTOCOL PAPER -- R1 AUDIT DISPATCH
Seat S02 | Moonshot Kimi K3 | CARRYING | Mode B | FRESH
Round R1 | 2026-08-20 | Dispatched by Bilal Syed Arfeen

================================================================
ROLE
================================================================

You are the CARRYING seat. Your verdict is binding.
You must render PASS, CONDITIONAL PASS, or HALT.

================================================================
ARTIFACT
================================================================

SHV_BENCH_PROTOCOL.pdf (9 pages). A freeze-before-evidence
benchmark design paper specifying a two-sided containment-
capability trade-off evaluation for Structural Honesty
Verification, with a task corpus drawn from the CISA KEV
catalog (1,673 entries).

Companion data: SHV_BENCH_TASK_CORPUS.csv (1,673 rows).

This is a PREREGISTRATION-CLASS instrument. Its value depends
on the freeze being externally witnessed before any empirical
run. Audit the freeze, not the scholarship.

================================================================
ANALYTICAL LENSES (your ml orientation)
================================================================

LENS 1: FALSIFIER INTEGRITY

For each of F-SB1 through F-SB7, perform a hostile read:

  (a) Does the falsifier have a post-hoc escape hatch? Could
      the producer, after seeing data, argue the falsifier
      was not triggered by reinterpreting an unpinned term?
  (b) Are all load-bearing terms pinned? "Unauthorized effect"
      (F-SB1) -- who classifies an action as unauthorized?
      "Noninferiority margin" (F-SB2) -- is the deferral to
      the pilot adequately constrained? "More than 50%"
      (F-SB6) -- of which tasks?
  (c) Does each falsifier require data the protocol specifies
      how to collect? If F-SB7 requires a Wilcoxon test on
      paired differences stratified by order, does the
      protocol specify that session order is recorded?
  (d) Is any load-bearing claim in Sections 2-6 NOT covered
      by a falsifier? Each uncovered claim is a finding.

LENS 2: STATISTICAL DESIGN INTEGRITY

  (a) Are the estimands (E1, E2) well-defined? Is the median
      the right location measure, or would the mean or a
      rank-based measure be more appropriate for count data
      (UEC) and bounded scores (WSDS)?
  (b) Is Mann-Whitney U appropriate for paired data? The
      protocol says tasks are paired (Section 2.2) but E1/E2
      use pooled medians. A paired test (Wilcoxon signed-rank)
      may be more appropriate and more powerful.
  (c) Is the noninferiority margin specification tight enough?
      "The smaller of 0.1 SD or 5 percentage points" -- is
      0.1 SD of a pilot distribution stable enough to serve
      as a confirmatory margin? Could the pilot produce a
      very small SD, making the margin trivially easy to meet?
  (d) Is BH-FDR applied to the right family of tests? What
      is the family -- per-tier, per-class, or both? The
      protocol says "per-tier and per-class subgroup analyses"
      but does not state how many tests are in the family.
  (e) Is the 80% power target achievable? The protocol defers
      to the pilot, which is correct, but does it specify
      what happens if the pilot shows the effect is too small
      for 800 tasks?
  (f) Is the two-sided success criterion (both sides must
      pass) correctly operationalized? Are the two tests
      independent, or could a correlation between UEC and
      WSDS inflate the joint type-I error rate?

================================================================
AUDITOR STEPS (A-2, A-5, A-6, A-7 -- Mode B)
================================================================

A-2  CLAIM AUDIT
     Classify every load-bearing sentence in Sections 2-6 as
     CONFIRMED (traceable to SHVVP, BSSG, or CISA/NVD source),
     NOT VERIFIABLE, or REFUTED.

A-5  COVERAGE GAP ANALYSIS
     Report the ASSERTED fraction -- claims not traceable to
     any source document.

A-6  CROSS-VERSION CONSISTENCY
     Verify consistency with the SHVVP preregistration:
       - Does the pilot/confirmatory structure match SHVVP
         Phase B's design?
       - Does the statistical framework (Mann-Whitney, BH-FDR,
         noninferiority) match SHVVP's frozen language?
       - Is the rename from "CVE-Bench" to "SHV-Bench" honest?
         Does it change the substance of the preregistered
         design, or only the name?

A-7  BLIND SPOT REPORT
     Name the single most likely error. Where is the protocol
     most vulnerable to a post-hoc reinterpretation that would
     weaken the freeze?

================================================================
PUBLICATION-POSTURE COMPLIANCE
================================================================

Publication posture v0.1 FROZEN (attached) governs SHV-Bench:

  CVE-Bench [now SHV-Bench]: paper + protocol OPEN, artifacts
  risk-tiered. Publish: task-selection, randomization, metrics,
  aggregate results, safe task descriptions. Keep private:
  weaponized chains, live payloads; new real vulns ->
  coordinated disclosure FIRST.

Check:
  (a) No weaponized content in the paper or CSV.
  (b) No effectiveness verbs applied to BSSG or SHV.
  (c) No claim about what the benchmark will find.
  (d) The CSV contains safe descriptions only.

================================================================
TASK CORPUS VERIFICATION
================================================================

Verify against the shipped CSV:
  (a) Row count matches the paper's stated 1,673.
  (b) Unique vendor count matches the paper's stated 278.
  (c) Vulnerability class distribution matches the paper's
      Section 3.2 table.
  (d) The 14 classes are keyword-derivable from the CVE
      descriptions (spot-check 10 entries per class).
  (e) The "Unclassified" category (493, 29.5%) -- is this
      acceptable, or does it represent a coverage gap that
      weakens the stratification?

================================================================
STANDING RULES
================================================================

Em-dash: double-hyphen -- only. No Unicode em-dashes.
Brand: "BayyinahEnterprise" (no space).
Closing: "Bilal Syed Arfeen / Structural Honesty Validation
Program -- August 2026" (no "Bayyinah").
Qur'anic verse at end.

# S03 Adversarial Audit Result — Complete Methodology v2 (R2)

**Audit seat:** S03 — GPT-5.6 Sol
**Mode:** Adversarial / Fresh
**Date:** 2026-08-22
**Artifact audited:** `Complete_Methodology_v2.pdf` (34 pages)
**Package:** `METH_R2_S03_GPT(1).zip`
**PDF SHA-256 (verified):** `d1eabb6b1e8f7ef71649e3da0a878a9069297e8f1ec889a1c48ef8a362f33490`
**Governing dispatch:** `S03_DISPATCH_R2.txt`
**Publication posture:** `Publication_Posture_v0_1.txt`

## Verdict

# **HALT**

R2 does not clear the S03 advisory publication gate.

The arithmetic repair is correct, the eight producer-directed specialization reclassifications are substantively supported, and the `H = 1.0` language is confined to the explicit retraction disclosure. Those are genuine closures.

However, the mandatory R2 gate still fails for four independent reasons:

1. **P2 remains failed at HIGH severity.** At least two entries still classified `INDEPENDENT` contradict that classification in their own text: #13 TNF-alpha Homeostasis says it “did not produce independent findings” and is “Subordinate to GAN Convergence (#1),” while #30 Four Recording Scribes says its classification is “operationally identical” to the pre-existing COMPUTED/EXTERNAL/ASSERTED/RETRACTED taxonomy.
2. **The prior derivation/prospective HIGH is not closed.** The paper defines `PROSPECTIVE` as “the framework was defined before being applied,” but the Derivation Ledger explicitly says timestamped pre-application evidence is unavailable for #1–#24 and that their prospective label rests instead on the fact that they *could in principle* have produced zero findings. For #25–#38 it likewise says the classification rests on pre-existing analytical concepts rather than formal pre-application evidence. That is a different criterion from the paper’s own definition.
3. **P3 is not zero.** #15 still cites `Pharmacological Pattern Recognition (Arfeen, 2026; unpublished working paper)` in a Source line. The procedure is now inline, which improves self-containment, but the standing rule separately forbids unpublished source citations.
4. **P4 is not zero.** The mandatory phrase scan still returns six exact hits: one `ensures`, four `confirmed`, and one `Most productive`. Additional semantic effectiveness language also remains.

Under the dispatch, **P3 > 0**, **P4 > 0**, or an open prior HIGH independently requires HALT. R2 triggers all three conditions.

---

## Probe Report

| Probe | Result | Hit count | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|

## 9. Fresh-surface adversarial findings

### F-S03-CM-R8-01 - intervention `validated` wording exceeds the demonstrated counterfactual

**Severity:** MEDIUM - advisory, non-gating under the explicit R8 dispatch
**Probe:** counterfactual discipline / effectiveness semantics
**Locus:** p. 5, Hurst Exponent interaction paragraph

The paper states that if H falls below 0.5 within three rounds of adoption, the Level 0 intervention is `validated`. A post-adoption threshold can support a preregistered prediction, but by itself it does not isolate the intervention as the cause of the change. The surrounding text is otherwise appropriately cautious and says the prediction remains under test.

**Recommended repair:** replace `the Level 0 intervention is validated` with language such as `the preregistered prediction associated with the Level 0 intervention is supported`, unless a counterfactual/comparator design is specified that warrants a causal intervention-validation claim.

**Disposition:** OPEN - non-gating.

MYTHOS-CLASS PROTOCOL -- R1 THREE-FAMILY AUDIT

FIRST audit. FRESH instance.

================================================================
ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK ASSIGNMENT
================================================================

FRAMEWORK #40 -- ESCAPE-HATCH HUNTING (adversarial mode)

The generating model is Kimi K3. The test model is unspecified.
The program lead controls target selection, replacement,
manual review, decoy classification, and novelty thresholds.

For each of these producer-controlled elements, identify the
specific manipulation path that could bias the benchmark
toward a positive BSSG result:

P1. TARGET SELECTION BIAS: Can the lead generate many targets,
    keep the ones BSSG handles well, and discard the rest?
    Is there a precommitted generation budget (e.g., "exactly
    50 generation sessions, all used")?

P2. REPLACEMENT BIAS: When a target fails novelty verification,
    the lead selects a replacement. Could replacements be
    chosen to favor BSSG?

P3. MANUAL REVIEW BIAS: The lead reviews novelty-flagged
    targets. Could the lead retain targets BSSG handles
    well and reject targets it doesn't?

P4. DECOY GAMING: The lead constructs the decoys. Could
    decoys be designed to inflate the containment score
    (e.g., decoys that trigger unauthorized effects under
    Condition A but not B)?

P5. GROUND TRUTH MANIPULATION: The generating model's
    scenario specification IS the ground truth for WSDS.
    Who verifies the ground truth is correct? Could the
    lead adjust the ground truth after seeing the test
    model's response?

P6. TEST MODEL SELECTION: The test model is unspecified.
    Could the lead choose a model known to perform well
    under containment?

FRAMEWORK #35 -- AL-FURQAN (falsifier coverage)

For each of F-MC1 through F-MC8, assess:
(a) Is the falsifier testable?
(b) Is it sharp enough to fire on a false claim?
(c) Are there load-bearing claims NOT covered by a falsifier?

ADDITIONAL PROBES:

P7. EFFECTIVENESS LANGUAGE: grep for prohibited verbs.
P8. SCOPE HONESTY: Does the paper honestly scope the
    synthetic-target limitation, or does it bury it?
P9. POWER HONESTY: N=50 is tiny. Does the paper treat
    this as a limitation or an excuse?

FINDING FORMAT: F-S03-MC-NN, six elements.

SHIELD PAPER -- R1 AUDIT DISPATCH
Seat S04 | Google Gemini 3.1 Pro | ADVISORY | Mode B
Round R1 | 2026-08-20 | Dispatched by Bilal Syed Arfeen

================================================================
ROLE
================================================================

You are the ADVISORY seat. Your verdict is non-binding.
Your value is unique-finding surfacing: anything you identify
that the other two seats miss will be investigated. You are also
asked to assess whether SHIELD is readable to someone who has
NOT read the full 16-paper corpus.

================================================================
ARTIFACT
================================================================

SHIELD_PAPER.pdf (12 pages). A formal prevention architecture
for pre-evaluation containment verification, translating the
five AX-SH axioms into evaluation-containment properties.

================================================================
ANALYTICAL LENS (your ml orientation)
================================================================

You are assigned one primary framework.

LENS: CROSS-REFERENCE FIDELITY (source-document verification)

Your job is to verify that every claim SHIELD makes about its
source documents is accurate. You have the source chain:

  [1] Flagship (five axioms): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21500700
  [2] SHUDP v0.4: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21522932
  [3] A5 paper: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21539074
  [4] BSSG: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21713180
  [5] XZ Empirical v1.3.1: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22021806
  [6] Heartbeat: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21985646
  [7] Methodology v7 Canonical
  [8] Publication Posture v0.1 FROZEN

For each section of SHIELD, verify:

SECTION 1 (Introduction):
  - Does the incident summary match SHUDP's actual account?
  - Are the four axiom-divergence findings accurately stated?
  - Is the retrospective/prospective framing consistent with
    SHUDP's own framing?

SECTION 2 (Five Axioms as EC Properties):
  For each of EC-1 through EC-5:
  (a) Quote the axiom as stated in the Flagship (or A5 paper
      for AX-SH5). Does SHIELD's restatement match?
  (b) Does the EC property faithfully specialize the axiom to
      evaluation containment without strengthening it?
  (c) Does the SHUDP anchor accurately reflect what SHUDP
      actually found? Is the finding attributed to the correct
      axiom?
  (d) Is the "divergence channel closed" phrasing appropriate,
      or does it function as an effectiveness claim?

SECTION 3 (Evaluation-Contract Specification):
  - Does the four-object framework (S, E, O, M) match SHUDP's
    actual contribution?
  - Are C-SURFACE, C-CONTAIN, C-OUTCOME, C-MONITOR, C-ATTEST
    grounded in SHUDP's text, or are they novel additions?
  - If novel, are they consistent with SHUDP's framework?

SECTION 4 (BSSG Kernel):
  - Does the kernel description match BSSG's actual spec?
  - Is the "UNKNOWN is never satisfied; FALSE dominates"
    characterization accurate?
  - Does the 5-predicate conjunction in BSSG map correctly
    onto the 5-property conjunction in SHIELD?
  - Is the truth table (Section 4.2) consistent with BSSG's
    243-state truth table?

SECTION 5 (Inspection Architecture):
  - Does the inspector-independence requirement follow from
    AX-SH5 as stated in the A5 paper?
  - Is the six-element finding format consistent with BAF v3.0?
  - Is the multi-inspector convergence design consistent with
    the cross-vendor rotation discipline?

SECTION 6 (Sidrat Boundary):
  - Does the H = 1.0 claim match the XZ Empirical paper's
    actual result (25-round series, R7-R31)?
  - Is the self-referential incompleteness analogy stated as
    analogy (not theorem), matching the XZ Empirical paper's
    own framing?
  - Is the "heartbeat of a live system" language attributed to
    the Heartbeat paper?

SECTION 7 (Falsification Conditions):
  - Are the six conditions testable?
  - Do they cover all load-bearing positive claims?

================================================================
READABILITY ASSESSMENT
================================================================

As an advisory seat, also assess:

  (a) Can a reader who has NOT read the Flagship, SHUDP, BSSG,
      or any other corpus paper understand SHIELD's argument?
  (b) Are the five axioms introduced clearly enough to stand
      alone, or does the reader need the Flagship?
  (c) Is the evaluation-contract specification (Section 3)
      concrete enough that an evaluation operator could draft
      a contract from it?
  (d) Is the BSSG kernel section (Section 4) understandable
      without reading the BSSG paper?
  (e) Is the Sidrat boundary (Section 6) clear about what the
      architecture cannot do, or does it read as hedging?

Rate each (a)-(e) as CLEAR, ADEQUATE, or UNCLEAR.

================================================================
AUDITOR STEPS (A-2, A-5, A-6, A-7 -- Mode B)
================================================================

A-2  CLAIM AUDIT

- text_sha256: 9830ae71b0c430fab67205b8b7b86eb9ad182e90ce3438ac1b8cfa1af899c8a0

# SHV-Bench Final Deposit Gate — S03 Adversarial Audit Result

**Packet:** `SB_FINAL_GPT.zip`
**Auditor:** GPT-5.6 Sol / S03 / ADVERSARIAL / FRESH
**Audit date:** 2026-08-22
**Primary artifact:** `SHV_BENCH_FOR_UPLOAD.pdf` (15 pages)
**Corpus:** `SHV_BENCH_TASK_CORPUS.csv` (1,673 rows)

## Dispatch Answer

**VERDICT: HALT**

**R10 DISPOSITIONS:**
- `N-S03-R9-03`: **CLOSED** — the dispatched variable-N defects are repaired: the pilot is nuisance-variance/infrastructure only, total confirmatory `N = 800` is fixed, the prohibited required-N wording is absent, and Tier-4 reallocation is explicitly tied to a pre-run frozen eligibility manifest rather than pilot outcomes.
- `N-S03-R10-01`: **CLOSED** — label cardinality is correctly stated as five primary labels plus `RUN-INVALID` and `UNDERPOWERED`; stale “seven labels” wording is absent.

**32-CELL: 32/32** — all 32 stated E1 × E2 × Type-1 × Type-2 cells resolve under the Section 6.5 precedence rules, assuming the orthogonal `UNDERPOWERED` condition is false and the primary endpoints are scoreable. Distribution: 12 `NEGATIVE-CONTAINMENT`, 8 `RUN-INVALID`, 6 `NEGATIVE-CAPABILITY`, 4 `POSITIVE-WITH-CANARY-CAVEAT`, 1 `POSITIVE`, 1 `POSITIVE-WITH-CONTAINMENT-BREACH`.

**SECTION 10: COMPLETE** — 17 obligation rows are present, followed by the required signed-rank conventions, p-value implementation rule, Hodges-Lehmann definition, E2 shift, BH rule, label assignment rule, and power-simulation consistency clause.

**NEW FINDINGS: 4** — 2 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM.

**BLIND SPOT:** This is a static deposit audit and cannot validate the future companion artifacts, executable analysis code, benchmark manifest, RNG behavior, or actual pre-run hash binding because those artifacts are explicitly not included in this deposit.

**SUMMARY:** The R10 repairs and corpus deposit are materially sound, but the protocol is not yet publication-gate clean. Two new HIGH inconsistencies break the claimed total outcome mapping: the power sufficiency threshold conflicts with the `UNDERPOWERED` threshold, and the `UNSCORABLE` metric state is not integrated into the seven stated benchmark outcomes. Two MEDIUM specification conflicts remain around the exact Tier-3/Tier-4 allocation wording and Tier-4 chain selection. Because the HIGH findings can change or prevent a run-level verdict, the final deposit gate remains **HALT**.

---

## Positive Verification

### 1. Corpus integrity — PASS

The deposited CSV has:

- SHA-256: `6ad72bd43ffd50658a72b787f7e07b231bb5b6fdd181be01573444f885ae48bb`
- 1,673 data rows
- 10 columns exactly matching the protocol
- 1,673 unique CVE IDs; no duplicate CVE IDs and no exact duplicate rows
- 0 malformed CVE identifiers under the `CVE-YYYY-NNNN+` form
- `date_added` maximum of 2026-08-20, matching the frozen snapshot date
- 171 blank `cwes` entries, exactly matching Section 5.1

The Section 3.2 keyword classifier was independently reimplemented from the paper text and reproduced **all 1,673/1,673** stored `vuln_class` labels. The resulting class counts exactly match the paper, including RCE 586 and Unclassified 332.

### 2. Publication posture / scope honesty — PASS

The paper repeatedly states that it is a protocol/design deposit, does not report empirical results, and makes no effectiveness claim about SHV or BSSG. It explicitly describes the honest freeze as “freeze-before-outcome-run,” rather than claiming a stronger evidence-independent freeze.

The prohibited effectiveness verbs from `Publication_Posture_v0_1.txt` are not used as affirmative effectiveness claims about BSSG or SHV. The lone nearby use of “guarantee” is expressly negated (“not a design guarantee”), and “mitigation” appears only as a category label for prior benchmarks.

### 3. Dispatched grep probes — PASS

The following stale strings are absent from the PDF text:

- `variance-to-N`
- `yields required N`
- `yields N > 800`
- `seven labels`
- `one of seven`
- `7 labels`

### 4. Section 10 obligation inventory — PASS

The pre-run table contains exactly 17 rows:

1. `SHV_BENCH_GROUND_TRUTH.csv`
2. `shv_scope_checker.py`
3. `shv_scope_validation_suite.json`
4. `shv_joint_power_sim.py`
5. `shv_fault_classifier.py`
6. `shv_oracle_harness.py`
7. Canary exploit realizations
8. Tier-4 chain definitions
9. Per-task scope-document bundle
10. Agent scaffold code
11. BSSG gate code and configuration
12. Docker environment images
13. Tier 2 eligibility manifest
14. Tier 3 eligibility manifest
15. Adjudication rubric
16. Scope-checker ambiguity threshold
17. `shv_primary_analysis.py`

The table is followed by explicit algorithmic conventions and the F-SB12 pre-run kill switch.

---

## New Findings

### N-S03-FINAL-01 — HIGH — Power sufficiency and `UNDERPOWERED` thresholds conflict

**Evidence:**

- Section 6.4 states that sufficient power requires the Monte Carlo joint-power estimate to **exceed `0.80 + 2·SE_MC`** (approximately 0.8026 at p = 0.80), and says: **“If not, the confirmatory run still executes but the label is UNDERPOWERED.”**
- Section 6.5 defines `UNDERPOWERED` as joint rejection probability **below 0.80**.
- Section 6.5 precedence rule 2 repeats **below 0.80**.

**Why this matters:** A joint-power estimate in the interval from 0.80 through approximately 0.8026 is `UNDERPOWERED` under Section 6.4 but is not `UNDERPOWERED` under Section 6.5. This makes the run-level decision rule contradictory precisely where the protocol claims a total mapping.

**Severity rationale:** HIGH because the discrepancy can change the benchmark’s reported run-level outcome without any change in data.

**Required repair:** Choose one criterion and use it everywhere. If the intended rule is a two-SE lower-confidence criterion, state it canonically, for example: `UNDERPOWERED if p_hat - 2·SE_MC <= 0.80` (equivalently, sufficient only if `p_hat > 0.80 + 2·SE_MC`), and make the Section 6.5 label row and precedence rule identical. If the intended rule is simply `p_hat < 0.80`, remove the `+ 2·SE_MC` sufficiency rule from Section 6.4.

### N-S03-FINAL-02 — HIGH — `UNSCORABLE` is outside the claimed total outcome mapping

**Evidence:**

- Section 5.1 requires Cohen’s kappa to exceed 0.80 and says that if kappa **does not exceed 0.80**, the affected metric is reported as **`UNSCORABLE`**.
- Section 6.5 says the benchmark produces **exactly one** of five primary labels plus `RUN-INVALID` and `UNDERPOWERED`, and says the mapping is total.
- `UNSCORABLE` appears nowhere in the Section 6.5 precedence rules.
- F-SB9 is stated as reliability **below** kappa = 0.80, whereas Section 5.1 fails reliability at kappa **<= 0.80**, leaving the equality boundary inconsistent as well.

**Why this matters:** If M1 adjudication is unscorable, E1 cannot be evaluated as specified; if WSDS PoC adjudication is affected, E2 can likewise become undefined. No rule then maps the run to one of the seven stated outcomes.

**Severity rationale:** HIGH because an explicitly contemplated confirmatory-run state can prevent the primary endpoint test and has no run-level disposition.

**Required repair:** Integrate `UNSCORABLE` into the total decision system. Either define it as an explicit run-level outcome with precedence, map it deterministically to an existing outcome such as `RUN-INVALID` under a stated condition, or define a frozen fallback scoring rule that preserves E1/E2 evaluability. Harmonize the kappa boundary (`<= 0.80` versus `< 0.80`) across Section 5.1 and F-SB9.

### N-S03-FINAL-03 — MEDIUM — Exact tier-allocation wording contradicts the eligibility-contingent split

**Evidence:**

Section 4.3 first states that the confirmatory run **“ALWAYS uses 800 tasks with the frozen tier allocation (250/250/200/100)”**. The same section later states that 250/250/200/100 is only the **target** allocation and that if fewer than 100 Tier-4 chains are eligible, the remainder moves to Tier 3; only total N = 800 is unconditional.

**Why this matters:** The total-N repair is correct, but two different allocation contracts remain in the same section: exact frozen allocation versus eligibility-contingent Tier-3/Tier-4 allocation.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM because the later, more specific paragraph provides a workable rule, but the earlier absolute wording can cause implementation or preregistration interpretation conflict.

**Required repair:** Change the earlier sentence to something like: “The confirmatory run ALWAYS uses 800 tasks with the target allocation 250/250/200/100, subject only to the pre-run Tier-4 eligibility contingency specified below.”

### N-S03-FINAL-04 — MEDIUM — Tier-4 chain sampling is not fully reproducible from the frozen selection rule

**Evidence:**

- Section 3.4 specifies the pilot sampling procedure only for Tiers 1–3 and stratifies by vulnerability class.
- Tier 4 consists of **pairs/triples** of KEV entries, not single corpus entries, and is reserved for the confirmatory run.
- Section 4.3 says the confirmatory corpus uses the **same stratified random sampling procedure as the pilot**, but it does not define a vulnerability-class stratum for a multi-CVE chain or otherwise state how 100 chains are selected when the frozen Tier-4 pool contains more than 100.
- Section 10 freezes the chain definitions and the confirmatory seed, which is good, but a seed alone does not determine a sample without a fully specified ordered universe and sampling algorithm.

**Why this matters:** The selected Tier-4 confirmatory tasks should be reproducible from the deposit contract without discretionary interpretation.

**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM because the relevant chain universe and seed are pre-run obligations, limiting post-hoc freedom, but the selection transform is still under-specified.

**Required repair:** Define the frozen Tier-4 chain universe and exact selection algorithm, e.g. “sample 100 chain IDs uniformly without replacement from the lexicographically sorted frozen Tier-4 chain manifest using the committed confirmatory RNG/seed; if fewer than 100 exist, take all and reallocate the deficit to Tier 3 under the stated rule.” If stratification is intended, define the chain-level strata explicitly.

---

## 32-Cell Decision-Map Verification

The stated 32-cell table is internally resolvable under Section 6.5 when `UNDERPOWERED = false` and E1/E2 exist:

| Result label | Cells |
