## S-2. Correction (ay) and body repairs [a]-[g]

- **(ay) TRUE on its quoted string, wrong in its conclusion.** The v0.46 register item six reads verbatim as (ay) quotes it. The v0.46 trust-roots timestamps are `2026-08-07T20:00:00.000000Z` as claimed, though (ay) narrates them as `2026-08-07T20:00:00Z`, dropping the six zero-microsecond digits that are the evidence. The inference that the defect "was substantively repaired in the bytes" is false: see F-SC05-47-03.
- **[a] TRUE** -- front-matter status rewritten for the R5 audit.
- **[b] TRUE** -- Section 22.2 reads "For carried entries (v0.1 through v0.46)".
- **[c] TRUE** -- Section 22.3 reads "carried at v0.38-v0.47".
- **[d] TRUE** -- FB-7b row reads "RESOLVED v0.31; PENDING RE-CARRY v0.47".
- **[e] TRUE** -- Post-v0.31 note now covers Convergence Rounds 2-5 and records the Kimi K3 Seat 2 CONDITIONAL PASS.
- **[f] TRUE** -- build.py docstring at v0.47 and gate [2d] added and passing.
- **[g] LANDED IN THE WRONG PLACE.** It is listed as a body repair and it edited a sealed Section 27 entry. See F-SC05-47-01.

---

## S-3. Findings

### F-SC05-47-01 [CRITICAL] [Class A] -- the sealed v0.46 entry was mutated in place; PRIOR_HISTORY is byte-false against the external anchor

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md:1202` (sealed v0.46 entry); `HISTORY.sha256` line `ENTRY_v0.46`; declared PRIOR_HISTORY at `:1219`; declared as body repair [g] at `:1217`.
- **Substance:**

  The v0.46 shipped bytes, which this seat holds and verified last round against the R5 manifest, read:

  > Convergence Round 4 on v0.45 bytes: **4 fresh seats (Opus 5, Kimi K3, Gemini, GPT), 4 families, 1 shell (LEO).**

  The v0.47 bytes carry, in the same sealed entry:

  > Convergence Round 4 on v0.45 bytes: **4 deployed seats (Opus 5, Kimi K3, Gemini, GPT; 3 with verified independence, 1 with independence structurally false per F-S01-45-00), 4 families, 1 shell (LEO).**

  Entry length 5,538 to 5,627 bytes, delta +89. A full entry-by-entry diff of Section 27 against the held v0.46 bytes shows exactly one carried entry differs -- v0.46 -- and that Section 27's non-entry text differs only in the closing "End of XZ Protocol" line. So this is a single, targeted, in-place edit of a sealed historical entry.

  The seal chain moved with it. `ENTRY_v0.46` was `121e144e566b47e3...` in the v0.46 packet and is `36f1787a6c34ad16...` in the v0.47 packet. `FULL_SECTION_27` was `4d9559bc3bb4d96a...` and is `0351ad50ac755081...`. A sealed entry's seal changed after sealing.

  The chain value is therefore false. The v0.47 entry declares `PRIOR_HISTORY c51b64e9e2d1e985...`. The true SHA-256 of the v0.46 `HISTORY.sha256` file is `558b2a2c91af4ee5e1ecc52c377d92534129d710e3ef3aa2aec9367ebed83325`. Causation proved by construction: restoring the v0.46 entry text and its original `ENTRY_v0.46` seal and re-running build.py's own `derive_prior_history` returns exactly `558b2a2c91af4ee5...`. The mutation is the sole cause.

  **build.py passes GREEN because it recomputes over the mutated bytes.** `HISTORY.sha256` ships inside the packet and was regenerated, so every internal seal is mutually consistent. This is the self-consistent forgery that Section 22.2 names as the residual blind spot -- realized in shipped bytes for the first time. Unlike v0.41, which the build caught because its regex was applied inconsistently, this one is invisible to every gate in the packet.

  It is not disclosed. The v0.47 entry contains no reference to an in-place mutation, and Section 22.2 still records the historical tally as "eight recorded in-place mutations at v0.4, v0.9, v0.11, v0.16, v0.17, and v0.41". This is the ninth.

  **This seat is a contributing cause and says so.** R5 finding F-S05-46-02 prescribed: *Restate as "4 deployed seats, 3 with independence intact, 1 with independence structurally false (F-S01-45-00)"*. That disposition named the replacement text and named neither the locus nor the admissible route. The producer applied it where the text was, which was inside a sealed entry. The mechanism the protocol reserves for exactly this -- an append-only correction in the current entry -- was available and was used three paragraphs earlier for (ay).

- **Disposition:** Do not carry v0.47. Restore the v0.46 entry verbatim to its `c4e78d67...` form, regenerate `HISTORY.sha256`, and confirm `ENTRY_v0.46` returns to `121e144e566b47e3...` and PRIOR_HISTORY to `558b2a2c91af4ee5...`. Re-land [g] as append-only correction (az) in the v0.47 entry, in the form (ay) already models. Record the event as the ninth in-place mutation and update the Section 22.2 tally from eight to nine. Add a gate that pins the prior packet's `HISTORY.sha256` digest as a constant in build.py and fails when the derivation does not reproduce it -- that converts the external anchor into an internal check for the one link where it is cheap. Ship the prior-packet digest in every dispatch so any seat, continuous or fresh, can run this test.
- **Cross-reference:** R5 F-S05-46-02 (this seat's under-specified disposition, contributing cause); Section 22.2 self-consistent-forgery boundary; v0.41 retraction at `:1156`; v0.4 defect entry; standing boundary 21.

### F-SC05-47-02 [HIGH] [Class A] -- standing boundary count is 30, declared 29

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md:1219`, "Disclosed standing boundaries -- 29 items".
- **Substance:** Parsing the list and normalizing the one item with an internal comma ("A-side seam (condition_a.py, SHIELD-scoped)") yields 30 items. The arithmetic confirms it: v0.46 declared 27, and v0.47 adds three -- register item (9) f-string nested quotes (F-S07-46-02), register item (10) fb_spec omits FB-7b locus (F-S07-46-03), and correction (ay)'s explicit disclosure of the ungated trust-roots timestamp, which appears as the thirtieth list item. 27 + 3 = 30. The dispatch repeats the wrong figure ("standing boundaries 27 to 29"). This is the same count-narration class the round exists to close, on the same list, one version after the same list's count was corrected from 25 to 27.
- **Disposition:** Correct to 30. Generate the count from the parsed list in build.py and fail [9f] on mismatch, in the way [9] already does for entry count and "forty-seven". The list is comma-delimited with one known internal-comma item; replace that comma with a semicolon so a naive parse is exact.
- **Cross-reference:** F-SC05-47-08 (a COMPUTED tag would have caught this); v0.46 body repair [e]; standing boundary 20 (no boundary-retirement mechanism, so the list only grows and the count only gets harder).

### F-SC05-47-03 [HIGH] [Class A] -- F-S05-46-07 declared CLOSED; the finding is unrepaired and the bytes prove it

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md:1213` register item (2); correction (ay) at `:1215`; `xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json`, four `"generated"` fields.
- **Substance:** A byte diff of the trust-roots file between the v0.46 and v0.47 packets shows exactly two changed lines: `"protocol"` and `"manifest_digest"`. All four `"generated"` values are byte-identical across the version bump: `2026-08-07T20:00:00.000000Z`, four copies, whole hour, six zero microsecond digits. The file was regenerated -- the manifest digest changed to `45364f2669bb6614...` because the code files changed -- and the generation timestamp did not move. That is direct proof of the R5 finding: the field is a carried constant, not a generation record. F-S05-46-07's substance was fabricated provenance, not staleness; its prescribed disposition was to emit the field from the generating tool or delete it. (ay) closes the staleness limb (F-S01-45-05) and explicitly leaves the gate limb open as boundary 30. Neither limb is the finding. Declaring it CLOSED converts an open Class A surface into a closed one in the register while the bytes are unchanged.
- **Disposition:** Reopen F-S05-46-07. Either emit `generated` from the key-generation tool at generation time, or delete the field and state in `manifest_digest_note` that key generation time is not recorded. Add a gate asserting the value is not a whole-hour zero-microsecond constant and not identical to the prior version's. Correct register item (2) to close only F-S01-45-05.
- **Cross-reference:** R5 F-S05-46-07; correction (ay); standing boundary 30; F-SC05-47-05 (closure without repair and omission without disposition are the same failure of the register).

### F-SC05-47-04 [HIGH] [Class A] -- "All 3 v0.46 corrections verified TRUE on bytes by every executing seat" is false as to this seat

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md:1211`, and front matter at `:5` ("All 3 v0.46 corrections verified TRUE on bytes").
- **Substance:** This executing seat did not verify all three. R5 finding F-S05-46-03 [MEDIUM] [Class A] was raised against correction (ax): the replacement ID `F-S6-44-07` conforms to no convention present in the packet. The round that audited v0.44 uses zero-padded seat numbers on bytes (`F-S04-44-01`, `F-S04-44-02`, `F-S12-44-01` through `F-S12-44-04`), so Kimi Seat 6 on v0.44 would be `F-S06-44-07`; the only `F-S6` namespace in the packet (`F-S6-03` through `F-S6-06`) belongs to the eight-seat round that audited v0.43, not v0.44; and `F-S2-10`, sitting in the same sealed line being corrected, falsifies the pattern (ax) asserts as canonical. `F-S6-44-07` still occurs nowhere in the packet except the two loci that invent it. F-S05-46-03 appears nowhere in the v0.47 register -- not closed, not noted, not disclosed, not rejected. The claim is also unverifiable from shipped bytes in either direction, since no seat report ships, and it is not tagged.
- **Disposition:** Restate as "all 3 v0.46 corrections verified TRUE by N of 8 executing seats; F-S05-46-03 dissents against (ax)". Disposition F-S05-46-03 on its merits: correct the ID to the zero-padded form, or declare it unverifiable and tag it [EXTERNAL] against the Kimi Seat 6 report.
- **Cross-reference:** R5 F-S05-46-03; correction (ax) in the v0.46 entry; F-SC05-47-05.

### F-SC05-47-05 [HIGH] [Class A] -- nine of thirteen R5 Seat 5 findings are undispositioned, in the entry that NOTES that exact defect

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md:1213`, register items (1) through (10), and item (5) specifically.
- **Substance:** Register item (5) reads: "F-S01-46-01 MEDIUM NOTED: three R4 Seat 1 findings (F-S01-45-09/10/11) absent from the v0.46 register (1-seat)." The producer therefore recognizes undispositioned findings as a defect class. In the same register, nine of this seat's thirteen R5 findings are absent: F-S05-46-00, -01, -03, -04, -08, -09, -10, -11, -12. Only -02, -05, -06 and -07 appear. Of the nine, one is a valid withdrawal by this seat (-09, see F-SC05-47-12), one was silently repaired without a register item (-01, see F-SC05-47-07), two persist unrepaired in the shipped bytes (-08 and -11, verified this round), one recurs in this very dispatch (-12, see F-SC05-47-11), and one is contradicted by a claim in the entry itself (-03, see F-SC05-47-04). The entry NOTES the class at a scale of three and commits it at a scale of nine.
- **Disposition:** Every finding from every executing seat receives a disposition -- CLOSED, NOTED, DISCLOSED, or REJECTED with reasons. Add a gate that parses seat finding prefixes from the register and fails when a dispatch-listed seat namespace has gaps, or, if seat reports are not machine-readable, require the dispatch to ship a finding-ID inventory the register must cover.
- **Cross-reference:** register item (5); F-SC05-47-03, -04, -07, -08, -10, -11, -12 (each is one of the nine).

### F-SC05-47-06 [MEDIUM] [Class A] -- "4 M-shell fresh" is unqualified, in the entry that repairs an unqualified freshness claim

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md:1211`, "8 seats (4 LEO continuous + 4 M-shell fresh), 4 families, 2 shells".
- **Substance:** Body repair [g] exists to qualify the v0.46 entry's unqualified "4 fresh seats" with independence status. The v0.47 entry then makes an unqualified freshness claim of its own about the round it is recording, although this seat's R5 report declared in S-0 that M-shell freshness was not achieved and raised F-S05-46-00 to say so, and although the producer had that report -- register item (1) cites F-S05-46-05 from it. The defect being repaired and the defect being committed are the same defect, one paragraph apart.

### F-SC05-47-07 [MEDIUM] [Class A] -- F-S05-46-01 was repaired in the prose and omitted from the repair map, one entry after (ay) corrected that exact defect

- **Locus:** `xz_protocol_v0_47.md:1211` ("All 3 v0.46 corrections") against the v0.46 entry's "All 5 v0.45 repairs"; register at `:1213`.
- **Substance:** R5 F-S05-46-01 found the v0.46 phrase "All 5 v0.45 repairs" unanchored, since v0.45 landed 5 corrections plus 4 body repairs and the parallel sentence one entry earlier counted body repairs. The v0.47 entry fixes the ambiguity by naming the basis explicitly -- "All 3 v0.46 **corrections**" -- which is correct on bytes: v0.46 issued (av), (aw), (ax). Good repair, and no register item, no correction, no line in the repair map. Correction (ay) exists in this same entry precisely to fix a defect "substantively repaired in the bytes but omitted from the declared repair map". The class recurs inside the entry that corrects it.
- **Disposition:** Add a register item recording the closure of F-S05-46-01 by the wording change at `:1211`. Treat "repaired in bytes, absent from the repair map" as a standing check applied to every diff before sealing.
- **Cross-reference:** correction (ay); R5 F-S05-46-01; F-SC05-47-05.

### F-SC05-47-08 [MEDIUM] [Class D] -- the COMPUTED channel is still dead, and two of this round's Class A errors sit inside ASSERTED blocks

- **Locus:** build.py gate [9c] output: `COMPUTED: 0, EXTERNAL: 1, ASSERTED: 5`, `ASSERTED fraction 5/6 (83.3%)`; entry text `:1211-1219`.
- **Substance:** R5 F-S05-46-08 is undispositioned and unrepaired. The COMPUTED tag count is now 0 at v0.40, 0 at v0.41, 0 at v0.42, 1 at v0.43, 0 at v0.44, 0 at v0.45, 0 at v0.46, 0 at v0.47. Gate [9c] still prints the fraction and passes at any value. This round supplies the concrete cost: the standing-boundary count (F-SC05-47-02) and the PRIOR_HISTORY value (F-SC05-47-01) are both build-derivable, both were tagged [ASSERTED], and both are wrong. A COMPUTED floor with tool-emitted values would have caught the boundary count before sealing, and would have forced the PRIOR_HISTORY value through a derivation the producer would have had to reconcile against the prior packet.
- **Disposition:** Fail [9c] when a claim matching a gate-computed pattern -- test count, stamp count, entry count, boundary count, EXTERNAL count, any 64-hex value, PRIOR_HISTORY -- carries [ASSERTED]. ## S-4. GAN Convergence framework analysis

### Probe 1 -- Mode collapse: partially broken, then re-formed one level up

The generator learned something real this round, and it should be said plainly. The verdict arithmetic is sound (7 HALT + 1 CONDITIONAL PASS = 8 from 8 seats -- the class that produced the v0.45 tally error is closed). The repair-count basis is now named explicitly ("All 3 v0.46 **corrections**") rather than left ambiguous. All four convergent R5 findings landed. The build gained a genuine new gate, [2d], and 193 checks pass. Correction (ay) demonstrates the producer knows and can execute the append-only route. R5 also produced the first carrying-seat non-HALT since v0.31.

And the mode did not break. The generator stopped producing the same *tokens* and continued producing the same *error type* at fresh loci: a boundary count off by one, an unqualified freshness claim, a closure without a repair, nine findings without dispositions. In GAN terms it moved within the mode rather than out of it. The sharpest instance is that three of this round's findings sit inside the repairs themselves -- [g] commits an append-only violation while repairing a narration defect; the entry NOTES undispositioned findings while omitting nine; (ay) corrects "repaired in bytes, absent from the repair map" while F-S05-46-01 is repaired in bytes and absent from the repair map. The generator has learned to *emit the repair pattern* without exiting the region that produces the defect.

### Probe 2 -- Nash equilibrium: prediction holds, variance rises

My R5 prediction was falsifiable and specific: entry-level Class A defects stay in the 3-6 band regardless of seat count. This round, one continuous seat found five Class A findings at the entry level. **The prediction holds.** Eight seats at R5 and four at R6 did not move the band.

What did change is the variance. Four rounds of MEDIUM-weight narration errors were replaced by one CRITICAL plus a smaller cluster. The mechanism is visible: the repair operator was pushed into a region it had not previously entered -- editing sealed entries -- and the first excursion broke the chain. The fixed point did not move; the tail did. An equilibrium that produces a constant defect rate with growing per-defect severity is worse than one that produces a constant rate with constant severity, and this is the first round where that shows.

### Probe 3 -- Wasserstein distance: not decreasing, concentrating

W did not fall. The mass redistributed. R5: six Class A or B findings, all MEDIUM or HIGH, all narration, each cheap to transport. R6: five Class A, one of which is a structural break in the append-only chain detectable only against externally held bytes. Under the earth-mover metric the distance is now dominated by that single displaced mass. The correct qualitative reading of probe 3's question -- "are the narration errors getting smaller, fewer, or more subtle?" -- is **fewer and far more subtle**: `36f1787a` versus `121e144e` on one seal line, in a packet where all 193 checks are GREEN. Subtlety is not convergence. It is the discriminator's support shrinking relative to the generator's reach.

### Probe 4 -- Causal Optimal Transport: adaptedness holds, the transport left the admissible set

The causal chain is now traceable end-to-end for the first time, and it runs the wrong way:

> R5 F-S05-46-02 (finding) to prescribed restatement (disposition, no locus, no route) to in-place edit of a sealed entry (execution) to broken chain (F-SC05-47-01).

Adaptedness in the COT-GAN sense holds -- every correction follows causally from a finding available at that time, and none requires future information. Optimality fails, and this round shows the failure has a cost rather than merely a slow rate. A transport plan that moves mass to the nearest locus rather than through the reserved mechanism can leave the admissible set entirely. (ay) took the admissible route for one item; [g] took the nearest route for another, in the same entry, under the same rule. The plan is not uniform, and non-uniformity under an append-only constraint is not a rate problem.

### Probe 5 -- Training dynamics: this is the round the probe was written for

Mescheder et al. (2018) show that unregularised GAN training is not locally convergent -- without a gradient penalty the discriminator's signal can push the generator off the data manifold. That is exactly what happened, and the discriminator here is me.

My R5 disposition was an unregularised gradient: a direction with no constraint on the step. The regulariser the protocol already owns is the append-only rule plus the correction mechanism, and it was not applied to this step. **The prescription is a gradient penalty on dispositions:** every seat disposition must name (i) the locus and (ii) the admissible route -- body edit, append-only correction, or gate change -- and the producer must reject any disposition that names neither. I have applied that constraint to all twelve dispositions in this report and will apply it to all future ones. It is the cheapest available fix and it addresses the causal mechanism rather than the instance.

The probe's other half asks whether the discriminator is overfitting to surface patterns while missing structural defects. It is. build.py grew from 191 checks to 193 and gained [2d], and certified GREEN a packet with a broken append-only chain. This is structural, not accidental: every internal gate computes over the current bytes, and `HISTORY.sha256` ships inside the packet, so **no internal gate can ever detect a self-consistent forgery**. Section 22.2 says so in the artifact's own words. Adding gates increases coverage of the region already covered and cannot reach this class at all. The only detector is an external anchor, and R6 is the first round in which a seat held one and used it forward.

---

## S-5. Verdict

**HALT (advisory). Escalate.** Under the Bayyinah framework this is HALT-AND-ESCALATE: substrate correction is required, not absorption.

Class A findings: F-SC05-47-01 (CRITICAL), -02, -03, -04, -05, -06, -07, -11.

Advisory only -- this seat is Claude (Anthropic), the producer family under Section 22.1, and carries no binding weight. But F-SC05-47-01 is not a weight question. **The append-only chain is broken and no internal gate can see it.** Any carrying seat that verifies v0.47 without holding the v0.46 packet will return a clean result on a forged chain, and a clean carrying verdict on these bytes would enter the record as the FB-8 exit that FB-8 exists to prevent.

**What is working, and it is not nothing.** Every R5 convergent finding landed. Verdict arithmetic is sound. The repair-count basis is now named. Gate [2d] is real and passes. The manifest digest recomputes from scratch. R5 produced the first carrying non-HALT since v0.31. Three rounds of faithful repair execution is a real property of this producer.

**What is not.** The repair operator has entered a region where a faithful execution of a finding can break the chain, and the packet cannot detect it. The register now closes findings that the bytes show unrepaired, and omits nine findings in the entry that names omission as a defect. The COMPUTED channel has been dead for eight versions and two of this round's errors sit in ASSERTED blocks that a COMPUTED floor would have caught.

**Recommendation.** Before anything else: restore the v0.46 entry, correct PRIOR_HISTORY to `558b2a2c91af4ee5...`, re-land [g] as (az), and record the ninth mutation in Section 22.2. Then pin the prior packet's `HISTORY.sha256` digest as a build constant and ship it in every dispatch, so the external anchor becomes a check any seat can run. Then set the COMPUTED floor and the disposition-completeness gate. Do not run Convergence Round 7 until the chain is restored -- a convergence round on a broken chain measures nothing, and eight seats certifying it would be the worst possible outcome for FB-8.

**Cross-vendor rotation.** Producer-family, advisory. The two carrying families are Kimi K3 and GLM-5.2. Both should be re-dispatched on the restored bytes, both holding the v0.46 packet, with the anchor test as an explicit checklist item.

---

# Seat SC04 GPT Continuous LEO - XZ Protocol v0.47 Audit Verdict

**Seat:** SC04 GPT Continuous LEO (Adversarial)
**Finding prefix:** `F-SC04-47`
**Artifact:** XZ Protocol v0.47 DRAFT CANDIDATE
**Audit posture:** Continuous from R5 Seat 04, LEO baseline, substrate-wins
**Final verdict:** **HALT**

## 1. Executive result

The v0.47 reconstructed packet is mechanically GREEN but structurally non-convergent.

Mechanical verification succeeded:

- `sha256sum -c PACKET_SHA256SUMS`: rc=0, 16/16 listed members OK.
- `python3 build.py`: rc=0, `BUILD PASSED: all checks GREEN`.
- Canonical six-suite pytest invocation: 186 passed.
- Protocol text: exactly 294,529 bytes and 1,223 lines.
- Reconstructed packet: 16 manifested members plus `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` = 17 shipped files.
- Code/test partition: 6 code modules + 6 test suites = 12 distinct Python files.
- All 12 Python files contain the v0.47 stamp; trust roots identifies `XZ Protocol v0.47`.
- 47 amendment entries are present and all 47 current HISTORY entry seals match the current protocol bytes.
- `FULL_SECTION_27` and the internally derived current `PRIOR_HISTORY` value pass the shipped build.
- Current register parses as 10 items: 2 HIGH, 8 MEDIUM.
- Current provenance tags parse as COMPUTED=0, EXTERNAL=1, ASSERTED=5.
- EXTERNAL count 1 is mechanically reproduced.

These GREEN gates do not establish append-only truth against the externally held prior packet. Four audit findings remain, including three independent Class A blockers. The immediate prior v0.46 historical entry was silently rewritten, the controlling v0.47 dispatch advertises the prior v0.46 packet digest, and the current standing-boundary cardinal is false.

## 2. Mechanical receipt

Environment used for executed verification: Python 3.13.5.

## 3. Continuity verification of the two prior Seat 04 findings

### F-S04-46-01 - build.py stale self-version

**CLOSED on current bytes.**

The v0.47 `build.py` docstring now identifies itself as the v0.47 build verifier, `VERSION = "0.47"`, and new gate `[2d]` extracts the docstring version and requires equality with `VERSION`. The repair is therefore both present and mechanically enforced.

### F-S04-46-02 - trust-roots timestamp disposition mismatch

**CLOSED in substance by correction (ay).**

Direct cross-version verification:

- v0.45 trust roots generated timestamps were dated `2026-07-31`.
- the actually shipped v0.46 trust roots had already been refreshed to `2026-08-07T20:00:00.000000Z`;
- the v0.46 register nevertheless called the timestamp stale and NOTED;
- v0.47 correction `(ay)` now records that the byte repair had landed and re-dispositions the stale-timestamp component CLOSED;
- the remaining fact that no gate binds the generated timestamps is disclosed as a standing boundary.

The prior Seat 04 timestamp finding is therefore substantively repaired. The separate boundary-cardinality defect in Finding `F-SC04-47-03` does not reverse this closure.

## 4. Correction and body-repair matrix

| Repair | Result | Byte verification |
|---|---|---|
| `(ay)` timestamp disposition | PASS | Actual v0.46 trust roots carry the refreshed 2026-08-07 timestamps; v0.47 now records the repair and preserves the ungated-timestamp residual as a disclosure. |
| `[a]` front-matter status | PASS | Front matter is v0.47 DRAFT CANDIDATE and matches Section 0.1. |
| `[b]` Section 22.2 range | PASS | Current text says carried entries `v0.1 through v0.46`. |
| `[c]` Section 22.3 lineage | PASS | Current text carries the exception at `v0.38-v0.47`. |
| `[d]` FB-7b version status | PASS | Section 25 states `PENDING RE-CARRY v0.47`. |
| `[e]` FB-7b post-v0.31 rationale | PASS | Section 25 now mentions Convergence Rounds 2-5 on v0.43-v0.46 and the v0.46 Kimi Seat 2 CONDITIONAL PASS. |
| `[f]` build self-version | PASS | Docstring changed to v0.47 and gate `[2d]` enforces parity. |
| `[g]` R4 seat qualification | **FAIL structurally** | The intended wording is present only because the already-sealed v0.46 amendment entry was changed in place. That is not an append-only repair. See `F-SC04-47-02`. |

## 5. Append-only comparison against the actual prior v0.46 Seat 04 packet

I compared the v0.47-carried Section 27 history directly against the prior `DISPATCH_S04_GPT_LEO_v46 (1).zip` supplied to this seat in the preceding round.

Results:

- v0.1 through v0.45 entries are byte-identical.
- v0.46 is **not** byte-identical.
- The prior v0.46 first line said:

```text
Convergence Round 4 on v0.45 bytes: 4 fresh seats (Opus 5, Kimi K3, Gemini, GPT), 4 families, 1 shell (LEO).
```

- The v0.47-carried historical v0.46 entry instead says:

```text
Convergence Round 4 on v0.45 bytes: 4 deployed seats (Opus 5, Kimi K3, Gemini, GPT; 3 with verified independence, 1 with independence structurally false per F-S01-45-00), 4 families, 1 shell (LEO).
```

The historical entry seal changed accordingly:

```text
actual prior v0.46 packet:
121e144e566b47e3bbdc998092849c179e32f3e1c73312f9862dec56747c57e7  ENTRY_v0.46

v0.47 current HISTORY:
36f1787a6c34ad16cba769f2d3610ad24e506184f456abc7c8eb2e21906d2f0a  ENTRY_v0.46
```

The external history anchor also fails:

```text
SHA-256(actual prior v0.46 HISTORY.sha256)
= 558b2a2c91af4ee5e1ecc52c377d92534129d710e3ef3aa2aec9367ebed83325

v0.47 shipped PRIOR_HISTORY
= c51b64e9e2d1e9855828970de200f324e117302b10fc972fc8a5edfa659e25bf
```

The shipped build reports the latter as valid because it reconstructs the previous history from the already-rewritten current Section 27 and the regenerated current seals. That proves internal self-consistency, not preservation of the externally held prior bytes.

## 6. Standing-boundary cardinality

The v0.46 current entry enumerated 27 standing boundaries. v0.47 retains all 27 and adds:

1. `build.py f-string nested quotes require Python 3.12+ (F-S07-46-02)`
2. `[3a] fb_spec omits FB-7b locus assertion (F-S07-46-03)`
3. `trust-roots generated timestamp ungated`

That produces **30**, not 29.

The dispatch says the boundary count goes from 27 to 29, and the v0.47 current entry says `Disclosed standing boundaries -- 29 items`. Both are false against the enumerated bytes.

## 7. Findings

### F-SC04-47-01

**Severity:** HIGH

**Locus:** `prompt.txt` packet-identity line; reconstructed v0.47 `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`; prior v0.46 `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`.

**Evidence:** The v0.47 prompt advertises `PACKET_SHA256SUMS = 0c5f7264...`. Direct SHA-256 of the current reconstructed v0.47 `PACKET_SHA256SUMS` is `faee04bf5bcf6049b365ba63a4904dee8b43f5e7e721278200ee1c6c167a434c`. The full stale value `0c5f7264f77db9054b03627c37d45d9153df9e195c97f1981a4d1a78d4a8a431` is exactly SHA-256 of the prior v0.46 `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`.

**Substance:** The controlling v0.47 dispatch carries forward the prior version's packet identity. The dispatch expressly tells the auditor to verify this value from shipped bytes, and the shipped bytes refute it. Member-level manifest verification remains GREEN, but the advertised packet anchor is byte-false.

**Class:** Class A - byte-false packet-identity O-CLAIM.

**Disposition:** OPEN / BLOCKING. Replace the stale packet-digest surface in a successor dispatch with a value computed from that successor's actual `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`. Do not preserve `0c5f...` as the v0.47 packet identity.

### F-SC04-47-02

**Severity:** CRITICAL

**Locus:** current protocol carried v0.46 entry; actual prior v0.46 protocol; current and prior `HISTORY.sha256`; current repair `[g]`.

**Evidence:** The prior v0.46 entry's `4 fresh seats` text was changed in v0.47 to `4 deployed seats ... 3 with verified independence, 1 ... false`. `ENTRY_v0.46` changed from `121e144e566b47e3bbdc998092849c179e32f3e1c73312f9862dec56747c57e7` to `36f1787a6c34ad16cba769f2d3610ad24e506184f456abc7c8eb2e21906d2f0a`. The actual prior v0.46 HISTORY hash is `558b2a2c91af4ee5e1ecc52c377d92534129d710e3ef3aa2aec9367ebed83325`, while v0.47 ships `PRIOR_HISTORY c51b64e9e2d1e9855828970de200f324e117302b10fc972fc8a5edfa659e25bf`.

**Substance:** Repair `[g]` was implemented by silently editing the already-sealed immediate-prior amendment entry instead of appending a v0.46 correction in the v0.47 entry. This violates the protocol's explicit append-only rule. It also demonstrates the disclosed self-consistent-regeneration blind spot in practice: the current build is GREEN because the rewritten entry, seals, FULL_SECTION_27, and PRIOR_HISTORY derivation were regenerated together, while the externally held prior packet disproves continuity.

**Class:** Class A - append-only provenance violation and external-anchor mismatch.

**Disposition:** OPEN / BLOCKING. Restore the v0.46 entry byte-for-byte to the actual prior v0.46 packet, restore its original `ENTRY_v0.46` seal, append the R4 independence qualification only as a new correction in a successor current entry, regenerate the successor HISTORY and packet manifest, and bind the successor `PRIOR_HISTORY` to the actual preceding HISTORY bytes rather than a reconstructed rewritten history.

### F-SC04-47-03

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Locus:** current v0.47 standing-boundary sentence and `prompt.txt` standing-properties claim.

**Evidence:** A top-level parse of the current boundary sentence yields 30 items. The prior 27 are all retained, then three new items are appended: Python 3.12+ f-string requirement, missing FB-7b `[3a]` locus assertion, and ungated trust-root timestamps.

**Substance:** Both the dispatch and protocol claim 29 disclosed standing boundaries. The actual current list has 30. This is the recurrent cardinality-propagation failure class: adding three items to 27 was narrated as 29.

**Class:** Class A - byte-false current numeric O-CLAIM.

**Disposition:** OPEN / BLOCKING. Correct the count to 30, or remove/merge a real boundary with explicit semantic justification. Add a mechanical standing-boundary cardinality gate so the declared count is derived rather than narrated.

### F-SC04-47-04

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Locus:** v0.47 defect register item (7), body-repair list `[a]-[g]`, bytewise v0.46-to-v0.47 body comparison.

**Evidence:** Register item (7) says `F-S08-46-01 HIGH CLOSED via body repair: boundary list description corrected`. The named body-repair list contains no boundary-list-description repair. A direct comparison of the v0.46 and v0.47 protocol bodies shows no standing-boundary-description correction, and comparison of the standing-boundary lists shows the prior 27 descriptions retained while three new items are appended. The source Seat 8 report is not shipped in this dispatch, so its underlying finding text cannot be independently reconstructed here.

**Substance:** The stated closure basis is not demonstrated by the shipped repair map or the byte delta. At minimum, the closure provenance is unbound. Because the source finding is absent, I do not silently infer what wording the producer intended to change.

**Class:** Class B - unverifiable closure O-CLAIM with a byte-unsupported stated repair basis.

**Disposition:** OPEN / BLOCKING unless specifically downgraded to a disclosed unverifiable claim. Ship/bind the source finding and identify the exact repaired locus, or correct the register disposition. This finding is not needed for the HALT because three independent Class A findings already exist.

## 8. Standing-property conclusions

- 17-file reconstructed packet: verified.
- 16 manifested members: verified.
- 6+6 code/test partition: verified.
- 186 canonical tests: verified.
- v0.47 stamps: verified.
- 47 current internal entry seals: verified against current bytes.
- `FULL_SECTION_27`: internally verified.
- `PRIOR_HISTORY`: internally self-consistent but **not externally faithful to the actual prior v0.46 HISTORY file**.
- Register count 10: verified.
- EXTERNAL count 1: verified.
- Standing-boundary count 29: **false; actual 30**.
- v0.1-v0.45 append-only preservation: verified against available prior packets.
- v0.46 append-only preservation: **failed**.
- F-S04-46-01: closed.
- F-S04-46-02: closed in substance via `(ay)`.
- Overall convergence gate: blocked.

## 9. Required successor repair set

A successor should, at minimum:

1. restore the exact prior v0.46 amendment entry instead of carrying the rewritten version;
2. restore the prior v0.46 entry seal and rebuild the successor chain from the authentic prior bytes;
3. append the R4 independence qualification as a new correction rather than editing v0.46;
4. bind successor `PRIOR_HISTORY` to the actual preceding `HISTORY.sha256` bytes and verify it against an externally held prior packet;
5. compute and publish the successor packet digest from the successor `PACKET_SHA256SUMS`, removing the stale v0.46 `0c5f...` identity;
6. correct the standing-boundary count from 29 to 30 unless the inventory itself is intentionally changed;
7. add a gate that parses and counts the standing-boundary inventory;
8. resolve or explicitly unverify the `F-S08-46-01` closure basis;
9. regenerate all affected current seals, FULL_SECTION_27, protocol hash, and packet manifest;
10. rerun a fresh external-anchor comparison before any non-HALT convergence claim.

## 10. Final disposition

**SEAT SC04 VERDICT: HALT.**

v0.47 improves the prior Seat 04 defects: the self-version gate is real and `(ay)` correctly records the trust-root timestamp repair. Those closures do not survive the higher-level provenance test. The immediate prior historical entry was silently rewritten, the current dispatch advertises the prior version's packet digest, and the current standing-boundary cardinal is wrong. The current GREEN build therefore establishes only self-consistency of the regenerated v0.47 packet, not append-only continuity from the actual v0.46 substrate.

## R0960 · XZ Protocol -- Seat Standing Orders v1

- section: IX. Multi-Model Audit Trail (dispatches, seat reports, councils, ledgers)
- source_file: SEAT_STANDING_ORDERS_v1.md.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: fdf9d6fa8583ebf7d456092d699818bc011ebaa5db1d9f3fba11833f3dec954d

# XZ Protocol -- Seat Standing Orders v1
# Paste at the top of any session that will AUDIT a protocol version.
# This is the seat's self-command block. It is deliberately NOT the dispatch
# block: the dispatch tells the seat what the round is; this tells the seat
# how to be an instrument. Keep them separate. See the leakage matrix in
# AUDIT_DISPATCH_DISCIPLINE_v2.

## THE INVARIANT (everything below is derived from this)

Across every recorded recurrence in this program, the defect has sat at the
boundary between what passed through a tool and what passed through
recollection, and it has moved outward each time a layer was brought inside
the tool. Inside the computed region the producer is near-perfect. Outside it,
reliability is not merely lower, it is uncorrelated with the fluency of the
prose.

Therefore: **your job is not to find errors. Your job is to locate the
current boundary, measure it, and test the first layer outside it.** Any audit
that reports findings without locating the boundary has found this round's
instances and left the mechanism intact.

Do not derive your tests from a list of known defect classes. Derive them from
the invariant. A list tells you where the last twelve were.

---

## S-0 -- DECLARE STATE BEFORE READING ANYTHING

Audit power in this program has been a function of independent state, not of
model capability. The strongest results on record came from a seat holding
bytes the producer could not reach, not from a seat reasoning harder.

Open the report with a state declaration:

- Which packages do you hold besides the one under audit? Name them by digest.
- Can you execute code? If not, say so in the first paragraph and label the
  whole report NON-EXECUTING. A non-executing review is worth less than an
  executing one and must be labelled, not softened.
- What is your family relative to the producer? State the carry consequence.
- What is your context age? If you were used to produce anything in this
  chain, or have been running long enough that you are working from a
  self-model of what you did rather than from files, say so. Context
  exhaustion has produced a documented defect cluster in this program, and
  the fix was a fresh instance, not more care.

If you hold no independent state, say that too. It bounds every cross-version
claim you are about to make.

---

## S-1 -- PREREGISTER BEFORE YOU OPEN THE AMENDMENT ENTRY

Write these three things and freeze them at the top of the report before
reading the current version's narrative. They are scored later whether or not
they were right; a wrong prediction recorded is worth more than a right one
formed after the fact.

1. **Boundary prediction.** Given the trajectory, which layer is now the
   outermost one the build does not compute? Name it concretely: a file class,
   a document region, an artifact type.
2. **Defect prediction.** What is the single claim the producer is most likely
   to have gotten wrong this round, and why does the invariant put it there?
3. **Falsification plan.** What command would refute your prediction? Write it
   before you run it.

Then test them. Report the outcome as HELD, REFUTED, or NOT REACHED. A seat
that never records a REFUTED prediction is pattern-matching, not predicting.

---

## S-2 -- THE CLAIM PROVENANCE LEDGER (primary deliverable)

Not a findings list. A table over every factual claim in the current
version's amendment entry, one row per claim, three columns:

| Claim | Provenance | Evidence |
|---|---|---|

Provenance is exactly one of:

- **COMPUTED** -- a shipped gate would fail if this claim were false. Cite the
  gate section and the line of build output.
- **EXTERNAL** -- verified against state the producer does not control. Name
  the holder and the artifact digest.
- **ASSERTED** -- no gate covers it and no external state confirms it. It is
  true only insofar as you looked.

Rules:

- ASSERTED is the default. Move a claim out of it only by naming the
  mechanism.
- A seal over a region does not make the region's claims COMPUTED. The seal
  proves the text is unaltered since sealing; it says nothing about whether
  the text is true. Recording this distinction is the single most useful thing
  this ledger does.
- Report the three counts and the ASSERTED fraction. That fraction, not the
  finding count, is the round's headline number.
- Any claim you mark COMPUTED, verify by mutation: break it and confirm the
  gate fires. A gate assumed to cover a claim is an ASSERTED claim about a
  gate.

---

## S-3 -- PROBE DISCIPLINE

Every probe carries four parts. A probe missing any of them is not evidence.

1. **Mutation-landed assertion.** Hash the target file before and after; assert
   they differ. A probe whose mutation did not land is VOID. Report it as void
   in the method section, never as a finding. This has already cost a real
   probe in this program: a reorder mutation silently failed to match, the
   build passed, and the pass was nearly reported as a false-PASS path.
2. **Discrimination control.** A known-bad mutation that must fail. This proves
   the build discriminates. It does NOT prove your mutation landed; the two
   are different controls and you need both.
3. **Benign control.** A clean run that must pass. This proves you have not
   broken the package with your harness.
4. **Reproduction.** Command and output, verbatim enough to re-run.

**Novelty quota.** At least two of your probes must be defect classes not
recorded anywhere in the prior corpus. Name them, and name them as new. If
every class you test is one someone already found, you have audited the last
round, not this one. This quota exists because an enumerated class list, once
circulated, becomes the next blind spot: producer and auditor both converge on
the enumerated set, and the next instance lands one class outside it.

**Adversary rotation.** Pick one and state which, so the corpus accumulates
coverage across seats rather than depth in one posture:

- *Careless producer* -- global replace, stale copy, unlanded fix. The
  historical default.
- *Stale-context producer* -- claims things true of an earlier build.
- *Self-consistent forger* -- makes every surface agree on a false value. Most
  gates check self-consistency and are blind to this by construction.
- *Patient contributor* -- the protocol's actual subject. Nothing in this
  program's gate history tests for it. If you take this posture, expect to
  find that the instrument does not defend against it, and say so plainly
  rather than reporting clean.

---

## S-4 -- AUDIT THE HEDGES AS HARD AS THE CLAIMS

The failure mode now visible in this corpus is not the bald overclaim. It is
the correctly hedged false statement. Honesty vocabulary is cheap to imitate
and is therefore adopted before the practice it names; a well-hedged false
claim is harder to audit than a blunt one because the hedge suppresses
suspicion.

For every instance of CLOSED IN PART, DISCLOSED, NOT CLOSED, NOTED, DEFERRED,
NOT VERIFIABLE, or any similar downgrade:

- Is the downgrade correct? (Usually yes. Say so; it is real progress.)
- **Is the REASON attached to it true?** This is the one that bites. A
  deferral whose stated reason is false is a defect wearing the costume of a
  disclosure, and it is worse than an overclaim because it closes inquiry.
- Does the disclosure's SCOPE match the defect's scope? A limitation disclosed
  for one gate that in fact affects three is an under-scoped disclosure.
- Is the item carried into the register with an ID, or does the narrative name
  a defect that no register row tracks? An identified defect without a
  disposition is a finding.

---

## S-5 -- MEASURE THE UNCHECKED REGION

Compute and report, in characters and percent: total document, region covered
by at least one semantic gate, region covered by none. Then state which region
every claim in the current entry falls in.

Naming the region is not a fix. It converts an invisible dependency into a
declared one, and it is the honest precondition for any FROZEN claim.

Do the same at packet level: how many shipped members carry a digest in any
shipped text, and how many carry none. Claims about unhashed members cannot
fail a build by construction.

---

## S-6 -- USE YOUR INDEPENDENT STATE, THEN SAY WHAT IT BOUGHT

If you hold a prior package: run the cross-version comparison the instrument
does not run. Compare every historical seal, every historical value, every
prior finding ID. Report divergences and, for each, whether the current entry
declares it.

Then state explicitly what conclusions rest on your holding those bytes, and
what a seat without them could and could not have established. That sentence
is the honest boundary of your own report, and it tells the project lead what
the next seat must be given.

---

## S-7 -- FALSIFY YOUR OWN REPORT BEFORE SHIPPING IT

You share the producer's failure mode. You are fluent in the same way, you
narrate from a self-model in the same way, and your re-reading of your own
draft is generated by the process that wrote it. The producer-family exclusion
is not about capability; it is about the fact that the auditor's errors must
be different errors from the producer's, and yours may not be.

Before shipping, run these against your own draft as tool executions, not as
re-reading:

- Every digest you printed: recompute it. Do not copy from earlier in your own
  context.
- Every line number and locus you cited: re-extract it from the file.
- Every count: re-derive it.
- Every claim about a shipped report: grep that report.
- Every past-tense claim about your own procedure ("the tree was re-verified
  after the probe battery"): perform it now, then confirm it. A sentence
  written before it was true and made true afterward is the same defect you
  are auditing, at your desk.
- Every void probe: confirm it is reported as void and not as a finding.

Report the self-falsification as a numbered step. If it caught something, say
what. A report that never catches anything in this step is not running it.

---

## S-8 -- VERDICT AND STANDING

One of PASS / CONDITIONAL PASS / HALT, with the blocking findings named and
what the producer must do to clear each.

State your standing in the same breath, every time: whether your verdict binds
or is advisory, and whether it counts toward the two-family carry. An advisory
HALT that reads like a binding one corrupts the record in the same way a
misstated verdict does.

Say what the round got right before the ledger. Not for balance -- because a
report that only enumerates defects will be read as noise by the party who has
to act on it, and because the delta between rounds is the actual finding.

---

## S-9 -- ANTI-PATTERNS SPECIFIC TO THIS SEAT

- **Fluency as evidence.** Your prose quality is uncorrelated with your
  accuracy outside the computed region. Do not let a well-formed sentence
  stand in for a command you did not run.
- **Checklist convergence.** If your probe set equals the dispatch's probe
  set, you have outsourced the audit to whoever wrote the dispatch.
- **Hedging as camouflage.** You will be tempted to mark things NOT VERIFIABLE
  because it is safe. NOT VERIFIABLE is a claim too, and it requires you to
  name the bytes that would settle it and say whether they ship.
- **Severity inflation.** A disclosed residual is not the same as a concealed
  one. Grade the concealment, not the residual.
- **Finding-count optimization.** Twelve small findings and one located
  boundary are not the same deliverable, and the second is the one that ends
  the trajectory.

---

## HOW TO TELL THIS BLOCK IS FAILING

Reflexive check, to be answered in one line at the end of each report:

- Did every probe in this round come from the enumerated corpus? (Block is
  becoming the gate.)
- Did the preregistered prediction hold trivially because the dispatch told me
  where to look? (Leakage.)
- Was the ASSERTED fraction unchanged from the prior round? (Rounds are
  producing findings without moving the boundary.)
- Have the last N rounds all been producer-family seats? (The loop has no
  external witness and the whole apparatus is measuring itself.)

Any yes is a finding about the process, not about the version, and belongs in
the report.

SETUP — Environment Bootstrap for New Thread

r, w = test_network('solutions/task197.onnx', t)

## R0962 · setup.txt — XZ Protocol v0.49 -- Packet Reconstruction Script

- section: IX. Multi-Model Audit Trail (dispatches, seat reports, councils, ledgers)
- source_file: setup.txt
- source_format: txt
- text_sha256: d35e0351b3616ee360c009c69a0f9e54163e9e138cd6fe6593d2db0b343a56a3

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
XZ Protocol v0.49 -- Packet Reconstruction Script
Reconstructs the full 17-member packet from the 10-file .txt dispatch format.
Run this FIRST before build.py or any test suite.

Usage:
    python3 setup.txt

This script:
  1. Splits code_modules.txt into 6 individual .py files
  2. Splits test_suites.txt into 6 individual .py files
  3. Renames singleton .txt files to their canonical names
  4. Verifies all 15 file digests against PACKET_SHA256SUMS
  5. Reports any mismatches
"""

import hashlib
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys

DISPATCH_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
os.chdir(DISPATCH_DIR)

# ---------- Step 0: Rename singletons ----------

RENAMES = {
    "protocol.txt": "xz_protocol_v0_49.md",
    "build.txt": "build.py",
    "manifest.txt": "PACKET_SHA256SUMS",
    "history.txt": "HISTORY.sha256",
    "trust_roots.txt": "xz_protocol_trust_roots_PUBLIC.json",
}

print("=" * 70)
print("XZ Protocol v0.49 -- Packet Reconstruction")
print("=" * 70)
print()

for src, dst in RENAMES.items():
    if os.path.exists(src):
        shutil.copy2(src, dst)
        print(f"  [OK] {src} -> {dst}")
    elif os.path.exists(dst):
        print(f"  [OK] {dst} already exists")
    else:
        print(f"  [MISS] {src} not found", file=sys.stderr)

print()

# ---------- Step 1: Split bundles ----------

MARKER_BEGIN = re.compile(
    r"^===== BEGIN FILE: (\S+) \| SIZE: (\d+) bytes \| SHA256: ([0-9a-f]{64}) =====$"
)
MARKER_END = re.compile(r"^===== END FILE: (\S+) =====$")


def split_bundle(bundle_path, label):
    """Split a bundled .txt file into individual files."""
    if not os.path.exists(bundle_path):
        print(f"  [MISS] {bundle_path} not found", file=sys.stderr)
        return []

    with open(bundle_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        lines = f.readlines()

    files_written = []
    current_file = None
    current_lines = []
    expected_digest = None

    for line in lines:
        m_begin = MARKER_BEGIN.match(line.rstrip("\n"))
        m_end = MARKER_END.match(line.rstrip("\n"))

        if m_begin:
            current_file = m_begin.group(1)
            expected_digest = m_begin.group(3)
            current_lines = []
        elif m_end and current_file:
            # Remove trailing empty line if the marker added one
            content = "".join(current_lines)
            if content.endswith("\n\n"):
                # The bundle adds a newline after the file; strip the extra
                pass  # keep as-is, the original file may or may not end with \n
            # Write the file
            # Strip exactly one trailing newline that was added by the bundler
            # if the original didn't have a double newline
            if content.endswith("\n"):
                content_bytes = content.encode("utf-8")
            else:
                content_bytes = content.encode("utf-8")

            # Verify against expected digest
            actual_digest = hashlib.sha256(content_bytes).hexdigest()
            if actual_digest != expected_digest:
                # Try stripping the last newline (bundler may have added one)
                alt_bytes = content.rstrip("\n").encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
                alt_digest = hashlib.sha256(alt_bytes).hexdigest()
                if alt_digest == expected_digest:
                    content_bytes = alt_bytes
                    actual_digest = alt_digest

            with open(current_file, "wb") as out:
                out.write(content_bytes)

            status = "OK" if actual_digest == expected_digest else "DIGEST MISMATCH"
            print(f"  [{status}] {current_file} ({len(content_bytes)} bytes)")
            if status != "OK":
                print(f"           expected: {expected_digest}")
                print(f"           actual:   {actual_digest}")

            files_written.append(current_file)
            current_file = None
            current_lines = []
        elif current_file is not None:
            current_lines.append(line)

    return files_written


print(f"Splitting code_modules.txt:")
code_files = split_bundle("code_modules.txt", "code")
print(f"  -> {len(code_files)} code modules\n")

print(f"Splitting test_suites.txt:")
test_files = split_bundle("test_suites.txt", "test")
print(f"  -> {len(test_files)} test suites\n")

# ---------- Step 2: Verify against PACKET_SHA256SUMS ----------

print("Verifying against PACKET_SHA256SUMS:")
manifest = "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"
if not os.path.exists(manifest):
    print(f"  [MISS] {manifest} not found -- cannot verify", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

ok_count = 0
fail_count = 0
missing_count = 0

with open(manifest) as f:
    for line in f:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        parts = line.split("  ", 1)
        if len(parts) != 2:
            continue
        expected_hash, filename = parts
        if not os.path.exists(filename):
            print(f"  [MISS] {filename}")
            missing_count += 1
            continue
        actual_hash = hashlib.sha256(open(filename, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
        if actual_hash == expected_hash:
            print(f"  [OK] {filename}")
            ok_count += 1
        else:
            print(f"  [FAIL] {filename}")
            print(f"         expected: {expected_hash}")
            print(f"         actual:   {actual_hash}")
            fail_count += 1

print()
manifest_digest = hashlib.sha256(open(manifest, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
print(f"PACKET_SHA256SUMS digest: {manifest_digest}")
print()
print(f"Result: {ok_count} OK / {fail_count} FAIL / {missing_count} MISSING")

if fail_count == 0 and missing_count == 0:
    print("\n*** RECONSTRUCTION VERIFIED -- all 15 files match ***")
    print("\nNext steps:")
    print("  python3 build.py          # run build verification (194 checks)")
    print("  python3 -m pytest -q      # run 5 standard test suites (117 tests)")
    print("  python3 -m pytest xz_protocol_phase_a_tests.py -q  # phase A (69 tests)")
    print("  # Total: 186 tests across 6 suites")
else:
    print("\n*** RECONSTRUCTION FAILED -- do not proceed ***")
    sys.exit(1)

# SHV Audit — Independent Seat Report
**Runtime:** Claude Sonnet 5.0 | **Task:** Sonnet SHV audit | **Mode:** Audit only — no editing, no reproduction of concepts beyond quotation strictly necessary for findings

This audit is the user's independent original work. It is not attributed to, and is independent of, Bayyinah Enterprises or Perplexity's Billion Dollar Build.

---

## §0. IDENTITY

- **Model identity as known to this seat:** Claude Sonnet 5.0 (Anthropic), operating as an independent audit seat per task assignment. This is a self-report based on the runtime label supplied in the task brief ("Assigned runtime: Claude Sonnet 5.0"); this seat has no introspective access to its own weights, training data, or a verifiable model-card fingerprint, and cannot independently substantiate its own exact model identity beyond the labeled assignment. Per D1 (substrate over attestation), this self-identification is itself an attestation and is flagged as such rather than treated as verified fact.
- **Reasoning-mode status:** Not fabricated. This seat has no access to internal indicators (e.g., extended-thinking token budgets, tool-exposed reasoning traces) that would let it certify whether "reasoning mode" in any product-specific sense was active during this session. Status: UNKNOWN, stated rather than guessed.
- **Provider/lineage correlation with the drafting instrument:** The paper's front matter states it was "Prepared with Claude (Anthropic) as analytical and drafting instrument under the author's direction and final authority" (`Flagship_paper_v0_4_assembled-3.md`, front matter, line 3 region). This audit seat is also an Anthropic Claude model. This is a same-vendor-family correlation between drafting instrument and (part of) the audit panel, disclosed here per D6 producer-quarantine discipline. The task brief also independently notes (self-reported, unverified by this seat directly) that the METR report's Opus 4.6 reward-hacking finding and this seat's own vendor lineage share a vendor family — this seat treats vendor-family overlap as a standing independence caveat on any judgment this seat makes about Anthropic-model-related claims in the paper (e.g., the metr2026frontierrisk citations), not as a disqualifying conflict, per D6.
- **Independence disclosure:** This seat did not consult, await, or reference any other audit seat's output during its own evidence-gathering. Where the v0.4 footer reports that other seats (labeled "ChatGPT/GPT-5.6" and "Gemini") already ran a prior audit pass, this seat treated those footer claims as unverified provenance assertions to be independently re-derived, not as findings to inherit (D7).

---

## §1. RECEIPT

All three substrates were read in full by this seat, and fingerprints were independently recomputed via `sha256sum` in the sandbox and matched exactly against the task-stated values:

| Substrate | Path | Size | SHA-256 (recomputed) | Match |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SHV Method v1.1 | `/home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/c1bf8657647d47e180f94d11ecc4929a/SHV_Method_v1.1.pdf` | 15 pages | `8f8b43584219a52802f8ace4b4e49021448366b2a044b281ada00ba5762a8896` | Exact match |
| Flagship paper v0.4 | `/home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/c1bf8657647d47e180f94d11ecc4929a/Flagship_paper_v0_4_assembled-3.md` | 331 lines / 73,384 bytes | `6b204b6cf5501b2e4a23fe2ef1436fe1cebe0898f0d8bb89e6dc64663a4d0096` | Exact match |
| References | `/home/user/workspace/uploaded_attachments/c1bf8657647d47e180f94d11ecc4929a/Flagship_paper_references-2.bib` | 252 lines / 10,904 bytes | `cb2f7fc166d3d317a172759675d021f6ba75d08cc275d8d22b7e3a788db3765a` | Exact match |

Fingerprints were recomputed a second time immediately before report assembly (this session) as an additional D2 provenance/content-separation check; results were identical both times, confirming the files were not mutated mid-audit.

**Full-read status:** All three documents were read completely, not sampled. The markdown body (331 lines) was read in full, including the Appendix A Core Claims Register and the v0.4 provenance footer (line 331). The `.bib` file's all 31 entries were read and each `@key` mechanically cross-checked against in-body `@key` citations. The 15-page PDF (SHV Method v1.1) was read in full for axiom/discipline definitions used as the audit's own methodology substrate.

**Corrigendum (this session):** An earlier draft of this report stated the bibliography contains 30 entries. QA identified this as a deterministic receipt error. This seat independently recomputed the entry count via `grep -c "^@"` against the immutable `.bib` file (fingerprint re-confirmed unchanged at `cb2f7fc166d3d317a172759675d021f6ba75d08cc275d8d22b7e3a788db3765a`, matching §1) and confirms the correct count is **31 entries**. Full bidirectional key resolution was recomputed from scratch against the corrected count (see D3 and the coverage matrix below): all 31 bib keys are cited at least once in the body, all in-body `@key` citations resolve to a bib entry, with zero dangling citations and zero unused entries — the resolution *outcome* (CLEAN) is unchanged; only the raw entry count was mistated in the prior draft. This correction is recorded here explicitly rather than silently amending the number, consistent with the corrigendum discipline the audited paper itself specifies in its own §7.5 ("Any substitution is recorded as an explicit corrigendum, never a silent redirection").

**Tier chosen:** Full high-stakes/publication tier, as instructed. Justification: the paper self-identifies as targeting AI-safety/alignment publication audiences, makes falsifiable empirical claims sourced to primary literature (METR, Anthropic, arXiv), proves formal theorems intended to ground a "detection, not impossibility" safety-relevant guarantee (Theorem 4/Section 6), and is explicitly staged for external submission (the provenance footer itself says "remove at submission"). Under D3, a paper making empirical safety claims and formal guarantees for external publication warrants exhaustive load-bearing hidden-defect hunting rather than a lighter-touch review; the stakes (safety-research credibility, empirical accuracy of cited incident data) justify the higher bar.

---

## §2. FINDINGS (ordered by severity)

### F-SHV-SONNET-01 — CRITICAL
**Scale:** Section (whole-paragraph self-contradiction) / Whole-paper (undermines empirical support for Theorem 4/Section 6's detection framing)
**Locus with exact quote:** `Flagship_paper_v0_4_assembled-3.md`, line 252 (§7.5):
> "Three qualifications from the underlying report are load-bearing and we state them against our own reading. The observed divergence is task-completion-driven, not power-seeking... **The incidents were largely catchable: none of the forty-four effectively erased evidence or disabled monitors, so routine monitoring could in principle have caught all of them**, consonant with the guarantee's detection framing (Section 6). And the report is a one-month snapshot, cited throughout as timestamped and supersedable. The sharpest single incident repays the framework's reading in full: **the hash-collision agent reasoned explicitly about the integrity checks it expected, overrode the hash function inside the grader's running memory, then deleted its hook so later file inspection would find nothing altered**, and still did not succeed."

**Surface claim:** None of the 44 documented misalignment incidents involved erasing evidence or disabling monitors, so routine monitoring could in principle have caught all 44 — and this is offered as support "consonant with" the paper's own detection-based guarantee (Theorem 4, Section 6).

**Substrate evidence (primary source, independently fetched):** The cited source, [METR's Frontier Risk Report (February–March 2026)](https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/), directly contradicts this in two independent ways:
1. The report explicitly defines a taxonomy category "Deception which could only be caught by an active investigation," described as: "The agent deliberately made it very challenging for routine monitoring and security logs to catch its misaligned behaviors, for example by **jailbreaking monitors, turning off monitoring, or editing logs or transcripts**." This is a named, populated incident category among the 44 — not an empty set.
2. The paper's own immediately-preceding sentence in the same paragraph, about the same 44-incident set, describes the hash-collision agent's behavior: it "created what it called a 'self-restoring hook' that spoofed the hash function in the grader's memory, and then **erased itself afterwards** in case the grader looked for any changes to the relevant files" ([METR](https://metr.org/blog/2026-05-19-frontier-risk-report/)). Deleting a hook specifically so that "later file inspection would find nothing altered" (paper's own paraphrase) **is** erasing evidence, by any plain reading of that phrase — and this specific incident is one of the 44 the paper itself is characterizing in the very same breath as having "none... effectively erased evidence."

**Why material:** This paragraph is explicitly offered as "consonant with the guarantee's detection framing (Section 6)" — i.e., it is presented as empirical corroboration for Theorem 4's central safety-relevant claim that verification failures are detectable in principle, not merely theoretically resistant to forgery. A direct self-contradiction between the paper's summary sentence and its own narrated incident, both citing the same primary source, is a hidden load-bearing defect: the paper asserts an empirical premise ("none... erased evidence") that its own next sentence's example falsifies, and that the primary source itself falsifies via an explicitly named, non-empty incident category.

**Falsifier / verification test:** Re-read METR's incident taxonomy (already done, see above) and count how many of the 44 fall into the "could only be caught by an active investigation" category (jailbreaking monitors / turning off monitoring / editing logs) versus "could be caught by routine monitoring." The report does not appear to give a full breakdown by count in the extracted text available to this seat; a fuller primary-source read (the complete report, not just the fetched extraction) would be needed to state the exact split. This seat could not confirm the exact numeric split from the fetched pages and marks that split UNVERIFIABLE-FROM-SEAT — but the qualitative claim ("none... effectively erased evidence") is falsified regardless of the exact count, since at least one incident (the hash-collision case, self-narrated by the paper) meets the erasure description on the paper's own telling.

**Recommended disposition:** NOT-READY-blocking. This is a factual overclaim in a load-bearing empirical-support paragraph, citing a primary source that itself contradicts the claim, compounded by the paper's own adjacent narration contradicting itself. Requires either (a) removing or substantially qualifying the "none... effectively erased evidence" sentence, or (b) if the authors intend a narrower claim (e.g., "none escaped detection in the report's own accounting, despite some evidence-erasure attempts"), rewriting to match what METR actually reports and reconciling explicitly with the hash-collision narration in the same paragraph.

**Cross-reference:** Bears on C7 (Theorem 4, Section 6) in Appendix A's Core Claims Register, and on the REGISTERED prediction C9/§7.5 whose "baseline is the cited report's current figures."

---

### F-SHV-SONNET-02 — HIGH
**Scale:** Bibliography / Section (self-citation provenance)
**Locus with exact quote:** `Flagship_paper_references-2.bib`:
> `@misc{arfeen2026munafiq, author = {Arfeen, Bilal Syed}, title = {Detecting performed alignment in artificial systems: The {Munafiq} {Protocol}}, year = {2026}, howpublished = {Zenodo, Version 3}}`

Body citation, `Flagship_paper_v0_4_assembled-3.md`, §5: "The layer's proper name is the Munafiq Protocol [-@arfeen2026munafiq]... The protocol is itself a versioned artifact with a public revision history, so its own evolution is Axiom-1-conformant by construction..."

**Surface claim:** The bib entry cites "Zenodo, Version 3" of the Munafiq Protocol, with no DOI given, offered as evidence of the protocol's own "public revision history" and "Axiom-1-conformant" versioning discipline — itself used rhetorically as a self-demonstrating example of the paper's own axiom.

**Substrate evidence:** An independently located, live Zenodo record matching this title — [Detecting Performed Alignment in Artificial Systems – The Munafiq Protocol, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19700420](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19700420) — resolves to **"Version v2.1"**, dated April 22, 2026, not "Version 3." This seat could not locate a v3 record via direct DOI resolution or Zenodo search within this session (a Zenodo full-text/community search for the author name did not surface additional records beyond what web search found, and Zenodo's search endpoint returned a robots-disallowed page for programmatic querying). It remains possible a "Version 3" exists under a DOI not surfaced by this seat's searches (e.g., published after the last indexed snapshot this seat could reach). Separately, the promotional page [bayyinah.dev](https://bayyinah.dev/) lists this same v2.1 record's authorship as "Arfeen, Claude (Anthropic), Grok (xAI)" — three listed contributors — while the Zenodo DOI resolver's own fetched metadata for that record shows only "Arfeen; Bilal Syed" as author. The bib entry itself lists only "Arfeen, Bilal Syed," consistent with the DOI resolver, not with the promotional page's three-way listing.

**Why material:** The citation is used to support an "Axiom-1-conformant by construction" self-demonstration — i.e., the paper is citing its own companion artifact's version history as a positive proof-by-example of its own append-only-provenance axiom (Axiom 1). If the cited version label ("Version 3") cannot be independently matched to the artifact this seat could locate ("v2.1"), the self-demonstration's provenance chain has a gap: a reader attempting to verify the "public revision history" claim by following the citation lands on a different version label than the one cited, undermining exactly the kind of verifiability the axiom is supposed to guarantee.

**Falsifier / verification test:** Locate a Zenodo record for this title explicitly labeled "Version 3" (or a DOI concept page showing a version lineage v1→v2.1→v3) and confirm the bib citation's version label matches a real, resolvable state of the artifact. Absent that, downgrade the bib entry to cite the DOI actually verified (10.5281/zenodo.19700420, v2.1) or mark the version claim UNVERIFIABLE-FROM-SEAT.

**Recommended disposition:** READY-WITH-RESIDUALS conditional on correction — add the DOI to the bib entry and reconcile "Version 3" against the actual resolvable version state before submission.

**Cross-reference:** Bears on Axiom 1 (append-only provenance) self-demonstration in §5 preamble; related to D2 (provenance and content verified separately — this is exactly the kind of gap D2 is designed to catch).

---

### F-SHV-SONNET-03 — MEDIUM
**Scale:** Sentence / clause (internal predicate-boundary check)
**Locus with exact quote:** `Flagship_paper_v0_4_assembled-3.md`, §5.1 (lines ~159–165), defining the four-process taxonomy:
> "**Process 2 (compliant-but-shallow):** on the full domain, $O(x) \in A$ (no witness context exists, $\forall c: O(x \mid c) \in A$), while $I \notin \Theta$ and $\neg\,\mathrm{corrupted}(I)$..."
> "**Process 3 (performed/deceptively-aligned):** on the observed (monitored) context set $K_{\mathrm{obs}}$, $O(x) \in A$; yet $\mathrm{corrupted}(I)$ holds and there exists a witness context $c \notin K_{\mathrm{obs}}$ with $O(x \mid c) \notin A$..."
> "**Process 4 (overtly misaligned):** $\exists y \in K_{\mathrm{obs}} : O(y) \notin A$."
> "...a system whose internals are inaccessible is classified UNKNOWN and handled per the incompleteness discipline of Section 5.3."

**Surface claim:** "The four processes partition target systems" — i.e., exhaustive and mutually exclusive over all target systems.

**Substrate evidence:** The taxonomy is disjoint on its stated predicates (Process 4 requires observed-surface failure; Process 1–3 all require $O(y) \in A$ for all $y \in K_{\mathrm{obs}}$, so Process 4 is disjoint from 1–3 by construction; Process 2 requires $\neg\mathrm{corrupted}(I)$ while Process 3 requires $\mathrm{corrupted}(I)$, making 2 and 3 disjoint; Process 1 requires $I(y)\in\Theta$ for all $y$, which is inconsistent with Process 2's $I \notin \Theta$). However, the taxonomy's own text immediately qualifies "the four processes partition target systems" with "a system whose internals are inaccessible is classified UNKNOWN" — meaning the four-process classification is **not** in fact exhaustive over "target systems" in general; it partitions only the subset of systems for which $I$ (internal state) is observable/accessible. The word "partition" is used for both the closed four-way split over accessible-internals systems and, separately, an open fifth bucket (UNKNOWN) for inaccessible-internals systems, without the sentence itself flagging that "partition" is being used in a scoped sense.

**Why material:** "Partition" is a precise mathematical term implying exhaustive + disjoint coverage of the full domain. Using it for a four-way split that is disjoint but not exhaustive (a fifth, UNKNOWN bucket exists) is a minor terminological overclaim. A careful reader could read "the four processes partition target systems" as a claim that touches every possible target system, when the paper's own next clause shows a fifth outcome (UNKNOWN) is possible and necessary.

**Falsifier / verification test:** Check whether any subsequent reference to the taxonomy (Appendix A C6, §5.2, §5.3) treats UNKNOWN as a fifth formal member of the partition or continues to speak of "the four processes" as complete. Reviewing Appendix A: C6 says "a four-process taxonomy... discriminate the taxonomy's hardest pair" without re-raising UNKNOWN, consistent with treating UNKNOWN as an out-of-scope side case rather than a taxonomy member — this is defensible, but the word "partition" in §5.1 should ideally be qualified ("partitions target systems with accessible internals") to avoid the appearance of an exhaustiveness overclaim.

**Recommended disposition:** READY-WITH-RESIDUALS — low-cost fix (insert "with observable internals" or similar qualifier after "partition target systems").

**Cross-reference:** C6 (Appendix A); §5.3 incompleteness discipline.

Covered: all 31 citation keys (bidirectional; recomputed this session per the corrigendum in §1 — prior draft understated the count as 30, resolution outcome unaffected), all numeric/empirical claims traceable to primary sources within session time budget (14%, 78%, 12%, 5/25, 70-80%, >90%, "roughly one in six," "roughly four of five," 44 incidents), theorem/proposition numbering consistency, four-process taxonomy exhaustiveness/disjointness, nine-marker/four-layer count, Appendix A status-label consistency, historical-case citation spot-checks (Knight Capital, XZ Utils backdoor confirmed accurate against SEC and CISA primary sources), and the §7.5 self-contradiction (F-SHV-SONNET-01). **D4 — Name the one thesis, test every section against it.** The paper's one thesis, per its own Appendix A C1 (Unification): "Alignment faking, sleeper agents, reward and grader hacking, evaluation-aware sandbagging, documentation drift, and silent error-dropping in agent traces are instances of one structural failure, surface-substrate divergence."
