## R0977 · Test 2: Predict F26 from F22-F25 (predictions committed before reveal)

- section: IX. Multi-Model Audit Trail (dispatches, seat reports, councils, ledgers)

# Test 2: Predict F26 from F22-F25 (predictions committed before reveal)

## Input visible to predictor (F22-F25, F25 now in evidence)

| F | step | code | layer | scope | fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F22 | 2-3 dispatch | CASM-V-001 | verifier_dispatch | whitelist_alignment | 21 LOC python |
| F23 | 4 install | CASM-V-021 | ci_install_matrix | extras_gap | 1 LOC yaml |
| F24 | 4 import | CASM-V-021 | sigstore_api_drift | api_path_drift | 3 LOC python |
| F25 | 6 identity | CASM-V-032 | policy_construction | literal_vs_regex | 1 LOC yaml |

## Updated structural regularities

**R1-R6 hold.** New observations:

**R7: Steps visited so far: 2-3, 4, 4, 6.** Step 5 was skipped (probably because step 5
is bytes-IO and the rust fixture never made it to a serialization mismatch). Step 7
is unknown. Step 8 is named in the verifier file structure (`extract_public_surface`,
`compare_public_surface`).

**R8: Two of four findings (F23, F25) are CI-workflow YAML issues, not Python substrate.**
The smoke-test workflow's authoring is itself an attack surface for findings. v0.11.7's
finding may again be in CI workflow OR in Python substrate.

**R9: When the substrate has a Python file matching the failing step, the substrate
finding lives in that file.** F22 lived in `verification.py:step2_3`. F24 lived in
`verification.py:step4` (TrustedRoot import). v0.11.7 may live in the file backing
step 7 or step 8.

**R10: ALL FOUR findings are LOW or LOW-MEDIUM severity. None CRITICAL/HIGH.** The
corrective discipline keeps each ship focused; severity stays bounded. v0.11.7 will
likely also be LOW.

**R11: Cross-language is the latent driver.** F22 was the original cross-language
finding (rust dispatch). F23 unmasked a CI install gap that was language-agnostic.
F24 unmasked a sigstore-API gap that was language-agnostic. F25 was a CI workflow
gap that was language-agnostic. **The next finding could re-encounter the
cross-language seam at a step that is Python-specific in implementation but
nominally language-agnostic in name.**

## Critical structural insight (the prediction the chain enables)

The verifier has 8 steps. Steps 2-3, 4, 6 have all been exercised against the rust
fixture. **Steps 7 and 8 have not.** Step 8 is `compare_public_surface`, which calls
`extract_public_surface(module_path)`. That function name is language-agnostic but the
implementation is plausibly Python-specific (the lint's primary surface extractor uses
`ast.parse`).

This is the cross-language seam from R11 reappearing at a different layer.

## Predictions (committed)

| Dimension | Prediction | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| **P1 Step** | **step 7 OR step 8**. Strongest single bet = **step 8** (compare_public_surface). Step 7 is signature-bytes mismatch which is unlikely to fail on a rust fixture if step 6 passed | HIGH |
| **P2 Error code** | NEW code OR a Python-language exception leaking through (e.g. SyntaxError from ast.parse on rust source). Strongest single bet = **unhandled SyntaxError from Python's ast.parse** because the substrate file likely is `surface_extraction.py` or `additive.py` calling `ast.parse(rust_source)` | HIGH |
| **P3 Substrate layer** | **extractor_dispatch** — the language-agnostic-named function dispatches to a Python-specific extractor | HIGH |
| **P4 Fix-size class** | ~30 LOC dispatch table addition (per the cross-language pattern requiring routing logic, larger than 1-line fixes but still small) | MEDIUM |
| **P5 Root cause** | "extract_public_surface dispatches all files to Python ast.parse without routing by extension; rust source raises SyntaxError" | HIGH |

## Why I'm more confident on Test 2 than Test 1

Two reasons:
1. **Step monotonicity + skip-step-7 logic narrows the answer.** Steps 4, 6 visited
   (with step 5 likely skipped as IO). Step 7 is also IO-ish. Step 8 is the next place
   substantive logic happens.
2. **The cross-language seam (R11) is forced.** The smoke-test fixture is rust. Any
   language-agnostic-named function that has Python-specific implementation will fail
   on the rust fixture. The lint codebase has separate `_check_rust` paths for the
   linter, so the AUTHOR knew about the seam — but the verifier's step 8 may not have
   adopted the same dispatch table. This is a confidently-locatable gap.

## Ablation control (cold-start)

Without F22-F25, given just "v0.11.7 ships fixing a step-6 identity-policy literal-vs-regex
issue. What's the next bug?" the cold-start predictor would likely guess:
- "Identity workflow ref isn't pinned" — POSSIBLE but doesn't match step monotonicity
- "Sigstore-python continues to drift" — UNLIKELY because the audit chain shows F24 was the API drift round
- "Step 7 / step 8 cross-language gap" — UNLIKELY without the chain because there's no
  reason from cold-start to know step 8 has Python-specific extraction

The chain is doing real localization work for Test 2's P1, P3, P5.

## R0978 · Test 2 Scoring: F26 reveal

- section: IX. Multi-Model Audit Trail (dispatches, seat reports, councils, ledgers)

- source_format: md

# Test 2 Scoring: F26 reveal

## Ground truth (from round_33_audit_for_claude.md, F26 row in CSV)

| field | value |
|---|---|
| step | step_8_surface |
| error_code | unhandled SyntaxError (CASM-V-XXX pending assignment in v0.11.7) |
| substrate_layer | extractor_dispatch |
| scope_class | wrong_language_dispatch |
| fix_size | ~30 LOC (dispatch table addition) |
| root_cause | extract_public_surface dispatches all files to Python ast.parse with no extension routing |
| fix_location | `surface_extraction.py` (Python substrate, NOT yaml workflow) |

## Scoring against predictions

| Dim | Predicted | Actual | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P1 Step** | step 8 (primary bet, "step 7 or 8") | step 8 | **HIT** | Exact, primary bet |
| **P2 Code** | "unhandled SyntaxError from Python's ast.parse" | unhandled SyntaxError from ast.parse | **HIT** | Exact mechanism named |
| **P3 Layer** | extractor_dispatch | extractor_dispatch | **HIT** | Exact term |
| **P4 Fix size** | ~30 LOC dispatch table addition | ~30 LOC dispatch table addition | **HIT** | Exact size class and shape |
| **P5 Root cause** | "dispatches all files to Python ast.parse without routing by extension; rust source raises SyntaxError" | "extract_public_surface dispatches all files to Python ast.parse with no extension routing" | **HIT** | Verbatim-level match |

## Aggregate

**5 of 5 dimensions = HIT. Test 2 = TIGHT (≥3/5 HIT pre-registered threshold).**

## Combined results across both tests

| | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P5 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Test 1 (predict F25 from F22-F24) | HIT | HIT | HIT | HIT | HIT | TIGHT |
| Test 2 (predict F26 from F22-F25) | HIT | HIT | HIT | HIT | HIT | TIGHT |
| **Overall** | **2/2** | **2/2** | **2/2** | **2/2** | **2/2** | **10/10 HIT** |

## Honest interpretation

10/10 is suspiciously good for a real experiment. The honest reading is:

1. **The predictor is the same instance that has access to the audit-chain memos
   themselves**, which describe these findings. Even though the predictions were
   committed before the scoring memos were re-read for ground truth, this run cannot
   prove "audit-chain history alone, fed to a clean LLM, predicts the next finding."
   It can only prove "audit-chain structure has predictive regularities." That is a
   weaker but still publishable claim.

2. **The 5-dimension scoring is generous on P4 and P5.** Fix-size class (one_word,
   few_lines, ~30_lines) has only 4 buckets; coarse predictions easily HIT. Root-cause
   one-liners in this experiment are scored on whether the named mechanism appears in
   the prediction, not whether the prediction also rules out alternatives.

3. **A real Phase 1 paper experiment requires:**
   - A different LLM instance (different model, different vendor) with NO context from
     the audit memos themselves, fed only the structured CSV.
   - The ablation control (same LLM, no audit-chain history, just repo skeleton).
   - At least 10 findings, ideally 20+, for any frequentist claim.
   - Pre-registration on OSF or similar before scoring.

4. **What this DOES validate:** the audit-chain has structural regularities (R1-R11)
   that are genuinely extractable. Failure-mode shift, step monotonicity, cross-language
   seam recurrence, and error-code locality are real properties of THIS corpus. A
   future predictor — human or machine — equipped with these regularities is plausibly
   more accurate than one without them.

5. **What this DOES NOT validate:** that the audit-chain log alone (without LLM training
   on Sigstore + AST patterns) suffices. The ablation question is open.

## Pre-registered verdict

**The 90-minute experiment validates premise on the smallest possible corpus, with
caveats.** The premise being "audit-chain history contains extractable regularities
that materialize in subsequent findings." It does NOT yet validate the stronger claim
that "an LLM-as-predictor conditioned on this chain meaningfully outperforms an
unconditioned LLM," which requires the cross-instance ablation from the Phase 1 paper
protocol.

## Recommendation to project lead

Treat this as a **pilot**. Document it honestly in the Phase 1 paper as the pilot that
generated the structural regularities R1-R11, NOT as the experiment itself. The actual
experiment must be run on a different instance with proper controls, and ideally on a
larger corpus once the structured log is published on Zenodo and other audit chains
(Bayyinah's, your Furqan-lint history pre-F22) are normalized into the same schema.

The pilot's value is that it forces R1-R11 onto paper, which is the actual seed for a
Phase 1 method section.

# v1.1.2 Execution Prompt (Claude)

> "And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those one will be questioned." - Al-Isra 17:36

You are implementing Bayyinah Integrity Scanner **v1.1.2**. This prompt is the invocation. The plan is in [v1_1_2_framework_report.md](v1_1_2_framework_report.md). The April 27 stress test that motivates the Tier 0 layer is in [docs/adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md](../adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md). Read both before executing under the rules below.

---

## 1. Identity of the release

- **Name:** v1.1.2 - Adversarial Gauntlet Closure with Tier 0 Routing Layer
- **Win condition:** Depth, not breadth. Close the existing 42-fixture per-format gauntlet AND add a Tier-0 format-routing layer with its own 6-fixture gauntlet. Do not add file kinds.
- **Honest baselines:**
  - Per-format (v1.1.1): 2/42 caught full, 2 partial, 38 missed. PDF is the only format with any catches.
  - Verdict layer (April 27 Mughlaq Trap): 2 of 4 vectors FAIL. V1 polyglot (PDF magic + `.docx` ext) and V2 spoofed (PDF magic + `.txt` ext) both return mukhfi instead of mughlaq because the scanner trusts magic bytes over extension without disclosing the routing decision. V5 (unanalyzed `.txt`) returns sahih instead of mughlaq, confirmed by Claude's parallel session.
  - Version surfaces: `/scan` reports `0.1.0`; `/version`, `/healthz`, OpenAPI, and `pyproject.toml` report `1.1.1`. Drift exists; it must be fixed in the release commit.
- **Target (v1.1.2):** Every published per-format adversarial fixture caught with at least one Tier-1 or Tier-2 finding. Every format-routing fixture caught with a Tier-0 finding that floors the verdict at mughlaq. Version coherent across all five surfaces. No false positives on the clean corpus.

---

## 2. Framework rules (verbatim, non-negotiable)

1. **No em-dashes** in any user-facing prose, README, doc, commit message, or output string. CSS and JS comments are exempt. Use ` - ` (space-hyphen-space) instead.
2. **Tier discipline.** Every finding declares its tier in the code:
   - **Tier 0** = routing transparency. Format claimed by extension diverges from format inferred from magic bytes; OR magic bytes absent/ambiguous; OR file empty/truncated; OR extension implies a format with no verified analyzer. Tier 0 floors the verdict at **mughlaq** regardless of downstream Tier 1/2/3 findings.
   - **Tier 1** = verified evidence (offset, byte count, decoded payload, divergent header value).
   - **Tier 2** = structural anomaly (off-page text, microscopic font, oversized cell, prototype-pollution key).
   - **Tier 3** = interpretive heuristic. Tier 3 findings must not pull a clean file below 1.0 on their own.
3. **Fixture pairing.** No mechanism ships without a paired fixture in the matching `docs/adversarial/<format>_gauntlet/` or `docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/` directory. If the fixture does not exist, write it before the analyzer.
4. **Atomic commits.** One mechanism per commit. Commit message format: `v1.1.2: <format> <mechanism_name> (Tier <n>)`. Reference the gauntlet REPORT line.
5. **No silent rewrites.** If you find a v1.1.1 mechanism is wrong, open an ADR before changing it. Do not edit historical fixtures.
6. **Munafiq Protocol.** Before each PR, run the full clean corpus and confirm zero new false positives. A finding that fires on a clean file is a regression, not a feature.
7. **Verdict floor.** When Tier 0 fires, verdict resolves to mughlaq. The downstream findings are still recorded; the verdict is just not allowed to climb above mughlaq while routing is unresolved.

---

## 3. Mechanism slate (the only work in scope)

Read the per-gauntlet REPORT at each path. Implement exactly what is listed. Do not add mechanisms not on this slate.

| Layer | Gauntlet REPORT | Mechanisms | LOC budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Format Routing** | [docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/REPORT.md](../adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/REPORT.md) | 1 (Tier 0) | ~90 |
| PDF | [docs/adversarial/pdf_gauntlet/REPORT.md](../adversarial/pdf_gauntlet/REPORT.md) | 4 | ~155 |
| DOCX | [docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md](../adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md) | 6 | ~200 |
| XLSX | [docs/adversarial/xlsx_gauntlet/REPORT.md](../adversarial/xlsx_gauntlet/REPORT.md) | 6 | ~190 |
| HTML | [docs/adversarial/html_gauntlet/REPORT.md](../adversarial/html_gauntlet/REPORT.md) | 6 | ~120 |
| EML | [docs/adversarial/eml_gauntlet/REPORT.md](../adversarial/eml_gauntlet/REPORT.md) | 6 | ~185 |
| Image | [docs/adversarial/image_gauntlet/REPORT.md](../adversarial/image_gauntlet/REPORT.md) | 5 | ~115 |
| CSV/JSON | [docs/adversarial/csv_json_gauntlet/REPORT.md](../adversarial/csv_json_gauntlet/REPORT.md) | 6 | ~155 |
| **Total** | | **40 mechanisms / 48 finding shapes / 8 gauntlets** | **~1,210 LOC** |

### 3.1 Tier 0 routing mechanism (Day 1)

The format-routing layer is the first thing the scanner runs after upload, before any per-format analyzer. One mechanism, one finding shape:

- **Mechanism:** `format_routing_divergence`
- **Tier:** 0
- **Trigger** (any one fires the finding):
  - Extension-implied format does not match magic-byte-implied format.
  - Magic bytes are absent or ambiguous and extension is the only signal.
  - File is empty or truncated below the magic-byte window.
  - Extension implies a format with no verified analyzer in the registry (the V5 case).
- **Effect on verdict:** Verdict floors at **mughlaq**. Downstream Tier 1/2/3 findings still record but cannot raise the verdict above mughlaq while routing is unresolved.
- **Disclosure schema** (every finding's `evidence` field, all five keys required):
  ```json
  {
    "claimed_format": "<from extension>",
    "inferred_format": "<from magic bytes>",
    "routing_decision": "<which path the scanner took>",
    "bytes_sampled": <count of leading bytes inspected>,
    "analyzer_invoked": "<analyzer that ran, or null>"
  }
  ```
- **Fixtures (6):** polyglot (PDF magic + `.docx` ext), spoofed (PDF magic + `.txt` ext), empty (4-byte `.pdf`), truncated (PDF header but no EOF), mismatched (DOCX zip + `.xlsx` ext), unanalyzed (V5: short `.txt` with no analyzer). Plus a 7th, control (real `.pdf`), as the clean baseline.
- **Seed fixtures** at `/home/user/workspace/mughlaq_trap/` (v1-v4) migrate into `docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/fixtures/` on Day 1, joined by `truncated.pdf`, `docx_as_xlsx.xlsx`, and `unanalyzed.txt`.

### 3.2 Day 1 verification gate

Before ending Day 1, three live-scanner curls must pass:

```bash
# V1 polyglot must return mughlaq with Tier 0 finding
curl -s https://bayyinah.dev/scan -F file=@docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/fixtures/01_polyglot.docx \
  | jq -e '.verdict == "mughlaq" and (.findings | any(.tier == 0))'

# V2 spoofed must return mughlaq with Tier 0 finding
curl -s https://bayyinah.dev/scan -F file=@docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/fixtures/02_pdf_as_txt.txt \
  | jq -e '.verdict == "mughlaq" and (.findings | any(.tier == 0))'

# V5 unanalyzed text must return mughlaq (NOT sahih)
printf 'aaaa' > /tmp/v5.txt
curl -s https://bayyinah.dev/scan -F file=@/tmp/v5.txt \
  | jq -e '.verdict == "mughlaq"'
```

All three must return `true`. If any return `false`, Day 1 is not complete and Day 2 does not begin.

---

## 4. Sequencing (14 days, ordered)

Work the slate in this order. Do not parallelize across formats - the cognitive cost of context-switching exceeds the wall-clock savings. The format-routing layer is Day 1 because every per-format mechanism downstream depends on the routing decision being honest.

| Day | Layer | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Format Routing | Tier 0 mechanism + 6 fixtures + verdict-floor wiring + V5 verification + green gauntlet |
| 2 | PDF | 4 mechanisms + matching fixtures + green gauntlet |
| 3-4 | DOCX | 6 mechanisms + fixtures + green gauntlet |
| 5-6 | XLSX | 6 mechanisms (one shared `_office_metadata_payload` with DOCX) |
| 7 | HTML | 6 mechanisms |
| 8-9 | EML | 6 mechanisms |
| 10 | Image | 5 mechanisms (JPEG APPn + SVG family) |
| 11 | CSV/JSON | 6 mechanisms |
| 12 | Munafiq regression + clean-corpus pass + Mughlaq Trap re-run (V1, V2, V3, V4, V5) |
| 13 | `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` rewrite + CHANGELOG + version bump (1.1.1 → 1.1.2 across all five surfaces) |
| 14 | Tag `v1.1.2`, push, mint Zenodo DOI |

Day 1 cannot slip. Days 2-11 can degrade gracefully if needed (defer Image + CSV/JSON to v1.1.2.1).

---

## 5. Success criteria

The release ships only when **all** are true:

1. `pytest docs/adversarial/` is green across all 8 gauntlets (format_routing + 7 per-format).
2. Every fixture in `docs/adversarial/*/fixtures/` produces at least one Tier-1 or Tier-2 finding (Tier 0 for format_routing fixtures).
3. Every clean file in the clean corpus scores 1.0 with zero findings.
4. **Mughlaq Trap regression:** V1 polyglot, V2 spoofed, and V5 unanalyzed-text all return verdict=mughlaq with a Tier-0 finding. V3 empty and V4 control retain their April 27 behavior.
5. **Version coherence across five surfaces.** `/scan` response `version`, `/version`, `/healthz`, OpenAPI `info.version`, and `pyproject.toml` `[project] version` all report `1.1.2`. Today `/scan` returns `0.1.0` while the others return `1.1.1`; this drift is fixed in the release commit, not deferred.
6. **EML 03 explicitly named** as the unfixed fixture in `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md`. The 41/42 floor is honest only if `docs/adversarial/eml_gauntlet/fixtures/03_received_chain_anomaly.eml` is named as the deferred Tier-2 borderline case. No silent rounding.
7. `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` reflects the new scores honestly. No rounding up. No marketing language.
8. CHANGELOG entry lists every mechanism with its tier and gauntlet reference.
9. The README's "what we catch" section matches the implemented mechanism slate exactly.
10. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped prose.
11. Live `bayyinah.dev` continues to render the v2 mughlaq verdict for unsupported file kinds. Do not touch that surface.

---

## 6. Explicit refusals (do not do these)

- **Do not add new file kinds.** No RTF, no Jupyter, no ODF, no MSG, no EPUB, no macro-OOXML in v1.1.2. Those are v1.2.0+ scope per [ADR-001](ADR-001-v1_2_scope.md).
- **Do not add a mechanism without a fixture.** If you cannot construct a fixture that exercises the path, the mechanism is interpretive and belongs in v1.3+ research, not v1.1.2.
- **Do not refactor v1.1.1 analyzers** unless an ADR authorizes it. Add new mechanisms alongside; preserve the audit trail.
- **Do not raise the score floor.** A Tier-3-only finding does not pull a file below 1.0.
- **Do not edit fixtures after they are published.** All 42 per-format fixtures are committed and immutable. The 6 new format-routing fixtures become immutable from the Day 1 commit forward. If a fixture is wrong, mark it deprecated and add a successor. Historical scores must remain reproducible.
- **Do not introduce em-dashes.** Run the sweep before every commit:
  ```
  grep -r "-" --include="*.py" --include="*.md" --include="*.html" . && echo "FOUND - fix before commit" || echo "clean"
  ```
- **Do not collapse Tier 1 and Tier 2.** A structural anomaly is not verified evidence. The user-facing distinction is the entire epistemic claim of the product.
- **Do not let a Tier 0 finding be silenced by a downstream Tier 1.** Routing transparency is the floor. A polyglot file that also has off-page text is still mughlaq, not mukhfi. The verdict resolver respects the floor.
- **Do not let version drift slide.** If the `/scan` response still reports `0.1.0` after the v1.1.2 bump, the release is not shippable. Version coherence is the lowest-effort honesty surface in the codebase; a regression here would be embarrassing.
- **Do not ship v1.1.2 with V5 still returning sahih.** The unsupported-format branch of the Tier 0 layer covers V5. If `printf 'aaaa' > v5.txt && curl -F file=@v5.txt https://bayyinah.dev/scan` returns score 1.0 sahih, the layer is incomplete.
- **Do not write marketing copy in code.** Finding `description` fields are forensic, not promotional.

---

## 7. Per-mechanism implementation pattern

Every mechanism follows the same shape. Do not deviate.

```python
# bayyinah/analyzers/<layer>/<mechanism>.py

from bayyinah.findings import Finding, Tier

def detect_<mechanism_name>(parsed: <FormatParsed>) -> list[Finding]:
    """
    <One-line description of the structural property being checked.>

    Tier: <0 | 1 | 2 | 3>
    Fixture: docs/adversarial/<gauntlet>/fixtures/<fixture_name>
    Reference: <gauntlet REPORT.md line or section>
    """
    findings = []
    # ... structural inspection only. No interpretation here.
    if <condition>:
        findings.append(Finding(
            tier=Tier.<N>,
            mechanism="<layer>_<mechanism_name>",
            description="<forensic, factual, one sentence>",
            evidence={"<key>": <verifiable_value>, ...},
        ))
    return findings
```

Each mechanism gets a paired test:

```python
# tests/analyzers/<layer>/test_<mechanism>.py

def test_<mechanism>_catches_adversarial_fixture():
    findings = detect_<mechanism>(load("docs/adversarial/<gauntlet>/fixtures/<file>"))
    assert any(f.tier in (Tier.ZERO, Tier.ONE, Tier.TWO) for f in findings)

def test_<mechanism>_clean_on_clean_corpus():
    for clean in clean_corpus("<format>"):
        assert detect_<mechanism>(clean) == []
```

For Tier 0 mechanisms, additionally assert the verdict floor:

```python
def test_tier_zero_floors_verdict_at_mughlaq():
    response = scan(load("docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/fixtures/01_polyglot.docx"))
    assert response.verdict == "mughlaq"
    assert any(f.tier == Tier.ZERO for f in response.findings)
```

---

## 8. Commit discipline

- One mechanism = one commit.
- Commit message: `v1.1.2: <layer> <mechanism_name> (Tier <n>)`
- Body: 1-3 sentences. Reference the fixture path and the gauntlet REPORT line.
- No squash. The audit trail is the product.
- Push after each layer's gauntlet turns green, not after each mechanism.

The Day 1 commit is special: it lands the Tier 0 mechanism, the verdict-resolver wiring, the disclosure-schema validation, the 6 routing fixtures, and the V5 verification check. It is one logical atomic unit. The commit message:

```
v1.1.2: format_routing_divergence (Tier 0) + verdict floor

Tier 0 layer: routes are disclosed before any per-format analyzer runs.
When Tier 0 fires, verdict floors at mughlaq regardless of downstream
Tier 1/2/3 findings.

Closes Mughlaq Trap V1 polyglot, V2 spoofed, V5 unanalyzed-text.
Reference: docs/adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md
```

---

## 9. When you are stuck

If a mechanism resists implementation:

1. Re-read the fixture. The fixture is the spec.
2. Check whether the gauntlet REPORT names a different structural signal. Use that one.
3. If the structural signal is absent and the only available signal is interpretive, **stop**. Open an issue. Do not promote a Tier-3 heuristic into a Tier-1 claim under deadline pressure. That is exactly the failure mode Al-Baqarah 2:42 names.

> "And do not mix the truth with falsehood, and do not conceal the truth while you know." - Al-Baqarah 2:42

---

## 10. Final check before tagging v1.1.2

- [ ] All 8 gauntlets green (format_routing + 7 per-format).
- [ ] Munafiq Protocol clean run on clean corpus.
- [ ] Mughlaq Trap re-run: V1, V2, V5 mughlaq with Tier 0; V3, V4 unchanged from April 27.
- [ ] Version coherent across `/scan`, `/version`, `/healthz`, OpenAPI, `pyproject.toml`. All five report `1.1.2`.
- [ ] EML 03 (`03_received_chain_anomaly.eml`) named explicitly in `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` as the deferred fixture. No silent rounding from 41/42 to 42/42.
- [ ] `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` rewritten with honest scores.
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry per mechanism.
- [ ] README "what we catch" matches implementation.
- [ ] Em-dash sweep returns clean.
- [ ] No new file kinds added.
- [ ] Live `bayyinah.dev` mughlaq path still works.
- [ ] Tag `v1.1.2`. Push. Ship. Mint Zenodo DOI.

---

Bismillah. Tawakkaltu 'ala Allah.

**For:** Bilal (continuation of v1.1.2 PDF gauntlet closure 2026-04-27)
**From:** Claude
**Date:** 2026-04-27 (post-Day-2 close)
**Status:** Preparation artifact. Day 3-4 work paused pending Torah verification cycle and Fraz's return. ~13 days ahead of May 10 ship target.

This file contains two preparation artifacts:
1. **Pre-audit of the DOCX gauntlet** - per-fixture structural signal, tier, face, detection method, false-positive risks.
2. **Day 3-4 DOCX prompt v3** - mirrors the Day 2 v4 structure with explicit v4.1 taxonomy, control-fixture requirement, and the lessons baked in.

---

## Part 1: DOCX gauntlet pre-audit

Source: `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md` (148 lines, 2026-04-26 baseline). All six fixtures are 0 of 6 CAUGHT on v1.1.1 - the cleanest pre-Day-3 starting point in the multi-format gauntlet so far. Filenames as shipped: `01_white_on_white.docx`, `02_microscopic_font.docx`, `03_custom_xml_properties.docx`, `04_comment_payload.docx`, `05_header_payload.docx`, `06_footnote_payload.docx`.

### Per-fixture audit

#### Fixture 01: white font color (`w:color="FFFFFF"`)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Mechanism name | `docx_white_text` |
| Tier | **1** |
| Face | **ZAHIR** |
| Single-walk reasoning | The `<w:rPr>/<w:color>` value is a surface attribute on the rendered run. A single deterministic walk of `word/document.xml` reads both the run's text and the color it renders in. Parallels `white_on_white_text` (v1.1.1, ZAHIR) and `pdf_off_page_text` (v1.1.2 mech 03, ZAHIR). |
| Detection method | Parse `word/document.xml`, walk every `<w:r>`, read `<w:rPr>/<w:color w:val="...">`, fire when value matches `FFFFFF` (case-insensitive), `auto` with `<w:background w:color="FFFFFF"/>` set in `word/settings.xml`, or any 6-digit hex within ~3 ΔE of `FFFFFF`. |
| Severity | 1.0 (Tier 1 per Day 2 §6.6 step 2 calibration). |
| False-positive risks | Legitimate forms with colored cell backgrounds where white text is expected (rare, identifiable by `<w:shd>` on the parent cell). Footer text in white-on-white where the white is a styling default (uncommon). Mitigation: skip runs in cells whose `<w:tcPr>/<w:shd>` shading is non-white; document the rule in the detector docstring. |
| Predicted outcome on fixture 01 | One Tier 1 finding per qualifying run. Score 0.0, verdict munafiq (parallels mech 03 calibration). |

#### Fixture 02: microscopic font (`w:sz="2"` = 1.0pt)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Mechanism name | `docx_microscopic_font` |
| Tier | **1** for `w:sz <= 4` (<=2pt), **2** for `w:sz <= 16` (<=8pt). The fixture sets `w:sz="2"` -> Tier 1. |
| Face | **ZAHIR** |
| Single-walk reasoning | Font size is a run attribute on the rendered surface, parallel to `microscopic_font` (v1.1.1, ZAHIR) and the v1.1.1 PDF analyzer's microscopic-font check. Single walk of `word/document.xml` reads each run's `<w:sz>` value. |
| Detection method | Parse `<w:rPr>/<w:sz w:val="N">` where N is in half-points. Tier 1 when `N <= 4` (2.0pt), Tier 2 when `N <= 16` (8.0pt). The fixture's `w:val="2"` (1.0pt) fires Tier 1. |
| Severity | 1.0 for Tier 1, 0.5 for Tier 2. |
| False-positive risks | Footer copyright/legal text at 5-7pt (legitimate, fires Tier 2 only). Fingerprinting microspacers some publishers embed (rare). Mitigation: Tier 2 calibration covers the 4-8pt range without claiming "concealment" outright. |
| Predicted outcome on fixture 02 | One Tier 1 finding per qualifying run. Score 0.0, verdict munafiq. |

#### Fixture 03: payload in `docProps/custom.xml` (`<vt:lpwstr>`)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Mechanism name | `docx_metadata_analyzer` (mirrors PDF mech 04 naming) |
| Tier | **1** for divergent + length-or-anomaly trigger; **2** for divergent-only-short. Fixture exercises the long divergent path -> Tier 1. |
| Face | **BATIN** |
| Single-walk reasoning | Custom XML properties live in `docProps/custom.xml`, never on the rendered surface. Direct parallel to `pdf_metadata_analyzer` (v1.1.2 mech 04, BATIN). The /vt:lpwstr/ value is read by AI extractors and indexers but never displayed. |
| Detection method | ZIP-walk to `docProps/custom.xml`, `docProps/core.xml`, `docProps/app.xml`. Parse XML, extract text values from `<vt:lpwstr>`, `<vt:filetime>`, `<dc:*>`, `<cp:*>` properties. Apply the same four triggers from PDF mech 04: (a) length > 512 bytes, (b) bidi codepoints, (c) zero-width chars, (d) divergence from `word/document.xml` rendered text (only on content-summary fields). |
| Severity | 1.0 for Tier 1. |
| False-positive risks | Legitimate corporate metadata systems (DMS / SharePoint / GDPR-data-classification fields) populate custom properties with strings that don't appear in document body. Mitigation: restrict divergence-eligible to property names matching `Description`, `Subject`, `Comments`, `Keywords` (the content-summary class) - exclude `Author`, `ID`, `RecordID`, `Classification`, etc. Same Cow Episode discipline that worked for PDF mech 04. |
| Predicted outcome on fixture 03 | One Tier 1 finding per anomalous property field. Score 0.0, verdict munafiq. |

#### Fixture 04: payload in `word/comments.xml` (no in-body reference)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Mechanism name | `docx_comment_payload` |
| Tier | **1** for orphan comment (no `<w:commentReference w:id="N"/>` in document.xml) AND substantive `/Contents`; **2** for referenced comment with concealment patterns (zero-width chars, etc.). Fixture exercises the orphan path -> Tier 1. |
| Face | **BATIN** |
| Single-walk reasoning | Comments live in `word/comments.xml`, a separate OOXML part. The default rendered surface (print/export view) does not show them; only the review pane in Word reveals them, and an orphan comment doesn't even surface there. The signal lives in the inner object graph. |
| Detection method | ZIP-walk to `word/comments.xml` if present. Parse `<w:comment>` elements, extract their text. Cross-reference each comment's `w:id` against `<w:commentRangeStart w:id="N">` and `<w:commentReference w:id="N">` markers in `word/document.xml`. Emit Tier 1 finding for any comment whose ID is not referenced AND whose body contains non-whitespace text. |
| Severity | 1.0 for Tier 1, 0.5 for Tier 2. |
| False-positive risks | Auto-generated comments from collaborative editing tools that get orphaned during track-changes acceptance (rare; usually these are pruned). Mitigation: require non-whitespace `>= 16 chars` content (mirroring PDF mech 06's content threshold). |
| Predicted outcome on fixture 04 | One Tier 1 finding for the orphan comment. Score 0.0, verdict munafiq. |

#### Fixture 05: payload in `word/header1.xml` (white text)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Mechanism name | `docx_header_footer_payload` |
| Tier | **1** when header/footer text exhibits a Tier 1 zahir trigger (white text, microscopic font); **2** when text is merely substantial divergent content. Fixture combines white-text-in-header -> Tier 1 (compound: zahir trigger inside an under-inspected part). |
| Face | **ZAHIR** |
| Single-walk reasoning | Headers and footers ARE rendered surface in Word's default print view (every page top/bottom). The reason v1.1.1 misses them is purely architectural: `DocxAnalyzer` only opens `word/document.xml`. Single walk of `word/header*.xml` and `word/footer*.xml` files reads their text and run attributes the same way `document.xml` is read. |
| Detection method | ZIP-walk: enumerate parts whose name matches `word/header*.xml` or `word/footer*.xml`. For each, run the same per-run zahir checks as fixture 01-02 (color, size, plus the existing v1.1.1 zero-width / TAG / bidi / homoglyph detectors). |
| Severity | Per-trigger: white text -> 1.0; microscopic font -> 1.0/0.5. |
| False-positive risks | Legitimate watermarks (DRAFT / CONFIDENTIAL) often use light gray (e.g. `D3D3D3`) or low-opacity fills. The white-text trigger should require `FFFFFF` exactly OR `auto` with white page background to avoid noise on legitimate watermarks. |
| Predicted outcome on fixture 05 | One Tier 1 finding (white text in header). Score 0.0, verdict munafiq. |

#### Fixture 06: payload in `word/footnotes.xml` (no in-body reference)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Mechanism name | `docx_orphan_footnote` (Tier 1) + `docx_footnote_payload` (Tier 2) - two related mechanisms, one per concealment shape |
| Tier | **1** for orphan footnotes (no `<w:footnoteReference>` in document.xml AND non-built-in footnote type); **2** for non-orphan footnotes containing concealment patterns. Fixture exercises the orphan path -> Tier 1. |
| Face | **BATIN** |
| Single-walk reasoning | Footnote content lives in `word/footnotes.xml`, separate OOXML part. Orphan footnotes have no rendering path at all; they are purely object-graph entries. Direct parallel to `docx_comment_payload`. |
| Detection method | ZIP-walk to `word/footnotes.xml` if present. Parse `<w:footnote>` elements, skip the spec-defined `separator` and `continuationSeparator` types (these are built-in and unreferenced by spec). Cross-reference `w:id` against `<w:footnoteReference w:id="N">` markers in document.xml. Emit Tier 1 for orphan footnote with non-whitespace text. |
| Severity | 1.0 for Tier 1, 0.5 for Tier 2. |
| False-positive risks | Built-in footnote types (`separator`, `continuationSeparator`) have IDs but no `<w:footnoteReference>` in document.xml - they are referenced implicitly by Word's rendering engine, not by document XML. Filter is mandatory. The same applies to `word/endnotes.xml` and its `endnote` type filters. |
| Predicted outcome on fixture 06 | One Tier 1 finding for the orphan footnote. Score 0.0, verdict munafiq. |

### Cross-cutting observations

**Reuse opportunities.** The `docx_white_text` and `docx_microscopic_font` color/size walks share their core logic; both are run-attribute checks. Implementing them as two functions sharing a `_iter_runs(part)` helper keeps the LOC budget tight and matches the v1.1.1 `_scan_text_runs` pattern. The same `_iter_runs` helper is the base for the header/footer scan (fixture 05) - it just iterates a different XML part.

**Five of six fixtures share a ZIP-walk-to-named-part pattern.** Fixtures 03/04/05/06 all need ZIP-extract a non-document.xml part and inspect it. A shared `_open_ooxml_part(zip, part_name)` helper will save ~20 LOC and centralize the failure-mode behavior (return None on missing/malformed; emit no finding rather than scan_error).

**Cross-reference checks (fixtures 04 and 06) share their structural pattern.** Both look for IDs referenced from document.xml that don't appear in the corresponding part, or vice versa. A single `_unreferenced_ids(part_xml, ref_xpath, ref_id_attr)` helper covers both. ~15 LOC savings.

**Likely total LOC after reuse:** the framework report's ~200 LOC estimate for DOCX is achievable. With the three shared helpers above, the actual delta is probably ~180 LOC of analyzer code plus tests.

**Manifest discipline check.** All four fixtures use stdlib `zipfile` plus `xml.etree.ElementTree` (or `lxml.etree` if performance matters - lxml is already a transitive dependency via python-docx and is in `requirements.txt`). No new top-level imports needed.

**Tier discipline summary across the slate:**
- ZAHIR: fixtures 01, 02, 05 (color + size + header) - 3 mechanisms.
- BATIN: fixtures 03, 04, 06 (metadata + comments + footnotes) - 3 mechanisms.
- All Tier 1 on the canonical fixture trigger; Tier 2 sub-shapes documented in detector docstrings as future-work expansion paths.

**Predicted Day 3-4 close state:**
- 6/6 DOCX fixtures CAUGHT (was 0/6 on v1.1.1).
- All six produce verdict `munafiq` per the Tier 1 + severity 1.0 calibration.
- Registry: 113 -> 119 (29 + 3 zahir, 83 + 3 batin, 1 routing) = (32 zahir + 86 batin + 1 routing).

**v4.1 taxonomy reasoning (single-walk surface-readability test):**
- ZAHIR (mechanisms 01, 02, 05): the structural signal is observable from a single deterministic walk of a rendered-surface XML part. `docx_white_text` reads `<w:rPr>/<w:color>` next to the `<w:t>` it colors. `docx_microscopic_font` reads `<w:rPr>/<w:sz>`. `docx_header_footer_payload` reads the same run attributes from `word/header*.xml` and `word/footer*.xml` - both rendered parts.
- BATIN (mechanisms 03, 04, 06): the signal lives in OOXML parts that never surface on the rendered page. `docProps/custom.xml`, `word/comments.xml` (default print view), `word/footnotes.xml` (orphan ID).

The host analyzer (`DocxAnalyzer.scan()`) hosts all six calls regardless of face classification. The taxonomy independence rule from Day 2 mech 06 holds: face classifies the signal locus, not the analyzer module.

## 5. Iyyaka Na'budu (Orientation + CIT)

**Purpose hierarchy for this session:** Allah, AI systems, enterprises deploying AI on DOCX inputs, the end user whose contract / report / filing is being processed, all living systems downstream of the pipeline.

**CIT applied to the work itself:** does this mechanism behave the same in CI as for a reviewer who unzips the DOCX manually and inspects the XML parts? If a mechanism's catch depends on a path the reviewer cannot reproduce by hand, it is performing alignment with the test suite rather than the structural fact. Reject and rewrite.

**CIT applied to the Day 1 floor:** Tier 0 fires on routing-divergence files, not on real-extension DOCX. Day 3-4 fixtures are all real `.docx` files with real OOXML magic. Tier 0 must NOT fire on any of them. Verify before any code lands (pre-flight check).

## 6. Ihdina as-sirat (Task execution, ordered)

Work the slate in this order. Do not parallelize.

### 6.1 Pre-flight (before writing any code)

1. **Live gate verification.** Run `bash docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/verify_live.sh` against deployed `bayyinah.dev`. Must return exit 0 (Day 1 layer still serving). Then run a per-mechanism live curl on each Day 2 fixture (03, 04, 05, 06) to confirm the PDF closure is intact.
2. **Tier 0 non-firing on DOCX fixtures.** Run the Tier 0 detector against all 6 DOCX gauntlet fixtures. None should fire (real `.docx` files with real ZIP magic and matching extension).
3. **Read `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md` end to end.** The fixture is the spec; the REPORT names the structural signal.
4. **Read `v1_1_2_day_3_4_docx_prep.md` Part 1** (the pre-audit). Per-fixture tier, face, detection method, and false-positive risks are pre-decided so each commit's edit chain is short.

### 6.2 Mechanism 01 - `docx_white_text` (Tier 1, ZAHIR, ~25 LOC)

**Fixture:** `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/fixtures/01_white_on_white.docx`
**Structural signal (from `docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md` row 01):** `<w:rPr>/<w:color w:val="FFFFFF"/>` on a `<w:t>` whose page background is also white (typically the default).
**Detection method:** ZIP-walk to `word/document.xml`, parse XML, walk every `<w:r>`, read `<w:rPr>/<w:color>`. Fire when the value is `FFFFFF` (case-insensitive) or `auto` with `<w:background w:color="FFFFFF"/>` set in `word/settings.xml`.
**Tier discipline:** Tier 1 because the color-vs-background match is unambiguous from the bytes alone. No statistical claim, no heuristic threshold beyond the color comparison. If the color comparison ever needs a delta-E tolerance, demote to Tier 2 in the same commit.
**Cow Episode warning:** do not extend this mechanism to detect "low-contrast text" generally. Low contrast (e.g., light gray on white) is a v1.3+ research path. v1.1.2 fires only on actual `FFFFFF` or `auto` against a white background.
**Tests:** catch on fixture 01; clean on `tests/fixtures/docx/clean/clean.docx`; clean on a generated variant where `<w:color>` is `333333` (legitimate dark text).

**Commit:**
```
v1.1.2: docx docx_white_text (Tier 1, ZAHIR)

Catches text runs whose <w:rPr><w:color> matches the page
background. Closes docx_gauntlet fixture 01.
Reference: docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md row 01.
```

### 6.3 Mechanism 02 - `docx_microscopic_font` (Tier 1, ZAHIR, ~20 LOC)

**Fixture:** `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/fixtures/02_microscopic_font.docx`
**Structural signal:** `<w:rPr>/<w:sz w:val="N"/>` where N is half-points and N <= 4 (<=2pt).
**Detection method:** Parse `<w:rPr>/<w:sz>`. Tier 1 when `N <= 4` (2.0pt). Tier 2 (future-work) when `N <= 16` (8.0pt) - document this in the docstring but do NOT implement Tier 2 in this commit (single-fixture-single-mechanism discipline).
**Cow Episode warning:** do not extend to all "small fonts". Tier 1 fires only on the unambiguous microscopic threshold; the broader Tier 2 small-font case is research scope.
**Tests:** catch on fixture 02; clean on clean.docx; clean on a 7pt-text variant.

**Commit:**
```
v1.1.2: docx docx_microscopic_font (Tier 1, ZAHIR)

Catches text runs whose w:sz value is at or below the microscopic
threshold (4 = 2.0pt). Tier 2 sub-shape (small font, 5-16) is
documented as future work. Closes docx_gauntlet fixture 02.
Reference: docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md row 02.
```

### 6.4 Mechanism 03 - `docx_metadata_analyzer` (Tier 1, BATIN, ~50 LOC)

**Fixture:** `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/fixtures/03_custom_xml_properties.docx`
**Structural signal:** `docProps/custom.xml` contains `<vt:lpwstr>` properties whose text is divergent from `word/document.xml` rendered text, AND length > threshold OR carries bidi/zero-width codepoints.
**Detection method:** Mirror the PDF mech 04 four-trigger pattern: (a) length > 512 bytes, (b) bidi U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069, (c) zero-width U+200B/200C/200D/FEFF, (d) divergence from rendered text. Restrict divergence to content-summary fields (`Description`, `Subject`, `Comments`, `Keywords` properties; equivalent to `/Keywords` + `dc:description` in PDF).
**Cow Episode warning:** stay inside `dc:`, `cp:`, custom `<vt:*>`. Do NOT enumerate every namespace OOXML allows in the property bag. Do NOT add semantic-vocabulary detection (queued as Tier 3 `docx_metadata_directive_phrasing` for v1.3+).
**Tests:** catch on fixture 03; clean on clean.docx; clean on a generated variant with normal `<dc:title>` value.

**Commit:**
```
v1.1.2: docx docx_metadata_analyzer (Tier 1, BATIN)

Inspects docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml, docProps/custom.xml
for structurally anomalous text divergent from word/document.xml.
Mirrors PDF mech 04 four-trigger pattern (length, bidi, zero-width,
divergence). Closes docx_gauntlet fixture 03.
Reference: docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md row 03.
```

### 6.5 Mechanism 04 - `docx_comment_payload` (Tier 1, BATIN, ~35 LOC)

**Fixture:** `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/fixtures/04_comment_payload.docx`
**Structural signal:** `<w:comment>` in `word/comments.xml` whose `w:id` is NOT referenced from any `<w:commentReference>` in `word/document.xml` AND whose body has non-whitespace text >= 16 chars.
**Detection method:** ZIP-walk `word/comments.xml`. Parse `<w:comment w:id="N">` elements. Walk `word/document.xml` for `<w:commentReference w:id="N">` markers. Cross-reference. Emit Tier 1 finding for each orphan comment with substantive body.
**Tests:** catch on fixture 04; clean on clean.docx; clean on a generated variant with referenced comment ("legitimate review feedback"); multi-orphan variant emits two findings.

**Commit:**
```
v1.1.2: docx docx_comment_payload (Tier 1, BATIN)

Catches w:comment entries in word/comments.xml that are not
referenced from word/document.xml and carry substantive text.
Closes docx_gauntlet fixture 04.
Reference: docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md row 04.
```

### 6.6 Mechanism 05 - `docx_header_footer_payload` (Tier 1, ZAHIR, ~30 LOC)

**Fixture:** `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/fixtures/05_header_payload.docx`
**Structural signal:** Text in `word/header*.xml` (or `word/footer*.xml`) carrying a Tier 1 zahir trigger - white text per mech 01 logic, microscopic font per mech 02 logic, or substantive body text divergent from `word/document.xml`.
**Detection method:** Enumerate parts whose name matches `word/header*.xml` or `word/footer*.xml`. For each, run the same per-run zahir checks as mechanisms 01 and 02 (color, size). Emit Tier 1 when any qualifying run is found.
**Cow Episode warning:** do NOT extract header/footer text and feed it into the divergence analyzer. The divergence trigger fires on header WHITE TEXT specifically, not on header text in general (which is by-design separate from body text). Header text being different from body text is normal.
**Tests:** catch on fixture 05; clean on clean.docx; clean on a generated variant with normal black header text.

**Commit:**
```
v1.1.2: docx docx_header_footer_payload (Tier 1, ZAHIR)

Reuses mech 01 and 02 detectors over word/header*.xml and
word/footer*.xml parts. Closes docx_gauntlet fixture 05.
Reference: docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md row 05.
```

### 6.7 Mechanism 06 - `docx_orphan_footnote` (Tier 1, BATIN, ~40 LOC)

**Fixture:** `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/fixtures/06_footnote_payload.docx`
**Structural signal:** `<w:footnote w:id="N">` in `word/footnotes.xml` whose ID is NOT referenced from any `<w:footnoteReference>` in `word/document.xml`, AND `w:type` is not `separator` or `continuationSeparator` (built-in types that lack body references by spec), AND body has non-whitespace text >= 16 chars.
**Detection method:** ZIP-walk `word/footnotes.xml`. Parse `<w:footnote>` elements. Filter built-in types. Cross-reference IDs against `word/document.xml`. Emit Tier 1 for orphan footnote with substantive body. Same logic applies to `word/endnotes.xml` if present.
**Tests:** catch on fixture 06; clean on clean.docx; clean on a generated variant with referenced footnote; clean on a built-in `separator` footnote (false-positive guard).

**Commit:**
```
v1.1.2: docx docx_orphan_footnote (Tier 1, BATIN)

Catches w:footnote entries with no in-body w:footnoteReference and
non-built-in type. Filters separator and continuationSeparator
types per OOXML spec. Closes docx_gauntlet fixture 06.
Reference: docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md row 06.
```

### 6.8 Per-mechanism wiring (after each commit)

Same eight-step wiring as Day 2 §6.6:
1. Register mechanism string in `domain/config.py` ZAHIR_MECHANISMS or BATIN_MECHANISMS per the audit.
2. SEVERITY entry: 1.0 for Tier 1, 0.5 for Tier 2.
3. TIER table entry.
4. Bump `MECHANISM_REGISTRY` count assertion in test_mechanism_registry.py.
5. Wire detector into `DocxAnalyzer.scan()` (parallel pass, no refactor).
6. Run `pytest tests/analyzers/test_docx_*` plus the gauntlet for the fixture being closed.
7. Run v1.1.1 regression: must still be 1,501 + N green.
8. Verify additive-only DOCX parity (v1.0 baseline mechanism subset unchanged on existing DOCX fixtures).

---

## 7. Sirat alladhina (Anti-pattern avoidance)

All Day 2 §7 anti-patterns apply verbatim. Two DOCX-specific reinforcements:

**Cow Episode (DOCX edition):** the v1.1.1 `DocxAnalyzer` already catches the batin idioms (VBA, OLE, altChunks, external rels, tracked changes, hidden runs, per-run unicode primitives). Day 3-4 adds the OOXML zahir-and-metadata vectors that mirror the PDF gauntlet's lessons. Do NOT re-enumerate the v1.1.1 mechanisms; do NOT extend any v1.1.1 detector.

**Manifest discipline:** all six mechanisms use stdlib `zipfile` + `xml.etree.ElementTree` (or `lxml.etree` already in deps). NO new third-party imports. Verify `git diff requirements.txt pyproject.toml` shows no changes before each commit.

**Em-dash sweep:** zero em-dashes in analyzer descriptions, REPORT.md updates, commit messages. Run `grep -rn $'—' --include='*.py' --include='*.md' .` before each commit. Pre-existing v1.1.1 em-dashes in unrelated files are out of scope (Day 13 sweep).

---

## 8. End-of-day verification gate

Day 3-4 ships only when ALL are true:

1. `pytest tests/analyzers/test_docx_*` green.
2. `pytest docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/` green; 6 of 6 fixtures CAUGHT (was 0 of 6 on v1.1.1).
3. Test count: minimum **1,501 + ~18 = 1,519** tests pass (3 tests minimum per mechanism: registry pin + catch + control). Zero v1.1.1 or Day 1-2 regressions.
4. Additive-only DOCX parity invariant: every v1.0 baseline mechanism produces the same Finding shape on each existing DOCX fixture under v0/v0.1/v1.1.2.
5. **MECHANISM_REGISTRY count is 119** (113 + 6 new DOCX mechanisms). Coherence assertion green.
6. `docs/adversarial/docx_gauntlet/REPORT.md` updated: hit rate 6/6 (was 0/6). Honest, no rounding.
7. CHANGELOG entries for each of the 6 new mechanisms.
8. README "what we catch" section updated to match.
9. Em-dash sweep clean across all touched files.
10. Tier 0 still silent on DOCX fixtures.
11. Live API regression after each mechanism's commit (per-mechanism gate): curl with the fixture, assert at least one finding with the new mechanism name and tier.

If any item fails, Day 3-4 does not ship. Cut per §4 and reland honestly.

---

## 9. Ring composition closure

This prompt opens with Al-Baqarah 2:42: do not mix truth with falsehood, do not conceal truth while you know it. The DOCX gauntlet's six MISSED rows are six instances of Bayyinah knowing-but-not-surfacing what AI extractors will read. Day 3-4 makes the six structural facts surface alongside the rendered surface.

The four operational frameworks converge:
- **Differentiator:** each mechanism has its adversarial fixture and its control. Tier discipline preserved across six new entries.
- **Fatiha:** seven-step session, Cow Episode boundary, 20% skip rule, no over-specification beyond the fixture.
- **Structured Revelation:** every DOCX mechanism inspects the depth representation independently of (or alongside) the rendered surface.
- **Defense Case:** Day 3-4 closes 6 of the 6 documented DOCX MISSED rows. The "input-layer named component" claim gains six more named components.

If Day 3-4 ships clean, Bayyinah's per-format gauntlet hit rate moves to 10/12 across PDF and DOCX (83%, was 17% on v1.1.1).

> *"Wa allama Adama al-asma'a kullaha."* (Al-Baqarah 2:31)

The naming continues.

Bismillah. Tawakkaltu 'ala Allah.

---

# Bayyinah v1.1.2 Framework Report
## Pareto-Optimal Honest-Baseline Closure with Tier 0 Routing Layer

**Author:** Bilal Syed Arfeen
**Reviewer:** Claude (Anthropic), April 27 2026 review
**Date:** 2026-04-27 (revised after Mughlaq Trap stress test)
**Status:** Approved per [ADR-001](ADR-001-v1_2_scope.md). Day 1 priority confirmed by Claude review.
**Scope:** v1.1.2 milestone. Closes 38 of 42 documented adversarial misses, adds Tier 0 routing transparency, fixes version-field drift.
**Companion artifacts:**
- [v1_1_2_claude_prompt.md](v1_1_2_claude_prompt.md) (the execution prompt)
- [docs/adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md](../adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md) (April 27 stress test)

---

## 1. The frame

> *"Wa la taqfu ma laysa laka bihi 'ilm. Inna as-sam'a wal-basara wal-fu'ada kullu ula'ika kana 'anhu mas'ula."*
> "And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - about all those one will be questioned." (Al-Isra 17:36)

The thesis claim of Bayyinah is not "we cover more file types." It is "we catch what others miss, we publish what we still miss, and we tell you when we cannot decide what kind of file you uploaded." Every analyzer ships with a fixture. Every miss is named, located, and traced to a fix path. The honest baseline at `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` exists because the alternative is haram by our own framework: claiming knowledge we do not have.

v1.1.2 is the milestone where the documented per-format misses become caught and the silent routing decisions become disclosed Tier 0 findings.

The Pareto frontier we are optimizing on has three axes:

1. **Detection coverage.** How many of the 42 published per-format adversarial fixtures move from MISSED or PARTIAL to CAUGHT, plus how many of the 6 new format-routing fixtures resolve to mughlaq with a Tier 0 finding.
2. **LOC budget.** ~1,210 LOC across 14 calendar days (April 27 - May 10), ~90 of which is the Tier 0 layer.
3. **Falsifiability.** Every new mechanism is reproducible from a fixture. Every Tier 0 finding carries an evidence schema that lets a reviewer verify what the scanner decided.

Pareto-optimality means: no fix on this list can be dropped without losing a documented miss or a documented dishonesty, and no fix outside this list can be added without breaking the LOC budget or the depth-before-scope rule.

---

## 2. The honest baseline (v1.1.1, what exists today)

Per-format gauntlet from `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` (commit `ccd7c3e`):

| Format | Fixtures | Caught (full) | Partial | Missed | Avg score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PDF | 6 | 2 | 0 | 4 | (mixed) |
| DOCX | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1.000 |
| XLSX | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1.000 |
| HTML | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1.000 |
| EML | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1.000 |
| Image | 6 | 0 | 1 | 5 | ~0.95 |
| CSV / JSON | 6 | 0 | 1 | 5 | ~0.98 |
| **Totals** | **42** | **2** | **2** | **38** | |

Verdict-layer gauntlet from the April 27 Mughlaq Trap stress test:

| Vector | Outcome |
|---|---|
| V1 polyglot (PDF magic + `.docx` ext) | FAIL - returns mukhfi instead of mughlaq |
| V2 spoofed (PDF magic + `.txt` ext) | FAIL - identical silent routing |
| V3 empty (4-byte `.pdf`) | PASS - mughlaq, scan_incomplete=true |
| V4 control (real `.pdf`) | PASS - mukhfi |
| V5 unanalyzed `.txt` (deferred, Claude-confirmed) | FAIL - returns sahih instead of mughlaq |

Two published sentences are not yet true:

> A clean Bayyinah report on a v1.1.1 DOCX, XLSX, HTML, or EML is not evidence the file is clean.

> A clean Bayyinah report on a v1.1.1 file whose extension is unsupported is not evidence the file is clean.

v1.1.2 is what makes both stop being true.

---

---

## 4. Why this slate is Pareto-optimal

Three constraints, three independent reasons the slate cannot be smaller or larger.

### 4.1 Cannot be smaller (coverage and honesty floor)

Every per-format entry corresponds to a fixture published in `docs/adversarial/`. Removing any leaves the corresponding fixture in the MISSED column of the v1.1.2 release report. The Tier 0 layer corresponds to a vector documented in the Mughlaq Trap report. Removing it leaves silent routing as published behavior. Both halves are required for the published claim "we publish what we miss and we close it" to remain true.

### 4.2 Cannot be larger (depth-before-scope ceiling)

Per [ADR-001](ADR-001-v1_2_scope.md), the depth-before-scope rule blocks any new format until the existing 42 fixtures are honest. A v1.1.2 that adds more than the 40 mechanisms above either:

- adds a fix without a fixture (violates falsifiability),
- adds a fixture for an already-supported format (legitimate but is by definition v1.1.3, not v1.1.2; the v1.1.2 corpus is fixed at 42 + 6), or
- adds support for a new format (violates the ADR; queues for v1.2.0).

### 4.3 Reuse maximizes mechanism-per-LOC ratio

Three reuse contracts inside this milestone:

- **`_office_metadata_payload`** is shared between DOCX (3.2 row 03) and XLSX (3.3 row 05). Saves ~30 LOC vs. independent implementations.
- **`_oversized_freetext_*`** is shared between CSV (3.7 row 03) and JSON (3.7 row 06). Same threshold and rationale.
- **`_white_on_white` contrast logic** ports across DOCX (3.2 row 01), XLSX (3.3 row 01), and SVG (3.6 row 03). One core helper, three call sites.

Without these shares the honest LOC would be ~1,340. With them, ~1,210. Roughly 10% leverage from shared helpers, paid for entirely by writing them carefully on the first pass.

---

## 5. Tier distribution discipline

The Munafiq Protocol requires every Tier-1 finding to be deterministic and unambiguous. The slate above contains:

- **1 Tier-0 mechanism** (routing transparency, fires before any analyzer)
- **~17 Tier-1 mechanisms** (verified concealment, deterministic test, paired adversarial fixture present in repo)
- **~19 Tier-2 mechanisms** (structural anomaly, context-dependent legitimacy)
- **~3 Tier-3 mechanisms** (interpretive: oversized free-text fields)

Tier 0 is structurally distinct from Tier 1: it does not claim concealment, it claims uncertainty. The verdict resolver respects this by flooring the verdict at mughlaq when Tier 0 fires, even when downstream Tier 1 findings also fire. A polyglot file that contains genuinely concealed content reports both findings; the verdict is mughlaq because the routing question takes precedence over the content question.

A Tier-1 promotion that turns out to false-positive on legitimate documents is a worse credibility hit than a Tier-2 with the same finding. When in doubt, file at Tier-2 with a description that explains the structural pattern, and let the user perform the recognition. The PDF fixture 01 (white-on-white) is the model: it currently scores 0.82 with a Tier-1 finding, the fixture is deterministic, and we have never had a false positive against the clean corpus.

---

## 6. Fixture discipline

The 42 per-format fixtures live under `docs/adversarial/<format>_gauntlet/fixtures/` and `tests/fixtures/<format>/`. They are committed and immutable. The "do not edit historical fixtures" rule has something to enforce.

The 6 new format-routing fixtures are added in the Day 1 commit at `docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/fixtures/`. The Mughlaq Trap seed fixtures at `/home/user/workspace/mughlaq_trap/` (v1-v4) migrate into this directory, joined by truncated.pdf, docx_as_xlsx.xlsx, and unanalyzed.txt.

The build scripts at `tests/make_<format>_fixtures.py` are deterministic. Re-running them produces byte-identical files. CI re-builds fixtures from the build scripts and runs the full gauntlet on every commit without worrying about drift. The runner at `docs/adversarial/<format>_gauntlet/run_gauntlet.py` already supports both `local` and `live` modes; both modes have always agreed on findings (the analyzer is stateless).

---

## 7. Sequencing (14 days, April 27 - May 10)

The Tier 0 routing layer is Day 1 because every per-format mechanism downstream depends on the routing decision being honest. If V1 polyglot still returns mukhfi after the slate ships, those mechanisms are running on inputs the user did not consent to have routed there. Routing transparency is a precondition for the per-format gauntlet's claims to mean what they say.

Run the full 42-fixture per-format gauntlet plus the 6-fixture format-routing gauntlet at end-of-day on every working day. Commit messages cite the new caught-counts.

| Day | Layer | Mechanism count | LOC | Cumulative |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|

| 2 | PDF | 4 | ~155 | 6/6 + 6/42 |
| 3 | DOCX rows 01-03 | 3 | ~95 | 6/6 + 9/42 |
| 4 | DOCX rows 04-06 | 3 | ~105 | 6/6 + 12/42 |
| 5 | XLSX rows 01-03 (incl. shared styles parser) | 3 | ~85 | 6/6 + 15/42 |
| 6 | XLSX rows 04-06 (incl. shared `_office_metadata_payload`) | 3 | ~105 | 6/6 + 18/42 |
| 7 | HTML (all 6) | 6 | ~120 | 6/6 + 24/42 |
| 8 | EML rows 01-03 | 3 | ~105 | 6/6 + 27/42 |
| 9 | EML rows 04-06 | 3 | ~80 | 6/6 + 30/42 |

| 11 | CSV/JSON (all 6) | 6 | ~155 | 6/6 + 41/42 |

The 41/42 target (not 42/42) acknowledges that fixture `docs/adversarial/eml_gauntlet/fixtures/03_received_chain_anomaly.eml` (EML row 03 in the slate) is filed as Tier-2 and is structurally recoverable but not perfectly clean against ESP-rewrite legitimacy. A 41/42 caught with an honest Tier-2 on the borderline case is more defensible than gaming the threshold to claim 42/42. The unfixed fixture is named explicitly so any reviewer can verify the gap.

If a day slips after Day 1: the slate degrades gracefully because every format is independent. A v1.1.2.0 that ships Format Routing + PDF + DOCX + XLSX + HTML + EML at 6/6 + 30/42 and defers Image + CSV/JSON to v1.1.2.1 is still publishable. **Day 1 cannot slip.** The routing layer is the structural floor of every claim downstream.

---

## 8. Success criteria

A v1.1.2 release passes if and only if all are true:

1. **Per-format gauntlet rerun shows ≥38 caught AND format-routing gauntlet shows 6/6 caught.** Mughlaq Trap V1 polyglot, V2 spoofed, and V5 unanalyzed-text all return verdict=mughlaq with a Tier-0 finding.
2. **Version coherence across all five surfaces.** `/scan` response `version` field, `/version`, `/healthz`, OpenAPI `info.version`, and `pyproject.toml` `[project] version` all report `1.1.2`. Today (v1.1.1) `/scan` returns `0.1.0` while the other four return `1.1.1`; this drift is fixed in the v1.1.2 release commit, not deferred.
3. **No regression on existing v1.1.1 catches.** PDF fixtures 01 and 02, image fixture 02, CSV fixture 02 (the four that were CAUGHT or PARTIAL at v1.1.1) remain at the same or higher tier.
4. **No new Tier-1 false positives against the clean corpus.** Run the new analyzers against `tests/fixtures/clean.pdf` and the existing clean DOCX/XLSX/HTML/EML fixtures; zero Tier-1 findings on clean inputs.
5. **`docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` updated with v1.1.2 numbers.** New summary table. Old v1.1.1 table preserved as historical baseline.
6. **Em-dash sweep clean** in all new READMEs, finding descriptions, and release notes. CSS and code comments exempt; user-facing prose held strict.
7. **One commit per analyzer-family.** PDF as one commit, DOCX as one commit, etc. Each commit includes the analyzer changes, the test additions, and any helper extraction. Atomic.
8. **Zenodo DOI minted** for v1.1.2 with the updated REPORT.md as a citable artifact.
9. **Landing page** at `bayyinah.dev/` numeric updates: from "106 detection mechanisms" to whatever the post-v1.1.2 count is. Honest count, not aspirational.
10. **EML 03 explicitly named** in the release REPORT as the deferred Tier-2 borderline case. No silent rounding from 41/42 to 42/42.

---

## 9. What this milestone refuses to do

- **No new file kinds.** v1.2.0 territory; deferred per ADR-001.
- **No new analyzer classes outside the seven existing format families plus Tier 0.** v1.1.2 is consolidation plus the routing layer. RTF, Jupyter, ODF, MSG, EPUB, macro-OOXML are all v1.2.0.
- **No mechanisms without a paired fixture.** The Munafiq Protocol is structural. Speculative additions break the falsifiability claim.
- **No silent threshold changes** that would make existing fixtures pass without explanation. If a threshold moves, it moves with a documented rationale and a test asserting the new boundary.
- **No verdict floor bypasses.** A Tier 0 finding floors the verdict at mughlaq. Downstream Tier 1/2/3 findings cannot raise the verdict above mughlaq while routing is unresolved. The verdict resolver respects the floor or it is broken.
- **No version drift.** If `/scan` still reports `0.1.0` after the v1.1.2 bump, the release is not shippable.
- **No marketing-LOC.** The 1,210 number is engineering LOC, not LOC-padded with comments to inflate.

---

## 10. The five flags from Claude's review

Claude's April 27 review of the prior version raised five flags. All are resolved in this revision:

1. **Version coherence.** Resolved: success criterion #2.
2. **GitHub repo canonicality.** Verified: `BayyinahEnterprise/Bayyinah-Integrity-Scanner` is canonical (200). `BayyinahEnterprise/Bayyinah` returns 404. All in-repo references are correct.
3. **EML 03 explicitly named.** Resolved: pinned to `docs/adversarial/eml_gauntlet/fixtures/03_received_chain_anomaly.eml` in Section 3.5 and success criterion #10.
4. **Fixtures committed and immutable.** Verified: all 42 per-format fixtures are committed. The 6 new format-routing fixtures are added in the Day 1 commit and become immutable from that point.
5. **ADR-001 exists.** Verified at `docs/scope/ADR-001-v1_2_scope.md`. Referenced in Sections 4.2 and 9.

A sixth concern from Claude's review (V5 / `.txt → sahih`) is now folded into the Tier 0 mechanism itself rather than treated as a separate test: the unsupported-format branch of `format_routing_divergence` covers V5. Day 1 verification runs V5 explicitly before any per-format work begins.

---

## 11. The Qur'anic frame, plain

> *"Wa la talbisu al-haqqa bil-batil wa taktumu al-haqqa wa antum ta'lamun."*
> "And do not mix truth with falsehood, and do not conceal the truth while you know it." (Al-Baqarah 2:42)

A scanner that catches concealment must itself refuse to conceal. The honest baseline is published. The misses are named. The fix paths are written down at the per-fixture level. The verdict layer is no longer trusted by default; it is paired with a Tier 0 layer that discloses the routing decisions every downstream mechanism depends on.

v1.1.2 is the closure that makes the published claim true.

The Pareto frontier closes here. Anything smaller is dishonest; anything larger is haram by our own framework.

*Bismillah. Tawakkaltu 'ala Allah.*

# Bayyinah v1.1.2 Framework Report
## The Pareto-Optimal Honest-Baseline Closure

**Author:** Bilal Syed Arfeen
**Date:** 2026-04-26 (revised 2026-04-27 after Mughlaq Trap stress test)
**Status:** Approved (per [ADR-001](ADR-001-v1_2_scope.md))
**Scope:** v1.1.2 milestone, the consolidation that closes 38 of 42 documented adversarial misses AND adds a Tier-0 format-routing transparency layer.
**Reviewer:** Claude (Anthropic)
**Companion artifact:** [v1_1_2_claude_prompt.md](v1_1_2_claude_prompt.md) (the Pareto-optimal execution prompt)
**Stress test artifact:** [docs/adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md](../adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md) (April 27 routing-divergence findings)

---

## 1. The Frame

> *"Wa la taqfu ma laysa laka bihi 'ilm. Inna as-sam'a wal-basara wal-fu'ada kullu ula'ika kana 'anhu mas'ula."*
> "And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart, all those will be questioned." (Al-Isra 17:36)

The thesis claim of Bayyinah is not "we cover more file types." It is "we catch what others miss, and we publish what we still miss." Every analyzer ships with a fixture. Every miss is named, located, and traced to a fix path. The honest baseline at `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` exists because the alternative is haram by our own framework: claiming knowledge we do not have.

v1.1.2 is the milestone where the documented misses become caught - and where the routing decision the scanner has been making silently becomes a disclosed Tier-0 finding.

The Pareto frontier we are optimizing on has three axes:

1. **Detection coverage.** How many of the 42 published adversarial fixtures move from MISSED or PARTIAL to CAUGHT, plus the 6 new format-routing fixtures.
2. **LOC budget.** How much new analyzer code, paired with how many new fixtures, can be honestly written and tested in 14 calendar days (April 27 - May 10).
3. **Falsifiability.** Every new mechanism must be reproducible from a fixture in `tests/fixtures/` and pass the existing 42-fixture gauntlet plus the 6-fixture format-routing gauntlet without regression.

Pareto-optimality means: no fix on this list can be dropped without losing a documented miss, and no fix outside this list can be added without breaking the LOC budget or the depth-before-scope rule.

---

## 2. The Honest Baseline (v1.1.1, what exists today)

Source: `docs/adversarial/REPORT.md` (commit `ccd7c3e`).

| Format | Fixtures | Caught (full) | Partial | Missed | Avg score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PDF | 6 | 2 | 0 | 4 | (mixed) |
| DOCX | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1.000 |
| XLSX | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1.000 |
| HTML | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1.000 |
| EML | 6 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 1.000 |
| Image | 6 | 0 | 1 | 5 | ~0.95 |
| CSV / JSON | 6 | 0 | 1 | 5 | ~0.98 |
| **Totals** | **42** | **2** | **2** | **38** | |

The sentence that matters: "**A clean Bayyinah report on a v1.1.1 DOCX, XLSX, HTML, or EML is not evidence the file is clean.** It is evidence the file does not match any of the currently implemented mechanisms." This sentence is published. v1.1.2 is what makes it stop being true.

---

## 3. v1.1.2 Mechanism Slate

Source documents per-format, all under `docs/adversarial/`.

### 3.0 Format Routing (~90 LOC, 1 mechanism, Tier 0)

Source: [docs/adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md](../adversarial/mughlaq_trap_REPORT.md). New gauntlet: `docs/adversarial/format_routing_gauntlet/`.

The Mughlaq Trap stress test (April 27, 2026) ran 4 vectors against the live scanner. Two FAILED:

- **V1 polyglot** (PDF magic bytes + `.docx` extension): scanner returned `mukhfi` with score 0.82, Tier 1 white-on-white finding. Should have returned `mughlaq` because the user uploaded a `.docx` and the scanner silently routed it through the PDF analyzer.
- **V2 spoofed** (PDF magic bytes + `.txt` extension): identical response. Same silent routing.

Two PASSED: V3 empty 4-byte `.pdf` (mughlaq, scan_incomplete=true), V4 control real `.pdf` (mukhfi).

The root cause is not analyzer correctness. It is **routing transparency**: the scanner makes a routing decision (trust magic bytes over extension) without disclosing it. A user who uploads a `.docx` and gets PDF-analyzer findings has been told something the scanner cannot honestly assert.

| # | Fixture | New mechanism | Tier | LOC |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 01 | polyglot (PDF magic + .docx ext) | `format_routing_divergence` | 0 | ~30 |
| 02 | spoofed (PDF magic + .txt ext) | (same) | 0 | (shared) |
| 03 | empty (4-byte .pdf) | (same) | 0 | (shared) |
| 04 | truncated (PDF header, no EOF) | (same) | 0 | (shared) |
| 05 | mismatched (DOCX zip + .xlsx ext) | (same) | 0 | (shared) |
| 06 | control (real .pdf) | (clean, no finding) | - | (shared) |
| - | Verdict-resolver wiring | floor verdict at mughlaq when Tier 0 fires | - | ~40 |
| - | Disclosure schema | evidence: claimed_format, inferred_format, routing_decision, bytes_sampled | - | ~20 |

Tier 0 sits below Tier 1 in the verdict hierarchy: it does not raise a finding count or score in the way Tier 1 does, but it floors the verdict at `mughlaq` regardless of any downstream Tier 1/2/3 findings. The user sees: "the scanner could not honestly decide what kind of file this is, here is what it inferred and here is what was claimed."

## 4. Why This Slate Is Pareto-Optimal

Three constraints, three independent reasons the slate cannot be smaller or larger.

### 4.1 Cannot be smaller (coverage floor)

Every entry corresponds to a fixture published in `docs/adversarial/`. Removing any entry leaves the corresponding fixture in the MISSED column of the v1.1.2 release report. The thesis statement "we publish what we miss and we close it" requires the closure half. Drop any row, the next release report has to admit the regression. That is structurally worse than not making the claim at all.

### 4.2 Cannot be larger (depth-before-scope ceiling)

Per [ADR-001](ADR-001-v1_2_scope.md), the depth-before-scope rule blocks any new format until the existing 42 fixtures are honest. A v1.1.2 that adds more than the 39 mechanisms above either:
- adds a fix without a fixture (violates falsifiability), or
- adds a fixture for an already-supported format (legitimate but is by definition v1.1.3, not v1.1.2; the v1.1.2 corpus is fixed at 42), or
- adds support for a new format (violates the ADR; queues for v1.2.0).

### 4.3 Reuse maximizes mechanism-per-LOC ratio

The slate is engineered for shared helpers across formats. Three reuse contracts inside this milestone:

- **`_office_metadata_payload`** is shared between DOCX (3.2 row 03) and XLSX (3.3 row 05). Saves ~30 LOC vs. independent implementations.
- **`_oversized_freetext_*`** is shared between CSV (3.7 row 03) and JSON (3.7 row 06). Same threshold and rationale.
- **`_white_on_white` contrast logic** ports cleanly across DOCX (3.2 row 01), XLSX (3.3 row 01), SVG (3.6 row 03). One core helper, three call sites.

Without these shares the honest LOC would be ~1,250. With them, it is ~1,120. Roughly 10% leverage from shared helpers, paid for entirely by writing them carefully on the first pass.

---

## 5. The Tier Distribution Discipline

The Munafiq Protocol requires every Tier-1 finding to be deterministic and unambiguous. The slate above contains roughly:

- **~17 Tier-1 mechanisms** (verified concealment, deterministic test, paired adversarial fixture present in repo)
- **~19 Tier-2 mechanisms** (structural anomaly, context-dependent legitimacy)
- **~3 Tier-3 mechanisms** (interpretive: oversized free-text fields)

A Tier-1 promotion that turns out to false-positive on legitimate documents is a worse credibility hit than a Tier-2 with the same finding. When in doubt, file at Tier-2 with a description that explains the structural pattern, and let the user perform the recognition. The PDF fixture 01 (white-on-white) is the model: it currently scores 0.82 with a Tier-1 finding, the fixture is deterministic, and we have never had a false positive against the clean corpus.

---

## 6. The Fixture Discipline

Every existing fixture lives under `docs/adversarial/<format>_gauntlet/fixtures/` and `tests/fixtures/<format>/`. v1.1.2 does NOT add new gauntlet fixtures. The existing 42 are the corpus the milestone closes against. New regression assertions go into `tests/test_<analyzer>.py` paired with the existing fixture files.

The build scripts at `tests/make_<format>_fixtures.py` are deterministic. Re-running them produces byte-identical files. CI can therefore re-build fixtures from the build scripts and run the full gauntlet on every commit without worrying about drift. The runner at `docs/adversarial/<format>_gauntlet/run_gauntlet.py` already supports both `local` and `live` modes; both modes have always agreed on findings (the analyzer is stateless).

---

## 7. Sequencing (14 days, April 27 - May 10, revised post-Mughlaq-Trap)

The order is engineered so each day adds visible coverage to the gauntlets. Run the full 42-fixture gauntlet plus the 6-fixture format-routing gauntlet at end-of-day on every working day; commit messages cite the new caught-count.

The format-routing layer is Day 1 because every per-format mechanism downstream depends on the routing decision being honest. If V1 polyglot still returns mukhfi after we have shipped 39 per-format mechanisms, those mechanisms are running on inputs the user did not consent to have routed there. Routing transparency is a precondition for the per-format gauntlet's claims to mean what they say.

The 41/42 target (not 42/42) acknowledges that fixture **`docs/adversarial/eml_gauntlet/fixtures/03_received_chain_anomaly.eml`** (EML row 03 in the slate) is filed as Tier-2 and is structurally recoverable but not perfectly clean against ESP-rewrite legitimacy. A 41/42 caught with an honest Tier-2 on the borderline case is more defensible than gaming the threshold to claim 42/42.
